target.recipe_text:
crock pot chicken with black beans   cream cheese

i love this crock-pot chicken recipe for two reasons: one, my family loves it and two, it is so easy to make! i got this recipe from my sister. she has two children of her own, and they love it too! it's also the best leftovers in the world -- if there are any!

1. take 4-5 frozen , yes , frozen , boneless chicken breasts put into crock pot
2. add 1 can of black beans , drained , 1 jar of salsa , 1 can of corn drained
3. keep in crock pot on high for about 4-5 hours or until chicken is cooked
4. add 1 package of cream cheese and let sit for about 1 / 2 hour
5. all done and enjoy !
target.review: Is this the best meal that I have ever had?  No, not even close, but I'm going to give this five stars because it is extremely easy to prepare, and it come out exactly as it states.  I got just what I was hoping for on a busy work evening, and it was very tasty and nourishing.  The sauce was very thin when I opened the crock pot lid, but if you let it set up for about 10-15 minutes, it thickens.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pasta with sausage  tomatoes  and cream

delicious and satisfying... i don't remember where this recipe comes from, but it's a pleaser! easily doubled.  also, works well with gf pasta and sausage

1. heat oil in a heavy skillet over medium heat
2. add sausage and crushed red pepper
3. cook until sausage is no longer pink , stirring frequently , about 7 minutes
4. add onion and garlic to skillet and cook until onion is tender and sausage is light brown , stirring occasionally , about 7 minutes
5. add tomatoes , cream , and salt
6. simmer until mixture thickens slightly , about 4 minutes
7. cook pasta in large pot of boiling water
8. drain
9. bring sauce to a simmer
10. add pasta to sauce and cook until pasta is heated through and sauce thickens , stirring occasionally , about 2 minutes
11. divide pasta between plates
12. sprinkle with parsley
13. serve , passing parmesan separately
demonstrations.review: My husband had three big helpings and my daughter had two.  My picky son ate his share without too many complaints (and that is a big success regarding him.)  I added fresh basil at the end, and thought that was delicious.  I will make this again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
awesome baked pork chops

these chops remain moist and tender, and the sauce is to die for! you probably have all the ingredients in your kitchen to make this! serve these chops over rice!

1. preheat oven to 350
2. rinse pork chops , pat dry , and season with garlic powder and seasoning salt to taste
3. place the beaten eggs in a small bowl
4. dredge the pork chops lightly in flour , dip in the egg , and coat liberally with bread crumbs
5. heat the oil in a medium skillet over medium-high heat
6. fry the pork chops 5 minutes per side , or until the breading appears well browned
7. transfer the chops to a 9 x 13 baking dish , and cover with foil
8. bake in the preheated oven for 1 hour
9. while baking , combine the cream of mushroom soup , milk and white wine in a medium bowl
10. after the pork chops have baked for an hour , cover them with the soup mixture
11. replace foil , and bake for another 30 minutes
demonstrations.review: The picture looks just like it does when it comes out of the oven.  I thought that the chops were very, very tender, and if I could give 5 stars just for that, I would.  However, I thought that the breading came out soggy in the end, and the browning time was too long.  Even on medium/high heat, 5 minutes turned my chops too dark.  If I were to make this again, I would brown it less, and add the sauce during the last 15 minutes, perhaps.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
thanksgiving turkey brine

brining the turkey with this recipe makes a very moist turkey!  delicious!

1. combine all ingredients in a stock pot , bring mixture to a boil , lower heat and simmer for 15-20 minute allow brine to cool completely
2. rinse turkey under cook running water , inside and out
3. pat turkey dry with paper towels , then immerse turkey in cooled brine
4. turkey should be completely submerged in liquid
5. my pot wasn't big enough , so the
6. cover the pot and refrigerate for 8-10 hours or up to 24 hours
7. remove turkey , rinse , pat dry and roast as usual
demonstrations.review: Very nice brine.  The oranges and spices were a good addition.

target.recipe_text:
kathy s cake mix cookies

my mom always makes her cookies this way. this recipe uses brown sugar, which many other cake mix cookie recipes do not. experiment with cake mix flavors and add-ins. vanilla with chocolate chip, chocolate with peanut butter chips, banana with butterscotch chips...!

1. mix all ingredients together
2. spoon balls , about 1 t , onto cookie sheets
3. bake at 350 for 10 minutes
4. cool completely on cooling rack
target.review: excellent cookies, followed recipe, added and mixed in crushed andie's mints to half the batter and sprinkled sugar on the top of the cookies from the other half of the batter, baked for 11 minutes on parchment paper. they were perfect, crisp on the outside, moist in the middle.  thanks for a great recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
amazing chicken marinade

this recipe came from allrecipes (ruth crickmer). my whole family loved it even though it cooked too fast. the original recipe said 'high heat' on the grill, which my husband did. it ended up cooking 8 minutes total, charred but not burnt tasting, and very juicy and flavorful. we'll turn down the heat next time for texture, but this is a keeper in our home!

1. in a large , non-reactive container , whisk together ingredients beginning with cider vinegar through salt
2. then whisk in olive oil and pepper
3. place chicken in the mixture
4. cover and marinate chicken in the fridge 8 hours or overnight
5. remove chicken from marinade just before you turn on your grill or broiler to let come up a few degrees
6. discard marinade
7. lightly oil your grill or broiler pan
8. grill or broil about 10 minutes per side
demonstrations.review: Made this as written except for the mustard, my husband is not a fan so I omitted it.  Otherwise followed the recipe.  I only marinated the chicken for 6 hours and it was still so delicous.  Can't wait to see how good it is after an over night marinade.  I made 12 drumsticks and baked them on a cookie sheet with parchment paper on the lowest rack position in the oven at 400 degrees and cooked for approx. 20 - 23 min. flipping the drumsticks over once 1/2 way through cooking.  Moist and full of flavor, thank you for a great marinade.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
tri tip roast    delicious

a tri-tip is also called a triangle roast. it's a very lean cut of meat that does not contain much fat. if you do not see it, ask for it. do not over cook this cut of meat. do not cook it more than medium. note: there are 24 hours of inactive prep time in refrigerator.

1. combine all ingredients , except garlic and rosemary , and blend well
2. place roast in an oven-proof baking dish
3. cover roast with the marinade and place in the refrigerator for 24 hours , turning and basting a few times , ending with the fat side down
4. preheat oven to 425 degrees
5. sprinkle the garlic powder and crushed rosemary over the top of the roast
6. puncture the roast with a fork all over the top , and bake for 30-40 minutes , or until a meat thermometer reads 135 degrees for medium-rare
7. remove from oven and allow to rest about 5 to 10 minutes
8. carve against the grain and serve , using the juices as a gravy
demonstrations.review: Excellent!  You can't go wrong, this is so easy and so delicious.  My family loves tri tip and I am horrible on the grill so this was a great alternative for me.  I did reduce the amount of oil to 1/3 cup and left out the worcestershire, I also punctured the meat prior to marinating.  I  used fresh crushed garlic and fresh rosemary for my rub.  I doubled the cooking time on a 2 1/2 lb. roast and the meat was perfect, moist and full of flavor! Thanks for a great recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mashed red potatoes with garlic and parmesan

the potatoes are ready in our garden, and this is the first recipe i reach for! these are so good!!

1. put potatoes and garlic in lg pan
2. cover with water
3. bring to a boil
4. reduce heat and simmer for 25 minutes , until potatoes are tender
5. drain well
6. mash with the butter , milk , and salt
7. stir in the parmesan cheese
demonstrations.review: Yummy!  The only change I made to the recipe was to saute an additional 2 cloves of garlice in the butter before adding the potatoes to mash.

target.recipe_text:
the ospidillo cafe italian salad dressing

i always offer two dressings on the table here at the ospidillo cafe; the stone pipe inn salad recipe #136181 and this one. when i place salads on the table, my guests typically query, "where's that good salad dressing that you make?" i just point to the two carafes and about half take one and half take the other; they taste nothing alike.

1. blend all ingredients in a mixer for 20 minutes
2. refrigerate for at least 30 minutes before serving
3. when dressing gets too cold it will solidify somewhat , due to the olive oil , so allow it to set out 1 / 2 hour or so if this happens
4. also , i prefer to use tupelo honey when i have it available which is much higher quality in flavor than regular clover honey
5. for the italian spices , i use 2 teaspoons of dee514's italian blend spice mix recipe #38293
6. here it is:
7. 2 tablespoons basil , 2 tablespoons marjoram , 1 tablespoon garlic powder , 1 tablespoon oregano , 1 tablespoon thyme , 1 tablespoon rosemary , 1 tablespoon crushed red pepper flakes
target.review: Really a good dressing. Went perfectly with dinner tonight. Thanks for sharing.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
creamy potato salad

have you ever posted a recipe and just love reading the reviews for it?  this is my signature potato salad.  whenever there is a pot luck function at work, i am told that i have to bring the potato salad.  no one else is allowed to and i am never given a choice.  thank you everyone who ever tried this potato salad and for leaving such glowing reviews for it.  you all have made me look so good.  i personally can not stand eggs or raw onions, so i leave them out but i know most people don't think a potato salad is complete without them.  thanks again for so many wonderful reviews. (psssst....check out my recipe #123107 as well.  it shares the dressing with this recipe but tastes much much different because of the different ingredients) please see recipe #242966 for bacon bit tips.

1. cook potatoes in boiling , salted water until tender
2. drain well
3. peel and cube potatoes
4. transfer to a large bowl
5. add celery , onion , sweet relish and bacon bits
6. combine mayo , sugar , celery seed , vinegar , mustard , and salt
7. add mayo mixture to potatoes
8. toss lightly to coat potato mixture
9. carefully fold in the chopped eggs
10. cover and chill thoroughly
11. bacon bit
12. use a sharp knife and cut the frozen bacon into long strips about 1 / 4 inch wide
13. turn the bacon and cut the strips into pieces also about 1 / 4 in wide
14. you now have perfect raw bacon pieces to fast fry
15. no need to separate
16. they will separate during cooking
17. perfect bacon bits
demonstrations.review: I have found the perfect potato salad! Outstanding!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
drew s homemade pimiento cheese   spicy or mild

you'll never buy pimiento cheese again! if you want a milder version, omit the cayenne pepper.  everyone asks for this very easy recipe. try this in a grilled cheese sandwich! yum.

1. chop pimientos into small pieces , or pulse in a food processor
2. in small bowl , stir all ingredients until well mixed
3. or put all ingredients into a food processor , and pulse until well-blended and pimientos are in small pieces
4. serve on crackers , with celery , or make pimiento cheese sandwiches !
5. you may prefer to add up to 1 / 2 cup mayonnaise to get the spreading consistency you like
demonstrations.review: I have been looking for a good pimiento cheese recipe forever.  Always just not quite right. Now I have it.  Added 2 jalepenos to it and cut back just a touch on the vinegar (I used apple cider vinegar) because of the peppers being in vinegar. Absolutely perfect.  Thanks BeachGirl. Now Mrs. Price will be loosing a customer for good.  No more over priced stuff for me, and so much better.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
tuna patties with ranch dressing

i got this recipe from a starkist tuna recipe booklet and it's so good. i think the ranch dressing and cheese make them extra good.

1. set aside 3 / 4 cup of the breadcrumbs
2. combine all ingredients , except oil and reserved breadcrumbs
3. form 8 patties , coating each side with the reserved bread crumbs
4. heat appx
5. 1 tbl
6. oil in nonstick skillet over medium heat
7. cook 4 patties for 4-5 minutes on each side
8. you may need to add additional oil when you're frying them
9. add more oil and cook remaining 4 tuna patties
10. serve immediately
demonstrations.review: These are the best tuna patties I have ever had. I did make just one slight change, added 1/2 tsp of Old Bay Seasoning. Served with my #237583  Spicy Avocado Tartar Sauce (the cayenne and Old Bay Method). These were just excellent.

target.recipe_text:
filipino menudo

comfort food filipino style! this is one of my husband's favourite filipino dishes. i make this in big batches because it freezes well, and it tastes better the longer you keep it. it can stay for up to 2 weeks in the freezer. this can also be cooked in a slow cooker like the usual slow cooker stew.

1. combine all marinade ingredients
2. divide the marinade in halves
3. save half
4. add pork cubes on the other half with the bay leaf and marinate for at least 30 minutes
5. remove pork from the marinade , drip dry
6. saut garlic and onion , add pork and the unused half of the marinade and bay leaf , simmer uncovered , reduce the liquid to half
7. add fresh pork liver if you prefer the fresh ingredient , cover and cook
8. add tomato sauce , liver paste , carrots , potatoes and raisins , simmer stirring occasionally
9. add peppers and adjust the seasoning
10. add the grated cheese , let it melt , stir and distribute evenly
11. serve hot
target.review: this is great and after making it , found it to be very authentic. the only thing i would do is to not put in the liver,( i hate liver) but substitute a little bit of red hot pepper to spice it up a bit... all in all its a great recipe and makes a great dish.   thanks for posting

demonstrations.recipe_text:
devilish deviled eggs

this is a very simple but wonderful deviled egg recipe that my mother use to make for me. this was always a favorite at barbecues and potlucks. thank you for trying it. enjoy!

1. peel and cut the eggs in two
2. place the yolks in a small bowl and set the whites aside
3. smash the yolks and whisk in the mayonnaise and mustard until smooth
4. add the onions and pickles and whisk until combined
5. spoon or pipe the yolk mixture into the egg whites and sprinkle with paprika
demonstrations.review: while the minced onion (red) was great,,i would suggest that instead of 1 tablespoon of whole grain mustard,,,cut it in half,,,the full tablespoon was over powering,,,,,the picles where a graat ida,,,,thanks for posting

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s onion patties latkes

i have been making these for over 20 years, i usually get about 15 patties but it depends on the size of the batter that you drop in the pan, these are better if fried to very brown and crispy, you can make a double recipe, fry them then freeze them on a tray then pop them into freezer bags, then just warm them in the oven to crisp up, they are very addicting and i can tell you i eat half before they even get to the table lol!  if you plan on doubling the recipe then make two separate recipes in two bowls, i have doubled the recipe into one bowl and for some reason they just are not as good ---  if desired you could add in a slightly beaten large egg and reduce the milk by 1/4 cup --- you will *love* these!  also see my
recipe#186700 *and*
recipe#244592

1. chop the onions finely then place into a bowl
2. in another large bowl mix together the flour , sugar , baking powder , seasoning salt , cayenne , garlic powder and a small amount of black pepper
3. mix to combine well
4. add in the milk and whisk until thoroughly combined
5. add in the chopped onions and green onions and mix with a wooden spoon until combined
6. in a large non-stick frypan , heat a small amount of oil to medium-hot , adding in more oil as needed as the patties will absorb too much oil if you add in a large amount of oil at one time
7. drop the batter from a tablespoon into about 1 / 2-inch of hot oil
8. flatten slightly with the spoon or spatula
9. sprinkle with a little salt
10. fry until crispy and brown on both sides
demonstrations.review: having read all the reviews i decided to try this out,,,,OMG this was fantastic. as i did not have cayenne pepper, i used the red pepper flakes, and it worked fine. used regular salt and added some spices, worked fine. well when the finished product came on tho the dinner table.  and there where 15 of us... not one did not want seconds....they loved it and the four pieces left are right in front of me and im finishing them off as i type this.... this is an outstanding recipe.. dont be afraid to try it , its easy and if you follow the recipe,,,,it will come out great....what a pleasure.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
boneless leg of lamb

nan

1. generously rub leg of lamb with olive oil
2. season lamb with all the ingredients listed , making sure that they are evenly distributed
3. place leg of lamb on a rack in a roasting pan
4. preheat oven to 325 degrees and bake leg of lamb uncovered for 30 minutes per pound or until internal temperature reaches 120 to 130 degrees at the thickest point
demonstrations.review: amazingly, i actually found a boneless leg of lamb  in the philippines. followed the recipe but did rub the meat all over with garlic.  the favor of the spices and the garlic was exceptional...this was a real treat for easter. served italian roasted potatoes and sauteed baby asparagus with the lamb. great meal.

target.recipe_text:
mushrooms and onions for steak

this is how i sauté mushrooms and onions to serve with grilled steak. i've been doing it this way for years and never really thought of it as a recipe until today when my husband mentioned that it was the best he'd ever had. if you have leftovers, make an omelet with them with smoked swiss cheese and serve with hot, steaming bowls of tomato soup with basil. just trust me on that.

1. melt the butter and olive oil together in a frying pan and add the mushrooms and onions
2. let them cook slowly , over medium heat , until the mushrooms are getting a little brown and the onions are nice and soft , about 20 minutes
3. while there's still some moisture left from the mushrooms , add the worcestershire sauce and garlic salt
4. the mixture will thicken and it's ready to serve
5. serve with grilled steak and use leftovers for omelets
6. makes 4 servings if served with steak
target.review: I did this with just mushrooms, i omitted the butter and just used olive oil but otherwise prepared it as stated. The mushrooms were very flavourful and complemented the steak beautifully. thanks for posting i will certainly be using this again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
roasted tomato  pepper  and red onion soup

this is an unusual recipe i found in a flemish woman's magazine. i like it alot, hope you will too !

1. wash and halve the tomatoes
2. halve the pepper , removing the core and seeds
3. cut the onion in quarters
4. place the vegetables and two sprigs of sage on a large bake pan
5. sprinkle with the olive oil
6. bake for 30 minutes in the oven at 400 degrees
7. remove the vegetables from the oven and place them in an ovenproof dish
8. add the bouillon , and bake uncovered in the oven 20 minutes or until the vegetables are cooked
9. allow the vegetables to cool
10. puree with a handblender
11. reheat in a pan on the stove when ready to serve
12. garnish with chopped sage
demonstrations.review: What a fantastic tasty soup. The only change I made was to use homemade chicken stock instead of vegetable stock. I will be making this over and over again as I am a big fan of soups, especially to take to work in my packed lunch I can see this becoming a firm favourite, thanks for posting

demonstrations.recipe_text:
hellmann s parmesan crusted chicken  low fat version

this is an unbelievably simple recipe that tastes wonderful. the way i make this low-fat is by using hellmann's 

1. combine mayonnaise and cheese
2. spread on chicken , then sprinkle with bread crumbs
3. bake at 425 degrees for 20 minutes
demonstrations.review: I have made this a couple of times now, the first time i followed the recipe exactly and althouth the chicken stayed wonderfully moist and tender the topping was a little bland. on the second occasion i added a little fresh garlic and sweet chilli dipping sauce to the mayonnaise topping and the depth of flavour it created was amazing, i also used low fat mayo which i felt did not compromise the flavour of the dish at all. Great basic recipe, I will definately be using this one regularly.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
irish carrot   parsnip mash

this dish is still widely made in ireland - it is sometimes called "green, white and gold" or "sunshine". lovely flavor combination with the carrots and parsnips

1. boil the carrots in a little lightly salted water with a pinch of sugar in it , until soft and drain
2. boil the parsnips separately in lightly salted water until soft and drain
3. marsh or puree them together
4. add the butter
5. season and sprinkle with the parsley
6. serve
demonstrations.review: Was served this at a dinner party recently, it was made exactly to your recipe and was a wonderful addition to the main course. this is definately going to be a regular in my household. thanks for sharing.

target.recipe_text:
oatmeal buttermilk pancakes

nan

1. mix oats and soda to buttermilk
2. let stand 5 minutes
3. sift together flour , baking powder , salt and sugar
4. add sifted dry ingredients , shortening and eggs to oats mixture
5. stir until combined
6. for each pancake , pour about 1 / 4 cup batter onto hot , lightly greased griddle
7. bake to a golden brown , turning only once
8. serve hot with butter and syrup
target.review: Was looking for a way to use up some buttermilk.  These tasty pancakes paired with Buttermilk Syrup did the trick.  Froze the left overs and reheated in the toaster oven - great for a weekend breakfast without needing to make up a whole batch of pancakes.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chicken ranch pizza

i like this recipe because it is easy and taste good. this recipe came from a bistro chef in death valley, ca. i just added my favorite crust

1. pre-heat oven to 360f
2. cook chicken meat on stove top thoroughly
3. spread low-fat ranch dressing on pizza crust , then place tomato , bell peppers and green onions
4. evenly place chicken all over pizza
5. spread out mozzarella cheese
6. place in oven for approximately 20 - 25 minutes or until desired crust
demonstrations.review: Just relized as I went to review this I forgot the tomato!  LOL  Anyway I used the Boboli thin crust, red onion instead of green and red bell pepper.  I also added fresh mushrooms.  Very yummy and tasted even better the next day reheated in the toaster oven.  Simple and good - just what I was looking for in a Boboli recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
asian inspired coconut crab cakes

i got the idea for this recipe taking an international cooking class in college..  i adapted it til it was perfect..

1. preheat oven to 375
2. place coconut in a mircowave safe dish and mircowave 3-4 minutes stirring often til lightly toasted
3. combine crab , ginger , green onions , pepper , carrot , lemon juice , may , egg , rice vinegar and garlic and mix well
4. combine bread crumsb and cayenne pepper and fold into crab mix
5. sprinkle half of the coconut on cutting board
6. with a measuring spoon form 16 even sized balls of crab mix
7. roll in coocnut mixture and sprinkle remianing coconut on top
8. flatten and place on cookie sheet
9. bake 20 minutes until coconut is golden brown
10. serve with asian style hot mustard
demonstrations.review: OK - I will try next weekend and then update- looks yummy.  Only question is did you use sweetened coconut or unsweetened??

demonstrations.recipe_text:
grilled cauliflower

i actually won a cash prize in our local paper for this recipe. my husband and i will eat the whole thing ourselves - make several if you're having guests. if someone you love doesn't care for cauliflower, this may be the ticket!

1. remove stem& leaves from cauliflower
2. wash& pat dry
3. spread the butter over the cauliflower
4. sprinkle with seasoned salt& cheese
5. wrap head of cauliflower in heavy duty aluminum foil
6. grill over medium heat about 40 minutes or until desired tenderness
demonstrations.review: YUMMY.  I mixed the parmesan in with the butter before spreading on the head - forgot the salt or I would have mixed that in too.  Minor amount of sticking to the foil.  Seemed easier to put together if I mixed it all up first and didn't seem to affect the flavor.

target.recipe_text:
spinach  apple and pecan salad

spinach, apples, red onion & pecans in a sweet-tart dressing.  to make this salad extra special, i like to glaze the pecans by stirring them with 1 tablespoon sugar in a medium non-stick frying pan over medium heat, stirring constantly until sugar melts.  pour them out on waxed paper and separate with your spoon while still warm.  if you do this, you don't need to toast the pecans.  it takes about 5 minutes or so for the sugar to melt.

1. in serving bowl , whisk oil , vinegar , mustard , sugar , salt and pepper until thick
2. add apple and onion
3. toss until apples and onions are covered with dressing
4. place spinach on top , then pecans
5. just before serving , toss
target.review: Made this last night and my husband and I loved it!  I made the recipe exactly as stated except for using a Fuji apple.  Next time I think I will add some strips of grilled chicken and make it a full meal.  This is a keeper :)  and sooo easy :)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chili blanco

a football weekend/cold weather family favorite.

1. heat oil in large saucepan over medium-high heat
2. add onion and cook until tender
3. mix in garlic , jalapeo , green chile peppers , cumin , oregano , and cayenne
4. continue to cook and stir until mixture is tender
5. mix in chicken broth , chicken and white beans
6. simmer 15-20 minutes , stirring occasionally
7. remove from heat , stir in cheese until melted
8. serve warm with tortilla chips and salad
9. we put tortilla chips in bottom of serving bowl , add the chili
10. good eating !
demonstrations.review: I've been using this recipe for at least a year now.  It is one of our go-to meals.  REALLY good.  I follow the instructions pretty exactly and add a little extra red pepper for some heat.  It's fun to eat it with tortilla chips too :)  Thank you for this recipe!  I will be making it for the rest of my life :)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
white chili   football soup

this recipe comes from the blue owl restaurant and bakery in historic kimmswick, mo. my daughter named it "football soup" because we always make it when we have a crowd over watching the game after church! incredibly easy, freezes beautifully, and my bean hating husband even loves it. i add an extra can of green chilies for more flavor. you can make it without the chicken for a cheaper meatless meal, and you can make it without the monterey jack cheese for a low-fat, less thickened soup (but the cheese adds a lot of flavor!)

1. heat oil in large pot over medium high heat
2. add onions and saute until translucent , about 10 minutes
3. stir in garlic , then chilies , cumin , oregano , and cayenne and saute 2 minutes
4. add undrained beans and stock and bring to a boil
5. reduce heat and add chicken and cheese to chili and stir until cheese melts
6. season to taste with salt and pepper and ladle into bowls
7. for freezing: pour soup into a rigid container , label and freeze
8. to reheat , thaw in refridgerator overnight or simply put frozen soup into a large pot and gently heat , with lid on and stirring often , till heated through
demonstrations.review: My fiance loved it!  It will be a permanent dish in our house.  I added twice as much red pepper and I seasoned the chicken with salt/pepper/chili powder/oregano & boiled in chicken broth (low sodium/no fat).   All I need now is a bigger pot.  Thanks for making me look like a great cook ;)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
calypso chicken casserole

island flavors in an easy and healthy casserole.  you can just hear the steel drums play...

1. combine chicken , peppers , beans , corn and pineapple in 2 quart glass casserole dish
2. dissolve cornstarch in pineapple juice and stir it in along with remaining ingredients except lime and coconut oil
3. bake at 350 for 30 - 40 min until chicken is done
4. stir in coconut oil
5. serve with lime wedges , or add fresh squeezed lime juice before serving
6. enjoy !
demonstrations.review: With all of these spices I expected more flavor.  The taste is really original, but I don't think I'll be making this again.  Thanks for posting it though.

target.recipe_text:
oven baked french fries

every once in a while i gotta have french fries! from cooking light. (add a little bite with a dash of dried pepper flakes).

1. preheat oven to 450f
2. combine cheese , paprika , 1 / 2 teaspoon salt and 1 / 4 teaspoon black pepper , or to taste
3. place potatoes in a medium bowl coated with cooking spray
4. sprinkle potatoes with cheese mixture , tossing well
5. arrange potatoes in a single layer on a baking sheet coated with cooking spray
6. bake at 450f for 13 minutes or until tender
target.review: MMMMMMmm  Such a nice change from the plain fries.  I like that they are baked too, so it saves on the calories.  Loved this recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
grilled chicken with sweet carolina barbecue sauce

this makes the best barbecue chicken on the planet. the extra effort of making the marinade is a definite payoff. the sweet mustard glaze gives the grilled chicken a wonderful crisp coating. the chicken does need to marinate overnight so plan ahead. this mustard sauce is also fantastic on pork chops. make ahead: the sauce can be safely stored in a lidded jar in the refrigerator for a month. wine: the sweet barbecue sauce mate well with a full-bodied, fruity grenache such as domaine lafond roc-epine lirac blanc 2004 or an off dry fruity reisling such as the very easy to drink 2002 reisling - domaine fernand engel.

1. in a medium saucepan , combine all of the sauce ingredients and bring to a simmer
2. stir well and remove from heat
3. let cool to room temperature , then pour into a glass jar with lid and refrigerate
4. in a large bowl or extra large ziplock , add the first 9 ingredients and mix well
5. let sit at room temperature for 30 minutes
6. then , add the chicken pieces and turn to coat
7. refrigerate overnight
8. light your grill or preheat broiler
9. remove the chicken from the marinade and arrange the pieces on a baking sheet / s
10. brush the chicken pieces with the barbecue sauce and grill over a medium-hot fire or broil 12 inches from the heat , turning often and rotating , until cooked through and nicely glazed , 8 to 10 minutes per side
11. serve hot or at room temperature
demonstrations.review: This makes the best barbecue chicken.  Loved the flavors!  I used dry Marsala wine.  I out this sauce on chicken and ribs that we had on the grill that was enjoyed by the whole family this holiday weekend.  Thanks for sharing!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
sausage gravy

this is a really easy and super deelicious recipe for sausage gravy over biscuits, you will want to make this one again and again!

1. cook sausage in skillet
2. drain fat
3. sprinkle flour over sausage and stir well
4. cook flour and sausage together for about 5 - 7 minutes
5. add milk
6. cook over medium heat until thickened
7. add pepper
8. serve over biscuits
demonstrations.review: I made Recipe #220639, and then made this gravy to pour over the top.  We loved it for breakfast along with some eggs over easy and home fries.  This is so easy to make, and with the homemade biscuits, it was deeeelicious!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
greek penne and chicken

posted for 2006 zaar world tour - greece. this recipe was adapted from a cooking website's newsletter.

1. in a large pot bring salted water to a boil
2. add penne pasta and cook until al dente , drain and set aside
3. using a large skillet and over medium-high heat melt butter
4. add onion and garlic to melted butter and cook for 2 minutes
5. stirring occasionally , add chicken and continue cooking until golden brown , approximately 5-6 minutes
6. reduce heat to medium-low , begin adding drained and chopped artichoke hearts , chopped tomato , feta cheese , fresh parsley , lemon juice , dried oregano , and drained penne pasta to the chicken
7. cook until heated through , approximately 2-3 minutes
8. season with salt and ground black pepper to taste , serve warm
demonstrations.review: I used olive oil instead of butter.  Also I added some capers.  The taste was so good! Thanks for sharing!

target.recipe_text:
creamy vegetarian lentil mushroom soup

creamy lentil soup cooked in a crockpot. serve with crusty bread or rolls for a comfort food fix! feel free to double this recipe.

1. in a saucepan , saute onions , mushrooms , garlic , and celery till just slightly browned , about 10 minutes
2. in a 3 1 / 2 or 4 quart crockpot , combine the lentils , carrots , onion , garlic , mushrooms , celery& parsley
3. stir in water , mushroom soup , and bouillon
4. cover
5. cook on low 10 to 12 hours or high 5 to 6 hours
6. top each serving with a dollop of sour cream
7. 4 servings
target.review:
Yummy!  My DH loves lentils but I don't - however I loved them in this one!  I had no problems cooking on high - but was home to stir it once per hour.  I ended up doubling, but using one less cup of water (because I opened an extra large can of mushroom soup and thereby reduced liquid)
Thanks for posting - will be making this again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
senegalese peanut soup

from a ww cookbook. very tasty and quick. low in calories and fat (chickpeas stretch the peanut butter flavor). only 4 ww points per serving!

1. puree chickpeas , 1 / 2 cup of broth , and peanut butter
2. heat peanut oil in saucepan , saute onions and ginger root 7- 8 minutes
3. stir in curry powder and cumin , saute another minute
4. add remaining broth , tomatoes , and chickpea puree
5. simmer 5 minutes
6. season with cayenne and sprinkle with cilantro
demonstrations.review:
Wow !  Interesting flavor, easy, delicious!  Like something exotic you could make for company that seemed like you slaved !  I followed the recipe exactly, except I drained the canned tomatoes - wasn't sure if I should but seemed the right thing to do.  My husband does not like tomatoes, so I will make again without.  I don't think the tomatoes changes the flavor too much, but adds nice color.

Will definitely make again and again!  Thank you!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chicken with honey

this dish is a native of africa. the chicken and honey mix to make a wonderful dish.
hope you enjoy!

1. in pan , heat butter and oil
2. brown chicken in this mixture
3. season with salt & pepper if desired , remove
4. in remaining fat , cook onion and garlic until clear
5. add ground or crushed almonds , basil , pepper , and honey and cook , stirring , until mixture is well blended
6. combine broth and cornstarch and add to pan
7. cook , stirring , over high heat until sauce thickens
8. remove from heat , stir in lemon juice
9. place chicken in a casserole dish , spooning sauce over
10. bake , covered , at 350 degrees for 1 hour , or until chicken is tender
demonstrations.review: Thank you - this was great!  Easy - ingredients all on hand - except I had no almonds so used sesame seeds instead - it was fine but next time I'll use the almonds.  Moist, juicy chicken.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
armenian nutmeg cake

armenia is famous for its sweet and spicy nutmeg cake. it has a crunchy base and light cake topping, and tastes delicious. this recipe was given to me 16 years ago by the mother of one of my son's kindergarten friends. tried and true!

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees f
2. grease a 9 inch square pan , and line with baking paper if desired
3. combine flour , baking powder and salt , then rub in the butter until the mixture resembles fine breadcrumbs
4. you can do this with the
5. then add sugar , and combine
6. press half this mixture evenly over the base of the prepared cake pan , and reserve other half
7. dissolve baking soda in milk , add beaten egg and nutmeg , then add to reserved mixture
8. combine well
9. pour into pan and sprinkle nuts , and some cinnamon if desired , over top
10. bake in oven for 45 minutes to 60 minutes
11. allow to stand for 10 minutes before turning onto a wire rack to cool
demonstrations.review: Very flavorful and easy.  I'll make again. - thank you!

target.recipe_text:
barbecued bat wings

these are fun to make and very tasty.  the bbq sauce is a hideous, tar like mixture, but it tastes great!

1. preheat the oven to 350 degrees
2. boil the chicken wings for twenty minutes in a large pot
3. while the wings are cooking , prepare the sauce
4. whisk together the ketchup , molasses , vinegar , worcestershire sauce , sugar , hot sauce , salt , and pepper until smooth in a large roasting pan
5. add enough black , blue , and green food colorings to the sauce to make a dark black sauce
6. place the pan in the oven and bake for 10 minutes , stirring once
7. drain the wings well and add them to the sauce and toss to coat evenly , poking the wings liberally with a fork
8. bake for 20 minutes , then increase the temperature to 450 degrees
9. toss the wings in the sauce again to coat evenly
10. bake until the sauce is thickened and slightly blackened , flipping the wings over occasionally , about another 15 minutes
11. serve hot or at room temperature
target.review: This is my son’s favorite Halloween dish and really his favorite wings, period! Very sticky and messy, but it wouldn’t be as much fun otherwise! I skimp on the hot sauce and just use black food coloring.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
meatball sub casserole

wonderful take on the italian meatball sandwich. taken from "quick cooking" magazine.

1. preheat oven to 400
2. in a bowl , combine onions , bread crumbs and parmesan cheese
3. add beef and mix well
4. shape into 1-inch balls
5. place on a rack
6. in a shallow baking pan , bake for 15-20 minutes or until no longer pink
7. reduce oven temperature to 350
8. meanwhile , arrange bread in a single layer in an ungreased 13x9x2" baking dish
9. combine cream cheese , mayo , italian seasoning and pepper
10. spread over the bread
11. sprinkle with 1 / 2 cup mozzarella
12. combine sauce , water and garlic
13. add meatballs
14. pour over cheese mixture
15. sprinkle with remaining mozzarella
16. bake , uncovered at 350 for 30 minutes or until heated through
demonstrations.review: The taste was fine, but we found the recipe to be really heavy.  We only managed to eat half, and we're not small eaters!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
green bean and eye of round steak skillet

i made this up on the fly!  it's a tasty way to prepare a cheap cut of meat!

1. 1
2. mix lime juice , dressing , garlic , and hot sauce in a large bowl to create a marinade
3. 2
4. salt and pepper steaks and add to marinade
5. refrigerate for approximately 8 hours
6. 3
7. cook steaks in large heavy skillet on medium heat for approximately 10 minutes , or until almost done
8. remove from skillet
9. 4
10. pour beer in the pan to deglaze
11. add onion and cook until tender
12. 5
13. add green beans and return the steaks to the pan
14. cook until green beans are warm
15. 6
16. serve with mashed potatoes and enjoy !
demonstrations.review: Nice, easy recipe.  I used red wine instead of beer because it's what I had on hand.  The steak turned out well, but the real star of the dish was the green beans.  They soaked up all the flavor and just tasted fantastic!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chickn ranch bbq crescent squares

i saw this on the rr show and had to try it. it was so-oooo easy and yummy that i had to share it here.

1. heat oven to 375f roll the crescent rolls out and place them on a cookie sheet
2. pinch 2 sheets together in the middle to create 1 large dough
3. bake 8-11 minutes , until golden brown
4. remove from oven and turn on broiler
5. spread the barbeque sauce over dough
6. sprinkle the chicken , bacon and cheese over the top
7. place the cookie sheet under the broiler until the cheese melts , about 3-5 minutes
8. combine the ranch dressing and chili powder in a small bowl
9. pour into re-sealable bag and cut off a small
10. drizzle the dressing over the top and garnish with the scallions
11. cut into squares and enjoy !
demonstrations.review: I halved the recipe and also cut down on the cheese and ranch, but it's perfect veging out food!  Cut into smaller pieces, I think it would make a good appetizer, too.

target.recipe_text:
dilly salmon and shell casserole

i like this recipe because it uses low fat ing. but really delivers on taste.

1. preheat oven to 350f degrees
2. spray med
3. nonstick sauce pan with cooking spray
4. heat over med
5. heat , add mushrooms , onion , and garlic
6. cook and stir 5 minutes
7. mix milk and flour in med
8. bowl till smooth
9. stir in lemon peel , dill weed , salt and pepper
10. stir into mushroom mixture
11. heat for 6 min , stirring constantly until thickened
12. remove from heat
13. stir in pasta , peas and salmon
14. pour into 2 quart casserole
15. bake , uncovered , 35-40 minutes
target.review: I really liked this...the dill and lemon had a nice flavor,and it wasn't heavy.I figured it at 3 WW points per serving,for those on WW.The only thing that kept it from being 5 star was the rest of the family wasn't crazy for it.Maybe next time I will use tuna,instead of salmon..they said it was too 'fishy'.They also wanted cheese on it,which I guess you could do,but that would add more fat.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
all american hot dish

i adopted this recipe in the february 2005 recipe adoption.  this makes an easy and quick weeknight meal that is good and filling.  dh really loves stuff like this.  personally, next time i make this, i will probably add some chili powder or garlic or both to spice it up a little.  i have tried the skillet version only; i have not tried the oven method.

1. cook and stir the meat and onion in a large deep skillet until the meat is brown
2. drain off the excess fat
3. stir in the undrained corn and the rest of the ingredients except the cheese
4. to cook in a skillet: heat the mixture to boiling then reduce the heat and simmer , uncovered , stirring occasionally , until the noodles are tender , about 20 minutes
5. top with cheese and serve hot
6. to cook in the oven: pour the mixture into an ungreased 2-quart casserole
7. cover and bake in a 375 degree f
8. oven for 30 minutes , stirring occasionally
9. uncover and bake until the mixture thickens , about 15 minutes
10. top with cheese and serve hot
demonstrations.review: This was pretty good.The kids liked it and it is a quick dinner.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chicken with peaches and basil

this is wonderful when peaches are fresh and in season, but canned peaches can be used when necessary.

1. in a shallow dish , combine flour and half of the salt and pepper , set aside 2 teaspoons for sauce
2. in remaining flour mixture , coat chicken well
3. shake of excess
4. in a large frypan , heat oil over medium heat
5. cook chicken , turning once , for 15 to 20 minutes or until no longer pink inside
6. transfer to plate and keep warm
7. meanwhile , peel and pit peaches
8. cut into wedges
9. add onion , garlic and reserved flour mixture to skillet
10. cook , stirring for 3 minutes
11. pour in stock and lemon juice
12. bring to boil , stirring to scrape up any brown bits from bottom of pan
13. add peaches
14. reduce heat to medium and cook , stirring for 3 minutes
15. stir in basil and remaining salt and pepper
16. pour over chicken to serve
demonstrations.review: I have an overabundance of fresh basil in my herb garden and this was an excellent way to use some. It was delicious and very easy to make. Nice and light for a hot summer night. I thought the flavors blended nicely. I had nectarines, so that is what I used. This one is definitely a keeper.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
vanishing oatmeal raisin cookies

oatmeal raisin cookie recipe from the quaker oats box.  bar cookie variation included.

1. heat oven to 350f
2. beat together margarine and sugars until creamy
3. add eggs and vanilla
4. beat well
5. add combined flour , baking soda , cinnamon and salt
6. mix well
7. stir in oats and raisins
8. mix well
9. drop by rounded tablespoonfuls onto ungreased cookie sheet
10. bake 10 to 12 minutes or until golden brown
11. cool 2 minutes on cookie sheet
12. remove to wire rack
13. makes about 4 dozen
14. bar cookies: bake 30 to 35 minutes in ungreased 13x9-inch metal baking pan
demonstrations.review: I omitted the cinnamon,and added a bag of those new cinnamon chips.I also used regular rolled oats instead of the quick cooking kind.The cookies were great!

target.recipe_text:
chicken in a metaxa cream sauce

metaxa is a greek brandy, good chance you won't have it in your drinks cabinet and it's no problem to use another brandy. i have been using spanish brandy the last few times i made this, but the metaxa does have a different flavor. if i make this for the two of us i do cut down on the chicken but make the same amount of sauce and serve it with pasta. it is a rich sauce with a distinct flavor. if you should use tarragon as an herb, taste the herb first it can be very strong sometimes and you should use less.

1. flatten the chicken breasts between 2 pieces of parchment paper
2. sprinkle them with lemon juice and then with salt and pepper
3. heat the butter in your frying pan and brown the chicken breasts then use a medium heat to cook them for about ten minutes , they should be almost done
4. then you add the metaxa bit by bit and let it gently evaporate
5. after that add the cream , let it heat through and thicken a bit
6. if using the herbs , add , mix and serve
target.review: This definitely a quality 5 star  recipe, we sure enjoyed every bite. I only had Christian Brothers Brandy, It had avery good flavor. I used basil, it was excellent. Thank you for sharing the recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
lemon crab cakes over greens

these crab cakes have a wonderful lemony, light, spicy flavor. perfect for a quick weekend brunch. note the lower fat comments, if you're watching the fat.

1. pulse bread in blender to make 1 cup fresh breadcrumbs
2. grate yellow rind of lemon to make 1 tsp zest
3. cut lemon in 2- 6 pieces and squeeze to make 2 tbsp juice
4. blend mayonnaise with lemon zest , juice and seasonings in a medium size bowl
5. stir in crab meat , breadcrumbs and onions
6. shape mixture into eight 3 inch"cakes" on a sheet of wax paper
7. heat a non-stick skillet over medium heat
8. melt 1 tbsp butter
9. cook crab cakes in skillet 4 minutes
10. add the other tbsp butter , turn the cakes carefully , and cook another 4 minutes
11. cook in batches , if necessary , you don't want to crowd them in the pan
12. meanwhile , toss greens with dressing in a large bowl
13. divide greens onto 4 plates
14. lay crab cakes over greens and serve with fresh tomato slices and hot garlic bread
demonstrations.review: Yummy, crab cakes, liked the flavor of the lemon. very light. I rolled them in panko crumbs before frying. These will make a great summertime dinner. Thank you for the recipe, PanNan.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
sunday chops and stuffing

this is a meal-in-one casserole with pork chops, apple slices, and stuffing. it's from the latest issue of taste of home's quick cooking magazine.

1. in a saucepan , combine the water , celery , 6 tbsp butter , and onion
2. bring to a boil
3. remove from the heat
4. stir in croutons
5. spoon into a greased 13x9x2-inch baking dish
6. set aside
7. in a large skillet , brown pork chops on both sides in oil
8. arrange over stuffing
9. sprinkle with salt and pepper
10. combine the apples , brown sugar , and pumpkin pie spice
11. spoon over pork chops
12. dot with the remaining butter
13. bake , uncovered , at 350 degrees for 30-35 minutes or until a meat thermometer reads 160 degrees and meat juices run clear
demonstrations.review: Very good,  Made these for company they really enjoyed then, Though next time I belive I will use a thiner Pork chop the ones I used was about 1 inch thick with no bone. The apples with the brown sugar and pumkin pie spice was delicious as was the dressing. Thank you Kree for the recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
applesauce oat pancakes

these are like having a slice of apple pie for breakfast except healthier. these are great spread with apple butter or topped with glazed apples.

1. in a large bowl , combine the oatmeal , flour , baking powder and spices , mixing well
2. in a separate bowl , combine the remaining ingredients
3. beat with a wire whisk until blended
4. add to dry mixture , mixing until all ingredients are moistened
5. let stand 5 minutes , then mix again
6. spray griddle with non-stick cooking spray and preheat over medium heat
7. using 2 tablespoonfuls for each pancake , drop batter onto griddle
8. turn pancakes when edges are dry and bottoms are lightly browned
9. cook until golden brown on both sides
10. serve with favorite toppings
demonstrations.review:
Light as a feather, yummy pancakes. DH really liked these. I made them with Splenda in stead of sugar, used old fashioned oats, fresh grated nutmeg then made as stated. Next time I think I will omit the cloves, my personal preference. Served them with real maple syrup,YUM.
Thanks Paula. for a real breakfast treat.

target.recipe_text:
white chili   football soup

this recipe comes from the blue owl restaurant and bakery in historic kimmswick, mo. my daughter named it "football soup" because we always make it when we have a crowd over watching the game after church! incredibly easy, freezes beautifully, and my bean hating husband even loves it. i add an extra can of green chilies for more flavor. you can make it without the chicken for a cheaper meatless meal, and you can make it without the monterey jack cheese for a low-fat, less thickened soup (but the cheese adds a lot of flavor!)

1. heat oil in large pot over medium high heat
2. add onions and saute until translucent , about 10 minutes
3. stir in garlic , then chilies , cumin , oregano , and cayenne and saute 2 minutes
4. add undrained beans and stock and bring to a boil
5. reduce heat and add chicken and cheese to chili and stir until cheese melts
6. season to taste with salt and pepper and ladle into bowls
7. for freezing: pour soup into a rigid container , label and freeze
8. to reheat , thaw in refridgerator overnight or simply put frozen soup into a large pot and gently heat , with lid on and stirring often , till heated through
target.review: Very good! Not as spicy than others I've tried (which is good for me because I'm prone to heartburn).

demonstrations.recipe_text:
healthy bean soup with kale

we've all heard how anti-oxidants fight cancer, save eyesight, and prevent clogged arteries. turns out lutein, a delicious 7 mg dose of which is supplied with each serving of this recipe, is even more beneficial than beta carotene. it delays lung aging and combats arthritis to boot! who knew improving your health could be so quick and easy, and taste so good? try it -- you'll see!
p.s. since i felt this lacked enough elements to chew on, i've been adding canned, sliced carrots (fast, easy & healthy!) for quite a while, and thought i'd update the recipe. also, sometimes i add another can of beans, for the same reason. glad so many of you have been enjoying this. there's a container in my frig right now - yum!

1. in a large pot , heat olive oil
2. add garlic and onion
3. saute until soft and the onion is transparent
4. wash the kale , leaving small droplets of water
5. saute , stirring , until wilted and a lovely emerald green , about 15 minutes
6. add 3 cups of the broth , reserving 1 cup , 2 cups of the beans , reserving 1 cup , all of the carrots , tomatoes , herbs , salt and pepper
7. simmer 5 minutes
8. in a blender or food processor , mix the reserved beans and broth until smooth
9. stir into the soup to thicken it nicely
10. simmer 15 more minutes
11. ladle into bowls
12. sprinkle with chopped parsley and shredded parmesan
13. serve with a nice loaf of crusty bread to soak up all the yummy broth !
14. for vegetarian use the vegetable broth
demonstrations.review: Wonderful recipe! Tasted a lot like my favorite Pasta E Fagoli soup, except chicken broth based and no noodles. It was thick and hearty and was borderline stew-like. My only mistake was not chopping the kale fine enough. I will definitely be making this again!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
vegetables in garlic cream sauce

use whatever vegetables you feel like, the sauce is the main thing.

1. place water in a large saucepan
2. bring to a boil
3. add vegetables
4. reduce heat to low
5. cook , uncovered , 9-12 minutes or until vegetables are tender-crisp
6. meanwhile , heat oil in small saucepan over medium heat
7. add garlic
8. cook and stir until golden brown
9. remove from heat
10. stir in mayonnaise and milk
11. drain vegetables
12. place in serving bowl
13. pour in garlic sauce
14. toss to evenly coat
15. sprinkle with parsley
demonstrations.review: I made this with green beans. I followed the directions, but it wasn't a very dimensional sauce; I tasted the mayo more than I tasted anything else. I added garlic powder, paprika, and chicken seasoning, and it was ok. I thought about adding cheese, but I wanted a garlic sauce more than a cheese sauce. I probably won't make it again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
baked ham slices

this ham is very tender. you could cut it with a fork. lots of flavour.

1. put ham slices in a single layer in a roast pan with a cover
2. combine apple juice , brown sugar , and dry mustard
3. pour over ham
4. bake , covered , at 350f for about 2 hours , or until liquid reduces to approximately 1 / 2 - 1 cup
5. turn ham slices occasionally during cooking time
demonstrations.review: I made this for myself and my boyfriend and it was very good. My slices were cut thin, it still turned out well, but next time I'll make the slices thicker. Great, simple, and tasty recipe! Thanks :)

target.recipe_text:
irish rosie s irish soda bread

this irish soda bread recipe was passed on to me by a dear friend of my mother's who was born and raised in ireland. it's the best irish soda bread i have ever had. it is much higher, lighter and softer than most other recipes i have seen. it has an excellent flavor and texture, as well.

1. combine dry ingredients together in a large bowl
2. in a small bowl beat eggs and stir in sour cream
3. add the egg and sour cream mixture to the dry ingredients and stir with a wooden spoon
4. batter will be very thick
5. add the raisins and caraway seeds and stir well with wooden spoon or knead in with your hands
6. place batter in a greased 9 inch springform pan
7. dust the top with enough flour so that you can pat the batter like a bread dough evenly in the pan without it sticking to your hands
8. with a knife make a shallow crisscross on the top
9. bake for 50 minutes in a preheated 350f oven
target.review:
Really, really good! Made it for Sunday dinner tonite, everyone loved it. Mom had a second piece of this instead of dessert! Didn't change a thing, even used the spring form pan! Perfect!
Thanks so much for sharing this recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
super creamy and cheesy mac and cheese

i always make a big batch of this because my husband and i both love this and always want more.

1. cook the macaroni and set aside
2. in a pot , melt the butter and mix in salt and pepper
3. slowly add in the flour , stirring continuously
4. gradually add the milk and stir the mixture until smooth
5. add the cheese on a low heat and melt into the mixture
6. once the mixture is at your desired consistency , mix in the drained macaroni
demonstrations.review: Excellent place to start then adapt to your own taste.  Very creamy. Didn't bake it, but may try next time for the flavor that brings. Did add about 1 T of a parm romano mix I had left over plus a T of just parm as well as 1/2 tsp dry mustard, additional salt and pepper. We enjoyed it every much!  Thanks for posting!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
honey oat quick bread

love this bread!!! i have been trying to eat 5 times a day (healthy food) and this bread fits perfectly into my plan.  it is easy, quick to make, very moist and really tastes good!  it is great on its own but would also be a wonderful accompaniment to soup.  the recipe calls for mild or clover honey, but i used a stronger flavored honey with great results.  from eatingwell magazine jan 2007.

1. position rack in middle of over and preheat to 375 degrees
2. generously coat a 9 x 5 inch loaf pan with cooking spray
3. sprinkle 1 tablespoon oats in the pan , coating the sides and bottom with the oats
4. thouroughly stir together whole-wheat flour , all-purpose flour , baking powder , baking soda and salt in a large bowl
5. using a fork , beat together 1 cup of oats , yogurt , egg , oil and honey in a medium bowl until well blended
6. stir in milk
7. gently stir the yogurt mixture into the flour mixture just until thoroughly incoporated but not overmixed
8. immedieatley scrape the batter into the pan , spreading evenly to the edges
9. sprinkle the reserved 1 tablespoon oats over the top of loaf
10. bake the loaf until well browned on top and a toothpick inserted in the center comes out clean , 40 - 50 minutes
11. let stand in the pan on a wire rack for 15 minutes
12. run a table knife around and under the loaf to loosen it and turn it outo the rack
13. let cool until barely warm , about 45 minutes
demonstrations.review: Made this to go with soup for a friend and myself.  We both thought it was very, very good.  Good texture, excellent honey flavor, went very well with our vegetable barley soup.  Very easy to mix up.  Will definitely make this again.  Thanks so much for posting.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
homemade chewy granola bars

nan

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. grease a 13x9-inch pan
3. in a large bowl combine brown sugar , peanut butter , corn syrup , margarine and vanilla , blend well
4. add remaining ingredients and mix well
5. press evenly into greased pan
6. bake at 350f for 15-20 minutes or until light golden brown
7. cool 1 hour
8. cut into bars
demonstrations.review: These were really good! Very chewy, just like the name promised.   I used 1/4 c honey and 1/4 c karo, will cut back on the brown sugar and just stick with the honey next time as there were quite sweet and I think they'd still be good with less.  love the peanut butter and the fact there's no flour added.  Saw another recipe that used flax meal, may try that instead of the wheat germ.  This recipe is so  versatile, the options are endless!   I gave a lot of these away so I could make another batch with nuts!  I cut them small so when I go back for the second one there's no guilt! Thanks so much for posting.

target.recipe_text:
basted baked potato

if you're like me, you'll know the best part of the baked potato is the skin, which is why i like to spice mine up a bit. this is a really easy way to add a bit more flavour, and because potatoes are so versatile you can try all kinds of different spice combinations.

1. mix the olive oil and spices together
2. wash the potatoes and pierce the skin a few times with a fork
3. smear the oil mixture over the potatoes , best done with a pastry brush
4. place the potatoes on a baking tray , lined with foil , and bake as you normally would
5. i do mine in a 200 c fan oven for 30-40 minutes
6. serve with lots of butter
target.review: Delicious!  I'll never cook "plain" baked potatoes again.  To go with grilled steaks I used just olive oil, salt, pepper and onion powder.  DH loved these, and he's a connoisseur of potato skins!  Thanks for posting this recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
roast leg of lamb with rosemary and garlic

this is a dish we eat once or twice a month. for a change, you can cook sliced potatoes and sauteed onions in stock under the lamb. they get all those yummy garlicky juices dripping on to them.

1. preheat your oven to 350f
2. with a small , sharp knife cut slits all over the lamb
3. insert the slivers of garlic , and the rosemary sprigs
4. brush the lamb with the oil and season with salt and pepper
5. place on a wire rack in a baking tin and pour in 3 / 4 cup of water
6. roast for about 2 hours basting often with the pan juices
7. remove from oven and cover loosely with foil
8. allow to"rest" for about 15 minutes before carving
9. we serve with roasted vegetables , peas , gravy and mint jelly
demonstrations.review: Absolutely delicious!  I've made this using both bone-in and boneless leg of lamb and it's fabulous.  It made the perfect Easter dinner with tiny new red potatoes and asparagus with hollandaise sauce.  As an added bonus we have enough leftovers to make lamb curry.  A wonderful, wonderful recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
fresh picked strawberry ice cream  electric ice cream machine

although this is a wonderful ice cream recipe (imho), it is an old one, and contains raw egg. please feel free to use a fresh egg substitute or pasteurized eggs in this recipe. you may leave out the egg altogether, but the texture may suffer. the "cook time" is for the processing time of my (your) ice cream machine. the 1/2 to 1 hour "chill time" was not included in the prep/cook time.

1. puree all ingredients in a blender
2. chill mixture for 1 / 2 to 1 hour until cold
3. process according to the freezing instructions for your ice cream machine
demonstrations.review: Wonderful!  With my little ice cream maker it came out the consistency of soft serve, but a trip to the freezer tightened it up.  Delicious flavor of fresh berries.  We'll definitely be making this when strawberries are in season.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
easy shake and bake chicken with mozzarella and tomato sauce

this is easy and my family loves it, you may increase the pasta sauce and cheese if desired to suit taste

1. remove about 1 / 4 of the package of seasoning mix and save for another time
2. place the coating mix in the shaker bag and add in the garlic powder , black pepper and seasoned salt
3. shake the bag to combine
4. add in one breast at a time to the bag and shake to coat with the crumb mixture
5. place the coated breasts into a greased 11 x 7-inch baking pan
6. set oven to 375 degrees f
7. bake for 20 minutes
8. remove from oven and drizzle about 1 / 4 to 1 / 3 cup pasta sauce over each breast then place a slice of mozzarella cheese or about 1 / 3 cup shredded cheese on top
9. return to oven and bake for for about 10-15 minutes or until the chicken is completely cooked
demonstrations.review:
I wish I could award more stars.  I've used Shake n' Bake for years to put a quick meal on the table, and this takes a simple piece of chicken up to a whole different level.

I made this last night at the end of a fairly busy, harried day.  I made it for just the 2 of us, and used an 8x8 square baking pan which worked perfectly.  I "guesstimated" the amount of coating mix and seasonings.  

I paired the chicken with green beans sauteed in olive oil with minced garlic, and what would otherwise have been a ho-hum "chicken breasts again" meal became special.  The only change I made was to use 2 slices of cheese (they were square) because one didn't cover the chicken.  DH raved yesterday, and was still raving today.  I'd give this 10 stars if I could, for ease of preparation and "yumminess."  You've gotta try this â€” you won't believe how good it is!

target.recipe_text:
amazing tuna fish casserole

my mother made this for me when i was growing up. now it is a favorite with my family. the cheese and soup create a wonderful flavor. can also use canned chicken instead of tuna. i serve tiny new peas with this. my kids love it!

1. prepare macaroni and cheese as directed on the box
2. drain tuna and add to the mac and cheese
3. add cream of mushroom soup
4. place noodle mixture in casserole dish
5. crumble crackers
6. cover casserole with crackers
7. melt butter and drizzle over crackers
8. bake at 350 for 20 minutes
target.review: I loved this recipe!  Very simple to make and delicious.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
golden chicken nuggets

this is one of my kids favorites. they have said, 'mom, your chicken nuggets are the best!!' for such picky eaters, that is a huge complement.

1. heat deep fryer
2. cut chicken into bite size pieces
3. soak chicken in milk
4. mix flour and seasoning in large bowl
5. dip chicken into flour
6. cook about 12 pieces at a time in fryer for 360 degrees for 6 to 9 minutes or until golden
7. serve with sweet and sour sauce or honey mustard !
demonstrations.review: These were very tasty.  We used ketchup and mayonaise mixed together for the dip. Had just enough spice with Tony's Seasonings.  Will definitely keep this one!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
exotic and sweet moroccan chicken with spicy rice

nan

1. cut the chicken breast into largish bite-sized portions
2. mix the flour with the cinnamon , confectioner's sugar , ginger , salt and pepper to taste
3. dredge the chicken pieces in the flour mixture
4. fry in shallow oil until browned and cooked through , turning once
5. keep warm in a low oven
6. saute the chile peppers , mushrooms and onion in oil until softened and golden
7. add the cooked basmati rice and continue sauteing until cooked through
8. add the salt and pepper to taste
9. spread the rice and a large platter
10. top with a pyramid of chicken pieces
11. garnish with fresh cilantro , if desired
demonstrations.review: This recipe was wonderful!  Very nice blend of seasonings.  Thanks for sharing!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cheesy tater tots casserole

my mom used to make this when i was little and i've always loved it. it's so easy to make and is always a big hit in our house.

1. cook ground beef and drain grease
2. pour ground beef in bottom of ungreased 8x8 pan
3. drain green beans and layer on top of ground beef
4. smooth cheddar cheese soup over the green beans
5. place tater tots strategically to cover entire casserole
6. if desired , sprinkle shredded cheddar cheese over tater tots
7. bake in the oven using the directions from the tater tot bag
demonstrations.review: Very quick and tasty!  I added 1 tsp of Tony's seasoning to the meat as I cooked it just because I like the taste.  I highly recommend this recipe!  Thanks!

target.recipe_text:
norwegian rice pudding   risengryn grod

we used to have this a lot when i was a kid. not only is it yummy and filling - it is cheap!

1. boil water and add rice , cover and lower heat to simmer for 15 minutes
2. add milk and , if using them , the raisins or currants and vanilla and bring back to a boil
3. cover , lower heat and simmer until the rice is tender , about 20-30 minutes
4. season with salt
5. serve with butter , milk , sugar and cinnamon
6. for a sweeter rice try adding 1 / 4 to 1 / 2 cup sugar with the milk
target.review: We have risengryn grod at least once per month. I actually cook it for longer (closer to an hour) to make the rice more mooshy and pudding like. If you have leftovers, you can chill it, then mix whipped cream into the grod. Serve that with strawberries in strawberry syrup. Yum.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kringle  cookies

the little norwegian store here makes these by the dozens. they either dunk them in their coffee or butter them on the bottom to eat them. yum! (yield depends on how thick and or big you make them, so judge accordingly).

1. cream butter and sugar add egg and villa and beat well
2. add sour cream and mix well
3. sift together baking soda , powder and flour
4. add to creamed mixture and mix well
5. chill overnite
6. take a teaspoon of dough and roll out in your hands into a snake about 8-inches long
7. form into a "figure 8" shape on a parchment-lined cookie sheet
8. bake at 375 for 10 minutes or until lightly browned
9. remove and cool completely
demonstrations.review: I was really excited about finding this recipe, but my first batch completely dind't work. I couldn't roll the dough, even after chilling it for 24 hours. I even tried it in the freezer. With much work, I was able to get a few figure 8s. When baked, they came out more like a bidcuit than a cookie. My dad even said that they tasted like airy pancakes. Anyhow, I tried to make them again, thinking that I had made a mistake. The same thing happened. I think that something is really wrong with this recipe. The only saving grace is that these are great with butter and served with soup.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
boca breakfast sandwich  meatless egg mcmuffin

i love mcdonald's sausage mcmuffin, but this healthy creation is just as tasty (boca burgers are scrumptious with the right fixings!).

1. toast bread
2. heat smart balance or oil in non-stick pan on medium high
3. meanwhile , microwave boca burger in package for 2 minutes
4. when pan is hot , crack egg into it and break yolk with edge of shell
5. sprinkle egg with salt and pepper
6. turn egg over with plastic spatula when ready
7. cook until yolk reaches desired consistency
8. while egg is cooking , spread mayo on one side of toast and put boca burger on top
9. put cheese on other piece of toast
10. when egg is done , put put it on top of cheese
11. put sandwich together and eat before it gets cold !
12. optional: add some hot sauce for extra kick
demonstrations.review: An actual egg mcmuffin from McDonald's (with egg and cheese) is 450 calories and has 27 grams of fat. This doesn't seem like a much healthier choice...though a Boca burger has got to be healthier than McDonald's sausage!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chicken breasts stuffed with artichokes lemon and goats cheese

it’s hard to believe that this delicious chicken with it’s rich filling is indeed low in fat and calories!  only 234 calories!

1. preheat oven to 190c / 375f
2. combine the first six ingredients , mixing well
3. set aside
4. place each chicken breast half between 2 sheets of heavy duty plastic wrap and pound to inch thickness using the side of a rolling pin , being careful not to tear the meat
5. top each breast half with 2 tbs of the cheese mixture
6. roll up jelly roll fashion
7. tuck in the sides and secure each with a wooden pick
8. heat a large non-stick skillet coated with cooking spray over medium high heat
9. add the chicken to the pan , and cook for 3 minutes one each side or until browned
10. wrap handle of the pan with foil and bake for 15 minutes , or until chicken is done
demonstrations.review: How has this recipe gone unrated? We just finished eating it for dinner tonight. WOW!!! As Rachel Ray would say...YUMMO! I have to admit that I took a shortcut and purchased the chicken that is already thin. I also used Panko with italian seasoning rather than Italian bread crumbs. This really is good!

target.recipe_text:
kittencal s easy tuna or chicken noodle casserole

this is a delicious casserole that can be made using either tuna or 1-1/2 cups or more of cooked cubed chicken or even cooked turkey
 --- for a thinner sauce use 1 cup of milk or half and half instead of 3/4 cup, prep time includes boiling the egg noodles, if you are not a garlic-lover then you may omit the garlic powder and to zing the flavor up even more add in 1-1/2 tablespoons of lemon juice

1. preheat oven to 375 degrees f
2. grease a 2-quart casserole dish
3. cook the egg noodles in boiling salted water
4. drain then toss with 2 tablespoons butter
5. in a large saucepan , mix the undiluted mushroom soup , garlic powder , parmesan cheese milk or half and half , sour cream , salt , pepper , chopped onion , pimiento , bell pepper and celery
6. cook over low heat , stirring frequently for 15 minutes
7. add in the tuna or chicken
8. mix to combine
9. combine the mixture with the cooked egg noodles
10. transfer to prepared greased baking dish
11. sprinkle top with the broken ritz crackers
12. bake for about 25 minutes
target.review: A very good and flexible recipe. I added peas and red peppers and used leftover parmesan chicken. Used cheese on top and left out the green peppers and celery rib.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
bella s whole wheat belgian waffles

a good friend gave me this recipe and it produces a waffle that is more substantial. it's not super light and fluffy like other recipes. they are more like "eggo" waffles (in terms of texture, not sweetness). makes 16 (4 1/2" x 4") waffles. when preparing them for freezing, i undercook them slightly, so they don't burn in the toaster.

1. combine flour , sugar , baking powder and salt in a bowl
2. add milk , eggs and oil to the dry ingredients and mix until combined
3. use approximately 1 / 3 cup of batter per waffle
4. bake on waffle iron as per manufacturers instructions
5. i didn't really miss having salt in this recipe , but i thought the first reviewer of this recipe probably had a point about blandness , so i amended the recipe to include 3 / 4 teaspoon of salt
6. other comments have prompted me to add vanilla to the recipe , with wonderful results
7. thanks for your comments !
demonstrations.review: I was worried about heaviness, so I made it using 1 cup whole wheat flour and 3/4 cup white flour. The other 1/4 cup was wheat germ. It turned out really good! Next time I'll try just whole wheat and wheat germ. Maybe some flax meal too. Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
moroccan chickpea salad

this tastes wonderful with all sorts of meals - especially anything done on the bbq. the beans do need to be soaked overnight.

1. put chickpeas in a large saucepan
2. add water to cover and stir in 1 tsp of salt
3. bring to a boil over high heat , then lower heat to medium and simmer until tender , about 1 hour
4. drain the chickpeas and discard any loose skins
5. in a serving bowl , combine all the remaining ingredients
6. add the chickpeas and toss well
7. cover and refrigerate for atleast 4 hours before serving
demonstrations.review: I actually changed this one a lot. I used canned chickpeas. I added the ingredients in a crockpot and let cook on low for several hours. Used a masher/fork to mash some of it after it was done and then added a little bit more spice. Used black olives and pureed onion instead of scallions. I can't remember why I did it that way, but there must have been a good reason. Oh well. Turned out great anyway!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
50  whole wheat bread

this is our "everyday" lunch bread. i make it every night for the next day. i originally got it from the oster bread machine recipe book but i adapted it somewhat. the 100% whole wheat recipe was just too heavy for our family. it makes a 2 lb loaf. once i started making this bread, i couldn't go back to store bought!

1. put the ingredients into the bread machine pan in the order listed
2. select the whole wheat bread cycle
3. remove from the pan when it's done and let cool for 15 minutes before slicing
4. during the summer i reduce the yeast to 1 tsp because it seems to rise so much more during the summer than the winter
5. or you could increase the salt slightly so if you're getting a really huge loaf try one of these 2 things and it should be better for you
6. for some reason atmospheric pressure makes a difference in how a bread rises
7. enjoy !
8. thanks for all your great reviews ! another thing i've been doing to make this even healthier is adding 2 tablespoons of ground flax seed with the flour
9. it doesn't really change the flavour but adds some good for you omega 3s !
demonstrations.review: Good bread - liked that I could use blackstrap molasses. Used oil instead of water.

target.recipe_text:
44 cordial

this recipe is from saveur magazine.  this is a orange, coffee and rum liquer from the west indies.  it takes 44 days to make.

1. poke 44 1 inch slits all over the orange with the
2. stuff a coffee bean into each slit
3. put the orange , sugar and rum in a wide mouthed jar with a tight sealing lid
4. place in a cool , dark spot , swirling the jar occasionally , for 44 days
5. remove and discard the orange
6. strain the liqueur through a cheesecloth lined strainer into a clean bottle and store in the refrigerator or freezer
7. serve neat or over ice
target.review: This is a winner! Easy to make and a show stopper.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
julia child s cherry clafouti

makes a simple and wonderful dessert, or a delicious and indulgent breakfast!

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees f
2. using a blender , combine the milk , 1 / 3 cup sugar , eggs , vanilla , salt and flour , and blend
3. lightly butter an 8-cup baking dish , and pour a 1 / 4-inch layer of the blended mixture over the bottom
4. set remaining batter aside
5. place dish into the oven for about 7-10 minutes , until a film of batter sets in the pan but the mixture is not baked through
6. remove from oven
7. distribute the pitted cherries over the set batter in the pan , then sprinkle with the remaining sugar
8. pour the remaining batter over the cherries and sugar
9. bake in the preheated oven for 45 to 60 minutes , until the clafouti is puffed and brown and a knife inserted into the center comes out clean
10. sprinkle with powdered sugar and serve warm
11. servings: 6-8 for dessert , 4 for breakfast
demonstrations.review: I was sorry to have wasted my valuable blackberries on this recipe. Not very tasty and only saved by ice cream on the side. Old fashioned cobbler would have been a better use of the berries. I was doing a complete Julia Child menu. The boef bourguignon was terrific.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
luscious silky mango ice cream

my entire family fell in love with this ice cream, i tell ya! instead of making my own mango puree, i just bought fresh unsweetened mango puree from the baking store.

1. mango puree:
2. peel and cut the mango into pieces
3. squeeze as much flesh off as possible
4. blend it in the blender or food processor along with the lemon juice
5. strain the mango mix into a bowl , so that the stringy bits are eliminated from the puree
6. you should have about 1 1 / 4 cups mango puree
7. gelato base:
8. whisk egg yolks and sugar till pale and lemony
9. in a medium / heavy saucepan , bring milk and cream to a simmer
10. turn off heat and whisk half of the mixture into the yolks
11. return everything to the sauce pan over a very low heat and keep on stirring it till it thickens
12. remove from heat and strain it into a large bowl
13. let it cool for 5 or 6 minutes and then mix in mango puree
14. refrigerate overnight
15. 10 mins before processing in the ice cream machine , put the mango custard into the freezer and also put the ice cream dasher into the freezer
16. process in your ice cream maker
