demonstrations.review: Luscious gelato! Used mango slices from the jar--Dole?- which worked fine.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kale salad with pine nuts  currants   parmesan

in a surprising twist, tuscan kale is served raw—and makes for a substantial and satisfying winter salad. be sure to choose bunches of tuscan kale with small leaves, which are more tender.  i adapted the recipe from one i found in this month's "bon appétit" (february 2009).  it's by acclaimed chef dan barber, of new york's famous blue hill restaurants.  allow the currants to marinated for at least a few hours.  after that, this dish takes minutes to throw together.

1. place currants in small bowl
2. add 5 tablespoons white balsamic vinegar
3. let soak overnight
4. drain currants
5. whisk remaining 2 tablespoons white balsamic vinegar , rice vinegar , honey , oil , and salt in large bowl
6. add kale , currants , and pine nuts
7. toss to coat
8. let marinate 20 minutes at room temperature , tossing occasionally
9. season to taste with salt and pepper
10. sprinkle cheese shavings over salad and serve
demonstrations.review: This was surprisingly good!. the secret is the macerating and very narrow slicing of the kale. Could not find the Tuscan kale but the ordinary curly worked fine.Loaded with antioxidants!

target.recipe_text:
peachy chicken with orzo

i make this often - the kids love it!  goes great with a salad.

1. drain the peaches
2. reserve the liquid
3. in a large skillet , bring the wine to a boil
4. add in the chicken and brown
5. stir in the onion and bell pepper and cook for 2-3 minutes
6. add in the reserved peach liquid , orzo , water , oil , and seasonings
7. bring to a boil
8. cover and reduce heat
9. allow to simmer for 20-25 minutes , or until orzo is cooked
10. stir in the peaches
11. heat through
12. adjust seasonings and serve
target.review: This was really yummy. I used rice instead of orzo, and it still cooked great. I also left out the bell pepper since I'm not a fan of them. The only bummer was that cooking the rice with the peach juice didn't get as much of the peach flavor that I thought it would have. I might throw in a splash of soy sauce next time for a little extra oomph

demonstrations.recipe_text:
copycat marie callender s cornbread

serve with honey-butter for a great treat!

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. combine all dry ingredients
3. combine remaining ingredients and add to dry ingredients and mix well
4. pour into greased oblong pan
5. bake 35 minutes
demonstrations.review: This was fantastic an sooo easy to make.  I made one batch for myself with a gluten-free pancake mix and another batch with the Bisquick heart health mix for my coworkers.  I also used egg substitute, I Can't Believe It's Not Butter, and Splenda for both batches.  My coworkers loved it, better than the cornbread that came with the bbq!  All the substitutions probably made it healthier as well!  And my bf told me that using the gluten-free mix did not change the texture that much.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
bisquick blueberry muffins

i love the soft texture the bisquick gives these muffins. they  remind me of the boxed muffins i enjoyed as a child. these can be mixed up faster than it takes for your oven to preheat!

1. heat oven to 400 degrees
2. grease muffin pan well
3. stir all ingredients except blueberries in medium bowl , just until moistened
4. fold in berries
5. divide batter evenly in 9 muffin cups
6. bake 13 to 18 minutes or until golden brown
7. cool slightly and remove from pan to wire rack
8. yield: 9 muffins
demonstrations.review: These were pretty yummy.  They were the perfect flavor of blueberry muffins.  I substituted a gluten free pancake mix (since I can't have Bisquick) and it worked out okay.  They did crumble a lot, but a lot less than the other gluten free muffins I've made.  Thanks for posting this!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chicken picante

it doesn't get any easier, or any better than this. the brown sugar mixed with picante sauce is a great new twist for chicken. we like this over rice.

1. place chicken in greased , shallow sided baking dish
2. mix picante sauce , brown sugar , and mustard
3. pour sauce over chicken
4. bake , uncovered at 400 for 30-35 minutes , or until juices run clear
demonstrations.review: I love how easy this recipe is!  I don't really know how to cook and this was one of the first recipes I cooked w/o someone beside me.  And the chicken comes out so juicy!  I served it with some cheese on top.  For another twist you can also add a pinch or two of cinnamon.

target.recipe_text:
awesome bacon tomato dip

oh, you have to try this one!! my family loves dips and spreads, and even the guys got really into this one. i even caught my uncle (who thinks guys are too "macho" for dips), eating it straight from the bowl with a spoon!! best when made day of, and lettuce added just before serving. it gets soggy:(

1. in medium bowl , with mixer , blend sour cream , mayonnaise , cream cheese , cheddar cheese , chopped onion and green pepper , garlic powder , and black pepper
2. crumble bacon into small pieces and add to mixture
3. add chopped tomato and stir well
4. garnish with shredded lettuce just before serving , if desired
5. serve with townhouse crackers or wheat thins
6. also good served in a bread bowl with bread cubes to dip
target.review: I used low-fat cream cheese, fat-free mayo, and fat-free sour cream. I took it to work and it was completely gone by 10:30am. The bowl was scraped clean and even the spoon had been scraped clean with crackers. I never had so many people ask me for a recipe. (I used 2 large fresh garden tomatoes and omitted the green pepper.) Delish! Thank you for the recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
perfect pot stickers  alton brown

i finally got around to making these last night and, while my photos don't exactly reflect it, they were awesome!  i made a very simple dipping sauce of about 2 parts yamasa soy sauce to 1 part rice wine vinegar with some sesame seeds sprinkled on top.  i froze the extra prepared, but uncooked pot stickers on a cookie sheet, each layer separated by waxed paper, then put them in a vacuum sealed food saver bag and back into the freezer. these got pretty consistent 5 star ratings on the foodtv.com site.

1. preheat oven to 200 degrees f
2. combine the first 11 ingredients in a medium-size mixing bowl
3. set aside
4. to form the dumplings , remove 1 wonton wrapper from the package , covering the others with a damp cloth
5. brush 2 of the edges of the wrapper lightly with water
6. place 1 / 2 rounded teaspoon of the pork mixture in the center of the wrapper
7. fold over , seal edges , and shape as desired
8. set on a sheet pan and cover with a damp cloth
9. repeat procedure until all of the filling is gone
10. heat a 12-inch saute pan over medium heat
11. brush with vegetable oil once hot
12. add 8 to 10 potstickers at a time to the pan and cook for 2 minutes , without touching
13. once the 2 minutes are up , gently add 1 / 3 cup chicken stock to the pan , turn the heat down to low , cover , and cook for another 2 minutes
14. remove wontons to a heatproof platter and place in the warm oven
15. clean the pan in between batches by pouring in water and allowing the pan to deglaze
16. repeat until all the wontons are cooked
17. serve immediately
demonstrations.review: Delicious. Next time I'll use less salt, though.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
bars to the stars

this recipe came from a calendar-like cookbook, from wisconsin electric.  the cook who submitted the recipe said it belonged to her aunt who was a caterer.  one of her clients was capt. kangaroo!  note:  cook time includes chill time.

1. melt butterscotch chips and peanut butter together
2. stir in cereal , and press 1 / 2 of mixture into a 9x13 , or smaller , cake pan
3. put in fridge
4. combine and melt chocolate chips , powdered sugar , butter , and water
5. spread over top of refrigerated cereal mixture
6. add remaining 1 / 2 of cereal mixture , and gently press down on top of chocolate layer
7. chill
demonstrations.review:
I have that same Wisconsin Electric cookie cookbook.
Everyone likes these bars- a step up from plain Rice Krispies treats!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mrs  geraldine s ground beef casserole

this recipe came from a local church fund raising cook book. mrs. geraldine is a good friend of the family. she reminds me so much of mrs. clause, that i can't help but smile every time i think of her. this recipe freezes well. do not bake before freezing. just put it together, freeze it, thaw it and cook.

1. brown meat in large skillet or dutch oven
2. add onions , pepper and celery and simmer for 15 minutes
3. add tomatoes and tomato sauce , mushrooms , brown sugar and worcestershire sauce
4. add salt and pepper to taste
5. cook in skillet for 1 hour
6. place cooked pasta in bottom of large casserole dish
7. spoon mushroom soup over pasta
8. pour sauce over the soup and top with cheese
9. bake in 350f oven for 30-45 minutes
10. can sizes do not have to be exact , just as long as they are within a close range , everything will work out
demonstrations.review: Wonderful. The mushroom soup adds an unusual element for a red-sauce-and-pasta casserole, and after baking, I couldn't see any trace of the mushroom soup-- it all soaked up into a heavenly mixed-up sauce. I really liked that the pasta stayed a little separate from the sauce- made for a nice looking serving. I don't think I would have been able to identify that there was soup in the sauce had I not known. Wonderful taste. Might be my favorite casserole now! Thank you, Mrs. Geraldine and Jellyqueen!

target.recipe_text:
mediterranean fish  flounder

you can use any firm fish for this recipe- i have used flounder-aka sole, mahi mahi, halibut and tilapia. it makes a wonderfully easy baked fish with tomatoes, kalamata olives, caper, onions and white wine. it is my absolute favorite way to make fish! i got the recipe from here but do not see it posted anymore so i will added it again for everyone to enjoy- it is so easy and so good!

1. preheat oven to 425 degrees
2. prepare tomatoes if using fresh by plunging them into boiling water , imediately removing them to a bowl of ice water and peeling the skins
3. or you can chop them with the skins on or use canned- it is a person preference thing
4. heat olive oil in a medium skillet over medium heat
5. add onions and saute until tender
6. add garlic and italian seasoning , stirring to combine
7. add tomatoes and cook until tender
8. mix in wine , olives , capers , lemon juice and half of the basil
9. if fresh basil- if fresh basil is not available add a couple teaspoons of dried basil-fresh is always better though
10. reduce heat , blend in parmesan cheese and cook until the mixture is hot and bubbly
11. if you prefer a thick sauce you can cook until the sauce has reduced to a thick sauce , about 15 minutes
12. place fish in a shallow baking dish
13. cover with the sauce mixture and bake in preheated oven 15-20 minutes depending on the fish used
14. fish should flake easily with a fork when done , except for the mahi mahi which flakes when done , just not easily
target.review: This turned out fine for me. I didn't have any capers or onions so I left those out, but I did put in an anchovy fillet and double the garlic. I also left out the italian seasoning and just went with fresh basil from my garden, and left out the parmesan cheese and served it over parmesan cheese polenta. People who didn't like the recipe may just need to tweak it to their own tastes. This is actually similar to a way I had been making tilapia before, baked with tomato sauce, but I think I like this way better. The olives add an excellent flavor to normally bland fish.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
balsamic honey pork tenderloin

this is also great with pork steaks --- make certain to marinate in the fridge for 24 hours.

1. to make the marinade
2. mix the honey , mustard , balsamic vinegar , oil , garlic , green onions and pepper in a large bowl
3. add in the pork tenderloins , and turn to coat
4. cover and place in the refrigerator for 24 hours
5. when ready to cook the pork , remove from the fridge and reserve the marinade liquid
6. place the pork on the grill , and brush with reserved marinade
7. close the grill lid and cook , turning and basting one or two times
8. cook for about 18-20 minutes , or until inside has a hint of pink
9. transfer pork to a cutting board , and let rest for 10 minutes
10. slice into about 1 / 2-inch slices
11. serve on a platter with roasted potatoes
demonstrations.review: I was a little disappointed that the marinade didn't contribute much to the meat. I ended up marinading it for two days, and while the very outside rim of the slices of pork were tasty, the inside tasted completely plain and dry. It would be nice to have some sort of sauce.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s italian melt in your mouth meatballs

cooking the meatballs in simmering pasta sauce  will not only add so much extra flavor to the sauce the meatballs will be melt-in-your-mouth tender, you may of course oven-bake the meatballs for about 25 minutes,  --- don't be afraid to add in more parmesan cheese and a little more milk, there is no need to measure exactly, this recipe is pretty much foolproof, leftover cooked meatballs make a wonderful pizza topping just slice thinly and freeze until ready to use ----- these also make wonderful juicy burgers shaped into patties-- for more of my tried and true recipes check out my food blog at www.kittencalskitchen.com

1. mix all ingredients together in a large bowl
2. shape into small meatballs
3. drop the meatballs into simmering pasta sauce , do not stir for at least 20 minutes or you will risk breaking the meatballs
4. continue cooking in the simmering sauce for another 20 minutes
5. after the 40 minutes cooking time continue cooking your sauce with the meatballs in for as long as desired
demonstrations.review: I used one pound of ground beef and half a pound of Italian sausage. Great texture and the cheese mixed into the meatballs made them really good. I baked my meatballs to drain off some of the fat. It made a big batch, so I froze the leftover meatballs and will try simmering them in pasta sauce to reheat them. I can see this being my go-to meatball recipe from now on.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
easy chocolate raspberry cheesecake

this is really easy, really good, and really gets the comments!

1. preheat oven to 350f degrees
2. with mixer , beat cream cheese until fluffy , gradually beat in sweetened condensed milk until smooth
3. add egg , lemon juice and vanilla , mix well
4. arrange raspberries on bottom of crust
5. slowly pour cheese mixture over fruit
6. bake 30-35 minutes until center is almost set , cool
7. top cheesecake with chocolate glaze and chill
8. glaze-----------
9. in a small saucepan over low heat , melt 2 oz of semi-sweet baking chocolate with 1 / 4 cup whipping cream
10. cook and stir until thickened and smooth , remove from heat
demonstrations.review:
This cheesecake is delicious. I'll only change one thing, and that is you should bake it at 300 degrees for 50 minutes. The more gentle baking makes it turn out even better.

Also, if you use frozen raspberries, make sure you thaw them first.

target.recipe_text:
yummy banana bread

this is the best banana bread i have ever had!! it is so moist, i believe it is due to the over ripe bananas and the sour cream. you must try it!!!

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. with an electric mixer , cream the butter and sugar until light and fluffy , next add the eggs
3. beat thoroughly
4. add the honey and mix well
5. sift in the dry ingredients
6. blend well
7. add sour cream , bananas and vanilla
8. again blend well
9. at this time if you are adding nuts add them and mix them thoroughly
10. you can bake this as muffins , mini breads or a bread , it's up to you
11. adjust the baking time to the choice you make
12. for a bread bake one hour or until a toothpick comes out of the center and its clean
target.review: This is the BEST banana bread I have ever had! It smelled wonderful while cooking and tasted even better. Very moist and delicious. Thank you!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
awesome bacon tomato dip

oh, you have to try this one!! my family loves dips and spreads, and even the guys got really into this one. i even caught my uncle (who thinks guys are too "macho" for dips), eating it straight from the bowl with a spoon!! best when made day of, and lettuce added just before serving. it gets soggy:(

1. in medium bowl , with mixer , blend sour cream , mayonnaise , cream cheese , cheddar cheese , chopped onion and green pepper , garlic powder , and black pepper
2. crumble bacon into small pieces and add to mixture
3. add chopped tomato and stir well
4. garnish with shredded lettuce just before serving , if desired
5. serve with townhouse crackers or wheat thins
6. also good served in a bread bowl with bread cubes to dip
demonstrations.review: I made this for our New Years Eve Party and it was crowd pleaser. Thanks for a great recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mashed sweet potatoes

this is our version for thanksgiving. wonderful fresh taste! not for those who want a marshmallow covered sweet potato! recipe can be double but you must allow for more cooking time.

1. combine butter , cream , salt , sugar , and sweet potatoes in large saucepan
2. cook , covered , over low heat , stirring occasionally , until potatoes fall apart when poked with fork
3. this will take between 30 to 45 minutes
4. take off heat and mash sweet potatoes in saucepan with potato masher
5. you can also put potatoes into kitchen aid mixer and mix
6. stir in salt and pepper to taste
7. serve immediately
demonstrations.review: This was super easy to make, and turned out wonderful!!! I used half & half (that is what I had on hand), other than that I followed the directions exactly. My daughter wants me to make this recipe all the time now. Definitely a keeper! Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
should be illegal oven bbq ribs

after not being able to find restaurant ribs that satified my hot sweet appetite, i carefully attempted various combinations of flavors until i found one that i and my family thought was perfect. hope you enjoy them too.

1. place all ingredients together in large roasting pan
2. cut ribs apart for easier serving
3. mix together making sure to coat all ribs with this semi-dry paste
4. spread ribs out evenly on bottom of pan
5. cover lightly with foil
6. bake at 375 degrees for approximately 1 hour
7. turning or stirring occasionally
8. you can use broiler for these ribs , just watch more closely , and adjust cooking time
9. these ribs are also great finished on the grill for a few minutes on each side
demonstrations.review: WOW! These are awesome! I would not change a thing. Thank you for sharing this great recipe! It is a new family favorite!!

target.recipe_text:
taco bell quesadillas

i used to love these when i was younger, i could eat two in one sitting! i haven't had fast food in a year or two, but these taste like i remember taco bell's quesadillas tasting. i hope you enjoy it as much as i do.

1. combine sauce ingredients and stir until smooth
2. grill chicken in vegetable oil and cut into thin slices
3. preheat skillet over medium heat
4. one at a time , lay tortilla into hot skillet and sprinkle with 1 / 4 cup of each shredded cheese and 1 / 2 cheese slice on one side of the tortilla
5. arrange about 1 / 4 cup chicken slices over tortilla on the same half covered with cheese
6. on the empty side , spread about one tablespoon of sauce
7. fold over , and press gently with spatula
8. cook until cheese is melted and slice each into 4 pieces
target.review: This was fabulous!  My family loved it.  I left out the jalapenos as I have 3 kids, 2 of which don't enjoy spicy foods.  The sauce added just enough kick without the peppers.  This recipe is a keeper!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s make ahead mashed potatoes

preparing this ahead will save you tons of time in the kitchen, you may make them up to 3 days in advance, use only russet potatoes for this reds will not work the same, you may also add in 1/2 cup half and half cream or milk if desired, also the cheddar cheese is only optional if i am serving it to guests at my holiday table i most always omit and sprinkle a light dusting of paprika on top, or you may add it into the potato mixture if desired, and if you are serving a large crowd you may want to double and bake and serve in two pans ---------- don't wait to make this for the holidays, these are that good i think you will find yourself making them all the time!

1. butter a 13 x 9-inch casserole dish
2. cook potatoes in a large pot of boiling water with 1 tablespoon salt and 1 tablespoon white vinegar until just fork-tender drain and place in a large bowl
3. using an electric mixer beat the hot potatoes until just semi smooth and still a little chunky
4. add in cream cheese , sour cream , butter , onion powder , salt and black pepper
5. mix until combined and smooth
6. spread the mixture into prepared baking dish
7. if desired you may sprinkle the top lightly with paprika , then allow to come down to room temperature
8. cover and refrigerate for up to 3 days
9. when ready to bake set oven to 350 degrees f
10. bake uncovered for about 25-30 minutes or until hot
11. if desired sprinkle the shredded cheddar cheese on top and return to oven to melt
demonstrations.review:
My kids hate potatoes (unless they are french fried).  They loved these though even asked for seconds. 
I used low fat cream cheese and sour cream and added a bit of 1% milk to make them a bit creamier, but still delicious.  Even the leftovers a couple of days after were great heated up.
Thanks for posting this recipe.  I will be using it for years to come!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
delicious fried chicken breast

better than fast food takeout, brining is the key to this tender juicy chicken, any leftovers can be stuffed in between a crusty bun topped with mayo, mustard and a leaf of lettuce, this also works well using bone-on chicken pieces but frying time will need to be adjusted ---  plan ahead the chicken needs to soak in the buttermilk for 8-24 hours (24 hours is even better). try to purchase large thick chicken breasts for this to make the slicing in half easier, use a sharp knife for slicing. i usually serve this with my recipe #149547 --- if you cannot find old bay seasoning, use 2 teaspoons of seasoning salt in place of regular salt --- you will *love* this fried chicken! :)

1. soak the chicken breasts in the buttermilk and salt for 8-24 hours
2. when ready to make the breasts , mix all coating ingredients together , and coat each chicken breast
3. place oil in a 10-inch heavy-bottomed skillet up to about 1 / 3 of the pan
4. heat to about 350f , then reduce heat a bit just before frying the breasts
5. cook / fry about 8 minutes per side
demonstrations.review: It is delicious!  Even better when tossed with Franks Red Hot a melted butter.  Fabulous for buffalo chicken.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
salt potatoes new york style

for real authentic upstate ny flavor use 1 cup of salt. try these for your next bbq or crab boil! yum! leftovers can be used for home fries.

1. place the potatoes and water in a large pot
2. pour the salt over the potatoes , cover , and bring to a boil over high heat
3. reduce the heat to medium and cook for 25 minutes , or until the potatoes are fork-tender
4. serve with the melted butter for dipping
demonstrations.review: Absolutely wonderful!  I wouldn't have though that salt (that much) would make potatoes taste so much better.  Left overs?  Not a chance.  Thanks for this recipe.  I won't cook new potatoes any other way.

target.recipe_text:
bahamian boiled  fish

boiled make it sound awful (& is really a misnomer as the fish is simmered gently until just done) but it is unbelievably delicious & soul satisfying. located in the miami herald who adapted it from culinaria the caribbean by rosemary parkinson, (konemann, 1999).
the miami herald article said: "bahamian people know there is nothing like a good fish broth or soup to give you strength for the day ahead. any white fish can be used but grouper is preferred (see source). serve with grits and cornbread." if you can locate fish peppers to use in this dish, they are wonderful.

1. place the fish in a non-reactive dish and add the lime juice
2. sprinkle with salt and pepper to taste
3. pour 2 cups of water into a pot and add the onions , garlic , parsley and thyme , potatoes , butter and chile pepper
4. bring to a boil and boil about 10 minutes or until the potatoes are almost done
5. add the fish with marinade juices , reduce the heat to low and simmer about 10 minutes , or until the fish is just cooked through and starting to flake
6. taste and adjust for salt and pepper
7. serve hot
target.review: Double the potatoes and rice.  Plus add some more heat with some hot sauce.  Serve over rice.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
delicious drumsticks

you have to try these drumsticks! they truly are delicious.

1. heat the oven to 425 degrees
2. mix flour , salt , paprika and pepper in a bowl
3. dip chicken drumsticks into margarine
4. roll in flour mixture to coat
5. arrange in an ungreased square pan , 8x8x2 inches
6. bake uncovered until juice of chicken is no longer pink when centers of thickest pieces are cut , about 50 minutes
demonstrations.review: Quick and simple.  Chicken cooked perfectly, but a little light on the spices.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chicken in cumin sauce

this is from the congo cookbook and one i have not tried yet. it sounds yummy though. when i do make it (which will be soon) i will post any changes or suggestions. note: the recipe calls for one can tomato paste, so i am assuming it is the small can.....and i am guessing as to the ounces.

1. in a large stew pot combine everything except the chicken
2. stir until all is well mixed
3. bring to a boil the reduce heat , cover and simmer for about 20 minutes stirring occasionally
4. add chicken , cover and simmer for another half hour or more , stirring occasionally , until chicken is cooked through
5. serve with rice
demonstrations.review: Try serving with a dollop of sour cream.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pierogi stir fry

a simple yet humble recipe courtesy of my mother in law.  heck, i didn't know what to call this recipe! ;) we use store bought cheemo brand frozen perogie from canada for this dish, but you can certainly use your own homemade perogie. (i hope one day to learn how to make them and spell the word correctly.) sometimes i add a potato to the mix to "stretch" the meal even though perogies already contain potatoes. the cheemo brand has a cheddar cheese/potato variety we really like and an herb/roasted garlic one, too. i noticed the cheemo site has a similar recipe to this one. check it out! serve with a tossed green salad that contains beets, in keeping with the ukrainian/russian/eastern european theme. a recipezaar member is going to have to set me straight on the correct spelling of pierogies/perogie/-both singular and plural forms.

1. in a large frying pan , cook the bacon until crisp
2. set aside to drain and cool
3. remove the bacon fat and add 2 tablespoons oil
4. add the frozen perogies , carrots , and potato and cook on medium-high heat for about 10 minutes
5. add the onion and bell pepper
6. cook another 5-7 minutes , until the onion and bell pepper start to char at the edges
7. stir in the cabbage and garlic
8. cook another 2-3 minutes
9. reduce heat if necessary
10. crumble the bacon and stir it into the pan
11. season with salt and pepper to taste
12. serve with sour cream
13. servings are estimated
demonstrations.review: A good idea gone bad.  Extremely flavorless.

target.recipe_text:
buttery shrimp and pasta

this is a really simple dish to make and it's quite elegant.

1. have pasta ready
2. in lg skillet , heat butter
3. add shrimp and garlic
4. saute 4 minutes , remove shrimp from skillet
5. add half and half
6. bring to a boil
7. reduce heat and simmer for 15 minutes , stirring frequently
8. add shrimp , basil , cheese , pepper and pepper flakes
9. pour sauce into a bowl
10. add pasta and toss well
target.review: Yummy! We added frozen peas that had been just defrosted (Trader Joes rocks!) and a pinch of salt. Both boys (9 & 10) rated it a GRRRREAT!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
toasted orzo with peas and parmesan

from cook's illustrated.  this is supposed to be a side dish, but i would also consider serving this as a light meatless entree.

1. heat butter in 12-inch nonstick skillet over medium-high heat
2. add onion and salt and cook , stirring frequently , until onion has softened and is beginning to brown , about 5 minutes
3. add garlic and cook until fragrant , about 30 seconds
4. add orzo and cook , stirring frequently , until most of orzo is lightly browned and golden , 5 to 6 minutes
5. turn off heat and add vermouth and chicken broth
6. go back to medium-high heat and bring to boil
7. reduce heat to medium-low and simmer , stirring occasionally , until all liquid has been absorbed and orzo is tender , 10 to 15 minutes
8. gently stir in peas , cheese , nutmeg , and pepper to taste
9. remove from heat and let it stand until peas are heated through , about 2 minutes
demonstrations.review: Just what I was looking for. Five kids and two adults give it a thumbs up!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
creamy cucumbers

cucumbers in sour cream. a wonderful summer side dish, cool and refreshing.

1. peel cucumbers and slice in half lengthwise
2. with a small spoon , scrape out seeds and slice cucumbers about 1 / 4 inch thick slices
3. in a storage bowl with a lid , combine the sour cream , vinegar , sugar , chives and salt and pepper
4. mix until well blended
5. add cucumbers , replace lid , and shake bowl to mix
6. store in refrigerator until ready to serve , at least 15 minutes
7. serve cold
demonstrations.review: Cool and refreshing at a picnic, T=this was a hit at our house. We'll be making it again soon!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
lick the bowl clean bacon broccoli salad

first time i had this at a church potluck, another lady and i were nearly fighting over the last serving--it was so good!  so we took the empty bowl and went looking for the owner to beg for the recipe.   here it is!

1. fry the bacon
2. break into pieces
3. set aside
4. trim broccoli stems , cut into 1 / 2 - 1-inch pieces
5. cut flower ends into small pieces , too
6. put into a large serving bowl
7. slice green onions into the broccoli
8. add raisins and nuts to the broccoli and onions
9. tossing well
10. add bacon now or wait until serving time if you don't like it to get soggy-ish
11. dressing: mix dressing ingredients in a small bowl until sugar dissolves
12. add dressing to the broccoli mixture
13. stir well to coat everything
14. if you didn't add the bacon earlier , add it now
15. best served at room temperature
16. options: leave out the raisins or nuts or bacon--just don't leave them all out at the same time
17. instead of 3 bunches of broccoli , add some cauliflower--very pretty , too !
demonstrations.review: Super easy and a new family favorite. I left the raisins out so my son would eat it. The whole family loved the salad.

target.recipe_text:
quick tomato barley soup

delicious and nutricious

1. puree tomatoes in food processor
2. pour into saucepan and add remaining ingredients
3. bring to a boil , reduce heat and simmer , stirring occasionally , for about 30 minutes or until barley is soft
target.review: This combines two of my favorite soups into one: Tomato and Barley, how can you go wrong? This was really easy to make and tasted just great. The only thing I added was some salt and pepper to taste. Well done PolishRuski!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
fish chowder

this is the best new england fish chowder ever. it is my mom's recipe. she is the best cook. it is simple and filling. whenever we came home from school and knew this was cooking it was a joyful day. hope you like it.

1. cook chopped bacon and onion in large pot
2. cook slowly
3. onion should be soft but not brown
4. remove onion and bacon from pot
5. set aside
6. leave 2 tablespoons bacon fat in pot
7. put potatoes in same pot
8. add just enough water to cover
9. cook 5-10 minutes
10. add fish to pot
11. cook until fish is flaky
12. remove skin from fish
13. thicken with flour mixed with a little water
14. bring to a boil
15. reduce heat until no longer boiling
16. add milk , bacon and onion
17. heat but do not boil
18. salt and pepper to taste
demonstrations.review: This is very much like my family's recipe, except we use salt pork cut into lardons instead of the bacon. I like to add a can of peas, or sometimes a can of cream corn as well.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
korean spicy chicken wings   restaurant recipe

this is a fantastic recipe i came across whilst roaming the 'net! it comes from the owner of a popular korean restaurant where these chicken wings were the most popular of all his special order dishes. time to make doesn't include chilling time.

1. rinse the wings in cold water , then lightly salt and pepper them
2. let stand about 10 to 15 minutes
3. place wings in a large bowl and pour the milk over them , then place in refrigerator for about one hour , turning three to four times
4. for the stir fry sauce: place the ginger and garlic into a blender with just enough water to liquefy the mix
5. pour into a small mixing bowl and add all other sauce ingredient & mix well
6. finely chop the green / spring onion and set aside
7. chicken wings: discard the milk and let wing section drain until just damp
8. heat oil in a large cooking pot
9. roll wings in starch and deep fry until golden brown then drain
10. transfer the chicken to a large stir fry pan or wok over medium to medium high heat , add the sauce , and stir fry until all liquid is gone
11. place onto a serving tray and garnish with the green onion and sesame seed
12. serve as an appetizer or with sticky rice and ban chan for a meal
demonstrations.review: These taste like the wings you would get at a bar in Seoul! Superb! My family and friends could not eat them fast enough. This is going to be my stand-by party fare for sure!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cornflake penuche

this is a very crispy and crunchy candy. the trick to this candy is to keep the candy in the pan, covered loosely with wax paper for 2 days before you eat it. if you try it too soon, it will be tough and chewy.

1. spray a 8x8x2 pan with cooking spray
2. line the pan with aluminum foil and spray again
3. in a 4 quart saucepan over low heat , melt butter
4. add sugar and stir well with wooden spoon until sugar is dissolved
5. stir and slowly add evaporated milk
6. keep the heat on low and add the cornflakes
7. stir until well mixed
8. remove from heat and press into prepared pan
9. cover loosely with waxed paper
10. let stand for 48 hours in cool dry place
11. do not refrigerate
12. turn candy out on smooth surface
13. remove foil
14. break into eating-size pieces
15. store in airtight container for no more that 3-4 days
demonstrations.review:
Delicious and wonderful. I made it just as described, and it was a hit! 
The next batch I added a small pinch of Kosher salt to counter the sweetness.
Both batches were great. 
I can see adding chocolate chips or coconut to boost the flavor.
All around a great recipe Corn Flake Candy!

target.recipe_text:
awesome turkey meatloaf

this is truly the best meatloaf recipe i've ever had, and it's actually pretty healthy! (i'm curious to see the nutrition label)  i got it originally from my step-mom but i've changed a couple things.  your kitchen will smell absolutely amazing, i love making this on cold winter nights!

1. preheat your oven to 500 degrees and spray a roasting pan with cooking spray
2. just throw ingredients together in a large bowl and work it up
3. don't handle the meat too much , or it may make it tough
4. form into a loaf in the bowl and then transfer to the dish and finish forming it there
5. do not cover
6. adjust the oven to 350 degrees and place the meatloaf inside
7. bake for approximately 1 hour and 15 minutes
8. enjoy !
target.review: Great recipe! This makes a beautiful presentation.  I used ground turkey, and the vegetables looked scrumptious with the light colored meat.  I didn't have seasoned bread crumbs so I added thyme and basil to the mix. (I may reduce the amount of bread crumbs next time.)  I also used Muir Glen's fire roasted tomatoes in place of regular tomatoes. This is a delicious meatloaf.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
julia robert s fresh peach crisp

celeb dish out of the august 07 good housekeeping.

1. preheat oven to 400f grease 13" by 9" glass baking dish
2. prepare filling: in large bowl , toss peaches with lemon juice
3. add whisky , granulated sugar , and 1 / 4 cup brown sugar
4. toss to coat
5. spread mixture in baking dish and dot with 2 tablespoons butter
6. prepare topping: in large bowl , mix flour , cinnamon , and 1 / 2 cup brown sugar
7. with pastry blender , cut in 10 tablespoons butter until coarse crumbs form
8. press crumbs together into 1 / 2-inch clumps
9. sprinkle over peaches
10. bake crisp 30-35 minutes or until topping is brown and fruit is hot and bubbly
11. cool 20 minutes
12. serve warm with frozen yogurt if you like
demonstrations.review: This is wonderful!  I made it for a dinner party and received many compliments.  My 1/2" clumps turned out to be 1/2" flat circles.  It gave a beautiful look to the topping.  I just pressed small portions of the topping mix between my fingers and placed them on top of the peaches until it was completely covered.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
old fashioned english lavender tea scones

when i was back home in england recently, i visited a local lavender farm called wold's way lavender in north yorkshire; we had tea and these delicious lavender scones in their delightful little tea room; this is my attempt to recreate those scones - using some of my home-grown culinary lavender from the garden here in france! i have made them several times now and they have turned out just as i remembered them, especially good if split whilst still warm, buttered and spread with lavender honey or lavender-infused cream! just a note of interest......lavender was often used during tudor and elizabethan times in the preparation of a wide variety of dishes and was a particular favourite of queen elizabeth i. the palace gardeners were required to have lavender flowers available at all times which were used to make conserve of lavender (a mixture of lavender flowers and sugar) and sweet lavender tisane, a drink made with lavender flowers, boiling water and honey.

1. pre-heat the oven to 220c / 450f , then lightly flour a baking tray
2. sift the flour with the baking powder & salt
3. rub the butter with the flour until the mixture resembles breadcrumbs
4. stir in the sugar
5. make a deep well in the flour , pour in the liquid and mix to a soft doughy texture with your hands
6. sprinkle on the lavender flowers and knead into the dough very lightly until it is just smooth
7. roll out the dough on a lightly floured board & cut out scone rounds
8. brush the scones with the beaten egg , and sprinkle a few lavender flowers on top if you wish
9. bake in oven for 7 - 10 minutes or until well risen and brown
10. leave to cool
11. serve with butter , lavender honey or lavender-infused cream
demonstrations.review: Light and lovely.  Peace fills the house when I make these.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
bannock

this is an adopted recipe. the original introduction stated "bannock is a native indian fry bread. simple and quick to make. this recipe comes from a magazine article. the woman who taught the author of the article to make bannock said that "rich indians add raisins to their bannock"."

1. mix flour , baking powder , sugar and salt together
2. mix with enough water so that the mixture becomes a dough
3. form into 4-6 large , thick patties
4. fry on lightly oiled frying pan , turning when the bottom is golden
5. good served warm
6. if desired , spread with honey , jam , butter , or peanut butter
7. traditionally bannock would have been made with whatever ingredients were on hand
8. for example , adding blueberries if they're in season
9. this freezes well
10. freeze , already baked , in a labeled ziploc bag with the air squeezed out as much as possible
11. to serve , bring to room temperature by removing from the bag and letting rest on the counter for a few hours
12. speed up the process , by baking or microwaving until the desired temperature is reached
demonstrations.review: This is a wonderful recipe.  It is delicious and a great way to add fresh bread to any meal without adding too much time.  Later this year I am taking a 16 day river trip through the Grand Canyon with 11 other people.  I am in charge of the menu planning and food supplies. I was thrilled to find and try this recipe. I am planning on taking several pre-mixed ziplocks of "Bannock Mix" with us on the river.  I am sure my fellow rafters will be delighted when the Bannock comes off the griddle.  Thanks for the recipe!

target.recipe_text:
very vanilla cupcakes

go the extra mile and make these with the vanilla sugar described below--sensational! these are really wonderful with coffee-cream cheese frosting (see my recipes for it).

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. grease and flour 24 standard-size muffin cups , or line with paper wrappers
3. set aside
4. whisk together the flour , baking powder , and salt
5. set aside
6. in a large bowl , using an electric mixer on high speed , cream the butter until light and fluffy
7. gradually add the sugar
8. continue beating until very light and fluffy
9. reduce mixer speed to medium
10. beat in the eggs , 2 at a time , then the vanilla
11. reduce mixer speed to low
12. alternately beat in the flour mixture with the milk , just until blended
13. spoon the batter into the prepared cups
14. bake for 20-25 minutes , until the tops are soft but springy
15. cool 5-10 minutes in the tins on a wire rack
16. carefully invert and cool completely
17. frost as desired
18. for a more intense vanilla flavor , make vanilla sugar: bury a halved vanilla bean in a container of granulated sugar
19. cover tightly and let stand for a few days to let the flavor develop
20. stir every so often
target.review: To put it mildly THESE ARE FANTASTIC!!! My one and only problem with these is the fact that I used all my butter making the cupcakes, and I really wanted to make buttercream frosting to put on them. But still was not disappointed in the least in the flavor and texture. What  a perfect cupcake! Never again will I buy them at the store, not with this recipe on hand. In order to not over mix these, I beat the dry ingredients and milk in the butter, sugar mixture by hand. Wonderful!! HMMM. It's 4am, I wonder if anyone would notice this only made 12 and not 24? yummmmie. Thank you for sharing

demonstrations.recipe_text:
rita s famous dressing balls

these are a tradition in my mother-in-law's family.  i never liked dressing until i had these.  they get a nice golden brown on the outside and taste great with gravy.

1. place bread in a large bowl and let sit overnight
2. preheat oven to 350
3. saut onions and celery in butter or margarine tender
4. pour over bread and toss with hands to mix
5. add chicken broth and mix with hands again
6. add salt and pepper to taste
7. add eggs and celery seed and mix thoroughly
8. form into 2" balls and put in a baking dish
9. bake for about 45 minutes or until golden brown
demonstrations.review: We loved these. They are going to definately be a part of our menu. Very simple to make, and goes a long way. They freeze really well.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
featherweight breakfast cake

the recipe was given to me 25 years ago. this is a very quick and light breakfast cake.  not too sweet and delicate.

1. preheat oven to 375 degrees
2. grease 8x8 square pan
3. melt butter and cool slightly and add milk and beaten egg , set to the side
4. in bowl , sift the next four ingredients , 2 times
5. add butter , milk , and egg mixture and stir only enough to smooth out any lumps
6. combine the remaining sugar and cinnamon for the topping , in a small bowl or in a ziploc bag
7. pour batter into greased pan and sprinkle the mixture of sugar and cinnamon over the top and bake 12 to 15 minutes
demonstrations.review: Absolutely fantastic. Sprinkle with powdered sugar for a touch of sweetness. This cake raises into a terrific breakfast cake. I had to make one small adjustment as I was out of eggs. I used 1 tsp. Baking Powder, 1 tsp oil and 1/4 cup water. Still this turned out wonderful. Perfect with coffee in the morning, or anytime! Thanks for this permanent addition to by cookbook!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
fudge upside down cake

this is a good one for chocolate lovers.

1. cream together 3 / 4 cup sugar and butter
2. stir in milk
3. sift flour , baking powder , salt and 2 tbsp cocoa together
4. add to creamed mixture and beat until smooth
5. stir in walnuts
6. spread batter into a square 9 inch pan
7. in a small bowl combine brown sugar , 1 / 2 cup granulated sugar and 1 / 3 cup of cocoa
8. sprinkle over the batter
9. pout the boiling water over the top
10. bake at 350 for 35-40 minutes
11. the cake will rise to the top and boiling water will combine with the sugar / cocoa mixture to make a rich syrup underneath
demonstrations.review:
I doubled this recipe because we were having company over. And I have to admit that I was doubting it would turn out when I poured 3 cups water over the top of it. 
 But this is and excellent cake with a very good hot fudge sauce. We ate it while it was still hot. Everyone enjoyed this. And I will definately make this one again. Thanks for the post.

target.recipe_text:
vegan banana bread

back when i was vegan...yeah, those interesting times. i have to say that whatever your food choices this is the best banana bread ever. seriously. even my family (non-vegan, food nazis) loved it. but you can always replace soy milk with cows milk and make this non vegan. recipe from http://www.theppk.com

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. spray a 8x4 bread pan with non stick cooking spray
3. sift together flour , baking soda , salt and spices
4. cream together the margarine and sugars
5. add bananas , soy milk , apple cider vinegar and vanilla
6. add the wet ingredients to the dry and mix well
7. pour batter into pan
8. sprinkle brown sugar on top
9. bake for an hour to an hour 10 minutes
target.review: Wow... Ã¼ber-tasty banana bread!!  Will definitely be making this one every time my nanners get too ripe.  Think I'll throw in some walnuts next time.  Thanks for posting!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
my favorite chocolate chip cookies

get a glass of cold milk ready! this has been my favorite chocolate chip cookie recipe of all time, found in a betty crocker cookbook years ago. once i made it for my hs latin class and it became a class tradition and a family favorite...thank you, betty!

1. cream shortening , butter , and sugars in large mixing bowl
2. blend in eggs and vanilla
3. combine dry ingredients and add to butter mixture
4. mix until well blended
5. stir in chocolate chips
6. drop by rounded teaspoon onto ungreased baking sheets
7. bake at 375 for 7-10 minutes until golden brown
8. i like chewy cookies and if you do too , adjust the baking time accordingly)
demonstrations.review: This recipe IS my new favorite!  They came out perfectly.  I followed the recipe to a "t", baking for 10 minutes (I made larger cookies, so it only made 4 dozen and they needed the extra couple of minutes to bake.)  Fantastic recipe; thanks for sharing!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
reduced calorie banana bread

this banana bread is  good & moist, lower in calories and fat. the recipe comes from ladies home journal with rave reviews. good with nutmeg, added with the cinnamon. i made this using splenda for baking,1/3 cup, was plenty sweet.

1. in a medium mixing bowl stir together flour , baking powder , baking soda , cinnamon , and salt , set aside
2. in a large mixing bowl stir together egg whites , banana , sugar , and oil
3. stir flour mixture into banana mixture until just moistened
4. spray a 8x4x2-inch loaf pan with nonstick cooking spray
5. spread batter in prepared pan
6. bake in a 350 degree oven 45 to 50 minutes or until toothpick inserted near middle comes out clean
7. cool bread in the pan for 10 minutes
8. remove from pan and cool throughly on a wire rack
9. for eaiser slicing , wrap the bread in plastic wrap and store overnight
10. make ahead directions
11. cool completely , wrap in release foil , then seal in a plastic bag , freeze for up to 3 months
demonstrations.review:
Great recipe.  I actually found it on bhg.com and was going to type it up here when I found this.
I substituted sugar with the same amount of brown sugar (no health benefits, just what I had) and it added a nice, caramel-y dimension to the recipe.  I also sprinkled the top with chopped walnuts before baking.  Came out fantastic!  Thanks for adding this recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
easy microwave polenta

my mom used to make this for us kids when we were little. we ate it with fried eggs instead of toast or bread. sometimes we had it with syrup on it like pancakes. i still make and love this. i had this with eggs this morning. really brings back childhood memories for me. may keep in refrigerator several days. use an old metal ice cube tray (minus divider) or pan equal to that size, or use a couple of canned vegetable cans, emptied and washed and sprayed with butter spray.

1. combine water , cornmeal and salt in a large glass bowl , stirring with a wire whip till well blended
2. put in microwave and cover with a sheet of wax paper
3. microwave on high for 6 minutes
4. stir well again
5. microwave on high for another 5 minutes
6. mixture should be very thick now
7. stir and put into sprayed container you have chosen
8. refrigerate till cold
9. remove from container , slice about 1 / 4 inch thick , and fry in butter flavored cooking spray till lightly browned
10. turn and brown on other side
11. eat with fried eggs , with syrup on it like pancakes , or italian style
demonstrations.review: Thank you for such a simple, great recipe!  I, too, had to play with the timing a bit-- probably my microwave's fault-- but a small price to pay for an easy side dish!  I've yet to try it as a breakfast food, but have made it 3 or 4 times with fresh, steamed string beans and a bowl of vegan chili.  A keeper!

target.recipe_text:
smashed fingerling potatoes

a great side dish to any meal, these unusually prepared potatoes are an attention-getter and taste divine!  spark them up even further with another herb of your choice.  prep/cook times are approximate. note: some of the photos posted are of baby yukon potatoes (i think!) which are very similar in taste, texture and color to fingerlings.

1. wash / scrub the fingerling potatoes and boil , unpeeled , for 12 minutes
2. drain and let cool
3. take each fingerling between your hands and squash it between your palms
4. the idea is to beak the skin and flatten the potato , but not to crush it completely
5. it should still stay intact as much as possible
6. heat a skillet with to 1 of oil on high heat
7. when the oil is hot , about 350f , deep-fry each fingerling , turning them over midway when each side is browned
8. drain on paper towels
9. in another pan , melt butter and add minced garlic and parsley
10. stir briefly over medium heat to release flavors , then toss fingerling potatoes into this mixture
target.review: My teeneaged sons loved this. I used the red,white and blue fingerlings. Did not go well smashing with fist so I used the flat side of the meat tenderiser. Used canola oil. I chopped 3 garlic cloves and fried in 2 Tbsp butter. As other reviewer suggested we sprinkled 1 Tbsp. parmesan cheese. Next time I will add a touch of paprika. Thanks for the recipe Sandi

demonstrations.recipe_text:
nestle toll house chocolate chip pan cookie

this recipe was in my paper recently and i made them for my co-workers. divine! i looked & looked and was surprised i couldn't find it already on zaar.

1. preheat oven to 375 grease a 15x10-inch jelly roll pan
2. combine flour , baking soda and salt in small bowl
3. beat butter , both sugars and vanilla in large mixer bowl
4. add eggs one at a time , beating well after each
5. gradually beat flour mixture into butter mixture
6. stir in chocolate chips and nuts
7. spread into prepared pan
8. bake 20-25 minutes or until golden brown
demonstrations.review: Yummy!  I pressed the dough into a jelly pan. 20 minutes. Super easy.  Thank you newspapergal!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
caramelized baked chicken legs wings

delicious! yummy  caramelized legs, kids love these! so quick and easy and no marinating required. just prepare the sauce, pour over the chicken and pop in the oven!  i actually like this with wings better ;-)
 

very important to leave it in the oven until it has caramelized to avoid disappointment. 

thank you to everyone for their positive reviews!

try adding sambal oelek as chef  #27416 has suggested in his review. what a great idea ;-)

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees fahrenheit or 180 degrees celsius
2. place chicken in a 9x13 inch baking dish
3. mix together the oil , soy sauce , ketchup , honey , garlic , salt and pepper
4. pour over the chicken
5. bake in preheated oven for one hour , or until sauce is caramelized
6. could also use wings or pork ribs
demonstrations.review: Simple and family enjoyed this.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
harvest pumpkin cheesecake

indulge!!

1. in a small bowl , combine cracker crumbs and sugar
2. stir in the butter
3. press onto the bottom and 2 inches up the sides of a greased 9-inch springform pan
4. bake at 350 degrees for 5 minutes
5. cool on a wire rack
6. in a mixing bowl , beat cream cheese , sugar and vanilla until smooth
7. add eggs , pumpkin and spices
8. beat just until combined
9. pour into crust
10. place cheesecake / pan in a large rectangular baking pan filled with 2 inches of hot water
11. place in a 350 degree oven and bake for 1 hour or until center is almost set
12. remove cheesecake from oven and water-filled pan and cool on a wire rack for 10 minutes
13. carefully run a knife around edge of pan to loosen
14. cool 1 hour longer
15. refrigerate until completely cooled
16. remove sides of pan just before serving
17. garnish with whipped cream
demonstrations.review: I followed the instructions, which did not instruct to wrap foil or do anything other than to place cheesecake pan straight into water. It was my first time so next time I will not place in water. Disaster and waste of money.

target.recipe_text:
toffee dip with apples

i served this at a party and people kept raving about it and asking for the recipe. i must admit, i was addicted and was hoping for left overs - but it was all gone.

1. combine first 4 ingredients in a bowl
2. beat at medium speed of a mixer until smooth
3. add toffee bits and mix well
4. cover and chill
5. combine juice and apples in a bowl
6. toss well
7. drain apples
8. serve with dip
target.review: Easy, easy, quick, great to make ahead, and very yummy! I have made this several times, always with great results. Most recently, I served it to a group at church, where it caused quite a stir with the crowd. Tart Granny Smiths seem to be the favorite to balance the sweetness of the dip. I use a handy corer/wedger device that makes it so easy to cut the apples in one quick motion. If I can't find pineapple juice, I have substituted orange juice with good results. I put the apples and juice in gallon-size ziptop bags and press out excess air. They stay nice for days! A heads-up about Heath toffee pieces: I have found that they dissolve after a few hours, so if you prepare this ahead (which I do, because it makes things so much easier) wait until just before serving to stir in the toffee pieces. Super recipe Lorrie!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
spiced sweet roasted red pepper   feta hummus

middle eastern style spread for pita bread. this recipe is very tasty and easy to make. this is a very popular dish in this region. the base is usually chickpeas and tahini, but the flavor added to the base vary widely from one chef to the next. tahini is a sesame paste, you can usually find it in the mediterranean section of your grocery store.

1. in an electric blender or food processor , puree the chickpeas , red peppers , feta , lemon juice , tahini , garlic , cumin , cayenne , and salt
2. process , using long pulses , until the mixture is fairly smooth , and slightly fluffy
3. make sure to scrape the mixture off the sides of the food processor or blender in between pulses
4. transfer to a serving bowl and refrigerate for at least 1 hour
5. sprinkle the hummus with the chopped parsley before serving
demonstrations.review: My teenage son has made this several times for get-togethers with friends. It's fast, easy and the wonderful flavor hands-down beats any of the pricey gourmet offerings at the grocery. Everyone raves about it, which makes him very happy!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
apple brickle dip

nan

1. in mixing bowl , beat cream cheese , sugars and vanilla
2. fold in brickle chips
3. serve with apples
4. refrigerate any leftovers
demonstrations.review: Absolute awesome! Anything with apples gets my attention, and this smooth and creamy dip (or could be used as a spread, I think) is a real winner. Served it the first time at a party this summer, and everyone raved. Have served it a number of times since then (it is that good), so it has become one of  my "signature" party treats! Soaking the apples in pineapple juice overnight allows me to prepare them the day before. If you prepare the dip ahead of time, be aware that some brickle pieces will dissolve in this mixture (I found out the hard way!). Wait until you're ready to serve, then add the tasty little bits that give this recipe an essential boost.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
reese s peanut butter cups

nan

1. combine everything but the chocolate chips , and press in a greased 8x8" pan
2. spread melted chocolate chips over top with a spatula , covering entire surface
3. chill 2 hours
demonstrations.review: This is my standby favorite for parties & Christmas gifts & exchanges, because it's so fast and easy! I have made these lovely darlings several times for groups large and small. They are usually the first to disappear, and fans invariably ask for the recipe. It's the texture produced by the graham cracker crumbs that really gives the mouth-feel of a Reese's Cup. Of course, the flavor is fabulous! They are extremely rich, so are best cut in small pieces. The chocolate topping does tend to crack if it is chilled too long (I've made the mistake of chilling overnight before cutting) so Tonkcats' 2 hour chill time is a good guideline to follow. Excellent contribution Tonkcats - thanks!!

target.recipe_text:
banana butter canning recipe

this recipe is posted by request and was found on the net. no name attached.

1. measure 3 cups mashed bananas into a large saucepan
2. add the lemon juice , cherries and sugar , mixing well
3. bring to a rolling boil and boil hard for 1 minute , stirring constantly
4. remove from heat and stir in the pectin
5. mix well
6. ladle into clean , hot sterile jars and seal
7. process in a boiling water bath for 10 minutes for pints
target.review: Exactly like the banana butter from the farm market we trek 2 hours to buy.  I left out the cherries, added a little vanilla, and used an immersion blender to make it smooth.  Thank you so much for the recipe!  My kids love it!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
5 minute wacky vegan microwave chocolate cake for one

you absolutely will not believe how fast you can make the most decadent, moist, one-serving chocolate cake without eggs or milk. this is a variation of the famous wacky cake or crazy cake. it's sooo good! you stir all the ingredients and microwave it in a coffee cup. try it. seriously.

1. stir together all the dry ingredients in a large coffee cup
2. add wet ingredients and mix well with a fork
3. microwave on 50% power for 3 minutes
4. i always have my cup on the rotating plate
5. enjoy !
demonstrations.review: Wonderful!  My daughter (6) and I made this together and loved it.  thanks for the vegan treat!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
ricotta bread for bread machines  1 pound loaf

a favorite i have been making for years. this isn't a very tall loaf and yes - the amount of flour is correct. note: (these days, most bread machines have much bigger pans, so if you have a larger capacity machine, you may instead wish to only mix the dough in the machine,let it rise, then bake the bread itself in a loaf pan (at 350 f for perhaps 30 minutes is a guess).  this can still be baked in a larger capacity machine, it will just have an odd shape.

1. place all ingredients into a 1-pound capacity bread machine according to the directions in your manual
2. select the basic bread cycle and light crust
3. after about 5 minutes , take a peek inside your machine to see if your dough is forming up a ball- if it is too wet , add up to 3 tbsp additional flour , a spoonful at a time , if too dry , add a little water
demonstrations.review: I mixed the recipe in the bread machine and baked it in a 8-1/2 X 4-1/2 pan.  I did have to add about 1/3 cup additional flour.  I baked the loaf for 35 minutes at 350; it could have used an additional 5 minutes or so.  Wonderful flavor, I'll make it again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
red lentil   caramelised onion soup

from an aww magazine, thick and satisfying soup.

1. rinse the lentils and rice in cold water and drain
2. combine the 4 cups of stock and the water in large saucepan and bring to boil
3. add the lentils , rice and cumin and return to the boil
4. reduce heat and simmer uncovered , stirring occasionally until just tender , approx 15 minutes
5. meanwhile , melt butter in large fry pan , add onion and cook until softens , add sugar and vinegar and cook stirring until onion caramelises , remove from heat
6. stir the cayenne , coriander and parsley into the lentil mixture and bring to the boil
7. stir in the caramelised onion mixture and the extra cup of stock , cook , stirring , until heated through
demonstrations.review: We did not care for it - my husband called it "cumin soup".  He tried to eat it, the rest of us went with a frozen pizza.  Some notes:  I put the rice on to cook first since it takes longer, then added the lentils.  I had to google "fresh coriander" to find that it was cilantro.  I used yellow onions since I don't know what brown onions are.  Overall I'm really annoyed to be throwing out a huge batch of soup after crying over the onions!

target.recipe_text:
irish rosie s irish soda bread

this irish soda bread recipe was passed on to me by a dear friend of my mother's who was born and raised in ireland. it's the best irish soda bread i have ever had. it is much higher, lighter and softer than most other recipes i have seen. it has an excellent flavor and texture, as well.

1. combine dry ingredients together in a large bowl
2. in a small bowl beat eggs and stir in sour cream
3. add the egg and sour cream mixture to the dry ingredients and stir with a wooden spoon
4. batter will be very thick
5. add the raisins and caraway seeds and stir well with wooden spoon or knead in with your hands
6. place batter in a greased 9 inch springform pan
7. dust the top with enough flour so that you can pat the batter like a bread dough evenly in the pan without it sticking to your hands
8. with a knife make a shallow crisscross on the top
9. bake for 50 minutes in a preheated 350f oven
target.review: I made this for St. Patrick's Day and everyone loved it. I only used half of the caraway seeds so that they wouldn't overpower the other flavors and it turned out great.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
fresh cream of mushroom soup

this quick and easy recipe is so much better than the canned stuff. great as a first course, or with salad or sandwiches. of course, you can use it in your favorite recipes, too.  to make it thicker, use less stock and/or use heavy cream instead of the half-and-half cream or milk.

1. lighly saute mushrooms in butter
2. add flour and stir constantly for about 5 minutes
3. slowly add stock , stirring until all is incorporated
4. simmer about 10 minutes
5. add cream , stir and serve
demonstrations.review: Thank you for this excellent recipe. I love mushrooms and ran across this and made it. It is much better than any premade mushroom soup that I've ever had. The only thing in making was that the paste formed when adding the flour was so extremely thick that I ended up putting some of the broth in early so that I could stir it. I served this with a crusty Italian style bread and my family loved it. I will definately be making this again. Next time I think I may try adding some Crimini mushrooms to the mix to see what that does to the flavor. I think it will be even better.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
corned beef in beer  crock pot

the best corned beef i've ever made was in the crock pot. (you can substitute water for beer, but the flavor won't be the same)

note:  if you make more than 3-4 lbs., cook it on high.  i've made 6-7 lbs., and it won't be done after 9 hours on low.

another note:  this makes wonderful sandwiches if you cook it, then chill it before slicing.

1. place potatoes , onions , carrots , and bay leaf in crock pot
2. trim excess fat from brisket
3. put meat on top of veges
4. mix molasses with beer and pour over all
5. cover and cook on low heat setting 9-11 hours
6. if desired , place cabbage wedges on top of meat
7. to steam for last hour
8. slice brisket thinly across grain
9. serve with vegetables
demonstrations.review: I made this and the corned beef was wonderful. The only complaint I had was that the vegetables were way too salty. I'll probably boil them separately next time. But it certainly made preparing the corned beef as easy as I've ever seen. Thanks.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
raisin bran muffins that work

i have always been disappointed when i've baked homemade bran muffins, but not anymore. these are moist and flavourful. i think the trick with the moistness is combining the bran with the wet ingredients, as no other bran muffin recipe i've tried had this step. i often cut this recipe in half and bake just 6 in my toaster oven. these freeze well, too.

1. preheat oven to 400f
2. prepare muffin pans by lining cups with paper muffin liners
3. in a large bowl , beat together eggs , milk , oil , molasses , sugar and vanilla
4. stir in bran
5. let stand for 5 minutes
6. in a small mixing bowl , combine flour , baking powder , salt and baking soda
7. add to egg mixture , stirring just until combined
8. carefully stir in raisins , being careful not to overmix
9. fresh blueberries , or unthawed frozen ones , can be substituted for raisins , by the way
10. spoon into paper-lined muffin cups , filling right to the top
11. bake in preheated oven for approximately 20 minutes , or until muffins are firm to the touch
12. do not overbake or muffins will be dry and tough
13. as mentioned in the description , i like to cut this recipe in half and bake the 6 in my toaster oven
14. after 20 minutes they are always done to perfection and i don't heat up my kitchen
15. remove muffins from pan and cool on rack
demonstrations.review: These are very good. The only problem I had was finding wheat bran. Finally did at Whole Foods in bulk so it was only like $0.55/lb., they also had prepackaged for over a $1 for 10 oz. The first time I made them I went exactly by the recipe and they were good, very moist. The next time I added a little honey and everyone loved them. Terrific recipe that has lots of flexibility.

target.recipe_text:
healthy no bake cookies

i played around with my family's no bake cookie recipe and produced a single portion of this cookie that i feel is healthy enough to eat as a meal.  they’re still very good but are much healthier. i keep getting asked for the recipe, so i finally decided to measure out the exact portions and post the recipe. this recipe is very flexible! when i make them i never measure out anything and i often add more or less of ingredients and they still taste great.  i sometimes leave out the wheat germ and flax seeds and just add more oatmeal.  i have made these replacing the sugar with about 3 tablespoons of honey.  i have changed the recipe from 1 tsp. to 1 tbsp. of cocoa powder.

1. heat milk , sugar and cocoa powder over high heat until boiling , stirring constantly
2. take off heat and stir in vanilla and peanut butter
3. stir until peanut butter has melted completely
4. stir in wheat germ and oatmeal
5. drop by large spoonfuls onto wax paper or eat immediately
6. as i
7. if you don't have wheat germ or flax seed , just use more oatmeal
8. the recipe above should work out just perfectly and does most of the time , but if your cookies come out crumbly , use less oatmeal next time
9. if they never set , use more oatmeal next time
target.review: These are AMAZING!!!  I used a little sugar and some honey as well.  Didn't have wheat germ, so just added more flax and oatmeal.  Only had creamy peanut butter.  They were perfect!!  I also added double the amount of cocoa powder for a more chocolate taste.  Thanks so much for this recipe!!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
peanut butter corn chowder

don't let the name scare you. it is very good

1. saute onion and celery in butter till tender
2. remove from heat and add peanut butter stirring until melted
3. stir in broth and corn
4. bring to a boil stirring frequently
5. reduce heat and simmer for 10 minutes , stirring occasionally
6. remove from heat and stir in cream
7. reheat just until hot not allowing to come to a boil
demonstrations.review: To interesting not to make this.  VERY good!  The only thing I did different - to cut down on fat and calories - was to add a can of cream style corn, and only 1/4 cup of half and half.  Thanks - will be making again!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
simple red beans and rice

i know there are already 3 pages of recipes, but the list of ingredients in most were to long for me. here is a recipe my family loves because is tastes great, and a recipe i love because it's so easy.

1. in a skillet cook sliced sausage for about 2 minutes
2. add onion , garlic , and bell pepper , and saute till veggies are tender
3. add beans and tomatoes with thier juice
4. season with thyme , caynne , and salt and pepper to taste
5. serve over rice
demonstrations.review: Sooo easy, and soooo good.  I use Cajun Chicken Andouille sausage, frozen diced green pepper and onion.  Makes for a quick meal.  Good with or without the sausage. Thanks for the recipe - it is a staple in my house!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
ww core chocolate banana smoothies

guilt-free pleasure!

1. in a blender , combine the skim milk , pudding mix , banana , and ice cubes
2. cover and process until blended
3. pour into chilled glasses
4. serve immediately
demonstrations.review: WOW!!  Thank you for posting this recipe..now I no longer need to fight my evening sweet tooth!  The possibilites  are endless!  This is VERY GOOD!

target.recipe_text:
buttery yeast rolls

these are the absolute best dinner rolls. they are light and fluffy and buttery. the dough can also be shaped in many other ways, so use your imagination. makes awesome cinnamon rolls too!

1. place all ingredients except the 1 / 4 cup butter into bread machine in the order recommended by the manufacturer
2. select the dough cycle and start machine
3. shape dough into 20 to 24 balls and place in buttered pan
4. melt the 1 / 4 cup butter and brush it over the tops of rolls , saving the excess for brushing on after baking
5. cover and let rise in a warm place about 1 hour , or until double in bulk
6. bake at 375 degrees f for 15 to 18 minutes
7. brush baked rolls with remaining butter
target.review: sorry, I just don't think 5 stars is enough!!!  this was wonderful... I don't recommend using Splenda in place of sugar unless you just want the best tasting biscuits ever!!  I can't wait til tomorrow to make them again, the way they're supposed to be made.  Thanks for sharing!!  UPDATE:  well I still don't 5 stars are enough.  Thanks to several people on the forum, I got the help that I needed, and now I can say that I have the best recipe for yeast rolls.  Thanks Donna!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
thanksgiving stuffing  cheat  using stove top

last year i used my method of making turkey/chicken stuffing and used the pre-made packaged mix. my family never knew the difference. easy and quick with that homemade taste.

1. saute onions and celery in butter
2. sprinkle with poultry seasoning
3. set aside to cool slightly
4. toss this mixture into your favorite dry stuffing mix
5. heat broth and set aside
6. read directions on your favorite stuffing mix box
7. add enough hot water to the broth to make up the required liquid needed
8. pour over stuffing / vegetables mixture and mix well
9. stuff your chicken or turkey
10. for a side dish place stuffing in a baking dish
11. cover and bake for 15 to 25 minutes at 325 degrees fahrenheit
demonstrations.review:
I didn't have celery on hand, and this was one of those last minute alterations/experiment on the family things.  It went VERY well, even with just the onions, and broth from the giblets and such.  The turkey we cooked this year was also a first...it was a wild turkey and not a store bought! 
Many thanks!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
sticken chicken

june 3, 2004. tastes great! very easy to make! i started it at 250-300 degrees and then up to 350 so i didn't have to wait so long. the results were still delicious! my family killed it!

1. preheat oven to 200 degrees
2. wash chicken
3. dry thoroughly
4. coat chicken with flour seasoned with garlic salt , paprika and ginger
5. arrange chicken skin side up in a single layer in baking pan
6. roast , uncovered , for 1 hour
7. drain
8. mix other ingredients in a pot over a low flame
9. pour over baked chicken when sugar has suitably melted
10. bake for another 2 hours at 250 degrees or until chicken is done and delicously glazed
11. basting and turning at least once will ensure an evenly coated glaze
demonstrations.review: This was tasty and easy to make, but its not for just anybody...my hubby didn't care for it too much, but he's not big on 'sweet' foods. but he still ate it.  I myself really liked it.  thanks for sharing.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
funnel cake

i love to get funnel cakes at the fair, but a fair is not always in town. this recipe is very good and perfect for a quick snack for the kids.

1. in a large bowl , mix all dry ingredients
2. beat egg , milk , and vanilla together in a separate bowl
3. add milk mixture to dry ingredients beating until smooth
4. fill 8" skillet with 1 inch oil and heat to 375 degrees
5. cover funnel hole with finger and fill with about 1 / 4 cup of batter
6. hold funnel over skillet and remove finger moving funnel around to form patterns with the batter
7. fry until golden brown , about 1 or 2 minutes
8. turn over with tongs and continue frying another minute or two or until both sides are brown
9. remove from oil , drain on paper towels , and sprinkle with powdered sugar
10. serve hot
demonstrations.review: great one!  like previous review, though, I added a touch of milk to thin out the batter.great for a quick midnight snack:)

target.recipe_text:
puerto rican red beans and rice

when we lived in puerto rico, this was a favorite meal. we're back in the states now, but when i make red beans and rice it transports me back to la isla del encanto! it can be eaten as a meal itself or with a simple salad.

1. over medium heat , heat oil in a large saucepan
2. add ham , chorizo , onion and green pepper , garlic and cumin
3. saut until vegetables are tender
4. add beans , tomato sauce and tabasco sauce
5. simmer for 5 minutes
6. add in remaining ingredients and 4 cups water
7. bring to boil
8. reduce heat , cover and simmer until rice is tender
target.review: Quite nice.  Wife and kid loved it.  I used Lousiana Hot Sauce instead of Tabasco.  Was pretty mild.  Definite addition to the permanent cookbook.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
wendy s copycat chili

for fast food lovers from an online source posted in response to a recipe request.

1. in a frying pan , brown the ground beef
2. drain
3. put the drained beef and the remaining ingredients into a 6-quart pot
4. cover the pot
5. let it simmer for 1 to 1 1 / 2 hours , stirring every 15 minutes
demonstrations.review: Very nice chili that is surprising like Wendy's.  The chili powder used makes a lot of difference.  I used HEB bulk San Antonio chili powder.  For you guys who are not in Texas, San Antonio powder is "sweeter" with less pungency.  The chili is "gentle" - my family likes it milder than I do.  Personally, I like butt  burning chili - this is not it.  For those who want a kinder, gentler chili, this is really good.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cold peanut noodles

serve cold or at room temp.  i prefer room temp.

1. bring a large pot of boiling water to a boil
2. cook spaghetti noodles according to package directions
3. drain
4. rinse in very cold water and drain again
5. place cooled noodles in a large bowl and toss with the carrots , scallions , bell pepper slices and cilantro
6. in a small bowl , whisk together the sauce ingredients until smooth
7. drizzle the sauce over noodles mixture
8. toss to coat well
9. serve room temp or cold
10. garnish with sesame seeds if desired
demonstrations.review: STOOPID GOOD!  You can take liberties with veggie additions, of course.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
red green cole slaw for pulled pork sandwiches

this is the slaw my mom puts on her pulled pork sandwiches. it's really, really great. this is from the martha stewart cookbook.

1. in a large mixing bowl , whisk together the ketchup , vinegar , sugar , salt and pepper
2. add the cabbage and toss until well coated
3. the slaw can be made several hours in advance and kept covered in the refrigerator until ready to use
demonstrations.review: Very nice with pork sandwiches. I added a pinch of celery seed.  I should not have done that.  Was better before, but still very good.  WIll definitely make again.  I could also almost see this as a sauce for pulled pork.

target.recipe_text:
magic soup

i don't know what it is...this soup cures what ails ya. a recipe for authentic jewish penicillin (chicken soup) tweaked by a sympathetic goy. i make a big pot of this when cold & flu season hits and freeze small containers to reheat whenever one of us feels the bug coming on. i pureed this for my baby last winter and he loved it.

1. place chicken in pot , cover with cold , good-tasting water
2. rough chop 1 onion , 1 parsnip , 1 turnip , 2 carrots and add to stock pot
3. add garlic , ginger and salt& pepper
4. bring all ingredients to a boil then reduce to a simmer
5. simmer stock for at least 2 hours , skimming any scum that rises to the top
6. the longer you cook this , the better it tastes
7. you can make the stock in a crockpot for 6-8 hours on low
8. remove vegetables and discard
9. remove chicken and debone
10. strain stock and taste for seasoning
11. add salt as necessary
