12. chop remaining parsnip , turnip , onion , and carrots into bite-size chunks and drop into simmering stock
13. replace deboned chicken
14. you can reserve some for another recipe , but i usually use all of it
15. add egg noodles
16. cook for an additional 10 minutes or until egg noodles are tender
17. add dill and parsley at the very end of the cooking process
target.review: Great Soup!!  I definately will make it again. The aroma was absolutely wonderful while it was cooking. It is as good, if not better on the reheat.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cornbread with corn casserole

tasty!

1. mix first 3 ingredients together
2. add: margarine and jiffy corn bread mix , pour into well greased 8x8 casserole dish
3. bake for 1 hour at 375 degrees
demonstrations.review: This is the best corn bread recipie ever! It is super easy to make and is an excellent emergency side dish. Great with barbecue!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
applebee s honey mustard sauce

sauce just like the restaurant, recipe came from a family friend.

1. combine ingredients in a small bowl
2. mix well
3. store in a covered container in the refrigerator until ready to serve
demonstrations.review: I love it!!! I made sure i used fresh Paprika and I like it best using white wine vinegar. Great as a dipper for chicken as well as on salads. A real winner!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
ranch glazed baby carrots

five minutes is all you need to make this savory-sweet glaze for cooked carrots.

1. cook carrots according to package directions , drain well
2. in the meantime , melt butter in a large saute pan over low heat
3. add sugar and stir until dissolved
4. add carrots and ranch mix , stir until carrots are coated
5. increase heat to medium , and stir until carrots are hot and glazed , about 5 minutes
demonstrations.review: What a great new way to fix baby carrots!!  We were not too sure at first about the combination of flavors, but it came out excellent, and was very easy to make. We will definately be having it again in the near future!  Thank You.

target.recipe_text:
weight watchers chicken and cheese casserole

this recipe came from a card that was handed out with my weekly weight watchers materials. it's comfort food for 6 points per serving.  note: substitute turkey for chicken if desired.

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees
2. in a large casserole , combine all ingredients , mixing well
3. bake , covered , 35-45 minutes
4. remove cover
5. bake 10-15 minutes longer
6. serve immediately
target.review: This was really easy and quite good.  I think next time I may try adding some free veggies to it!  Thanks for sharing!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
weight watchers general tso s chicken

great ww recipe from a meeting. 8points plus per serving.

1. in a medium bowl , whisk together broth , cornstarch , sugar , soy sauce , vinegar and ginger
2. set aside
3. heat oil in a wok or large skillet over medium-high heat
4. add scallions , garlic and pepper and cook 2 minutes
5. add chicken and cook until browned all over , about 5 minutes
6. add reserved sauce and simmer until sauce thickens and chicken is cooked through , about 3 minutes
7. serve chicken and sauce over rice
8. yields about 1 cup of chicken and sauce and 1 / 2 cup of rice per serving
demonstrations.review: Great Substitute for the real thing!  Quick and easy to make as well.  If you like a little less spicy kick to it, just cut down the red pepper flakes.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
weight watchers chicken pot pie

4-6 points per serving

1. preheat oven to 400
2. spray 8x8 casserole dish with cooking spray
3. mix together veggies , chicken and soup
4. pour into casserole dish
5. in another bowl , mix bisquick , milk , and egg
6. pour over top of chicken mixture
7. bake for 30 minutes , or until crust is golden
8. 6 servings=4
9. 5 points
10. 4 servings=6
11. 5 points
demonstrations.review: Great recipe, super easy.  Great for busy nights.  Do be careful though with the one review...egg substitute is 1 point where regular eggs are 2.  It probably won't make a difference in the recipe spread over the number of servings though.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
inside out stuffed green bell peppers

this is a lot easier to make than the regular stuffed green peppers. my husband just loves it this way.

1. in a skillet , brown beef
2. drain
3. transfer to a greased 2-quart casserole dish
4. add the next 8 ingredients
5. cover and bake at 350f for 1 hour or until rice is tender
6. uncover and sprinkle with the cheese
7. return to the oven until cheese melts , about 5 minutes
demonstrations.review: Delicious!  I substituted lean ground turkey breast for the beef and low fat cheddar cheese to make a healthier version!

target.recipe_text:
iranian potato salad

a traditional iranian dish made for special occasions. it is similar to american potato salad, but with chicken and lots of lemon. very refreshing. a great summer side dish. cooking time includes setting time.

1. boil , bone and cool the chicken
2. grate the potatoes & eggs
3. tear chicken into small pieces
4. mix together with mayonnaise and salt
5. mold the salad to your personal preferences by starting out using 3c of mayonnaise and adding more
6. do the same with the salt
7. when mold is to your liking , add lemon juice and mix
8. cover mold with a layer of baby sweet peas
9. let set in the ice box overnight
10. do not eat right away or lemon juice will be too overpowering
target.review: The salad is called  "Salad Olvieh" ( comes from the russian salad " Salad Olivier")the spelling might be off since the iranian letters are different.You forgot the salt pickels. Use about 4-5 medium size finely chopped pickels ( originally salt pickeld) and mix in the other ingredients. That way the mix will stick better and you need less mayonaise. Use a dollop of Mayo to smooth down the mix on a platter or in a bowl and decorate with remaining pickels and peas ( or whatever you like). Iranian housewifes are masters in the kitchen including decorating their dishes in a big way.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
german kasekuchen

nan

1. crust: in a large mixing bowl , blend all the ingredients , cutting in the butter and working the mixture with your hands until it is well mixed and workable
2. divide the dough into 2 equal portions
3. use one half to line the bottom of a greased 9-inch springform pan , the other half to line the sides of the pan
4. either roll out the dough or press it in with your fingers
5. chill before filling
6. cheesecake: preheat the oven to 375 degrees f
7. press the cottage cheese through a sieve
8. combine the cornstarch and the baking soda and set aside
9. in a large mixing bowl , combine the cottage cheese with the sugar , eggs , lemon rind and vanilla
10. beat until very smooth
11. add the dry mixture to the cheese and blend well
12. stir in the sour cream and raisins
13. pour the cheese mixture into the prepared crust and bake for one hour , or until done
14. the center will remain soft
15. turn off the oven and prop the door open
16. allow the cake to cool to room temperature
17. serve at room temperature as well
demonstrations.review:
Kayline is right. This looks exactely like the ones my mom and grandma made back in Germany. Yes they get brown on top ...oh  I got such a craving for one by looking at the authentic pictures. I'll bake one tomorrow, just for me cause my kids and hubby do not like them. Can you imagine a whole springform of cheesecake just for you?!
Love this recipe with the fruit , try to use raisins like I do, or cherries. Oh Yum. Think of this as just another version of cheescake, there are several versions in america ,too.
Good tio with the propped oven door and the center of the cake still wet. Right on!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
iranian yogurt soup   ashe mast

i originally posted this with the wrong name, so please ignore the bad review. it doesn't seem the reviewer tried making the soup and is posting based on mistaken name only. 

this recipe is passed down from my grandmother to my mother to me and it is fantastic!

the challenge of making this soup is in keeping the yogurt from curdling. it needs to be stirred consistently while cooking.

enjoy!

1. put the meat in a bowl
2. add grated onion and salt and pepper and mix well
3. make meat balls the size of walnuts
4. put yogurt in a 3-qt pot
5. add rice , egg , flour and mix well
6. add water
7. cook over low heat , stirring constantly for about 20 minutes or until it thickens and rice cooks
8. add meat balls to the yogurt mixture and let simmer for 10 minutes
9. add greens and beans and let simmer for 15 minutes
10. can substitute fresh beans for canned
11. stir often to avoid curdling
12. as a soup garnish , chop one or two cloves of garlic and saute in butter , add dried mint , about 1 tablespoon , and put a teaspoonful of this hot garlic sauce on each plate of yogurt soup when serving
demonstrations.review: Ash-e -reshte does not contain ground beef. You eather cook it in water or beef broth. I have never seen joghurt in this soup. You serve it  with kashk ( whey) as a dollop on top with fried dried mint and fried chopped garlic. There is also no egg in that soup. You forgot red beans ,lentils and chick peas. Trust me that soup is always served at special religous gatherings and I have cooked it a lot and eaten a lot from many, many housewifes.I will try to post my mother in laws and my recipe on this web site, do not know if that requires premium member ship.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mom s cheap and easy goulash

my mom used to make this for us all of the time. this is a quick, inexpensive and delicious one pot meal. she always served it with homemade garlic rolls, but i love to serve it with recipe #256914.

1. cook macaroni- reserving the cheese packet for later
2. brown ground beef with onion , garlic powder , italian seasoning , salt and red pepper flakes
3. cook until the ground beef is completely cooked through and the onions are soft
4. drain the macaroni and add tomato sauce , butter and reserved cheese packet
5. mix until well combined
6. add the ground beef mixture , again , mix until well combined
7. serve hot !
demonstrations.review: This is actually one of my childhood recipes,too. And I grew up in Germany. I always thought only my mom had dreamed this up. We used tomato ketchup instead of the tomato sauce. Hmm, this brings back childhood memories. Thanks for sharing.

target.recipe_text:
polish appetizer

this is a must at every holiday in our family. i suggest doubling the recipe...it always goes fast!

1. in a medium sauce pan , combine all ingredients except kielbasa
2. mix well , and cook over low heat until well balanced
3. cut kielbasa into bite size pieces
4. add kielbasa and heat thoroughly
5. make sure heat is low , and cook for at least an hour until the sauce cooks down
6. the longer it cooks , the better
target.review: wonderful recipe.  I followed the directions exactly the first time.  The second time I made it, I did the last part in the crock pot and it still turned out terrific.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
funfetti cookies

this recipe is a favorite from the pillsbury bake-off. it is a simple cookie recipe that always pleases my family. it is also much more economical than buying those sprinkle cookies from the grocery store.

1. heat oven to 375
2. in large bowl , combine cake mix , oil and eggs
3. stir by hand until thoroughly moistened
4. stir in decorator sprinkles from the cake mix
5. shape dough into 1-inch balls
6. place 2 inches apart on ungreased cookie sheets
7. flatten to 1 / 4 inch thickness with bottom of glass dipped in flour
8. bake at 375 for 6 to 8 minutes or until edges are light golden brown
9. cool 1 minute
10. remove from cookie sheets
11. spread frosting over slightly warm cookies
12. immediately sprinkle each with decorator sprinkles from frosting
13. store in tightly covered container
demonstrations.review: These tasted good and were so easy to make.  We brought them to a family gathering and people were asking for the recipe:)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
ground beef with hoisin

i 

1. combine orange juice& cornstarch and set aside
2. saute meat over medium high heat until cooked
3. drain off excess fat , remove and set aside
4. add sesame oil to skillet , stir fry ginger , garlic and orange peel briefly
5. add green onion and stir fry 1 minute
6. return meat to skillet , add hoisin and stir until blended
7. add orange juice mixture and stir until thickened
8. can serve over rice or couscous or"fusion" it as i do
demonstrations.review: I didn't care for this recipe very much at all.  I didn't have any fresh ginger so not sure if that makes the difference or not.  I put this in a tortilla like others suggested and only topped it with some cheese.  The ground beef had a strange flavor, I didn't taste the orange at all, there was a bit of a kick to it but other than that it was somewhat on the dry side.  I can't imagine putting this over rice as there was no extra sauce.  My husband thought the recipe was just ok.  only one of my kids would even try it, and I did not like it at all.  This isn't a recipe I will be making again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
garlic chicken breasts

just dip and bake! chicken breasts flavored with garlic steeped olive oil, and parmesan cheese breading. so simple and so delicious. recipe found on the internet.

1. preheat oven to 425 degrees
2. warm garlic and olive oil to blend the flavors
3. in a separate dish , combine the bread crumbs and cheese
4. sprinkle salt and pepper lightly onto chicken breasts
5. dip chicken in olive oil / garlic mixture , then into bread crumb mix
6. place chicken in a greased baking dish
7. bake for 30 minutes or until done
demonstrations.review: very good flavor.  Was hoping they would have a bit more crunch.  Maybe put them in a broiler for a few seconds after baking? or tent with tinfoil like another poster suggested.  I will try that next time. Other than that they were very yummy:)

target.recipe_text:
edna s apple crumble  aka  apple crisp

a simple and easy to make but oh so yummy recipe. known as apple crumble in the uk and apple crisp in the us

1. put apples in an 8 or 9 inch square baking dish
2. combine the rest of the ingredients in a separate bowl and mix
3. spread crumble mixture over apples and bake for 35 minutes in a 375f degree oven
4. for an added treat top off with a little english custard
target.review: I have made this twice and the topping is excellent, however..Next time I make this I think I will add a bit of sugar and cinnamon with the apples, I felt the apples lacked something.  I used spy apples the first time and the suggested granny smith apples this time.  Some nuts in the topping would be good too..but I reitterate the topping is excellent as is and there is plenty, no need to increase amount of topping as I have with other recipes.  Good with vanilla ice cream! Enjoy!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
coconut papaya rice

for safe keeping have not tried yet

1. heat all ingredients except papaya to boiling in 2-quart saucepan , stirring once or twice
2. reduce heat
3. cover and simmer 19 minutes
4. remove from heat
5. fluff rice lightly with fork
6. cover and let steam 5 to 10 minutes
7. mash half of the papaya
8. reserve 2 tablespoons chopped papaya
9. stir mashed papaya and remaining chopped papaya into rice
10. heat , stirring occasionally , until mixture is hot
11. sprinkle with reserved papaya and , if desired , additional cinnamon
12. substitution
13. if youre in the mood to experiment , go ahead and replace the papaya with an equal amount of chopped mango
demonstrations.review: Flavorful rice dish.  I added a dash of allspice.  I served it with a jerk marinaded chicken breast and plantains fried in peanut oil.  A good addition to a tropical meal!  Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
snow peas with ginger

from the best recipes in the world by mark bittman.  "a small and perfectly easy dish.  the finishing touch of hot sesame oil is a common garnish in hong kong and a nice one."

1. put the oil in a 10- or 12-inch skillet , preferrably non-stick , over high heat
2. a minute later , add the ginger and peas and stir and toss occasionally , until they are lightly browned and their green color is vivid , about 2 minutes
3. add the soy sauce and transfer to a platter
4. add the sesame oil to the same pan and heat for about 10 seconds
5. pour over the snow peas , season with salt and pepper , and serve immediately
demonstrations.review: Nice easy and tasty recipe!  I might be inclined to add some toasted sesame seeds next time...and there will be a next time!  Thank you for an easy veggie side dish that's different!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
roasted asparagus with mushrooms

simple understated elegance for your table.

1. preheat oven to 425
2. in a non-stick baking baking sheet with sides , toss the asparagus and mushrooms with the oil and season with salt and pepper
3. spread the vegetables in a single layer
4. roast for 10 minutes or until the vegetables are tender and browned , turning once or twice
5. place vegetables on a serving platter
6. sprinkle vegetables with vinegar and toss gently to combine
7. season with additional salt and pepper as desired
8. serve warm or at room temperature
9. makes 4 servings
demonstrations.review: Quick, easy and delicious!  Thanks for helping my dinner dilemma!

target.recipe_text:
three cup cobbler

this recipe appeared in an old community cookbook from searcy, arkansas. it's the simplest cobbler recipe around!

1. preheat the oven to 375 degrees
2. place the stick of butter in a 9x13 baking dish , and pop in the oven until the butter is melted
3. stir together the milk , flour , sugar and baking powder
4. pour mixture into the hot pan
5. spoon the pie filling into the pan
6. do not stir !
7. bake for 40 minutes until the crust is brown
8. delicious served warm with a dollop of whipped cream or a scoop of vanilla ice cream
target.review: I make this recipe using Bisquick, which eliminates the flour, baking powder and salt. It is always a hit at our house.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cheesy pasta and sausage

i originally saw this recipe on kevin&amanda.com. i tweaked it slightly and it is fabulous! it reheats well too. you can use just about any shape pasta you like: penne, shells, armoniche, wagon wheels, farfelle, or my favorite, tri-colored campanelle. i used turkey sausage for this and it was fantastic.for those to an aversion to anything spicy, you could easily substitute petite diced tomatoes for the rotel.

1. slice the sausage diagonally into 1 / 4" slices
2. place olive oil in a large , lidded skillet
3. add sausage and onion
4. saute until onions are almost clear
5. add the pressed garlic and saute for one minute longer
6. add the salt , pepper , tomatoes , pasta , half and half and chicken broth
7. mix until combined , then bring to a boil
8. reduce heat and cover
9. cook over medium-low heat for about 15 minutes , stirring occasionally
10. uncover and stir in the shredded cheese
11. scatter scallions over the top and serve
demonstrations.review: This is simply delish!  I used plain tomatoes, not rotel, because my husband and I do  not like spicy food.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
melt in your mouth chicken breasts

the mayonnaise make these chicken breast very moist and tender--enjoy!

1. mix mayonnaise or yogurt , cheese and seasonings
2. spread mixture over chicken breast and place in baking dish
3. bake at 375f for 45 minutes
demonstrations.review: I made this for dinner last night, it was a big hit with my husband.  Thanks for a really good recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cinnamon pie

i love cinnamon anything.  this is one of my favorite pies and is really easy.  you are sure to have all the ingredients in your kitchen too.

1. preheat oven to 375 degrees
2. mix all ingredients together with a whisk
3. batter will be slightly lumpy
4. pour into the shell and bake for 45 minutes or until set
demonstrations.review: I changed the recipe a little. I used l cup of sugar and l cup of Spenda.  The next time I make it, I will use probable 2/3 cup of Spenda, just my personal preference.  My husband loved the pie as is.  It is good to find a recipe with ingredients that I have in my kitchen. Thank you

target.recipe_text:
sausage breakfast muffins  oamc

this is a recipe i found online and adapted to suit my family's taste. you can use either chorizo or regular bulk breakfast sausage, depending on your tastes. they're both good. if you like spicy foods, add a 4 oz can of chopped and drain green chilies.

1. line muffin tins with paper liners , and set aside
2. fry , crumble and drain sausage
3. preheat oven to 375 degrees
4. mix together bisquick , cornmeal , eggs , and milk
5. add drained sausage , and cheese , and stir well
6. ladle the filling into the prepared muffin tins , filling almost to top
7. bake for 11-15 minutes
8. allow to cool completely
9. store in freezer in a large airtight container
10. or place each in a sandwich bag , and then place a dozen in a large ziploc bag
11. microwave on high for approx 90 seconds
target.review: I just finished making this wonderful recipe. The muffins turned out perfect. I did some in a regular large muffin pan (about a dozen) and the rest of the batter I used in a mini-muffin pan. I skipped the pan liners and added a can of drained Rotel diced tomates with chili peppers. They turned out GREAT!! We love them!! I put 2-3 mini-muffins in a snack-sized zip locked baggie they fit just right, then into the freezer.  Canâ€™t wait to pop them in the microwave in the mornings for breakfast on my way out the door! Thanks for sharing this wonderful recipe!! I plan to try your recipe breakfast tacos next!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
no bake cookies

a quick, easy to make family favorite.

1. mix butter , cocoa , sugar and milk in saucepan and heat to boiling
2. add salt , peanut butter , and vanilla
3. mix well , then add 2 cups quick uncooked oats
4. mix well , drop from spoon onto waxed paper and let cool
demonstrations.review: LOVED THIS COOKIE!!  I have never make no-bake cookies before but the recipe looked interesting.  I did have to add 2 extra cups of oats (4 total) but I figured it just makes them more healthy! :)  Everyone who had one loved them!  Thanks for sharing!  Mamma Bug :)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
orzo  feta and tomato salad

this makes a lovely side dish to a bbq, from bon appetit

1. cook orzo according to package directions until al dente , drain and rinse under cold water drain well and put in a large bowl
2. whisk lemon juice , marjoram , mustard , and lemon zest in a small bowl
3. whisk in olive oil
4. reserve 2 tbsp of dressing , add the rest to the orzo
5. mix in feta , scallions , olives , season with salt& pepper and let it stand for 1-2 hrs toss tomatoes with reserved dressing , stir into orzo , serve
demonstrations.review: THIS WAS A GREAT SALAD!  I left out the marjoram and addes 1 clove of fresh garlic, and a can of artichoke hearts to the mix!  I also had to use plenty of salt and pepper to make it tasty.  Overall it was the perfect edition to our BBQ!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crock pot spinach stuffed pasta shells

i love the spinach in these shells. it makes a good hearty meal.

1. cook jumbo shells according to package directions
2. drain and set aside
3. pour 1 / 2 of spaghetti sauce into crock pot
4. in a medium bowl , combine spinach and remaining ingredients , mixing well
5. stuff each pasta shell with spinach mixture and layer in crock pot
6. pour remaining spaghetti sauce over shells
7. cook on low for 4 hours
demonstrations.review: Wonderful!  My husband ate this for 3 days straight!  He couldn't get enough!  Thanks for posting.

target.recipe_text:
lynnie the k s greatest chocolate icing

mom's best icing - we couldn't wait to lick the bowl! if she didn't get the cake frosted quick enough we could eat all of it!

1. melt butter in pan- remove immediately and add cocoa
2. mix until smooth
3. add milk , powdered sugar , vanilla and salt
4. can add more powdered sugar to make thicker or more milk to make thinner depending on consistency desired
target.review: It really is the best icing I have tried! I assumed that you meant 1/2 a 2 pound bag of powdered sugar. You must have because that was perfect! I mixed by had with a whisk and it was just fine. I can't wait to see how it tastes on the "whatever Floats Your Boat" Brownies! Thanks for posting.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
2 minute microwave fudge

all i have to say, is that i'm obsessed with this recipe... i've never tasted better fudge! it's so good... although it's very sweet and very rich! prep time includes chill time.

1. sift powdered sugar , cocoa , and salt into a 1 quart microwave safe bowl
2. stir in milk and vanilla
3. mix well
4. place butter on top
5. microwave on high , 2 minutes
6. beat with wooden spoon until smooth
7. stir in nuts
8. spread in 8 x 8 x 2 inch baking pan
9. chill about 1 hour or until firm
10. cut into 36 pieces
demonstrations.review: This is a very tasty fudge! And quick to make, too! The amount of powdered sugar required seems to vary for me and it's still sticky at room temp, but it's soo good I don't care. I make it runny and use it as icing for brownies! Oh, and I make it on the stovetop since I don't use microwaves.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
gluten free awesome chocolate chip cookies

gluten free? you might not think so because these even fooled my husband! chewy, crunchy or how ever you like them - these are a real treat.

1. by hand blend margarine , sugars , egg , & vanilla until creamy
2. in a separate bowl blend flours , baking soda salt
3. combine both bowls and mix well
4. add chocolate chips and mix
5. roll into balls
6. bake at 375 for 12-15 minutes on a lighty greased preheated cookie sheet
demonstrations.review: I used Bob's Red Mill gluten free flour blend and butter (for added nutrition). These really are great. They remind me of Betty Crocker's chocolate chippers which I used to make before going gluten free.<br/>I even though the raw dough tasted good, if grainy.<br/>Yum!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
butterscotch oatmeal

kids of all ages love this ---  i also added in some cinnamon and raisins but that is optional --- you can also make this in the microwave, i use an 8-cup pyrex measuring cup just remove a few times and stir --- i top this with a bit of 18% cream and sprinkle with a sugar/cinnamon topping --- the recipe is enough for 2-4 servings but i can eat the whole thing myself this is so good :)

1. in a heavy-bottomed saucepan over medium heat , whisk together the egg with milk , brown sugar , pinch salt and cinnamon
2. mix in the oats
3. bring to a simmer
4. when the oats begin to boil , cook and stir with a wooden spoon until thickened
5. remove from heat and stir in the butter until melted
6. serve immediately
7. delicious !
demonstrations.review: This was great! I made it with real whole milk from my cow, real farm fresh eggs, and sucanat instead of brown sugar. I know I will make this again. It's like dessert for breakfast.

target.recipe_text:
pronto pups aka corn dogs

these are also known as corn dogs, but our school and church term for them are pronto pups. my family loves these friday nights, i can never seem to make enough for the kids!

1. combine cornmeal , flour , baking powder , salt , egg and sugar
2. add milk until batter has a pancake type consistency
3. dry off hot dogs with paper towels , coat with flour , and skewer through the center of the corndog
4. heat 2" deep oil to 370 degrees f
5. dip skewered hot dogs into batter mix and coat evenly
6. fry until golden brown about 2 1 / 2 minutes
7. let cool and drain on a paper towel
8. with left over batter drop like dumplings into the oil until golden brown and drain
9. serve with ketchup , mustard tarter sauce or a dressing of your choosing
target.review:
I made these last night for the first time.....really good.  Had a little trouble telling when the dough was done enough and overcooked them a little but still edible lol.  Take the advice of another reviewer....use something other than skewers...the point end hurts!!!! lol  Thanks for a great recipe. :) 
Prissy

demonstrations.recipe_text:
panini sandwiches

when i got my george foreman grill, i made up this recipe to be like the ones that i had bought. it has been a big hit with everyone.

1. start heating the grill
2. place 1 slice of mozzarella on each of 4 slices of bread
3. place 1 slice of provolone on each of the other 4 slices of bread
4. top the mozzarella with pepperoni , salami and pepperoncini
5. top the provolone with turkey , ham and cheddar
6. place the two halves of the sandwiches together
7. brush the top of the first sandwich with the melted butter
8. place the sandwich butter side down on the grill
9. brush the other side with melted butter
10. grill till bread is toasted and the cheese has melted
11. continue with the other sandwiches
12. a george foreman grill works great with these sandwiches but even a stove top grill would work
demonstrations.review:
Love this recipe. When I try something new, I can tell by the look on my hubby's face if it is a keeper.....he LOVED these. I didn't have a clue what pepperoncini peppers were so I used jalepeno peppers in some and banana peppers in the others. Both worked great. Thanks again for a great recipe :) Prissy

I do have one question I forgot to ask....Where do you get sour dough bread?  I couldn't find it anywhere in the bread section.  I used texas toast instead.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
slow cook down home pork chops and gravy

i don't even like pork, but was tricked into tasting this dish when i was told it was chicken. wow! the meat was sooo tender and juicy; so tender in fact, that it was literally falling apart! it was like nothing i'd ever tasted before! definitely not like my mother's hard, crusty pork chops! lol! this recipes goes hand in hand w/ some mashed potatoes. just pour the leftover gravy on the taters' and enjoy!

1. combine 1st four ingredients in a shallow dish
2. dredge chops in flour mixture and set aside
3. combine what is left of the flour mixture w / the chicken broth and pour into your crock pot
4. pour oil into a large skillet and cook the chops in hot oil until browned on both sides
5. place chops in crock pot and cook covered on high for about 2 to 5 hours or until tender
6. serve w / hot rice and / or mashed potatoes
7. ++if the gravy becomes too thick just add a little water
8. if you accidentally add too much water then add a little more flour
9. season w / salt and pepper too your taste
demonstrations.review: I just made this recipe for the first time.  My 13 yr old son came in from school and said "WOW something smells goooood!" lol.  My husband looked at and kinda grimaced. After tasting it he said "I really thought I wasn't going to like this but it awesome!!"  For sure a keeper.  Thanks for such a great and easy recipe....real comfort food. :)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
layered pumpkin loaf

you'll love the surprise inside this delicious, smart-choice pumpkin bread: a creamy center.

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. grease a nonstick 9x5-inch loaf pan
3. set aside
4. mix pumpkin , 1 cup granulated sugar , the brown sugar , 3 of the egg whites , milk and oil in large bowl
5. add flour , baking powder , pie spice and salt
6. stir just until moistened
7. set aside
8. beat neufchatel cheese , remaining 2 tablespoons granulated sugar and the remaining egg white with wire whisk until well blended
9. spoon half of the pumpkin batter into prepared pan
10. spoon neufchatel cheese mixture evenly over the batter
11. cover with remaining pumpkin batter
12. bake 1 hour to 1 hour 5 minute or until wooden toothpick inserted in center comes out clean
13. run knife or thin spatula around edges of pan to loosen bread
14. cool in pan on wire rack 10 minute
15. remove bread from pan to wire rack
16. cool completely
demonstrations.review:
I must have done something wrong even though I followed the recipe exactly.  The outer layer...the bread part tasted good but the center wasn't creamy at all.  It was clumpy and broke into pieces all over the place.  I will admit I am a somewhat inexperienced baker so could have been something I did wrong.  Doubt I will be making this again.

Thanks for submitting it, was worth a try for a pumpkin roll type dessert.

Prissy

target.recipe_text:
authentic no refrigeration bakery frosting icing

a frosting just like the bakeries use on their cakes and there is no refrigeration required--it may be kept for 3 months covered in the refrigerator  just bring to room temperature before using.  recipe yields 8 cups of frosting.  you will love this!

1. in a large mixing bowl beat the shortening creamer and extracts
2. gradually beat in the confectioners sugar
3. add in enough water until frosting reaches desired consistency
4. add in food coloring until the desired shade is achieved
target.review: This is great...especially during the warmer months.Plus it makes alot and stores easily in the fridge so you can frost another cake at some other time. Thanks, as usual your recipes are always winners!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
copycat  green giant niblets corn in butter sauce

i had to come up with this quick. every thanksgiving my mom serves green giant niblets corn in butter sauce and i promised i would pick it up for her and bring it on thanksgiving day. when i went to the store, they were sold out! i made this recipe and brought it already prepared to thanksgiving dinner. nobody was the wiser! i saved some money too, because i used store brand corn! this recipe makes a lot...you may want to half it.

1. add corn to large sauce pan along with all ingredients except water and cornstarch
2. stir corn mixture over medium heat until butter is melted
3. combine water and cornstarch and stir until cornstarch is disolved
4. slowly add water to corn in sauce pan , stirring constantly
5. reduce heat to simmer and stir until sauce thickens
6. let simmer , stirring occasionally , until corn is tender , about 10 minutes
demonstrations.review: Worthy of five stars! Tastes great! Thank you.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
jiffy corn muffins mix clone

sometimes a recipe will call for a box of jiffy corn muffin mix. here's a clone recipe you can make at home. if another recipe calls for a box of corn muffin mix, leave out egg and milk from this recipe.

this recipe is equal to one 8.5 ounce box of jiffy corn muffin mix. makes 1-1/2 cups dry muffin mix.

1. preheat oven to 400f combine flour , corn meal , sugar , baking powder and salt
2. mix well with whisk
3. whisk in vegetable oil and mix until dry mixture is smooth and lumps are gone
4. combine above mixture with egg and milk and mix well
5. batter will be slightly lumpy
6. for best rise , let batter rest for 3 or 4 minutes
7. stir once or twice after rest
8. fill muffin tins 1 / 2 full
9. bake 15-20 minutes
10. makes 6 muffins
demonstrations.review: Thank you...this has come in handy for several recipes.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
very moist banana nut bread

this is a very easy, "no mixer" bread to make. it is very moist and a little heavy type banana bread. the really important thing to remember is using all black bananas to get my same results. i always use 5 medium sized bananas and this recipe makes 2 loaves. also, i've never used buttermilk, but sour milk instead..a little vinegar added to regular milk. i've used this recipe since 1972 and last year made 32 loaves to give away for christmas! it's truly a wonderful bread. i only bake it until the toothpick comes out almost clean, as we like it really moist. if you over bake it, or wait til the toothpick is completely clean, the bread will be a lot dryer. i realize some like it this way, so thats why i've given this hint. my family and friends would rather have it a little under done than over. it's so good with coffee, butter/jelly or i like mine just plain. i bake it in tin foil pans and it freezes wonderfully. i try to always have one or two in the freezer for company, or a little gift. this recipe came from a ladies club cookbook. the kind where everyone contributes recipes, they are made into a recipe book and sold to make money for charities. all the cooks are just plain "down home" country gals that produce miracles in the kitchen. it's my favorite cookbook and i've almost worn it out and it can't be replaced. i know there are many banana bread recipes here, so thanks for trying this recipe. i hope you enjoy it!

1. heat oven to 350
2. grease or spray 2 loaf pans
3. in a large bowl , mash bananas with a masher or by well washed hands
4. dissolve soda in buttermilk-- use a larger container as it will foam up quite a bit
5. mix all ingredients by hand and add in 1 cup chopped nuts
6. bake at 350 for 1 hour , or until toothpick comes out almost clean
7. totally clean will mean a dryer loaf
8. let cool 15 minutes after removing from oven and remove from pans
9. or , let cool , cover with foil , slide into freezer bags and freeze
10. great when using tin foil pans
demonstrations.review: It seems like I always come back to this recipe over and over. Simple, moist and no fancy ingredients makes two loaves of wonderful bread. Thanks for a winner.

target.recipe_text:
mile high crock pot lasagna with zucchini or spinach

this is such a wonderful lasagna recipe! very hearty  and delicious with nice deep layers, plenty of meat and cheese, and just the right amount of seasoned sauce--- plus it's a great way to sneak some veggies into your family's meal!! very easy to prepare, and any leftovers are great reheated the next day. equally good with chopped spinach or zucchini.

1. brown the beef , onions , zucchini , and garlic in 2 tablespoons olive oil in a large skillet , stirring to break up meat
2. stir in the oregano , basil , pepper , crushed anise seeds , sliced mushrooms , parsley , spaghetti sauce , and wine
3. in a separate bowl , stir together the beaten egg and the ricotta cheese , beating well until mixture is smooth
4. stir in the grated parmesan cheese , combine well
5. grease the bottom and sides of the crock pot
6. layer about 1 / 4 of the meat sauce mixture in the bottom of the crock pot
7. put a layer of noodles on top of that
8. put about 1 / 3 of the cheese mixture and sprinkle with 1 / 4 of the mozzarella
9. repeat with sauce , noodles and cheese for another two layers
10. top with meat sauce and a little parmesan and shredded mozzarella on top
11. cover and cook on low for 4-6 hours , or until noodles are tender
target.review: I've been making lasagna most of my life.  I've been called the lasagna wizard but, this one tops them all!  I use Italian sausage and I use a couple different cheeses in addition to what is mentioned here.  This is THE BEST lasagna recipe ever.  I look at recipes as a "suggestion" and then go from there.  This one is so good, I even converted it to an oven lasagna and it was just as good.  Thank you for sharing!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
low fat oven fried scallops

easy, tasty, low-fat says it all about these scallops!

1. rinse the scallops & pat dry
2. set aside
3. place the egg substitute in a shallow dish
4. place bread crumbs in another shallow dish
5. dip scallops in the egg substitute and then roll them in the bread crumbs
6. coat a 9 x 13 inch pan with the olive oil cooking spray and arrange the scallops in a single layer in the pan
7. spray the tops lightly with the spray
8. bake at 500 degrees f for about 8-10 minutes or until the scallops turn opaque and nicely browned
9. remove pan from oven and sprinkle with parsley
10. squeeze the lemon over the scallops and serve
demonstrations.review: Loved this recipe.  We have always been great fans of scallops, this is on the top of my "go to" recipes.  I'm making it again tomorrow.  I agree, Panko really did make this better.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
fried catfish  2

dh has been catching so.. much catfish, that we've come up with another different tried and true. this one is fried in oil with lots of spice. soaking in buttermilk is good, but if you're not into buttermilk, you may sub milk.  enjoy.

1. fillet and clean catfish
2. soak in buttermilk or milk for 1-2 hrs
3. drain well
4. spinkle fish with salt , pepper , and herbs
5. dredge in corn meal and flour mixture
6. cook in a small skillet of 1 / 2 cup oil , being careful not to overcrowd fillets , probably cooking in two batches
7. fry about 6-8 minutes , watching closely so as not to burn , turn once
8. serve with a lemon wedge if desired
demonstrations.review: I also added all the spices to the flour mixture, the only thing I would add is some more cayenne.  This is a keeper!  Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
quick butternut squash soup

here's a quick, light and creamy soup that warm you on the coldest night. add some hearty whole grain bread and a tossed salad to make a very satisfying meal.

1. add oil , garlic and onion to large stockpot over medium heat
2. saute for 3-4 minutes
3. add sage , salt , pepper , broth and squash
4. bring to a boil
5. cover , reduce heat and simmer for 20 minutes
6. use stick blender to lightly puree , leaving some chunks , or puree half of the soup in a food processor or blender and return to pot
7. garnish with parmesan cheese and more fresh sage
demonstrations.review: I made this almost to the letter.  I used shallots instead of onions, I also added 1/2 t. of finely chopped fresh ginger and 1/4 cup of half and half. I pureed it to the point of no chunks. One of the best and easiest butternut soups ever.  This is a keeper.  Thanks.

target.recipe_text:
anytime slushy punch

my mother-in-law makes this punch for christmas. the kids love it. it's easy to make, no cooking required. you can triple the batch and have it in the freezer for any special occasion.also good for weddings,baby showers, superbowl parties or a cool drink in the summer.

1. in large bowl or pot mix first three ingredients together until dissolved
2. stir in frozen lemonade and pineapple juice
3. place in two freezer bags and freeze over night
4. take out of freezer two hours before serving time
5. place one bag in punch bowl and add half of ginger ale
6. break up big chunks of frozen mixture
7. punch will become slushy
8. ready to serve
target.review: This punch is fantastic! My sister-in-law makes one that tastes exactly like this, but her recipe is more complicated. I just made this over the weekend for my daughter's 2nd birthday party, and it was a huge hit. There wasn't a drop left. I used lemon jello. An important note: the instructions do not specify this, but you must chill the gingerale. Otherwise, when you pour it over the frozen punch it will just melt it into liquid rather than making it slushy. Anyway, great recipe. I'll make it again and again. Thanks for sharing!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
better than olive garden pasta pomodoro

i have always loved olive garden's pomodoro. this is what i came up with when i experimented at home. this does not heat up your kitchen and is a light supper dish for those hot summer evenings. if you like spice, add some crushed red pepper flakes to taste. just don't use anything but the freshest ingredients--you'll end up with something that tastes pasty/chemical/bitter/etc.

1. heat olive oil over high heat and add garlic
2. saute for 30 seconds
3. add tomatoes , salt , and pepper
4. saute for another 30 seconds , stirring constantly
5. remove from heat
6. add cooked pasta and chopped basil
7. toss gently
8. turn into serving bowl / dish , add 1 / 2 grated cheese , and toss again
9. serve immediately and pass the last 2 oz
10. of grated parmesan
demonstrations.review: YUM! This was excellent. I don't like tomatoes, but DH does, so I just picked around them. The flavor was perfect. I added sauteed chicken breast to mine. Made a great dinner, and so quick and easy. I'll make this again and again. Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pms bars

another variation of those famous magic layer bars, this one gets it's title from the combination of salty, sweet, crunchy, and creamy (which is what most of us chickies clamor for when having an "attack"). i think some of my male coworkers pretend to suffer from pms occasionally, just so i'll bring them a pan of these treats!

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. melt butter in 13x9" pan in the oven
3. remove from oven and sprinkle graham cracker crumbs over butter
4. mix well and press firmly into bottom of pan
5. pour condensed milk evenly over crust
6. sprinkle chips over condensed milk
7. sprinkle broken pretzels over chips , and press everything down firmly with a spatula or fork
8. bake for 25-30 minutes
9. for best results , cool in pan completely before cutting into bars
10. optional: serve with diet coke
demonstrations.review: Oh these are sooooo sinful but they are really, really good! I used butterscotch chips instead of peanut butter, and I also added half a cup more pretzels to the top. So yummy. I made 2 batches and sent most of them to work with my husband for him to share with his co-workers! They are too sinful to have too many in the house!! I have another batch in the oven now for a get-together we are having tomorrow. Thanks for such an easy and yummy recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
the best goulash

i can't even remember where i found this recipe, but i've been making it for years. it is great on a cold night or for a quick dinner. i usually serve it with bread sticks or garlic bread. yum!

1. brown ground meat in skillet with onions and garlic
2. drain fat from meat
3. add salt , pepper , paprika , tomatoes , tomato sauce and frozen corn
4. while the meat is cooking , boil the macaroni until almost done
5. drain water from macaroni and stir into meat mixture lightly grease a casserole dish
6. pour enough mixture to cover bottom of dish and then sprinkle with cheese
7. add another layer of meat and top with cheese
8. bake at 350 degrees until cheese melts and casserole is bubbling
demonstrations.review: This is really good, and so easy! I made it just a few weeks ago, and my husband liked it so much he wanted it again tonight, and I misplaced my copy of the recipe, so I had to come and look for it again. Thank goodness I had it bookmarked! Thanks, Paige, for an easy and tasty recipe for some good comfort food! We'll make it again and again!

target.recipe_text:
italian pasta salad for 20

this simple, delicious recipe uses common ingredients and can be made ahead of time. it's inexpensive and perfect for entertaining, potlucks, barbecues, parties, family reunions, or any time you need a large quantity of salad.

1. bring 6 quarts water to a boil
2. add salt , if desired
3. add dry pasta
4. cook al dente
5. drain and rinse with cold water
6. while the pasta is cooking , rinse broccoli heads
7. remove stems and chop florets into bite-sized pieces
8. rinse peppers and halve them
9. remove stem , seeds , and pith
10. slice lengthwise into 1 / 4" strips , then chop crosswise into 1 / 4" dice
11. quarter pepperoni slices by stacking 5-8 at a time
12. combine all ingredients in a large bowl
13. to keep the pepperoni slices from sticking together too much , "roll" them between your palms as you drop them into the mixing bowl
14. pour italian dressing over all
15. toss thoroughly
16. chill at least 2 hours
17. may be prepared the day before
18. toss again before serving
19. serves 20
target.review: Very tasty and so easy!  Pleased the crowd.  I did add quite a bit of garlic salt and salad seasoning as my store brand dressing was a bit bland.  Next time I'll be sure to get the good stuff.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
the best one bowl hash brown potato casserole

my family loves this and i make it on regular rotation, it's so easy to make just mix everything in one large bowl then bake, you may prepare the complete casserole and refrigerate until ready to bake, which makes this a perfect potluck dish! --- i have even made this using frozen french fries that i cut up into small pieces when i had no hash browns on hand and can also be made using cooked cubed potatoes --- cream of chicken soup may be used in place of mushroom soup, you may even throw in some chopped cooked ham or chicken also, i most always increase this by using two cans of soup, 1-1/2 cups sour cream and using half a 5-pound bag of hash browns --- you will love this! :)

1. set oven to 350f
2. butter a 13x9-inch casserole dish
3. in a large bowl stir together the undiluted soup , milk , sour cream , melted butter , seasoned salt , black pepper , garlic powder and 1 / 4 cup parmesan cheese
4. whisk or mix until well combined
5. mix in the cheddar cheese , onions and hash browns
6. spread into prepared baking dish
7. sprinkle with about 1 / 2 cup parmesan cheese
8. bake uncovered for 40 minutes or until hot and bubbly
9. if desired sprinkle about 2 cups grated chedar cheese on top and return to oven for 3 minutes to melt the cheese
demonstrations.review: The flavor was yummy but the consistency of my casserole was mushy and a bit greasy.  I will make it again and try cooking it longer.  I will also let it come to room temp before I bake it (it was refrigerated for about 2 hours and didn't sit out for longer than 15 minutes).  I may also cut the butter back a little as well.  Easy and tasty though!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
classic saffron rice

this is easy, simple and wonderful.  the original recipe which was printed in the spring 2005 penzeys catalog, calls for long-grain rice; however, i liked it much better with basmati. also, the original recipe called for minced onion but i found it worked very well with dried onion.  i indicated that the butter is optional, because i did not add it.

1. rinse the rice well , drain
2. in a medium size saucepan , add the rinsed rice and remaining ingredients
3. bring to a boil , cover and reduce heat
4. simmer for 15 to 20 minutes or until stock is absorbed and rice is tender
5. fluff with fork and serve
demonstrations.review: I love this rice, and I'm not a rice person unless it's covered in sauce.  I used jasmine rice, onion powder, about a tsp of powdered saffron (it's what I had), threw it in the rice cooker, turned it on and then let it sit on warm for at least an hour once done before eating. Yummy!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crock pot ranch potatoes

beat the heat and keep your kitchen cool by serving this delicious and creamy potato dish to go with your grilled dinner. this is one recipe where i break my "no canned soups" credo. it's just too good to pass up. this recipe is from bhg's slow cooker book.

1. place the cut up potatoes in the crock pot
2. in a small bowl , mix together the remaining ingredients and then spoon over the potatoes
3. stir to blend well
4. cover
5. cook on low setting for 7 hours
6. stir gently before serving
demonstrations.review: I've made this as directed twice now for BBQs and am going to have to start doubling the recipe since!  The first time I used well scrubbed russets (it was what I had) and left the skins on, the second time I used both russets and red potatoes and it turned out beautiful and yummy each way, the kids loved it.  I cooked it on High for 3 1/2 hours.

target.recipe_text:
balsamic blueberries and peaches

found on epicurious.com.  sounds like a unique twist to me...........  used for zwt 3 with midwest and south as the regions, blueberries in michigan and peaches in georgia.

1. in a 1 to 1 1 / 2 quart heavy saucepan , bring 3 tablespoons sugar with vinegar and 1 cup of the blueberries to a boil while stirring constantly
2. boil 1 minute
3. remove from heat
4. combine remaining 2 cups of blueberries with peach slices in a large bowl
5. toss with hot blueberry syrup and black pepper
6. add additional sugar , if desired
7. let stand 30 minutes , tossing occasionally
target.review: DIVINE! Needed a last minute low cal dessert, and this fit the bill. I used a mix of frozen fruit that I had, and picked out the mangos to make the sauce with. I can't wait to try this with other fruit combinations, and try it as an ice cream topping. Thank you for posting!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chocolate peanut butter bundt cake

i thank my awesome neighbor, alison for this fine recipe.  i am not a huge fan of chocolate, but i must say, this is a great (and easy) cake.  
because i only have a regular standard bundt cake pan, i make this in the oven. but if any of you have the pampered chef's stoneware bundt pan, this cake bakes in the microwave in 12 minutes!!!  alison always makes it in the microwave.  when she gave me this recipe, i almost fell on the floor at how easy it was and she made it in the microwave?????
i increased the amount of p.b. cups because i love peanut butter.  ;)

1. preheat oven to 350
2. if your bundt pan is dark coated / black , preheat oven to 325
3. grease and flour and bundt cake pan
4. set aside
5. ignore the cake mix package directions
6. in a large bowl , beat together the cake mix , sour cream and eggs until smooth
7. pour half of this batter into the prepared bundt cake pan
8. evenly spread out the 12 halved pieces of mini peanut butter cups over the batter
9. evenly top with remaining batter
10. bake at 350 for about 50-60 minutes or until toothpick tests done
11. allow to cool for 10 minutes and turn upside down to release the cake
12. cool completely
13. after completely cooled , place the choc chips and peanut butter in a saucepan or microwave-safe bowl
14. melt over low heat stirring constantly until melted and smooth
15. drizzle over the cooled cake
16. if you own the pampered chef's bundt stoneware , follow these directions , but microwave for about 12 minutes and proceed as written
demonstrations.review: I made this for my DH's birthday, and he was quite pleased. Great recipe, and I love how easy it was! Next time I'll probably add more pb cups, but will make no other changes. Thank you for submitting!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
creamy crab topped tilapia

my family loves the parmesan topped tilapia recipe.  i adapted it to a slightly (i hope) healthier version with a little bit more meatiness in it.  it's great served with rice and veggies.

1. lay tilapia fillets out on baking pan and season with season salt
2. bake at 350 for 6-8 minutes or until mostly cooked
3. while the fillets are in the oven , mix remaining ingredients
4. take fish out of the oven and top with crab / parmesan mixture
5. turn oven to broil
6. broil fish until bubbly and light brown
demonstrations.review: My DH really liked this dish, but I wasn't as fond. The topping was really good, but it was so strong that the tilapia was totally over-powered. Maybe this topping would go better on a stronger flavored fish? Thanks for submitting! The rest of my family loved it!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
100  whole wheat low fat pancakes

i created these one day for my kiddies when i couldn't find a recipe that fit my bill. they turned out great! note: if you like fluffy pancakes stir wet ingredients into dry with a wooden spoon leaving some lumps (more lumps=bigger cakes), alternately if you like thin pancakes, like me, use your blender to mix all the ingredients at once and blend until smooth update: sept '07: for those who don't like really thick pancakes try reducing flour by 1/2cup and replacing it with milk, this will give a runnier batter and should give a thinner pancake :)thanks for the comments everyone!!! (good and bad, we all learn from critisism too ;) )

1. depending on your preference blend / mix all ingredients except fruit
2. heat pan on medium till drop of water "dances" in pan
3. pour batter into pan to desired size of pancake , if using fruit add small handfuls to individual cakes after pouring into pan
4. when bubbles appear on surface and begin to "sink" flip and cook on other side until brown
5. repeat with remaining batter until all gone
6. serve with favorite topping i
7. e
8. , fruit , syrup , jam etc
demonstrations.review: These were quite good! I added about 1/4 cup flax meal in place of the flour. My DH usually complains when I do this, but he didn't even notice. The sweetness of the pancakes is great for adding additional grain types. I'll probably play around with this in the future, but it's a very good base recipe. I topped with a blueberry/splenda topping, and it was fantastic. Thank you for the great recipe!

target.recipe_text:
crock pot french dip roast

nan

1. place onion in slow cooker
2. add roast
3. combine wine and gravy mix
4. pour over roast
5. add enough broth to cover roast
6. cover
7. cook on high 5-6 hours or low 10-12 hours remove meat from liquid
8. let stand 5 minutes before slicing thinly across grain
9. but it ended up being shredded beef on our french dip sammiches !
10. we put it on hoagie rolls which i had buttered and toasted in the oven-- and a slice of swiss cheese--
target.review: I made this Saturday night with french rolls & swiss & on the side if we didn't want the roll I made Garlic Mashed Potatoes & it was amazing. Thank you for sharing.  My husband brought it to work that night & everyone wanted to know the recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
slow cooker chicken   biscuits

precooked chicken and refrigerated biscuits make this family friendly classic a snap to prepare.

1. combine chicken , canned soups , water , bouillon and pepper in slow cooker
2. cut biscuits into quarters
3. stir into mixture
4. cover
5. cook on low 4 to 6 hours , stirring occasionally , or until biscuits are cooked
demonstrations.review: Was really good, i also used 2 cans of cream of chicken, and added a splash of white wine.  Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
simple grilled red potatoes

just thought i would try these roasted red potatoes on the grill and they were so good that i thought i would post the recipe.  you can also add chopped onions, and green or red peppers, too.

1. preheat grill
2. dice up the red potatoes and place on heavy duty foil or a grill pan
3. spray foil or pan with pam or a cooking spray of choice
4. add potatoes to foil or pan
5. mix together melted butter with seasoning salt and pour over potatoes
6. stir gently
7. sprinkle salt and black pepper to taste
8. close foil sightly and grill until tender
9. time depends on how fast your grill cooks
10. mine was about a hour on low heat
11. also you can make this recipe in oven at 350' for 1 hour
demonstrations.review: My husband & I loved these.  We used 2 tbs of butter & 1 tbs olive oil; and served them with pork tenderloin.  Thank you very much!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cheeseburger potato chowder

quick as a wink to make.  you can vary the cheese to suit your taste and use fresh potatoes instead of hashbrowns if you prefer.

1. in a skillet , brown beef until almost done
2. stir in the onions and cook till onions are soft and meat is no longer pink
3. drain off any remaining fat
4. in a soup pan over medium heat , combine milk & cheese , cooking until just beginning to boil , stirring often
5. add beef , onion and potatoes to cheese sauce
6. lower heat and simmer for 20 minutes or until potatoes are tender
7. season with pepper
demonstrations.review: This was a really good soup!  I love how fast it cooked up.  I didn't have the Cubed potatoes so I did use the shredded ones, and really liked it.  I am thinking about next time adding some corn and tomatoes.  :)  Thank you so much for sharing!

target.recipe_text:
broccoli   cheese soup

a great soup, one of the deli classics.

1. saute onion and celery in butter in saucepan over medium heat until tender
2. add flour , and salt and pepper , cooking and stirring until mixture is smooth and bubbly
3. add broth and milk , stirring constantly until mixture comes to a boil and begins to thicken
4. add cooked broccoli , stirring until all is heated through
5. remove from heat and stir in cheese until melted and smooth
target.review: Definitely the best Broccoli Soup recipe soup I've come across.  Wonderfully rich, creamy, and tasty.  Adding this to my regular meal rotation.  Thank you!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pinto beans and rice in a crock pot  or on stove top

this is one of those good ol' down home meals. add a pan of cornbread and you've got it made! you can obviously make this spicier by adding more chili powder, cayenne, jalapenos or just pass the tabasco.  please note that the time shown is an estimate only as there will be a variance of heat from one crockpot to the next.

1. rinse beans in colander
2. put in a crock pot
3. cover with water , plus about 2 inches over top of beans
4. add all ingredients , except rice
5. cook on high in crock pot about 3 hours til tender
6. may also cook on low overnight
7. add rice and cook until rice is warm
8. serve with cornbread
demonstrations.review: I was looking for uses for my home canned beans, and this was perfect!  I'd just reduce the chili powder a bit next time because I'm not big on heat.  (Now that I'm making it again I realized I used one cup DRY rice, which is why my picture doesn't look soupy. I like it that way though!)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
baked garlic sweet potatoes

great as a side for the holidays, or really anytime! a little fact: in 1543 desoto’s spanish explorers found sweetpotatoes growing in “indian gardens” in what became louisiana. the sweetpotatoes were also cultivated in the carolina area of north america before the european colonization. adapted from the north carolina sweet potato commission.

1. cut top off garlic bulb and discard
2. place garlic bulb , cut side up , in small baking dish
3. drizzle with olive oil
4. bake at 400f
5. for 30 minutes or until garlic is really soft
6. cool , remove garlic cloves
7. use oil in baking dish to grease 1 1 / 2 quart baking dish
8. cook sweet potatoes and white potatoes in boiling salted water 20 minutes or until potatoes are tender
9. drain and combine potatoes with garlic cloves in large bowl
10. mash until smooth
11. add remaining ingredients , reserving 1 / 4 cup parmesan cheese , blend
12. spoon into prepared baking dish
13. sprinkle with remaining 1 / 4 cup parmesan cheese
14. bake at 350f
15. for 30 minutes , until golden on top
16. enjoy !
demonstrations.review: I used the converter to make 2 servings which filled a 15 ounce stoneware dish.  It worked perfectly, and tasted great.  I've never roasted garlic before, it was a nice touch.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
broiled banana crisp

a truly unique sweet treat that apple crisp lovers should really give a try! note: this recipe is specifically created for individual ramekins/portions...any attempt to make it into a 'one pan' dish may alter the recipe beyond the intended results...alter this recipe at your own risk, lol!

1. peel bananas and drizzle with lemon juice
2. then cut in half lengthwise and then again across
3. you should have a total of 16 quarters of banana
4. then distribute these banana quarters equally among 4 broil-and-serve dishes
5. in a small bowl , combine the brown sugar , uncooked oats , flour and allspice --
6. cut butter into the mixture until it resembles crumbs and then spread the crumbs equally over all the bananas
7. turn on your broiler and place these dishes under the broiler , 5" from the heat source and broil 3 min
8. the idea is to brown it and warm it at the same time
9. watch carefully , don't burn it or yourself !
10. serve warm with vanilla ice cream
demonstrations.review: This has a wonderful flavor :)  I made a single serving and it worked out fine.

target.recipe_text:
uncle bill s french dip and roast beef sandwich

this recipe goes back many years, very simple to make, and it tastes delicious.

1. process dry onion soup mix in a coffee grinder until fine
2. in a one quart microwave safe casserole dish or glass measure , add water , instant beef bouillon and dry onion soup mix
3. microwave on high for 4 to 5 minutes until mixture has fully dissolved , stirring at least once
4. remove , cover and set aside to keep hot
5. if you are using your own cooked roast beef , use an adjustable mandoline set on very thin , slice the amount of meat as required
6. you may also use a very sharp knife to slice the meat very thin
7. if you desire the meat warm , place the thinly sliced meat on a micro-safe plate , cover with a paper towel and microwave on medium-high for 1 to 2 minutes or until meat is just warm
8. cut buns partialy through lengthwise , leaving a hinge
9. butter each piece and spread some horseradish over each half
10. layer warmed sliced beef into buns
11. about 1 / 4 pound for each bun
12. salt and pepper to taste
13. close sandwich bun and place on individual plates and cut sandwich in half
14. pour beef broth mixture into individual small bowls
15. dip sandwich into beef broth mixture and enjoy
target.review: I used this to fix a craving for roast beef, and it was yummy! I did not use deli meat, but sirloin sliced very thin that was sauteed for 2 minutes first and the juices used in the au jus with Uncle Bill's recipe above.  I really enjoyed it!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
taco cheesecake

this appetizer proves that cheesecake is not just for dessert. very good and the presentation of this is impressive. enjoy! helpful hint: when cutting or seeding hot peppers, use rubber or plastic gloves to protect your hands and avoid touching your face. prep time includes overnight refrigeration.

1. sprinkle bottom of greased 9-inch springform pan with cornmeal
2. set aside
3. in mixing bowl , beat cream cheese until smooth
4. add the taco seasoning , sour cream and salsa
5. stir in the eggs , pepper jack cheese and chilies
6. fold in olives
7. pour over cornmeal
8. place pan on a baking sheet
9. bake at 350 degrees for 30-35 minutes or until center is almost set
10. cool on a wire rack for about 10 minutes
11. carefully run a knife around edge of pan to loosen
12. cool for 1 hour
13. refrigerate overnight
14. remove sides of pan
15. spread sour cream over top and sides of cheesecake
16. arrange olives , onions , tomatoes and jalapeno slices on top in a circular motion
17. i do tomatoes on the outer edge , then green onion , jalapeno , then scatter black olives randomly , within the circle
18. serve with assorted crackers
demonstrations.review: MUCH more fun than a 7-layer dip, and it satisfies the ever-existent need to have one at a gathering. I added a few sliced tomatoes on top of mine to give it a bit of color.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crab tomato bisque

although the ingredients may sound strange this is really refreshing and delicious!

1. melt butter in a heavy saucepan
2. add 3 / 4 of the crabmeat , 1 / 3 c basil , and garlic
3. saute 2 minutes
4. stir in flour , stir for 2 minutes
5. add clam-tomato juice , cream , ketchup , clam juice , old bay and pepper sauce reduce heat to low , simmer for 10 minutes
6. puree soup with an immersion blender add water and lemon juice , simmer
7. season to taste with salt& pepper
8. pour into 6 bowls , garnish with remaining crab and basil
demonstrations.review: Oh. My. Gosh.  I had planned on making shrimp bisque, but ended up using the shrimp for another recipe.  I am so glad I didn't have shrimp, because I never would have found this!  Amazing!!  I actually used half & half instead of cream and tomato sauce for the Clamato because that is what I had.  This is the creamiest most amazing soup! A *perfect* beginning to our dinner of steak and pasta!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
reeses squares   5 ingredients   no bake  reese s

these bars are extremely rich and not for people with a fear of chocolate and peanut butter (if those people actually exist)!!! very easy no bake 5 ingredient recipe!

1. combine graham crumbs , sugar and peanut butter and mix well
2. blend in melted butter until well combined
3. press mixture evenly into a 9 x 13 inch pan
4. melt chocolate chips in microwave or in double boiler
5. spread over peanut butter mixture
6. chill until just set and cut into bars (these are very hard to cut if the chocolate gets "rock hard"
demonstrations.review: Like this needs another review!  I made thcker bars by scaling the recipe to 2/3's and using an 8x8 pan.

target.recipe_text:
amish macaroni   cheese

this is a great recipe. easy to make and delicious. i tried it at a party and really enjoyed it. this recipe is so simple i am embarassed to even post it.

1. put cottage cheese in 9 x 13 cake pan
2. add macaroni
3. add water
4. add shredded cheese
5. stir together
6. place in preheated 300 oven
7. take out after 30 minutes and stir
8. place back into oven for 30 more minutes
target.review: THis was not my favorite, was to dry and not as creamy as I would like my mac-cheese, but everyone has their own taste. May try again adjusting somethings.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pineapple scallop

i have made this for years, i cannot have ham without this, and who cares about the ham. you will not be disappointed.

1. cream butter and sugar , beat in eggs
2. fold in milk and bread , add pineapple
3. bake at 350 for 1 hour in greased casserole
demonstrations.review: MAde this as a side dish, very easy to make. Everyone liked it. Think next time I'll cut back on the butter and sugar a bit. But tasted very good.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
best and easiest pork chops ever

this is a complete meal in a pan. it is easy and delicious, cleanup a breeze, and can be either baked in the oven, crockpot, or pressure cooker. it can be easily coverted for a crowd - amounts don't matter. this is my families favorite supper.

1. in a roasting pan put the potatoes , carrots , celery , and onion
2. sprink with seasonings
3. mix the cream of mushroom soup with the milk and pour half of it over the vegetables
4. arrange the pork chops over the top of the vegetable mixture and season the chops to taste
5. pour remaining mushroom soup mixture over the chops
6. cover and bake at 375 degrees about 1 hour or until vegetables are fork tender
7. this can also be made in a crock pot , slow cooker , or pressure cooker
8. it can be converted easily for a crowd or potluck dinner
demonstrations.review: I used a crockpot, became to watery and the pork chops were more or less just boiled. Not much flavor.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
key lime pie

nothing better to beat those dog days of summer. cool & creamy (and easy as pie)

1. preheat oven to 250-degrees
2. combine milk and egg yolks in a blender on low speed
3. slowly add lime juice , mixing until blended
4. pour into pie shell and bake 20 minutes
5. let cool and refrigerate
6. top with whipped cream& lime slices
demonstrations.review: Tasted OK, D.H. liked it, I thought it was a bit heavy guess I was expecting something light and fluffy. I give this a so-so rating was very easy to prepare and would do in a pinch.

target.recipe_text:
cheesecake bites

these are always a hit when i take them to parties. i found this recipe in a spirit of christmas book.

1. mix brown sugar , flour , and nuts
2. stir in margarine until blended
3. reserve 1 / 3 cup of mixture
4. pat remainder in a greased 8-inch square baking pan
5. bake in a pre-heated 350 degree oven fo 12-15 minutes
6. beat cream cheese and sugar until smooth
7. beat in remaining ingredients
8. pour over baked crust
9. sprinkle with reserved pecan mixture
10. return to oven and bake 25 minutes
11. cool slightly
12. then cut in two-inch squares
target.review: I loved the crust. I loved the addition of the pecans in the crust. I made these for a party so I doubled the recipe and I put different topping on them, like for a bunch I drizzled chocolate sauce, some caramel sauce, some I put a cherry from cherry pie filling, and some I put a fresh strawberry slice on top. The only think is I wish they would have been a little thicker, but that may have been my doing; not sure. All in all they are a hit.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
turkey stuffed peppers

there was a sale at the grocery store for ground turkey.  seems like there is one every week!  this is a really simple recipe, even to make ahead a reheat later.  really tastey and good for you!

1. remove the tops from the peppers , seed and remove membrane
2. steam in a microwave save container
3. do this by putting one tbs
4. water in the bottom of the container , and cover with plastic wrap
5. cook until tender , approximately 3 minutes on high
6. brown the turkey in 1 / 2 the olive oil until almost cooked through
7. saute the onion , mushrooms and garlic in the olive oil on medium high heat
8. add the thawd spinach and seasonings after the onions and turkey are browned and nicely caramelized
9. cook the complete mixture until heated through
10. divid the mixture among the 4 peppers
11. this is depend upon how big your green peppers are
12. top with 1 / 4 cheese and broil in the oven until the cheese is browned
13. about 2 minutes , but be careful not to burn !
demonstrations.review: This was really quick and easy and really yummy! I liked the idea of steaming the peppers in the microwave-quick and easy. I added a couple things, simply because I'm used to stuffed peppers having rice and marinara, so I added some brown rice and a little pizza sauce I had on hand just to hold it altogether. I loved the spinach in it, although I used fresh and sauted it with the onions and mushrooms and turkey. I didn't have sage so I added oregano. Eh, it worked. Thanks for a great easy recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
maple syrup pork chops

an easy to prepare main dish that is delicious too!

1. preheat the oven to 400f
2. lightly brown the pork chops in a small amount of oil , then place them in a flat baking dish with sides
3. combine the other ingredients in a small saucepan and heat until warm
4. pour over chops
5. cover and bake for 45 minutes , basting occasionally
6. place the pork chops on a warming platter and pour the sauce into a saucepan
7. thicken it slightly with flour to make a gravy , salt to taste , and serve it over the chops
demonstrations.review: I loved this! The pork chops were so flavorful and delicious. The only thing I did was I didn't have chili powder, so I used cayenne pepper-it definitely had a KICK to it!! But my fiance' and sister both loved them.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cornmeal breaded grilled chicken

this recipe is designed for a contact grill, such as a george foreman. it is adapted from a recipe at about.com by linda larsen. be sure to leave yourself time for the breaded chicken to rest 30 minutes before grilling.

1. rinse chicken and pat it dry
2. it works best thin , so put the chicken breasts between two sheets of waxed paper and pound them to about 1 / 3" thick
3. pour beaten egg in shallow bowl
4. in a shallow dish or pan , combine basil , oregano , pepper , salt , and grated cheese
5. brush chicken with the lemon juice , then dip both sides in the beaten egg
6. next , coat chicken with the cornmeal mixture
7. let chicken sit on a wire rack for 20-30 minutes
8. spray george foreman two sided grill with nonstick cooking spray
9. cook chicken for 4-7 minutes until thoroughly cooked , brown and crisp
demonstrations.review: i really liked this chicken. The crust itself was dry but I couldn't believe how juicy and succulent the chicken was inside. The crust was flavored nicely and I liked how the crust didn't just fall off like say, shake n bake does in the oven.

target.recipe_text:
soft batch chocolate chip cookies

a soft & chewy cookie. one of my favorites

1. preheat oven to 375 degrees
2. mix butter , sugar , brown sugar , vanilla and eggs together until creamy
3. add the remaining ingredients and blend well
4. bake until lightly browned
5. store in an air tight container
target.review: These were delish...but not anything different from my ordinary chocolate chip cookies. Thank you for sharing:)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
lemon curd  stove top or microwave method  lime or orange curd

a british tea time favorite. this is sweet and tart. try it on scones, muffins, and tea breads or layer on angel food cake with raspberries and recipe #54868!  i've also microwaved this just watch and stir a lot. for orange or lime curd, substitute appropriate fruit rind and juice. proceed as directed.
fyi- when filling a cake with this be sure to pipe a rim of frosting on the edge of the first layer, then fill inside with the chilled lemon curd, place top layer then frost.

1. stove top method:
2. in a medium saucepan over medium-high heat , combine lemon zest , lemon juice , and sugar
3. bring just to a boil
4. reduce heat to medium-low and simmer 5 minutes
5. add butter and stir until it has melted and combined
6. remove from heat and cool to room temperature
7. beat eggs into cooled lemon mixture until well blended
8. return to heat and cook over medium-low heat , stirring constantly , 10 to 15 minutes or until mixture thickens and coats spoon
9. remove from heat
10. cover and refrigerator at least 1 hour
11. microwave method:
12. place butter in a large glass measure or bowl
13. microwave on high for 10 seconds or until the butter is soft , but not melted
14. whisk in the sugar , lemon rind and lemon juice
15. add the whole eggs and yolks and blend well
16. cover with parchment paper and microwave on high for 3 minutes , stirring well after each minute or until mixture thickens and coats spoon
17. cover and refrigerator at least 1 hour
18. pour into a sterilized glass jar and leave to cool
19. store in the refrigerator
demonstrations.review: Not only did I quadrupile this recipe, I messed up the process and it still came out delicious! I will keep this in my cookbook to use in the future:)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
yummy crunchy apple pie

great pie!

1. use foil on bottom of oven rather than a cookie sheet under pie pan
2. prepare pastry for single-crust pie
3. place in pie plate and trim and crimp the edge
4. refrigerate 30 minute loosely covered with plastic wrap
5. in a large mixing bowl , stir together the sugar , flour , cinnamon , nutmeg , allspice , and salt
6. add apple slices and gently toss until they are coated well
7. transfer mixture to pie
8. for crumb topping: stir together brown sugar , flour , and oats
9. using a pastry blender , cut in the butter until topping resembles coarse crumbs
10. sprinkle over apple mixture in pie
11. to prevent over-browning while baking , cover edge of pie with foil
12. bake at 375 degrees fahrenheit for 25 minutes
13. remove foil and bake 25 to 30 minutes more , or until top is golden
14. remove from oven
15. cool on wire rack about an hour and serve !
demonstrations.review: Easy like Sunday morning.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
texas red enchilada sauce

this sauce can be used with beef or cheese enchiladas. the amount of "heat" in the sauce depends on the type and amount of chili powder you use.

1. melt butter / margarine in a sauce pan
2. make a roux by browning flour in melted butter / margarine
3. add spices and tomato paste
4. stir until well blended into roux
5. add water gradually , stirring constantly
6. heat until boiling
7. continue simmering and stirring until desired thickness is achieved
8. taste every so often and adjust spices as needed
9. once desired consistency and taste is reached , coat the bottom of a pan with the sauce , add freshly rolled enchiladas , then pour the remainder of the red sauce over enchiladas
10. place pan in oven and cook until enchiladas are done
demonstrations.review: This is wonderful!! I made tofu chorizo enchiladas using this sauce and I can't get enough! I did add a little extra chili powder, cumin, and cayenne pepper for a bolder flavor:)

target.recipe_text:
tuscan white bean   spinach soup
