this delicious casserole has become a tradition at my family's thanksgiving. and everyone agrees we should make it more often, it's so good, and not hard to make. i've changed this recipe only slightly from the chilean squash in the moosewood cookbook. you can substitute mashed pumpkin or yams (unsweetened, of course!), but the butternut is best and worth the effort. a tip for easier clean up: i just mash the squash right in the casserole and mix everything there. i wipe off the upper sides wih a clean, damp dish towel and pop it in the oven. i've been tempted to add a cup or two of cooked rice or other grain to make it even more hardy, but i haven't tried that yet... note: cook time does not include time for baking the squash; that can be done ahead and refrigerated.

1. cut squash in half lengthwise and scoop out seeds
2. bake cut sides down at 425 45- 50 min
3. or until very soft at thick end
4. let squash cool and scrape out of the shell
5. mash as smoothly as you can
6. meanwhile , saut onion , garlic and spices in olive oil until onion is translucent
7. add peppers and salt , stir , cover and leave on low heat 5 min
8. preheat oven to 350
9. stir beaten eggs into mashed squash
10. add corn , sautd vegies and grated cheddar
11. stir to mix well
12. bake 20 min
13. covered
14. uncover and bake 20- 30 min
15. more
demonstrations.review: This was really delicious. I used it as a filling for bell peppers (and used only 1 bell pepper in the recipe) and added soy crumbles for my vegetarian husband. It was a fantastic flavor combination and I feel lucky to have found your recipe! Thank you so much for sharing it.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
french beef au gratin

comes from "our house to yours" cookbook by the pulaski business & professional women's organization.

1. in large , heavy bottomed pan , over medium heat , melt butter
2. add onions
3. saute , stirring often , until caramelized , but not burned , 15 to 20 minutes
4. with slotted spoon , remove onions to medium bowl
5. add beef to pan
6. brown well on all sides
7. return onions and any juices to pan
8. in small bowl , mix flour , sugar , cumin , salt and pepper and add to pan
9. stir 1 minute until bubbly
10. gradually add broth , stirring to scrape drippings from pan
11. simmer 10 minutes
12. cook pasta according to package directions
13. heat broiler
14. place 1 / 2 cup fettucine in each of 4 ovenproof bowls
15. divide beef mixture over pasta
16. in medium bowl , stir cheeses together
17. sprinkle evenly over beef
18. broil until cheese is melted and lightly browned , about 5 minutes
19. makes 4 servings
demonstrations.review: This is a terrific recipe my dad would make on special days. it is wonderful. I think he got it from an old issue of Reader's Digest! Thanks for posting.

target.recipe_text:
rosemary roasted salmon

nan

1. place half of rosemary sprigs in a single layer in the center of a baking pan
2. place sliced red onion ontop of the rosemary
3. place salmon filet on top of the onion with skin side down
4. sprinkle salmon with salt and pepper
5. cover salmon with remainder of rosemary sprigs
6. place lemon slices over rosemary
7. drizzle olive oil over filet
8. sprinkle with salt
9. in a preheated 500 degree oven , roast salmon for about 20 minutes or until cooked through
10. serve salmon with onion and lemon
target.review: i made this recipe for my grandparents 60th anniversary dinner. i used 1 1/2 red onions and  the garlic salt instead of regular salt (as reccomended in other reviews). it was amazing. everyone said it was the best salmon they had ever tasted. thanks for sharing such a great recipe! i'm sure we will be using it again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pommes anna

potatoes layered with garlic butter, onion slices and parmesan and baked until crisp on top, tender underneath. this is the best pommes anna i've ever had. it takes a little time to put together but the results are well worth it. please don't try to lower the amounts of butter or cheese in this dish, it's supposed to be decadent. i make this in a white quiche plate with fluted edges and it is very beautiful and impressive. from flavors, a san antonio junior league cookbook, credited to mrs. edgar m. duncan (linda wyatt)

1. slice potatoes in 1 / 8-inch thick rounds and soak in ice water for at least 30 minutes
2. drain slices and pat dry with paper towels
3. combine butter and garlic
4. in a deep 10-inch greased pie plate or casserole , arrange 1 / 3 of the potato slices in slightly overlapping fashion , beginning with the outside edges and continuing the circle design to center of dish
5. layer 1 / 3 of onion slices , broken into rings , on top of the potatoes , then 1 / 3 of butter mixture , salt , pepper , paprika and cheese
6. repeat this process 2 more times , ending with cheese on top
7. bake , covered at 400 degrees for 1 hour
8. if cheese is not brown on top , place under broiler for 4-5 minutes
9. cut in wedges to serve
demonstrations.review: this was so good! i only had red potatoes so i used them. i also did not have time to soak them the full 30 min and they turned out fine. (although this may be due to the fact that they were not baking potatoes.) the only thing i did differently was i added fines herbs in between the layers and a little olive oil on top. it turned out great. there was none left over, and i am tempted to make it again tonight! thanks longhornmama!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
beth s pizza crust

this is an excellent crust that requires no time to rise. why order out when you can just throw this pizza together?

1. combine yeast and warm water
2. stir until dissolved
3. add remaining ingredients and mix well
4. let rest 5 minutes
5. roll out to size and shape you need
6. bake at 450 for 15 minutes or until golden
7. a couple
8. instead , i add several good shakes of italian seasoning mix
9. use your imagination , this is hard to mess up
demonstrations.review: It's quick, easy, and delicious. My whole family really enjoyed this. Thanks for sharing your recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
bubba gump s greenbow county okra gumbo

i found this recipe in honor of two of my okra lovin' friends-enjoy!

1. cook okra in 2 tbsp butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat , stirring constantly , until lightly browned
2. set aside
3. combine remaining butter and flour in a large dutch oven , cook over medium high , stirring constantly until roux is chocolate colored-around 20-25 min stir in green onions , celery and garlic , cook stirring constantly until veg is tender
4. add okra , water and the next 6 ingredients
5. bring to a boil , reduce and simmer uncovered 2 hours , stirring occasionally
6. peel and devein shrimp , add that and crab to okra mixture
7. simmer an additional 10 minutes , stirring occasionally
8. remove and discard bay leaf
9. serve gumbo over rice
10. sprinkle with file if desired
demonstrations.review: i don't know who princess is but it is obvious that something is wrong with her taste buds! im working on making this for the second time right now and just wanted to thank you for this great recipe. it is amazing how spicy 1/2 t. of red pepper makes this. im not huge on spicy food so i added a little less this time. my dad- who likes spicy though loved it. thanks again!

target.recipe_text:
awesome and simple italian garlicky meatloaf

this meat loaf is so flavorful, but doesn't require endless ingredients! it is simple and soooo good. i almost always have the ingredients on hand straight from the pantry.    my family loves it, it tastes even better leftover, and it makes the house smell delicious! can be frozen for oamc. i have adjusted the breadcrumbs per the reviews, the key is to use only as much as you need to make a moist dough.  if your ground beef is very low in fat, like sirloin, you will need fewer breadcrumbs, however higher fat beef, like chuck, will absorb a larger amount of breadcrumbs.

1. preheat oven to 350f and grease a large loaf pan
2. mix 1 / 2 cup bread crumbs , cheese , parsley , garlic , salt and pepper , reserving the remaining bread crumbs to use as necessary
3. add the meat and use a fork to mix the ingredients uniformly
4. add the eggs and knead it with your hands until a "dough" ball forms , it should hold its shape and not be too dry and crumbly or too sticky sloppy
5. mold the meat mixture into the loaf pan and top with a layer of ketchup as desired
6. bake for 70 minutes
7. slices best when cooled and tastes even better reheated as leftovers !
8. for oamc: slice cooled loaf and flash freeze slices on a cookie sheet
9. once frozen , store in a freezer bag or container
10. to reheat: remove as many slices as necessary and reheat in microwave
target.review: This recipe generally tasted good, but it came out very dry. I think the cook time may have been too long. Perhaps it was because I didn't cook it in a loaf pan, but a dutch oven instead? I'll give one more star than I normally would because I'm giving the recipe the benefit of the doubt. Also, the ketchup definitely did not go with it.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
italian butter cookies   1952

add a cherry to the tops before baking,  or afterwards, pair them up with raspberry jam, and dip ends into melted chocolate.  a bakery special.

1. preheat the oven to 350 degrees
2. in a large mixer bowl , cream lightly the butter and sugar until really fluffy and pale , about three minutes
3. add the egg and vanilla and mix until combined
4. at low speed add the combined dry ingredients and mix until just blended
5. do not overmix
6. place into a pastry bag fitted with a star
7. if dough is too thick to pipe , pour in a few tablespoons of milk
8. if you make wreath or stars , you can add a cherry as decoration now before baking
9. or you could just roll into small bals and flatten with a fork if desired
10. bake for 10 to 14 minutes just until the bottoms and edges begin to turn golden brown
11. remove from pans by sliding thw whole piece of parchment onto a large wire rack , and cool completely
12. dip fingers or one side of each into melted chocolate and sprinkles if desired
13. sandwich with raspberry jam also if desired , dip in melted white chocolate and crushed almonds
14. leave plain also
15. store in an airtight container
demonstrations.review:
I combined this recipe with another recipe for Italian butter cookies on this site. I did not get to have a finished cookie because my dog got to them first. However, I tried a plain half once they were done baking, and it was okay, Not like the ones from the bakery but still good. Kind of like a heavy cake. I could taste the flour for some reason. I will definitely make them again, so next time I'll stick to the given measurements and see if that helps. Here are the ones I used:

1 cup butter
2 1/4 cups flour
2/3 cup sugar
1 egg
1 1/2 tsp vanilla extract
1/2 tsp baking powder
dash salt

demonstrations.recipe_text:
colcannon  mashed potatoes with cabbage

i know there is a ton of different styles.  this is the one i found that i like the best.

1. put cabbage , onion , and water in saucepan
2. bring to boil over high heat and reduce to simmer , cover and cook for 8 minutes or until tender , but not mushy
3. drain cabbage and onion
4. add mashed potatoes , milk , butter and salt and pepper to taste
5. mix well to blend and heat through
6. serve warm , as a side dish with meat , chicken or fish
demonstrations.review:
This was so simple and delicious. I used the water from boiling the potatoes and cabbage/onions as the the water added to the recipe. I think next time I will cook the cabbage a bit softer, but that's just my taste.

Thank you!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
soft chewy molasses cookies

these are rich, sweet, chewy cookies.

1. preheat oven 350f
2. mix on low speed electric mixer shortening , molasses , 1 cup sugar and egg
3. cream mixture
4. slowly add the remaining ingredients except 1 / 2 cup of white sugar
5. mix on medium
6. get 1 / 2 cup white sugar and pour into plate
7. by teaspoonful roll dough into ball then into sugar
8. place each cookie on greased baking sheet
9. bake 5-10 minutes
10. you are looking for cookie to puff up and start to crack slightly
11. take out as soon as cookies appear to have cracks allover
12. this will ensure you have a chewy cookie
demonstrations.review:
These cookies were simply amazing. Perfect in every way. I would like to note though, that instead of using 3/4 cup of shortening, I used 6 tbsp of shortening and 6 tbsp of lard.

Anyhow, thank you! I'll definitely make these again.

target.recipe_text:
copycat bahama mama crab dip

from a copycat web site. delicious! can use imitation crabmeat.

1. in food processor or with an electric mixer on low speed , mix sour cream , old bay seasoning , and cream cheese until creamy
2. stir in celery , onion , and lemon juice
3. fold in crabmeat
4. serve with crackers or chips
5. variation: add 1 / 2 cup chopped pecans
target.review: This was really great.I used FF cream cheese, low-fat sour cream and also added Old Bay and some FF mayo but loved the flavors.  I used imitation crab and with the lemon juice it really made the difference.  Thank you.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
fisherman s wharf cioppino

this is a recipe adapted from one at catalina offshore products, purveyors of fresh seafood. i've prepared this with great results. it reminds me of dinners at alioto's restaurant in san francisco at fisherman's wharf, where in 1938 rose alioto created an italian seafood stew called cioppino, now a san francisco culinary legend. in addition to or in lieu of the ingredients listed, you can add clams, mussels or lobster.

1. in a large deep pot , cook onion , parsley and garlic in the olive oil for 3 to 5 minutes
2. add tomatoes , wine , tomato paste and seasonings
3. cover and simmer for 30 minutes
4. add seafood and simmer for another 20 minutes
5. you can use a little more seafood , especially if you're adding crab claws
6. serve in heated bowls with crusty french bread and green salad
7. top with fresh shredded parmesan cheese , chopped parsley or cilantro and lemon , if desired
demonstrations.review: If my husband tells me after one bite that this is the best I have ever made, then I know it's a winner.  I kept to the recipe but wanted it to make more so I used up 2 cups of leftover vegetable juice and used the whole can of tomato paste.  Cooked the vegs in less than 1/4 c olive oil.  No fresh parsley so added Italian seasoning and Old Bay.  Added 2 c of steamed diced red potatoes at the end with 1 lb. tilapia, 1 lb. shrimp and 1 lb. crawfish meat.  Can't wait to add the crab next time. I have finally found the recipe like the one I had in St. Augustine Florida. When you live in Texas, you crave seafood.  Thank you, thank you!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
louisiana oyster casserole

another favorite of former canadian prime minister lester b. pearson

1. pour the oysters into a shallow 9" pie plate
2. sprinkle with parsley and onions
3. scatter the cracker crumbs on top
4. melt butter and add lemon juice , mustard and worcestershire sauce
5. pour mixture over the crumbs and bake 450f until oysters curl slightly and crumbs are brown appro 10-15 minutes
demonstrations.review: This was great.  Can't get fresh oysters so I used 2 of the canned.  Still loved it and will make this often.  Thank you!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
sugar free coconut cream pie

this is the best recipe for coconut cream and chocolate silk pies that i have ever eaten.  you don't miss the sugar.

1. bake pie crust according to directions on back of package
2. while baking heat skillet and toast 1 tbsp coconut flakes until golden brown
3. mix milk , coconut extract and pudding mix together
4. when well blended add coconut flakes then half of cool whip
5. once blended well pour into baked pie crust and smooth
6. let set for 10 minutes in refrigerator
7. when ready to serve top with remaining cool whip and toasted flakes
8. you can use the same concept with chocolate pudding mix and make a chocolate silk pie that is wonderful
demonstrations.review: This was great.  Used small box of sugar free french vanilla pudding and didn't have the extract and I put it in the 6 mini graham cracker pie crusts.  Loved the texture of the toasted flakes and think I'll do half in the pudding next time.  It was hard not to eat more than one, but my husband and I will have dessert two more times.  Can't wait to try the chocolate. Thanks!

target.recipe_text:
hawaiian macaroni salad

i made this pasta salad for my son's birthday party. it was a huge hit! now everytime someone wants be to bring something to a get together, they tell me to make it :) . this recipe is best after its been refigerated for at least 4-6 hours.i hope you enjoy it

1. cook pasta
2. combine remaining 7 ingredients in a large bowl
3. let cool in refrigerator for 4-6hours
4. remove from fridge and give the salad a mix , if you find it too dry add a bit more miracle whip
5. transfer to presentation bowl ! enjoy !
target.review: could we add chicken and have it feel like a HAWAIIAN MACARONI SALAD//???  Have you seen it done before .ALYSE

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mrs  fields banana nut cookies

this is an original recipe from debbie fields, which i found and posted in a recipezaar forum in response to a request.  it prompted such positive replies that i thought i should post the recipe for others who might be searching for it, too.  (servings are calculated at 3 cookies each.)

1. preheat oven to 300f
2. in a medium bowl , combine four , soda and salt
3. mix well and set aside
4. in a large bowl with an electric mixer , blend sugars at medium speed
5. add butter and mix to form a grainy paste , scraping down the sides of the bowl
6. add egg , liqueur and banana , and beat at medium speed until smooth
7. add flour mixture , 1 cup of the chocolate chips and walnuts , and blend at low speed until just combined
8. drop by rounded tablespoons onto ungreased cookie sheets , 2 inches apart
9. sprinkle cookies with chocolate chips , 6 to 8 per cookie
10. bake 25-27 minutes until cookie edges begin to brown
11. transfer immediately to a cool surface
demonstrations.review: I make these all of the time!  They are the banana bread cookies that everyone always asks for!! It's a great use for almost black bananas!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
redneck casserole

my brother and i cook up this quick and easy recipe every friday night when my mom is out with her friends/family. it's yummy yummy and has the potential to evolve into much more...but we like it just the way it is. i hope you enjoy!!

1. set your oven to 450
2. dump your can of baked beans into a casserole dish
3. set the dish aside
4. cut up your hotdogs into bite sized pieces and throw those into your casserole dish and mix until dogs are well coated with baked bean sauce
5. cover the bean and dog mixture with tatertots
6. we usually use a couple handfuls
7. use as many as you'd like
8. just make sure to cover the mixture completely
9. place the casserole dish in the oven for 1 / 2 an hour or until tater tots are golden brown
10. when redneck casserole is all cooked up , turn off the oven and sprinkle the top with cheese
11. redneck casserole is completely done when cheese is melted and you just can't take it anymore -- dig in !
demonstrations.review: A kid pleaser for sure!  It was fun to make with the kids and they  loved it.  I will make it again for sure!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
shrimp egg foo yong   low carb and low fat

you will never know that this is low carb and low fat. it is just as good and even better than any other recipe.

1. place 2 tablespoons oil in large skillet , and cook onions and cabbage over medium-high heat until tender
2. remove from heat and drain off excess liquid and set the onions and cabbage to the side
3. whisk eggs in a bowl and mix in soy sauce , sesame oil , spices , onion and cabbage mixture , and sprouts
4. using a non-stick pan over medium-high heat , heat the remaining 2 tablespoons of oil
5. ladle about 4 ounces of the mixture into the hot pan , as you would for pancakes , and sprinkle the shrimp evenly on top of each
6. cook for about 3 minutes , or until edges begin to brown , and when jiggled , they slide in the pan
7. flip them over and cook another 2 to 3 minutes until cooked through
demonstrations.review: I really liked this recipe!! I did make a couple of changes... I added more onion, LOTS! And I added sriracha sauce... I do agree with the author, about finishing it in the oven.  It is so much easier !!

target.recipe_text:
thai chicken balls

i got this recipe from a cooking show - they were demonstrating the oven i think!! very popular at parties!!

1. combine all the ingredients in a bowl and mix well
2. roll into balls
3. bake in the oven for 10-15 minutes- basically until they are cooked though and look cooked !
4. i line the tray with baking paper
5. serve with extra sweet chilli sauce for dipping
6. i often add more breadcrumbs / coriander and chilli sauce-- just judge how wet / dry the mixture is
target.review: These Thai chicken balls were very easy and tasted great. They were a little dry so I will add more sweet chilli sauce next time. Thanks for posting them mylanos, I will be making them again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
oven roasted green beans

this is another simple yet tasty side dish. please feel free to use any dried herb that you like in place of the basil. sometimes i even add a few shakes of crushed red pepper flakes to give a little "heat" to the beans. if you'd like to cut back a little on the olive oil, a few tablespoons of water in the bottom of the pan will keep the beans from drying out too much.

1. preheat oven to 450 degrees
2. line a baking or roasting pan with foil , and spray with a bit of non stick spray
3. combine all ingredients on pan , and toss well with your hands to be sure all the beans are evenly coated
4. bake in the oven for about 10 minutes , or until the beans are tender and slightly browned
5. feel free to toss beans a couple of times as they are cooking
demonstrations.review: We really enjoyed beans cooked this way KB. The only change I made was to use fresh garlic and I had run out of almonds.  I did need to cook them for another 10 mins and they were still crisp but perfect.  I made them again a night or two later, still haven’t got the almonds.  I much prefer them to the steamed beans we usually have.  Thanks so much.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chocolate banana cake

this is a very moist & very fudgey cake. it tastes best the second day.

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees f
2. cream margarine with sugar and eggs
3. mix in banana and vanilla
4. mix flour with remaining dry ingredients
5. add flour mixture to margarine mixture in 3 parts , alternately with sour milk
6. begin and end with flour
7. spread in 2 greased 8" cake pans
8. bake in oven about 40 minutes
9. when cool , frost generously with chocolate butter frosting
demonstrations.review: One of my very favourite cakes, I love the combination of banana and chocolate.  This is the same as my own recipe. Thanks you Deb.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
vicki s gourmet potatoes

this has been a holiday tradition and special occasion dish in our home and with our friends...i usually serve them with baked ham, but when the meal calls for mashed potatoes, and you want to give your family a treat, i suggest you try these! yum!

1. cook potatoes in salted water until tender
2. drain
3. combine potatoes with salts , onion , butter , cream cheese , and sour cream
4. whip until mixture is smooth and fluffy
5. place in buttered 2-qt
6. casserole
7. top with grated cheese if desired
8. bake at 350 for 30 minutes or until golden brown
demonstrations.review:
Wow!  These were great Martha, thank you.
I had some freshly grated parmesan left over so I used that instead of regular cheese, I didn't use a cup though.  Next time I will do it exactly as you suggested. Glen

target.recipe_text:
southwest chicken black bean soup

an extremely flavorful way to combine chicken and the ever growing popularity of black beans. lots of flavor and a great thick broth. its very healthy for you too! serve with recipe #43730.

1. in a medium sized skillet cook chicken that's been seasoned with seasoned salt until done and no longer pink
2. dice and set aside
3. finely chop bell peppers , onion and jalapeo slices in food processor or by hand if you like larger pieces
4. combine all peppers , onion and jalapeo and add lemon juice and a pinch of salt
5. melt margarine in a large stock pot
6. saut pepper and onion mixture until soft
7. add can of crushed tomatoes , stirring
8. add three cans of black beans , undrained
9. add chicken to pot , stirring carefully
10. then add chicken broth to soup and stir
11. next , add bay leaf , about a teaspoon of season salt , tarragon and cinnamon
12. let simmer until flavors are combined and peppers and onion are soft and tender about one hour , or until it smells so good you cannot wait
13. serve with recipe #43730
target.review: This is wonderful, I did take the suggestion of omiting the cinnamon, I added celery and a can a green chilis instead of jalapenos and used 2 cans diced tomatoes and 2 cans black beans rinsed and replaced the liquid with chicken broth. This was awesome. Thank you!!! *also* I threw this in the crockpot to cook on low for 6 hours.. delish..

demonstrations.recipe_text:
homemade banana pudding

here's another pudding that is so easy and good

1. beat yolks with sugar , milk , salt , banana flavor and corn starch heat on medium heat , stir constantly don't let it burn
2. line the bottom and sides of a baking dish with vanilla wafers when pudding thickens pour about half of it over the wafers
3. lay a layer of banana slices on this and top with another layer of wafers then another layer of pudding use the egg whites for your meringue if so desired
demonstrations.review: AWESOME!! This is a fab. recipe.. I didn't go the extra with the wafers and bananas. I made this as reg. pudding and put in dessert serving cups and my kiddos went crazy over this.. I will def. put this at the top of my dessert list.. Thank you so much for an outstanding and oh so easy recipe..

demonstrations.recipe_text:
homemade apple pie liquor

the combination of apples and cinnamon is one of my favorite flavor combinations.  i had this cocktail at a party and when i found out that it was homemade, i had to find the recipe.  i couldn't find it here in recipezaar (!!!), so i turned to the www.

1. put the cider , juice , sugar and cinnamon sticks into a large kettle
2. bring to almost a boil and then let cool
3. pour in the everclear and mix
demonstrations.review: I made this to take to my parents camping trip, my cousin's showed up and they all loved it. I was emailing out the recipe when I got back home. This is awesome and it goes so smooth so be very careful.. I always have it on hand. I put it in the crockpot on low for the holidays to warm it a bit. Everyone goes crazy over it. Thank you for this wonderful recipe..

demonstrations.recipe_text:
sneak up margarita

i love a good margarita and this one is quite tasty. a very relaxing drink. a bartender told me what the basic ingredients are in one. after a few tries i finally came up with the right amounts of the ingredients to suit my taste you can't taste the tequila in it, so be careful. a beer afterwards or a second margarita may make the drink sneak up on you, hence the name. you may add more tequila for a stronger drink.

1. pour the 1 tablespoon of lime juice onto a saucer
2. spread it around the saucer
3. pour the tablespoon of salt onto another saucer
4. dip a glass into the lime juice and then in the salt
5. you can skip this step if you don't want salt on the rim
6. place ice cubes into the glass
7. pour the rest of the ingredients into the glass and stir well
8. you can also put the ingredients in a blender and blend well for a frozen / blended margarita
9. garnish with a lime wedge for a nice little touch !
10. cheers !
demonstrations.review: WOW! ~This is fantastic~ I can't wait to have company so I can share this. Made exactly as the recipe states.  Thank you for the recipe. I will be keeping this one close.

target.recipe_text:
vegan biscuits and gravy for lovers

when it's raining outside and you're hankering for some soul food whip up some vegan biscuits and gravy for your loved one(s) and spend the rest of the morning working them off in bed!

1. preheat oven to 450
2. mix together dry ingredients in a large bowl
3. mix together liquid ingredients into a small bowl
4. cut margarine into pea sized pieces
5. don't cut too small
6. add liquid ingredients and mix with a fork until it just starts to come together
7. push into a ball , knead just once or twice and roll out to 1 / 2 thick slab
8. cut into circles or squares , place on cookie sheet and bake at 450 for 10-15 minutes
9. now , on to the gravy
10. mix together 3 / 4 cup liquid , flour , salt , pepper and thyme into a bottle and shake vigorously
11. heat margarine in pan and whisk in flour / stock mix
12. once it's incorportated add the rest of the liquid and stir over a low heat until it's set
13. pour over the piping hot biscuits and watch for the smiles
target.review: I didn't work them off in bed, but they were very good.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
vegan heart attack chocolate doughnuts

nan

1. beat the egg replacer and sugar together until creamy in consistency
2. melt the margarine and chocolate together in a small saucepan over low heat
3. beat into the sugar mixture until well combined
4. combine the soy milk , vinegar and vanilla
5. stir this into the sugar / chocolate mixture
6. in another bowl , combine the flour , baking powder , baking soda and salt
7. stir this into the liquid mixture until it forms a dough
8. chill this for about 1 / 2 hour to make it easier to handle
9. roll 1 / 2 the dough out onto a lightly floured board to a 1 / 2" thickness
10. cut out the doughnuts with a 3" diameter doughnut cutter
11. let them rest for about 10 minutes before frying
12. repeat with the rest of the dough
13. deep fry in hot oil for about 90 seconds each , turning every 15 seconds
14. remove from the hot oil and allow them to drain on paper towels
15. cool , and ice , glaze or sprinkle with powdered sugar as per your desires
demonstrations.review: These are very, very good.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
garlic mashed potatoes and cashew gravy

a savory dish for the holidays. always a winner.

1. peel and dice the potatoes and then boil until they are soft
2. heat oil over medium heat in small pan
3. saute the garlic for about 30 seconds
4. add the soy milk and reduce to a simmer
5. keep this mixture warm until the potatoes are cooked
6. mash the potatoes in a large bowl
7. add the margarine , and then add the soy milk mixture and nutritional yeast and mix until creamy
8. for the gravy , saute the onions in margarine until golden
9. stir in the flour and cashews and cook for another 3 minutes , stirring constantly
10. add the broth gradually , whisking constantly to form a smooth mix
11. add the soy sauce , garlic and pepper
12. bring to a boil , and then turn down heat and simmer until thick
13. puree in the blender until smooth
demonstrations.review: Really creamy and rich.  Delicious.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
tofu scramble with hollandaise sauce

the hollandaise sauce makes this dish truly decadent. i often eat this atop a piece of toast.

1. -----------tofuscramble-----------
2. drizzle enough oil to cover bottom of fry pan
3. heat over medium heat and add onion , bell pepper and tofu
4. cook , stirring frequently , until tofu loses most of it's moisture
5. add the rest of the ingredients and turn the heat up a little
6. continue cooking until mixture resembles scrambled eggs
7. ---------hollandaisesauce----------
8. put nutritional yeast flakes , flour , soy milk , paprika and salt in a saucepan and whisk over medium heat until mixture thickens and bubbles
9. cook for one more minute after you see it start bubbling
10. remove from heat and add margarine and mustard
11. whisk together until margarine is incorporated
12. drizzle over tofu scramble and serve
demonstrations.review: This was excellent on sourdough toast.

target.recipe_text:
homemade jello  regular and sugar free

make your own jello flavors!

1. put 1 cup water on to boil
2. sprinkle gelatin into 1 cup cold water
3. mix in sugar and 1 tsp kool-aid powder
4. stir until thoroughly dissolved
5. add boiling water and stir
6. adjust amount of sugar and kool-aid to taste
7. chill until firm
target.review: looks like a good recipe to use to make a sugar-free version of the blue Jell-O since Kraft Foods doesn't make a sugar-free version of that flavor just gotta be careful though as I don't know what sweetener this person used but on the website for Splenda, the sweetener I use, it says that the equivalent to 3/4 cup of sugar is 18 packets, not 10....though I could probably just measure out 3/4 cup of the granulated Splenda too

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s foil wrapped grilled corn

you may adjust all amounts to suit taste, i like to use seasoned salt for this but white salt will do fine -- to kick this up a notch, in a small saucepan or microwave melt 1/2 cup butter, mix in 1 tablespoon mustard, 1 teaspoon worcestershire sauce, 1/4 teaspoon lemon pepper and 2-3 teaspoons horseradish, brush on the corn then wrap in foil and grill as stated :)

1. place each corn on top of one piece the heavy-duty foil
2. brush each ear generously with soft butter
3. season lightly with seasoned salt or white salt and black pepper
4. wrap the corn then seal the foil loosely but leave room for expansion , then cut a very small hole in the foil to allow steam to escape
5. grill over medium coals for about 15-20 minutes
6. unwrap very carefully and serve
7. delicious !
demonstrations.review: I wonder if this would work with olive oil instead of butter?

demonstrations.recipe_text:
slow cooker bloody mary chicken

found this recipe when i joined a yahoo group, slow cooker recipes.

1. rinse chicken with cold water and pat dry with paper towels
2. remove any fat from the chicken and place in the slow cooker
3. pour the bloody mary mix over the chicken breasts and add the chopped vegetables
4. cook on low for 8 hours
5. serve with rice or hot noodles
demonstrations.review: Rats! No vodka in the recipe LOL!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pasties

my mum made the best pasties on earth, but she's gone so i had to make them today from my memories. pasties were a food we ate when we were poor, so there wasn't much meat in them compared to veg. swede turnip is very important in pasties. mum made her own pastry with dripping, but i don't save dripping!

1. preheat oven to 160c for a fan forced oven or 180c for non fan forced
2. seperate pastry sheets and defrost
3. using the largest dinner plate that will fit on the pastry square , cut circles
4. mix filling ingredients together and divide into 5
5. place 1 / 5th of the mixture along the centre of a pastry circle , then moisten edges with water and bring together crimping to seal
6. repeat with remaining 4 circles of pastry
7. place on a baking tray and brush with the glaze
8. cut a small hole in pastry to allow steam to escape
9. cook in preheated oven for 45 minutes or until golden
demonstrations.review: Sounds good but I think the Swedes might get a little put out if I start kidnapping their babies and putting them in pasties LOL!

target.recipe_text:
strawberry coffee cake

good for a special occasion breakfast.

1. in a mixing bowl , add the flour , sugar , baking powder and salt
2. stir to mix
3. in a second bowl , add the egg , milk and butter
4. stir to mix
5. add to dry ingredients and stir just until moistened
6. pour mixture into a greased 8-inch square baking dish
7. place strawberries evenly over the top of batter
8. to make the topping: combine the flour and sugar in a bowl
9. with a pastry blender , cut in the butter until consistency of coarse crumbs
10. stir in pecans
11. sprinkle mixture evenly over the strawberries
12. bake at 375 for 30-35 minutes or until wooden pick comes out clean
target.review: Made this the other night. It was a big hit. Omitted pecans in topping. Everyone loved it. It was so easy to make.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
ribs my way

this is the way i always prepare my bbq ribs. they result in fall off the bone tender ribs, and they are always a hit. the spices listed are what i submitted for this recipe, however i probably never use the same thing twice. play around with those ingredients you enjoy the most. prep time includes marinating time.

1. mix brown sugar , garlic powder , and cayenne together in bowl
2. add salt and pepper if you wish
3. rub spice mixture onto ribs , both sides
4. wrap ribs in aluminum foil , using two sheets of foil
5. place ribs in fridge for at least 24 hours
6. remove ribs when ready to prepare and place in oven on warm
7. (my oven goes from warm to 250f , so i say place on warm , if your oven does have temps
8. lower than 250f , i would suggest 200f bake ribs on warm for at least 4 hours , up to 6 hours
9. remove ribs , and let them sit in foil , allowing them to cool to almost room temperature
10. place ribs on hot fire , and baste with your favorite sauce
11. let ribs cook on grill for approx 15 minutes or until hot
12. remove ribs and let them rest for approx 10 minutes before serving
demonstrations.review: I made the ribs the other day. They were a big hit. I may cut down on the cayenne pepper the next time. Very easy to make. Will make again soon.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
dry rub for barbecued ribs

this is a great dry rub. my friend barb gave it to me.

1. mix all herb and spice ingredients
2. rub over both sides of ribs
3. let sit in refrigerator for a couple hours or overnight
4. bake in covered pan at 325 degrees f
5. for 2 1 / 2-3 hours or until done
6. at this time you can refrigerate until ready to barbecue or immediately put on moderately heated grill and brush your favorite barbecue sauce over them while turning and heating through
demonstrations.review: Great rub. Used this rub with the ribs my way recipe. Perfect.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crock pot bread   sausage stuffing

i love stuffing and have always been disappointed that there is just never enough of it.  this makes a large quantity and tastes delicious.  handy too because you can serve it right from the crock pot insert. you could also add mushrooms or apples to this recipe.

1. in large bowl put 1 loaf bread broken up and dried overnight
2. season crumbs with salt , pepper , poultry seasoning & garlic powder
3. in pan , saute 1 chopped onion , chopped celery and the chopped parsley in the butter
4. in another pan brown & break up the bulk sausage
5. pour the sauteed vegetables and sausage over the bread crumbs
6. moisten with the chicken broth
7. place in slow cooker on low for about 3 hours
8. i recommend giving it a stir and checking to see if it is getting too dry around the edges from time to time
9. you can always add a little more broth to suit your taste
demonstrations.review: Made this for thanksgiving since we smoked a turkey. It was great. I used turkey sausage. Even my dad liked it. And he does not like anything. Will definitely make again when we smoke our turkey.

target.recipe_text:
toasted ravioli

these italian appetizers are crunchy and delicious dipped in a warm marinara sauce. they are very addictive! make a bunch, you'll need to have a lot!

1. cook ravioli in boiling salted water until they float to the top
2. remove from water and drain
3. set aside to cool
4. heat vegetable oil in fryer at least 2" deep to a temperature of 375 degrees
5. dip ravioli in beaten egg , then cover in breadcrumbs
6. fry in batches in hot oil until golden brown , about 5 minutes
7. drain
8. sprinkle hot ravioli with parmesan cheese
9. heat marinara sauce and set aside in serving bowl
10. serve ravioli with dipping sauce
target.review:
I have only really cooking for about 2-3 years, and this was soo simple!! I have made this for a handful of friends and I have been getting tons of request for them, even request froms friends who have not had them yet!! In fact, my closest girlfriends, who have just begun to cook, are arranging a girl's night so I can teach them this recipe!!
my only change is I use half olive oil half vegetable oil.  The olive oil really gives it an extra flavor!!
Thanks for posting this!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
beef or chicken fajita marinade

ive tried lotsa fajita marinades, and so far this one is the best..try it and see if you like it as much as we do.

1. combine all ingredients
2. mix well
3. enough for 2-3 pounds beef or chicken
demonstrations.review: Thought it was really good! thanks

demonstrations.recipe_text:
poppy seed chicken

this is a great and easy chicken dish. it is a way to use up leftover chicken or turkey and it can be prepared beforehand. the cracker mixtures is what makes this dish so good. i have taken it to people for dinner several times and had lots of requests for the recipe.

1. combine chicken with soup and sour cream in a bowl
2. in another bowl add crushed crackers and poppy seeds to melted butter
3. mix well
4. mix half of cracker mixture in chicken
5. put in casserole dish
6. spread remaining cracker mix on top
7. bake 30 minutes at 350 degrees
8. cover for first 15 minutes and then uncover for last 15 minutes
demonstrations.review: We used leftover mojo chicken from publix and served with green beans rolls and mashed potatos..yum!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
quick spanish rice

great side dish for your mexican fiesta. try with recipe #17130!  it is as good as you'll find in any mexican restaurant.  update:  1 teaspoon cumin was added to original recipe.  i took some of my reviewers suggestion and added 1 teaspoon of cumin to the recipe. they were right. cumin definitely adds to the taste.

1. in medium saucepan , combine all ingredients
2. bring to a boil
3. reduce heat to low
4. cover and simmer 25 minutes or until rice is done
5. garnish with green onions and / or cheddar cheese
demonstrations.review: great recipe!! Word of caution: DO NOT USE QUICK COOKING RICE!! I did that the first time and tried to adjust cooking time accordingly, and it didn't turn out right.  But a week later, bought normal white rice, and turned out great! thanks!

target.recipe_text:
kittencal s baked potato salad casserole  or cold potato salad

this may be served hot as a casserole or reduce the melted butter amount down to 2 tablespoons and serve as a cold potato salad, either way it's delicious! --- if you are serving hot as a casserole i strongly recommend to have the potatoes cooled to room temperature before using in this recipe or use cold potatoes that have been cooked a day ahead, i have even made this using about 5 cups of thawed frozen hash browns, the complete casserole may be assembled and refrigerated for up to 2 days ahead before baking although it's so delicious cold it might not even make it to the oven, and also makes a large amount which makes this *perfect* dish for potlucks --- if you are baking as a casserole use only mayonnaise such as hellman's using salad dressing will not be as good.

1. to serve hot as a casserole
2. grease a 13 x 9-inch baking dish
3. set oven to 350 degrees f
4. in a large bowl , mix mayonnaise , sour cream and melted butter , garlic powder , seasoned salt and black pepper until well combined
5. mix in green onion and yellow onion
6. add in the cooked cubed potatoes , cubed cheese and ham mix with a large spatula until well combined
7. transfer / spread the mixture to prepared casserole dish
8. at this point you may cover and refrigerate for up to 24 hours until ready to bake
9. bake 25-30 minutes or until hot and bubbly
10. remove from oven and sprinkle the grated cheddar on top
11. return to oven and bake 5-8 minutes more or until the cheese has melted
12. to serve as a cold potato salad
13. make as stated in steps 3-5 reducing the melted butter to 2 tablespoons
14. place in a bowl , cover and refrigerate for at least 4 hours or more before serving
15. delicious !
target.review:
Wish I could give this 10 stars! I've made this 3 times in the past 6 weeks, the first time for the 4th of July celebration. It was wiped-out in minutes!

Then a friend gave us new potatoes from their garden and oh, my Goodness! Heaven in a bowl when I used them for this salad! I use some crumbled bacon, because I didn't have the chicken or ham. You can't go wrong putting bacon in anything, right?

This salad is perfect, as written...don't change anything!

Thanks, Kittencal, for another keeper!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s italian melt in your mouth meatballs

cooking the meatballs in simmering pasta sauce  will not only add so much extra flavor to the sauce the meatballs will be melt-in-your-mouth tender, you may of course oven-bake the meatballs for about 25 minutes,  --- don't be afraid to add in more parmesan cheese and a little more milk, there is no need to measure exactly, this recipe is pretty much foolproof, leftover cooked meatballs make a wonderful pizza topping just slice thinly and freeze until ready to use ----- these also make wonderful juicy burgers shaped into patties-- for more of my tried and true recipes check out my food blog at www.kittencalskitchen.com

1. mix all ingredients together in a large bowl
2. shape into small meatballs
3. drop the meatballs into simmering pasta sauce , do not stir for at least 20 minutes or you will risk breaking the meatballs
4. continue cooking in the simmering sauce for another 20 minutes
5. after the 40 minutes cooking time continue cooking your sauce with the meatballs in for as long as desired
demonstrations.review: PERFECTION, KITTENCAL!   I used half beef & half pork for these and they're wonderful!  Mixed them up this morning and baked them at 350 for 30 minutes, just because I wasn't sure what 'small' size was.  These are a little smaller than a golf ball and I got 40 using a pound of each meat.  All other ingredients were exactly as you'd written.  I've been simmering them all afternoon,  (for meatball sandwiches tonight), in some of my homemade sauce that I had in the freezer, along with some leftover pizza sauce I'd frozen, too.  I couldn't help it...I had to snitch one...uh, two...no...I actually have eaten 4 of these, (so far!), and it's not even suppertime, yet!!  My grandson thinks these are KILLER!!  Thanks, so much for a delicious recipe that I'll use forever!  :)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
most refreshing lemonade you will ever taste    quick   easy

this is the best tasting, most satisfying, easiest homemade lemonade you will ever drink. what could be more satisfying on a hot summer day than the cool, brisk refreshing taste of lemonade? this is so easy with the help of a citrus juicer to juice the lemons.

1. combine lemon juice , sugar and club soda stirring well to dissolve sugar
2. add sliced lemon to pitcher
3. chill
4. enjoy !
demonstrations.review: A true 5-STAR beverage for 4th of July...or any hot day for that matter!  I don't like it when people change a recipe, then rate it negatively, but I did change it, only by adding Sprite, instead of club soda.   It was a winner, as I'm sure it would be with the club soda, too!  Thanks for a 'keeper' of a recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
m   m dream bars

these are yummy! the original recipe called for red and green christmas m&ms, but i see no reason to relegate this delicious treat to just the holidays. :)

1. combine oatmeal , brown sugar , flour , coconut , baking soda , and salt
2. add melted butter and stir until moist
3. reserve 1 1 / 2 cups and press remaining crumbs into a greased 13x9-inch baking pan
4. bake 12 minutes at 375f
5. combine milk and peanut butter
6. carefully spread over baked crust
7. sprinkle on m&m's and chocolate chips
8. sprinkle reserved crumbs over chocolate pieces and lightly press crumbs down
9. bake 20 minutes , or until golden brown
10. cool completely before cutting
demonstrations.review: My 9-year-old grandson comes to my house every Monday and loves to bake. He measures and mixes everything out by himself and does a fantastic job. So, when I saw this recipe and showed it to him, he wanted to try it. LUCKY FOR US! These were so-o-o-o good! We cut them into small 1" squares and they were just the right size, because they are so rich. (Of course, we'd want 2 or 3 at a time, but,... oh, well.....!) This recipe's DEFINITELY A KEEPER!! Kudos and many thanks to GaylaJ for sharing this great recipe!

target.recipe_text:
southern living s tarragon cream chicken

this is my go-to recipe when company is coming. everyone who tries this chicken thinks it is absolutely delicious. i just love it! it is my favorite recipe to eat and to make. i serve it with a light salad, my garlic butter new potatoes (also posted), and some lightly roasted asparagus. i have also used boneless, skinless chicken thighs in the past instead of the chicken breasts. this adds great flavor. i believe i made 5-6 thighs. i took this recipe from southern living magazine, and it is also in their ultimate quick and easy cookbook. enjoy!

1. place chicken between two sheets of heavy-duty plastic wrap
2. flatten to 1 / 4 inch thickness , using a meat mallet or rolling pin
3. combine 1 / 2 teaspoons each of salt and white pepper
4. sprinkle over both sides of flattened chicken
5. melt butter in a large nonstick skillet over medium-high heat
6. add chicken
7. cook five minutes on each side or until done
8. remove from skillet , and cover with aluminum foil to keep warm
9. add lemon juice to the skillet , and cook over for thirty seconds , stirring to loosen particles from the bottom of the skillet
10. add cream and next five ingredients
11. bring to a boil
12. cook , stirring constantly , 4 minutes or until the sauce is slightly thickened
13. i always place the chicken on a serving plate , and then pour the sauce over the chicken
14. i then garnish with lemon slices and tarragon sprigs
15. enjoy !
target.review: Oh yeah, the sauce is divine. I was swiping the last of it off my plate with my finger and licking it.  It's that tasty. I enjoyed it with a nice Australian Chardonnay.  Thanks for this.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
vanilla  buttercream frosting  from sprinkles cupcakes

my sister got this buttercream frosting off the box of a sprinkles cupcake mix, made famous by oprah.  my sister said this was amazing.  update:  i have finally gotten around to making this myself.  i will say, that i don't like my desserts overly sweet and. though this was very good, i think i would probably decrease the amount of sugar for my personal taste.  i'm glad everyone else has liked it as-is, though.  :)

1. in a bowl add sugar then add butter
2. beat till blended
3. next add salt
4. then add the milk and vanilla and beat for an additional 3 to 5 minutes or until smooth and creamy
demonstrations.review: very nice, creamy frosting!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
roasted garlic herb new potatoes

tender and savory with garlic. a fine accompaniment to roasts.

1. preheat oven to 375 degrees f
2. fill a large pot with salted water and bring to a boil
3. add potatoes and garlic and bring back to a boil
4. reduce heat and cook for 10 minutes
5. drain well
6. arrange the potatoes and garlic on a baking pan and toss with the olive oil
7. sprinkle with the thyme , salt , and pepper
8. place in the preheated oven and bake for 20-25 minutes or until the potatoes are tender and cooked through
9. place on a serving platter or dish and garnish with parsley ,
demonstrations.review: I never do well with roasted potatoes, but these turned out nicely.  Unfortunately, my family doesn't care for roasted potatoes at all. Oh well!  I baked these maybe 10 minutes longer and I think it was a good choice.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
red velvet cupcakes

a beautiful cupcake for christmas -- or valentine's day.  the cake has become almost traditional for the upcoming season and now here is an individual-sized serving to highlight a dessert tray.  the recipe came from a book of cupcake recipes and decorating ideas.  i'm sorry to say i know neither the name of the book nor the author but am grateful to have gotten such a great recipe!  note that the recipe for a suggested frosting is included at the end of the recipe, but any white frosting of your choice may be used.
edited to add:  the recipe comes from the book "hey there, cupcake!" by clare crespo.  it contains lots of decorating ideas.

1. preheat the oven to 350 degrees
2. grease 12 cupcake cups or line with paper liners
3. cream butter and sugar until fluffy
4. add eggs and blend well
5. make a paste of cocoa and food coloring and add to the butter mixture
6. sift flour and salt togethr into this mixture
7. one at a time , add the following ingredients: buttermilk , vanilla , and water
8. in a small bowl , combine the vinegar and the baking soda
9. fold it into the cake batter
10. make sure it's incorporated , but don't beat it
11. pour the batter into the cupcake cups
12. bake for 15 to 20 minutes , until the cake springs back when touched
13. remove from oven and let cool for about 10 minutes , then turn out of pan and onto a rack to finish cooling completely
14. cream cheese frosting: blend together the following: 1 package cream cheese , softened , 1 / 2 cup unsalted butter , softened , 1-1 / 2 cups powdered sugar , and 1 teaspoon vanilla extract
15. blend until smooth
demonstrations.review: I've made many cupcakes before, but I usually stick to chocolate or vanilla.  I made these for a friend's birthday because she loves red velvet.  It was a little more involved than a regular cupcake recipe, but the results were fantastic.  The cake had great texture and was deliciously moist.  They were a hit at the party!  I made a double batch of the frosting and added extra confectioner sugar, which I will recommend to anyone who likes to pile the frosting high.

target.recipe_text:
chewy chocolate chip oatmeal cookies

this is the best oatmeal cookie i have ever tasted and it is my family's favorite. add your favorite spicy if you like. great gift for christmas too!

1. preheat the oven to 325f
2. in a large bowl , sift together flour , baking soda and salt
3. set aside
4. in another another bowl , cream together butter , brown sugar and white sugar until smooth
5. beat in eggs one at a time , then stir in vanilla
6. stir dry ingredients in the cream mixture until just blended
7. mix in quick oats , walnuts and chocolate chips
8. drop by heaping spoonfuls onto ungreased baking sheet
9. bake for 13 minutes in the preheated oven
10. allow cookies to cool on baking sheet for 5 minutes before transferring to a wire rack to cool completely
target.review: This is a great cookie! Thanks, Darshirl, for posting this recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
whole wheat banana nut bread

this is a really quick and easy recipe. most of all its healthy, moist and tasty. the recipe has been in the family as long as i can remember. not really sure where it came from. kids still ask for it when they're coming home from college on the weekend.

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees
2. in a large bowl cream butter and sugar together until very light and creamy
3. beat in egg
4. add vanilla extract and blend , set aside
5. into a medium bowl or on a sheet of wax paper sift together whole wheat , unbleached flours and baking soda
6. in a small bowl blend buttermilk and mashed banana
7. add dry ingredients alternately with the banana mixture to the butter mixture
8. stirring just enought to combine well
9. stir in walnuts and chocolate chips , raisins if you like
10. turn into a greased and floured 9 x 5 loaf pan or bundt cake pan
11. bake for 50-55 minutes on middle rack
12. until tooth pick comes out clean
13. let cool in pan for 5- 10 minutes
14. remove from pan and cool on rack
15. after it is cooled just a light dusting with icing sugar if you like
demonstrations.review: This is a keeper. Thanks for the recipe, Marlitt. You can make it even more healthy by substituting unsweetened applesauce for the butter, dropping the calories per serving down to around 200 calories.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
southern black eyed peas

i love black-eyed peas! i'd much rather have fresh peas than dried, but i'll take them anyway i can get them. i don't remember where i found this recipe, but i really like it.  the original recipe used salt pork, but i use bacon. give me a bowl of these peas, a dash of tabasco, a slab of hot-from-the-oven cornbread, some green onions and tomato slices then stand out of the way!

1. in a 5 quart dutch oven , cook bacon until crisp
2. set aside to drain on paper towels
3. cook onion , celery and garlic in bacon drippings until tender
4. add broth , salt , pepper and peas
5. bring to a boil and skim top if necessary
6. lower heat to simmer
7. crumble bacon and add to peas
8. adjust seasonings to taste , cover and simmer until peas are tender
demonstrations.review: Thank you for this recipe. It was very good. I've only had black-eyed peas once when I was 3 or 4  and always wanted to try to make my own. I think I will definitely try salt pork or ham the next time, rather than bacon. Thanks again!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
yummy crunchy apple pie

great pie!

1. use foil on bottom of oven rather than a cookie sheet under pie pan
2. prepare pastry for single-crust pie
3. place in pie plate and trim and crimp the edge
4. refrigerate 30 minute loosely covered with plastic wrap
5. in a large mixing bowl , stir together the sugar , flour , cinnamon , nutmeg , allspice , and salt
6. add apple slices and gently toss until they are coated well
7. transfer mixture to pie
8. for crumb topping: stir together brown sugar , flour , and oats
9. using a pastry blender , cut in the butter until topping resembles coarse crumbs
10. sprinkle over apple mixture in pie
11. to prevent over-browning while baking , cover edge of pie with foil
12. bake at 375 degrees fahrenheit for 25 minutes
13. remove foil and bake 25 to 30 minutes more , or until top is golden
14. remove from oven
15. cool on wire rack about an hour and serve !
demonstrations.review: An absolute hit! Thanks, Wendy!

target.recipe_text:
western macaroni

this is a very inexpensive, easy, and well-rounded dish sure to feed the heartiest of appetites. very bachelor and college-student friendly!:) i used to absolutley love this dish when i was younger (before i decided to forgo the red-meat thing), but my family still enjoys it often.(i'm thinking of trying it with chicken?!?!) let me know how it turns out if you do!!

1. prepare macaroni and cheese according to pkg
2. directions
3. brown meat , green pepper , and onion
4. cook until veggies are tender and meat is cooked through
5. stir in corn , tomato paste , water , salt , and pepper
6. add prepared macaroni and cheese dinner and mix well
7. simmer 10-15 minutes
target.review: I added bacon bits and substituted tomato sauce for tomato paste. It's a good dish but the flavors aren't as distinct as I normally like. However, it is inexpensive and easy to make.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
hamburger quickie

quick and very easy

1. fry hamburger with onions until browned
2. add tomato soup and stewed tomatoes
3. mix in the cooked macaroni
demonstrations.review: I added the remainder of a bag of frozen green beans which went over well.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
shepherd s cheddar pie

nan

1. make topping by combining 1 / 2 can condensed soup with hot mashed potatoes
2. set aside
3. in non-stick frypan , brown ground beef at medium-high heat until coo ked through
4. drain excess fat
5. meanwhile , cook mixed vegetables according to package directions
6. add to frypan and stir into beef with remaining soup , worcestershire sauce and pepper
7. spoon meat mixture into 8 x 8 x 2 in
8. square baking pan
9. spread reserved potato mixture evenly over surface
10. bake at 400 f for 20 minutes or until topping is light golden
demonstrations.review: I lined the pan with white bread that toasted in the oven and helped soak up some of the oils from the heated cheese soup. I also sprinkled the top with parmesan before baking.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
hamburger skillet supper

this is something new that our family tried that i got from a magazine. we were surprised that we would all like it so much! it doesn't take very much time at all so it is great when time is limited.

1. in a skillet , cook beef until no longer pink
2. drain
3. add noodles with contents of seasoning packet and water
4. bring to a boil
5. cook for 3 minutes or until noodles are tender
6. add the veggies and cook until tender , about 3 minutes as well
7. makes about 4 servings
8. here is another way to do it: cook the beef as stated previously
9. during this time , heat up a saucepan of water to cook the ramen noodles in
10. rather than just using 1 packet , use 2 packets of the beef flavor ramen noodles
11. when cooking the noodles , cook them without the flavoring
12. during this time , add the veggies to the meat and continue to cook
13. as the veggies become cooked , add the two packets of flavoring to the beef-veggie mixture
14. the ramen noodles don't take long to cook , so be sure to watch them
15. when they are done , drain them , and add them to the beef-veggie mixture
16. the completed dish will have more flavor , and more noodles for the noodle lovers ! enjoy !
demonstrations.review: I used two packages of noodles. I also added the seasoning packets and a tsp. of worcestershire sauce to the meat and cooked the noodles separatly.

target.recipe_text:
japanese mum s chicken

we have a japanese girl, tomoko, living with us, and tonight she and i cooked a japanese dinner for us and her friends. she phoned her mum,toshiko, in japan for this, as it's her favourite recipe, and i wanted to share it here. it's simple and so good, and tomoko, who is only 16, did such a good job of cooking this, then translating the recipe to english for me.

*the liquid will thicken to a glaze if you are patient. it just takes a bit of time. if you feel your chicken is cooked (and going to overcook) remove it before going on to reduce the liquid. same thing, if you must use breast meat, remove it (so it doesn't dry out) and continue reducing the liquid . if you do it this way rather than thickening with cornstarch you will get a richer glaze and not need to add stock or broth instead of the water. it just takes patience. and note: a glaze is sticky and coats the meat, this is not a sauce.

1. place all the ingredients in a saucepan over a high heat
2. bring to the boil , then reduce to a simmer for about 20 minutes
3. remove any scum that rises to the surface
4. increase the heat , turning the drumsticks frequently in the liquid , and cook until the liquid has reduced to a sticky glaze
5. arrange the chicken on a serving platter , remove the garlic clove and chili from the liquid , and spoon the glaze over
target.review: Very happy with this recipe!  I simmered the sauce for 15 minutes first.  In a separate pan, I browned a few chicken breasts coated in flour for 5 minutes, then poured the sauce on them and continued cooking.  I added broccoli and water chestnuts about 2 minutes before I turned the heat off.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
black bean chilaquile

chilaquile is colorful, jumping with flavor, and filling to boot!  this is from the moosewood low fat favorites cookbook!

1. preheat the oven to 350f
2. saut the onions in the oil for about 8 minutes , until translucent
3. stir in the tomatoes , corn , black beans , lime juice , salt , and pepper and continue to saut for another 5 to 10 minutes , until just heated through
4. meanwhile , in another saucepan , blanch the greens in boiling water to cover for 1 to 3 minutes , until just wilted but still bright green
5. drain immediately and set aside
6. prepare an 8x8-inch casserole dish or baking pan with a very light coating of oil or cooking spray
7. spread half of the crushed tortilla chips on the bottom
8. spoon the sauted vegetables over the tortilla chips and sprinkle on about two-thirds of the grated cheddar
9. arrange the greens evenly over the cheese and spoon on half of the salsa
10. finish with the rest of the tortilla chips and top with the remaining salsa and cheddar
11. bake for about 35 to 40 minutes , until the cheese is bubbling and beginning to brown
12. serves 4 to 6
13. try serving this with a simple tossed salad , perhaps with avocado
14. try pineapple buttermilk sherbet for dessert
demonstrations.review: I made this a while ago and really liked it.  It took me awhile to find it again so I could make it again and rate it!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
moosewood italian stuffed portabellas

these are good for an everyday supper since they're so easily prepared, yet look no further of you want something elegant enough to present at a dinner party. this dish is nice served on a bed of pasta topped with tomato sauce.

1. preheat the oven to 400 degrees f
2. lightly oil a baking dish
3. carefully brush or wipe off any soil from the mushrooms
4. twist off the stems and discard
5. rinse the mushroom caps and pat dry with a towel
6. in a skillet , warm 2 tbs of the olive oil and saut the onions for about 5 minutes , until they begin to soften
7. add the garlic and peppers and saut for 5 minutes more
8. remove from the heat and set aside
9. in a bowl , mix together the basil , ricotta cheese , mozzarella , parmesan , salt , and bread crumbs
10. stir the sauted vegetables into the cheese mixture
11. brush the portabellos with the remaining tbs of oil and place them gill side up in the prepared baking dish
12. mound cheese mixture in each
13. bake uncovered for 20-25 minutes , until the mushrooms release their juices and the cheese is melted
14. serve hot
demonstrations.review: Thanks very much- I made it exactly as posted and it was excellent.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mashed red potatoes with garlic and parmesan

the potatoes are ready in our garden, and this is the first recipe i reach for! these are so good!!

1. put potatoes and garlic in lg pan
2. cover with water
3. bring to a boil
4. reduce heat and simmer for 25 minutes , until potatoes are tender
5. drain well
6. mash with the butter , milk , and salt
7. stir in the parmesan cheese
demonstrations.review: I added sour cream like the others suggested and these turns out wonderful.

target.recipe_text:
big and yummy choc chip cookies

i know, i know, there are tons of chocolate chip cookies on this site, but this one is the first that came out perfect and bakery-style like for me so i really think it deserves to be posted. i hope you agree with me! :)

1. in a big bowl cream butter , nutella and sugar for about 5 minutes
2. add the egg and beat it inches
3. in a second bowl combine baking powder , flour and vanilla bean
4. add this to the wet mixture and mix to combine
5. fold in both types of chocolate chunks
6. use your hands to form large round heaps of dough
7. flatten slightly on the baking sheet
8. these will spread , so leave enough room between them
9. bake in the preheated oven at 180c / 350f for about 15 minutes
10. take them out when theyre still a bit soft , theyll crisp up while cooling
11. allow to cool on the baking sheet for 2 minutes , then transfer to a wire rack to cool completely
target.review: These were big and fluffy and chocolately! I used banana-chocolate spread from World Market in place of Nutella. I did think they were missing a bit of salt though. Thanks for sharing

demonstrations.recipe_text:
italian tortellini soup vegetarian

cheese-filled tortellini turns this hearty bean and vegetable soup into a family favorite! add other vegetables of your choice. you can add vegetarian sausage to this if you wish! :) from cambell's.

1. place the carrots , onion , celery , garlic , thyme and 2 cups of the broth in a 6-quart saucepot
2. heat to a boil
3. reduce the heat to low
4. cover and cook for 10 minutes or until the onion is tender
5. add the remaining broth , zucchini , tomatoes , tortellini and beans
6. heat to a boil
7. reduce the heat to low
8. cover and cook for 15 minutes or until the tortellini is tender
9. serve with grated parmesan cheese if desired
demonstrations.review: This was great! I very hearty and delicious dinner. It filled up the whole house with its savory aroma while cooking. The only change i would make is that it needed about twice as much broth (and therefore spices) as it called for. After cooking for the full 30min, most of the broth just boiled away and I kept on having to add more. Once I did though, it was perfect!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
one pot veggie pasta

clipped from an old issue of parade magazine, this easy and healthy pasta dish truly is cooked all in one pot!

1. bring a large pot of water to a boil
2. add linguine and boil 7 minutes , stirring occasionally
3. gradually , so that the water doesn't stop boiling , add broccoli and asparagus
4. cook 2 minutes more
5. gradually add the zucchini , snow peas , and green peas
6. cook 3 minutes longer
7. during this final cooking time , put the half & half , parmesan , butter , salt , and pepper in a large serving bowl
8. drain pasta and veggies well and immediately pour into the serving bowl
9. toss to coat all with cream mixture
10. serve at once
demonstrations.review: What I loved about this dish was how easy it was, that it only required one pot and that there were so many veggies! That being said, I found it a tad bit bland and ended up adding extra of everything that went in the sauce (plus some garlic). Also, for future chefs - this makes a lot of pasta! Make sure to use a big pot and have lots of hungry mouths ready and waiting :) Thanks for the post!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
lentil spaghetti sauce

a delicious low-fat vegetarian (if not using beef broth) pasta sauce. from the dietitians of canada.

1. in a large saucepan cook onion and garlic in oil for about 5 minutes , or until tender
2. add lentils and water
3. cover and cook on low heat until lentils are tender
4. add tomato paste , 3 / 4 cup water and seasonings
5. cover and cook until lentils are soft and mushy
6. serve over cooked spaghetti
7. if desired , sprinkle with grated parmesan cheese
demonstrations.review: Delicious - protein pasta! I used veggie broth and added a fresh diced tomato. I rarely find this to be true but the seasoning on this was perfect!

target.recipe_text:
creamy cajun chicken pasta

n'awlin's style of chicken with an updated alfredo sauce.

1. place chicken and cajun seasoning in a bowl and toss to coat
2. in a large skillet over medium heat , saut chicken in butter or margarine until chicken is tender , about 5 to 7 minutes
3. reduce heat add green onion , heavy cream , tomatoes , basil , salt , garlic powder , black pepper and heat through
4. pour over hot linguine and toss with parmesan cheese
target.review: Who knew something this easy could be so good?? We added andouille sausage which I think really gave it some great flavor.  Put only 1 tsp Tony Sach's in because we have toddlers, but then added about 1 tsp to our own after the kids were served.  We've made it with half & half as well as with heavy cream and both work great.  Thought the sauce was a little thin, so I added some corn starch---WOULD NOT recommend that.  It was too thick after putting in the parmesan which thickened it as well, so I ended up adding more cream.  GREAT recipe.  Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
weight watchers 1pt pancake best ever

hey guys! well, after lots of searching i finally found a recipe for a large, yummy, fluffy, high fiber, filling 1 pt pancake! here is the recipe:

whole wheat apple-cinna pancakes
this recipe was found at: 
http://www.healthdiscovery.net/forums/showthread.php?t=122138 
it's a great recipe which really does produce fluffy delicious 1pt pancakes

1. mix all ingredients until smooth
2. if it is too thick for you , add a tablespoon of water at a time until desired consistency
3. heat a large skillet or griddle that has been sprayed with non-stick butter flavored cooking spray
4. spoon two good sized heaping tablespoon fulls of the batter into the skillet per pancake and spread out slightly
5. let cook like a regular pancake and then flip , allowing to cook another minuet or so
6. serve !
7. dietary info:
8. per pancake: 67 calories
9. 2 gm fiber
10. trace fat
11. for three pancakes: 202 calories
12. 6 gm fiber , 1 gm fat
demonstrations.review: Awesome!  These are better than regular pancakes!  We loved the cinnamon flavor and they were filling too!  Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
weight watchers shepherd s pie

seasoned meat and vegetables are nestled under creamy mashed potatoes and then baked to form a sensational, savory pie.  5 points per serving.

1. preheat oven to 400f
2. place potatoes in a large saucepan and pour in enough water to cover potatoes
3. set pan over high heat and bring to a boil
4. reduce heat to medium and simmer 10 minutes , until potatoes are fork-tender
5. drain potatoes , transfer to a large bowl and add sour cream and margarine
6. mash until smooth , season to taste with salt and set aside
7. meanwhile , heat oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat
8. add onion , carrots and celery
9. cook until soft , about 3 minutes
10. add turkey and cook until browned , breaking up the meat as it cooks , about 5 minutes
11. add flour , rosemary , thyme , salt and pepper
12. stir to coat
13. add broth and bring to a simmer
14. simmer until mixture thickens , about 3 minutes
15. transfer turkey mixture to a 9-inch , deep-dish pie plate
16. spread mashed potatoes over top and using the back of a spoon , make decorative swirls over the top
17. bake until potatoes are golden , about 30 minutes
18. slice into 6 pieces and serve
demonstrations.review: Very good recipe, but next time I'd use alot less rosemary.  It was overpowering.  I think next time I'd use 1/2 a can of tomatoes and french style green beans instead of carrots and celery.  I cut this recipe in half and it still made a huge amount.  Very good!  Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s tuna melt sandwich

trust me you will be craving this often once you try it! --- you may use regular white salt but the seasoned salt is better, also use as much cheese and tomato slices as desired, i sometimes add in some chopped sweet yum yum pickles to the tuna filling too --- low-fat mayonnaise and cheese may be used :)

1. set oven to broiler heat
2. in a bowl mix tuna , mayo , lemon juice celery , green onions and parsley
3. mix well
4. add in seasoned salt and lemon pepper to taste
5. place the bread slices on a baking sheet and broil for 1 minute or until lightly toasted
6. remove from heat , divide and spread the tuna mixture on top of each bread slice
7. place one cheese slice over the tuna , then one tomato slice then another slice of cheese on top
8. return the layered bread to oven and broil for about 3 minutes , or until the cheese is melted
demonstrations.review: Another awesome recipe!  Love it.  I didn't have celery, but I think that would really make the recipe.  I used 2 pieces of bread instead of open-faced.  Sooo good!  Thanks again Kittencal!

target.recipe_text:
baked grilled cheese

my family loves grilled cheese so when they asked for it i wanted to try something new.  this was the best grilled cheese, nice crunchy bread with melted cheese.  i had to post this so i wouldn't forget it.  family loved it served with homemade milkshakes and fries. this is a great way to make a bunch at one time and the clean-up was nothing. ;)

1. preheat oven to 450f
2. lightly butter one side of each slice of bread
3. place on a cookie sheet butter side down
4. place 2 slices cheese on each piece of bread
5. place other piece of bread on top , lightly butter side up
6. bake for approximately 5 minutes
7. then flip each sandwich over
8. bake additional 3-4 minute until done
target.review: I made these last night and they were a huge success! For people who thought they didn't like grilled cheese, these will definitely change their mind. great idea for an old favorite.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
rotisserie vinaigrette chicken salad

a simple and delicious chicken salad you can put together in no time. the flavors of the rotisserie chicken mingled with the vinaigrette dressing and veggies are delightful. this recipe makes extra dressing, so keep some in the fridge for another salad. i always make extra and this recipe accounts for that ;)

1. vinaigrette:
2. place all the ingredients in a screw-top jar and shake to combine
3. taste and adjust the seasonings
4. in a large bowl toss romaine lettuce , chicken , cucumber , tomatoes , onion , celery and
5. dressing until evenly coated
6. refrigerate at least 30 minutes
demonstrations.review: This is a great salad. Not complicated, just throw it together in minutes. Quick and easy. The dressing does make this salad pop. It makes alot and I enjoyed having the left over dressing for the next day. I thought the dressing was great and would make it to have on hand in the refrigerator. I would make this salad again! Good luck.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
thai style burgers

------a medley of thai flavorings livens up ordinary burgers and makes them extraordinary. lovely and spicy and great topped with your choice of lettuce, tomato slices, basil leaves, cilantro, mint, thai peanut sauce, mayonnaise, cucumber slices, and garlic or chile paste.------

1. in small bowl , whisk together all spice mixture ingredients
2. in large bowl , stir together ground beef , carrots , onion , chiles , bell pepper and salt
3. add spice mixture
4. stir until well-combined
5. stir in egg and bread crumbs
6. shape mixture into 8 patties
7. to bbq when the coals are at medium temperature place the burgers on the barbecue close to the coals and cook for about 3-4 minutes on each side
8. brush slices of crusty bread with a little oil and place on barbecue to toast
9. or , heat large nonstick skillet over medium-high heat until hot
10. add 1 tablespoon of the oil
11. heat until hot
12. add 4 of the patties
13. cover and cook 8 to 10 minutes or until browned and no longer pink in center , turning once
14. repeat with remaining burgers , adding remaining 1 tablespoon oil
15. serve in buns
16. top with favorite condiments
demonstrations.review: I'm not a huge fan of Thai spice but wanted to try something different than the ordinary hamburgers. This had subtle flavors which made it a delicious difference. My son and I really enjoyed these.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
brandied chicken wings

these chicken wings really perk up when they're seasoned with a hint of brandy. they are by far the best chicken wings i've ever tasted.

1. in saucepan melt butter and mustard
2. add brown sugar until dissolved
3. add soy , brandy , and stir until warm and thoroughly blended
4. place chicken in a 9 x 12 pan
5. pour mixture over drummettes , and bake until brown at 275 for 3-4 hours
6. baste about every 45 minutes
demonstrations.review: Wow, these are the best chicken wings I've ever tasted! Bravo on such a wonderful recipe. I'll make these again for sure. The chicken was so tender they just melted in your mounth. thanks for sharing.

target.recipe_text:
breaded pork chops   from the oven

these chops are tender and juicy with a nice crisp coating. you'll like these!

1. preheat oven to 375 degrees f
2. beat egg with evaporated milk
