demonstrations.review: So easy and wonderful! I used Turkey Italian Sausage and my 6 year old and I loved it.

target.recipe_text:
balsamic pork chops

this is out of a weight watcher's cookbook.

1. sprinkle both sides of pork chops with lemon / herb seasoning
2. coat a non-stick skillet with cooking spray and place over medium-high heat until hot
3. add chops and cook for 3-4 minutes on each side or until lightly browned and cooked through
4. remove chops from skillet and keep warm
5. wipe drippings from skillet with paper towel
6. combine vinegar and broth in skillet
7. cook over medium-high heat until mixture is reduced to a thin sauce , stirring occasionally
8. spoon sauce over chops
target.review: I'm sorry I can't give this a higher ratig.  But, the taste of the vinegar was too overwhelming, adn I am a balsamic vinegar fan.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
yummy baked mac   cheese

this recipe is a better adaptation of the "perfect" macaroni and cheese recipe from the ms website. to save $$, i get the various cheese "ends" that most grocery deli counters offer at a discount. the greater the variety of cheeses used, the better this recipe tastes!

1. preheat oven to 350f coat a casserole dish with butter or olive oil spray
2. melt the butter in a large saucepan , stir in flour gradually and whisk until smooth
3. cook 1 minute
4. whisk in the warm milk & cook until thickened , stirring constantly
5. remove from heat and stir in all the spices and the 4 cups cheese
6. not the parmesan
7. stir until all cheese is melted
8. stir in the cooked macaroni until well coated with sauce
9. pour mixture into buttered casserole
10. sprinkle parmesan cheese over top
11. bake for 30 minutes , or until hot & bubbly with slightly browned edges
demonstrations.review: I had real high expectations for this dish.  All of the ingredients together sounded like it would make an amazing tasting mac & cheese.  Not so much.  It was very creamy, but kind of bland. But, the nutmeg taste was very visible. Which surprised me (and my family).  I used mild cheddar and Swiss cheese as suggested, for the cheese sauce and then added the Parmesan cheese to the top. I think I will stick to my tried and true recipe from my Betty Crocker cookbook. Made for PAC Spring 2010.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
brides bars

nooo...i don't think you need to be a bride to eat these bars!! i got this recipe on "some other website" (not sure where). sounds good!! quick and easy!! variations: chocolate cake mix/cherry pie filling, spice cake mix/apple pie filling, banana cake mix/blueberry pie filling, strawberry cake mix/stawberry pie filling.

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. in large mixing bowl , combine mix , eggs , filling and nuts
3. spread this mixture on a greased jelly-roll pan
4. bake 30 minutes
5. frosting: combine ingredients in bowl and spread over cooled cake
6. cut into bars
demonstrations.review: These were so easy to make!  I had a house full of teenage boys, with nothing to offer them.  Found this recipe, and 1/2 hour later I had these moist little bars! They were almost all gone by the end of the night! I used frozen blueberries, 3 eggs and yellow cake mix.  Thank you for sharing your recipe, you saved the day! :-)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
e z banana creme bundt cake

you will love this banana pecan bundt cake made easy with cake mix. yummy!

1. in large mixing bowl , mash bananas
2. add rest of ingredients , except pecans and mix for 2 minutes at medium speed of mixer
3. add chopped pecans
4. pour into greased and floured bundt pan
5. bake at 350 degrees for 60 minutes
6. cool in pan for 15 minutes
7. remove from pan and let cool
8. sprinkle with powdered sugar before serving
demonstrations.review: This cake is so easy to put together and so moist!  I used 3 medium banana's , vanilla pudding and walnuts. I think using 3 banana's made up for not using banana pudding, because this definitely was not lacking in banana flavor! I also baked it in a 9 X 13 pan for 50 minutes (Since I didn't use a bundt cake pan I wasn't sure how long to bake it for, so I set the timer to 35 minutes and kept increasing the time by 5 minutes), and then sprinkled it with powdered sugar.  I will be making this again when I have those ripe banana's sitting on my counter begging to be eaten!  Thank you for sharing your recipe.

target.recipe_text:
chewy gingersnaps sparkle cookies

these cookies are chewy, delicious and easy to make.  they stay fresh for quite a long time and also aren't too sweet.  this recipe does not double well.

1. in a large bowl , cream butter and sugar together using a hand mixer
2. add other wet ingredients and mix
3. add dry ingredients and mix
4. dough should be easy to handle and not sticky
5. add a little more flour if necessary
6. the dough should not be dry
7. shape dough into one inch balls and roll in white sugar
8. bake on an ungreased cookie sheet at 350 degrees for about 10 minutes
9. remove immediately from cookie sheet onto cooling rack
10. enjoy !
target.review: This is hands down the best ginger cookie recipe on recipezaar!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
the only chocolate cake recipe you ll ever need   devil s food

this chocolate cake is absolutely thee best we have ever had. it is so moist and rich, i never make anything else (unless i am short on time :) the frosting recipe included goes perfectly with this cake, but you can use any frosting you like. try this once and you'll see why i call it "the only chocolate cake recipe you'll ever need"!!  adding 2/18/06: i want to note that i recently used sweetened whipped heavy cream with vanilla and it was just as fabulous as the frosting recipe listed, plus much easier.  i also used hazelnut coffee in the cake and it added even more of a little extra something!

1. preheat oven to 325f
2. in a large mixing bowl , sift together dry ingredients
3. add oil , coffee and milk and mix at medium speed for 2 minutes
4. add eggs and vanilla and beat 2 more minutes
5. expect batter to be thin
6. pour into a 9" x 13" greased and floured pan or 2- 9" round pans
7. bake 9 x 13 pan for about 45 minutes or 9" pans for about 30 minutes
8. cool in pans for about 15 minutes and then cool completely on racks
9. while cake is cooling make the icing: combine the milk and flour in a saucepan and cook over low heat until thick , whisking constantly
10. cover and refrigerate until chilled
11. in a medium bowl , beat butter , shortening , sugar and vanilla until creamy
12. add chilled milk and flour mixture and beat for 10 minutes
13. frost cooled cake and enjoy ! the frosting sounds intimidating , but it is worth it ! by the way , for some reason , we prefer this cake chilled , right out of the refrigerator
14. the rich chocolate and cool frosting just seem to taste best this way
demonstrations.review: This cake was amazing! Seriously, this is the best chocolate cake I've ever eaten. The frosting turned out more like a runny icing though. Maybe it was because I used skim milk?

demonstrations.recipe_text:
spanish class enchiladas

ok, these are nowhere near authentic, but on "fiesta days" in mrs. suarez's class, she would always bring these.

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. pour a bit of the enchilada sauce in the bottom of a 9x13 baking pan to coat the bottom
3. scoop some beans straight from the can onto a flour tortilla in a line from top to bottom
4. sprinkle a bit of cheese on the beans
5. fold filled tortilla into a roll shape and place into the baking dish
6. repeat this method until baking dish is full
7. pour the enchilada sauce all over the rolled up enchiladas
8. sprinkle any remaining cheese on top
9. bake for 20 minutes , or until heated through , and cheese is melted
10. my teacher cut them all in small pieces after they were finished baking to ensure everyone got a piece , but you don't have to !
11. come mucho !
demonstrations.review: Very easy and quick. Great for a night when you are short on time. Everyone in my family loved them!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
really good vegetarian meatloaf  really

high in fiber and protein, low in fat, easy and really yummy! i've always thought meatloaf looks and smells so delicious and savory so, as a vegetarian, i decided to make a no-meat version! this is basically our favorite meatloaf recipe but with cooked mashed lentils instead of ground meat. the result is a very tasty dinner!

1. add salt to water and boil in a saucepan
2. add lentils and simmer covered 25-30 minutes , until lentils are soft and most of water is evaporated
3. remove from fire
4. drain and partially mash lentils
5. scrape into mixing bowl and allow to cool slightly
6. stir in onion , oats and cheese until mixed
7. add egg , tomato sauce , garlic , basil , parsley , seasoning salt and pepper
8. mix well
9. spoon into loaf pan that has been generously sprayed with pam or well-greased
10. smooth top with back of spoon
11. bake at 350 degrees for 30- 45 minutes until top of loaf is dry , firm and golden brown
12. cool in pan on rack for about 10 minutes
13. run a sharp knife around edges of pan then turn out loaf onto serving platter
demonstrations.review: I was skeptical, but you're right.. it was REALLY good! Even my picky eater loved it. Thanks! (I followed the recipe exactly)

target.recipe_text:
the best rice pudding

left over rice never had it so good ! this creamy pudding is the perfect way to use up the extra white rice from chinese take-out or from tonight's supper, and delicious enough to make you cook some up fresh, just so you can have this for dessert! tastes great warm or cold--enjoy!!

1. in large bowl , combine sugar , salt , cornstarch and nutmeg
2. add milk , egg yolks , and vanilla , using wire whisk to beat until smooth
3. add cooked rice , and pour into a 1 and 1 / 2 quart baking dish--you can also use a 9 x 9 square baking dish , but you'll need to decrease the cooking time by at least 15 minutes , if not more , so check carefully after the first hour
4. place baking dish into larger pan , and pour hot water into outer pan to create a 1 inch deep water bath
5. bake at 350 degrees , stirring occasionally , for 1 1 / 2 hours , or until pudding is creamy and milk is absorbed
target.review: OMG!!! This was amazing!!! The smell while cooking was unbelievable, I couldn't wait for it to be done!!  I added 1/2 tsp. cinnamon with the dry ingedients. I can't say enough about this recipe.. Excellent!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
holiday gingerbread muffins

a wonderful treat to make for the holidays. if you make gingerbread or fruitcake (heh) you really should try something different like these, you just might love them! 8)

1. preheat oven to 350
2. grease 12 muffin cup / tins
3. in medium bowl , beat the egg , applesauce , oil , molasses and 1 / 2 cup sugar
4. combine dry ingredients in a medium bowl and add to first mixture
5. stir in the water , mixing well
6. fill the muffin cups two-thirds full
7. lightly sprinkle with sugar
8. bake at 350 for 20 to 25 minutes or until done
demonstrations.review: These muffins are AWESOME!!!! I do childcare at home and all my kids LOVE them! I'll definitely be making these year round.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chewy chocolate chip cookies

soft, chewy cookies that have a remarkable 

1. preheat oven to 350f degrees
2. in a large bowl , cream margarine and brown sugar together
3. beat in eggs one at a time
4. add vanilla
5. sift dry ingredients together
6. add to wet mixture
7. stir in chocolate chips
8. do not overmix
9. drop onto a greased cookie sheet
10. bake for 10 to 12 minutes
demonstrations.review:
These cookies are awesome! they're so easy to make, and the kids love them.
I will be making these all the time

demonstrations.recipe_text:
christmas biscotti

a colorful red and green dotted biscotti.. i love it and i don't really like biscotti. my mother said to make her this if nothing else for christmas!

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees
2. butter and flour a baking sheet
3. in a bowl , cream together the butter and sugar until light and fluffy
4. beat in the eggs , vanilla , and orange zest until blended
5. in another bowl , stir together the flour , baking powder , cloves and salt
6. add the flour mixture to the butter mixture and beat until blended
7. stir in cranberries and pistachios
8. divide the dough in half
9. one at a time , place the 2 dough portions on the prepared baking sheet and form each into a log about 1 / 2 inch high , 1 1 / 2 inches wide and 14 inches long
10. space logs at least 2 inches apart
11. bake the logs for 25-30 minutes or until set and light brown
12. transfer to a cutting board and let cool 6-8 minutes
13. reduce the oven temperature to 300 degrees
14. using a very sharp knife , cut the logs in the diagonal into slices 3 / 8 inch thick
15. stand the slices upright on the baking sheet and return the sheet to the oven for 15 minutes to dry the cookies thoroughly
16. transfer to racks to cool
17. store the cookies in an airtight container for up to 4 weeks
demonstrations.review: This has become my favorite biscotti!!  It's easy to make and tastes awesome!! I've had many compliments and requests to make more. Thanks for a great recipe.

target.recipe_text:
puffed wheat squares

i couldn't believe this quick snack was not a part of recipezaar yet!! i grew up loving this and now my kids enjoy it too. i like to vary the sprinkles to match the season. wilton has some awesome festive sprinkles that i like to use. adding the cocoa will produce a chocolate flavour and omitting it will give a caramel flavour.cook and prep time doesn't include cool time.

1. measure puffed wheat into a large bowl
2. melt butter in a saucepan
3. add syrup , sugar , cocoa
4. when mixture begins to boil , boil for 3 minutes and then remove from heat
5. add vanilla
6. pour over puffed wheat and mix well
7. press into a 9x12 inch cake pan
8. scatter sprinkles while still warm and pat down to be sure they will stick
9. cool completely
target.review: I've been making this recipe for years. Always a kid pleaser. Thanks for posting.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
belly buster

this recipe is in about its third or fourth generation, passed down from grandma to mom to me. it became my children's favorite, and now my grandchildren love it. it was a staple in each household, with or without the hamburger. the children named it 

1. this recipe can be made vegetarian , leave out the hamburger and add 2 cups of fresh mixed vegetables , i
2. e
3. broccoli , mushrooms , spinach , carrots , etc
4. cook elbow macaroni "al dente" , according to instructions on box , drain , add to large casserole
5. scramble fry hamburger with spanish onion and garlic , if using , until no longer pink , drain any fat through colander , add drained mixture to casserole
6. add cheese soup , no water , to casserole
7. add tomatoes to casserole
8. add salt and pepper to taste
9. mix thoroughly , in casserole , to evenly distribute ingredients
10. spread grated or sliced cheddar evenly over top of casserole
11. preheat oven to 400 degrees , bake , uncovered for 30 minutes or util bubbling around edges of casserole and cheese topping is melted and slightly browned
12. serves 4-6 or with a salad 8
demonstrations.review: This is a great recipe. I made it with diced tomatoes & added a little Italian spice. This is a good, filling meal. Thanks.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
easiest beef enchiladas ever

best enchilada recipe i've found. we love the spicy, cheesy flavor of these.

1. brown meat and onions in large skillet
2. add 1 cup enchilada sauce and 1 cup cheese
3. mix well
4. put filling along center of each tortilla
5. roll up and place seam side down in a 9x13 pan
6. pour remaining sauce over
7. sprinkle remaining cheese over
8. bake at 350f degrees for about 30 minutes till cheese is bubbly
demonstrations.review: So good & so easy. I used a mild salsa because the kids won't eat spice. Still tasted great. Thanks for another great recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pizza skillet

a quick and easy supper for the working moms and dads out there. this is one the kids will like.

1. cook noodles as package directs , drain
2. set aside
3. in skillet brown beef and onion
4. drain
5. add tomato sauce , spaghetti sauce mix and water
6. bring to a boil
7. cover , reduce heat and simmer for 10 minutes
8. stir in cooked noodles
9. top with cheese , cover and cook on low for 5 minutes , until cheese melts
demonstrations.review: My family really enjoyed this one. It's quick & easy. A real kid pleaser. Thanks

target.recipe_text:
sea scallop and cod pie topped with mashed potatoes

a wonderful comforting irish dish. this is good for those of you that are fasting not eating red meat during lent. try it with shrimp in place of scallops.i made this again using bay scallops because that's all the store had and i enjoy the sea scallops so much more.

1. clean the scallops and cut in half , leave fish whole then simmer in the milk for 15 minutes
2. strain , reduce the liquid cooking for 5 more minutes
3. heat 2 tablespoon of the butter and stir in the flour , cook for about a minute , stirring , then add the milk gradually , stirring all the time to avoid lumps
4. season with salt and white pepper , add the sliced mushrooms and simmer for about 10 minutes longer
5. then add the sherry and finally the scallops and fish
6. when hot , transfer to an oiled 2 quart ovenproof dish and cover with mashed potatoes , making sure they cover the fish right to the edges
7. dot with the remaining butter sprinkle with paprika and bake in a moderate oven , 350f , for 20-30 minutes , or until the top is turning brown
8. 04 / 29 / 04- i made this again adding 2 sliced scallions and 1 / 4 cup green peas to the fish just before topping with potatoes
9. and used vermouth because i ran out of sherry
10. 3 ? 18 / 11 i made it this yer topped with recipe #367251
11. i also did add scallions and green peas
target.review: This recipe was very good.  I made a few changes by using Basa fish and shrimp.  It's great for the cold days of winter.  I will make this again for sure.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
honey garlic meatloaf

i just whipped this together one night with ingredients i happened to have on hand.  it turned out pretty good.

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees
2. grease an 8x10 glass baking dish
3. set aside
4. in a bowl , combine all ingredients then transfer to bakind dish
5. top with desired amount of ketchup
6. bake at 350 for 1
7. 25 hours
8. let stand for 3-5 minutes before serving
demonstrations.review: The meatloaf turned out great. My husband loves meatloaf and this recipe had the differnet twist with the honey and the garlic. I served it with scalloped potatoes.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cheesy drop biscuits

i found this in home magazine several years back. they taste very similar to the cheddar biscuits at red lobster.

1. pre-heat oven to 450f
2. in a large bowl shift together the first 5 ingredients then
3. add both cheeses
4. in a small bowl combine buttermilk and oil
5. add to dry ingredients just until moist
6. drop about 1 / 4 cup full of batter on to a greased baking sheet
7. bake at 450f for about 10-12 minutes or until golden brown
8. serve warm refrigerate any left-over biscuits
demonstrations.review: This recipe was quick and easy.  I made a pot of goulash and wanted something to go with it.  I'm glad I found the recipe. Thanks

demonstrations.recipe_text:
red lobster cheddar bay biscuits

don't you just love the copycat recipes? here's another one, and if you like red lobster's biscuits, this is the recipe for you. they may not be the exact biscuits, but you will not notice a difference in the taste.

1. heat oven to 450
2. combine baking mix , water and grated cheese in a bowl
3. roll out on a lightly floured surface , until 1 inch thick
4. cut biscuits , and place on an ungreased pan
5. melt butter and spices together
6. brush the biscuits with the butter and bake for 8 to 10 minutes
demonstrations.review: Graet recipe easy to prepare.  I did not have bisquick on hand.  But if you click on the ingredient bisquick baking mix and it give you a substuition mix you can make at home.

target.recipe_text:
slow roasted tomatoes

adapted from a martha stewart recipe. these are amazing on their own as a side dish or with pasta.

1. heat oven to 250
2. slice tomatoes thickly , to yield about three slices per tomato
3. place on a baking sheet
4. mix spices and sugar
5. brush tomatoes with olive oil , and sprinkle with a large pinch of seasoning mixture
6. roast the tomatoes for 3 hours
target.review: The taste on these was so delicious! Intense, and sweet at the same time. I did reduce the time, to adjust for my oven. Excellent recipe, Mirakle!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
garlic spinach   bell peppers

a delicious way to get that vitamin k (as well as a bunch of other healthy stuff). this recipe comes from canadian living magazine. enjoy.

1. shred spinach and cook in dry skillet until wilted , transfer to plate
2. heat oil in same skillet
3. cook garlic and pepper for one minute
4. add spinach , red pepper , salt and pepper
5. cook , stirring often , for 4 minutes or until red pepper is tender crisp
demonstrations.review: Also reduced the oil a bit, and had to substitute chili pepper for red pepper flakes - satisfying side, and tasty! Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
asparagus omelet

simple and delicious!

1. cut trimmed asparagus in 1 inch pieces
2. cook in boiling salted water until tender , about 4 minutes
3. drain thoroughly
4. melt 1 tablespoon butter in 8 inch skillet , preferably one with non-stick lining , and saute garlic and mushrooms until done and moisture has evaporated
5. remove from pan and keep warm
6. in a small bowl , combine eggs , milk , salt , basil , and pepper
7. melt remaining butter in skillet until foamy , swirling it around pan to coat evenly
8. when hot enough that a drop of water sizzles when dropped in , pour in egg mixture
9. as eggs cook , periodically lift up cooked edges , tilt pan and let uncooked egg run underneath
10. when eggs are cooked , but surface is still shiny , place asparagus and mushrooms on one side
11. slide out of pan , folding side without vegetables over top
12. serve immediately
13. also good sprinkled with a bit of grated parmesan
demonstrations.review: I made this last weekend, and wowed my audience! Yummy way to start a lazy Sunday....only change I made was to add some salt to the mushrooms as they cooked - drew out the moisture. Great recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mocha crumble bars

these are incredible!!! everyone who ate one at the party said "oh wow!" as soon as they put them in their mouth. bet you can't eat just one!!

1. preheat oven to 350f line a 15x10x1-inch baking pan with foil
2. in a medium bowl , using an electric mixer set on high speed , beat butter and brown sugar until light and creamy
3. on medium speed , beat in egg
4. in another bowl , combine flour , baking soda and 1 / 2 teaspoon cinnamon
5. gradually add flour mixture to butter mixture and mix until dough is smooth
6. stir in oats and walnuts
7. reserve 1 cup dough for topping
8. press remaining dough into bottom of prepared pan
9. in a medium saucepan , heat 1 1 / 2 cups chocolate chips , condensed milk , instant coffee and remaining cinnamon over medium heat
10. stir until smooth
11. spread mixture evenly over the dough in the pan , smoothing the surface with a spatula
12. crumble reserved dough on the top
13. sprinkle with the remaining chocolate chips
14. bake until lightly browned , about 20 minutes
15. cool completely on a wire rack
16. lift foil to remove from pan
17. cut into 2-inch bars
demonstrations.review: Only one thing can possibly improve these - freezing them! They are PHENOMENAL when snuck directly out of the bag that's supposed to keep them out of my snacky reach, and safe in the freezer. These bars are the perfect combination of chocolate, cookie, and the sweetness of condensed milk (although I've been asked if they contain coconut, honey and even caramel!) YUM!

target.recipe_text:
shake a pie crust

my mother always told me the less you handle dough, the better it will be. this is too simple! and it makes the flakiest crusts for pies.

1. put flour , sugar , salt and crisco shortening in a plastic bowl with a lid
2. seal and wink
3. shake until it sounds like sand
4. add water
5. seal and wink
6. shake until it sounds like a rock
7. roll out for your favorite pie or pastries
target.review: We used this recipe for a youth fundraiser -- 22 teenage girls made 90 pies from scratch.  They made the crusts themselves, and several people came up to me afterward asking if the leaders made all the crusts because they were so good! I love this recipe and will never use another!  When I make pot pie, I leave out the sugar and stir some finely grated cheddar cheese into the "sand" before adding the water.  Even my grandmother's pie crust didn't come out this flakey -- it's that amazing!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chocolate bread

an easy chocolate quick bread. not too sweet. tastes better the next day!

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees
2. grease a 9x5x3 loaf pan
3. combine all dry ingredients and set aside
4. stir togethe the egg , butter , milk , sugar , and vanilla
5. add dry ingredients and stir until evenly moistened
6. fold in pecans
7. pour batter into the greased loaf pan
8. smooth out the top
9. bake for 45-50 minutes
10. let bread sit in pan on a cooling rack for 10 minutes
11. remove from pan and let cool completely
demonstrations.review:
After reading the other reviews, I decided to prevent dryness by adding 1/4 cup of applesauce and using canola oil instead of melted butter.  I omitted the nuts, because the kids dont' like them, and threw in a handful of mini chocolate chips.  The bread came out nice, and fairly moist, although I think it would have been terribly dry without the addition of the applesauce and chocolate chips.  I made mini loaves and baked for 35 minutes, which is 5 minutes less than I usually bake quick breads in my mini loaf pans.  Also important to note, is that I am baking this at a high altitude, which usually requires less oil.  If I were baking this at sea level, I would increase the oil / butter to at least 1/3, maybe 1/2 cup. or add 1/3 cup applesauce in addition to the butter called for in the recipe.
Overall, with the additions I made, it was a nice bread with a good flavor.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cranberry oatmeal muffins

these are moist, tasty muffins which are especially nice to serve around christmastime.

1. preheat oven to 400 degrees f
2. soak oats in yogurt or sourcream just enough to make it moist
3. sift dry ingredients into a bowl
4. in a separate bowl , add oil , sugars , and egg
5. beat until well blended
6. gradually fold in dry ingredients
7. add chopped cranberries and orange zest
8. put in greased muffin tins
9. bake for 20 minutes
demonstrations.review: These are really great tasting muffins, especially if you can wait for them to cool.  They are even better cool than when warm from the oven! They do not, however, raise much at all when baking.  They were the flattest topped muffins that I have ever made.  At first that was disappointing, but the flavor made up for it.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cracker barrel old country store biscuits

i like these because they are so quick and easy. even though you use bisquick, they don't come out tasting like bisquick or like baking powder. i always have to double the batch to make sure i get some!

1. preheat oven to 450f
2. mix the bisquick , buttermilk and sugar together in a bowl
3. add the melted butter into the batter
4. stir until a soft dough forms
5. turn out onto a well floured work surface
6. knead 20 times , and don't be afraid to get additional flour into the dough
7. roll 1 / 2 thick , or thicker if you prefer towering biscuits
8. cut out into 2" rounds
9. place close together on an ungreased baking sheet
10. brush tops with melted butter
11. bake for 8 to 10 minutes
12. i usually find 8 minutes is enough
13. when you remove the biscuits from the oven , brush the tops with melted butter again
demonstrations.review: These ar ethe best biscuits I have ever made!! Thanks  for sharing!

target.recipe_text:
gluten free apple cake

delicious moist gluten free cake. it's great with cream cheese icing, powdered sugar, or just plain.plus it stays moist and tasty for days!!i found the cake to be a little bit crumbly, but it was so delicious it didn't matter.i got this recipe from one of bette hagman's recipe books.

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. grease either 9 inch round springform pan , or 8 inch square cake pan , and dust with rice flour
3. in a medium bowl , whisk together the flour mix , xanthan gum , baking soda , baking powder , and cinnamon
4. set aside
5. in the bowl of your mixer , cream the butter for about 1 minute or until softened
6. add both sugars , and beat for about 2 minutes
7. add the eggs , one at a time , and beat until well incorporated
8. blend in the milk
9. then turn mixer to low and add the dry ingredients half at a time , beating after each addition , until they are well absorbed
10. remove the bowl from the stand and gently fold in the shredded apples
11. spoon the batter into the prepared pan and bake for 40-45 minutes , or until toothpick inserted tests clean and the cake pulls away from the edge of the pan
12. if serving from the pan , cool at least 10 minutes before removing
13. dust lightly with icing sugar , if desired
target.review: Excellent!  This apple cake was the lightest, moistest GF cake I've ever made!  It was very tasty without changing anything in the recipe.  I skipped the frosting and topped with thin apple slices.  Yum!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
rhubarb cream cheese bars

this recipe is from my daughter, jodi.  it's a favorite at all of our early summer family gatherings.

1. combine crust ingredients
2. spread in 9x13" pan and bake at 375 for 10 minutes
3. toss together ingredients for rhubarb layer and pour over crust
4. bake for 15 minutes
5. mix together cream cheese and sugar
6. beat eggs in one at a time , pour mixture over rhubarb and bake 25 minutes at 375
7. mix glaze ingredients and spread over bars as soon as they come out of the oven
demonstrations.review: These tasted terrific, were super easy, and I got many compliments!  I made my crust gluten free using crushed GF gingersnaps (store bought), and got many compliments on the ginger/rhubarb combo.  I will definitely use this recipe again when more of my rhubarb is ready to harvest!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
to die for crock pot roast

amazing flavor, and so simple! no salt needed here. in fact, you may wish to use half the ranch dressing mix to cut back on the saltiness. found this crock-pot pot roast recipe on of a website called www.recipegoldmine.com. it's all the rage there, so i thought i'd try it.

1. place beef roast in crock pot
2. mix the dried mixes together in a bowl and sprinkle over the roast
3. pour the water around the roast
4. cook on low for 7-9 hours
5. use onion soup mix instead of ranch
6. add one cup , of red wine
7. add potatoes , carrots , mushrooms , celery and onion 2-3 hours before end
demonstrations.review: Like many others, I reduced the seasoning packets (by about 1/4 each) and it wasn't too salty for my tastes.  I also added extra water to have extra gravy, as well as potatoes and carrots.  The end result was super easy, super quick, and very moist and tasty (though not quite as amazing as all of the hype).  I'd definitely recommend it as a solid standby meal.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
edna s apple crumble  aka  apple crisp

a simple and easy to make but oh so yummy recipe. known as apple crumble in the uk and apple crisp in the us

1. put apples in an 8 or 9 inch square baking dish
2. combine the rest of the ingredients in a separate bowl and mix
3. spread crumble mixture over apples and bake for 35 minutes in a 375f degree oven
4. for an added treat top off with a little english custard
demonstrations.review: Excellent as written!  Apples were perfectly tender and the top perfectly crispy!

target.recipe_text:
puyallup fair scones  fisher scones

first, these scones are quick, easy, great and a perfect project for a beginning baker.  second...you need to know how to pronounce puyallup...i wouldn't want anyone to embarrass themselves!!..."pew-allup", not pooyloop!!...here in western washington the puyallup fair is a huge annual event.  it is one of the largest in the us.  the fair is all about food for me!  and fisher scones are the biggest draw...they sell something like 80,000 a day or something like that!! i have many fond memories of fisher scones. i found this recipe on-line, the poster said that she came across the recipe in a 1930's fisher cookbook her grandmother had.  the original recipe called for raisins, but they no longer make them that way.  the only way to eat these is warm with a big slab of butter and raspberry jam, just like they serve them at the fair!!  store them in an air tight container and they keep well.  they taste nice cold, but way better heated up in the microwave, and don't forget the butter and jam!
fyi...make sure you sift, then measure the flour per instructions.
note:  i took this recipe and made some changes to it and i think this new recipe is even better mrs. g's fair scones recipe #184105...try them both and see what you think!

1. sift and measure the flour
2. re-sift with other dry ingredients
3. work shortening into dry ingredients with the fingers
4. add rasinins to flour-fat mixture and mix thoroughly
5. add milk to mixture
6. turn out on to a floured board and divide into two equal pieces
7. roll or pat each into a round and to the thickness of biscuits
8. cut into wedge shaped pieces like a pie and bake about 15 minutes at 450 degrees on an ungreased baking sheet
9. to serve like they do at the fair
10. split open but do not cut clear through
11. fill with jam and close
12. eat and enjoy !
target.review:
"You can do it in a run, you can do it in a gallup! You can do it real slow so your heart don't palpitate! Just don't be late! Do the Puyallup"!! That little Puyallup fair jingle has been running through my head all day... Thank you so much for this recipe, it brought back a lot of memories! I was born and raised in Washington state and now live in Ohio... These came out just like the ones I remembered at the fair. But I didn't have to wait in a line that stretched for about a half mile! I agree, you have to have the slab of butter and raspberry jam... Stawberry is good too! Thanks Again!! Now all I need is a little rain... (wink)

Take two:
I made these again today. This time I brushed them with melted butter and sprinkled cinnamon sugar on the top just before I put them into the oven...  Yummy!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
english bishop

relax and celebrate with this warming port-wine drink, made with baked spiced oranges.

1. cut the orange almost in half
2. sprinkle the inside with crushed cloves
3. and place cinnamon stick inside
4. pierce the orange with small slices to make easier placing the cloves into the orange
5. bake it in the oven on low heat for 30-40 minutes
6. cut the baked oranges into quarters and squeeze juice into a saucepan with peels
7. add 1 cup water , simmer 5 minutes
8. pour in the remaining ingredients
9. simmer gently for 10-15 minutes - do not boil or the flavor of the port will be spoiled
10. strain and serve in warm mugs or in cordial glasses
demonstrations.review:
I have not made this yet, but it looks just like some Gluvine (sp?) Glog that I had at a German festival.  And it was wonderful!!  I have also made some spiced wine that is very similar to this, but your recipe looks better. I really like the idea of cognac!  Yummmmm!!

Do you have any idea how one could bottle this for a gift?
I have a friend that would love it, but doesn't have the time to cook.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
dark chocolate cake

while it takes slightly longer to prepare this recipe than a box mix, the resulting moist, delicious cake makes it very worth the little extra time. i consider this 'perfect' chocolate cake. this cake is excellent with  both with recipe #261024 and recipe #208959 (the dark flavor version). (i use recipe #95416 when i'm decorating the cake.) i love how the leftovers are still moist even a day or two later. (i store my loosely covered with plastic wrap.)
my father adores this cake with recipe #261024 on it. for his birthday, father's day etc. i make him cupcakes with the icing on them and individually wrap them. he keeps them in his freezer for when he wants "a piece of cake". he claims they are as good as when they are fresh. 
(even though it isn't where i got the recipe from so i can't vouch for it, reviewers have said it is the recipe on the hershey's cocoa can. i would recommend using their special dark cocoa if possible.)

1. heat oven to 350f
2. grease and flour two 9 inch round baking pans or one 13x9 inch pan
3. in large mixer bowl , stir together dry ingredients
4. add eggs , milk , oil , and vanilla
5. beat on medium speed for 2 minutes
6. stir in boiling water by hand
7. i usually use between 2 / 3 & 3 / 4 cups
8. the cake is still very moist but it doesn't seem to "fall" as much as it cools
9. this might have to do with our high humidity or brand of flour or other factors so i don't know if it will work for everyone
10. pour into prepared pan
11. bake 30 to 35 minutes for round 9-inch pans , 35 to 40 minutes for rectangular pan or until wooden pick inserted in center comes out clean
12. because they have a tendency to overflow if you fill them more than 2 / 3 full , i usually get about 27-28 cupcakes per batch
13. bake for approximately 18-20 minutes
14. cool 10 minutes
15. remove from pan to wire racks
16. please
17. chocolate drink mixes that you add to milk or water to drink will not work in this recipe
demonstrations.review:
Beautiful!!!  
I followed the recipe to the letter... Accept that I added a hand full of chocolate chips to the batter.
I used the Kittencal's Easy Chocolate Buttercream Frosting/Icing.  All I can say is Yummmmmmmmm!!!  This one is a keeper. Thanks!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
real swedish pancakes  pannkakor

this is how we make them here in sweden. my mother always does them this way, and in every other swedish family i have visited. the other recipes i have seen here have little resemblance with the original.

the pancakes should be thin like crêpes. it's also important that the skillet is thoroughly and evenly hot before starting (even then, the first few may not turn out perfect). mark 4 on a 1-6 hob is good.

note: the recipe is very easy to remember in metric: 2 eggs times 3 (deciliters) flour equals 6 (deciliters) milk.

1. mix eggs , flour and salt
2. add the milk , a little at the time , and whisk to a smooth batter
3. the batter will be very thin
4. in a hot skillet , add one teaspoon butter and just as much batter to cover the bottom
5. fry the pancakes golden brown on both sides
6. add more butter for each new pancake
7. roll or stack them on a serving plate
8. keep warm
9. serve hot , preferably with whipped cream and jam
demonstrations.review:
Love, Love, love, this recipe!!!  They came out just the way my Mother-in-Law makes them...  She is Swedish.
I did add a little sugar to mine (aprox 2 Tbls), as I have a sweet tooth.  My husband loves them!!! He likes to sprinkle them with cinnamon sugar. I can't get them out of the pan fast enough for him...  LOL!!
Thanks for this wonderful recipe.

target.recipe_text:
ranch chicken thighs

needed a quick & easy weeknight meal. this is adapted from an old taste of home magazine. the chicken is tasty & juicy, with a nice crunchy crust. you won't miss the skin!  
eta -- some say this is too bland.  the ranch dressing is not enough seasoning.  i do add season salt to taste (nature's seasonings) to the bread crumb mixture for more flavor.  hopefully as a cook, you will know what to add to suit you and your family's taste.

1. in a shallow bowl , combine crumbs , parmesan cheese , cornmeal , italian seasoning , and seasoned salt
2. dip chicken into salad dressing , then coat with crumb mixture
3. place chicken in a greased 13x9 baking dish
4. bake , uncovered , at 375 degrees for 45 minutes or until juices run clear
target.review: My family loved it.  It turned out very crispy; had lots of flavor and of course my kids love ANYTHING ranch flavor.  I would definatley do this again with any chicken part.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
creole crock pot ribs

juicy, falling off the bone tender ribs in a very flavorful sauce.

1. place ribs in crock pot
2. mix all remaining ingredients
3. pour over ribs
4. cover and cook on low for 8 hours
demonstrations.review: These turned out dry, and yucky.  I put bbq sauce on it and put in the oven and broiled just so we could eat'em.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crock pot cheesy meatloaf

i found this recipe in the 1975 edition of crockery cookery, and made a few adaptations. this meatloaf is so easy to put together. pop it in the crock pot, and let it simmer all day.

1. crush the crackers with a rolling pin or blender
2. in a bowl , mix together the crushed crackers , shredded cheddar , onion , green pepper , chili sauce , milk , eggs , salt , and pepper
3. mix in ground beef , and form into a 7-inch round loaf
4. place in crock pot
5. cover and cook on low for 8 hours , or until done
demonstrations.review: Everyone in the family love this one.  They get really excited when I make it in the morning. It makes for a long day when everyone is looking forward to dinner.  Normally no leftovers.  This one is to become one of our family favorites.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crock pot bananas foster

a nice dessert for your trusty crock pot! i found this recipe on the internet.

1. melt margarine in slow cooker by turning cooker on low
2. it will take about 10 minutes
3. mix in brown sugar when margarine or butter is melted
4. gently stir in fresh bananas and rum
5. cook on low for 1 hour
6. spoon banana mixture over vanilla ice cream and serve
demonstrations.review: LOVED IT!!!  Very simple and extremely delicious.  My whole family love it. Would definately make it again. Thanks for sharing this recipe.

target.recipe_text:
cornbread dressing

this is my favorite cornbread dressing i use for special holidays. i make my own white bread using my bread machine and my own skillet cornbread to use in this recipe. if you prepare the bread ahead of time, you can freeze them until ready to use. i really like this dressing. it is easy to do and has a great flavor. i like to add fresh mushrooms to the mix. happy holidays!

1. melt butter in a skillet
2. add the onions and celery and saute until tender
3. combine toasted bread and cornbread in a large bowl and mix
4. add onions and celery plus their cooking liquid , the salt , pepper , sage , and poultry seasoning and mix throughly
5. using a bulb baster , add just enough turkey giblet broth to make a very moist mixture , then stir in the eggs and scrape the dressing into a large greased baking pan or dish
6. bake in 400 degree f oven until dressing is nicely browned , about 30-40 minutes
target.review: Bev, you get another 5 stars.  I am a yankee who moved to the south 25 years ago.  Learned to love everything southern except cornbread dressing.  Decided this year to make it for my southern husband and it is great.  Thanks for helping me make him happy.  Gloria

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pasta shrimp toss

a versatile and quick gourmet dish - tastes  equally good with chicken or scallops.  i got this from the land o' lakes web site.  (it always reminds me of eating out in boston's north end.)

1. cook linguini or spaghetti according to package directions , drain and set aside
2. meanwhile , melt butter in 10" skillet until sizzling
3. add onion , shrimp , bell pepper , garlic , salt and pepper
4. cook over medium heat , stirring occasionally , until shrimp turn pink
5. stir cream and flour together in small bowl until smooth
6. stir into shrimp mixture
7. continue cooking until mixture comes to a boil
8. stir in tomatoes and basil
9. place hot cooked pasta in large pasta bowl or onto serving platter and top with shrimp mixture
10. sprinkle with parmesan cheese
demonstrations.review: Very easy and VERY good.  DH said 4 stars because he liked more salt.  I said 5 stars because it was flavorful as was.  Thank you MA.  Gloria

demonstrations.recipe_text:
the last peanut butter cookies recipe you ll ever try

these are the most amazing cookies. they are crispy on the outside, soft on the inside and freeze so well. you can't even tell they were frozen! the best part - they are drop cookies, no shaping necessary. if you love nuts, use crunchy peanut butter and add the nuts, if not, use creamy pb and 2 cups of peanut butter chips. cook time is for one batch. dough keeps well in fridge so you can bake a batch every day and have fresh cookies!

1. cream peanut butter and margarine , add sugars and mix well
2. add eggs and mix until creamy
3. add remaining ingredients
4. chill for one hour-i usually skip this step and chill between batches
5. drop by teaspoonful onto cookie sheets- do not flatten
6. bake at 325f for 15 minutes
7. cool on cookie sheets for about 5 minutes then transfer onto newspaper- the newspaper soaks up extra grease so the cookies don't become crumbly , little trick i learned from my mil- this is also optional
8. edited to add - immediately after the cookies are completely cooled i always transfer them to an airtight container
9. several posters have mentioned the cookies get hard if you leave them out
10. i have never had that problem - these cookies have always stayed soft and moist if they are stored in an airtight container
demonstrations.review: I'm not a sweet eater nor a baker.  All of a sudden DH wants something SWEET in the evening--there goes the diet.  Oh well, I made your cookies and they are wonderful.  I'm going to bake a couple of batches at a time.  I plan on dividing the rest of the dough, wrapping it and keeping it in the frig until we're ready for it.  You can buy it that way so I don't see why it won't work.  Gloria

demonstrations.recipe_text:
hot italian sausage  venison

i am always looking for new things to do with my deer meat.  i found a hot italian sausage recipe and altered it for venison.  you can use it in any recipe that calls for hot italian sausage. it will give your pasta that little extra kick.

1. mix meats together
2. in a seperate container mix dry ingredients thoroughly
3. combine meat and spices , mix thoroughly
4. add water
5. can be used right away , but for best results , put it into an air tight container and set in refrigerator for 24 hours
6. can be stuffed into medium casings or used in bulk form depending on your recipe
demonstrations.review: Excellent flavor.  It tastes just like any hot Italian sausage I have eaten except there is no fat.  I cant wait to use this in my next spaghetti and meatball recips.  Thanks for the recipe.

target.recipe_text:
caramelized sweet potatoes   apples

our favorite sweet potato side dish. it's a great fall comfort food and easy to prepare with ingredients on hand. enjoy!

1. melt butter in an oven safe casserole
2. add the brown sugar and cinnamon
3. mix well
4. add the apples and potatoes
5. stir well to thoroughly coat with the caramel mixture
6. cover with a lid or foil and bake at 375 for 30 minutes , stirring once halfway through
7. after 30 minutes , remove the cover , stir again , and bake for 10 more minutes , or until caramel is thickened and the potatoes are tender
target.review: This was a huge hit! Both my kids loved it, and my husband has requested it for Thanksgiving. I only used 2Tbsp butter and Splenda Brown Sugar blend. I'll definitely make it again and again and again!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
oatmeal raisin applesauce cookies

modified from a recipe from lifescript.com

1. heat the oven to 375f lightly grease cooking sheet
2. in a large bowl combine the flour , baking powder , baking soda and salt
3. in the bowl of an electric mixer , cream the butter and both sugars together
4. beat until smooth , about 1 minute
5. add the applesauce , egg and vanilla and mix until blended about 2 minutes
6. add the flour to the applesauce mixture and mix well
7. remove the bowl from the mixer and stir in the oats and raisins
8. drop rounded teaspoonfuls onto the prepared baking sheets about two inches apart
9. bake until slightly golden , about 10 to 12 minutes
10. remove the baking sheets from the oven and cool on wire racks for 5 minutes
11. remove the cookies and cool completely
demonstrations.review: These are a great healthy treat! I had dark brown sugar, so they are a bit of a molasses cookie, but they are wonderful! I also added about 1tsp fresh grated ginger and 1tsp cinnamon. Yum!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chicken breasts in sour cream with mushrooms

wow is this ever good! i had some friends over for dinner and they loved it so much they wanted the recipe.

1. arrange chicken in a shallow baking dish so that pieces do not overlap
2. cover with mushrooms
3. combine undiluted soup , sherry and sour cream , blending well
4. pour over chicken , completely covering it
5. dust with paprika
6. bake at 350 degrees for 1 1 / 2 hours
7. serves 4
demonstrations.review: This was wonderful! I did saute an onion, red pepper, and fresh mushrooms in a little olive oil before I added them to the chicken. We really enjoyed it over brown rice. YUM!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
jack o  lantern cheeseburger pie

it's just plain fun for us and the kids will love to eat their dinner. it's a tiny bit fiddly but so much fun you won't mind at all. i have to admit that, my "doesn't like anything" dh loves it!

1. cook first 5 ingredients in a large skillet over medium-high heat , stirring until beef crumbles and is no longer pink
2. drain
3. stir in ketchup and worcestershire sauce
4. cool
5. unfold 1 piecrust , and place on a lightly greased baking sheet
6. spread mustard evenly over crust
7. stir together meat mixture and 2 cups cheese
8. spoon onto center of crust , leaving a 2-inch border
9. unfold remaining piecrust , and cut out a jack-o'-lantern face , reserving pastry cutouts to use as a stem
10. place crust over meat mixture
11. crimp edges of crust , and fold under
12. place stem on top of jack-o'-lantern face
13. whisk together 2 tablespoons water , egg , and 1 drop each of red and yellow food coloring
14. brush over crust
15. bake at 425f for 20 minutes
16. remove from oven , and brush again with egg mixture
17. fill eyes , nose , and mouth with remaining 1 cup cheese
18. bake 5 to 10 more minutes or until golden brown
demonstrations.review: We really enjoyed this fun and delicious dinner before taking the kids out trick-or-treating. It was great fun, and really yummy!

target.recipe_text:
ice cream pail pickles  bread   butter pickles

the recipe came from an old friend many years ago. easy to make, tastes great, everyone likes them, in the summer you want them at most meals & they go great with your bbq.

1. fill ice cream pail 3 / 4 full of sliced cucumbers and red onions
2. mix ingredients together and then pour into ice cream pail
3. mix everything together , stir a couple times a day for 2 days
4. store in the fridge
5. lasts a month or more
target.review: Ok I put the spices in a bag...did not work. Just have to tolerate and shake them off before eating...Otherwise very good recipe

demonstrations.recipe_text:
peppermint patties

these are amazing! better than york's because the chocolate is so much thicker. the yield is a guess as the recipe is from a friend who made them at christmas and gave them as gifts. fortunately, i was one of the recipients.
this recipe has been updated to add more details after questions from reviewers. cooking time is really drying time for the centers.

1. combine the sweetened condensed milk and peppermint extract
2. slowly add the powdered sugar and beat
3. knead on a surface sprinkled with more sugar until dough is stiff
4. add more sugar while kneading if the dough is sticky
5. roll 1 / 4 inch thick
6. cut into approximately 1 1 / 4 to 1 1 / 2 inch circles
7. if they are much bigger than that they fall apart when you dip them
8. my girlfriend said she uses a screw-off wine bottle cap !
9. let the cut patties dry for at least 2 hours on each side
10. they need to be really dry
11. melt chocolate & shortening it a double boiler
12. stirring constantly until smooth
13. using 1 tbls of shortening for every 6 oz
14. of chocolate
15. keep chocolate hot for dipping
16. dip patties in melted chocolate
17. the method my friend has found to work best: she places them on a long 3-tined fork , puts them in the chocolate , flips them over to coat the other side , lifts them out again with the fork underneath the patty , shakes the fork to shake off the excess chocolate & then places the patty on waxed paper to harden
demonstrations.review: Great recipe.. Is a keeper.. I made some..and wrapped them in aluminum foil just like the york. They are very cute in my candy dish.. I did not roll them out and cut them. I rolled them in balls and flattened them in my palm and put them on the pan.. easy...

demonstrations.recipe_text:
zucchini orange bread

a variation on zucchini bread.

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. grease and flour bottoms only of two 8x4 or 9x5 loaf pans
3. in large bowl , beat eggs until thick and lemon-coloured
4. gradually beat in sugar
5. add oil , orange juice and zucchini
6. stir in remaining bread ingredients
7. mix well
8. pour batter into prepared pans
9. bake at 350f degrees for 45-55 minutes or until cake tester inserted in centre comes out clean
10. cool 10 minutes
11. remove from pans
12. cool slightly on a rack
13. in small bowl , blend glaze ingredients
14. spread over warm loaves
15. cool completely on wire rack
16. wrap tightly and store in refrigerator
demonstrations.review: I just made this recipe.. I did not have any orange juice but I have orange consentrate... so since I had no orange I used 2/3 cup of the consentrate in place of the juice and zest.... is WONDERFUL...good texture good flavor.. I also used the mini pans. that way I can share easier. I baked them for 30 minutes.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
gyro burgers

this is not your ordinary hamburger! if you like hamburgers and you love gyro sandwiches, then you may enjoy this combination of those two ideas. adapted from "365 ways to cook hamburger." i borrowed this cookbook from a local library and copied out this tasty recipe. purists beware - this is not pretending to be an authentic recipe from any particular culture, but is merely influenced by the flavors & style of greek cuisine. prep is about 15 minutes plus 2 hours chilling time. cook time is a guess and varies based on how thik you make each patty - also, even though the original suggested 4 huge patties, you can certainly make smaller ones and just cook them for a little less time. you can broil these if you prefer.

1. in a bowl , combine lamb , beef , bread crumbs , minced onion , garlic , allspice , coriander , cumin
2. add just 1 tsp of the salt and 1 / 8 tsp of the pepper and mix well
3. form into 4 patties , cover and chill 2 hours
4. in another bowl , whisk together vinegar , oregano , 1 / 4 tsp salt , and 1 / 8 tsp pepper
5. gradually whisk in the oil until blended well
6. add tomatoes , sliced onions , and cucumbers and stir to coat
7. cover and let marinate at least 2 hours
8. when you are ready to cook your burgers , oil& preheat your grill and grill as you would any hamburger
9. when burgers are fully cooked , slit pita pockets open on the sides to form open pockets and place a burger inside
10. have bowls of the tomato topping , the shredded lettuce , and some tzatziki on the table for guests to add as desired
11. the yogurt sauce is available in the dairy case near dips or at the deli counter or some markets or you can prepare a homemade version
demonstrations.review: This is all "make ahead". I made the meat mixture and the tomato mixture the day before along with I made recipe #10901 "Pita Bread" the day before and also recipe# 57747 Gyro Sauce. For the meal I cooked my burgers on the grill and the rest was easy to assemble. Very Yummy! and WOW dont you just love this web site too.Got all the recipes I need to make it all "homemade".Excellant recipe

target.recipe_text:
luby s cafeteria macaroni and cheese

this is a classic favorite of all of the luby's cafeteria customers. from the luby's 50th anniversary recipe collection cookbook. the taste of this m&c might be a little bland, but you can always kick it up.

1. cook macaroni according to package directions
2. heat oven to 350f
3. in a large bowl , mix dry milk , flour , and butter
4. gradually add boiling water , beating constantly
5. add 1 1 / 2 of the cheese and continue beating until smooth and creamy
6. stir in macaroni , 1 cup of the remaining cheese , and salt
7. transfer to lightly greased 2-qt baking dish
8. cover with foil
9. bake 25 minutes
10. remove foil
11. sprinkle with remaining 1 / 2 cup cheese
12. continue baking 1 minute or until cheese melts
target.review:
While the recipe calls for 3 cups of cheese, the directions are a bit sketchy.  It first says to use 1 1/4 cheese, fine.  Then it says to add 1 more cup cheese, fine.
The last part says to use the remaining 1/2 cup cheese.  Well that only adds up to 2 3/4 cup cheese...what happened to the other 1/4 cup?

demonstrations.recipe_text:
jeanie s cake frosting

my friend, jeanie is a great cook. we took a cake decorating class together and she came up with this frosting recipe that tastes incredible yet it will hold its shape for decorating.

1. whip margarine until smooth
2. slowly add 1 cup shortening
3. whip until fluffy
4. add vanilla , powdered sugar and flour
5. whip until smooth
6. may add up to one cup more powdered sugar to increase stiffness of frosting
7. decorate cake as desired
demonstrations.review: This frosting is so incredible!  I chose to use butter, and I used 1 tsp vanilla, and 1 tsp almond extract...I wound up w/ a frosting reminiscient of sugar cookies...yum!  It was very easy to make, and it holds shape beautifully!  Do NOT pass this recipe up, it should be at the very top and should receive some high ratings, b/c it's so light and airy and not sickingly sweet. The hardest problem I had w/ the recipe was not saying it was "my own"!  This is a keeper for sure!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
quincy s yeast rolls

i've finally tried this recipe and tweaked it enough to get it reasonably close.  these are the closest i've seen to my favorite rolls in places like quincy's, grandy's, etc.  it's a nice soft squishy yeast roll, perfect with any meal.

to clarify the directions since one reviewer mentioned that they had a problem with their first batch: make sure that your machine's dough cycle includes the rising time!  i thought everyone's did, but apparently not.  (my own personal machine mixes up the ingredients and then there's a total rise time of a little over an hour (closer to 1.5 hours).  so, if you think your abm just mixes things up but doesn't allow for rising time, add a 2 hour (approx) rise time between steps 1 and 2.  if your machine's dough cycle does have a built in rising time, then you're all set, and you can follow the instructions exactly, no need for extra rising time.  

1. place all ingredients in above order in bread machine
2. after dough cycle completes , remove and shape as rolls , placing them in a pan lined with parchment paper
3. let rise for 30 minutes
4. brush tops with butter prior to baking
5. bake 20 to 25 minutes at 350 degrees until golden brown , on the highest rack possible in your oven
6. brush the tops with honey butter to give it a slightly sweet taste , as soon as you get them out of the oven
7. now eat , and enjoy !
demonstrations.review: Absolutely awesome rolls.  I chose to prepare the old fashioned method.  Scrumptious!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
dorito rotel chicken casserole

great with sour cream and rice.

1. saute onions in butter
2. add soups & tomatoes
3. cube velveeta , add & simmer until it melts
4. add chicken
5. crumble doritos in bottom of casserole
6. add chicken mixture and top with remaining doritos
7. bake at 350 for 30 minutes
demonstrations.review:
5 stars ONLY w/ the noted changes.
Replace the butter w/ 1 cup of milk.
Add in 1 tsp chili powder, and use 8 ounces of grated sharp cheddar.  Add in chopped bell pepper (any colour you like).

The reason I chose to leave out the butter is that the vegetables will get soft in the oven, and not to mention milk is a LOT more figure friendly!!

target.recipe_text:
green beans with feta cheese

a wonderful greek style side dish that can be served hot or at room temperature.

1. saute onion and garlic in olive oil for a minute- be careful not to burn
2. add tomatoes , olives and oregano and simmer for about 5-8 minutes
3. add green beans and simmer for another 5 minutes
4. just before serving sprinkle feta cheese on top
5. these are delicious hot or cold
target.review: I made this for the first time for company tonight and it was such a hit, the lady asked me for the recipe.  The only thing I did different was added about a 1/4 tsp. of salt and allowed all of it to simmer for about 30 min. to allow the flavors to blend.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
patti labelle s macaroni and cheese

got this off of the "good morning america" website after i saw her cook this on the show. this is the best macaroni and cheese i have ever tasted!!

1. preheat oven to 350
2. lightly butter a deep 2 1 / 2 quart baking dish
3. fill a large pot with water and bring to a rapid boil
4. add macaroni and the 1 tb oil
5. cook for 7 minutes , or until somewhat tender
6. drain well , and return to the pot
7. meanwhile , in a small saucepan , melt 8 tb of the butter
8. stir into macaroni
9. in a large bowl , combine all of the shredded cheeses
10. to the macaroni , add 1 1 / 2 cups of shredded cheeses , half and half , the cubed cheese and the eggs , and the seasoned salt and pepper
11. transfer to the prepared casserole dish , and top with remaining 1 / 2 cup shredded cheese
12. dot with remaining 1 tb of the butter
13. bake for 30-35 minutes or until the edges are golden brown and bubbly
14. serve hot
15. serves 8
demonstrations.review: This had no flavor.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
salmon rice pie

a good way to use leftover rice and get your omega-3s. this is a good way to use leftover white rice from chinese take-out. this a great recipe to improvise with different filling ingredients.

1. preheat oven to 350 deg f
2. for crust: combine rice , cheese , egg and onion
3. press into a buttered 9-inch pie plate
4. for filling: drain salmon , reserving liquid
5. break salmon into large chunks and distribute over bottom of rice crust
6. sprinkle broccoli over salmon
7. add enough milk to reserved salmon liquid to equal 2 / 3 cup
8. combine with eggs , dill , salt and pepper
9. pour milk mixture carefully over salmon and broccoli
10. bake at 350 deg f for 40 to 45 minutes or until a knife inserted near center comes out clean
demonstrations.review: I followed the recipe exactly.  We did not enjoy this at all.  Very bland.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
yes  virginia there is a great meatloaf

absolutely delicious meatloaf and sauce! those who claim they don't believe there can be such a thing as a great meatloaf will love this. based on a meatloaf given to me by a dear friend, virginia strehl, memphis, and leesburg, fla. nita holleman, 2000

1. meatloaf: combine meat loaf ingredients and place into a loaf baking dish
2. smooth out top
3. sauce: combine sauce ingredients and pour on top and sides of meatloaf
4. bake at 350f about 1 hour to 1 hour 15 minutes or until done
5. enjoy !
6. the addition of 1 or 2 teaspoons of kitchen bouquet makes this recipe very good
7. recipe should be"plump" from the addition of the milk or half & half
8. it should not be runny
9. a second batch of sauce served hot is good to serve with the meatloaf
10. nita's
11. it is wise to have some fat added to the deer -- especially to ground deer
12. maybe 25 % fat , , otherwise your results will be poor
13. i don't know about some of the other game meat some are using
14. please consult an expert
15. the recipe is delicious as it stands ! enjoy ! nita holleman
demonstrations.review: I like to add garlic and green pepper to this.  I also use quick cooking oatmeal to bind it together instead of the bread.  Overall, this is the ONLY meatloaf recipe I will ever make again!!!

target.recipe_text:
super peanut butter filled brownies

my most-requested dessert recipe. moist brownie bottom topped with a thick peanut butter filling and topped off with a chocolate glaze. please watch the brownies carefully and remove from the oven when toothpick comes out with moist crumbs clinging to it. if your toothpick comes out completely clean then they are overbaked and you will end up with a "cake-like" brownie. glass pyrex baking pans have yielded the best results in my experience. note: this recipe doubles beautifully!

1. preheat oven to 350
2. in a small saucepan , melt unsweetened and semisweet chocolates with butter over low heat , set aside to cool slightly
3. in a mixing bowl , beat eggs and sugar until light and pale colored
4. mix in 1 tsp vanilla
5. add flour , salt and melted chocolate
6. stir to combine
7. pour into a greased 9 in square baking pan
8. bake at 350 for 20 - 25 minutes or until brownies test done with toothpick coming clean but with moist crumbs clinging to it
9. do not overbake
10. cool
11. for filling , add peanut butter and butter in a mixing bowl and mix until thoroughly combined and smooth
12. slowly add powdered sugar , mixture will be a bit crumbly
13. blend in cream until mixture is fluffy and reaches desired spreading consistency
14. spread over cooled brownies , cover and chill until firm
15. for glaze , melt chocolate and butter in saucepan , stir until smooth
16. drizzle over the filling
17. chill well before cutting
18. let sit at room temperature for 10 - 15 minutes before serving
19. you don't want to serve these ice cold out of the refrigerator
target.review: This is heaven for those of us who are addicted to chocolate and peanut butter! I didn't bother to chill mine, because I wanted the peanut butter topping to stay nice and soft and fluffy. Thanks so much for a great recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cheese burger alfredo casserole

the recipe is dedicated to all those single parents and career people that don't have a lot of time at the end of the day to prepare dinner and that don't mind using prepared ingredients for a quick meal. i made this up because my daughter was sick with a cold and a sore throat and wanted something soft and easy to eat.  granted the french fried onions did not fit in with that idea, but they did add a nice taste and crunch to this casserole and she managed them just fine despite her sore throat.  since i was caring for both her and my baby grandson, i didn't have a lot of time to spend on making dinner.  the entire casserole (except for the spices) cost me about $20 and after feeding 3 adults, there is plenty left over for another meal or lunches at work the next day.  if you don't like leftovers, halve the recipe.  i much prefer using ingredients that do not come from a jar or a can, but sometimes, you just have to do what you have to do to put a meal on the table on a budget, and this was my attempt.  it is pretty tasty if i may say so for myself.

1. preheat oven to 400 degrees
2. brown the ground beef with the onions and spices
3. drain and rinse off the fat
4. in the meantime , cook the pasta according to the package instructions
5. in a large casserole dish , mix together the ground beef and onion mixture , the vegetables , cooked pasta , jarred alfredo sauce , and cheese cubes
6. bake for 10 minutes
7. stir
8. top casserole with the french fried onions
9. bake for another 5 to 10 minutes or until hot and onions are browning
demonstrations.review: As a previous poster said, this is a very versatile casserole. I halved the recipe (there's just the two of us) and it made plenty. We'll have it for leftovers one night, and my husband packed up two more servings for his work meals. It was very mild, though, and I will probably add a few more spices next time to liven it up a little. But overall, very good!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
beef and green chili soup  sure to warm you up

it's the season for soup! here is an outstanding recipe, that originated in a ski lodge in montana. the flavor combinations are amazing and it is now one of our new favorites.

1. zaar will not let me enter the green chilis amount ! please
2. :-)
3. heat a large dutch-oven over meduim-high heat
4. add beef and cook until browned , stirring to crumble
5. remove beefand set aside
6. add veggies to pan and cook until tender
7. add spices and garlic
8. cook 1 minute to combine
9. return beef to pan
10. ad broth and chilis
11. bring to a boil
12. add maccaroni and reduce heat to simmer
13. cook about 8 more minutes until noodles are done
14. yield 6 1cup servings
15. hint: i boil my noodles separately and add them to each serving ! that way leftover soup when reheated does not have gummy / loppy noodles in it ! :-)
demonstrations.review: According to my husband, this soup gets five stars. I made it for him, as hot/spicy dishes are not for me. He really enjoyed this, but, since he likes things really hot, I added extra red pepper flakes, and increased the 1/4 teaspoon amount of spices to 1/2. I also added a beef bouillon cube for extra flavor. So, for those who like milder soups, use the recipe as is--it's great. For those who are like my husband, though, feel free to spice it up. It only gets better!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
margaret s sour cream coffee cake

my mom made one of the best sour cream coffee cakes that i have ever tasted. i've tried other recipes and none of them were as moist as my mom's. if you are looking for a moist and delicious sour cream coffee cake, well look no further and make this one. i've added a couple of variations at the bottom. my neighbors son always asks me when i am going to make him this cake with the chocolate chips.

1. combine 1 / 2 cup sugar and cinnamon and set aside
2. combine flour , baking powder , baking soda and salt
3. cream the butter , add sugar , eggs , vanilla and sour cream
4. add the flour mixture to the creamed mixture and mix until combined , do not overmix
5. this batter will be thick
6. spoon half the batter into a greased and floured 10" bundt pan
7. sprinkle the sugar and cinnamon mixture on top and spoon the remaining batter on top
8. bake at 375 for 35-45 minutes or until toothpick inserted comes out clean
9. cool 10 minutes and invert onto a plate
10. cool for another 20 minutes and place the cake into a large plastic bag which really makes the cake moist
11. for variations:
12. - add walnuts or pecans with the sugar / cinnamon mixture
13. - spread chocolate chips in place of the sugar / cinnamon mixture as this tastes excellent
demonstrations.review: I was looking for something quick and easy to make for a light breakfast when my sister comes over in the morning to help me garden. This fit the bill perfectly. Very easy, simple ingredients, and wonderful flavor. I subbed in Splenda for half the sugar and used light sour cream. I also added some coarse ground walnuts to the topping. Although the batter is very thick on this, the cake itself is very moist and light. I used a 9x5 loaf pan and baked for 35 minutes. Perfection.

target.recipe_text:
n e  crab rolls

total summer food, this is great with lobster too.

1. whisk together mayo , lemon juice , zest , cayenne
2. add crab meat and scallions and mix carefully , trying not to break up large lumps season to taste with salt& pepper
3. spread butter on insides of hot dog buns , place buttered side down in a warm skillet , cook for 5 minutes until toasted place a lettuce leaf in each bun , fill with crab mixture , serve
target.review: This was Epic! Reason I gave it 4 stars is I added about 1/2 teaspoon of Old Bay Seasoning. Everything else i did exact. Honestly I don't measure when I cook so I may have added more Lemon Juice. You just can't mess this one up. Also I don't have fresh crab this time of year but had some frozen imitation snow crab and it tasted awesome. Thanks for the post.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s famous barbecue sauce for chicken and ribs

this is the best barbecue sauce, and trust me i have experimented with hundreds of different combinations over the years,  this is even better than any of the popular bottled sauces! ---plan ahead this sauce must be made one day in advance to allow the flavors to blend and intensify, don't even think about using it the same day it is made,  this sauce will take on a whole different flavor when simmered for 1 hour and left overnight in the fridge--- the ingredients can easily be doubled but keep the garlic amount no more than 2 tablespoons, and for the best flavor use only heinz ketchup and a good quality brand of yellow mustard, i use french's mustard it really will make a difference in the taste, please do not omit the liquid smoke --- yield is only estimated as the sauce will reduce after simmering for 1 hour or more  ---*note* for a smoother low fat sauce omit the oil, onion and fresh garlic, then in the saucepan mix all remaining ingredients together and add in 1 teaspoon each garlic powder and onion powder then simmer for 1 hour -----you will love this sauce!

1. heat oil over medium heat
2. add in onion and saute for about 3 minutes , then add in garlic and saute for 2 minutes
3. add in chili powder , paprika , cayenne , salt and black pepper
4. stir for 1 minute
5. add in all remaining ingredients
6. bring to a boil stirring with a wooden spoon to combine
7. reduce heat to low and simmer uncovered stirring occasionally for 1 hour over low heat
8. cool to room temperature then cover and refrigerate for 24 hours or more before using
demonstrations.review: Best BBQ Sauce I ever made. I didn't follow exact but really you cant go wrong with this one. The key is liquid smoke, gotta have it or it won't work. I have made sauce before but didn't have the smoke and wow what a difference. It literally tastes like right off the shelf just better.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
french dressing for the lazy

from my recipe collection.

1. put all the ingredients in a blender and pulse to blend in a smooth paste
2. season with salt and pepper
3. fill up in a clean bottle and refrigerate for 1 hour before using
demonstrations.review: Just made a salad and didnt realize we had no dressing. Only thing i did different was used apple cider vingegar as had no tarragon and no lemon juice. It was better than store bought. Thanx for the post.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
edna s apple crumble  aka  apple crisp

a simple and easy to make but oh so yummy recipe. known as apple crumble in the uk and apple crisp in the us

1. put apples in an 8 or 9 inch square baking dish
2. combine the rest of the ingredients in a separate bowl and mix
3. spread crumble mixture over apples and bake for 35 minutes in a 375f degree oven
4. for an added treat top off with a little english custard
demonstrations.review: So simple and delicious. The girls flied thru their bowls and looked at me like lost puppies. <br/>Thanks for the recipe.

target.recipe_text:
best banana bread

you'll never need another banana bread recipe ever again!

1. remove odd pots and pans from oven
2. preheat oven to 350 / 180
3. cream together butter and sugar
4. add eggs and crushed bananas
5. combine well
6. sift together flour , soda and salt
7. add to creamed mixture
8. add vanilla
9. mix just until combined
10. do not overmix
11. pour into greased and floured loaf pan
12. bake at 350 / 180 for 55 minutes
13. keeps well , refrigerated
target.review: Made this around the holidays and it has excellent moist flavor.  I even tried a lowfat version of this with the egg substitute and light margarine and it still came out tasting wonderful.  I am adding this to my collection.  Thanks for posting it!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
easter nest rice krispies treats

these are such a big hit with all kids-adults too!  :)

1. make rice krispies treats as directed on box
2. lightly butter your hands
3. pinch out a handful of the prepared rice krispies treats , roll in a ball , and place on wax paper
4. form ball into a "bird nest" formation
5. while rice krispies nests are cooling , dye the coconut
6. place coconut in a bowl and add green food color-shake until coated well
7. put one peep in the middle of the nest
8. place green coconut around the peep
9. place 3-6 jellybeans around each peep
demonstrations.review: Loved this recipe!  So fun to make.  I made these in the mini muffin tins without the liners (sprayed with Pam) and still had enough rice krispies to make 7 in the full size muffin tins.  I put two jelly beans in the "little nests" and 4 in the "larger" nests.  I used a 7oz bag of coconut and had quite a bit leftover. I always add 1 tsp of vanilla to my rice krispie mix to keep them chewy.  Thanks for the great recipe that I cane take to my new job for treat day!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cream of mushroom soup  weight watchers

just like julia...if you liked the movie, you'll love the recipes.  weight watchers has updated the beloved chef's timeless classics, keeping the french flavor, but trimming the fat.  the original:  7 points values - ww remake:  2 points values.  so why not serve a few of your favorites when you host a julia-inspired oscar fete this year?  bon appetit!

1. melt butter in a nonstick dutch oven over medium-high heat
2. add onion , celery and carrot
3. cook , stirring occasionally , until onion is softened , about 5 minutes
4. add mushrooms and cook , stirring occasionally , until softened , about 10 minutes
5. stir in broth , salt and pepper
6. bring to boil
7. reduce heat
8. cover and simmer until vegetables are tender , about 30 minutes
9. remove dutch oven from heat
10. uncover and let cool 30 minutes
11. puree soup in batches in food processor or blender
12. return soup to dutch oven
13. stir in half-and-half , sage and thyme
14. cook , stirring occasionally , over medium heat until heated through , about 10 minutes
15. optional: top each bowl of soup with a couple slices of sauteed mushrooms
demonstrations.review: Excellent Soup! I decided to make this on a cold Iowa winter evening.  I used the pack of two big size portabello mushroom caps and used regular chicken broth since store didn't have the low sodium in the big can. For the fresh sage & thyme I ended up using 1/4 tsp each of ground sage and ground thyme.  This recipe did take a little longer to make than I thought with 30 minutes to simmer & 30 minutes to cool but the outcome of this soup is SO worth it!  Will definetly be making this again.  A keeper!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
soft and chewy rice  krispies  crispy  treats

an extra-chewy recipe that will have everyone wishing theirs turned out as well!

1. melt margarine in a large pan over medium heat
2. melt in marshmallows and stir continuously until smooth
3. add vanilla
4. without removing from heat , add cereal
5. stir until cereal is completely covered with marshmallow mixture
6. pour into a greased 9x13 pan
7. let cool 2 minutes
8. press flat with greased hands
