9. cool completely and cut into squares
10. enjoy !
demonstrations.review: This is my Go-To recipe for rice krispie treats.  Always come out chewy! I usually add a tsp. of maple syrup to my batch for an added splash of sugary goodness. The syrup also seems to eliminate some of cereal sticking to the pan.

target.recipe_text:
chocolate cinnamon hazelnut bars

prep time includes cook time.

1. ---forcookie crust---
2. beat flour , 3 / 4 cups of softened butter , sugar , baking powder and cinnamon in a large bowl until mixture is crumbly
3. stir in hazelnuts
4. press into bottom of ungreased 9x13 inch baking pan
5. bake in preheated 350 degree oven for 15-18 minutes or until firm
6. ---forchocolate layer---
7. melt chocolate chips , 1 / 4 cup of butter that you cut into pieces in a medium saucepan over lowest heat , stirring constantly until smooth
8. remove from heat
9. stir in brown sugar , eggs and vanilla
10. pour over hot crust
11. bake at 350 degrees for 20-25 minutes or until center is set
12. cool completely in pan on wire rack
13. sprinkle with confectioner's sugar
14. cut into 30 bars
target.review: I never thought chocolate and cinnamon went together very well, but its seems to work in this recipe. It was a little dry but very tasty.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
szechuan fish

very tasty easy dish. you can use other seafood in this same sauce just be careful if you are doing prawn, that you don't over cook them. marinate them in the sauce, remove and cook in the wok for 3 minutes,remove from wok, cook sauce and put the prawns in for about 1 more minute

1. in a wok brown the fish on all sides with the green onion& garlic
2. combine remaining ingredients and pour over the fish
3. cover& cook on low heat for 20 minutes
demonstrations.review: My Husband loves Szechuan So this was the perect dish for him. He loved it. The flavours blended well, I served it with a veggie stir-fry. Thank-you so much. Polly.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cucumber salad with spicy wasabi dressing

rice wine vinegar is milder than most western vinegars. 

1. mix the wasabi with 1 / 2 teaspoon warm water in the bottom of a mixing bowl and let it stand for 5 minutes
2. peel the cucumbers , cut each one in half lengthwise , and use a melon baller or spoon to scoop out the seeds
3. cut the cucumbers widthwise into 1 / 4-inch crescents
4. add the vinegar and sugar to the wasabi and whisk until smooth
5. whisk in the sesame oil , salt , and pepper
6. just before serving , add the cucumbers , green onion , and sesame seeds to the dressing and mix well
demonstrations.review:
My husband and I both loved this, easy and fast,
it made the meal. Thanks.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cheese  cheese  macaroni and cheese and ham and cheese

nan

1. cook the macaroni in a large saucepan according to package directions
2. drain
3. add the butter
4. stir until melted
5. stir in the remaining ingredients , except paprika
6. pour into a lightly greased 2-quart shallow casserole dish
7. sprinkle paprika lightly over top
8. bake at 350f for 40 minutes
demonstrations.review:
This should get a 10, even a 20. 
Great taste, creamy, and my kids ate like they were starving, finally a recipe they fight over
Great Great recipe miller. thanks.

target.recipe_text:
poor man s granola bar

just a basic granola bar from what you have in your cupboard.  i've added a little of this and a little of that to make a great bar!

1. preheat oven to 350
2. mix dry ingredients in large bowl
3. beat remaining ingredients in another bowl
4. fold into dry ingredients
5. mix in raisins
6. mush into bottom of greased "bar" pan
7. bake for about 20 minutes
8. let cool
9. cut into 2 x 4 bars and store
target.review: Really easy bar to make.  I added the sam amount of Grape Nuts and another cinnamon cereal and it came out well.  You can pretty much use any fruit, too.  I found them to be cakey v. a boxed bar that is crumbly. I enjoy these for a pre-workout snack.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
peanut butter banana cookies

these are a good variation to plain peanut butter cookies. they are especially good when chocolate chips are added.

1. cream butter , peanut butter & sugars
2. beat in banana , eggs & vanilla
3. stir in flour , baking powder & salt
4. stir in chocolate chips
5. drop on greased cookie sheets
6. press lightly with fork
7. bake at 375 for 10-12 minutes
demonstrations.review: What a great cookie!  It has a crunchy outside and cakey inside.  It has a lot of versatility in that you can add raisins, add spices (cinnamon, cloves, ginger, pumpkin spice) and I topped mine with walnuts.  This were easy to make and great to eat!  To lower the fat, use egg substitute, cut the sugar, use applesauce.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
zucchini and tomatoes with parmesan dumplings

this simple-to-prepare side accompanies blander dishes nicely. i particularly like it with simply grilled salmon or other fish.

1. heat oil in a large skillet over medium heat , and saute onion and garlic until tender , but not browned
2. add tomatoes , basil , sugar , salt and pepper
3. simmer , covered , for 20 minutes and stirring occasionally
4. add zucchini and simmer covered for 15 minutes , or until they are tender and stirring as needed
5. mix the beaten egg and the parmesan cheese together in a small bowl until it forms a mass
6. with the aid of a tablespoon , drop the dumplings onto the tomato mixture
7. simmer , covered , for 5 to ten minutes , until dumplings are firm
8. when they are firm , gently flip them over to completely cook the top side
9. serve each portion with one dumpling atop the tomato-zucchini mixture
demonstrations.review: Excellent!  What a great flavor for dumplings.  I paried 1-fresh tomato w/ 1-can diced petite toms in water.  I let it simmer with spices, onions, garlic and balsamic vinegar for 10-min. Added zuchinni (w/ peel) and simmered for 15-min and then mushrooms at the end (they cook quickly).  I was amazed at how the parm. cheese took on body w/ the egg.  Strong parm. flavor requires a distinct like for it.  I like it!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
healthier oatmeal apple cookies

these are soft cakelike cookies that are low in fat, loaded with fruit, and delicious. no eggs or oil.  you could probably make these even better for you by adding wheat flour.

1. combine all ingredients
2. drop by rounded teaspoons on lightly greased cookie sheet
3. bake 12 minutes in 350 degree oven
4. enjoy
demonstrations.review: These are great!  Very easy to make and healthy (no eggs or oil) I substituted applesauce 1:1 instead of prune juice (didnt have any) and it worked out well.  A little dry before you add the apples in so you may need 1Tbsp of applesauce for more wet.  I sprinkled a little more cinnamon, adding pumpkin spice and a dash of cloves as well.  You can pretty much use any complimentary spice and it will make this very tasty!

target.recipe_text:
sour cream drop cookies

this heirloom cookie was originally made with homemade sour cream stored in a crock in the basement.
 
the dough for drop cookies is soft enough to drop from a spoon.  use an ordinary teaspoon rather than a measuring spoon.  use slightly rounded spoonfuls rather than level ones.  push the dough off the spoon with a rubber spatula or another spoon.  make the drops all the same size so they will bake evenly.  bake them just until done.  remove immediately from baking sheet.  if cookies are left for only a few minutes on a hot sheet, they will continue to bake and will be overdone and dry.

1. sift together flour , baking powder , baking soda , salt and nutmeg
2. set aside
3. cream together butter and 1 1 / 2 cups sugar in bowl until light and fluffy , using electric mixer at medium speed
4. add eggs , one at a time , beating well after each addition
5. blend in sour cream and lemon extract
6. gradually stir dry ingredients into creamed mixture , blending well
7. drop mixture by rounded teaspoonfuls , about 3 inches apart , on greased baking sheets
8. sprinkle each with sugar
9. bake in 375f oven 8 minutes , or until golden brown around the edges
10. remove from baking sheets
11. cool on racks
12. makes 5 1 / 2 dozen
13. farm journals complete home baking book
target.review:
I have been searching for this recipe for some time. My gr-grandma used to make these but my grandma's SILs took all the recipes when she died.. even my grandma (the daughter) got none. So, we've been on the hunt for a number of years. I made these based on what Mom & Grandma told me was in these cookies. I didn't know about the lemon extract--just about the nutmeg. I took them to Mom.. she said this WAS the recipe!! She confirmed with a call to my grandma.. we'll be taking her some of these next visit. So, thank you from an entire family for posting something we've been trying to find for years.  Our undying gratitude!!

The cookies taste awesome.. had a number of compliments at a Christmas Eve gathering. Have had a number of requests for the recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
laura s gingerbread

laura ingalls wilder's recipe from the little house on the prairie cookbook. she wrote in her original recipe, "chocolate frosting adds to the goodness." my children and i agree! this recipe works well with or without the eggs.  i tried it both ways--with the eggs gives you a more cake-like texture, without eggs is slightly denser.  the results are so similar it was difficult to tell one from the other--wonderful either way!

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. grease an 9 x 13 inch baking pan
3. blend sugar and shortening in a small bowl
4. stir in the molasses
5. measure 1 cup of boiling water in a 2-cup measuring cup
6. add the baking soda and mix well
7. in a large bowl , sift together the flour and the spices
8. add remaining ingredients and mix well
9. pour into prepared pan
10. bake for 45 to 55 minutes or until cake is done
11. serve warm or at room temperature
12. gingerbread is delicious with applesauce , lemon sauce or whipped cream
13. laura herself liked to add chocolate frosting !
demonstrations.review: Absolutely scrumptious!!! I have finally found the ultimate gingerbread recipe!!! I must add... I have made this about 5 times now. I tried the choc. frosting last night--I couldn't believe how DELICIOUS it was!!!! It enhances the ginger & is positively scrumptious!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
hidden valley ranch crunchy pea salad

i've had this recipe for several years and its always a crowd pleaser. i got the recipe out of a woman's magazine.

1. combine all ingredients except bacon
2. mix well and chill for several hours
3. just before serving sprinkle with crumbled bacon
demonstrations.review: Delicious... & I didn't even have all the ingredients!!! I threw in some corn as I had no celery, & had to forgo the cashews (:() as well. I used chives from my garden instead of green onions. It was absolutely delicious--can't wait to try it with the celery & cashews!! Thanks for posting--I'll use this often!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
rhubarb sour cream crunch pie

i came accross this recipe yesterday and had'nt made it in ages. i remembered how easy and delicious it was so went ahead and made it. it was even better than i remembered.......

1. on a lightly floured surface , roll out pastry& fit into a 10" pie plate
2. in a bowl , whisk egg with sour cream
3. combine sugar , cornstarch , cinnamon& nutmeg
4. stir into egg mixture
5. stir in rhubarb slices and spoon into pastry shell
6. topping: in bowl , mix rolled oats , brown sugar and flour
7. cut in butter until mixture is crumbly
8. stir in lemon or orange rind
9. sprinkle over rhubarb filling
10. bake at 400 for 15 min
11. reduce heat to 375 and bake for 40 minutes or until topping is golden brown and filling is puffed and set
12. serve warm with a scoop of vanilla ice cream
demonstrations.review: Absolutely delicious!! Everyone loves it..there won't be any left by morning (made it after dinner tonight). I served it warm with Coolwhip & it is great. I'll definitely make this often.Thanks for posting!!

target.recipe_text:
grape salad with a twist

the twist is butterfinger candy bars!  i received this recipe from a coworker after she brought it to a potluck.  and wow, the flavor is unbelievable.  thanks wendy h!

1. wash grapes
2. cream together cream cheese , sour cream and sugar then fold in the grapes
3. put mixture into a 9 x 13 dish
4. sprinkle top with crushed butterfingers then top off with crushed pecans
5. press and chill
target.review: This was sickly delicious!  The cream cheese/sour cream mix is yummy on it's own as a dip, but once you add it all together...mmmm GOOD!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kmt s low fat ricotta spinach rolls

this is a treasured adoptee.  here is kmt's original description of it:  delicious, low fat, italian dish. very filling too!

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees
2. start chopping basil and parsley
3. prepare lasagna pasta according to package lay a few sheets of wax paper on the kitchen table
4. in a mixing bowl , combine riccota , 1 / 2 of the mozzarella , parsley , basil , spinach , salt , pepper , egg and carrots
5. mix well by hand
6. lay cooked lasagna on wax paper spread a thin layer of spinach mixture down the length of the lasagna
7. you may have leftover pasta and / or spinach filling
8. just store it or chuck it
9. spread a little sauce on the bottom of large shallow casserole dish
10. roll each filled lasagna and place in casserole dish
11. spoon the pasta sauce onto spinach roles
12. top with remaining mozzarella cheese
13. bake for 20-30 minutes
14. serve hot with a crusty garlic bread and salad
demonstrations.review: This was delicious.  I omitted the carrots and added extra-lean ground beef.  Because there is only two of us in the house, I prepared and froze half the recipe.  We have plenty to eat for lunch this week and a whole pan waiting in the freezer.  Great recipe, thanks for sharing it!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
perfect fingerling potatoes

this recipe is from alton brown's eat this rock! you cook the potatoes in heavily salted water and the salt crystallizes on the outside of the potatoes. it seems like a lot of salt but it works. the reviews rave over it! i have slightly adapted it. they are even good cold!

1. in a large pot , combine the salt , water , and potatoes and bring to a boil
2. cook until the potatoes are fork-tender , about 25 to 30 minutes
3. remove from the pot to a cooling rack and let stand for 5 to 7 minutes
4. the salt crystals will form on the outside of the potatoes
5. serve as is , or with butter , pepper , chopped scallions , or parmesan cheese
demonstrations.review: I swear I followed this recipe to a tee and they were awfully salty.  Even my boyfriend who adds salt to everything thought these were too salty to enjoy.  What did I do wrong???

demonstrations.recipe_text:
homemade baked macaroni and cheese

this is a very easy recipe that my mom used to make when i was growing up-you can change the types of cheese to add a different flavor too. i like it spicy !

1. grease or spray with non-stick cooking spray a casserole dish
2. melt butter in medium saucepan
3. when melted , add flour , stirring constantly for about 1 minute
4. whisk in hot milk , cook for 3 minutes
5. add 1 cup each of the cheeses , and stir until smooth
6. cook macaroni , drain , rinse under cold water , and drain again
7. combine everything together and pour into casserole dish
8. sprinkle the rest of the cheese on top , and bake at 400ffor 20 minutes
demonstrations.review: This was so simple and delicious.  I have been craving some good ol' mac and cheese for ever now.  This beats any box variety...BRAVO!!!  So yummy and comforting!

target.recipe_text:
ground beef curry  kima curry

this recipe is from one of my new favorite cookbooks, extending the table.  the notes on this recipe say that this swahili dish is served by a restaurant in the heart of nairobi.  i have only modified it to make the recipe fit into zaar format, to preserve the authenticity of the recipe.  this is a very mild, very easy to make curry.

1. in a skillet , heat oil over medium high heat
2. saute onion and beef until browned
3. drain fat
4. add in curry powder , garlic , ginger , and tomatoes and fry briefly
5. stir in the rest of the ingredients
6. turn down heat to medium and cook for 20 minutes to blend the flavors
7. serve over rice or with chapatis
target.review: Very tasty! Made some subs for missing ingredients but still came out excellent.<br/><br/>Had to use a can of unsalted diced tomatoes since I didn't have whole and used a little ketchup instead of plain tomato paste. <br/><br/>I messed up part of the cooking instructions for the onions/beef (Forgot to put the oil first, whoops!) but it didn't seem to matter much. It's not a very spicy curry, which is perfect for me, since I'm kind of a spice-wimp. X3 but it's wonderful over some hot rice!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
wicked  chocolate chip muffins

i found this recipe in and 'old school" muffin mania cookbook, tried it this evening with the kids and it was a huge hit. really nice texture, light & fluffy. a+ in my book.

1. pre-heat oven to 375 degrees
2. grease and flour your muffin tray
3. mix togeher the dry ingrediants & the chocolate chips in a medium bowl
4. mix togeher , butter , egg & milk , and add to dry mixture
5. do not over mix , 30 strokes should do it
6. fill muffin tins 3 / 4 full and bake for 20 minutes
7. enjoy !
demonstrations.review: Pretty good! I've never really made muffins from scratch before but these are really good! They domed up nicely just like bakery muffins. I used semi-sweet chocolate chips and it was super tasty. The Recipe made 11 Average to Jumbo muffins (I only had a jumbo pan but it fit average sized paper muffin cups nicely), and probably could have made an even 12 or a few more but I think I misjudged how I divided the batter. X3 The second batch came out a little smaller then the first. Still awesome though! I think I'll have to try this recipe with other flavor chips, like white chocolate or peanut butter, just to see! :o

demonstrations.recipe_text:
bobbie q sauce  barbecue sauce

a versatile barbecue sauce - sweet and spicy. kind of like magic -- anything i prepare with this sauce disappears! it's a hit with all ages. i've started preparing it with xylitol, also known as birch sugar, instead of sugar, and it works just great, plus it's easier on blood sugar levels.

1. combine ingredients , bring to a boil and simmer over low heat for 5 minutes
2. use this as a basting sauce for barbecue , or combine with chopped or shredded beef , chicken or pork , and simmer until heated throughout and flavor is well through the meat
3. if you want to make up a batch of this to keep in the freezer , leave out the water , and it will not freeze solid
4. you can take out the container and just scoop out however much you need
5. i sometimes make it up by the gallon just to have it on hand for easy meals
demonstrations.review: Been looking for a sauce to make myself, since all the good ones are changing their recipes lately it seems, and I'm not liking the new flavors much. So gave this one a try, and ooh was it good!<br/><br/>I used about an either of water for the cooking (if that) of the sauce itself, and some Vegan Worcestershire I found on this site, and poured it over some chicken tenders before it went in the oven. Came out wonderfully! Definitely going to be making more of this recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
harvest corn   black beans

this is a pretty thanksgiving side dish that adds something special anytime.  this recipe can easily be adapted for large gatherings.  happy holidays & enjoy!  :)

1. heat olive oil in medium saucepan over medium-low heat
2. add garlic and onions , and cook , stirring occasionally , until translucent and soft , about 10 minutes
3. drain black beans and reserve 1 / 4 cup of liquid
4. add beans , reserved liquid and remaining ingredients to sauce pan and cook on medium , about 10 minutes
5. remove from heat and transfer to serving dish
demonstrations.review: Good but bit bland for my tastes. Didn't have plain oregano so used Italian Seasoning instead, and Ketchup instead of tomato paste. Will probably make again.

target.recipe_text:
creamy corned zucchini and peppers

a really nice recipe for summer ingredients.  very healthy, very satisfying.  and easy!

1. clean and small dice zucchini , onion , and pepper
2. heat oil in skillet
3. add onion , cook until onions are clear but not browned
4. add zucchini , pepper , corn , and spices , cook over medium high while stirring often , until desired tenderness
5. add goat cheese , stir until the cheese it melted and evenly distributed
target.review: very tasty and easy to fix. I chose to use cream cheese. I also added peppermint leaves and basil

demonstrations.recipe_text:
burst o  lemon muffins

only try these if you love lemon as they are pretty intense. i used the grater on the zest of one lemon and it was no where near 1-2 tbs  but i think it was plenty. we liked them but my son preferred his without the glaze. 
i'd like to try the glaze with confectioners sugar and try the muffins with vanilla yogurt some time.

1. in a large bowl , combine the flour , sugar , baking powder , baking soda and salt
2. in another bowl , beat the yogurt , egg , butter , lemon peel and lemon juice until smooth
3. stir into dry ingredients just until moistened
4. fold in the coconut
5. fill greased muffin cups two-thirds full
6. bake at 400f for 18-22 minutes or until golden brown and muffins test done
7. cool for 5 minutes before removing from pan to wire rack
8. in a saucepan , combine the lemon juice and sugar
9. cook and stir until sugar is dissolved
10. stir in coconut
11. using a toothpick , poke 6-8 holes each muffin
12. spoon the coconut mixture over muffins
13. serve warm or cool to room temperature
14. we have found we prefer them cooled as the lemon flavor isn't as overwhelming once they reach room temperature
demonstrations.review: Overall, it is a very light, moist muffin. I used vanilla yogurt and left out the coconut. I added a few strawberries. I dont think I used enough lemon zest (only one tablespoon). Being a lemon lover next time I will use lemon yogurt and add a little extra lemon juice. For the topping I didn't used coconut or sugar. Instead I used some honey and lemon juice. There are a lot of different things you can add to this recipe and still come out with something delicous

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cabbage and kielbasa

my husband didn't think he liked cabbage until i served this. the bacon and onion really give this recipe a lot of flavor.

1. cook bacon in a large skillet until crisp
2. remove bacon
3. crumble , and set aside
4. add next 7 ingredients to bacon drippings
5. cover and cook over medium heat for 10 minutes , turning cabbage once
6. add sausage and cover and cook an additional 5 minutes or until sausage is heated
7. transfer to a serving dish with a slotted spoon
8. sprinkle with the crumbled bacon
demonstrations.review: Loved this recipe. I served it over brown rice

demonstrations.recipe_text:
healthy pumpkin pudding  south beach diet

sugar-free quick pumpkin pudding...south beach diet friendly.

for the milk: unsweetened soy, lower fat milk, or milk/water mixture.

1. mix pumpkin , spices , and half the milk
2. while stirring , slowly add mix and remainder of milk
3. stir until smooth
4. let sit for 30 minutes if you prefer a thicker consistency
demonstrations.review: this was very tasty however I would have liked it to be thicker. so I don't know if I did something wrong. will try it again maybe with less milk or add something to thicken it up a bit

target.recipe_text:
barbecue baked beans

i've adapted this recipe from "the barbecue bible" by steven raichlin. if you like your barbecue beans on the sweet side, then these are the beans for you. i know that the list of ingredients is long, but most of them are probably already in your pantry. don't be tempted to leave out the fresh garlic or fresh gingerroot--it makes a difference. this is mandatory with our ribs--all you need is a potato salad and coleslaw and you're all set.

1. preheat oven to 325f
2. put bacon in large , heavy pot over medium heat and cook until lightly brown , about 5 minutes
3. discard all but 2 tablespoons fat
4. add onion , garlic , and ginger and saut until soft , about 5 minutes
5. remove pot from heat and stir in remaining ingredients
6. pour into baking dish
7. bake , covered , for 1 hour
target.review:
Excellent !  A really nice recipe for summer bbq's.

I used canned white navy beans and included the liquid smoke.  I may have gotten a little carried away with the ginger since I didn't measure it while grating.  I thought it was too gingery, but the guests at the bbq really liked it as is and commented that the ginger gave it a 'fresh' taste.  It wasn't as sweet as I'd anticipated, but I could probably fiddle with the ingredients a bit (e.g., eliminate the liquid smoke) to turn up the sweetness. 

Guests were asking me for the recipe, so I think that qualifies it as a winner - thanks for sharing it tt !!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
japanese mum s chicken

we have a japanese girl, tomoko, living with us, and tonight she and i cooked a japanese dinner for us and her friends. she phoned her mum,toshiko, in japan for this, as it's her favourite recipe, and i wanted to share it here. it's simple and so good, and tomoko, who is only 16, did such a good job of cooking this, then translating the recipe to english for me.

*the liquid will thicken to a glaze if you are patient. it just takes a bit of time. if you feel your chicken is cooked (and going to overcook) remove it before going on to reduce the liquid. same thing, if you must use breast meat, remove it (so it doesn't dry out) and continue reducing the liquid . if you do it this way rather than thickening with cornstarch you will get a richer glaze and not need to add stock or broth instead of the water. it just takes patience. and note: a glaze is sticky and coats the meat, this is not a sauce.

1. place all the ingredients in a saucepan over a high heat
2. bring to the boil , then reduce to a simmer for about 20 minutes
3. remove any scum that rises to the surface
4. increase the heat , turning the drumsticks frequently in the liquid , and cook until the liquid has reduced to a sticky glaze
5. arrange the chicken on a serving platter , remove the garlic clove and chili from the liquid , and spoon the glaze over
demonstrations.review: This was definitely easy and tasty.  Quick too.  I like my food with alot more punch so I might add more garlic and/or chili pepper next time.  Picky DH loved it and that, in and of itself, makes it a winner in my book.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
basil  cilantro and macadamia nut chicken

not your ordinary weeknight chicken, but after marinating, the dish is ready in about 1/2 hour! make it the night before and you have a quick, delicious treat for dinner. the flavor will have you filling your plate again and again.

1. put ginger , garlic and peppers into a food processor and process til smooth
2. add macadamia nuts and continue to process
3. add oil , lime juice yogurt , basil , cilantro and spices and process again until smooth
4. put the chicken in a medium bowl , and add the mixture , stirring to coat all pieces
5. cover and refrigerate chicken for 12 hours
6. this step is not necessarily required
7. heat a bit of oil in a wok , or deep dish fry pan
8. add chicken and its marinade to pan and cook thoroughly , stirring frequently , until marinade sticks to chicken
9. this will take about 20 minutes to 1 / 2 hour
10. the mixture will look soupy at first , and then begin to thicken up as the sauce reduces
11. i like a little heat , so i also add a little chili oil to the dish
12. serve with steamed jasmine or basmati rice
demonstrations.review:
Delish.  Loved the marinade - tasty and colourful (it was a beautiful minty green!).  My husband and I love Indian food, so this was a winner.

Next time, I plan to hold off a little on the spices.  (The garam masala, coriander AND cumin were - for me - overkill since they are so similar).  I prepped the dish the night before and it was great to just dump it in a pan and cook for a quick and yummy meal the next night.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
la madeleine s tomato basil soup

nan

1. combine tomatoes , juice / and or stock in saucepan
2. simmer 30 minutes
3. puree , along with the basil leaves , in small batches , in blender , food processor
4. return to saucepan and add cream and butter , while stirring , over low heat
5. garnish with basil leaves and serve with your favorite bread
6. excerpted from an article by beverly bundy of the fort worth star-telegram around may 20
7. 1994
8. she wrote , "once a year , in january i run a column of our most requested recipes -- this year , that column included the recipe for la madeleine's popular tomato basil soup
9. i continue to get at least 10 calls a week asking for the recipe
10. so here it is , once again -- "
demonstrations.review: I cut the cream in half, opted for tomato juice and canned crushed tomatoes.  This was good, though I was expecting more flavour.  Perhaps more basil would do it?  Some sauteed onions would go well too.  It would do well as a fresh, light pre-dinner opening in lieu of a salad.

target.recipe_text:
english muffins  bread machine method

when i landed on this recipe while surfing the web, i had to try it. i'm so glad it did. they are delicious. tip i: the dough should be soft but not sticky. it took me two attempts to get that just right. tip ii: i posted the recipe as written. after, several batches, i don't press the dough into a rectangle anymore. i divide it into eight equal pieces and pat each piece into a 1/2" thick round. then, turn each round in dish of cornmeal.

1. put ingredients in the machine in the order listed
2. start the dough cycle
3. when the cycle is finished
4. sprinkle corn meal over your work area
5. use your hands to pat the dough into a 1 / 2 inch thick rectangle
6. turn the dough so that each side gets lightly coated with cornmeal
7. cut into 8 to 10 rounds
8. an empty large tuna can works well when you run out of dough gather up the trimmings and cut more rounds
9. place the rounds on a baking sheet , cover and let rise for 20- 30 minutes--until not quite double
10. heat a dry cast iron skillet or griddle over a low flame
11. cook the muffins about 5 to 7 minutes on each side
12. they should be golden brown when you turn them
13. split the muffins with a fork or serrated knife and serve warm
14. these freeze well and can be reheated in the microwave or toasted
target.review: These were very easy to make, and I had no trouble with the dough even on my first try. I used your suggestion to pat out the dough instead cutting the rounds and that worked just fine.  I used an electric skillet set at 325 degrees to brown them. I split the muffins before I froze them, and put a piece of waxed paper in between the halves. They are just delicious toasted!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cranberry nut scones

this is an adaption of najwa's great scone recipe.

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. spray a baking sheet with non stick cooking spray
3. combine the sour cream and baking soda in a small bowl
4. combine flour , sugar , baking powder , cream of tartar and salt in a large bowl
5. cut in butter until mixture resembles fine breadcrumbs
6. combine egg and vanilla extract with sour cream mixture
7. gently stir into the flour until moistened
8. do not overmix !
9. knead dough 10 times only
10. place dough on baking sheet and pat into 3 / 4" thickness
11. cut into 6 wedges and separate so the scones are not touching
12. leave adequate space for expansion
13. dust with sugar
14. bake 15-20 min or until golden brown
demonstrations.review:
I couldn't rate this yet because step 4 instructs you to "add sugar", but the amount is not stated in the ingredients list, just the sugar to dust the scones.
I'd like to make this recipe, but need to find out the amount of sugar to put into the dough. Also,
when do you add the nuts and cranberries?

demonstrations.recipe_text:
banana yogurt muffins

i had bananas and yogurt in the house, and i wanted to bake some muffins, so i combined two recipes and came up with these moist muffins. because they have yogurt in them, they have less oil and no butter, making them healthier than most!

1. in a large bowl , combine flour , sugar , baking powder , salt and cinnamon and mix in another bowl , combine yogurt , egg , milk , and oil
2. add contents of wet mixture to dry ingredients and mix- do not over mix
3. stir in bananas place batter in muffin tins
4. bake at 400 degrees for 20-25 minutes or until golden
demonstrations.review: This made 12 large, delicious,moist and tender muffins.  I used banana creme yogurt.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
caramelized chicken wings

nan

1. preheat oven to 375f
2. place chicken in a 9x13-inch baking dish
3. mix the oil , soy sauce , ketchup , honey , garlic , salt and pepper and pour over the chicken
4. bake at 375f for one hour or until sauce is caramelized
demonstrations.review: I made these for my faculty's Christmas party and they disappeared fast!  I did bake them another 15 minutes.

target.recipe_text:
arabian pita bread

this doesnt taste exactly like arabian pita, but it is close. so quick and easy, and tastes better with arabian dishes (hummous, falafel, shawerma, etc). i make it when i can't get arabian pita, great with "fooll muddames" as well. this is my mom's recipe.

1. mix yeast , water and sugar
2. set aside
3. in a large bowl , combine flour , dried milk and salt
4. pour in the oil and yeast / water mixture and stir well
5. you might need to add more flour or water , depending on the absorbency of the flour
6. knead dough briefly , divide into 18 egg sized balls
7. place on a floured surface , cover and let rest for 15-30 minutes
8. roll one ball out and cook in a skillet until large "bubbles" form
9. flip pita over and cook the other side for a few more minutes
10. i flatten it out with a spatula
11. keep bread warm while cooking the rest of the bread
12. these freeze well
target.review: These were very easy to make and tasted great with our dinner.  I did have to add a lot more flour than called for (probably at least 4 cups total, instead of 3 cups).  I will add a little more salt next time, too.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
bulk taco seasoning mix

i adopted this recipe from the recipezaar account in 2005 and when i tried it, i agreed with the reviewer that the recipe was too salty as posted; therefore i decreased the salt from 3 tablespoons to 1 tablespoon. add more if desired or leave it out entirely.

1. combine the ingredients
2. store in an airtight container in a cool dry place for up to 1 year
3. add 2 tablespoons to 1 lb cooked and drained beef and 1 / 3-1 / 2 cup water and cook until done
demonstrations.review: This is very similar to the recipe I've used for years.  I use 2 tsp. garlic powder, 1-1/2 Tbsp. cumin, and about 1 tsp. oregano but otherwise, it's the same recipe.  We love it for beef tacos, chicken tacos, soups, enchiladas, taco salad, etc.  It is much better than the packets!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
go go garlic bread

i found this recipe in a simple and delicious magazine and changed it to suit our tastes.

1. in a small mixing bowl , beat butter and mayonnaise until smooth
2. beat in the parmesan cheese , garlic , oregano , basil and seasoned salt
3. stir in monterey jack cheese
4. spread over cut sides of bread
5. place on an ungreased baking sheet
6. bake at 350 degrees for 10-15 minutes or until cheese is melted
7. slice and serve warm
demonstrations.review: We really like this recipe.  It is great on split Ciabatta bread!  I do use a little less mayo, about 1/3 cup.  We sometimes sprinkle parsley & paprika on top.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
easy enchiladas  beef or chicken

these easy enchiladas are my husband's favorite recipe of mine. because of the many different options, it is very versatile.

1. if using chicken , boil chicken in water
2. then rinse and shred with fork
3. add onion and garlic
4. if using ground beef , brown with onion and garlic , drain
5. add next 7 ingredients
6. in another skillet , heat oil
7. add tortillas , one at a time , for 10 seconds on each side
8. drain on paper towel
9. in 10x13 baking pan , pour just enough enchilada sauce in the bottom to coat the bottom of the pan
10. fill each tortilla with a spoonful of meat mixture
11. cheese , onions , and / or olives can be put inside each enchilada at this time , if desired
12. roll tortilla and place seam side down in pan
13. continue with remaining tortillas
14. pour remaining enchilada sauce over tortillas and top with cheese
15. at this time , pan may be refrigerated for several hours or overnight
16. bake in 350 degree oven for 20 minutes
17. top with sour cream
18. enjoy !
demonstrations.review: These were great!  We used ground beef for the filling, 2 (10 oz) cans enchilada sauce (one for bottom of pan and one on top of enchiladas), plus we used flour tortillas ( what I had on hand).  The kids really liked these.

target.recipe_text:
giant peanut butter cookies

my favorite peanut butter cookie. not too peanuty and a nice texture.  makes 20 regular-size or 10 3-inch cookies.

1. heat oven to 375
2. in large bowl , combine sugars , margarine , peanut butter , vanilla and egg
3. beat well
4. lightly spoon flour into measuring cup and level off
5. add flour , baking powder , baking soda and salt
6. mix well
7. if you are making the large cookies , it helps to chill the dough for an hour or so at this point , before shaping
8. it seems to make a firmer cookie--less likely to break
9. if you aren't concerned about that , you can skip this step
10. shape about 1 / 4 cup dough into a ball and place 4 inches apart on ungreased cookie sheet
11. bake at 375 for 13-16 minutes
12. remove from cookie sheet and cool completely on wire rack
target.review: I was disappointed with the recipe when I made the cookies regular sized, but I also used half of the dough to make a cookie cake.  It was awesome! I will definitely use this recipe next time I need a PB cookie cake.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
basic stir fry sauce

this is a good basic sauce. feel free to add ,perhaps a little lime juice, a pinch of cilantro, some peanut butter? have fun!

1. combine all ingredients except cornstarch in a small bowl or a 2 to 4 cup liquid measuring cup
2. place the cornstarch in a separate small bowl , and whisk in the mixture from step 1
3. just before mixing in to vegetables and / or meat , whisk the mixture one more time
4. add about 2 / 3 of the way through stir frying
5. enjoy !
demonstrations.review: Good taste!  I left out the mirin because I don't care for the flavor, and just poured everything ontop of the stir fry and added the corn starch and water last- saving one dish :-)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
easter nests with jelly bean eggs

originally from a peanut butter company, these no-bake treats are easy and oh-so-fun for the kiddos! :o)

1. break chow mein noodles into small pieces
2. set aside in large mixing bowl
3. combine sugar and corn syrup in large saucepan
4. cook on medium heat until the sugar is melted and there are bubbles at the edge of the pan
5. add peanut butter and stir until smooth
6. pour peanut butter mixture over crunched up noodles
7. toss until completely coated
8. let cool slightly to avoid burns
9. butter hands lightly and use approx 1 / 4 cup mixture to form a compact ball
10. make indention in the middle of each ball to resemble a bird's nest
11. place on waxed paper and let cool completely
12. place 2-3 jelly beans inside each nest
13. serve on a bed of green-tinted coconut for extra festive look
demonstrations.review: Simple and delicious!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cardamom buns

from sons of norway, so these are authentic and sound delicious. i will try them this week. posted for zwt 9.

1. scald milk
2. add butter and shortening to melt
3. let cool
4. soften yeast in the warm water , with 1 t sugar
5. let sit 5 minute
6. in lg bowl , add sugar , salt and cardamom
7. pour in milk
8. pour in yeast
9. add enough of the flour to make a stiff dough
10. knead for 5-8 minutes
11. place dough in greased bowl , cover and let rise until doubled
12. punch down dough and form into ping-pong sized balls
13. place balls 1" apart on greased baking sheet
14. cover with tea towel and let rise until doubled in size
15. preheat oven to 450f
16. bake for 5 minutes
17. remove from oven and brush with melted butter
demonstrations.review: These were delicious!  Although they weren't done after 5 minutes :)  I really liked the cardamom, and my picky eater loved them as well.  For ZWT family picks

target.recipe_text:
smoked paprika chicken breast

a nice simple recipe using smoked paprika. feel free to use the ordianary sweet hungarian if you have as much trouble getting smoked paprika as i do.

1. mix together the paprika , oil , garlic , basil , salt and cayenne
2. massage this mix into the chicken breasts and allow to stand for about 20 minutes
3. heat a pan over medium heat , and saute on both sides until chicken is golden brown and cooked through-about 8 minutes each side depending on the thickness of your fillets
4. add a little more oil if you need to , though there should be enough from the marinade
5. slice on the diagonal and serve
target.review: Smoked paprika is what makes this dish..... I have made this a few times now using the grill pan.. its wondeful.. the flavor and presentation is very gourmet....give it a go guys.. you won't be disappointed!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
tamale peppers

colorful and delicious dish!  i am marking serving sizes for use as an entree, but we also enjoy to serve this as a side by serving them halved.  this is based off of a recipe card i picked up in the grocery.  use the salsa of your preferred heat level to adjust it to your taste, or use pepperjack cheese to add some extra zip.

1. preheat oven to 350
2. slice off the top of each pepper and clean out the seeds
3. combine tomatoes , black beans , corn , onion , salsa , 3 / 4 c of the cheese , cornmeal , cilantro , cumin and water
4. mix well
5. spoon veggie mixture into the peppers
6. sprinkle the remaining cheese on top of each pepper
7. place peppers in an 8x8" baking pan and fill with 1 / 2" of water
8. bake 50 minutes , or until peppers are tender and the filling is heated through
9. let stand 5 minutes before serving warm , garnished with green onions and cilantro
demonstrations.review: I am sooo glad that I went onto this site this morning and found the perfect recipe for this evenings dinner... I will admit.. I was a little skeptical of how this would turn out.. but I'm sooo glad that I took the chance.. the taste is amazing!!  The only thing that I changed was that instead of fresh chopped tomatoes (which I will do next time). i added drained chopped canned tomatoes (its what I had in the pantry..) and it still worked really well. topped with the cilantro, green onion, a couple of dollops of sour cream.. dinner was served. thank you so much for posting this.. its a keeper!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s moist cheddar garlic oven fried chicken breast

this is for serious garlic lovers. the chicken bakes out so moist and tender! grated cheese may be sprinkled on top of the breast the last 5 minutes of cooking if desired but that is optional. double all ingredients for more than four breasts and adjust the amount of garlic to suit taste. for the coating amount you might be able to get away with 5 or maybe 6 very small chicken breasts, but i would suggest to increase the amount slightly --- to take this dish to yet another level, about 10 minutes before the cooking time is finished, drizzle the top of the chicken with a little pasta sauce, then sprinkle mozzarella cheese on top. return to oven for about 10 minutes until the chicken is completely cooked and sauce is hot and cheese has melted. for a lemon-garlic flavor add in 3 tablespoons lemon juice to the melted butter/garlic mixture ---  *note* for a healthier alternative smart balance butter blend may be used in place of the melted butter --- you will love this chicken!
visit my food blog, www.kittencalskitchen.com, for more of my recipes.

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. butter an 11 x 7-inch pan
3. in a bowl , combine melted butter with fresh minced garlic , 1 teaspoon garlic powder and salt
4. in another bowl , combine the dry breadcrumbs with 1 / 2 cup finely grated cheddar cheese , parmesan cheese 1 teaspoon garlic powder and coarse ground black pepper
5. dip chicken in butter mixture
6. then in crumb mixture
7. place in prepared pan and bake uncovered for 35-45 minutes or until cooked through , larger breasts may take more time
8. top with shredded cheddar or mozzarella the last 5 minutes of cooking (this is only optional
demonstrations.review:
I totally didn't add my stars here!!! 5 stars.. wish I could give it more though.. and remember.. FULL FAT VERSION is the best on this ..
thanks again Kittencal!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
greek style oven roasted lemon butter parmesan potatoes

i my family could make a meal just with these potatoes, they so delicious! adjust all seasonings to taste, for a more lemon flavor then increase the lemon juice.

1. set oven to 375 degrees
2. butter a shallow baking dish large enough to hold the potatoes
3. peel and cut the potatoes into large wedges and place into the prepared baking dish
4. in a bowl combine the broth , lemon juice , butter , oregano , salt , pepper and minced garlic
5. mix well to combine
6. pour over potatoes in the dish and stir to coat well
7. cover the dish tightly with foil
8. bake for about 40 minutes
9. uncover and turn potatoes
10. sprinkle with parmesan cheese , and return to oven
11. bake for another 20-30 minutes , or until potatoes are done to desired tenderness
12. sprinkle with chopped fresh parsley and serve
demonstrations.review: Oh wow!! is all I gotta say.. this recipe is simple with a gourmet flair and taste! I made this last Saturday 5/1 with filet mignon with balsamic glaze.. OH what a great review at this house!! I added the parmesan on the last oven roast (with out the foil on top). I actually screwed this up in the beginning.. i cut my potatoes into slices with the skin.. I was going to make another recipe; but decided on this.. they turned out EXCELLENT! not only did the chopped italian flat leaf add a wonderful presentation note; the flavor.. oh my .. I wish i could give this 10 stars here.. I'm gonna make this again and again.. thanks Kittencal for a wonderful recipe...

target.recipe_text:
stuffed peppers with pork and rice

making the most out a little minced pork, this dish makes for a tasty and different lunch. originally i came up with a slightly different version without meat which was inspired by holidays to cyprus, this is a twist on that.

1. cook the rice as you normally do leave to one side
2. soften the onions in a large pan
3. add the diced celery
4. add the pork and stir in well allowing to colour
5. then put in the garlic , tomato pure , dried oregano , smoked paprika , salt and pepper and stir inches
6. cook the mixture together for a minute then add the vegetable stock , stir in well and allow to reduce by about half
7. at this point cut your peppers in half and scoop out any seeds or white ridges
8. when the pan mixture has reduced mix in the rice and then stuff the peppers with the mix
9. give a little drizzle of olive oil and an optional sprinkle of grated cheese
10. bake in a medium hot oven for about 30-60 minutes
11. serve
target.review: I had bought some large Lozano peppers from the market and just happened to have some sausage meat around. This recipe was just what I needed, my only real change was to replace the celery with courgettes (zucchini) as they were available. I did five huge peppers and strongly suggest you cook them first, wrap them in cling film and then reheat the next day for delicious leftovers. Make sure you buy good quality peppers too. The longer this dish is left after cooking, the better it will taste!  ?Qu? bueno, qu? bueno!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
lemon garlic olives

refrigeration time not included in preparation time.

1. drain and rinse the olives , reserving brine
2. layer olives , oregano sprigs , garlic , lemon wedges and peppercorns in olive jar
3. add fresh lemon juice and top off with reserved brine
4. shake well and let olives marinate for at least 1 week in refrigerator
demonstrations.review: This is a really great recipe. I didn't reserve the brine because  didn't want the sodium but added some white wine vinegar mixed with a little olive oil to top up the mixture. The taste is so tangy after a week that it's tough not to eat the whole jar at once. Thanks for posting this.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
minty asian chicken noodle salad

cheer up a chicken salad, make it minty and then add some asian flavours.

1. soak the noodles for 5 mins in boiling water or according to pack instructions , until softened
2. drain , then cool under a running tap
3. drain again well , then
4. mix together the soy sauce , lime zest and juice and sugar , then pour over the noodles
5. toss through the mint leaves and serve
demonstrations.review: Easy to throw together and very tasty. Lovely Jubbly as Jamie says!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
barley and tuna salad with lemon and dill

not sure where i found this but it was on my computer and still looks good to me.  with summer coming salad entrees that require little or no cooking work especially well.  cook some barley one night for dinner and reserve some to make this the next day.  though this is good after a couple of hours, it's even better the next day as the dill flavor really infuses the dish and the tuna flavor mellows. (please don't eat this right away, not very tasty.) for ww followers, this is core or 3 points for flexers. cooking time is minimum chilling time.

1. combine salad ingredients together in a large bowl
2. whisk together dressing ingredients in small bowl
3. pour on salad and toss to coat
4. refrigerate a minimum of 2 hours to blend flavors
demonstrations.review: Great -- and the longer you leave it refrigerated the better it gets!

target.recipe_text:
crock pot beanie weenies

great to have after a long work day.

1. in a crock pot , combine all ingredients
2. mix well
3. cover and cook on low for 7-8 hours
target.review: This is a great recipe! My family loved it. I didn't have bacon on hand so I subbed liquid smoke. That did the trick. I'm sure its even better with the bacon. Thanks for posting!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
microwave scalloped apples

delicious cooked apples with just the right amount of sweet and tart. this is a favorite recipe that is very easy to make (especially if you have an apple peeler).

1. place apples in a 2 1 / 2 quart microwave safe bowl
2. combine the sugar , cornstarch , cinnamon and nutmeg
3. sprinkle over apples and toss to coat
4. dot with butter
5. cover and microwave on high for 5-10 minutes or until apples are tender , stirring occasionally
demonstrations.review: I scaled this down to just one, left the peels on and my apples are quite tart, so I added a pear to it.  So ended up with one apple and one pear.  Cooked about 5 minutes.  They were great!  I can't eat gluten and don't need the calories anyway.  I decided I didn't want then then, so put them in the fridge and they were good cold too!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
true lemon chicken

i wanted to make lemon chicken like the chinese restaurants have. after trying many recipes, i found one that was ok. i played with the recipe and tweeked it to my liking...a lemon sauce that is lemony with a good balance of sweet. i hope you enjoy this as much as i do.

1. chicken: saute cubed chicken in olive oil until done
2. set aside
3. sauce: in a small sauce pan , combine first 7 ingredients and bring to a low boil
4. slowly stir in cornstarch solution
5. depending on how thick you want the sauce determines how much cornstarch solution you use
6. careful- sauce tends to boil up when cornstarch solution is added
7. serve chicken over a bed of rice
8. pour sauce over chicken& rice
9. enjoy !
demonstrations.review: My family absolutely loved this! I just made it again tonight. We followed the instructions completely. It is just like lemon chicken from a restaurant. Thank you for sharing this recipe! :)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
gingerbread  for cookies or a  gingerbread house

this dough is very easy to work with.  we use this gingerbread to make our annual gingerbread houses.  one recipe makes 3 fair sized gingerbread houses.  this is also works excellent for gingerbread people. from good housekeeping dec 94

1. in a medium saucepan , heat sugar , molasses , ginger , allspice , cinnamon , and cloves to boiling , stirring occasionally
2. remove from heat
3. stir in soda
4. stir in margarine till melted
5. with a fork , stir in egg , then flour
6. on a floured surface , knead dough till mixed
7. divide dough in half , wrap half with plastic wrap
8. set aside
9. roll half the dough , with a rolling pin , slightly thinner than 1 / 4 inch
10. cut with cutters
11. bake at 325f on a cookie sheet for 12 minutes
12. cool on a wire rack
13. makes about 3 dozen 3" gingerbread people
demonstrations.review: Very good recipe! Thank you! :)

target.recipe_text:
kittencal s juicy hamburger burger

we all have our different tastes for burgers i like mine flavorful and juicy this recipe will give you the best of both! see the bottom of the recipe for tips on even more extra juicy burgers! --- making a indentation in the middle of the uncooked burger will prevent the burgers from puffing up into meatballs shapes while cooking and keeps them flat --- do not add any salt into the burger mixture as the dry onion soup already has a lot of salt content, you can sprinkle some on towards the end of cooking if needed, if desired you may add in 3-4 tablespoons of your favorite barbecue sauce to the ground beef mixture

1. in a bowl crumble the ground beef with clean hands
2. add in the dry soup mix , egg , garlic , breadcrumbs or crushed soda cracker crumbs , worcestershire sauce , black pepper and hot sauce
3. using clean hands mix until combined , add in more breadcrumbs or cracker crumbs if needed to just hold the mixture together
4. divide the ground beef into 6 equal patties
5. using your large finger or the back of a small spoon make a shallow dent into the center of each patty
6. place the patties onto a large plate or a small cookie sheet
7. cover with plastic wrap and refrigerate for a minimum of 6 hours or up to 24 hours to blend flavors
8. grill or pan fry the burgers as desired until cooked through
9. serve burgers in toasted buns with choice of condiments
target.review: OUTSTANDING burgers!! My boyfriend was quite skeptical when a) he saw me putting an egg in the meat and b) he saw the onion dip go in (he hates onions)...he loved these...as did i!  Had 'em for leftovers the next day and they were even MORE flavorful.  The only thing i did differently was substitute the BBQ sauce for Teriyaki Sauce...YUMMY!  Really added a nice flavor.  Thanks for another GREAT recipe Kittencal!!  Making anything you submit...you just CAN'T go wrong.  :-)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
slow cook down home pork chops and gravy

i don't even like pork, but was tricked into tasting this dish when i was told it was chicken. wow! the meat was sooo tender and juicy; so tender in fact, that it was literally falling apart! it was like nothing i'd ever tasted before! definitely not like my mother's hard, crusty pork chops! lol! this recipes goes hand in hand w/ some mashed potatoes. just pour the leftover gravy on the taters' and enjoy!

1. combine 1st four ingredients in a shallow dish
2. dredge chops in flour mixture and set aside
3. combine what is left of the flour mixture w / the chicken broth and pour into your crock pot
4. pour oil into a large skillet and cook the chops in hot oil until browned on both sides
5. place chops in crock pot and cook covered on high for about 2 to 5 hours or until tender
6. serve w / hot rice and / or mashed potatoes
7. ++if the gravy becomes too thick just add a little water
8. if you accidentally add too much water then add a little more flour
9. season w / salt and pepper too your taste
demonstrations.review: this was WONDERFUL!  the gravy was ABSOLUTELY DELICIOUS (i added a little thyme too). i didn't feel like doing it in a slow cooker, so i put 3 chops in a 8x8 glass baking dish and cooked them at 350 for about 2 and a half hours and they were unbelievable.  so tender you didn't even need a knife...served them up with some garlic mashed potatoes and we were in heaven.  Thanks for a great recipe!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
oven style scotch eggs

this is another recipe i adopted from recipezaar on feb.14 2005.  i've changed the recipe to make it fabulous.  a delicious treat.  brings back great childhood memories.  enjoy!

1. shell hard-boiled eggs
2. in a small bowl combine sausage meat with sage , garlic powder , onion powder , cayenne pepper and black pepper
3. divide sausage into 8 equal portions , flatten each portion to about 1 / 8-inch thickness
4. roll each egg in flour and place on top of each sausage patty
5. use each sausage patty to wrap around each egg until it is completely encased , pressing edges together to seal
6. beat the egg in a shallow dish and place breadcrumbs on a flat plate
7. dip each sausage-coated eggs in beaten egg and roll in crumbs
8. place on baking tray lined with aluminum foil and bake in oven at 375f for 25 to 30 minutes until golden brown
9. for a crispy crust spray very lightly with pam baking spray before baking
10. when ready to serve , line platter with lettuce and arrange scotch eggs , cut in half , among the lettuce
demonstrations.review: these are delicious and were a big hit when i brought them to work for out Thanksgiving Brunch.  the one thing i did notice is that i really had to cook them a loooong time, i think they were in at LEAST 45 minutes, however, they came out crispy and yummy and VERY flavorful (i made have wrapped the sausage too thick).  regardless, they really are superb.  thanks for a great recipe

demonstrations.recipe_text:
emerils new orleans style red beans and rice

"oh yeah, this is it!" - are the words my husband declared when he tried this recipe for red beans and rice. he was craving new orleans-style red beans and rice and i had never made it before- so this is the recipe i searched for and tried and it was delicious!! the kids thought it was great too. i only made a few small changes to emeril's, like adding more sausage than the recipe called for and letting a smoked ham hock cook with the beans for the first two hours..other than that everything is the same. this is not a quick meal, but great for a lazy day at home.

1. heat the oil in a large saucepan over med-high heat
2. saut the onions , bell pepper , celery , salt , cayenne , black pepper and thyme for about 5 minutes
3. add the bay leaves , ham and sausage and saut for 5 to 6 minutes
4. add the beans , garlic and 10 cups water to the pot
5. bring to a boil , reduce the heat to medium , and simmered uncovered , stirring occasionally for about 2 hours
6. add more water if the mixture becomes dry and thick
7. after about 2 hours of initial cooking use a wooden spoon to mash about half of the mixture against the side of pot
8. continue to cook , stirring occasionally , for about another hour or until the mixture is creamy and the beans are soft
9. add more water if it becomes too thick
10. the mixture should be soupy but not watery
11. remove the bay leaves and serve with steamed rice
demonstrations.review: "oh yeah, this is it!" is 1 million % right!!!  THIS IS OUTSTANDING!! As good if not better than some of the spots in the French Quarter. My boyfriend and i went to N.O. for the weekend for the NFC Championship game and we ate this dish A LOT and when we got back to Cali, decided to do a Big Easy Super Bowl party and make some of the "staples"...this was a HIT, everybody raved and most went back for seconds.  I followed the recipe EXACTLY, the only thing i added was a tablespoon of worstechire sauce and i used a pound and a half of andouille sausage...that's it.  i SCOURED recipezaar looking for an authentic RB&R recipe that would take me to Bourbon St. and beyond and THIS IS IT!!  look no further...this is the recipe you want.  10 cups of water sounded like a lot, but it's PERFECT, the exact consistency after about 3 hours-ish of simmering...also, the ham hock, although gross looking, is really key too...don't leave it out 'cause it adds SO much flavor.  i can't thank you enough...this is the ONLY Red Beans and Rice recipe i will ever use!  :-)   WHO DAT!!!!

target.recipe_text:
corn  crab  and chipotle chowder

sweet and spicy.the cob add a little more flavor but can be ommitted.

1. heat butter in a large saucepan add onions , peppers , celery , potatoes , and garlic seasoned with salt and pepper cooking till translucent
2. add chipotle peppers , clam juice and corn kernels and cobs
3. simmer 15 minutes remove cobs and leave as much broth in pot toss cobs
4. add cream simmer 5 more minutes
5. add crabmeat to heat and season with salt and pepper to taste
target.review: This is a great chowder that has a wonderful taste.  I followed the recipe expect I used a 10oz container of frozen corn, use only 1lb. of crab meat and used skim evaporated milk for the cream. I'll will be making this again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
caramelized onion dip spread

this is fantastic on grilled burgers, and also can be served as a dip for crackers or potato chips, make as spicy as you like by adjusting the tabasco sauce

1. heat the butter and oil in the frypan over medium heat
2. add in onions , cayenne , salt and pepper
3. saut for about 8 minutes
4. add in garlic and cook for 2-3 minutes
5. reduce heat to medium-low and cook stirring occasionally for 20 minutes more until onions are brown and caramelized
6. cool
7. in a bowl , beat the cream cheese , sour cream and mayonnaise until smooth
8. add in onions
9. mix well to combine
10. add in tabasco sauce if using
11. cover and place in fridge for 2 or more hours before using
demonstrations.review: This is a great dip.  I chopped the onions for ease of eating.  I didn't add the butter and I cut back on the oil.  I'll be making this often as it will go great on many things.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
amazing homemade pizza rolls

my dh loves those frozen tony's pizza rolls....i'll eat them too, but....what exactly is in them?? we probably don't want to even know! these are much better and at least we know what we're eating!! buy extra sauce for dipping if you'd like, but they really don't need it. also, add/omit any ingredients you like or don't like. make them to your own taste of course. this is what we like in them.

1. combine above ingredients except wrappers
2. place a cup filling in center of each egg roll
3. fold bottom corner over filling
4. fold sides toward center over filling
5. moisten remaining corner w / water and roll up tightly to seal
6. fry in 1 of 375 oil for 1-2 minutes til golden brown
7. serve with addition pizza sauce for dipping if desired
demonstrations.review: These rolls are great.  They came together fairly quickly. Once folded, I brushed the seams with water.  I baked them at 400 for 15 to 20 mins. instead of frying them.  What we didn't eat I froze.  This is now our new Pizza fix.  thanks for sharing.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
scallion sesame turkey burger

i found this in some random cookbook.  one of the best turkey burgers ever.  full of flavor.  make an extra for lunch the next day, reheats beautifully.

1. mix togeter , gently
2. the turkey , sesame seeds , soy , scallions , cilantro , garlic , sesame oil , 1 teaspoon of salt , and bread crumbs
3. form into patties
4. i usually mix all this together and make patties in the morning and leave in the refrigerator till i'm ready for them
5. sometimes that is the next day
6. brush with a little oil before grilling if desired
7. grill on the george foreman , in a grill pan
8. if you're using the outside grill increase the breadcrumbs a bit to insure they don't fall apart
demonstrations.review: These tasty crunchy burgers are wonderful.  I did make them the night before and let them sit overnight in the  refrigerator.  They grilled up beautifully.

target.recipe_text:
pumpkin pie crunch

several reviewers complain about the recipe being too sweet and/or too buttery as originally written. i've included the amounts i use, which i think are 'just right'. also, since i usually don't have pumpkin pie spice in the house, i use 1 1/2 tsp. cinnamon, 1/2 tsp. nutmeg, 1/4 tsp. cloves and 1/2 tsp. ginger instead. (tip: using 2/3 of the cake mix instead of half makes it easy to make 8 cupcakes with the remaining box since the mix calls for 3 eggs.)

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. grease bottom of 13x9x2-inch pan
3. combine pumpkin , evaporated milk , eggs , sugar , pumpkin pie spice and salt in large bowl
4. pour into pan
5. sprinkle dry cake mix evenly over pumpkin mixture
6. top with pecans
7. drizzle with melted butter
8. bake at 350f for 50 to 55 minutes or until golden
9. cool completely
10. serve with whipped topping
11. refrigerate leftovers
target.review: That recipe was a big hit. I made 2 because I only used half the cake mix for each pie and half a cup of margarine to put on the top but it did not last long because they loved it. I just made another one but I only put half the sugar because I found it too sweet the first time. Thank you for sharing.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
ultimate brownies

from the 1990 collection 

1. preheat oven to 325f degrees
2. melt chocolate and butter together in large bowl
3. add sugars
4. mix well
5. add eggs and vanilla , mix well
6. add flour and salt
7. stir until blended
8. add walnuts
9. pour into greased 13x9 pan
10. bake 25 minutes
11. let cool
12. make frosting-------------
13. melt chocolate and butter together
14. stir in milk
15. add powdered sugar
16. beat for 3 minutes or until smooth
demonstrations.review: These are very good but the frosting is a little too sweet.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
tex mex tortilla casserole for a crowd

this is great to take to a church function or a get together as it makes two casseroles.

1. set oven to 350 degrees f
2. grease two 13 x 9-inch baking pans
3. in a large dutch oven , cook the first 4 ingredients , stirring often until the ground beef is browned and cooked
4. drain fat
5. add in fresh garlic , season with salt and pepper and stir for 2-3 minutes
6. line the 2 baking dishes with 6 tortillas
7. divide the beef mixture between the two dishes on top of the tortillas
8. top the ground beef with 1 can of beans , then sprinkle with 2 cup cheese
9. top with the remaining tortillas
10. spread two jars salsa over each casserole
11. sprinkle with remaining cheese
12. cover casseroles with foil
13. bake for 45 minutes
14. remove foil , bake 10-15 minutes more , or until cheese is golden
demonstrations.review: I made this recipe for Easter and everybody loved it, even one of my daughter that does not like ground beef.  Thank you for sharing that recipe that makes a different meal (a special meal).

demonstrations.recipe_text:
deviled chicken crock pot

slow cooked chicken with a honey, mustard, garlic and curry sauce.

1. place chicken in slow cooker
2. combine all remaining ingredients and pour over chicken
3. cook for 4 to 6 hours on high or 6 to 8 hours on low
4. to freeze: prepare and cook recipe as directed
5. allow to cool and freeze in a freezer bag or container
6. to serve: reheat in the microwave
demonstrations.review: It was very good and moist. The chicken looked darker than the one in your photo. Thanks for sharing. I will make this again.

target.recipe_text:
crispy baked potatoes

this is a fantastic way to enjoy crispy potatoes. i love to serve this with my recipe for recipe #99104. i hope you enjoy it! the recipe is from better homes & gardens / great cooking for two.

1. scrub potatoes thoroughly with a vegetable brush
2. cut potatoes in half lengthwise
3. in an 11" x 7" x 1 1 / 2" or 9" x 9" x 2" baking pan , combine melted butter , garlic or seasoned salt , and pepper
4. place potatoes , cut side down , in butter mixture
5. bake in a 450f oven for 25 to 30 minutes or until tender and cut sides of potatoes are browned and crispy
6. lift out with a spatula
7. if desired , serve with sour cream and / or chives
8. enjoy !
target.review: Simple, quick & yummy!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
oven roasted potatoes with garlic and rosemary

the original version came from cuisine at home.  this is a truly easy side dish that is great for company.  it goes wonderfully with roasted meat or chicken.  prep time includes 20 minutes resting time prior to roasting.

1. in a saucepan large enough to hold all of the potato chunks , bring water to a boil
2. add potatoes , and boil for 2 minutes
3. you are not trying to cook the potatoes through at this point
4. in a large bowl , combine the oil , garlic , rosemary , salt and pepper
5. be generous with the salt , or the potatoes will be bland
6. drain the potatoes well , and add to the oil and garlic mixture
7. mix gently , but thoroughly
8. cover bowl , and let sit for at least 20 minutes , and up to 2 hours
9. preheat oven to 450
10. place potato mixture in a roasting pan
11. bake for 20 minutes
12. toss potatoes with a spatula
13. return to the oven for 10 more minutes until cooked through and golden brown
14. check seasonings , and add more salt or pepper as needed
15. serve immediately
demonstrations.review: I make this all the time! Such an easy, yummy side. Today, after roasting I am going to toss the potatoes with feta and fresh dill!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
best blueberry muffins  cook s illustrated

from the cook's illustrated website: this recipe does not require a standing mixer, but when making the batter, be sure to whisk vigorously in step 2, then fold carefully in step 3. there should be no large pockets of flour in the finished batter, but small occasional sprays may remain. do not overmix the batter. these muffins are great unadorned, but for an extra flourish, give them a dip in sugar by following one of the variations.

makes 12 muffins

1. adjust oven rack to middle position and heat oven to 350 degrees
2. spray standard muffin tin with nonstick vegetable cooking spray
3. whisk flour , baking powder , and salt in medium bowl until combined
4. whisk egg in second medium bowl until well-combined and light-colored , about 20 seconds
5. add sugar and whisk vigorously until thick and homogenous , about 30 seconds
6. add melted butter in 2 or 3 steps , whisking to combine after each addition
7. add sour cream in 2 steps , whisking just to combine
8. add frozen berries to dry ingredients and gently toss to combine
9. add sour cream mixture and fold with rubber spatula until batter comes together and berries are evenly distributed , 25 to 30 seconds
10. do not overmix
11. use ice cream scoop or large spoon to drop batter into greased muffin tin
12. bake until light golden brown and toothpick or skewer inserted into center of muffin comes out clean , 25 to 30 minutes , rotating pan from front to back halfway through baking time
13. invert muffins onto wire rack , stand muffins upright , and cool 5 minutes
demonstrations.review: BEST recipe! I have yet to make the glaze, no need to! Love Cook's Illustrated, and this is why! Thanks for sharing!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
quick homemade applesauce   no sugar added

a quick, easy homemade applesauce recipe that i served with potato latkes this year. it has no added sugar, which makes it a better option for diabetics and low-carb people and others who avoid cane sugar. but if you prefer a sweeter sauce, add 1/2 cup of sugar. i recommend using 1/2 sweet apples (i like braeburn) and 1/2 tart apples (granny smith, for example). don't leave out the salt, it's a necessary ingredient for a good applesauce!

1. peel and core apples
2. cut apples into approximately 1 inch cubes
3. add all ingredients to pot , and turn heat on high
4. bring to a boil , then cover and reduce heat to low
5. simmer for 20 minutes or until the apples have softened significantly
6. stir frequently , making sure that the apples are not sticking to the bottom of the pot
7. add more water if necessary
8. remove lemon slices
9. mash with a potato masher or use a food mill for a smoother consistency
10. serve warm or at room temperature
demonstrations.review: wonderful & simple. I made this recipe for my baby & she loves it (0h, so does my DH!!) !

target.recipe_text:
best banana bread

you'll never need another banana bread recipe ever again!

1. remove odd pots and pans from oven
2. preheat oven to 350 / 180
3. cream together butter and sugar
4. add eggs and crushed bananas
5. combine well
6. sift together flour , soda and salt
7. add to creamed mixture
8. add vanilla
9. mix just until combined
10. do not overmix
11. pour into greased and floured loaf pan
12. bake at 350 / 180 for 55 minutes
13. keeps well , refrigerated
target.review: Awsome, easy and really great to give to family.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
non alcoholic korean strawberry punch

desserts are not common in korea but they do enjoy some fresh fruit or a fresh fruit punch like this one. very nice end to a korean dinner or any other dinner this recipe was originally from 

1. boil the water and sugar together , stir until the sugar is dissolved , boil ten minutes and let it completely cool place strawberries& ginger in a large bowl and pour in the sugar syrup
2. cover and put in the fridge for about 2 hours to chill
3. remove ginger and pour into glasses or punch cups garnish with a few pine nuts on top and serve
demonstrations.review: Great to serve during the summertime, thank you!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
foolproof  dark chocolate fudge

i make this at christmas, but why not try it any time of year. summer is not the best time for fudge, especially if it is hot, but this one seems to turn out whenever...enjoy!

1. over low heat , melt the chips in the sweetened condensed milk
2. remove from the heat and stir in the nuts and vanilla
3. spread evenly into an aluminum foil lined 8x8 or 9x9 pan
4. chill and pop out of pan
5. peel off foil and cut into 1-inch squares
demonstrations.review: easy quick and awsome!! Super fast prep time and great for anyone who loves chocolate!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
rio grande valley style carne guisada

this texmex beef stew recipe was adapted from the recipe used by sylvia's enchilada kitchen, a popular houston restaurant.  i add one chopped jalapeno pepper with the green bell pepper (not listed below), and serve it with a mound of mexican rice (like #41167) in the bowl.

1. cube meat , removing all fat and gristle
2. sear meat in oil
3. add water and cook on medium-low heat for about 30 minutes , stirring occasionally
4. toast cumin seeds in a small saut skillet on medium-high until they begin to smoke slightly
5. grind the hot cumin seeds with a mortar and pestle
6. add oregano , ground toasted cumin , black pepper , salt and garlic to the meat
7. add vegetables and continue to cook about 30 minutes
8. add tomato sauce , chili powder and paprika
9. continue to simmer for another 15-20 minutes
10. while the meat is simmering , heat 2 tbsp oil in a small saut pan and add flour over medium-low heat
11. stir the flour and oil constantly until the flour turns a light golden brown
12. add the roux to the meat and continue to simmer for about another 30 minutes
13. serve carne guisada with rice and beans and flour or corn tortillas
demonstrations.review: Wow, Is all I have to say, it does take some time to make but it is well worth it. The meat came out tender and flavorful and I will be using this again A++.

target.recipe_text:
chicken salad for sandwiches

simple old-fashioned chicken salad which is perfect for sandwiches or stuffing tomatoes. although the recipe calls for boiling uncooked chicken leftover chicken would also work fine and give wonderful flavor to the chicken salad. recipe source: local newspaper

1. place chicken , celery stalk and onion in saucepan with water to cover
2. bring to a boil and simmer 20 minutes or until chicken is done
3. drain and discard onion and celery
4. let chicken cool
5. in a food processor chop chicken
6. in a medium sized bowl combine chicken with mayonnaise , salt& pepper , parsley , dill seed , chopped celery and lemon juice
7. cover and refrigerate until chilled
target.review: This is a quick and easy recipe. I didn't put all of the mayo in and added a bit of ranch dressing. This is a definite keeper.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pineapple glaze for baked ham

posted at the request of my sister. glazing a ham while cooking is wonderful but the first person to the platter usually makes off the the glazed ends and the rest of the people get a "glazed rim". the solution in our house is to make lots of glaze and pour it over each slice!

1. place all ingredients in a small saucepan including the juice / syrup from the pineapple
2. turn heat on to medium and stir constantly to prevent burning
3. continue to heat until mixture thickens and comes to a boil
4. allow mixture to boil for approximately 1 minute
5. if mixture refuses to thicken , add more cornstarch- a little at a time
6. pour finished sauce into a serving bowl , complete with a ladle , and let your guests pour it over baked sliced ham
demonstrations.review: This is a to die for glaze for my ham on Easter!!!!! I'll definitely make it again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
panera broccoli cheese soup

a very good broccoli cheese soup. served with crusty bread.

1. saut onion in butter
2. set aside
3. cook melted butter and flour using a whisk over medium heat for 3-5 minutes or until you see a noticeable golden brown color in your pan
4. slowly add in the chicken stock and whisk again to combine
5. simmer contents covered for 20 minutes on medium heat
6. add the broccoli , carrots and the sauteed onions , into the pot
7. stir , add the milk and half & half
8. cook covered over low heat 20-25 minutes but do not bring to a boil
9. this may cause the milk to curdle
10. add salt , pepper & nutmeg
11. continue to cook the soup on low heat and slowly add the grated cheese a handful at a time and stir to avoid clumps
12. once all the cheese has been added is melted , remove from heat , and serve immediately
13. suggestion: serve with crusty bread or in a breadbowl
14. refrigerate leftovers after they have cooled and store in a airtight container up to 5 days in the refrigerator
demonstrations.review: Awesome soup!! It goes great with a few slices of sour dough bread. I did puree it and it turned out so wonderfully thick!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
the best almond paste bars

a dutch treat, these are better than any you will find in a bakery. be careful not to eat the whole pan ;)

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. beat together butter , flour , oil , first cup of sugar , baking powder , and first round of eggs until smooth and set aside
3. beat together the almond paste , second cup of sugar , second round of eggs and almond flavoring until smooth
4. combine both mixtures
5. grease a 9x13" pan , and evenly pour in mixture
