6. bake for 30 to 45 minutes until toothpick comes out clean
7. enjoy !
demonstrations.review: If you like almond, these are great! I didn't have any almond flavoring so I skipped that and they still taste great. I can't wait to gt some flavoring and try it again. They are very moist and a bit chewy. I'll definitely do these again!

target.recipe_text:
ghirardelli brownies

here's a copycat recipe worth keeping!

1. grease a 8x8 inch baking pan and set aside
2. preheat oven to 400 degrees
3. in a medium bowl stir together the eggs , sugar and vanilla
4. mix well
5. add butter mixing to incorporate
6. sift the ground chocolate with the flour , baking powder and salt
7. stir into the egg mixture and add the walnuts
8. spread into the prepared baking pan
9. bake for 20 minutes or until a toothpick inserted in center comes out clean
target.review: An excellent recipe! My wife made this the other day and I've never had better brownies in my life!  I've had ones layered with coconut flakes, different icings,different nuts even but this recipe is so simple and yet produced the most exquisitely delicate melt -in-your-mouth brownie nirvana:)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cabbage and potato fry

an indianised way to cook cabbage, and our favorite preparation of the vegetable. if you have a grinder, take the trouble to roast and grind the coriander seeds - the freshly roasted flavor is worth the effort.

1. quarter , core and shred cabbage
2. heat oil over medium heat
3. when hot , add cumin and mustard seeds and wait till they sputter
4. then add finely sliced onion
5. allow onion to soften and then throw in the shredded cabbage
6. add salt , turmeric and coriander powders
7. close pot , reduce heat slightly and allow to cook until cabbage wilts
8. as soon as cabbage reduces in volume , add small pieces of diced potatoes and continue cooking on medium heat till potatoes soften and cabbage is tender
9. if desired , add in shredded coconut with potatoes as allow to cook as in previous step
10. garnish with coriander sprigs
11. goes well as a low-fat option with parathas
demonstrations.review: I have eaten this often enough so it's about time I added my 5-stars with the rest of the reviewers. For a person who normally doesn't like cabbage which I had only ever found bland, this was a dish that got me hooked onto it. An added bonus is the nutrition-specs: it's low-cal, low-fat and zero-cholesterol.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kachumber   fresh tomato  cucumber  and onion relish

a spicy tomato, cucumber and onion relish that is a refreshing accompaniment to most indian meals. i like it a bit on the spicy side, but you can adjust the amount of peppers to your own taste.

1. combine all ingredients , mixing well
2. serve chilled
3. goes well with spicy curries
demonstrations.review: this is a really tasty relish to temper the heat of curries. this is made very often by my mom and sisters back home too.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mattar paneer

this was one of the first dishes i cooked for my husband when i was newly married, and it's the recipe i get most requested to make. i have managed to make it less fattening so we can eat it more often by successfully substituting the cream with fatfree half&half or even fatfree yoghurt sometimes (of course it won't taste quite as good as it does with heavy cream). i always use my own homemade paneer in this, and i also roast and grind my own cumin and coriander to bring out the best flavors, but you don't have to do that.

1. heat oil and fry paneer cubes till they turn golden brown
2. set aside
3. in a separate pot , heat oil and mustard and cumin seeds , until they turn color and sputter
4. add chopped onions , ginger and garlic and cook until onions soften
5. add tomato , salt , sugar , and cook till the tomatoes soften
6. then add garam masala , chilli powder , turmeric powder coriander powder and cumin powder
7. add the water and stir it in , using your discretion depending on how dry the dish is
8. if you added too much water , just let it simmer away until much of it evaporates - you want your tomatoes soft anyway
9. add the peas
10. cook just until the peas are tender
11. pour in the cream , mix , and add the paneer and let simmer on medium heat for the paneer to absorb the flavors
12. garnish with cilantro
demonstrations.review: I made this today and can't recommend this highly enough! Would give it dozens of stars:) Varsha, I haven't had a better paneer dish at  even places like Leela Palace or the Oberoi. Kudos on an amazing recipe - so fragrant, flavorful and colorful. Wonderfully creamy as well which left a lingering smooth satisfying aftertaste with every mouthful of this heavenly indulgence:)

target.recipe_text:
thunder thigh pecan pie

our community recently had an old fashioned pie contest and this is the winning pie by cindy tymkiw. it looks easy and the raves about it could be heard miles away. cindy says 

1. beat together sugar , flour , cornsyrup , vanilla and eggs
2. stir in the pecans& butter pour into the pie crust
3. bake at 350f for 40-50 minutes or until the center is puffed and golden , cool& serve
target.review: Terrific!  I made two different pecan pies on Thanksgiving and let my pecan pie loving father-in-law choose his favorite...yours won!  Thanks for a great recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
baked ziti

good italian comfort food!

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees fahrenheit
2. cook ziti according to package directions
3. drain
4. set aside
5. mix ricotta , egg , parsley , 1-1 / 2 cups of the mozarella cheese , and parmesan cheese in a large bowl
6. mix cooked sausage and pasta in with ricotta mixture
7. mix in 3 / 4 jar of sauce
8. transfer mixture into a 2 quart casserole dish
9. top with the rest of the sauce and mozarella cheese
10. bake for 30 to 35 minutes , or until hot and bubbly
11. to freeze: cover dish with foil and freeze
12. when frozen you can pop it out of the container and put in a freezer bag if desired
13. to heat: thaw
14. preheat oven to 350 degrees fahrenheit
15. cover and bake for 20 minutes
16. uncover and bake for 10-15 minutes more
demonstrations.review: Very good! A big hit with adults and children.  It made enough for leftovers with our family of 5.  Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pasta with sausage  tomatoes  and cream

delicious and satisfying... i don't remember where this recipe comes from, but it's a pleaser! easily doubled.  also, works well with gf pasta and sausage

1. heat oil in a heavy skillet over medium heat
2. add sausage and crushed red pepper
3. cook until sausage is no longer pink , stirring frequently , about 7 minutes
4. add onion and garlic to skillet and cook until onion is tender and sausage is light brown , stirring occasionally , about 7 minutes
5. add tomatoes , cream , and salt
6. simmer until mixture thickens slightly , about 4 minutes
7. cook pasta in large pot of boiling water
8. drain
9. bring sauce to a simmer
10. add pasta to sauce and cook until pasta is heated through and sauce thickens , stirring occasionally , about 2 minutes
11. divide pasta between plates
12. sprinkle with parsley
13. serve , passing parmesan separately
demonstrations.review: So delicious, so pretty!  I made this using stewed tomatoes and macaroni pasta (it was all I had on hand), and it turned out well.  Visually, I'd prefer to stick with the long tubular pasta.  I would serve this to guests or anyone!  Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
spooktacular halloween graveyard cake

this is a great cake, perfect for halloween parties, that is a take-off of the stand-by graveyard pudding. i noticed pudding is less popular than cake, and of course, cake is more suited for parties, especially those with kids. you can use your choice of cake flavor, but pay attention to the cookie crumbs you use in that case so they are compatible flavors. you also probably wouldn't want to use chocolate icing with a pumpkin cake, but if you wanted a pumpkin frosting, that would be good, or else use vanilla.you can use whipped cream to make the ghosties, but be aware that if you do this, the cake needs to remain chilled, and the whipped cream does try to sag and run after awhile (so don't do that too far in advance). the marshmallow ghosties are more durable at room temp. those are often sold near displays of halloween candy, not necessarily by the bags of marshmallows.

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. mix together cake mix , water , oil , and eggs according to package directions
3. if your package requires different ingredients to make cake , follow those instructions instead
4. grease and flour a glass 13x9-inch cake pan
5. if you use a dark or coated pan , do your baking at 325f
6. pour batter into prepared pan and bake in a preheated oven for approx 35 minutes or until cake is done
7. allow cake to cool in the pan
8. spread frosting evenly on cooled cake
9. sprinkle frosting with crumbled cookies
10. using gel frostings , write sayings on 1 / 2 of the milano cookies
11. press 1 / 2 of cookie down into cake and icing to resemble a standing tombstone
12. arrange ghost marshmallows in a standing position on top of cake
13. scatter candies and / or sprinkles or sugars on cake to garnish
demonstrations.review: Delicious & Fun cake!  I made a buttercream icing to go with it.  I threw a little Halloween party for our family & the cake was a big hit!

target.recipe_text:
autumn apple cheesecake

mmmmm good

1. --------crust-------------
2. heat oven to 350f degrees
3. mix crumbs , pecans , sugar , cinnamon and marg:press onto bottom of a 9-inch springform pan
4. bake 10 minutes
5. ---------filling---------
6. beat cream cheese and 1 / 2 c of the sugar at med
7. speed until well blended
8. add eggs , 1 at a time , mixing well after each
9. blend in vanilla
10. pour over crust
11. toss apples with combined 1 / 3 c sugar and the cinnamon
12. spoon mixture over cream cheese layer
13. sprinkle with chopped pecans
14. bake 1 hour and 10 minutes
15. loosen cake from rim of pan
16. cool before removing rim of pan
17. refrigerate
target.review: My family put together a fall-themed meal. Everyone thought this cheesecake was a hit! Even my husband who normally doesn't like cheesecake, liked it! I will definitely use this recipe again!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
beth s pizza crust

this is an excellent crust that requires no time to rise. why order out when you can just throw this pizza together?

1. combine yeast and warm water
2. stir until dissolved
3. add remaining ingredients and mix well
4. let rest 5 minutes
5. roll out to size and shape you need
6. bake at 450 for 15 minutes or until golden
7. a couple
8. instead , i add several good shakes of italian seasoning mix
9. use your imagination , this is hard to mess up
demonstrations.review: Delicious! Such a quick and easy recipe that tastes good, too! I made this with our favorite toppings-ham & pineapple! I just baked the crust for 10 min. added the toppings, and then baked another 5. Thinking about making homeade pizza every friday night:)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
amanda s thai peanut

by far the best and healthiest thai peanut i've ever tasted. it's highly requested by family and friends!!!  this quick recipe is just for two people, but it doubles and triples extremely well when we have company over. give it a try!!

1. in a large pot , cook fettucini as directed
2. towards the end of the pasta cooking , add the broccoli into the pot to cook for approximately 3-4 minutes
3. in a greased large saucepan , heat garlic on med-high heat for 2 minutes
4. add red pepper flakes , ginger , and brown sugar into the saucepan
5. allow to cook another 2 minutes
6. add soy sauce , rice wine vinegar , and peanut butter to the saucepan
7. use a spaghetti spoon or whisk to mix in the peanut butter to the liquid to form a sauce
8. when the sauce begins to bubble , add the cooked pasta / broccoli to the saucepan
9. mix well
10. add the carrot
11. mix well to prevent clumps
12. enjoy !
demonstrations.review: For some reason I was hungry for ethnic food-and something with peanut butter. I wasn't too sure about this recipe because of some of the reviews. I added a lot less hot pepper so it was spicy, but not overpowering. It really did have great flavor! The sauce seemed a bit dry-kind of that "stick-to-the-roof-of-your-mouth-peanut buttery" taste. It was good for something different, but probably wouldn't make it again

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chicken and sweet potato curry

from bc best chicken cookbook.

1. in a heavy-duty plastic zip-lock bag , add the flour , curry powder , and salt
2. shake to mix
3. add in the chicken
4. seal bag , shake until the chicken is evenly coated
5. heat oil in a large nonstick skillet over medium-high heat
6. add in the chicken
7. stir-fry for 2-3 minutes or until browned
8. stir any remaining flour mixture into the apple juice
9. add apple juice , sweet potatoes , and chili to the chicken
10. stir
11. cover and cook 10-15 minutes , stirring occasionally , until the chicken is no longer pink and potatoes are tender
12. stir in jelly until melted
13. serve over hot cooked couscous
demonstrations.review: Curry is definitely one of my favorite seasonings! I love trying new recipes and this one caught my eye. The only change I made was adding a little chili powder instead of an actual chili. Delicious with couscous!

target.recipe_text:
shortcake  sockerkaka

nan

1. butter a cake pan , cover sides with breadcrumbs
2. turn on oven 350 f
3. whip sugar and eggs until almost white
4. mix flour , baking powder and flavoring
5. melt the margarine
6. add all ingredients to batter
7. stir quickly until smooth
8. pour into cake pan , bake for about 30-40 min , until golden brown
target.review: Yes, ridiculously easy and fast!  I'm not much of a baker, but this turns out great for me every time.  I'm up to my elbows in strawberries and this cake is a wonderful accompaniment.  Thanks.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
simple shrimp and zucchini saute

this is super easy. we really like to just dump this on top of boiled potatoes.

1. melt butter in non-stick skillet on med-hi heat
2. add shrimp
3. saute 1 minute
4. add zucchini , saute 2 minutes
5. add tomato , seasoning , salt and red pepper
6. cook and stir for 3 minutes
7. transfer to plate
8. sprinkle with parmesan
demonstrations.review: This recipe is great for when you have frozen shrimp and a zucchini and no idea what to do with either of them.  I used grape tomatoes, and a combo of butter and olive oil.  This tasted great and was dead easy.  It rocked our entire house. thanks.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
stuffed red bell peppers with tuna

i know this sounds different, but they are very good.  if you are trying to loose a few extra pounds they are great because they are low fat, low cal, and low carb.  i ate these a lot when i lost all my weight.  they are great for lunch, or you can even heat them up for dinner.  recipe is for one person.

1. slice red pepper in half and remove seeds
2. fill each half with equal amounts of tuna
3. sprinkle almonds on top of tuna
4. spread on salsa
5. cover each pepper with 2 slices of cheese
6. enjoy !
7. you can also heat them up in the microwave until they are warm
demonstrations.review: So easy and economical if you can find the red bell peppers on sale.  Here's a variation that worked well too:  I skipped the nuts, mixed in a tablespoon of sour cream with the salsa and used imitation crab when I had no tuna.  I zap the peppers in the microwave for three minutes because I like them slightly wilted rather than cold and crisp.  Great for lunch, portable and filling.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
tasty salisbury steak

good! good! good! i serve the gravy over mashed potatoes with a side salad and hot rolls. not sure of prep and cook times.

1. mix together first 5 ingredients and shape into 4 oval patties about 3 / 4" thick
2. cook patties in skillet until brown on both sides
3. drain
4. add onion slices , broth and mushrooms
5. heat to boil then reduce to low and simmer about 15 minutes or until patties are done
6. remove patties to plate and keep warm
7. heat onion mixture to a boil
8. mix together water and cornstarch
9. stir into onion mixture in skillet and boil 1 minute , stirring
10. serve over patties
demonstrations.review:
You know what I really love about this recipe?
NO Campbell's cream of whatever soup.  Frugal and health conscious cooks like me really appreciate it. Thanks!

target.recipe_text:
le lasagne autentiche siciliane supreme

(authentic sicilian lasagna supreme)
this is a very old lasagna recipe handed down through many generations, and was given to me by an older sicilian woman. it takes a while to make, but is it ever worth the wait.

1. prepare the lasagna noodles according to package directions
2. drain and set aside
3. cook the ground beef and sausage
4. drain off the grease
5. add the onion , garlic and mushrooms to the meat / sausage mixture
6. saute until onion is tender
7. add the sugar , salt , basil , fennel seed , pepper , tomatoes and tomato paste
8. blend well
9. simmer for 1 hour
10. combine the eggs , ricotta cheese , parsley and salt
11. blend well
12. in the bottom of a very large baking pan , spread just enough of the meat mixture to cover the bottom
13. layer lasagna noodles , meat sauce , black olives , ricotta cheese mixture , mozzarella cheese , asiago cheese and parmesan cheese
14. repeat layering making sure to end with the parmesan cheese
15. cover with foil
16. bake at 375 degrees for 25 minutes
17. remove the foil and bake for 25 additional minutes
target.review: Ever since my honeymoon in Italy, I am always looking for authentic Italian dishes.  This was very good.  The sauce was scrumptious.  I made it in a 15 x 10 glass baking dish.  I had enough sauce and ricotta for 4 layers.  Before I tasted this, I was suspicious of the black olives.  They were great, though!  Also, when I made this, I bought 9 oz. olives, 16 oz parmesean and asiago cheese.  Next time, I won't do that.  I will measure the olives and cheese in a measuring cup rather than using the equivalent in ounces.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
whole wheat carrot cake with cream cheese frosting

i love carrot cake with cream cheese frosting. i make several different kinds. this one incorporates whole wheat flour.

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees f
2. butter 13 x 9 inch pyrex baking dish
3. combine oil , sugars and eggs in mixing bowl
4. sift together flours , cinnamon , soda and salt
5. mix into liquid ingredients
6. stir in carrots , pineapple with reserved juice and walnuts
7. bake about 45 minutes or until tester comes out clean
8. cool
9. ice with cream cheese frosting
demonstrations.review: I found a darn similar recipe in a Junior League cookbook.  It is the most amazing carrot cake that you will EVER eat.  My recipe calls for 1 1/4 c. vegetable oil, 1 c. less 2 T. whole wheat flour, 2 tsp. baking powder (in addition to the soda), 3 c. packed, finely shredded raw carrots, and 1/2 c. chopped nuts.  My lemon cream cheese frosting is substanially different.  Seriously, this cake is twice as good if you let it rest one day.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
creamy bean   tortilla soup

this is a hearty, quick meal that will get some food on the table fast. it's good too!

1. saute onion and celery in bacon grease you get from frying your bacon strips
2. combine all ingredients including the crumbled bacon and heat till hot
3. add water to desired consistency
4. soup should be creamy
5. serve with tortilla chips
demonstrations.review: This is very good. I used no salt added Rotel tomatoes, reduced the salt to 1/4 tsp, and drained off some of the bacon grease before adding the rest of the ingredients. Also, I used an immersion blender to make the soup smooth. I topped each bowl with crumbled bacon. Next time, I will cut the cayenne down to 1/8 tsp.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
sheila s black bean soup

i was shopping in a bulk food store one day and overheard a young man asking the clerk where some ingredients would be....said he had to buy for "the best black bean soup in the world"...had the recipe in his hand. long story short....clerk made a copy for me, and he was right!! turns out, i see now as i go to post, that it is from 'moosewood restaurant cooks at home'. i had never heard of moosewood restaurant 'til i came to 'zaar.....must be a super place to eat! prep. time includes cook time.

1. cover the sundried tomatoes with the boiling water and set aside
2. in a large pot heat oil and saute the onions , garlic and jalapeno pepper , stirring frequently until soft
3. add the cumin , 1 / 3 cup water and tomatoes
4. bring to a boil
5. cover and simmer over low heat for 5 minute
6. add the undrained black beans and continue to simmer , stirring occasionally to prevent sticking
7. drain and chop the sundried tomatoes and add to soup
8. cook 5-10 minutes longer
9. stir in cilantro and remove from heat
10. puree half the soup in food processor or blender and return to pot
11. if soup is too thick , add some water or tomato juice if you prefer
12. serve with a dollop of sour cream
demonstrations.review: This is a cross between chili and black bean soup, IMO.  It wasn't bad for a vegetarian black bean soup.  My tomatoes were also julienne sliced.  I used 1 c.  Also, I prefer whole canned tomatoes instead of diced.  I cut them when I put them in the soup.  Next time, I will blend everything except one can of black beans.  I think the cilantro really makes this soup.

target.recipe_text:
chocolate macaroons   no bake

i have been making this recipe since i was in the first grade. it was my teachers favourite.

1. boil first 4 ingredients for 2 minutes
2. remove from heat and add vanilla
3. pour over oatmeal and coconut and mix well
4. drop tsp fulls onto wax paper and wait until dry and easy to lift off paper
target.review: So good. I made this five days ago. My husband ate almost half of them in a day. I'm making them again right now. I might let the mixture boil a wee bit longer this time. I think I took them off early, because they were much softer than I expected.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mint julep kisses cookies

perfect for st. patrick's day or any day,these small green puffs are light, airy bites of mint flavored meringue with tiny bits of chocolate inside. they are very tasty and can be a little addictive! these don't keep long - plan to serve these very soon after making them. if you try the overnight method, make these before bedtime and your cookies will be ready and waiting in the morning. you can also make them early in the day and once the oven is completely cooled, they should be ready.

1. preheat gas oven to 325 degrees f
2. beat egg whites until stiff peaks form , gradually adding in the sugar while beating
3. add mint extract and food coloring
4. stir in the mini chocolate chips by hand
5. drop by teaspoonful onto parchment lined cookie sheets
6. set pans into oven and immediately turn off the heat and leave in the oven overnight - as the oven cools down , the cookies will cook
7. or set the pans in the preheated oven and immediately reduce the heat to 275 f and bake for 50 minutes
8. check 10 minutes early in case your oven runs hot- when done , they should be airy , light puffs that are very crisp and fragile on the exterior
9. instead , if you have an electric oven , simply preheat your oven to 275f and cook for 40-50 minutes
demonstrations.review: I liked this recipe- but I had a few problems with it. First I added the peppermint extract too early, and the whole shebang collapsed, then, on my second attempt, I added the sugar too late, and the whole thing collapsed. When I finally spooned it onto the sheet they looked kind of gross, but when they came out they tasted fine. So, thank you for this easy enough recipe. :)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mild spicy homemade salsa

we finally came up with a salsa recipe we enjoy making almost as much as we enjoy eating it! this is a big hit with our friends and family, and hope you enjoy it too. alter the quantities to fit your taste.

1. mix all ingredients together in saucepan
2. simmer until proper thickness- approximately 30-45 minutes
3. chill in fridge until ready to serve
demonstrations.review: I loved this recipe- but I did add some bell peppers- for colour more than anything else. But it's darned good.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
classic strawberry jam

this is a classic canadian recipe.  simple and delicious.  it's not thick, like pectin-based jams, but i think it's truer to the fruit and more delicious.  try it with recipe #62942 - perfect pairing.  eta:  many people have asked me why this recipe contains butter.  the butter prevents the jam from foaming while you're cooking it - the foam is unattractive and spoils the appearance of the jam.  adding a little butter eliminates this problem.

1. in a large saucepan , bring strawberries up to a simmer over medium-low heat , mashing roughly with a potato masher or flat spoon
2. add sugar and lemon juice , stir , and bring up to a simmer for 2 minutes
3. add butter and bring to a vigorous boil , stirring often , and cook for 10 to 20 minutes , periodically measuring the viscosity of the jam by dabbing a spoonful onto a plate and
4. once the jam slows its drip down the plate , remove from heat and skim off foam
5. fill jars that have been washed , rinsed , dried and boiled in a pot of water for 3 minutes to 1 / 4 inch from the top
6. fasten lids securely and boil jars in a vat of water for 15 minutes
7. remove jars with tongs and let cool upright
8. check for secure seals on jars and store in a cool place away from light for up to a year
9. any jars that do not achieve a proper seal should be refrigerated
demonstrations.review: My son and I picked somewhere near 16 ltrs of strawberries yesterday, and since I wanted to make jam, I tried this. Great recipe. I might add a bit of lemon rind next time to get it to jell a bit more, but the taste is wonderful. Now, what do I do with 10 jars of jam??? Yum.

target.recipe_text:
big breakfast cookie

i put the dry ingredients into baggies and store several baggies in the cupboard.  all i have to do in the morning is add the wet ingredients and bake while i am doing my animal chores and i have an amazingly filling breakfast.

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. spray cookie sheet with baking spray
3. mix all ingredients together
4. spoon 1 large mound on the baking sheet
5. bake 15-20 minutes
target.review: I made this yesterday and my daughter and I both thought it was so delicious! I used whole wheat for the flour and brown sugar instead of splenda. I also plumped my dry raisins with a touch of water in the micro for a few seconds and let sit while I got the other stuff together. Chewy but soft,just sweet enough, healthy, filling, and easy to make. I will be making these often. Thank you so much Budgiegirl for a fantastic recipe!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
oven baked pork chops

these are so good and tender. i don't remember where i got the recipe.

1. preheat oven tho 425 degrees
2. place butter or margarine in a 13x9x2 pan
3. put pan in oven for 3 minutes or until butter is melted
4. stir together egg and milk
5. put stuffing mix in a resealable bag and crush
6. dip pork chops in egg mixture
7. coat with stuffing mix
8. put chops on top of melted butter in pan
9. bake 20 minutes
10. turn
11. bake 10-15 minutes more
demonstrations.review: This is my most favorite chop recipe!! I always use cornbread mix and StoveTop seems to work the best for some reason. I don't crush the mix and I brine my chops first so they don't end up being tough and chewy. My fam thinks they are good but I think they are fabulous and so easy! Gonna have to buy some stuffing mix and make these again!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
stuffed green bell pepper soup

nan

1. in 6-quart saucepan or dutch oven , brown beef
2. drain
3. add remaining ingredients
4. bring to boil
5. reduce heat
6. cover and simmer for 30 to 40 minutes or until tender
7. makes about 16 servings
demonstrations.review: I loved this soup so much I may never make stuffed peppers again! This was so fast and easy to put together and so yummy! I halved the recipe but used less sugar and salt, a half pound ground beef, some chopped onion, 2 cloves of garlic, and about 3/4 cup uncooked instant brown rice instead of white rice for a thicker soup. I served with "Momma's Bestest Biscuits" for a fantastic dinner! Thank you for sharing this wonderful recipe Debe!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
easiest penne with vodka

hands down, this is the easiest version of a delicious main dish. it suits a busy family night or dinner with good friends. adapted from the 

1. heat butter in large skillet over medium-low heat
2. stir in vodka , seasoned or crushed red pepper , and cayenne
3. heat gently for two minutes
4. carefully add tomatoes and salt
5. increase heat to high and cook until mixture thickens , about 5 minutes
6. lower heat , and stir in heavy cream and parmesan cheese
7. add the penne , and toss with sauce
demonstrations.review: This was easy, fast, and delicious. I used margarine,a pinch of crushed red pepper, no cayenne, about 1 cup or so of half and half, and rotini pasta. I also added some Italian spice mix and a couple of sliced, cooked chicken breast. I loved this dish but sadly, the fam was not excited by it so I will probably not make again. Thanks for a yummy recipe rochsann!

target.recipe_text:
pete s scratch pancakes

it was the fall of 1987 when pete nyhus walked into our office, just to visit. we started talking about breakfast, and he reached into a wastepaper basket and pulled out a scrap of teletype paper. he wrote out this recipe, and my family has never used pre-mix since.

1. mix the dry items first
2. combine the eggs and melted butter to the milk and slowly stir into the flour mixture
3. let sit at least 10 minutes while heating the pan
4. these will be high , but light and fluffy --
target.review: great recipe for pancakes! and ingredients i usually have in hand. thanks for sharing!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
uncle bill s fried potatoes and onions

i remember my grandmother making this marvelous dish over 65 years ago.  we were the only vegetarians in our family and therefore grandma cooked just to please me.
a very easy, simple but tasty side dish.
young potatoes are especially good.

1. peel and slice potatoes about 1 / 8 inch thick or thinner
2. slice onion thinly
3. in a large frying pan on medium-high heat , melt butter , add olive oil
4. add sliced potatoes and onions , cover and fry for 10 minutes
5. using a spatula , turn the potatoes and onions over so they do not break apart
6. if potatoes appear too dry , add some additional butter
7. sprinkle with granulated garlic powder , dried dill weed , salt and pepper and continue to fry with cover removed for another 5 minutes or until potatoes begin to turn slightly brown
8. turning occasionally
9. serve hot with your meal
10. add to the potatoes after the first 10 minutes of cooking time
demonstrations.review: love how easy and quick this was to make. nice easy way to make potatoes w/ out having to have the pain of baking it.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
katsudon

this can also be made with turkey or chicken and is a japanese dish. if you can't find mirin or panko, you can substitute sherry and breadcrumbs, but the flavor will be different

1. prepare rice , set aside to keep warm
2. simmer onions , broth , mirin , soy , and seasonings in a large pan over low heat for 15 minutes
3. meanwhile beat the eggs in a large bowl
4. mix flour , salt and pepper in a plate and pour panko in another plate
5. dredge pork in flour , dip into eggs , dip into panko--- then dip into eggs again and back into panko
6. double dipping insures a nice crust
7. cook in oil until browned on both sides , drain on paper towels
8. dip cutlets into broth , warm for 1 minute , slice and serve over rice , ladle onion broth over , sprinkle with scallions
demonstrations.review: omigosh chia....i gotta say I LOVE YOU!!! lol. i lived in japan for a year. and one of the famous signature food was katsudon. it was just my favorite. ate it all the time. but once i moved back to the states...i wasn't able to find any restaurants that could replicate that flavor that i miss. and then i found your recipe..and omigosh...it's VERY AUTHENTIC in taste. only difference in japan was that it had a thin layer of egg that was obviously dipped in the yummy sauce around the crispy pork cutlet.  this really was delicioius and it took me back to japan. this has beat out all my favorite recipes on recipezaar. this is now going on my #1. katsudon is originally made w/ pork but i made mine w/ thin sliced chicken breast. i think i like it better w/ chicken! THANK YOU so much for posting and sharing this recipe. you have no idea how happy you've made me and my family to have found this!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
shish kabob marinade

i got this recipe from a friend of mine. it is so easy to make and works for chicken, pork, beef or venison. cook time is 

1. mix all ingredients together
2. add meat and vegetables
3. marintate in refrigerator for at least a couple hours
4. thread onto skewers and grill
demonstrations.review: delicious! and the best part is that this has ingredients that i normally have around. wasn't too sweet at all. just perfect. will use this from now on and will go into my favorites.

target.recipe_text:
chicken scaloppine with lemon glaze   low fat and delicious

this is a wonderful lower-fat restaurant-quality dish that is easy to make, i also like to add in a few tablespoons of capers and cook with the lemon glaze if you are a lover of capers then add them in as it really adds to the flavour of this dish ---  this lemon sauce is not a heavy creamy sauce which is what makes this dish lower in fat, it is more like a glaze that soaks into the chicken, and i would strongly suggest to double or even triple the glaze i most always do, and please be certain to use only dry breadcrumbs as fresh will not stick to the chicken as well --- this is *very* good!

1. in a small bowl or shallow dish whisk together mustard and eggs
2. set aside
3. combine the dry bread crumbs with poultry seasoning , garlic powder and seasoning salt
4. spread on a piece of waxed paper
5. dip the breasts firstly in egg / mustard mixture then coat well with the crumb mixture , pressing downs with hands to adhear the crumbs to the breast
6. heat the olive oil in a skillet over medium heat
7. add in the chicken and cook for about 5 minutes on each side , or until it is no longer pink inside
8. remove and transfer to a plate to keep warm
9. for the glaze
10. in the same skillet add in the broth , lemon juice and 1 / 4 teaspoon salt bring to a boil scraping any brown bits from the pan
11. add in lemon slices and parsley
12. mix to combine for about 1 minute
13. spoon the glaze / sauce over chicken
14. delicious !
target.review: Delicious and so easy to prepare.  Definately taste like a meal at a 5 star restaurant.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
sweet potatoes with red curry paste

so simple, so tasty

1. place potatoes in a saute pan , cover with chicken stock and swirl in the red curry paste
2. cook covered until tender
3. reserve liquid for another use like cooking rice
4. mash potatoes , add butter , salt and pepper to taste
demonstrations.review: Actually this was a very tasty recipe.  Except for the fact that I used the whole tablespoon of red curry.  Haven't worked our way up to someething quite this hot so next time  will decrease the curry to maybe 1 1/2 tsp. and work my way up.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
so it s bekah s pulled pork now

i have adopted this recipe from mean chef. this is one of my favorite recipes. the pork is sweet, succulent and falling apart tender. fabulous served alone, on rolls, in tortillas.

1. for rub: mix all ingredients in a bowl
2. for sauce: combine in nonreactive saucepan , bring to boil and simmer until it reduces to 1 1 / 2 cups
3. for pork: rub pork with rub
4. place in plastic bag and refrigerate overnight
5. take out pork and re-rub
6. let sit at room temperature for 2 hours
7. roast on rack uncovered in oven at 250-275 degrees until falling apart tender
8. it will take 7-8 hours , the internal temperature of the pork when done should be between 195 and 200 degrees
9. pull pork into pieces , toss with sauce
10. serve with extra sauce (if you prefer , the pork can be served with pig pickin sauce )
demonstrations.review: Made this for Father's Day.  Fantastic and so-o-o easy!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
julia child s cherry clafouti

makes a simple and wonderful dessert, or a delicious and indulgent breakfast!

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees f
2. using a blender , combine the milk , 1 / 3 cup sugar , eggs , vanilla , salt and flour , and blend
3. lightly butter an 8-cup baking dish , and pour a 1 / 4-inch layer of the blended mixture over the bottom
4. set remaining batter aside
5. place dish into the oven for about 7-10 minutes , until a film of batter sets in the pan but the mixture is not baked through
6. remove from oven
7. distribute the pitted cherries over the set batter in the pan , then sprinkle with the remaining sugar
8. pour the remaining batter over the cherries and sugar
9. bake in the preheated oven for 45 to 60 minutes , until the clafouti is puffed and brown and a knife inserted into the center comes out clean
10. sprinkle with powdered sugar and serve warm
11. servings: 6-8 for dessert , 4 for breakfast
demonstrations.review: This is truly a keeper.  It tastes like a gourmet dessert.  I used blueberries instead of cherries.  DH can't wait to have it again.

target.recipe_text:
treva s stuffed bell peppers

a hearty meatless stuffed pepper

1. cut peppers lenghtwise and seed
2. beat 4 eggs with water
3. stir in breadcrumbs , cheese , and parsley
4. the consistancy should be like wet sand---add a little more water if necessary
5. spoon filling into peppers
6. place in baking dish and bake at 350 degrees for 45 minutes
7. filling should be firm
8. spoon sauce over peppers and top each with a slice of cheese
9. reutrn to oven 5 minutes or until cheese melts
target.review: Absolutely wonderful stuffed peppers.  I will never make them any other way again.  I used an Italian Blend shredded cheese to top them and they were great.  One word of caution, and this was entirely MY fault.  Follow step 4 and don't have your mixture too thick.  I didn't thin the mixture like I should have and the filling was a little denser than they should have been.  BUT!, the peppers were still delicious.  Thank you Richard for sharing such a great recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
oven baked maine fish

here's a maine tradition. the lemon juice adds a great flavor to the fish and the mayonnaise keeps the fillets moist. sure to please!

1. spray a 9x13-inch pan with pam and wipe gently with a paper towel
2. add lemon juice and water to pan
3. salt& pepper the fillets , and lay evenly in pan
4. smother fillets liberally with mayonnaise
5. top with dill and generously sprinkle on old bay seasoning
6. if old bay seasoning isn't available , try emeril's version at foodtv
7. com
8. bake in 350f oven for 25 to 30 minutes or until fish flakes
9. serve with lemon wedges
demonstrations.review: What a wonderful recipe.  I used orange roughy and it turned out very moist and tender.  The flavor was wonderful.  I went a little light on the dill weed so I think I may increase it some more next time.  Thank you for posting.  I am always looking for tasty ways to prepare fish and you certainly provided a flavorful way to do this.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
wonderful salsa

this is the best salsa recipe i've found so far and i've tried about a dozen. i got it from one of the local hospital cookbooks that are sold in my area. i changed it a bit and have been canning it for years. the reason i plant a garden is for this salsa. we would be lost without it. hope you like it as much as we do.  one of our members who is a food scientist took this salsa to work, tested the ph and found it measured under 4.0 (well within the safety limit for boiling water bath processing).

1. mix all together and bring to a slow boil for 10 minute
2. seal in jars and cook in hot water bath for 10 minute
3. this is a medium salsa
4. this is also a chunky salsa so if you want a smoother salsa cut your veggies into smaller pieces
5. yields 3-6 quarts or pints
demonstrations.review: This turned out absolutely delicious.  I also am going to freeze it rather than canning.  This is the first time I have made homemade salsa and I'm glad I picked this recipe.  The only change I will make is a minor one, and that is to add less sugar next time.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
graciela s baked ham

this recipe makes the whole house hungry! be prepared to answer 

1. make a paste with mustard and brown sugar
2. add pineapple juice to thin it a little
3. put ham into roasting pan and rub the mixture all over it
4. bake as directed on the ham label , adding pineapple rings for the last half hour
demonstrations.review: Wanted to try something with a little more kick than our usual pineapple juice and brown sugar.  The Dijon mustard I used was just what I wanted.  I also used a cup of brown sugar, added enough mustard to make a paste and used about 1/4 to 1/3 cup of pineapple juice.  It was a very tasty sauce and I will be using this mixture on my ham from now on.

target.recipe_text:
cajun sauteed shrimp

many cajun shrimp dishes have loads of butter. this is a very tasty version that is much lower in fat. you won't miss it. serve with french bread and a salad. fabulous dinner on the table in less than 15 minutes.

1. combine first 8 ingredients in a large zip-top plastic bag
2. seal bag and shake to coat
3. heat oil in a large non-stick skillet over medium high heat until hot
4. add shrimp
5. saute 4- 5 minutes or until shrimp are done
target.review: Fantastic!  My whole family gobbled this up, including my 2 yr old son!  We like our food spicy and healthy, and this did not disapoint!  Thank you for posting!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
creamless broccoli soup

you will never miss the cream in this soup. it is a filling vegan recipe anyone would enjoy. found in one of my favorite moosewood cookbook

1. combine in a soup pot the oil , onions , celery , garlic and salt
2. cook covered on medium heat for 10 minutes , stirring often
3. meanwhile , rinse the broccoli , cut into 4-5 cups of florets , and peel and chop the stems to make about 2 cups
4. reserve 1 cup of florets
5. when the onions are clear , add 4 cups of the water or stock and all the broccoli except for the reserved florets
6. cover and bring to a boil
7. lower the heat and simmer for 5 minutes
8. add the oats and simmer gently for about 10 minutes , stirring often , until the broccoli is tender and the soup begins to thicken
9. remove from the heat and then stir in the lemon juice , dill and pepper
10. working in batches , puree the soup until smooth
11. bring the remaining 1 / 2 cup water to a boil in a small sauce pan
12. add the reserved broccoli florets and cook , covered , until they are bright green and crisp tender , about 3-5 minutes
13. stir the florets and their cooking water into the soup
14. garnish with lemon slices and chives if desired
15. serve
demonstrations.review: This is fantastic!  I needed ideas to use up all the fresh broccoli we grew in our garden this winter.  My husband just can't get enough of this yummy soup!  I used 1/2 chicken broth & 1/2 water.  Also steamed the 1 c. reserved broccoli instead of cooking in a saucepan.  This soup freezes well, too!  Thanks again, it's a keeper!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
christmas rum balls or bourbon balls

these balls are so quick and easy to make. they make a nice addition to the baked goodies that you give as gifts. make these about a week before you want to serve them as they mellow and the sharp strong alcohol taste blends  in more with the other ingredients. store in a tin with a tight lid.  this year i couldn't find the vanilla wafers so i used chocolate and i like them even more.  to form the balls i use two teaspoons as the dough is quite moist.  i store them in the freezer - they don't go hard and they are so good ice cold

1. sift the cocoa with 1 cup sugar
2. stir in the spiced rum mixed with the syrup
3. add crushed vanilla wafers and nuts
4. mix thoroughly
5. shape mixture into walnut sizes balls and dredge with remaining sugar or leave them plain
6. store in a tin
demonstrations.review: Awesome!  This is my 2nd year to make this recipe. Last year DH took them to work & this year everyone is demanding more!!  I found it's easiest to form the balls if you chill the mixture for an hour or so 1st.  Thank you for posting!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
easy general tso s chicken

we love chinese food and general tso's has long been a favorite. however the high fat content of the regular version in a restaurant isn't always a great option.

this is a moderately spicy version of the recipe. reduce the ginger, garlic, scallions or red pepper flakes as your tastes desire. you can also substitute higher calorie options, such as regular sugar for the splenda, or vegetable oil instead of pam cooking spray.

1. whisk together broth , splenda , soy sauce , vinegar and ginger
2. set aside
3. wait until just before pouring over the meal to add in the cornstarch
4. spray a wok or non-stick skillet liberally with pam
5. add scallions , garlic and red pepper flakes
6. cook for 2-3 minutes
7. add chicken and brown
8. use more spray if necessary to assist with the browning
9. cook about 5-8 minutes
10. the chicken should be almost done before you add the sauce
11. add cornstarch to your sauce bowl and whisk to create a slurry
12. add to your chicken in the pan and heat until boiling , then reduce to a simmer
13. the boiling of the sauce will cause the cornstarch to thicken
14. soon it will be as thick as the general tso's sauce you're used to !
15. serve over rice
demonstrations.review: Yummy-yummm!!  Thanks for posting this!  I didn't realize until too late that I didn't have any red pepper flakes so I substituted 1 tsp crushed habinero pepper.  It was HOT, but we still really liked it!  We'll definately try this again!

target.recipe_text:
baklava salmon  salmon with honey  butter  walnuts  and mustard

one of my friends deemed this "baklava salmon" and the name stuck. the salmon & mustard go well with the honey, butter, and walnuts. we usually serve this with rice and steamed carrots or broccoli.

1. preheat oven to 400
2. line shallow roasting pan with non-stick aluminum foil , or spray with non-stick pan spray
3. in small bowl , blend butter , mustard , and honey , set aside
4. in another bowl , mix together bread crumbs , nuts , and parsley
5. place salmon fillets on prepared pan , sprinkle with salt and pepper , and brush with honey-mustard mixture
6. sprinkle tops with crumb / nut mixture
7. if any remains , press into sides of salmon
8. bake salmon 12-15 minutes in preheated oven , or until it flakes easily with a fork
9. serve with lime or lemon wedge
target.review: Absolutely to die for!!  Perfect exactly as is....I wouldn't change a thing!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
amazing roasted shrimp with garlic

this is one of the best shrimp dishes i've ever had. it was inspired by a similar dish i had at bobby flay's restaurant bolo a while back. this is fantastic with a good crusty italian bread to spread the garlic on and soak up the sauce, but you might also try it served over pasta, maybe with a splash of lemon juice.

1. preheat the oven to 350 degrees f
2. separate garlic cloves and peel them
3. place oil , chilies and garlic in a baking dish , small enough so that the oil completely covers the bottom , but large enough that the shrimp will fit in one layer roast the garlic covered for about 30 minutes , or until golden brown and easily mushed add the shrimp , stir to coat with oil and roast covered for another 5 minutes or so , just until the shrimp turns translucent serve hot with italian bread , spreading roasted garlic on the bread and soaking up the sauce with the bread
4. yum !
5. important
6. five minutes is not enough time for the shrimp to absorb the flavor of the oil , garlic and chilis through the shell
demonstrations.review: We loved this!!!  Wouldn't change a thing!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
awesome baked pork chops

these chops remain moist and tender, and the sauce is to die for! you probably have all the ingredients in your kitchen to make this! serve these chops over rice!

1. preheat oven to 350
2. rinse pork chops , pat dry , and season with garlic powder and seasoning salt to taste
3. place the beaten eggs in a small bowl
4. dredge the pork chops lightly in flour , dip in the egg , and coat liberally with bread crumbs
5. heat the oil in a medium skillet over medium-high heat
6. fry the pork chops 5 minutes per side , or until the breading appears well browned
7. transfer the chops to a 9 x 13 baking dish , and cover with foil
8. bake in the preheated oven for 1 hour
9. while baking , combine the cream of mushroom soup , milk and white wine in a medium bowl
10. after the pork chops have baked for an hour , cover them with the soup mixture
11. replace foil , and bake for another 30 minutes
demonstrations.review: I've had this recipe for a while...can't remember where I got it.  It's my husband's favorite dish EVER, and I usually end up making it once a week.  One little note..this recipe is much better with real white wine than with cooking wine.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mexican flan  baked caramel custard

this is a traditional mexican and spanish dessert and by far my favorite. it is very easy to make and looks beautiful.

1. heat 1 / 2 cup sugar in a heavy skillet or saucepan , stirring constantly until it melts and turns a dark golden color
2. remove from heat and immediately pour into a 4 1 / 2 cup metal ring mold , swish it around so it evenly coats the bottom of the ring mold
3. in a large mixing bowl , lightly beat the eggs
4. stir in milk , 1 / 2 cup sugar , vanilla and orange peel
5. place caramel coated ring mold in another pan and place on an oven rack
6. pour egg mixture into the ring mold and pour the hottest tap water possible around the ring mold to a depth of 1 inch
7. bake at 325ffor close to l hour or until a knife comes out clean
8. cool flan on a wire rack , chill for at least 3 1 / 2 hours
9. to unmold the flan loosen edges with a spatula , slip spatula down the sides to let air in
10. place the serving platter over the mold and flip to allow the flan to slip onto the platter
11. spoon the caramel that may remain in the mold on top of the flan
12. pile sliced fruit in the center and serve
demonstrations.review: I couldn't believe how well this turned out!!  I, like the others, have no idea what a metal ring mold is, so I just used 2 pyrex dishes and that worked great.  Also, I used 1 tsp of lemon extract in place of the orange rind (just didn't have any on hand), and that also worked great.  Thanks a bunch!!

target.recipe_text:
puffy french toast

my dh did not like french toast until i found this recipe in an old book. now he loves it. it works best with day old bread.

1. stir dry ingredients in a medium sized mixing bowl
2. in another bowl , blend milk and egg
3. add milk and egg mixture gradually to dry mixture
4. beat until smooth
5. dip bread slices in batter
6. turn to coat both sides evenly
7. fry in greased skillet until golden brown on both sides
8. serve with syrup if desired
target.review: Not really to our liking we found.  Easy recipe to follow, and although we enjoyed the results, I wouldn't make again...we missed the lightness of French toast dipped in egg and milk.  This one is dense and heavier, understandable with the thick batter.  Glad I made it, however, because I do like trying things in new and different ways.  Thanks, angelfan.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
asparagus  artichoke  and avocado salad

this recipe came from a friend and i always get rave reviews on it.  it is extremely easya d delicious and goes well with almost any meal!

1. rinse and cut the bottoms off of the asparagus , then blanch in boiling , salted water for 2 minutes , remove from water and immediately rinse with cold water
2. place on large platter
3. cut drained artichoke hearts into quarters and spread over top ot the asparagus
4. chill until just before serving
5. just before serving cut up the avocados , slice each avocado in half , remove seed and slice into chunks
6. spread chunks over asparagus and artichoke hearts
7. mix salad dressing according to directions except replace white vinegar with balsamic vinegar
8. pour dressing over salad and top with blue cheese , serve immediately
demonstrations.review: This salad was a meal! Halved it to make 4 servings, and had leftover cooked ham and a slice of garlic toast on the side. Very flavourful, filling ingredients. Don't have the good seasons packaged dressing so instead drizzled salad with extra virgin olive oil and balsamic vinegar and sprinkled with dried basil, marjoram and a dash of Italian herbs. Straight "A"s across the board for this salad!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
glazed rutabaga   apricots

another simple, good presentation for an under-appreciated vegetable.

1. cook the prepared rutabaga in a small amount of water until just tender
2. drain well
3. meanwhile , snip the apricots into quarters and soak them in a little boiling water
4. add the drained apricots , the butter and the dark brown sugar to the drained rutabaga and cook over low heat until glazed , stirring frequently
5. about 3 or 4 minutes
demonstrations.review:
Very much appreciated dish at our Thanksgiving dinner.  Cut butter and brown sugar down to 1 tbsp each, kept dried apricots at 12, and had about 6 cups rutabaga.  Delectable taste, easy to make.
Thanks for a keeper!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
parsnip and carrot dice

from the best of gourmet, 1987...a heavenly combination of sweet root vegetables with a dash of cream and mustard. you will be able to practice your knife skills prepping this dish!

1. in a large saucepan , cook the onion in the butter over moderately low heat , stirring until it is just softened
2. add the carrots , parsnips and season to taste
3. stir the vegetables to coat them with the butter
4. add the broth , bring the liquid to a simmer and cook the vegetables , covered , over moderate heat for 5-7 minutes or until they are just tender -- not mushy
5. in a small bowl stir together the mustard and the cream and stir this into the vegetables along with parsley and salt and pepper to taste
demonstrations.review: DELISH!!!! Cut back to serve 4, so used 2 large parsnips and 2 large carrots, and 1 tbsp of cream, leaving the rest the same. This is definitely heavenly for root vegetable lovers, thanks for posting!

target.recipe_text:
chocolate chocolate chip sour cream banana bread

do not let this banana bread's long name fool you! very easy to make, and wonderful bread is the result.

1. cream the butter , sugar and vanilla together
2. then add the eggs and mix
3. then put in the dry ingredients and mix well
4. add the bananas and sour cream and mix
5. then add in the chocolate chips and pour into 3 greased loaf pans
6. bake at 350 for 1 hour , or until a toothpick that has been inserted into the center comes out clean
target.review: Made this for the in-laws and they loved it! This is quite the feat because my mother-in-law is hard to please! This will definitely be a popular go to recipe! Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
coffee cake over night

this will go like hotcakes. i use to make it up just before a lake trip and take it along. was always gone in a matter of minutes.

1. grease 9x13 pan
2. in large bowl mix flour , sugar , brown sugar , shortening , buttermilk , soda , baking powder , cinnamon , salt , and eggs
3. blend on low speed of mixer
4. in small bowl mix brown sugar , granulated sugar , cinnamon , and nuts
5. pour half of the cake batter into pan
6. sprinkle half of the topping mix over
7. repeat a second time
8. cover and refrigerate overnight
9. pre-heat oven to 350f
10. bake at 350f for 30-40 minutes
demonstrations.review: Very good coffee cake!  I made it and baked it up right away because we just didn't want to wait.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pork chops yum yum

i copied this from the orlando sentinel months ago and just now found it. we eat pork chops at least once a week and this is our favorite.

1. brown chops on both sides
2. place in greased casserole dish
3. mix all remaining ingredients and pour over pork chops
4. bake , uncovered , at 350 for one hour
demonstrations.review: These were delicious and so easy!  Only thing I changed was adding a bit of red pepper flakes.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mexican salad with honey lime dressing

i found this at the myfooddiary.com forums, but originally it comes from self magazine. the original salad used radishes, but i substitute green onions instead. healthy fats in this salad, but i've also reduced the amount of oil in the dressing. sometimes i eat the leftovers in a tortilla as a sort of veggie or salad wrap.

1. mix the dressing ingredients together in a bowl and set aside
2. toss all the salad ingredients together in a large bowl
3. drizzle salad dressing over the salad and toss
4. season with salt and pepper , if desired
demonstrations.review: Took this to a Mexican themed dinner party and everybody loved it (especially the dressing).  The only change was that I left out the jicama.  Thanks!

target.recipe_text:
three corn and cheddar spoon bread

a delicious and easy side dish i like to serve with tacos or anything mexican!

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. beat eggs in medium bowl
3. add 1 cup cheese , cream style corn , whole kernel corn , muffin mix , sour cream and melted butter
4. mix until thoroughly combined
5. pour mixture into greased 2-quart baking dish
6. bake in oven 45 minutes to 1 hour or until center is set
7. top with remaining cheese
8. bake 2 minutes more or until cheese is melted
9. for another option: add 1 small can drained , diced green chilies or chopped pimiento to batter before baking)
target.review: We loved it! I accidentally added the whole bag of cheese to mix (2 cups) but it still turned out wonderful!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s moist cheddar garlic oven fried chicken breast

this is for serious garlic lovers. the chicken bakes out so moist and tender! grated cheese may be sprinkled on top of the breast the last 5 minutes of cooking if desired but that is optional. double all ingredients for more than four breasts and adjust the amount of garlic to suit taste. for the coating amount you might be able to get away with 5 or maybe 6 very small chicken breasts, but i would suggest to increase the amount slightly --- to take this dish to yet another level, about 10 minutes before the cooking time is finished, drizzle the top of the chicken with a little pasta sauce, then sprinkle mozzarella cheese on top. return to oven for about 10 minutes until the chicken is completely cooked and sauce is hot and cheese has melted. for a lemon-garlic flavor add in 3 tablespoons lemon juice to the melted butter/garlic mixture ---  *note* for a healthier alternative smart balance butter blend may be used in place of the melted butter --- you will love this chicken!
visit my food blog, www.kittencalskitchen.com, for more of my recipes.

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. butter an 11 x 7-inch pan
3. in a bowl , combine melted butter with fresh minced garlic , 1 teaspoon garlic powder and salt
4. in another bowl , combine the dry breadcrumbs with 1 / 2 cup finely grated cheddar cheese , parmesan cheese 1 teaspoon garlic powder and coarse ground black pepper
5. dip chicken in butter mixture
6. then in crumb mixture
7. place in prepared pan and bake uncovered for 35-45 minutes or until cooked through , larger breasts may take more time
8. top with shredded cheddar or mozzarella the last 5 minutes of cooking (this is only optional
demonstrations.review: Wonderful! I accidental used onion powder instead of garlic powder but it was still wonderfully garlic.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
stove top rice oriental ground beef

i used to use the hamburger helpers but desided it was cheaper to go this way with it. it is better and warms up easier.

1. cook lean ground beef drain if needed
2. add chopped onion and minced garlic and onion soup mix , rice , water with soy sauce
3. cook for 20mins or till the rice is done and water gone
4. add mushrooms heat though
demonstrations.review: My family liked it! My kids weren't crazy about it though!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
human puppy chow

this is the best recipe in the world!! it is great to have anytime but it also makes great christmas gifts.

1. in a large sauce pan , melt together butter , peanut butter , and chocolate chips
2. stir until all is evenly distributed and all is completely melted
3. measure out chex into a large bowl
4. pour chocolate mixture over chex and fold until all the chex are completely covered in the chocolate mixture
5. put powdered sugar into large paper bag
6. put chex into the bag with the sugar and shake until all chex are covered
7. add more sugar as needed
demonstrations.review: Wonderful!!!! soo good and easy to make!

target.recipe_text:
easy crock pot scalloped chicken

my sister made this one week-end when we had been out shopping all day.  it was really nice to come home and just eat.  serve with a salad and some crust rolls and you are good to go!!

1. in crock pot , layer in this order
2. potatoes from package , seasonings from package , chicken breast , onion , green beans , and carrots
3. pour water over everything
4. cook on low for 8-10 hours
5. enjoy !
target.review: sorry, but we really didnt like this, i made it as directed, and used sour cream and chive flavour scalloped potatoes. i reduced the cooking time to 5 1/2 hours on low and the chicken was cooked fine, but the whole lot was way too dry and had no flavour. The potatoes just ended up mushy. It really wasnt appetizing

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crock pot angel chicken

this is from a nice site called baby center. this is a delicious dish that the whole family will love, even the kids!

1. place the chicken in crock pot
2. melt butter in a saucepan
3. stir in italian salad dressing mix , can of soup , cream cheese & wine
4. pour over chicken
5. cook on low in the crock pot for 4-5 hours
6. pour over cooked angel hair pasta or other noodles or rice
7. enjoy !
8. makes 6 breasts
demonstrations.review: i was a little concerned when i mixed all the ingredients for the sauce together (i didnt change anything), it didnt smell all that appetizing, so i was pretty sure it wasnt going to go down well with DH, but after it was all cooked, the chicken was delicious, and the sauce was good. Hubby loved it, he licked my crockpot clean. xx

demonstrations.recipe_text:
stuffing coated baked chicken

cooking for yourself or a crowd can be pretty difficult if you have to alter recipe sizes (unless you have zaar to do it for you!)  this recipe is soo simple to multiply, you can do it for one or one hundred!

1. wash the chicken breasts and pat dry
2. salt and pepper to taste
3. in a shallow bowl , pour the soup and completely coat the chicken breasts with the soup
4. let it sit for a few minutes
5. place the stuffing mix in a zip-top bag and crush slightly with a rolling pin
6. place each breast in the bag and toss to make sure each is coated well
7. it might work better for you to pour the crumbs in a bowl and roll the breasts
8. place the breasts in a shallow baking dish sprayed with non-stick spray and drizzle with the melted butter
9. bake at 375 uncovered until the juices run clear
demonstrations.review: This was a really nice alternative to shake n bake. I used celery soup, and i thought it kept the chicken nice and moist. It took about 20 mins to cook. I definately agree with you that it would probably be easier to coat chicken if crumbs were is a dish rather than a zip lock bag, i'll be doing that next time. A definate keeper! thanks xxx

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crock pot broccoli cheese chicken

chicken breasts in a golden cheese and broccoli sauce. serve this over noodles or rice, accompany with a veggie and warm bread to complete the meal. this recipe is courtesy of the fix it and forget it crock pot cookbook.

1. place the chicken in the crock pot
2. mix together the remaining ingredients and pour over the chicken
3. cook on high for 1 hour
4. reduce to low and cook for another 5-6 hours
5. serve over noodles or rice
demonstrations.review: this was so easy, cheap and tasty!! DH loved it. I served it with fresh broccoli and mashed potatoes and it was delicious. the chicken was so tender. I will definately be making this again.

target.recipe_text:
chili s fajitas by todd wilbur

update: this recipe was created by todd wilbur for his cookbook "top secret restaurant recipes" (penguin random house 1997). www.topsecretrecipes.com. 

serve on flour tortillas with cheese, guacamole, sour cream, tomatoes, and lettuce.

1. combine the lime juice , water , oil , garlic , soy sauce , salt , liquid smoke , cayenne pepper , black pepper and either the sirloin or the chicken in a tupperware container , cover , and refrigerate at least 2 hours or overnight
2. discard leftover marinade
3. grill meat over medium flame 4-5 minutes on each side
4. cut meat into thin strips
5. set aside and keep warm
6. combine the 2 tbls
7. water , soy sauce , lime juice , salt , pepper and olive oil
8. set aside
9. cook onion and peppers in oil until brown
10. remove from heat
11. pour reserved mixture over onions and peppers
12. combine meat , onions , and peppers
target.review: Wow! What an amazing recipe! Thanks so much for sharing! I made these for my brother and his family as well as my own and they were a huge hit! I added more veggies, since we all love them!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cabbage and potato soup  caldo verde

traditional portuguese soup, very good!! (the wine and food of europe - marc & kim millon) 

1. peel and cut up potatoes , and boil in salted water , with garlic
2. when soft , mash and add olive oil and cabbage or kale
3. boil uncovered for about 3 minutes
4. season to taste
5. serve in bowls with a drop of olive oil in the bottom of each
demonstrations.review: It has great potential. We thought it very bland, added garlic salt, onion powder more pepper and more salt. Thinking next time we will use chicken broth instead of water.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
beef   elbow macaroni casserole with sour cream

affectionately coined "debbie's casserole" in our household.  named after a family friend from church named debbie n.  this was a staple in our house and didn't last very long. my father in particular loved this recipe.

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees
2. brown ground beef with diced onion , salt , pepper & garlic salt
3. cook elbow macaroni until tender , drain and mix sour cream & noodles together
4. once noodles are coated with sour cream
5. combine beef with tomato sauce and place 1 / 2 of mixture in a 8x10 dish
6. add a layer of noodles and top with 2 slices of cheese
7. repeat this once more , topping casserole with remaining cheese slices
8. bake at 350 degrees for approximately 20 minutes
demonstrations.review: Yummy! Loved the ease, and easy to adjust to your tastes! We will add more garlic : )

demonstrations.recipe_text:
perfect potato  leek and onion soup with garlic cheese toasts

comfort food at it's finest!  this creamy, flavor-full soup is perfect to curl up with on a cold day or any time of year.

1. soup:
2. heat 4 tablespoons of extra-virgin olive oil in a heavy large pot over medium-low heat
3. add leeks , potatoes , and onion
4. saute until onion is tender , stirring occasionally , about 12 minutes
5. add broth and bring soup to a boil
6. reduce heat to medium-low
7. simmer until all vegetables are tender , about 20 minutes
8. working in batches puree cooled soup in a blender
9. return puree to pot
10. season with salt and pepper
11. garlic cheese toasts:
12. preheat oven to 350f
13. stir olive oil and garlic in a small skillet over low heat until garlic is fragrant , about 1 minute
14. remove from heat and cool
15. add cheese to garlic in skillet
16. toss and combine
17. arrange bread slices on baking sheet
18. spoon cheese mixture onto bread slices , dividing equally
19. bake toasts until cheese melts , about 10 minutes
20. bring soup to a simmer over medium heat , stirring frequently
21. ladle into bowls
22. sprinkle generously with chives
23. serve with the garlic cheese toasts
demonstrations.review: Amazing! Wish we would have doubled it, the family loved it so much there were no leftovers! Thanks for sharing!

target.recipe_text:
4 minute spicy garlic shrimp

recipe is originally from the food network courtesy of rachael ray, but i tweaked it to fit our tastes. very quick & easy shrimp recipe that's done on the stovetop. if your tastes desire spicy & garlic, then this recipe is just for you.

1. heat a large skillet over medium high heat
2. add olive oil , garlic , red pepper flakes , and shrimp
3. season with grill seasoning or salt & pepper
4. cook shrimp 3 minutes or until just pink
5. toss with lemon zest , juice , & chopped parsley
6. remove shrimp to a serving platter , leaving the garlic cloves in the pan
target.review: This was fantastic and so easy and quick to make. Definately a keeper.  We enjoyed it with rice pilaf and zucchini that I put in a pot with onion and a little butter.  My husband normally doesn't care for that steak seasoning but loved this meal.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chinese bbq pork with garlic sauce

an excellent recipe to enjoy on a cold day. intense flavours.

1. make barbecued pork: preheat oven to 350f and line a shallow baking pan with foil
2. in a small bowl whisk together hoisin sauce , ketchup , soy sauce , garlic , and sugar
3. put pork tenderloin in baking pan and coat with hoisin sauce mixture
4. roast pork in middle of oven 35 to 40 minutes , or until a meat thermometer inserted in center registers 160f
5. cool pork completely in baking pan
6. make garlic sauce while pork is cooling: in a small bowl stir together sauce ingredients until sugar is dissolved
7. transfer pork to a cutting board and with a knife held at a 45 angle cut meat across grain into thin slices
8. arrange pork , overlapping slices slightly , over noodles
9. spoon garlic sauce over pork and sprinkle pork with coriander
10. serve with curried , stir-fry noodles
demonstrations.review: This was very tasty!  I marinated it for several hours and served it with white rice and broccoli.  The side sauce was a good accompanyment but not necessary as the pork was just so moist and yummy either way.  Thanks for a yummy meal!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
thai coconut rice

creamy coconut combined with a little bite from red pepper flakes and ginger, create a delicious rice dish to accompany a wide range of entrees.

1. combine all ingredients in a saucepan , except the crystallized ginger and sliced almonds
2. stir well to combine
3. cook over medium high heat , stirring until mixture comes to a low boil
4. immediately reduce heat to low
5. cover and cook for about 18 minutes
6. fluff with a fork
7. the cover , and let sit for 5 more minutes
8. garnish the finished rice with the candied ginger and the sliced almonds
demonstrations.review: This rice was excellent! I had no tumeric and left out the red pepper and ginger.  I made this with Sweet and Garlicky porkchops(found here).  A definate keeper!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
sesame pecan chicken tenders with apricot dipping sauce

good hot or cold!

1. for the sauce , combine the hoisin sauce , mustard and preserves in a small bowl
2. beat the egg whites in a small bowl until frothy and set aside
3. combine the sesame seeds and pecans in a small bowl and set aside
4. dip the chicken strips in to the egg whites and then the nut mixture
5. fry chicken pieces in hot oil for about 3-4 muntues or until golden brown
6. drain on paper towels
7. serve chicken with dipping sauce
demonstrations.review: This was awesome!  I added panko bread crumbs to give it extra crunch, and the sauce was excellent! This is definately a keeper.

target.recipe_text:
sugar cookie cut outs

i had misplaced this recipe and recently found it again. when dd was in kindergarten the children had to take turns bringing a snack to school for everyone to share and dd loved to bring these cookies. i love this recipe because it doesn't require refrigeration before rolling out and because the cookies always turned out beautifully. the recipe is from a little booklet called wilton christmas recipes & ideas.
note: if you're using margarine, be sure to use the hard margarine that comes in a brick like butter, not soft tub margarine.

1. preheat oven to 400f
2. in a large bowl , cream butter and sugar with an electric mixer
3. beat in the egg and vanilla
4. in another bowl , mix together the flour and baking powder
5. add the flour / baking powder mixture one cup at a time , mixing after each addition
6. do not chill the dough
7. divide dough into 2 balls
8. on a floured surface , roll each ball into a circle approximately 12 inches in diameter and 1 / 8 inch thick
9. cut cookies into desired shapes , dipping cookie cutters in flour before each use
10. decorate with gel and crystal sprinkle decorations , if desired
11. bake on ungreased baking sheet on middle rack of oven for 6 to 10 minutes , or until cookies are lightly browned
12. cool 2 to 3 minutes before removing and cooling on a baking grid / cooling rack
13. you can sprinkle cocoa powder on the cookies if desired
14. cookies may be frozen in a tightly sealed container for up to 2 months
target.review: Great for a sugar cookie.  Loved that I didn't have to cool the dough; suitable for impatient bakers and their children.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
corn and red pepper medley

this is a very quick side dish that pairs well with grilled foods.  it's very colorful and easy to make. (i wish my camera was not broken so i could show you how pretty it is!) it comes from light & tasty magazine.

1. in a large skillet , heat the oil and cook the corn for about 2 minutes
2. add the red peppers , onions , and garlic , and saute for 4-6 minutes
3. stir in the parsley , chili powder , salt and pepper and cook for another minute or two
demonstrations.review: I enjoyed this recipe. I am trying to eat more vegetables and this was a nice variation that was easy to make. It looks pretty too!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
baked king fish  cod in tomato sauce

this is a wonderful madhur jaffrey recipe for fish. king fish is my favourite fish and i get the freshest fish right at my door (at 9.00 a.m.)from my fish vendor named jai singh. it is almost as fresh as just out of the sea. hmmm... one of the pluses of living near the sea. we have fish almost 4 days a week and i love variety so have a host of recipes that i have tried and used over and over again for 8 years now. this is definitely the top of the list.

1. wash and dry the fish slices
2. marinate the fish with the salt , turmeric and chilli powder for 1 / 2 an hour
3. heat 2 tbslp oil over medium heat and when hot put in the fennel and mustard seeds as soon as the mustard seeds pop add the onions and garlic and ginger root saute until the onions are light brown
4. then add the 2 tsps of cumin and the green chilli
5. stir and then add the tomatoes , the rest of the cumin and the garam masala
6. boil and then simmer covered for 15 mins on low
7. pre heat oven to 180c heat a little more oil in a non stick and when hot put in the fish slices and just brown all the steaks on both sides
8. put the fish in a baking dish
9. now just pour the sauce over and bake uncovered for 15 mins or until the fish is cooked
demonstrations.review: Flavour was good, but not sure if I would make it again.  Three onions would have been excessive in my estimation, so I used one large onion which seemed sufficient.  As a whole, it just didn't jump out at me as being as awesome as some others felt.  Different tastes I guess!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
traditional english cheddar cauliflower cheese   gratin

when i was growing up, we never called this dish a "gratin" - it was always cauliflower cheese and was invariably our main meal and not an accompaniment! my mother had to be very clever and thrifty in what she bought & cooked, and in the absence of meat on the table, she used cheese as the protein! this dish has become very "fashionable" again is served in many guises, cauliflower noisette, cauliflower gratin, cheese and cauliflower bake...but to me, it will always be just cauliflower cheese, and it remains one of my favourite meals! i do serve it as an accompaniment now, but you have to be very careful what you serve it with, as it is very cheesy and rich. alternatively, just have it as a main meal and serve some homemade bread and butter with it and maybe some salad or steamed spring greens! by the way, if you make a large batch, it freezes very well - either in small plastic containers or in zip lock bags; defrost and microwave to re-heat or reheat over a bain marie. try wherever possible to use english mustard and a good mature cheddar cheese in the sauce, it does make a huge difference to the taste, and other types of mustards & cheeses do not work as well.

1. if oven baking , pre-heat oven to 225c or 450f
2. trim the cauliflower & break into small florets
3. boil in salted water for 10-15 minutes or until just tender
4. drain in a colander and then place in a buttered ovenproof baking dish
5. add the milk , flour and butter to a saucepan
6. heat and whisking with a wire whisk continuously until the sauce thickens , boils and is smooth
7. allow to simmer for a further 2 minutes
8. add three-quarters of the grated cheese , mustard , a pinch of nutmeg and seasoning
9. cook for further minute stirring well
10. pour the sauce over the cauliflower
11. mix the remaining cheese , and breadcrumbs , if using , together , sprinkle over the top
12. place under a hot grill until golden brown , or , bake in a pre-heated oven 225c / 450f for about 15 to 25 minutes until golden brown and bubbling
13. serve immediately
demonstrations.review:
Excellent.  For those without a kitchen scale:
220 g of cheddar worked out to 2 cups shredded and packed
25 g of breadcrumbs was about 1/4 cup
50 g of butter was 1/4 cup

target.recipe_text:
boboli pizza crust clone

tasty "premade" pizza crust.

1. add all ingredients to breadmaker in order listed by your manufacturer
2. set breadmaker on dough setting
3. when cycle is done , form two crusts on pizza pans , sprinkle with parmesan cheese , cover and let rise again
4. bake 5-10 minutes at 450 f until light brown
5. cool
6. wrap tightly in foil and freeze
target.review: I made these small for mini pizzas. My son smelled them cooking and couldn't even wait for sauce or cheese before he ate one! He said they were great plain out of the oven. I didn't have any parmesan in the house so I left it out. Also, I don't do breadmakers--I love making yeast breads by hand. Thanks for sharing!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chewy cocoa brownies

taken from http://www.verybestbaking.com/

1. preheat oven to 350 f
2. grease 13 x 9-inch baking pan
3. combine sugar , butter and water in large bowl
4. stir in eggs and vanilla extract
