5. combine flour , cocoa , baking powder and salt in medium bowl
6. stir into sugar mixture
7. stir in nuts
8. spread into prepared baking pan
9. bake for 18 to 25 minutes or until wooden pick inserted in center comes out slightly sticky
10. cool completely in pan on wire rack
11. sprinkle with powdered sugar
12. cut into bars
demonstrations.review: Just a great baking cocoa brownie recipe. Very easy!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
paul and linda mccartney s split pea soup

another celebrity recipe. i do not know if you should chop up the tomatoes or not, but this sounds great. this would be vegan if you don't use the butter.

1. place split peas , lentils , onions , celery , tomatoes and leeks in large pot and cover with water
2. bring to boil , lower heat and simmer about 1-1 / 2 hours , until split peas and lentils are soft
3. add butter and stir until melted
4. add peppercorns and sea salt to taste
demonstrations.review: My 20 year old is a big fan of Paul Mccartney. I took her to see him perform in Atlanta for her 19th birthday. Based just on this, I decided to try this recipe and was glad I did! Very good. I did cut way back on the butter though. When it was done, I ran it all through the blender for a smoother texture. My husband usually hates split pea soup, but he enjoyed this.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
yeast waffles

wonderful waffles! the batter improves each day and will keep up to a week (if it lasts that long!) refrigerated. i usually mix the batter at least two days before i plan to use it. i originally got this recipe from the aunt of a dear friend over 15 years ago. they're yummy topped with sliced strawberries, blueberries, and whipped cream! prep time does not include overnight chill time.

1. mix eggs , salt , sugar and oil in a large bowl
2. heat milk to lukewarm
3. sift flour into bowl and add warm milk and yeast dissolved in water
4. mix well
5. cover and refrigerate overnight
6. heat waffle maker according to instructions and make waffles
7. one cup batter makes four waffles
demonstrations.review: My family just didn't care for these. The taste was okay, but the texture wasn't to their liking.

target.recipe_text:
linda s chinese duck sauce

i use this on crab rangoon, chicken fingers, spare ribs, egg rolls, marinated chicken wings, beef teriyaki, chicken teriyaki, and of course rice.

1. combined all ingredients in a med-sized pan , and bring to a boil
2. turn the heat down , and simmer uncovered until all the fruit is very soft , about 30 mins
3. , or longer
4. when room temperature , mix well
5. put in a container , and store in the refrigerator
target.review: This sauce was so good with our Recipe #72124.  I used both plums and apples.  This is so much better than the orange stuff you get in many Chinese restaurants, that I can't even begin to tell you!  This is something I will keep as a staple, because it is so versatile and it is really delicious!  I drizzled it on our Fried Rice too!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
grandma vi s green jello salad

served at my grandma's house for every holiday occasion as long as i can remember. you wouldn't know there is cabbage in this unless you saw the ingredient list! tastes like fruit and whipped cream!

1. drain juice from can of crushed pineapple into a measuring cup
2. add enough pineapple juice to make 2 cups
3. bring the 2 cups of juice to a boil
4. remove from heat and dissolve completely 2 pkgs
5. of lime jello in the juice , stir , stir , stir
6. add all the cream cheese pieces using a gravy whip to blend
7. add 6 ice cubes and pineapple , stir until ice dissolves
8. put in the freezer until cool and syrup-like
9. fold in chopped nuts , cabbage , and cool whip
10. refrigerate several hours
demonstrations.review: Made as a test run for our annual halloween party.  The kids loved it even with the cabbage.  I added in some shredded carrots to make it even more festive for the occasion.  We will be using this one.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
authentic italian meatballs

meatball recipes are often challenged by chefs who claim, "mine are the best!" even though my meatballs are the best, i will make no such claim. try them for yourself! this meatball recipe was given to me by my father who got it from a little old lady from italy that he knew. it's amazing that she gave up her recipe to him, but i sure am glad she did!

1. mix all ingredients in a large bowl by hand
2. use your bare hands for best results
3. roll meatballs to about the size of a golf ball
4. drop raw meatballs into large pot of sauce
5. simmer for about 3 hours
demonstrations.review: I made these to test run to use in a recipe for bloody eye balls for our annual halloween party.  Very good meatballs, that I think everyone will enjoy.  I know my kids loved them.  We will be using this recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
caramel apples with crushed peanuts

these delicious caramel apples are just the thing to make when you want something quick and easy to make for halloween, or for a party!

1. remove the stem from each apple , and press a craft stick into the top , and almost through the apple
2. butter a large baking sheet
3. place caramels and milk in a microwave safe bowl , and microwave on high for 3-4 minutes until caramels are melted , stirring once or twice during cooking time , allow to cool briefly
4. roll each apple in caramel sauce , until well coated
5. roll in chopped nuts , candy bars , or candy pieces , and let set on baking sheet , until cool
demonstrations.review: Kids had so much fun decorating these.  Made for trial run for a Halloween party this year.  This is one of the winners so far.

target.recipe_text:
harvey wallbanger

use tequila and it is a freddie fudpucker

1. shake the vodka with the sugar , juice and ice
2. serve in a highball glass or strain into a martini glass
3. float the galliano on top
target.review: swap letters for an obscenity in the second version(trust me to find that!) I dont know what galliano is... or why it should float

demonstrations.recipe_text:
sinus aid hot sauce

this hot sauce is a good remedy for a stuffy nose. it may not seem real hot at first, but it will sneak up on you. if you don't enjoy heat, this isn't for you. there are hotter sauces out there i'm sure, but this isn't for sissies. i eat it on many things, from meat to vegetables.

1. boil peppers in water for about 10 minutes , or until jalapenos turn from deep emerald-like green to an olive green
2. remove peppers from water and cut off stem caps , but do not remove seeds
3. place peppers , tomatoes , garlic , and a teaspoon of salt into a food processor
4. blend in the food processor for 20-30 seconds , depending upon desired consistency
5. taste the sauce , and if necessary , add more salt
6. pour into a re-sealable container or jar and enjoy with chips or use as a condiment
7. when sinuses begin to"clear up , " and they will , use kleenex
8. the fumes from processing boiling hot peppers can take your breath away
demonstrations.review:
Yummy... But what do you do with all that pepper-water... Must be usefull fo something (?!). as a substitute for "smelling salts" possibly :))) LOL
unfortunatly my BF hates hot peppers... he was not ammused ROFLOL.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
brownies in a jar

nan

1. pour sugar into a clean and dry one quart jar
2. press down firmly
3. add cocoa powder and press down firmly
4. pour in chopped pecans , making sure they are evenly layered
5. combine flour , baking powder and salt , pour into jar and seal
6. attach following directions to jar: empty mix into large bowl
7. stir to blend thoroughly
8. add 3 / 4 cup butter or margarine and 4 beaten eggs
9. mix until completely blended
10. spread batter onto lightly greased 9x13 pan
11. bake at 350 f for 30 minutes or until done
12. cool in pan and cut into 2 inch squares
demonstrations.review: I just *HAVE* to send this to some friends for X-Mas!!! What a great fun gift for someone.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cilantro scented tofu rice salad

a very unique salad that tastes great!

1. cut the tofu into 1 / 3 inch thick slices and drain in a colander for 15 minutes
2. crumble to tofu in small pieces and place in a mixing bowl
3. add the rice , cilantro , cucumber and carrots , tossing evenly
4. combine the dressing ingredients in a blender and process until well mixed
5. pour the dressing into the tofu / rice mixture and toss to coat evenly
6. let the flavors blend for 20 minutes in the refrigerator
7. season with salt and pepper to taste , garnish with toasted pumpkin seeds if desired
8. put the lettuce leaves on 4 plates
9. evenly divide the rice and place on top of the lettuce
10. sprinkle the onion over each salad and serve
demonstrations.review: This I loved! just made it for lunch... unfortunatly my BF said it tasted "strange"...I guess the combo of cilantro and tofy just didn't go down too well with him... he's more into steak and chips...shame, because I really enjoy experimenting with "different" things (diffferent to him that is, I love cilantro...and tofu). Refreshing and just a little bite from the cilantro and the onion. Nice textures from the rice and the tofu and just the right zing from the vineagrette

target.recipe_text:
chili relano s squares

fast, easy and a no fail dish, unless you burn it! it's also mild so you wont blow the roof of the mouths off your guests!

1. drain and slice open the chilies
2. take 1 cans worth and lay flat in a small , buttered casserole dish
3. cover with 1 / 2 the cheese
4. repeat
5. whip together the eggs and sour cream
6. lightly salt and pepper
7. pour over casserole and bake at 350 for 45 minutes
target.review: Served this as a side dish last night. Simple and easy prep,loved the cheesey flavor with the green chiles. Plan make this again and DH and I agreed that it was delicious! I think it would be equally as good with a hotter pepper for those how like a little more ZING!!! But it is definitley worth a try for anyone who want to try a different side dish!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
healthy cucumber tomato salad

since i don't like salad dressing, i created this simple salad. not only is it yummy but it is better for you since the only dressing it does have is the one it creates. after we finish eating the veggies, i like to strain the seeds out of the juice and use it as a salad dressing substitute on a green salad. since you make it in a bowl with a sealable lid, it is great for picnics or potlucks. the prep time also includes refrigeration time.

1. add cucumber , tomato and onion to a bowl with a cover
2. add garlic salt , pepper and basil to taste
3. seal bowl and shake
4. refrigerate for at least 1 hour
demonstrations.review: This is definitley a keeper. The longer it marinates the better it gets. Can hardly wait for fresh Illinois tomatoes as will make this one time and again. Took to work and fellow workers scarfed it down and asked for recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
jalapeno pickle relish

this is fantastic on hot dogs and hamburgers! kind of a sweet hot relish that wont kill you!

1. combine jalapenos , cukes , onions and the salt in a large glass bowl , cover with cold water and let stand for 2 hours-drain and press veg to remove excess water
2. combine the sugar and vinegar in a large pot , tie the spices in cheesecloth and add to the liquid
3. bring to a boil and simmer 15 minute
4. add veg and simmer for 10 min-remove spice bag
5. pack into clean hot jars and process 10 minutes in a boiling water bath
demonstrations.review:
I submitted my infamous Jalepeno Pepper Relish but this sounds wonderful and may just have to try this instead this year for a change of pace!
Sounds really good!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
sirloin tips

serve this over a bed of hot buttered noodles. yum!

1. brown the meat in butter and oil in a lg skillet
2. place in a 2qt baking dish
3. in the skillet , saute mushrooms and garlic for 2 minutes
4. pour all over meat
5. cover and bake at 325 for 1-1 / 2 hour or until tender
6. in skillet , mix broth , vinegar , and soy sauce
7. bring to a boil
8. boil for 2 minutes
9. mix mustard , cornstarch and cream , stir into broth mixture
10. bring to a boil
11. boil for 1 minute , stirring constantly
12. drain juices that have accumulated around the beef into broth mixture
13. cook on med heat , stirring , until bubbly
14. add the meat , mix well
demonstrations.review: My Husband said to be sure and rate this a 5 star if not more! It smelled wonderful while it was cooking and the meat was so tender. We had it over hot buttered noodles. The sauce was so rich and tasty! A definite keeper and will make it again!!!

target.recipe_text:
market street clam chowder

this is an excellent chowder recipe from a restaurant in salt lake city. it has great flavor. very much worth the effort!!

1. combine melted butter and flour in oven-proof container and bake at 325 for 30 minutes in large saucepan , combine remaining ingredients except half-and-half
2. simmer until potatoes are thoroughly cooked
3. stir butter-flour mixture into chowder and stir until thick
4. mixture will be slightly less thick than cookie dough
5. remove chowder from heat
6. stir in half-and-half until blended
7. heat to serving temperature , stirring occasionally
8. serve immediately
target.review: This is a great recipe! I love that it has a little "spice" to it. I used green onions in place of leeks. I will make this again for sure. Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
outstanding orange rolls

next time you want to do something truly creative in the kitchen, try these rolls. they're really easy to make, but no one will think that! i kid you not__these are really fabulous! you will have 30 rolls, and they won't last long. prep time is for rising.

1. in small bowl , dissolve yeast in water
2. in lg bowl , mix milk , shortning , sugar , salt , and egg
3. add yeast mix
4. blend well
5. stir in enough flour to make a soft dough
6. kneed on floured board for about 7 minutes
7. put in greased bowl , turn to grease top
8. cover and let rise until doubled , about 1 hour
9. punch dough down
10. divide in half
11. roll each into a 15x10 rectangle
12. mix filling ingredients until smooth
13. spread half on each rectangle
14. roll up , starting with the long end
15. cut each into 15 rolls
16. put in 2 greased 11x7 baking pans
17. cover and let rise until doubled , about 45 minutes
18. bake at 375 for 20-25 minutes , until lightly browned
19. mix glaze ingredients , spread over warm rolls
demonstrations.review: These are so yummy! I was really impressed. I wanted to make orange rolls and this was the first recipe I tried. I was thinking I would have to try several recipes before finding one I'd like--not the case! These are fantastic! I did not have quite enough orange rind so I added a little orange flavoring to the filling which worked fine. Warning --these are addicting!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
spicy thai peanut noodles

a lovely spicy, peanuty sauce over spaghetti noodles and vegetables. i really prefer natural peanut butter in this, but that is up to you. altering the peanut butter and honey can dramatically change this dish, so if you don't like it one way, try it again altering some ingredients.

1. cook 8oz pasta until done and set aside
2. saute your veggies of choicein a pan with a little oil , until cooked
3. set aside
4. stir together vegetable stock , soy sauce , peanut butter , honey , ginget , cumin , coriander , red pepper flakes and garlic in a small sauce pan
5. cook over medium heat until peanut butter and honey melt and sauce is heated through
6. add noodles , stir fried veggies , any meat you may include and toss to coat
demonstrations.review: This is a good basic recipe to start from and make adjustments. I made exactly as recipe stated (less 1/2 tsp red pepper flakes). These are just suggestions based on my results! :) I would double the peanut butter and also lessen the cumin by at least half (I felt it kind of overpowered the dish). I liked all the veggies. Also, I think halving the red pepper flakes was a good idea. I'll be trying this recipe again soon.  Thanks for the recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
golden peach muffins

nan

1. in a bowl , combine the dry ingredients
2. in another bowl , combine the eggs , oil and vanilla
3. stir into dry ingrediants just until moistened
4. fold in peaches
5. fill paper-lined muffin cups two-thirds full
6. bake at 350 for 25-30 minutes or until toothpick comes out clean
7. cool for 5 minutes before removing from pan to a wire rack
demonstrations.review: Great Recipe. Almost reminds me of eating a peach dessert! I've made these twice. Once with fresh peaches and once with canned. Both were great, although if you have fresh on hand, they are unbelievably yummy!

target.recipe_text:
kittencal s technique for perfect easy peel hard boiled eggs

the one and only method i use for perfect hard-boiled eggs and the only one you will use also, this is a no-fail method your eggs will come out perfectly cooked!--- don't omit the vinegar it makes peeling the eggs easier and your eggs will be bright yellow and the whites a pure white! -- it doesn't matter what amount of water or eggs that you use just make certain that you add in about 2 teaspoons of vinegar, i don't even measure i just pour the vinegar into the water from the bottle the exact 2 teaspoons does not really matter,  of course use as many eggs as you wish and the exact amount of ice is not necessary you can use more, also try to use eggs that are at least 2 weeks old fresh eggs are somewhat harder to peel.

1. place the eggs in a saucepan
2. cover the eggs with lukewarm water
3. add in vinegar and pinch salt
4. bring to a full boil over medium heat
5. boil for 2 minutes
6. remove from heat cover with a tight lid
7. allow the eggs to stand for 11 minutes
8. drain the eggs a couple times under very cold water
9. cover the eggs with cold water then add in some ice
10. allow the eggs to sit in ice water for about 3 minutes
11. drain and peel
target.review: I used rice wine vinegar bc that's all I had. Eggs turned out perfectly. Used them to make Chipotle Deviled Egg Recipe #187793 - which is also fabulous. Thanks again for a technique that is perfect!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
apple sausage quiche

this cheese and sausage quiche is slightly sweet from the chopped apple.  prebaking the pastry, without the filling, ensures a crisp crust.  i found this recipe in a southern living cookbook.  we enjoyed it!

1. fit pastry into 9 inch quiche dish
2. prick bottom and sides of pastry with fork
3. bake at 450 for 8-10 minutes
4. cool on wire rack
5. combine apple , and next 3 ingredients
6. toss well
7. cook apple mixture and onion in butter in large skillet over medium-high heat , stirring constantly , until onion is tender
8. remove from heat , and cool 20 minutes
9. brown sausage in large skillet , stirring until it crumbles and is done
10. drain well
11. combine eggs and next 3 ingredients in large bowl
12. add apple mixture and sausage to egg mixture
13. stir well
14. pour mixture into prepared pastry shell
15. gently stir in cheese
16. bake uncovered at 350 for 35 minutse or until cheese melts and knife inserted in center comes out clean
17. let stand 10 minutes before serving
demonstrations.review: I made this for breakfast this morning! What a wonderful fall treat! I followed the recipe exactly except I used Pink Lady apples (picked fresh last weekend). I did cook the onions for a few minutes before adding the apples, which has led to a perfect soft onion and crisp sweet apple in my breakfast. Thanks so much for a keeper!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
black bean orzo salad

nan

1. mix beans , olives , tomatoes , onions and cilantro in large bowl
2. mix oil , lime juice , cumin , pepper and salt
3. toss with bean mixture
4. stir in pasta
5. let stand for 1 hour to blend flavors
6. serve at room temperature as a side dish or on spinach
demonstrations.review: Simply delicious. The only thing I changed was using salsa instead of tomatoes b/c I didn't have any on hand. It came out perfect, but slightly spicy, which I LOVE!! I had this as a side dish, but used the leftovers in a wrap with fresh spinach and chicken for lunch the next day. YUM!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
best ever drop biscuits  small batch

drop biscuits are best the same day they are made...no comparison!!!  perfect for 4 people.  when you stir slightly cooled melted butter into cold buttermilk, the butter will clump. although this might look like a mistake, it's one of the secrets to this recipe.  you can double the recipe...if needed!

1. adjust oven rack to middle position and heat oven to 475 degrees
2. whisk flour , baking powder , baking soda , sugar , and salt in large bowl
3. combine buttermilk and 1 / 4 cup melted butter in medium bowl , stirring until butter forms small clumps
4. add buttermilk mixture to dry ingredients and stir with rubber spatula until just incorporated and batter pulls away from sides of bowl
5. using greased 1 / 4-cup dry measure , scoop a scant amount of batter and drop onto parchment-lined rimmed baking sheet
6. repeat with remaining batter , spacing biscuits about 1 1 / 2 inches apart
7. bake until tops are golden brown and crisp , 8 - 12 minutes
8. they can be made up ahead of time and gently re-heated in a 300 oven for 10 minutes
9. brush biscuit tops with 1 tablespoon melted butter
10. transfer to wire rack and let cool 5 minutes before serving
11. test if baking powder is fresh: mix 2 teaspoons of the baking powder into a cup of water
12. if there is an immediate reaction of foaming and fizzing , the baking powder is okay to use
13. if the reaction is at all delayed or weak , throw it away and buy a fresh can
demonstrations.review: I made these for breakfast this morning. Great staple recipe, especially when cooking for two :) Thanks so much!

target.recipe_text:
15 bean soup

yummy 15 bean soup.  i cook this a lot. i like to serve it with fried chicken and cornbread.

1. wash the beans
2. put in large pot and cover with water
3. bring to boil
4. stir and remove from heat
5. cover and let sit 1 hour
6. after that hour , drain beans and set aside
7. add oil to pot
8. saut your ham hocks , onion , and celery until tender
9. next add garlic and saut 2 minutes more
10. add your beans and cover with water
11. add tomatoes with the juice , parsley , rosemary , black pepper , bouillon cubes , and about 1 teaspoon of salt to start with
12. mix well
13. bring to boil
14. stir , reduce heat cover and simmer for 2 to 21 / 2 hours or until all the sizes of the beans are tender
15. keep watching it and stirring it every once in a while
16. you may need to add more water
17. you want it to keep a consistency a little thicker than a soup
18. taste it after it cooks--you may need more salt or pepper
19. during the last 15 minutes of cooking , add the flavor package that comes with the beans
20. serve by itself or over rice
target.review: My family really enjoyed this soup. I wouldn't change a thing. Thank you for the recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
most refreshing lemonade you will ever taste    quick   easy

this is the best tasting, most satisfying, easiest homemade lemonade you will ever drink. what could be more satisfying on a hot summer day than the cool, brisk refreshing taste of lemonade? this is so easy with the help of a citrus juicer to juice the lemons.

1. combine lemon juice , sugar and club soda stirring well to dissolve sugar
2. add sliced lemon to pitcher
3. chill
4. enjoy !
demonstrations.review: My Husband thought this was unbelievable, I will definitely make it again!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
grilled shrimp    mmmmmm

a nice modernized version of the old classic shrimp cocktail. watch 'em disappear!

1. in a 1 gal plastic food bag place shrimp and olive oil , toss to coat , sprinkle enough rub to coat the shrimp
2. the bag should look dark red
3. refrigerate for 1-4 hrs , the longer you wait the hotter they'll be
4. light the grill and while it's heating place shrimp on skewers
5. when coals are very hot , clean the area that the shrimp will be on and rub with a bit of canola oil on a rag
6. immediately place shrimp on greased grill for 2-3 minutes , turn and cook an additional 2-3 minutes
7. remove from skewers and serve hot
8. no dipping sauce required
9. this rub works well on chicken wings too !
demonstrations.review: With out a doubt I will make this again! Once again thank you for the recipes!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
bacon rollups

from an old 1979 issue of southern living. my 21 year old son still requests this treat often.

1. combine cream cheese and milk stirring until of spreading consistency
2. spread 1 teaspoon of cheese mixture on each halved bread slice
3. roll tightly from the smallest end
4. wrap with bacon and secure with toothpick
5. place on broiler pan
6. bake at 350 degrees fahrenheit for 30 minutes
7. turn if necessary
8. garnish with parsley if desired
9. to serve , remove frozen rollups from freezer and allow to thaw in the refrigerator over night
10. then bake at 350 degrees fahrenheit for 30 to 40 minutes
demonstrations.review: I found that they were a little boring. It could of been the bread or the bacon. I just thought it would of had a lot of more flavor.

target.recipe_text:
italian sausage pie

this pie makes a lovely light supper dish. it takes very little time to put together and bake. serve it with your favorite salad. this recipe is adapted from a cookbook by the sons of italy florida foundation.

1. place pie shell in oven during the pre-heating time for about 5- 10 minutes in order to firm the bottom some
2. don't overcook !
3. remove casing from the sausage and crumble
4. saut sausage and onions
5. drain well and spoon into prepared pie shell
6. blend eggs , milk , cheese , salt and pepper
7. pour over sausage mixture
8. bake at 350 degrees f
9. for 35 minutes , or until custard sets and tests clean with a knife
10. allow to cool slightly
11. cut into 8 wedges and serve
target.review: This was EXCELLENT and so easy.  I have literally never made a pie of any sort so I wasn't sure if it would be hard or not, but it wasn't at all!  Like a few other posters, I also added portobello mushrooms and used hot sausage rather than sweet.  My husband asked me to put it in rotation and keep it up.  Thanks!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
creamy cajun chicken pasta

n'awlin's style of chicken with an updated alfredo sauce.

1. place chicken and cajun seasoning in a bowl and toss to coat
2. in a large skillet over medium heat , saut chicken in butter or margarine until chicken is tender , about 5 to 7 minutes
3. reduce heat add green onion , heavy cream , tomatoes , basil , salt , garlic powder , black pepper and heat through
4. pour over hot linguine and toss with parmesan cheese
demonstrations.review: Holy cow was this dish awesome.  My husband, who rarely says anything about what he's eating wouldn't shut up about it.  We stuffed ourselves silly and my 3 year old ate it too!  <br/><br/>Speaking of that, if you have young kids, there is a Cajun rub called Louisiana Spice that indicates it's "mild enough for table use".  It was very mild and while I missed the spiciness a bit, my kids were able to eat it which was nice.  Look for that spice at your grocery store if you're worried about it!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
lasagna soup

i couldn't believe how easy and tasty this recipe is.  i love the half-melted pieces of cheese in the soup!  this is from cuisine at home.

1. brown sausage in a large saucepan over medium-high heat
2. add onions and carrots
3. saute 3 minutes
4. stir in mushrooms and garlic , and saute another 3 minutes
5. add broth , stewed tomatoes , and tomato sauce , and bring to a boil
6. drop in pasta and simmer until cooked , about 10 minutes , or according to package directions
7. stir in spinach and cook until wilted
8. place 1 / 4 cup cheese into serving bowls and pour soup on top
9. garnish with parmesan and basil
demonstrations.review: A friend of mine gave me a recipe for lasagna soup which didn't sound all that appetizing, but I liked the idea.  So I came online to find another more suited to my tastes and this was AWESOME.  I agree the prep is a bit time consuming but I didn't mind at all once I realized how much of a hit it was.....I'm also slow at chopping so it's probably my fault.  In addition to the cup of pasta, I added a package of Buittoni's cheese tortellini and it was amazing!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
sticky pork chops

a mouth watering yummy pork chop asian style. double the recipe, you'll want more. :)

1. heat frying pan over medium heat
2. cook meat for 2 minutes each side , or until meat is well browned
3. remove meat , set aside - keep warm -
4. add cooking wine , soy sauce , ginger , chili sauce / flakes and honey to the same pan without washing the pan
5. cook for 3 minutes
6. return the meat to pan and cook on each side for 1 minute
7. simmer until the sauce thickens , and pork is cooked through
8. serve with rice and greens
demonstrations.review: I changed a few things on this but it was AWESOME.  I didn't put any ginger in because I can't stand it, and I cut down srirachi sauce to one tablespoon.  Still very spicy....almost too much.  I might cut back a little more next time!  We also added some garlic and it was fantastic!  I will make this over and over again.

target.recipe_text:
the best chili you will ever taste

this is the best chili recipe i have ever tried. i'm not sure where the recipe originated, but it is amazing! sometimes, i don't bother adding all four cans of the kidney beans and it still turns out wonderful. once anyone tastes this chili, they will be begging for the recipe!! enjoy!

1. heat oil
2. cook onions , garlic and meat until brown
3. add tomatoes , beer , coffee , tomato paste and beef broth
4. add spices stir in 2 cans of kidney beans and peppers
5. reduce heat and simmer for 1 1 / 2 hours
6. add 2 remaining cans of kidney beans and simmer for another 30 minutes
target.review: I wish I had read the reviews! This is too sweet for my taste. Now I have a gigantic pot of chili and have no clue what to do with it.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pear bread delight

nan

1. combine flour , soda , baking powder , salt and cinnamon in a large bowl
2. make a well in center of mixture
3. combine oil , eggs , sugar , pears , nuts and vanilla
4. add to dry ingredients , st irring just until moistened
5. spoon mixture into 2 greased 8 1 / 2 x 4 1 / 2 x 3 inch loaf pans
6. bake at 325 degrees for 1 hour and 10 minutes or until done
7. cool 10 minutes before removing from pans
8. yields: 2 loaves
9. good with coffee
demonstrations.review: Yummy! I live in Florida and have a ton of sand pears to use right now. Because these are grated, the pears cooked great in this recipe. They are a very hard pear. Thanks for giving me a great use for them now!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
original carrabba s chicken bryan  not copycat

my hometown newspaper (the orlando sentinel) finally published this, my favorite chicken dish ever, in their "thought you'd never ask" column.  there are copycats on zaar, but this is the actual recipe, as given by carrabba's.  not for the dieter, but a divine dish perfect for company and easy to throw together!

1. brush chicken on both sides with olive oil , season to taste with kosher salt and cracked pepper
2. grill chicken until done - prepare lemon butter sauce while chicken is grilling
3. sautee onion and garlic in 2 tbps butter until soft and fragrant
4. add white wine and lemon juice , reduce heat to medium-low and simmer 10 minutes to reduce
5. add remaining 6 tbsp butter , a little at a time , until it melts and mixture is emulsified
6. add chopped sun-dried tomatoes and basil , heat until hot
7. top nearly-done chicken breasts with 2 oz each of the goat cheese until cheese warms and softens
8. to serve , spoon lemon butter sauce over chicken breasts
9. enjoy ! i serve this dish with pasta tossed in butter or olive oil , garlic mashed potatoes and a green salad -- yummmm !
demonstrations.review: I wish I had re-read the posts about lemon juice. I should have used less. One lemon does not equal 1/2 cup. I used 3 lemons...it overwhelmed the dish.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crockpot pulled bbq chicken

very easy recipe to make bbq chicken for sandwiches or nachos using chicken breasts in the crockpot!  received this recipe from a good friend, nicki!

1. add all ingredients to a crockpot
2. cook on high for 3-4 hours
3. about half way through the cooking time , shred the chicken using two forks
4. chicken will easily fall apart !
5. serve with potato rolls , hamburger rolls , or nacho chips and cheese
demonstrations.review: I really liked this. I thought the chicken turned out moist and soft.

target.recipe_text:
roast pork with herb crust

succulent and delicious

1. preheat oven to 400 degrees f
2. trim fat off meat
3. score top of loin in diamond pattern , about 1 / 4" deep
4. combine garlic , parsley , pepper , thyme , rosemary , salt set aside
5. in small bowl mix the mustard and olive oil
6. line a shallow roasting pan with foil lightly greased or pan sprayed
7. place pork roast on foil , spread mustard mixture on sides and top
8. take the garlic herb mixture and sprinkle over top and sides , press in gently
9. insert oven proof meat thermometer near the center of the roast
10. roast at 400' first 10 minutes
11. reduce oven temp to 325' and continue roasting for 1-1 / 4 to 1-3 / 4 hours or until the thermometer registers 155'
12. remove roast to a platter , and let rest for 15 minutes
target.review: Turned out absolutely delicious, another recipe on my keep list.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
broccoli pork

this is my favorite marinade for pork, oriental with just a hint of lemon. you would never know that it was low fat.

1. ------marinade-------mix garlic , onions , lemon juice , soy sauce and honey together
2. -------pork--------
3. trim fat from pork
4. cut pork into 1 / 2" pieces
5. place into a resealable plastic bag and pour marinade over pork
6. seal bag
7. marinade pork for 20 minutes , or refrigerate until ready to use , no longer than 24 hours
8. drain pork , reserving marinade
9. spray skillet with nonstick spray
10. add olive oil and heat until oil is hot
11. add pork
12. stir-fry until no longer pink in the center
13. remove pork from skillet
14. add broth to skillet
15. bring to a boil
16. add broccoli , pork and marinade
17. reduce heat to medium , cover and cook about 3 minutes or until broccoli is crisp tender
18. heat until boiling
19. mix cornstarch and water
20. stir into pork mixture
21. cook and stir until thickened
22. serve over pasta or rice
23. sprinkle with lemon peel
demonstrations.review: Found the finished dish to be quite bland, I will make it again as I like the combination of pork and broccoli. This dish needs some spice so when I make it again I will add some fresh grated ginger to the marinade and some finely sliced chilli as a garnish

demonstrations.recipe_text:
oven baked fish in white wine

this is a simple dish. the fish is baked in white wine and parsley. the fish is very moist and tender when cooked. a simple but elegant dish

1. preheat oven to moderate 180c
2. place fish side by side in a lightly greased baking dish
3. season with salt and pepper
4. pour the wine over the fish
5. bake about 20 minutes- check the fish has cooked
6. remove fish to a warmed plate and cover with aluminium foil to keep the fish warm
7. place the baking dish over a high heat , or alternatively pour the juices into a saucepan
8. boil the liquid rapidly until slightly reduced
9. serve the fish with the sauce poured over the top
10. garnish with the parsley and serve with lemon wedges
11. great accompanied by a light sald or steamed green vegetables
demonstrations.review: Delicious!! Baking in wine keeps the fish tender and moist. Didn’t like the look of the reduced juices so I added 2 tablespoon of creme fraiche to finish

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pork loin chops cacciatore style

i found this on a supermarket leaflet. the original recipe used lamb chops-i changed that to pork. the sauce is enough for 4 servings according to the original recipe, but we love lots of sauce over pasta.

1. heat 2 tablespoons of the oil in a frying pan and cook the onions over a low to medium heat for 5 minutes or until translucent
2. add the garlic and cook a further 2 minutes
3. add the tomatoes , herbs , stock , wine , and olives , bring to the boil then simmer for 5 minutes
4. sprinkle the paprika over the chops and season them
5. heat the remaining oil in another frying pan and sear the chops for 3-4 minutes each side until golden
6. add the chops to the tomato sauce pan and continue to cook a further 10 minutes over a low heat
7. scatter with torn basil leaves to serve
demonstrations.review: This was delicious and well received by my wife. Have plenty of sauce leftover so will be freezing for another meal. Followed the advice of other reviewers and cooked it in one pan. Needed a little extra time as the chops were quite thick.

target.recipe_text:
cheezy popcorn vegan

this is a low fat snack and is wonderfully delicious. 
serve it at parties or when watching your favorite movies.
 adapted from the ultimate uncheese cookbook by jo stepaniak.
cook time is estimated time to pop  popcorn.

1. place warm popcorn in a large bowl and mist it with olive oil
2. toss gently and mist again
3. repeat until all kernels are lightly coated with oil
4. combine remaining ingredients in a zippered plastic bag
5. seal bag and shake until well mixed
6. drop in popcorn , a little at a time , seal bag , and shake and turn bag to coat
7. continue to add a little amount of popcorn to the bag until all kernels are well coated
8. store zippered bag
9. shake gently again before serving
target.review: Fantastic!  I don't like nutritional yeast by itself on popcorn, but this was a perfect mix.  Thank you!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
thicker than pea soup  pea soup

i love soup and this soup is easily a meal in of itself.  it's also a testament to the fact that meat does not need to be added to everything to make it taste great.  the beauty of this recipe is its simplicity and it tastes delicious.  it is great with some fresh white bread for dipping.

1. throw all the ingredients into a large pot , bring to a boil , then simmer for about 2 hours , or until the peas have completely softened
2. make sure you stir this frequently as it will have a tendency to stick to the pot
3. add more water if gets too thick
demonstrations.review: Wonderful, thick pea soup.  I added an extra 2 cups of water and allowed to boil a bit longer up front to make sure my large chunks of carrots and potatoes cooked through.  Cut the salt down to 1 tsp.  Thanks for sharing!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
gee whiz spread

this spread is an amazing, versatile, whole food that is remarkably fast and simple to prepare. it's great on crackers and sandwiches or in almost any recipe that calls for dairy cheddar cheese. spread it on buns for cheez burgers, or add a few spoonfuls to your favorite soup or sauce to turn them into cheezy delights. adapted from the ultimate uncheese cookbook by jo stepaniak.

1. place all ingredients in a food processor and process until completely smooth and evenly colored
2. stop processor and scrape down sides of bowl as necessary during processing
3. chill completely before serving
4. keeps 5-7 days in the refrigerator
5. variations:
6. in place of the red peppers , use 1 / 2 cup cooked chopped carrots , or 3 / 4 teaspoons paprika , or 2 tbls
7. unsalted tomato paste
8. for an "aged cheddar" flavor , add 1-2 teaspoons light or chickpea miso
demonstrations.review: This is an amazing spread!  I followed the directions as written except excluded the lemon juice as I didn't have any.  I mixed this in with plain mashed potatoes to add some flavor, and even ate this warm on toast with sliced tomatoes as a grilled cheese substitute with vegetable soup.  Thanks for sharing!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
lynn s famous gazpacho

my dear friend lynn shared this recipe with me and it was absolutely addicting!!! i was so enamoured with it that i began eating it for breakfast!!!! hope you enjoy it as well!!!

1. in a blender or very large food processor puree the tomatoes , red pepper , garlic , carrots , lemon juice , spices , olive oil , @ 1 / 2 of the cucumber chunks and a 1 / 2 cup of water
2. pour into a large bowl or tupperware container , stir in the remainder of the diced cucumber
3. cover and chill overnight or for at least three hours
4. to serve , garnish soup with onion , avocado , cilantro , radishes , etc
demonstrations.review: Great!  Left out the olive oil, avocado, and sour cream, deseeded the tomatoes, and added some stale whole grain bread while blending.

target.recipe_text:
unsweetened crock pot applesauce

i eat a lot of applesauce (as a side dish, for breakfast, for a snack with a piece of cheese, you name it) and it seems silly to be buying it so frequently. i'm not always able to find unsweetened kind every single time i go to the store, so i make my own when i can, the way i like it and i finally got around to writing things down last night when i made a batch. some may prefer a little more sweet in this recipe or may need to compensate for the apples being more more tart occasionally than other times. the types of apples i use vary, but i try for 2 or more kinds, any combination except red or golden delicious as these types don't seem to make good applesauce. organic seem to be best, but the selection wasn't very good for buying for this batch, so i peeled the non-organic apples before coring and chopping because i didn't want all the wax, but peeling is not an absolutely necessary step. throwing it all in the crock pot is so easy and makes the house smell so nice!

1. put all ingredients in crock pot , using 1 c cranberry juice if you prefer a thicker sauce , 1 1 / 2 c if you like a thinner sauce
2. stir to coat
3. cook on low for 7 hours or high for 3 hours
4. check consistency of applesauce , adding more cranberry juice if too thick
5. mash apple chunks with potato masher to desired texture , leaving it as chunky as you like
6. taste for preferred tartness or sweetness , adding any sugar , honey or sugar substitute for your tastes
7. cook on low for 1 to 2 more hours
8. remove vanilla bean and star anise
9. vanilla bean can be rinsed and kept for a few more similar uses
10. serve warm or cold
11. can be easily frozen and can be used when substituting for oil in reducing fat in some recipes
target.review: Used Braeburn, Fuji and Granny Smiths...Fabulous, and no additional sweetener needed!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
best grilled pork chops

this is a simple recipe i have adapted from company's coming.it is simple to throw together the marinade in the morning before going off to work and coming home to an easy dinner to prepare at night.

1. in deep bowl mix all marinade ingredients
2. marinate at least 2 hours
3. remove from marinade and cook over medium-high heat on greased grill for no more than 15 minutes or until done
4. cooking time for second side is shorter by 1-2 minutes
5. 3 / 4" or thinner , 5-6 minutes maximum per side , thicker than 3 / 4" 6-7 minutes maximum per side
6. do not over_grill , chops will become tough
7. after 2 minutes grilling on a side , rotate chops 45 degrees for even cooking
8. turn over when juices pool on upper surface and meat appears to be cooked half-way through
demonstrations.review: This marinade was delicious! I used thin, bone-in loin chops and they cooked in less than 10 minutes.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
flank steak with smoked paprika rub

flank steak grilled with a sweet spicy rub.

1. combine dry ingredients and rub all over steaks
2. cover and put in refrigerator for about 45 minutes
3. in the meantime get your grill going
4. bank your fire on one side
5. sear over high heat first , then move to cooler side of grill and cook for 3 minutes each side
6. longer for more well done
7. remove from grill and cover for a few minutes with foil
8. remove foil and cut across the grain and serve
9. corn on the cob and zucchini go well with this
demonstrations.review: I have been making this rub for a while and really regret I have not given its due, sooner. Whole family loves flank steak, and this makes a great change from the standard marinade. From my experience, good spices always make a difference, but kosher salt and fresh ground pepper really count here.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
horseradish top sirloin steak

this is a great, easy way to make steak, especially on the grill. the marinade is simple and flavorful. we easily use this once per month.

1. in a small bowl , mix together the pepper , salt , horseradish , garlic , and olive oil
2. place steaks in a shallow dish , and rub the mixture all over the meat
3. marinate at room temperature for 1-2 hours , or covered in the fridge for longer
4. turn the meat from time to time to coat evenly
5. preheat the broiler or grill and cook the steak for about 5 minutes per side , or until done to your liking
demonstrations.review: Just a bit too much pepper for our tastes, but will definitely make this again. Next time, I'll bump up the olive oil, as another reviewer suggested.

target.recipe_text:
spinach con queso

this is an adopted recipe that i have adjusted to include exact amounts for the ingredients.  i used a pint of canned basic salsa (recipe #39094) when i prepared it and found that while it was flavorful, it wasn't spicy at all.  you may want to add hot sauce, cayenne pepper or diced jalapenos if you like things kicked up a notch. i also melted my cheese in the microwave and stirred in the other ingredients  before pouring into a mini crockpot for serving.  you will want to keep an eye on it, if you serve it this way.  the cheese can separate if it gets too hot in the crockpot.

1. in a large , heavy bottom sauce pan add cheese , salsa , and spinach
2. stir constantly until cheese is melted and bubbling
3. remove from heat and add sour cream
4. stir well and add to a corningware bowl so it stays warm for a long time
5. eat with chips and enjoy !
6. to re-heat: put a lid on the bowl and put in the microwave for a few minutes and stir well
7. or , pour it back into a heavy bottom pot and stir until hot again
target.review: This is very good and easy dip. Once I started dipping I couldn't stop

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chunky blue cheese salad dressing

i love a good blue cheese salad dressing. unfortunately, i have yet to find a good one in the stores. i dug out all my cookbooks, combined this and that and here is the final result.

1. combine mayonnaise , sour cream and buttermilk , mixing well
2. add remaining ingredients mixing thoroughly
3. must refrigerate for 24 hours before serving for best flavor
demonstrations.review: I will never again use store bought blue cheese dressing, this recipe is the only one I'll ever make from here on. Fantastic. Thanks for posting

demonstrations.recipe_text:
beef rouladen

this recipe, from the dec/jan 1996 issue of taste of home has been a family favorite since the first time i made it. it does require a little effort, but it's worth every minute. i make this on a regular basis, as well as when we have company over. i always serve homemade dinner rolls with it but traditionally it may have been served with potato dumplings. i usually will slice my 8 meat slices in half, lengthwise, to create 16 smaller slices, which are easier to handle.  *note:  most recipes include a dill pickle slice in each roll, and after trying it with pickles my family loves this recipe even more!  i've added the pickle as an optional ingredient.  :)

1. spread mustard on one side of each slice of meat
2. sprinkle with salt and pepper
3. place one strip of bacon , dill pickle slice , and a few onion wedges on each slice of meat
4. roll up and secure with wooden toothpicks
5. put oil in dutch oven or other large pan and brown meat
6. drain
7. add broth and bring to a boil
8. reduce heat and cover and simmer for 1-1 / 2 hours or until meat is tender
9. remove meat and keep warm
10. combine flour and water until smooth and slowly stir into broth
11. bring to a boil , stirring constantly until thickened
12. remove wooden pics from meat and return to gravy
13. heat through
14. sprinkle with parsley if desired
demonstrations.review: The only problem I had was that I cooked it a little too long so it dried out a little. Never the less the flavor was excellent and it was easy to prepare. I'll definaely make this again, everyone enjoyed it throughly

demonstrations.recipe_text:
jan s key lime pie

delicious and tart this pie is very refreshing. use only juice that specifically says "key lime" juice. egg whites can be beaten with sugar and added to top if desired.

1. combine condensed milk , egg yolks and juice and blend with mixer until smooth
2. pour into crust and bake at 350 degrees for 10 minutes
3. let stand 10 minutes and refrigerate
demonstrations.review: This was not at all like Key Lime Pie I've had in the past, sorry but none of us were impressed with it

target.recipe_text:
fannie farmer s classic baked macaroni   cheese

to me fannie farmer's recipe is the only "real" macaroni & cheese. it's from my 1946 edition of "fannie farmer's boston cooking school cookbook". with time on it's side - this recipe is hands down the best for traditional, homemade baked macaroni & cheese - comfort food.

please note: if you use cheap cheese you will end up with a bland and flavorless dish!

1. preheat oven to 400f
2. cook and drain macaroni according to package directions
3. set aside
4. in a large saucepan melt butter
5. add flour mixed with salt and pepper , using a whisk to stir until well blended
6. pour milk and cream in gradually
7. stirring constantly
8. bring to boiling point and boil 2 minutes
9. reduce heat and cook 10 minutes
10. add shredded cheddar little by little and simmer an additional 5 minutes , or until cheese melts
11. turn off flame
12. add macaroni to the saucepan and toss to coat with the cheese sauce
13. transfer macaroni to a buttered baking dish
14. sprinkle with breadcrumbs
15. bake 20 minutes until the top is golden brown
16. (you can also freeze this recipe in zip-lock bags for later use - once you have mixed the macaroni along with the cheese sauce allow to cool to room temperature before adding to your freezer - i generally pull it out the night before and allow macaroni and cheese to reach room temperature
17. i then add the macaroni and cheese to a buttered baking dish , sprinkle with bread crumbs and then bake for 20 to 30 minutes , until golden brown on top and bubbling
target.review: This macaroni was decent but not spectacular. I used Sargento mild cheddar fine shredded. The recipe is vague and what it doesn't tell you is that you may need 1 to 1 1/4 additional cups milk to make the sauce more fluid and less tacky.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s bakery buttercream  frosting icing

this is similar to bakery frosting and so much better than any canned!  ---  for extra fluffy frosting use heavy cream and make certain to beat for at least 3-5 minutes and remember to sift the confectioners sugar before using.  for flavor and color you can add 1-2 envelopes 3-grams each, duncan hines frosting creations flavor mix, any flavor desired.

1. in a large bowl using an electric mixer at medium speed beat together the shortening and margarine or butter with cream , salt almond extract and vanilla until smooth
2. add in sifted confectioners sugar starting with 4-1 / 2 cups
3. beat very well until smooth and fluffy , adding more confectioners sugar or cream or milk until you achieve desired consistency
4. add in the food coloring or flavor creation powder until the desired shade is achieved
demonstrations.review: It's very good. I used about three cups to cover 12 cupcakes with a generous frilled layer of icing. It worked very well and was just the right consistency. Yummy!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s chocolate frosting icing

a wonderful frosting i have used for years made in very little time with perfect results and 100% better than any canned, this frosting is so good you will find yourself eating a fair amount of it before even using it to frost with! --- choose the amount of cocoa powder you desire for either a light, medium or dark frosting, and make certain to sift the cocoa powder and the confectioners sugar before using for the recipe--- this frosting *freezes* very well so double the recipe and freeze one batch for next time --- *note* for an ultra creamy fluffy milk chocolate frosting add in 1 to 1-1/2 cups thawed cool whip topping at the end of mixing the frosting and beat on low speed until blended ------- also see my recipe#80118 ---- recipe#282040 --- recipe#90142

1. cream the butter in a small bowl
2. blend in the cocoa powder , vanilla , confectioners sugar , alternately with the cream
3. beat with an electric mixer , until the desired texture is achieved
demonstrations.review: This icing was delicious and easy to make. I added a little extra powdered sugar, about a third of a cup to make it thicker. Why buy prepackaged icing ever again? You avoid the trans fat that is currently in ALL brands of shelved icing, too.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
delicious chicken pot pie

this chicken pot pie recipe takes a little time, but it is well worth it!! this is an all-time favorite in our family. great on a cold winter day.

1. preheat oven to 400f
2. saute onion , celery , carrots and potatoes in margarine for 10 minutes
3. add flour to sauteed mixture , stirring well , cook one minute stirring constantly
4. combine broth and half and half
5. gradually stir into vegetable mixture
6. cook over medium heat stirring constantly until thickened and bubbly
7. stir in salt and pepper
8. add chicken and stir well
9. pour into shallow 2 quart casserole dish and top with pie shells
10. cut slits to allow steam to escape
11. bake for 40-50 minutes or until pastry is golden brown and filling is bubbly and cooked through
demonstrations.review: I tried this but forgot to add the potatoes. Still, it was delicious! I will make this one again. Parent had two helpings of it...

target.recipe_text:
strawberry rhubarb crunch

delicious with fresh strawberries and rhubarb.

1. preheat the oven to 350f
2. in a large bowl , combine the flour , brown sugar , oatmeal , butter , sugar , and cinnamon
3. mix until crumbly then press half of the mixture into a greased 9"x13" baking pan
4. cover with the rhubarb and strawberries
5. in a small saucepan , heat the water , cornstarch , and vanilla over medium-low heat until thick and clear , stirring often
6. this should take about 5 minutes
7. pour over the rhubarb / strawberry layer
8. top with the remaining crumb mixture and bake for 60 minutes
target.review: So my neighbor gave me a bunch of rhubarb this weekend, and I just had to do something with it. This turned out great! Was fairly simple to make (I don't bake much, so it has to be simple :) ) The crunch was sweet and tart at the same time, and I loved the crust! I will make another one tonight to give to my neighbor. Thank you! - I made the recipe exact, no tweaks.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
herbed top round roast

taken from the everyday low-carb slow cooker cookbook

1. pour the red wine and water into the slow cooker crock
2. set aside
3. in a small bowl , combine the herbs , pepper , salt , and olive oil
4. stir to combine
5. using clean hands , rub the oil and herb mixture all over the beef roast
6. place the roast into the slow cooker crock
7. sprinkle the garlic and onions aroudn the raost and lay the bacon strips over the top of the roast
8. cover and cook on low for 10 hours
9. before serving , flip the roast over in the slow cooker , then turn the slow cooker off and let the roast rest in the slow cooker for about 15 minutes
10. remove roast to a platter and let it drain for a few minutes
11. to serve , use a sharp knife to slice the meat against the grain
12. if you like , dip the roast slices into the cooking juices before serving , or serve the cooking juices alongside the beef
demonstrations.review: The flavor in this recipe is amazing. I absolutely (and my husband too) loved it. That being said... I pretty much followed the recipe exactly, only i didn't measure the spices, I just added them by hand. Again, the recipe itself is great. The disappointing part was that my roast was awful. It is so tough, I don't know what to do with it. I am going to try shredding it for sandwiches or make fancy tacos from it. I think I over cooked it. I will definitely use this recipe again, I think I will try either a shorter cooking time (I did do the recommended) or using a different cut of meat. The roast itself might be a loss, but hey, my veggies turned out great and taste amazing!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
soft and chewy rice  krispies  crispy  treats

an extra-chewy recipe that will have everyone wishing theirs turned out as well!

1. melt margarine in a large pan over medium heat
2. melt in marshmallows and stir continuously until smooth
3. add vanilla
4. without removing from heat , add cereal
5. stir until cereal is completely covered with marshmallow mixture
6. pour into a greased 9x13 pan
7. let cool 2 minutes
8. press flat with greased hands
9. cool completely and cut into squares
10. enjoy !
demonstrations.review: Excellent! I looked at the reviews and followed the advise given here. Was totally worth it! I adjusted the recipe in the following way:<br/>1/2 stick butter<br/>A  little vanilla (I didn't measure)<br/>15oz marshmallows<br/>7 cups rice crispies (I used 4 cups rice crispies and 3 cups "fruity pebbles" as these were for a birthday treat, oh and I used off brands of everything and they turned out fine!)<br/>I took the marshmallows off before they were 100% melted so no scorching or hard treats. I used wax paper instead of oil in one pan and the spray oil in another as I made two batches of these. I would use the wax paper again, they came right off and it was much easier clean up! I also wet my hands as suggested by another reviewer, and that was a GREAT help, they didn't stick to my hands at all after I did that!  Then for an added bonus I got some white chocolate and dipped them in it and put sprinkles on top :) They were a big hit for my daughters treat for her birthday at school. Thank you so much! As someone who had never made rice crispy treats before, this was an easy and SUPER yummy recipe! Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crustless bacon  spinach   swiss quiche   low carb

i've read through a lot of recipes to come up with my version of this quiche.  i wanted to make one that is crustless and low carb, and this one is a winner!  but once i start eating it, i just don't want to stop!  i thought i could make it ahead so i could have a quick breakfast on work mornings, but this rarely lasts out the day it was made!

1. on a foil lined pan , cook bacon in 350 degree f
2. oven until crisp
3. while bacon cooks , chop onion and shred cheese
4. heat 1 tablespoon butter and 1 teaspoon oil in skillet over medium heat
5. add chopped onion , and stir to coat
6. when onion turns glossy , add thawed spinach , and stir to mix
7. heat about 5 minutes , then remove from heat to cool
8. remove bacon from oven , and place on a paper-towel lined plate to drain
9. stir together eggs , salt , pepper & heavy whipping cream in a medium bowl
10. add in cheese , onion / spinach mixture , and bacon
11. stir thoroughly to mix
12. butter a glass pie plate or quiche dish , pour mix in , and pat evenly with a fork
13. bake in 350 degrees f
14. oven 25-30 minutes , or until a knife inserted in the center comes out clean
15. let rest 5 minutes before cutting & serving
16. i bet you can't eat just one slice !
demonstrations.review: Loved it! Even my picky 8yr old thought this quiche was great :) Thanks for the wonderful recipe.

target.recipe_text:
obama family chili recipe

this is presidential candidate barack obama's family chili recipe that he's been using for years.  i live in denver and saw something about the brown hotel making this recipe for the guests during the 2008 democrat national convention.

1. saute onions , green pepper and garlic in olive oil until soft
2. add ground meat and brown
3. combine spices together into a mixture , then add to ground meat
4. add red wine vinegar
5. add tomatoes and let simmer , until tomatoes cook down
6. add kidney beans and cook for a few more minutes
7. serve over white or brown rice
8. garnish with grated cheddar cheese , onions and sour cream
target.review: Since this chili had different ingredients that what I generally use for my own chili creations I wanted to try it.  It was nothing too spectacular so I ended up adding ingredients to the end product to make it more palatable.  I felt the fresh tomatoes didn't really add much broth to the chili so I ended up adding 1/2 of a large can of tomato sauce.  I also added 3 jalapenos, garlic salt, chili con carne seasoning, ancho chili, crushed red peppers and cumin.  I am not a fan of turmeric but added it initially.  Still not a fan of it (lol).

demonstrations.recipe_text:
m   m   cookies

these were a staple in college. never had a boyfriend who didn't like them (not like a male college student is a hard sell for homemade cookies!)

1. cream margarine and sugars , then add eggs and vanilla
2. add dry ingredients and finally add 1 / 2 m&m's
3. drop by teaspoon onto greased cookie sheet placing remaining m&m's on top of each cookie
4. bake at 350 for 10 minutes or lightly browned
5. can make frozen balls of dough to take out and bake as needed
demonstrations.review: An old time favorite and classic cookie recipe.  I like to use different colored candies to coordinate with themes...... football colors, school colors...etc.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
yummy french onion biscuits

great with soups and stews.

1. whisk together first 3 ingredients until smooth
2. stir in baking mix until well-blended
3. divide dough into 12 equal portions , and arrange on a lightly greased baking sheet
4. brush tops of dough with melted butter
5. bake at 450 degrees for 7-8 minutes or until lightly golden
6. let stand 5 minutes before serving
demonstrations.review: These were so good and simple easy to make.   Good way to use up leftover dip from a party.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
barbecued spiced fish

this is out of "the backyard barbecue cookbook". i have it marked as being excellent! please note: "not for sensitive tongues" hope you enjoy!

1. dry fish fillets with paper towels and brush with melted butter , set aside
2. to make the dry marinade: combine all the dry spices and sprinkle over the buttered fish fillets
3. cook the fillet on a lightly greased grill for 8-10 minutes , tuning once during cooking time
4. store in a covered airtight jar in the freezer for best results
5. it adds flavor to seafood , poultry and beef
demonstrations.review:
I have this same cookbook and have made this recipe..........FANTASTIC.  So glad you posted it here so now I can post a picture.

I highly recommend this recipe.   I happened to use cod fish loins that were really thick but I ended up cutting them in half before grilling.

target.recipe_text:
brady bunch pork chops

i think this recipe is an absolute gem. really, in all my years of cooking, i don't think i have ever made chops as delectable as these! crispy-crunchy on the outside, meltingly tender and moist on the inside. the key, i think, is the salty milk marinade/brine, and making sure not to overcook them. thanks to gourmet magazine for this one.

1. in a large shallow dish , like a 9x13 pan , stir together milk and first amount of salt
2. add pork chops and marinate , covered and in fridge , for at least one hour
3. turn chops once , halfway through marinating / brining time
4. when ready to cook chops , preheat oven to 200f and have ready an ovenproof platter
5. in a shallow dish , combine freshly made bread crumbs with garlic powder , rosemary , thyme and remaining amount of salt
6. remove chops from milk and let excess milk drip off , then dredge chops in bread crumbs , lightly patting crumbs onto both sides of chops so they adhere
7. place breaded pork chops on a tray , keeping chops in one layer
8. in a large 12-inch skillet over high heat , place butter and oil
9. saute chops , 2 1 / 2 to 3 minutes per side only
10. do not overcook , do not crowd chops in skillet , and turn only once
11. chops should be golden brown and just cooked through
12. place cooked chops on platter and keep warm in preheated oven
13. cook remaining chops
14. add more oil and butter to pan if necessary
15. i recommend serving with applesauce
target.review: This was very good, but it took longer then the 2 to 3 minutes.  We plan on using this recipe again but this time we plan on using it to make schnitzel instead.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
tootsie rolls

an easy recipe like the ones you can buy -- only better!

1. mix all ingredients together
2. knead like you would for bread
3. roll into rope shapes and cut into desired lengths
4. wrap with plastic wrap to keep
demonstrations.review:
I really enjoyed these and so did everyone who tried them.  Yes, they are not as hard as the orginal tootsie rolls, but that is what I like about them. The ingredients are easy to find and the product is easy to make.
Thank you
Faith77

demonstrations.recipe_text:
strawberry julius

the ultimate mall fruity shake at home! i modified this recipe one day from one i found online. i have sensitive teeth so i don't like ice much anyway. guaranteed not to give you "slushie headache".

1. slice up fresh strawberries until you have enough to fill a one cup measure
2. add to a blender or food processor , or if you only have a stick mixer , just put it in a large pyrex jug
3. add rest of ingredients
4. blend until smooth
5. you may want to try this a little bit cooler for summer days , omit the water and add a few ice cubes
6. i only leave out the ice cubes because my food processor can't handle hard ice
7. also it does tend to separate if you leave it sitting around for a minute , don't let this put you off , just stir it up a bit , it tastes the same , just tends to be more frothy at the top then
demonstrations.review:
This was okay, but way to sugary for us.  I will make again sometime and omit the sugar.  
Thank you.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
turkey barley soup

this is a fabulous recipe, especially when made with my rescued turkey stock (#24576). it also freezes very well.

1. in a large skillet , heat oil and saute onions , carrots , celery and mushrooms
2. sprinkle thyme on veggies and continue to saute until softened , about 6 to 8 minutes
3. pour turkey stock into a large pot and whisk in the tomato paste
4. stir in sauteed veggies
5. turn heat to high
6. stir in barley , vinegar , salt and pepper
7. when soup comes to a boil , turn heat down to a simmer and cook , covered , for about 1 hour , or until barley is tender
8. stir in turkey meat and continue to simmer just until soup is heated through
demonstrations.review: I too used your turkey stock recipe and found it to be good soup.  I will make again.  Thank you.

target.recipe_text:
honey lemon chicken thighs

here's another recipe with chicken thighs, which are actually considered one of the favorite parts of the chicken in chinese cooking, as they aren't as dry as the breast. (this recipe isn't particularly chinese; i'm just going off on tangents.) enjoy!

1. grate 1 tsp of zest from the lemon , and press 1 tbs of juice
2. combine the zest and juice with stock , honey , and soy sauce
3. heat oil in a large wok with a cover and brown the thighs
4. remove the thighs from oil and add the onion
5. saute until soft
6. add the rice , pepper , and broth mixture
7. top with the browned thighs
8. cover and simmer for 30 minutes or until the liquid is absorbed
target.review: I was disappointed in this recipe. The rice got mushy and tasted too much of the oil and the chicken was like "steamed" chicken.  Not one of my favorites.............

demonstrations.recipe_text:
slow cooker cheesy chicken

almost too easy, the chicken cooks in a creamy, cheesy sauce that is delicious over noodles. this freezes well, too

1. place chicken breasts in the crock pot
2. mix the undiluted soups together with the garlic powder and pour over chicken
3. cover and cook on low 6-8 hours , until chicken is tender
4. serve with the delicious sauce over rice or noodles
demonstrations.review: LOVED IT!!!  I cut up the chicken into bite size pieces, added diced red peppers and some hot sauce.  I served it over mashed potatoes with a salad.  My husband loved it too!  Will definitely make this again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crock pot chili pork chops     a must try

i found this recipe on the web somewhere and decided to try it. it is absolutely wonderful and the meat just falls off the bones. as my husband describes it "they are succulent!" this is a must in our family at least every other week!

1. cook onions in oil until lightly brown
2. add garlic , worcestershire sauce , chili powder , water , ketchup and salt and pepper
3. cover and simmer the sauce for 10 minutes
4. arrange pork chops in crock pot , pour sauce over the chops
5. cover and cook on low heat for 6-7 hours
6. i find that the longer you cook them , the more tender they are
7. i normally serve them with mashed potatoes and a vegetable
8. i put the sauce over the mashed potatoes
demonstrations.review: These were good. I added some V8 juice (a can) because it looked like it didn't have enough sauce. I should have only added 1/2 can because i think I watered it down too much. I served it over white rice and we enjoyed it. Next time I think I will double the sauce recipe, it was a little bland and I think if you add more sauce it would be better!  Will try again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cauliflower fromage

my father-in-law's all time favourite vegetable. i have to make it just about every time they come for dinner. you can make this ahead of time and pop it in the oven just before you need it.

1. preheat oven to 400
2. butter a shallow baking dish
3. break cauliflower into bite size pieces and cook for about 10 minutes or til still slightly firm
4. drain and rinse under cold water
5. prepare the sauce by melting butter in a small saucepan
6. add garlic& cook over med-low heat , stirring often , for 2 minutes
7. stir in breadcrumbs , pepper and nutmeg
8. stir constantly until mixture thickens , about 3 minutes
9. spoon over cauliflower
10. sprinkle with cheese
11. bake in preheated oven for 15 minutes or til cheese is melted and bubbly
demonstrations.review: I liked the taste of this dish, but I would prefer it to be creamier. It was sort of dry, not enough liquid. I used cheddar, maybe the swiss would have been creamier??  The texture wasn't what I thought it would be

target.recipe_text:
sweet and sour skillet chicken

from weight watcher's magazine. if you use non fat chicken stock, there is only 180 calories and 1 gram of fat in this.

1. cut chicken in strips
2. in large skillet bring chicken and stock to simmer over medium high heat
3. add celery , onion and sweet peppers
4. cook , stirring often , for about 5 minutes or until chicken is no longer pink and vegetables are tender crisp
5. mix together juice , vinegar , brown sugar , corn starch and soya sauce until blended stir into skillet and bring to a boil
6. cook , stirring , for about 2 minutes until glossy and thickened
7. add pineapple
8. simmer for about 2 minutes or until heated through
target.review: Great recipe... very tasty and so easy! I will make this one again. I also found it on kraftcanada.com

demonstrations.recipe_text:
my dad swears my sister makes the best pork chops in the world

my sister learned the basic flour mix from her former mother-in-law, who grew up in carruthersville, missouri.  my sister kept hearing emeril say how well garlic went with pork, so she added it to her seasoning mix.  my dad still swears that my maternal grandmother (his former mother-in-law) made the best fried chicken ever.  born in 1919, she was the eldest daughter, and second of ten children, raised on a farm outside the town of black oak, arkansas.  even after my parents divorced, dad was occasionally invited to eat grandmommy's fried chicken.  he always relished those meals, and still talks about them today.  my grandmother never told anyone, except my grandfather, her secret to breading her chicken, but she did tell my sister her trick to frying it.  my sister has incorporated that method into her pork chop recipe.

1. mix dry ingredients in a resealable bag
2. rinse pork chops under running water
3. toss them into a ziplock bag and shake , to coat well
4. in a cast iron skillet , cook chops in enough oil to come 1 / 2 way up the side of the chops , for example - 1 inch chops need 1 / 2 an inch of oil , on medium high heat for approximately 4 minutes each side , until golden brown
5. for the last 30 seconds of cooking the second side , increase heat to high , to cook the grease out of it
6. blot on paper towels before serving
demonstrations.review: Thought these were okay. I used the coating on boneless chops and was hoping for a thicker, crunchy-type breading however the result was a thin coating. I also had WAY too much flour mixture left in the dish afterwards... guess I will save this to try on chicken next time!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
easy cake mix carrot pineapple cake

so easy, don't drain the pineapple juice from the crushed pineapple! serving are only estimated depending on the size you cut the pieces. my recipe#90142 works great with this cake ;-)

1. set oven to 350 degrees
2. grease a 13 x 9-inch baking dish
3. in a large bowl whisk eggs , then add in all remaining ingredients except the cream cheese frosting
4. mix to combine well
5. transfer to prepared baking pan
6. bake for about 30-35 minutes or until cake tests done
7. cool completely then frost with cream cheese frosting
demonstrations.review: Great carrot cake! I took the advice of another reviewer and used a carrot cake mix as I couldn't find cinnamon or nutmeg in my cupboard. Also added coconut and raisins. I used a big can of pineapple, might have been bigger than what the recipe calls for, but still turned out great! I needed to cook it longer because of that. It made two 9" cakes. My company really enjoyed it but I didn't tell them how easy it was!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pineapple meatballs

this is a family favourite; my teenage son eats at least 2 servings himself. cooking time includes the browning of the meatballs, although you can brown them in the oven on a cookie sheet and make the sauce at the same time, saving yourself a little time.

1. preheat oven to 350f degrees
2. first , make the meatballs: combine all meatball ingredients in a bowl and mix well
3. shape into 1-inch balls
4. brown them in a nonstick frying pan until browned all over
5. drain on paper towel then place in a large ungreased casserole dish
6. to make sauce , combine brown sugar and cornstarch in a large saucepan , then whisk in the 1-3 / 4 cup pineapple juice / water combination until mixture is smooth
7. add vinegar , soy sauce and worcestershire sauce
8. stir
9. simmer , uncovered , on medium-low heat for about 8 minutes , or until thickened
10. pour sauce over meatballs and add pineapple tidbits
11. stir gently to combine until meatballs are coated with sauce
12. bake in preheated oven for 30 minutes
13. if you want a lot , this recipe doubles well
demonstrations.review: Yummy! I halved this recipe and didn't have enough brown sugar but it still turned out really good. Thanks Lennie!

target.recipe_text:
rice seasoning mix

never buy rice mixes again! this is ready anytime you need a tasty side dish. very good!

1. mix all together well
2. store in airtight container
3. when ready to make rice , combine 1 cup rice , 2 cups water , and 3 t seasoning
4. bring water to a boil
5. add rice and seasoning
6. reduce to simmer , cover , and cook for 18 minutes
target.review: Wonderful!!  Thank you for sharing this recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chicken scaloppine with lemon glaze   low fat and delicious

this is a wonderful lower-fat restaurant-quality dish that is easy to make, i also like to add in a few tablespoons of capers and cook with the lemon glaze if you are a lover of capers then add them in as it really adds to the flavour of this dish ---  this lemon sauce is not a heavy creamy sauce which is what makes this dish lower in fat, it is more like a glaze that soaks into the chicken, and i would strongly suggest to double or even triple the glaze i most always do, and please be certain to use only dry breadcrumbs as fresh will not stick to the chicken as well --- this is *very* good!

1. in a small bowl or shallow dish whisk together mustard and eggs
2. set aside
3. combine the dry bread crumbs with poultry seasoning , garlic powder and seasoning salt
4. spread on a piece of waxed paper
5. dip the breasts firstly in egg / mustard mixture then coat well with the crumb mixture , pressing downs with hands to adhear the crumbs to the breast
6. heat the olive oil in a skillet over medium heat
7. add in the chicken and cook for about 5 minutes on each side , or until it is no longer pink inside
8. remove and transfer to a plate to keep warm
9. for the glaze
10. in the same skillet add in the broth , lemon juice and 1 / 4 teaspoon salt bring to a boil scraping any brown bits from the pan
11. add in lemon slices and parsley
12. mix to combine for about 1 minute
13. spoon the glaze / sauce over chicken
14. delicious !
demonstrations.review: We love,love,love this recipe!  I also double the sauce and I add capers, a small can of drained sliced mushrooms and artichokes if I have them on hand.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
yummy n  easiest  warm blueberry sauce

serve it liberally on pancakes, ice creams or just have a spoonful of it any time!

1. place all ingredients in a saucepan
2. bring to a boil
3. reduce the heat and simmer for 5 minutes
4. yum , it is ready !
demonstrations.review: Very good! So easy to make and it was delicious on French Toast.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s spinach   four cheese manicotti  vegetarian

i have been making this recipe for years, it is *the best* manicotti recipe hands down! --- i have made this many times for dinner parties and have made it for socials and large gatherings increasing amounts of coarse, i have even served this at my thanksgiving and christmas holiday table as an extra dish along with a turkey or ham --- to save time i always mix up the filling a day ahead and refrigerate this will also give the flavors a chance to blend together, or you may prepare up to step #9 cover and refrigerate for up to 24 hours --- don't forget to cook the spinach first before using for this recipe

1. set oven to 350 degrees f
2. butter a 13 x 9-inch baking dish
3. in a skillet , saute onion in oil for about 4 minutes or until softened
4. in a mixing bowl combine the ricotta cheese , 1-1 / 2 cup mozza cheese , cream cheese , 6 tablespoons parmesan cheese , italian seasoning
5. beat with a wooden spoon until smooth and well combined
6. season with white salt or seasoned salt and black pepper to taste
7. stir in onion mixture and spinach
8. mix well to combine
9. spoon into cooked and cooled manicotti shells
