10. pour half of the pasta sauce into the prepared baking dish
11. arrange shells over sauce
12. top with the remaining sauce , use a spoon to spread the sauce over the shells
13. sprinkle about 1 / 4 cup parmesan cheese over the sauce
14. cover and bake for 25 minutes
15. uncover and top with mozzeralla cheese
16. bake 5 mins longer , or until cheese is melted
17. let stand 10 mins before serving
demonstrations.review: Wowzer!  These are delicious!  I made exactly as written and used the Spaghetti/Lasagna Sauce recipe I posted (Christy's Spaghetti Sauce) on the Zaar.   I will make these often.

target.recipe_text:
rouladen or rinderroulade

german /hungarian meat roulade consisting of bacon, onions, mustard and pickles wrapped in thinly sliced beef and then cooked.  reminds me a little of mini morkon, a dish my dad makes often.  found on cookipedia.

1. spread the mustard on the inside of the steak
2. arrange a few slices of onion , gherkin and bacon on top then roll up and secure with toothpicks or tie with kitchen string
3. coat in seasoned flour then in a large pan or dutch oven , fry in a little oil until browned
4. remove and set aside
5. in the same pan , saut the onion , celery , carrot and garlic for 6 minutes
6. add a little red wine and stir to deglaze the pan
7. place the rouladen on top of the vegetables and pour the remaining wine over the top
8. heat for 5 minutes to reduce the wine a little
9. add a little beef stock , tomato puree , bay leaf and season well
10. simmer gently for 1
11. 5 hours
12. strain the gray before serving and thicken a little if needed
13. serve hot with boiled or mashed potatoes , carrots and broccoli
target.review: Beef rouladen is my favorite German dish, and this version is fantastic!  Flavorful, tasty and authentic - and easy to make.  I used thin breakfast steaks which I pounded further, and followed the recipe as written.  Just wonderful - will make this again.  Made for ZWT7, for the Witchin Kitchen.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
hispaniola coffee chili

the flavors in this really interesting chili are drawn from ingredients used by the spaniards who settled in the west indies on the islands now called cuba and hispaniola. it's not your everyday chili!

1. brown the meat in a large dutch oven , cook the beef over medium-high heat , about 4-5 minutes
2. remove contents from the dutch oven and set aside
3. reduce heat to medium low and add onions and saute until translucent , about 3 minutes
4. add garlic and cook 1 minute
5. replace meat and add bay leaves , chili powder , cumin , nutmeg , pepper , allspice , salt , thyme , capers , olives , chiles , coffee , molasses , and tomatoes
6. simmer uncovered for 20 minutes
7. finish the chili: add raisins and simmer uncovered for 10 minutes
8. garnish with almonds
9. serve hot over cooked rice
demonstrations.review: I absolutely loved the combination of flavors in this!  It reminded me a lot of picadillo, and it was absolutely delicious.  And it was so easy to make for this novice cook!  Will definitely make this again!  Made for ZWT9.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
tomato gratin

this recipe uses sourdough bread along with the tomatoes and crumbled goat cheese or feta cheese.  this dish can be baked and served immediately or assembled and refrigerated overnight before baking.

1. heat the oven to 350 degrees
2. lightly coat a shallow 2-quart baking dish with olive oil or cooking spray
3. arrange 4 slices of bread over the bottom of the baking dish , tearing to fit
4. top with half the tomato slices
5. sprinkle the garlic over the tomatoes , then sprinkle with half the chives
6. season with salt and pepper
7. crumble the goat cheese or feta over the chives and drizzle with half of the oil
8. top with remaining bread slices , pressing firmly to fit
9. arrange remaining tomato slices on top , then sprinkle with the remaining chives , the parmesan cheese , and additional pepper to taste
10. drizzle with remaining 1 1 / 2 teaspoons oil
11. bake for 40-45 minutes or until the cheese on top is golden and the tomatoes are soft
demonstrations.review: Very good!  I used shallots, goat cheese and some home-grown zebra tomatoes along with some tomatoes-on-the-vine.  This is a great side dish, and I think it would pair wonderfully with a steak, or eggs from brunch.  Made for ZWT8.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
anzac cookies

this is based on a recipe from beatrice ojakangas’, great holiday baking book.  she explains, “australians still participate in the tradition of four o’clock afternoon tea, which can be a simple or formal occasion, and features a selection of sandwiches, scones, cookies, and cakes that are fancy and plain. this is the time to rest and ‘restoke the furnace.’ these thin, crisp oat and coconut drop cookies are a welcome part of the simplest or most elaborate tea."  i haven’t yet tried this.

1. preheat oven to 350f lightly grease two baking sheets or cover them with parchment paper
2. in a medium-sized bowl , mix well oats , coconut , flour , and sugar
3. mix in butter and honey
4. in a small bowl , mix boiling water and baking soda together and add to the flour mixture
5. drop rounded teaspoonfuls of dough 3 inches apart onto prepared baking sheets
6. bake for 10 to 12 minutes , until crisp and golden brown
7. cool on the baking sheet for 30 seconds
8. loosen with a thin spatula and cool on wire racks
9. if the cookies stick to the sheet , return to the oven for 1 minute , then loosen with a spatula
10. when cool , store in an airtight container
demonstrations.review: Yum - these are delicious!  Really good, will be making these again.

target.recipe_text:
doog s meatloaf

i've been making this meatloaf recipe for approximately 40 years - i've tried many others but keep coming back to this one - it is more moist & tastier than any other i've tried - i hope you enjoy it as well. i generally fix mashed potatoes and green bean casserole with this - always brings a smile to my husbands face when i make this meal.

1. mix all ingredients well - split the mixture evenly between two loaf pans
2. bake @ 350 for 1 1 / 2 hours
3. before applying the topping pour off any grease
4. mix ketchup & brown sugar together & spread evenly over the two loafs
target.review: One of my favorite recipes!  A heavy recipe that is perfect for a cold winter night!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
saag khumb  spinach and mushrooms

bill's recipe.

1. place ginger , garlic and chile into food processor or blender with 1 / 4 cup water and puree
2. heat 1-2 tablespoons ghee in a large skillet over medium heat
3. add mushrooms and saute until tender , about 5-10 minutes
4. add puree and saute , stirring for 30 seconds-1 minute or until fragrant
5. add spinach to pan and season to taste with salt , cooking for an additional minute
6. reduce heat to medium-low , cover , and cook , stirring occasionally , until spinach is soft
7. stir in garam masala , cayenne , cream , and a small amount of water if needed
8. cover and simmer 5-10 minutes
9. serve garnished with chopped cilantro , if desired , along with freshly steamed rice
demonstrations.review: This was delicious!  My DH had requested this and said it tasted just like what you would get at an Indian restaurant - he was raving about it.  I liked the hint of hot spice in it - not too much, just enough.  Thanks for posting :)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
veal scallopini with tomato caper sauce

you can have dinner on the table within 30 minutes with this dish.  the sauce was particularly nice served over green beans and basmati rice.

1. add wine , tomatoes and anchovies to a pot
2. bring to boil , reduce heat to medium low and simmer for 5 to 8 minutes or until thickened
3. stir capers and butter into sauce
4. keep warm
5. heat olive oil and butter in a large skillet over high heat
6. season scallopini with salt and pepper
7. dip scallopini into flour and shake off excess
8. place in skillet and working in batches as necessary , cook about 30 seconds a side or until browned
9. remove to a platter
10. place the scallopini on serving dishes and pour sauce over
11. sprinkle with parsley
demonstrations.review: I'm sorry to say, but this did not turn out well for us.  The veal was very slimy in texture, instead of a breaded texture.  The tomato sauce tasted very fishy/capery.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
creole shrimp and lobster bisque

i watched paula make this on tv today- boy does it look good. if lobster is not affordable, you might substitute with canned crab, extra shrimp or as a last resort imitation crab meat.

1. remove lobster meat from shell
2. coarsely chop and set aside
3. in a large saucepan , melt butter over medium heat
4. add onion , celery , and garlic
5. cook for 5 minutes , stirring occasionally
6. stir in flour , and cook for 2 minutes
7. stir in chicken broth
8. cook for 10 minutes , stirring occasionally , until thickened
9. add lobster meat and shrimp
10. stir in half-and-half and creole seasoning
11. cook for 10 minutes , or until heated through , stirring occasionally
12. meanwhile cut out the center portion of a round loaf of bread
13. brush with olive oil and place on a sturdy cookie sheet
14. bake at 350f for about 15 minutes to seal bowl
15. ladle soup into bread bowl and sprinkle on parmesan and parsley if desired
16. serve immediately
demonstrations.review: This was phenomenal!  I did not put the soup in a bread bowl, instead I served it in regular bowls with crusty bread on the side.  There was not an empty bowl left!  Very easy to make as well :)

target.recipe_text:
chipotle chops

i love chipotle peppers in adobo sauce!  here is a skillet pork chop recipe that i threw together, using the chiles with garlic and onions.  hope you like it!!

1. season both sides of the chops with salt and pepper
2. heat 1 tbsp of the oil in a large texas skillet on medium heat and brown the chops on both sides for about 1 minute per side
3. remove the chops to a plate
4. in the same skillet , heat the other tbsp of oil and add the onions , garlic , and chopped chipotle peppers
5. saute the vegetables until the onions are soft , about 2 or 3 minutes
6. turn the heat down to low
7. stir in the oregano , cumin , and adobo sauce
8. stir all together and heat through , about 2 or 3 more minutes
9. add the chops back to the skillet and keep the heat on low
10. spoon the pepper and onion mixture over and around the chops
11. cook the meat on low for 10 minutes on each side until no longer pink
target.review: My husband & I liked it but thought it was very hot (are we wimps?  Maybe.).  I would cut down on the chipotle next time for us.  I used celery and red pepper instead of onion cuz I hate onion and served over Mexican rice w/ a dollop of guacamole and sour cream on top.  I might add a diced tomato or 2 next time to up the "sauciness" as it wasn't very saucy (I did add some water to help).  Overall good!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
balsamic herbed marinade for goat cheese

this is a great appetizer on crisp french bread, tossed on a salad or topped on cooked steak or hamburger!

1. mix vinegar , lemon juice , orange juice , lemon peel , garlic , basil , rosemary , and oregano in medium bowl
2. gradually whisk in oil
3. season to taste with salt and pepper
4. pour mixture into glass baking dish or a pickling jar
5. add goat cheese
6. turn to coat
7. refrigerate at least 2 hours or up to 2 days , turning occasionally
8. transfer goat cheese to platter
9. spoon marinade over
10. top with sun dried tomatoes and or black olives
demonstrations.review:
Made this for a book club meeting and everyone loved it and asked for the recipe!

OK, I made it again for a ladies' get together and it was loved once again!  I really recommend it. :)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
surin s coconut soup

surin, a thai restaurant with 3 locations in alabama, makes this really really good coconut soup. i found a recipe on yahoo! answers in response to someone's inquiry about the soup. give it a whirl!

1. heat the oil in a large stockpot or dutch oven over medium heat
2. add the lemon grass , ginger , and garlic and cook , stirring constantly , until aromatic , 30 to 60 seconds
3. add the curry paste and cook , stirring constantly , for 30 seconds
4. add 1 / 2 cup chicken stock to the pot and stir to dissolve the curry paste
5. add the remaining stock , fish sauce , and sugar and bring to a boil over medium-high heat
6. reduce the heat to low , partially cover , and simmer to blend flavors , about 20 minutes
7. stir in the coconut milk , chicken , mushrooms , and lime juice
8. bring back to a simmer and cook until the stock is hot and the chicken is no longer pink , about 5 minutes
9. taste for seasoning and add salt if desired
10. serve immediately , garnishing each bowl with cilantro and scallions
11. variation: thai shrimp and coconut soup
12. substitute 1 / 4 pound peeled and deveined medium shrimp for the chicken in step 3
demonstrations.review: I made this tonight for the "New Kids on the Block" tag game.  My husband, myself and my 3 year old son really liked it.  In all fairness I don't think I used quite as much red curry paste, but it was all I had left.  Any more curry and it would have been too spicy for the 3 year old!  I added chopped red, yellow & green peppers for extra veggie and color and served over brown basmati rice.  Great soup that we will make again!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crock pot cream of mushroom soup

very tasty soup. many compliments on this soup. you may use top of stove for this soup, but it might be a little thick so adjust liquid.  energy wise cooking.

1. melt butter or margarine in large skillet over medium heat
2. add mushrooms and onion and saute until tender , about 5 to 7 minutes
3. sprinkle flour , salt , pepper and nutmeg over vegetables
4. stir to blend well
5. place in 5 quart slow cooker
6. using wire whisk , beat in water , cream or half and half , sour cream and chicken broth
7. cook covered , on low for 4 hours
8. turn setting to high
9. cook 1 hour longer , stirring occasionally
10. stir in parsley and serve
demonstrations.review: My family loved this and so did I because it just simmered away all afternoon without me.  I did use 2% Greek yogurt instead of the sour cream (what I had in the house) and it turned out just fine. Used veggie broth for the house vegetarian.

target.recipe_text:
peanut butter chocolate chip mini muffins

perfect for snacking, breakfast on the go, school lunches, preschool snacks...and don't forget a big cold glass of milk to wash them down!

1. preheat oven to 350
2. lightly butter 24 1 3 / 4-by-3 / 4-inch miniature muffin cups
3. i just spray with non-stick spray
4. stir together flour , brown sugar , baking powder and salt in a large bowl
5. in another bowl , stir together milk , peanut butter , oil , egg and vanilla extract until blended
6. make a well in the center of the dry ingredients
7. add liquid ingredients and stir just to combine
8. add the mini chocolate chips
9. spoon batter into prepared muffin cups
10. bake 15 to 20 minutes , or until a toothpick inserted into middle of muffin comes out clean
11. place muffin tin on wire rack and cool for five minutes before removing muffins
12. serve warm or cool completely and store in an airtight container at room temperature
target.review: I made these for a ladies brunch at church and they were delicious!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
apple swirl cake

nan

1. peel , core , and chop apples into small pieces
2. mix together with 3 tablespoons sugar and cinnamon
3. set aside
4. in large bowl , combine sugar and cooking oil
5. beat
6. add eggs , orange juice , and vanilla
7. sift together flour , baking powder , and salt
8. add to creamed mixture
9. beat until smooth
10. pour one third batter into greased and floured 12 cup bundt pan alternating with one half apple mixture
11. repeat
12. end with layer of batter on top
13. bake at 325 degrees f for 60 minutes or until cake tests done
14. cool in pan 10 to 15 minutes
15. turn out on wire rack or serving plate to complete cooling
16. sprinkle with confectioners sugar
demonstrations.review: Great cake!  I added extra apples and had to bake a bit longer but it turned out lovely.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
light   easy creamy dessert

this is a very refreshing dessert, i've tried it with several different flavors of gelatin and it has not dissapointed me yet. cook time is for refrigeration.

1. mix boiling water and gelatin dessert until gelatin is disolved completely
2. add ice cubes , stir until ice is melted
3. whisk in yogurt until smooth
4. refrigerate until set
demonstrations.review: Great recipe!  I am looking forward to mixing flavors and my husband suggested freezing for a different texture since I'm not a big fan of the texture of yogurt.  Going in the healthy dessert file.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
spanish chicken   rice bake

a throw-it-together and pop it in the oven supper. use more chili powder or add hot sauce if you really want to spice it up!
i just want to add:  many people who have tried this recipe have had to cook it longer than i have specified. a hint:  i always use a casserole dish with a heavy tight-fitting lid. i sometimes presoak my rice in cold water for 10 minutes or so.  hope this helps! =)  barb
ps...to freeze : cool, portion and freeze in a ziploc bag.
to reheat: thaw, place in a covered casserole dish and bake until heated through.

1. mix soup , salsa , water , corn , and beans and rice in 2-quart shallow baking dish
2. top with chicken and sprinkle with chili powder
3. cover tightly with casserole lid or foil
4. bake at 375f for 45 minutes or so
5. sprinkle with cheese
demonstrations.review: Instead of salsa I used a can of Rotel and increased a few things to feed a larger group of people like the cream of soup, chicken and corn.  It took a bit longer to cook and looked a little off but tasted great.

target.recipe_text:
margie s marvelous bonbons

don't remember where i got this recipe. i haven't timed how long it takes to prepare this so time is a guess. the recipes says it makes 150 bon-bons but the yield depends on the size you make them.

1. combine sweetened condensed milk , sugar and butter
2. mix until smooth and creamy
3. add coconut and walnuts
4. mix thoroughly
5. chill 1 hour
6. form into balls
7. chill 2 hours
8. melt chocolate in a double boiler over hot water
9. dip bon-bons into melted chocolate
10. cool until chocolate is set
11. store in fridge
target.review:
1 halved the sugar mentioned in the recipe....but it was extremely sweet.what if i use unsweetened condence milk?
Any suggestions?

demonstrations.recipe_text:
lamb chops with minted hollandaise sauce

instead of the traditional mint sauce, lamb chops are served here with a creamy hollandaise sauce flavored with fresh mint. the sauce is not difficult to make, as long as it is cooked over gentle heat. enjoy!

1. brush the chops on both sides with a little oil and season with black pepper
2. put the chops under the broiler , 4 inches from the heat , and cook for 3-4 minutes on each side for medium-rare chops , slightly longer for well-done
3. arrange the lamb chops on warmed serving plates and serve immediately with the warm minted hollandaise sauce
4. good served with asparagus and a carrot salad
5. hollandaise sauce: whisk together the lemon juice , viegar , and egg yolks
6. put over a saucepan of simmering water and whisk until thick
7. melt the butter and add , a little at a time , to the egg-yolk mixture , whisking constantly until the sauce thickens
8. stir in the fresh mint and season with salt and pepper to taste
9. transfer to a gravy boat and serve immediately
10. variation: lemon and thyme hollandaise: make the sauce as directed , substituting 1 tsp grated lemon zest and 1 tbls chopped fresh thyme for the chopped mint
11. serve with the lamb chops
demonstrations.review: First time ever I have made lamb chops & hollandaise sauce,was extremely nervous.The sauce turned out delicious I used 2 small egg yolks also decreased the vinegar by 1/2 a spoon.The chops I  boiled with bay leaf, cloves,cinnamon & whole black pepper.then dabbed them with olive oil,pepper& salt & grilled them.they turned out perfect.Thank you.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mushrooms stuffed with feta cheese and garlic

nan

1. clean and remove stems of mushrooms and baste mushrooms with melted butter
2. combine all ingredients except for the mushrooms and stir until mixture is well blended
3. fill the mushrooms with the mixture , mounding the mixture high into the caps
4. bake in a 350 f oven until hot
5. then broil for a few seconds until lightly browned
demonstrations.review: WOW.Thanks,they were just wiped out as soon as I served them,did'nt get to taste one.Going to make another batch soon & this time I will make sure I get to taste them.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
emeril s creamed spinach

i saw this recipe on food tv's web site and had to try it. i love his recipes and this one is no exception. i make it several times a year.

1. preheat the oven to 375 degrees
2. lightly grease a 6 cup casserole
3. in a large saute pan , melt the remaining butter
4. add the onions and season with salt and pepper
5. saute for about 2 minutes , or until the onions are soft
6. add the spinach
7. season with salt and pepper
8. saute for 3 to 4 minutes
9. add the garlic and cream
10. mix well
11. season the mixture with salt and pepper
12. bring the liquid to a boil and reduce to a simmer
13. simmer the mixture for 6 minutes
14. remove the pan from the heat and turn into the prepared pan
15. add 1 / 2 of cheese to casserole and stir
16. sprinkle the top with the remainder of the grated cheese and place in the oven
17. bake for about 4 to 6 minutes or until the cheese is slightly brown and bubbly
demonstrations.review: I've eaten creamed spinach plenty of times,but never tried to make it.This recipe is superb.will keep making it again & again.Thank you Mystery girl.

target.recipe_text:
wonderful salsa

this is the best salsa recipe i've found so far and i've tried about a dozen. i got it from one of the local hospital cookbooks that are sold in my area. i changed it a bit and have been canning it for years. the reason i plant a garden is for this salsa. we would be lost without it. hope you like it as much as we do.  one of our members who is a food scientist took this salsa to work, tested the ph and found it measured under 4.0 (well within the safety limit for boiling water bath processing).

1. mix all together and bring to a slow boil for 10 minute
2. seal in jars and cook in hot water bath for 10 minute
3. this is a medium salsa
4. this is also a chunky salsa so if you want a smoother salsa cut your veggies into smaller pieces
5. yields 3-6 quarts or pints
target.review: This really should be named "To Die For Salsa." So easy and sooooo tasty. I did add 1/4 cup of cilantro but other than that I didn't change anything and it was exceptional......to die for !! Thanks a bazillion for sharing.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mexican tortilla casserole

i really enjoy making this dish as well as eating it and my family will agree to that!  i hope you all enjoy it as much as we do. :o)

1. brown and drain meat
2. stir in onion , bell peppers , chilies , and season mix
3. cook until veggies are slightly tender
4. blend salsa in blender and pour 1 / 2 cup on bottom of a greased 9x13-inch baking dish
5. cover with 5 tortillas , spread with 1 / 2 of meat mix and 1 / 2 more salsa , sprinkle with 1 cup of cheese and layer rest of ingredients
6. bake for 20 minutes at 350f or until top is golden brown
7. top with lettuce , sour cream tomatoes , whatever you like
8. enjoy
demonstrations.review: This recipe is delicious and a real keeper. I used chicken instead of ground beef. I cut 4 skinless and boneless breasts into small bite size pieces and also used 3 cups of salsa instead of 2. Other than those changes, I followed the recipe exactly. Yum yum. Thanks a bunch for sharing.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
grandma s breakfast casserole

another breakfast dish you can make the night before if you wish. i like the stewed tomatoes and oregano in this dish.

1. prepare 9" quiche dish or pie plate by spraying with non-stick cooking spray
2. layer the onions , ham , and tomatoes into pie pan
3. mix together the eggs , milk , oregano , and bisquick
4. pour on top of layered mixture
5. top with cheese
6. may be refrigerated overnight at this point
7. bake at 350f degrees for 45 minutes
8. preheat oven to 350
demonstrations.review: I made this this morning for breakfast using ham and we loved it. Not only very tasty but beautiful. I'll definitely make this again. The only thing I added was salt and additional cheese. Thanks for sharing.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
best ever fudge

i've been making this recipe at holiday time for 25 years and it never fails!

1. mix together sugar , evaporated milk , and 2 sticks butter in electric skillet at 250 degrees until comes to a boil
2. time and stir for 10 minutes
3. unplug skillet
4. add hershey bar and chocolate chips , stirring until smooth
5. add marshmallow creme and stir until smooth
6. add walnuts and vanilla and mix well
7. pour into greased 9 x 13 baking pan
8. cool and cut into serving pieces
demonstrations.review: I have never "stirred" so much in my life, but every stir was worth it....and more! It's very creamy and absolutely delicious. I recommend this recipe to anyone who is a fudge lover and even those who are not. Thanks Annie.

target.recipe_text:
hubby s low fat yummy dried berry muffins

my husband has started creating his own wonderful low-fat recipes and this one is delish! fabulous for breakfast. he actually uses just shy of 1/4 cup of applesauce, but i couldn't figure out how to note that!

1. preheat your oven to 400 degrees
2. in a bowl mix the milk , the egg , the applesauce , the oil , and the vanilla
3. mix well and set aside
4. in another bowl combine the flour , wheat germ , baking powder , and salt
5. add the wet to the dry , mixing just until combined
6. add the dried berries and just mix until combined
7. bake at 400 degrees for 20-25 minutes or until brown
target.review: These were quite tasty! I used dried cranberries, and some pecans. Also added a bit of cinnamon.  Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
microwave chocolate mug brownie

this makes a delicious brownie for one in about a minute. 60 seconds makes a molten center brownie. 75 seconds make a uniformly done brownie. be careful not to overcook.

1. in a coffee mug , add water / milk , melted butter / oil , a dash of salt and vanilla extract
2. whisk well
3. add cocoa powder , whisk well
4. add sugar , whisk well
5. add flour , whisk well
6. microwave for 60 seconds
7. center should be slightly molten
8. careful not to overcook
9. enjoy with a spoon
10. careful , brownie will be hot
demonstrations.review: Oh man, too good. Mine was done in 55-60 seconds.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
black bean and tortilla bake

great quick and healthy dinner.

1. preheat oven to 350 f
2. spray a large skillet with cooking spray
3. add garlic , onions , tomato , green onion , cumin , and chili powder
4. cook on medium heat until onion is tender
5. add tomato sauce and cook 5 minutes more
6. stir in beans , cilantro , salt and pepper
7. spray a 9 inch square baking dish with cooking spray
8. layer 4 tortillas , 1 / 3 cheese , and 1 / 3 of the bean mixture
9. repeat 2 more times
10. top with reserved 2 tablespoons of cheese
11. bake 20 minutes , covered , then 10 minutes uncovered or until bubbly
demonstrations.review: Ahhh I love this! Very easy, and very flavourful.  I would recommend doubling the filling. Served with sour-cream, so good.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
horse muffins  oat and carrot

a moist, tasty, and healthy muffin!  perfect for breakfast, snacks, or tea.  these muffins are sugar-free, but if you prefer a sweeter muffin, add a bit of sugar to the batter or sprinkle on top before baking.

1. preheat oven to 350f spray 9 muffin cups with no-stick cooking spray
2. combine oatmeal , applesauce , and water
3. stir to combine
4. add flour through allspice
5. stir until just combined
6. stir in carrots
7. fill muffin cups 3 / 4 full
8. bake for approximately 20 minutes
demonstrations.review: Yummy!

target.recipe_text:
low carb pizza

i got this delicious recipe from www.atkinsdietbulletboard.com the orginal chef is bikergoddess. we all thank her for creating this great recipe. it's not exactly like pizza, but it's pretty close. i like it alot. i've made it twice now, and will be making it over and over again.

1. preheat oven to 375 degrees f
2. beat together cream cheese and eggs until smooth
3. add cream , parmesan , chives , italian seasoning and garlic
4. spray 9x13 pan with cooking spray or oil
5. place 2 cups mozzarella cheese in bottom of pan
6. pour egg mixture over cheese
7. bake for 30 minutes
8. remove from oven and spread sauce over baked mixture
9. add toppings of choice
10. cover with remaining mozzerella cheese
11. bake until bubbly and brown
12. let stand for 5 minutes
target.review: Really surprisingly good!! Thanks for a recipe to get you thru those first two weeks of low carb dieting!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
low carb custard

i got this off another recipe website. i 'tweacked' it to fit my taste. i also would like to try this recipe with an egg substitute to help reduce the fat. i used 6 oz ramekin dishes and had plenty to fill 8+ dishes. i made it for dessert and i enjoyed it as breakfast the next several mornings.

1. set oven to 350 degrees f
2. beat the eggs and add heavy cream , water , flavor extract , and artificial sweetner together
3. blend well
4. pour mixture into 6 to 8 ramekin dishes
5. sprinkle with the cinnamon or nutmeg on top
6. place ramekin dishes inside a larger baking dish of cool water
7. be sure the level of the water is 1 / 2 way up the dishes
8. bake for 30 minutes or until center is firm
9. let sit for 5 minutes before serving or refrigerating
demonstrations.review: You need AT LEAST 1/2 cup of splenda and I would definitley put the cinnamon in the custard in addition to a sprinkling of pumpkin pie spice or nutmeg on top. It is really good though..especially when you're on Atkins or SBD!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
low fat french toast casserole

a warm breakfast casserole that is full of flavor.

1. preheat oven to 400 degrees
2. spray 13 x 9 inch baking pan with nonstick coating
3. layer bread evenly in bottom of baking pan
4. beat together milk , 1 / 4 cup honey , salt , vanilla and 1 teaspoon cinnamon until well blended
5. then mix in beaten eggs with above mixture
6. pour batter evenly over torn bread
7. core and slice apples , leaving peelings on
8. layer apple slices evenly over top and drizzle with 1 / 2 cup of honey
9. sprinkle remaining cinnamon over top of casserole
10. bake for 35 to 45 minutes or until bread layer isn't soggy
11. cut into 12 pieces while warm and serve with additional honey , if desired
demonstrations.review: I followed JVO's review and used 11 slices of bread, egg beaters, and skim milk, also I peeled the apples. This was absolute PERFECTION!!!! We all LOVED it!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
banana bread pancakes

these are like a cross between banana bread and pancakes. they are on the heavy side and very filling. recipe courtesy the shooting star bed & breakfast

1. for the pancakes: in a large bowl , combine flour , salt , sugar , cinnamon , baking powder , nutmeg and ginger
2. in a medium bowl , combine egg yolks , butter , milk , and vanilla
3. add to flour mixture and mix briefly
4. beat egg whites until stiff peaks form
5. gently fold into batter
6. gently fold in bananas and walnuts
7. cook pancakes until golden brown on both sides
8. top with caramelized bananas and reserved walnuts
9. serve with warm applesauce
10. for the bananas: melt butter in a non-stick saucepan over medium heat
11. add brown and white sugar and nutmeg
12. cook until sugars dissolve
13. add bananas
14. cook until mixture thickens and bananas start to brown
demonstrations.review: YUM! I just used this recipe for the banana sauce only, so I can only speak for how wonderful that was! Note--it takes several minutes for the sugars and butter to cream together...

target.recipe_text:
kittencal s moist cheddar garlic oven fried chicken breast

this is for serious garlic lovers. the chicken bakes out so moist and tender! grated cheese may be sprinkled on top of the breast the last 5 minutes of cooking if desired but that is optional. double all ingredients for more than four breasts and adjust the amount of garlic to suit taste. for the coating amount you might be able to get away with 5 or maybe 6 very small chicken breasts, but i would suggest to increase the amount slightly --- to take this dish to yet another level, about 10 minutes before the cooking time is finished, drizzle the top of the chicken with a little pasta sauce, then sprinkle mozzarella cheese on top. return to oven for about 10 minutes until the chicken is completely cooked and sauce is hot and cheese has melted. for a lemon-garlic flavor add in 3 tablespoons lemon juice to the melted butter/garlic mixture ---  *note* for a healthier alternative smart balance butter blend may be used in place of the melted butter --- you will love this chicken!
visit my food blog, www.kittencalskitchen.com, for more of my recipes.

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. butter an 11 x 7-inch pan
3. in a bowl , combine melted butter with fresh minced garlic , 1 teaspoon garlic powder and salt
4. in another bowl , combine the dry breadcrumbs with 1 / 2 cup finely grated cheddar cheese , parmesan cheese 1 teaspoon garlic powder and coarse ground black pepper
5. dip chicken in butter mixture
6. then in crumb mixture
7. place in prepared pan and bake uncovered for 35-45 minutes or until cooked through , larger breasts may take more time
8. top with shredded cheddar or mozzarella the last 5 minutes of cooking (this is only optional
target.review: Oh my...this is so delicious!  And also quick and easy.  The chicken was so moist and has such a great flavor.  One thing to mention,  there is no need to double the coating ... this works out almost perfect for the 4 chicken breasts as stated in the directions.  Thanks for another fabulous recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
world s best chicken noodle soup

my mom started making this soup after finding it in a magazine (?), but i made a few adaptions and here it is!

1. bring water and bouillon cubes to boil in 5 quart pan
2. add noodles
3. when noodles are cooked , add chicken and soup , stir until combined throughly
4. remove from heat and add sour cream
5. salt and pepper to taste
6. enjoy !
demonstrations.review: This was fabulous!  I did add a 12 ounce package of frozen mirepoix blend (carrots, celery and onions) along with 6 cans of chicken broth instead of water and bouillon cubes.  I used a rotisserie chicken and this was ready in less than 45 minutes start to finish!  This will be my go to Chicken soup from now on!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
world s best ribs

this recipe is quite simple and the results are incredible. i usually double the rub recipe and store it in a jar for next time. if you've never tried ribs before, try this recipe. this recipe can be made on the grill or in the oven.

1. mix brown sugar , emeril's essence , salt , pepper , paprika , cumin , garlic and cayenne pepper thoroughly , and sprinkle on both sides of ribs to taste
2. for grilling , carefully wrap in aluminum foil and cook bone side down approximately 1 1 / 2 hours on low temperature
3. no need to turn
4. after ribs become tender , remove from foil and continue cooking on both sides to desired crispness
5. apply barbecue sauce liberally to both sides and allow approximately 10 minutes for barbecue sauce to caramelize
6. brush a second time if desired , and allow to caramelize
7. remove from grill and enjoy !
8. for oven baking , wrap in aluminum foil and place on a cookie sheet in a 275f oven for 4 hours
9. place a pan with water in the oven also to keep them moist
10. remove and discard foil and brush with barbecue sauce and allow 10 minutes to caramelize
11. brush a second time if desired
12. remove from oven and enjoy !
demonstrations.review: I had never made ribs before and I bought some danish baby back ribs and tried this recipe.  It was out of this world!  The meat was falling off the bone while I was serving!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mrs  geraldine s ground beef casserole

this recipe came from a local church fund raising cook book. mrs. geraldine is a good friend of the family. she reminds me so much of mrs. clause, that i can't help but smile every time i think of her. this recipe freezes well. do not bake before freezing. just put it together, freeze it, thaw it and cook.

1. brown meat in large skillet or dutch oven
2. add onions , pepper and celery and simmer for 15 minutes
3. add tomatoes and tomato sauce , mushrooms , brown sugar and worcestershire sauce
4. add salt and pepper to taste
5. cook in skillet for 1 hour
6. place cooked pasta in bottom of large casserole dish
7. spoon mushroom soup over pasta
8. pour sauce over the soup and top with cheese
9. bake in 350f oven for 30-45 minutes
10. can sizes do not have to be exact , just as long as they are within a close range , everything will work out
demonstrations.review: Very easy recipe and delicious too!  The only tweek I made was adding about 5 oz of cream cheese to the mixture (like other reviewers, I mixed everything but cheese together before putting in 9 x 13 baking pan) and it was so good.  An added bonus it that this recipe calls for basic pantry items.  Thanks so much!

target.recipe_text:
crock pot chicken vindaloo

for the vegetarian version: use your favorite veggies, omit the cinnamon stick. this is my sister's recipe (thank you najla! xoxo), she made it on the stove top. it's really yummy!!

1. puree first 10 ingredients in a blender
2. pour into the crock pot , add tomato sauce , cinnamon stick and onion and mix well
3. add chicken and turn to cover
4. cook on low for 5 hours
5. sprinkle with chopped parsley before serving
6. serve with rice or rolls , enjoy !
target.review: Thank you, this recipe was great. Very easy to make and had an excellent flavor.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
best cream of broccoli soup

this recipe is thick and flavorful. simple, delicious, and quick to make. hope that you enjoy it as much as my family does. i have added chicken to this soup, very good

1. melt 2 tablespoons butter in medium sized stock pot , and saut onion , garlic and celery until tender
2. add broccoli and broth
3. cover and simmer for 10 minutes
4. pure soup or mash with potato masher
5. return to heat
6. in small saucepan , over medium heat melt 3 tablespoons butter , stir in flour and add milk
7. stir until thick and bubbly , add to soup
8. add cheese
9. stir until melted
10. season with pepper and serve
demonstrations.review: We are hooked on this recipe. This is the easiest and best tasting broccoli soup I have made. Thank you!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cinnamon muffins

muffins are good anytime of the day.

1. mix flour , sugar , baking powder , salt , nutmeg and allspice
2. add egg , milk and butter
3. stir into dry ingredients until moistened
4. spoon into greased or paper-lined muffin cups
5. bake at 400 degrees for 20 minutes or until done
6. for topping combine sugar and cinnamon
7. brush top of warm muffin in butter and dip top of muffin into sugar / cinnamon mixture
demonstrations.review: These muffins were so good I couldn't stop eating them. They were very easy to make and the sugared tops were the best.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
creamy greek salad dressing

greek salads are usually only dressed with olive oil and maybe lemon juice or red-wine vinegar. but this dressing is made of 'greek' ingredients so, it's my greek dressing.

1. in a blender or food processor , whirl all the ingredients except the buttermilk for one minute
2. with the blender running , slowly pour in the buttermilk and blend until thick and creamy
3. chill at least 1 hour so the flavours meld
4. refrigerate , tightly covered
5. this makes nearly 2 cups of dressing and stays fresh for 3-4 days
6. if the dressing separates , just give it a whizz in the blender again
demonstrations.review: My wife and I really enjoyed this dressing. I would change nothing about it. Thank You

target.recipe_text:
buttered wine rice

from a women's weekly dinner party cookbook.
a nice change from plain rice!
if you have any leftovers, add some cooked peas, canned tuna & some cream for an easy tuna rice dish, yum!

1. heat butter in a pan , add onion and cook gently until onion is tender and lightly golden
2. add rice and stir for 3 minutes
3. add 1 cup of hot chicken stock to pan and stir until almost completely dissolved
4. add remaining stock & wine , bring to the boil , reduce heat & simmer gently for approximately 10 mins until rice is tender
5. season with salt & pepper & serve
target.review: This was a great change from regular rice.  Loved it.  Will definitely make it again.  I had to use medium grain rice since I discovered (too late) that I was all out of long grain.  It came out very much like a risotto but without all the work.  Next time I may try adding some Parmesan cheese & see how it tastes.  Thanks for a great recipe Mandy.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
easy baked italian chicken

easy and yummy! dump it all in a pan and bake. serve with potato bakers done in same oven for a wonderful meal.

1. mix together oil , vinegar and garlic in a covered jar and shake well
2. arrange chicken in a shallow baking pan and sprinkle with salt , pepper and poultry seasoning
3. pour oil and vinegar mixture over chicken and bake at 350 for about an hour or until done
demonstrations.review: I used 2 leg quarters & marinated them in the vinegar/oil for about 15-20 minutes before cooking.  I took them out, sprinkled them with seasoning & put them in the dish along with some cut-up potatoes.  Poured the vinegar/oil liquid over the potatoes but did not disturb the seasoning on the chicken.  Later I basted the chicken & potatoes with the liquid several times.  Turned out great.  The only thing I'll do different next time is precook the potatoes somewhat.  They took longer than expected to cook.  Thanks Marie, for a good & easy chicken recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
grilled pork chops with lime  cilantro   garlic

these sound so good i am posting the recipe before trying it. i will add comments after i make them. the recipe is from american cooking club magazinejune/july 05 edition

1. blend the first 5 ingredients , cover and place in the fridge for an hour or longer
2. reserve 1 / 2 cup
3. grill or bbq brushing the chops with the mayo blend , continue brushing and cooking until the chops are done turning them halfway through
4. serve with the reseved mayo mixture on the side
demonstrations.review:
This made the most moist pork chops I think I've ever eaten.  My husband & I just loved them...and we liked the sauce so much we used the left-over on a steak a few nights later.  Now I make up the sauce just to use on our Friday night steaks.
I made only small changes, I used ground coriander instead of cilantro (didn't have any) & reg. chili powder instead of chipotle powder (same reason).  This sauce is always in our refrigerator.  
PS Also good with grilled fish.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
potato rolled tacos

potatoes with jalapeños and cheese rolled in a corn tortilla and fried till crispy. i started making these because i miss the potato tacos in san diego.

1. chop jalapeo peppers finely
2. chop cilantro
3. boil potatoes till easy to mash but still a little firm
4. mash potatoes and add jalapeos , taco seasoning , cilantro and cheese together
5. prepare tortillas by fast steaming so they are easy to roll
6. i usually boil water in a small pot a little smaller than the tortilla's then place a double paper towel on top and place one tortilla at a time for 2 or 3 seconds till steamed , then remove and replace as you go
7. take a steamed tortilla and spoon about 1 tablespoon of potato mixture in and roll gently
8. place in baking dish with the rolled side down
9. continue doing this lining them up in dish as you go
10. place in freezer for 15 minutes or until they become slightly stiff
11. i like this method better than toothpicks
12. heat oil on medium heat
13. when oil is ready , place 4 tacos at a time with the rolled side down in pan
14. flip to other side when brown
15. remove and drain on paper towels
16. garnish as desired
17. i use sour cream mixed with taco sauce drizzled over the top
demonstrations.review:
These were really good.  I never thought of potatoes in tacos, but wow.  DH said he'd definitely like them again.  I'll have to improve my rolling ability, but I will do these again.  Thanks Jamilah's Kitchen.
Made for ZWT5.

target.recipe_text:
cheesy ham and potato soup

comfort soup at its finest!  i usually make this to use up leftover ham.  this is easy to adapt with other ingredients.  i don't put celery in mine.  i have added garlic sometimes as well.

1. combine potatoes , celery , carrots , onion , ham , and water / broth in stockpot and bring to boil
2. then cook over medium heat until potatoes are tender
3. stir in the chicken bouillon , salt , and pepper
4. in separate saucepan , melt butter over medium-low heat
5. whisk in flour and cook stirring constantly until thick
6. slowly stir in milk as not to allow lumps to form and all milk is added
7. turn up to medium heat
8. continue to stir until thick
9. add in cheese and stir until melted
10. stir the cheese mixture into the stockpot and cook until heated through
target.review: I added my ham bone to the cooking water, it was fantastic!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
my favorite sub  hoagie  rolls

when it comes to sub rolls, i prefer mine light and fluffy. i make up a big batch of these and freeze them for later use.

1. dissolve sugar in water and add yeast to proof
2. rest one to two minutes
3. melt butter and , along with the salt , stir into yeast mixture
4. mix in flour , 1 cup at a time until desired consistency is reached
5. knead until very well developed
6. your dough is finished when you can tear a small piece off , roll into a ball and stretch to form a nearly transparent "window" between your fingers without it tearing
7. cover with plastic wrap and let stand until doubled in bulk
8. lightly dust a small amount of corn meal over well-greased pans , roll your dough into long , thin "logs" and place about 3" apart on the pans
9. slash each loaf every inch and a half with a knife , brush with egg white and sprinkle with sesame seeds if desired
10. let double in size
11. bake in a 400f oven until golden brown
demonstrations.review: These were great!  I subbed 2 cups wheat flour.  They came out perfect for my roast beef sandwiches.  Thanks Wildflower.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
stir fry chicken with garlic sauce

nice and simple. prep time includes marinating time.

1. combine garlic , soy sauce , water , honey , 1 tablespoon oil , cornstarch and black / red pepper
2. stir chicken into marinade and mix to coat
3. cover and refrigerate at least 2 hours , stirring once to twice
4. in large skillet , heat remaining oil
5. using slotted spoon , transfer chicken to skillet
6. stir-fry about 5 minutes
7. add reserved marinade
8. continue to cook and stir about 30 seconds until thickened
9. remove to platter
10. garnish with green onion
11. serve with snow peas , if desired
demonstrations.review: Yum!  I didn't have time to marinate and it still tasted great.  As an added bonus, I was able to use up some fresh veggies I had in the fridge!  Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
french toast sticks   oamc

i got this basic recipe from another site but changed it a little for my family.  the original recipe called for orange juice as the liquid instead of milk.  i also added the vanilla as we think it gives it a nice flavor.

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees fahrenheit
2. cut each slice of bread into 3 pieces to make sticks
3. texas toast is a very thick sliced bread about 3 / 4" thick
4. you could substitute french bread if texas toast is not available
5. in a bowl , mix together melted butter , eggs , sugar , cinnamon , vanilla and milk
6. beat well
7. dip sticks into egg mixture and place on a cookie sheet that has been sprayed with cooking spray
8. if there is any dip left , you can drizzle it over the sticks
9. bake for 25 minutes on middle rack of oven
10. turn halfway through baking time
11. allow to cool
12. flash freeze on cookie sheet , remove and place in a ziploc bag
13. to reheat: place 3 sticks on a microwave-safe plate and heat on high for 1 minute until warm
14. serve with syrup
demonstrations.review: These were great fresh out of the oven.  I have to agree with a previous reviewer, they are not as good reheated in the microwave (they seemed to get a little rubbery)

target.recipe_text:
thai chicken fried rice with basil   kao pad krapao

another delicious way to enjoy fried rice, fragrant with the heady aroma of basil!

1. in a wok or large skillet , stir-fry garlic in oil until golden
2. then add chilies and chicken and stir-fry until chicken is cooked
3. add rice , sugar , fish sauce , and soy sauce , and stir-fry , mixing gently
4. when well mixed , add shallots , basil leaves and cilantro
5. cook another minute or so , and serve
6. if you desire , serve with lime wedges , chile sauce , fish sauce , or soy sauce at the table
target.review: Excellent recipe.  Extremely easy to make - in fact, this was all I made for dinner.  Wonderful aroma while cooking, and a great flavor.  I actually used aborito rice because that's all I had, but I cooked it as rice and not risotto.  Wonderful!  Thanks, Sue!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chicken and mango curry

i haven't made this yet but it sounds amazing. it's a thai curry. i'm storing here on zaar so i'll know where to find it!

1. in a deep frying pan or wok heat oil over medium heat until hot
2. add curry paste and garlic and cook , stirring , for about 30 seconds
3. slowly stir in coconut milk and chicken broth
4. reduce heat to simmer
5. add chicken and cook for 10 to 15 minutes
6. remove and discard garlic
7. add ginger , onion , and peppers
8. cook until tender , about 7 minutes
9. add mango , straw mushrooms , fish sauce , and sugar
10. when heated through , serve over individual plates of hot rice
11. garnish with cilantro
demonstrations.review: This was excellent.  I don't know the ff milk/coconut extract suggestion, but wish I did to make it lower fat!  Either way, this was great.  I used low fat coconut milk, and 3 tbsp red curry paste.  It was pretty hot!  But maybe I have strong curry.  We loved it.  Great recipe, can't wait to make it again.  Next time we will add a few more veggies too:  some snow peas and julliened carrots.  Thanks for a great recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chocolate wine truffles

i referred to these in a post as raspberry wine truffles, because i had used raspberry wine. i've also used black cherry. so the name is up to the wine you use. you can also make white wine truffles by using white instead of red. these do improve with age. at least a few weeks of aging and the flavor is so good.

1. heat the chocolate chips and honey in a 3 qt
2. saucepan on low heat , and stir constantly until chocolate is melted
3. remove from the heat
4. stir in wafers , nuts and wine
5. shape mixture into 1 inch balls and roll in sugar
6. an easy way to do this: put your sugar in a shallow pan with sides , then add some rolled truffles , and just kind of shake the pan gently back and forth , and from side to side
7. they roll around and coat themselves
8. store truffles in tightly covered cookie jar or metal can
9. let stand for several days to blend the flavors
10. flavor improves with age up to 4 weeks
11. you can also do this with white wine: omit the chocolate and do not heat the honey
12. use dry white wine instead of the red
13. mix all ingredients except sugar
14. continue to shape balls and roll in sugar
15. this way makes 2 1 / 2 dozen truffles
demonstrations.review: I made these as part of Christmas gifts (that get passed out at Thanksgiving) and everyone loved them.  I used Cherry Wine (since they were going to MI).  It was SO SO easy, I am making them again this weekend for more Christmas goodies.  Thanks for a great recipe.  Oh, also, I let them sit for about 3 weeks before we ate them.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
greek style turkey burgers

the best turkey burgers i have ever tried .... i freeze left-overs, and heat in the microwave later ...

1. combine all the ingredients in a large bowl
2. form into 4 patties , then grill
3. i have served this on regular burger buns with tomatoes and mayo , and on pita with tahini , tomatoes and lettuce
demonstrations.review: Wonderful, wonderful burgers.  Even my picky husband thought it was phenominal.  I did omit the onion powder because I didn't have any, and the olives because I don't like them.  Great recipe, I know I'll make it again.

target.recipe_text:
hot pepper jelly

this is my signature jelly. i make it for everyone and every occasion. i have even made some and tinted purple for dreamgoddess' daughters wedding. it is very easy and can be made as hot or as mild as you want. for really hot i use 4 habarnero peppers, for milder, use in the amount called for in recipe using your preference in peppers. i just throw the peppers in the blender in large chunks with the vinegar and let the blender to the chopping for me.

1. chop peppers and put in blender with vinegar
2. blend well and pour into large boiler
3. add sugar and mix well
4. bring mixture to a rolling boil and boil for 1 minute
5. remove from heat , strain through sieve and return liquid back to a boil
6. boil for 5 minutes
7. remove from heat
8. add certo and food coloring quickly
9. put into 6 jars and seal
10. i use heated seal method , where i heat the lids in boiling water , place on jar , secure ring tightly and turn jar upside down for 5 minutes
11. turn jar up correctly and allow to cool completely before storing
12. newer studies show that it is safer to seal with the hot water bath method
13. to do this , put into a large boiler with rack on bottom , cover with 1-2 inches of water and boil for 5 minutes
14. remove to rack to cool
target.review: This was amazing.  I used the 5 habanero base and jalapenos for the rest.  I used one foil pkg. of Certo and didn't strain.  Perfect!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
catfish parmesan

southern living; living in the south, catfish is always plentiful and fresh. my family really likes it prepared this way.

1. mix together cheese , flour , salt , pepper , and paprika in large bowl or plastic bag
2. in another bowl , combine egg and milk
3. stir well
4. dip fillets in egg mixture
5. dredge in flour mixture
6. place fillets in a lightly greased oblong baking dish
7. drizzle with butter
8. bake at 350 degrees for 35-40 minutes or until fish flakes easily
demonstrations.review: Big fan.  This was easy and so good.  I even ate it cold as a snack the next day.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
armadillo eggs  stuffed jalapenos

these are so yummy. the cheese and bacon are a great compliment to the jalapeno flavor and reduce the heat of the peppers. this is my adaptation of an appetizer i had many years ago.

1. slice jalapenos in half and clean out seeds
2. mix cheese , onion and garlic salt together and spoon into jalapeno halves
3. wrap each with 1 / 2 strip of bacon
4. place on cookie rack placed over a cookie sheet to catch the drippings
5. bake at 350 for about 45 minutes or until the bacon is crisp
6. the thin bacon wraps easier
7. i just tuck the ends under the bottom
8. amazingly , these are not hot if you get all the seeds out
9. there are never enough of them no matter how many i make because they are so popular
demonstrations.review: Wow!  I don't eat bacon but my family does.  I gave this recipe to my mom who took them to a party.  They were the big, big hit.  She took the very next weekend to annother function and got rave reviews. Sounds like a keeper!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
toasted ravioli

these italian appetizers are crunchy and delicious dipped in a warm marinara sauce. they are very addictive! make a bunch, you'll need to have a lot!

1. cook ravioli in boiling salted water until they float to the top
2. remove from water and drain
3. set aside to cool
4. heat vegetable oil in fryer at least 2" deep to a temperature of 375 degrees
5. dip ravioli in beaten egg , then cover in breadcrumbs
6. fry in batches in hot oil until golden brown , about 5 minutes
7. drain
8. sprinkle hot ravioli with parmesan cheese
9. heat marinara sauce and set aside in serving bowl
10. serve ravioli with dipping sauce
demonstrations.review: These were a huge hit.  I used an artichoke ravioli and they were so good, next time I don't think I'll even bother with the sauce.

target.recipe_text:
tomato cakes

a dish from the depression that appeals to weight-watchers and vegetarians and vegans. makes a great light meal or a different side dish.

1. variation: you may add a teaspoon or more of salsa to spice these up , just don't add so much that they get goopy !
2. empty tomatoes into medium-to-large bowl
3. add chopped onion , salt and pepper , and crushed saltines
4. mix well
5. let set in refrigerator for 15-30 minutes
6. mix again and form mixture into cakes , then fry on both sides until golden brown on each side
7. serve as main dish for a light meal or a side dish--great with macaroni and cheese !
target.review: These were wonderful and are a perfect side for macaroni and cheese.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
ultimate pizza sauce

this pizza sauce recipe was given to me as a wedding present, written on the inside cover of a pizza cookbook. it is thick, saucy, spicy and delicious. i'll never use anything else on my homemade pizzas. i like to double or triple it and put it in ziploc bags in my freezer.

1. in a large skillet , melt butter with the oil
2. add the onion , celery and garlic and saute until soft and transparent
3. add tomato sauce and tomato paste and stir until smooth
4. add remaining ingredients and bring to slow simmer
5. simmer for 30-60 minutes
6. remove the bay leaf and spread the sauce on your prepared pizza dough
demonstrations.review:
Fantastic sauce! It should be called Ultimate Pizza/Marinara sauce. I've found this a fantastic base for many sauces. Without the fennel and little white wine, makes a great ziti sauce. Anyway, I also found a great pizza crust recipe (#70165), so I never need to buy frozen pizza again! I usually double the recipes and have enough stuff in freezer to have pizza once a week for a month! 
Thank You!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cinnamon applesauce pancakes

these pancakes use applesauce for a moister pancake.  the recipe doesn't use eggs or milk, due to my daughter's food allergies.  it also makes great waffles.

1. combine dry ingredients , then add remaining ingredients and beat together
2. pour the batter onto a hot , lightly oiled griddle or skillet
3. cook until pancakes have a bubbly surface and slightly dry edges
4. turn pancakes
5. cook for an additional 2-3 minutes until golden brown
demonstrations.review:
These really were fantastic! I cut the recipe in half, and only used 3/4 cup water. I only had plain unsweetened applesause, so added 1/4 tsp cinnamon. After they were all done, I realized I forgot the vanilla, they were still awsome. 
Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
fettuccine all alfredo

i found this recipe in my "four ingredient cooking" by joanna farrow.  she states that this is a simple recipe invented by a roman restaurateur called alfredo and that he served it with a gold fork and spoon.  this recipe says it serves four, but i would imagine alot of people will think it only serves two, so up this recipe as you see fit to serve your families appetites.  this is not a garlic flavored recipe but one for the original recipe, so might want to serve with very seasoned tasty main dish/meat.  or you might want to add some minced 1/2 tsp. minced garlic to the butter in the beginning before adding the cream.

1. melt butter in a large pan
2. add the cream and bring it to a boil
3. simmer for 5 minutes , stirring constantly , then add the parmesan cheese , with salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste , and turn off the heat under the pan
4. bring a large pan of salted water to a boil
5. drop in the pasta all at once and quickly bring the water back to a boil , stirring occasionally
6. cook the pasta for 2-3 minutes , or according to the instructions on the packet
7. drain well
8. turn on the heat under the pan of cream to low , add the cooked pasta all at once , and toss until it is thoroughly coated in the sauce
9. taste the sauce for seasoning
10. serve immediately , with extra grated parmesan cheese at the table
demonstrations.review: Hi - You tried some of my recipes during the adoption and just wanted to check out some of your recipes. I have a bunch I want to try, but this one was the first one I made. This is was fantastic! I had to substitute a concoction of 2% Milk and cream cheese for the Heavy Cream, and it was still delish! Can't wait to try more of your recipes.

target.recipe_text:
banana yogurt muffins

i had bananas and yogurt in the house, and i wanted to bake some muffins, so i combined two recipes and came up with these moist muffins. because they have yogurt in them, they have less oil and no butter, making them healthier than most!

1. in a large bowl , combine flour , sugar , baking powder , salt and cinnamon and mix in another bowl , combine yogurt , egg , milk , and oil
2. add contents of wet mixture to dry ingredients and mix- do not over mix
3. stir in bananas place batter in muffin tins
4. bake at 400 degrees for 20-25 minutes or until golden
target.review: My family loves these.  It's a great way to use up the old bananas I am always throwing in the freezer before they go bad!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cream wafers

these yummy cookies are so cute and very delicate. my family has always made these cookies at christmas time, and made a red and green filling. but i found that making them once a year wasn't enough, so i've been known to make them once a month! you'll love them!

1. mix flour , butter , and whipping cream
2. cover and refrigerate about 1 hour or until firm
3. preheat oven to 375
4. roll 1 / 3 of the dough at a time on a floured surface
5. roll the dough until it is 1 / 8 inch thick
6. cut dough into 1 1 / 2 inch rounds
7. dip both sides of cookie in sugar
8. place sugared cookies on ungreased cookie sheet
9. prick each cookie about 4 times with a fork
10. bake cookies in preheated oven for 7-9 minutes , until set but not brown
11. remove cookies from sheet and allow to cool completely
12. meanwhile prepare the creamy filling
13. creamy filling: mix all ingredients until smooth
14. smooth about a teaspoon of the filling onto a cookie , and top with another cookie
15. keep cookies refrigerated for up to 7-10 days
16. if they last that long !
demonstrations.review: I was going to submit this recipe because my sister wants it and these are such delicious cookies.  My mother and I have been baking these cookies for quite a few years now.  They are a light flaky buttery cookie almost pastry like with a fluffy filling.  They cookies are very delicate so it is important to use a small cookie cutter or they break very easily!  I love PetesNina's Ideas to make the job less time consuming I am definatly going to give them a try next time I make them!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
slow cook down home pork chops and gravy

i don't even like pork, but was tricked into tasting this dish when i was told it was chicken. wow! the meat was sooo tender and juicy; so tender in fact, that it was literally falling apart! it was like nothing i'd ever tasted before! definitely not like my mother's hard, crusty pork chops! lol! this recipes goes hand in hand w/ some mashed potatoes. just pour the leftover gravy on the taters' and enjoy!

1. combine 1st four ingredients in a shallow dish
2. dredge chops in flour mixture and set aside
3. combine what is left of the flour mixture w / the chicken broth and pour into your crock pot
4. pour oil into a large skillet and cook the chops in hot oil until browned on both sides
5. place chops in crock pot and cook covered on high for about 2 to 5 hours or until tender
6. serve w / hot rice and / or mashed potatoes
7. ++if the gravy becomes too thick just add a little water
8. if you accidentally add too much water then add a little more flour
9. season w / salt and pepper too your taste
demonstrations.review: The pork chops were pretty good, but we didn't care for the gravy.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
easy skillet cheese topped chili macaroni

this is a quick and easy recipe for a weeknight meal. its very tasty and very filling. dh loves it when i make this and always takes leftovers to work!

1. in a large skillet , brown onion and garlic with ground beef
2. drain and return to pan
3. add kidney beans , tomato sauce , water , chili powder , and salt
4. cover and simmer for 15-20 minutes
5. add cooked macaroni and stir
6. add grated cheddar to top , cover and simmer just until cheese melts
demonstrations.review: This dish was great and the kids loved it, my son was still telling me 2 days later how much he liked it so we will definatly be making it again. Great substitute for Hamburger helper which for some reason my family and I can not eat.

target.recipe_text:
buttered egg noodles  best ever

the creamiest buttered egg noodles you will ever taste. always a hit and easy to prepare.

1. bring water , 2 boullion cubes and 1 / 2 stick of butter to boil using med to high heat
2. add egg noodles
3. cook until noodles are desired texture
4. during last minute of cooking add remaining 1 / 2 stick of butter
target.review: Served this last night and DD loved it.  Very easy.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
ravioli casserole

my family is cheese crazy and this uses lots of it. a quick meal that we all love.

1. in a bowl , add the spaghetti sauce , oregano , and basil
2. stir to combine
3. spread 1 / 2 cup of spaghetti sauce into an ungreased 13x9 inch baking dish
4. layer with half of the ravioli , 1 1 / 4 cups of sauce , 1 cup of cottage cheese , and 2 cups of mozzarella cheese
5. repeat
6. season with salt and pepper as needed
7. sprinkle with parmesan cheese
8. bake , uncovered , at 350 degrees for 30-40 minutes or until bubbling
9. let stand 10 minutes before serving
demonstrations.review: This recipe was wonderful to eat and prepare. I omitted the cottage cheese (because I was out of it) and there was enough cheese in the ravioli to compensate. It tasted just like homemade lasanga.  My family loves lasagna and I am always talking my way out of making it because of the prep work involved in the noodle part. Now my family is happy, they plan on eating this recipe a couple of times a month.  Thanks much to NurseDi.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
double coconut cream pie

the best coconut cream pie ever!!

1. for filling , in a saucepan , combine the 1 cup sugar and cornstarch
2. gradually stir in the milk
3. cook and stir over medium-high heat till mixture is thickened and bubbly
4. remove the saucepan from heat
5. in a bowl , beat the egg yolks with a fork
6. gradually stir about 1 cup of the hot filling into yolks
7. return all to saucepan
8. bring to a gentle boil
9. cook and stir for 2 minutes more
10. remove mixture from the heat
11. stir in the 3 / 4 cup coconut , the butter and vanilla
12. pour filling into baked piecrust
13. for meringue , in a mixing bowl , beat egg whites with an electric mixer till soft peaks form
14. gradually add the 1 / 4 cup sugar , beating till stiff peaks form and sugar dissolves
15. immediately spread meringue over hot filling
16. in piecrust , carefully sealing to edge of pastry to prevent shrinkage
17. sprinkle the 1 / 4 cup coconut over the top
18. bake the pie in a 350 oven for 15 minutes or till golden
19. cool the pie completely on a wire rack
20. store in the refrigerator
21. makes 8 servings
demonstrations.review: This was a hit at Christmas!!  Everyone loved it.  It was my first attempt at merinque and it was a challenge, but it turned out pretty good.  Thanks ~Bliss~

demonstrations.recipe_text:
easy chicken chow mein

this is fresh-tasting and easy to make. i enjoy it much better than take-out.

1. in a large pot , saute celery in oil for apx 5 minutes or until crisp-tender
2. add bean sprouts , mushrooms , water chestnuts , and chicken
3. in a large bowl , blend cornstarch with water
4. when smooth , add chicken broth and soy sauce to bowl
5. mix well and pour over meat and vegetables
6. bring to a boil , stirring until sauce thickens
7. reduce heat to low
8. cover and simmer 10 to 15 minutes
9. serve over hot , cooked rice and chow mein noodles
demonstrations.review: OMG - This was amazing!!  I was high-fiving all over the place last night!  We loved it (I did leave out the mushrooms as my DD doesn't like them, but I don't think it compromised the recipe).  I will NEVER call for take-out Chinese again. It is quicker to prepare than the time it takes to call, order and pick up or have delivered from the local take-out place and less expensive. This will certainly be on our menu plan again and again.  Thanks! to Lisa1

target.recipe_text:
artichoke pasta

a quick weeknight supper.

1. pour the artichokes , with their oil into a pan and mash them down with a fork
2. add the garlic , parsley and thyme and heat through for a couple of minutes and then pour over the warm pasta
3. add the lemon juice and toss thoroughly
4. serve in bowls topped with shavings of parmesan cheese
target.review: Love it!  Have made again & it's become an easy go-to side dish!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
outback steakhouse outback special

found in the current issue of woman's day magazine.

1. heat an outdoor grill , stovetop grill pan , or broiler
2. mix spice rub ingredients
3. rub on both sides of steak
4. grill or broil 5 minutes on each side for medium-rare
5. remove to plates
6. let rest 5 minutes before serving
demonstrations.review:
Good steak recipe. Not similar to the Outback Special, had a strong cumin taste. Thanks for the recipe :)

We will eat at Outback & make some adjustments.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
spanakoryzo  spinach and rice

a simple greek side dish, a nice change from basic rice. using chicken broth in place of the water adds extra flavor.

1. saute rice and onion in olive oil , stirring occasionally for 10 minutes
2. add boiling water and salt
3. simmer covered for 10 minutes
4. meanwhile , wash spinach well then cut into 1 / 2" strips
5. after rice has simmered for 10 minutes add spinach and mix well , cover and continue to simmer for 15 minutes , stirring occasionally
demonstrations.review: OMG This is an awesome receipe to dress up rice!!  I used frozen spinach rinsed and drained.  I also added some corn.  Served with some meatballs and had a fantasic meal.  Thank you so much for posting it!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chicken and spinach rigatoni casserole

quick, easy and delicious. the recipe calls for 4 garlic cloves, but i only added 2 and should have added 3-4 cloves. i also added more parmesan because of preference. this is a hit with the kids.  my friend kathy sent me this recipe and now i am indebted to her forever.

1. cook pasta according to pkg directions and drain
2. place spinach on paper towel and squeeze until barely moist
3. add oil to a large non stick skillet and place over medium heat until hot
4. add onion and garlic and saut until tender
5. add chicken and cook until it loses its pink colour , stirring constantly
6. stir in tomatoes , tomato paste , basil , oregano and crushed red pepper flakes
7. bring to a boil and then reduce heat
8. simmer 5 minutes , uncovered stirring occasionally
9. combine pasta , spinach , chicken mixture and 1 / 4 cup cheese in a bowl
10. stir well
11. spoon into 13 x 9 baking dish coated with cooking spray
12. sprinkle with remaining 1 / 4 cup parmesan cheese over the top
13. bake at 350 for 20 minutes
14. makes 8 servings
demonstrations.review:
Absolutely amazing!  Made some variations with what I had at home biggest variation was stewed tomatoes rather than the paste and artichokes rather than spinach.  I can't wait to get home and eat the leftovers.

Thanks for posting!

target.recipe_text:
my southern pineapple dressing

this is a very old recipe that i have doctored over the years! can be a side dish or dessert!

1. in large bowl , cream butter , sugar and vanilla
2. add eggs , milk and pineapple , mix well
3. stir in "craisins" and pecans
4. fold in bread
5. pour into greased 13x9-inch glass baking dish , do not smooth flat--leave tiny peaks
6. bake , uncovered , in 350f oven for 35-45 minutes until caramelized and peaks are tinged brown
7. i serve this warm , not hot
8. goes great with turkey , ham , chicken , and pork as a side dish
9. leftovers even go great re-heated with vanilla or butter pecan ice cream !
target.review:
I took this to Thanksgiving dinner shared by 6 adults. Everyone oohh'd and aahh'd. The hostess decided to serve it warm for dessert. Pineapple haters loved it and requested the recipe. That to me is a ten star recipe! This will be my new covered dish contribution.
I also will take this dish to neighbors as a Christmas plate, dang the cookies and candy! Thank you for a lovely addition to my recipe file. Wish my mom was here to try it!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
maple krispie cookies

perfect for those after school or late night snacks.

1. preheat oven to 350f degrees
2. in large bowl , mix all ingredients well
3. roll into 1-inch balls
4. place 2 in apart on lightly sprayed cooking sheet
5. bake for 10-12 minutes
6. cool for 1 minute
7. remove and cool completely
demonstrations.review:
I HATE to make cookies! But my gosh, this recipe has made me a believer. My kind of
cookie. Soft & chewy, but surprise...a crunch. The flavor is divine for those who just aren't
died in the wool chocolate chip lovers. I used 2 tsp. maple flavoring, a 1" cookie ball scoop
and flattened the ball a little to have a flatter cookie than the 1 picture posted. My oven time
was 10 minutes. Will make again and again. Thank you very much for this rx. Laurel

demonstrations.recipe_text:
swedish mushroom meatloaf

for zwt 6. this recipe comes from the world hearth circle of international cooking. i can't wait to try this. it sounds delicious.

1. saute scallions and mushroom in butter
2. remove from heat and mix in sour cream
3. in a separate bowl , mix all other ingredients except parsley
4. place 1 / 2 of the meat mixture into a loaf pan
5. make an indentation down the loaf , lengthwise , and spoon mushroom mixture into indentation
6. put the other half of the meat mixture on top and make sure that mushroom mixture is completely covered
7. bake at 350f for one hour
8. garnish with parsley to serve
demonstrations.review: DH & I enjoyed this very much.  As I was serving he said I had given him too much...so good he went back for seconds.  Excellent recommendation.  I was getting ready to ask him if he could taste the horseradish and he said what's in this, I then said mushrooms and he said no, does it have horseradish, gosh I was searching for the flavor and he found it.  Will make this many times in the future.  I used canned mushrooms, that's what I had, can't wait to have it with the real mccoy.  Thanks for sharing this recipe.  Laurel

demonstrations.recipe_text:
perfect divinity

this delicious recipe came from my sis in law and turns out perfectly every time and is soo easy to make! i get many requests for this recipe.

1. in a 2 quart saucepan combine sugar , corn syrup , water , and salt
2. cook to hardball stage , , stirring only until sugar dissolves
3. meanwhile , as temperature of syrup reaches 250 degrees , beat egg white till stiff peaks form
4. when syrup reaches 260 degrees , very gradually add the syrup to egg whites , beating at high speed with electric mixer
5. add vanilla and beat until candy holds its shape , 4-5 minutes
6. stir in the chopped nuts or cherries , if desired
7. quickly drop candy from a teaspoon onto waxed paper , swirling the top of each piece
8. let cool
demonstrations.review: You've made an old woman very very happy...finally I have made divinity successfully! I can die now!  This recipe made it all come together for me and simple instructions to follow made it so doable.  It's far from looking pretty but oh my gosh it tastes sooooo good.  Flavored it with Black Walnut extract.  Thank you so very much.

target.recipe_text:
spinach and bacon strata

got a similar recipe from giada de laurentiis's show and made it for easter morning. it was a hit! we dubbed it "giada strata" and plan to keep it as a regular holiday meal. i've made a few tweaks of my own to the recipe based on my family's taste and what i had available. this is really good and great when you have company.

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees
2. saute chopped bacon in large skillet until crisp
3. using slotted spoon , remove bacon from skillet to paper towel-lined plate to drain
4. reserve small amount of bacon drippings in skillet
5. add onion to skillet and saute until soft , about 5 minutes
6. add garlic and spinach and saute 2 minutes
7. stir in 1 / 2 teaspoons seasoning salt and reserved bacon
8. place half bread cubes in a buttered 9x13" baking dish
9. sprinkle half of the cheese over the bread , top with half of the spinach mixture
10. repeat layering
11. whisk milk , eggs , and remaining 1 / 2 teaspoons of seasoning salt in a large bowl and pour evenly over the strata
12. gently push surface of bread down into milk to coat
13. chill strata , covered with plastic wrap , at least 2 hours or up to overnight
14. bake strata uncovered until puffed , golden brown , and cooked through , about 45 minutes
15. let stand 5 minutes before serving
target.review: This was incredible.  I usually change all sorts of things in recipes, but the only thing I did different was 2% milk instead of whole.  Everyone raved about this.  It was even good cold the next day.  Easy to make.  I froze the bacon and then chopped it before frying it.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
amish onion cake

this is a rich, moist bread with an onion-poppy seed topping. it is wonderful with soup or salad and goes well with any meat. prep time is approximate. cook time only includes baking time. i got this recipe from one of my amish cookbooks.

1. in a large skillet , cook onions in 1 / 2 cup butter over low heat for 10 minutes
2. stir in the poppy seeds , salt , paprika and pepper
3. cook until golden brown , stirring occasionally
4. remove from the heat
5. set aside
6. in a bowl , combine the flour , cornstarch , baking powder and sugars
7. cut in 1-1 / 4 cups butter until mixture resembles coarse crumbs
8. melt the remaining butter
9. in a bowl , whisk the eggs , milk , sour cream and melted butter
10. make a well in dry ingredients
11. stir in egg mixture just until moistened
12. spread into a greased 10-inch springform pan
13. spoon onion mixture over the dough
14. place pan on a baking sheet
15. bake at 350 degrees for 35-40 minutes or until a toothpick inserted near the center comes out clean
16. serve warm
