demonstrations.review: Absolutely incredible.  Will certainly be served every Thanksgiving. Thanks for posting such a terrific recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
layered cookie bars

chocolate, toffee, and walnut cookie bars.

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. melt butter in 13"x9"x2" baking pan in oven
3. combine crumbs , cocoa , and sugar
4. sprinkle over butter
5. pour sweetened condensed milk evenly on top of crumbs
6. top with chocolate chips and toffee bits , then nuts
7. press down firmly
8. bake until lightly browned
9. cool completely in pan
10. cut into bars
11. store covered at room temperature
demonstrations.review: Couldn't be easier to make.  Couldn't be easier to eat!  Incredible.  Next time I might cut back a little on the butter.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
easy hershey s bar swirl cake and glaze

this is the easier-to-prepare version of the classic hershey bar swirl cake. the recipe comes from hershey's holiday recipes.

1. preheat oven 350f
2. generously grease and flour pan 12 cup flute pan
3. prepare cake mix batter as directed on package with oil , water , and eggs
4. remove 2 cups batter , stir in corn syrup and pecans
5. place chocolate bar pieces and chocolate syrup in a small microwave safe bowl
6. microwave on high 1 minute or until smooth when stirred
7. blend into remaining plain batter
8. pour into prepared pan
9. spoon vanilla nut batter evenly over top
10. bake 40 to 45 minutes or until wooden pick comes out clean
11. cool 15 minutes
12. remove from pan to wire rack
13. cool completely
14. glaze with milk chocolate glaze , allowing to drip down sides
15. glaze: place chocolate bar pieces and shortening into micro-safe bowl on high until melted when stirred
16. cool slightly , glaze cake
demonstrations.review: Unbelievably easy.  I think it's the moistest cake I've ever made.  What a hit!

target.recipe_text:
mexican rice

versions of this dish - a relative to spanish rice - are popular all over south america. this is a delicious medley of rice, tomatoes and aromatic flavors.

1. put the rice in a large heatproof bowl and pour in boiling water to cover
2. stir once , then let sit for 10 minutes
3. transfer to a strainer over the sink , rinse under cold water , then drain again
4. set aside to dry slightly meanwhile , pour the tomatoes and their juice into a food processor or blender , add the onions and garlic and process until smooth heat the oil in a large , heavy bottom skillet , pour in the rice and cook over medium heat until the rice turns a delicate brown
5. stir occasionally to ensure that the rice does not stick add the tomatoe mixture and stir over medium heat until the liquid has been absorbed
6. stir in the stock , salt , and whole chiles and peas
7. continue to cook , stirring occasionally , until the rice is tender and all of the liquid has ben absorbed remove the pan from the heat , cover it with a tight lifting lid and let it stand for 5-10 minutes
8. remove the chiles , fluff up the rice lightly and serve , spinkle with the black pepper
9. the chiles may be used to garnish if desired
target.review: Used two fresh jalapenos w/o the seeds and omitted the green peas because my daughters don't care for them.  Recipe turned out great.  I'll be making it again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
bacon club macaroni salad

cooked cubed ham can be used in place of bacon if desired. cooking time does not include boiling the pasta. this complete recipe may be doubled.

1. cook the macaroni until firm-tender
2. drain well
3. in a bowl , combine the oil and vinegar
4. add in the bacon , cheese , celery , green onion , olives and the cooked macaroni
5. toss well to combine
6. in another bowl , combine mayo , cream , horseradish , salt and pepper
7. blend in with the macaroni mixture
8. toss well to combine thoroughly
9. chill in the fridge for 3 hours before using
demonstrations.review: This salad is a nice change of pace, will make it again but wasn't a family favorite.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
emaw s chili pie

emaw is my momma and this is her recipe. she is very specific in her instructions and she guarantees (if you do what she says, lol) a family pleasing dish. great flavor and great on a cold night.

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees
2. heat chili and water in small saucepan over medium heat till hot
3. put fritos in a 2 or 3 quart baking dish
4. scatter chopped onions over the fritos
5. place 4 slices of american cheese on top
6. pour heated chili and water over all this
7. put remaining cheese on top of chili
8. pour tomatoes and juice over this and do not stir !
9. bake at 350 degrees for an hour or until bubbly in the center
demonstrations.review: Easy dinner, I reduced the water a bit but the fritos were still a bit too mushy.  However, my family still ate it up!  Next time I will reduce the water a bit more and cutback on the cooking time a few minutes.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
best ever  and most versatile  muffins

these are wonderful for just throwing in your favorite ingredients---i don't need any other muffin recipes. editing to add, based on a recent review: be sure not to overmix muffins; if you do, they will be tough. they should still be lumpy when you are finished mixing them.

1. preheat oven to 400f
2. stir together the flour , baking powder , salt and sugar in a large bowl
3. make a well in the center
4. in a small bowl or 2-cup measuring cup , beat egg with a fork
5. stir in milk and oil
6. pour all at once into the well in the flour mixture
7. mix quickly and lightly with a fork until moistened , but do not beat
8. the batter will be lumpy
9. do not overmix
10. this will create tough / heavy muffins
11. pour the batter into paper lined muffin pan cups
12. variations: blueberry muffins: add 1 cup fresh blueberries
13. raisin muffins: add 1 cup finely chopped raisins
14. date muffins: add 1 cup finely chopped dates
15. cheese muffins: fold in 1 cup grated sharp yellow cheese
16. bacon muffins: fold 1 / 4 cup crisp cooked bacon , broken into bits
17. bake for 25 minutes , or until golden
demonstrations.review: The kids loved making these, we used 1 Tbsp poppy seeds and a tsp of almond extract. They turned out great and disappeared quickly!

target.recipe_text:
kittencal s best chicken stock broth  crock pot option

plan ahead this method takes 2 days to create the best most richest flavorful stock, far better and cheaper than any canned broth, once you try this you will never purchase cans of broth again! --- this can be done either on a stove top or in a crock pot but start the stock firstly on the stove top then transfer to a crock pot --- the same method may be used for turkey stock use the carcass and leftover legs, thigh and wing bones from your roasted turkey in place of the chicken pieces, also save your carcass and bones from roasted chickens and freeze them to throw in the pot, roasted bones will produce a richer golden colored stock but uncooked chicken works just as well --- i freeze the cooled cooked broth in 2 or 4-cup plastic freezer containers and store in the freezer until ready to use, you may do a quick defrost in the microwave when needed --- yield depends on size of pot and how much water is used, use this broth to make the best tasting chicken soup, don't remove the skins from onions they add color and taste to the stock adding in another onion won't hurt :)

1. place the chicken pieces and / or carcass in an extra large stock pot , along with all remaining ingredients
2. fill with cold water to cover ingredients , and up to almost three quarters of the stock pot
3. place on stove element
4. cover and bring to a full boil
5. reduce heat
6. simmer and remove any fat or scum that is floating on top of the water
7. at this point you can transfer to a crockpot
8. simmer covered with a lid on low heat for about 4-5 hours for stove top
9. adjust salt to suit taste
10. after the 5-6 hours of simmering time turn off heat and allow the pot to sit until room temperature with all ingredients still in the pot , do not remove bones or veggies
11. transfer the pot to the fridge and chill overnight
12. the following day: remove the pot from the fridge
13. remove any fat that has gathered on top
14. heat again until just to a liquid
15. remove all chicken pieces and strain in a large strainer , if desired you may strain again in a cheesecloth , but it is not necessary
16. let cool completely and freeze in containers
target.review:
WOW!  So simple, so delish!  My whole house has been sick, and I made a wonderful chicken soup with the stock.  Everyone agreed it was so much better than canned, and it made everyone feel so much better.  Even the super fab smelling steam in the kitchen seemed to help everyone breathe better!
Thanks for a keeper - again!  I love all of your recipes!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
thai rice noodles with chicken and asparagus

oooooooh this is good! my husband said he now has no reason to leave me for an asian woman.  thanks alot!! i got this off of a rice noodle box. i like spicy food so its not too spicy for me but it does have chili sauce in it and also, i used salt instead of fish sauce.

1. pour noodles into bowl and cover with very hot tap water
2. soak for 15-20 minutes
3. heat oil in large skillet over medium-high heat
4. add garlic and stir fry until golden
5. add fish sauce or salt and chicken
6. stir fry until done
7. add soy sauce , chili pepper sauce , and brown sugar
8. mix until sugar is dissolved
9. drain noodles and add to skillet along with asparagus
10. stir fry noodles until firm but tender
11. serve and enjoy !
demonstrations.review: We really enjoyed this!  Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
brown sugar meatloaf

i use chili sauce or salsa instead of ketchup to give a nice contrast to the sweetness of the brown sugar.  a lighter version can be made using splenda brown sugar blend, skim milk, and egg beaters. got this one from the allrecipes website. it's one of their most popular recipes.

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees
2. lightly grease a 5x9 inch loaf pan
3. press the brown sugar in the bottom of the prepared loaf pan and spread the ketchup over the sugar
4. in a mixing bowl , mix thoroughly all remaining ingredients and shape into a loaf
5. place on top of the ketchup
6. bake in preheated oven for 1 hour or until juices are clear
demonstrations.review: Very Good!  i usually make a more savory meatloaf, so this was a nice change form my norm.  My six year old daughter helped cook it and it turned out so moist and juicy I told her she was the best meatloaf chef ever!  :)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
aurora s hungarian goulash

a quick hearty meal that is ready in 20 min. note: this is a "hungarian goulash" typical of recipes found in north american cookbooks and magazines from decades past. not to be confused with authentic hungarian goulash.

1. saute onions and bell pepper in oil until tender
2. add beef , garlic , and paprika
3. cook until beef is browned
4. add undrained tomatoes and sauce and add tomato paste to taste starting with half a can
5. add pasta to mixture
6. add salt to taste
7. cook on medium-high heat 8-10 minutes
demonstrations.review: Very yummy and easy to throw together with what I had in the kitchen...even doubled the recipe for leftovers!  Was even better the next day!

target.recipe_text:
corn flake drumsticks bake

this recipe has been passed around my family and it is quick and easy. it tastes like true southern fried chicken.

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. line a shallow roasting pan with aluminum foil
3. spray with cooking oil spray
4. in a large bowl , mix corn flake crumbs , salt , parmesan cheese , black and cayenne pepper and mix well
5. lightly beat eggs in a bowl
6. dip each drumstick in egg and roll in corn flake mixture coating well
7. place each drumstick on the roasting pan
8. spray a light coating of cooking spray over the drumsticks
9. bake at 350f for 1 hour to 1 hour & 10 minutes
target.review: Excellent, tasty recipe.  We had baked potato, sweet potato and squash with it and they went together nicely.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mushroom smothered chicken

this is too good to pass up! a 5-star, i promise. it's easy and presents beautifully over my instant gnocchi (#113377) or a toasted baguette. a bh&g recipe.

1. in a plastic bag combine flour , salt , and black pepper
2. then add chicken pieces , a few at a time , shaking to coat
3. in a 12-inch skillet brown chicken in hot oil over medium-high heat for 8 minutes , turning occasionally
4. remove chicken from skillet
5. set aside
6. add onions , mushrooms , and garlic to skillet and cook 4 minutes , stirring occasionally and scraping up any browned bits
7. return chicken to pan and add white wine or chicken broth , broth , basil , and thyme
8. bring to boiling
9. reduce heat
10. cover and simmer for 25 to 30 minutes or until chicken is no longer pink and remove chicken
11. cover and keep warm
12. increase heat to medium and gently boil sauce , uncovered , for 5 minutes- if desired , stir in whipping cream
13. serve chicken and sauce over toasted baguette slices and season to taste with salt and freshly ground black pepper
demonstrations.review: Found this recipe to be bland and quite greasy. Even though I cut off as much fat from the chicken as possible, it was very greasy as the fat came out in the simmering. In the reducing process at the end when the chicken was removed, the water was boiled off leaving the grease. Might be better with skinless breast fillets (less fat)???

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mango chicken

this is an old "canadian living" recipe that has become a family favourite. we all love it, and sometimes i increase the amount of curry paste, depending on who is coming for supper! i normally make it with a pot of rice and a salad. it's a nice "different" dish when you have company. everyone seems to love it!

1. cut chicken into three 4 inch pieces
2. seed , core and cut peppers into 1-inch pieces
3. slice onions into 1 1 / 2-inch lengths
4. peel and pit mangoes and cut into 2 / 3-inch pieces
5. whisk together stock , sugar , soy sauce , vinegar , cornstarch and curry paste
6. in wok or skillet heat half of the oil over high heat
7. stir fry chicken for 4 minutes or until no longer pink inside
8. transfer to plate
9. add remaining oil to wok
10. stir-fry peppers for 2 minutes
11. stir in ginger , cook for 30 seconds
12. add stock mixture and chicken , cook stirring for 2 minutes or until sauce is thickened and chicken is hot
13. stir in onions and mango
14. sprinkle with cashews
demonstrations.review: Excellent recipe!  It will become one of our gourmet favourites at our home.  I made with one of our large local Aussie mangoes right off the tree and it was suburb.  Any more of these treasures Susan?

demonstrations.recipe_text:
guacamole

traditional mexican dip that can be used as a topping or with chips.

1. halve avocados
2. remove fruit by running spoon next to skin
3. discard seed or save for other uses
4. place avocado in bowl and mash with fork
5. immediately mix in lime juice , incorporating well
6. mix in remaining ingredients
7. serve immediately
demonstrations.review: Used 10 drops Tobasco instead of cayenne pepper.  Excellent recipe and very easy to make in minutes!

target.recipe_text:
barley  black bean and corn burritos

this recipe came from slow cooking magazine, and it is one of our family's favorites.  i don't go to the bother of rolling each burrito as instructed in the recipe, but rather just stick the crock of barley mixture on the table along with tortillas, shredded lettuce and cheese, sour cream and salsa so everyone can make his/her own.  it's super yummy, super easy and super filling.  (i also omit the cilantro as we're a family of cilantro haters.)

***note: the nutritional information shown with the recipe includes all the ingredients, but one serving of the barley filling alone is 145 calories.  you can save lots of calories by going with light sour cream and cheese, and by choosing a lighter tortilla.

1. place first 11 ingredients in slow cooker , stir well
2. cover and cook on low for 3-4 hours or until barley is tender and liquid is absorbed
3. stir in cilantro
4. heat tortillas according to package directions
5. spoon 1 / 3 cup barley mixture down center of each tortilla , sprinkle with 1 tbsp of cheese
6. roll up
7. place one cup of lettuce on each of 9 plates
8. top each with 2 burritos
9. spoon 1 / 4 cup salsa and 2 tbsp sour cream over each serving
target.review:
Amazing!  We so enjoyed this and it was incredibly easy!!!  I didn't change a thing to the barley mixture, but I used four large, burrito-sized tortillas.  There are tons of leftovers, so I'm looking forward to enjoying this dish again.  
I also added avocado to the table.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
my family s favorite sloppy joes  pizza joes

i've tried many recipes, this is the best. i once 'dec-tupled' (10x) this recipe to sell sandwiches at a craft fair at my church. people were waiting in line to buy leftovers. freezes well, goes up to the lake or camping well and is a hit on halloween...it's no-fail. easy to double, triple, etc. i've been making joes this way for over 20 years.
***03-08-09, i just reinvented this recipe tonight when i went to make it for dinner and found i didn't have an 8-oz. can of tomato sauce (shame on me).  the family was upset with me when i subbed an 8-oz. can of pizza sauce and told them to suck it up and call them 'pizza joes' and then served them up with shredded mozzarella cheese on the toasted buns, top and bottom.  they loved it.  i left out the bbq sauce in this preparation and just used a 1/2 cup ketchup.  pizza joes are good to go!

1. in a large skillet , brown ground beef , celery and onion
2. drain the fat , who needs it ?
3. stir in remaining ingredients , simmer covered , 15-20 minutes , stirring occasionally
4. if joes appear too'loose' , leave cover off and let moisture evaporate
5. cook until it's the consistency you like for serving on toasted buns , with french fries and cole slaw
demonstrations.review: Delicious tangy and rich sauce!  Added finely diced veggies to up the nutritional value and it worked great!  My boys love it!  Great recipe because you don't really need to measure ingredients.  Just throw in and adjust flavor as needed. Really great and will make again!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kicking buffalo chicken dip

got this spicy cheesy dip from hope a friend of mine. yes i adapted it. yes you can used canned chicken. recipe can be easily halved.

1. melt cream cheese and blue cheese dressing in a pot over low heat
2. place that in a large casserole
3. add shredded monterey jack cheese , shredded cheddar , shredded chicken , and hot sauce
4. give a good stir
5. bake at 375 degrees for about 15 minutes until its hot a bubbly
6. serve with chips , cucumber slices , pepper sticks , celery
demonstrations.review: We really enjoyed this recipe. It was rich and tasted great on both crackers and veggies.  The blue cheese added a delicious tang to the dip.  Unfortunately, I made a mistake and used a wing sauce instead of a hot sauce, which made the dip very greasy.  I'll try it again next time with just the hot sauce.  Thanks Rita L. for a wonderful dip!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
homestyle beef stroganoff

this is a real fast and easy way to make great stroganoff, the meat is very tender and delicous!

1. saut onion in olive oil until softened
2. add steak to the skillet and simmer meat covered for 30 minutes
3. remove 3 / 4 of the juice from steak
4. add red wine , cream of mushroom soup , salt and pepper and cover lid again
5. in separate pan saut mushrooms in butter , add parsley and paprika
6. when done add sauteed mushrooms to the steak and bring to a boil
7. add 4 tbls of sour cream to steak
8. serve over medium or wide egg noodles
demonstrations.review: This is DELICIOUS!!!  We really enjoyed this dish and the preparation was very simple!  I did not quite follow the directions and sauted the onions and mushrooms at the same time.  It still came out wonderful.  I also only used half, but there was plenty of flavor.  Thanks - we'll be having this again soon!

target.recipe_text:
simply sour cream chicken enchiladas

easy to assemble, deliciously creamy and a great choice for once-a-month cooking. and there is no canned cream soup in my enchiladas -- hope you give them a try!

1. in a frying pan , cook chicken and onion together in oil over medium-high heat until chicken is just done
2. divide cooked chicken evenly between 8 tortillas
3. add 1 1 / 2 tablespoons cheese to each tortilla
4. roll enchiladas and place seam-side down in a 9x13" baking dish that has been lightly sprayed with no-stick cooking spray
5. melt butter in a medium saucepan
6. stir in flour to make a roux , stir and cook until bubbly , and gradually whisk in chicken broth then bring to boiling , stirring frequently
7. remove from heat
8. stir in sour cream and green chilies
9. pour sauce evenly over enchiladas
10. top with remaining 3 / 4 cup cheese and bake at 400 f for 20 minutes until cheese is melted and sauce near edges of baking dish is bubbly
target.review: WARNING: Once you start, you can't stop!! This was sooo comfort-food-good. DH and I ate 2/3 of this by ourselves tonight!! >>blush!<< We didn't have the canned chillies, so I substituted two "medium" green chillies & 1 whole orange bell pepper (pureed together). This worked really well/had a similar taste to the canned chillies. I doubled the onions, and added 1 minced courgette/zucchini to the chicken mixture for added health. Also, I used cheddar cheese.  Maybe for these reasons I had no "bland" issues.  It seemed to swim in a LOT of (gorgeous) sauce, though (maybe my puree trick added water). And while my spoon and I took care of that NO problem, next time I'd try 12 ounces of broth or allow for a longer baking time.  GORGEOUS! XOX, Deb!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
the fluffiest cupcakes in the world

i couldn't believe that it was my first time making cupcakes--these turned out absolutely perfect.  they are light and fluffy and just utterly gorgeous. if heaven has a taste, i'm sure this is it. i used "fluffy white frosting" from recipezaar, but honestly, these are perfect by themselves. [from crazyaboutcupcakes.com]

nb: the directions call for an electric mixer but i don't own one, i did all the beating by hand and it was just fine.

1. preheat the oven to 350f line cupcake pans with liners
2. with an electric mixer on medium speed beat the butter until soft , about 2 minutes
3. add the sugar and beat until light and fluffy , about 3 minutes
4. add the egg yolks , one at a time , beating after each addition
5. add the vanilla and beat until combined
6. in a separate bowl combine the flour , baking powder , and salt
7. with the mixer on low speed , alternately add the flour mixture and milk until combined
8. in a small bowl with a clean mixer on high speed beat the egg whites until foamy
9. add the cream of tartar and continue beating until stiff peaks form
10. with a rubber spatula stir a little of the whites into the batter to lighten it , then fold in the remaining whites until combined
11. do not overmix
12. fill the cupcake liners three-quarters full
13. bake for about 1520 minutes or until a toothpick inserted in the center of a cupcake comes out clean
14. cool cupcakes in the pan
demonstrations.review: I thought I followed this recipe carefully (substituting only vinegar for the c. of tartar), but the cupcakes turned out much denser than I had imagined, they stuck to the roof of our mouths, and their flavor was plain-jane (I had high hopes for the 2T. vanilla!).  My experience departs from everyone else's testimonies, but I've rehearsed in my mind what I did,  and can't see that I went astray.... Sorry!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
whole crock pot chicken

i made this one day when i was in a very big hurry to get to work, but i also wanted a nice dinner to come home too. since my fiance works the same hours almost that i do...well, that wasn't happening. so, i decided to see how a whole frozen chicken would do in a crock pot, and it was great!

1. place the chicken and the mushrooms in a crock pot set to low
2. place all the other ingredients in a food processor and blend them into a paste
3. pour the paste over the chicken and mushrooms , cover with the lid , and let it cook for about 10 hours enjoy
4. ps it will be very very tender so be careful when you are taking it out of the crock pot because it will just fall apart
5. also , the stock that the chicken makes is great for chicken noodle soup !
demonstrations.review: The flavor was just alright for me (DH liked it better than I did), but a recipe that promises a meal from a frozen bird is worth its weight in gold.  It definitely produced a lot of liquid which I found handy for use in soups/curries.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
spicy beef satay with peanut sauce

this originates from a small cookbook that was attached to australian table magazine.  the satay sauce is good with chicken or beef.  if you wish to lighten the fat you could use half and half or fat reduced cream with 2 or 3 drops of coconut essence (add one drop at a time and taste).  diabetic friendly using low fat option and substituting brown sugar with splenda (depending on your tolerence to sugar).  does not include chill time.

1. finely chop onion and crush garlic
2. finely slice rump into thin strips , place in a non-reactive dish
3. mix marinade ingredients together in a small jug , then pour over rump , cover and chill for 1 hour
4. for satay sauce put peanut butter , coconut milk , sugar and chilli in amall saucepan and stir over a medium heat until peanut butter melts and becomes thick
5. remove from heat and stir through coriander
6. assemble beef satay by threading one or two strips onto presoaked wooden skewers , reserve marinade
7. preheat a chargrill or barbecue on high
8. cook for about 4 minutes basting with marinade , turning frequently
9. serve with satay sauce
demonstrations.review: This is gorgeous and pleased the in-laws tonight! RE Marinade: I worried the 2t. cumin wd make this too "Mexicany", but the strong cumin flavor cooked away. I added a garlic clove and put in <1/4c. olive oil & 1T. peanut butter instead of p. oil. It made for a lovely, FLAVORFUL, thick marinade that stuck well to the meat (it marinated overnight). I plan on using this marinade for our Spring BBQ! RE Sauce: I went shy on the chili flakes (1/4t.), but the richness of the sauce can definitely handle the 1/3t. I was disappointed that the coriander got a bit lost in the richness & thought that going lite next time wd improve this sauce for me. MIL wd have no changes, though, and requested the recipe!

target.recipe_text:
jan s reuben casserole

if you like the reuben sandwich you will love this casserole.

1. line bottom of 9x13 pan with frozen peirogie
2. spread sauerkraut on top
3. add the corned beef
4. top with thousand island dressing
5. top all with provolone cheese
6. bake at 350 deg
7. for 45 minutes
target.review:
My husband just loves all of the above items that composed this dish. He and I think it is a 5!
Thanks MewMew for a great dish!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mexican rice casserole

a great way to use a pound of ground beef and make a dinner that all will love.  it's so easy too!  if you cannot find mexicorn by green giant, you can use a regular can of corn or frozen corn.  to control the heat of the dish, you can choose mild, medium or hot salsa!

1. place the 2 cups of water and long grain rice in a medium sauce pan and bring to a boil
2. reduce heat to a simmer , place a lid on , set timer for 20 minutes and cook rice until done
3. preheat oven to 350f
4. in a skillet , brown ground beef and drain
5. place in a large mixing bowl
6. in large mixing bowl , add the jar of salsa to the ground beef
7. also add chili powder , mexicorn , rice and salt
8. mix with a wooden spoon until combined well
9. spray a 2 quart casserole dish
10. put rice mixture into dish
11. cover with a lid or foil and bake in preheated oven for 30 minutes
12. at 30 minutes , take off lid / foil
13. add shredded cheddar cheese evenly over top and bake for an additional 5 minutes
14. remove from oven and serve
demonstrations.review: excellent! Try it soon.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
soulfully good pork spareribs with pineapple and ginger

marinates overnight. made in a slow-cooker.

1. in a large deep bowl , combiner the reserved pineapple juice , soy sauce , and the next 6 ingredients
2. add the ribs
3. cover and marinate overnight in the refrigerator
4. grease the slow cooker with oil and add the ribs and marinade
5. if you have a round cooker , stack the ribs , alternating them with the reserved pineapple chunks
6. if you have an oval cooker , put the ribs in the crock and scatter the pineapple around the ribs
7. cover and cook on low for 8-9 hours or until tender and the meat starts to separate from the bone
8. serve immediately
demonstrations.review: I tried this yesterday, and the family just raved on and on about the flavors! Many thanks for posting!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
baked brie in puff pastry with apricot or raspberry preserves

this baked brie puff pastry is rich, creamy, and dessert-like. it always disappears. i'm always asked for the recipe. raspberry preserves goes great in this as well. bringing in 2012 i made this using recipe #463563!

1. preheat oven to 425
2. lightly grease cookie sheet
3. roll puff pastry out slightly
4. place cheese wheel on top
5. place preserves on top of cheese
6. place almonds on top of preserves
7. bundle puff pastry up and around the cheese
8. bake for 20-25 minutes
9. let cool for five minutes
10. serve with your favorite crackers
demonstrations.review: Excellent !!! Used Mushrooms instead of jam, everyone scoffed it up! Thanks for a great treat.

target.recipe_text:
crock pot pork roast and stuffing

i enjoy the fruitiness of this roast as well as the delicious stuffing...and it's so easy to prepare.

1. grease the inside of a crock pot
2. mix together the stuffing , broth , apricots and onions in the crock pot
3. place pork roast on stuffing mixture
4. mix jam and balsamic vinegar and brush over the pork
5. cover and cook on low for 7-8 hours , or until meat is tender
6. slice the meat and serve with the stuffing
target.review: Nice tender pork loin roast.  I am afraid our stuffing was too soggy to eat. Thanks for sharing your recipes with us, Geema!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
buttermilk chicken

this is one of the easiest, most flavorful chicken recipes. the chicken is extremely tender... but it's the gravy that makes this dish remarkable.

1. preheat oven to 425 degrees f
2. melt margarine in a 9x13 inch casserole dish or baking pan
3. mix flour , salt , pepper
4. dip chicken in 1 / 2 cup of buttermilk
5. dredge chicken in flour mixture
6. place chicken in melted margarine
7. bake for 30 minutes , uncovered
8. turn chicken and bake for 15 minutes
9. mix soup and remaining cup of buttermilk
10. pour soup / buttermilk mixture over chicken
11. bake another 15 minutes , until bubbly
12. take care , if 425 degrees f seems to be too hot , turn oven down a bit to prevent margarine from burning
demonstrations.review: Vicki, I dont know where you originally found this recipe, but it is absolutely wonderful!  I don't remember that last time that I tried a chicken recipe that was this easy and this flavorful, moist and delicious!  As you said, the gravy truly does make this dish remarkable! I won't let this recipe get far away, trust me on that!  I prepared as directed, reducing the temperature to 375 degrees after the first 15 minutes and continued cooking for the remaining 45 minutes at 375. Thank you so much for sharing this recipe with us, Vicki!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
authentic italian meatballs

meatball recipes are often challenged by chefs who claim, "mine are the best!" even though my meatballs are the best, i will make no such claim. try them for yourself! this meatball recipe was given to me by my father who got it from a little old lady from italy that he knew. it's amazing that she gave up her recipe to him, but i sure am glad she did!

1. mix all ingredients in a large bowl by hand
2. use your bare hands for best results
3. roll meatballs to about the size of a golf ball
4. drop raw meatballs into large pot of sauce
5. simmer for about 3 hours
demonstrations.review: These meatballs were excellent, Allie!  I made them to go along with your sauce and the combination made a delicious supper! I changed nothing about the recipe and used Parmesan.  Thanks, Allie!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
bleu cheese beef tenderloin

if you like bleu cheese...you should love this easy meal. prep time is the length of time to let the meat marinade as well as to create the final sauce. (this is a copykat with a few adjustments but for the life of me i don't know where i got it)!

1. place beef in a shallow dish
2. combine , teriyaki sauce , red wine& garlic
3. pour mixture over beef and allow to marinate for at least 30 minutes turning at least once
4. place tenderloin on broiler pan and cook in preheated oven at 450 degrees for 15 minutes
5. reduce heat to 375 degrees and cook for 30 to 40 minutes longer
6. allow to set for appx 10 minutes before slicing keeping in mind it will continue to cook as it sets
7. in a saucepan over low heat , combine the bleu cheese , mayo , sour cream and worcestershire sauce
8. stir until smooth and creamy and serve over the sliced tenderloin
9. when i made this , i saved the marinade , minced some garlic and added a little more of each ingredient
10. i then put it in a saucepan with a sprig of rosemary and small red potatoes and let them simmer while the meal cooked
11. as always , garlic and bleu cheese can be overpowering for some but you can indeed adjust these to taste
demonstrations.review: Rise, this tenderloin roast is absolutely incredible!  The meat was tender and flavorful and the bleu cheese sauce was the perfect complement.  I marinated the meat for 5 hours and made the rest of the recipe exactly as directed.  I do believe I have just found another scrumptious Company Worthy recipe! This one is going in my permanent collection!  Thanks, Rise!

target.recipe_text:
fudgy orange brownies

these are just amazing, you may find it hard to quit eating them!

1. preheat oven to 325
2. mix together oil and sugar
3. add eggs , vanilla , zest , and juice
4. mix well
5. sift together dry ingredients
6. add to wet mixture , stirring gently until just combined
7. pour into greased 8x8 baking pan
8. bake 20-23 minutes until done
9. allow to sit at room temperature at least 30 minutes before cutting
10. let me know how long it took you to bake them
target.review: You are right,Sleepy. These are truely amazing. Made these last night and all were gone 1/2 hour after I started to cut them.Tastes just like the chocolate covered orange jelly sticks that I love so much. I baked them for exactly 22 minutes and they were just right. Thanks again,Sleepy for a recipe that will truely impress my friends and family.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
grilled peaches with whipped cream and caramel

epicurious had this posted from bon appetit august 2003 carey paquette, arlington, va too busy to cook? i did add my touch to it! just in time for summer peaches.

1. prepare barbecue
2. arrange peach halves , cut side up , on baking sheet
3. sprinkle peaches with sugar , cinnamon and nutmeg
4. let stand until sugar begins to soften , about 10 minutes
5. place peaches on grill , sugared side down
6. grill until tender and slightly charred , about 4 minutes per side
7. transfer peach halves to plates
8. using electric mixer , beat whipping cream in bowl until peaks form
9. fold in 1 / 4 cup warm caramel sauce just until streaks appear
10. spoon caramel whipped cream alongside peaches
11. serve , passing remaining caramel sauce
demonstrations.review: Unbelievable! We used vanilla ice cream. WOW!Thanks Rita, for the keeper.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
death chicken

thanks to chef queen of cups for posting a lower-fat version of this recipe. here is the original...low-fat it is not (!), but to me, it is the ultimate comfort food. it gets its name from the strong southern tradition of bringing a covered dish to families in mourning (with a double meaning resulting from the saturated fat content!) --this was the favorite of all the comfort foods brought on one such occasion. it's from the book 

1. line a 9x13-inch baking pan with the bacon
2. pour the uncooked rice over the bacon , then lay the chicken breasts on top of the rice
3. whisk together the remaining ingredients-- using a pinch of nutmeg and a few shakes of garlic salt / powder-- butdon't eliminate the nutmeg , because i promise , it's what makes the dish !
4. pour the whisked mixture over the rice , then cover the dish with heavy duty foil
5. bake at 300 degrees f for 2 hours
demonstrations.review: This is very yummy.Was pleasantly surprised at the wonderful smokey flavor from the bacon.I didn't put the nutmeg in,only because DH(very picky eater) asked me not to.I also added extra water from the start,,as I thought the rice would absorb quite a bit and it turned out perfect. This was very delicious.A keeper. Thanks for sharing a wonderful recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
fruit salsa with cinnamon sugar tortillas

from creating a stir, in the bluegrass and beyond, lexington medical society auxiliary cookbook. this looks delicious and very kid-friendly! posted for the strawberry recipe swap.

1. combine fruits with jelly and brown sugar
2. squeeze juice of one sweet orange over salsa and stir gently
3. brush tortillas with water and sprinkle with cinnamon and sugar
4. bake tortillas at 350 for 5 minutes
5. cut tortillas into pieces and serve with fruit salsa
demonstrations.review: Made this as an appetizer to an indian taco dinner. It was a huge hit. The salsa was delicious. I did leave out the apple jelly as I didn't have any on hand. Didn't miss it though. I also did not make the tortilla chips. I was going to, then I saw a huge bag of them at Sam's club and thought it would save on some time. It did, and they were delicious with the fruit salsa.This is a keeper for sure. Thanks.

target.recipe_text:
coconut bundt cake with powdered sugar glaze

coconut milk gives this cake a velvety texture.  canned coconut milk is available in the asian foods aisle at the market or at the asian market.

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. butter and flour a 12 cup bundt pan
3. sift flour and salt together
4. beat butter and sugar in a large bowl until fluffy
5. add extracts and the eggs one at a time until well mixed
6. mix flour mixture into the batter alternatively with one cup of the coconut milk
7. fold in two cups of flaked coconut
8. transfer batter to the prepared bundt pan and bake until top is golden brown
9. cool in cake pan for about five minutes then invert onto cooling rack
10. whisk powdered sugar and remaining 1 / 4 cup of coconut milk
11. spoon glaze over cake and sprinkle with additional coconut
target.review:
This is one really yummy cake. Wow!The directions are a bit incomplete, I added the sugar in step 5, and I added the coconut milk alternately with the flour beginning and ending with flour in step 7.
I didn't have any coconut extract so I used almond extract instead (I added 1/2 tsp. almond extract to the glaze as well)and it tastes amazing.  I will make this one again and again!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
rhubarb crunch

nan

1. mix flour , rolled oats , brown sugar , margarine and cinnamon until crumbly: press half of this mixture into a 9" greased pan
2. cover with chopped rhubarb
3. combine sugar , cornstarch , and water
4. cook until thick and clear in a small saucepan
5. remove from heat and add vanilla
6. pour over rhubarb
7. top with remaining crumbs
8. bake at 350f for 1 hour
demonstrations.review: This recipe is SOOO good.  I have friends who don't like rhubarb and they LOVED this and had second helpings, and even took home the recipe with some rhubarb. Yummy!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
entenmann s pound cake

i have divine childhood memories of entenmann's pound cake, which my mother rarely buy since she would usually bake her own. i found this recipe on a copycat site, and never ever thought of using powdered sugar before.

1. preheat the oven to 325 degrees f
2. spray an 8-1 / 2 inch pyrex loaf dish with pam
3. cream the butter with the powdered sugar on high speed of mixer for 5 minutes
4. add 1 egg and then a little flour , beating 2 minutes
5. add 2nd egg and half of remaining flour and beat 2 minutes
6. add 3rd egg , the rest of the flour and the extract , beating 2 minutes
7. spread thick and creamy batter evenly in prepared loaf dish
8. bake 65 minutes or until tester inserted into the center comes out clean
9. cool in the baking dish on a wire rack for 30 minutes
10. remove from the dish
11. slice into 1 / 2 inch thick slices
12. if you are going to be freezing the cake , be sure to slice before freezing the loaf
13. thaw to use within 6 months
demonstrations.review: This is a really yummy cake. I made it in a stoneware loaf pan and it turned out great, but the bake time was significantly longer.  Served it with raspberry sauce and whip cream.  Delicious!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pumpkin sour cream pancakes

please don't let this one review you. i came across this recipe in a magazine. it originally came from a b & b in boston. if you are a pancake lover, this one is awesome! why go out for breakfast when you can make such fabulous pancakes at home.  i found it very easy and having great results!!

1. mix flour , baking powder , salt , and sugar together in medium-size bowl
2. combine remaining ingredients in small bowl
3. slowly whisk liquids into dry ingredients
4. spray a grill pan with cooking oil
5. ladle approximately 1 / 3 cup of batter per pancake onto pan and cook over medium heat until bubbles appear in top
6. turn over and cook for a few minutes on the other side
7. do not overcook
8. serve with butter and syrup
demonstrations.review: Sorry, but no matter how long I kept these in the pan they never seemed to be done.  The comments I got from others were, THEY'RE NOT DONE. I guess we prefer fluffier, instead of mushier. The flavour was ok, but I won't make these again.

target.recipe_text:
berry cream muffins

these were entered into a taste of home muffin contest by linda gilmore. this recipe was in the top 12! sounds yummy!

1. in a large bowl , combine flour , sugar , baking powder , baking soda and salt
2. add berries and toss gently
3. combine eggs , sour cream , oil and vanilla
4. mix well
5. stir into dry ingredients just until moistened
6. fill greased or paper-lined muffin cups two-thirds full
7. bake at 400 for 20-25 minutes or until toothpick comes out clean
target.review:
We need more stars to indicate how much we liked
this recipe.  Made it exactly as recipe calls for.
They turned out perfectly each time--wonderful
texture, taste and appearance.  Will have to freeze more blueberries so we can have these often!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
buttermilk apricot salad

favorite at potlucks or any time.

1. in small saucepan heat undrained pineapple until boiling
2. stir in apricot gelatin until dissolved
3. remove from heat
4. stir in buttermilk
5. transfer mixture to medium bowl
6. cover and chill for 25 to 30 minutes or until cool
7. fold in dessert topping and nuts
8. spoon mixture into a 2-quart baking dish
9. cover and chill for 4 to 24 hours or until set
10. to serve , cut into squares
demonstrations.review:
A friend gave me a recipe very
similar but w/no nuts, and a small
can of drained mandarin oranges.
It is easy, most people like it, and
can be served w/the meal or as
a dessert.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
potato kielbasa skillet

a very hearty, tasty supper. this is very easy to make and a real pleaser.

1. in dutch oven , brown potatoes , kielbasa , onion and peppers in oil
2. add seasonings and water
3. bring to a boil
4. cover tightly and cook for 20 minutes on low , stirring occasionally
5. uncover and put cheese on top
6. simmer until cheese is melted
demonstrations.review:
This has been reviewed many
times but I must add another
5-star review.  Followed the
recipe exactly--like it that
for a change it thickens and 
gets creamy w/o having to use
a cream soup.  Has anyone tried this w/other than sausage?

demonstrations.recipe_text:
lemon orzo primavera

i was looking for a recipe that could use up some of the zucchini from the garden that the hubby and the kids wouldn't turn up their noses to and i came across this gem!  my 6-year-old's comment after he tasted this was: "mommy, i love, love, love this!"  i hope that you enjoy it nearly as much as he did.

1. heat the oil in a pot over medium heat
2. stir in orzo and cook 2 minutes , or until the orzo starts to turn golden
3. stir in garlic , zucchini and carrot and cook for 2 minutes , stirring often
4. add broth , lemon zest and thyme and bring to a boil
5. reduce heat to low and simmer for 10 minutes or until the liquid has been absorbed and the orzo is tender
6. top with parmesan cheese to serve
demonstrations.review:
I have saved this one for a
long time, but the family kept
saying "no more zucchini"./
But I found some tiny asparagus and tried that.  Oh
please, try it with this.  It is
so great/  Family loved it and
couldn't be easier.  Truly a
5 star recipe

target.recipe_text:
sugar and spice almonds

sugar and spice and everything nice, that's what little girls are made of? maybe almonds, too!

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees f
2. spray a large baking sheet with non-stick cooking spray , or pour a small amount of oil , and evenly spread with a paper towel
3. in a small dish , mix together the sugar , cinnamon , and nutmeg , set aside
4. in another bowl , combine the almonds with the corn syrup until the almonds are evenly coated
5. sprinkle on the sugar , stirring to make sure it gets mixed in evenly
6. spread the coated almonds on the greased baking sheet and bake for 10-12 minutes or until bubbly , and the almonds are browned
7. remove from oven
8. allow to cool on the baking sheet , stirring to prevent sticking and to separate the nuts
9. store in an airtight container , if they last that long !
target.review:
I made these last night and they were great.  I had a moments doubt when it seemed like there would be way too much cinnamon, but it was right on.

I was only slightly disappointed that they weren't sweeter, but it didn't matter much since the flavor was so good.  I did expect a sweeter taste though.

Great recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
sourdough whole wheat bread

great sourdough bread that can be made in the bread machine with the dough cycle.

1. measure the culture into bread machine pan
2. add remaining ingredients , with flour being last
3. set machine for dough cycle and start
4. at end of cycle , remove dough from machine and shape into desired loaf
5. cover and let rise in warm place until doubled--this can take as little as 1 hour or several hours , depending on what type of starter you use and how active it is
6. top of loaf can be slashed at this stage , if desired
7. uncover and bake at 375 degrees for 30 to 40 minutes , or until done
8. remove from baking pan and cool on wire rack
demonstrations.review:
I signed up just to write this review.  This was the first successful sourdough recipe I have used.  It worked great and tasted great!

I substituted the sugar for honey (and I used a bit more to add to the flavor) and I let this rise twice to increase the sourdough flavor.  My sourdough starter is very active (rises a dough within 2 hours), so I wanted to give it the extra time to develop flavor.

Great recipe.  I will use this one again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
shepherd s pie with garlic potato topping

i had a favorite recipe for shepherds pie that i have misplaced. i searched recipe sites like crazy trying to find it, or one similar to it, and this is what i came up with. mine was not a garlicky topping but very similar in the fact that you beat egg into the topping(and a little cheddar cheese) and i would top it with a little bit of fine, dry breadcrumbs and a shake of parmesan once i spread it over the meat layer.if you are not a garlic fan you could probably just leave it out. sometimes i would spread a can of cream corn over the meat layer,however this recipe calls for corn kernels to be mixed right in,you could probably still do either.my recipe also called for the thyme & savory which i like the flavor of. this recipe was credited to "new canadian basics"

1. brown ground beef , drain fat
2. add onions& garlic , cook until softened
3. stir in flour , salt , pepper , thyme& savory
4. add stock , worcestershire , bay leaf , & carrots
5. cover loosely and simmer , stirring occasionally for 20 minutes or until quite thick and carrots are tender
6. stir in corn
7. add salt to taste , remove bay leaf
8. spread in 11x7 baking dish , let cool slightly
9. for the topping: in boiling salted water , cook potatoes with garlic until tender
10. drain well and mash , beat in milk , salt& pepper
11. reserve 1 tbsp beaten egg , beat remainder into potatoes
12. spread over meat mixture
13. brush with reserved egg
14. bake at 400 for 20 minutes or until filling is bubbling
demonstrations.review:
Great recipe!

This is my first attempt at Shepherd's Pie, and boy am I glad I finally made this.  It came perfect.

Just a few notes on changes I made:

I added butter to my mashed potatoes.  Instead of corn I used peas.  And I didn't have savory, so I used some Cajun seasoning.

Also, I needed to crack an extra egg to brush the top with.

But as I said, this was a perfect recipe.  I'll definitely be making it again.  And soon!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
best seller caramel corn

when i used to regularly do christmas craft shows, i always sold this packaged up in christmas tins; it was a big seller for me. my sil always hoped it wouldn't sell well, though, so she could eat what didn't sell! based on a bonnie stern recipe.

1. when i make this recipe , it's the only time i haul out my hot-air popcorn popper
2. use 1 / 3 cup popcorn to achieve the 8 cups of popped corn
3. preheat oven to 275f
4. have ready a jelly roll pan
5. place popped corn in a very large bowl
6. in a large , heavy saucepan over high heat , combine the sugar , butter and corn syrup and bring to a boil
7. let boil for two minutes , stirring continuously
8. remove from heat
9. add baking soda and vanilla to sugar mixture and combine well
10. pour this mixture over popped corn and combine , then spread mixture out onto jelly roll pan
11. bake in preheated oven for 40 minutes , stirring well every 10 minutes
12. let cool before eating
demonstrations.review:
Very very good caramel corn.

Just a couple notes though.  First, I have to say, this recipe yielded a different texture than I am used to.  Usually I make caramel sauce from white sugar and I cook it on the stovetop longer, which results in a harder candy coating on the popcorn.

However, I think I prefer this texture, which is airy and light, almost like cheese doodle puffs.    

The other note is that I found 1 tablespoon of vanilla to be overkill.  There was a slight burned taste to the finished product which I think was partly due to the amount of vanilla.

Lastly, I added some peanuts, which for me is a must.

Overall, a great recipe.  But I think next time I will reduce the vanilla amount.

target.recipe_text:
crock pot pumpkin pie pudding

just in time for the holidays. a family favorite.

1. in a large bowl mix together the first eight ingredients
2. transfer to crock pot coated with pam
3. cover and cook on low 6-7 hours
4. serve in bowls with whip cream , if desired
target.review: I gave this five stars because I know if I had made it as the recipe directed it would be out of this world.  My DH shouldn't have sugar and other church members were were diabetic, so I made it with Splenda as others had suggested and it was still really, really good.  I took it to a church "Christmas in a Crockpot" luncheon and was asked for the recipe about twenty times.  There isn't anything that makes you feel that good.  Thanks DebM.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chicken turkey pot pie

this came from a pillsbury ad around thanksgiving time one year. my kids ask for this.

1. heat oven to 425
2. prepare pie crust for a two-crust pie
3. in a medium saucepan , melt margarine over medium heat
4. add onion
5. cook two minutes or until tender
6. stir in flour , salt and pepper until well blended
7. gradually stir in broth and milk
8. cook , stirring constantly , until bubbly and thickened
9. add chicken and mixed vegetables , remove from heat
10. spoon chicken mixture into crust-lined pan
11. top with second crust and flute
12. cut slits in several places
13. bake at 425 for 30-40 minutes or until crust is golden brown
14. let stand 5 minutes before serving
demonstrations.review: I have never made a regular pie, much less a chicken pot pie.  This was SO easy and yummy.  Like everyone else, even my super picky kids gobbled it up and said it was a "make again".  Thanks Heidi for making me look like I can cook!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
oprah winfrey s deviled eggs

best i've ever had!!

1. hard boil eggs
2. cut each in half lengthwise
3. remove yolks and place in bowl with all other ingredients
4. mix well
5. spoon into egg whites and sprinkle with parsley & paprika
6. cover and refrigerate at least one hour or more
7. serve chilled
demonstrations.review: We made these with our Christmas dinner and they were great!  These will be our keeper recipe from now on.  I also used a little prepared horseradish instead of horseradish sauce and I used sweet pickle relish rather than chopped sweet pickles.  Easy and good.  Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
paula deen s 5 minute fudge

easy candy

1. combine sugar , milk , butter and salt in a medium sized saucepan
2. bring to a boil , cook 5 minutes , stirring constantly
3. add in chocolate chips
4. cook until melted
5. remove from heat
6. stir in marshmallows , vanilla and nuts
7. mix well
8. pour into a 8-inch pan
9. cool cut into squares
demonstrations.review: Taste was great, consistency was great.  I needed it much quicker than the five hours it took to set up.  I even beat it when it came off the heat.  o well.  i will use this recipe again.

target.recipe_text:
spicy grilled shrimp skewers

i suggest to use fresh shrimp for this as frozen thawed will create a watery marinade, do not marinade for longer than 30 minutes or the acid in the lemon juice will "cook" the shrimp, adjust the cayenne to suit heat level, i have left the tabasco as optional you may add it or omit --- this shrimp is very good!

1. in a small bowl crush the garlic with coarse salt
2. mix in cayenne pepper and paprika
3. add in olive oil and lemon juice
4. mix until combine , then add in tabasco if using
5. in a large bowl toss the shrimp with the garlic oil until evenly coated
6. cover and refrigerate for 30 minutes
7. meanwhile soak the wooden skewers in cold water for 30 minutes
8. preheat grill to medium heat , then lightly oil the grill grate
9. thread the shrimp onto the wooden skewers
10. cook the shrimp for 2-3 minutes per side or until opaque
11. serve with lemon wedges
target.review: These are fantastic! Paired them with some grilled chicken breasts...yummmm Entire family of 8 gave 5 stars! Thanks for posting!....Gina :)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
broccoli salad with bacon

a favorite salad i tasted at a pot luck and had to have the recipe!

1. clean and cut the whole broccoli into small pieces
2. use all of the broccoli except the end chunks
3. mix together broccoli , onion , sunflower seeds , raisins and mushrooms
4. make the dressing by mixing the mayonnaise , vinegar and sugar
5. twenty minutes before serving the salad , toss and then toss again with the bacon and the dressing
demonstrations.review: This was pretty good. I left out the sunflower seeds due to some family members not being able to eat nuts and seeds, but otherwise followed the recipe. I don't think I would use the mushrooms again just due to personal preference, but this is a quick and tasty little salad. Thanks for posting; it's a keeper! Gina :)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s jumbo chewy bakery style chocolate chip cookies

yes,  finally a cookie that really does taste just like the ones sold at the bakery! ---  these taste almost similar to pillsbury chocolate chip cookie dough (the dough that is wrapped in a tube-like shape) but this is better! the dough amount may be reduced to make about 40 (one-heaping tablespoonful) smaller cookies, be aware that baking times will need to be slightly reduced for smaller cookies---  note do not double the recipe in one bowl it will not have the same texture if your going to double make two separate recipes in two bowls --- you will love these cookies!

1. grease a cookie / baking sheet / s
2. in a bowl mix together the flour with the next 3 dry ingredients
3. in a mixing bowl using an electric mixer at medium speed beat the melted butter with maple extract and both sugars until blended
4. add in the whole egg and yolk
5. continue beating until the mixture resembles a thick caramel texture
6. add in the flour mixture and beat until just blended
7. mix in chocolate chips and nuts
8. if you find that the dough is too soft place in refrigerator for 2 hours
9. set oven to 350f
10. drop about 1 / 4-cup of the dough onto the baking sheet spacing about 3" apart
11. for jumbo cookies bake for about 12-15 minutes or until the edges are just slightly browned , for smaller cookies bake 8-10 minutes
12. cool on baking sheet for about 5 minutes then transfer to wire racks
demonstrations.review: Oh, baby...these are goooood! I doubled the recipe and used half milk and half white chocolate chips. Man, my kids mowed through these. lol Good thing I doubled it! Thanks for a goodie!...Gina :)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
best oatmeal cookies

this is a family favorite that i have been making for years. it's the most requested oatmeal cookie recipe i've ever made. i found it somewhere years ago, but have lost the source. the secret is soaking the raisins which makes all the difference.

1. this is a very important first step that makes the cookie: combine eggs , raisins and vanilla and let stand for one hour
2. cream together butter and sugars
3. add flour , salt , cinnamon and soda and mix well
4. blend in egg-raisin mixture , oatmeal , and chopped nuts
5. dough will be stiff
6. drop by heaping teaspoons onto ungreased cookie sheet , or roll into balls and flatten slightly
7. bake at 350 degrees for 10 to 12 minutes or until lightly browned
demonstrations.review: I have made a lot of cookies in my 48 years and since my husband's favorite is Oatmeal Raisin, most have been this kind. These are by far the best I've ever tasted. Hubby LOVES them! Thanks for a top-notch recipe and description. :)

target.recipe_text:
barbecups alla ellen

this is my version of a pillsbury recipe. i just think they are better if you add the cheese after partially baked and not at the beginning. when i made it the cheese was over-baked and hard. i also tried them with bulls-eye bbq sauce and the open pit was liked much more. i made them for my neice and nephews for one of their birthdays and this recipe has been a staple in their house also. good for kids, but i like them too.

1. heat oven to 400 degrees
2. grease muffin cup pan
3. as many as you have biscuits , usually 10
4. in skillet , brown ground beef , with onions
5. drain off fat
6. add barbecue sauce and brown sugar
7. simmer 10 minutes
8. place 1 biscuit in each muffin cup pressing down in bottom and up the sides
9. spoon about 1 / 4 cup into each biscuit cup
10. bake for 8 to 10 minutes , until almost done
11. sprinkle each with cheese and return to oven for 2 to 3 minutes more , until cheese is melted
12. cool 1 minute and remove from pan to serve
target.review: Yum!  My 6 yr old daughter even helped with preparing this recipe. The whole family said this is a keeper!  Easy to make.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
stove top salisbury steak

my mom's salisbury steak recipe that i adore, though nursedi's comes in a close 2nd;)

1. mix the first 7 ingredients together in bowl
2. form into patties
3. melt butter in pan , flour the patties and brown on both sides
4. mix water& soup together and pour over patties
5. simmer for 45 minutes
6. covered
demonstrations.review: Wow-good and easy to make!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mandel bread  traditional jewish holiday cookie

the original jewish biscotti. great dunked into coffee, perfect gift for chanukah!

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees f
2. beat eggs , add sugar and oil and mix well
3. add remaining ingredients and mix well
4. refrigerate dough for several hours or overnight
5. on heavily floured surface , shape into 3 narrow loaves
6. bake on floured sheet for 20- 25 minutes
7. slice diagonally while hot
8. place slices on greased and floured sheet and toast for 2 minutes per side at 450f
demonstrations.review: Wow-easy and yummy!  You're my hero!  I made these along with the brownie biscotti for a teacher's gift.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
lipton onion pork chops

a very quick weekday meal, and very tasty too...the coating keeps the pork chops moist.

1. set oven to 350 degrees
2. grease a shallow baking pan
3. mix the crushed crackers with the dry soup mix
4. coat each pork chop in egg
5. roll in cracker / soup mix crumbs
6. place on baking sheet
7. drizzle with melted butter
8. bake 45-50 minutes , turning over at halfway point
demonstrations.review: I can't begin to tell you how yummy this recipe was!  Even my husband who is skeptical about pork chops loved them!  I used bread crumbs instead of crackers because I didn't have any and it worked out fine.  Thank You.

target.recipe_text:
potato  onion   tomato bake

a fabulous twist to scalloped potatoes, this is the only way i like tomatoes hot - i'm referring to the temperature!

1. layer potato , tomato& onion in a greased , ovenproof baking dish , finishing with a potato layer
2. dot each layer with pieces of butter and season with salt& pepper to taste
3. combine milk , cream& stock and pour over potato mixture
4. top with cheese
5. dot with any remaining butter
6. bake in preheated 350f oven for 1 hour or until potato is tender& golden brown
target.review: I like this a lot. Delicious.  So easy.  I used waxy potatoes like yukon gold and did not peel them nor the tomatoes.  I didn't have any cream so I used sour cream.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pasta with mushroom garlic sauce

this recipe is for garlic lovers.it is a quick easy meal when you are rushed and want some comfort food

1. in a skillet melt 2 tbsp butter
2. add garlic , allow to brown , then add mushrooms , basil , salt& pepper
3. cook until the mushrooms are just tender
4. add remaining butter and olive oil
5. stir and remove from heat
6. when pasta is cooked reheat the sauce add parsley
7. mix with pasta and enjoy
demonstrations.review: Delicious.  And easy.  What could be better?  I cut the recipe in half and I did add some white wine and let it reduce.  However it was the garlic and mushrooms that I loved.  I also used gluten free noodles.  It was my first time to try the noodles.  They are a little different but were not bad at all.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
leftover chicken or turkey rice casserole

i had a look at some of the other recipes like this on recipezaar but mine is a little different so here it is. occasionally we will have a roast turkey as a treat and this is what i make with the leftovers. i haven't made it with chicken yet but i'm sure it is just as tasty as with the turkey. it is also kid friendly, my 17 month old daughter will eat this no problem. (cooking time includes 10 mins approx for cooking of rice)

1. pre-heat oven to 180c and spray a casserole dish with nonstick cooking spray
2. heat oil in a frypan and add garlic and onion , saute for 3 minutes
3. add the capsicum , corn , 1 / 4 cup stock , thyme and pepper , cook until capsicum softens , approx 3 minutes
4. stir in the remaining stock , rice , sour cream and mustard
5. add the chicken and remove from heat
6. stir in 1 / 3 of the cheese and parsley until well combined
7. transfer mix to the prepared casserole dish and sprinkle with the remaining cheese
8. cook for approx 20-25 mins until the casserole is heated through and the cheese has melted
demonstrations.review: Delicious!  I made this with turkey.  I made some very minor changes based on what I had on hand.  Will be making this again.  I did use 1 1/2 tsp. of dried Thyme and 2 tbsp of Dijon mustard.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
black bean stuffed bell peppers

makes a great low fat main dish. my kids actually loved this!

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. in large bowl , mix all ingredients except bell peppers and cheddar cheese
3. add salt and pepper to taste
4. cut top of bell peppers , clean the inside and rinse well
5. stuff with mixture and sprinkle cheddar cheese on top of each bell pepper
6. add 1 / 2 cup water to shallow baking dish
7. add bell peppers and cook for 30 minutes or until peppers are tender
demonstrations.review: Very tasty and I love how easy this is to make.  Looked great with red and yellow bell peppers.  I used a mild salsa instead of the tomatoes with green chilies.  I also layered in a mix of shredded cheeses.  After prepping the peppers and before stuffing them, I cooked them in the microwave with some water for 5 minutes. I like the peppers to be very tender.

target.recipe_text:
tons of blueberry coffee cake

i don't know where i got this recipe from, but every time i make it..someone wants the recipe!!  thought i'd post it, so i would have it for my cookbook!

1. preheat oven to 375
2. grease 9 inch springform pan
3. sift together flour , baking powder and salt , set aside
4. in a large bowl cream together the butter and sugar until light and fluffy
5. beat in egg
6. beat in the flour mixture alternately with the milk , mixing just until incorporated
7. stir in blueberries
8. pour batter into prepared pan
9. in a small bowl , combine topping ingredients cut in butter until crumbly -- then add nuts
10. sprinkle over batter
11. bake for 45 minutes until toothpick inserted into the center comes out clean
12. allow to cool
13. i like to remove cake to cake plate and dust with powdered sugar
14. update
15. i feel awfully silly , but i have figured out why the times vary -- when using frozen blueberries -- the time is closer to an hour
16. fresh berries -- 45 minutes
17. thank you for everyone's suggestion of using vanilla
18. i have added 1 tsp to the recipe with good results
19. thank you again
target.review: Lots of blueberries + crumbly topping = absolutely scrumptious.  I set my timer for 45 minutes and the topping burnt a little bit.  The next time I make this, and I will definitely make this again,  I will check it at 40 minutes. Thanks for a yummy recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
white chocolate chip cranberry oatmeal cookies

i originally made these at the request of my old chorus director john kelleher, who also worked at seattle area starbucks (i think he'd had the combo in a cookie there, once). i was surprised but very pleased they came out so tasty! these days, these are pretty much the only cookies which are requested and i make on a fairly regular basis.

1. preheat oven to 375f
2. in a large bowl using an electric mixer combine the sugar , brown sugar and butter
3. mix well to cream together
4. add in egg and vanilla extract and mix until combined
5. add the cinnamon , baking soda , salt and flour and mix well
6. fold in the oatmeal , dried cranberries and white chocolate chips- making sure that all ingredients are uniformly distributed
7. roll dough into 1-inch balls and place 3 inches apart onto a greased cookie sheet and bake at 375 for 10-12 minutes , just until the edges are lightly golden
8. remove from oven and let cool for 2-3 minutes on the cookie sheet , then transfer cookies to cooling rack
demonstrations.review: This was a really flavorful oatmeal cookie. Liked it much better than the traditional oatmeal raisin. I took the advice of an earlier post and used less cinnamon. As a matter of fact I used 1/4 tsp of pumpkin pie spice and added pecans.  Absolutely yummy!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
broccoli with toasted garlic crumbs

my dh is threatening to throw away all of my old magazines so i am placing all of the recipes i can find here. this one is from gourmet. i haven't tried this one yet, because i haven't had the panko bread crumbs. i love broccoli and this sounds like a lovely way to serve it...something out of the ordinary! **note: i made this tonight and omg is it good! i made my own breadcrumbs and went for it! it turned out great!! the sliced garlic is a crisp little treat.......yummy goodness!!!

1. put 1 inch of water in a 5-quart wide heavy pot , then put a steamer basket inside pot and bring water to a boil
2. add broccoli and steam , covered until just tender , 8-10 minute
3. meanwhile , cook garlic in oil in a 12-inch heavy skillet over moderately low heat , stirring occasionally
4. cook until garlic is a pale golden color , about 5 minute
5. stir in breadcrumbs , pepper , and salt , then increase heat to medium and cook , stirring occasionally until crumbs are golden - about 3 minute remove from heat and stir in zest
6. transfer broccoli to crumb mixture in skillet and toss to coat
demonstrations.review: I was in the mood to try something different with broccoli and I'm glad I did. This was absolutely yummy. I had leftover breading from pecan crusted mahi mahi which was similar in ingredients and voilá. The addition of pecans was scrumptious. Thanks for a great recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
hot sausage links and beans casserole

potatoes, beans sausage and cheese, who could ask for more. it's savoury, spicy and slightly sweet all at the same time. one of my dh's favourites and easy to throw together. delicious!!!

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. in a medum skillet , heat 1 tbs of the olive oil over medium heat
3. add the garlic and cook for 30 seconds
4. stir in the onion , oregano , parsley , salt and peppr
5. cook for 1 minute and remove from the heat
6. grease the bottom of an 8x8x2inch baking dish with the remaining tbs olive oil
7. on this layer the cubed cooked potatoes
8. top the potatoes with the onion mixture
9. on the onion mixture , evenly distribute the sliced hot links
10. ina small bowl , combine the brown sugar , baked beans and the barbecue sauce
11. pour this evenly over the sausage
12. top with the shredded cheddar cheese
13. place in the pre-heated oven for 45 minutes
14. serves 4
demonstrations.review: MarieAlice, loved this recipe. It was my first casserole ever. I used Hot and Spicy bbq sauce (that's all we eat)and I didn't have baked beans so I made my own using 2 small cans of pinto beans. I only used about a 1/2 c of the liquid from one can, but I should have used all of the juice from one can because the casserole was a little on the dry side but otherwise yummy. Will definitely try again. Think I will make some cornbread to eat with the leftovers. Thanks Again!

target.recipe_text:
lime garlic chicken with guacamole noodles

marinate time is 30 minutes.

chicken part: breast | preparation method: marinade, pasta, stir-fry | cuisine style: southwestern 
joan dean 
corrales, nm

1. place chicken in medium bowl and sprinkle with garlic powder
2. add wine cooler , cover and refrigerate at least 30 minutes
3. using colander , thoroughly drain marinade from chicken
4. mix together flour , salt and pepper
5. add chicken , turning to coat well
6. in large frypan over medium-high heat , place olive oil
7. add chicken and stir-fry about 4 minutes or until fork can be inserted with ease
8. drain noodles and mix with guacamole and sour cream
9. arrange on serving platter and top with chicken
10. sprinkle with cheese
11. garnish with lime wedges and thin slices of avocado
target.review: this was very good! my family loved it! different twist on mexican food...thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
meatloaf with potato topping

this one excels as comfort food with a creamy potato topping.

1. in nonstick skillet , heat oil over medium heat
2. cook onions , garlic , carrot , celery and green pepper until softened , 5 to 8 minutes
3. let cool
4. in bowl , bet egg , chili sauce and 2 tablespoons water
5. mix in vegetables , crumbs , salt , basil , thyme , mustard and pepper
6. mix in beef
7. pat into 9-inch pie plate
8. bake in 350f oven for 50 to 60 minutes or until meat thermometer registers 170f drain off fat
9. topping: meanwhile , peel and cut potatoes into quarters
10. in saucepan of boiling salted water , cook potatoes for 15 to 20 minutes or until tender
11. drain and return to pot
12. mash with potato masher
13. beat in buttermilk , butter , salt and pepper
14. spread over meat loaf
15. broil for 1 to 2 minutes or until golden
16. makes 6 servings
17. canadian living
demonstrations.review: very good! my family devoured it!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
low calorie shrimp asparagus penne with red pepper cream sauce

this in addition to a salad makes for a great 500 calorie meal.  we've found that it freezes incredibly well, and divides perfectly into 10 ounce portions.

1. preparing penne:
2. in a large stockpot , add 4 quarts of water and 1 tbsp crushed red pepper and bring to a boil
3. add the 16oz package of penne rigate and stir every 2-3 minutes , maintaining a rolling boil
4. after approximately 14 minutes drain pasta and rinse in cold water to keep the pasta from cooking further
5. let pasta sit for 5 minutes after the rinse , and the starchiness will come back to the surface of the pasta , allowing the sauce to stick to each noodle
6. red pepper and tomato cream sauce:
7. dice red bell pepper and saute in a small skillet until it begins to soften
8. add fresh sliced mushrooms and saute for an additional 3 minutes
9. blanch chopped asparagus in a pan with 2 cups of water for 4 minutes , then drain
10. season shrimp with creole seasoning and fry in a large skillet
11. add alfredo sauces , shrimp , pepper-mushroom mixture , italian seasoning , tomato sauce , and asparagus to a sauce pan , and bring to a simmer
12. reduce heat to low and add penne
demonstrations.review: this was amazing! the only change i made was i did not use the tomato sauce (only because i forgot to buy it) i have had everyonr asking me to make it over and over again!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chocolate eclair dessert

who would have thought something so easy could be so delicious!

1. mix together vanilla pudding mix and milk
2. fold in whipped topping
3. line 9 x 13 pan with one layer of graham crackers
4. put half of the pudding mixture over the graham crackers
5. place a second layer of graham crackers over the pudding mixture
6. put the remaining pudding mixture over the graham crackers
7. place a third layer of graham crackers over the pudding mixture
8. heat the tub of frosting in the microwave for 30 seconds to soften
9. spread frosting on the top of the last layer of graham crackers
10. cover with plastic wrap and let set a couple hours or overnight in the refrigerator
11. cut in squares
demonstrations.review: this is easy and amazing....i took it with  me to a get together and had to email the recipe to everybody there.....definetly a croud pleaser you can make on a budget with little time

target.recipe_text:
low fat koo koo roo original flame broiled chicken

from top secret recipes, lite! serving size is 2 pieces and has 195 calories and 8 grams fat per serving. needs to marinade 24-72 hrs.

1. combine all ingredients for marinade in medium bowl
2. mix well
3. add chicken and marinate 24 hours even better if you let marinade 48-72 hours
4. before chicken is done marinading , prepare the basting sauce by heating 1 tsp oil in medium skillet
5. saute onions until begins to blacken
6. pour onions in medium saucepan with other baste ingredients
7. bring to a boil , then reduce and simmer 5-7 minute
8. remove from heat
9. when cool , cover the baste and chill until needed
10. to cook chicken , start grill to med heat
11. grill chicken for 5-6 on each side
12. turn chicken again and baste with sauce
13. grill 5-6 minute and baste again
14. continue turning and basting until done
target.review:
Sadly we couldn't eat this chicken.
I didn't change anything from the recipe. I was hoping for a sweet and sour kind of taste. It didn't even smell good while cooking. Waste of money and time.
I'm sorry mariposa13

demonstrations.recipe_text:
peking style chicken

this is a dish we were served one night on one of the princess cruise ships.  tender, with a wonderful flavour.  of course when they served it, it was "dressed to the nines".  when i make it at home, i serve it with rice and a vegetable.  ;)  this is also great served in a wrap. note:  for those thinking of substituting splenda for the sugar, please read the review posted by oolala on feb 11/09.  thanks oolala for the heads up.

1. in a small bowl , mix together the mustard , sugar , soy sauce , sesame oil , chili peppers and vinegar
2. blend thoroughly and set aside
3. coat chicken pieces in cornstarch
4. dip into beaten egg whites
5. saute the chicken in hot oil until crispy and brown
6. drain oil from the pan and add sauce
7. cook for 5 minutes over low heat
demonstrations.review: Great recipe! It taste wonderful, it is easy and looks so nice. I didn't have cornstarch so I used Wondra Flour instead and it worked perfect. I thought 3 eggs whites was going to be to much, but it was just enough. I don't know if I was suppose to, but I whipped the egg whites until they looked like meringue. Thank you so much Diana #2 for such a delicious recipe. (Next time I hope I will have it with the Princess Cruise on the side instead of rice.)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
gorgonzola stuffed chicken breasts wrapped in bacon

another recipe using my favorite gorgonzola cheese...

1. preheat oven to 375 degrees f
2. spray an 8x8-inch baking dish with cooking spray
3. using a sharp knife , cut a slit into the thick side of each chicken breast about 2 inches long and 1 1 / 2 inches deep
4. mash together the gorgonzola cheese , parsley , shallot , and garlic in a small bowl
5. season with salt and black pepper
6. divide the filling in half , and stuff each chicken breast with cheese filling
7. wrap 2 slices of bacon around each breast , and secure with wooden toothpicks
8. heat 1 tbs olive oil in a saute pan over medium heat and brown chicken on all sides
9. place the chicken breasts into the prepared baking dish
10. bake in the preheated oven until the bacon is browned and the chicken is no longer pink inside , about 30-35 minutes
11. an instant-read thermometer inserted into the center of a breast should read about 165 degrees f
demonstrations.review: Great recipe. Chicken, bacon, gorgonzola...how can you go wrong? Next time I will cook the garlic that goes on the filling. It was too strong for me. I do love garlic but I think my chicken breast were to big and it didn't allow to "cook" the filling; the raw taste of the garlic overpower a little the rest.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
bbq style chick pizza pie

this is a great st. louis style pizza!!!

1. preheat oven to 460 degrees
2. place crust onto pizza stone in oven and bake 4 minutes
