demonstrations.review: Before you read this review, go directly to the store for the ingredients. I'll wait. ..........  Back? Good.  Now, how is it that no one else has reviewed this gem yet? What a decadent, but simple starter (or, as you say, breakfast, brunch, lunch or dinner....or any and all things in between!)  I used 6 medium portobello mushrooms and garnished with slivered scallion tops. We had a guest this morning/afternoon who, when asked just before I served this if he liked mushrooms, answered, "Uh, no."  As I was blushing with embarrassment at not having clarified this beforehand, I whipped up a salad and was secretly pleased that I'd be able to eat his mushroom portion if I liked mine enough.  Then he offered to try it, brave man that he is, so I fixed our three plates using thinly sliced and toasted Recipe #196201 (the seedy version - LOVE that stuff).  He FINISHED HIS. {*insert bugged eyes here*} At first I wondered if he was trying to be polite (while secretly sneaking bits of it under the table to the cats), but that was obviously not the case when he demanded upon pain of death that I give him the recipe. Hmm... do you think my husband bribed him? Anyway, it might go without saying that my husband and I, both rabid mushroom lovers, adored this, but that it got a non-fan to just about lick his plate was nothing short of a miracle.  Hey... I've rambled, haven't I.  Thank you, NurseDi, for a reallyREALLYreally great recipe. (An "Encore" cookbook entry for me!)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
filet mignon with goat cheese and balsamic reduction

filet mignon is my favorite cut of beef, and i travel to philadelphia's italian market to a butcher who knows how to cut it right. this is yet another easy way to serve this delectable steak, from food network.

1. boil the balsamic vinegar and sugar in a heavy small saucepan over medium-high heat until reduced to 1 / 3 cup , stirring occasionally , about 18 minutes
2. meanwhile , preheat the broiler
3. melt the butter in a heavy large skillet over medium-high heat
4. sprinkle the steaks with salt and pepper
5. cook the steaks to desired doneness , about 3 minutes per side for medium-rare
6. transfer the steaks to a baking sheet
7. crumble the cheese over the steaks and broil just until the cheese melts , about 1 minute
8. sprinkle with pepper
9. transfer the steaks to plates
10. drizzle the balsamic sauce around the steaks and serve
demonstrations.review: A really nice and unexpected combination of flavors. Thank you, Chia!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mediterranean edamame salad

this was posted in a local newspaper. wonderful, strong mediterranean flavors and very healthful =]

1. cook edamame according to package and let cool
2. mix oil and vinegars in separate bowl with garlic and oregano
3. toss with other ingredients
4. season with salt and pepper
5. let marinate at room temperature for 30 minutes before serving
6. enjoy !
demonstrations.review: Very tasty! I omitted the sun-dried tomatoes for our tastebuds, subbed white onions for red, regular balsamic for white and kalamata for black olives, but it turned out very nice and something I'll definitely make again. Thank you, Chef #338124!

target.recipe_text:
cream cheese cinnamon crescents

these are so yummy.  would be perfect for breakfast or brunch or anytime!  i just made a batch late this evening.  a parent brought these in for a teacher's luncheon and everyone loved them.

1. roll out one can of crescent rolls in bottom of 9x13 pan
2. i sprayed pan with cooking spray
3. cream together: 2 8oz
4. cream cheese
5. 1 cup sugar
6. 1 teaspoon vanilla
7. spread this mixture over crescent rolls
8. lay second tube of crescent rolls over mixture
9. melt 1 / 2 cup butter , mix in 3 / 4 cup sugar ,
10. 1 teaspoon cinnamon , and pour over top
11. bake at 350 for 30-35 minutes
target.review: I've made this 3 times in the past few weeks. Twice with fuul cream cheese and 1 time with a little less(it was all I had). I like it with less DH loved it with full.  All three times I used spreadable raspberry on the bottom rolls before I added the cheese and I wouldn't make it any other way.  Each time I got rave reviews.  This is definitely a favorite.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
welfare cookies

this is good!!! i tasted it at a party and was so surprised to learn that the base of the cookie was a saltine cracker. i haven't made this myself, but plan to do so in the near future. just thought i would submit it because it is so different.

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees
2. spray your baking pan with cooking spray or line with aluminum foil
3. line cookie sheet with the crackers , breaking the end pieces to fit the pan
4. melt the butter in a saucepan , stir in the sugar
5. bring to a boil stirring constantly until the the sugar is melted and turns a light caramel color
6. spread sugar mixture on crackers and place in oven for 10 minutes
7. remove pan from oven& sprinkle chocolate chips over all
8. spread with a knife when chips melt enough to do so
9. sprinkle with crushed walnuts
demonstrations.review: These were GREAT!!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
snickers candy bars

no kidding--these are better than you buy at the store!

1. melt together 1 cup milk chocolate chips , 1 / 4 cup butterscotch chips , and 1 / 4 cup creamy peanut butter then spread on bottom of 9 x 13 cake pan- put in refrigerator or freezer to set up while next layer is prepared
2. boil 1 / 4 cup butter , 1 cup sugar , and 1 / 4 cup evaporated milk together for 5 minutes
3. take off stove and add 1 1 / 2 cups marshmallow creme , 1 / 4 cup creamy peanut butter , 1 teaspoon vanilla , and 1 1 / 2 cups salted and chopped peanuts
4. pour over first layer that was chilling then place back in freezer
5. melt 14 ounces of caramels with 1 / 4 cup whipping creme until smooth then pour over second layer that is chilling- place back in freezer
6. melt together 1 cup milk chocolate chips , 1 / 4 cup butterscotch chips , and 1 / 4 cup creamy peanut butter then spread on the top of of third layer in the pan
7. return to chill until set up
8. store in refrigerator to keep from getting too soft and to aid in cutting and serving
9. too wonderful for words !
demonstrations.review: These are by far my favorite and most requested sweet.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chocolate toffee graham treats

these are delicious and easy (only 5 ingredients)! if you like toffee bars like heath or skor, then you will enjoy these treats.

1. preheat oven to 350
2. arrange graham crackers in a single layer in a 15 x 10 baking sheet
3. combine butter and sugar in saucepan and bring to a boil over medium heat , stirring constantly until butter melts
4. then boil 2 minutes
5. remove from heat and stir in pecans
6. pour mixture evenly over crackers and spread carefully to edge of pan , covering crackers completely
7. bake for 10 minutes
8. remove from oven and sprinkle evenly with chocolate chips
9. when chips melt , smooth evenly to cover top
10. cool in pan for 5 minutes
11. carefully separate and transfer squares to a wax paper lined cookie sheet
12. refrigerate until chocolate hardens
demonstrations.review: What a delicious wasy treat to make.  Great addition to Christmas goodies...if it lasts that long. :-)

target.recipe_text:
baked pork chops and apples

i found this in a pamphlet from the orchard (about maryland apple orchards) a few years ago when we were picking apples. it is one of the tastiest things i have ever made!

1. peel , core , and slice the apples
2. preheat the oven to 350 degrees
3. melt the butter in a skillet
4. brown the pork chops on both sides in the butter
5. grease a large baking dish
6. put the apple slices in the bottom of the dish
7. mix the brown sugar and cinnamon
8. sprinkle the cinnamon and sugar over the apples
9. place the pork chops on top of the apples
10. cover with foil and bake for 1 and 1 / 2 hours
target.review: Outstanding recipe.  I used 5 apples and just eye-balled the brown sugar and cinnamon.  I also fixed a package of stove top dressing and spread that on top before baking.  Smelled delicious and tasted wonderful.  DH said this is a keeper.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
roasted kielbasa   potatoes

another recipe from mom. these are good and easy to throw together.

1. preheat oven to 425 degrees
2. mix all ingredients in a large bowl
3. pour into a 9x13" baking pan
4. cook in oven , covered with foil for approximately 1 hour
5. you can stir after 1 / 2 hour of cooking
demonstrations.review: This was delicious and definitely a keeper to be made over and over.  I also used turkey kielbasa to cut down on the fat.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
libby s famous pumpkin pie

well, after looking for this recipe on here and not having any luck, i decided to find it and post it. in my opinion, this is the best pumpkin pie. make your own graham cracker crust or buy an already prepared one.

1. preheat oven to 425 degrees fahrenheit
2. mix sugar , salt , cinnamon , ginger , and cloves in small bowl
3. beat eggs in large bowl
4. stir in pumpkin and sugar-spice mixture
5. gradually stir in evaporated milk
6. pour mixture into pie shell
7. bake at 425 degrees fahrenheit for 15 minutes
8. reduce temperature to 350 degrees fahrenheit
9. bake for 40 to 50 minutes or until knife inserted near center comes out clean
10. cool on wire rack for 2 hours
11. serve immediately or refrigerate
12. top with whipped cream before serving for best results !
13. do not overcook
14. overcooking leads to pie cracking in the middle
15. try to bake the day you will serve the pie
16. cooking in advance can make the crust soggy
17. if you have to bake a day before serving , pop the pie in the oven for 5 to 10 minutes and it should bring the crust back to life !
demonstrations.review: I have been using this recipe for as long as I have been making pumpkin pie.  At the suggestion of my new DH, I added a capful of vanilla to the ingredients (that's the way his father made pumpkin pie).  The vanilla gave it a little more flavor--I will probably add 2 capfuls next time.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
make ahead garlic mashed potatoes

this is a wonderful recipe i found in a betty crocker magazine. it is a great comfort food with the added make ahead benefit. it is great with any roast or poultry dish.

1. place potatoes and garlic in medium saucepan with enough water to cover
2. cover and heat to boiling , reduce heat and simmer until tender
3. drain and shake potatoes to dry over low heat
4. mash potatoes and garlic in pan until lump free
5. heat rest of ingredients stirring over low heat until butter melts
6. reserve 1 / 4 c of mixture
7. add rest of milk mix in small amounts stirring after each addition until light and fluffy
8. grease a 2 quart casserole and spoon in potatoes
9. cover and refrigerate up to 24 hours
10. heat oven to 350
11. pour reserved milk mixture over potatoes and bake uncovered 40-45 minutes or until hot
12. stir before serving
demonstrations.review: What a great way of making mashed potatoes--no last minute scrambling.  I also recommend using all the liquid--between the time in the frig and the oven, they were a little stiff since I didn't use all the liquid (but the gravy made them more creamy).

target.recipe_text:
whatever floats your boat  brownies

these are absolutely the chewiest, moistest, fudgiest brownies ever! i have tried adding so many different things to the batter, and they always comes out great.  they are also great without any add-ins! but by varying the add-ins, you can make different brownies every week (or day!!) super easy prep! so, add "whatever floats your boat" and you will not believe how yummy they come out :) oh, and the recipe doubles just fine--use a 9 x 13 inch pan instead and add a few more minutes of baking!

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. grease an 8 inch square pan or line with foil
3. in a medium bowl combine melted butter and cocoa and stir until cocoa is dissolved
4. add sugar and mix well
5. add eggs one at a time and stir until well combined
6. stir in vanilla , flour and salt until you no longer see any flour
7. fold in "whatever floats your boat" !
8. spread in pan and bake for approximately 25 minutes
9. do not over-bake -- your brownies will come out dry
10. adjust time / temp accordingly for your oven
11. if you do the knife / toothpick test , it should come out with moist crumbs , not clean
12. cool completely before cutting into squares
13. for vegetarian omit the marshmallows
14. for double recipe , bake in 9x12 pan and add 5 minutes to baking time
target.review: Yummy! My family loves this recipe.  They always turn out great no matter what you put into the batter, they are amazing.  I made them in mini muffin cups and put mini peanut butter cups in the middle of them after I pulled them out of the oven.  They turned out wonderful. Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chicken with black beans and rice

this is a variation of a cuban dish. the balsamic vinegar gives it an exceptional flavor!

1. in a large pan , heat olive oil and add red pepper flakes
2. add onion and garlic , and cook until onion is tender
3. increase heat , add chicken , stirring until cooked
4. lower heat to medium , add 1 tsp oregano , 1 tsp cumin , and simmer 1 minute
5. add black beans , pimentos , remaining spices , and balsamic vinegar
6. blend and simmer uncovered for 30 minutes , reseasoning if needed
7. while beans are simmering , bring broth to boil in a pan , add rice
8. lower heat to simmer , cover , and cook 20 minutes until rice is fluffy
9. serve bean mixture over rice
demonstrations.review: This was amazing! I used a package of chicken flavored rice instead of the broth and it was wonderful! My picky grandson couldn't get enough of it.  Thanks for sharing, I'll make this one over and over again!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
dill buttermilk bread

nan

1. preheat oven to 350 f
2. combine flour , baking powder , sugar , dill , baking soda , salt and pepper in a bowl
3. add buttermilk a little at a time until a soft dough forms
4. turn into a greased 9 inch by 5 inch loaf pan
5. bake for 50 minutes or until loaf is golden brown
6. serve warm
7. reheat when needed
8. the globe and mail -----
demonstrations.review: I have made this several times and continues to be a favorite for sandwiches at my house.  It's so amazingly easy, even when I don't have any buttermilk in the house I either use lemon juice in the milk or vinegar.  No matter what I make it with it always turns out spectacular, thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
ravioli with creamy pesto sauce

easy and incredible to taste.

1. combine whipping cream and pesto sauce in a saucepan
2. add capers
3. cook mixture over low heat until thoroughly heated , stirring frequently
4. cook pasta according to package directions , and drain
5. toss pasta with sauce , and sprinkle with toasted pine nuts
6. serve immediately
demonstrations.review: Love this recipe! I added some fresh garlic to the pan too, probably a little more seasoning too.  I have made it several times.

target.recipe_text:
kittencal s easy no fail make anytime turkey gravy

i have been using this recipe for many years, my family loves this gravy and i have served it to dinner guests over the holidays and always receive rave reviews! --- you don't need to make this gravy using all pan drippings, if you do not have 4 cups of drippings you may mix with chicken broth to make the 4 cups, or it may be made with only chicken broth, please see note on the bottom of the recipe--- this may be made slightly ahead and kept uncovered on top of the stove until ready to serve, just whisk before using if you have any left over this gravy freezes very well or you may reduce all ingredients down to half and for a thinner gravy reduce flour by 1 tablespoon  --- also see my recipe#314890
for more of my recipes visit www.kittencalskitchen.com

1. drain the pan drippings for the roasted turkey through a fine strainer
2. let sit and then remove any fat from the top of the drippings
3. add in chicken broth or water to make 4 cups if necessary
4. in a medium saucepan , melt margarine or butter
5. add in lots of black pepper
6. add in 1 / 2 cup flour plus 3 tablespoons
7. constantly whisk for about 3 minutes over low heat
8. slowly add in the 4 cups turkey broth / drippings
9. whisk constantly over medium-low heat until bubbly and thickened
10. use right away or keep warm over lowest heat setting , whisk again before serving
11. options to make this gravy using all chicken broth prepare as directed using 4 cups low sodium chicken broth and 1 tablespoon chicken boullion powder ---- or you may add in low sodium chicken broth omitting bouillon powder to pan drippings to make up 4 cups
target.review: Delicious!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
to die for crock pot roast

amazing flavor, and so simple! no salt needed here. in fact, you may wish to use half the ranch dressing mix to cut back on the saltiness. found this crock-pot pot roast recipe on of a website called www.recipegoldmine.com. it's all the rage there, so i thought i'd try it.

1. place beef roast in crock pot
2. mix the dried mixes together in a bowl and sprinkle over the roast
3. pour the water around the roast
4. cook on low for 7-9 hours
5. use onion soup mix instead of ranch
6. add one cup , of red wine
7. add potatoes , carrots , mushrooms , celery and onion 2-3 hours before end
demonstrations.review: Awesome! Thanks for sharing! I added carrots and potatoes to mine too. Everyone loved it.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
thanksgiving turkey brine

brining the turkey with this recipe makes a very moist turkey!  delicious!

1. combine all ingredients in a stock pot , bring mixture to a boil , lower heat and simmer for 15-20 minute allow brine to cool completely
2. rinse turkey under cook running water , inside and out
3. pat turkey dry with paper towels , then immerse turkey in cooled brine
4. turkey should be completely submerged in liquid
5. my pot wasn't big enough , so the
6. cover the pot and refrigerate for 8-10 hours or up to 24 hours
7. remove turkey , rinse , pat dry and roast as usual
demonstrations.review: Used this recipe to make my first turkey ever. It was wonderful! Thank you for psoting, I will definitely be using this one again!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
whatever floats your boat  brownies

these are absolutely the chewiest, moistest, fudgiest brownies ever! i have tried adding so many different things to the batter, and they always comes out great.  they are also great without any add-ins! but by varying the add-ins, you can make different brownies every week (or day!!) super easy prep! so, add "whatever floats your boat" and you will not believe how yummy they come out :) oh, and the recipe doubles just fine--use a 9 x 13 inch pan instead and add a few more minutes of baking!

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. grease an 8 inch square pan or line with foil
3. in a medium bowl combine melted butter and cocoa and stir until cocoa is dissolved
4. add sugar and mix well
5. add eggs one at a time and stir until well combined
6. stir in vanilla , flour and salt until you no longer see any flour
7. fold in "whatever floats your boat" !
8. spread in pan and bake for approximately 25 minutes
9. do not over-bake -- your brownies will come out dry
10. adjust time / temp accordingly for your oven
11. if you do the knife / toothpick test , it should come out with moist crumbs , not clean
12. cool completely before cutting into squares
13. for vegetarian omit the marshmallows
14. for double recipe , bake in 9x12 pan and add 5 minutes to baking time
demonstrations.review: A-MAZING!! My boyfriend loved them. Will definitely make these again.

target.recipe_text:
bacon feta stuffed chicken breasts

a flavorful chicken  with feta cheese bacon, and diced tomatoes.  a real inevpensive, low calorie recipe.

1. in a small bowl , lightly mix bacon and cheese together
2. cut a pocket in the thicker side of each chicken breast
3. fill each with 1 / 4 of the bacon / cheese mixture
4. pinch shut and secure with a toothpick
5. place chicken in slow cooker , and top with tomatoes , and sprinkle with basil
6. cover and cook on high 2-3 hours or until chicken is tender , but not dry or mushy
target.review: This was delicious!  I used feta with basil and tomoto, and I used the Italian style tomatoes, to add extra flavor.  I think next time I will make this in the oven to be even quicker.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
lisa s swirled chocolate chip cookies

this is a chocolate chip cookie recipe that my friend delynn's best friend gave to us. this is the recipe i use for normal chocolate chip cookies, but i've recently been making them with nestlé's new white & milk chocolate swirled chips. this is a yummy soft and delicious cookie!

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees fahrenheit
2. mix butter , granulated sugar , brown sugar , vanilla and eggs in a large bowl
3. stir in the flour , baking soda and salt
4. stir in 2 cups of swirled chocolate chips
5. drop dough by rounded measuring tablespoons , about 2-inches apart , onto ungreased cookie sheet
6. place the several of the reserved swirled chocolate chips on top of each cookie
7. bake 9 to 12 minutes or until light brown
8. cool slightly
9. remove from cookie sheet
10. cool on wire rack
demonstrations.review: I made these with just semi-sweet chips, because that's what I had.  Definitely the best cookies I've ever made!  This recipe is going in the archives.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chicken and rice soup

i do this one to use up leftover chicken.  it's quick, easy, and makes a good hearty meal.  we have along with chicken pot pie, which uses similar ingredients and is nearly as quick and easy.

1. heat about 5 or 6 cups of water to a boil and add the carrot , celery , bouillon cube , and salt
2. boil for about 5-10 minutes
3. add the chicken meat and rice
4. also , if you have leftover chicken skin and fat from remaining meat , this adds a bit of flavor
5. periodically check rice for cooked texture
6. once it is done or nearly done , slowly stir in the corn starch to obtain a slightly thicker texture
7. add water or rice to desired quantity and texture
8. adjust flavor with salt and pepper to desired
9. you can also add another bouillon cube for more flavor
demonstrations.review: I ended up making this as "chicken noodle soup" because when it was time to put the rice in I discovered I didn't have any in the pantry!  So I added noodles instead and it was great.  I added some extra seasoning, and it still didn't have a lot of flavor, but otherwise turned out great!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
monterey chicken rolls

butter...garlic...cheese? chicken rolled in all? how can this recipe not be a keeper?!! my sister-in-law gave me this recipe some 25 years ago. it's just as good today as it was then - maybe even better since my garlic tastes have increased over the years as well as my "eye-balling" measurements (meaning more garlic!). just be sure not to overcook as the chicken will be dry - follow these directions and the chicken will be moist. this is a great prepare ahead meal that will impress.

1. pound chicken breasts flat
2. slice monterey jack cheese about 1 / 4" thick , roll chicken around cheese
3. dip chicken in butter sauce , then in breadcrumb combination
4. place seam side down in 9x13 baking dish
5. bake covered for 30 minutes at 350 degrees in preheated oven
6. uncover and bake for 15 minutes more or until browned
demonstrations.review: This recipe is a keeper.  I went to make this for dinner tonight and I thought I had 6 chicken breasts, but I only had 3.  So I also used 4 boneless pork loin chops with this recipe.  They were not bad, but not as good as the chicken.  The chicken was so tender and juicy, I was so pleasantly surprised.  It had fabulous flavor.  I cooked it exactly as written.  I am thinking about trying it with mozzarella cheese and serving it with marinara sauce over pasta for another twist.

target.recipe_text:
potato blue cheese soup

this ordinary potato soup takes the turn to fantastic with the addition of blue cheese! (that's if you enjoy blue cheese!) love this stuff

1. melt butter in large saucepan over medium high heat
2. add onion
3. cook 5 minutes or until soft
4. add garlic
5. cook 1 minute
6. add potatoes
7. cook 5 minutes
8. add broth
9. bring to a boil
10. reduce heat to medium low
11. cover and simmer 20 minutes or until potatoes are tender
12. stir in half-and-half , 1 / 2 cup of the cheese , salt and pepper
13. before serving , sprinkle with remaining 1 / 2 cup cheese
target.review: Loved it, I also added more cheese, but I always feel one can never have enough cheese! Easy to make and fun to eat on a cold night.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
no bake fudge cookies

this recipe is from a church library book 

1. mix first 6 ingredients in a sauce pan and cook until it boils
2. boil for 1-3 minutes
3. remove from heat and add peanut butter and oatmeal
4. drop by teaspoonfuls on to wax paper
5. chill until set
demonstrations.review: YUMMMMM! I added Coconut, because I love Coconut and they were the best EVER! Thank you so much.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pan fried tofu with spicy peanut sauce

a tasty snack or appetizer. tofu cubes are very crispy outside, yet warm and soft inside. sort of like asian 

1. drain tofu
2. cut into bite-sized cubes
3. toss with cornstarch , coating the cubes
4. sprinkle a little salt and pepper
5. heat some oil
6. fry the tofu cubes in batches , making sure all sides are lightly browned
7. drain on paper towels , then sprinkle with salt and pepper if desired
8. sauce: heat the milk in small saucepan
9. add peanut butter , stirring well
10. add other seasonings , according to personal taste
11. if you use coconut milk , add 1 / 2 - 1 tsp of lime juice too - it will be great !
12. serve hot , as a snack or appetizer
13. sometimes i serve them with a sweet chinese dessert: green bean soup
demonstrations.review: I love tofu, but my husband is a bit picky about texture. He loved this and asked for seconds and thirds. Peanut sauce was awesome!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
easy sloppy joe biscuit cups

kids of all ages enjoy this easy recipe!

1. set oven to 400 degrees
2. prepare 10 ungreased standard-size muffin cups / tins
3. in a large skillet brown the ground beef with onion , garlic , celery and bell pepper for about 6-8 minutes , or until the beef is no longer pink
4. drain fat and season with salt and pepper to taste
5. add in barbecue sauce and simmer about 5 minutes , stirring occasionally
6. meanwhile place one biscuit in each ungreased muffin tins and press the dough down firmly onto the bottoms and sides of the cups
7. spoon about 1 / 4 cup beef mixture into each biscuit cup
8. sprinkle the tops with parmesan cheese and bake for about 10-12 minutes or until the edges of the biscuits are golden brown
9. remove from the oven and sprinkle grated cheddar cheese over the tops of each , return to the oven for about 1-2 minutes or until the cheese is melted
10. let stand for 1 minute then loosen edges of biscuits cups before removing them from the pan
demonstrations.review: Amazing... all of the guys in my house beg me to make these and i don't complain. They are super easy  and very tasty.

target.recipe_text:
chicken and dumplings like cracker barrel s

this tastes just like cracker barrel's, if you have ever tried it. from book "old fashioned country cooking" found at cracker barrel.

1. place chicken in a dutch oven
2. add water and 2 teaspoons salt
3. bring to a boil
4. cover , reduce the heat , and simmer for 1 hour or until tender
5. remove the chicken from the broth and cool
6. bone the chicken and cut meat into bite-sized pieces
7. bring the broth to a boil and add pepper
8. combine the flour , baking soda , and salt
9. cut in the shortening
10. add the buttermilk , stirring with a fork until moistened
11. knead the dough 4 to 5 times , and pat to 1 / 2-inch pieces and drop into boiling broth
12. reduce the heat to medium-low , and cook for about 8 to 10 minutes , stirring occasionally
13. stir in the chicken and serve
14. i make it in the pressure cooker , much quicker and easier
15. i pressure it for only 30 minutes
16. it can also be done in the crockpot with 3-4 cups water but someone has that book so at this time i cannot give cooking times
17. good luck ! hope you enjoy
target.review: Great dumplings! I like this recipe so much better than the one I was using - I think it is the buttermilk. I cannot compare to Cracker Barrel, as I never ate there - but if this is a representative of their food, I have to go find one!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
german chocolate bars

these mouthwatering bars taste just like german chocolate cake! a great change of pace from the standard brownie. the recipe comes from betty crocker. chill time is 2 hours not included.

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees
2. lightly grease bottom and sides of rectangular pan , 13x9x2 inches
3. cut butter into cake mix in medium bowl , using pastry blender or fork , until mixture looks like crumbs
4. press half of the mixture in the bottom of pan
5. bake 10 minutes
6. sprinkle chocolate chips over baked layer
7. drop frosting by tablespoonfuls over chocolate chips
8. stir milk into remaining cake mixture
9. drop by teaspoons onto frosting layer
10. bake 25 to 30 minutes or until cake portion is slightly dry to touch
11. cool completely
12. refrigerate until firm
13. for 48 bars , cut into 8 rows by 6 rows
demonstrations.review: These are rich beyond belief! Made them for a picnic and they disappeared fast. Didn't change a thing.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cinnabon cinnamon rolls for the abm

found this on recipegoldmine.com and love it! the ingredients are similar to other cinnabon copycats on this site, but this is simplified by using the bread machine. hope you enjoy it as much as me and my family!(=

1. roll: place ingredients in the machine following manufacturer's instructions and set for dough cycle
2. after completion of cycle , remove from machine and roll out to 17x10-inch rectangle
3. filling: mix together brown sugar and cinnamon
4. spread softened butter over dough and sprinkle brown sugar / cinnnamon mixture over the top
5. roll tightly from long end , pinching edges closed when finished
6. slice into sizes of your choice
7. place on greased cookie sheet and let rise until doubled
8. bake at 350f for 15-20 minutes , until golden-do not overbake !
9. frosting: mix together and spread over hot rolls
10. enjoy !
demonstrations.review: These are fantastic! I followed the directions exactly except I used chopped pecans instead of walnuts and no raisins. Yummy! A real keeper!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
refrigerator pickles

these pickles are wonderful for busy people. no need to can. my husbands grandmother gave me this and they are just great whole family loves them.

1. heat vinegar , sugar , salt , and celery seed
2. pour over cucumbers , onions and green pepper
3. store in refrigerator
4. these will keep for many months
demonstrations.review: These are fantastic! I doubled everything to pack into a gallon jar -- using red pepper instead of green. We ate them all within a week!

target.recipe_text:
awesome baked ham

i love this recipe because it is so easy and it calls for hardly any ingredients, and i always have these ingredients in my pantry. this recipe came from a good friend's mother, who was always asked to bake the ham for get-togethers and family dinners. now i get those requests. people who ordinarily aren't too fond of ham rave over this one. after i carve, i spoon a little of the glaze over the meat in the platter - yummmm!

1. in a medium size mixing bowl , mix yellow mustard and brown sugar until you have a thick"paste"
2. take all wrappers off of ham and trim away excess fat
3. line baking pan with aluminum foil
4. place ham on foil and spread brown sugar / mustard paste on top
5. fold and seal foil
6. do not open again until ham is done
7. bake at 350 for 4 hours
8. let set for about 1 hr then carve
9. one of the best tasting hams you will ever have !
target.review:
Great and Easy recipe.
This made one wonderful Easter Dinner.
Thanks Boopster

demonstrations.recipe_text:
fillet of beef  beef tenderloin whole

how to cook a whole or large piece of beef tenderloin. note from unknownchef86: this is a recipe i adopted in 2006.

1. preheat the oven to 500 degrees f
2. place the beef on a sheet pan and pat the outside dry with a paper towel
3. spread the butter on with your hands
4. sprinkle evenly with the salt and pepper
5. roast in the oven for exactly 22 minutes for rare and 25 minutes for medium-rare
6. remove the beef from the oven , cover it tightly with aluminum foil , and allow it to rest at room temperature for 20 minutes
7. remove the strings and slice the fillet thickly
demonstrations.review:
Great recipe.  Very Easy.  I used a 3 lb tenderloin for 25 minutes. A bit rare for me but everyone else thought it was wonderful.
Also crushed tri-color peppercorns for the pepper.  Super.
Thanks for a special recipe and a wonderful dinner, UnknownChef86.
Purdyman

demonstrations.recipe_text:
best beef stew

company stew but the family loves it too, like all stews it is even better the next day, can be refrigerated and reheated. serve with a light salad and soft rolls to sop up the gravy.

1. dredge beef in flour , seasoned with your favorite seasonings
2. heat large dutch oven
3. whisk together olive oil and dry mustard , add to heated dutch oven
4. add spanish onion and caramelize
5. add dredged beef , brown on all sides
6. add garlic , brown , being careful not to burn
7. add wine , deglaze the pot and simmer 10 minutes
8. add carrots , rutabaga , celery , mushrooms , cayenne , thyme , worcestershire sauce , horseradish salt to taste
9. stir and simmer another 10 minutes
10. add water and potatoes
11. stir and bring back to simmer
12. preheat oven to 300f
13. cover tightly and slow simmer until potatoes are fork tender , about 2 hours
demonstrations.review:
The recipe was pretty easy and the results were terrific.
The only thing I added were peas.  The Port wine gave it a very slightly sweet flavor though I'm sure a good red would have been fine as I could have drank the red with the meal.
Thanks Derf

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s german apple puff pancake

this is a recipe i developed years ago, a small amount of baking powder is what makes this recipe special! it's a family favorite and takes very little time to throw together, i sometimes just bake the complete recipe in a 10-inch round cake pan, but two smaller pans will do fine also, you will *love* this!:)

1. set oven to 400 degrees f
2. spray two 8-inch round cake pans with cooking spray
3. place 2 tbsp butter in each of the pans
4. place the pans in the oven and bake until the butter has melted
5. remove from oven
6. in a bowl , beat the flour , 1 / 4 teaspoons baking powder , sugar salt , milk and eggs until smooth , then allow to stand for 30 minutes
7. arrange the apple slices into the two pans onto the melted butter
8. re-whisk the flour / egg mixture again then divide the batter evenly between pans , over the apple slices
9. mix the sugar and cinnamon
10. sprinkle over the batter in each pan
11. bake until puffed , and golden brown , about 20-25 minutes
demonstrations.review:
Another winning recipe from Kittencal.  It was the apple pancake recipe I've been looking for and set the tone for a wonderful Sunday brunch.
Thanks Kittencal

target.recipe_text:
pork chops yum yum

i copied this from the orlando sentinel months ago and just now found it. we eat pork chops at least once a week and this is our favorite.

1. brown chops on both sides
2. place in greased casserole dish
3. mix all remaining ingredients and pour over pork chops
4. bake , uncovered , at 350 for one hour
target.review: This was sooo good!!  As of now, these are the best pork chops I have ever made.  I also lowered my cook time to 45 minutes.  Thank you so much, Brad, for posting this recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
creamy italian noodles

a very quick and delicious side dish!

1. cook the noodles and drain well
2. combine the rest of the ingredients and blend well
3. enjoy !
demonstrations.review: I, too, would give this more than 5 stars if I could!  No leftovers, and my BF actually said that he 'certainly wouldn't mind' if I made these at least once a week!!  That says alot, too, since he is a really finicky eater!! Thank you for this super easy and quick recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
amish macaroni salad

i really love amish macaroni salad, and this is my favorite recipe for it. amish macaroni salad is somewhat on the sweet side, so if you don't mind your salads sweet, i think you'll like it too. it's even better the next day, so if you can, let it sit overnight. i got the recipe from a berk's county website a while back. note: it does make a lot of salad, so if you wanted a smaller amount, it halves easily. just use the 3 eggs chopped up and just garnish with paprika. time does not including cooking the macaroni.

1. cook macaroni as directed on package
2. drain& cool
3. in a bowl , whisk together the dressing ingredients so they are well-combined and smooth
4. in a large bowl , gently combine the macaroni , celery , carrots , onions , and remaining eggs
5. fold the dressing gently into the macaroni salad mixture
6. place into your serving bowl and garnish with the reserved slice egg and paprika
7. let sit overnight for the best results
demonstrations.review: Well, I certainly will be making this recipe often this summer!  This is the best macaroni salad I've had!  I did include the green peppers, and the taste was amazing!  Praise from my extended family as well, thank you!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
supper in foil

pop it in the oven, and take a break, easy, delicious and no mess!! add a few mushrooms or other veggies as you like.

1. place aluminum foil in baking pan
2. place meat on foil
3. stir together soups and water , spread on meat
4. top with veggies
5. fold foil over and seal securely
6. cook 1 1 / 2 hours in a 350f degree oven
demonstrations.review: This is such an easy meal!  I didn't add the jalapeno, only because I couldn't get out to the store, and I used baby carrots as well.  Great taste, as well as easy clean-up... what more could you ask for??  Thanks for posting!

target.recipe_text:
scallops with cilantro and lime  jack nicholson

from a newspaper clipping from cooking for jack (nicholson, the actor) by tommy baratta,1996. the blurb before the recipe says "you have to like the tart taste of lime and the pungent flavor of cilantro to enjoy this dish. it's very quick and easy to make."

1. coat a large nonstick skillet with cooking spray
2. heat over medium-high and add garlic and cook , stirring , 30 seconds
3. add scallops , scallions , and hot pepper sauce
4. cook , stirring , over medium-high heat 2 minutes
5. add wine and lime juice and continue cooking and stirring 3 minutes or until scallops are just cooked
6. do not overcook or scallops will toughen
7. use a slotted spoon to transfer scallops to a platter
8. season with salt and pepper and garnish with cilantro and lime slices
target.review: Yummy! I used bay scallops and served this over linguini. Takes no time at all to put together and is very tasty. :)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
orange beef

slice meat against the grain, serve with sticky white rice. add broccoli if desired.

1. into a small bowl , finely grate zest and squeeze juice from 1 orange
2. add garlic and soy sauce
3. peel remaining two oranges with a paring knife to remove both peel and pith
4. slice oranges crosswise in 1 / 2 inch thick circles
5. cut circles in half , discard seeds
6. in a medium bowl or ziplock toss meat with cornstarch
7. heat 1 tbsp oil in a large nonstick skillet over high heat
8. brown beef on all sides , working in batches and adding more oil if necessary , about 3-5 minutes then set aside
9. pour juice mixture into skillet , boil until syrupy , about 1 minute
10. add beef , oranges and scallions to pan , toss until coated and heated through
11. serve hot over rice
demonstrations.review: Yummy!! And it freezes well too. :)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
summer chopped salad with arugula vinaigrette

take the freshest greens, add chopped ripe tomatoes, raw sweet corn, a sprinkling of parmesan or goat cheese and dress it with an arugula balsamic vinaigrette and you have a winner every time!

1. peel the shallot and mince in a food processor using the metal blade
2. add the vinegar , lemon juice and mustard and process to combine
3. with the machine running gradually add the oil to emulsify
4. add the salt , pepper and arugula and pulse to blend well
5. taste and adjust seasonings if required
6. in a large salad bowl , combine all salad ingredients and the cheese
7. add the vinaigrette and toss until well coated
8. divide the salad amongst individual plates and serve
9. you may make the dressing up to 1 day in advance
10. just whisk well before using
11. the salad can be prepared 2 hours ahead and refrigerated
12. dress just before serving
13. you may use 1 / 4 cup crumbled goat's cheese instead of the parmesan if you wish
demonstrations.review: I made this for the My Three Chefs game. This is fantastic! Very easy to put together, and it tastes like summer! The dressing doesn't congeal when you refrigerate it, like most olive oil dressings do. I was going to bring the leftovers for work today, but there weren't any! I'll make this again for sure. Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
zucchini stuffed with corn and cheese

this recipe is one of only a handful of ways that i will eat zucchini. corn, cheese and zucchini are just made for each other...a perfect combination for summer time meals. i don't bake this too long because i like it to just be crisp-tender.

1. blanch squash in boiling salted water for 5 minutes
2. place under cold water and drain
3. halve and scoop out the seeds , forming a hollow boat
4. coarsely puree the corn , chives and ricotta cheese in a food processor and season with cayenne , salt and pepper
5. fill the squash halves with the mixture , mounding slightly
6. cover with the grated cheese
7. place in a buttered casserole and bake , covered , in a preheated 350 degree f
8. oven for 15 minutes
9. uncover and bake 20 minutes more or longer until the squash is tender and the topping is browned
10. serve topped with fresh cilantro
demonstrations.review:
YUM!! I made these last night for PAC 2006. I used frozen corn and fat-free ricotta. They were really easy to make and really yummy. Don't skip the cayenne. It really adds flavor to the dish. You can taste all the different components of the dish. I think next time I will thaw the corn first to get a smoother consistancy. I served this with a mixed green salad. I think the stuffing would be excellent in tomatoes too. Thanks for sharing. :)

Just wanted to add that this doesn't reheat very well. The cheddar gets oily in the microwave. Still yummy, just oily.

target.recipe_text:
drunken garlic crock pot roast

don't be afraid of all the garlic in this! it gets really mild from the long cooking process and gives the meat a wonderful flavor. this is a favorite for me, and i hope it will be for you, too. different brands of beer will give you different amounts of sweetness ranging from bitter to malty (common beer characters). try going with less sugar until you know how your beer will taste (as most of them add some amount of sweetness regardless).

1. in a large skillet , heat 1 tablespoons of the oil and brown roast on both sides , seasoning with salt and pepper
2. remove to a platter and keep warm
3. add the remaining tbsp of oil to the pan and add the onions , cook until they just start to wilt then add the garlic , them cook until the onions are tender , a few minutes more
4. add the bouillon cubes to the hot water and stir to dissolve
5. add that to the skillet along with the beer , brown sugar , mustard , and vinegar
6. stir to mix well
7. pour mixture into the bottom of the crock pot
8. place roast on top of liquid , cutting into pieces if it doesn't lay flat
9. set the crock pot on low and cook for 7-8 hours
10. remove meat from crock pot and pour liquid into a pan on the stove
11. heat to a boil , and mix a slurry out of the cornstarch and water
12. thicken pan liquid with slurry to make a gravy
13. serve gravy over meat or with potatoes or noodles
target.review: I thought this was awesome! The flavor is surprisingly sweet and mild. My kids had some friends for dinner (age 9 and 10) and they were dueling over the last bits! Plus, I am a confirmed pot roast hater and I liked it :-)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chicken thighs with lemon garlic

don't be put off with large amount of garlic, this recipe is really full of flavour and has excellent sauce.  i used on the bone chicken thigh cutlets because i think the chicken has much more flavour if it's kept on the bone and it is much tender. the original recipe comes from ‘taste of the sun’ by jacqueline clark & joanna farrow but i twinkled with it to suit our family.  if you don't like a lot of salt in your diet you could use salt reduce liquid chicken stock but this will alter the flavour.

1. to make the "garlic flavoured chicken hot stock" put the stock into a pan and bring to the boil
2. add the garlic cloves and simmer gently for 40 minutes
3. strain the stock and reserve both stock and garlic
4. preheat the oven to 190oc / 375of / gas 5
5. fifteen minutes before stock is ready , heat large saut or frying pan , then add the butter and oil and allow the butter to melt
6. add the chicken thighs and cook gently on both sides until golden brown
7. transfer them to an ovenproof dish
8. distribute the garlic and lemon slices among the chicken pieces in the ovenproof dish
9. add the flour to the pan which you browned the chicken and continuously stirring for one minute
10. add the extra chicken stock , stirring constantly and scraping the bottom of the pan , and then add the hot stock to the same pan
11. stirring , until the sauce has thickened and is smooth
12. season with salt and pepper
13. then pour the sauce over the chicken , cover and cook in the oven for 40 minutes
14. serve chicken on dinner plates and garnish with chopped parsley
15. you could serve with boiled new potatoes or rice
demonstrations.review: Absolutely divine recipe! My family is not a big fan of dark meat but loved it in this recipe. My boys were running over to the baking dish to dip their rolls in the sauce and didn't even realize they were eating whole cloves of garlic, LOL.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
creamy macaroni and cheese

i got this recipe from a food magazine. tastes great, easy to make, and affordable for anyone.

1. cook macaroni according to package directions
2. meanwhile , in a large saucepan , melt butter
3. stir in flour until smooth
4. gradually add milk
5. bring to a boil
6. cook and stir for 2 minutes
7. reduce heat
8. stir in the sour cream , process cheese , parmesan cheese , salt , mustard and pepper until cheese is melted and smooth
9. drain macaroni
10. toss with cheddar cheese
11. transfer to a greased 3-qt
12. baking dish
13. add cream sauce and mix well
14. bake , uncovered , at 350 for 35-40 minutes or until golden brown and bubbly
demonstrations.review: I use this same recipe at my house. It is delicious and the only one my husband craves! I like to melt a little butter and mix it with italian bread crumbs to make a crunchy topping. I also add 1/2 cup more milk as I think it can get too thick otherwise :-)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mennonite sloppy joes

i know, i know, everyone has a sloppy joe recipe.  but nobody else's matched ours, so i've got it posted for posterity.  originally from esther shank's mennonite country-style recipes cookbook.

1. saute beef in skillet and drain off fat
2. add remaining ingredients and simmer 15 - 30 minutes
3. serve on hamburger buns
demonstrations.review: Yumm-o! My kids and I really enjoyed these. Easy to make and less gloppy than Manwich (which I hate anyway, LOL).

target.recipe_text:
baked ham glazed with pineapple and chipotle peppers

sweet, smokey and spicy! go ahead and leave the seeds in if you enjoy the heat.

1. mix cornstarch with a little cold water to dissolve
2. place all ingredients except for ham in a blender and blend smooth , in a small saucepan over medium heat bring to a boil them simmer till thickened
3. preheat oven to 375 f
4. place ham , cut end down , in a large baking pan and score skin
5. bake ham for 15 minutes
6. brush glaze over ham and bake for another hour or until internal temperature reads 140 f
7. baste half way through baking
target.review: LOOK NO FURTHER!  The ham glaze search stops here.  I could drink this -- it's that good!  I just happened to have a whole nutmeg and it made such a difference (I'm sure pre-grated would be fine, though).  It didn't take much to give it a fabulous flavor and I saved a little to dip my ham.  Love the little kick the chilis gave it.  You are a GENIUS!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cheesy ham and potato soup

comfort soup at its finest!  i usually make this to use up leftover ham.  this is easy to adapt with other ingredients.  i don't put celery in mine.  i have added garlic sometimes as well.

1. combine potatoes , celery , carrots , onion , ham , and water / broth in stockpot and bring to boil
2. then cook over medium heat until potatoes are tender
3. stir in the chicken bouillon , salt , and pepper
4. in separate saucepan , melt butter over medium-low heat
5. whisk in flour and cook stirring constantly until thick
6. slowly stir in milk as not to allow lumps to form and all milk is added
7. turn up to medium heat
8. continue to stir until thick
9. add in cheese and stir until melted
10. stir the cheese mixture into the stockpot and cook until heated through
demonstrations.review: Delicious!  Thanks for an easy recipe that allowed me to feed the family quickly!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
bestest hamburger soup

i think this is our #1 all time family favorite and it's often requested for birthday dinners. it's the 'bestest' because my daughter described it as such when she was little.  this freezes well and i've added directions for that and for reheating.

1. in a large saucepan , brown meat , drain excess fat
2. add salt , pepper , oregano , basil , seasoned salt , and onion soup mix
3. stir in boiling water , tomato sauce , and soy sauce
4. cover and simmer for about 15 minutes
5. meanwhile , prepare celery , celery leaves , and carrots
6. then add to simmering mixture with split peas and continue to cook for 30 minutes
7. add macaroni and simmer for 30 minutes longer , adding more water if necessary and stirring occasionally
8. serve sprinkled with parmesan cheese over individual servings
9. to freeze: place soup in a rigid container and freeze
10. to reheat: remove from freezer and thaw
11. place soup in saucepan and heat , stirring , until hot
demonstrations.review: CRAZY good!  Can you believe my son actually said "Mom!  This is is the Best Soup Ever!" when he ate it.  I laughed and told him the name of it.  We didn't add beans or noodles but put rice in the bottom of our bowls.  And I was out of soy sauce so I used Worcestershire -- nice addition.  Excellent soup that is sure to be a family favorite for many years!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
spicy red beans and rice

these beans smell so good when they are cooking and the results are a tasty, new orleans style red beans and rice. i have tried several recipes but this one is easier than the others i've tried with an excellent result. serve with cornbread or corn muffins and your meal is complete. recipe is from taste of home magazine.

1. sort and rinse beans
2. in a large dutch oven or kettle , place all ingredients except parsley and rice
3. bring to a boil , then simmer , covered for 3-4 hours or until beans are tender
4. stir occasionally , adding water as needed to make a thick gravy
5. just before serving remove bay leaves and stir in parsley
6. serve over rice
demonstrations.review: I like to add link sausage and cut back a bit on the spice so my kids will eat it.  Perfect recipe!

target.recipe_text:
beef taco noodle bake

this is kindof like a "taco lasagna" of sorts. we love this stuff!!!!!!!

1. in deep frying pan , cook ground beef and onions
2. drain grease
3. stir in tomato sauce , water and taco seasoning
4. simmer 10 minutes
5. set aside
6. in bowl , combine cottage cheese , sour cream , flour , and beef bouillon
7. fold in cooked noodles , green onion and green chilies til well mixed
8. spoon noodle mixture into greased 13x9 baking dish
9. smooth level
10. top with meat mixture , smooth level
11. top evenly with cheese
12. bake in 350 oven for 25-30 minutes
13. let stand 5-10 minutes
14. serve with tossed salad and cornbread
15. 6 servings
target.review: This was delicious.  The whole family agreed that this recipe is a keep, one that will be placed in our permanent recipe file.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
best ever beef barley soup

soups are my very favorite thing to cook! many great soup recipes have been collected over the 57 years i've been cooking.....and this is one of the best. it is easy and the catsup gives it a unique taste that everyone, kids especially, seem to really like. the recipe came from a daughter, who is a great cook.....sarahloves2cook.

1. in dutch oven or soup pot , saute ground beef until it loses its red color , breaking it up as it cooks
2. add all other ingredients
3. simmer for 1 1 / 4 to 1 1 / 2 hours
4. adjust seasonings , if necessary
demonstrations.review: This was really good.  They only adjustment I made was to use a 28 oz can of tomatoes.  The recipe made a good sized amount but it had all disappeared by the next day!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pumpkin streusel muffins

another great pumpkin muffin recipe. made these last night--ooh baby!!

1. in a large bowl , cream together the margarine and the sugars
2. add the next 5 ingredients
3. stir to mix well
4. mix together the dry ingredients
5. gradually add the dry ingredients to the creamed mixture and stir just until combined
6. fill greased or paper line muffin cups two-thirds full with batter
7. for streusel topping: mix together the flour and brown sugar
8. cut in the margarine with a pastry blender until resembles coarse meal
9. sprinkle evenly over each cupcake batter
10. bake at 375 degrees for 20-25 minutes or until tests done
11. cool in pan for 5 minutes , then remove to a wire rack
demonstrations.review: Made these over the weekend and my family loved them.  This recipe is a keeper.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
ground turkey paprikash and macaroni

great goulash by rachael ray

1. bring a pot of water to boil add pasta and salt
2. cook pasta 6 minutes to al dente
3. heat a deep skillet over medium high heat
4. add extra-virgin olive oil then butter then ground meat and brown
5. add garlic , onions , red bell peppers and seasonings to the turkey
6. cook 5 or 6 minutes then add chicken stock and sour cream to the pan
7. bring to a boil and reduce heat to low
8. add cooked pasta and stir
9. let pasta absorb some sauce , a minute or so
10. adjust seasonings and serve
11. garnish the prepared dish with chopped parsley
demonstrations.review: This was simple to prepare and delicious.  Got a resounding approval rating from my family.

target.recipe_text:
no bake rice krispies peanut butter granola bars  lower fat

this is a delicious lower fat bar if using reduced-fat peanut butter, these are perfect for kid's lunch boxes, feel free to add in some chopped nuts or sunflower seeds or coconut in place of the raisins,

1. lightly grease 11 x 7-inch , can use a 13 x 9-inch baking dish but you will have a thinner bar
2. in a large bowl combine rice krispies cereal , oats and raisins
3. in a saucepan stir the corn syrup or honey and brown sugar until just at a boil
4. immediately remove from heat and stir in the peanut butter and vanilla until well combined
5. pour over the dry ingredients in the bowl
6. mix to combine
7. mix in mini chocolate chips work fast the mixture hardens quickly
8. transfer the mixture into prepared baking dish , then using slightly wet hands push evenly down into the pan
9. while the mixture is still soft , for easier slicing take a sharp knife and slice into desired size bars
10. chill until firm
target.review: These were yummy, tasted/looked like granola bars from the store.  They kept falling apart, though, making them difficult to eat!  As tasty as they were, I probably won't make them again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
secretly delicious spinach pie

the tortilla adds a delicious crunchy shell and it smells so good while it is cooking. i actually made up this recipe from items in my kitchen and couldn't believe how wonderful it tasted! it is now a hit in my family and so easy to make. please rate and give feedback.  


update: since i first made this five years ago, we still enjoy this at least once a month. i have found that i can alternate the ingredients to use up items i have in the fridge. i have used mushrooms, sauteed onions, cherry tomatoes and even feta cheese instead of cheddar cheese. and it always comes out fantastic. i have also found that there are times i need to use more or less eggs depending on the ingredients. also, a glass pie pan is so much better than a metal as it toasts the tortilla just right. such an easy recipe with gourmet taste!

1. mix the first six ingredients in a bowl
2. set aside
3. lay the flour tortilla in a glass pie dish , press gently - does not need to lay perfectly flat against dish
4. i don't spray it prior and have never had any issues with it sticking
5. especially when made using a glass pie pan
6. sprinkle only 1 / 2 cup cheese on tortilla
7. sprinkle remaining cheese and the spinach onto tortilla in layers , and press gently
8. i don't chop or tear the spinach but you might opt to do this
9. pour egg mixture evenly over spinach , be careful not to pour any outside of tortilla as this causes it to stick to pan
10. bake in oven at 365 degrees for 35 to 45 minutes
11. insert fork in center and it should come out clean
12. use sharp knife to cut into pie slices and serve hot
13. other options: instead of garlic , you can use 1 / 4 cup onions
14. for added flavor , serve with homemade salsa
demonstrations.review: My tortilla wasn't big enough to cover my pie dish, so I made "mini pies" in my muffin tin (I just had to trim my tortillas a bit).  I called them "mini quiches."  I steamed my spinach for a few minutes before putting it in the tins.  We loved the crunchy crust on these!  It was even better than pie crust, I thought.  The only downside of making it this way is that you can't fit as much cheese into a muffin tin!  I will be keeping them in mind for future brunches.  Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
taco bell quesadillas

i used to love these when i was younger, i could eat two in one sitting! i haven't had fast food in a year or two, but these taste like i remember taco bell's quesadillas tasting. i hope you enjoy it as much as i do.

1. combine sauce ingredients and stir until smooth
2. grill chicken in vegetable oil and cut into thin slices
3. preheat skillet over medium heat
4. one at a time , lay tortilla into hot skillet and sprinkle with 1 / 4 cup of each shredded cheese and 1 / 2 cheese slice on one side of the tortilla
5. arrange about 1 / 4 cup chicken slices over tortilla on the same half covered with cheese
6. on the empty side , spread about one tablespoon of sauce
7. fold over , and press gently with spatula
8. cook until cheese is melted and slice each into 4 pieces
demonstrations.review: These didn't taste exactly like Taco Bell to me.  There was something not quite right that I couldn't put my finger on.  I may try a little less sugar next time.  However, they were delicious and a great late night snack for my husband (and me) who was pulling an all-nighter writing a paper!  He loved them.  Both of us thank you for the recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
oven fried chicken chimichangas

a fast and healthier way to serve chimichangas than the traditional deep fried. these are very good, and you may dress them up to you own preference. i like to serve with green chile sauce sometimes instead of the picante sauce.

1. mix chicken , picante sauce or salsa , cumin , oregano , cheese and onions
2. place about 1 / 4 cup of the chicken mixture in the center of each tortilla
3. fold opposite sides over filling
4. roll up from bottom and place seam-side down on a baking sheet
5. brush with melted margarine
6. bake at 400f for 25 minutes or until golden
7. garnish with additional cheese and green onion and serve salsa on the side
demonstrations.review: We loved the crispy crust on these!  They were absolutely delicious with sour cream on the side.  Thank you!

target.recipe_text:
roast  sticky  chicken

beautiful and delicious, this incredibly moist roasted chicken puts kenny roger's roasters, boston market, and other rotisserie style chickens to shame! please don't let the word 

1. blend all spices together and set aside
2. remove neck and giblets from chicken cavity , rinse well inside and out , and pat dry with paper towels
3. rub with spice mixture , both inside and out , then stuff cavity with onions
4. wrap in a resealable"food grade" plastic bag , tie closed , and refrigerate overnight
5. remove from plastic bag and place in a shallow baking pan
6. roast uncovered in a 250 f oven 5 hours
7. if the chicken contains a pop-up thermometer , ignore it
8. this recipe is safe
9. according to the united states department of agriculture food safety and inspection service , a whole chicken should reach an internal temperature of 180 f
10. for more info check out their"thermy" campign web site !
11. baste with drippings every 30 minutes after the first hour
12. let rest for 10 minutes before carving
target.review: Amazing chicken!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
banana orange frozen sorbet

except for the small amount of fat in the bananas, there is hardly any fat in this recipe, and it's very very refreshing! if you don't have an ice cream maker you can spread the mixture into a shallow pan and freeze, just give it a stir with a fork every 45 minutes, once it gets fairly firm, briefly toss it in a blender to break up the ice crystals and then refreeze.

1. in a saucepan combine sugar and water
2. bring to a boil , stirring occasionally until all the sugar is dissolved
3. remove from heat , let cool to room temperature , then refrigerate until col
4. put the bananas in a blender along with the orange juice and cold sugar / water syrup
5. blend until smooth
6. freeze in an ice cream maker according to the manufacturers directions or place in a shallow pan
demonstrations.review: This is an easy, sweet, nutritious treat. It could actually use less sugar; seemed too sweet for me with a full cup. I prepared it in a blender with the sugar, a cup of ice cubes, the bananas and OJ; blended well; poured into a Ziplock bag; and laid flat in my freezer. After a few hours I massaged the bag. It was totally set and ready to eat after a total of about 4 hours. This is a nice sweet treat for a hot summer day.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
parmesan broiled flounder

this easy and delicious recipe is a classic!

1. place fillets in a single layer on a lightly greased or pan sprayed , shallow oven-to-table type broiler pan
2. brush with lemon juice
3. in a small bowl , combine remaining ingredients to make the cheese topping mixture
4. set aside
5. broil fillets 4 to 6 minutes or until fish flakes easily when tested with a fork
6. remove fillets from oven
7. spread with parmesan topping
8. broil an additional 30 seconds or until cheese is lightly browned and bubbly
9. garnish with lemon twists and parsley , if desired
10. since the flounder in the recipe is not marinated , if the fish comes out mushy i suspect the results are the from overcooking
11. either the fish was left under the broiler for too long , the temperature of the broiler is too high , or the rack on which the the pan placed under the broiler is too close to the heat
demonstrations.review: This was very tasty. After reading many other reviews, I omitted the butter and added the lemon to the parm/mayo mix instead of putting it directly on the fish. I sprinkled a little salt and pepper on the fish as it was broiling and added Lowry's seasoning salt and parsley to the parm mix instead of salt. I loved the creamy lemon flavor that came through the sauce. I used Pacific Flounder but had none of the "mushy" problems that others wrote about. I broiled the fish very carefully on both sides on low before topping with the parm mix and then broiling on high till browned. Yum!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
luscious lemon frosting

lovely frosting, makes enough frosting to cover tops and sides of two 9-inch layers

1. add lemon rind to butter
2. cream well
3. add part of sugar gradually , blending after each addition
4. combine lemon juice and water
5. add to creamed mixture , alternately with remaining sugar , until of right consistency to spread
6. beat after each addition until smooth
7. add salt
8. makes enough frosting to cover tops and sides of two 9-inch layers , or to cover the top and sides of golden sponge loaf
demonstrations.review: Delicious, sweet, and tangy! I used this recipe as frosting for Moist Lemon Orange Zucchini Muffins (Recipe #70915). Great combination!

target.recipe_text:
cajun sausage and red beans

this is a spicy and zesty dish. you may serve it over rice, or as a soup. this is great served with cornbread, or corn muffins and green onions.

1. combine all ingredients in crockpot
2. cover and cook on low 7-8 hours
3. may be served over cooked rice , if desired , or as a thick and zesty soup
target.review: Well, This dish was real easy to throw together and it did smell real good cooking in the crockpot all day, but, it really wasn't anything I would go out of my way for. Just SO-SO in my book. Don't think I'll be making it again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
bbq ribs

this is an excellent dish for a barbeque party. make the ribs in advance, and when your guests have arrived, all that's left is to grill them. you'll have them wondering how they got so tender and tasty so fast.

1. place ribs in a large skillet
2. cover with salted water and bring to a boil
3. reduce heat and simmer over low heat for 1 hour , or until meat is tender , but not falling off the bone
4. melt the butter in a saucepan and saute the onion and garlic until the onion is tender
5. remove from heat and pour into a blender with all remaining ingeredients
6. puree for 1 minute , then pour back into saucepan
7. bring to a boil , then remove from heat
8. place the boiled ribs in a shallow dish and pour sauce over them
9. place in the refrigerator for at least 2 hours
10. barbeque ribs on an outdoor grill over moderately hot coals , basting with the sauce and turning often until well browned
demonstrations.review: Very good!!! Sauce was a little thin so like the other review I was a little worried about blending, but it seemed like the sauce did get a little thicker with blending. I did add 1/2C. honey and a 1/4C. hot sauce. And I do have to say "damn" it turned out great. Thanks for a awesome receipe. I will be making this one again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
no bake fudge cookies

this recipe is from a church library book 

1. mix first 6 ingredients in a sauce pan and cook until it boils
2. boil for 1-3 minutes
3. remove from heat and add peanut butter and oatmeal
4. drop by teaspoonfuls on to wax paper
5. chill until set
demonstrations.review: I use to make this reciepe when I was a kid. I forgot all about it. Now I can pass this one one to my kids. Thanks for a quick, easy and tasty receipe. and some great childhood memories with "my mommy". Thanks again

demonstrations.recipe_text:
so it s bekah s pulled pork now

i have adopted this recipe from mean chef. this is one of my favorite recipes. the pork is sweet, succulent and falling apart tender. fabulous served alone, on rolls, in tortillas.

1. for rub: mix all ingredients in a bowl
2. for sauce: combine in nonreactive saucepan , bring to boil and simmer until it reduces to 1 1 / 2 cups
3. for pork: rub pork with rub
4. place in plastic bag and refrigerate overnight
5. take out pork and re-rub
6. let sit at room temperature for 2 hours
7. roast on rack uncovered in oven at 250-275 degrees until falling apart tender
8. it will take 7-8 hours , the internal temperature of the pork when done should be between 195 and 200 degrees
9. pull pork into pieces , toss with sauce
10. serve with extra sauce (if you prefer , the pork can be served with pig pickin sauce )
demonstrations.review: WOW!!! this was fabulous. the only bad thing was I didn't double the recipe. between my son and DH we almost didn't have enough for dinner. I counldn't keep there hand off. this one is a keeper. I can't wait to make it again. Thanks for posting.

target.recipe_text:
real shepherd s pie

a traditional british dish, cottage pie may be made by the same method substituting lamb and lamb stock with beef and beef stock,it may also be topped with grated cheese and tomato before browning, my recipe serves 2 hungry people with good appetites,but it can serve 4.

1. brown meat and chopped onion together for about 5 minutes , add stock and simmer slowly , occasionally stirring until cooked , about 20 minutes
2. mix 2-3 teaspoons of flour or cornflour to a smooth cream with water and slowly add to meat mixture over a low heat stirring continuously until thickened
3. pour into ovenproof dish and set aside , allowing to cool , depending on the quality of the meat used you should not need to skim the fat , however , this is to personal taste
4. peel , boil and mash potatoes with salt , pepper , freshly chopped mint if required , and a generous knob of butter
5. cover the meat mixture with the potato and bake in a medium oven for 30-40 minutes
6. if required dish can be browned under a grill
7. serve with fresh vegetables
8. i also like thickly sliced fresh bread and butter with my real shepherds pie
target.review:
This is an excellent recipe and absolutely authentic just as I, my mother, grandmother and probably great-grandmother have been making it all these years. If lamb was used, often left-overs from the Sunday roast, it was called Shepherd's Pie (Sheepherd) and if beef 
then "Cottage Pie". It needs no extra bits added,  and certainly NO baked beans - sacrilege.You could, of course experiment, but it would no longer be Shepherd's Pie.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
magnificent 1st prize risotto

this recipe was part of what helped me win a cooking competition at school against 7 other people. i got it out of an excellent appetizer book and continue to make it!! excellent served with any meal. (vegetarians can substitute vegetable stock for chicken stock)

1. bring stock to a boil , then reduce to a low simmer
2. ladle a little stock into a small bowl
3. add the saffron threads and let infuse
4. melt 4 tablespoons of butter in a large sauce pan until foaming
5. add onions , stirring frequently , and cook for 2 minutes , then add garlic and cook for 1 more minute
6. cook only until softened , not brown
7. add the rice and stir until the grains start to swell and burst
8. then add a few ladles of stock , saffron liquid , and salt and pepper to taste
9. stir over low heat until liquid has beed absorbed
10. keep adding stock , letting the rice absorb the liquid before adding more
11. stir constantly test frequently just for the hell of it !
12. after about 20-25 minutes , the rice should be just tender and the risoto golden and creamy
13. take off heat and add 2 / 3 cup parmesan cheese and remaining 1 tablespoon butter , mixing until butter has melted
14. season to taste
15. transfer to serving plates and serve hot
16. sprinkle remaining parmesan cheese
17. enjoy !
demonstrations.review: No wonder you got first prize; this really is the business, Mallina. I think the secret is adding the stock little by little. Thank you,this will be a regular..

demonstrations.recipe_text:
capsicum dip for cheese

this really is a capsicum jam, that you pour over cream cheese. it's great at parties, is easy to make, and tastes amazing.

1. combine first 6 ingredients in a saucepan and simmer approximately 20 minutes until reduced to a jammy consistency
2. cool
3. pile the cheese on a serving platter and pour the dip over
4. serve with crackers
demonstrations.review: Capsicum "Jam", what a great idea. This is very tasty and already popular here -  I will be making this often, I know.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mince and tatties

mince and tatties is a common dish in scottish households.

1. heat the oil in a pan and saut the onion until it is brown
2. add in the mince and cook until well browned
3. drain off the liquid
4. add the carrots and oatmeal , mix well and pour in enough water to just cover
5. crumble in the stock cubes , season and stir
6. cover the pan and simmer the mince for about 20 minutes
7. once the mince is cooked thicken the mince with about 3 teaspoons of gravy powder or cornstarch mixed with a little cold water
8. serve the mince with boiled potatoes
demonstrations.review:
Common in English households too, without the oatmeal. Many an English person will have fond memories of coming home from school or work on a raw, wet winter evening to "mince and Taters".
N ot only carrots, but turnips and parsnips went in too. Just make sure the fat is well drained after meat and onions are cooked.  Often mistakenly regarded as "peasant" food. No way! Good tosee it on an American site.

target.recipe_text:
country hamburger lentil soup   crock pot

i created this on a busy hockey weekend - i wanted something warm to come home to after spending a long day at the hockey rink.  this was just the ticket... and i got to clean out my cupboards too!

1. brown ground beef
2. combine all ingredients in 4-5qt crock pot
3. cook on low at least 12 hours or high for 6 hours
4. i do a combination of high / low , when i made this i did low for 5 hours and high for 4 hours
5. remove bay leaves before serving
6. it made very yummy leftovers !
target.review: This was so easy and truly a clean out the cupboards soup.  I had one carrot, so I added a few small potatoes, no beef bouillon, so I used chicken broth, running low on spices, so ended up using italian seasoned canned tomatoes. Even with these changes, it was great.  My 2 yr old ate licked her bowl clean.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
borsofozelek

this is super easy hungarian transylvanian comfort food. cheap, easy, and delicious. serve this with fried eggs or sausage for a nice meal.

1. heat oil in a saucepan on medium heat
2. add onion , saute until transparent
3. add peas and water
4. cook for 5-10 minutes on medium
5. whisk together milk and flour
6. add to the peas
7. cook until it begins to thicken , about 5 minutes
8. add seasonings and cook 5 minutes more
9. serve with fried eggs or sausage
demonstrations.review: Simple and cheap.  I added some diced potato too.  Served with sausage and it was very filling.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chicken capri   sb diet phase 1

a great recipe that i adapted from the sb diet cookbook. great for phase 1 or beyond. this is pretty close to the original, with a few changes.

1. in a small bowl mash ricotta cheese , parmesan cheese , salt , pepper , oregano& parsley together until well blended
2. toss the chicken with the garlic powder and brown in the olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat for 10 minutes per side
3. when done remove to a shallow casserole dish to cool slightly
4. preheat oven to 350 degrees
5. spoon 1 heaping serving spoon of ricotta mixture onto each chicken breast and top with 1 tablespoons of crushed tomatoes
6. place one slice of mozzarella cheese on each one and place in the top rack of the oven
7. bake for 20 minutes until a meat thermometer registers 170 deg
8. farenheit
demonstrations.review: My family really enjoyed this. I added some spinach to the ricotta mixture. Next time I may stuff the breasts.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crock pot chicken stew with cheddar cornmeal dumplings

i got this recipe from msn lifestyles and couldn't find this recipe posted on here.  this is really quick and easy to make on a busy or cold weeknight.  i have posted my slightly modified version.

1. in a 4 or 5 quart slowcooker combine the carrots , potatoes , onions , garlic , bay leaves , sage and pepper and stir to combine
2. place chicken on top of the vegetables
3. in a medium bowl , gradually whisk broth into soup and pour this mixture over the chicken
4. cover
5. cook on low heat for 8-10 hours or on high heat for 4-5 hours
6. turn slow cooker to high heat
7. remove and discard bay leaves
8. combine water and cornstarch and stir into stew until combined
9. in a medium bowl combine flour , cheese , cornmeal , baking powers and salt
10. in a small bowl combine egg , milk and melted butter
11. add egg mixture to flour mixture
12. stir with a fork until just moistened
13. use 2 spoons to drop dough directly on top of stew
14. cover and cook for 25 to 30 minutes or until a toothpick inserted into dumpling comes out clean
15. do not life cover during cooking
demonstrations.review: Cyaos, by chance do you have the original recipe?  I missed placed it and like the parsnips in it.  I make this soup all the time and it turns out every time!  Sometimes, I'll put in frozen egg noodles instead of making the dumplings.  You need to add a bit more water and/or broth to the soup because the noodles will absorb liquid.

target.recipe_text:
daube de boeuf

posted by request,from fine cooking 3/07

1. heat oven to 325f
2. in a dutch oven heat oil and bacon , stirring until bacon is browned , remove to a plate
3. season beef with salt and pepper and cook in batches until browned on all sides , remove to plate
4. drain all but 1 tbs of drippings and add shallots , season with salt and pepper , cook until softened
5. add cognac and boil down
6. add tomato paste , garlic , herbes , stirring
7. add wine and liquid from tomatoes , bring to a boil
8. crush tomatoes by hand and add to pot , stirring
9. add zest and bacon to pot , add beef and carrots
10. lower to simmer , cover , and place in oven
11. cook 2-3 hours until beef is tender , stirring every 45 minutes
12. add parsley , serve
target.review: My daughter's new favorite. We all really enjoyed it. Thank you for sharing the recipe with us!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
baked spaghetti  weight watchers friendly

i adapted this from a light & tasty cookbook. it was so delicious that i had to put it in the fridge before it was cool just to stop myself from eating it all! for wwers, this works to 6 points per serving. i use ragu no sugar added tomato & basil sauce to keep the calorie/fat content as low as possible.  note: ww has changed their points system several times since this is posted, and you should recalculate the points by the current system.

1. cook spaghetti according to package directions
2. in a large skillet , brown beef , onion , and garlic
3. drain fat
4. add spaghetti sauce and heat through
5. meanwhile , combine cottage cheese , 2 cups mozzarella , and 1 / 4 cup parmesan
6. in a 9x13 casserole dish sprayed with nonstick cooking spray , layer 1 cup of meat mixture , half the spaghetti , half the cheese , and half the remaining meat mixture
7. repeat layers
8. dish will be very full
