demonstrations.review: This is a truly delicious recipe.  I don't always rate all of the recipes I try, but this one is worthy of a good rating.  I served it at a casual dinner and received rave reviews.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
the ultimate greek salad

this is the most delicious salad - fresh and wonderful-tasting.  fyi, lettuce can very much be a part of any greek salad - if you want it to.  we like lettuce in my family and i often add it.  it would not be 'authentic' in a horiatiki (village) salad, but who cares?

1. whisk dressing ingredients together until blended
2. season to taste
3. drain onion from ice water and pat dry with paper towels
4. combine all salad ingredients , except cheese , in large bowl
5. toss with dressing
6. sprinkle cheese over and serve
demonstrations.review: Excellent salad.  I made it according to directions.  Next time I may add beets.

target.recipe_text:
savory crescent chicken squares

these are very good. you can also make them smaller using the "triangle" instead of the "square" and have as an appetizer instead of the main course.

1. blend cream cheese with 2 tbsp butter until smooth
2. add next five ingredients and mix well
3. spoon 1 / 2 c meat mixture onto 2"triangles" of dough
4. pull 4 corners to the top , center of mixture and twist slightly and seal edges by pinching
5. brush tops with remaining butter and sprinkle with croutons bake on ungreased cookie sheet for 20-25 minutes in a 350 oven until golden brown
target.review: I got this recipe off of the pillsbury site, and it was absolutely amazing.  It was easy and looked like it took hours to make in the kitchen.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
the best turkey burger ever according to my hubby

this is a southwestern stuffed burger that will knock your socks off. my hubby hates ground turkey. when he took a bite of it, he yelled #*@$ that's good. then, he went to the grocery store and got more ground turkey the next day.

1. blend 3 tbsp mayo , 1 pkg taco seasoning , and meat
2. divide into 4 for big burgers and 6 for smaller ones
3. divide each burger in half then press each out to make 8 or 12 thin patties
4. mix shredded cheese and 2 tbsp salsa in a small bowl
5. spoon mixture over half of the patties
6. cover each with another patty and press the sides into a nice seal
7. grill about 7 minutes on each side
8. while grilling , mix remaining mayo with remaining salsa
9. spread on your buns
10. add lettuce , tomato , and whatever extras you like
11. we usually don't add anything
12. assemble your burger like usual
demonstrations.review: this was absolutely delicious.  i can't say mine held together too well, especially because i pan fried it instead, but i'm rating this on flavor.  i made a couple of adjustments... i added about 1/2 a cup of crushed corn chips... i didn't have shredded cheese on hand, so instead, i took regular american cheese, and folder it into fours... then put a dollop of salsa on top... the cheese just oozed out... GREAT RECIPE!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
moist and tender turkey  or turkey breast

please read this regarding temp & time! there is no "right" temperature. if you roast it at 250°f it will just take longer to cook than at 325°f. (just like picking high or low on a crock-pot) i cannot tell you exactly how long it will  take. it depends on what type of oven you have & how warm/cold your turkey is when you put it in the oven. you have to use an instant read thermometer to know when it is cooked.   (i roast my 18-20 lbs. fresh turkey at 250°f. it took about 4 hours to reach the correct temperature in my old convection oven. it took 5 hours in my new one.) 
because of the mayo, the skin is crisp and flavorful and the meat is tender, moist and delicious. if you don't use the butter & broth, you will not have enough pan drippings to make gravy. i've also added 1/2 cup of beer or wine to the mixture before & it was also spectacular. with slow roasting it, the meat stays so juicy i've actually had it squirt out when i insert the thermometer! i've never had a better turkey.

1. place turkey or turkey breast in a roasting pan
2. combine melted butter and chicken broth
3. pour over turkey
4. rub mayonnaise all over turkey's exterior
5. salt and pepper lightly if desired
6. roast at 300-325f until internal temperature reaches 170f on an instant read thermometer
7. remove from oven and let sit for about 30 minutes before slicing
8. to make gravy: pour pan drippings into a saucepan and bring to a simmer over medium heat
9. add 1 tbls
10. cornstarch per cup of broth / drippings to 1 / 4 cup cold water
11. mix well to dissolve
12. stir cornstarch mixture into broth and stir until thickened
13. add salt and pepper to taste
14. if too thin , dissolve more cornstarch in water and add until desired thickness
15. if too thick , add water or more broth to thin
demonstrations.review: I've never made turkey breast before, and I had bought a boneless, skinless turkey breast that I didn't know what to do with, so I decided to try this recipe.  I didn't have chicken broth or bouillon on hand, so I used Lipton Onion Soup packet and added water.  I used fat free mayo on the skinless breast, anyways.  The breast was very tender, and I usually skip out on turkey during Thanksgiving.  For the gravy I used the leftover broth and mixed in corn starch and fat free evaporated milk.  I served it to my boyfriend as an open faced hot turkey sandwich.  He loved it :)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s italian melt in your mouth meatballs

cooking the meatballs in simmering pasta sauce  will not only add so much extra flavor to the sauce the meatballs will be melt-in-your-mouth tender, you may of course oven-bake the meatballs for about 25 minutes,  --- don't be afraid to add in more parmesan cheese and a little more milk, there is no need to measure exactly, this recipe is pretty much foolproof, leftover cooked meatballs make a wonderful pizza topping just slice thinly and freeze until ready to use ----- these also make wonderful juicy burgers shaped into patties-- for more of my tried and true recipes check out my food blog at www.kittencalskitchen.com

1. mix all ingredients together in a large bowl
2. shape into small meatballs
3. drop the meatballs into simmering pasta sauce , do not stir for at least 20 minutes or you will risk breaking the meatballs
4. continue cooking in the simmering sauce for another 20 minutes
5. after the 40 minutes cooking time continue cooking your sauce with the meatballs in for as long as desired
demonstrations.review: my boyfriend could not stop raving about this.  they were extra moist.  i would love to try to coat these with eggs and extra bread crumbs, then fry them as a fried meatball appetizer.

target.recipe_text:
banana oatmeal bread

i love bananas and oatmeal, so when i saw this in the september 2004 issue of cooking light, i just knew i had to make it! i wasn't at all disappointed. the oatmeal makes it hearty and somewhat chewy, while the bananas and buttermilk make it sweet and moist - yet it is not as sweet or sticky-moist as some other banana breads i've had. this makes a smaller loaf than some recipes. i made 2 mini-loaves instead of one large one, and they were done in 30-35 minutes.  edited to mention- since i posted this recipe, i've made it several times.  it has become the banana bread recipe for this household, and when i give it as gifts it never fails to receive compliments.  it is extremely versatile also.  i have made it with yogurt in place of buttermilk, walnut oil for the vegetable oil, and i have cut back the sugar and added cinnamon as a couple reviewers suggested.  this last time i made an eggless version by substituting 2 tablespoons ground flax seed + 6 tablespoons water for the eggs.  (i think next time i will try a vegan version by also replacing the buttermilk with soymilk.)  every time it has turned out perfect!

1. preheat oven to 350f and spray a 8 x 4 inch loaf pan with cooking spray
2. combine dry ingredients together in a large bowl
3. combine banana , buttermilk , oil , vanilla , and eggs in a small bowl or measuring cup
4. pour wet ingredients into the dry ingredients and stir gently just until the dry ingredients are moistened
5. spoon batter into the prepared pan and bake for 55 minutes , or until a toothpick inserted in the center comes out clean
6. cool on a wire rack , in the pan , for about 15 minutes
7. remove the bread from the pan after 15 minutes and cool thoroughly on the rack
target.review: I made a double recipe (with 50% whole wheat flour and some cinnamon), and definitely preferred the second batch, the one that sat out while the first loaf was in the oven. The first batch had oatmeal that was firm/hard and bright white when cut. It was still good, but not quite as delicious as the second.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
spinach and potato frittata

great for breakfast or brunch as well as a light dinner.

1. heat olive oil in a medium skillet over medium heat
2. place potatoes in the skillet , cover and cook about 10 minutes until tender but firm
3. mix in spinach , green onions and garlic
4. season with salt and pepper
5. continue cooking 1 to 2 minutes , until spinach is wilted
6. in a medium bowl , beat eggs and milk
7. pour into skillet over the vegetables
8. sprinkle with cheddar cheese
9. reduce heat to low
10. cover
11. cook 5 to 7 more minutes or until eggs are firm
12. cut into wedges and serve
demonstrations.review: Absolutely wonderful! Here are the modifications I've incorporated, to rave reviews. My preference is for yellow-flesh potatoes, so I use those whenever possible. Once in the skillet, sprinkle potatoes to taste with black pepper and oregano. To avoid burning, I tend to use a medium low heat and cook the potatoes until they are mostly browned on at least 1 side, up to 20 minutes. After the spinach has wilted I add 2 sundried tomato halves, julienned and cut crosswise, and 2 TB fresh basil, chopped, in addition to the garlic and green onions; substitute 1/2 cup crumbled feta cheese for the cheddar. It takes about 30 minutes for my eggs to set on low heat when covered.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
lemon herb marinade

i got this recipe from my best friend. she always uses it on chicken but i find it also works very well with halibut, but don't marinate the halibut as long as you would chicken.

1. mix all ingredieants well
2. pour over chicken and marinate at lease 2 hours
3. if using fish , only marinate 1 / 2 hour
4. grill chicken or fish on b-b-q , or broil in broiler
5. this makes enough for 6 boneless , skinless chicken breasts
demonstrations.review: Wonderful lemony marinade, without salt. Except for omitting the salt I followed the recipe and marinated salmon fillets for about 20 minutes before baking. The fish was delicious and moist and didn't need any fresh lemon. Can't wait to try this on chicken.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
savoury couscous

simple cous cous perfect for side dish.

1. heat butter in sauce pan
2. add chopped onions , stir and allow to cook until soft
3. stir in crushed garlic
4. add couscous , stir
5. add chicken stock , stir and bring to boil
6. remove off heat , cover and allow to stand for 5 minutes
7. stir in coriander or parsley
8. add salt and pepper to taste
9. serve as a side dish
demonstrations.review: My experience with most couscous dishes is that they are bland, and this one was no different. I used regular vegetable broth (not low sodium) instead of chicken stock because there were vegetarians at the table, the full 2 cloves of garlic and chopped cilantro/coriander. I suspect the onions lose some of their flavour sitting in the broth for 5 minutes. If there is a next time, I'd consider removing the onions and garlic from the pot before adding the broth, then stir them back in with the cilantro after the couscous has cooked.

target.recipe_text:
heavenly apricot white chocolate chunk cookies

a must try. the butter and brown sugar give the cookies a caramel-like taste that is pure heaven when paired with the apricots and white chocolate. source: the neighborhood bakeshop by jill van cleave

1. preheat the oven to 350
2. cream the butter and brown sugar in a medium-size mixing bowl until smoothly blended
3. beat in the egg and vanilla
4. add the flour , baking soda , and salt , stirring the mixture into a smooth dough
5. add the apricots and white chocolate , stirring until the pieces are thoroughly dispersed
6. drop the batter by tablespoonfuls onto ungreased cookie sheets , spacing 2 inches apart
7. bake for 10 minutes , until the edges are lightly browned
8. let the cookies set on the sheet for 1 to 2 minutes before transferring them with a spatula to wire racks to cool
target.review: These were great.  I made three batches and froze two of them and put them in my dad's freezer.  He had eaten them within a week.  They were just right, soft in the middle and crispier outside.  Thanks.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
surfer bars

these are a very rich, bar type cookie. easy to prepare, a favorite with young and old alike. great for picnics, potlucks, holiday cookie trays or any get together. warning!! they can become "addictive" ;)

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. grease an 8 inch square baking pan
3. in a large saucepan over medium heat , melt butterscotch pieces , sugar and butter , stirring constantly until all is melted
4. remove from heat
5. cool butterscotch mixture slightly
6. add egg and beat well
7. add flour , baking powder , baking soda and salt , mix well
8. stir in remaining ingredients
9. spread mixture evenly in 8 inch square pan
10. bake at 350f for 20-25 minutes
11. cool in pan on wire rack
12. when cool , cut into bars
demonstrations.review: These are just evil little things!  Evil I tell you!  Stay away from them or at least make a few for me!  Very good, very rich and came out perfectly every time.  Great recipe, thank you!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pork spread

this is my father's recipe and brings back such fond memories of my family. we always enjoyed this during the holidays. we would have this in the mornings, spread on toast. always served it with crackers for an appetizer. my father enjoyed it in a sandwich, with mustard and always had to have bread and butter pickles on the side.

1. combine all ingredients in a saucepan with enough water to make mushy
2. simmer on low heat , stirring occasionally for 2 hours until water is evaporated
3. put in bowl and keep refrigerated
4. serve in a sandwich , on crackers , or on toast
demonstrations.review: I made this for my father who loves unusual meat dishes.  He ranted and raved about it for a week until I gave him the recipe.  This has become a permanent fixture in his fridge.  I did double the spices though as he and I both like more spice.  I liked it mostly on crackers as a spread.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
simple baked chicken

recipe is from sil...easy enough (kinda one of those fix and forget...until the timer goes off)and the kids like it!

1. pour water in 8 inch baking dish
2. rinse chicken and then coat with butter
3. holding chicken up , sprinkle all over with seasoned salt
4. place chicken in baking dish , top with any extra seasoned salt
5. put celery and onion in chicken's"cavity"
6. cover with aluminum foil and bake for at least 1 hour at 350 degrees
7. uncover and bake an additional 10 to 15 minutes for chicken to"brown" lightly
demonstrations.review: This just was so bland!  I expected it to taste like rotissiere chicken and it just wasn't tasty.  It also needs to cook way longer than an hour as it comes out too tough.

target.recipe_text:
yummiest ever baked mac and cheese

a friend brought a big pan of this to a potluck and i had to have the recipe to make for my family.  it is so yummy and creamy that it's hard to stop eating.  we like it as a main dish with a salad, but you could serve it as a scrumptious side dish.  these are directions for the full batch which will serve a crowd.  it halves easily.

1. preheat oven to 350
2. cook pasta according to pasta directions just until done - you don't want it mushy , because it will absorb a little of the cheesy liquid in the oven
3. combine soup , evaporated milk , butter , salt , and pepper in a large microwaveable bowl
4. cover with plastic wrap , leaving a small vent , and cook for 6-7 minutes until the butter is melted and the mixture is warm-to-hot throughout
5. in a large baking dish , spread 1 / 3 of the cooked noodles
6. top with 1 / 3 of the sauce
7. sprinkle with 1 / 3 of the cheddar
8. repeat layers twice , ending with the cheese
9. bake for 40-45 minutes
10. when it comes out of the oven , sprinkle with a little dried parsley if desired
11. this gives it visual interest , and you can also pretend it's healthier
12. let stand for 5 minutes before serving
target.review:
Best mac and cheese recipe I've tried. Super easy and quick. Everyone loved it, but two out of five thought it could be a little cheesier taste wise. I used sharp cheddar. Wish the recipe stated how many ounces of cheese instead of cups, a finer grate would be less than a thicker grate per cup, mine was about medium. Next time I'll add more, maybe a little velveeta, or dry mustard? Half the recipe fed 5 with a little left over. Used half & half instead of canned milk.
Can't wait to try it again, with tweaks for my family's preferences.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
rodeo hash

from best recipes from the backs of boxes, bottles, cans & jars. campbell soup recipe.

1. in skillet , brown beef nin shortening with potatoes and celery , stir to separate meat
2. pour off fat
3. add remaining ingredients
4. cover
5. simmer 10 minutes
6. stir oftne
demonstrations.review: I've been making this for over 20 years. Great for a simple week night meal.  The first time I made it I didn't have Chili Sauce so I used  salso, I've made it that way ever since. Be sure and get the potatoes browned up, it really makes the flavor better.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s chicken crescent roll casserole

this will also work great with turkey; if you do not have chicken breasts, then use any leftover cooked chicken. if desired you can fill the crescents just with the filling mixture and omit the soup, just brush with butter before baking. they are wonderful just stuffed with the filling! a few members have experienced a soggy bottom, so you might want to consider just drizzling half (or even a little less) of the soup mixture on top and a little around the sides of the crescents, then save the rest of the soup mixture for another time (this will help prevent a soggy bottom). you may use the jumbo crescent rolls and stuff with more chicken mixture :)

1. set oven to 350f
2. butter a casserole dish
3. in a saucepan , mix half and half cream , 3 / 4 cup grated cheese and undiluted chicken soup
4. heat just until the cheese melts
5. for the filling --- in a bowl , mix the soft cream cheese with butter until very smooth , then add in garlic powder
6. add in the chopped chicken , onion and cheddar cheese
7. mix well until combined
8. add in 2 tablespoons whipping cream or mayonnaise
9. mix to combine
10. season with seasoned salt or white and black pepper to taste
11. unroll the crescent rolls
12. place 1 heaping tablespoon chicken mixture on top of each crescent triangle , then roll up starting at the thicker end
13. drizzle a small amount of soup mixture on the bottom of the dish
14. then place the crescent rolls seam-side down on top of the creamed mixture in the casserole
15. drizzle the remaining sauce on top and sprinkle with 1 cup grated cheese , or amount desired
16. bake for about 30 minutes
demonstrations.review:
Amazing!  Everyone loved it.  I used the cream cheese with onion and chives.  This one went straight to the keeper file.
Thanks Kittencal!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
best ever potato casserole

there are many similar recipes but none are as good! i got this out of a church cookbook by karla m. and roberta g. besides my mother in-law they are the best cooks in the church! i have made this so many times and it always turns out so yummy! beware you will be tempted to eat more than you need.

1. thaw out hash browns
2. dice up onion nice and fine
3. in a large bowl , put hash browns , melted butter , and rest of ingredients and mix well
4. salt and pepper to taste
5. pour mixture in a 9x13 inch baking dish and sprinkle chips
6. bake at 350f for 40 minutes or until it is bubbling around the side of the pan
demonstrations.review: This is our favorite "hash brown" potato casserole. I just made it for Memorial Day and it was a big hit. I've been making this for a couple of years now. I love the red onion in it.  I usually make half the casserole for 4-5 people and I kept putting a little more than half a can of soup in it because I felt like I was wasting the rest of the can. When I made the full recipe this time I put close to two full cans of soup plus an extra scoop of sour cream and it turned out really creamy and amazing. It's great leftover too!

target.recipe_text:
lemon pepper marinade

ive only ever tried this with chicken

1. combine all ingredients
2. cut chicken breast in cubes
3. marinate for at least 2 hours
4. place on skewers and bbq til done
5. serve with rice
target.review: Loved it!  I used about 1/4 pound of chicken filets with this, and they were tender and full of great flavor.  This ingredients list works very well together.  I could have added more chicken for the amount, but not much!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
braised cod with chickpeas

from "shabat shalom" by susan friedland, this is a typical moroccan-jewish dish.  it's great as a main course, or would serve 8 as a starter.  prep time does not include time for making dried chickpeas (if you choose to use them).

1. if using canned chickpeas , rinse and drain them
2. combine the cooked or canned chickpeas in a saucepan with the garlic , peppers , 3 tablespoons of olive oil , and 1 / 4 cup of water , bring to a simmer , cover , and simmer for 20 minutes
3. preheat oven to 400f
4. remove and discard the red peppers
5. add the cumin to the chickpeas and spread half the chickpea mixture in the bottom of a 9" square baking dish
6. place the fish on top , sprinkle with salt and pepper , cover the fish with the remaining chickpeas , drizzle the remaining olive oil over the top
7. cover the baking dish and bake for 30 minutes until the fish is just flaky but not falling apart
8. serve hot , garnished with sprigs of parsley or cilantro and lemon wedges
demonstrations.review: This is a really good, nicely flavored family dish.  The chickpeas soak in all the flavors and go soft. The cod I cooked took only 10 minutes to be fully done, so the spices don't overpower the cod flavor.  This is a dish that would be much appreciated by the young and the elderly because the texture is basically soft.  Something crunchy is needed as a side dish.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kentucky kocoa cocoa

recently purchased a bottle of creme de cacao and began looking for recipes that included this chocolate flavored liquor. since i am not much of a cocktail drinker, but love hot drinks this one really appealed to me. have not tried it yet but decided to share my find.

1. mix the heated cocoa , bourbon and creme de cacao together and pour into glass mugs or any vessel you would use for an irish whiskey
2. top each beverage with half the whipped cream
3. dust with a small amount of cocoa
4. serve
demonstrations.review: My hot cocoa was so chocolate rich, I could barely taste the bourbon!  This is an outstanding cocoa!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
asian summer pasta salad

this is an easy light supper or lunch pasta salad.  it's simple to add chicken, bacon or shrimp to make it a little heartier if you like.  thanks to jackie for submitting this to our new church cookbook.

1. when you cook the spaghetti , break it into thirds or fourths upon dropping it in the boiling water
2. mix cooked and cooled spaghetti and vegetables in a large bowl
3. set aside
4. in a small bowl mix the vegetable oil , rice vinegar , soy sauce , sugar , pepper , ginger root and garlic
5. whisk to combine
6. add dressing to pasta and vegetables
7. stir well to combine
8. chill in the refrigerator for at least an hour to combine flavors
9. garnish with chopped peanuts or cashews and cilantro
demonstrations.review: This is a great recipe, light but flavorful.  The next time I have leftover pasta, I will think of this recipe, and make it!

target.recipe_text:
mexican taco pinwheels

i had these at a party today and i couldn't quit eating them. i'm not a big fan of black olives or chilies but these were incredible. very popular with everyone. cook time is refrigeration time. (in response to reviews, i use old el paso taco mix and hidden valley ranch dressing mix and have never had any complaints about the saltiness. hth!)

1. mix all ingredients except tortillas
2. divide mixture evenly among tortillas , spread slightly and roll up
3. refrigerate 1-2 hours and cut into 1-inch slices
4. can be served with sour cream if desired
target.review: These were good!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pork and vegetable lo mein  easy and delicious

my family loves this hearty main dish. i get requests for it often. it's very quick and easy to prepare, great for when you're in a hurry. you can buy a couple of the ingredients already prepared in the produce section of the grocery store, if you like.

1. already shredded--a real time saver
2. heat 2 tbsp olive oil in a large skillet or wok
3. saut pork , onion , garlic and pepper flakes until meat is no longer pink
4. remove this mixture from pan and keep warm
5. add remaining tbsp of oil to pan and saut cabbage , bok choy or celery , carrots and peppers until crisp tender
6. add spaghetti to cooked veggies in the pan
7. stir in soy sauce and add pork mixture back to the pan
8. cook for 5 minutes or until heated through
demonstrations.review: Yummy, this was really good! I used beef instead, it tasted well! Thank you for sharing this recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cocoa mocha frosting

this is an easy, yet yummy chocolate frosting with just enough mocha taste that both my husband and i like it.  i love coffee, he hates it.  this makes enough frosting to cover the top of two 9 inch layers or one 9 x 13 inch cake.

1. combine sugar , salt and cocoa together
2. cream butter until soft
3. add part of sugar mixture gradually , beating throroughly
4. add remaining sugar mixture , alternately with warm coffee , beating well after each addition
5. add vanilla
demonstrations.review: It worked!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
baked caramel apple pudding

i am specifying baked in this pudding title as opposed to the creamy, soft set, chilled type. this old fashioned pudding is sticky, rich and oh so wonderful. a bit more dense than sticky date pudding with toffee sauce. but if you like date pudding then chances are you will like this too. this is also a self saucing pudding.

1. for pudding: combine flour , sugar , baking powder , cinnamon , salt , milk , and apples in a medium mixing bowl until well blended
2. preheat oven to 375f
3. spread in a greased 1 1 / 2 quart casserole or 1-9 inch square or round , greased , metal baking pan
4. for sauce: mix brown sugar , butter , and water
5. stir until butter is melted
6. pour sauce over pudding batter and bake for 40-50 minutes until brown and set
7. serve with ice cream , heavy whipped cream or let it stand on it's own
demonstrations.review: This was really sweet and really tasty! I think it could do a bit more apples. Thanks!

target.recipe_text:
so yummy baked potato salad

my deli carries a yummy baked potato salad. i asked them what was in it and they told me. i had some leftover baked potatoes that i needed to use so i tried making it and it was a big hit at my house. it disappeared before i got it to the dinner table...lol !

1. gently stir together all the ingredients in a large bowl using a large spoon , reserving a little cheddar , green onion and bacon for garnish
2. transfer to a serving dish
3. top with reserved shredded cheddar , green onion slices and bacon crumbles for a beautiful presentation
target.review: Fab! All my guests loved it! It certainly wasn't a potato salad they would expect!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
died   went to pimento cheese heaven  pimiento

a true southern delicacy! i didn't know i even liked pimento cheese! this stuff is addictive... so addictive i am having a lock installed on my refrigerator (not to keep me out - but in case the neighbors find out!). i have picked at pimento cheese spreads at parties and potlucks but never have the desire to make my own... and then i was asked if i would make a batch for a friend...this is a cross between her mom's recipe and my creativity. great on celery sticks, crackers, bread... even straight out of the bowl! even picky four year olds liked it!

1. using a hand held mixer , beat cream cheese until soft
2. add the remaining ingredients and beat until creamy and combined
3. cover and refrigerate for about an hour
demonstrations.review: People go crazy when I make this! LOL Delicious! Tastes great with crackers and pretzels.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
bison meat loaf  1  buffalo

whenever possible, i buy grass fed bison instead of ground beef. the flavor is much sweeter and because of the higher protein content, smaller portions are more satisfying. no antibiotics, no pesticides in the feed, no preservatives and no growth hormones. even better, less fat, cholesterol and calories plus more iron, protein and b-12 than ground beef! a richer flavor and completely healthy! i hope you enjoy this yummy recipe as much as we do.

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. mix all ingredients together in a large bowl
3. using your hands works best
4. spray a shallow , oval casserole dish or small roasting pan with pam
5. pat meat mixture into dish / pan
6. lightly spray top of loaf with pam
7. bake for 1-1 / 4 to 1-1 / 2 hours
8. can be served as is or with italian-style sauce
demonstrations.review: This was excellent! Very flavorful! I was pleasantly surprised :) I topped the meatloaf with marinara sauce after baking.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
whatever floats your boat  brownies

these are absolutely the chewiest, moistest, fudgiest brownies ever! i have tried adding so many different things to the batter, and they always comes out great.  they are also great without any add-ins! but by varying the add-ins, you can make different brownies every week (or day!!) super easy prep! so, add "whatever floats your boat" and you will not believe how yummy they come out :) oh, and the recipe doubles just fine--use a 9 x 13 inch pan instead and add a few more minutes of baking!

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. grease an 8 inch square pan or line with foil
3. in a medium bowl combine melted butter and cocoa and stir until cocoa is dissolved
4. add sugar and mix well
5. add eggs one at a time and stir until well combined
6. stir in vanilla , flour and salt until you no longer see any flour
7. fold in "whatever floats your boat" !
8. spread in pan and bake for approximately 25 minutes
9. do not over-bake -- your brownies will come out dry
10. adjust time / temp accordingly for your oven
11. if you do the knife / toothpick test , it should come out with moist crumbs , not clean
12. cool completely before cutting into squares
13. for vegetarian omit the marshmallows
14. for double recipe , bake in 9x12 pan and add 5 minutes to baking time
demonstrations.review: I doubled the recipe, using 3/4 cup mini semi-sweet chocolate chips and 3/4 cup M&M's. They were FANTASTIC! Very fudgy and done after 25 min. in my 9 X 13 metal pan. Got lots of compliments. Would make again :)

target.recipe_text:
cola burgers

different but has fabulous flavor.

1. combine the egg , 1 / 4 c
2. cola , crackers , 2 tbsp
3. dressing , cheese and salt
4. add the beef and mix well
5. shape into six patties
6. in a bowl , combine the remaining cola and dressing
7. grill patties , uncovered , for 3 min
8. a side
9. brush with cola mixture
10. grill 8-10 min
11. longer or until juices run clear basting and turning as needed
12. serve on buns
target.review: Must try

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cranberry pecan tarts

its different and its good. it came from a robinhood booklet.

1. preheat oven to 350
2. beat eggs lightly in mixing bowl
3. add sugar , syrup , melted butter and vanilla , mixing until blended
4. sprinkle cranberries and pecans in tart shells , dividing evenly
5. pour filling on top , filling two-thirds full
6. bake for 20 to 25 minutes or just until set and golden
7. ideal for freezing
demonstrations.review: Thank you Nora marie

demonstrations.recipe_text:
love em bars

my mom's recipe for basic bar cookies. this can be adapted very easily to many different flavors.

1. mix butter , water and eggs
2. add cake mix and powdered sugar and beat well
3. add any mix-ins desired
4. pour into greased 9x13 pan and bake at 350 for 30-35 minutes or until test done with toothpick
demonstrations.review: I certainly do

demonstrations.recipe_text:
easy banana muffins

nan

1. mash bananas , add sugar and the slightly beaten egg
2. stir in melted butter
3. stir in dry ingredients
4. spoon into medium size muffin pan
5. bake 20 minutes at 350f degrees - 375f degrees
demonstrations.review: Whenever the bananas look ripe

target.recipe_text:
dijon pork roast with cranberries  crock pot

new to slow cooking, i recently came across this recipe while perusing a cookbook from mom's collection.  though i have not tried this yet, i'm keeping it here safe for when the time comes.  i'm guessing that the honey mustard can be replaced with a combination of equal parts dijon mustard and honey.

1. combine the allspice , salt and pepper
2. rub over the surface of the roast
3. place roast in slow cooker
4. blend mustard , honey , orange zest , and onion flakes
5. pour over the roast
6. sprinkle cranberries on top
7. cook for 4 to 6 hours on low or 2 to 3 hours on high
8. pork should be fork tender but not falling apart
9. remove pork and allow to rest for 5 to 7 minutes
10. skim fat from the top of the sauce
11. slice meat and serve with sauce on top or allow diners to ladle on themselves
target.review: Delicious!! I used pork chops (cut up in chunks) instead of the roast, so it only took 2 hours on low in the slow cooker. I also substituted the orange rind with about 2 oz of orange juice. I served it with mashed potatoes and stuffing! Very easy! Turned out great! Will be making this again!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crispy baked chicken strips

these are delicious! and much more cost-effective than buying chicken nuggets. nice and juicy, yet crisp on the outside, too. yummy, yummy! for an italian twist, omit chili powder and substitute italian seasonings. makes two dinner servings, or 4 lunch/appetizer servings.

1. cut chicken breasts into thin strips , about one inch wide
2. longer sections can be cut in half to have uniform pieces
3. mix cracker crumbs and seasonings well
4. dip chicken pieces into egg mixture , then dredge in crumb mixture
5. place on baking sheet sprayed with cooking spray
6. bake at 375 degrees f , for 10-12 minutes , until crispy on outside and lightly browned
7. dip into favorite sauce , or enjoy just as they are !
demonstrations.review: Mmmm...delicious! So quick and easy and goes great with home-made french fries!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
apricot rosemary glazed pork loin

this takes only 10 minutes to prepare for the oven. it looks awesome when removed from the oven. the meat is very tender and the sauce provides a hint of orange and rosemary. the recipe is courtesy of betty crocker.

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. remove any excess fat from the roast
3. place roast in a 13x9-inch baking dish that has been sprayed with non-stick cooking spray
4. sprinkle with salt and pepper
5. in a small saucepan , heat the preserves , sherry , rosemary and garlic over medium heat , stirring frequently
6. when thickened , spoon 1 / 4 cup mixture onto pork reserving remainder
7. insert meat thermometer so
8. bake uncovered 1 hour 15 minutes to 1 hour 30 minutes or until the thermometer reads 155f
9. cover pork with foil and allow to stand 15 to 20 minutes or until thermometer reads 160f
10. cut roast into slices
11. heat the reserved apricot mixture and serve with roast
demonstrations.review: Delicious!! I used the apple juice, added a little more rosemary, more pepper, and less salt. It turned out fantastic! The hardest part was waiting the hour for the pork to cook while smelling that fantastic aroma through the apartment!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
honey curried chicken

this is a deliciously sweet and spicy chicken recipe.  you can easily make this recipe spicier by adding more ginger to suit your taste.

1. in a well greased / buttered baking dish , arrange the chicken skin side down
2. in a bowl combine all other ingredients and stir until smooth
3. pour over chicken and refrigerate 1 hour
4. drain and reserve excess sauce
5. bake chicken , uncovered in a preheated 375 degree oven for 20 minutes
6. baste periodically with remaining sauce
7. turn chicken over and baste with remaining sauce
8. bake chicken another 20 to 30 minutes or until tender and no pink remains
9. basting periodically
10. serve along side your favorite basmati rice recipe and enjoy !
demonstrations.review: Delightfully sweeter than what I had expected. I didn't add the hot pepper sauce or the ginger (none on hand), but it still turned out great!

target.recipe_text:
marinated tofu for meat eaters who hate tofu

this is the tofu recipe that opens everyone's closed minds about this much maligned ingredient. the texture of the tofu was described as "similar to chicken and fish but not." i came up with it after many (failed) attempts at creating the perfect meatlover's tofu dish. the key is in the freezing of the tofu, so make sure you plan ahead. prep time does not include freezing time.

1. place the tofu into the freezer for at least 24 hours
2. keeping it in there longer doesn't hurt it
3. remove the tofu from the freezer and defrost by bringing a pot of water to a boil and placing the frozen block of tofu in the pot for 10 minutes or until defrosted
4. remove the tofu from the packaging and cut the block laterally in half so you have two block-sized slabs that are half the width
5. slice each slab lengthwise into three and place on a clean dish towel or paper towels
6. cover the six pieces with another dish towel and place a cutting board or baking tray or other flat object on top
7. place heavy cans or books onto the board and let sit for 15-30 minutes
8. cut the tofu lengths into cubes and place into marinade for a minimum of 30 minutes
9. remove from the marinade and dust the tofu cubes with flour
10. heat the oil in a frying pan over medium heat
11. shallow fry the cubes until all sides are golden brown and crispy
12. serve hot with rice or couscous and a puddle of the marinade as a dipping sauce
target.review: I cannot believe how much it tastes like chicken/fish.  I used chicken-type seasonings, and it's so much like chicken it almost made me sick.  My non-veggie husband devoured it, and we both agree we'll be making it again!  Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
tofu nut balls

this recipe is adapted from a cookbook called vegetarian creations. it is a big hit with meat eaters and vegetarians alike! even kids love it. a great substitute for meatballs and they even look like meatballs.

1. place oats and pecans in a blender or food processor and process until finely ground
2. remove to a large bowl
3. add garlic , sage , oregano , salt , pepper , and lemon juice to bowl
4. process tofu and water in blender until smooth
5. add to bowl with other ingredients and stir until mixture holds firmly together
6. shape into 1
7. 5 inch balls
8. heat a little bit of olive oil in a non-stick skillet and skillet fry balls until reaching the desired level of brownness on all sides
9. adding more oil if needed
10. remove to brown bags or newspaper covered paper towels
11. place in a baking sheet and bake at 350 for 30 minutes or until done in the middle
12. i sometimes skip this step and just flatten the balls slightly , so they will cook well on top of the stove
13. yields about 16 balls
14. serve over pasta cooked just al dente with some nice tomato sauce or as an appetizer
demonstrations.review: I have to write fast because my non-vegetarian husband is scarfing these before I can get to them! Instead of sage, oregano, & lemon, I used onion powder, italian seasoning, and a liberal sprinkling of a Grill Mates chipotle pepper marinade packet. It added some smokiness to the mix which I liked. I will be using this again! Thanks, P_S!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
turkey tenderloins with spiced cranberry sauce

a tasty option to the whole bird. tenderloins or fillets are the feather-shaped part of the breast. this recipe featuring tenderloins serves four to six people, depending on the size of the tenderloins. the recipe can easily be doubled for a larger crowd.

1. brown tenderloins in butter in skillet
2. lower heat to simmer and cover
3. cook about 20 minutes until meat juices run clear
4. remove tenderloins and keep warm
5. pour off excess drippings
6. add cranberry sauce , cloves and sugar to skillet
7. heat over low heat
8. add orange pieces
9. spoon sauce over tenderloins to serve or spoon some sauce onto serving plate and top with sliced tenderloins
10. garnish with orange twists if desired
11. serve with wild or brown rice
12. enjoy
demonstrations.review: Made this yesterday and hubby, who is very picky about sauces, liked it.  I was out of clove so I substituted with ginger and it was still great.  I made the sauce seperately so that I could use any excess for vegetarian dishes.  I've been using it on burgers with teriyaki sauce and it's great!  I'm hoping to use it again this holiday season, and maybe earlier!  Thanks, Little Elf!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cheap vegetarian tuna salad

many other vegetarian tuna salad uses tofu or other relatively expensive ingredients, but not this one!  just a can of chickpeas and a couple other ingredients you probably already have in the fridge.  it has a pretty realistic texture - add whatever you like, and would normally put in tuna salad.  the ingredient measurements are approximate - i have never actually measured how much to put in, just eyeballed it.  please put in as much or little as you want, or whatever you want.

1. mash the chickpeas or great northern beans with a potato masher or fork
2. please post suggestions if you have a good way to speed this up
3. combine other ingredients and mix
4. chill if desired
demonstrations.review: I was curious so I went out and picked up the ingredients.  I'm pleseantly surprised!  It's not tuna fish but it makes a good sandwich.

target.recipe_text:
dutch apple bread

the crumb topping on this bread makes it extra special. it's an old taste of home recipe.

1. preheat oven to 350
2. grease a 9x5x3" loaf pan
3. in a mixing bowl , cream butter and sugar
4. beat in eggs and vanilla
5. combine flour , baking soda and salt , and stir into the creamed mixture alternately with the buttermilk
6. fold in apple and nuts
7. pour into prepared pan and sprinkle topping evenly over the bread
8. bake for 55 to 60 minutes , or until knife inserted into bread comes out clean
9. cool in pan for 10 minutes before removing to a wire rack to cool completely
10. topping:
11. combine the flour , sugar , brown sugar and cinnamon well
12. cut in butter until the mixture is crumbly
target.review: My husband liked this a lot more than I did. So, I know I'll be making it again, especially in Autumn. For me, there wasn't enough flavor in the bread itself, so next time I'll add some cinnamon and sugar to the batter. I used one gala apple and it worked well. We both liked the topping and was excited at how delicious the house smelled after baking the bread.  Thanks for posting, I put this in my favorites for another chilly day.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
shrimp   clam chowder

this is a very rich, great tasting chowder. perfect for fall and winter, or if your in the mood for some comfort food. note: i've only used smoked paprika in this dish, not sure how regular paprika will taste, (if you decide to include it) it is optional...**this recipe has been updated, thank you to my reviewers :d

1. boil potatoes in separate pot about 10 minutes , drain , and set aside
2. in a large pot melt butter on medium heat
3. add onion and garlic , do not brown and cook until onion is iridescent
4. slowly stir in flour & half and half
5. add mushrooms , potatoes , white wine , and milk or water
6. drain the clam juice into the pot and set clams to the side
7. add paprika , bay leaf , salt & pepper
8. simmer for 10 minutes
9. add clams & shrimp and continue to simmer for another 8 - 10 minutes
10. add parsley right before serving
11. and -- your done !
demonstrations.review: My husband prepared this chowder exactly as posted and it was delicious! He added hot sauce to his bowl and enjoyed it that way. Can't wait to have it again; thanks for posting a fabulous recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
ground beef gravy

toh

1. in a large skillet , cook beef until browned
2. drain
3. add 1 1 / 2 c
4. beef broth then add onion , parsley , basil , garlic powder , seasoned salt , and pepper
5. simmer , uncovered , for 5-10 minutes or until onion is tender
6. in a small bowl , combine the cornstarch and remaining broth until smooth
7. stir into beef mixture
8. bring to a boil
9. cook and stir for 2 minutes or until thickened
10. serve over mashed potatoes or pasta
demonstrations.review: Nice and easy...

demonstrations.recipe_text:
spicy thai scallops with lime   chili

do you like scallops?  do you like limes and chilies, well this is the dish for you.  it is so flavorful and delicious, that you won't believe how easy it is to make.

1. wash and pat dry your scallops
2. slice each scallop in half horizontally
3. heat the butter and oil in a pan and add the garlic and ginger and fry for 1 minute
4. next add the scallions and fry for 1 minute , you do not want to brown
5. now add the scallops and fry over high heat for 5 minutes , stir in the lime rind , chili , lime juice and sugar and cook for another minute
6. serve the scallops over the rice
7. add the pan juices and garnish with the lime wedges
demonstrations.review:
An exceptional receipe, I knew it would be, when I read the ingredients. 
Prepared as shown, except for the chili pepper (my store didnt have any, so I substituted with a bit of red pepper flakes from my spice rack). Also did not use the brown sugar option. 
I bet it would be great with shrimp, if the scallops werent available. 
Spend the few extra pennies for the jasmine rice, its worth the investment.
This is going into my favorites file, and we will be making this again, again and again.
Easy to prepare, took about 30 minutes. Thank you SoOO much, Baby Kato!!!

target.recipe_text:
andrea s oatmeal raisin cookies

i love oatmeal raisin cookies, but they have to be homemade. this is the way i make them.

1. heat oven to 350 degrees
2. mix brown sugar , lard , milk , and vanilla
3. stir in remaining ingredients
4. drop the dough by tablespoons onto ungreased cookie sheet
5. bake 15 minutes
6. immediately remove from cookie sheet and cool
target.review: don't change a thing in this recipe....just fantastic

demonstrations.recipe_text:
balsamic chicken for crock pot

i got a similar recipe of this a long time ago, got bored with it back then, and changed some ingredients. my husband and daughter get so excited when we're gonna have this for dinner. i don't measure some things, so if you need me to explain further, let me know. the liquid is so good that i keep sipping it! ha!

1. put the first 7 ingredients in a crock pot and cook for 4-5 hours on low
2. cook the rice or pasta separately
3. when chicken is done , remove the bones and skin and throw them away
4. put either rice or pasta in a bowl and then ladle the balsamic chicken on top with some of the liquid from the crock pot
demonstrations.review: when I cook this...they come running..great dish never any left overs

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chive dumplings

these are the dumplings i use for my recipe #248713.

1. cut the shortening into the flour , baking powder and salt until mixture looks like fine crumbs
2. stir in milk and chives
3. drop onto hot chicken
4. cook uncovered 10 minutes , then covered 20 minutes
demonstrations.review: have with a beef stew and you've got a complete meal very good daved it to my favorites

demonstrations.recipe_text:
joe s chili

my best friend's husband made this up. i only had it once, but i loved it!

1. put cut-up chuck roast in dutch oven with oil , salt , and pepper
2. brown meat
3. add everything else
4. simmer for 2-3 hours on low
5. keep checking it often to stir
demonstrations.review: great to have on a cold winters day warm you to your toes

target.recipe_text:
crock pot bbq pork sandwiches

this is so easy and the kids love it. the meal makes itsself.

1. pour whole bottle of bbq in crock pot
2. add pork , salt and pepper
3. put your lid on and cook on low for 6 hours
4. the meat will start to shred
5. when it does , i flip it on high heat and cook it another 1 / 2 hour until all is shredded
6. add to hamburger bun / rolls
target.review: Quick, easy, and good!  Who could ask for anything more?  We used Cajun Spicy barbecue sauce to give it a little extra kick!  This one was so easy even my hubby could handle it!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chicken garlic bites

simple and fun to make, great to eat! prep time includes marinating the chicken.  use matzo meal instead of the breadcrumbs and this is good for passover as well.

1. place chicken in shallow dish
2. in small bowl , mix olive oil , garlic , and black pepper
3. pour over chicken
4. cover and marinate 30 minutes
5. drain
6. preheat oven to 475f
7. mix bread crumbs and cayenne
8. coat chicken
9. arrange in a single layer on cookie sheet
10. bake 10 minutes or until brown
demonstrations.review: I've served this w/ a honey mustard dipping sauce.... terrific compliment.  I also marinated it all day and it tastes great.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
tuna melt on english muffins for 2

fantastic lunch, even dinner with a bowl of soup.

1. preheat broiler
2. combine first 7 ingredients in a medium bowl
3. divide evenly among muffin halves , sprinkle with cheese
4. place on a baking sheet , broil 4 minutes or until golden
demonstrations.review: My hubby loved it, and Oh so simple!  Great for a busy Saturday afternoon lunch! We didn't have artichoke hearts on hand but the melts were perfectly fine.  Also, great idea for work... mix ahead and simply throw in the toaster/broiler at work.  Better than ham and cheese!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
french toast sticks   oamc

i got this basic recipe from another site but changed it a little for my family.  the original recipe called for orange juice as the liquid instead of milk.  i also added the vanilla as we think it gives it a nice flavor.

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees fahrenheit
2. cut each slice of bread into 3 pieces to make sticks
3. texas toast is a very thick sliced bread about 3 / 4" thick
4. you could substitute french bread if texas toast is not available
5. in a bowl , mix together melted butter , eggs , sugar , cinnamon , vanilla and milk
6. beat well
7. dip sticks into egg mixture and place on a cookie sheet that has been sprayed with cooking spray
8. if there is any dip left , you can drizzle it over the sticks
9. bake for 25 minutes on middle rack of oven
10. turn halfway through baking time
11. allow to cool
12. flash freeze on cookie sheet , remove and place in a ziploc bag
13. to reheat: place 3 sticks on a microwave-safe plate and heat on high for 1 minute until warm
14. serve with syrup
demonstrations.review: I used leftovers from a loaf of bread I made for dinner the night before from my bread maker (it's never quite as good the next day!)  This was the perfect solution for the unused bread.   I let the bread get a little stale and then let it soak a little longer in the liquid.  Fantastic!  My 4 year old loved it!  As she said, it was "just like the restaurant!"  Froze a bunch for those mornings we're rushing out the door for preschool.  Thanks!

target.recipe_text:
coffee and sour cream cake

this is a nice cake which is quick and easy to make. great with afternoon tea or a cuppa.

1. cream butter and sugar , add egg , mix
2. add coffee , mix
3. add milk and flour alternately
4. add sour cream
5. bake 25 minutes 350
target.review:
Are you sure you used self raising flour??
The cake doesnt rise very much, although this doesnt matter because the texture is what you are looking for, not how high it rises.  I got this recipe in my food tech. class at school, so it is a very basic cake.  In my opinion, i didnt see anytihng wrong with the cake, and i felt that the texture was fine,- so the lack of rising didnt matter..  we used a ring cake tin, if that helps.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
sour cream chocolate cookies

from a toh special edition--i haven't tried them yet, but they look delicious!

1. in a mixing bowl , cream butter with sugars
2. beat in egg , sour cream and vanilla
3. combine dry ingredients in separate bowl and gradually add to the creamed mixture
4. stir in chips
5. drop by rounded tablespoons 2 inches apart onto greased baking sheets
6. bake at 350 for 12-15 minutes , or until set
7. cool for 2 minutes on pan before removing to wire racks
demonstrations.review: Very good! Very smooth tasting biscuit. Soft, but not too chewy. I wouldn't call these 'cakey' either. I'll definately make these again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
buttermilk chocolate bread

tender slices of chocolaty quick bread will satisfy your cravings!

1. heat oven to 350
2. grease bottom only of 8x4 or 9x5-inch loaf pan
3. in a large bowl , combine sugar and margarine
4. blend well
5. add eggs
6. blend well
7. stir in buttermilk
8. add flour , cocoa , baking powder , baking soda and salt
9. stir just until dry ingredients are moistened
10. stir in nuts
11. pour into greased pan
12. bake at 350 for 55 to 65 minutes or until toothpick inserted in center comes out clean
13. cool 15 minutes
14. remove from pan
15. cool completely
16. wrap tightly and store in refrigerator
17. yield: 1 loaf
demonstrations.review: Very nice.  Has a great consistnacy, and not too sweet.  I enjoyed th 'bread' feel, instead of a cake.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cappuccino crinkles

a double rolling in granulated sugar makes these crackled cookies extra sparkly. from bh&g

1. heat oven to 350 degrees f
2. beat butter in a large mixing bowl with an electric mixer on medium to high speed for 30 seconds
3. add the brown sugar , cocoa powder , coffee granules , baking soda , and cinnamon
4. beat until combined , scraping sides of the bowl occasionally
5. beat in egg whites and yogurt until combined
6. beat in as much of the flour as you can with the mixer
7. stir in remaining flour with a wooden spoon
8. place granulated sugar in a small bowl
9. drop dough by heaping teaspoons into sugar and roll into balls
10. roll again in sugar
11. place balls 2 inches apart on an ungreased cookie sheet
12. bake for 8 to 10 minutes or until edges are firm
13. transfer cookies to wire racks and cool
demonstrations.review: I expected these cookies to be crunchy, but they turned out soft and cake-y.

target.recipe_text:
deluxe potato ham bake

this is an excellent pot luck dish! it was served at our church dinners and was always a big hit!

1. in a large bowl , combine first 5 ingredients
2. mix well
3. stir in ham and potatoes
4. spread in greased 9x13x2 baking dish
5. combine topping ingredients and sprinkle over casserole
6. bake uncovered at 350 for 1 hour or until potatoes are tender
target.review: This was very good.  I didn't know what to have for supper, so I made this with leftover ham.  Very good!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
potato casserole with corn flakes

this is a recipe that my grandma made at all our family dinners. i can't eat it and not think of her! it is yummy and everyone can't help but love the taste!

1. combine potatoes , melted butter , salt and pepper
2. add onion , soup , sour cream and cheese
3. mix well
4. put in 9x13-inch casserole dish
5. top with topping mixture
6. bake at 350 for 45 minutes
demonstrations.review: I just made this for the 2nd time last night.  Both times I have had company over for supper.  Everyone loves it.   The 1st time, I tripled the recipe (I had 17 people over)- last night I made 1 pan (7 people).  The only thing I did different was to cook about 30 min. longer. Very good!  Thanks for sharing!  I will definatly be making again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
easy snickers bar pie

this recipe is so easy. make it to take to a potluck and keep one at home for yourself! the cook time mentioned is the chill time in the fridge

1. in a large mixing bowl , beat cream cheese , sugar and peanut butter until creamy
2. stir in chopped candy bars
3. gently fold in the cool whip just until mixed
4. pour into crusts and refrigerate overnight
demonstrations.review: Excellent- made for a potluck at work-kept one at home-everyone loved!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
apple sausage stuffing for turkey

i found this recipe in an old homemaker's magazine. i made it for a thanksgiving dinner a few years ago, and now whenever it's my turn to cook a holiday meal, i have to make this! it's easy and delicious. i prefer making the stuffing as a side dish, rather than stuffing the turkey, so the turkey cooks quicker and it makes less of a mess.

1. cook sausage until no longer pink , about 10 min , stir often
2. drain most of the fat
3. add onions and celery , cook another 3 minute
4. stir in apples , sage , thyme , and marjoram , cook another 5 minutes
5. add 1 cup of chicken stock , and bring to a boil
6. remove from heat , stir in bread , parsley , salt and pepper
7. spoon into a lightly greased casserole dish
8. bake , covered , in 325f oven for about 40 minutes
9. halfway through cooking time , drizzle with the remaining chicken stock
10. remove the lid and bake 10 more minutes , until the stuffing has a crusty top and is heated through
demonstrations.review:
Fantastic!
I made this for Thanksgiving this year.  Everyone loved it.  This is definatly a keeper!

target.recipe_text:
popcorn balls

i made these for a valentine's day bake sale and they were the first to go! the recipe was given to me by a friend.

1. bring to boil butter , sugar , syrup
2. add condensed milk- boil 5 minute
3. remove from heat and add vanilla
4. strain seeds from popcorn
5. pour hot mixture over popcorn and mix
6. grease hands and make balls out of mixture
7. extra
8. to remove the seeds , i usually take two bowls and lift out the popcorn by the hand fulls and shaking it , then dumping it into the extra bowl
9. when i get to the bottom , there lies most of the seeds
10. i just discard them and go on with the rest
11. hope you can visualize that and that it helps !
target.review: Great recipe. Fun and easy to make with kids, great flavor and they stick together really well. The kids loved them. Thanks for sharing!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chicken pot pie with 2 crusts

this is old-fashioned, from scratch, comfort food. this has been a family favorite for years. i like to take this to other families when they are in need of a meal. it's always a winner. i like making it with leftover turkey, too! i often add some cooked diced potatoes.

1. heat butter over low heat until melted
2. blend in flour , onion , salt and pepper
3. cook over low heat , stirring constantly until smooth and bubbly
4. remove from heat
5. stir in broth and milk
6. heat to boiling
7. stirring constantly
8. boil and stir one minute
9. stir in chicken and veggies
10. reserve
11. line pie plate with prepared bottom crust
12. pour in filling
13. top with top crust
14. cut slits in center to vent
15. flute edges
16. cook uncovered in 425f oven until crust is brown
17. approximately 30-35 minutes
demonstrations.review: Made with homemade crust. Very good and will make again. Thanks for sharing!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s fried egg sandwich

i've have been making this for years, it's still a family favorite! adjust all ingredients to taste.

1. in a skillet melt the butter over medium heat
2. crack the eggs and add to the pan and cook to desired doneness
3. just before the eggs are cooked place one slice of cheese over each egg
4. after the cheese has melted place each egg on a toasted piece of bread then sprinkle with salt and black pepper
5. spread the mayo and ketchup on the remaining slices of bread and cover the eggs with the bread slices
6. serve warm
demonstrations.review: Great to make on a busy morning when I don't have much time. I also like to butter the bread right after I toast it and then top with mayo. Thanks for sharing!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
starbucks mocha frappuccino

a friend of mine told me this was the actual recipe used by starbucks.  i do not believe him, but it does taste surprisingly similar.  i have quadrupled the recipe as i like to make it in advance and keep it in the fridge to surprise guests.  note: if you make it in advance, do not store it any longer than you would milk.

1. make coffee , follow directions for your favorite brand of espresso roast coffee
2. mix coffee , still hot , and sugar in your mixer until sugar is dissolved
3. add milk and chocolate syrup and continue mixing , about one minute
4. pour mix into a sealable container for easy storage
5. store in fridge until ready to use
6. to make drink , combine equal parts mix and ice in a blender and blend on high until smooth
7. pour into glasses
8. top each glass with whipped cream and drizzle with chocolate syrup
9. serve
demonstrations.review: Delicious!!!! Thanks for sharing!

target.recipe_text:
breakfast bagel sandwiches  oamc

while searching for a great make ahead breakfast i tried this and it worked great! hope you enjoy it too :)

1. slice each bagel in half
2. lightly butter each side
3. to cook eggs , lightly grease a mug or small bowl or ramekin
4. beat eggs in that bowl and microwave 30 seconds
5. remove egg in one piece and repeat for remaining eggs
6. or take swan valley tammi's idea and pre-cook the bacon , chop it up and add it to the eggs
7. pour into greased muffin tins
8. bake at 400 degrees fahrenheit for 12 minutes so all 12 egg / bacon 'patties' are done at the same time
9. on the bottom half of the bagel place cooked egg
10. top each egg with approximately 1 tablespoon grated cheese
11. stack bacon on top
12. complete sandwich with top of bagel
13. cool slightly
14. wrap in plastic wrap individually
15. place in a large labeled zipper freezer bag
16. to serve , remove 1 bagel sandwich from bag and remove wrapping
17. place upside down in microwave and heat for 30 seconds
18. place right side up and microwave for 30 seconds more or until heated through
19. time may vary in your microwave
20. eat warm
target.review: If the eggs were easier to cook, this would easily be a 5 star recipe! I didn't want to cook each egg separately, so I tried the muffin pan trick. The other reviewers aren't kidding - the eggs REALLY stuck to my muffin pan. All the scrubbing in the world wouldn't get them out, so I had to replace my muffin tin. I'd love to make these again, I'm not sure I will because of all the trouble to cook the eggs.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s 5 minute cinnamon flop brunch cake

except for the the milk and small amount in the egg, the cake itself has very little fat and using low-fat milk will keep the fat to a minimum, i have stated the egg as optional, i strongly suggest to add it in for a more cake-like texture --  if you are looking for a fancy cake to serve then this is not it however for the ease of this cake it is darn good and makes a great weekend brunch cake, it's like a combination of a cake and cinnamon bun all in one,  ridiculously simple to make as it's all mixed by hand and takes like 5 minutes to throw together, try adding in some chopped strawberries, apples or blueberries, raisins or dried cranberries, this recipe is a blank canvas, so go ahead and add in fruit, nuts chocolate chips whatever you wish, and to kick this up a notch drizzle recipe#120835 on top :) --- servings are only estimated

1. set oven to 350 degrees f
2. prepare a greased 13 x 9-inch baking dish , or two 8 or 9-inch round cake pans
3. in a bowl mix the 2 cups flour , 1-1 / 4 cups white sugar , milk , vanilla or almond extract , baking powder , pinch of salt and egg until just combined careful not to overmix
4. pour into prepared baking pan / s
5. generously spread brown sugar and cinnamon on top
6. if desired sprinkle chopped walnuts or pecans over top
7. drizzle melted butter over top
8. bake for about 20-25 minutes for 8 or 9-inch round cake pan , and about 30 minutes for a 13 x 9-inch pan
demonstrations.review:
This recipe doesn't need a another great review, but I had to review away! 

I agree with one other reviewer though - when using the 13 x 9 baking pan, it does need to cook closer 30 - 35 minutes.

Thanks for another great recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mama s supper club tilapia parmesan

you asked for it. here it is. thanks so much to mama's supper club. wish we could all go there.

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees
2. in buttered 13-by-9-inch baking dish or jellyroll pan , lay fillets in single layer
3. do not stack fillets
4. brush top with juice
5. in bowl combine cheese , butter , mayonnaise , onions and seasonings
6. mix well with fork
7. bake fish in preheated oven 10 to 20 minutes or until fish just starts to flake
8. spread with cheese mixture and bake until golden brown , about 5 minutes
9. baking time will depend on the thickness of the fish you use
10. watch fish closely so that it does not overcook
11. makes 4 servings
12. broil 3 to 4 minutes or until almost done
13. add cheese and broil another 2 to 3 minutes or until browned
14. thank you mama's supper club in wisconsin
demonstrations.review: Really great recipe! So easy too! Used more of the topping than suggested, and broiled for the last minute to brown the cheese. Sprinkled a little Old Bay on top for color. Big, big hit!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
bacon and potato frittata

feel free to add any ingredients you have on hand. recipe is from woman's world.

1. place bacon in 10-inch nonstick skillet over medium-high heat
2. cook , stirring occasionally , until browned , 5 minutes
3. add potatoes and onion
4. cover
5. cook , stirring occasionally , until tender , 6-7 minutes
6. beat eggs , 1 / 2 cup water , 1 / 2 t salt and 1 / 4 t pepper
7. stir in broccoli and 1 / 2 cup cheese
8. add to skillet , cover
9. over medium heat , cook until set , 8-10 minutes
10. remove from heat
11. sprinkle with remaining cheese
12. cover
13. let stand until cheese is melted , 2-3 minutes
demonstrations.review:
Thank you SO much for this recipe! It's now on my meal plan at least every other week. To make it a heartier dinner, I reduced the broccoli to slightly under 1 cup and added 1 cup diced ham. I've used a mixture of cheese - depending on what I have on hand. My family said I can make this anytime! 

Also - I've found it reheats very well. Microwave a slice for 20-30 seconds and finish in the toaster oven.

Making this for more people was easy too: To increase for a 12" pan, increase by 2 eggs and add an extra 1/4 of everything else. Cooking takes slightly longer.

target.recipe_text:
to die for crock pot roast

amazing flavor, and so simple! no salt needed here. in fact, you may wish to use half the ranch dressing mix to cut back on the saltiness. found this crock-pot pot roast recipe on of a website called www.recipegoldmine.com. it's all the rage there, so i thought i'd try it.

1. place beef roast in crock pot
2. mix the dried mixes together in a bowl and sprinkle over the roast
3. pour the water around the roast
4. cook on low for 7-9 hours
5. use onion soup mix instead of ranch
6. add one cup , of red wine
7. add potatoes , carrots , mushrooms , celery and onion 2-3 hours before end
target.review: I've made this several times and actually never found it too salty when I used all the seasoning packets. I use baby carrots, little red potatoes, pearl onions, and a 4-5 lb roast and never had a problem with saltiness. To each their own, but I think using all those veggies compensates for the extra salt. Make this with a loaf of crusty bread, and it's the perfect cool weather meal. Love this recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
gingersnaps  soft   chewy

i found this recipe in a old church fundraising book.  it's been a while since i've made them.  submitting for zwt3.

1. cream shortening and sugar
2. add molasses and egg
3. stir in sifted , flour , salt and baking soda
4. then cinnamon , cloves , and ginger
5. dough will be soft and sticky
6. roll , into walnut-sized balls and roll in granulated sugar
7. place on greased cookie sheet and bake at 350f for 7 to 8 minutes
8. cookie will flatten out while baking
demonstrations.review: Delicious! This is very similar to an old family recipe. The only thing I changed is the baking temperature and time. 375 degrees for 9 minutes baked these to my personal preference.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
enchilada sauce

this is a very easy, quick enchilada sauce to use instead of the canned variety. we prefer to eat freshly made foods without alot of preservatives. this has a wonderful flavor.

1. heat the oil in a large saucepan over medium heat
2. add the garlic and saute for 1 to 2 minutes
3. add onion , oregano , chili powder , basil , ground black pepper , salt , cumin , parsley , salsa and tomato sauce
4. mix together and then stir in the water
5. bring to a boil , reduce heat to low and simmer for 15 to 20 minutes
6. use in place of canned enchilada sauce
demonstrations.review: Very good flavor. I had two complaints about this recipe. The first, was that it was too watery. Next time I will definitely take the advice of the reviewer who mentioned adding water gradually until you reach a desired consistency. My other complaint, also mentioned by other reviewers, is that this recipe doesn't make enough sauce for my personal needs. I like a decent amount of sauce with my enchiladas, and this was barely enough to coat every tortilla with not much left to pour over top. That being said, I really loved the taste of this! I added a teaspoon of crushed red pepper and it was perfect!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
ground beef stuffed green bell peppers with cheese

we had these not too long ago and we both decided that they needed a little more seasoning. we put a little hot pepper sauce on them and they were much better. i would probably include 2 teaspoons in the meat mix the next time that i make them.

1. cut off the tops of green peppers
2. discard seeds and membranes
3. chop enough of the tops to make 1 / 4 cup , set aside
4. cook the whole green peppers , uncovered in boiling water for about 5 minutes
5. invert to drain well
6. sprinkle insides of the peppers lightly with salt
7. in a skillet cook ground beef , onion and 1 / 4 cup chopped pepper till meat is browned and vegetables are tender
8. drain off excess fat
9. add drained tomatoes , salt , worcestershire , and a dash of pepper
10. in a separate pot put water bring to boil add rice cook until rice is soft
11. if needed add more water
12. add rice to beef mixture
13. stir in cheese
14. stuff peppers with meat mixture
15. place in a 10x6x2 baking dish
16. bake , covered in a 350 degree oven for 30 minutes
17. in the last 5 minutes add any remaining cheese to the top of the peppers
demonstrations.review: Excellent base recipe! I did find the filling to be a tad bland, so I followed a few of another reviewers suggestions and added garlic salt, onion powder, and more Worcester. I also used a can of hot rotel in place of the tomatoes and it provided plenty of kick. I had to keep adding water as the rice absorbed it to keep it from sticking to the pan and to let it cook completely. I also used red bell peppers rather than green. They're just a slight bit sweet, which goes great with the spicy filling. Great base recipe to build on.

target.recipe_text:
cheap beef in potato nests

here is an inexpensive quick supper! when we were kids my mom used to serve the tomato soup version of this recipe...we called it sos and would make 

1. place potatoes in a med
2. sauce pan with just enough water to cover
3. simmer until tender
4. heat oil in fry pan
5. saute onion and pepper in oil
6. add ground beef and brown well
7. add tomato soup to meat mixture
8. heat through
9. drain , mash potatoes
10. add enough milk to moisten and mash again
11. season to taste
12. divide potatoes equally onto four serving plates
13. make an indentation in the middle of each mound
14. fill with beef mixture
15. top with green chopped green onion and a sprinkle of cheddar cheese
target.review: Good dish, easy to make.  I wasn't, however, able to make the ten minute prep/ten minute cook times.  It was more like an hour prep & 40 minutes cooking.  Of course, I'm not any great shakes at being a cook so I know I am slower than most people.  I used the tomato soup version.  OK, but not 'aggressive' enough for me.  I'll use the barbecue sauce next time or maybe a combination of the two.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pronto pups aka corn dogs

these are also known as corn dogs, but our school and church term for them are pronto pups. my family loves these friday nights, i can never seem to make enough for the kids!

1. combine cornmeal , flour , baking powder , salt , egg and sugar
2. add milk until batter has a pancake type consistency
3. dry off hot dogs with paper towels , coat with flour , and skewer through the center of the corndog
4. heat 2" deep oil to 370 degrees f
5. dip skewered hot dogs into batter mix and coat evenly
6. fry until golden brown about 2 1 / 2 minutes
7. let cool and drain on a paper towel
8. with left over batter drop like dumplings into the oil until golden brown and drain
9. serve with ketchup , mustard tarter sauce or a dressing of your choosing
demonstrations.review: We have a mess of grandkids and this is a perfect recipe for even the picky eaters.  Easy to make and fun.  A great recipe if you're looking for that 'carnival' atmosphere. A solid addition to my cookbook.  Thanks, ShannonBecker

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mexican hamburgers

here is a good recipe for hamburgers:

1. mix ground beef , taco seasoning mix , green chilies , finely chopped onion
2. shape into patties and grill
3. serve with salsa
demonstrations.review: Basic, easy, flavorful recipe.  We made it the first time doing as the recipe called for and found it good but the chilis were a little overwhelming for us.  Tried it again a few days later adding another half pound hamburger to the recipe and were much more pleased.  Will definitely do this one again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
15 minute garlic lemon chicken

so quick and so good.

1. flatten chicken slightly
2. dust with flour
3. salt and pepper chicken
4. fry in hot oil 5 minutes each side
5. remove chicken from pan
6. to pan add broth , garlic , lemon juice and butter
7. cook 2 minutes
8. pour over chicken
demonstrations.review: Great recipe, Inez! Totally easy but with great flavor. I made this with Mirj's Creamy Crockpot Potatoes and Miss Annie's Thai Zucchini and the three dishes went together perfectly. I did find it took me longer to cook it than the recipe called for but that just ensured a beautiful golden color to the chicken. I might try this with thighs next time but, thighs or breasts, there will be a next time and a next time and....

target.recipe_text:
tsr version of ihop buttermilk pancakes by todd wilbur

from www.topsecretrecipes.com. these are my favorite pancakes...so light and fluffy.

1. preheat a skillet over medium heat
2. mix all of the ingredients til combined
3. melt a little bit of butter in the pan
4. pour the batter by spoonfuls into the hot pan , forming 5-inch circles
5. when the edges appear to harden , flip the pancakes
6. they should be golden brown
7. cook the pancakes on the other side until they are also golden brown
8. enjoy
target.review: These are the best pancakes... they are really really light. They have little air holes in them. I didn't have buttermilk so I made my own. 1 TBS white vinegar to one cup of milk and let set for 5 minutes. This will be my go to pancake recipe

demonstrations.recipe_text:
asian sauteed spinach

spinach sauteed with asian flavors

1. heat vegetable oil and sesame oil in a large pan
2. add garlic and cook briefly
3. add spinach and cook until the spinach is mostly wilted
4. add soy sauce to taste and continue cooking just until the spinach has all wilted
5. serve immediately
demonstrations.review: Simple and tasty. I made this to go with Ahi Tuna with wasabi butter and avocado.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
p  f  chang s chicken lettuce wraps by todd wilbur

update: this recipe was created by todd wilbur for his cookbook "top secret restaurant recipes 2" (penguin random house 2007). www.topsecretrecipes.com. 

another version of the chicken lettuce wraps.

1. make the special sauce by dissolving the sugar in water in a small bowl
2. add soy sauce , rice wine vinegar , ketchup , lemon juice and sesame oil
3. mix well and refrigerate this sauce until you're ready to serve
4. combine the hot water with the hot mustard and set this aside as well
5. eventually add your desired measurement of mustard and garlic chili sauce to the special sauce mixture to pour over the wraps
6. bring oil to high heat in a wok or large frying pan
7. saute chicken breasts for 4 to 5 minutes per side or done
8. remove chicken from the pan and cool
9. keep oil in the pan , keep hot
10. as chicken cools mince water chestnuts and mushrooms to about the size of small peas
11. prepare the stir fry sauce by mixing the soy sauce , brown sugar , and rice vinegar together in a small bowl
12. when chicken is cool , mince it as the mushrooms and water chestnuts are
13. with the pan still on high heat , add another tbsp of vegetable oil
14. add chicken , garlic , onions , water chestnuts and mushrooms to pan
15. add stir fry sauce to pan , saute mixture a couple minutes then serve in lettuce leaves
demonstrations.review: I'm only giving this 3 stars because I thought it was too much work without a ton of flavor.  I have a lettuce wrap recipe that I make all the time and will stick to that.  This wasn't bad.. it just did not wow me.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
olive garden copycat zuppa toscana

this is a clone of the olive garden zuppa toscana. tried and true, approved by former olive garden chefs.

1. chop or slice uncooked sausage into small pieces and cook until browned and meat is ground in bottom of your soup pan over med-high heat
2. add onions , garlic , salt , pepper , and red pepper flakes to sausage and cook until onions are clear and aromatics of the seasonings blend together
3. reduce heat back to medium and place , potatoes , in the pot
4. and slowly add the chicken stock and water and stir
5. cook on medium heat until potatoes are done and stir occasionally
6. once potatoes are done , add flour or cornstarch and simmer for another 15 minutes
7. reduce heat to lowest setting and sprinkle in your kale and cooked bacon and slowly pour cream while stirring
