8. check for taste and then serve
demonstrations.review: VERY VERY GOOD!! My hubby who is not a fan of soup loved loved loved this... I told me at least 7 times how good it was.. Will for sure make again

target.recipe_text:
creamy cajun chicken pasta

n'awlin's style of chicken with an updated alfredo sauce.

1. place chicken and cajun seasoning in a bowl and toss to coat
2. in a large skillet over medium heat , saut chicken in butter or margarine until chicken is tender , about 5 to 7 minutes
3. reduce heat add green onion , heavy cream , tomatoes , basil , salt , garlic powder , black pepper and heat through
4. pour over hot linguine and toss with parmesan cheese
target.review: This is a wonderful recipe!  I followed the recipe almost exactly, using 1 and a half cups of cream.  I did end up using just a bit more sun-dried tomatoes. I do think it makes more than 2 servings.  My husband went back for seconds, and we still had leftovers!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
peanut butter chocolate chunk cookies

these are impossible to stop eating.

1. cream the butter and peanut butter together until fully incorporated
2. add the sugars and cream on medium speed
3. add the egg and vanilla and mix until completely incorporated
4. add the flour and baking soda , mix until no white remains , then add the chocolate and mix on low just until everything comes together
5. drop by teaspoonfuls onto parchment-lined baking sheets
6. bake at 350 for 9 minutes or until golden brown
demonstrations.review: Cookies were chewy, soft, and really quite good!  I used JIF Natural Crunch PB and added 6 ounces of dark chocolate chips because that is what I had on hand.  My only complaint is that I thought they tasted just a BIT too much like flour.  It may have been "baker-error" though;  I started these with severe weather and got interrupted a couple times.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
blueberry cheesecake bars

easy summer dessert from kraft. i actually made these as blackberry, rather than blueberry, and substituted a 21-ounce can of blackberry pie filling i had on hand for the jam and the blueberries.

1. preheat oven to 350f combine butter and graham cracker crumbs and press firmly and evenly onto bottom of 9 x 13-inch baking pan
2. beat cream cheese until smooth
3. add sugar , eggs and vanila , beating until well blended
4. set aside
5. stir jam until softened and spread evenly over crust
6. sprinkle with blueberries
7. top with cream cheese mixture
8. bake 30 minutes or until slightly puffed
9. cool completely in pan
10. refrigerate leftover bars for up to 3 days
demonstrations.review: These were pretty good.  I halved the recipe and put the bars in a 8x8 inch glass pan.  As I was making it, the crust seemed to be a little crumbly for me and it was hard for me to spread the preserves over it without mixing them in.  I was concerned the bars wouldn't stay together, but actually held their shape very well and tasted great!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crumb topped banana muffins

these are so good. we love the topping.

1. in a large bowl , mix the flour , baking soda , baking powder , and salt
2. mix bananas , sugar , egg and melted butter
3. stir into dry mixture until thoroughly combined , then stop mixing
4. fill muffin cups 3 / 4 full
5. combine brown sugar , flour , and cinnamon topping ingredients
6. cut in cold butter until crumbly
7. sprinkle over muffins
8. bake at 375 degrees fahrenheit for about 20 minutes , until muffins test done
9. cool in pan for 10 minutes
demonstrations.review: These muffins are amazing!  We especially loved the topping.  I followed the recipe exactly, but next time will try some substitutions to lighten them up a bit more.  Easy, quick, and delicious!  Thank you!

target.recipe_text:
a chicken in every pot pie

easy and my kids love this.

1. in a saucepan , combine chicken and next 6 ingredients
2. bring to a boil , stirring occasionally
3. meanwhile , combine bisquick and next 3 ingredients
4. pour the hot chicken mixture into eight greased 10 oz
5. ramekins
6. immediately spoon 1 / 4 cup of biscuit mixture evenly on top of each
7. sprinkle with paprika
8. bake , uncovered , at 350 degrees for 30-35 minutes or until topping is golden brown
target.review: This was really easy to make and the flavor is really good, but mine came out a bit too runny for my taste. I think next time I will substitute another can of the cream of mushroom for a cup of the chicken broth to thicken it up a bit.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
easiest beef enchiladas ever

best enchilada recipe i've found. we love the spicy, cheesy flavor of these.

1. brown meat and onions in large skillet
2. add 1 cup enchilada sauce and 1 cup cheese
3. mix well
4. put filling along center of each tortilla
5. roll up and place seam side down in a 9x13 pan
6. pour remaining sauce over
7. sprinkle remaining cheese over
8. bake at 350f degrees for about 30 minutes till cheese is bubbly
demonstrations.review: This was super easy and tasted great! I didn't realize that enchiladas could be so easy and still come out so good. Thanks for sharing!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cinnamon bun icing

this is just like the sweet, gooey icing that comes inside tiny tins inside those tubes of refrigerated cinnamon bun doughs. by changing the extract flavor, you can make orange cinnamon buns, lemon cinnamon buns, whatever you like.

1. mix together sugar and enough cream to achieve a spreading consistency
2. add extract flavor of your choice and salt
3. to use: spread over warm biscuits or sweet bread still warm from the oven or drizzle over gingerbread cookies
4. this also makes a nice icing for quick breads like banana bread or zucchini bread
demonstrations.review: Very easy and great on cinnamon buns. I ended up using about 6 Tbs on Heavy cream in order to get the right consistency, but it tastes great.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
best twice baked potatoes

family favorite - tried and true - the only recipe we use.

1. microwave the potatoes until done
2. allow to cool a bit
3. slice about a 1" strip of the skin off the top of each potato
4. carefully scoop out the pulp , placing in a large bowl , and leaving potato shells intact
5. mash the potato pulp along with the margarine
6. add milk , sour cream , cheese , salt and pepper
7. combining well
8. spoon the mixture back into the potato shells , piling high
9. top with the crumbled bacon or bacon bits
10. bake at 400 for 15 minutes
demonstrations.review: These were awesome. I had to cheat a little because I only had a little over 45 minutes to make these, so I put them  in the oven for 20 minutes at 450 and then turned them down to 400 for 20 minutes. The skin came out nice and firm/crispy which helped make a perfect bowl to put the inners back in. I realized that in my rush I forgot to put the sour cream in, but I did use a cup of cheddar cheese instead of 1/2 a cup and they were delicious. Would make them again and again.

target.recipe_text:
beth s melt in your mouth barbecue ribs  oven

i almost didn't want to share this ribs recipe because this is one of the dishes that i make that keep my sons coming back home! these can be done with baby back or regular pork ribs. i have also made split chickens this way. the ribs are tender, moist and just slide off of the bone. i know that your family will love them just as much as my family does.
i noticed that some are unable to find hickory smoked salt. you can use smoked paprika or just brush the ribs with liquid smoke before applying the rub. the smoke flavor is nice because it helps give the ribs a cooked-on-the-grill flavor.
also, the easiest way to remove the membrane is to work a spoon, or i use the tips of my kitchen shears, into the bottom center of the membrane, work it back and forth to form a "pocket," then i slide my thumbs in and work the membrane off from the center outward to the ends.

1. preheat oven to 300 degrees f
2. line a baking sheet with two layers of foil , shiny side out
3. peel off tough membrane that covers the bony side of the ribs
4. season the ribs on both sides with salt and pepper
5. if using , divide the hickory liquid smoke evenly over the ribs
6. in a medium bowl , combine the light brown sugar , paprika , garlic powder and ground red pepper
7. apply the rub to all sides of the ribs
8. lay ribs on the prepared baking sheet , meaty side down
9. lay two layers of foil on top of ribs and roll and crimp edges tightly , edges facing up to seal
10. transfer to the oven and = bake for 2-2 1 / 2 hours or until meat is starting to shrink away from the ends of the bone
11. remove from oven
12. heat broiler
13. cut ribs into serving sized portions of 2 or 3 ribs
14. arrange on broiler pan , bony side up
15. brush on sauce
16. broil for 1 or 2 minutes until sauce is cooked on and bubbly
17. turn ribs over
18. repeat on other side
19. alternately , you can grill the ribs on your grill to cook on the sauce
target.review: I have used this recipe a dozen times but have never reviewed it.  It is the ONLY way I cook ribs.  I leave out the smoke salt and also use Stubbs BBQ Sauce and they always turn out delicious!  I have used this technique with both pork and beef ribs and it is delicious!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
luby s cafeteria butternut brownie pie

from luby's 50th anniversary cookbook for those fans of cafeteria cuisine.

1. preheat oven to 300f
2. lightly grease or spray with cooking spray a 9" pie plate
3. in large mixing bowl , beat egg whites and baking powder until soft peaks form
4. add cream of tartar , beating constantly
5. add 1 cup of the sugar , a tablespoon at a time , beating constantly until stiff peaks form
6. using a rubber scraper , fold in graham crackers and pecan pieces
7. spoon into pie plate
8. bake 30 minutes or until wooden pick inserted in center comes out clean
9. cool completely on wire rack
10. in chilled small bowl using chilled beaters , beat cream just until it begins to thicken
11. add remaining 1 / 4 cup of sugar and vanilla and continue beating until stiff peaks form , taking care not to overbeat
12. top pie with whipped cream
13. sprinkle with pecans and refrigerate until served
demonstrations.review: AMAZING!   That is what my husband told me after eating his 2nd piece.  I will be making this pie, instead of my usual pecan pies, for Thanksgiving this year.  It is wonderful!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
sugar cookie frosting

this is the frosting i like to use for my soft sugar cookies, "recipe#286412". it uses heavy whipping cream and i like to add green or red food coloring to it when i make the cookies for christmas. it should make enough to frost about 4-5 dozen cookies, depending on how thick of layer you use on each cookie and how big the cookies are. update: 12/21/2009: i have changed the recipe to increase the amount of whipping cream. i agree with the other reviewer that more is needed but be sure to add the whipping cream gradually and then add the rest if needed.

1. in mixing bowl , combine butter , confectioners' sugar , extract and enough cream to achieve spreading consistency
2. add food coloring , if desired
3. frost cookies
demonstrations.review: I have a fabulous go to recipe I always use that calls for half shortening, half butter, and milk, but I was out of shortening and milk so I thought this recipe would be perfect, boy was I wrong.  I desperately WANTED to like this frosting, but unfortunately myself and my family did not like it at all.  I followed the recipe exactly and to be blunt, the taste was quite unsatisfactory.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s best deviled eggs

these have been a favorite for years, when i serve these at my get togethers or make them for socials and large events they are always the first to go and everyone wants the recipe, i suggest to use large, extra large or even jumbo eggs for this, i like to make the yolk filling a day ahead and refrigerate this will blend the flavors --- for a nice presentation place each egg half in a colored paper muffin liner --- all ingredient amounts may be adjusted to taste --- see my recipe#259573

1. slice the eggs in half lengthwise
2. remove the yolks , and set whites aside
3. in a small bowl , mush yolks well with a fork , leaving no small lumps
4. add next 10 ingredients mix well to combine
5. spoon or pipe egg yolk mixture evenly into the whites
6. sprinkle with paprika
7. cover tightly with plastic wrap
8. store in the refrigerator until ready to serve
demonstrations.review: By far the BEST deviled egg recipe!!!  The wonderful thing about these is that if you can wait to eat them (which is hard to do) until they have been in the fridge for a few hours then the flavor is even better!  My husband and I always fight over the last one!  Thanks Kittencal!  Your recipes are always spot on! :-)

target.recipe_text:
never weep  whipped cream

i don't know where i got this, but it works. the whipped cream will keep for a week in the fridge without deflating... great for party make-ahead.

1. whip all ingredients together until firm peaks form
2. cover leftovers tightly , preferably in an air-tight plastic container
3. this stays the same consistency until used
4. it will keep for a week in the fridge without deflating
target.review: I made this to directions and it was great. My sister who does not like whipped Cream even liked it for it was not to sweet at all. I used it on our Pumpkin Pie and then in some Hot Chocolate so that I could use it up. It lasted almost a week before it was all gone.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chocolate chocolate chip cookies in a jar mix

be sure to place a ribbon on the jar with directions for baking.

1. combine flour , soda , and powder
2. place in a 1 quart jar
3. layer remaining ingredients pressing firmly after each layer
4. recipe to attach to jar:
5. preheat oven to 375f
6. beat 12 tablespoons softened unsalted butter , 1 egg and 1 teaspoon vanilla in a large bowl until well blended
7. place cookie mix in an other bowl and mix to combine ingredients
8. add butter mixture and blend in to smooth any clumps
9. drop tablespoon full onto ungreased pan and bake 9-11 minutes
10. cool on pan then remove to rack to completely cool
demonstrations.review: I made these up and the jar looked great. I made the cookies last night and they are a great cookie. they srpead out a lot more that I like and are very thin and crispy. DH liked them and he is not a big chocolate fan. This makes a great gift idea, and I will be makeing again at some point.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
jolean s cheese potato   smoked sausage casserole

this was another one of our favorites in the 70's  very inexpensive and very easy to make.  just recently found this recipe hand-written by my mom, and the warm feelings flood back to me, because this was a true favorite in our house.  little did i know that she was on such a tight budget, yet made things like this that we all loved!!  note:  the meat that was used in this recipe always varied, according to whatever we had available at the time.

1. cut skinless smoked sausage in half , lengthwise , and then chop into 1 / 2 inch "half moon" cuts
2. cook in a frying pan for about 15 minutes , turning frequently to slightly brown
3. meanwhile , put cooked & diced potatoes in 2 quart casserole
4. add cooked meat and give it a gentle toss
5. mix all remaining ingredients in a saucepan over medium heat until warm , melted and smooth
6. pour white / cheese sauce over potatoes and meat
7. sprinkle shredded sharp cheddar cheese on top , and then sprinkle paprika evenly over the top
8. bake in preheated 350f oven for 35-45 minutes
9. hot dogs , sliced into 1 / 2-inch slices or 1 / 2 lb
10. ham diced into 1 / 2-inch dices or 12 oz
11. can of spam diced into 1 / 2-inch dices , instead of the smoked sausage
demonstrations.review: I made this tonight and we liked it very much. I used what I had on hand and that was a Hot smoked sausage. I added peas to it so we would have our vegetable too. Turned out to be very good this way. I will be useing this one again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
reeses squares   5 ingredients   no bake  reese s

these bars are extremely rich and not for people with a fear of chocolate and peanut butter (if those people actually exist)!!! very easy no bake 5 ingredient recipe!

1. combine graham crumbs , sugar and peanut butter and mix well
2. blend in melted butter until well combined
3. press mixture evenly into a 9 x 13 inch pan
4. melt chocolate chips in microwave or in double boiler
5. spread over peanut butter mixture
6. chill until just set and cut into bars (these are very hard to cut if the chocolate gets "rock hard"
demonstrations.review: I love peanut butter and chocolate and this is a GREAT one. It is just like the real thing. I think next time I am going to roll the peanut butter mix in to ball or ever small patties and dip them into the chocolate for a smaller bit size piece. OUTSTANDING

target.recipe_text:
human puppy chow

this is the best recipe in the world!! it is great to have anytime but it also makes great christmas gifts.

1. in a large sauce pan , melt together butter , peanut butter , and chocolate chips
2. stir until all is evenly distributed and all is completely melted
3. measure out chex into a large bowl
4. pour chocolate mixture over chex and fold until all the chex are completely covered in the chocolate mixture
5. put powdered sugar into large paper bag
6. put chex into the bag with the sugar and shake until all chex are covered
7. add more sugar as needed
target.review: This was a great and easy recipe! It was very very tasty!! Just wondering why my chex mix tasted a little stale after a couple of days? Great recipe..THANKS!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
strawberry pretzel jell o

a crisp salty pretzel crust complements the creamy marshmallow-fluff-like "white" layer, with a  tangy topping of strawberries in gelatin. much like a strawberry cheesecake, but with the surprise of pretzels!  for best results, make strawberry pretzel jell-o only one day in advance, to preserve the  crunchy texture of the pretzels.

1. crust: combine pretzels , butter , and 1 / 4 cup sugar
2. press into 9" x 13" baking dish and bake at 350 for 10 minutes
3. cool to room temperature
4. white layer: cream together cream cheese and 1 cup sugar
5. fold in cool whip
6. spread over pretzel crust
7. red layer: dissolve gelatin in boiling water
8. stir in frozen strawberries , chill until partially set and spread over white layer
9. chill until set and serve
demonstrations.review: Excellent! The only thing I changed was that I used only 1/2 butter otherwise perfection! Thanks for a great recipe Loves!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
oven baked mostaccioli

great make ahead meal for parties and family dinners.

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees
2. in large skillet , combine beef , green peppers and onion
3. cook until meat has browned
4. stir in spaghetti sauce , tomato sauce and water
5. bring to a boil , then simmer 5 minutes
6. pour 1 cup of meat sauce mixture into the bottom of a 9x13 baking dish
7. top with half of the pasta
8. then a layer of 2 cups of mozzarella cheese and all of the parmesan cheese
9. for the next layer , add 2 cups of sauce , remaining pasta and mozzarella cheese
10. top with remaining sauce
11. bake at 350 degrees for 30-45 minutes or until hot and bubbly
12. cook the assembled meal right before serving
13. you may have to add some cooking time because of the refrigeration
14. to make clean up easier , consider foil lining the baking dish
15. easy clean up is so nice when entertaining !
demonstrations.review: Wonderful Donna! This was my very first time making mostaccioli and thought this was a perfect recipe. Only thing I did different was added a little sugar to my sauce mixture and only used mozzarella cheese and no parmesan. Thanks!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cream peas

these peas are so yummy! sweet and creamy!

1. melt butter over medium high heat , and drain peas
2. add all remaining ingredients and bring to a boil
3. reduce heat to medium low and simmer for 10 minutes , or until cream has thickened
4. stir occasionally
demonstrations.review: Great and easy recipe! I made this last night to serve with recipe #289738...Delish!! Thanks for posting!

target.recipe_text:
baklava salmon  salmon with honey  butter  walnuts  and mustard

one of my friends deemed this "baklava salmon" and the name stuck. the salmon & mustard go well with the honey, butter, and walnuts. we usually serve this with rice and steamed carrots or broccoli.

1. preheat oven to 400
2. line shallow roasting pan with non-stick aluminum foil , or spray with non-stick pan spray
3. in small bowl , blend butter , mustard , and honey , set aside
4. in another bowl , mix together bread crumbs , nuts , and parsley
5. place salmon fillets on prepared pan , sprinkle with salt and pepper , and brush with honey-mustard mixture
6. sprinkle tops with crumb / nut mixture
7. if any remains , press into sides of salmon
8. bake salmon 12-15 minutes in preheated oven , or until it flakes easily with a fork
9. serve with lime or lemon wedge
target.review: The walnut mixture gave the salmon a nice crunch and wonderful sweet flavor. I will definately be making this again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
onion lentils and rice

this recipe is adapted from "what to cook" cookbook. other than slicing the onions, it doesn't take a lot of prep time. this is what i make when i come home from work hungry and exhausted and want something yummy and filling for dinner.

1. heat olive oil in skillet , saute the onions with 1 tsp cumin until lightly browned
2. remove 1 / 3 of the onions and set aside
3. continue cooking the rest of the onions until dark brown and black in places
4. in the meantime , bring water to a boil in a saucepan , add the lentils , reduce heat , and cover , simmering for 15 minutes
5. to the lentils , add the 1 / 3 lightly browned onions , rice , salt , and remaining 1 tsp cumin
6. cover and simmer 15 minutes or until rice is tender
7. remove from heat and stir in the well-browned onions
8. cover and let stand for 5-10 minutes
9. serve !
10. especially good with chopped lettuce , tomatoes , and a dollop of yogurt or sour cream on top
11. also good with cooked spinach
demonstrations.review: This will easily become a regular dish for us. Delicious!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
creamy potato salad

have you ever posted a recipe and just love reading the reviews for it?  this is my signature potato salad.  whenever there is a pot luck function at work, i am told that i have to bring the potato salad.  no one else is allowed to and i am never given a choice.  thank you everyone who ever tried this potato salad and for leaving such glowing reviews for it.  you all have made me look so good.  i personally can not stand eggs or raw onions, so i leave them out but i know most people don't think a potato salad is complete without them.  thanks again for so many wonderful reviews. (psssst....check out my recipe #123107 as well.  it shares the dressing with this recipe but tastes much much different because of the different ingredients) please see recipe #242966 for bacon bit tips.

1. cook potatoes in boiling , salted water until tender
2. drain well
3. peel and cube potatoes
4. transfer to a large bowl
5. add celery , onion , sweet relish and bacon bits
6. combine mayo , sugar , celery seed , vinegar , mustard , and salt
7. add mayo mixture to potatoes
8. toss lightly to coat potato mixture
9. carefully fold in the chopped eggs
10. cover and chill thoroughly
11. bacon bit
12. use a sharp knife and cut the frozen bacon into long strips about 1 / 4 inch wide
13. turn the bacon and cut the strips into pieces also about 1 / 4 in wide
14. you now have perfect raw bacon pieces to fast fry
15. no need to separate
16. they will separate during cooking
17. perfect bacon bits
demonstrations.review: This was my first time making potato salad and I decided to do so for the Superbowl. There was no leftovers (good thing I tried some while making it) and a friend even took the recipe home! Will definitely be making it again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
delicious chicken pot pie

this chicken pot pie recipe takes a little time, but it is well worth it!! this is an all-time favorite in our family. great on a cold winter day.

1. preheat oven to 400f
2. saute onion , celery , carrots and potatoes in margarine for 10 minutes
3. add flour to sauteed mixture , stirring well , cook one minute stirring constantly
4. combine broth and half and half
5. gradually stir into vegetable mixture
6. cook over medium heat stirring constantly until thickened and bubbly
7. stir in salt and pepper
8. add chicken and stir well
9. pour into shallow 2 quart casserole dish and top with pie shells
10. cut slits to allow steam to escape
11. bake for 40-50 minutes or until pastry is golden brown and filling is bubbly and cooked through
demonstrations.review: OH. MY. GOD. I have only ever had chicken pot pie from the frozen food isle at the grocery store... This was AMAZING! This recipe is a keeper. Thanks so much!

target.recipe_text:
potato salad

the secret is in the type of potato, which is dry and absorbs the flavor of the dressing. letting it sit overnight imparts the flavor to the potatoes.

1. boil potatoes in their skin till cooked
2. cool and peel
3. mix all dressing ingredients together
4. depending on preference , you can make more dressing
5. the mayo to miracle whip ratio is 2-1
6. when potatoes are peeled , cut into bite sized chunks
7. layer dressing and potatoes as you cut them
8. lightly toss till potatoes are covered in dressing
9. cover and let sit in fridge overnight to absorb flavors
target.review: Hi susan, it is me again. I feel silly, I don't think I have posted my potato salad recipe yet. But I will soon. I am inschool, so when I get time, I will. sorry about that.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cinnamon toast delight

an easy quick treat that tastes & smells like a fresh baked cinnamon streussel!!!

1. preheat the oven to 400 degrees
2. smear butter over both surfaces of each slice of bread
3. add lots of brown sugar to the tops , enough to cover the tops without seeing the butter
4. sprinkle the cinnamon over the top of the brown sugar
5. let bake for about 5-6 minutes , then turn to broil till the top of the brown sugar is bubbling
6. remove from oven and let cool for 1-2 minutes
demonstrations.review:
This is a sweet little treat, have been eating it for years! Thanks lil' butt! :)~
~}i{ ~ }i{ ~ }i{ ~ }i{~

demonstrations.recipe_text:
malva pudding  south african baked dessert

this is more delicious than the sum of its parts! it's a real traditional oldie. retested on 22 oct 07: after reading the reviews, i have just made this again. i cut down a little on the sugar in the sauce (it was 5 oz originally), but it should actually be a sweet pudding!! the sauce was quite enough to moisten the entire pudding -- it should not be dripping with sauce, as you can see in the photographs. do not serve immediately, but let it stand, keeping warm, to give the sauce a chance to soak in properly. real cold-weather comfort food. it's rich, so a little goes a long way, and this pudding yields up to 6 servings. this winter you must try this!

1. preheat oven to 350 deg f / 180 deg celsius
2. grease an oven dish
3. i used a 7 x 7 x 1 1 / 2 inch pyrex dish
4. beat or whip the sugar and eggs
5. it's quickest in a food processor , or use electric beaters
6. beat until thick and lemon coloured , then add the jelly and mix through
7. melt the butter and add the butter and vinegar to the wet mixture
8. sieve , or simply mix together: the flour , soda and salt
9. add this mixture with the milk to the egg mixture in the processor or mixing bowl
10. beat well
11. pour into an oven-proof dish and bake until pudding is brown and well-risen -- depending on your oven and oven dish this will be between 30 - 45 minutes
12. in a pot , melt together the ingredients for the sauce , and stir well
13. pour it over the pudding as soon as it comes out of the oven
14. leave to stand awhile before serving
15. serve warm
16. because it's rich it does not really need enhancement , but if you want , serve with vanilla ice cream
demonstrations.review: Sounds interstingly good! Will have to try soon!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
red hot biscuits

if you are tired of garlic bread or dinner rolls with you meal, then try these tasty little biscuits.  a little on the spicy side, but really good.  had this with our steak dinner last night.  found this cut out of a magazine in my mom's recipe book, but could not tell which one. really easy to make.

1. preheat oven to 425 degrees
2. combine bisquick , red pepper and 1 / 2 tsp garlic powder
3. with a fork , stir in milk and cheese until mixture forms a soft dough
4. drop dough by 1 / 4 cupful onto greased cookie sheet
5. combine butter and remaining garlic powder
6. bursh on dough tops
7. bake 10-12 minutes or until golden brown
demonstrations.review: sounds good!

target.recipe_text:
best cornbread ever

this is the best cornbread i've ever had. the cottage cheese melts into the batter and tastes great. try the optional add-ins. this is a great complement to chili.

1. preheat oven to 375 degrees
2. combine all ingredients and mix well -- it will be thicker than you expect
3. pour into buttered 9" x 13" casserole dish
4. bake in oven for 35-40 minutes until golden brown
5. this cornbread is very moist and dense
6. for a little variation , add one or more of the following: a can of chopped green chiles , 1 cup of cheddar cheese , 1 cup of pepperjack cheese , 1 / 2 cup chopped fresh cilantro
7. let it cool for 10 minutes for best flavor
target.review: Wow!  Wonderful!  We loved this cornbread! I added an extra pinch of sugar and some cheddar cheese. Even my 8 year old son loved it!  This goes into the Favorites folder!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
the best banana bread

this is one of the recipes i am known for. super moist and super yummy. i have tried many over the years and always come back to this. i often give it as a gift around the holidays. just may be the last banana bread recipe you ever try! can also make 3 mini-loaves

1. cream butter and sugar
2. mash bananas and add by hand to creamed mixture
3. by hand add eggs , vanilla , baking soda , flour and salt
4. gently stir in buttermilk and chocolate chips
5. pour into a greased loaf pan
6. bake at 350f for 1 1 / 4 hour or until it tests done with a toothpick
7. i find that coarsely mashing bananas is best and make sure they are over ripe for best flavor
8. i also find that doing the majority of the mixing by hand makes for better texture in the end
9. even though the recipe says it makes 1 loaf , i usually use 2 loaf pans or 3 mini loaf pans because it seems to yield a moister bread
10. just adjust baking time down
11. if you do not have buttermilk you can put 1 teaspoons vinegar into a 1 / 2 cup measuring cup and fill to top with milk
12. let rest 5 minutes before adding to recipe
13. this freezes well
demonstrations.review: This deserves more stars!  Excellent!  My family loves it.  I make it with chocolate chips for my husband and two of my sons.  I then make some with walnuts for me and my 12 year old son.  Yum!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
marvelous broccoli salad

you may want to make a double batch of this salad. there won't be any left!!

1. combine all ingredients for salad
2. combine dressing ingredients
3. add to salad just before serving and toss
demonstrations.review: Wonderful!  I served this for company and everyone raved about it!  My husband really loved it!  I will be making this often. I think next time I will take someone's suggestion and try it with sunflower seeds added.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
melt in your mouth chicken breasts

the mayonnaise make these chicken breast very moist and tender--enjoy!

1. mix mayonnaise or yogurt , cheese and seasonings
2. spread mixture over chicken breast and place in baking dish
3. bake at 375f for 45 minutes
demonstrations.review: This was very good and easy.  My family and I loved it.  I put a thin layer of the mayonnaise mixture on the  chicken and then flipped  it over and added a generous portion to the top.  I doubled the garlic and added some salad supreme seasoning on the top.  It was so tenderful and bursting with flavor.

target.recipe_text:
peanut butter pork tenderloin

this recipe comes from a local cookbook called recipes and memories of patrick w. cox.  it's different and tasty.  i made a slight change in the ingredients but not much.

1. preheat oven to 375 degrees fahrenheit
2. trim fat from tenderloin
3. sprinkle with fresh ground black pepper to taste
4. line a baking dish with parchment paper or aluminim foil
5. mix the soy sauce , peanut butter , red pepper and minced garlic together
6. spread mixture over pork loin
7. bake uncovered for 30 minutes
8. remove from oven
9. carefully spread pineapple preserves on top of pork loin
10. bake another 10 mintes or until meat reaches 150 degrees fahrenheit
11. let stand for 5 minutes before serving
target.review:
This was delicious! My husband was very skeptical but admitted after trying it that it was actually "really good"
next time i will double the recipe for the sauce and pineapples but yes, there will definitely be a next time!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chicken stroganoff   crock pot

nan

1. put frozen chicken in bottom of crock pot
2. mix soup , sour cream , and onion soup mix
3. pour over chicken
4. cook on low for 7 hours
5. serve over rice or noodles
demonstrations.review: meh... i must have made this wrong because i don't agree with these 5 star reviews at all.  It was just OK for me

demonstrations.recipe_text:
ro tel chicken spaghetti

easy, easy, easy!!! i got this recipe from an aunt who made it for a family reunion. it has a great flavor and makes alot. very good! does not include cooking time for the chicken.

1. in a bowl mix together the soup , broth& ro-tel tomatoes
2. in a 13x9 greased casserole dish layer as follows: spaghetti , chicken , soup mix , cheese
3. bake in a preheated 350 degree oven until heated through and cheese melts about 30-45 minutes
4. as soon as you remove from the oven stir to mix well , adding salt and pepper to taste
demonstrations.review: My family loves this recipe. I've made it a few times now and everyone raves about it.  My grandmother has her chicken spaghetti recipe but i have never made it because it just seems as if it is too much of a pain!  Then i came across this one and tried it out and loved it even more than hers! and it's so easy!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
my family s favorite sloppy joes  pizza joes

i've tried many recipes, this is the best. i once 'dec-tupled' (10x) this recipe to sell sandwiches at a craft fair at my church. people were waiting in line to buy leftovers. freezes well, goes up to the lake or camping well and is a hit on halloween...it's no-fail. easy to double, triple, etc. i've been making joes this way for over 20 years.
***03-08-09, i just reinvented this recipe tonight when i went to make it for dinner and found i didn't have an 8-oz. can of tomato sauce (shame on me).  the family was upset with me when i subbed an 8-oz. can of pizza sauce and told them to suck it up and call them 'pizza joes' and then served them up with shredded mozzarella cheese on the toasted buns, top and bottom.  they loved it.  i left out the bbq sauce in this preparation and just used a 1/2 cup ketchup.  pizza joes are good to go!

1. in a large skillet , brown ground beef , celery and onion
2. drain the fat , who needs it ?
3. stir in remaining ingredients , simmer covered , 15-20 minutes , stirring occasionally
4. if joes appear too'loose' , leave cover off and let moisture evaporate
5. cook until it's the consistency you like for serving on toasted buns , with french fries and cole slaw
demonstrations.review: Delicious!  I'm always thrilled when i can find a recipe that my kids eat!  Will definitely make again.

target.recipe_text:
bev s macaroni and cheese

this is the recipe i have been using for macaroni and cheese since the beginning of time! truly a classic and a staple on our family table. i hope you enjoy it as much as we do. a great side dish to be served with my meatloaf barbecue style!

1. melt butter in medium saucepan
2. stir in flour , salt , mustard and pepper until smooth
3. remove from heat and gradually stir in milk until smooth
4. stirring constantly , cook over medium heat until thickened
5. remove from heat
6. stir in 1 1 / 2 cups cheese until melted
7. combine cheese mixture with macaroni in greased 2 quart casserole
8. sprinkle remaining cheese on top
9. bake in 375 degree oven for 25 minutes or until lightly browned
10. makes 6 servings
target.review: Wonderful recipe! It is fairly easy and everyone loved it. I like a bread crumb topping on my mac and cheese so I put some butter and a teaspoon and a half of dried herbs (I used Pampered Chef Italian Seasoning) in the food processor with the bread crumbs. I pulsed it a few times until everything was incorperated then sprinkled on top of the mac and cheese before putting it in the oven. Yum!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
easy crock pot macaroni and cheese

from company's coming slow cooker recipes. i love to make this when my kids have skating lessons. i can throw it into the crockpot after school and when lessons are over, dinner is waiting. if you are lucky enough to have two crock pots, you can have a glazed ham going in the other one and your dinner is ready to go!

1. spray crockpot with non-stick spray for easy cleaning
2. in a saucepan , combine first 5 ingredients
3. pour in milk and stir with a whisk until no lumps remain
4. heat and continue stirring until mixture boils and is thickened
5. add cheese and then macaroni
6. stir until well mixed
7. pour into 3 1 / 2 quart slow cooker
8. cover and cook on low for 2-2 1 / 2 hours or on high for 1 hour
demonstrations.review: So easy and such a wonderful flavors. I am very picky when it comes to mac and cheese, the stuff from the box just will not do! Added more cheese, one can never have too much cheese.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crock pot chicken with black beans   cream cheese

i love this crock-pot chicken recipe for two reasons: one, my family loves it and two, it is so easy to make! i got this recipe from my sister. she has two children of her own, and they love it too! it's also the best leftovers in the world -- if there are any!

1. take 4-5 frozen , yes , frozen , boneless chicken breasts put into crock pot
2. add 1 can of black beans , drained , 1 jar of salsa , 1 can of corn drained
3. keep in crock pot on high for about 4-5 hours or until chicken is cooked
4. add 1 package of cream cheese and let sit for about 1 / 2 hour
5. all done and enjoy !
demonstrations.review: Very easy and very tasty! I served this with tortillas, black olives, shredded cheddar and rice to make burritos. We all liked it so I will be making this again soon!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
easy pumpkin coffee cake

versatile fall favorite in our house. great with spiced coffee or chai. tasty kid approved treat - our toddler loves slices of this cake when it's still warm from the oven. serve warm slices of cake with vanilla ice cream or warm homemade custard sauce and whipped cream for an excellent dessert. fabulous, no matter how you slice it!

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. in a large bowl or bowl of a stand mixer , combine cake mix , pumpkin , brown sugar , oil , eggs , and pumpkin pie spice
3. blend at low speed for 1 minute if using stand mixer or until completely moistened if mixing by hand
4. beat 2 minutes at medium speed if using stand mixer , or whisk for 2 minutes until batter is smooth and slightly lighter in color than when you began
5. fold in the nuts
6. spread batter in a greased and floured 13x9x2-inch pan
7. in a medium bowl combine the sugar , flour , softened butter , and cinnamon with a fork or pastry blender until the mixture is crumbly
8. sprinkle crumbs evenly over batter
9. bake at 350f for 40-45 minutes , until center springs back when touched lightly
demonstrations.review: Easy and it tastes wonderful! I made it on a night family was coming for dinner, everyone liked it and asked to take some home. I will be making this often this fall I can already tell! I added the nuts to the topping rather then the cake itself otherwise I followed it exactly.

target.recipe_text:
soft snickerdoodle cookies

these snickerdoodle cookies are so delicious, and they have the best texture. they are so fast to put together too! i actually got it from an old recipe that my great grandma had clipped out of a newspaper. grandma always knows best!

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. mix softened butter , 1 1 / 2 cups sugar , 1tps of vanilla extract and eggs thoroughly in a large bowl
3. combine flour , cream of tartar , baking soda and salt in a separate bowl
4. blend dry ingredients into butter mixture
5. chill dough , and chill an ungreased cookie sheet for about 10-15 minutes in the fridge
6. meanwhile , mix 3 tablespoons sugar , and 3 teaspoons cinnamon in a small bowl
7. scoop 1 inch globs of dough into the sugar / cinnamon mixture
8. coat by gently rolling balls of dough in the sugar mixture
9. place on chilled ungreased cookie sheet , and bake 10 minutes
10. remove from pan immediately
target.review: These were so easy to make and bake. Only change I made was to chill the dough for 30 minutes before rolling into balls. Next time I'll space further apart before baking. As they ended up square shaped lol.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
easy lemon self saucing pudding

been looking for the lemon delicious recipe i cooked many years ago but somewhere along lost the clipping (before zaar time) and this seems to come close to it though called a pudding (maybe searching in the wrong area) but it was good though sweeter than i remember (would need to work on the sugar content), certainly don't remember having the sprinkle sugar on top as per this recipe but i believe that what gives it its crispy top in this recipe.  serving suggestion was 4 but i think could be easily stretched to 6 served with cream and or icecream.  i found that 1 lemon gave me the rind and juiced that but needed to juice a second lemon to get the full 1/2 cup (got a little more than that and added the lot).

1. preheat oven to 180c
2. grease a 4 to 6 cup casserole dish
3. batter base - sift flour and a pinch of salt together and then add sugar and grated lemon rind , mixing well together
4. stir in melted butter , vanilla and milk mix and stir until all flour mix is incorporated
5. pour into prepared casserole dish
6. sauce - sprinkle the mixture with the sugar and lemon rind
7. combine the boiling water and lemon juice and carefully spoon some of over the batter and sugar topping , until fully covered and then pour the rest of the mix over the back of the spoon
8. bake for 30 to 40 minutes and let stand for 5 to 10 minutes before serving
9. serve with cream and or icecream
demonstrations.review: Have made this pudding twice in the last week! Used ingredient amounts exactly as listed and it turns out scrumptious!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mean s dutch babies

a simple and tasty breakfast/brunch treat.
this is an adopted recipe from the recipezaar account, and i am delighted to be the new owner of such a winning recipe.
if you would like the inside of the finished dish to be a little less "egg-y" then cut the number of eggs down to 3, and many many reviewers also found that just 3 tablespoons of butter worked better for them. either way they did it, they all agreed that the taste was great. enjoy!

1. mix flour , salt and milk well
2. add sugar
3. add eggs one at a time , beating well after each addition
4. this can be done by hand or with a stand mixer
5. melt butter in an ovenproof dish or cast iron pan in the oven
6. when butter is completely melted and pan is hot , pour in batter
7. bake at 425 degrees fahrenheit for 25 minutes
8. serve with maple syrup , jam or powdered sugar with a squeeze of lemon
demonstrations.review: Love to make this easy hearty dish for brunch. I follow the suggestion to use 3 eggs, and also leave out the salt. We devour this with softly whipped cream and maple syrup.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
yummy cheesy corn

i know this may seem silly to post this simple recipe, but this corn is soooooo good!  i make this at least once a week with a meal and my hubby only likes this kind of corn.  plain corn has gone out the window.  this is so easy and yummy.  anyone could make it in a jiffy!

1. melt butter in medium skillet and add corn
2. add salt and pepper and fry for about 5 minutes
3. add the cheese and stir until it's nice a melted
4. serve immediately !
5. ohhhh -- it's soooo good !
demonstrations.review: Just made this for dinner tonight. Used a 4-blend low fat ready grated cheese mix, and smoked garlic seasoning instead of salt. Added the cheese at the end, put a lid on the pot and turned the heat off, so it would be ready when my hubby got home from work. Turned out great. And was a hit with my hubby!!

target.recipe_text:
cinnamon pumpkin empanadas   empanadas de calabazas

from esperanza's cafe (joe t. garcia's bakery), fort worth courtesy of texas monthly magazine.

1. for the filling: mix ingredients together and set aside
2. preheat oven to 350 degrees
3. combine water , sugar , salt , yeast , baking powder , and cinnamon
4. using an electric mixer , gradually blend in half of the flour
5. add shortening and thoroughly mix , then gradually blend in remaining flour
6. divide dough into 4 equal parts , then shape each of those parts into 4 dough balls
7. slap the dough balls between the palms of your well-floured hands until somewhat flattened , then roll out on a floured surface into circles approximately 4 inches in diameter and 1 / 8-inch thick
8. put about 1 1 / 2 tablespoons of pumpkin filling in the center of each circle , fold over , and seal edges by moistening slightly and pressing lightly with a fork on both sides
9. bake on a greased cookie sheet until golden brown , 18 to 20 minutes
target.review: These were okay. I made a bunch for a faux-Thanksgiving meal. I added a bit of vanilla and nutmeg to the filling to sweeten it up. I am a huge baker but I've never baked anything with yeast before. I ended up letting the dough rise a bit between batches and it was easy to work with. I also brushed the dough with egg wash before baking. Completed product was okay but just okay. This is probably personal preference, but I did not like the texture of the filling. (I know, I know, what kind of texture did I think pumpkin has?). The dough was soft and the filling was a squishy too. Just needed a little more contrast for me. If I made this again, I would absolutely add some nuts into the filling!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
tilapia al ajillo  garlic tilapia

you can do this with any white fish, sea bass is great this way. fish is often served this way in the canary islands, though usually it is the whole fish instead of fillets. yum!

1. season tilapia fillets with salt and pepper
2. heat oil in a skillet over medium heat
3. put fillets in first , and when they start to turn color a bit add garlic slices
4. continue cooking about 4 minutes or so , then flip fillets
5. fry until cooked through , and fish flakes easily with a fork-- this will depend entirely on the thickness of your fillets , so you will need to watch them carefully
6. the garlic should turn a dark golden brown , but not be burned , if you notice that the garlic is starting to burn , spoon it over the fish , so it is no longer in contact with the pan
7. serve with freshly squeezed lemon juice and garnish with chopped parsley
demonstrations.review:
I was underwhelmed by this recipe. It was pretty bland and didn't have enough going on for my taste. I feel like it's not a recipe, just a cooking method- saute fish in olive oil, voila! For me, tilapia tastes like dirt, and you have to add a little bit of something-something to cover that up. I liked the idea of slicing the garlic, because it was easier to move around in the pan than if it were crushed/minced. 
I ate this with roasted broccoli and sriracha mayo, which definitely helped to liven it up a bit.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s italian melt in your mouth meatballs

cooking the meatballs in simmering pasta sauce  will not only add so much extra flavor to the sauce the meatballs will be melt-in-your-mouth tender, you may of course oven-bake the meatballs for about 25 minutes,  --- don't be afraid to add in more parmesan cheese and a little more milk, there is no need to measure exactly, this recipe is pretty much foolproof, leftover cooked meatballs make a wonderful pizza topping just slice thinly and freeze until ready to use ----- these also make wonderful juicy burgers shaped into patties-- for more of my tried and true recipes check out my food blog at www.kittencalskitchen.com

1. mix all ingredients together in a large bowl
2. shape into small meatballs
3. drop the meatballs into simmering pasta sauce , do not stir for at least 20 minutes or you will risk breaking the meatballs
4. continue cooking in the simmering sauce for another 20 minutes
5. after the 40 minutes cooking time continue cooking your sauce with the meatballs in for as long as desired
demonstrations.review: This recipe hardly needs any more 5-star ratings, but I have to add mine anyway. This was my first attempt at meatballs and I can't find anything to change to make it better!  I did sub Italian sausage for about 1/2 lb of the beef, which changed the texture (but I prefer the taste of sausage!). I found the recipe as written to be a little too wet to hold together, so next time I'll add less than 1/3 c milk and more breadcrumbs. I did half the meatballs in the oven and the other half in the sauce, and I preferred the taste of the baked ones, but they were both great!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chicken  shrimp and andouille jambalaya

a cajun classic, meal in one pot! have the hot sauce ready to splash on. serve with some crusty french bread, a nice crisp salad, and some of your favorite wine. :)

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees f
2. in a large pan or dutch oven , brown chicken in hot oil on both sides
3. remove and drain
4. add andouille , onion , celery , bell pepper , thyme , oregano , paprika , salt , and cayenne pepper to the pan , cooking and stirring for about 5 minutes until onions are tender
5. add rice , tomatoes with juice , and broth
6. bring to a boil
7. place rice mixture in a baking dish or oven-proof casserole
8. top with chicken
9. cover and bake at 350 degrees f for 40-45 minutes or until rice and chicken are done and tender
10. stir in shrimp , parsley , and green onions
11. cover and cook 5-8 minutes longer or until shrimp curl and turn bright pink and serve
demonstrations.review: This was good! I added chopped garlic in with the sauteeing veggies and did not add the extra salt (didn't think it needed it!). I sprinkled the chicken thighs with Cajun seasoning but next time I wouldn't use them at all- why get a pan dirty- and would just saute chicken breasts in with the veggies. I served this with Louisiana hot sauce and it was great!

target.recipe_text:
ultimate bruschetta

i came across this in a homemakers magazine and it was an instant favourite, we have used this recipe ever since(with a little of our own tweaking!)the longer the mixture sits the better!( for prep time i just put the 1 hour standing time, add how ever long it will take you to chop your other ingredients). cook time is just how long it takes you to toast your bread. everyone we serve this to really likes it.

1. cut tomatoes in half , squeeze out seeds and juice
2. chop into small dice and place in bowl
3. add onion , garlic , basil , vinegar , half the olive oil , salt and pepper to your taste
4. let stand at room temperature for about 1 hour , drain liquid
5. on broil , toast bread on both sides until golden
6. quickly brush one side of each slice with remaining olive oil
7. spoon tomato mixture on top& serve
8. also we have made this using dried basil instead of fresh and although it does not call for it in the recipe we also use some fresh parsley
target.review: This is the lightest bruschetta I've ever had.  Nothing was overpowering, and tasted absolutely wonderful.  It reminded me of the bruschetta that the finest Italian restaurants serve.  Great recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
big john s baked escargot

while not everyone enjoys escargots, i've converted a large number with this recipe.

1. rinse escargot in a colander in order to remove any sand and set aside
2. grind spices together in a mortar until fine
3. clean mushrooms and completely remove stems , making sure to create a place for escargot
4. place in a large skillet with 1 tablespoon of the butter and saut over medium heat for 10 minutes , stirring often
5. remove from heat and place mushroom caps on escargot dishes stem side up
6. heat oven to 350 degrees f
7. chop half of the mushroom stems up and place in small sauce pan with remaining butter , garlic and spices , discard the rest
8. cook over medium heat for 3 minutes
9. place one escargot on each mushroom cap
10. spoon butter mixture over escargots and sprinkle with parmesan
11. place escargot dishes onto a cookie sheet and bake in oven for 15 minutes or until cheese is browned and sauce is bubbling
12. use bread for cleaning up the sauce
demonstrations.review: I took a chance and made this for a dinner party.  Everyone raved over them.  The escargot came out perfect, meaty not chewy and the flavours complimented each other to perfection.  My b/f ate 16 of them!  This is the first time I've made these and they weren't overcooked or bland tasting.  Thanks for a great recipe. I have my dinner guests begging for it now.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
4 minute spicy garlic shrimp

recipe is originally from the food network courtesy of rachael ray, but i tweaked it to fit our tastes. very quick & easy shrimp recipe that's done on the stovetop. if your tastes desire spicy & garlic, then this recipe is just for you.

1. heat a large skillet over medium high heat
2. add olive oil , garlic , red pepper flakes , and shrimp
3. season with grill seasoning or salt & pepper
4. cook shrimp 3 minutes or until just pink
5. toss with lemon zest , juice , & chopped parsley
6. remove shrimp to a serving platter , leaving the garlic cloves in the pan
demonstrations.review: I have a fatal allergy to shellfish and tried this recipe with the soy shrimp product (sometimes I'll be adventurous).  I have to admit I was pretty surprised on how this turned out.  It was a huge hit around here and thanks so much for a very simple and easy recipe to follow.  My son makes these all the time now. - cgyvegan

demonstrations.recipe_text:
3 onion  mushroom and garlic soup

this is a buttery, hearty, warming soup. has leeks, red onions, scallions, lots of garlic, and dried porcini mushrooms. you can top it with cheese if you like.

1. melt butter and olive oil in a large pot
2. saut leeks , onions , salt , pepper , sugar , 8-10 minutes adding garlic and cook 3 more minutes
3. add strained chopped mushrooms , water , beef base , strained liquid from mushrooms and parsley
4. bring to a boil lower heat to a simmer and cook for 20 more minutes
5. if desired , toast bread in over and top with your favorite cheese and place on top of soup and serve topped with a garnish of scallions and pepper
6. for vegetarian use only the vegetable base
demonstrations.review: This is the best homemade onion soup I've ever made.  I followed the recipe exactly.  To darken the broth I added 2 tblsp of soy sauce and 3 dashes of worchestire sauce.  Thanks for a great recipe, we are adding it to our xmas menu.

target.recipe_text:
cashew chicken curry

an epicurious recipe i tried recently and loved! easy chicken curry with a nice nutty sauce.

1. heat butter in a 5- to 6-quart wide heavy pot over moderately low heat until foam subsides , then cook onions , garlic , and ginger , stirring , until softened , about 5 minutes
2. add curry powder , salt , cumin , and cayenne and cook , stirring , 2 minutes
3. add chicken and cook , stirring to coat , 3 minutes
4. add tomatoes , including juice , and cilantro and bring to a simmer , then cover and simmer gently , stirring occasionally , until chicken is cooked through , about 40 minutes
5. just before serving: pulse cashews in a food processor or electric coffee / spice grinder until very finely ground , then add to curry along with yogurt and simmer gently , uncovered , stirring , until sauce is thickened , about 5 minutes
target.review: This was fantastic.  My husband said it was better than anything he'd eaten in a restaurant.  I cut the salt in half and it was still plenty flavorful.  Served it on basmati rice with a side of sauteed purple cabbage.  Not a fast meal -- better for a weekend or when you have a good bit of time.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
dad s best brisket

my dad knows how much i love this. thanks for the recipe.

1. center brisket on a large heavy piece of foil in a roaster
2. sprinkle with liquid smoke
3. sprinkle brisket with celery salt , garlic salt , onion salt , and pepper
4. fold sides of foil over to seal
5. refrigerate overnight
6. 6 1 / 2 hour before serving , open foil and season with salt , pepper , and worcestershire sauce
7. reseal and cook in a slow oven at 300 degrees for 5 hours
8. uncover and pour barbecue sauce over brisket
9. cook 1 additional hour , uncovered
10. let sit 20 minutes before slicing
demonstrations.review: Made this for a holiday meal.  It was excellent and oh so tender and flavorful.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
the best browned beef stew ever

i originally found this recipe at recipe goldmine but have added and subtracted after trial and error. the original recipe called for a 10 oz pkg of frozen peas to be added during the last 15 minutes of cooking. i usually add a little rosemary and cayenne. can add the spices you wish. this is very good!

1. put flour , salt and pepper in a large ziploc bag
2. heat oil over medium heat in a large dutch oven
3. place meat in bag with the flour and shake until well coated
4. shake off meat pieces and add them to the oil and stir until slightly browned , add remaining flour from the bag and the finely chopped onion
5. stir until well browned
6. add finely chopped carrot and next 4 ingredients
7. cover and cook over low heat for 1 1 / 2 hours
8. add diced potatoes , carrots , and onions , cook for another 45 minutes or until potatoes are tender
demonstrations.review: Easy and excellent taste.  Takes a while so it's better for a weekend meal but so worth it.  My son ate seconds, a rare feat!  We added back the peas and also a few finely chopped mushrooms.  Yum.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
absolute best ever lasagna

my family's favorite. this is a very meaty lasagna. we prefer it with cottage cheese, but you can easily substitute ricotta.

1. brown ground meat , onion and garlic
2. add salt , pepper , parsley , oregano , basil , chopped tomatoes with juice
3. stirring until well mixed
4. cover and simmer 1 hour
5. cook lasagna noodles according to package directions
6. drain and set aside
7. spray a 13 x 9" baking pan with cooking spray
8. combine riccota cheese , eggs , pepper , 2 tablespoons parsley , parmesan cheese and 1 / 2 1lb of mozzarella cheese
9. in a lasagna pan , layer noodles , meat sauce , and cheese mixture
10. repeat
11. top off with layer of noodles
12. sprinkle evenly with remaining mozzarella cheese
13. make sure to cover noodles completely
14. bake at 375f for 40-60 minutes , or until cheese mixture is thoroughly melted
15. (i cover w / foil for about 40 minutes , then uncover for 15-20 minutes
16. let sit for 15-20 minutes before cutting and serving
demonstrations.review: YUM. Made this polenta instead of noodles and all italian sausage, no beef. So tasty.

target.recipe_text:
kansas city steak and vegetable soup

a hearty beef soup with chunks of sirloin. very yummy.

1. heat the oil in a large soup pot over medium-high heat
2. season the beef with salt and pepper
3. add the beef to the soup pot and brown in the hot oil , stirring frequently
4. add the onion , garlic , celery , and carrots
5. cook and stir about 4 minutes or until the vegetables begin to soften
6. add the soup mixes , water , and potatoes
7. bring to a boil
8. change heat to medium-low and simmer 45 minutes to 1 hour or until beef is tender
9. add in the corn and green beans and cook until beans are tender
10. adjust seasoning to taste with salt and pepper if needed
target.review: Easy to make and a hit with the family.  I couldn't find any soup mix brand that came in beef tomato so I added beef broth and half a can of tomato paste instead.  I served it with herb and cheese biscuits and the leftovers went quickly also.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
easy zucchini and ground beef pizza casserole

this is a fast and really tasty dish!  you can use your own favorite pizza sauce for this, i use my own recipe #65641.

1. set oven to 400f
2. grease a 13x9 pan
3. place zucchini in strainer
4. sprinkle with salt
5. let drain for 10 minutes
6. squeeze out moisture
7. combine zucchini with eggs , parmesan cheese , and half of the cheddar and mozzarella cheese
8. press into greased 13x9 baking pan
9. bake at 400f for 20 minutes
10. meanwhile , brown ground beef with garlic and onions , season with salt and pepper
11. drain any fat , and add / mix the tomato sauce
12. spoon over baked zucchini mixture
13. top with remaining cheeses , and sprinkle with green pepper
14. return to oven and bake for another 20 minutes more
demonstrations.review: I am always looking for things to do with my abundant zucchini crop and this one is a keeper.  I split the recipe into two smaller dishes and had one for dinner and put the other in the freezer for later.  I am not sure how well it will freeze but I will let you know.  Hubby even liked it and he is not a big zucchini or casserole lover. Thanks for a great recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
italian pork hoagies

so yummy. i adapted this from toh's quick cooking magazine.

1. place hoagie buns , cut side up on baking sheet
2. spread pizza sauce on the bottom half of each bun
3. top evenly with pork slices
4. drizzle with salad dressing
5. sprinkle with desired amount of salt and pepper
6. sprinkle with mozzarella cheese
7. bake at 350f for 5-10 minutes or until cheese is melted and tops of buns are lightly toasted
8. place tops of buns over the sandwiches
demonstrations.review:
It is not very often I find a recipe that both the hubby and 4 kids like.  This is one of those recipes, each gave you a star!!!
Thanks for a great, quick way to use leftover pork!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
paradise pumpkin pie

looking for something different from the same old pumpkin pie? this is a wonderful alternative! how about a pastry shell filled with a creamy layer of cheesecake, a layer of sweet and spicy pumpkin,and topped off with a crunchy pecan praline topping.absolutely the best!

1. beat cream cheese until smooth
2. add sugar and vanilla
3. mix well
4. add egg , beat until smooth
5. spread over bottom of pie shell
6. chill 30 minutes
7. beat filling ingredients until smooth
8. carefully pour over cream cheese layer
9. cover edge of pie with foil to prevent crust from over-browning
10. bake at 350 degrees for 30 minutes
11. remove foil
12. bake 25 minutes longer
13. meanwhile , mix flour , brown sugar and margarine until crumbly
14. mix in pecans
15. sprinkle over pie
16. bake 10-15 minutes more or until knife inserted near center comes out clean
demonstrations.review: This takes a little longer than a traditional pumpkin pie but boy is it worth it!  Thanks Carrie for a pie that I'll be fixing every fall.  Everyone that tried it wanted the recipe.  It was a big hit.

target.recipe_text:
easiest peanut butter fudge

this is unbelievably easy. i prefer using creamy peanut butter for this mouth-watering fudge. however, the chunky style works just as well.

1. in saucepan , bring sugar and milk to a boil
2. boil for 3 minutes
3. add peanut butter , marshmallow creme and vanilla
4. mix well
5. quickly pour into a buttered 8-inch square pan
6. chill until set
7. cut into squares
target.review: Very good and easy... Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
jiffy scalloped corn casserole

nan

1. beat eggs slightly
2. add sour cream , butter and corn
3. fold in dry jiffy corn mix
4. put in baking disk
5. sprinkle cheese on top
6. bake at 350 for 45-60 minutes
7. make sure center comes out clean
8. another rendition is to mix in the cheese-- this was very good since it spread the cheese throughout the corn
demonstrations.review: Love it!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
bar  cheese

a friend shared this with me last year. i have made a batch a month since then. it is an adaptation of a famous restaurants signature cheese. everyone likes it. it makes a great present. it will keep for extended periods when refrigerated but mine has never lasted more than a week. enjoy.

1. in a large sauce pan over low heat , melt the velveeta
2. add the jar of horseradish and mix
3. allow this to heat on low for 15 minutes , stirring often
4. add the mayo , worcestershire , and tabasco
5. mix and allow to heat another 10 minutes , stirring often
6. cool slightly and pour into 4 or 5 containers
7. refrigerate
8. serve on your choice of crackers
demonstrations.review:
This was awesome and so easy! The only thing I did different was I heated everything together at the same time so I never had any problems with the cheese scorching... Thanks for an awesome recipe... :)

p.s. I tried it as a sandwich spread as well and loved it...

demonstrations.recipe_text:
creamed carrots  recipe from the titanic  ship   not the movie

nan

1. peel and slice carrots
2. cook , covered , in a small amount of water over medium heat until tender
3. drain
4. in a medium size skillet , melt butter over medium-high heat
5. saut onions in butter until tender
6. stir in flour , salt , pepper and sugar
7. cook for 1 minute
8. gradually add milk , stirring constantly until mixture thickens and starts to boil
9. pour over cooked carrots and stir to coat
demonstrations.review: I left out the sugar and added dill... Used McCormicks "Hot Shot" for pepper and a couple grinds of McCormicks "Black Peppercorn Grinder" Sooooo yummy!

target.recipe_text:
cranberry ginger drop cookies

perfect for fall.

1. heat oven to 375f lightly grease cookie sheets
2. combine sugar , brown sugar and butter in large mixer bowl
3. beat on medium speed until well mixed
4. add milk and egg
5. beat until smooth
6. add flour , baking powder , ground ginger and baking soda
7. beat on low speed until well mixed
8. gently stir in cranberries , pecans and crystallized ginger
9. drop dough by rounded teaspoonfuls 2 inches apart onto greased cookie sheet
10. bake for 9 to 12 minutes or until edges are light golden brown
11. immediately remove from cookie sheet
12. cool on wire rack
13. combine powdered sugar and enough milk for desired glaze consistency in small bowl
14. mix well
15. spread glaze on cooled cookies
target.review: These sound so good I want to write them into my cookbook before even trying them.. as I can't get any cranberries here, will have to wait.. looking forward to this recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
tropical fruit salad with banana cream

dessert

1. cut a thick slice off each side of the mango to reveal the large , flat stone
2. cut the flesh away from the stone , peel the fruit , then cut into slices
3. halve the papaya , scoop out the black seeds , peel away the skin then slice the fruit
4. cut the top and skin away from the pineapple
5. cut it into quarters then core and slice it
6. mix the fruits with the juice of the oranges , then chill until ready to serve
7. mash the bananas and stir them into the fromage frais
8. spoon the fruits into bowls and top with the fromage frais and a sprinkling of the muscavado sugar
demonstrations.review: thanks for the banana cream idea!  will be perfect with the kiwi granita i've just made for tonights bbq!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
oat  coconut and raspberry bars

this recipe comes from coup de pouce and can be frozen.

1. spread 1 / 2 cup of coconut on a small baking sheet
2. cook in a preheated oven of 375 f for about 5 minutes or until coconut is golden
3. let cool
4. in a bowl , mix flour , brown sugar and salt
5. add butter , and with a pastry knife or 2 knives , mix until the mixture looks like rough crumbs
6. add oats and toasted coconut and stir well
7. set aside 1 / 3 cup of the oat mixture
8. press remaining oats in a cake pan of 9 inches in the side
9. spread the raspberry preserve , then sprinkle with the oats you set aside and remaining coconut
10. cook in the center of a preheated oven of 375 f for about 15 minutes or until the top is golden
11. put the pan on a rack and let cool
12. cut in 16 bars
demonstrations.review:
Unbelievably yummy!!  Have made these twice now, once with the coconut as stated in recipe (dried coconut here in France is exceptionally dry and absolutely not sweet in the least, so ours did not have a problem there, as reviewer sam found)
and the second time with flaked almonds and half the jam used was apricot.  Found that raspberry is by far superior in these, but equally liked both the toasted coconut and toasted flaked almonds.  Thank you so much for the recipe, will be making these regularly as soon as the weather goes cool again!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
big john s killer caesar salad dressing

this is the result of years of trying to create the best caesar dressing in the world & i believe this recipe comes very close. (bold, don't you think?)

1. combine all ingredients in a medium bowl
2. whisk for 1 minute
3. cover and refrigerate for a minimum of 2 hours
demonstrations.review: I've just made this, and it already tastes FABULOUS! No egg, don't have any and seems extra as it would originally have been the binding agent to form the mayonnaise if whisking it all up from scratch.Thank you for an awesome recipe!

target.recipe_text:
easy crawfish etouffee

there are hundreds of recipes for crawfish etouffee. this is the old fashion way to cook crawfish etouffee. very simple yet very flavorful.

1. in dutch oven melt butter over medium heat
2. add onions , bell pepper , celery and garlic
3. saute vegetables until soft , about 30 to 45 minutes
4. add crawfish tails and seasonings
5. cover and simmer for 10 minutes
6. add the mushroom sauce , let it simmer for 5 minutes
7. add to crawfish mixture , cover and simmer for 10 more minutes
8. serve on hot rice
target.review: A TEN STAR recipe for sure!!!<br/>This is a fantastic recipe....it is almost idetical to my late sister's mother-in-law's recipe.  Effie was Cajun and raised a large family with wonderful recipes like this.  My sister sometimes "extended" the recipe with crabmeat or shrimp, and usually added a Tbls of tomato paste or ketchup to the sauce.  She used Tony Chacere's seasoning (of course!!!), & hot sauce to taste.  Yummmmm!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
stove top tamale pie

this is a quick and easy one-dish meal.

1. in a large skillet , brown ground beef over medium-high heat
2. drain
3. stir in tomato sauce , beans , water and taco seasoning mix
4. bring to a boil
5. reduce heat , cover and simmer 5 minutes
6. prepare corn muffin mix according to package directions
7. drop small spoonfuls of muffin batter over meat mixture in a skillet
8. cover and cook over medium-low heat 15-17 minutes or until corn bread is done
9. top with cheese and green onion
10. cover and cook over low heat until cheese melts
demonstrations.review:
This was WONDERFUL!!! & was super easy too!

This is such an versitile recipe & is easily adaptable to whatever ingredients you have on hand. I added diced green chilies & chopped onion to the ground beef as it browned. I substituted a can of Hot Chili beans in place of thre kidney beans & used a pkgt of chili seasoning instead of taco seasoning as I wanted to use it up.
Could also add some whole kernal corn. Topped the cooked cornbread with a half can of sliced black olives then the shredded cheese (use whatever you like....Mexican blend, sharp, etc.)
Oh, I omitted the green onions...OK, I forgot them :-}but my DH LOVED it & this's what counts!!!! He said to put a star by this recipe! How about I just put 5 STARS instead?!!!

This is going to be a regular at our house now & a very pleasant addition to our menus after 41 yrs of marriage. Thanks Fluffy!!!!!



Read more: http://www.food.com/recipe/stove-top-tamale-pie-78897#ixzz1WcY7O2fl

demonstrations.recipe_text:
absolute best ever lasagna

my family's favorite. this is a very meaty lasagna. we prefer it with cottage cheese, but you can easily substitute ricotta.

1. brown ground meat , onion and garlic
2. add salt , pepper , parsley , oregano , basil , chopped tomatoes with juice
3. stirring until well mixed
4. cover and simmer 1 hour
5. cook lasagna noodles according to package directions
6. drain and set aside
7. spray a 13 x 9" baking pan with cooking spray
8. combine riccota cheese , eggs , pepper , 2 tablespoons parsley , parmesan cheese and 1 / 2 1lb of mozzarella cheese
9. in a lasagna pan , layer noodles , meat sauce , and cheese mixture
10. repeat
11. top off with layer of noodles
12. sprinkle evenly with remaining mozzarella cheese
13. make sure to cover noodles completely
14. bake at 375f for 40-60 minutes , or until cheese mixture is thoroughly melted
15. (i cover w / foil for about 40 minutes , then uncover for 15-20 minutes
16. let sit for 15-20 minutes before cutting and serving
demonstrations.review: This is EXACTLY the same as the lasagna recipe I got from my best friend back in high school...in the late 60's.   It is INCREDIBLE & believe me, I've made lots of lasagnas over the past 45 years!  This recipe takes a bit more time, but what good Italian cooking doesn't? Leftovers freeze well too...if there are any.  I've even caught my dear SIL making a "sandwich" using cold lasagna, sliced into thick slices.  Oh...be sure to use a deep straight-sided baking dish. The Bobby Flay line of stoneware sold at Kohl's has a very nice one with handles that is great for this lasagna. This recipe is so generous it will overflow a standard 9x13 glass pan. And be sure to let it "rest" about 10 minutes before cutting or it will ooze it's cheesy goodness all over the plate!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
creamy hash browns  aka    evil potatoes

the chef at the captain lord mansion, a bed and breakfast in kennebunkport, maine served this side dish at breakfast one morning and was kind enough to share the recipe with our group. i also think it would be great with ham or roast beef as a side dish. the chef also told us that he had used the same "sauce" ingredients with cooked elbow macaroni and cubed ham, baking it for about 30 minutes.

1. mix all ingredients together except for the onion rings
2. pour into a 9 x 13 baking dish that has been sprayed with cooking spray
3. bake at 350 degrees for 50 minutes
4. remove from oven and sprinkle with the crushed onion rings
5. return to oven and bake an additional 5 to 8 minutes , or until onion rings are slightly browned and heated through
demonstrations.review:
I can't believe this hasn't had more reviews...it is incredibly delicious!!!  I think I read in a review that someone added a 1 lb pkg of hot breakfast sausage, browned & drained??? At any rate, that's how I've always made it & it is soooooo yummy!  This year I decided to increase the Ranch dressing to 1 cup due to the added sausage & that was just what it needed.  It would be perfect as written too, without the sausage, but my husband said "why fix it if it ain't broke", right? It's a very versatile recipe.    
My husband and both sons-in-law requested the dish again this year for Christmas.  When the men in the family ask for it, well you know it's a winner!!! Figured I'd better review this great recipe.
Thanks so much for the original posting....this is a family favorite now!

target.recipe_text:
cauliflower au gratin

nan

1. preheat oven to 375
2. lightly butter 6-cup dish
3. in pot of boiling water , cook cauliflower for 3 to 5 min or until tender-crisp
4. drain and transfer to baking dish , sprinkle with red pepper
5. in non stick saucepan , melt butter
6. add flour and garlic , cook stirring over low heat for a minute or so
7. add milk bring to simmer and stir constantly until thickened
8. add cheddar and parmesan , dill , salt and pepper , stir until cheese melts
9. pour over califlower
10. toppig: mix parmesan and bread crumbs and sprinkle on top
11. bake , uncovered for 25 to 30 minutes
target.review:
A great tasting dish that we both loved. Made it pretty much as written mixing 1 red potato in with half cauliflower and half broccoli. I will make this again. I will however mix vegetables with half of the cheese sauce before putting in in the baking dish and add a little more milk or cream.
Topping was easy. Dropped a piece of whole wheat bread into the food processor and turned on  for a few seconds. Instant bread crumbs and minimal expense. Added the grated cheese to the breadcrumbs (added a little cheddar also) to make it extra crunchy.
Just happened to have some fresh dill and it made the dish pretty and made it taste WONDERFUL. If you have some in the garden, fridge, or freezer, suggest you use it here. Use what the recipe calls for also.
Give it a try - it is in our permanent cookbook for repeat recipes. Hey, it is also easy and a snap to make with things often in the fridge.
Jim in So. Calif.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
suppertime turnip greens

my husband loves any type of greens. so i make this for him, he loves it. it's really simple.

1. remove and discard tems from greens
2. i do this by rollin up leaves , from stem to
3. coarsely chop leaves
4. bring 4 cups water and bacon slice to a boil in a large dutch oven
5. add greens , seasoned salt , and remining ingredients
6. cook over medium heat 35 to 45 minutes or until tender
demonstrations.review: This is a very simple, very basic, low fat, low sugar, and low salt recipe with a broth and resultant greens that are very easy to make. The simple broth tasted so good that even my cat drank my bowl clean (yes, I know it was the tiny hint of bacon grease and odor). It is nutritious and an easy way to get rid of a pile of turnip greens (I used greens from 4 large turnips). My wife did not care for it but she cannot be taken as any kind of judge as she usually rejects all greens unless in a very heavy and unhealthy cheese sauce. I found it very good and so simple to make and I will make it again as I have a truckload of turnips out in the garden. I used recipe #197885 (cut in half) for the bottoms and my wife said they were "delicious" (Slow Roasted Balsamic Turnips) so I'd end up with a "slew of greens" to fix again. Enjoy! Jim in So. California

demonstrations.recipe_text:
linguine with broccoli and bay scallops

an attractive and yummy combination from the frog commissary cookbook.  though i've never tried it, this would probably work with shrimp as well.

1. peel broccoli stems and cut into 1 / 4 inch thick slices
2. blanch broccoli in boiling salted water , drain and refresh under cold water , drain and set aside
3. cook linguine til al dente in a large pot of boiling water
4. drain well and toss with 1 / 4 cup butter
