5. heat remaining 1 / 2 cup butter in a large skillet
6. add garlic and saute till softened
7. add scallops , salt and pepper
8. saute 3 minutes or till scallops are opaque
9. add broccoli and heat 1 minute
10. add pasta and heat through
11. add cheese and serve at once
demonstrations.review: A basic good type of family recipe that will be accepted well by adults and children. My wife LOVED this dish. I used the little broccoli I had and a few spears of asparagus, a couple of califlower florets, a shallot, a quarter sized piece of fresh ginger, a dash of dried red pepper flakes, and pepper and salt to taste. To punch up the acidity as suggested by others, I added halfed cherry tomatoes (and the wine)and for extra color, the rest of a red bell pepper. The extra red vegetables also made it look very pretty. To make the sauce extra creamy, I added 1/4 cup of white wine, 1/4 cup of chicken stock, and a heaping tsp. of corn starch right at the end. Don't overcook the pasta or vegetables with this dish. Take the pasta out al dente and using the same water, cook the cut to size fresh vegetables, and remove also when just cooked al dente. This way your entire dish will all be cooked to each of its needs and it won't be like a mushy crock pot meal but more like a Asian stir fry. It is easy and fast to put together in spite of the involved steps. Jim in So. Calif.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
asian style green beans

a great addition to your next asian inspired meal.  the recipe is adapted from southern living.

1. cook green beans in boiling water 4 to 6 minutes or until crisp-tender
2. drain
3. plunge into ice water to stop the cooking process
4. drain
5. saut green onions , garlic , and ginger in hot sesame oil in a large nonstick skillet over medium heat 1 minute
6. add green beans and bell pepper
7. cook 1 minute
8. add oyster sauce and pepper , stirring until thoroughly heated
9. sprinkle with almonds , if desired
demonstrations.review:
A great way to make your green beans shine into a new taste. Didn't have the roasted red peppers so omitted. It would have been nice for color but a fresh red sweet pepper would have worked just as well if I had one. I did add a pinch of red pepper flakes, a rib of bock choy, a few sliced mushrooms, a tsp. of rice wine vinegar for a little extra bite, and a tiny bit of cornstarch to make sure the juice stuck to the veggies. Instead of almonds, I used the traditional sesame seeds that I toasted a few minutes in a small pan first.
Very delicious and a great side dish to get in an additional green item into your daily intake.
Definitely will make again!
PS - If you don't have oyster sauce, use soy sauce or hoisin  sauce instead. In addition, if you are using toasted sesame oil as I did, cook up your initial flavors in vegetable or peanut oil and add the toasted sesame right at the end for seasoning. I was taught that toasted sesame oil is for seasoning only as it has a low smoke point. It also smells so great that you want the aroma really fresh. Hope this all helps.
Jim in So. Calif.

target.recipe_text:
our favourite lemon loaf

this is soooo nummmmy!! for lemon lovers. very good warm or cold. (have been making this for years and cannot remember where it came from, probably from my mom.)

1. in a large bowl , cream butter and sugar
2. add eggs , one at a time , beating until creamy
3. blend in milk
4. in another bowl , mix together flour , baking powder , salt and lemon rind
5. pour into batter
6. stir to moisten
7. scrape into greased 9 x 5 inch loaf pan
8. bake in 350f degree oven for 55 to 60 minutes
9. cool in pan for 5 minutes
10. remove to rack and while still hot , with a toothpick poke holes all over the top of the loaf , and spoon glaze evenly over
11. cool
12. glaze: combine lemon juice and sugar in saucepan
13. stir and heat till sugar is dissolved
14. spoon evenly over top of hot loaf
target.review: Years ago I'd had a great lemon cake and always wanted to find the perfect recipe....I think I just did!!  This was really yummy, lemony and wonderful! I follwed your recipe exactly as stated. The only deviation that I made was to add a tablespoon of lemon juice to the batter just before putting it in the oven....for that extra kick of lemon flavour. The glaze was really the 'icing on the cake'! My family and I loved the loaf and I know its going to be a regular  feature in our house. Thanks for sharing.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
perfect chocolate brownies

this is the best brownie recipe i've ever used and i've used several!

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees
2. grease a 9x13" pan
3. melt shortening in a large saucepan over low heat , then stir in cocoa
4. remove from heat
5. mix in sugar and vanilla then mix in eggs one at a time
6. stir in remaining ingredients then stir in nuts
7. bake for 30 minutes
8. cool completely , before cutting into 2x2" squares
9. i have read all the great reviews and learned from them , thank you all
10. now i line my pan with buttered alumunin foil or parchment paper
11. this works very well
demonstrations.review: Very good, indeed! Very easy to make and wonderful results. Will be making them often...thanks for posting the recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
asian banana chai bread

never tasted it, don't know what it's like, but sounds interesting. not as nice as the easiest (non-machine) white bread in the world. i've tasted that, its gorgeous, as is the chef.

1. in a medium bowl mix together flour , baking powder , and salt
2. in a separate bowl mix sugar , cream cheese , and eggs until light and fluffy
3. mix mashed bananas and chai into cream cheese mixture
4. add flour mixture and mix until smooth
5. pour mixture into a greased 9x5 inch loaf pan
6. bake in a preheated 350 degree f oven for 60 minutes
7. cool on rack
8. remove from pan after 10 minutes
demonstrations.review: How cute!! No, I haven't made the banana bread but believe me I will now! Celine and Scar I wish you both the very best in life. Long live the web!! God bless :))

demonstrations.recipe_text:
old fashioned date bars

wrap in festive packaging to give as hostess gifts!

1. preheat oven to 375f
2. cream together butter and sugar until light and fluffy
3. beat in eggs one at a time
4. stir in vanilla
5. mix together flour , baking powder , and baking soda
6. and gradually add to the creamed mixture
7. fold in the dates and nuts
8. spread the batter evenly in a greased 13x9 baking pan and bake at 375f for 25 minutes or until golden
9. cool in pan
10. cut into approximately 24 bars
demonstrations.review: I'm surprised no one else has made these delicious bars before! I made them yesterday and what an absolute hit they were with everyone! I followed the recipe exactly as given...the only deviation that I did do was to substitute pecans with walnuts (because I did not have pecans). The date bars were amazing! I will definitely be making them again and again. In Hindi, 'bar-bar', means 'again and again'. Well this is what my family calls your date bars....'date bar-bar'! Needless to say, I will be making them bar-bar!! A definite keeper and deserves a big 5 star rating by any standards. Thank you for sharing your recipe.

target.recipe_text:
lime shrimp in tortillas

this recipe was published by mccormick/schilling.  i found the recipe card on a display in my local grocery store.  i haven't tried it yet, but plan to soon.  it appears to be quick and easy to prepare and tasty to boot.

1. combine lime juice , oil , garlic pepper and parsley flakes in zippered plastic bag
2. add shrimp and marinate 15 minutes
3. saute onion and green pepper in 2 teaspoons oil for 3-4 minutes
4. add shrimp and cook 4-5 minutes
5. serve with tortillas and desired condiments
target.review: I made this and marinated the shrimp for about an hour...because i LOVE lime and wanted it to be really flavorful...to be honest it wasn't what i expected...i could barely tast the lime and I put WAY more than the recipe called for...we still ate it but i dont think i will make it again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
stir fried shrimp with spicy orange sauce

serve over rice or udon noodles. we just nibbled on them! quite yummy and love the sambal! from cooking light.

1. place shrimp in medium bowl , sprinkle with cornstarch , toss well to coat and set aside
2. combine juice , soy sauce , honey , vinegar , and sambal , stirring until well mixed
3. set aside
4. heat canola oil in large nonstick skillet over med-hi heat
5. add minced ginger and garlic , stir fry for 15 seconds or until fragrant
6. add shrimp mixture , stir-fry for 3 minutes
7. add juice mixture and onions , cook 2 minutes or until sauce thickens and shrimp are done , stirring frequently
8. serve immediately
demonstrations.review: Yum! I made this for the first time today. I didn't have cornstarch so I coated the shrimp with flour. It was good, but I can imagine cornstarch tastes better. I didn't have sambal oelek so I added chili flakes and brown sugar. I also added siracha sauce to the sauce. I thought it needed more time to thicken, so I took out the shrimp so it wouldn't overcook and I thought it was just perfect. I will make this again and again!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
ground turkey tortilla casserole

this is a recipe that i adapted from a few other tortilla casseroles and it is a quick & easy tummy satisfier!

1. brown turkey and small onion until meat is completely done
2. add taco seasoning packet and follow directions for cooking on back
3. spray non-stick casserole dish with non-stick cooking spray
4. cut flour tortillas into bite size pieces and layer 1 / 2 of tortillas on bottom of casserole dish
5. add 1 / 2 of the cheese , sour cream , salsa and black beans
6. start with the remaining tortillas and repeat layering
7. you may top with extra cheese or salsa if preferred
8. other options include: corn , red pepper , green pepper , jalapenos , or any other ingredient
9. play with ingredients , if you like more sour cream , simply add more , if you like less , add less
10. don't be afraid to test different options
11. bake at 350 until all cheese is melted and everything is heated thoroughly
12. you may wish to cover the dish with foil to prevent overbaking the top -- then removing it for the last 5-10 minutes
demonstrations.review: MAde this with ground beef because I couldn't find the turkey in the freezer. This was AWESOME! The flavor was really wonderful and to be honest, I didn't expect this meal to be so good. I thought it would taste like an enchiliada casserole but it tastes completely different. Besides the meat, I made it exactly to the recipe...and I wouldn't change anything! I will make again and again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
grilled lime shrimp

nan

1. mix together the first 8 ingredients in a bowl
2. add shrimp
3. toss to coat
4. let stand at room temperature for 10 minutes to marinate
5. thread shrimp on metal skewers
6. reserve marinade
7. place skewered shrimp on grill over medium heat
8. cook 3-7 minutes or until shrimp turn pink , turning once and brushing with marinade occasionally
demonstrations.review: I was excited about this recipe but it ended up being a big fail. It was SUPER salty. To the point where it was inedible and I had to toss all of them. I made exactly to recipe including the grilling directions. The shrimp were super tough. I know it wasn't the shrimp either because I made a different recipe on the same day with the same batch of shrimp. Sad...and sorry for the bad review but having to throw it out really sucked

target.recipe_text:
soy glazed salmon with cucumber avocado salad

another delicious recipe from food network magazine july/aug. 2012 edition. the recipe called for 4 salmon filets, but i only did 2 and still made the salad as is, to make a more substantial meal for my husband and i. of course you can always make 4 portions if you like.

1. preheat oven to 400
2. rub fish all over with 1 / 2 tsp of the sesame oil and season lightly with salt
3. place in oven and bake 5 minutes
4. in a small microwavable bowl , combine the honey , 2 tsp soy sauce and the cornstarch
5. microwave on high for 30 seconds
6. baste the filets with the honey soy mixture and return to the oven to continue baking for another 9 minutes
7. in a large bowl , mix together the vinegar , mayo , the remaining 1 / 2 tsp sesame oil , soy sauce and 1 / 4 teaspoons salt
8. toss with the cucumber and gently fold in the avocado
9. serve with the fish
target.review: This was easy to make quickly, which is what I needed.  The recipe doesn't say where to add the onions, but I assume it goes in the cucumber salad.  The glaze was a little too sweet for me personally, and it didn't stick to my fish at first, rolling off the oil.  I had to baste several times during baking.  I also left out the extra salt, and added pepper to the cucumber mixture (my taste).

demonstrations.recipe_text:
garlic roasted butternut squash

this is always a hit with the family at holiday time.

1. peel and discard seeds of the squash
2. clean out peppers
3. cube vegetables in small dice and place in large bowl
4. peel and mince garlic and add to squash
5. add the oil , rosemary , cheese , salt and pepper
6. mix all together well and place in a greased baking dish
7. bake uncovered at 350f for 1 hour
demonstrations.review: This was exactly what I was looking for!  I didn't want to do the usual "sweet" roasted squash, and I'm so glad you have this here!  I added an extra garlic clove since we love it, and I only had 1/2 a red and 1/2 a green pepper to add.  I also threw in half a chopped onion, since the leftovers are being made into a quick squash soup, and that's all that was missing from the other recipe!  Thank you for providing TWO different meals with your recipe!  Next time I might roast even longer, since I like the crispy bits.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
classic apple pie

use your favourite apple variety, just make a note to alter the amount of sugar based upon the sweetness of the apples used!

1. pastry for double crust pie-------------
2. combine flour , lard and salt with a pastry blender or fork until balls are the size of a large pea
3. add cold water by the spoonful and blend until the bowl starts to clean itself as you work the dough
4. then it is ready for rolling
5. preheat oven to 450f
6. combine sliced apples with sugar , flour , cinnamon , nutmeg and lemon rind
7. line pie plate with unbaked pie crust , trim pastry , crimp to edge of pie plate
8. fill pie crust with apple mixture and dot with softened butter
9. brush crust edge with water and place pie crust top on top of pie , crimp to the bottom crust
10. make some slits in the top crust for steam to escape
11. bake for 10 minutes
12. turn oven down to 350f and bake for 45 minutes longer
demonstrations.review: Made this for 4th of July bbq party- I used only 4 apples, but left the rest the same.  Made "mini pies" by cutting circles in the rolled out crust, and put them in a muffin tin, filled and topped with smaller circles.  Served the individual pies with a dollop of vanilla ice cream, and had rave reviews!  Many said it was the best they had tasted.  Thank you!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pork chops with scalloped potatoes and onions

i found this recipe in a taste of home over 13 years ago.  it is a tried and true recipe that is especially satisfying on cold evenings.

1. in a saucepan melt butter over low heat , stir in flour , salt and pepper
2. add chicken broth
3. cook and stir constantly until the mixture comes to a boil
4. cook for one minute then remove from heat and set aside
5. season pork chops with additional salt and pepper as desired
6. brown pork chops in a skillet coated with vegetable oil
7. grease a 9 x 13 baking pan
8. layer potato and onion slices in pan
9. pour broth mixture over the potatoes and onion
10. place browned pork chops on top of potatoes
11. sprinkle paprika and parsley
12. cover with aluminium foil and bake at 350 for 1 hour or until potatoes are tender
13. remove foil and bake an additional 30 minutes , or until potatoes are tender
demonstrations.review: My family used to make something like this when I was young.  I browned the chops first, then made the sauce in the same pan.  Saves on dishes since I'm lazy.  :)  Next time, I will either use less salt, or use a no-salt broth.  Thank you for bringing back a yummy memory.

target.recipe_text:
bread machine cinnamon buns

bread machine cinnamon buns.

1. put yeast in bread machine first on bottom , then flour , sugar and salt
2. then melt butter in microwave
3. add beaten egg , milk and water
4. pour onto dry ingredients in bread machine on the dough setting
5. when dough is done , put it onto a lightly floured surface
6. knead in enough flour to make it easy to handle
7. if it is too elastic , cover and leave 10 minutes
8. use floured rolling pin to roll out dough on floured surface
9. roll out into rectangular shape to approx 1 / 4-inch thick
10. use filling and spread over entire surface of dough with spoon
11. roll up dough
12. cut into circle with a sharp knife about 1-inch thick
13. place these in a greased 9x13-inch pan
14. cover with a tea towel and leave in a warm place for approx 30 minutes , until double in size
15. bake in a 350 oven for about 25 minutes , light brown on top
16. when done , make glaze and swirl over buns
target.review: good! I used half cream half milk. I also used a ceam cheese icing. I cut the buns thicker my second time making them

demonstrations.recipe_text:
whatever floats your boat  brownies

these are absolutely the chewiest, moistest, fudgiest brownies ever! i have tried adding so many different things to the batter, and they always comes out great.  they are also great without any add-ins! but by varying the add-ins, you can make different brownies every week (or day!!) super easy prep! so, add "whatever floats your boat" and you will not believe how yummy they come out :) oh, and the recipe doubles just fine--use a 9 x 13 inch pan instead and add a few more minutes of baking!

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. grease an 8 inch square pan or line with foil
3. in a medium bowl combine melted butter and cocoa and stir until cocoa is dissolved
4. add sugar and mix well
5. add eggs one at a time and stir until well combined
6. stir in vanilla , flour and salt until you no longer see any flour
7. fold in "whatever floats your boat" !
8. spread in pan and bake for approximately 25 minutes
9. do not over-bake -- your brownies will come out dry
10. adjust time / temp accordingly for your oven
11. if you do the knife / toothpick test , it should come out with moist crumbs , not clean
12. cool completely before cutting into squares
13. for vegetarian omit the marshmallows
14. for double recipe , bake in 9x12 pan and add 5 minutes to baking time
demonstrations.review: very good! I doubled the recipe and added 1 tsp baking powder. the came out perfect!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
quick yellow cake

you can mix this up in a hurry.

1. heat oven to 350
2. mix dry ingredients in lg bowl
3. add shortening , milk and vanilla
4. beat on med for 2 minutes
5. add eggs and beat for 30 seconds more
6. bake in greased 13x9 pan for 35 minutes , or until pick comes out clean
demonstrations.review: I added a bit of extra vanilla and used butter not shortening it came out great!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
strawberries   cream bread  strawberry or blueberry

a wonderful recipe using fresh strawberries from netherhill strawberry farm in australia. this recipe also yields a tried and true (and reviewed) great blueberry & cream bread.

1. combine flour , baking powder , baking soda , salt and cinnamon
2. set aside
3. in small bowl , beat butter until creamy
4. gradually add sugar , beat 1 minute or until light and airy
5. add brown sugar
6. beat in eggs , one at a time
7. beat in sour cream and vanilla
8. stir into flour mixture only until dry ingredients are moistened
9. fold in strawberries and nuts
10. pour into a greased 8 x 4 inch loaf pan
11. bake at 350f for 60 to 65 minutes or until toothpick comes out clean
12. let stand 10 minutes in pan
13. turn out on rack to cool
demonstrations.review: I have made this lovely recipe as a cake as muffins and as a loaf each time it came out great! I doubled the cut strawberries the last time as it was wonderful :)

target.recipe_text:
impossible coconut pie

i love this dessert. it tastes like a coconut macaroon, and it is simple to make. drizzle melted chocolate on top and it tastes like a "mounds" bar. this comes from bisquick.

1. heat oven to 350f
2. grease 9-inch pie plate
3. stir all ingredients until blended
4. pour into pie plate
5. bake 50 to 55 minutes or until golden brown and knife inserted in the center comes out clean
6. cover and refrigerate any remaining pie
target.review: I had this dessert at a card party yesterday and it was heavenly!  I was going to enter it, but found you already had done so; thanks.  I will definately be making this in my home for friends and family.  It's simple, delicious and most folks usually have these ingredients on hand.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
easy crock pot chicken cacciatore

very simple recipe that tastes like you spent a lot of time in the kitchen.

1. throw everything but the chicken in the crock pot and stir it up
2. add chicken
3. cook on low or high until chicken easily comes off bone with tongs
demonstrations.review: We made this for guests over the weekend--very tasty!  I used mostly thighs, but half way through added a couple breasts.  I also added a whole sweet onion, red, yellow and green peppers and fresh halved mushrooms.  Served it with bowtie pasta and a large green salad.  Since I had a 28 oz. can of crushed tomatoes with added puree I added my own garlic and basil.  I also included about 1/3 cup of dry red wine.  I will definitely make this again--it is so easy and delicious!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
full meal zucchini casserole

simply delicious casserole.

1. place sliced zucchini in bottom of 9" x 13" pyrex baking dish
2. brown ground beef , garlic and onion in skillet
3. add cream of mushroom soup and oregano
4. mix well
5. pour this mixture over zucchini
6. sprinkle with rice
7. layer with cottage cheese then cheddar cheese
8. bake , loosely covered , at 350 degrees f for 45 minutes
9. place slices of tomato and parmesan cheese
10. bake an additional 15 minutes , uncovered
11. just serve with a fresh green salad and garlic bread
12. you'll be a winner !
demonstrations.review: You're right; this is a delicioius winner.  I prepared it precisely as written and wouldn't change a thing!  A simple salad and glass of wine makes this a perfect dinner.  We'll be making this for company next time.  Thanks for posting, Judekins.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
my favorite oriental coleslaw

i know there are other recipes for oriental coleslaw here. i mentioned in a thread on 

1. in a large bowl , break up ramen noodles into smaller pieces
2. add coleslaw mix , sunflower seeds , green onions , and water chestnuts
3. stir to combine
4. to make dressing: in a small bowl whisk together vinegar , oil , sugar , soy sauce and seasoning packets until combined
5. pour over salad , toss well to make sure dressing is evenly distributed
6. if you want the noodles to soften , refrigerate overnight
demonstrations.review: Very tasty, indeed.  I added some chopped chicken to mine for a complete meal and a little protein as well as some slivered almonds.  I also tried the teriyaki-chicken ramen noodle with flavor packet and really enjoyed it.  Also used only 2 pkg. of the noodles and flavor pkg.  I preferred this ratio.

target.recipe_text:
light peach upside down cake

this makes a beautiful cake. i made it this week for a lunch at work. the recipe comes from the february/march 2002 taste of home's light and tasty magazine. i made some minor adjustments to reduce the amount of sugar.

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. spray a 9 inch round baking pan with nonstick cooking spray and set aside
3. drain peaches , reserving 2 tablespoons of the juice
4. pat peaches dry between layers of paper towels and cut the peaches in half lengthwise
5. in small bowl , combine the brown sugar , cinnamon , nutmeg , reserved juice and 1 tablespoon of the melted butter
6. spread into prepared baking pan and top with peaches
7. in a large bowl , combine the flours , sugar , baking powder , baking soda and salt
8. in separate bowl , combine the buttermilk , egg or egg substitute , vanilla and remaining butter
9. add to dry ingredients and stir until blended well
10. spoon over peaches and bake in preheated oven for 30-35 minutes or until toothpick inserted near center comes out clean
11. cool for 10 minutes before inverting onto serving plan
12. best served warm
13. please
target.review: It might have been because I didn't serve it warm (it was a hot day, so we served it room temp with ice cream), but it smelled WAY better than it tasted. I mean it tasted good, but not as pungent and spicey since the spices were only in the top. Next time I would put cinnamon and nutmeg in the cake as well.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
oven fried eggplant  aubergine

this recipe appeared in "cooking light" magazine. this is a non-traditional way to prepare eggplant, but it really cuts the calories.

1. combine first 2 ingredients , stir well
2. spread evenly over both sides of eggplant slices
3. combine breadcrumbs , cheese , and italian seasoning in a shallow bowl
4. dredge eggplant in breadcrumbs mixture
5. place eggplant on a baking sheet coated with cooking spray
6. bake@ 425 degrees for 12 minutes
7. turn eggplant over
8. and bake an additional 12 minutes or until golden
demonstrations.review: I loved this recipe! I used veganaise and fake parm cheese. It turned out great and my husband liked it too. I cut it quite thin and that helped it get crispy.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
fat free chewy chocolate cookies

these are so fudgy and chewy they almost melt in your mouth. i was looking for a low-fat chocolate cookie but never expected to find something this good. these make me feel like i'm in chocaholic's heaven! i found these online, but they're originally from a karo pamphlet.

1. spray cookie sheets with cooking spray
2. in large bowl , combine flour , sugar , cocoa , baking soda and salt
3. stir in corn syrup and egg white until blended
4. drop by rounded teaspoon onto prepared cookie sheets
5. bake at 350 degrees for 7 to 9 minutes or just until set
6. do not overbake
7. cool on wire rack
demonstrations.review: The dough was SO hard to work with. I couldn't get it to mix well, and I was using my kitchenaid. They did taste pretty good, and got stars for the calorie count. Just really  hard to make!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
frijoles negros  cuban black beans

ay caramba, these are good!

1. fry the onion and pepper in a little oil
2. add the garlic and saute a little
3. introduce a little of the bean liquid until all previous ingredients are soft
4. add the beans with the remaining liquid
5. add spices and simmer about 30 minutes
6. add the vinegar just before serving
7. these are quite good when served over a bed of rice seasoned with just lime
demonstrations.review: This is a great easy recipe that can be made out of the pantry. I love that it is so easy, and so good for you! I eat it over rice, or drained a bit and in a tortilla. Yum.

target.recipe_text:
pickled eggs and red beets  pennsylvania dutch style

learned to love this when we lived in pennsylvania. it's a special treat for my son.  from the us regional cookbook, chicago culinary arts institute, 1947

1. cook , drain , and skin beets if not using canned
2. combine remaining ingredients , except eggs
3. pour over beets and cook for about 5 minutes
4. cool
5. place eggs in a large jar and pour cooled beet mixture over
6. place in the refrigerator
7. let pickle at least two days before using
target.review: I had fresh beets and looked to Food.com for something different to do with them. This recipe tastes wonderful already, Can't wait for the 2 or 3 days to be up so I can "legally" start eating! I made my own pickling spice, with one of the recipes on this website. It is kind of nice to be able to customize the flavors. When I was a kid in the early '50s rural local bars would have huge glass jars of pickled eggs on the bar. They were neither red nor sweet nor very good, as I recall. With that in mind, it is a wonder I chose this recipe. Very glad I did! Thank you, MollyPaul!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
salmon fillets with fresh tomatoes

nan

1. heat oven to 450 degrees
2. cut 4 square pieces of parchment paper or foil
3. and coat each with cooking spray
4. in medium bowl , combine the garlic , tomatoes , onions , oil , lemon rind , dill , parsley and capers
5. season with the salt and pepper
6. mix well
7. place each fillet on the prepared parchment paper or foil
8. top with equal amounts of tomato mixture
9. for each packet , bring 2 opposite edges of paper or foil together over the top of the fish and fold over several times
10. twist each of the open ends to close the packet and make a tight seal
11. place the packages on a baking sheet
12. bake for 10 minutes for every 1 inch of thickness of fish , or until the center portion of the fish flakes easily when tested with a fork
demonstrations.review: THE most delicious salmon recipe I have ever sunk my teeth into.  The blend of flavors is tantalizing; just perfect. The topping does mask the flavor of the salmon considerably but that works for us.  The fresh tomatoes and herbs from our garden most certainly made a great recipe even better.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kale and potato soup

nan

1. peel and chop potatoes
2. combine with vegetable oil and water
3. cook for 20 to 30 minutes or until potatoes are tender
4. remove potatoes and reserve liquid
5. mash potatoes through a sieve and return to potato liquid
6. add salt and pepper and simmer for 20 minutes
7. wash kale discarding all tough leaves and cut into shreds
8. add to potatoes and cook for 25 minutes
9. add sausage
10. simmer gently for 5 minutes
demonstrations.review:
My first attempt at using kale.  My husband, an avowed greens hater, said it is rather odd- tasting, but he actually liked it.  I, too, like it and will add it to my standards.

The changes I made:  no oil, and while pressure-cooking the potatoes I added a bit of hot dried pepper and beef "Better-than-Boullion".  Great recipe for the pressure-cooker.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
southern fried oysters

my dad loves to have a good old southern fish/seafood fry. this is the recipe he uses for fried oysters.

1. in a mixing bowl , add the first 3 ingredients
2. stir to combine
3. in another bowl , combine the egg and milk
4. whisk to combine
5. dip oysters in egg mixture , then dredge in flour mixture
6. add oil to 2-3 inch depth in a cast-iron dutch oven
7. heat to 375 degrees
8. fry oysters in oil until golden , turning once
9. drain on paper towels and serve immediately
demonstrations.review: Our family considers fried oysters a very special treat.  This is an easy, fast, wonderful recipe.  I would add either "Old Bay" or Tony Cachere's seasoning, but we thoroughly enjoyed it as written.  As I don't use self-rising flour, I just added a bit of baking powder and baking soda to the flour and corn meal.  I am sure there are conventions for the correct quantities, but my slap-dash method worked fine.   Thanks, "Rather be Swimming'".

target.recipe_text:
cooking light s creamy stove top macaroni and cheese

from the june 2006 issue of cooking light magazine and featured in their dinner tonight section.  this is a simple and quick main dish that is recommended to be served with a 7-layer salad for a full meal.  they suggest assembling the salad while the water comes to a boil for the pasta and making the sauce while the pasta cooks.  quick and easy for a weeknight meal.

1. cook pasta according to package directions , omitting salt and fat
2. drain and set aside
3. while the pasta cooks , place flour , salt , and pepper in a large saucepan
4. add milk , stirring with a whisk until well blended
5. drop cream cheese by teaspoonfuls into milk mixture
6. bring to a boil over medium-high heat , stirring constantly
7. reduce heat
8. simmer 2 minutes or until thick and cream cheese melts , stirring occasionally
9. stir in mustard , worcestershire , and garlic
10. simmer 1 minute
11. remove from heat
12. add cheddar cheese , stirring until cheese melts
13. combine pasta and cheese sauce in a large bowl
14. toss well
target.review: This is a great recipe, my husband and I really enjoyed it.  I liked that you don't have to bake it so it came together very fast. Thanks so much for the recipe! :0)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
honey roasted nuts and fruit

tasty snack from cooking light that provides a concentrated source of carbohydrates from the raisins, along with protein and "good" fats from the nuts. feel free to substitute nuts and fruit according to your preference, or what you have on hand. i don't care for raisins, so i used craisins (dried cranberries) ; i found i was out of slivered almonds, so i substituted some chopped macadamias. i especially loved the addition of cardamom--added an unexpected element.

1. line a baking sheet with parchment paper or foil and coat with cooking spray
2. in a large nonstick skillet , heat butter over medium-high heat
3. stir in honey and cook 2 minutes or until mixture bubbles around edges of pan
4. add nuts and next 5 ingredients , and cook over medium heat until nuts are golden , about 8 minutes , stirring frequently
5. stir in raisins
6. immediately spread onto prepared baking sheet
7. cool completely
demonstrations.review: This is a great recipe! I made it for the holidays but will be making it all year long. We go camping a lot and this would be such a great snack to take! Very easy and SO GOOD! Thanks for sharing. :0)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chocolate chip cookies  from cooking light

these yummy cookies have a wonderful texture and just the right amount of chocolate chips. just as good, if not better than, the ones full of fat and calories. one of the "greatest hits" in cooking light's june 2007 issue.

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees
2. combine flour , baking soda , and salt , stirring with a whisk
3. combine sugars and butter in a large bowl
4. beat with a mixer at medium speed until well blended
5. add vanilla and egg whites
6. beat one minute
7. add flour mixture and chips , beat until blended
8. drop dough by level tablespoons 2 inches apart onto baking sheets coated with cooking spray
9. bake at 350 degrees for 10 minutes or until lightly browned
10. cool on pans 2 minutes
11. remove from pans
12. cool completely on wire racks
demonstrations.review: Really good cookies! I made M&M cookies and they turned out great

demonstrations.recipe_text:
oreo balls

my sister's co-worker brought these to a party and they were quite a hit. i don't know where the recipe came from originally.

"bark" is an artificial chocolate or vanilla candy coating/confectioner's coating used to make a treat called almond bark and can be found at most grocery stores near the chocolate chips. 

you can use chocolate chips and white chocolate chips if you don't have almond bark, but i have found that almond bark melts better and is easier to work with.

1. using a blender or hand held mixer , mix oreos and cream cheese together
2. roll into walnut size balls
3. chill for an hour
4. melt approximately 3 / 4 package of white almond bark
5. stick a toothpick in an oreo ball and dip it in the melted white almond bark
6. allow to harden on wax paper
7. takes about 15 minute
8. while waiting , melt about 1 / 4 package of chocolate almond bark
9. when oreo balls are no longer sticky to the touch , decorate with drizzles of chocolate and white almond bark
10. i just use a sandwich bag with a tiny hole cut in one corner to drizzle the almond bark
demonstrations.review: Oh my gosh, these were soooo good and really easy! Will be making them often, thanks so much for sharing the recipe! :0)

target.recipe_text:
garlic   lemon roast chicken thighs

the 

1. puree garlic , lemon juice , worcestershire sauce& salt
2. combine marinade and chicken in a plastic bag
3. marinade at room temperature for 15 minutes
4. arrange chicken on greased rack in a broiler pan
5. roast chicken at 425 for 25-35 minutes until cooked
target.review: Tasty, different, and a good use for chicken thighs which can be inexpensive when on sale.  My picky husband even liked them.  Will definitely make again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crock pot potato and leek soup  vichyssoise

i got the original recipe for this from cooks.com.  i love potato and leek soup and didn't want to spend the time watching this or heating up the kitchen so doing it in my crock pot was perfect.  when this was finished cooking i pureed the soup.  you don't have to do this if you don't want to, but this is the way i like it.

1. cut all the above vegetables into bite size pieces
2. put all the ingredients into the crock pot except the milk and chives
3. cover and cook on high for 3-4 hours
4. you could also cook this for 10-12 hours on low if you prefer
5. stir in the milk during the last hour of cooking
6. serve with chopped chives as a garnish
7. bon appetit
demonstrations.review: My family loved this...I made some changes based on what I had in the house.  Used all cream of mushroom and left out the celery...next time I will not do this...I think the celery taste would improve it.  I used chicken soup packets instead of bouillon cubes...that may have made it less salty because I think it could have used a bit more salt.  Next time will check 1/2 hr before done and add salt if needed.  Also used skimmed evaporated milk which was fine.  Didn't puree...loved it 'chunky' but now I have a reason to get that immersion blender for my bday!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
white fish in herbed butter

frequently requested, easy to make.

1. mix all but fish in small bowl
2. heat skillet
3. add butter mixture
4. add fish and saute for about 6-7 minutes on each side
5. garnish with lemon wedges
demonstrations.review: My husband and children practically licked their plates clean...and I have a very picky bunch.  I used all garlic powder instead of half onion, half garlic because I was out of onion powder.  Served with a boxed mix of thai coconut ginger rice and broccoli.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
jenni s spinach   artichoke dip

i love spinach and artichoke dip.  however, i never really found one i didn't mess with.  i came up with my own after many experimentations.  i even once added some mushrooms, i didn't like it.  it wasn't your average button mushrooms, i might try those sometime.  anyway, this is usually a hit with my family when we have get-togethers.

1. preheat oven to 400 degrees
2. thaw spinch according to package directions
3. drain well
4. chop up artichoke hearts
5. add all ingredients in a medium sized casserole dish
6. bake in middle oven rack for 25 to 30 minutes , or until slightly golden and bubbly
7. serve with tortilla chips
demonstrations.review: Made this for my NYE party and WOW...I could have eaten the whole thing myself and it makes ALOT.  My company love it and said "This one is a keeper!"

target.recipe_text:
romaldo s carnitas

i got this delicious and tasty and easy recipe from the abilene chuckwagon cook-off. romaldo was the 

1. place roast on heavy duty foil
2. combine all the rest of the ingredients , and spread on top of the roast
3. seal foil securely and place in roasting pan
4. bake at 300 degrees f for 3-1 / 2 to 4 hours
5. use 2 forks and shred roast while still warm
6. for each serving , spoon meat on a hot flour tortilla
7. serve with guacamole and salsa and extra onions
target.review: Very easy and tasty. We made as directed ate some in burritos and froze some of the mix. It freezes and thaws very easily, you may want to taste and adjust seasonings once re-heated . Thank you for a simple mexican dish.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
roasted brussels sprouts

i got this from the barefoot contessa cookbook. so good.

1. preheat oven to 400f
2. cut off the ends of the brussels sprouts and pull off any yellow outer leaves
3. mix them in a bowl with the olive oil , salt , and lemon-pepper seasoning
4. transfer them to a sheet pan and roast for 35 to 40 minutes , until crisp outside and tender inside
5. shake the pan from time to time to brown the brussels sprouts evenly
6. sprinkle with more kosher salt , if you like , and serve hot
demonstrations.review: I absolutely love these. I am a huge fan of veggies and really, there isn't a better way to cook these little guys. Easy prep, cooks in no time. Excellent.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
italian style kidney beans

can be well prepared ahead or frozen.i usually serve them with polenta and a green salad, but it is good over brown rice or with crusty bread, too.a savory dish, make it spicier by adding some red pepper flakes.

1. cook bacon in oil over medium high heat until transparent , 1-2 minutes
2. reduce heat to medium
3. add onion , carrots , celery , parsley and rosemary and cook , stirring occasionally , until soft , about 5 minutes
4. add tomatoes , bay leaf and red pepper flakes if using
5. cover , reduce heat to low and let simmer 10 minutes
6. rinse and drain beans and add to tomato sauce
7. cook another 15-20 minutes without cover , until thickened to a sauce consistency
8. taste with salt and pepper
9. be careful with the salt , as the bacon is already salty
demonstrations.review: These were delicious, I love beans and they would be a wonderful side dish for any meal. Excellent and easy recipe, thanks Inge.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
poached eggs in catsup

surprisingly good.

1. melt butter and catsup in skillet till hot
2. break eggs into catsup mixture separately
3. cover with tight fitting lid and cook on low heat till desired doneness is reached
4. remove with slotted turner and place on buttered toast
5. 2 servings
demonstrations.review: It seems too good to be true, but it it  delicious. I didn't have any ketchup on hand but I had lots of chili sauce so I used that with a little bit of Salsa to cut sweetness. This is a keeper. Cheers

target.recipe_text:
apricot thumbprint cookies

i included the chilling time in the prep time.

1. preheat oven to 350
2. combine butter , sugar and cream cheese
3. mix until well blended
4. blend in egg and lemon juice
5. mix well
6. add flour and baking powder
7. mix well
8. chill at least 3 hours
9. shape into 1" balls
10. place on ungreased baking sheet
11. make indentation in center with your thumb or the back of a spoon
12. fill indentation with 1 tsp of apricot preserves
13. bake for 15 minutes
14. remove from cookie sheet to cool
15. dust with powdered sugar
target.review: These are very good..I love the cream cheese dough..which I quick-chilled in the freezer. I chopped up dried apricots & soaked them in a small amount of boiling water & a bit of vanilla extract, then mixed them with apricot preserves to make it even extra apricot-tasty. Wonderful! Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mountain dew apple dumplings

i found this recipe while surfing the net. i've not tried it yet. sounds really easy to "dew"....

1. spray a 13x9 baking dish or pan
2. peel and slice apples into 16 pieces
3. roll each apple slice in 1 section of crescent roll
4. place rolled slices in pan in two rows , put extras along side
5. melt butter , add sugar and cinnamon and pour over apples
6. pour can of mountain dew over all
7. bake at 350 degrees for 45 minutes
8. serve warm with vanilla ice cream
demonstrations.review: This recipe is so good, quick, and easy!!  I was wary of the Mt.Dew in the recipe, but after the liquid cooks off, you are left with a delicious little apple dumpling/turnover thing. Yummy!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
macadamia lemon bars

from taste of home, april/may 2004.

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. combine the flour , confectioners' sugar and butter
3. stir in nuts
4. press onto the bottom and 1 / 2 inches up the sides of a greased 8-in
5. square baking dish
6. bake for 15-20 minutes or until lightly browned
7. in a small mixing bowl , combine the sugar , flour , baking powder and salt
8. beat in the eggs , lemon juice and lemon peel until light and fluffy
9. pour over hot crust
10. sprinkle with nuts
11. bake for 10-15 minutes or until lightly browned
12. cool completely on a wire rack
13. cut into bars
14. sprinkle with the confectioners' sugar
demonstrations.review: These are to die for.  I love lemon bars and the nutty twist is so yummy!  I found that I liked the nuts in larger chunks so there is no reason to chop them up fine...they sink to the bottom anyway and sort of fuse into the crust.  The flavor is delightful.  I agree...add more lemon zest. Thanks so much!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
perfect rice everytime

i adopted this recipe.  here is the original poster's description:  this will yield perfect rice. you can , of course add other things to your rice if you wish. dried cranberries or raisins work well.

1. preheat oven to 400 degrees
2. use a saute pan with straight sides with a tight fitting lid
3. saute onion or shallot in butter until soft , add uncooked rice and saute , stirring for 3 - 4 minutes
4. add chicken broth , salt and pepper
5. bring to a boil , cover and put into oven for 16 minutes
6. remove from oven and let sit covered for 10 minutes
7. remove lid , fluff with a fork and serve
demonstrations.review: What an easy way at rice..very good and no stove-top stirring. You gotta love that!! I think I'll experiment..I like cinnamon & brown sugar rice in the morning...many possibilities!!  Thanks riffraff!!

target.recipe_text:
oven  fried  fish

the other day, my husband was asking for fish and chips but with my high cholesterol, i have to avoid things like that.  i found in a magazine at the doctor's office this recipe for oven fried fish, which is nice and crispy like the deep fried kind but without all the fat.  this is excellent served with evelyn/athens' spicy oven fries and your favourite cole slaw recipe.

1. position rack on top shelf in oven
2. preheat oven to 500 degrees f
3. line a rimmed baking sheet with foil and set a wire rack on top
4. lightly spray or brush rack with vegetable oil
5. pat fish dry with paper towels
6. slice fillets in half lengthwise to form long pieces
7. in a pie plate or wide shallow dish , whisk egg white with buttermilk
8. in another dish , stir flour with bread crumbs , paprika , cayenne and salt
9. working with 1 piece of fish at a time , lightly coat with flour mixture
10. shake off excess flour , then dip into buttermilk mixture
11. turn to evenly coat
12. shake off excess liquid
13. coat fish in flour mixture again
14. shake off excess coating , then place on rack
15. repeat with remaining fish , 1 piece at a time
16. discard any remaining buttermilk or flour mixtures
17. lightly spray fish with oil or , using a brush , lightly dab about 1 tbsp oil as evenly as possible over coating
18. do not skip this step -- it is essential for crispy fish
19. bake on top rack of preheated oven until coating is crisp and golden , 12 to 15 minutes
20. do not turn
target.review: Very good! I used sole filets and panko rather than regular crumbs. No buttermilk, so I thinned yogurt with white wine, also added Tiger Sauce for extra heat. These cooked up very quickly, and smelled awesome. Turned out nice and crispy and basic, just what we were hoping for.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
incredible oven fried chicken

this recipe is the most flavorful home made fried chicken i have ever had. also great picnic food.

1. whisk buttermilk , oil , hot pepper sauce , mustard , garlic , 1 tsp salt and 1 / 2 teaspoon pepper in a large bowl
2. add the onion and then the chicken turning to coat each piece with the marinade
3. cover
4. chill at least three hours or up to one day turning the chicken occasionally
5. combine breadcrumbs , cheese , flour , thyme , paprika , cayenne and 1 tsp salt in a large baking dish
6. remove the chicken from the marinade and roll in the breadcrumb mixture
7. set chicken on a rack to dry for about 30 minutes
8. preheat oven to 400f degrees
9. place chicken in large baking dish and pour butter over the chicken
10. bake until crisp and brown , approximately 50 minutes
demonstrations.review: In one word, wonderful!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
virginia apple pudding

my next door neighbor steve is a pretty darn good cook imo, and he has given me permission to post and share another one of his favorites he made last night. i told him his other one got a 5 and i'll bet this one does too. try it...you'll love it.

1. preheat oven to 375 degrees
2. melt butter in a 2 quart casserole dish
3. combine sugar , flour , salt , baking powder , cinnamon and milk to make a batter
4. pour the batter on the butter
5. put apples in the center of the batter
6. bake in 375 degree oven until batter covers apples and crust browns , approximately 30 to 40 minutes
demonstrations.review: As easy as it is to put this together, it's shocking how tasty it turns out! We've had it a couple of times now and I've used granny smiths. Good stuff.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
best ever drop biscuits  small batch

drop biscuits are best the same day they are made...no comparison!!!  perfect for 4 people.  when you stir slightly cooled melted butter into cold buttermilk, the butter will clump. although this might look like a mistake, it's one of the secrets to this recipe.  you can double the recipe...if needed!

1. adjust oven rack to middle position and heat oven to 475 degrees
2. whisk flour , baking powder , baking soda , sugar , and salt in large bowl
3. combine buttermilk and 1 / 4 cup melted butter in medium bowl , stirring until butter forms small clumps
4. add buttermilk mixture to dry ingredients and stir with rubber spatula until just incorporated and batter pulls away from sides of bowl
5. using greased 1 / 4-cup dry measure , scoop a scant amount of batter and drop onto parchment-lined rimmed baking sheet
6. repeat with remaining batter , spacing biscuits about 1 1 / 2 inches apart
7. bake until tops are golden brown and crisp , 8 - 12 minutes
8. they can be made up ahead of time and gently re-heated in a 300 oven for 10 minutes
9. brush biscuit tops with 1 tablespoon melted butter
10. transfer to wire rack and let cool 5 minutes before serving
11. test if baking powder is fresh: mix 2 teaspoons of the baking powder into a cup of water
12. if there is an immediate reaction of foaming and fizzing , the baking powder is okay to use
13. if the reaction is at all delayed or weak , throw it away and buy a fresh can
demonstrations.review:
we are in LOVE with this recipe! it makes a nice batch for 2, enough for dinner (provided you're hungry) and breakfast (while they're still reasonably fresh) the next day- without leftovers. i never have buttermilk around so, have been using yogurt which has worked beautifully. so far, i've tried them plain and found them very good, also adding 1/4 cup cheddar and topping with garlicparsley butter (mmm!), also adding a big handful of shredded parmesan and lots of black pepper (not as good as the cheddargarlic but still, mm!).

eta: i forgot to say, i've never used parchment for these. i never have it and have only used a greased cookie sheet-no problems yet.

target.recipe_text:
chicken scaloppine with lemon glaze   low fat and delicious

this is a wonderful lower-fat restaurant-quality dish that is easy to make, i also like to add in a few tablespoons of capers and cook with the lemon glaze if you are a lover of capers then add them in as it really adds to the flavour of this dish ---  this lemon sauce is not a heavy creamy sauce which is what makes this dish lower in fat, it is more like a glaze that soaks into the chicken, and i would strongly suggest to double or even triple the glaze i most always do, and please be certain to use only dry breadcrumbs as fresh will not stick to the chicken as well --- this is *very* good!

1. in a small bowl or shallow dish whisk together mustard and eggs
2. set aside
3. combine the dry bread crumbs with poultry seasoning , garlic powder and seasoning salt
4. spread on a piece of waxed paper
5. dip the breasts firstly in egg / mustard mixture then coat well with the crumb mixture , pressing downs with hands to adhear the crumbs to the breast
6. heat the olive oil in a skillet over medium heat
7. add in the chicken and cook for about 5 minutes on each side , or until it is no longer pink inside
8. remove and transfer to a plate to keep warm
9. for the glaze
10. in the same skillet add in the broth , lemon juice and 1 / 4 teaspoon salt bring to a boil scraping any brown bits from the pan
11. add in lemon slices and parsley
12. mix to combine for about 1 minute
13. spoon the glaze / sauce over chicken
14. delicious !
target.review: This was amazing ! I tripled the sauce as suggested I also baked the chicken instead of frying it. I didn't have bread crumbs so I used ritz crackers it turned out so moist and yummy !! Thanks for the recipe !

demonstrations.recipe_text:
vanilla poached pears

a delicious, elegant, and healthy dessert to serve to your family or friends.  your dinner party guests will be impressed with the appearance of this special dish.  little do they know how easy it was to make! (cooking time includes cooling time.)

1. place the pears in a large saucepan and pour apple juice in to cover the pears
2. add vanilla bean and bring the pears to a simmer over medium heat
3. simmer until tender , being careful not to burn
4. allow pears to cool , then serve in the center of a dessert plate
5. spoon sauce over the pears , then sprinkle with cinnamon powder and garnish with a sprig of mint
6. enjoy !
demonstrations.review: This was very tasty and really hit the spot. I was looking for a way to use up my pears and this was it. I will be making this again for dinner parties. Thanks for the recipe

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crab stuffed chicken  aka fancy chicken

i was searching the internet 2 valentines days ago for a romantic, not too foo-fooey recipe and found this (don't remember what site). this is now my bh's version of comfort food, whenever he feels down he asks me to make "that fancy chicken". i like to serve it with garlic mashed potatoes.

1. combine cream cheese , crabmeat , and soup mix , set aside
2. cut a 'pocket' into the side of each chicken breast
3. fill each pocket with the cream cheese mixture and close the opening with toothpicks
4. dip chicken breasts in flour-> eggs-> breadcrumbs
5. in large skillet , melt oil and butter over medium-high heat
6. add chicken to skillet , cook for 10 minutes , or till golden brown , turning once
7. transfer chicken to 13x9 pan and bake in a 350f oven , uncovered , for 15 minutes or until chicken is done
demonstrations.review: I made this for my boyfriend for valentine's day. We both really LOVED it . I added some spinach and garlic to the stuffing mixture per some recommendations of reviews. I also added half of the soup mix( onion soup couldn't find other one) since some of the reviews said it was too much with the whole thing. I also did not fry in the pan before putting in the oven due to watching calories and also used fat free cream cheese. The outside was nice and crisp with the bread crumbs and the chicken was nice and tender. I will be making this again. Thanks for the recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
butternut squash souffle or kugel

this is a delicious healthy side dish. pretty enough for company, but kids enjoy the sweet taste! fresh squash is easy to cook in the microwave, but frozen tastes just as good. for the milk, i used nonfat, my neighbor uses mocha mix to make it non-dairy. from my neighbor, tiffanie, who is the best kosher cook ever!!

1. preheat oven to 350
2. if using fresh squash , microwave- cut in half , remove seeds , place cut side down in small amount of water , cover with plastic wrap and cook on high 15 minutes
3. scrape flesh from skin- should be 3-4 cups
4. beat together flour , sugar , oil , eggs , and milk
5. add squash and mix well
6. bake in 9x13 glass or ceramic baking dish for 60 minutes
7. can sprinkle cinnamon sugar on top after 30 minutes in oven
demonstrations.review: I made this the other night and my boyfriend LOVED it !!! I did forget the flour which probably would have made it rise but it was still very good Thanks !

target.recipe_text:
kittencal s chicken crescent roll casserole

this will also work great with turkey; if you do not have chicken breasts, then use any leftover cooked chicken. if desired you can fill the crescents just with the filling mixture and omit the soup, just brush with butter before baking. they are wonderful just stuffed with the filling! a few members have experienced a soggy bottom, so you might want to consider just drizzling half (or even a little less) of the soup mixture on top and a little around the sides of the crescents, then save the rest of the soup mixture for another time (this will help prevent a soggy bottom). you may use the jumbo crescent rolls and stuff with more chicken mixture :)

1. set oven to 350f
2. butter a casserole dish
3. in a saucepan , mix half and half cream , 3 / 4 cup grated cheese and undiluted chicken soup
4. heat just until the cheese melts
5. for the filling --- in a bowl , mix the soft cream cheese with butter until very smooth , then add in garlic powder
6. add in the chopped chicken , onion and cheddar cheese
7. mix well until combined
8. add in 2 tablespoons whipping cream or mayonnaise
9. mix to combine
10. season with seasoned salt or white and black pepper to taste
11. unroll the crescent rolls
12. place 1 heaping tablespoon chicken mixture on top of each crescent triangle , then roll up starting at the thicker end
13. drizzle a small amount of soup mixture on the bottom of the dish
14. then place the crescent rolls seam-side down on top of the creamed mixture in the casserole
15. drizzle the remaining sauce on top and sprinkle with 1 cup grated cheese , or amount desired
16. bake for about 30 minutes
target.review: This recipe is awesome!  I made it twice in one week, nothing but rave reviews!  Thanks Kittencal!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s creamy greek feta salad dressing

plan ahead the dressing needs a few hours chilling time before serving,  you may want to adjust some ingredients after you make this, i would suggest to start with the stated amounts and add in more after mixing, you may use 3 tablespoons freshly grated parmesan cheese in place of the feta cheese --- if you are not a lover of garlic then i suggest to pass this by! --- servings are only esitmated.

1. in a food processor or blender process all ingredients together except the salt and pepper until blended and smooth
2. add in a little more crumbled feta cheese if you prefer a chunky-style dressing
3. season with salt and black pepper
4. refrigerate for at least 2 or more hours before serving
demonstrations.review: Best dressing ever!  This is the only dressing I ever need, it's that good!  Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s famous greek salad

be prepared for the best greek salad on the planet! --- plan ahead the dressing needs at least 2 or more hours to blend the flavors, i sometimes add in 1/4 cup parmesan cheese to the dressing for a more cheesy dressing, all amounts may be adjusted to taste ----  to marinade the salad allow to sit at room temperature before serving, see bottom of instructions --- you will find this and many more of my recipes posted here http://kittencalskitchen.com/2009/04/13/kittens-famous-greek-salad/  ---also see my recipe #359292

1. for the dressing
2. in a processor or use a wire whisk process / whisk the olive oil with lemon juice , 2 teaspoons dried oregano , garlic , dried , basil , red wine vinegar , salt and sugar until smooth
3. season with black pepper
4. chill in fridge for a couple of hours before using to blend flavors
5. place the salad ingredients in a large bowl
6. pour dressing over
7. toss to combine
8. if desired allow the salad to sit at room temperature for 20 minutes before serving , or you can refrigerate for 1 hour
demonstrations.review: Fantastic Greek Salad and I made both of your dressings!  Thanks for 3 great recipes!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s moist cheddar garlic oven fried chicken breast

this is for serious garlic lovers. the chicken bakes out so moist and tender! grated cheese may be sprinkled on top of the breast the last 5 minutes of cooking if desired but that is optional. double all ingredients for more than four breasts and adjust the amount of garlic to suit taste. for the coating amount you might be able to get away with 5 or maybe 6 very small chicken breasts, but i would suggest to increase the amount slightly --- to take this dish to yet another level, about 10 minutes before the cooking time is finished, drizzle the top of the chicken with a little pasta sauce, then sprinkle mozzarella cheese on top. return to oven for about 10 minutes until the chicken is completely cooked and sauce is hot and cheese has melted. for a lemon-garlic flavor add in 3 tablespoons lemon juice to the melted butter/garlic mixture ---  *note* for a healthier alternative smart balance butter blend may be used in place of the melted butter --- you will love this chicken!
visit my food blog, www.kittencalskitchen.com, for more of my recipes.

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. butter an 11 x 7-inch pan
3. in a bowl , combine melted butter with fresh minced garlic , 1 teaspoon garlic powder and salt
4. in another bowl , combine the dry breadcrumbs with 1 / 2 cup finely grated cheddar cheese , parmesan cheese 1 teaspoon garlic powder and coarse ground black pepper
5. dip chicken in butter mixture
6. then in crumb mixture
7. place in prepared pan and bake uncovered for 35-45 minutes or until cooked through , larger breasts may take more time
8. top with shredded cheddar or mozzarella the last 5 minutes of cooking (this is only optional
demonstrations.review: Best recipe ever, the chicken was so juicy and delicious.  Everyone was absolutely wild about the chicken!  Thanks Kittencal!

target.recipe_text:
franks in blanks  blankets or hot dog puffs

i can't believe this is nowhere to be found on this website as this is so incredibly delicious; i can't be the only one making this can i? by the way i don't know the actual sizes of the hot dogs or puff pastry but this recipe is for one package each.

1. lay a square of pastry dough down and coat with mayo , mustard , and garlic powder mixture
2. wrap around cooked hot dog
3. with fingers or pastry brush coat the dough with raw egg white
4. you may sprinkle the dough with sesame seeds at this point
5. bake in a 350f oven for about 30 minutes or until the dough is nicely browned
6. serve and enjoy !
target.review: My family really likes these. We use beef hotdogs and vegetarian hotdogs. We have done many different variations now after trying these, like adding shredded cheese inside the wrap which comes out really good. I used I Can't Believe It's Not Butter spray instead of egg whites and that works fine also.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
peanut butter banana wraps

from eat better america.

1. spread 2 tablespoons of the peanut butter evenly over each tortilla
2. drizzle 1 tablespoon of the honey over each tortilla
3. top with banana slices and chocolate chips
4. roll up tortillas
5. secure with toothpicks
demonstrations.review: This was good and very easy to make. I think I will use a little less peanut butter next time because i think I went a bit overboard. My 2 1/2 year old son was able to help easily too by spreading the peanut butter and placing the banana slices, and he loves to help as much as he can so that is always a big plus.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
easy veggie quesadilla

this makes a wonderful afternoon snack or appetizer.

1. lightly spray a small frying pan with cooking spray
2. cook the diced vegetables in the pan for about 3 minutes
3. remove from the heat & add the taco sauce
4. lightly spray another small frying pan with cooking spray
5. place 1 of the tortilla shells into the pan
6. put a thin layer of cheese onto the shell
7. scatter the vegetable mixture over top of the cheese
8. add another thin layer of cheese & cover with the second tortilla shell
9. cook on both sides until slightly brown
10. cut into quarters & serve hot
demonstrations.review: I really, really like this. I've made it quite a few times now and I think it will be something I keep making. The only thing is that I don't like spicy food, so I have lowered it from 2 tablespoons to 1 of the taco sauce.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
poor man s pizza

this seems really corny but its good!
use as an appetizer if you like or just a great snack for yourself.

1. place ritz cracker salt side down and top with a little ketchup
2. add cheese and pepperoni
3. heat in microwave until cheese melts
4. !
demonstrations.review: I give a 3 star rating beacuse I liked them, but my husband who is a real pizza lover really didn't like them at all. He said it was way too ketchup-y, and I didn't use too much ketchup either. He said maybe with pizza sauce instead of the ketchup, we may try that sometime.

target.recipe_text:
stir fry chicken with garlic sauce

nice and simple. prep time includes marinating time.

1. combine garlic , soy sauce , water , honey , 1 tablespoon oil , cornstarch and black / red pepper
2. stir chicken into marinade and mix to coat
3. cover and refrigerate at least 2 hours , stirring once to twice
4. in large skillet , heat remaining oil
5. using slotted spoon , transfer chicken to skillet
6. stir-fry about 5 minutes
7. add reserved marinade
8. continue to cook and stir about 30 seconds until thickened
9. remove to platter
10. garnish with green onion
11. serve with snow peas , if desired
target.review: I made this recipe exactly as stated and it was delicious! I sauteed the chicken first, than the bag of frozen stir-fry veggies, than threw in the sauce and simmered till thickened. Served over rice ... quick and yuuummmy!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
garlic sauteed artichokes

artichokes are sauteed in garlic butter before steaming. a simple and delicious way to use artichokes!

1. rinse artichokes under cold water , and use a sharp knife to cut the top 1 / 3 off of each one
2. trim the stems to about 1 inch , and remove the smaller leaves from around the base
3. use scissors to remove any remaining leaf
4. cut each artichoke in half from the bottom to the top , then use a spoon to scrape out the hairy choke
5. rinse again to remove any residual hairs
6. melt the butter in a large skillet over medium heat
7. add the garlic , and saute for about 1 minute to flavor the butter
8. arrange artichoke halves cut-side down in the skillet
9. saute for about 5 or 10 minutes , or until lightly browned
10. reduce heat to low , and pour in water& chicken broth , cover , and let steam for 15 to 20 minutes , or until the artichokes are tender
11. a fork should easily pierce the stem
demonstrations.review: Can't say these were any better than if I had simply steamed them plain. Still needed to be dipped in something in order to taste good. Glad I tried it though!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
healthy hamburger and green bean soup

i make this thick comforting soup often for my family during the cold winter months. it is so fast and easy to fix and it is rather low in fat and calories. this makes 4 very large servings. to reduce sodium, you may use low sodium green beans if you prefer. i adapted this recipe from "fast, cheap and easy," by joanna lund. condensed cream of tomato soup and condensed regular tomato soup are interchangeable in this recipe; no alterations necessary.the important part is that it is indeed a condensed version of tomato soup, as opposed to ready to serve.

1. spray a large saucepan with cooking spray
2. brown beef and chopped onions over medium heat until cooked though
3. drain any fat
4. to the browned meat and onions , add the cream of tomato soup , tomato sauce , and water
5. bring to a boil
6. add uncooked instant rice , green beans , parsley , and black pepper
7. stir well
8. cover and reduce heat to low
9. simmer for 15 minutes or until rice is tender , stirring once or twice
demonstrations.review: Considering how simple this was to prepare, this was pretty good. I, too, used a can of low sodium tomato soup and 1 cup of milk. I may try using cream of tomato soup next time and 1.5 c beef broth to see if that improves the flavor. Oh, and I left out the rice and served this with cornbread. May, or may not, make this again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
millet porridge

looking to add other grains to your diet? try millet as a hot breakfast cereal. note: i adopted this as an 

1. in a small saucepan , combine millet , water , milk , cinnamon , vanilla , salt and raisins
2. bring to a boil
3. reduce heat to low , cover and simmer for 25 minutes without stirring
4. if the liquid is not completely absorbed , cook for 3-5 minutes longer , partially covered
5. remove from heat
6. drizzle with maple syrup or honey
7. serve
demonstrations.review: Truly delicious. Substituted chopped prunes for the raisins (chopped dates, many dried fruits - including cranberries, cherries, blueberries -- would work well, too), and poured a little maple syrup on top when finished. This will be a regular in my home for breakfast!

target.recipe_text:
chicken with fettuccine alfredo

juicy chicken with a great creamy alfredo sauce. very easy to make!

1. cook fettuccine according to package
2. drain
3. while fettuccine is cooking , prepare chicken
4. heat 12-inch skillet
5. add 2 tbsp butter
6. flatten chicken slightly
7. salt and pepper chicken
8. roll in flour , add to skillet
9. cook and brown until juices run clear , about 10 minutes
10. remove from skillet
11. add to skillet 2 tbs butter , onions , and garlic
12. cook 1 minute
13. add cream , cook for 3 minutes until reduced a bit
14. add cheese , parsley , and red pepper flakes
15. stir well
16. add last 1 tbsp butter and stir well
17. bring back chicken and coat with sauce
18. place chicken on plates , put fettuccine in sauce and swirl around to coat well
19. add to plate with chicken
target.review: What can i say? This is one of my personal favourites. i LOVE LOVE LOVEEE this recipe, i've made it so many times, with and without chicken. I have, on some occasions, made it with some missing ingredients e.g parsley or pepper flakes, and it's still good, but it's waaaay better with everything included! Perfect solution for a quick dinner. 5 Star Pasta MizzNezz Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kate s basic crepes

this is my foolproof method for crepes.  there are step-by-step photos in the french forum to go with it.  use oil for savory crepes, sweet butter for dessert crepes.  depending on your taste and the weather (humidity affects the batter), use anywhere from 6 - 8 eggs.  and check out the crepes! cookbook for dozens of crepe fillings and recipes posted here on 'zaar.

1. first , combine the flour , eggs , salt and oil in a large bowl so you have plenty of room to whisk and combine these ingredients well
2. then add about a quarter of the milk and mix till smooth
3. when it is smooth , add the balance of the milk all at once and mix gently until you have achieved a homogenous batter --no lumps
4. then let the batter sit at room temperature for at least half an hour -- now your batter is ready
5. heat your skillet or , if you are lucky enough to have one , your crepe pan , add oil or butter or a combination of both--just enough to give the pan's surface a sheen , and add just enough batter to make a very thin veil across the pan
6. then , using a spatula , carefully turn your crepe once it begins to brown around the edges and cook it on the other side
7. when it is lightly browned on both sides , remove it from the pan and lay it on a warm plate
8. repeat the process , stacking your crepes one on top of the other
demonstrations.review: Best Crepes Ever!!! Apart from the fact they looked so yummy, they could also be used as pita bread with the use of oil. I made mine sweet, i added sugar, vanilla and butter, and i used canola oil for frying, then ate them with Jam. Perfect texture, perfect consistency, so easy to make and i quartered the recipe to make 5 crepes. This is one recipe i will definately keep and use regularly. Next time i make these savoury, i will try them with a smear of Danish cheese with cucumber or tomato and capsicum, or kebabs, or with an indian curry dinner.. the ideas are endless!! I'm checking out the Crepes! cookbook for more. This recipe needs more ratings!! Everyone needs to try this. THANKS KATE.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
bev s spaghetti sauce

this is a recipe i have developed over a number of years. this is the only spaghetti sauce my family will request! very easy to make. i hope your family enjoys it as much as mine does!

1. brown the ground beef , onion and garlic in olive oil with bay leaves , oregano , basil , italian seasoning , salt and pepper
2. add tomato paste , tomato sauce and diced tomatoes
3. stir well and bring to a simmer over medium heat
4. cover and simmer for 1 1 / 2 hours
5. use sauce to top your cooked spaghetti
6. top with sauteed mushroom
7. pass the parmesan
demonstrations.review: I've already made this several times, this is my number 1 spaghetti sauce. I love it, my family loves it, everyone asks for seconds. Love making this with fresh pureed tomatoes, fresh basil, i also recommend fresh mushrooms. I sometimes leave out the ground meat, still great tasting. This is my special pasta sauce, i make it on days when we really feel like spaghetti because its the best and most satisfying. I now also regularly buy oregano, basil and italian seasoning to have them on hand for this recipe because its a keeper(will be making it tonight). Well worth 5 stars! Thanks Bev.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
linda s cheesecake stuffed strawberries

omg.. these are like heaven in your mouth!  talk about great taste sensations...  i made these for one of my cooking and recipe events that i hold monthly, and these were a huge hit... a must try for sure!  you can use low fat cream cheese to make these lighter if you like.  you can also dip the ends with any kind of finely chopped nuts, mini chocolate chips, graham cracker crumbs, sprinkles, or dip the ends in chocolate or drizzle with chocolate.  you might even try adding some cocoa powder to the cream cheese and make it a chocolate filling.  the sky is the limit here, just use your imagination!

1. place cream cheese in a bowl , and microwave for 30 seconds , so that it's soft
2. whip together the cream cheese , vanilla , and sugar
3. in the center of each strawberry , using a sharp knife , make a hole in each one , as deep as you can without going out the bottom
4. spoon or pipe the filling into each hole
5. dip cheesecake end of strawberry into chopped almonds , making sure you completely cover the cheesecake filling with the nuts
6. lay strawberries in a pretty serving dish
7. sprinkle with any leftover nuts around the dish
8. chill , and serve
9. makes 24 servings
demonstrations.review: THESE WERE TERRIFIC! I used Light Cream Cheese for these. Next time i will dip them in biscuit crumbs to make the cheesecake experience even more real. (I think I'll try Arnotts Scotch Finger crumbs first!) THANK YOU!

target.recipe_text:
apple crisp ii

dessert

1. with pastry cutter or steel blade in food processor add flour , brown sugar , oatmeal , baking powder , salt and butter
2. process until mixture no longer looks "floury"
3. add walnuts and process just a second
4. set aside
5. half and core apples , peeling is up to you
6. slice apples
7. arrange apple slices in a buttered 9x13 baking dish
8. combine sugar and cinnamon
9. spread over apples
10. sprinkle with lemon juice
11. distribute topping over apples
12. bake at 350 degrees fahrenheit for 45 minutes
13. serve warm with whipped cream or ice cream
target.review: Super Delicious! I used granny smith apples (11), and found that the entire recipe needed to be doubled for a 9 x 13 pan. I added a bit more oatmeal after processing to retain more of the full oatmeal texture. Perfect with Vanilla Bean Ice Cream. Thanks for a great recipe jinx.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
oven roasted asparagus and leeks

i can't remember where i found this simple recipe, but it is awesomely good!

1. preheat oven to 400 degrees
2. trim each leek at root end , then cut off top where the thick green leaves begin
3. cut in half lengthwise and soak in cold water 10 minutes
4. rinse , then pat dry
5. trim tough ends of asparagus
6. combine leeks and asparagus in a large bowl
7. drizzle with olive oil and add salt and pepper
8. toss to coat
9. place in a large roasting pan and roast until vegetables start to turn brown , about 25 minutes
10. let cool 5 minutes , then drizzle with balsamic vinegar
demonstrations.review: Delicious! Even good minus the balsamic.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
halibut veracruz

rick bayless of frontera grill in chicago distills mexican seafood into three basic preparations: lime-cured (seviche), fried with garlic (al mojo de ajo), and served with chunky tomato sauce (a la veracruzana). named for the city of veracruz, pescado a la veracruzana is widely served throughout 
mexico. this  simple, light version skips the usual bay leaf and heavy stewing, allowing the delicate halibut to shine.seafood makes a great base for a delicious mexican feast. just add the heat, the spice is right! text and recipes by kathryn jessup from the november 2008 issue of coastal living. adapted from dona tomas (ten speed, 2006).

1. place tomatoes on a large rimmed baking sheet
2. bake at 450f for 20 minutes
3. turn tomatoes
4. bake 20 more minutes or until skins are blistered and lightly browned
5. pulse tomatoes and pan juices in a food processor until roughly chopped
6. saut onion in 2 tablespoons hot oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat 3 minutes or until tender
7. add garlic and serrano
8. saut 15 seconds
9. adding olives , capers , and chopped tomatoes
10. bring to a boil
11. reduce heat , and simmer 5 minutes
12. remove from heat
13. stir in oregano
14. sprinkle halibut with salt and pepper
15. melt butter with remaining 2 tablespoons oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat
16. add halibut
17. cook 5 minutes on each side or until fish flakes easily with a fork
18. serve with sauce , fluffy white rice and a green vegetable
demonstrations.review: The sauce for this halibut has a great flavor. I usually fiddle around with ingredients, but this requires one to be pretty exact to keep it subtle enough for a mild fish. The smokey flavor of the tomato is rich and warm and slightly sweet making a nice contrast to the acid of the tomato/olives/capers.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
peppered tenderloin with mustard sauce

a recipe that i am posting for safe keeping, found in my land o lakes cookbook.  
great steaks, topped with this flavorful sauce, make the perfect entertaining entrée.

1. heat gas grill on medium or charcoal grill until coals are ash white
2. press cracked pepper onto both sides of steaks
3. place steaks onto grill
4. grill , turning once , until internal temperature reaches 145f or until desired doneness
5. meanwhile , combine beef broth , garlic and sherry in small saucepan
6. cook over medium heat until mixture comes to a boil
7. continue boiling for 5 minutes
