8. stir in sour cream and mustard with wire whisk
9. continue cooking until heated through
10. serve sauce over grilled steaks
11. sprinkle with additional cracked pepper , if desired
demonstrations.review: Great flavor! I reduced a little more than recommended and added a bit more garlic & mustard for a little extra punch. I think this could be really good with some horseradish or wasabi too! Could get watery if heated too much after whisking in the sour cream.

target.recipe_text:
real german potato salad   direct from my friend in frankfurt s

i adopted this recipe from recipezaar as it didn't have a loving home. i haven't yet been able to make it, but since i am german and generally like a good german potato salad, i thought i would put my name on this great looking recipe! ;) if you make it before i get a chance, please let me know what you think!

1. in a large skillet , cook onion until tender
2. stir in flour , blend well
3. add vinegar and water
4. cook and stir until bubbly and slightly thick
5. add sugar and stir until it dissolves
6. add mayo or"miracle whip"
7. chop pickles
8. gently stir in pickles and potatoes
9. serve chilled
target.review: Loved this!  Made it as written and it was quick and tasty.  Also, I'd like to add that there are several types of authentic German potato salad that tend to vary by region.  My family is from southern Germany and many of our handed-down recipes include mayonnaise-based salads.  So don't be disappointed!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
white bean olive salad

from everyday food

1. whisk in a large bowl , olive oil , lemon juice and dijon mustard
2. add salt and pepper to taste
3. add beans , onions and olives and toss to combine
demonstrations.review: This was great and wicked fast!  I was out of lemon juice and red onion, so I bastardized a little bit by subbing red wine vinegar and then adding some cucumbers and feta.  I have a feeling that the lemon juice would have been better, but even with the red wine vinegar, it was very tasty.  I will definitely be making this for quick lunches from now on.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pan fried tofu with spicy peanut sauce

a tasty snack or appetizer. tofu cubes are very crispy outside, yet warm and soft inside. sort of like asian 

1. drain tofu
2. cut into bite-sized cubes
3. toss with cornstarch , coating the cubes
4. sprinkle a little salt and pepper
5. heat some oil
6. fry the tofu cubes in batches , making sure all sides are lightly browned
7. drain on paper towels , then sprinkle with salt and pepper if desired
8. sauce: heat the milk in small saucepan
9. add peanut butter , stirring well
10. add other seasonings , according to personal taste
11. if you use coconut milk , add 1 / 2 - 1 tsp of lime juice too - it will be great !
12. serve hot , as a snack or appetizer
13. sometimes i serve them with a sweet chinese dessert: green bean soup
demonstrations.review: I made this as written and it is GREAT!  I use the peanut sauce on other things as well, such as chicken and plain rice noodles.  So good.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cajun jalapeno poppers

this recipe came from taste testing poppers all over. i combined what i liked and discarded the rest. you can use fresh peppers or prepackaged peppers (not recommended,to soft). if i use fresh, i sometimes like to slice them in half, leaving the stem, de-vein and seed them and saute' them in my favorite beer to soften them up just a little (2-4 minutes). another tip is to always use protective cooking gloves when dealing with peppers.

1. halve the jalapenos leaving the stem attached , de-vein and seed them
2. setting the halved jalapenos and bread crumbs aside , mix all of the other ingredients together
3. take your mixture and completely fill the jalepeno cavities to their brim and set aside
4. put bread crumbs on a flat plate
5. take jalapeno halves , one at a time , and roll cheese side only in bread crumbs and place cheese / crumb side up on a baking pan once completed if you like a thick crumb layer , you can repeat this step
6. if you do not intend to bake finished product skip the rolling part and just lightly sprinkle the top of the jalepenos with the bread crumbs
7. bake at 350 for 15 minutes or until mixture starts to bubble
8. i like to refrigerate at least 1 hour prior to baking sometimes i prepare the day before , cover and refrigerate
9. serve warm , room temperature or chilled with any or all of the recommended sauces
demonstrations.review: This was surprisingly easy to make.  I tend to avoid things with too many ingredients or too complicated of instructions (and it doesn't take much to fall into either category for me), but I found this to be very simple.  The worst part was seeding the jalapenos, which I did very thoroughly.  My German mouth doesn't tolerate much beyond pepper, so I got rid of all the membranes; which, to be honest, made them a little too bland.  In the future, I'll leave just a little bit, but definitely no seeds.  Mine didn't brown very much, probably because I used panko, but I just trusted the cooking times and they turned out great (without any of the optional additions).

target.recipe_text:
lebanese walnut cookies

these are so good! little nut filled bites, with a hint of cinnamon. translated from "cocina libanesa," by anne wilson.

1. line cookie sheets with parchment paper , and heat oven to 375f
2. cream butter and sugar in a large bowl
3. add orange water and sifted flour , and stir until the mixture forms a thick dough
4. set aside
5. to prepare the filling , combine the nuts , sugar and cinnamon in a small bowl
6. form 1 inch balls with the dough , and press the center to form a dent for the filling
7. fill each cookie with about a teaspoon of the filling , and place the cookies on the parchment
8. bake 15-20 minutes or until golden
9. cool on wire racks
target.review: I wanted to try these because I like orange blossom water. These were good. I did add a little extra powdered sugar to the dough, but otherwise made as directed.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
julia child s cuisinart pie crust

easy and so tender!!!!  i love this crust.

1. blend flour , butter , oil and sale in cuisinart until crumbly
2. add water by dribbling and blend until ball forms
3. is ok to not use it all
demonstrations.review: I've tried this recipe before and it is a good one. I usually reduce the salt a bit, and try not to process it too much. It also freezes well.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
vegetarian ceviche that looks not so vegetarian

i use hearts of palm to mimic octopus rings. it's really pretty (even though i always hated octopus). it requires no cooking and all the flavor. amounts vary with size of vegetables.

1. cut hearts of palm in circles and pop out the middle
2. chop everything else and mix together
3. serve in martini or margarita glasses with a little cilantro and fresh black pepper on top
demonstrations.review: This was prety good. Next time I'll reduce the hearts of palm and add more avocado. Shrimp can be added to those not wanting it vegetarian. Good served with tortilla chips.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
copycat  green giant niblets corn in butter sauce

i had to come up with this quick. every thanksgiving my mom serves green giant niblets corn in butter sauce and i promised i would pick it up for her and bring it on thanksgiving day. when i went to the store, they were sold out! i made this recipe and brought it already prepared to thanksgiving dinner. nobody was the wiser! i saved some money too, because i used store brand corn! this recipe makes a lot...you may want to half it.

1. add corn to large sauce pan along with all ingredients except water and cornstarch
2. stir corn mixture over medium heat until butter is melted
3. combine water and cornstarch and stir until cornstarch is disolved
4. slowly add water to corn in sauce pan , stirring constantly
5. reduce heat to simmer and stir until sauce thickens
6. let simmer , stirring occasionally , until corn is tender , about 10 minutes
demonstrations.review: Great! Thanks for sharing.

target.recipe_text:
turkish marinade for chicken

i love yogurt based marinades for chicken; they seal in the moisture well.  i found this one while browsing for recipes for zwt 2006 - african/middle east region.

1. combine all ingredients in a non-reactive bowl
2. add chicken , cover & refrigerate 6 hours or overnight
3. grill , broil or bake chicken as desired
target.review: This is an awesome marinade. I had it at work and had to get the recipe and try it myself! I did cut the chicken into pieces and broil them on skewers on the second rack. At first I left them under the heat for 5 minutes then I continued to flip them until they were perfectly cooked. I used the cumin but might reduce the amount next time- personal preference. Thanks, Susie.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
beef  cheese  and noodle bake

from cooking light, february 2006. yummy, filling casserole.

1. preheat over to 350
2. cook pasta , drain and set aside
3. saute onion , carrot , and garlic for about 3 minutes
4. add ground beef and brown breaking up the meat
5. add tomato sauce , 1 / 2 tsp salt , and pepper
6. continue to cook for about 2 minutes
7. add macaroni
8. put mixture into a 11 x 7 baking dish that has been sprayed with cooking spray
9. heat milk , flour , remaining 1 / 2 tsp salt , and nutmeg over medium heat whisking constantly for about 2 minutes , until smooth and thickening
10. stir in 1 cup of grated cheese until smooth
11. pour cheese mixture over pasta and stir in to blend
12. spread remaining cheese over the top
13. bake for 20 minutes or until cheese is starting to brown
14. let sit for about 5 minutes before serving
demonstrations.review: We enjoyed this recipe. I halved the recipe but kept the beef the same for my boyfriend. I did not have carrots so I mixed in some corn for the crunch. I also used whole grain shell pasta and pasta sauce  instead of tomato sauce just because of what I had in the cupboard. So much better than hamburger helper and I actually know what I'm putting in the pan, thanks!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
grilled parmesan broccoli

this delicious grilled side dish will add nutrition and flavor to any meal. recipe is from light and tasty’s april/may 2005 issue. i love broccoli anyway, and grilling veggies always kicks them up a notch.

1. place broccoli in large bowl
2. combine next four ingredients , drizzle over broccoli , and toss to coat
3. let stand for half an hour
4. spray grill rack before preparing grill for indirect heat
5. toss broccoli again and drain marinade
6. place parmesan in large ziploc bag and shake broccoli , a few pieces at a time , with the cheese to coat
7. grill broccoli , covered , over indirect medium heat for 8-10 minutes on each side or until crisp-tender
demonstrations.review: I've made this several times now and it never gets old! I also discovered while sneaking bites that the marinade is just as good if you leave the broccoli raw. I gave an aunt the recipe because she loved it so much and since it was raining and they sauteed it and said it was still delicious. FIVE STARS!!!! EDIT: also great sauteed...

demonstrations.recipe_text:
low fat broccoli  rice and cheese casserole

nan

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees
2. spray a 9x13-inch baking dish with buttered flavored cooking spray
3. set aside
4. spray a medium skillet with butter flavored spray
5. saute celery and onion over medium heat until onion is clear
6. transfer onion and celery to a large mixing bowl
7. add soups and cheese
8. stir until well blended
9. add remaining ingredients and pour into prepared pan
10. bake uncovered 35-40 minutes or until bubbly and golden brown
demonstrations.review: this is delicious! i'm not a huge broccoli fan but i tried it anyways and was very surprised! i too used 2% velveeta because i could not find a jar of low fat american cheese. thanks for sharing gingerbear!

target.recipe_text:
monterey jack casserole

my sis-inlaw gave this to me

1. preheat oven to 350
2. in skillet , brown ground beef
3. add onion
4. reduce heat and saute 5 minutes
5. drain excess fat
6. place 2 cups of crushed corn chips in bottom of greased 1 1 / 2 quart dish
7. layer ground beef over chips
8. pour enchilada sauce over beef
9. top with cheese
10. bake 20-30 minutes or until bubbly and heated through
11. sprinkle remaining corn chips over top of casserole
12. bake additional 5 minutes
13. top individual servings with sour cream , if desired
target.review:
Thank your sister-in-law, for the recipe and thank you for posting it.
I fixed it last night for my husband and I.
WE really liked it, but my husband thought it was a little too much, sauce.Will cut back next time.
Also, i used a combination of colby and monterey cheese, combined.
Worked out great.
Thanks, MayorLady.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
peanut butter crispy brownies

this is an adaptation of a "brownie goody bar" recipe i found on the back of a better crocker brownie box a few years ago.  we also call them scotcharoo brownies, because they have a butterscotch, peanut butter, rice crispy layer on top of a fuggy brownie. this is my family's favorite sweet treat!  they are sooo good.  i usually wrap them individually in suran wrap and store in the refrigerator so that they do not all get eaten at once.  this slows the guys down a little.

1. heat oven to 350
2. make brownies as directed for a 9 x 13-inch pan
3. cool completely
4. melt butterscotch chips and peanut butter in a 1-quart saucepan or in a glass bowl in microwave stirring frequently
5. stir cereal into peanut putter butterscotch mixture
6. pour cereal mixture over brownies
7. spread evenly
8. refrigerate about 30 minutes or until set before cutting
demonstrations.review:
I fixed this last night and I was very pleased with the results.
I like peanut butter a lot, so next time I make this, I am going to use peanut butter chips.
Really, give it a peanut  butter taste.
I guess you could use any flavor of chips ,that suits your taste.
Thanks for posting.
Bjtaillights.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
sugarhouse apple rings

this apples are wonderful served with baked beans.  we eat them year round.

1. in a shallow bowl , combine the flour eggs , syrup and buttermilk
2. dip apple rings on both sides into the batter
3. deep fry
4. sprinkle with confectioner's sugar and enjoy !
demonstrations.review:
I tried these apples for dinner, tonight.
They were very good.
I used delicious apples, but they were not very sweet.
I think next time I make them, I am going to add a little bit of sugar to the batter.
Other than that, they were good.
Thanks, for posting.
Bjtaillights.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
fruit cocktail cake  from a cake mix

this delicious cake comes together fast, starting with a cake mix. i think the flavor is very subtle, and the cake is quite moist. the original recipe had a syrupy sweet icing on it, but i added the coconut/brown sugar on top instead, and i think it makes this a nice snacking cake. (*note: i used a fruit cocktail i've found that has guava, mango, etc., and found the pieces a little large, so i chopped it up a bit before adding to mixture. the regular fruit cocktail with grapes, etc., should be fine w/o that)

1. preheat to 325
2. combine cake mix , fruit cocktail with juices , 1 cup of coconut and eggs in a large mixer bowl
3. blend , then beat at medium speed for 2 minutes
4. pour batter into greased 9x13 pan , or two 8x8 pans
5. sprinkle batter evenly with remaining 1 / 2 cup of coconut , and then 1 / 2 cup of brown sugar
6. bake at 325 for 45 min
7. serve warm or room temp
8. stays moist for several days
demonstrations.review:
Hi,newspapergal,

I tried your cake today, and the only word I can come up with, is delicious.
I added about a 1/1/2 cups of coconut to the mix, instead of just a cup.
I also followed your tip and used the coconut and brown sugar on top.
I will be sure and keep  this great recipe.
Very easy to put together, also.
Maybe, nest time I fix it , I will add nuts, also, but even without the nuts, it was a fantastic cake.
Thanks, for posting it.

Bjtaillights@cs.com

target.recipe_text:
delicious chili and pasta skillet

a wonderful one-skillet meal that's very tasty, and even tastes better if left for next day

1. in a skillet , cook ground beef with onion , bell pepper until no longer pink
2. drain fat then add in garlic and chili flakes and continue cooking until the meat is browned
3. stir in canned chili beans , tomatoes with juice , 1 cup shredded cheddar cheese , sour cream and chili powder
4. mix the mixture with cooked pasta , until well coated then season with salt and pepper
5. sprinkle with remaining 1 cup shredded cheese
6. cover and cook in the same skillet for 20 minutes on med-low heat , until bubbly
target.review: Looking for a quick and satisfying meal?  This is it!  I also loved the fact that it calls for most of the ingredients that I usually have on hand anyway.  I served a simple garden salad and the meal was complete.  You did it again, Kittencal.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chicken penne salad with green beans

from cooking light magazine, august 2002, as requested.

1. 1
2. cook pasta in boiling water 7 minutes
3. add green beans
4. cook 4 minutes
5. drain and rinse with cold water
6. drain
7. 2
8. combine pasta mixture , chicken , onion , basil , parsley , and bell pepper in a large bowl , tossing gently to combine
9. 3
10. combine oil and remaining ingredients in a small bowl , stirring with a whisk
11. drizzle over pasta mixture
12. toss gently to coat
13. yield: 4 servings
demonstrations.review:
This is a wonderful light salad and a great way to get those vegetables in your diet.  Very colorful and makes a nice presentation too.  I can't wait to make this again.  Thanks for sharing, shanna bennet.
This is a winner.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
blt dip  taste is amazing

this dip is easy and delicious!!! your friends and family will not be able to get enough! it is important that you do not substitute the miracle whip for any other mayonnaise, because it will not have the same flavor. this is the true taste of bacon, lettuce, and tomato! please come back and rate this recipe after you have enjoyed it!!!

1. blend all ingredients well in large bowl
2. refrigerate at least 2 hours before serving
3. i like to take a large loaf of italian bread , and cut a section of the bread out of the top , to form a"well" , and cut up the bread that i remove from the"well" into large cubes for dipping , and pour the dip into the"bread bowl"
4. then place the bread loaf on a large platter , and arrange the cubes of bread around it !
5. this makes for an attractive and delicious presentation !
6. can also be served with cocktail rye , or chips
7. this makes a lot of dip , so for smaller groups , cut recipe in 1 / 2
demonstrations.review: This really DOES taste like a BLT. We also let this dip sit for almost 24 hours before serving which lets the flavor blend well and the extra added bonus of having it made ahead of time.  I personally do not care for Miracle Whip so I used Hellman's Mayo and it worked great for us.  Thanks for sharing, Mrs. Gottrocks.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
yummy kahlua pancakes

these are wonderful tasting. we loved the taste the kahlua and hint of lemon gave to these rich and filling pancakes. i tested these on all of my family and changed some things around according to their comments. the last were my dd and her bf and they gave them a thumbs up. this makes 12 6" pancakes. made for rsc #10

1. soak raisins in warm water for 20-30 minutes
2. in a medium bowel mix together flours , baking powder , baking soda , salt and brown sugar
3. in a large bowel , using an electric mixer , beat eggs until frothy
4. add vanilla yogurt , butter and kahlua and mix well
5. add flour mixture to the yogurt mixture and beat on medium speed just until blended and smooth
6. place shredded apples in the microwave for 60 seconds
7. drain raisins on paper towels
8. fold raisins and apples into batter and combine well
9. if batter is too thick , add a little more yogurt or more kahlua
10. heat griddle to medium heat
11. spoon batter , cup at a time , onto hot griddle and spread out to approximately 6-7 inch pancakes
12. cook for 5-6 minutes or until bubbles form on top
13. flip and cook for another 5-6 minutes or until golden brown
14. serve with toasted pecans and maple syrup
demonstrations.review: We found these pancakes to be perfect in flavor and texture.  They were a tad thick so I added some extra Kahlua and milk.  PERFECT!!!  The raisins, apples and pecans really puts this over the top.  You don't want to miss these pancakes.  Thanks for sharing, Nimz.

target.recipe_text:
oriental chicken salad with crunchy ramen noodles

this is a salad that even non-cabbage eaters love. it is nice and crunchy with great flavor. i once took it to a potluck in my apartment complex and then had to put the recipe up on the bulletin board because everyone wanted the recipe!

1. prepare dressing and set aside
2. smash noodles of top ramen and brown over medium heat in 3 tbs oil
3. once noodles have begun to slightly brown , add slivered almonds
4. if you start to brown the ramen and almonds at the same time , the almonds will burn before the ramen browns
5. once the ramen noodles have turned a dark golden brown , remove from heat and set aside
6. combine cabbage , green onions , chicken and sunflower seeds in a large bowl
7. add the ramen / almond mixture and stir well
8. add dressing and stir to coat
9. i generally prepare the dressing right before serving
10. if it sits in the refrigerator too long , it gets very thick and won't remix well
11. also , this amount of dressing is just the right amount to give the salad a good coating
12. if you are one of those who likes more dressing , i would recommend making 1 / 2 batch of extra dressing
13. if you plan on eating this left over , keep in mind that the noodles will not stay crunchy
target.review: First off, this salad converted me to 'crunchy' ramen noodles. The idea of eating them without boiling to noodley form has always been such a peciular idea to me - Nope, they rock, very nutty! Will do anytime now. And this salad is savory delicious too. Super easy and a real hit. I just bought the pre made slaw at the store, super good with a little carrot too! Also, per other similar salad recommendations added 1 ramen noodle seasoning packet to the dressing - yummers.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
low cal  fat free garlic mashed potatoes

these potatoes have a wonderful flavor with no calories from fat.  i developed this dish for just my wife and i but anyone should be able to easely multiply the servings.

1. chop potatoes into 1 / 2" cubes
2. combine potatoes and garlic and add water to cover
3. boil about 30 minutes or until potatoes are tender
4. don't overcook
5. drain potatoes and garlic and place in a food processor
6. gently process until almost smooth
7. sprinkle with butter buds
8. process while adding half & half until desired texture is achieved , being careful not to overprocess
demonstrations.review: Very nice recipe! Used yukon gold potatoes to complete a buttery flavor.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
toasted ravioli

these italian appetizers are crunchy and delicious dipped in a warm marinara sauce. they are very addictive! make a bunch, you'll need to have a lot!

1. cook ravioli in boiling salted water until they float to the top
2. remove from water and drain
3. set aside to cool
4. heat vegetable oil in fryer at least 2" deep to a temperature of 375 degrees
5. dip ravioli in beaten egg , then cover in breadcrumbs
6. fry in batches in hot oil until golden brown , about 5 minutes
7. drain
8. sprinkle hot ravioli with parmesan cheese
9. heat marinara sauce and set aside in serving bowl
10. serve ravioli with dipping sauce
demonstrations.review: Hot damn these are great! Super simple to make - though I am often intimidated by the hot oil (dont have a deep fryer yet) I soldiered through and we were stoked with the outcome! These were gobbled up right away by my guests. I have none for later! Guess its time to heat up some more oil!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
maple sausage and waffle casserole

i found this recipe in cook's country magazine. they did a taste test on frozen waffles and it turned out that eggo homestyle waffles were the best out of eight brands that they tasted. 
depending on the size and shape of your waffles, you will need 6 to 8. don't use belgian style because they are too thick for this recipe.  you can double the recipe and use a 9 x 13-inch baking dish. 
time does not include refrigerating one hour or overnight.

1. heat oven to 350
2. arrange waffles in single layer on baking sheet
3. bake until crisp , about 10-minutes per side
4. brown sausage in non-stick skillet over medium heat , breaking it apart with spoon , 8-10 minutes
5. drain on paper towel-lined plate
6. butter 8-inch square baking dish
7. add half of waffles in single layer
8. add half of sausage and 1 / 2 cup cheese
9. repeat layering of waffles , sausage , and 1 / 2 cup of cheese
10. whisk eggs , milk , maple syrup , salt , and pepper in medium bowl until combined
11. pour egg mixture evenly over casserole
12. cover with plastic wrap and place weights on top
13. refrigerate for at least 1 hour or overnight
14. adjust oven rack to middle position and heat oven to 325
15. let casserole stand at room temperature for 20 minutes
16. uncover casserole and sprinkle remaining 1 / 2 cup cheese over top
17. bake until edges and center are puffed , 45 to 50 minutes
18. cool 5 minutes
19. cut into pieces and serve
demonstrations.review: This came together beautifully! We really enjoyed it. I was hesitant with it but it sounded so good I had to try it. Sure glad I did! Will surely make this awesome dish again.

target.recipe_text:
pasta with sausage and peppers

for those people (such as my husband) who are not too fond of the intense tomato flavor found in many pasta dishes....this is for you. the ease of preparation is a big bonus for cooks, too. an italian cookbook that has been in my collection for almost fifty years includes this recipe.

1. in large skillet , cook sausage , peppers , onion and garlic until meat is browned and vegetables are tender
2. drain off fat , if necessary
3. stir in cream , parsley , marjoram , salt and pepper
4. bring to boiling , reduce heat
5. cook and stir over medium heat for 6-8 minutes or until slightly thickened
6. toss sausage mixture and cheese with pasta until coated
7. serve immediately
target.review: This is a hearty, beautiful dish that was wonderfully easy and fast to make! I'll bet the sausage mixture, if thickened a bit more with extra parmesan cheese, would be fabulous on an Italian roll, too. I served it with farfalle pasta, and my family loved it!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
oven fried chicken chimichangas

a fast and healthier way to serve chimichangas than the traditional deep fried. these are very good, and you may dress them up to you own preference. i like to serve with green chile sauce sometimes instead of the picante sauce.

1. mix chicken , picante sauce or salsa , cumin , oregano , cheese and onions
2. place about 1 / 4 cup of the chicken mixture in the center of each tortilla
3. fold opposite sides over filling
4. roll up from bottom and place seam-side down on a baking sheet
5. brush with melted margarine
6. bake at 400f for 25 minutes or until golden
7. garnish with additional cheese and green onion and serve salsa on the side
demonstrations.review: This was a big hit with my family and a recipe my husband said to "please" make again! The tortillas came out of the oven crispy and the filling was delicious. I love recipes that are versatile, when you can use a variety of ingredient combinations -- and this one is a great example. Next time I think I'll use beef, or maybe I'll add some black beans. This would be great to make ahead then bake 30 minutes before dinnertime. Love it!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
vanilla oat cake

this is a finnish coffee cake. it literally takes 30 minutes total and it tastes wonderful!

1. preheat oven to 400
2. mix all the ingredients for the cake in a mix master for approximately 4 minutes or until well blended and slightly fluffy spread on a greased or lined 9 by 13" pan
3. mix all the ingredients for the topping and pour over the top
4. cook for 20 minutes or until inserting a toothpick in the center comes out clean
5. let the cake stand for about 10 minutes
demonstrations.review: Moist, buttery cake with a scrumptous cinnamon/oat topping -- what could be better with coffee? Not for the calorie conscious, however, but definitely worth baking now and then! Fast and easy, too.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
awesome chocolate chip cookies

this is the best recipe i've tried so far. moist and chewy and they disappear in the blink of an eye!

1. pre-heat oven to 375 degrees
2. combine shortening , brown sugar , milk , and vanilla in large bowl
3. beat at medium speed until well blended
4. beat egg into mixture
5. combine flour , salt , and baking soda
6. mix into creamed mixture just until blended
7. add chocolate chips and nuts and mix
8. drop rounded teaspoons of dough on ungreased baking sheet about 3 inches apart
9. bake 8-10 minutes for chewy , 11-13 minutes for crisp cookies
10. cool 2 minutes on baking sheet then transfer to foil to cool completely
11. if nuts are used decrease chips to 1 cup
demonstrations.review: I didn't think there would be much difference in this chocolate chip cookie recipe and others I've tried ... but, boy, was I wrong! These have great flavor and a wonderful soft texture. I made as written except I used regular shortening instead of butter flavor; and I substituted a coarsley chopped Ghiradelli semi-sweet chocolate bar (4 oz.) for the chocolate chips. This will be saved in my "favorites" cookbook!

target.recipe_text:
tortilla chicken casserole

easy tasty casserole just right for lunch or dinner. serve with a green salad and perhaps some refried beans.  if you wish you may skip the center layer of tortillas and only use 6 tortillas (personally i like the center layer). if you skip the center layer still put in half of the cheese after you have poured in half of the chicken mixture.

1. lightly grease 8'x11 1 / 2' casserole dish
2. spray a non stick skillet with vegetable oil and brown the chicken along with the garlic & onions
3. remove from skillet
4. add corn , red pepper , jalapenos and warm through
5. add tomato sauce , cumin , cilantro , hot sauce , all spice , salt & pepper , bring to a simmer
6. add tomatoe & return the chicken to the skillet , stir , bring to a simmer
7. line the greased pie plate with 3 tortillas
8. pour in half the chicken mixture & top with half the cheese
9. cover with 3 more tortillas
10. pour in the remaining sauce , top with 3 more tortillas
11. sprinkle the top with the remaining cheese
12. bake in 350f oven for apprx 25 minutes or until the casserole is heated through the cheese has melted and is nicely browned
13. let it rest 5 minutes , slice & serve
target.review: I amde this twice and both times my husband loved it.  I skipped the cilantro (I hate the taste of it) and the tomatoes (didn't have any)  but the recipe is really easy and tasty.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
banana in coconut cream

this is a thai recipe creamy and not too sweet, with all the healthy benefits of bananas, so rich in bone-building phosphorus and calcium, heart-healthy potassium, vitamins a and b6. great for those leg cramps!

1. in a saucepan , heat the coconut milk with the cinnamon , sugar and salt , and cook gently until the sugar has dissolved
2. add the banana pieces and cook gently for 5 minutes
3. remove cinnamon and discard
4. divide the mixture into 6-8 small bowls and serve warm
demonstrations.review: I followed the directions exactly and was not disappointed.  This is a delicious dish.  IT took about 5 minutes to put together and another 5 to cook it.  My husband and I absolutely loved it.  The slight salty taste really went well with the sweetness of the sugar  and the smooth, rich coconut milk.  This is addictive.  Thanks for a great, easy recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s  brown sugar caramel sauce or ice cream topping

with only very few ingredients and five minutes to make it just couldn't get any easier and it tastes so good! ---it goes great with bread pudding, over ice cream and with desserts :)

1. in a small saucepan melt butter with salt
2. add the brown sugar
3. whisk until combined and thickened
4. whisk in the whipping cream , until thoroughly blended
5. mix in vanilla until combined
demonstrations.review: This sauce is fantastic.  It is so easy to make and so yummy!  I have made other caramael sauces ans none were easier OR tastier than this one.  It was done in 10 minutes! Thank you for this keeper!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
gingerbread pound cake

what a treat to serve to those you love! great as an appetizer, dessert or just for breakfast.

1. in a mixing bowl , cream butter beating well on medium speed with an electric mixer
2. gradually add sugar
3. add eggs , one at a time , beating after each egg is added
4. combine flour , soda , and spices
5. set aside
6. combine molasses and sour cream
7. add flour mixture to creamed mixture alternately with molasses mixture , beginning and ending with flour mixture
8. mix just until blended after each addition
9. pour batter into a greased and floured 10 inch bundt pan
10. bake at 325 degrees for 1 hour or until wooden pick inserted in center comes out clean
11. cool in pan for 15 minutes then remove and cool completely on a wire cake rack
12. sprinkle with powdered sugar
13. serve with lemon sauce , if desired
14. lemon sauce: combine first 3 ingredients in a saucepan , stirring until smooth
15. cook over medium heat , stirring until smooth and thickened
16. add remaining ingredients
17. cook until heated
demonstrations.review: This recipe is awesome! Our entire house was filled with a delicious, spicy, warm fragrance while it was baking.  It is very easy to prepare and the result is so delicious, we never got the lemon sauce on it.  We couldn't wait.  The outside is crunchy and the inside is moist and tender.  It tastes just like gingerbread! YUMMO!  My Mom is taking my printed version of this one!

target.recipe_text:
gabriels sauteed fava beans

this basic method of cooking fava beans was taught to me by chef gabriel claycamp of culinary communion.  when i was recently able to get ahold of fresh fava beans, i wanted to cook them in a way that highlighted the taste of the beans themselves, and here’s how gabriel suggested i fix them.  although fresh fava beans are, as he said, about 70% waste (and the prep time is shelling and peeling), the remaining 30% after you’ve prepared and eaten them are *well* worth the effort!  we loved them!

1. first , shell the beans from the fava pods
2. in a large saucepan , bring water to a boil , then add salt the amount depends on how much water you have , but it should be very salty , like seawater
3. in a bowl , combine ice and tap water to make ice water
4. set aside
5. add the shelled beans to the boiling water and let cook for about 3 minutes , then remove from saucepan and immediately plunge into the ice water to halt the cooking
6. let the beans cool , then peel the outer skin from each of them
7. over medium heat in a skillet , melt together the butter and olive oil , then add the garlic and saut for 1 minute
8. add the peeled fava beans and saut for about 5 to 7 minutes , or until they are done to your preference
9. season to taste with salt and freshly ground pepper , serve , and enjoy !
target.review: I am so glad that Gabe showed her how to fix fava beans. I want her to make these whenever she is able to find fresh fava beans!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cuban roast beef

nan

1. preheat oven to 350f degrees
2. mix the first 7 ingredients to make a stuffing
3. make an incision 1 1 / 2" to 2" deep along the length of the roast
4. stuff the stuffing into the incision
5. salt and pepper the roast
6. brown the roast on all sides in bacon fat in a large heavy casserole add all the rest of the ingredients and cook in the oven for 2 1 / 2 hours or until the meat is very tender
7. check once or twice to make sure that the liquid is not boiling away
8. add water or unsalted stock as necessary
demonstrations.review: I like roasts that have ingredients cooked inside, so I really liked this one.  It was very flavorful.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
palak paneer  indian fresh spinach with paneer cheese

creamy and rich, a delight to eat. a dish i fell in love with at a local restaurant and adapted a recipe to closely resemble theirs.

1. cut spinach into shreds and cook in 3 tablespoons water until tender
2. remove from heat
3. saute onion , cinnamon , cardamom , and ginger in 1-2 tablespoons ghee or oil until onion is translucent
4. then add garlic and chopped tomatoes , and reduce heat
5. cook this briefly and slowly blend in yogurt a little at a time to prevent curdling
6. add coriander , garam masala , paprika , and salt , mixing well
7. add cooked spinach with liquid , cover and simmer on low heat for approximately 20-30 minutes
8. remove from heat
9. take half of spinach mixture and puree in food processor or blender , and return to mixture and stir
10. slowly stir in heavy cream , and heat through on low heat
11. add paneer cubes
12. serve
demonstrations.review: My wife thanks you.  I thank you.  This is good stuff.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
swedish grilled kebabs

the linneas of texas, swedish recipes. gathered from the internet 1998.  choose any quick cooking veggies your family will enjoy in this recipe.  we like to use cherry or grape tomatoes, chunks of red or green bell pepper, quartered red or sweet onion, mushrooms, slices of yellow or zucchini squash and lemon slices.

1. skin the chicken and cut off all visible fat
2. cut each breast into 6-8 pieces
3. season w salt& pepper
4. mix ingredients for marinade , add chicken and marinate several hours or over night
5. arrange chicken on skewers , alternating with veggies of your choice
6. cherry tomatoes , quartered red onions , thick slices of lemon , large pieces of green pepper , mushrooms or summer squash may be used
7. broil on charcoal fire 4 minutes on each side
8. garnish w bay leaves
9. marinade can be boiled down and spooned over chicken when done
demonstrations.review: I liked these a lot! They didn't taste like I expected, but were nice. Like piccata. I would make them again!

target.recipe_text:
lee s whole wheat and nut pancakes

my daughter hates pancakes but she loves these ones. whole wheat, oats, almonds, pecans, sunflower seeds and wheat germ.

1. mix oats , whole wheat flour , flour baking soda baking powder , salt sugar , almonds , pecans , sunflower seeds , wheat germ together in food processor pluse until nuts and seeds are finely ground
2. transfer to bowl
3. in small bowl combine buttermilk egg and oil whisk together
4. mix butter milk mixture with dry ingredients stir well
5. lightly oil griddle
6. with a 1 / 3 cup measuring cup pour batter onto hot griddle
7. cook til lightly browned and flip
8. serve with maple syrup or topped with fresh fruit
target.review: I made these this morning and it was my first time making pancakes without a box mix.  They were excellent and I will probably never use a box mix again.  The only change I made was walnuts instead of pecans because of what I had on hand.  They cooked nice and brown, and YUM-YUM-YUM!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
super healthy hummus

taken off a website, don't have the reference. an excellent hummus, the only one i make anymore. you really need a blender or food processor to get the consistency right. 1/4 cup = 1 point ww.

1. combine everything in blender or food processor and process until smooth
2. the blender gives the best result
3. if you need more liquid to make a nice consistency , add a bit more yogurt
4. chill
5. serve with pitas or as a veggie dip
demonstrations.review: Made this last night and am looking forward to snacking on it all weekend.  I love a healthy hummus with baby carrots.  Also like the low Weight Watcher points, as I am (you guessed it) a proud member of Weight Watchers.  Thanks Kasha!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
fat free chocolate muffins

a wonderfully moist fat free chocolate muffin, and a sneaky way to get that nutritious beta carotene! my kids have no idea they are eating pumpkin! they actually ask for these babies. the pudding mix is optional, it adds some sweetness and moistness, but you don't need it. the addition will add to your baking time 5-10 minutes.

1. spray muffin pans with non-stick coating
2. mix all ingredients together
3. you will need to use an electric mixer , the batter is very dry , like brownie batter , keep mixing it will mix together
4. do not add eggs or milk
5. baking soda is your leavening agent , and pumpkin sbstitutes your fats
6. bake at 350f for 15 minutes , for regular muffin pans , 20 minutes for jumbo pans
7. test with a toothpick to see if they are done
demonstrations.review: I have made these twice now.  They are moist and satisfy my chocolate cravings.  The second time I added some applesauce I needed to use up and also used Splenda instead of sugar.  Liked these even better than the first time.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
emily s cheese and tomato cracker appetizer

a basic, yummy recipe that you can get creative with. fast and so easy to make!

1. add chives , marjoram , and garlic to cream cheese
2. cream together until ingredients blended
3. smear about a half teaspoon on each cracker , and add sliced cheese and sliced tomatoes on top
demonstrations.review: Served these last night and they were a hit. I used whipped cream cheese, and I think next time I will use block cream cheese and whip it myself as the cream cheese mixture was sort of runny. And I used Ritz WW crackers and a bigger cracker might have worked better. But the taste was very good.

target.recipe_text:
bob s red mill easy gluten free banana bread

this comes from the back of bob's red mill all purpose gf flour packaging.  it's a quick and easy recipe.  the bread is especially good toasted with butter!  i have substituted 1/2 almond meal and 1/2 white rice flour for the all purpose flour, and just about any combination of gf flours seems to work.  i always leave out the raisins & nuts, too.

1. preheat oven to 350
2. grease 9x5-inch non-stick loaf pan
3. for smaller loaves , use three 5x3 inch loaf pans
4. cream together oil , sugar , eggs , and vanilla in large bowl
5. add flour , xanthan gum , salt , baking powder and cinnamon to egg mixture , alternating with bananas
6. beat until smooth
7. stir in nuts and raisins
8. batter will be somewhat soft
9. transfer to pan
10. bake 9x5" loaf for 1 hour , 5x3" loaves for 45 minutes
target.review:
Wow...

This was delicious.

My first taste of banana bread since diagnosis (celiac), and WHAT A TREAT!

Thanks so much...

Modifications:
- omitted nuts and raisins, added 3/4 cup chocolate chips. In my opinion, two sweet, would have left the chips at 1/2 cup instead

demonstrations.recipe_text:
blueberry pudding

a nice change of pace from the same old desserts. warm and comforting, especially for blueberry lovers.

1. preheat oven to 350 and grease a 9-inch pie plate
2. place blueberries in medium bowl
3. combine 1 / 4 cup of the brown sugar and 1 tbsp
4. of the flour
5. toss with blueberries to coat
6. spoon mixture into pie plate
7. in separate bowl , rub remaining 1 cup flour and butter together with finger
8. mix in remaining 1 / 2 cup brown sugar
9. add milk , egg , lemon peel and vanilla , and blend well
10. pour batter over blueberry mixture
11. bake until firm and golden brown , about 55 minutes
12. cool at least 10 minutes before serving
13. top with whipped topping if desired
demonstrations.review: This was soo good! I made a GF (gluten-free) version using Schar "Mehl Glutenfrei", and it was very very good. No GF flavour at all! I omitted the lemon peel because I didn't have any, but used lemon juice and it tasted fine. It took the whole 55 min to bake.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
basil pesto

this is a wonderful lemon-flavored pesto. this was my first taste of pesto and i've never gone back!

update as of 2/13/04
i'm glad that you all like this.  i freeze this now and keep it on hand for my spaghetti sauce or others sauces.  it freezes great!

1. mix everything together in food processor except the oil and lemon
2. once everything is mixed well , drizzle with lemon and oil
3. mix until well blended
4. serve on pasta or just about anything that needs a pick me up
5. will keep in refrigerator for 2-3 days
6. enjoy !
demonstrations.review: First time making basil pesto, and it was delicious!<br/><br/>Used a combination of red (correct term?) and green leaf basil, used almonds instead of pine nuts, and left out the parmesan cheese (lactose intolerant). It was so good!<br/><br/>Mixed with spaghetti, served with pan-fried shrimp.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
raspberry  nectarine and mango crumble

this recipe i first tasted in guatemala on a mission trip.  i loved it so i found the recipe and here it is.  it is very tender and tastes the best when served warm with vanilla ice cream

1. preheat oven to 375f
2. with an electric mixer , combine 1 cup flour , brown sugar , cinnamon , salt , and oats
3. mix on low for 30 seconds , add butter , and mix until clumps form
4. transfer to a bowl , cover , and refrigerate until ready to use
5. peel and pit nectarines , and cut into 1-inch chunks
6. place in a large bowl
7. halve mangoes lengthwise , angling the knife slightly to cut around the pit
8. remove and discard pit and peel
9. cut flesh into 1-inch chunks and add to nectarines
10. add raspberries
11. add remaining 1 1 / 2 tablespoons flour , granulated sugar , and lime juice
12. toss gently to combine
13. transfer fruit to a shallow 12-inch round gratin dish
14. distribute topping evenly over fruit
15. bake until topping is golden brown and juices bubble remove from oven and let cool slightly
16. serve warm with ice cream
demonstrations.review: This recipe is really good, and simple! I used frozen mango chunks and frozen raspberries (a bit more mango than raspberry), and the flavour was very good.

target.recipe_text:
parmesan chicken fingers or filets

there are a gazillion recipes for this, but i searched them all, and none are just like mine. my kids' absolute favorite. i get requests for this dish all the time....soooo good with potatoes and green beans!

1. mix all dry ingredients together
2. dip chicken in butter , then into dry mix
3. bake on greased pan , uncovered , at 400 for 20 minutes
4. serve with your favorite dipping sauce: ranch , bbq sauce , sweet and sour , honey --
target.review:
WONDERFUL! DH and I both LOVED this. The chicken was moist and tender--the breading had awesome flavor. I used shredded parmesan, because that's what I had and I think I'll stick to that. I'll be making this over and over and over and ov............
Thanks for this recipe. It's a DEFINATE keeper!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
country white bread or dinner rolls  bread machine

we think this is the best white bread recipe ever! it is a tender bread with a slightly sweet taste. my dinner rolls using this dough are so good, everyone always loves them. it doesn't take to long to make them when the bread maker does most of the work. the cook time is listed for the rolls only because everyone's bread makers cooks at different rates. mine is older and a regular loaf will take 4 hours and 10 minutes. i have found that 15 balls of dough fit perfectly in the 9x13 pan with sides touching after raising the 2nd time but they can be made whatever size you want. i hope you enjoy this great bread as much as we do.

1. in bread machine pan , place all ingredients from flour through yeast in order as recommended by the manufacturer
2. select the basic bread setting
3. check dough after 5 minutes of mixing , if needed add 1-2t of water or flour
4. bake as normal
5. for dinner rolls
6. mix in bread machine but use only the dough option
7. lightly grease a 9 x 13 baking pan
8. when dough is finished shape into 15 uniformly sized balls
9. i always grease my hands with shortening to smooth the dough out and it helps keep the dough from drying out
10. cover and let the rolls rise in a warm , draft free place until risen to the desired size
11. i let them about double in size
12. bake in a 350 oven about 12-15 minutes until golden brown
13. after removing from the oven , brush the tops of the rolls with melted butter
14. take out of pan and let completely cool before storing
demonstrations.review:
I can't believe that I forgot to rate this WONDERFUL bread! I tried recipe after recipe and DH would just say "it's OK". But he said that he LOVED this bread. I make it every 3 days. DH told me not to try any more recipes because this is THE one.
It makes great toast too. I make the dough in the bread machine and bake it in the oven...it's prettier that way. 
Some days I have to add more flour. Some days more water. It depends on how dry or damp the weather is, so don't be discouraged with this recipe for that reason. As I said, this is THE bread! Try it once and you'll be hooked!
Update 2/2/10... I'm still making this bread every 3 days for my hubby, but now I also make it regularly for my daughter and her family. Here is a tip from her: this bread makes the very very best French toast. Ever!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chili s crispy honey chipotle chicken crispers bytodd wilbur

these sweet and spicy chicken tenders can be served as either an appetizer or an entree.  this recipe was created by todd wilbur from top secret recipes - www.topsecretrecipes.com.

1. make honey-chipotle sauce by combining all ingredients in a small saucepan over medium heat until boiling
2. reduce heat and simmer for 2 minutes
3. remove from heat
4. heat shortening or oil in fryer or dutch oven to 350 degrees f
5. whisk together all ingredients for the batter , excluding flour , in a shallow bowl for at least 30 seconds
6. whisk in the flour
7. make the breading by combining all ingredients in another shallow bowl or pie pan
8. when you are ready to fry the chicken , dip each piece of chicken into the batter
9. lift the chicken out of the batter and let some of the excess drip off
10. toss the chicken into the dry breading and coat completely
11. repeat with 2-3 other pieces
12. carefully drop the breaded chicken into the hot oil and fry for 4 minutes , or until golden brown
13. remove chicken from oil and allow to drain on paper towels
14. repeat steps 8-13 until all the chicken tenders have been cooked
15. when all the chicken tenders are done , drop them into a large glass or metal bowl
16. pour the sauce over the top , and toss gently until all the chicken tenders are coated with sauce
demonstrations.review: I made the sauce only, so my review is about only the sauce. It was WONDERFUL! Absolutely wonderful. The only substitution was white wine instead of vinegar because I can't stand the smell of vinegar. This sauce is quite spicy, so if you don't like a lot of heat, you may want to add less chipotle pepper. The first night we spooned it over B/S chicken that I had baked. The second night we had pre-made chicken strips and drizzled the sauce over them. It was even hotter than the night before. Tonight I made a double batch to use with country style boneless pork ribs. We LOVE this sauce. Thank you for sharing!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
bacon wrapped jalapeno poppers

these bacon-wrapped jalapeno poppers are unbelievably good! you'll love them!

1. cut stems off of peppers and cut them all in half longways
2. remove seeds from peppers
3. fill each pepper with cream cheese and sprinkle cheddar cheese on top
4. wrap 1 / 2 slice of bacon around each pepper half
5. place on baking sheets and place in 450 degree oven for 10 to 15 minutes or until bacon is fully cooked
6. remove and serve when cooled
7. enjoy !
8. i always freeze them after they are made for about 20 minutes to a hour before putting them in the oven or on the grill
9. doing this will keep the cheese from melting out as much
demonstrations.review: I can't believe I haven't rated this yet! We have been making these WONDERFUL poppers for 2 years now. DH and I don't like cream cheese, so I stuffed them with chunks of cheddar instead. That's the only thing I did differently. These are amazing!!

target.recipe_text:
caramel chocolate bars

found my old recipe box and this one was in it. can't even remember who the mcp was that gave me the recipe any more, but it sounds wonderful and she says that is is very easy.

1. preheat oven to 350
2. cream brown sugar and margarine
3. add dry ingredients reserving 3 tbsp of flour and stir in the oatmeal
4. press 1 / 2 of the mixture in the bottom of a greased 9 x 13 pan and bake for 10 minutes
5. sprinkle chocolate chips over crust
6. mix caramel topping with the reserved flour
7. drizzle this over the chips
8. sprinkle the top with the remaining crumb mixture
9. bake for an additional 15 minutes
target.review:
YUMMO!!! I had a package mix for these once and loved them!! I much prefer homemade - so I made these - so glad I did!

I used the whole jar of caramel sauce as I saw in another recipe and, since I buy choc chips in bulk - just added a layer of choc chips without measuring.

I found the baking time to be right on.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
oven rice

this dish has come in handy many times when i am making the entree, the side dish is baking. it is a very good with pork, chicken or beef.

1. thoroughly combine all ingredients in a covered casserole
2. cover and bake 45 minutes at 350 degrees f
3. remove cover and bake another 15 minutes
4. fluff with a fork before serving
demonstrations.review: I just love oven rice.  I made a couple of changes - though I have made this exactly as written too.  I sauteed the onion and 2 cloves fresh minced garlic in just 2 TBS butter along with the rice (I used half brown and Half long grain white).  Then I added the broth and baked it for 1 hour at 350.  I was out of mushrooms so I left them out, but when I have them I use fresh and it is extra good!  Thanks for posting - this is such a great side dish, I served it tonight with grilled salmon and snow peas!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
homemade rice a roni

this is a big hit at my house and pretty cheap to make too!

1. in medium skillet saute' broken spaghetti pieces in butter , stirring constantly , until the spaghetti begins to brown
2. add rice , stirring until the rice is well coated with the butter and the spaghetti browns a little more carefully pour in broth
3. simmer until liquid is absorbed
demonstrations.review: Loved this recipe.  My kids love Rice a Roni chicken flavor - and I hate that it is so high in sodium - this was easy and fabulous - I doubled the recipe - and added some extra garlic powder and onion powder as well as dried parsley - I plan to make this often!!!! I will make baggies of the dry ingredients to keep in my pantry ready to go - then I can make it any flavor by changing the broth flavor and spices!!! THANK YOU!!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
to die for crock pot roast

amazing flavor, and so simple! no salt needed here. in fact, you may wish to use half the ranch dressing mix to cut back on the saltiness. found this crock-pot pot roast recipe on of a website called www.recipegoldmine.com. it's all the rage there, so i thought i'd try it.

1. place beef roast in crock pot
2. mix the dried mixes together in a bowl and sprinkle over the roast
3. pour the water around the roast
4. cook on low for 7-9 hours
5. use onion soup mix instead of ranch
6. add one cup , of red wine
7. add potatoes , carrots , mushrooms , celery and onion 2-3 hours before end
demonstrations.review: Not sure where I went wrong after reading all these rave reviews ...  this was okay, but nothing special.  I used the full amount of seasonings for a 3 pound roast and about 1 cup of red wine in place of water. The roast was tender and all, but lacked flavor, as did the gravy.  I will try again, with more spices or something.

target.recipe_text:
slow cooker orange chicken

so many recipes call for chicken breast, but my dh prefers dark meat.  so when i found this in kraft food and family, i thought it would be perfect for him.

1. toss chicken with flour in slow cooker
2. stir in all remaining ingredients
3. cover with lid
4. cook on low for 6-8 hours or on high for 3-4 hours
5. serve with hot cooked rice and green beans
target.review: Thisd was excellent!  I added garlic and left out the flouring the chicken step (running late again!).  I added 1 tablespoon of corn flour and 1/3 cup of fresh orange juice (and mixed) to the last 15 minutes to thicken.  I served it with steamed rice, broccoli and carrots - yum!  Thanks for posting.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
strawberries   cream bread  strawberry or blueberry

a wonderful recipe using fresh strawberries from netherhill strawberry farm in australia. this recipe also yields a tried and true (and reviewed) great blueberry & cream bread.

1. combine flour , baking powder , baking soda , salt and cinnamon
2. set aside
3. in small bowl , beat butter until creamy
4. gradually add sugar , beat 1 minute or until light and airy
5. add brown sugar
6. beat in eggs , one at a time
7. beat in sour cream and vanilla
8. stir into flour mixture only until dry ingredients are moistened
9. fold in strawberries and nuts
10. pour into a greased 8 x 4 inch loaf pan
11. bake at 350f for 60 to 65 minutes or until toothpick comes out clean
12. let stand 10 minutes in pan
13. turn out on rack to cool
demonstrations.review: 10 stars!!!  I made this in a bunt tin sprinkled with cinnamon sugar (about 2 tablespoons).  I had no walnuts, so added white chocolate chips - what a winner!  I took this to a friends house, who had bought raspberry and white chocolate muffins, this was eaten first and the muffins left on the plate (and they were from a gourmet bakery).  I got many compliments, this is going to be made again and again when strawberries are in season.  Thanks for posting.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
amazing chicken marinade

this recipe came from allrecipes (ruth crickmer). my whole family loved it even though it cooked too fast. the original recipe said 'high heat' on the grill, which my husband did. it ended up cooking 8 minutes total, charred but not burnt tasting, and very juicy and flavorful. we'll turn down the heat next time for texture, but this is a keeper in our home!

1. in a large , non-reactive container , whisk together ingredients beginning with cider vinegar through salt
2. then whisk in olive oil and pepper
3. place chicken in the mixture
4. cover and marinate chicken in the fridge 8 hours or overnight
5. remove chicken from marinade just before you turn on your grill or broiler to let come up a few degrees
6. discard marinade
7. lightly oil your grill or broiler pan
8. grill or broil about 10 minutes per side
demonstrations.review: An interesting flavour, something about it was not quite us.  It was not bad, just not for our family.  It is always nice to try something new, so thank you for that opportunity!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
soft  sugar cookie cutouts

these are my oldest sons favorite cutouts.  the sour cream helps them stay soft , moist and get kind of "puffy" when you bake them.  prep time does not include chilling time for dough.

1. in a large mixing bowl , beat together sugar and butter until creamy
2. beat in eggs , vanilla and sour cream until fluffy
3. mix in orange peel
4. in a seperate bowl , combine flour , baking powder , baking soda , and salt
5. gradually add flour mixture into creamed mixture
6. beat until well-combined
7. divide dough in half and wrap each half in plastic wrap or wax paper
8. chill for about 2 hours
9. when dough is chilled , preheat oven to 400
10. roll dough on to lightly floured surface to about 1 / 8"-1 / 4" thickness
11. cut with cookie cutters and place cookies on ungreased cookie sheets about 2" apart
12. bake at 400 for 6-9 minutes or until edges slightly golden
13. cool about 2 minutes before removing to wire racks to cool
demonstrations.review: Made these for the kids to decorate as our arts and crafts time today.   I made the dough yesterday and kept it in the fridge o'night.  These were surprisingly better than I had thought they would be! I liked that they are "strong" enough to with stand little hands as they are decorating them - shortbread is my personal fav. but far too brittle to decorate.  Thanks for a great recipe.  I halved the recipe and still got 3 doz. medium sizes biscuits/cookies!

target.recipe_text:
pepperoni ziti casserole

i adapted this recipe for my crock-pot.  having 2 devout carnivores and 1 devout vegetarian in the house, it pleased both.  i have a smaller crockpot that i use for my vegetarian crockpot and i added meat last.

1. cook pasta until just tender
2. cook ground beef until no longer pink , drain
3. transfer meat to a large bowl
4. add 29 oz tomato sauce , 1 c mozzarella cheese , mushrooms , spinach , ricotta cheese , italian seasoning , garlic , garlic powder , red pepper flakes and pepper
5. fold pasta into meat mixture
6. pour into crockpot
7. combine water and remaining tomato sauce and pour over pasta mixture
8. sprinkle with parmesan cheese and remaining mozzerella cheese
9. top with pepperoni
10. cover and bake on low for 5 to 6 hours
target.review: I have had this recipe cut out forever, and just finally tried it! The version I use is Weight Watchers friendly, substituting ground turkey for ground beef, and turkey pepperoni for pepperoni. (6 pts per 1 cup serving on weight watchers prepared this way.)  I then take mixture and cover and bake at 350 for 30 minutes, and another 5 minutes uncovered.  Since our family is small and the servings were large, I prepared dish and then baked 1/2, and the other 1/2 I froze for another meal later. Great, easy dish for weeknights.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
tangy citrus chicken

i found this in a preschool newsletter publication.  haven't tried it yet, but the recipe intrigued me!

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. place chicken breasts in 9x13 pan coated with nonstick cooking spray
3. in a small bowl , combine remaining ingredients
4. mix well
5. pour half the sauce over the chicken
6. bake , uncovered at 350f for 20 minutes
7. turn chicken
8. pour remaining sauce on top
9. bake 15-20 minutes longer or until meat juices run clear
demonstrations.review: This is an easy recipe overall. I cut the recipe in half, as there are only 2 of us - and thought that the sage overpowered the other ingredients in taste. It wasn't bad, but nothing spectacular - I probably won't be making again. We served with a lemon mushroom orzo pilaf which was complementary. Thank you for posting.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
turkey and mashed potato empanadas   empanadas de pavo

a terrific way to use up turkey feast leftovers from the wonderful rachael ray.  chicken would make an excellent substitution for turkey.

1. pre-heat the oven to 400f
2. remove one sheet of puff pastry from the freezer and thaw in the refrigerator for about 30 minutes
3. meanwhile , make the filling by combining the leftover mashed potatoes , shredded turkey , chili powder , parsley , cilantro , salt and freshly ground black pepper in a bowl
4. once the dough has defrosted , use a little flour to roll out the dough to about 1 / 8 of an inch thick and cut it in half horizontally
5. cut each half vertically into 3 equal pieces
6. you should have 6 squares
7. place 1 / 3 cup of the turkey / potato mixture in the middle of each square
8. fold over each square so one corner meets the other , making a triangle
9. press the sides down using a fork or pinch with your fingers
10. repeat with the other five
11. lay them out onto a parchment-lined baking sheet
12. brush empanadas with the egg wash so they will get nice and brown
13. transfer to the oven and bake for 10-15 minutes , until golden
14. serve either hot or cold
demonstrations.review: We made this tonight from leftovers. It was really good. One change I would make when making these again would be to add abit of cheese, because everything is better with cheese!!! The great thing is that since there is just the 2 of us and these are such large portions, we have some meals to freeze! Thanks for posting this recipe from my request. I love recipezaar members!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
banana split delight

a little different take on a very popular dessert.  cut small servings because this dessert is very rich.

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees
2. combine vanilla wafer crumbs and melted margarine and press evenly onto bottom of a 9x13-inch baking dish
3. bake crust in 350 degree oven for 5 to 8 minutes or until lightly golden
4. set aside to cool completely
5. in mixer bowl , beat cream cheese , powdered sugar , and vanilla until creamy
6. stir in 1 cup of cool whip
7. spread cream cheese mixture over cooled crust
8. gently spread well-drained pineapple over cream cheese layer
9. slice bananas and dip in reserved pineapple juice to keep bananas from getting brown
10. arrange banana slices over pineapple layer
11. spread remaining cool whip over bananas
12. sprinkle walnuts over cool whip
13. garnish with cherries and chocolate syrup as desired
demonstrations.review: I made this for a "red hat" party that I hosted for my mom and her friends. It was a big hit!

target.recipe_text:
double layer pumpkin pie

this recipe comes from the kraft people. it sounded so good i just had to share.

1. mix cream cheese , 1 tablespoon milk and sugar in large bowl with wire whisk until smooth
2. gently stir in whipped topping
3. spread on bottom of crust
4. pour 1 cup cold milk into large bowl
5. add pumpkin , pudding mixes and spices
6. beat with wire whisk 2 minutes
7. the mixture will be thick
8. spread over cream cheese layer
9. refrigerate 4 hours or until set
10. garnish with additional whipped topping and chocolate-dipped pecan halves
11. store in the refrigerator until just before serving
target.review: Oh boy, what a treat! It dosen't get any better than this if you are a pumpkin lover like myself! I doubled the cream cheese layer but I don't know why I even bothered. The pumpkin mousse layer is what makes this pie so dreamy! I had admired this recipe for years in magazines during the holiday season and I have no idea why I waited so long to make it! I could eat the top layer by itself by the bowlfuls! Thanks Sackville Girl! Awesome recipe! BTW, I'm thinking that this pie in frozen state would be awesome for summertime!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
dan s favorite baked beans

this is a very old recipe given to me by my mother-in-law. my husband loves these beans and requests them often. if you have an occasion coming up, give them a try! you won't be disappointed!

1. combine all ingredients except bacon
2. lay bacon across the top
3. bake at 325f for 2 hours
demonstrations.review: Whoa Bev! Awesome beans! I have been looking for a recipe for a good baked bean dish and this is definitely it! Thanks for helping me be a better cook!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
caramel sauce

you can use this on so many different things. by adjusting the cooking time, you can make it as thick as you like according to what you are going to use it on. i like to make it thicker to use on ice cream and thinner for desserts. i often double the recipe so i have some left over for later.

1. combine butter , brown sugar , water , and salt in a medium sauce pan , over medium heat , stirring constantly
2. bring to boil for 3 to 5 minutes depending upon thickness desired
3. remove from heat and stir in evaporated milk and vanilla
demonstrations.review: Good.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
coconut creme fudge

i came up with this last year to satisfy my husbands love for coconut! it is delicious! enjoy!

1. in large pot over medium heat , cook and stir butter , sugar and milk
2. bring to boil and boil for 5 minutes or candy temperature of 230 degrees
3. remove from heat
4. add marshmallow creme and white chips stirring til well blended and chips are melted
5. add in coconut and coconut flavoring
6. mix well and pour into greased or sprayed medium baking dish
7. cool completely , then chill til firm
demonstrations.review: DIVINE! This was such a clever fudge recipe! I surprised my coconut-loving friends with this fudge and they all loved it! Copies of this recipe had to be handed out! A unique twist on fudge; something different than the usual chocolate or peanut butter confections! When I make this again I'm thinking of dipping individual pieces in melted chocolate and maybe adding some almonds! Thanks Brenda!

target.recipe_text:
banana banana bread

why compromise the banana flavor? my banana bread is moist and delicious with loads of banana flavor! ultimate comfort food, and it's wonderful toasted!! (make sure to use bananas with a lot of black on them for the best flavor! the blacker the bananas, the stronger the banana flavor of the bread.)

1. preheat oven to 350
2. lightly grease 9 x 5 loaf pan
3. in large bowl , combine flour , soda and salt
4. in separate bowl , cream together butter and brown sugar
5. stir in eggs and mashed bananas until well blended
6. stir banana mixture into flour mixture
7. stir just to moisten
8. pour batter into prepared loaf pan
9. bake in preheated oven for 60-65 minutes until a toothpick inserted into center of loaf comes out clean
10. let bread cool in pan for 10 minutes , then turn out onto a wire rack
target.review: WOW! These turned out great! The baking time listed was spot on, and by covering the loaf with foil after 40min it prevented the top from getting too dark. It really does take quite a few bananas to make up 2 1/3 cups, I had to use 7 medium size ones. I 'mashed' the bananas using a hand mixer which is much easier and faster than mashing by hand, and also aerates the mashed bananas making the batter a little lighter. A great recipe and I will definitely be making it again and again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
best in the west berry cobbler

the name says it all! it has a delicious sugar crackle topping that forms by pouring the boiling water over the top before baking. this is my favorite cobbler recipe. easy, impressive, and versatile. can use any combination of berries, frozen or fresh.

1. spread berries in a greased 8 inch square pan
2. cream shortening and 3 / 4 cup sugar well
3. sift flour , baking powder , and salt together
4. add alternately with milk to creamed mixture
5. batter will be thick
6. spread batter over berries
7. combine remaining sugar and cornstarch together then sprinkle evenly over batter
8. pour boiling water over all
9. do not mix
10. bake at 350 for 30-45 minutes , until golden brown and toothpick inserted into middle comes out clean
11. serve warm or at room temperature with whipped cream or ice cream if desired
demonstrations.review: I have tried several other top rated cobblers and this one is by far the best! The only changes I made were using butter instead of shortening, adding 1tsp of lemon zest and 1tsp vanilla to the batter. Thanks for the great recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
apple french toast casserole

here's another make-it-the-night-before breakfast casserole. you don't need syrup with this one. prep time does not include refrigerating overnight.

1. melt the butter in a large skillet and add apples
2. cook and stir for 5 minutes
3. add brown sugar , water , and cinnamon and continue to cook and stir for 10 minutes until apples are tender
4. spoon mixture into 13x9 baking dish
5. cover apples with bread slices , making sure to cover the entire surface
6. trim the bread to fit if you must
7. beat eggs until foamy , then beat in milk and vanilla
8. pour egg mixture over the bread slices
9. cover the dish with plastic wrap and refrigerate overnight
10. in the morning , remove the dish from the refrigerator and let it stand while oven is preheated to 375 f
11. bake uncovered for 35 minutes , or until bread is golden and firm
12. let sit 10 minutes before serving
13. to serve on a platter , run a knife around the edges of the casserole , place platter on top of casserole , and carefully flip
14. to serve individually , use a spatula to remove serving , place serving plate on top of serving and carefully flip so apple side is up
demonstrations.review: The flavors of this dish are really great although I found it to be a little on the dry side. Also, I found that it definitely served closer to 4 people than 6. If i were to make this again I would add in extra apples and double the recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
honey garlic grilled chicken

i saw the word garlic that is all it takes for me to try a recipe!

1. mix first seven ingredients
2. add chicken breasts , turning to coat
3. cover and let stand at room temperature no longer then 30 minutes , turning once
4. grill over medium heat for 10 minutes , or until cooked through
demonstrations.review: This marinade is delicious! My only addition was a dash of cayenne for some heat. I probably left the chicken marinade for about 2 hours in the fridge and it was incredibly tender. We will definitely be having this again!

target.recipe_text:
chicken breasts stuffed with feta   sun dried tomatoes

the soaking water from the sun-dried tomatoes can be refrigerated for several days. the liquid adds a layer of flavor to salad dressings, or can be used in place of part of the chicken or vegetable broth in recipes.

1. soak sun-dried tomatoes in enough boiling water to just cover them
2. set aside
3. heat oil in nonstick skillet over medium high
4. add onion and cook , stirring , for 3 to 4 minutes , or until softened
5. remove skillet from heat and transfer onions to small bowl
6. drain tomatoes , discarding the soaking liquid or reserving it for another use
7. add chopped tomatoes to onions and stir in basil and feta
8. cut a horizontal slit in each chicken breast to form a pocket
9. stuff each with 1 / 4 of cheese mixture
10. return skillet to medium-high heat
11. add the chicken breasts and saute for 6 minutes
12. carefully turn them and cook another 6 minutes , or until chicken is cooked through
target.review: Delicious. Quick and easy enough for everyday, good enough for company. I did find there was a lot of filling (I may have measured generously) but did get it all in there. Cooking time was perfect. I'll be making this again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
orange  beet  and parmigiano reggiano salad

by now you all know i love parmigiano-reggiano, the "king of cheeses". here's a lovely salad from a book on cheeses by nancy radke.

1. pat beets dry
2. arrange beets and orange slices on chilled plates
3. toast walnuts in a preheated 350 degree oven until light golden brown , about 10 minutes
4. chop finely sprinkle over the beets and oranges
5. whisk together orange juice , lemon juice and salt
6. add oil in a thin , steady stream , whisking constantly
7. pour dressing over salad
8. make 1 / 2 cup of thin slivers of parmigiano-reggiano with a vegetable peeler
9. scatter over the salad
10. season with salt and pepper
11. serve immediately
demonstrations.review: I served this over a bed of mixed greens. All the flavours played off each other very well, although I did think the cheese got a little lost in the crowd. I do love oranges in a salad and the contrast of the beets and oranges was particularly nice.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chocolate sauce or frosting

adopted from the recipezaar account. apparently, this is an excellent recipe! i'll be trying it soon!

1. in a double boiler or heavy saucepan , melt the butter in the cream , heating until just warm to the touch
2. stir in sugar and salt until dissolved
3. mix in cocoa powder until well blended
4. heat mixture over low heat , stirring continuously until shiny and smooth and hot , but not bubbling
5. for sauce , serve hot or warm
6. for frosting , refrigerate until thick enough to spread
7. may be reheated
demonstrations.review: Excellent frosting - intensely chocolatey, not overly sweet. Very quick to make. This made just enough to cover the tops and sides of a 9" 2-layer cake - good thing I did not plan to put it in the middle. My sifter is rather coarse; next time I will sift the cocoa twice; but 5 minutes of furious whisking got it smooth.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
segedin goulash

a good czech recipe from 

1. fry onion in shortening over medium heat until wilted , add meat , paprika , caraway seeds , and salt and brown well
2. add 1 / 2 cup water , cover and simmer over low heat for 45 minutes
3. add about 2 / 3 of the sauerkraut and simmer for 30 minutes more
4. brown the flour in lard , stirring well , and add to meat with remaining water
5. allow to simmer for 5 minutes
6. add sour cream and the remaining sauerkraut
7. bring to a boil , then remove from heat and serve
demonstrations.review: Very good! Much enjoyed by myself (a kraut lover) AND my partner (not too keen on kraut.) I used a bit less fat than called for, as well as low-fat sour cream. I also used 2 tsps sweet Hungarian paprika and 1 tsp caraway.

target.recipe_text:
incredible grill cheese sandwiches

originally from southern living; given to me by my lifelong best friend. comfort food

1. combine first 6 ingredients
2. spread 1 side of bread slices evenly with butter
3. turn 8 slices buttered side down
4. spread evenly with cheese mixture
5. top with ham , if desired , and remaining bread slices , buttered side up
6. in a large nonstick skillet over medium heat , cook sandwiches two at a time until golden , turning once
target.review: Wonderful! Easy! Yummy! Instead of grilled cheese sandwiches, we made quesadillas. Another thing that's great about the cheese mixture is that it can be made far in advance of when you need it. Thanks for sharing your recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mexican charro beans

posted by request.

1. rinse and pick over beans
2. bring the beans to a boil in a large pot of water and cook over medium heat for 1 to 2 hours until they tender but still firm
3. before the beans are done , fry the bacon in a large skillet until halfway cooked
4. add garlic , tomatoes , onions , and green pepper
5. continue cooking with bacon until the bacon crisp
6. add a can of beer to bacon mixture and simmer a few additional minutes , or longer if you like your beans softer
7. add chopped cilantro and jalapenos
8. combine everything in one large pot
9. add salt and pepper to taste
demonstrations.review: I'm So Happy that I found this recipe!! I have been looking for a really wonderful Mexican pinto bean recipe and this is IT! I used two anaheim green chilis for the green pepper and  prepared as stated except I softened the beans in the crockpot, drained, then combined with the cooked sauce and let it cook on low all night.  In the morning I pureed about 3 cups in my blender and stirred it back into the pot.  It was a little too juicy so I left the lid off for a couple of hours to let it condense. Terrific! I doubt that I will make pinto beans any other way. Thank you, Thank you, Thank you!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
herbed lemon chicken breasts    ww friendly

this is so good and so easy. i got this off the ww website. it is also easy to halve this recipe, or even quarter it.

1. on a large plate , combine mrs
2. dash seasoning with flour
