3. pat chicken dry and roll in flour mixture
4. heat butter in large skillet
5. add chicken and brown on both sides , about 3 minutes on each side
6. meanwhile , remove zest from lemon , squeeze juice from lemon , and mix zest and juice with broth
7. pour over chicken , cover , and cook for 15 minutes
8. remove lid and cook for another 5 minutes or until juices run clear
9. serve immediately
demonstrations.review: This is a delicious recipe and one I will make often. The only change I made was to remove the chicken (which I had pounded to an even thickness) after the 15 minutes of cooking and covered it loosely with foil. Then I cooked the liquid down a bit until it was more saucy. This took about 5 to 7 minutes. Then I returned the chicken to the sauce and reheated it. It was so tender we could cut it with a fork! Yummy, yummy, yummy! Thank you for a great recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
asparagus with thyme

love asparagus and this one is very good!! from cooking light.

1. preheat oven to 400 degrees
2. rub the cut sides of the garlic over a 13 x 9 inch baking dish , place garlic in dish
3. snap off tough ends of asparagus
4. add asparagus to dish , drizzle with oil
5. sprinkle asparagus with thyme and salt and fresh ground pepper to taste
6. toss gently and bake at 400 degrees for 20 minutes , stirring once
demonstrations.review: This is a terrific asparagus recipe. Nothing could be simpler to make. I put it together earlier in the day and popped it in the oven at dinner time. One thing that I did do a little  differently however was to press the garlic and rub it all over the dish. We LOVE garlic! Thanks a lot for your recipe!

target.recipe_text:
olive garden fettuccine alfredo

just like the famous restaraunt's dish.

1. in a medium saucepan , melt butter
2. when butter is melted , add cream cheese
3. when the cream cheese is softened , add heavy cream
4. season with garlic powder , salt , and pepper
5. simmer for 15-20 minutes over low heat , stirring constantly
6. remove from heat and stir in parmesan
7. serve over hot fettucine noodles
target.review: VERY tasty. Tastes very similar to Olive Garden. I thought it made a lot of extra sauce though. I made it for 6 and still have over a half a cup of sauce leftover.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chimichurri

this too easy sauce, of argentine origin, makes your steak taste like it was just dragged through the garden! great on rare, chargrilled, flank steak.

1. pulse parsley in processor to chop
2. add remaining ingredients and blend
3. separate sauce into equal parts
demonstrations.review: Just made it for dinner, I kept adding more and more to my plate. Finally I brought the food processor bowl over to the table to save the trip. I actually topped it over a simple baked tilapia and it was great!!! It was tangy and fresh and summery. I loved the raw red onion. My only teeny tiny comment is the prep time, with preminced garlic this only took me about 5 minutes to make!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mom s m m cookies

my mom made these cookies often when we were children. always a big favorite. my nephew has graduated from high school and asked that i make m&m cookies for his graduation party. i had forgotten how wonderful they are. try them...ummmm..

1. mix butter , sugars and vanilla until blended
2. beat in eggs
3. save 1 / 4 cup of flour to coat candies
4. add dry ingredients to mixture
5. mix until well blended
6. stir in the flour coated candies and the rest of the flour until well mixed
7. some people like to save half of the candies out and use them to decorated the top of the cookies before putting them in the oven
8. drop round teaspoon of cookie dough on ungreased cookie sheet about 2 inches apart
9. bake for 8-10 minutes in 375 oven
demonstrations.review: I have never given a recipe a bad review before but these were pretty awful! They were flat as can be! I'm talking like 1/16 of an inch with the M&M's poking out. The taste was only ok. I felt like it was a waste of food.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
baked pasta with asparagus  pasta al forno con asparagi

i love fresh asparagus recipes.  got this one out of 100 pasta sauce recipes.  serve with some crusty bread and a salad and you have a great dinner. it turns out great!


1. wash asparagus
2. remove any tough stalks and cut into short lengths
3. you may want to split the length in half
4. melt about 3 tbs of butter in pan and cook the asparagus over a low heat for about 20 min
5. every so often , add a little chicken stock to keep it moist
6. when the asparagus is done , season to taste
7. while the asparagus is cooking , process the ricotta cheese with the oil
8. cook the pasta for half the time stated on the package
9. drain and immediately toss in the remaining butter and half the parmesan
10. butter a deep oven dish
11. make a thin layer of pasta , then one of asparagus , then one of pasta again and then one of ricotta
12. repeat , finishing with the layer of pasta
13. beat together the eggs and the remaining cheese and pour over the top
14. sprinkle with black pepper
15. bake in a medium oven , 350 degrees for 20 minutes
demonstrations.review: This is a very subtle recipe, not for those who want huge flavors but nonetheless really really good. This is just plain simple tasty food. Kick it up with some white pepper or crushed red pepper flakes.

target.recipe_text:
turkey divan bake

a number of years ago, at a bank staff christmas get-together, one of the employees served this meal along with a few other of her creations. for days afterwards we all raved about how absolutely delicious it was and begged her for the recipe. lucky for us she obliged.

1. heat oven to 350 degrees
2. cook spaghetti according to package directions , drain
3. in 2 quart saucepan melt 2 tbsp butter
4. stir in flour until smooth& bubbly
5. add chicken broth
6. cook over medium heat stirring constantly until mixture comes to full boil
7. boil 1 minute
8. remove from heat
9. stir in 1 1 / 2 cups cheese and milk until cheese is melted
10. in a greased casserole dish combine spaghetti , turkey , broccoli , mushrooms& cheese mixture
11. top with remaining 1 / 2 cup cheese
12. bake for 25 to 30 minutes or until bubbly around edges
13. serve
target.review: This recipe was exactly what I was looking for - I was glad to find one without "cream of" soup and it turned out creamy and perfect!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pumpkin ginger pancakes with ginger butter

from sunset magazine , these are nice for a change of pace on saturday mornings. 45 minutes combined prep and cook time.

1. combine flour , brown sugar , soda , cinnamon , powdered ginger , nutmeg and salt in a large mixing bowl
2. in a separate bowl , combine egg , milk pumpkin , yogurt and butter until well blended
3. add wet to dry , stirring just until evenly moistened
4. cook on nonstick griddle over medium heat until edges look dry about 2 to 3 minutes per side
5. serve with ginger butter and real maple syrup
6. to make the ginger butter , simply cream the chopped candied ginger into the butter , then chill before serving
demonstrations.review: These were great! Pumpkiny enough for me, but not too pumpkiny for my husband. Tasty enough to eat plain, even better with butter and syrup. (Next time I'll do the ginger butter!)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chili maple glazed dump chicken oamc

i love dump recipes and this one is an easy 4 ingredient one!

1. for immediate cooking: pre-heat oven to 350f place all ingredients into a large baking dish , turn chicken to coat
2. bake until chicken juices run clear
3. for freezing: place all ingredients into a 1 gallon freezer bag
4. lay flat in freezer
5. to thaw and cook: take the bag out of the freezer the night before , make sure the bag is sealed completely
6. for the oven: preheat the oven to 350f empty the contents of the bag into a large baking dish and bake until the juices run clear
7. for the crockpot: cook on low for 6-8 hours or on high for 4-6 or until done
8. on the grill: cook over medium heat until juices run clear
demonstrations.review: I wonder if the reviewers that had poor results are using maple-flavored pancake syrup rather than real maple syrup - the real thing is critical, because the sweetness and maple flavor is much more pronounced. I love this recipe - it's so simple, and tasty, and I never would have thought to use chili powder with maple syrup.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
quick n easy quiche crust

need a fast, flaky crust? this delicious recipe is so much cheaper than ready-made pie crusts! high altitude tested.

1. mix flour and salt with fork
2. beat oil and water with whisk or fork to thicken
3. pour into flour and mix with fork
4. press into 9" pie crust
5. fill with quiche mixture and bake at 400f until done
6. you can double the recipe , divide dough in half , and roll out into a pair of rounds for two-crust pies
7. this recipe is not suitable for baked pie crust shells
8. it makes a nice , flaky crust that's suitable for everyday use
demonstrations.review: I would have been skeptical but for the abundance of positive reviews, and the crust came out wonderful with my quiche. I think the key is to really and truly follow the recipe exactly as stated - use ice-cold water, really whisk it with the oil before mixing everything together, press it into the pie pan, bake at 400 (and not what your filling recipe might say). I used a glass pie plate which I think added some crispiness as well. And it was so easy!

target.recipe_text:
creamy banana cream pie

from connie griffin at hope lodge. this is the best banana cream pie you will ever eat. check the reviews for different ways to go on this. the crust is dead easy , and adds a lot to the recipe. i like banana pudding also .

1. combine flour , butter and pecans
2. press into the bottom and up the sides of a greased 9 inch pie plate
3. bake at 350 degrees fahrenheit for 25 minutes
4. cool
5. beat cream cheese and sugar together
6. fold in 1 cup cool whip
7. spread over crust
8. slice bananas and arrange on top of cream cheese
9. whisk pudding mix and milk
10. mix in remaining cool whip
11. spread on top of bananas
12. refrigerate
target.review: I made this twice, the first time using regular cool whip and cream cheese, the second time with light.  Although both tasted good, the regular made a noticeably better presentation and had a better texture.  I also used a graham crust.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
brown sugar peach pie with coconut streusel

make sure you use fresh peaches in this recipe, canned just doesn't do it justice.

1. preheat oven to 425 degrees
2. fit dough into a 9-inch pie plate
3. fold edges under
4. flute
5. line dough with a piece of foil , and arrange pie weights or dried beans on foil
6. bake at 425 degrees for 10 minutes
7. reduce oven temperature to 350 degrees
8. remove pie weights and foil
9. bake at 350 degrees for 5 minutes
10. cool crust on a wire rack
11. combine 1 / 3 cup sugar , flour , and cinnamon in a bowl
12. sprinkle over peaches
13. toss gently
14. spoon into prepared crust
15. bake at 350 degrees for 30 minutes
16. combine 1 / 3 cup sugar , oats , coconut , and butter
17. sprinkle over peach mixture
18. shield edges of crust with foil
19. bake an additional 30 minutes or until golden
20. cool on a wire rack
demonstrations.review: I'm giving this 5 * because I think that if i had followed Ms*Bindy's advice about adding 1/4 c. cornstarch I would have been happy with it.  Mine was a little soupy, but I was able to make it work.  I had a 8 1/2" pie pan, so with using large peaches it took about 8.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
orange poppy seed biscotti

i found this on healthdiscovery.net and began making a few changes to suit my own tastes and preferences. the original was for lemon biscotti and can easily be switched back. one point per cookie.

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees
2. combine the dry ingredients together in a bowl
3. combine the zest , egg , egg whites and extract in a second bowl
4. add the dry mixture and mix well
5. form the dough into 2 logs each 8-9 inches long
6. place logs onto a cookie sheet lined with parchment paper
7. bake for 30 minutes
8. let cool slightly and cut diagonally into 1 / 2 inch slices
9. put cut slices soft sides down back on the cookie sheets and bake slices another 8 to 10 minutes until dry
10. cool completely and store in an airtight container
demonstrations.review: Good flavor, soft yet still crunchy. Used the advice to add salt.  I also cut the recipe in half.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
brownies on steroids

my friend larry, a lover of all things dessert, declared these are the most outrageous brownies he has ever tasted and nicknamed them 

1. in a food processor , combine the flour , sugar , and cocoa
2. add the butter and process just until mixture resembles coarse crumbs
3. press firmly into a greased 13 by 9 baking pan
4. bake at 350 degrees for 10 minutes
5. while crust is baking , combine milk , vanilla , and one cup of chocolate chips in a medium saucepan
6. heat , stirring constantly , until mixture is smooth
7. remove crust from oven
8. pour chocolate mixture over crust
9. sprinkle with coconut , nuts , toffee bits and remaining chocolate chips
10. press down firmly
11. return to oven and bake for 18 to 20 minutes
demonstrations.review: Pretty darn good!.  I don't know if I'd consider them brownies...more like 7-layer bars with a brownie crust.  My only problem was with the crust...i had to add a little water(about 5 TBS)

target.recipe_text:
mexican pork cubes

simple, yet delicious meat.  this is something i came up with one night when i was craving the usual mexican flare and had pork on hand.  i served it with my recipe #150134 and a side of corn.  good eats!

1. sprinkle meat with spices and place meat in saucepan with onion and butter and brown on both sides of pork chops
2. then add in the salsa and red wine vinegar and remove pork chops one at a time cutting into cubes , and place back in pan when finished cutting
3. once all pork is cooked through take off heat and sprinkle with cheese and place lid on pan and leave until melted
target.review: YUM!!  This was a hit with the whole family.  I used garlic infused olive oil instead of butter and only 1 Tbsp of chili powder (kids).  Instead of browning the whole PC first, I cubed the meat first went from there (scrapping the pan long the way for all the flavoring).  Can't wait to try this again.  Thanks

demonstrations.recipe_text:
south africa tomato salad

posted for zwtii tour . . .another qeth (quick, easy, tasty and healthy) recipe from the galley wench

1. arrange tomato slices in a serving dish
2. sprinkle with salt , sugar , and minced chile pepper
3. drizzle on the vinegar
4. let salad sit for about 15 minutes before serving
demonstrations.review: This was easy and tasted great.  I used unseeded jalapenos and it just right.  The different tastes came together nicely.  Thanks

demonstrations.recipe_text:
butterscotch bundt rolls

similar to monkey bread. pecans work best but you can use other nuts or leave them out. will become a fast favorite.

1. arrange frozen rolls in a greased bundt pan
2. sprinkle pudding , brown sugar , and pecans over rolls
3. drizzle butter over all
4. cover bundt pan with a dish towel or plastic wrap and let rise at room temperature overnight , or about 12 hours
5. remove towel
6. bake at 350f for about 25 minutes
7. cool 5-10 minutes before inverting to a serving plate
8. serve warm
9. makes 18 rolls
demonstrations.review: This was so good and didn't last long.  I followed the directions exactly and it turned out great.  This is a keeper.  Thanks

demonstrations.recipe_text:
heavy on the garlic hummus

i was going through some old recipe files and came across this recipe from a local mediterranean restaurant no longer in business. i had never made it so i decided to give it a try and i'm glad i did.

1. place all ingredients except oil and parsely in food processor
2. blend until smooth
3. slowly add 1 / 4 cup olive oil and continue processing until mixed well
4. if mixture is too stiff add water a little at a time until it reaches a smooth and creamy consistency
5. remove from processor and add parsley
6. chill for at least four hours
7. spread on plate in a thin layer
8. drizzle additional oil on top
9. sprinkle with paprika and served with pita bread
demonstrations.review: This was great, made as directed except I subbed black pepper for white. Will certainly make this again.

target.recipe_text:
grilled ham and cheese sandwich with pineapple

okay, ham, cheese and pineapple what a wonderful combination!  this recipe was printed in food everyday, march 2005.

1. on the sandwich bread , layer cheese , ham , pineapple , basil and a second slice of cheese
2. top with remaining bread
3. melt the butter in a heavy skillet over medium heat
4. when butter is melted , place sandwich in skillet and cook until golden , 2 to 3 minutes
5. flip the sandwich and cook another 2 to 3 minutes or until second side is golden and cheese is melted
6. enjoy !
target.review: Nummy! My husband was skeptical at first, then demanded that I go back to recipezaar and review it!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crock pot chicken provencal supper

this recipe came from a weight watchers cookbook on crock pot cooking. i have been making it almost once a week since. so quick and easy and very few ingredients. most importantly...my kids will eat it.

1. place chicken in slow cooker and sprinkle with basil , salt and pepper
2. pour tomatoes and beans over chicken and sprinkle with the yellow peppers
3. cover with lid and cook on high 1 hour and low 5 hours
4. spoon bean mixture into each of 4 shallow bowls
5. top each with 1 breast and 3 / 4 cup bean mixture
demonstrations.review: Wow...how easy was that to make!?! I used a cup of frozen pepper stir-fry(red, yellow, and green bell peppers with some onion), and I added a bay leaf to the pot. It was very good. I will definitely make it OFTEN.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crock pot chicken   vegetable  easy clean up

i made this up one day and it worked perfectly. very flexible, use any of your favorite chicken seasoning, or your fave veggies!

1. place your chicken in 1 bag with the packet of seasoning
2. do not add liquid , it will make it's own
3. seal up the bag and put it in the crock pot , set on low for 8 hours
4. with 3 hrs to go , break the ears of corn in half and put in the other oven bag
5. add the butter , salt& pepper to taste
6. seal it up and put it on top of the chicken or next to , depending on the size of your crock pot
7. i put both bags in a serving bowl and cut them open , serve out of the bag for informal dinners--less clean up !
demonstrations.review: Wow...you are my hero, cookbook carrie! I'm on a new schedule at work that leaves me with no time at all to cook in the evening, so I've been using my crockpot at least 4 days a week(no joke). This is awesome! I didn't have Southwestern seasoning, so I made a rub for the chicken with some garlic and herbs de provence, and it was excellent. I also made corn per your directions(I did add a little bit of fresh sage to flavor the butter), and also sealed up a bag of zuchinni and yellow squash with some butter and rosemary. I just put the corn and zuchinni in before I left for work, and when I stopped back by the house for supper 4 hrs later, it was perfect! I will use this technique again, often. Thanks so much!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
hot milk posset

in victorian england, children were allowed small glasses of wine at the dinner table. alcohol was a traditional sleep aid for all ages back then. this posset was a classic drink that nannies would prepare for kids in their care who were having trouble falling asleep.  posted for zaar world tour ii (2006)

1. heat in a saucepan the milk , lemon peel , sugar and almond extract
2. when it begins to scald , remove from heat
3. beat egg white and add
4. now add rum and brandy
5. serve hot
demonstrations.review: Very good...but wow! this is strong stuff!!! I had to use all rum 'cause I didn't have brandy and vanilla extract instead of almond.

target.recipe_text:
spinach and onion couscous

colorful and a delicious side dish or main dish.

1. in a saucepan , cook and stir onion and garlic in hot oil until tender
2. add the broth and spinach
3. cook and stir frequently until the spinach thaws
4. bring mixture to a boil and stir occasionally
5. add in couscous
6. stir to combine
7. cover , remove pan from heat , and let stand 5 minutes or until liquid is absorbed
8. add remaining ingredients
9. stir to combine
10. serve immediately
target.review:
This was unbelievable! Everyone raved about it.(I cooked it with the Greek chicken with artichokes-recipe #69442). Rave reviews for both and perfect with a crusty loaf of bread.
I used Whole wheat couscous and 2 packages of raw packaged spinach- it cooks down a lot! I also added some garlic salt with the onions,garlic and olive oil.  I topped it off with feta before serving and think that this really made the dish!
This will be a regular recipe in my family as well as the chicken- both so easy and great presentation!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chicken curry in a hurry

watch out or you might get pulled over for a speeding ticket in the kitchen! ready in 20 minutes. :)

1. mix together flour , salt and cayenne pepper in a plastic bag
2. add chicken in small batches , shaking to coat
3. heat oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat
4. add chicken and cook until lightly browned
5. then add curry powder and toss to coat
6. remove from pan
7. add onion and garlic to pan , adding a little more oil if necessary , and cook for 2 minutes , then add broth , raisins , and tomato paste
8. return chicken to pan and simmer uncovered for 8 minutes or until chicken is cooked through and sauce has thickened
9. garnish with cilantro and a dollop of yogurt
10. serve with quick cooking minute rice , if desired
demonstrations.review: Excellent recipe and so easy too.  I also mixed the yogurt and cilantro into sauce at end instead of serving on the side.  Very flavorable and the raisins are so good (I might add a tad more next time because I like the contrast so much.) I will be making this for company in a few weeks. Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
skillet parmesan chicken

this is real comfort food. a family favorite. if you can, buy the fresh mozzarella. you won't believe the difference and it's worth it. the texture isn't rubbery like the typical mozzarella. i got it from watching an emeril show on the food network.

1. pound the chicken breasts between two slices of plastic wrap until about 1 / 4" thick
2. season with salt and pepper
3. dredge chicken in flour and shake off excess
4. dip in egg / milk mixture , then in breadcrumb / parmesan mixture
5. heat the butter and olive oil in a large deep skillet
6. brown the chicken breasts over medium heat until golden on each side
7. remove to a plate and keep warm
8. add the marinara sauce to the skillet
9. heat to boiling and simmer 10 minutes
10. add the chicken breasts to the sauce and sprinkle parmesan over them
11. place a slice of mozzarella on each piece of chicken
12. cover and simmer about 8- 10 minutes or until the cheese has melted and the chicken is tender
13. serve with your favorite pasta- we like linguine
demonstrations.review: Absolutely wonderful! I will not be ordering chicken parm from any restaurants anymore.  This is sooo moist and tasty. I used just a simple store bought chunky tomato, garlic, onion sauce and shredded mozzarella (didn't have the fresh stuff handy.)  A real crowd pleaser.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
triple chocolate brownies  light

you won't believe these are light!  they are just wonderful!  fast to make... and delicious to eat! a great recipe from rose reisman. these are great baked 1 day in advance and will keep frozen for up to 1 month.

1. preheat oven to 350f spray an 8-inch square metal pan with cooking spray
2. to make brownies: in a bowl , combine sugar , oil , egg , and vanilla until well mixed
3. add cocoa
4. mix well
5. add flour , baking powder , yogurt , and chocolate chips , mixing just until combined and smooth
6. dont overmix
7. pour batter into pan
8. bake in centre of oven for 15 to 20 minutes just until set
9. do not overbake
10. cool
11. to make icing: in a blender or food processor , blend icing ingredients until smooth
12. spread over brownie batch
13. cut into squares
demonstrations.review:
Loved this recipe- very moist brownies and great icing. I didn't have chocolate chips handy so I left them out and still great- I'm sure they would be even better with! As other reviews, I found myself checking them frequently as to not overcook. 
It's nice to have a light dessert recipe that tastes soo good.

target.recipe_text:
butter caramels

these are so good. i should make them all year instead of just at christmas

1. place sugar in a clean dry saucepan
2. pour the water around the wall of the pan to avoid any splashing of sugar crystals onto the sides of the pan
3. bring to a boil and continue cooking on high until amber colored
4. turn heat off and with a wooden spoon , stir in the butter and then the cream
5. pour into an 8 by 8-inch pan that has been lined with foil and well-buttered and let the caramel cool and set until firm
6. once firm , cut into squares
7. wrap in decorative clear plastic
8. store at room temperature
target.review:
Anyone interested in Caramel making should read the instructions at About.com. It has a great recipe that has detailed instructions and pictures. That way when you are using a recipe like this you can figure out temps and processes.
I make butter caramels frequently.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
simple pasta with parmesan

another stupidly simple side dish made from pantry staples that my family asks for over and over. the savory combination of flavors goes well with many other foods. it can be made with freshly-cooked pasta or with leftover, cooked pasta that has no sauce on it. i've included options for some variations to create not-so-simple but extremely tasty side dishes or complete, one-dish meals by adding ingredients you probably have on hand.

1. put pasta into a microwavable dish large enough to give you a little room for stirring and tossing
2. dot pasta with butter or drizzle with olive oil
3. sprinkle parmesan over top
4. add plenty of fresh-ground , black pepper
5. heat in microwave on high 3 to 5 minute at a time , stirring frequently , until thoroughly hot
6. serve , passing the pepper grinder at the table
7. you can add 1-2 cups of cooked meat , and / or 1-3 cups pre-cooked , chopped vegetables
8. i particularly recommend broccoli , zucchini , onions , and / or green , snap , or snow peas
demonstrations.review:
I discovered doing this many years back. It is simple and delicious. An Italian cook friend of mine seen me eating it one time and said "I see someone knows how to make pasta" so I guess that was an endorsment.
Thanks to 3KillerBs for posting this. It will get you out of a bind in a hurry when you need a side dish or even a main dish for that matter, little salad on the side, some bread, glass of wine and wah lah a dinner party.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
best seller caramel corn

when i used to regularly do christmas craft shows, i always sold this packaged up in christmas tins; it was a big seller for me. my sil always hoped it wouldn't sell well, though, so she could eat what didn't sell! based on a bonnie stern recipe.

1. when i make this recipe , it's the only time i haul out my hot-air popcorn popper
2. use 1 / 3 cup popcorn to achieve the 8 cups of popped corn
3. preheat oven to 275f
4. have ready a jelly roll pan
5. place popped corn in a very large bowl
6. in a large , heavy saucepan over high heat , combine the sugar , butter and corn syrup and bring to a boil
7. let boil for two minutes , stirring continuously
8. remove from heat
9. add baking soda and vanilla to sugar mixture and combine well
10. pour this mixture over popped corn and combine , then spread mixture out onto jelly roll pan
11. bake in preheated oven for 40 minutes , stirring well every 10 minutes
12. let cool before eating
demonstrations.review:
I made a couple of batchs of this and never tried it but gave it to a friend. She called and said, "you know I have never had caramel corn I like and I almost told you that but didn't want to hurt your feelings. Now I am glad I didn't say anything because I couldn't keep my hands out of it. Can you teach me how to make it"
So I said sure.  Thanks so much for a winning recipe. Easy to make,just follow the instructions and it comes out perfectly. Don't need to change or substitute anything

demonstrations.recipe_text:
lemon curd  stove top or microwave method  lime or orange curd

a british tea time favorite. this is sweet and tart. try it on scones, muffins, and tea breads or layer on angel food cake with raspberries and recipe #54868!  i've also microwaved this just watch and stir a lot. for orange or lime curd, substitute appropriate fruit rind and juice. proceed as directed.
fyi- when filling a cake with this be sure to pipe a rim of frosting on the edge of the first layer, then fill inside with the chilled lemon curd, place top layer then frost.

1. stove top method:
2. in a medium saucepan over medium-high heat , combine lemon zest , lemon juice , and sugar
3. bring just to a boil
4. reduce heat to medium-low and simmer 5 minutes
5. add butter and stir until it has melted and combined
6. remove from heat and cool to room temperature
7. beat eggs into cooled lemon mixture until well blended
8. return to heat and cook over medium-low heat , stirring constantly , 10 to 15 minutes or until mixture thickens and coats spoon
9. remove from heat
10. cover and refrigerator at least 1 hour
11. microwave method:
12. place butter in a large glass measure or bowl
13. microwave on high for 10 seconds or until the butter is soft , but not melted
14. whisk in the sugar , lemon rind and lemon juice
15. add the whole eggs and yolks and blend well
16. cover with parchment paper and microwave on high for 3 minutes , stirring well after each minute or until mixture thickens and coats spoon
17. cover and refrigerator at least 1 hour
18. pour into a sterilized glass jar and leave to cool
19. store in the refrigerator
demonstrations.review:
Rita,
I don't know if there is a Hall of Fame for people that post recipes on the internet but if not there should be and you should have your statue at the entrance.
Great recipe, easy, and delicious. Thanks for posting this it is simply great.
By the Way for some reason this site wouldn't let me give this 5 stars, only 3 but this is an 11 star recipe at least!!. So I am re-posting it now because for some reason it is now allowing 5 stars (still not enough) Also the only tip is to mix the eggs and yolks really well or you can end up with chunks of eggs in the recipe when you cook it. Mix the eggs thoroughly and mix them in thoroughly before you put heat to it and you will be fine

target.recipe_text:
fillet of beef  beef tenderloin whole

how to cook a whole or large piece of beef tenderloin. note from unknownchef86: this is a recipe i adopted in 2006.

1. preheat the oven to 500 degrees f
2. place the beef on a sheet pan and pat the outside dry with a paper towel
3. spread the butter on with your hands
4. sprinkle evenly with the salt and pepper
5. roast in the oven for exactly 22 minutes for rare and 25 minutes for medium-rare
6. remove the beef from the oven , cover it tightly with aluminum foil , and allow it to rest at room temperature for 20 minutes
7. remove the strings and slice the fillet thickly
target.review: Perfect!  I used sea salt instead of kosher, and added two cloves of garlic (put through the garlic press) to the rub.  The rave reviews made me feel like a Christmas Eve Dinner rockstar!  Thanks for the great recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
oven fried eggplant  aubergine

this recipe appeared in "cooking light" magazine. this is a non-traditional way to prepare eggplant, but it really cuts the calories.

1. combine first 2 ingredients , stir well
2. spread evenly over both sides of eggplant slices
3. combine breadcrumbs , cheese , and italian seasoning in a shallow bowl
4. dredge eggplant in breadcrumbs mixture
5. place eggplant on a baking sheet coated with cooking spray
6. bake@ 425 degrees for 12 minutes
7. turn eggplant over
8. and bake an additional 12 minutes or until golden
demonstrations.review: Very easy, and good! I think that kids would love to dip these into marinara or ranch dressing!  I am going to try the leftovers in a lasagna tomorrow night!  Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
creme brulee french toast

although this is really a breakfast/brunch dish, my daughters occasionally beg to have this for supper. occasionally i indulge them.

1. combine butter , brown sugar and honey in a heavy saucepan over medium heat
2. cook , stirring constantly , until melted and smooth
3. pour into a 13 x 9 inch baking dish
4. trim crusts from bread and arrange in one layer in the baking dish
5. whisk together the eggs , half and half , grand marnier , vanilla and salt in a large mixing bowl
6. pour evenly over the bread
7. cover and refrigerate 8 hours or overnight
8. preheat oven to 350 degrees f
9. remove the dish from the refrigerator and let come to room temperature
10. bake , uncovered , for 35-40 minutes or until puffed and edges are light golden brown
11. serve immediately with individual pieces turned over with the caramel on top
demonstrations.review: Excellent recipe!! I didn't follow it exactly- I didn't have any honey, and used two layers of cinnamon raisin bread.  Either way, it was fantastic, and very easy to throw together the night before a brunch.  One guest described it as similar to a maple bread pudding, and it got rave reviews from everyone! Thanks!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
ground turkey tortilla casserole

this is a recipe that i adapted from a few other tortilla casseroles and it is a quick & easy tummy satisfier!

1. brown turkey and small onion until meat is completely done
2. add taco seasoning packet and follow directions for cooking on back
3. spray non-stick casserole dish with non-stick cooking spray
4. cut flour tortillas into bite size pieces and layer 1 / 2 of tortillas on bottom of casserole dish
5. add 1 / 2 of the cheese , sour cream , salsa and black beans
6. start with the remaining tortillas and repeat layering
7. you may top with extra cheese or salsa if preferred
8. other options include: corn , red pepper , green pepper , jalapenos , or any other ingredient
9. play with ingredients , if you like more sour cream , simply add more , if you like less , add less
10. don't be afraid to test different options
11. bake at 350 until all cheese is melted and everything is heated thoroughly
12. you may wish to cover the dish with foil to prevent overbaking the top -- then removing it for the last 5-10 minutes
demonstrations.review: Very good, and easy to throw together! I used taco seasoning from recipe #4292, and froze half of the ground turkey to use another time.  Scaled down to 8x6 pyrex pan for our small family, so only used 4 tortillas, and one-half can beans.  I didn't realize my sour cream was expired until I went to use it, so I substituted one-half package of cream cheese (yum!).  I just sandwiched all the filling between torn-tortilla "crusts", then covered it in cheese.  At any rate, it was fantastic, and will become a regular at my house!

target.recipe_text:
crock pot chicken chow mein

from about.com: southern recipes.  i haven't made this recipe yet, but am posting in on 'zaar for easy keeping (and finding).

1. heat oil in skillet
2. brown chicken , stirring to brown all sides
3. put chicken pieces in crockpot
4. stir in all ingredients except cornstarch and water
5. cover and cook on low for 6 to 8 hours
6. turn to high
7. combine cornstarch and cold water in a small bowl
8. stir until mixture is smooth and cornstarch is dissolved
9. stir into the slow cooker liquids
10. keeping cover slightly ajar to allow steam to escape , cook on high until thickened , about 15 to 30 minutes
11. serveover rice or chinese noodles
target.review: Love this recipe, the flavor is perfect and it is so healthy!  Thanks for posting this recipe, it is quite flexible and so easy!  I put the chicken in the crockpot without browning, used a fresh bag of bean sprouts, fresh ginger, a yellow onion, no water chestnuts, sucralose for sweetener and no sides for a lower carb meal.  This goes in my favorite recipes and meal rotation.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
bisquick impossible tuna melt pie

i have always made this, i got the recipe from the back of the bisquick box.

1. preheat oven to 400 degrees
2. grease baking dish
3. cook and stir onions and butter in skillet over low heat until onions are light brown
4. sprinkle tuna , 1 cup of the cheese and the onions in baking dish
5. beat eggs , milk , baking mix , salt and pepper until well blended
6. pour into baking dish
7. bake 25 minutes
8. top with remaining cheese to within 1 inch from edge
9. bake 5 to 8 minutes longer or until knife inserted in center comes out clean
10. the pie can be done even though some melted cheese adheres to knife
demonstrations.review: This is a nice change from my usual tuna recipes. I added mixed veggies and used raw onions, my homemade bisquick (1/2 whole wheat) and sharp cheddar cheese. I did not measure the salt and think I did not use enough, because I thought it needed a bit more. I made half the recipe, perfect for dinner for two with a side salad and maybe leftovers for one for lunch.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
splenda hot cocoa

steamed milk with wonderful cocoa and splenda - need i say more?

1. mix cocoa , splenda and water into a paste
2. steam milk
3. mix & enjoy !
demonstrations.review: This warmed me up on this dreary Sunday morning and it is delicious, easy and quick. Next time I will cut back on the splenda a bit, just personal preference. I don't often drink plain milk and hot cocoa is a good way for me to increase my intake and to use up the milk and get the health benefits of cocoa.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
lime jello cabbage salad

this jello salad is a tradition in our family to serve with ham or pork.  it has shredded cabbage and carrots in it which give it a nice crunch.  my mom always served it when i was a kid and she can't remember where she got the recipe from.  my kids love it.  you can make with with regular or sugar free jello.

1. shred cabbage in food processor to be very fine and to equal 1 cup
2. grate carrots to equal 1 / 2 cup
3. add both to an 8 x 8 square dish
4. drain crushed pineapple , reserving liquid in a measuring cup
5. add ice to the juice so it will equal exactly one cup
6. set aside
7. in a small pan on low heat , heat one cup water
8. add jello to dissolve and turn off heat
9. add the pineapple juice / ice to the pan and stir until ice melts
10. pour jello mixture into the 8 x 8 dish with the cabbage , carrots and pineapple
11. refrigerate for 2 hours unti firm
12. cut into 9 square servings and and enjoy !
demonstrations.review: A light and refreshing salad. I used sugar free lime jello and the pineapple juice and did not find it too sweet. It is OK with a dallop of mayo on top, but I think I prefer it without. I also remember this being served at family gatherings when I was growing up.

target.recipe_text:
authentic black bean chicken

fermented black beans are found in asian markets and once you buy them, they last pretty much forever! also called salted black beans, they're used in the black bean chicken you order from chinese take-out and has a much different flavor than the mexican type of black beans. from chef fuchsia dunlop with my addition of some red pepper for color! also check out my review of recipe#247607.

1. cut the chicken into bite sized chunks
2. put them in a bowl and add salt and soy sauce
3. mix well and set aside
4. heat peanut oil in the wok over high heat
5. add the chicken and stir-fry until it changes color , then remove from the wok with a slotted spoon
6. drain off all but 3 tablespoons oil from the wok , then return it to medium heat
7. add the ginger and garlic and stir-fry for a few minutes until they are fragrant and the garlic cloves are tender
8. add the black beans and stir-fry until fragrant , splashing in the wine as you do so
9. add the chili flakes and stir-fry for a few moments
10. return the chicken to the wok
11. add the red bell pepper and toss both in the fragrant oil , splashing in the vinegar and adding salt to taste
12. when everything is sizzly , throw in the scallions and stir a few times until barely cooked
13. then , off the heat , stir in the sesame oil and serve
target.review: This is a great recipe. My husband loved it!<br/>However I didn't have the fermented black beans so I substituted that with the Lee Kum Kee black bean sauce. I applied the same 4 tbsp though I think 3 will be suffice. No additional salt needed for marinating as the Lee Kum Kee sauce is salty

demonstrations.recipe_text:
broiled tilapia with thai coconut  curry sauce

this dish is loaded with flavor and makes a lovely, colorful presentation. you'll want to serve with plenty of rice to absorb the wonderful sauce. (noted added 11/05/07: i like to credit original recipe sources when known, but wasn't sure about this one when i submitted the recipe. fortunately, a reviewer pointed out that the recipe came from cooking light, so i searched their site--indeed, it was originally published in their september 2002 issue. thanks to the reviewer for bringing this to my attention, and thanks to cooking light for developing the recipe! :) )

1. preheat broiler
2. heat 1 / 2 teaspoon oil in a large nonstick skillet over medium heat
3. add ginger and garlic
4. cook 1 minute
5. add peppers and onions
6. cook 1 minute
7. stir in curry powder , curry paste , and cumin
8. cook 1 minute
9. add soy sauce , sugar , 1 / 4 teaspoon salt , and coconut milk
10. bring to a simmer
11. remove from heat and stir in cilantro
12. brush fish with remaining 1 / 2 teaspoon oil and 1 / 4 teaspoon salt and place on a baking sheet coated with cooking spray
13. broil 7 minutes or until fish flakes easily when tested with a fork
14. serve fish with sauce , rice , and lime wedges
demonstrations.review: Well balanced flavour. Didn't have any tilapia so sub with Hake. This a keeper!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chicken  rice  and spices bake

i got this recipe from my friend kasey a long time ago (i have adjusted the spices to my taste) and it is very easy--even for those that just can't seem to get basmati rice to cook "just right". so long as you cover the baking dish tightly with foil, it will not fail! i brought this to a pot-luck at work one day and ever since this dish was always requested by everyone at all of our potlucks.***i am cutting the salt to around half since there are quite a few reviews saying it is too salty. i don't measure the spices when i cook so i think i guessed the amount wrong.***
*** the cinnamon amount should be 1/2 tsp to 3/4 tsp only, not 2 teaspoons.  i have tried changing it twice now and get email confirmation that the changes have been approved but it still says 2 tsp of cinnamon.

1. preheat oven to 375f and grease a 9x13-inch baking dish
2. bring water to boiling and add chicken bouillon cubes , lower heat and simmer till dissolved--keep it hot
3. sprinkle chicken with half the spices
4. heat the olive oil in a large skillet on med-high to high heat and fry the chicken till both sides are brown , lower heat to medium and remove the chicken to a plate
5. in that same skillet saut the onions for 2 minutes , then add the garlic and remaining spices and saut another 2 minutes , then turn off the burner
6. add the rice and stir for about 30 seconds to 1 minute , till well coated
7. spread rice in the baking dish and place the chicken thighs over the rice
8. gently pour in the chicken stock and cover tightly with foil
9. bake for 40-45 minutes
demonstrations.review:
Big hit with my husband to the point he said "SAVE IT"
Delicious, full of flavour, definitely will be making more of it now

demonstrations.recipe_text:
spicy stir fried green beans and scallions

originally from cook's magazine.  can be a side dish (4 servings) or a vegetarian main course (2 servings)

1. mix soy sauce , vinegar , sugar , pepper flakes and 1 tablespoon water in a small bowl
2. set aside
3. heat a heavy skillet over high heat until extremely hot
4. carefully swirl 2 tablespoons oil to coat the bottom
5. fry green beans , flipping every 30 seconds or so with a wide spatula , until slight charred and crisp-tender - about 4 minutes
6. add scallions , continue cooking in same manner until scallions are charred and beans are tender
7. make a well in the center of the pan
8. mash garlic and remaining 1 t
9. oil together
10. fry until fragrant - about 5 seconds - and stir into vegetables
11. add soy mixture and toss into vegetables to coat
12. cook until liquid is reduced by about half , about 15 seconds
13. serve immediately
demonstrations.review: Yummy. Brings back memories when my mom made it

target.recipe_text:
cream of asparagus soup  vegan

a creamy, yet low-fat soup. i have substituted all kinds of vegetables for the asparagus when making this - including broccoli, cauliflower and potato.

1. chop the asparagus , reserving the
2. put the asparagus , onion , garlic and broth in a large saucepan
3. bring to a boil , then reduce to medium heat and cook until the vegetables are tender , about 15 minutes
4. put contents of saucepan into blender
5. add the flour , soy milk , soy sauce and basil
6. process until smooth
7. return the soup to the saucepan and add the asparagus
8. cook over medium heat until the soup thickens and is heated through
9. season to taste with salt and fresh cracked pepper and serve
target.review: I used rice milk that needed to be used and left-over asparagus. I blended the flour into the broth with the soy sauce. This then went into the food processor and the soup was reheated after processing. I found this soup to be quite thick and very delicious. I will definitely make this again with other vegetables.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
parmesan basil perch

husband is dieting. he loves this!recipe from- betty crocker's healthy new choices cookbook.

1. move oven rack to position slightly above middle of oven
2. heat oven to 375 degrees
3. spray rectangular pan , 13 x 9 x 2 with cooking spray
4. mix all ingredients except fish , margarine , and parsley
5. brush one side of fish with margarine , dip into crumb mixture
6. place fish , coated sides up , in pan
7. bake uncovered 15 to 20 mins , or until fish flakes easily with fork
8. sprinkle with parsley !
demonstrations.review: This dish was easy to make and very flavorful. I used wild caught ocean perch. My SO enjoyed it very much, so I will be making this again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
bleu cheese beef tenderloin

if you like bleu cheese...you should love this easy meal. prep time is the length of time to let the meat marinade as well as to create the final sauce. (this is a copykat with a few adjustments but for the life of me i don't know where i got it)!

1. place beef in a shallow dish
2. combine , teriyaki sauce , red wine& garlic
3. pour mixture over beef and allow to marinate for at least 30 minutes turning at least once
4. place tenderloin on broiler pan and cook in preheated oven at 450 degrees for 15 minutes
5. reduce heat to 375 degrees and cook for 30 to 40 minutes longer
6. allow to set for appx 10 minutes before slicing keeping in mind it will continue to cook as it sets
7. in a saucepan over low heat , combine the bleu cheese , mayo , sour cream and worcestershire sauce
8. stir until smooth and creamy and serve over the sliced tenderloin
9. when i made this , i saved the marinade , minced some garlic and added a little more of each ingredient
10. i then put it in a saucepan with a sprig of rosemary and small red potatoes and let them simmer while the meal cooked
11. as always , garlic and bleu cheese can be overpowering for some but you can indeed adjust these to taste
demonstrations.review: This was awesome! I made this with the potatoes and then used the left-overs for #87171 Roast-Beef Hash. This was also awesome because you can use all the same ingredients as #18487-Bleu Chesse Beef Tenderloin.....

demonstrations.recipe_text:
streusel plum cake

this cake is low in fat and not too sweet. the glaze is optional, it takes a minute to prepare and adds only a few more calories. great way to use up fresh plumbs in season. we like it best without the glaze, which also helps the diabetic.

1. in a large bowl , cream together sugar , margarine and egg yolks until fluffy
2. combine flour with baking powder
3. beat into egg mixture alternately with milk
4. beat egg whites until stiff but not dry
5. fold into batter
6. pour batter into greased 9 inch square cake pan
7. halve and pit plums
8. arrange over batter
9. streusel topping-------------
10. in a small bowl , combine brown sugar , margarine and cinnamon
11. sprinkle over fruit
12. bake in 350f oven for 35-45 minutes or until top is golden and tester inserted into centre of cake comes out clean
13. glaze --------------
14. combine icing sugar , milk and vanilla
15. drizzle over cooled cake
demonstrations.review: I have some canned plums that I need to use and I used a quart jar of plums in this recipe. I also used Pamela's Pancake and Baking Mix from the health food store. This mix eliminates the need for some of the ingredients and less sugar; also quicker to make. All and all this is a delicious recipe!

target.recipe_text:
my family s favorite sloppy joes  pizza joes

i've tried many recipes, this is the best. i once 'dec-tupled' (10x) this recipe to sell sandwiches at a craft fair at my church. people were waiting in line to buy leftovers. freezes well, goes up to the lake or camping well and is a hit on halloween...it's no-fail. easy to double, triple, etc. i've been making joes this way for over 20 years.
***03-08-09, i just reinvented this recipe tonight when i went to make it for dinner and found i didn't have an 8-oz. can of tomato sauce (shame on me).  the family was upset with me when i subbed an 8-oz. can of pizza sauce and told them to suck it up and call them 'pizza joes' and then served them up with shredded mozzarella cheese on the toasted buns, top and bottom.  they loved it.  i left out the bbq sauce in this preparation and just used a 1/2 cup ketchup.  pizza joes are good to go!

1. in a large skillet , brown ground beef , celery and onion
2. drain the fat , who needs it ?
3. stir in remaining ingredients , simmer covered , 15-20 minutes , stirring occasionally
4. if joes appear too'loose' , leave cover off and let moisture evaporate
5. cook until it's the consistency you like for serving on toasted buns , with french fries and cole slaw
target.review: It was a bit sweet for me, so I added about 2 tbsp of Louisiana hot sauce, and it was much better! Thanks for the recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
healthy grilled herbed fish

a little dish i created a couple of years back. extremely healthy. the fish turns out really moist, and the juice is out of this world. i usually add a little more garlic, but i am crazy about garlic. has become such a staple with my family that it is requested for at least once a month. don't worry about adding any salt, i personally feel that it isn't needed. the herbs and juices mixed together makes it all natural and tasty enough. but if you feel some salt is lacking, just sprinkle a little before digging in. enjoy!

1. cut a piece of tin foil big enough to wrap round the fish twice
2. brush the middle portion of foil with olive oil
3. place the fish fillet on top of the greased foil
4. rub ginger juice into fish
5. sprinkle a pinch of pepper on top of fillet
6. spread the oregano and basil evenly over the top of fillet
7. sprinkle the finely chopped garlic over the top of herbs
8. rest the tomato slices on top
9. arrange the onion rings over the fillet
10. squeeze the juice of both the orange and the lemon over the whole fillet
11. grate the zest of both the orange and lemon on the top
12. wrap up the fish with all the ingredients in the foil
13. place the envelope in the grill and grill at 400f for 20 minutes
14. turn the grill off and let it sit in the grill for another 10 minutes
15. remove the envelope , cut an "x" on the top , place on plate and serve
demonstrations.review: My family loved this! I used garlic powder, and ginger powder bc thats all I had on hand, and my husband put the fish directly on the grill..it was fish we had caught and he left the skin and scales on. Tomatoes were delicious! I'll put on more next time! Thanks for a great recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cream cheese banana nut bread

for a request from southern living, january edition.  submitted by willie monroe, homewood, alabama.   prep time does not include making toppings.  the nutrition facts includes all of the topping ingredients.

1. beat butter and cream cheese at medium speed with electric mixer , until creamy
2. gradually add sugar , beating until light and fluffy
3. add eggs , 1 at a time , beating just until blended after each addition
4. combine flour and next 3 ingredients
5. gradually add to butter mixture , beating at low speed just until blended
6. stir in bananas , pecans , and vanilla
7. spoon batter into 2 greased and floured 8 x 4 inch loafpans
8. bake at 350 for 1 hour , or until tests clean
9. (shield with foil the last 15 minutes to prevent browning , if necessary
10. cool bread in pans on wire racks 10 minutes
11. remove from pans , and cool 30 minutes on wire racks before slicing
12. orange pecan topping:
13. sprinkle pecans over batter before baking
14. cool bread 10 minutes , remove from pans
15. stir together sugar , orange juice and orange rind
16. drizzle evenly over warm bread
17. cinnamon-crisp topping
18. stir together brown sugar , toasted pecans , flour , melted butter and cinnamon
19. sprinle mixture evenly over batter
20. bake and cool bread
demonstrations.review: I don't care what anyone says, this was amazing! the center was so moist, and like my grandfather said, the topping was like Christmas lol. Everyone who ate it gave it 5 stars, and I'll defiantly be making this again. Thanks for the great recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
easy taco stew

this is so easy to make. very flavorful. this recipe can easily be doubled.

1. brown the beef and onion in a dutch oven , then drain
2. add all ingredients to the beef / onion mixture , except for the tortilla chips and cheese
3. cook over medium heat until thoroughly heated
4. to serve: crumble a handful of either tortilla chips or doritos in individual serving bowls and cover with a generous helping of stew
5. sprinkle with cheese
6. hint: you can reduce the heat by substituting the pinto beans in chili sauce with either red kidney beans , plain pinto beans , etc
demonstrations.review: YUM! This was awesome! My husband got seconds, and my grandfather went back for thirds! The only things I did different were that I used tomato sauce instead of soup, and no beans. I'll be making this again soon! Thanks for the recipe!

target.recipe_text:
baked chicken tenders

these baked chicken tenders are super simple and quick for those hectic weekday meals.  i've put them on top of a salad with homemade honey mustard dressing.  they would also go great with some french fries.  the variations are endless.

1. preheat oven to 425f
2. mix chicken tenders and mayonnaise in a bowl to lightly coat chicken with mayonnaise
3. mix bread crumbs and cheese in a gallon-size zippie bag
4. prepare baking sheet with cooking spray
5. put 1-2 chicken tenders in the zippie bag with the bread crumbs and shake to coat
6. place chicken tenders in a single layer on prepared baking sheet
7. continue until all tenders are coated and on the baking sheet
8. bake in preheated oven for 8 minutes
9. gently flip each one , so as not to remove the breading , and bake an additional 8 minutes
10. serve with your favorite dipping sauce
target.review: I make this quite often using thin cut chicken breasts. I like to over cook it a bit so the coating is nicely browned and crispy. Easy and yummy!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
to die for crock pot roast

amazing flavor, and so simple! no salt needed here. in fact, you may wish to use half the ranch dressing mix to cut back on the saltiness. found this crock-pot pot roast recipe on of a website called www.recipegoldmine.com. it's all the rage there, so i thought i'd try it.

1. place beef roast in crock pot
2. mix the dried mixes together in a bowl and sprinkle over the roast
3. pour the water around the roast
4. cook on low for 7-9 hours
5. use onion soup mix instead of ranch
6. add one cup , of red wine
7. add potatoes , carrots , mushrooms , celery and onion 2-3 hours before end
demonstrations.review: I've tried so many pot roast recipes but never found one I thought was outstanding until I came upon THIS! I followed the instructions to the letter and it was the best I've ever had! There are only two of us so I cut it in half and it worked perfectly. I ran across another that is identical other than it has you mix the water into the combined mixes first. I tried that and it did not come out as well. I also bought a much cheaper roast so that could be the problem. I'm making this tonight! Thanks so much for this wonderful recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pork chops with blue cheese gravy

boy, does this look good.... if you like blue cheese. i highly recommend a moist blue cheese as opposed to a more crumbly one to facilitate making the sauce. nabbed with no shame whatsoever from allrecipes.com.

1. melt butter in a large skillet , over medium heat
2. season the pork chops with black pepper and garlic powder
3. fry the chops in butter until no longer pink and the juices run clear , about 20 to 25 minutes
4. turn occasionally to brown evenly
5. remove chops to a plate and keep warm
6. stir the whipping cream into the skillet , loosening any bits of meat stuck to the bottom
7. stir in blue cheese
8. cook , stirring constantly until sauce thickens , about 5 minutes
9. pour sauce over warm pork chops
demonstrations.review: WOW!! I have never made such a SIMPLE dish and had it turn out to be so DELICIOUS! I followed the recipe exactly and really would not change a thing. Served it with peas and mashed potatoes.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
so simple cowboy caviar

had this at a potluck picnic and it was wonderful. i sought out the woman who made it and got the recipe. the secret is to drain it before serving so it isn't swimming in dressing. serve with tortilla chips. i use cider vinegar but feel free to use white, red, raspberry or any other flavor of your choice. can sizes are given for the current commonly available sizes in the us. adjust ingredients for your taste. times do not include marinate or draining time.

1. in small saucepan , combine oil , sugar and vinegar
2. heat and boil 1 minute and then cool completely
3. in large bowl , combine beans , peas , corn , peppers and onions
4. pour vinegar mixture over bean / pepper mixture and mix to thoroughly coat
5. cover and marinate overnight
6. drain for 2-3 hours before serving
demonstrations.review: One of my very favorites for summer! I originally got the recipe from our librarian. Instead of green pepper it had chopped celery. It never dawned on me to drain this before serving! Thank you for that tip.

target.recipe_text:
boursin cheese  homemade

boursin-style cheese can easily be made at home. not just more economical, but fresher and tastier.  rub all the dried herbs used between your fingers before adding.

1. have cheeses and butter at room temperature
2. crush garlic
3. mix cheeses , butter and garlic
4. add remaining ingredients , mix well
5. pack into a container just large enough to hold the boursin and store in refrigerator
6. to serve , bring to room temperature
7. serve with crackers
target.review: I have made this many times and love this recipe!  So much less expensive than the premade stuff!  I have found it keeps well in the refrigerator too.  Great to have on hand.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
delicious corn muffins

these delicious corn muffins were served at kenny roger's restaurant. i found the recipe on "top secret recipes". i love to serve them with bbq. they are so good it is almost like eating a dessert.

1. preheat oven to 400 degrees
2. mix butter , sugar , honey , eggs , and salt into a large bowl
3. add flour , cornmeal , and baking powder and blend thoroughly
4. add milk while mixing
5. add corn to mixture and work into mixture
6. do not mash corn , the whole kernel is baked into the muffin
7. fill a muffin pan with 12 paper / foil muffin cups and fill 2 / 3 full with batter
8. bake for 20-25 minutes until muffins are light brown
demonstrations.review: This is now my go-to recipe for corn muffins!  The muffins are moist & tasty, just the right amount of sweetness, and just the right texture with the added corn.  Love them!  I made a big batch of these and had some leftover, so I wrapped them up and put in the freezer.  Pulled out a couple the other day and microwaved them on HIGH for about 45 seconds--WONDERFUL!  Thanks for posting!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
breakfast casserole supreme

this is a wonderful almost do ahead breakfast. great for company or christmas morning.

1. melt margarine and place in the bottom of 9" by 13" baking pan
2. spread potatoes in bottom of the pan
3. sprinkle chopped vegetables over potatoes
4. add salt and pepper to taste
5. sprinkle meat over potatoes and vegetables
6. pour beaten eggs over potatoes
7. bake at 350 degrees for 45 minutes
8. remove from oven and sprinkle cheese evenly over top
9. bake another 5-10 minutes or until cheese is hot and bubbly
10. remove from oven and let set for approximately 5 minutes
11. cut into 2
12. 5"-3" squares and serve with a spatula
13. enjoy
demonstrations.review: Had high hopes for this recipe but was disappointed.  Not much flavor and the texture of the potato layer was wierd.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
perfect chocolate brownies

this is the best brownie recipe i've ever used and i've used several!

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees
2. grease a 9x13" pan
3. melt shortening in a large saucepan over low heat , then stir in cocoa
4. remove from heat
5. mix in sugar and vanilla then mix in eggs one at a time
6. stir in remaining ingredients then stir in nuts
7. bake for 30 minutes
8. cool completely , before cutting into 2x2" squares
9. i have read all the great reviews and learned from them , thank you all
10. now i line my pan with buttered alumunin foil or parchment paper
11. this works very well
demonstrations.review: I've made these a few times now and they are wonderful!  Be sure to use less salt if you use butter or margarine as a substitute for shortening.  Iced with #88255 and sprinkled with some colored jimmies to increase the yum factor.  Definitely one of the best brownie recipes I've tried!

target.recipe_text:
snickers dessert on a diet

no snickers bars were killed in the making of this recipe. prep time includes time for cooling.

1. let frozen yogurt sit at room temperature to soften slightly
2. in a large bowl , combine the frozen yogurt , pudding mix and peanut butter
3. fold in whipped topping
4. spoon into a 13x9-inch pan
5. if desired drizzle lightly with the fudge or chocolate topping in an attractive pattern
6. freeze until firm about 2 hours
7. cut into 16 pieces
target.review: Outstanding dessert!!! I used fat-free fudge ripple frozen yogurt (I couldn't find vanilla at our grocery store) and a chocolate graham craker crust. The flavor was rich and everyone LOVED it! I will make this dessert again and again. Thanks for a great recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
creamy wild rice soup with smoked turkey

this came from cooking light 2001 magazine and it has been our favorite since i found it. it is the best cold, rainy, gloomy, any day soup ever!!

1. melt butter in a dutch oven over med high heat
2. add carrot and next 5 ingredients
3. saute 8 minutes or until brown
4. stir in broth scraping pan to loosen browned bits
5. stir in turkey and rice
6. cover and simmer 1 hour 15 minutes or until rice is tender
7. combine flour and milk in a small bowl stirring with a whisk
8. add flour / milk mixture to pan and cook over medium heat about 8 minutes or until thick
9. stir in sherry and salt
demonstrations.review: This soup was excellent. My whole family enjoyed it, and with two picky teenagers, that doesn't often happen. The dry sherry really added depth to the flavor, so don't leave it out. I doubled the recipe and froze the leftovers, which I plan to serve at a holiday dinner party.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
amish sugar cream pie

my whole family loves this recipe, even my husbands family loves it!  this came from an amish family in indiana.

1. in sauce pan combine , white sugar , salt , half-and-half and whipping cream
2. bring to a boil
3. in another sauce pan , combine br
4. sugar & cornstarch
5. gradually whisk in hot mixture into br
6. sugar mixture
7. add margarine / or butter
8. cook over med
9. heat , whisk constantly , 5 min or until thick
10. simmer 1 minute and stir in van
11. pour into uncooked pie shell and sprinkle w / cinnamon and nutmeg
12. bake at 375f for 25 minutes
13. i recommend recipe #126072 for this pie
demonstrations.review: This is a wonderful recipe for sugar cream pie. Really delicious and fairly simple to make. The flavor and texture are outstanding. We live in Pennsylvania Dutch/Amish country and have tried many wonderful Amish-inspired dishes and desserts. This pie is by far the best Amish-type dessert we have ever had.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mix and match bundt cake

this cake is unbelievably moist and sooo tasty.you can interchange the ingredients to make different flavors and it is as easy as 1 2 3.only 4 ingredients!!!please read the example below instructions for flavors of cake and fruit.

1. mix cake mix , extract , eggs together , will be very thick
2. add the fruit pie filling and fold into cake batter , again , will be very thick
3. spread into a greased and floured bundt pan and bake at 325f till toothpick inserted in middle comes out clean
4. let cake cool for a few minutes and invert cake onto a platter and wrap with saran wrap until cake has completely cooled , this allows the cake to create steam which insures moistness
5. examples of flavors: devils food cake mix with cherry pie filling and almond extract spice cake mix with apple pie filling and vanilla extract white cake mix with blueberry pie filling and lemon extract
demonstrations.review: Easy to make and delicious! I used yellow cake mix, apricot pie filling, and almond extract. Covering in plastic wrap while the cake cools resulted in a wonderfully moist cake with intense flavor. I drizzled a white chocolate glaze over the cake before serving. Next time I will skip the glaze. This cake is so moist and flavorful that a glaze isn't needed. I will make this cake again and again. Thanks for posting this great recipe!

target.recipe_text:
ethiopian lentils with berebere spice mix

recipe includes spice mix if you can't find it in the supermarkets.

1. lentils:
2. bring lentils and broth to boil and simmer 10 minutes
3. add chiles , onion , garlic , and berebere spices
4. cook covered for another 30 minutes , until most of liquid is absorbed
5. serve with ground black pepper to taste
6. for a vegetarian meal , these lentils are good with a dollop of yogurt , brown rice and sliced tomatoes
7. berebere spice mix:
8. toast all the seeds and whole cloves in a small frying pan for 2 minutes , stirring constantly
9. grind the spices in a spice grinder
10. if you are using pre-ground spices , ignore and go on to the next step
11. mix all remaining ingredients
12. place in a tightly covered container and refrigerate
13. this mixture can used with many combinations of legumes , rice or vegetables
14. the first way gives you a more powerful flavor , but it may be more practical the second way , particularly if you don't have a spice grinder
15. yield: 6 to 10 servings
target.review: I read the reviews first so I only used 2 tablespoons of the pepper flakes, I could probably do 3 and be just fine. Also, I felt like it was missing something so I added a small amount of brown sugar and yams for texture. It was wonderful and I will be making this regularly.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
copycat marie callender s cornbread

serve with honey-butter for a great treat!

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. combine all dry ingredients
3. combine remaining ingredients and add to dry ingredients and mix well
4. pour into greased oblong pan
5. bake 35 minutes
demonstrations.review: This was wonderful! I have always loved Marie's cornbread and never been too fond of others. This tasted just like Marie's! It fell apart a lil more than the original but it still tasted great!! Great recipe!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
scrumptious barbecue chicken or spareribs

i got this one out of a church cookbook. it has excellent flavor and is very easy to prepare.

1. cook onion in a little water until soft
2. mix the remaining ingredients with onions and simmer for 15 minutes
3. brown the meat and put into a baking dish
4. pour sauce over the top and bake at 250 degrees f
5. for 2 1 / 2 hours
demonstrations.review: My girlfriend made this as a surprise romantic dinner. We ended up eating close to midnight...but it was so amazing. You would think chicken baked for 2 hours or more would be dry, but it was perfect. Great recipe!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pumpkin seeds

one of the best things about halloween when i was a kid was the pumpkin seeds baking while we were finishing up the details on the carving. serving size depends on the pumpkin

1. wash your pumpkin seeds
2. boil 1 quart of water
3. after water has boiled , place the clean seeds and 1 / 8 cup of salt into water for 10 minutes- stir the whole time
4. melt 2 tbs of butter
5. drain the seeds and mix them with the butter
6. place the seeds on a 2 layer tin foiled pan and place in oven at 350 f for 30 minutes
7. do not refrigerate seeds- put them in a sealed bowl and leave them on the kitchen table
demonstrations.review: Turned out just how I like them, CRUNCHY! Thank you!

target.recipe_text:
vegetable quiche cups  sbd

these are a breakfast option in the south beach diet (phase 1). they can be eaten hot or cold and can also be frozen. these make a handy and healthy snack to take to work too.

1. heat oven to 350f
2. line a 12 cup muffin pan with foil baking cups , spray the cups with cooking spray
3. thaw and drain spinach , wring it out well by hand
4. mix the spinach , egg whites or substitute , cheese , peppers , onions , hot pepper sauce and salt in a bowl
5. fill the foil cups with the mixture
6. bake at 350f or 20 minutes , testing so that a knife inserted in the middle comes out clean
7. remove from cups to serve
target.review: I love these.. I am not a spinach person so i ditch it and add a can (drained) of asparagus. I put it all in my food processor and pulse a few times and voila! put in the muffin tin and into the oven. I keep them in the freezer and microwave when i want one. these are great.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cheese topped vegetables

nan

1. preheat oven to 400: f
2. in a large saucepan , bring 2 quarts of water to a boil
3. add broccoli and cauliflower
4. cook for 3 minutes
5. add carrot and cook for 2 minutes
6. drain vegetables in a colander
7. place mixture in a 2 quart baking dish
8. stir in peas
9. set aside
10. to prepare the sauce , in a small saucepan , heat oil over medium heat
11. add flour
12. cook , stirring constantly , for 1 minute
13. gradually whisk in milk and broth
14. bring to a boil and cook , whisking frequently , for 3 minutes
15. remove from heat
16. stir in = cup of cheddar and the pepper
17. pour sauce over vegeta bles
18. stir until coated
19. sprinkle remaining cheddar over top
20. bake until cheese is bubbling , about 5 minutes
21. serve immediately
demonstrations.review: This didnt quite come out how i was hoping it would. I think could be really good with some tweaking. The sauce was VERY runny and i think there should be atleast double the cheese. The veggies were perfectly cooked however.  I might make this again but change a few things around and maybe add some spices to this as well to give it a little more flavor. Made this for a Bargain Basement Tag. Thanks for posting!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cheese and wine chicken

this is a very 

1. place cut up chicken in a shallow pan
2. mix all ingredients except cheese and paprika
3. pour over chicken
4. sprinkle with cheese and paprika
5. bake at 325 for 1 1 / 2 hours
demonstrations.review: I used 3lbs of boneless skinless chicken breast and left out the sliced mushrooms (and baked it for 1hr 15min) Im suprised that this hadnt been reviewed yet, ITS FABULOUS!! I will be making this again, for sure! Made this for a Bargain Basement Tag.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chicken squisito

this recipe comes from sorrento. if you like cheese then you'll enjoy this.

1. preheat oven to 375 degrees
2. season chicken with salt and pepper and powders
3. heat oil over medium-high heat
4. when pan is hot , add chicken and saute 2 minutes each side
5. remove chicken
6. saute onions in pan for 4 minutes
7. add tomatoes and broth and cook for approximately 8 minutes to blend flavors
8. place reserved chicken in pan and stir to combine
9. transfer chicken w / mixture to a 9x13 baking dish
10. mix cheeses together and sprinkle over chicken
11. bake for about 15 minutes
demonstrations.review: i made this using what i had on hand soo... i didnt have any onion powder so i used some dried minced onions, also used fresh cracked pepper and salt, and didnt have any ramano cheese so i grated a bit extra of both the others.  this was super easy and super yummy! made this for a Bargain Basement Tag

target.recipe_text:
apple blackberry crisp

this is an easy and delish desert that is excellent on a summer day served warm with a scoop of vanilla bean ice cream.

1. preheat oven to 400 degrees in a big bowl combine blackberries , apples and 1 / 2 cup of sugar and two tsp of flour
2. toss to coat
3. pour mixture into a 11x17 baking dish that has been sprayed
4. next combine one cup sugar and the 3 / 4 cup of flour
5. cut in butter until the mixture looks crumby
6. sprinkle crumbs over fruit and bake at 400 degrees for 35 minutes or until golden and apples are tender
target.review: A very nice dessert,so easy to make, and so lovely to look at.  I used huge (really, really, really huge) blackberries and some McIntosh apples.  The combination of these fruits and the "crisp" topping was delightful.  It was simply divine!  The combinations are unlimited (thinking peaches)!!!  Thanks for sharing this great summer dessert recipe.  It will definately be used again soon :-)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
spicy mexican coleslaw

this is ideal picnic food since it has no mayo in it. you can use more or less hot pepper depending on how hot you like it/can take it.

1. combine all salad ingredients and mix well
2. combine all dressing ingredients and toss well with salad ingredients
3. refrigerate until ready to serve
4. this slaw gets better if it has a chance to sit for a few hours before serving and it's even good the next day
demonstrations.review: This was a surprising dish.  I loved the harmony of the citrus flavors in the dressing.  The jicama and cabbage had a wonderful crunchiness that I enjoyed too.  I used this dish as a side to a chicken and salsa recipe, and it was wonderful.  Thanks, Mirj for sharing this keeper.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pasta with scallops and lemon butter mustard sauce

my favorite pasta recipe, the mustard is tangy and elegant. very fast to make, use the small and less expensive scallops.

1. simmer wine and lemon zest in medium saucepan
2. add scallops and cook and stir for 1 minute
3. take out scallops , raise heat and reduce wine to about 1 / 4 cup
4. reduce heat to low , whisk in mustard , then butter , in small pieces
5. add scallops and any juice and heat through
6. season with salt and pepper
7. put sauce over cooked pasta-angel hair is good , and sprinkle on chives
demonstrations.review: This recipe is restraunt gormet!  The scallops with dijon and lemon were delectable.  Flavor wise, it was light, yet rich.  Served over angel hair pasta, and garnished with fresh chives from my garden, made a lovely presentation!  Thanks, Kasha for sharing this wonderful recipe.  I can definately recommend it.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
sneaky  gotcha flavored tender chops

this is very good but you have to like citrus with your pork. they come out so tender and moist! once you've tried them they gotcha coming back again,

1. in the top of a double boiler , over simmering water , mix all the ingredients except the pork chops heat until the sugar has completely dissolved
2. place the chops in a casserole with a lid
3. spread the seasoned mixture over the chops and bake covered in a slow 300f over for 2 hours
demonstrations.review: Wow!  These tasty, moist chops have it all!  Citrus, fresh herbs, spices.  I had a time finding some fresh mint right now, but I persevered, and was rewarded by the refreshing taste of it in the sauce.  This is an excellent dish with contrasting ingredients, but they were in harmony.  Thanks Bergy for a real taste treat.

target.recipe_text:
basic machine french bread

this is my winner with tammiev and our friends. this recipe is for a 2 pound loaf and has never failed me. i think it is the lack of oil and sugar that they like in this one.

1. add to the bread pan in the order yours needs
2. for mine it is water first
3. then i add half the flour and the salt followed by the rest of the flour and the yeast on top
4. this will run well on the normal , rapid , and delay start cycles
target.review: What a great recipe!  So simple to make, I'll be making it many more times.  Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
tropical coconut bread

having a luau party? then this is a must but, you'll want to make this throughout the year. the smell alone will get your significant other to release their grip on the remote, the kids will drift out of their bedrooms and the neighbors might come knocking. i dare to say, this might even be an aphrodisiac! it's great alone but if you're adventurous, slice some strawberries on it or drizzle chocolate syrup over it and top it with some whipped cream.

1. preheat oven to 325 degrees f
2. grease and flour two 9 1 / 2" x 5 1 / 2" loaf pans
3. do not use a mixer with this recipe
4. use a spoon or spatula and stir by hand
5. in medium mixing bowl , combine flour , baking powder , baking soda , and salt
6. mix well
7. in large mixing bowl , combine sugar , oil , beaten eggs , and coconut extract
8. mix well
9. alternately add flour mixture and buttermilk to sugar mixture and stir only until moist
10. stir in shredded coconut
11. pour batter into the two prepared loaf pans , place on middle rack and bake for 1 hour
demonstrations.review: I had just decided to be more strict with giving 5 stars to any given recipe, then I made this.  It's definately "5 stars worthy" in my book!
