I'm so excited to take the extra loaf (that I have hidden) to my friends jewelry party tomorrow night.  I DID take it out of the oven 15 minutes early.  We just moved into a new home with a brand new KitchenAid double oven in June, so I'm assuming it is because my oven is still breaking in.  (Many things are baking faster than usual.)  Other than that, I followed the recipe as given.  Thanks for a great bread for breakfast, tea, snack or dessert!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cheesy salsa rice

this is a quick and delicious side dish that i make all the time to serve with mexican food. i know it's not authentic, but my family loves it!

1. cook rice according to your preference
2. when rice is done , quickly add salsa , cheese , and salt and pepper to taste
3. mix well
4. additional cheese may be sprinkled on top
5. serve
demonstrations.review: I had to throw a large family meal together fast and decided to make this rice with my crockpot carnitas.  I had precooked brown rice on hand and heated that up with the salsa and cheese.  I added a little cilantro and it was great!  Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crock pot whole chicken

tender, fall-off-the-bone chicken! skip the overnight refrigeration if you are in a hurry. for variety, eliminate the onion and substitute a quartered lemon or two, stuffed into the chicken cavity.  chef shapeweaver had a good suggestion:  use fajita seasoning mix #28011 as another variation.  thanks!  the standard size slow cookers are a bit too small and a whole chicken won't fit.  you'll need a 6-quart slow cooker for this recipe.

1. in a small bowl , combine the spices
2. remove any giblets from chicken and clean chicken
3. rub spice mixture onto the chicken
4. place in resealable plastic bag and refrigerate overnight
5. when ready to cook , put chopped onion in bottom of crock pot
6. add chicken
7. no liquid is needed , the chicken will make its own juices
8. cook on low 4-8 hours
demonstrations.review: I have a few recipes that I make on a regular basis that I buy a rotisserie chicken for.  Not anymore...this was simple, cheaper and has much more flavor.  Thanks!

target.recipe_text:
crisp cucumber freezer pickles

this is a sweet cucumber pickle. these pickles stay crisp for up to a year in the freezer. they are so easy to make and very good.  i have just defrosted a bag (pictured here) after 8 months in the freezer and they are still as crisp as the day i  made them.

1. combine all the ingredients in a bowl
2. stir well , cover and refrigerate for 3 days
3. stir every day
4. pack into freezer containers and cover with brine
5. freeze thaw before serving
target.review: These are incredible! I'd never heard of frozen pickles until my neighbor told me about them. I couldn't wait for her receipe as I was done canning and wanted to freeze what I had cut up already.  I found this receipe and  WOW.  I only kept them in the mixture, without red peppers, for 24 hours and that was because my husband kept eatting them!! If I didn't freeze them then I wouldn't have had any left to freeze. I can't wait to try them in a couple of weeks. Thank you for sharing this wonderful receipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
zero points veggie soup  weight watcher friendly

the office i work at is doing our version of the biggest looser. in an effort to still serve soup, and everyone being able to enjoy it, i came up with this simple and easy recipe. it must have been good because 5 minutes after putting out the soup i went to get some for myself ...but it was all gone!

1. over medium high heat , in a large pot add the extra virgin olive oil and the onion , celery , garlic , and cabbage
2. fry for 10-15 minutes or until onions and cabbage have a nice brown color , stirring frequently to make sure you get all the little goodies off the bottom of the pot
3. add mushrooms and cook for another 10 minutes
4. season with salt and pepper to your taste
5. add the frozen vegetables , tomatoes , vegetable stock , bay leaves , thyme , oregano , allspice , and salt and pepper
6. cook for 45 minutes
7. remove from heat
8. add the sugar and vinegar
9. this does two things
10. it helps neutralize the gas of the cabbage and also the acid of the tomato
11. enjoy ! on weight watchers this is a zero point soup
demonstrations.review: 1 POINT - according to the WeightWatchers points finder this is 1 point per serving. This is also according to the nutrition facts the poster has listed to the left.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
refried beans  crock pot

very easy to make! makes a great side dish or filling for burritos. enjoy!

1. sort and rinse dried beans
2. place in crockpot and cover with water and soak overnight
3. in the morning , drain and rinse beans
4. return beans to crock pot , and add 6 cups water and the salt
5. cover and cook on low for 10-12 hours or until beans are nice and tender
6. drain cooked beans , reserving cooking liquid
7. mash beans and return to crock
8. in a small skillet , saute onion and garlic in lard or butter until tender and lightly golden
9. add to crock pot
10. stir in chopped green chillies and ground cumin , adding some of the reserved cooking liquid to adjust the consistency as desired
11. cover crock , and cook on high for 15-30 minutes or until heated through nicely , stirring occasionallly
12. adjust salt , if necessary , before serving
13. garnish with cheese or chopped onion , if desired
demonstrations.review: I will NEVER buy canned refried beans again. This was so easy and so good. I had a Mexican Fiesta Dinner with 17 people and everyone loved these.  Only change I made was I used about 1/2 tablespoon of butter instead of lard or oil. I kept my reserved juice and used it throughout the cooking process up until the time we ate. I found the longer the beans cooked, after mixing everything together, the darker the beans became like you get at the restaurant.   With the little liquid that was left I put in the leftover beans and froze them to eat with the leftover tamales at a later time. Don't worry if your onions didn't saute all the way they will finish cooking in the crock pot. Oh, one other thing I did since I was short on time. I cooked the beans on high for about 3-4 hours before turning them to low.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
weight watcher pesto sauce

pesto sauce that is legal on ww! and better than regular pesto!

1. place pine nuts in a small skillet and set pan over medium heat
2. cook until nuts are golden , shaking pan frequently to prevent burning , about 3 minutes
3. transfer nuts to a plate to cool
4. in a blender or food processor , combine nuts , basil , broth , cheese , oil , garlic and salt
5. process until smooth and thick
6. yields about 1 / 4 cup per serving
7. pesto is traditionally a basil and pine nut-based sauce that's crammed with olive oil
8. this version is lightened up by swapping chicken broth for oil
9. the flavor is fresh and wonderful - spoon it over meat , fish , poultry and vegetables , or toss it with cooked pasta
demonstrations.review: 5 POINTS - according to the WeightWatchers points finder this is 5 points per serving. This is also according to the nutrition facts the poster has listed to the left.

target.recipe_text:
bannock

this is an adopted recipe. the original introduction stated "bannock is a native indian fry bread. simple and quick to make. this recipe comes from a magazine article. the woman who taught the author of the article to make bannock said that "rich indians add raisins to their bannock"."

1. mix flour , baking powder , sugar and salt together
2. mix with enough water so that the mixture becomes a dough
3. form into 4-6 large , thick patties
4. fry on lightly oiled frying pan , turning when the bottom is golden
5. good served warm
6. if desired , spread with honey , jam , butter , or peanut butter
7. traditionally bannock would have been made with whatever ingredients were on hand
8. for example , adding blueberries if they're in season
9. this freezes well
10. freeze , already baked , in a labeled ziploc bag with the air squeezed out as much as possible
11. to serve , bring to room temperature by removing from the bag and letting rest on the counter for a few hours
12. speed up the process , by baking or microwaving until the desired temperature is reached
target.review: Delicious, brought back memories of my grandma's kitchen, we ate them with dark Steen's syrup back then....pure comfort food for me. This is also a go to breakfast for me, when I haven't been to the grocery store in a while and the kids need something filling. I made them with raisins added in, served with a lil butter and syrup...Yum!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
baked ham and cheese omelet roll

this is an easy way to serve omelets. in our house, it takes me forever to make breakfast on the stove top! baking this is soooo much easier. feel free to add or subtract to suit your tastes (bacon, sausage, onions, peppers, etc.)

1. preheat oven to 450 degrees
2. beat eggs and milk until fluffy
3. add flour , salt and pepper and beat or whisk until smooth
4. pour into a buttered or greased 9 x 13 baking dish or pan
5. bake for 10 - 15 minutes or until eggs are just about set
6. sprinkle with chopped ham or lay slices of ham evenly on top
7. sprinkle with cheese
8. bake for about 5 minutes more or until cheese is melted
9. starting at short side , roll up omelet while still in pan
10. place seam side down on serving dish
11. cut into slices
demonstrations.review: Great recipe, came together very quickly, the presentation was beautiful, the taste was delicious and the kids loved it, even my finicky dauthter. I followed recipe, with just a little extra salt and pepper, I will try different fillings in the future.....my son declared me the best mommychef in the world, and said I should have my own cooking show, lol...plus I got great big hugs from them both.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cherry pie filling bread

this bread is out of this world delicious. wonderful served with with cream cheese.

1. beat together oil , eggs and vanilla
2. sift dry ingredients together and add to egg mixture
3. stir in cherry pie filling and nuts by hand
4. pour into 2 greased and floured loaf pans
5. bake at 350 for 50 minutes to 1 hour
demonstrations.review: Absolutely delicioso! We barely let it cool before we were slicing into it. So moist, so flavorful...cherries and nuts perfect..what else is needed...oh yes, a big ice cold glass of milk. Will make again. I also subbed applesauce for part of the oil, and 1 cup of instant oatmeal for flour, and half the sugar with splenda...and it was still out of this world great!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
should be illegal oven bbq ribs

after not being able to find restaurant ribs that satified my hot sweet appetite, i carefully attempted various combinations of flavors until i found one that i and my family thought was perfect. hope you enjoy them too.

1. place all ingredients together in large roasting pan
2. cut ribs apart for easier serving
3. mix together making sure to coat all ribs with this semi-dry paste
4. spread ribs out evenly on bottom of pan
5. cover lightly with foil
6. bake at 375 degrees for approximately 1 hour
7. turning or stirring occasionally
8. you can use broiler for these ribs , just watch more closely , and adjust cooking time
9. these ribs are also great finished on the grill for a few minutes on each side
demonstrations.review: Finger licking good, easy recipe to follow, had all the ingredients on hand. Sauce was thin, but it still was delicious, will use recipe again.

target.recipe_text:
rich chocolate loaf cake

these taste almost like a brownie,  they rise nice and high with a wonderful texture...this recipe makes two loaves

1. set oven to 350f
2. set oven rack to second-lowest position
3. generously grease two 9 x 5-inch loaf pans or 6 mini loaf pans
4. in a large bowl cream butter , shortening , sugar and vanilla until fluffy
5. add in eggs one at a time beating well after each addition scraping the bowl frequently
6. dissolve the coffee granules in hot water
7. sift together the flour , cocoa , salt and baking powder
8. add alternately with coffee and buttermilk to the creamed mixture , beating until well blended
9. mix in the chocolate chips
10. divide the batter equally between well-greased prepared baking pans
11. bake for 1 hour or 40 minutes
12. cool 10 minutes before removing to a wire rack
target.review: This was pretty damn amazingly awesome. I upped the vanilla to 4 tsp considering i was using imitation and i always do that when i use imitation and upped the instant coffee granules to 4 tbsp. Plus i made my own buttermilk because i forgot to defrost mine that i had in the fridge. It was insane, it burned a bit in one pan but think it was my ovens fault. Other than that, it was perfect.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
funfetti cookies

this recipe is a favorite from the pillsbury bake-off. it is a simple cookie recipe that always pleases my family. it is also much more economical than buying those sprinkle cookies from the grocery store.

1. heat oven to 375
2. in large bowl , combine cake mix , oil and eggs
3. stir by hand until thoroughly moistened
4. stir in decorator sprinkles from the cake mix
5. shape dough into 1-inch balls
6. place 2 inches apart on ungreased cookie sheets
7. flatten to 1 / 4 inch thickness with bottom of glass dipped in flour
8. bake at 375 for 6 to 8 minutes or until edges are light golden brown
9. cool 1 minute
10. remove from cookie sheets
11. spread frosting over slightly warm cookies
12. immediately sprinkle each with decorator sprinkles from frosting
13. store in tightly covered container
demonstrations.review: I just made these tonight and used a homemade cake mix "Homemade Yellow Cake Mix (Subtitute 18.25oz Betty Crocker Box)" from second2none. It worked beautifully. I also made the shortening based frosting from a different recipe and i made a mistake a didn't add enough powdered sugar but the cookie itself is great and the frosting too, just a bit more sweet.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
grandma s soft sugar cookies

not sweet. great with coffee or tea. more like biscuits and not chewy-crunchy!

1. beat together eggs , oil , vanilla and sugar
2. add flour , baking powder and salt and mix well
3. drop by heaping teaspoon approx 3" apart on an ungreased cookie sheet
4. flatten with bottom of glass moistened with water and dipped in sugar
5. bake at 400f for 6-10 minutes or just until lightly golden
demonstrations.review: These were great. They weren't too sweet at all, just right. Although i did contemplate replacing some of the flour with cocoa to make chocolate cookies i didn't. Which i'm glad for because these were great as is. I don't know what everyone that said they had a weird after taste means, mine didn't. These are a keeper.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
moist chocolate cupcakes  super easy  budget

i actually found this recipe in a book entitled "the i don't know how to cook cookbook" and it is very tasty. the cupcakes turn out moist and delicious! they are very easy to make, and contain no eggs or milk. pair with your favorite icing.

however, buttermilk or milk may be substituted for water and melted butter may be substituted for the oil.

1. mix all of the dry ingredients well with a mixer or wooden spoon first then add in all your liquid ingredients
2. it should be brown and smooth , free of lumps
3. bake at 350 f for 15-17 minutes if you are baking cupcakes for a cake i'd say 17-25 minutes
demonstrations.review: These were GREAT! I listened to a previous reviewer and added an egg. I also mixed some instant coffee granules with the water. The egg made it rise beautifully. I wanted to make these for my bestfriend's birthday, and i'm sure she'll love them. These will be part of my chocolate cupcake collection. And i also forgot to add, i added about a 1 tsp vanilla.

target.recipe_text:
soft oven polenta

comfort food! most polenta recipes (at least the ones i've seen) call for stove-top cooking and a lot of stirring. this recipe gives excellent results without all that. this recipe was adapted from one in the l.a. times. give credit to their test-kitchen staff.

1. preheat oven to 350 deg f
2. spray a 2-quart oven-proof casserole with non-stick spray
3. combine broth , salt , cornmeal and butter in the casserole and stir well
4. bake for 40 minutes
5. remove from oven and add shredded cheese
6. stir well
7. return to oven and bake for 5 more minutes
8. remove from oven and set aside to rest for 5 minutes before serving
9. garnish with parsley to serve as a side dish , or use instead of pasta with sauces
target.review: Had never made polenta at home but had it at a restaurant recently and it was delicious so I wanted to try.  This was a great, easy recipe and with the other reviewer tips came out very well.  I used a 32oz low sodium veg broth to save the trouble mixing with water.  (Not hard I know but just as easy to purchase so...). I also only grated in about 1/4-1/2 cup of pecorino Romano and even that was a bit too much.  One of the great things about polenta is its blandness to go with a more flavorful counterpart.  I used hodgeson mills course cornmeal and cooked for 45 min then added the cheese, stirred, and cooked another 5 min as instructed.  Very good and scary easy.  A little less cheese next time and it was e perfect match to "Kelly's crock pot "smoked" beef roast" (for which I subbed worstechire for liquid smoke and halved the salt).  Dinner was almost no effort at all.  Great weeknight meal!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
edgar allen poe pizza

there is a pizza chain called dewey's that makes this. of course, i don't have their fabulous crust recipe here (if i did i'd be out selling pizza). just use the best, lightest, average thickness crust you have (preferably home made). if it turns out even halfway like the pizza at dewey's, i promise your desire to eat other pizza will be "nevermore". and yeah, i am still working on bringing you that crust recipe!

1. prepare dough
2. spread a thin layer of oil on dough , then sprinkle with fontina and mozzarella
3. arrange the toppings with the chevre in little chunks
4. bake in a hot oven on a preheated baking stone if you have it , till browned and bubbly
demonstrations.review: Wow! Stumbled onto this when googling reviews for the Poe pizza.  I'm a huge Deweys devotee too and it sounded good. Now I have confirmation from multiple sources that it is and a recipe that I can make it myself should I ever desire.  Thanks for posting!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
triple chocolate brownies  light

you won't believe these are light!  they are just wonderful!  fast to make... and delicious to eat! a great recipe from rose reisman. these are great baked 1 day in advance and will keep frozen for up to 1 month.

1. preheat oven to 350f spray an 8-inch square metal pan with cooking spray
2. to make brownies: in a bowl , combine sugar , oil , egg , and vanilla until well mixed
3. add cocoa
4. mix well
5. add flour , baking powder , yogurt , and chocolate chips , mixing just until combined and smooth
6. dont overmix
7. pour batter into pan
8. bake in centre of oven for 15 to 20 minutes just until set
9. do not overbake
10. cool
11. to make icing: in a blender or food processor , blend icing ingredients until smooth
12. spread over brownie batch
13. cut into squares
demonstrations.review: Forgot to mention I didn't even do the frosting and they were still delicious!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
gluten free dairy free tuna casserole

so tasty, like it has cheese sauce or dairy. i serve this with a salad on the side. this is a personal recipe i created.

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. grease a shallow baking dish i use 9" x 13"
3. heat 2 tablespoons olive oil in a pan over medium heat , add onion & sliced mushrooms , cook until tender then remove from pan
4. add 2 more tablespoons olive oil to pan and stir in flour whisking until smooth and frothy
5. gradually add broth until it forms a sauce consistency
6. then stir in the mayonnaise , salt and pepper
7. stir until mixture is smooth
8. mix in drained tuna , mushroom , onions & thawed peas if using
9. spread pasta in baking dish and pour sauce to cover
10. tear bread into crumbs and sprinkle on top if using sift paprika over entire pan to give a lovely colour and drizzle the additional olive oil
11. bake in the preheated oven for 30 minutes until slightly browned on top
demonstrations.review: Loved!! I've been making a similar dairy free version for years that was a little lacking in thickness. I hate mayonnaise on sandwiches so I was really reluctant to try this but I knew the kids missed the good stuff and I still could do dairy. Used regular wide egg noodles and whole wheat flour since no gluten issues here. And I didn't bother with onion and mushrooms. Went straight to Evoo with flour and added the rest and it was DELICIOUS!!!! Thanks! I ended up eating 2 bowls and am now stuffed.

target.recipe_text:
ribbon pudding pie

this pie is cool, smooth, and creamy. this pretty pie is a slice of heaven - especially considering it only takes 10 minutes of prep time!

1. in a mixing bowl , beat 1 1 / 3 c
2. milk and vanilla pudding mix on low speed for 2 minutes pour into graham cracker crust in another bowl , beat 1 1 / 3 c
3. milk and butterscotch pudding mix for 2 minutes spoon evenly over the vanilla layer beat chocolate pudding mix and remaining milk for 2 minutes spread evenly over butterscotch layer spread with whipped topping sprinkle with pecans refrigerate for at least 30 minutes
target.review: WOW, how easy!  Very simple dessert, the only downside: tastes simple, too.  I was hoping for a dessert that would be a little more extravagent, but then again, that would have involved more work!  I didn't realize before I made it that it was simply crust with pudding layers - my fault!  For the amount of work you put into it, a great dessert!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pizza snack cups

i make these all the time. they are good for quick suppers or kids birthday parties. my husband loves them.

1. pre heat oven to 375
2. in 12 cup muffin pan , evenly press each biscuit in bottom and up the side of each cup
3. chill until ready to fill
4. in skillet brown beef , drain and add pizza sauce
5. evenly spoon mixture into each one of the cups
6. bake for 15 minutes
7. sprinkle with cheese and bake an additional 5 minutes until cheese is melted and biscuits are golden
8. let stand for 5 minutes before serving
demonstrations.review: One of my all-time favorite recipes!  My mom used to make these when I was a kid and there would never be any left over.  I've started making them in huge batches because they are just as good the next day.  We've made them with pepperoni before, or with pepperoni and hamburger mixed.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crock pot apple berry crisp

an easy and versatile dessert recipe for the crock pot.

1. remove crockery pot from heating element and turn on the heat to high to preheat the unit for 15 minutes
2. in large mixing bowl , combine all ingredients except pie crust and stir until well mixed
3. roll pie crust into a circle slightly larger than crockery pot and place crust into bottom of the pot
4. the crust should come up the sides of the pot about 1 inch and can be folded down to make a thicker crust"lip" if desired
5. spread apples and berries evenly over crust
6. in small bowl , blend topping ingredients then sprinkle the mixture evenly over the fruit
7. place crockery pot into the preheated base
8. cover with the lid and cook on high for 1- 1 / 2 hours or until apples are tender
9. length of time depends on your crock pot , but leave the lid on the unit for at least 1 hour without removing it even once !
10. this is important to keep the moist heat in the crock pot
11. serve warm with ice cream and a dash of cinnamon
12. if you prefer a brown crust , cook the unfilled crust in the crock pot for 15 minutes before adding the fruit filling and topping
demonstrations.review: Very easy!  Everybody enjoyed it - thanks for a healthy, tasty dessert!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
lighthearted fettuccine alfredo

easy and low fat to boot! : ) i don't remember where i got this recipe, but i have written down here with it: per serving: 312 calories, 5g fat, 349 sodium, 64 mg cholesterol, 46 carbs, 19g protein, and 251 mg potassium.

1. in a large pot of boiling water , cook fettuccine until tender but firm
2. drain and return to saucepan
3. meanwhile , in a food processor , process cottage cheese until smooth
4. add parmesan cheese , milk , egg , nutmeg , and pepper
5. blend until smooth
6. pour into saucepan with hot cooked pasta
7. cook over medium heat for 1 minute , stirring constantly
8. sprinkle with parsley or basil
9. serve immediately
demonstrations.review: Very good recipe, I'll definitely be making this one again!  I was surprised at how easy it was to make.  I added a bit of garlic and ginger, which turned out great, and also included chicken and spinach.  Topped with parmesan cheese, it made a great meal!

target.recipe_text:
garlic and sapphires sauted brussels sprouts  try this

adopted from recipe zaar.  i noticed that there was no garlic added to the recipe, so i've updated to include the garlic.  this is very very good.

1. over medium heat , saut the garlic in the butter for about a minute then add the brussels sprouts and saute until wilted , about 7 minutes
2. we like to cook until they get a bit brown which took about 10 minutes
3. add salt and pepper to taste
4. add cream and serve
5. feel free to adjust proportions to suit your taste !
target.review: I had never used a cream sauce with my sprouts before, but this was fantastic! I roasted my garlic and it made it even more creamy. I just sliced mine as well for a nicer texture. Very good with lots of fresh ground black pepper. Will make this often. Made and Reviewed for Please Review My Recipe Tag - Thanks! :)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
best lemon blueberry bundt cake

what a cake!!  delicious!  not too sweet - not too heavy - just perfect for summer!  and the glaze is to die for!!  can't wait to make it again!  i adapted this recipe from a family circle magazine where it was named "the best bundt cake ever"!! and i believe it's true!!

1. heat oven to 350f butter a 12-cup bundt pan
2. in a large bowl , whisk together flour , baking powder , baking soda and salt
3. set aside
4. in another large bowl , beat butter until smooth
5. add sugar and beat for 2 to 3 minutes until fluffy
6. beat in eggs , one at a time , beating well after each addition
7. add lemon juice , lemon zest and vanilla and beat until combined
8. beat in flour in three additions , alternating with buttermilk
9. beat for 2 minutes
10. fold in blueberries
11. spoon into prepared pan
12. bake at 350f for 50 minutes or until a toothpick inserted in center of cake comes out clean
13. cool on a wire rack for 20 minutes
14. run a sharp knife around edges of the pan
15. turn out and cool completely
16. glaze: in a small bowl , mix together confectioners' sugar , lemon juice and corn syrup until smooth
17. drizzle over top of cake and let it roll down the sides
demonstrations.review: Very very good cake! It rounded out our all oven dinner (we are warming our cold house) tonight just perfectly. My DH mixed up all the dry ingredients, and I creamed all the wet. We met in the middle at the mixer. It was fun! :) I use the powdered buttermilk mix, so I just threw the powder in with the flour and the water in while mixing them all together. It worked like a charm. The lemon flavor didn't come through in the cake as much as we had hoped, but it was still delicious. I made 6 mini bundt cakes, and 1 regular sized one. The regular one was an old pan and it really stuck inside the pan. The mini slipped out perfectly. The glaze was a bit strong for us, so I added a little vanilla and a touch of milk to smooth it out. Awesome. I can't wait to try this with raspberries in the summer! made and Reviewed for Zaar Stars tag - Thanks! :)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pop rocks no bake strawberry lime cheesecake

i love anthony bourdain's no reservations. i was watching the northwest episode and the gypsy dining group came up with a fabulous dessert that engulfed all of the senses. seeing as how i am in no way going to do this dessert justice, i just wanted to quote what gypsy described it as:

"the second dessert was a lime cheesecake mousse set over the top of an “aural” crust. strawberry pop rocks were implanted into the graham cracker crust for a surprising aural firework display with every bite. the dish was accompanied by strawberry sorbet over a salad of black pepper and strawberries, a strawberry sauce, and a fresh grating of lime zest."

i have researched the lime mousse techniques and i have just run out of patience on how to keep the rocks from popping before the cake is consumed. so it's basically, no bake, low heat, keep it cool. 

i cannot come close to coming up with the black pepper and strawberries concoction so i am going to make my cop out, easy version. it might not be completely gourmet, but it is still  poppin'. 
**i plan on revisiting this to make a diet friendly version.

1. in a bowl , mix together crushed cookies and graham crackers with melted butter and the 3 tablespoons sugar
2. wait , a little bit for the butter to cool down and then combine the pop rocks gently into the crushed mixture
3. press into a 7 inch spring-form pan
4. place in refrigerator until ready for use
5. in another bowl , beat cream cheese , 1 / 3 cup of sugar and lemon juice
6. whip cream , and fold into cream cheese mixture
7. spread into pan
8. top with sliced strawberries
9. freeze for 1 hour , covered with foil
10. place in refrigerator 30 minutes before serving
11. garnish with lime zest before serving
demonstrations.review: I don't know what I did wrong, but this did not work out for me. The crust was a little weird for us. I think maybe we are too grownup for poprocks, which makes me a little sad. We didn't like the topping much either. I do like the addition of the pecan sandies cookies. I will try this again. Made for Everyday Holiday Tag. Thanks. :)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
lovely lemon bar cookies

while on vacation this summer i enjoyed the book "chocolate chip cookie murder" by joanne fluke.  not only was the plot a fun read but the author interspersed some good recipes throughout the book.  this is one of the recipes.  i want to forward the book to my zaar used media swap partner today and i am posting the recipe here so i can try it later.  the author did not indicate the serving size, prep time, etc. so i am guessing.  i will update after i make the recipe.  prep time does not include cooling time.

1. preheat over to 350 degrees , rack in middle position
2. grease a 9 x 13 pan
3. cut each stick of butter into eight pieces
4. zoop it up with the flour and powdered sugar in a food processor until it looks like coarse cornmeal
5. spread it out in a greased 9 x 13 pan and pat it down with your hands
6. bake at 350 degrees for 15 to 20 minutes or until golden around the edges
7. remove from oven - but don't turn the oven off !
8. mix eggs with white sugar
9. add lemon juice & zest if you want to use it
10. add salt and baking powder and mix
11. add flour and mix thoroughly
12. pour this mixture on top of the pan you just baked
13. stick it back into the oven
14. bake at 350 degrees for another 30-35 minutes
15. remove from oven and sprinkle on additional powdered sugar
16. let cool thoroughly and cut into brownie-sized bars
demonstrations.review: Wow Queenie! I have never made lemon bars from scratch before, and never will I make them from a box again. These are so good! They have a light and delicate taste, but they are not overwhelmingly sweet. The lemon zest was fantastic mixed in, as usually it is only on top which can lead to a bitter taste. It's nice to find a recipe that is perfect as is, without changes. This one is definitely on it's way to becoming a star! Fabulous! :)

target.recipe_text:
my family s favorite sloppy joes  pizza joes

i've tried many recipes, this is the best. i once 'dec-tupled' (10x) this recipe to sell sandwiches at a craft fair at my church. people were waiting in line to buy leftovers. freezes well, goes up to the lake or camping well and is a hit on halloween...it's no-fail. easy to double, triple, etc. i've been making joes this way for over 20 years.
***03-08-09, i just reinvented this recipe tonight when i went to make it for dinner and found i didn't have an 8-oz. can of tomato sauce (shame on me).  the family was upset with me when i subbed an 8-oz. can of pizza sauce and told them to suck it up and call them 'pizza joes' and then served them up with shredded mozzarella cheese on the toasted buns, top and bottom.  they loved it.  i left out the bbq sauce in this preparation and just used a 1/2 cup ketchup.  pizza joes are good to go!

1. in a large skillet , brown ground beef , celery and onion
2. drain the fat , who needs it ?
3. stir in remaining ingredients , simmer covered , 15-20 minutes , stirring occasionally
4. if joes appear too'loose' , leave cover off and let moisture evaporate
5. cook until it's the consistency you like for serving on toasted buns , with french fries and cole slaw
target.review: Really good. Used a local favorite BBQ sauce Uncle Joe's and turkey burger. Tasted great and fit my diet's budget.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
olive garden pollo limone  lemon chicken

this recipe originally came from the olive garden website but i have changed a few of the steps after trial and error in my home chicken. we have a thing for lemony chicken in my house and this is one of the favorites.

1. pound chicken to 1 / 4 inch thickness
2. season chicken with salt and pepper
3. heat 1 teaspoon of the oil over high heat
4. lightly coat chicken with flour shaking off excess
5. cook in skillet until brown and nearly cooked through
6. remove chicken and reserve on the side
7. add 1 / 2 tsp oil to the skillet reducing heat to low
8. saute green onions and garlic until tender
9. deglaze the pan with broth and wine
10. add lemon juice and parsley
11. bring mixture to a boil over high heat
12. add lemon peel and salt and pepper to taste
13. return chicken to skillet and coat with sauce
14. cover skillet for 5 minutes over medium-low heat turning chicken once
15. plate the chicken and top with sauce and parsley for garnish
demonstrations.review: I found this to be OK. It wasn't bad, but I was a little unimpressed. I haven't eaten the original dish at Olive Garden, so maybe that's why I didn't enjoy it more. It's a good idea for a change-of-pace dinner, though.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
bang bang shrimp   copycat from bonefish grill

we had these at bonefish grill. they are a great app. since then, i have been trying many recipes looking for one that tastes close. this is the best that i have found. sometimes i fix these and just serve with a salad for lunch - very delicious!

1. mix mayo and sauces for coating
2. bread shrimp in cornstarch
3. deep fat fry the shrimp until lightly brown
4. drain on paper towel , put shrimp in a bowl and coat with the sauce
5. serve in a lettuce lined bowl , top with chopped scallions
6. -----------------------------------------------------
demonstrations.review: What an awesome recipe. This is one of those copycats that is so close to the real thing you wouldn't know the difference. I've made this 5 or 6 times, and my only advice is to be careful with the mayo/thai chili sauce. If you use too much, it can be too sweet. I usually use slightly under the recommended portions.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
best grilled pork chops

this is a simple recipe i have adapted from company's coming.it is simple to throw together the marinade in the morning before going off to work and coming home to an easy dinner to prepare at night.

1. in deep bowl mix all marinade ingredients
2. marinate at least 2 hours
3. remove from marinade and cook over medium-high heat on greased grill for no more than 15 minutes or until done
4. cooking time for second side is shorter by 1-2 minutes
5. 3 / 4" or thinner , 5-6 minutes maximum per side , thicker than 3 / 4" 6-7 minutes maximum per side
6. do not over_grill , chops will become tough
7. after 2 minutes grilling on a side , rotate chops 45 degrees for even cooking
8. turn over when juices pool on upper surface and meat appears to be cooked half-way through
demonstrations.review: Great recipe. I double the light soy sauce and marinate it overnight. Man oh man it is delicious!

target.recipe_text:
2 step pumpkin cheesecake

nan

1. beat cream cheese , pumpkin , sugar and pumpkin pie spice in large bowl with wire whisk or electric mixer until smooth
2. gently stir in whipped topping
3. spoon into crust
4. refrigerate three hours or until set
5. garnish as desired
6. store leftover cheesecake in refrigerator
target.review: I was slightly disappointed because I was hoping for more of a thick cheesecake, but instead it was fluffier like a mousse. My husband and I both enjoyed it and I would definitely make it again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
4 minute spicy garlic shrimp

recipe is originally from the food network courtesy of rachael ray, but i tweaked it to fit our tastes. very quick & easy shrimp recipe that's done on the stovetop. if your tastes desire spicy & garlic, then this recipe is just for you.

1. heat a large skillet over medium high heat
2. add olive oil , garlic , red pepper flakes , and shrimp
3. season with grill seasoning or salt & pepper
4. cook shrimp 3 minutes or until just pink
5. toss with lemon zest , juice , & chopped parsley
6. remove shrimp to a serving platter , leaving the garlic cloves in the pan
demonstrations.review: VERY easy to make, and QUICK! Already getting requests for it again!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
how i got my family to eat spinach  spinach casserole

if spinach scares you, this is one recipe that contains spinach that you do not have to be afraid of! it is so delicious that even my picky kids like it. my mother-in-law makes this for get-togethers and she passed the recipe on to me. you can also use broccoli instead of the spinach, which she does often, but i have never tried...it is great the way it is! she also eats this hot or cold, but i only like it hot :) enjoy!

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees
2. place spinach in strainer and squeeze all extra liquid from it
3. in a large bowl , combine spinach with the rest of ingredients , except croutons , and combine well
4. pour into a 2 quart casserole dish and top with croutons
5. bake for 35 to 40 minutes , or until bubbling around edges
demonstrations.review: YUMMY! Followed the recipe exactly except I added a little extra cheese.  I happen to LOVE spinach, but I can see how people that didnt like it might like this recipe. Creamy and delicious! I will be making this recipe again, and again, and again!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
the best jiffy cornbread

omg! i can't make a southern meal without this cornbread to go with.

1. mix cornbread as directed on package
2. add in corn and cheese
3. if using milk add at the end and only use enough to make the consistency like thick pancake batter
4. recommend using a 9x13 if you want it done in 20 minutes
5. bake 400 degrees for 20-25 minutes or until golden brown and a toothpick comes out clean
demonstrations.review: I baked this in a 9x13 pan and we added Pepper Jack cheese, which gave it a little kick-and I added a little more than 1 cup:-) This was my first time adding corn to the Jiffy mix, we weren't fans of it, but it was still yummy! Simple and quick!

target.recipe_text:
microwave rice pilaff

foolproof and easy to prepare.
dish can be made ahead and reheated before serving. you can freeze the leftovers; it works!
feel free to add other herbs of your choice; when fresh herbs are around i am very generous and produce all kind of taste senstions.

1. in a 2 qt casserole dish , combine butter , rice , onions , celery and garlic
2. microwave 5 minutes on high
3. add chicken broth , thyme and parsley
4. cover and cook 15 minutes stirring twice during cooking time
5. let stand 10 minutes to finish cooking before serving
6. serves 6
7. use fresh herbs for best results
target.review: This was easy to put together, and the method was absolutely foolproof. Unfortunately, I was expecting more flavor from a pilaf-type dish, and found this a bit plain.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
tex mex pork chops

choppers with a kick.

1. heat oil in frying pan over medium high heat
2. brown chops on one side , about 2 minutes , and then flip them
3. add the salsa , chilies and cumin to skillet and mix well
4. lower heat , cover and simmer 8 minutes
5. remove cover and top each chop with one quarter of the cheese
6. cover and simmer for an additional 2 minutes , until cheese melts
7. serve immediately
demonstrations.review: I, too, enjoyed the addition of cumin. I think I could have used a little more guidance about the *amount* of meat that the sauce was meant to cover. The 1 1/2 c. of salsa was far too much for the chops I had (about 1 lb.) The final result was quite runny, even too much so to serve over rice (not trying to be a smart alek, but I did pour the excess into a bowl and serve with chips). I also might have liked more cheese; perhaps 1/2 c.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cinnamon muffins

muffins are good anytime of the day.

1. mix flour , sugar , baking powder , salt , nutmeg and allspice
2. add egg , milk and butter
3. stir into dry ingredients until moistened
4. spoon into greased or paper-lined muffin cups
5. bake at 400 degrees for 20 minutes or until done
6. for topping combine sugar and cinnamon
7. brush top of warm muffin in butter and dip top of muffin into sugar / cinnamon mixture
demonstrations.review: Didn't rise enough. A little plain.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
louisiana burger

this was created by lafayette, la resident, george graham and was a finalist in the sutter home build a better burger contest. it was called bluesiana burger with zydeco sauce, mardi gras slaw and root beer glaze. however, i've posted all those recipes separately because they're all great on their own. see separately these recipes or for the best burger, brush this patty with root beer glaze, spread the buns with zydaco sauce, and top with mardi gras slaw!

1. prepare a medium-hot fire in a charcoal grill with a cover , or preheat a gas grill to medium-high
2. for the patties , place the ground chuck in a large bowl and refrigerate for 1 hour prior to using
3. add the pepper sauce , green onions , salt , and pepper
4. handling the meat as little as possible to avoid compacting it , mix well
5. quickly shape the beef mixture into 6 round , equally-sized patties
6. cover with plastic wrap and set aside until ready to grill
7. brush the grill rack with oil
8. place the patties on the grill , cover , and cook , turning once , until done to preference , 5 to 7 minutes on each side for medium
9. meanwhile , brush the melted butter on the top and bottom buns
10. position the buns , cut side down , on the outer edges of the grill for the last 2 minutes of grilling to toast lightly
11. when the patties are cooked , remove from the grill and keep warm while resting
demonstrations.review: I am a bit unsure how to rate this. I liked them. In fact, everyone in my family liked them, even the picky ones. My husband even was disappointed at the lack of leftovers. (My daughter ate two the day of, and I ate the leftover one not knowing he would want it.) The reason for my surprise is that they are spicy. Very spicy. I was getting complaints about the heat while people were eating, but they kept eating. So I guess that there was good flavor and not just heat. I should have expected the heat level from the ingredients and I do recommend these burgers if you are into that. I am still not sure if I will make them again, though.

target.recipe_text:
chocolate amaretto pound cake

dusted with confectioner's sugar, this appears to be a simple pound cake...however, in the mouth it is anything but simple!  this cake is moist, dense, and very chocolatey-almondy-buttery..... just down right delicious!!  i have been making this recipe for years and like to serve it with real whipped cream.  this is another creation by boston caterer, ellen helman, from the uncommon gourmet.

1. position an oven rack in the center of the oven
2. preheat the oven to 325f
3. grease a 10-inch bundt pan
4. in the bowl of an electric mixer , cream the butter
5. gradually add the sugar , beating until light and fluffy
6. add the eggs , one at a time , beating well after each addition
7. add the amaretto , beat to blend
8. in a medium bowl , combine the flour , cocoa , salt , and baking powder
9. add the dry ingredients alternately with the buttermilk , mixing until evenly blended
10. pour batter into the prepared pan
11. bake for 1 hour and 15 to 20 minutes , until a tester inserted in the center comes out clean
12. let the cake cool in the pan for 15 minutes
13. remove the cake from the pan to a rack to cool completely
14. dust with confectioner's sugar
15. great with real whipped cream
target.review: This recipe is absolutely amazing. I've been making it since December 2008, and it just occurred to me today that I really needed to write a review so more people will try it! It's rich, delicious, moist, and amazing. I've always followed the recipe exactly, but right now I'm getting ready to make it for my own birthday cake, and I'm going to try it in a cupcake tin for the first time. You will not regret making this cake!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
asparagus and cashew stir fry

the combination of fresh asparagus and crunchy, salty cashews is a winner. as a side vegetable it goes well with simple grilled fish, pork, and poultry. or, i've just sauteed some cubed, boneless chicken breasts to the skillet before adding the asparagus. it's delicious either way.

1. cut off the tough ends of the asparagus , and then slice diagonally into 2-3 pieces
2. heat the oil together in a large skillet or wok over medium high heat
3. add the ginger and stir fry for 1 minute
4. add the asparagus and stir fry until tender but still a tiny bit crisp , 4-5 minutes
5. stir in the cashews and soy sauce
6. serve immediately
demonstrations.review: Yummy!  Thanks for this recipe.  Yesterday asparagus showed up at the Farmer's Market for the first time this year, and this was the first dish I made with it.  I served it with rice, and added veggie chicken chunks, which I cooked in the oils before adding the asparagus.  Also, I used 1 tsp dried ginger since I didn't have fresh- I bet fresh really makes this incredible!  I bet I'll find out sometime soon.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crunchy granola

this granola makes a great, filling snack. good dry or with milk. it is very addictive, but it's good for you, so enjoy!

1. heat oven to 275 degrees f
2. line 2 cookie sheets with parchment paper
3. combine brown sugar and water in a 4 cup microwave proof cup
4. microwave on high 5 minutes until sugar is completely dissolved
5. remove from microwave and stir in vanilla and salt
6. in large mixing bowl , mix oats , nuts , and brown sugar mixture
7. mix thoroughly
8. spread onto cookie sheets and bake 45 minutes-1 hour until golden brown
9. when granola has cooled completely , add fruits if you wish and store in airtight container
demonstrations.review: I've made this recipe so many times I can hardly believe I haven't reviewed it yet!  It's like a state of emergency around our house when we're out.  I will never search for another granola recipe. This is simple and perfect.  The only change I've made is that I add two heaping teaspoons of cinnamon.  Enjoy!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
secretly delicious spinach pie

the tortilla adds a delicious crunchy shell and it smells so good while it is cooking. i actually made up this recipe from items in my kitchen and couldn't believe how wonderful it tasted! it is now a hit in my family and so easy to make. please rate and give feedback.  


update: since i first made this five years ago, we still enjoy this at least once a month. i have found that i can alternate the ingredients to use up items i have in the fridge. i have used mushrooms, sauteed onions, cherry tomatoes and even feta cheese instead of cheddar cheese. and it always comes out fantastic. i have also found that there are times i need to use more or less eggs depending on the ingredients. also, a glass pie pan is so much better than a metal as it toasts the tortilla just right. such an easy recipe with gourmet taste!

1. mix the first six ingredients in a bowl
2. set aside
3. lay the flour tortilla in a glass pie dish , press gently - does not need to lay perfectly flat against dish
4. i don't spray it prior and have never had any issues with it sticking
5. especially when made using a glass pie pan
6. sprinkle only 1 / 2 cup cheese on tortilla
7. sprinkle remaining cheese and the spinach onto tortilla in layers , and press gently
8. i don't chop or tear the spinach but you might opt to do this
9. pour egg mixture evenly over spinach , be careful not to pour any outside of tortilla as this causes it to stick to pan
10. bake in oven at 365 degrees for 35 to 45 minutes
11. insert fork in center and it should come out clean
12. use sharp knife to cut into pie slices and serve hot
13. other options: instead of garlic , you can use 1 / 4 cup onions
14. for added flavor , serve with homemade salsa
demonstrations.review: I made this for dinner tonight, and we really like it! My whole wheat tortilla was only big enough to cover the bottom of the pie plate, but it wasn't a problem.  I just made sure to butter the pie plate well.  Also, I used soy bacon and it turned out great!  We will definitely be making this recipe with some regularity.  My 3-year-old was much more into it when we all started picking it up to eat it like pizza.

target.recipe_text:
scalloped potatoes

i love yukon potatoes, a great side dish, i found this recipe in one of my favorite magazines, traditional and scrumptious, this crusty-topped, layered potato favourite never goes out of style. enjoy. :-)

1. sauce: in saucepan , melt butter over medium heat
2. add flour , salt , pepper and thyme
3. cook , stirring , for 1 minute
4. gradually whisk in milk
5. cook , whisking constantly , for 5 to 8 minutes or until boiling and thickened
6. set aside
7. peel and thinly slice potatoes
8. layer one-third in greased 8-inch square glass baking dish or casserole
9. spread half of the onions over top
10. repeat layers
11. arrange remaining potatoes over top
12. pour sauce over top
13. cover and bake in 350f oven for 1 hour
14. uncover and bake for 30 minutes longer or until lightly browned and potatoes are tender
15. let stand for 5 minutes before serving
target.review: Very good and easy recipe.  I made this for Thanksgiving.  I used red bliss potatoes and they were fine.  I substituted nutmeg for the thyme or marjoram and topped the potatoes with paprika for color.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pasta with shrimp and wine

this is one of the best pasta/seafood dishes i have ever tasted! i know the recipe came from a cookbook, but a friend gave it to me several years ago (xeroxed the page) and the title of the book doesn't appear. sorry i can't give credit!
i've made it with scallops, too, and it's just as good.

1. thaw shrimp , if frozen
2. in a saucepan , cook onion in 2 tblsp
3. butter and olive oil until tender but not brown
4. stir in wine , bouillon granules , basil , salt and pepper
5. bring to a boil , reduce heat and simmer , uncovered , for 12 to 15 minutes or until about 1 / 3 of the liquid is evaporated
6. halve shrimp lengthwise and add to wine mixture
7. cover and simmer about 5 minutes until shrimp is just tender
8. stir in tomatoes and heat through
9. toss pasta with 1 / 4 cup butter , melted
10. add shrimp mixture , cheese and parsley
11. toss until pasta is coated
demonstrations.review: I made this last night and it was fabulous.  I added sliced mushrooms with the onions, I used "Better Than Bouillon" instead of granules and omitted the salt.  I added a few handfuls of baby spinach with the tomatoes and left out the parsley.  It's definitely a keeper. Thanks Wineaux

demonstrations.recipe_text:
low carb shrimp salad with aioli mayonnaise

nan

1. steam or boil shrimp until pink and then plunge into ice water to stop additional cooking
2. for aioli mayo , mix together: sourcream , mayonnaise , garlic , parsley and lemon juice
3. in a medium bowl , toss shrimp and veggies together
4. add enough of the aioli to hold the shrimp salad together
5. add seasoned salt to taste
6. chill and serve
demonstrations.review: I used frozen shrimp.  Extremely easy and very delicious.  I served stuffed in a great, ripe, summer tomato. Wonderful summer dinner.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
shari s baked brie

this recipe came to me from a good friend. i think it comes out best when using crescent rolls. it is amazing!

1. bring mini round of brie to room temperature
2. slather top with preserves
3. wrap the round with puffed pastry sheets or 1 package of crescent rolls
4. cover all seams on top of cheese with decorative dough shapes- cookie cutter stars , leaves , etc
5. brush top with egg yolk
6. bake at 350 degrees about 20-30 minutes , until golden brown
demonstrations.review: Great appetizer. I skimmed off the top rind, used raspberry jam and added sliced toasted almonds. I also used crescent roll dough. Deeelicious. Ritag

target.recipe_text:
cheating scalloped potatoes

i know puritans will scream "you can't do this, it's not right etc. etc." but if you are in a hurry and want delicious scalloped potatoes take this shortcut. if you wish you can put some cheddar cheese on top for the last 15 minutes and add a few extra mushrooms.

1. in a bowl mix the cream of mushroom soup , milk , salt and pepper
2. set aside
3. grease a 13"x9"x2" oven proof dish
4. put 1 / 3 of the potatoes , 1 / 3 of the onions , 1 / 3 melted butter , 1 / 3 flour and a 1 / 3 of the soup mixture in the greased dish
5. repeat with two more layers , ending with the soup mixture
6. bake uncovered at 350 degrees fahrenheit for 1 and 1 / 2 hours or until potatoes are done and golden
target.review: This was a very easy dish to make. Even my kids enjoyed it, and they are fussy eaters.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chicken  shrimp and andouille jambalaya

a cajun classic, meal in one pot! have the hot sauce ready to splash on. serve with some crusty french bread, a nice crisp salad, and some of your favorite wine. :)

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees f
2. in a large pan or dutch oven , brown chicken in hot oil on both sides
3. remove and drain
4. add andouille , onion , celery , bell pepper , thyme , oregano , paprika , salt , and cayenne pepper to the pan , cooking and stirring for about 5 minutes until onions are tender
5. add rice , tomatoes with juice , and broth
6. bring to a boil
7. place rice mixture in a baking dish or oven-proof casserole
8. top with chicken
9. cover and bake at 350 degrees f for 40-45 minutes or until rice and chicken are done and tender
10. stir in shrimp , parsley , and green onions
11. cover and cook 5-8 minutes longer or until shrimp curl and turn bright pink and serve
demonstrations.review: This was the first time trying Jambalaya. It was great!Had friends over to enjoy this and they too were amazed. Awesome !!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
rainforest cafe rasta pasta for two or three

fast, easy and can easily be doubled.  makes two large servings

1. cook pasta according to package directions
2. in a large skillet saute the garlic in olive oil
3. add spinach and broccoli , red pepper and grilled chicken
4. toss to combine
5. stir in alfredo sauce and pesto , simmer for 5 minutes
6. drain pasta and pour into a bowl
7. top with sauce and toss well
8. sprinkle with italian seasoning and parmesan cheese
demonstrations.review: This is a terrific , very easy and quick meal to make. The roasted red pepper really adds color and a nice flavor. I will be making this one again and again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
christina s killer dip

this is my sister's dip. she got the recipe while backpacking in europe a few years ago. she is now forced to make it at every party she has. people smell it cooking and stand drooling by the oven until it comes out! (many have not been able to wait for the cooling part and burned their mouths to get to it first).  you might have to make 2 portions.

**note: please check the sodium content before you choose a ranch dressing mix, because it will affect the flavor! some people have complained it is "too salty". please also make sure you are using only a 1 ounce packet; there are other sizes from various manufacturers. too much mix throws off the balance of flavors. my sister and i always use the hidden valley ranch original and we do not have any problems with it :)

you can also substitute half the sour cream for prepared ranch dressing and skip the dry mix. it will come out a bit wetter.

1. defrost the spinach
2. place it in a colander and press it until as much moisture as possible is removed
3. mix all ingredients , and blend well
4. put it in a shallow baking dish in the oven for 20 minutes at 350f
5. remove from oven
6. while still hot top it with remaining cheese , heat in oven again for 5 minutes
7. remove and cool below lava stage and serve
8. goes well with tortilla chips
demonstrations.review: This is a very good Recipe. Very close to a local restaurants spinach dip. Loads of flavor. Thx

target.recipe_text:
andy s all meat chili

this is the best chili i've ever had.  no beans, lots of flavor, and lots of heat, the way chili should be.

1. remove any casings from sausages , crumble meat into a large , deep , pot
2. cook over medium-high heat , stirring often until lightly browned
3. to pot add ground turkey , beef , and pork
4. mix together and crumble meat until it begins to brown
5. to browned meat add onion , bell pepper , and pablano pepper
6. continue to cook over medium-high heat until onion is soft
7. add all other ingredients
8. bring to a boil , cover , reduce heat and simmer for about an hour
9. don't forget to occasionally stir , so it doesn't burn !
10. uncover and cook over medium-low heat until liquid starts to evaporate , continue to stir so it doesn't burn
11. remove pot from heat and let cool about 15-20 minutes
12. return to burner and heat throughly
13. repeat the last 2 steps as needed until chili is thick
14. serve with crackers
15. leftovers can be easily frozen in a ziplock freezer bag or tupperware
target.review:
Love this -to watch calories I added italian pre-season ground turkey and because I don't have the greatest meat market close to us to get decent sausage
Big fan - questioned the orange but it was awesome.
We both liked it. -thanks

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mag s extra special extra delicious candied pecans

these are fabulous! this is my friend, mary ava's recipe and they are so great. easy and get rave reviews. 

1. preheat oven to 225
2. mix water and egg white--whisk
3. mix with pecans
4. mix together sugar , cinnamon , and salt
5. mix with pecans
6. spread on cookie sheet
7. bake for 45 minutes at 225 stirring occasionally
8. increase temp
9. to 275 and continue baking for 15 minutes
10. cool
11. enjoy
12. taste better after a day or so
demonstrations.review: Excellent w/ Almonds too -I made this recipe the exact same way.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mock mashed potatoes cauliflower

this is a great substitute for the real thing if you are on a low carb diet like atkins. good way to get your veggies too,even if you don't like cauliflower.

1. steam or microwave cauliflower until very soft
2. put cauliflower in blender or food processor with butter and sour cream
3. process or blend until creamy like mashed potatoes
4. add seasonings to taste and serve immediately
5. grated cheese or minced chives make a nice topping
demonstrations.review: Thank you! loved 'em

demonstrations.recipe_text:
the best chicken tortilla soup

i'm in love with this soup!! a very good friend of mine made this for me recently and i fell in love. i'm very picky about my tortilla soup and this by far the best ever. she makes hers in the crock pot and i have to agree, that it's easy and tastes just wonderful!! whatever you do, do not skip the garnishes! they are the icing on the cake! update april 2010:  obviously i've made this so many times i never even look at the recipe anymore!  but i wanted to add some variations that i play around with that are great.  like many reviewers black beans and corn are great additions.  sometimes i add them to the leftovers (if there are any :-) so that is feels like something new the next day!  i have also made it several times with shredded pork which turns it into a pork carnitas type of soup.  if you like it on the spicy and smoke side buy a can of chipotle peppers in adobo sauce and mince up one or two and add it.  and lastly, a little swizzle of half and half or heavy cream just minutes before serving makes it a creamy tortilla soup that is wonderful and it is also a good way to tone down the heat if it got away from you...

1. throw everything except the garnishes in your crock pot and let it cook on high for 5-6 hours
2. dress with garnishes and give it a squeeze of lime and you're good to go !
3. enjoy !
4. if you are not using a crock pot , saute the garlic and onion in 2 tablespoons olive oil before adding the remaining ingredients
5. simmer for at least an hour so that the flavors mix together
demonstrations.review: Easy and spicy -but not too much burn.....delicious. Thank you for sharing, Awesome.

target.recipe_text:
mini muffin quiche

quick, easy, delicious crustless quiches in a fun single serving size! this original recipe was shared with me by a friend, i love how adaptable, frugal, and healthy this recipe is. my kids love having their own quiche "muffins" its a great way to pack in their veggies! have fun adding in your own veggies and playing with the cheeses- i use a mix of colby, cheddar, and mozzarella.

1. preheat oven to 350
2. spray muffin tins with nonstick spray
3. soften diced onion and peppers in 1 tbsp butter
4. add spinach , corn , and broccoli and sautee for 2-3 minutes
5. beat eggs
6. mix cheese and seasonings into eggs
7. stir in vegetable mix
8. pour into prepared tins
9. bake for approximately 30 minutes or until properly set
target.review:
First time making quiche! They are very cute and delicious!
I doubled the spinache and left out the broccoli and corn, did half cheddar and half parmesan cheese.
Thansks for the receipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
honey ginger grilled salmon

super easy, sweet and spicy!

1. in a large self-closing plastic bag , combine first six ingredients
2. mix well
3. place salmon in bag and seal tightly
4. turn bag gently to distribute marinade
5. refrigerate 15 minutes or up to 30 minutes for stronger flavor
6. turn bag occasionally
7. lightly grease grill rack
8. preheat grill to medium heat
9. remove salmon from marinade
10. reserve the marinade
11. grill 12-15 minutes per inch of thickness or until fish flakes easily with a fork
12. brush with reserved marinade up until the last 5 minutes of cooking time
13. discard leftover marinade
demonstrations.review:
MAde this tonight for my boyfriend, served with fresh rice and green beans. He really liked the flavor! I followed the advice of Rick B and baked in the over with the marinade. It turned out very moist and tender. A little too sweet he thought, I may make without the honey next time.
Thanks for sharing!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
linzer torte bars

named after a classic austrian dessert, these bars have a great raspberry filling and are so easy to make. they make a great addition to the cookie jar.

1. preheat oven to 375f
2. mix together flour , sugar , walnuts , cinnamon , and butter in a bowl until crumbly
3. press 2 / 3 of mixture into an ungreased 9x9-inch baking pan
4. spread preserves over crust
5. sprinkle remaining crumb mixture over the top of preserves , patting mixture down lightly
6. bake at 375f for 20-25 minutes or until light golden brown
7. cool completely before cutting into bars
demonstrations.review:
Very very good!
I used sugar free jam and it turned out fabulous.
Will make again.
Perfect for any occasion and so easy make!
Thanks for sharing Sue :)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
stroopwafels

this is a dutch favorite, though i've seen them recently at starbucks (horribly overpriced, of course). if you don't have a "pizzelle" iron, don't despair. there's a super-easy shortcut: just buy waffle cookies at your supermarket (and trader joe's has some really fantastic cookies for sure). that's what i ended up doing, so don't think i am a whiz at pizzelle making! 

i halved this recipe, and was still able to have filling leftover when i made 12 cookies. i think this recipe is for filling full sized (6-8 inch) cookies. so plan on having quite a few cookies if you are using store bought cookies (3-4 inch). i found this recipe through google, and preferred it over the one already posted on recipezaar, so here it is!

1. preheat a pizzelle iron
2. to make waffles: dissolve the yeast in the warm water
3. cut butter into the flour
4. mix in the sugar , cinnamon , eggs and yeast mixture
5. mix well and set aside to rise for 30 to 60 minutes
6. roll dough into 12 small balls
7. squeeze each ball into the preheated pizzelle iron and bake for about 30 seconds
8. cut the waffles into two thin waffles and spread with filling
9. to make filling: in a saucepan boil the brown sugar , the remaining one cup of the butter , cinnamon , and dark corn syrup until it reaches the soft ball stage , stirring constantly
10. to assemble: cut each waffle into 2 thin waffles and spread with filling
11. repeat this process until all the filling is used
12. if using store bought , simply spread about 1 tablespoon of filling on one waffle cookie , let it cool about 1 minute , and squeeze a second cookie on top
13. makes 12 servings
14. best if eaten after they've cooled , less messy that way !
demonstrations.review:
made these last night for a friend whos been craving the real thing all week.
She said they tasted exactly like the real ones!
Couldn't find a pizelle maker, but found the cookies at Trader Joes, great price.

So Yummy and easy.

The caramel didn't turn out just right, may not have cooked it long enough. Next time I am planning on trying to melt caramels instead and add cinnamon to the mix.
Thank you for posting this recipe!

target.recipe_text:
pork roast over sweet potatoes for the crock pot

my husband always requests this recipe. i cook it 11 hours so the meat barely holds together. works for low glycemic index diets.

1. combine first 6 ingredients
2. rub into pork
3. put potatoes in the crock pot
4. place pork on top of potatoes
5. pour broth over all
6. cover and cook on low for 8 to 10 hours
target.review: My husband LOVED this.  I didn't have fennel, so I used rosemary as others have, personally, I didn't like it as much as he did.  Next time I will use the fennel and I will add a bit of brown sugar too...it was a little bland for me, but still very good.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
quick spanish rice

great side dish for your mexican fiesta. try with recipe #17130!  it is as good as you'll find in any mexican restaurant.  update:  1 teaspoon cumin was added to original recipe.  i took some of my reviewers suggestion and added 1 teaspoon of cumin to the recipe. they were right. cumin definitely adds to the taste.

1. in medium saucepan , combine all ingredients
2. bring to a boil
3. reduce heat to low
4. cover and simmer 25 minutes or until rice is done
5. garnish with green onions and / or cheddar cheese
demonstrations.review: This was fantastic!  SO easy to make!  I followed the recipe with the exception of using brown rice (simmered for 60 minutes), petite diced tomatoes and I did add two dashes of cayenne pepper for an added kick.  I didn't top with cheese and it was still great. thanks for sharing!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s  brown sugar caramel sauce or ice cream topping

with only very few ingredients and five minutes to make it just couldn't get any easier and it tastes so good! ---it goes great with bread pudding, over ice cream and with desserts :)

1. in a small saucepan melt butter with salt
2. add the brown sugar
3. whisk until combined and thickened
4. whisk in the whipping cream , until thoroughly blended
5. mix in vanilla until combined
demonstrations.review: HOLY COW is this good!  I was making the Yummy Crunchy Caramel Apple Pie (#31128) last night and I realized I didn't have caramel topping.  Found this recipe.  I had to use Half & Half instead of whipping cream and it was still delicious!  I let it come to a boil, then let it cool so it would thicken - it was PERFECT!  So easy and delicious.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
yummy crunchy apple pie

great pie!

1. use foil on bottom of oven rather than a cookie sheet under pie pan
2. prepare pastry for single-crust pie
3. place in pie plate and trim and crimp the edge
4. refrigerate 30 minute loosely covered with plastic wrap
5. in a large mixing bowl , stir together the sugar , flour , cinnamon , nutmeg , allspice , and salt
6. add apple slices and gently toss until they are coated well
7. transfer mixture to pie
8. for crumb topping: stir together brown sugar , flour , and oats
9. using a pastry blender , cut in the butter until topping resembles coarse crumbs
10. sprinkle over apple mixture in pie
11. to prevent over-browning while baking , cover edge of pie with foil
12. bake at 375 degrees fahrenheit for 25 minutes
13. remove foil and bake 25 to 30 minutes more , or until top is golden
14. remove from oven
15. cool on wire rack about an hour and serve !
demonstrations.review: This was my first apple pie - and WOW was it awesome!  I didn't have caramel topping so I found another recipe (#78088) and made that (with Half & Half, not whipping cream) and it was PERFECT for this pie.  Everyone said they were too full to eat and the pie was almost gone 5 minutes later!  Thank you!

target.recipe_text:
kittencal s pizza sauce

this is a full-flavored rich pizza sauce that i have been making for over 20 years, the longer you simmer this sauce the thicker and richer it will be ---  this sauce freezes very well and even tastes better if made a day ahead and left in the fridge overnight to blend flavors --- also see my recipe#232188

1. in a saucepan , heat the olive oil
2. saute the onions , italian seasoning and oregano for about 2-3 minutes , stirring until soft but not brown
3. add in garlic and saute for 2 minutes , stirring constantly
4. add in the tomato paste
5. stir and cook 1 minute
6. add in the remaining ingredients
7. cook and simmer on low heat for 1 / 2 to 3 / 4 hours , stirring occasionally , adding more salt if needed
8. cool slightly and use immediately or refrigerate up to 5 days or you may freeze
9. delicious !
target.review: Wow! I am super hard to please when it comes to any tomato based sauce and even pickier when it comes to pizza sauce. This was awesome! I could not stop sneaking a taste as it was simmering on the stove. My search for the perfect pizza sauce is over and I can't wait to try it as a dip for bread sticks and garlic fingers!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
brioche loaf   breadmaker 1 1 2 lb  loaf

this recipe is from fleischmann's yeast company. i love egg breads, especially for french toast and bread pudding.

1. measure all ingredients into bread machine pan in the order suggested by manufacturer
2. process on sweet or basic / white bread cycle
3. use light or medium / normal crust color setting
4. remove bread from pan
5. cool on wire rack
demonstrations.review: YUM! I am not a bread person, but this was awesome! Great for sandwiches or just a plain 'ol buttered slice!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cherry pound cake

this is one of my annual christmas recipes...it keeps very well if wrapped properly and absolutely delicious to set out with your other holiday goodies.

1. beat butter , sugar , eggs and extract in large bowl on low speed of electronic mixer until blended , then on high speed 5 minutes until light and fluffy
2. combine flour , baking powder and salt
3. add dry ingredients alternately with evaporated milk to creamed mixture , mixing lightly after each addition
4. fold in cherries
5. turn batter into greased and floured bundt or tube pan
6. bake at 350 for 55 minutes
7. cover loosely with foil , shiny side out
8. continue baking 15-20 minutes , until toothpick inserted in center comes out clean
9. let cool in pan for 5 minutes
10. invert cake onto rack and let cool completely
11. sprinkle with icing sugar to finish
demonstrations.review: Made this cake this morning and it is so good! This recipe will definitely be a part of my Christmas line up. I made it in two loaf pans and they came out beautifully! I think next time I will replace the cherries with gumdrops and see how that goes. Thanks Lorrie!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s chocolate frosting icing

a wonderful frosting i have used for years made in very little time with perfect results and 100% better than any canned, this frosting is so good you will find yourself eating a fair amount of it before even using it to frost with! --- choose the amount of cocoa powder you desire for either a light, medium or dark frosting, and make certain to sift the cocoa powder and the confectioners sugar before using for the recipe--- this frosting *freezes* very well so double the recipe and freeze one batch for next time --- *note* for an ultra creamy fluffy milk chocolate frosting add in 1 to 1-1/2 cups thawed cool whip topping at the end of mixing the frosting and beat on low speed until blended ------- also see my recipe#80118 ---- recipe#282040 --- recipe#90142

1. cream the butter in a small bowl
2. blend in the cocoa powder , vanilla , confectioners sugar , alternately with the cream
3. beat with an electric mixer , until the desired texture is achieved
demonstrations.review: OMG HEAVEN! This was sooo good. It took all the will power I had to pipe the icing on to the cake and not directly in to my mouth. I made the medium recipe and used whipping cream. Will definitely make again and again. Thanks Kittencal I can always count on you for an awesome recipe!

target.recipe_text:
the best apple pie muffins ever

i got this  recipe from a friend.  i make these often and take them to many potlucks, office parties, the cottage, picnics, children's lunch and the list goes on. recipe from the cookbook "just the best."

1. cinnamon could be added to the batter
2. topping: in a small bowl toss together sugar , flour , butter and cinnamon until crumbly
3. set aside
4. muffins: in a large bowl whisk together brown sugar , oil , egg and vanilla until smooth
5. in a separate bowl , sift together flour , soda and salt
6. stir oil mixture into flour mixture alternately with buttermilk
7. fold in apples , mixing just until combined
8. spoon into greased muffin cups filling 3 / 4 full
9. sprinkle topping over evenly
10. bake at 350f for 25-30 minutes or until golden brown and tops spring back
target.review: I agree very moist and not too sweet.  Suggestions - I would cut back on the vegetable oil (muffins had a oil after taste) and add a little cinnamon and nutmeg to the apple mix.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
asian vinaigrette salad dressing

this is simple to throw together, light and tangy. i often vary the ingredients, using honey or orange juice instead of sugar, adding wasabi powder -- whatever i'm in the mood for.

the joy of cooking is being creative! 

if you wish to substitute the oil, use a bland vegetable oil, extra virgin olive oil or "light" olive oil. regular olive oil is too strong for this recipe.

1. mix first 5 ingredients in a bowl or food processor
2. if using a bowl: slowly drizzle in the sesame and peanut oil , whisking constantly so that the dressing will emulsify
3. if using a food processor , leave it running while you drizzle in the oil
4. when dressing is well combined , add sesame seeds and scallions
5. serve immediately or refrigerate and use within a week
demonstrations.review: Very good recipe, its light, sweet and tangy.  I used peanut oil and omitted the sesame seeds and scallions. Next time, like most fellow reviewers, I'll use honey instead of sugar and cut back on the oil (1/2 cup is a tad too much). Added to a mixed greens salad, with white onions, grape tomatoes and avocado (so yummy with the ginger/garlic twist) and served with Vietnamese Chicken Curry with Sweet Potatoes over basmati rice.  Thank you for sharing this great recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
buttermilk pancakes

this is our favorite pancake recipe. i got it from williams-sonoma site. try it.. it's great.

1. in a bowl , using an electric mixer , beat the eggs on medium speed until frothy
2. add the buttermilk , melted butter and vanilla and mix well
3. add the flour , sugar , baking powder , baking soda and salt , and beat on medium speed just until blended
4. you can also mix this together using a wooden spoon or whatever you have
5. heat lightly greased griddle at 350 degrees
6. pour about 1 / 3 cup of the batter onto griddle for each pancake
7. cook until the tops of the pancakes are covered with tiny bubbles and the batter is set , about 4-6 minutes
8. flip pancakes and cook until the undersides are golden brown , about 4 minutes more
9. repeat with remaining batter
demonstrations.review: Great pancakes - variations include 1 cup fresh blueberries for blueberry pancakes or 1 cup chocolate chips for chocolate chip pancakes.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
roasted garlic mashed potatoes   the best you ve ever had

nan

1. separate head of garlic into individual cloves
2. toss in olive oil and wrap tightly in small piece of aluminum foil
3. bake in 350f oven for 45 minutes
4. when the garlic has cooled to the touch you should be able to squeeze it out of the 'paper' shell of the individual cloves
5. mash the roasted garlic with a fork , or force through a fine strainer
6. if you use a ricer as recommended below , simply rice the garlic along with the potatoes
7. peel and boil potatoes in salted water until tender
8. force the cooked potatoes through a ricer or mash by your usual method
9. put the riced potatoes , garlic , sour cream , butter , and salt and white pepper in a mixer bowl , and whip at medium speed until smooth
10. add cream or milk to adjust consistency
demonstrations.review: Very good.

target.recipe_text:
hidden valley quiche

hearty egg quiche that is equally good for supper, brunch or breakfast.

1. preheat oven to 400
2. sprinkle bacon and cheese into the pie shell
3. beat eggs until frothy
4. add cream and dressing mix , mixing well
5. pour into pie shell covering the cheese
6. bake 20 minutes at 400
7. reduce heat to 350 and bake 15-20 minutes until center in set
8. cool 10 minutes before cutting
target.review: I've been using this recipe for years. I vary the filling by using a one pound bag of frozen mixed vegetables -- like the oriental mix or the winter mix -- rinsed, with two cups of the shredded cheese of the day, with or without some kind of meat, maybe some green chili or chopped olive ... you get the idea. Baked in a deep dish quiche pan. It always gets rave reviews because of the Hidden Valley Ranch Mix.
