demonstrations.recipe_text:
maria cruz champurrado

it's been in our family since i can recall.  we usually make it during the christmas or winter days.  it's also a "feel good" drink, when there's symptoms of a cold and so forth.  usually a cup of "champurrado" is served with some sugar "churros" or some mexican bread on the side.  deliciossso!!!

1. dissolve in two cups of water the corn "masa" and drain
2. boil the 6 cups of water in large pot and add the strained "masa" , the shredded chocolate , stick of cinnamon and the shredded "piloncillo"
3. simmer
4. it's important not to stop stirring until well blended and dissolve or it will burn
5. add more shredded chocolate and shredded "piloncillo" to taste
demonstrations.review: This is just what I was looking for! It came out creamy and chocolaty with the right hint of cinnamon. My hispanic friends make it all the time, but I can never get the recipe out of them. I've tried a few others here on the zaar, but this one has the taste I've been seeking!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
emeril lagasse s pumpkin cheesecake

emeril suggest that if you buy and extra pumpkin and puree it you will have the most fantastic cheesecake for the holidays. sounds amazing!

1. preheat the oven to 350 degrees f
2. combine the graham cracker crumbs , pecans , brown sugar , and 1 / 2 teaspoon of the cinnamon in a bowl
3. pour in the melted butter and stir well to blend
4. press the mixture evenly into the bottom and 1 inch up the sides of a 9-inch springform pan
5. combine the cream cheese , sugar , cornstarch , vanilla , the remaining 1 / 2 teaspoon of cinnamon , and the nutmeg in the bowl of an electric mixer
6. beat until fluffy
7. add the eggs and yolks , beating on low speed until just blended
8. fold in the cream and pumpkin pure
9. pour the batter into the crust-lined pan , and place on a baking sheet
10. bake until the center is nearly set , about 1 hour to 1 hour and 10 minutes
11. remove from the oven and cool for 15 minutes
12. carefully run a small , sharp knife between the cake and the sides of the pan
13. release the sides of the pan and cool at room temperature for 30 minutes
14. cover the cheesecake tightly with aluminum foil or plastic wrap , and chill in the refrigerator at least 4 hours , or up to 8 hours , before serving
demonstrations.review: Made this for Thanksgiving - giving. Divided the recipe into two pumpkin-shaped foil pans -- the kind they sell for Jack-o-lantern cakes -- and had enough filling left over for a third. First time I've had an argument over who gets the baked goods!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
layered mexicasserole

my kids love this casserole.  it's quite simple to make, yet tasty.

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. brown beef in large skillet with onion and green pepper
3. drain
4. return to skillet and add corn and salsa and cumin and chili powder
5. mix well
6. cook until heated through , stirring occasionally
7. set aside
8. mix cottage cheese and sour cream
9. layer 5 cups of the chips , 1 / 2 of the meat mixture , 1 / 2 of the cottage cheese mixture , and 1 1 / 2 cups cheddar cheese in a 13" x 9" casserole dish
10. repeat layers of chips , meat mixture and cottage cheese mixture and finally remaining cheddar cheese
11. cover lightly and bake 35-40 minutes
demonstrations.review: I brown my beef (or substitute ground turkey) and onions in the microwave in a pan with a colander. I can use the cheapest ground beef and easily get out all the fat, since I'm using spices anyways I don't need to fry the fat in for flavor. It's fast -- 6 minutes per pound in the average micro. and you can through all the disgusting guck away instead of eating it. I'm allergic to bell peppers, so I leave them out, but no one notices. I like Safeway's Southwest Salsa the best with this recipe, it has a lot of chunky vegetables in it. Great recipe! You can make the whole thing in the micro, but you use a little of the crunch of the chips. To figure out how long to cook it, weigh the pan  before you put in the ingredients, then weigh it again when it's full, and cook it 6 minutes per pound of ingredients. Of course you have to be using a microwave safe pan.

target.recipe_text:
ila s pecan pie squares

why go to all the hassle of making and cutting a pecan pie when you can easily have these, as ila called them bombdiggity squares?

1. mix all crust ingredients until dry and crumbly
2. press crust firmly into the bottom of a greased 15 1 / 2 x 10 1 / 2 - 1 pan
3. bake until golden brown for 20 minutes at 350 degrees
4. mix together filling ingredients except pecans
5. when mixed thoroughly add pecans and pour over baked crust
6. bake until filling is set approx 25 minutes - at 350 degrees
target.review: These were fantastic! A word of warning though, grease the pan VERY well - I apparently did not and it was quite a challenge to get the bars out...very much worth the effort though! Thanks for a great recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
yummy crispy baked fish

easy and healthier way to get crispy tasty fish. note: you must use the right pan! please be sure to use a broiler pan so the breading gets hot air on the bottom too and isn't soggy on the bottom when you go to turn it. or use a cooling rack on a cookie sheet. do not use a pan with sides as that will steam the fish, not make it crispy. i have never had the breading fall off using the correct methods. if you don't care for cornmeal use panko. 

i have used mostly mild whitefish like catfish or tilapia with great results. don't be scared by the number of ingredients—it is mostly spices and herbs. please adjust the spices, especially salt, to your taste. i have tried to post a balanced blend here but feel free to adjust mild, spicy, lower sodium etc...

1. mix milk , vinegar and mustard and let set for 15 minutes
2. this will make a mustardy , buttermilky dressing to coat the fish
3. in a separate bowl mix cornmeal or panko with all the seasonings
4. dip fish fillets in the milk mixture and then in the dry mixture
5. spray broiling pan with cooking spray or brush with a little olive oil
6. place fillets on prepared pan and place pan under broiler 4 inches from heat
7. broil for 4 minutes per side or until fish flakes easily with a fork
8. serve with lemon wedges if desired
demonstrations.review: This fish was so easy to make and unbelievably moist and flavorful. We could still taste the fish through all of the spices which suprised me - and my family said that this was the "greatest fish ever". Thanks for sharing

demonstrations.recipe_text:
artichoke crab spread  for the crock pot

this is a great tasting dip that can be put together quickly.  it has a thick spread consistency, but can easily be thinned with milk for dip with chips based on personal preference.

1. spray inside of 1-3 quart slow cooker with cooking spray
2. place all ingredients except crackers in cooker
3. cover and cook on low setting for 1 to 1 1 / 4 hours or on high setting for 30 to 45 minutes or until cream cheese is melted
4. stir until cheese is smooth
5. scrape down side of cooker with rubber spatula to help prevent edge of spread from burning
6. turn to low heat setting and hold for up to 3 hours
7. serve with crackers
demonstrations.review: WOW! WOW! WOW! This dip was great! I didn't have enough time to make this in the crock pot so I put it in the microwave for a couple of minutes, stirring after each minute and it turned out great.I did use 2 pkgs of Starkist's (?) real crabmeat instead of immitaion and added a little salt and crushed red pepper for some umph. Definitly a keeper and will be appearing on my holiday table- thank you for sharing!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cold wild rice   orzo salad

had a similar salad at a restaurant, and reconstructed from memory. you may need or want more salad dressing and don't be afraid to add extra almonds for more crunch! you can play around with the ingredient quantities as well.

1. i cook both the instant wild and white rice together in a rice cooker along with the chicken bouillion cube til done
2. let cool or chill in the fridge
3. cook orzo according to package directions and drain with cold water
4. once rice and orzo are both somewhat cool , mix together and add the chopped peppers , onion , chopped cilantro , almonds , & salt
5. in a separate small container , mix the oil , red wine vinegar , lemon juice and spices
6. i've been making this salad dressing so long , i'm estimating the amounts , so adjust to taste
7. pour over rice salad , mix thoroughly , add more salt if needed and splash with balsamic vinegar to taste
8. salad is best if chilled for at least an hour or two before serving to blend flavors
demonstrations.review: I took this to a potluck dinner and I dont think I have ever been asked for recipe more than I was for this one. I did make a few convienence changes - I used a box of long grain/wild rice blend and I accidently added the seasoning packet before I realized what I had done, so I left out the boullion cube. Also, instead of making my own vinagrette I used Archer Farms balsamic vinegrette. This was such a hit that I took it to Easter dinner at my mother's house and I had the same response - this is a fantastic recipe and I am so glad that you shared it.  I did try this salad warm as well, and it was JUST as good!

target.recipe_text:
warm and cozy bottom round roast crock pot style

the aroma of this roast made dh and ds drool.  i had a beautiful roast from the market and wanted to try simple spices yet aromatic!  this is what the doctor ordered for a very chilly january day. dh and ds loved it!

1. mix all dry ingredients together in a plate
2. rub roast in oil
3. roll roast in dry mix
4. place onions on bottom of crock pot
5. place roast in crock pot
6. cook on low for 6-8 hours
7. throw in remaining rosemary 1 / 2-1 hr before dinner to send the aroma once again through the house
8. with juice from roast i made a gravy to pour over top of sliced beef just before serving
9. i served with roasted potatoes , broccoli , and fresh made italian bread
10. leftovers were shredded for beef sandwiches the following day mixed with the gravy
11. i use fresh herbs when possible so measurements are approximate for herbs
12. adjust seasonings to taste
13. i do not use salt and at times am heavy on herbs
target.review: Very good. Used for a for sandwiches with the dripings as au jus dip. Yummy!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
herb wine  dump  chicken   oamc

another oamc dump recipe!

1. for immediate cooking: pre-heat oven to 350f place all ingredients into a large baking dish , turn chicken to coat
2. bake until chicken juices run clear
3. for freezing: place all ingredients into a 1 gallon freezer bag
4. lay flat in freezer
5. to thaw and cook: take the bag out of the freezer the night before , make sure the bag is sealed completely
6. for the oven: preheat the oven to 350f empty the contents of the bag into a large baking dish and bake until the juices run clear
7. for the crockpot: cook on low for 6-8 hours or on high for 4-6 or until done
8. on the grill: cook over medium heat until juices run clear
demonstrations.review: Yum, I used white wine 'cause that's what I had.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
butter pecan pie squares

for fall holidays.

1. combine 1 1 / 4 cups flour and 1 / 3 cup sugar in a medium bowl
2. cut in 1 / 2 cup butter with a pastry blender until mixture resembles coarse meal
3. press mixture evenly into a greased 9-inch square pan
4. bake at 375 degrees for 15 minutes
5. combine next 7 ingredients , and beat well
6. stir in pecans
7. pour filling over prepared crust
8. bake at 350 degrees for 25 minutes or until firm
9. let cool on a rack
10. cut into squares
demonstrations.review: Yum, next time I might add rasins.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
raw brownies

i found this recipe online and really wanted to try it. it comes from a website called 28 cooks. you may substitute the dates and cherries for other dried fruits. the cooking time is freezing time.

1. process all ingredients in a food processor or blender
2. press into a small square baking pan and freeze for 1 hour
3. slice brownies into 12 pieces
4. store in fridge
demonstrations.review: Yum! So easy and so good.

target.recipe_text:
sauteed mushrooms with sesame and ginger

adapted from cook's illustrated magazine, these have all the flavors i love!

1. heat 1 tbls
2. of the peanut oil in a 12" skillet over medium high heat until they shimmer
3. add the mushrooms and cook , stirring occasionally , until the mushrooms release their liquid , about 5 minutes
4. increase the heat to high and cook , stirring occasionally , until the liquid has evaporated , about 8 minutes longer
5. add the remaining peanut oil , reduce the heat to medium and continue to cook , stirring once every minute , until the mushrooms are dark brown , about 8 more minutes
6. add the sesame seeds and ginger and cook , stirring constantly , until the ginger is fragrant , about 30 seconds
7. add the rice vinegar , sugar and soy sauce and cook , stirring constantly , until the liquid has evaporated , about 30 seconds
8. remove from the heat and stir in the sesame oil
9. move to a serving dish , sprinkle with the scallions , and serve
10. enjoy !
target.review: so easy to whip up! will make again, Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
simple stir fried udon

made this up today for lunch - feel free to use any vegetables and/or leftover meat you have.

1. partially cook broccoli and udon in salted boiling water for a few minutes
2. drain and reserve 1 / 4 cup of the water
3. beat the egg with 2 tb water and a pinch of salt
4. heat 1 tb of oil in a wok
5. when hot , pour the egg in and cook until set
6. remove and set aside
7. heat remaining 1 tb oil in the same wok over high heat
8. when hot , saute the onions until soft
9. add garlic and saute for 30 sec
10. add ham slivers and saute for another 30 sec
11. stir in udon noodles
12. add hoisin , oyster , soy sauces , white pepper , wine , chilli flakes
13. saute for 1 minute
14. adjust heat to medium-low , add broccoli and reserved cooking water , cook for another minute
15. taste and adjust seasonings if necessary
16. add the cooked egg to the noodles , breaking it into pieces as you stir
17. stir in sesame oil
18. sprinkle with the reserved chopped spring onion and squeeze some fresh lime juice over noodles , then serve immediately
demonstrations.review: i used 200g of udon but still found it a bit salty. great dish but will reduce the amount of oyster/dark soy sauce next time. Thanks.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
vietnamese clay pot pork

one of our everyday dish. if you don't have a clay pot, use a normal saucepan, big enough to hold about 1 1/2 lbs. pork and some sauce. i prefer pork tender loin with a bit of fat, but many people like pork shoulder or pork chops. if you use pork chops, change to about 1 3/4 - 2 lbs.

1. put oil in pot or pan over medium heat , add sugar and cook , stirring frequently till it dissolves
2. add ginger , garlic , shallots , chili , cook for about 4-5 minutes turn up the heat to high , add pork , stir till the meat has browned a little , then add water
3. when it comes to a boil , lower heat to simmer
4. cut hard boil eggs in half and put into pot
5. this step is optional , but the eggs will absorb all the sauce and taste heavenly !
6. cover the pot and let it simmer
7. i find the longer you leave it , the better it taste
8. but after 30-35 minutes it's done
9. serve with cooked white rice or basmati , and that's a meal there
10. normally we just steam cabbage or water spinach for vegetables
demonstrations.review:
great recipe. Add water after step 2. 

u can cut the eggs at the very last step to prevent the egg yolk from crumbling apart and getting messy. 
i sometimes add the full size eggs in step 2 and let it brown a bit for more flavour.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
singapore chilli prawns  shrimp

i found this and thought it sounded really good. i haven't tried it (intend to soon) but wanted to share it anyway. from a supermarket give away.

1. heat oil and stir fry prawns until they change colour
2. remove to a plate
3. add garlic , ginger , black bean paste and chilli , stir fry for 1-2 minutes
4. return prawns to wok with ketchup , vinegar and sugar , stir fry until hot
5. sprinkle with chives and serve with rice
demonstrations.review: didnt have black bean paste so i used the black bean sauce.. still tastes great!

target.recipe_text:
marinade for beef

this marinade gives an 

1. combine all ingredients in a glass deep or large zip-lock bag and mix well
2. add beef and marinate for several hours
3. grill steaks , basting with marinade to desired doneness or place roast along with marinade in a baking dish and bake@ 350 degrees for 40-50 minutes for rare
4. if whole tenderloin cook 45-60 minutes@ 425 degrees for rare
5. i bake the tenderloin@ 350 degrees for about 2 hours for medium well
6. let sit about 10 minutes before slicing
target.review: With the economy being what it is I have been having to buy cuts of meat that turn out tougher than shoe leather so I decided I would try a marinade that consisted of things I already had in my home. I had 4 good size chuck steaks and marinaded them for 12 hours....my husband would not stop moaning. I think this is the marinade that will be used from here on out. Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
wicked pumpkin whoopie pies

these are fantastic. the pumpkin version.  this recipe is from a small business owner in maine. she sells many variations on her website at www.wickedwhoopies.com. this recipe was published on a local television website when she appeared on it and made them.

1. preheat oven to 350
2. beat pumpkin , eggs , oil and brown sugar together until fluffy
3. combine dry ingredients together
4. then add molasses and dry ingredients to your mix until well blended
5. scoop large rounded spoonfuls of batter onto a greased cookie sheet and space at least 2-inches apart
6. bake for 10-13 minutes or until done
7. filling: add all ingredients in a bowl and beat until fluffy
8. when whoopie shells are cooled , place a scoop of filling between two shells
9. wicked good !
demonstrations.review: Well my hubby is a "Mainah" and I just love everything Maine so this includes the whoopie pie. It was hard not to eat the shells by themselves. They were OH SO GOOD!!! I would say the only 'problem' I had with the recipe is the filling was a little too sweet and not as stiff as I remember it but that didnt stop anyone from eating them. There will be a next time when I make these but I will adjust the filling to my liking. Totally recommend it!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
sour cream and apple coffee cake

this is a scrumptious coffee cake that is sure to please everyone - even those not having coffee.

1. for topping: blend walnuts , brown sugar , flour , cinnamon in processor until nuts are finely chopped
2. add butter and cut in using on / off turns until clumps begin to form
3. cover and chill
4. for filling: mix apples , sugar , cinnamon , and lemon juice in a bowl
5. for cake: preheat oven to 350f
6. butter 13 x 9 x 2 inch glass baking dish
7. in a small bowl , whisk sour cream and buttermilk to blend
8. in a medium bowl , sift flour , baking powder , baking soda , and salt
9. in a large bowl , beat butter and both sugars until creamy
10. add eggs , one at a time , beating well after each addition
11. mix in lemon juice and vanilla extract
12. beat in dry ingredients alternately with sour cream mixture in 3 additions each , mixing just until smooth
13. spread half of batter in prepared pan
14. spoon apple filling on top of batter
15. spread remaining batter over filling
16. sprinkle with topping
17. bake cake until tester inserted into center comes out clean , about 45 minutes
18. if the top starts browning too quickly , cover with foil
demonstrations.review: Great cake! My hubby liked it and he is not a sweets kind a  guy. A friend of ours had made this for a church potluck and when I asked her for the recipe she said she couldnt because it was the family recipe, so I did the next best thing - I came to the "zaar". I also think that this cake came out better. Thanks for posting it!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s best and easiest baby back ribs

plan ahead these ribs need to marinate 8-24 hours, you can also cook these on the outdoor grill, punch a few holes on top of the foil to allow steam to escape and to absorb the smoke flavor --- use your own favorite bbq sauce sweet baby ray's good to use,  the honey needs to be added into the bbq sauce to tenderize so do not omit, the best thing about this is there is easy clean-up! --- and yes you can also make them on the grill

1. spray the inside of each piece of foil liberally with non-stick cooking spray
2. in a bowl mix the barbecue sauce with honey until well combined
3. brush both sides of the ribs liberally with the bbq sauce reserving some to brush on towards the end of cooking
4. place each rack onto top of the greased side of foil , then wrap tightly
5. refrigerate 8-24 hours
6. set oven to 300 degrees f
7. bake the ribs wrapped tightly in foil for 2-1 / 2 hours , opening up the foil the last 20-30 minutes and basting with more sauce
8. if desired you may place the ribs under the broiler heat for about 7 minutes per side
demonstrations.review: OH SO GOOD. We had these last night. My husband is learning how to become the grill master and he wanted to do these on the grill without the foil. He kept them on a low heat, turning them and basting them consistantly and they turned out so delicious. Marinading them with the sauce was awesome. He is having the leftover ribs for lunch as I type. Thanks  for posting such a helpful recipe.

target.recipe_text:
german warm cabbage salad  krautsalat

german deli. posted by request. garlic is optional. some german krautsalat recipes do not have garlic at all.

1. cut the bacon into tiny bits
2. fry it in a big deep frying pan and fish out all the bits after they are crisp
3. cut up the onion and garlic and fry them in the bacon fat
4. when they are brown , pour in the vinegar
5. bring it just up to a simmer , add all the cabbage and bacon , toss it as you would a salad , and serve it
6. the cabbage doesn't cook , but it wilts a little under the hot vinegar
target.review: This is so delicious. I also add a little extra vinegar for more kick, and sometimes will let the cabbage sit in the pot a little longer to wilt a bit more, but if you make this and put it in the fridge, the longer it sits the more wilted it gets, but still with crunch. Just absolutely delicious, as soon as my first batch was gone I had to make another one. Thank you for this!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
texas roadhouse cinnamon butter

texas road house is known for their delicious rolls. i am posting this to try someday

1. place all ingredients in a food processor and blend until mixture is smooth
2. serve with hot rolls or muffins
3. this may be stored in the refrigerator
demonstrations.review: This was incredibly delicious!  Someone asked if anyone tried anything besides corn syrup?  I used agave instead (healthier and still syrupy) and it came out great.  I used more agave, more condensed milk, and extra cinnamon, and it came out mouthwateringly good.  No problem with separation, but I did use a food processor and whipped it within an inch of its life!  I just hope it lasts a long time in the fridge.  Thank you for posting this!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
quinoa tabouli

i love new twists on classic dishes. in this one, quinoa - a latin american grain rich in protein - replaces bulgar as the base of this mediterranean-middle eastern salad.

1. place quinoa in a colander and rinse several times rubbing the grains together to remove the bitter outer layer
2. place water and quinoa into a 2-quart saucepan
3. bring to a boil
4. reduce heat to a simmer and cover
5. cook for 10 to 15 minutes or until all water has been absorbed
6. while the quinoa is cooking , finely chop the tomatoes , parsley , and scallions
7. add lemon juice , olive oil and fresh mint to the tomato mixture
8. stir in cooked quinoa and salt
9. mix well
10. let tabouli sit in the refrigerator for a day to blend flavors
11. tabouli is traditionally served at room temperature so remove from fridge 30 to 60 minutes before serving
demonstrations.review: excellent!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
walnut taco wraps with cashew cheese

tacos filled with a delicious, rich "cheeze" made of cashews and cilantro, topped with crumbled nut "meat"! the cheeze keeps for 3-4 days in the fridge and the nut meat for  up to a week. you may also scoop the cashew mixture on top of a salad, or serve as a dip with sliced carrots and cucumbers! the walnut mix is also good sprinkled over salad or soup! great raw food! adapted from delicious living magazine.

1. to make cheeze:
2. place garlic and salt in a food processor
3. process into small pieces
4. add cashews and process into paste
5. add lemon juice , cilantro , and water and process to mix well
6. set aside
7. makes 1 cup
8. to make meat:
9. place walnuts , cumin , coriander , liquid aminos , and salt in a food processor
10. process into small pieces until the mixture looks like ground meat
11. be careful not to overprocess , it will turn into butter
12. makes 1 cup
13. scoop 2 tablespoons cashew mixture down the inside spine of each romaine leaf
14. sprinkle with 2 tablespoons walnut mixture
15. add salsa and avocado slices
16. wrap and serve
17. enjoy !
demonstrations.review: Yummy and creative. I think next time I would use less lemon and less cilantro for the cheeze, as I found it a bit overpowering. I used red cabbage leaves, which were nice, but I was also thinking about using collards and making a burrito out of it. Topped with Tapatio and Sriracha, which worked nicely. Thanks!! Definitely easy to make and will be making them again.

target.recipe_text:
pan roasted chicken with mushrooms and rosemary

this is a tyler florence recipe. i tweaked it just a bit, and the results were heavenly. easy easy easy! tastes fancy!

1. preheat the oven to 350f
2. season the chicken on both sides with a generous amount of salt and pepper
3. place a cast-iron or regular ovenproof skillet on the stove over medium heat
4. drizzle the pan with the oil and lay the chicken in the pan
5. cook for about 5 minutes until the begins to brown
6. throw in the mushrooms , shallots , and rosemary
7. stick the whole thing in the hot oven and roast for 15 minutes until the chicken is cooked , and the mushrooms and shallots are soft and roasted
8. the last thing to make is a quick gravy using the flavors left in the bottom of the skillet
9. take the chicken out of the pan and arrange on a dinner plate to keep warm while preparing the gravy
10. return the skillet to the stovetop
11. drizzle olive oil in the pan , and whisk in the flour
12. stir in the broth and lemon juice and cook over medium heat , scraping up the flavors with a wooden spoon
13. stir gravy , about 5 minutes
14. remove rosemary , and spoon gravy over the chicken
target.review: I can't believe I haven't reveiwd this yet. I have made this several times. I always make as written. I always serve with rice and a veggie. Very easy, VERY GOOD!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
fresh turnip salad

a simple salad with a refreshing flavour.

1. wash and dry turnips
2. cut off ends and leave unpeeled
3. grate turnips
4. a julienne hand grater or food processor are ideal
5. place in medium bowl
6. combine rest of ingredients
7. mix into turnips
8. chill well
demonstrations.review: This was OK. I don't think I will make again. It didn't have hardly any flavor at all.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
fudgsicles  frozen fudge pops

these taste just like the fudge pops you can buy from the icecream truck - only much cheaper!

1. in a heavy saucepan , whisk together sweetened condensed milk , sugar and cocoa until smooth
2. stir the mixture over medium-low heat until it comes to a simmer , continue stirring for 1 minute
3. very gradually , whisk in the low-fat milk , stirring to dissolve all the cocoa-sugar mixture
4. remove from heat and stir in vanilla
5. pour into individual frozen-treat molds or small paper cups
6. freeze until firm
demonstrations.review: These are great. I made them several times this past summer. We made them as written well recieved by my family

demonstrations.recipe_text:
egg drop soup  restaurant style

i came up with this recipe while searching for the perfect "egg drop soup". my picky 9 year old likes it, so i feel it is kid friendly.

1. reserve 3 / 4 cup of chicken broth , and pour the rest into a large saucepan
2. stir the salt , ginger and chives into the saucepan , and bring to a rolling boil
3. in a cup or small bowl , stir together the remaining broth and cornstarch until smooth
4. set aside
5. in a small bowl , whisk the eggs and egg yolk together using a fork
6. drizzle egg a little at a time from the fork into the boiling broth mixture
7. egg should cook immediately
8. once the eggs have been dropped , stir in the cornstarch mixture gradually until the soup is the desired consistency
demonstrations.review: This was good my grandkids love egg drop soup. I think I will cut back on amount of eggs next time

target.recipe_text:
shirley s corn casserole

this is my cousin's recipe, it looks so pretty on a christmas buffet and tastes great too.

1. drain the whole kernel corn
2. mix together everything except for the cheese and bake in a greased baking dish at 350 degrees for 35 minutes
3. remove and sprinkle cheese on top and bake until cheese is melted
target.review: Made this for Thanksgiving.  Everyone said it was ok, but not great.  Most of it got thrown out.  It wasn't horrible, and it could possibly just be my family.  They aren't always open to new things.  Probably won't make again though. Sorry.  The recipe was really easy to do, and mine was not runny like some others had said they had trouble with.  Thanks for the recipe

demonstrations.recipe_text:
butternut squash fries

5oz.fries=  65 calories, 0g fat, 6mg sodium, 16.5 carbs, 4g fiber, 3g sugar,  1.5g protein

1. pre-heat oven to 425 degrees
2. peel and de-seed your butternut squash
3. slice squash in half
4. cut it up into french fry shapes
5. place on a cookie sheet sprayed with non-stick spray
6. cover lightly with kosher salt
7. place tray in your pre-heated oven and bake for 40 minutes or so , flipping halfway through baking process
8. fries are done when they are starting to brown on the edges and get crispy
9. serve with ketchup or syrup if desired
demonstrations.review: I got this recipe from hungry girl.  Just tried it for the first time last week. MMMMMMM Good.  Honestly, this was the first time I have ever eaten squash, (except for when I was little and used to gag).  I have tryed it with regular salt, and I have also put season salt on.  Wonderful!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
fast fry pork chops

i'm adding this dish in response to the eater's digest article on 5 ingredients or less. this is so simple it doesn't seem to really be a recipe. it's also the only way my dh wants pork chops.

1. generously sprinkle pork chops on both sides with garlic salt and freshly ground black pepper
2. fry in small amount of oil until browned
3. they can also be cooked on a grill with good results
demonstrations.review: Make these all the time for my hubby. He's a very picky eater and her loves them!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
olive garden toasted ravioli

you can make these easily at home by using a package of ravioli. we like to use other types of ravioli for this dish. from copykat.com (http://www.copykat.com)

1. mix water with eggs and beat well , set aside
2. mix italian seasonings and garlic salt with the bread crumbs and set this aside
3. measure flour in bowl and set aside
4. heat vegetable oil in deep fryer or skillet to 350 degrees for deep frying
5. dip ravioli in flour then in the egg wash then in bread crumbs and carefully place in hot oil
6. fry until golden , remove from oil and drain
7. serve with you favorite marinara sauce
demonstrations.review: Made these for my husband tonight.  VERY VERY PICKY EATER!!!  He loved them.  I didn't eat them because I eat a very lowfat/low calorie diet.  They smelled good though.  The only changes I made were that I didn't have any italian seasonings and only had plain breadcrumbs.  I didn't measure, but I added a few shakes of seasoning salt, pepper, regular salt, alot of garlic powder and some garlic salt.  Atleast the hubby likes garlic :)  Anyway, he was really skeptical about eating them, but said he wants them regularly because they were AWSOME!!.  Thanks for the great recipe

target.recipe_text:
healthy no bake cookies

i played around with my family's no bake cookie recipe and produced a single portion of this cookie that i feel is healthy enough to eat as a meal.  they’re still very good but are much healthier. i keep getting asked for the recipe, so i finally decided to measure out the exact portions and post the recipe. this recipe is very flexible! when i make them i never measure out anything and i often add more or less of ingredients and they still taste great.  i sometimes leave out the wheat germ and flax seeds and just add more oatmeal.  i have made these replacing the sugar with about 3 tablespoons of honey.  i have changed the recipe from 1 tsp. to 1 tbsp. of cocoa powder.

1. heat milk , sugar and cocoa powder over high heat until boiling , stirring constantly
2. take off heat and stir in vanilla and peanut butter
3. stir until peanut butter has melted completely
4. stir in wheat germ and oatmeal
5. drop by large spoonfuls onto wax paper or eat immediately
6. as i
7. if you don't have wheat germ or flax seed , just use more oatmeal
8. the recipe above should work out just perfectly and does most of the time , but if your cookies come out crumbly , use less oatmeal next time
9. if they never set , use more oatmeal next time
target.review: I just whipped these out in five minutes, and I can tell they are going to become one of my favorites to make and eat. I used creamy all-natural peanut butter, and skipped the flax. I didn't measure anything and they've come out perfect. Thanks for the recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
hot jalapeno pepper jelly

i am addicted to this jelly.  hope there are jalapeno lovers out there.  enjoy!!

1. wash hot peppers , cut off stem and halve the peppers , remove membrane and seeds
2. put peppers in food processor and process off and on a couple of times until the peppers are coarsely chopped
3. in a medium saucepan combine peppers , cranberry juice , and vinegar
4. bring to boiling
5. reduce heat , cover and simmer for about 10 minutes
6. in a 4 quart pot combine the pepper mixture and sugar
7. bring to a full rolling boil over high heat , stirring constantly
8. stir in pectin
9. return to a full rolling boil
10. boil for 1 minute , stirring constantly
11. remove from heat and quickly skim off foam with a metal spoon
12. pour at once into hot , sterilized half-pint jars , leaving a 1 / 4" headspace
13. wipe jar rims
14. adjust lids
15. process in a boiling water canner for 5 minutes
16. remove jars and cool on a wire rack till set
demonstrations.review: I also use two packets of pectin; this stuff is awesome. We've used it in place of grape jelly in the standard coctail weiner recipe - cranberry jalapeno jelly, cocktail sauce and lil' smokies. It's super easy and always goes over very well.  Thanks for the recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
low carb spinach cheese  bread

makes a great sandwich wrapper.  make thick or thin, depending on your desires.  stays flexible, yet is sturdy enough to stand up to fillings.  add herbs or spices to vary the flavor - caraway seeds give the illusion of a rye type bread.  my favorite way is to make thin for a wrap, seasoned with some garlic and cayenne pepper.

1. thaw spinach , then squeeze out as much liquid as you can
2. place the dry spinach in a bowl and break up into small clumps
3. preheat oven to 350
4. line a baking sheet or pan with parchment paper , or spray well with non-stick spray
5. add remaining ingredients to spinach and stir to break up the spinach into small pieces and combine the ingredients well
6. spread batter evenly into prepared baking pan
7. bake about 20 minutes , or until dry and turning golden brown
8. remove from oven , loosen from parchment paper , let cool
9. cut into desired serving sized pieces
10. i usually use a cookie sheet that measures 10x13 , the batter spreads out to about 1 / 4 inch in this pan
11. when it is cooked it makes a thickish wrapper that can be rolled up around whatever ingredients
12. you can use a smaller pan to have thicker "bread" if desired
13. keeps well in a plastic bag for a couple of days
14. i have never had enough to last longer than that , it usually gets eaten by the second day
demonstrations.review: I made this for the base of a chicken alfredo pizza.  I sprayed my pizza stone and baked it on there for about 10-12 minutes, then added toppings and baked again. It was awesome- thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cream of poblano soup

poblano peppers are a mild mexican pepper and this soup showcases them beautifully! this is a delicious, rich soup that will transport you to old mexico! originally published in a 1995 newspaper food section, from cavanaugh's restaurant in webster, texas.

1. cut three tortillas into ninths
2. place in food processor and chop until fine
3. add flour , chili powder , cumin , salt , and pepper
4. blend to the consistency of cornmeal
5. place oil in stockpot over medium high heat
6. add onion , 1 / 2 cup poblano pepper , and garlic and saut until the onion is transparent
7. add butter and let it melt
8. add tortilla-flour mixture to the pan and mix to form a roux
9. cook 4-5 minutes stirring constantly with a whisk- do not let mixture burn
10. while stirring , slowly add broth , scraping down sides and bottom often
11. add half and half , bring to a slow simmer and cook 7-10 minutes
12. do not let soup come to a hard boil
13. turn off heat and let cool a bit
14. add chicken before serving
15. top each serving with shredded cheese , diced poblano pepper and tortillas strips
demonstrations.review: Everyone in my house loved this soup.  I doubled the recipe, and added an entire extra poblano.  I also melted in some low-fat cream cheese at the end to make it a bit creamier.  Yum! Thanks for a great recipe.

target.recipe_text:
puppy chow or monkey munch

kids love this and it makes a lot.  i got this recipe from a friend of mine.

1. measure cereal in large bowl
2. set aside
3. microwave chocolate chips , peanut butter and butter for 1 minute on high
4. stir
5. cook for 30 seconds longer or until smooth
6. add vanilla
7. pour mixture over cereal , stirring until coated
8. pour mixture into large ziploc bag and add powdered sugar
9. shake until well coated
10. spread on waxed paper to cool
11. store in ziploc bags or large sealed bowl
12. recipe
target.review: Loved this! Made it last night with my grandson.  He couldn't get enough and he was so proud helping me prepare this. I used the cinnamon Chex cereal and this added to the flavor.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
baked shrimp in italian dressing

very delicious!!! i'm not sure where my mom got this recipe but i loved it as a teenager and even more as an adult.....
very easy and fast

1. dehead shrimp-leave in peels
2. place in a baking dish
3. pour dressing over shrimp - it's good to cover them with dressing
4. place butter on top
5. bake at 350f until no longer gray , 7-11 minutes
6. serve immediately with french bread for dipping
demonstrations.review:
I made this last night and I thought it was a bit salty. But, that could have been the brand of the dressing I used. It was not the brand I normally buy.
Next time I will use less dressing, 16 oz, why to much for me.  Others might like that much for dipping. It was good and very easy to prepare.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
a 1 pot roast  chuck steak

a great recipe for a chuck underblade steak that is usually inexpensive,  but too often turns out tough.  this one melts in your mouth and my family asks for it often.  good over mashed or small boiled potatoes, or rice.

1. in 12-inch dutch oven , over medium-high heat in hot oil , cook chuck steak until well browned on both sides
2. meanwhile , in a cup , combine steak sauce , water , brown sugar , mustard and lemon juice until blended
3. pour mixture over steak
4. heat to boiling
5. reduce heat to low
6. cover and simmer steak for 2 to 2 1 / 2 hours , or until fork-tender , turning steak once
7. this also comes out really tender with a "falling apart" texture if you cook it on low heat in a crockpot for 6-7 hours
8. to serve , remove steak to a warm platter
9. garnish with parsley , if desired
10. with a spoon , skim fat from liquid and discard
11. pour sauce over steak or serve separately
demonstrations.review:
This was SO easy to put together and the taste is to die for!
My husband has a lot of health problems and does not like to eat most of the time really liked this and ate everyting on his plate!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pernil  puerto rican pork shoulder

this is a delicious way to cook pork.  i got this recipe from my boyfriend who is from puerto rico. this also makes excellent, moist meat for cuban sandwiches.

1. wash the pork shoulder
2. with a sharp knife , make 1 inch deep cuts into the pork
3. with mortar and pestle crush garlic , oregano and black pepper together
4. add olive oil , vinegar and salt
5. mix well
6. spoon some of the garlic mixture inside the small cuts around the pork , and spread remaining mixture all over the pork
7. place pork in an aluminum turkey pan
8. cover with aluminum foil tightly
9. refrigerate at least 8 hours
10. bake in pre-heated 325 degree fahrenheit oven for about 5 to 6 hours
11. remove aluminum foil and bake at 375 degrees fahrenheit for another hour or until skin is crisp
12. closely watch this so you don't burn the skin
13. pork should be well-done and tender
demonstrations.review: Wonderful!! Just the way my Puerto Rican Mom cooked this.  The only thing I changed was the oregano (I was out ) so I used Italian seasoning instead.

target.recipe_text:
to die for crock pot roast

amazing flavor, and so simple! no salt needed here. in fact, you may wish to use half the ranch dressing mix to cut back on the saltiness. found this crock-pot pot roast recipe on of a website called www.recipegoldmine.com. it's all the rage there, so i thought i'd try it.

1. place beef roast in crock pot
2. mix the dried mixes together in a bowl and sprinkle over the roast
3. pour the water around the roast
4. cook on low for 7-9 hours
5. use onion soup mix instead of ranch
6. add one cup , of red wine
7. add potatoes , carrots , mushrooms , celery and onion 2-3 hours before end
target.review: very easy and very good. This is a definite keeper in our home!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
unbelievable baked buffalo wings

here's a healthy alternative to fried wings: one of my famous recipes! the meat will fall off the bone! unbelievable!

1. fill a large pot half way with water and then add the first 4 ingredients
2. bring water mixture and wings to a boil and then boil for 15 minutes
3. transfer wings to an oven safe container coated with cooking spray
4. bake wings on "broil" for 15 minutes on each side
5. while waiting for wings , combine the hot sauce and margarine in a microwave safe container and cook in microwave for 2 minutes or until melted
6. when wings are done , shake 'em up with the sauce and enjoy !
demonstrations.review: I have not tried this but it is similar to my recipe!!!! Sometimes I grill it after parboiling!!! I also add the powdered italian seasoning packets to the hot sauce and margarine mix....yummers, I promise you!!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
asparagus chicken with hollandaise sauce

this recipe came from another recipe site. it is mouthwatering delicious. beautiful presentation. simple, simple, simple to make. originally found the recipe in february and just got around to making it. i'm sorry i lost all of that time eating it! i'll make up for it now. cook time does not include 2 hours for marinating.

1. to marinate: place chicken in a nonporous glass dish or bowl
2. pour wine over chicken , then sprinkle with tarragon
3. cover dish and refrigerate to marinate for 2 hours
4. preheat oven to broil
5. remove chicken from dish or bowl discarding remaining marinade and broil for 25 minutes or until cooked through and juices run clear
6. meanwhile , steam asparagus to desired degree of doneness
7. prepare hollandaise sauce according to package directions
8. when chicken is cooked , arrange the breasts on a platter , place 4 spears of asparagus on each chicken breast and dribble with prepared hollandaise sauce to taste
9. sprinkle with cheese and serve
demonstrations.review: This is a nice change from eating with the kids. As a single mom I tend to wind up eating kiddie food like chicken nuggets, mac and cheese, pizza, etc.... Tonight I decided to treat myself and I am glad I did. No more kids meals for me...lol

demonstrations.recipe_text:
twinkie strawberry surprise

this is a no bake, no cook recipe that tastes like strawberry shortcake and starts with twinkies!! it is very easy to prepare, but it does need to chill several hours, so plan ahead :)

1. slice twinkies in half lengthwise and lay evenly flat side up in a 9 x 13 inch pan
2. pour strawberries all over the top
3. in a large bowl , mix pudding , milk and whipped topping until well combined
4. spread over strawberries
5. cover and refrigerate several hours overnight
demonstrations.review: I made this for my Aunt's Birthday and everyone loved it!! I felt it needed a few more twinkies to fit my 13x9 pan so buy an extra box and then you can have twinkies on the side...hehe!!!

target.recipe_text:
chicken and barley stew

nice stew with a tossed green salad and sourdough bread.

1. toss all of the ingredients , except the parsley into a large stock pot
2. bring to a boil , cover loosely and reduce the heat to low
3. let the stew simmer for about 1 1 / 4 hours , stirring occasionally
4. use tongs to remove the chicken from the stew and slice it into bite-sized pieces
5. then return the chicken to the stew and continue to simmer for 15 min more
6. swirl the parsley into each bowl before serving
target.review: I made this for dinner tonight and it was very good, which was a pleasant surprise because I have a hard time finding barley recipes that I enjoy. The flavor was delicious. Even my husband liked it a lot. I added pepper. I do think it was too salty, but I think I might have measured in too much bouillon--some days I just can't count to five without problems! thanks for a great recipe! This is going to become a staple meal in our home.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
debbie s sticky chicken

yum

1. preheat oven to 350f and lightly grease a baking dish
2. place chicken in a baking dish , and sprinkle chicken pieces with salt and pepper to taste
3. bake in oven for about 45 minutes
4. pour off the fat
5. pour half the sauce over the chicken return to the oven uncovered for another 15 minutes , basting with the other half of the sauce
demonstrations.review: Fantastic! I will make this often. I made it with chicken tenders, but definitely will do it as the recipe directs next time--the tenders didn't quite cut it. This sauce is also great as a stir fry sauce and I've made it for that purpose twice since trying out the sticky chicken (two weeks ago). We'll probably be using this in a stir fry once a week from now on because we keep craving the sauce--it is so yummy!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
yes  virginia there is a great meatloaf

absolutely delicious meatloaf and sauce! those who claim they don't believe there can be such a thing as a great meatloaf will love this. based on a meatloaf given to me by a dear friend, virginia strehl, memphis, and leesburg, fla. nita holleman, 2000

1. meatloaf: combine meat loaf ingredients and place into a loaf baking dish
2. smooth out top
3. sauce: combine sauce ingredients and pour on top and sides of meatloaf
4. bake at 350f about 1 hour to 1 hour 15 minutes or until done
5. enjoy !
6. the addition of 1 or 2 teaspoons of kitchen bouquet makes this recipe very good
7. recipe should be"plump" from the addition of the milk or half & half
8. it should not be runny
9. a second batch of sauce served hot is good to serve with the meatloaf
10. nita's
11. it is wise to have some fat added to the deer -- especially to ground deer
12. maybe 25 % fat , , otherwise your results will be poor
13. i don't know about some of the other game meat some are using
14. please consult an expert
15. the recipe is delicious as it stands ! enjoy ! nita holleman
demonstrations.review: Fabulous! I've always liked meatloaf, but I never knew it could be exciting. I didn't have apple cider vinegar, so I used red wine vinegar instead and it was great.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
40 minute hamburger buns

homemade hamburger rolls with only a 10 minute rising time.  these are really good.  recipe from taste of home.

1. in a mixing bowl , dissolve yeast in warm water
2. add oil and sugar and let stand for 5 minutes
3. add the egg , salt and enough flour to form a soft dough
4. turn onto a floured surface and knead until smooth and elastic , about 3 to 5 minutes
5. do not let rise
6. divide into 12 pieces and shape each into a ball
7. place 3" apart on greased baking sheets
8. cover and let rest for 10 minutes
9. bake at 425 for 8 to 12 minutes or until golden brown
10. remove from pans to wire rack to cool
demonstrations.review: Very easy recipe.  Will be my go to from now on. Takes as much time as running to the store for buns, and tastes ten times better.

target.recipe_text:
kidney beans and rice

easy, hearty, stick-to-your ribs dinner.

1. in a skillet , cook beef , onion , and garlic until meat is browned
2. drain
3. stir in the beans , tomatoes , and seasonings
4. cover and simmer for 5 minutes
5. add rice
6. cover and simmer for 30 minutes or until thoroughly heated
7. discard bay leaf
8. serve
target.review:
This was pretty good and very filling.  It made a lot.  Could easily feed 8 hungry people.  I'm vegetarian so I substituted morning star farm griller crumbles for the ground beef.  I didn't have any cajun-style stewed tomatoes so I used regular tomatoes and added cajun seasoning.  I didn't want it to be too salty so I left out the seasoning salt, since the cajun seasoning had salt in it.  
I liked the idea to use the left overs for enchilada filling.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
green beans with lentils

another spartan vegetable side that we make at home, but this one's always been my favourite and is the reason why i love french beans! once when i was a kid, i sat on my kitchen platform and ate the entire 4 servings of this dish that my mom made, while she was cooking the rest of dinner!

1. heat oil in a saucepan on a low flame and add the mustard seeds
2. when they begin to sputter , add the chopped french beans , lentils , salt , turmeric powder and water
3. the water should be sufficient to cover the beans , so add some more if necessary
4. cover the saucepan tightly and cook on a low flame for about 30 minutes or until the beans are well cooked
5. check to see that the water is sufficient every 10 minutes , with stirring , and add more water if necessary
6. after 30 minutes most of the water should have evaporated
7. switch off burner , remove from flame and serve hot
demonstrations.review: I thought this was quite bland.  I ended up adding some garlic, more turmeric and some ground mustard seed, sauteed onions and more salt.  It was better but nothing fabulous.  Won't bother to make again

demonstrations.recipe_text:
legal seafood style baked scallops

whenever we get back to the boston area, it's a priority to to have a meal at legal seafoods.  i recently "re-discovered" this recipe buried in old newspaper clippings. i had tried to recreate it in the past but now know i was missing the most important ingredient - buttermilk. i made it again after posting the recipe so i have edited the original description. it's even better than i remembered, you might want to try just a dash (or more) of cayenne pepper. it's delightful !

1. preheat oven to 400f
2. place scallops in a bowl , season with salt and pepper , add thyme and buttermilk and toss to coat
3. place scallops , with buttermilk , evenly in the bottom of an oven proof dish , sprinkle with cracker crumbs and top with melted butter
4. bake for 20 minutes , squeeze lemon over scallops and serve immediately
demonstrations.review: I made this using frozen salmon fillets.  Loved it!  And so did hubby!  Will make it again!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
linda mccartney s magical mystery tacos

i was first attracted to this recipe because i'm a big beatles fan, and secondly because it's a good vegan recipe. pretty easy to make, and delicious!

1. saute the onion , garlic and bell pepper in oil for 2 to 3 minutes
2. add tofu , chili powder , cumin , oregano and soy sauce
3. cook for 3 minutes
4. add tomato sauce and simmer over low heat until mixture is fairly dry
5. heat tortillas in a heavy , ungreased skillet , turning each from side to side until soft and pliable
6. place a small amount of the tofu mixture in the center , fold the tortillas in half , and remove from heat
7. garnish with chopped lettuce , onions , tomatoes , salsa and avocado
demonstrations.review: The flavor was great but I didn't care for the mushy texture.  I made it a 2nd time substituting Griller Crumbles (MorningStar Farms) for the tofu.  I liked this much better.

target.recipe_text:
spinach pasta salad with feta

this is a delicious and light pasta salad that my sister-in-law denise makes at family gatherings.  it is so easy to make and the kids like it too!  if you can find "girard's light champagne salad dressing" in your grocery, use this.  otherwise, a light italian will substitute fine. (fat frees are too sweet)!

1. boil the pasta till done and cool
2. toss all the ingredients together , except baby spinach
3. add about 1 / 2 the bottle of the dressing and refrigerate
4. when you are ready to serve , add spinach and more dressing to your taste
5. serve
target.review: This is really tasty!  I made this for photo swap #7.  Thanks, I will definitely make this again! :)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
m   m s cookie mix in a jar

i vary the color of the m&m's to the different holiday currently approaching when i give these as gifts..another favorite of the grandchildren

1. mix baking soda and baking powder with flour
2. so you can add flour mixture into one layer
3. layer ingredients in order given into a wide-mouth
4. press each layer firmly so it will all fit in the jar
5. attach these instructions to your gift
6. instructions
7. empty jar of cookie mix into large mixing bowl
8. use your hands to thoroughly blend mix
9. add 1 stick butter or margarine , very soft
10. 1 large egg , slightly beaten , and 1 tsp vanilla extract
11. mix until completely blended
12. you will need to finish mixing with your hands as this is stiff
13. shape into balls the size of walnuts
14. place 2" apart on sprayed cookie sheet
15. bake in preheated 375 for 12-14 minutes until edges are lightly browned
16. cool 5 minutes on baking sheet
17. remove cookies to racks to finish cooling
demonstrations.review: Wow!  These are amazing!  I have always had trouble with cookies, but these came out perfect first time!  Thanks for sharing this recipe, family and friends will be enjoying this many times in the future! :)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
meow s healthy tomato mushroom sauce  ww

this is my healthy recipe for marinara sauce. i use it is a dipping sauce and i also use it for pasta dishes. i love it! you could add fresh oregano, too, if you wanted, as well as some fresh black pepper. (ww: i think this is about 1 point/cup. the only thing that has points in this recipe is the stewed tomatoes, and those are 1 pt/ cup.)

1. saute garlic in nonstick cooking spray over low to medium heat
2. once garlic is tender , add mushrooms and tomatoes
3. mash tomatoes as the mixture becomes more sauce-like , about 10 minutes
4. add basil close to the end of cooking time
5. you'll know when it's done !
6. this is fantastic with whole-wheat pita triangles toasted in the oven with nonstick cooking spray !
demonstrations.review: Thanks for posting :)  I have made this  a lot in the past since it does not need oil.  I prefer the taste of fresh mushrooms though and usually use 1-2 cloves of garlic depending on the size.  Depending on my mood and contents of the fridge I also add other veggies like zucchini (sliced using cheese slicer), peas, carrots, sweetcorn...

demonstrations.recipe_text:
rosemary scones

these little scones are lovely served hot with butter or egg-plant pate,goes great with soup.

1. sift dry ingredients in a bowl and rub in butter , add rosemary and milk and combine to form a soft dough
2. roll out on to a floured board to 1 1 / 2 inch thickness and cut into 2 inch rounds
3. place on a greased baking tray , brush with a little milk and bake in a pre-heated oven 220c for12 minutes
demonstrations.review:
Thanks, I will make these again!
:)

target.recipe_text:
green bean mushroom casserole  by paula deen

this is a highly rated recipe from paula deen of the food channel and worth making! i have tweaked it slightly and doubled the complete amounts to suit our tastes --- paula has a house seasoning blend mix which is 1/2 cup salt mixed with 2 tablespoons black pepper and 2 tablespoons garlic powder, she uses a small amount in this casserole, you have the option of omitting the fresh garlic and adding it in, store the remaining mix in an air tight container for up to 6 months, i strongly recommend using low-sodium cream of mushroom soup

1. melt the butter in a large skillet over medium heat
2. add in mushrooms and garlic
3. cook stirring until mushrooms loose their moisture then set aside
4. place the green beans in a medium saucepan
5. cover with chicken broth and bring to a boil
6. cook for about 8-10 minutes or until just fork-tender drain but do not rinse
7. butter a 3-quart casserole dish
8. place the mushroom soup , onion / mushroom mixture , parmesan cheese , black pepper and onion rings in a large bowl
9. mix well to combine , add in the cooked green beans
10. mix to combine
11. transfer to the prepared casserole dish
12. bake in a preheated 350 degrees f oven for 20 minutes
13. remove from oven and sprinkle the grated cheddar cheese on top
14. return to oven for about 5-7 minutes or until the cheese has melted
target.review: I made this at Thanksgiving and forgot to rate it.  It was the most delcious green bean casserole I have ever had.  My nephew is still talking about it.  Thank you Kittencal.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s easy no fail make anytime turkey gravy

i have been using this recipe for many years, my family loves this gravy and i have served it to dinner guests over the holidays and always receive rave reviews! --- you don't need to make this gravy using all pan drippings, if you do not have 4 cups of drippings you may mix with chicken broth to make the 4 cups, or it may be made with only chicken broth, please see note on the bottom of the recipe--- this may be made slightly ahead and kept uncovered on top of the stove until ready to serve, just whisk before using if you have any left over this gravy freezes very well or you may reduce all ingredients down to half and for a thinner gravy reduce flour by 1 tablespoon  --- also see my recipe#314890
for more of my recipes visit www.kittencalskitchen.com

1. drain the pan drippings for the roasted turkey through a fine strainer
2. let sit and then remove any fat from the top of the drippings
3. add in chicken broth or water to make 4 cups if necessary
4. in a medium saucepan , melt margarine or butter
5. add in lots of black pepper
6. add in 1 / 2 cup flour plus 3 tablespoons
7. constantly whisk for about 3 minutes over low heat
8. slowly add in the 4 cups turkey broth / drippings
9. whisk constantly over medium-low heat until bubbly and thickened
10. use right away or keep warm over lowest heat setting , whisk again before serving
11. options to make this gravy using all chicken broth prepare as directed using 4 cups low sodium chicken broth and 1 tablespoon chicken boullion powder ---- or you may add in low sodium chicken broth omitting bouillon powder to pan drippings to make up 4 cups
demonstrations.review: The best turkey gravy I ever made.  My thanksgiving was exceptional this year thanks to Kittencal.  She is my hero.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chicken shwarma   chawarma lahme

as part of a mezze, or as the main ingredient in a sandwich, or pita wrap, this is a flavorful, homey recipe.  this recipe is translated from cuisine du liban by pomme larmoyer.

1. cut the chicken breasts , or just white chicken meat , into long , slim strips , then into lengths that are about an inch long
2. put them into a bowl or other container , and allow them to marinate in the lemon juice , olive oil , crushed and diced garlic , yoghurt , tomato paste , salt , pepper and spices
3. allow 24 hours for the flavors to develop
4. the following day , remove and drain the chicken pieces from the marinade , and saute them for 10 minutes
5. serve hot as a mezze or for sandwiches along with thinly sliced onions , deseeded tomato , and any other crudites , or pickled crudites
demonstrations.review:
I wasn't goingt to be home last night so I left this for my DH's dinner.  I tasted it and thought it was good but I don't love chicken.  My husband called me this morning just to tell me how much he loved this and said he wants it every night for the rest of the week at least.  
Thank you for posting this recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
hide the zucchini

most people who taste this are surprised it contains 3 pounds of zucchini. this was mom's most popular recipe ever. the title is my idea.  mom called it zucchini casserole. boring, yes, but it gets right to the point. mom made this as long as i can remember, and we took it everywhere: potlucks, family reunions, picnics. there were never any leftovers. mom had quite a collection of zucchini recipes. she needed them. dad planted zucchini annually - lots of plants in case some died out before maturing. none of them died. ever. we weren't quite up to our ears in them, but they were just about up to our bellybuttons. we never tried to sell them - they were hard enough to give away. folks would look at us and say, "but what do i do with it?"  mom had an idea. we could con folks into taking some squash by providing recipes. guess who got the typing job? me - the one who typed at 15 words per minute. being my first major typing job, it was a bit sloppy, and i left out the part of this recipe that says, "cover with water, add salt & pepper to taste and boil just until tender"  ooops. most experienced cooks would figure out the squash must be boiled first, because it says to drain and mash it. our neighbor, ellen, however, didn't cook from scratch too much. and when she did, she followed recipes exactly. after making this, she asked mom why the squash was so hard after she baked it. she had tasted mom's casserole, and wanted to try it herself. fortunately, ellen's the type who could laugh at herself, so she didn't mind when we just about fell over, roaring with laughter. well, it was funny at the time. do be sure to file this one away for that approaching day, when you answer your doorbell and find nothing there, but a lone sack of zucchini. because now you know what do to with it.

1. cut up the squash into chunks and dice the onion
2. cover with water , add salt& pepper to taste and boil just until tender - let's say about 15 minutes
3. drain and mash , adding the butter after draining the zucchini , but while the zucchini is still hot enough to melt it
4. mix one cup of the cheese and all the remaining ingredients with the mashed squash
5. pour into buttered oblong pan and top with remaining 1 / 2 cup cheddar cheese
6. bake at 350 degrees for 30 to 40 minutes , or until center is set
7. check it with a knife blade near the center
8. does it come out clean ? it should
9. i made this once with mild cheddar
10. never again
11. it was very bland
12. use sharp or even extra sharp cheese
demonstrations.review: This recipe makes eight servings.  I gave one to my husband and I had seven.

target.recipe_text:
human puppy chow

this is the best recipe in the world!! it is great to have anytime but it also makes great christmas gifts.

1. in a large sauce pan , melt together butter , peanut butter , and chocolate chips
2. stir until all is evenly distributed and all is completely melted
3. measure out chex into a large bowl
4. pour chocolate mixture over chex and fold until all the chex are completely covered in the chocolate mixture
5. put powdered sugar into large paper bag
6. put chex into the bag with the sugar and shake until all chex are covered
7. add more sugar as needed
target.review: I first tried this one year at a Christmas party and I thought it was so good.It's really fun to make during the holidays and kids always seem to love it.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
raspberry banana bread

nan

1. in a large bowl combine flour , sugar , baking soda and salt
2. in another bowl , combine eggs , bananas , oil and water
3. stir into dry ingredients just until moistened
4. fold in raspberries and walnuts
5. pour into two greased 8x4x2 inch loaf pans
6. bake at 350 for 55-65 minutes or until a toothpick comes out clean
7. cool for 10 min
8. before removing from pans
demonstrations.review: Wow! I thought this bread was delicious! I don't think I'll ever make plain banana bread again after trying this.I only had a bag of frozen mixed berries so I just picked all the raspberries out.I didn't have quite a cup so I went ahead and added a few of the blackberries and strawberries chopped up as well.I loved all the berries in this! I think next time I'll add even more.It tasted like it had berry jam baked in the bread.I used 3 large bananas and I added about a tsp of cinnamon and vanilla.I baked mine in an 8x4 pan and 1 mini loaf pan.Mine was a little underdone in the center but I actually prefer it that way.I just had some for breakfast this morning with my coffee and I couldn't quit eating it it's so good! I'm so glad I decided to try this because I think this is now my favorite banana bread recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
excellent carrot cake

chock full of flavor, this is the best carrot cake! it tastes even better the next day after the flavors meld. a tad more time consuming than the average carrot cake, but well worth it!

1. combine first 5 ingredients
2. beat well
3. mix flour , soda , salt and cinnamon
4. add to creamed mixture
5. stir well
6. add carrots , walnuts , pineapple and coconut
7. stir well
8. pour batter into greased and floured 13x9 baking pan
9. bake at 350 for 55 minutes , or until pick comes out clean
10. buttermilk glaze: combine first 5 ingredients in large saucepan
11. bring to a boil
12. cook 4 minutes on medium heat
13. remove from heat
14. add vanilla
15. pour buttermilk glaze over warm cake
16. let cake cool
17. cream cheese frosting: mix cream cheese and butter
18. beat until smooth
19. gradually add sugar , beating until light and fluffy
20. stir in vanilla
21. spread cream cheese frosting on top of cooled cake
demonstrations.review: This carrot cake is just amazing! I made it for New Years and we couldn't quit eating it.It's so moist with the pineapple and the buttermilk glaze.It's definately the most delicious carrot cake I've ever made.I was worried the buttermilk glaze would be too rich so I only made half but next time I'll go ahead and use it all.I plan on making it again for Easter.It's sooo good but beware it's also addictive!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
betty s proto pups  corn dogs

this recipe was published in the memphis commercial appeal back in the mid 1970's.  at the time, this recipe was used to make the pronto pups at the mid south fair in memphis.  my children love it when i make these.  they taste just like the ones you pay $3.00 for at the fair!

1. mix all dry ingredients together
2. add egg and milk
3. beat until smooth
4. place skewers into each frankfurter
5. dip franks into batter and fry in hot , deep oil until brown
6. serve hot with mustard
demonstrations.review: These corn dogs are so delicious and easy to make.I've always used 1 cup of cornmeal and 1 cup flour and I leave the pepper out.I refrigerate my batter for a few hours before using it and if it seems too thick I'll thin it with a little more milk. I like to flour the hot dogs first and then cut them in half and make mini dogs.These remind me of the corn dogs I get from the fair and they are even good the next day reheated in the oven.

target.recipe_text:
three cup chicken

this is a traditional taiwanese dish that we always order in our favorite chinese restaurant. i begged the chef for this recipe and he very reluctantly gave it to me! i just made it for dinner tonight and couldn't wait to post this to share it with all of you!

1. heat up the sesame oil in a wok or a large skillet on high heat
2. add garlic , ginger and serrano peppers , stir fry until fragrant , about 2 minutes
3. add the chicken pieces and cook until it's white in color , about 5 minutes
4. stir together the soy sauce , rice wine and sugar in a bowl , pour over chicken
5. bring to a boil , then turn down the heat to low
6. let cook , uncovered , until sauce thickens , about 30 minutes
7. turn heat back up to high and add basil and scallions , cook for another 2 minutes
8. serve over steamed rice
target.review: Good recipe. Added mushrooms that needed to be used up...everyone liked it.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
dark chocolate cake

while it takes slightly longer to prepare this recipe than a box mix, the resulting moist, delicious cake makes it very worth the little extra time. i consider this 'perfect' chocolate cake. this cake is excellent with  both with recipe #261024 and recipe #208959 (the dark flavor version). (i use recipe #95416 when i'm decorating the cake.) i love how the leftovers are still moist even a day or two later. (i store my loosely covered with plastic wrap.)
my father adores this cake with recipe #261024 on it. for his birthday, father's day etc. i make him cupcakes with the icing on them and individually wrap them. he keeps them in his freezer for when he wants "a piece of cake". he claims they are as good as when they are fresh. 
(even though it isn't where i got the recipe from so i can't vouch for it, reviewers have said it is the recipe on the hershey's cocoa can. i would recommend using their special dark cocoa if possible.)

1. heat oven to 350f
2. grease and flour two 9 inch round baking pans or one 13x9 inch pan
3. in large mixer bowl , stir together dry ingredients
4. add eggs , milk , oil , and vanilla
5. beat on medium speed for 2 minutes
6. stir in boiling water by hand
7. i usually use between 2 / 3 & 3 / 4 cups
8. the cake is still very moist but it doesn't seem to "fall" as much as it cools
9. this might have to do with our high humidity or brand of flour or other factors so i don't know if it will work for everyone
10. pour into prepared pan
11. bake 30 to 35 minutes for round 9-inch pans , 35 to 40 minutes for rectangular pan or until wooden pick inserted in center comes out clean
12. because they have a tendency to overflow if you fill them more than 2 / 3 full , i usually get about 27-28 cupcakes per batch
13. bake for approximately 18-20 minutes
14. cool 10 minutes
15. remove from pan to wire racks
16. please
17. chocolate drink mixes that you add to milk or water to drink will not work in this recipe
demonstrations.review: Everyone loved it. Used Kittencals butter cream frosting. Delish.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
best ever banana cake with cream cheese frosting

this is one of (if not) the best banana cake i have ever tasted! i thought the oven temp of 275° sounded a little low, but this cake baked up (and rose) beautifully in my oven at this temp after pretty much exactly one hour. i do not know if the little "freezer trick" to this recipe is what ensured its moistness or not, but i did it, and it was exceptionally moist & delicious. would be interesting to see if it still came out as great if this step was skipped. all i know is that i followed this recipe exactly as stated (except that i had no buttermilk, so i subbed with a mix of lemon juice & milk) and i got exceptional results. so moist and yummy...a dense cake, similar in texture to a carrot cake... i personally would not call this frosted banana bread :o)  depending on the amount of frosting you like you can decide whether to half the recipe or not. i used the full recipe and had some leftover. i sprinkled on the chopped walnuts and threw this baby in the fridge and cut it the next day...to die for! i really liked it slightly chilled, but great at room temp too! it got better each day it sat, i always make this cake at least the day before i need or want it.  i was extremely pleased with this cake and will be making it over & over again!! so glad i came across this one!! (on another website).


(* * just to update the recipe, (based on some of the reviews), the baking time may vary based on individual ovens. it was right on for my oven, but some others have stated it has taken 1 hour 10 minutes, 1 hour 20 minutes, and my sister just informed me that it took 1 hour 30 minutes in her oven!!!!!)

1. preheat oven to 275f
2. grease and flour a 9 x 13 pan
3. in a small bowl , mix mashed banana with the lemon juice
4. set aside
5. in a medium bowl , mix flour , baking soda and salt
6. set aside
7. in a large bowl , cream 3 / 4 cup butter and 2 1 / 8 cups sugar until light and fluffy
8. beat in eggs , one at a time , then stir in 2 tsp vanilla
9. beat in the flour mixture alternately with the buttermilk
10. stir in banana mixture
11. pour batter into prepared pan and bake in preheated oven for one hour or until toothpick inserted in center comes out clean
12. remove from oven and place directly into the freezer for 45 minutes
13. this will make the cake very moist
14. for the frosting , cream the butter and cream cheese until smooth
15. beat in 1 teaspoon vanilla
16. add icing sugar and beat on low speed until combined , then on high speed until frosting is smooth
17. spread on cooled cake
18. sprinkle chopped walnuts over top of the frosting , if desired
demonstrations.review: Some how I goofed this cake up...I did increase the temp. a little and maybe my mixer mixed to much...but it tasted great! It just didn't look so hot, flat and stuck to the pan. I'll have to try it again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s chocolate frosting icing

a wonderful frosting i have used for years made in very little time with perfect results and 100% better than any canned, this frosting is so good you will find yourself eating a fair amount of it before even using it to frost with! --- choose the amount of cocoa powder you desire for either a light, medium or dark frosting, and make certain to sift the cocoa powder and the confectioners sugar before using for the recipe--- this frosting *freezes* very well so double the recipe and freeze one batch for next time --- *note* for an ultra creamy fluffy milk chocolate frosting add in 1 to 1-1/2 cups thawed cool whip topping at the end of mixing the frosting and beat on low speed until blended ------- also see my recipe#80118 ---- recipe#282040 --- recipe#90142

1. cream the butter in a small bowl
2. blend in the cocoa powder , vanilla , confectioners sugar , alternately with the cream
3. beat with an electric mixer , until the desired texture is achieved
demonstrations.review: Great frosting. My hubby and daughter loved it!

target.recipe_text:
ww 0 point weight watchers cabbage soup

you can eat as much of this 0-point weight watchers cabbage soup as you like. it's so good for you.

1. spray pot with non stick cooking spray saute onions carrots and garlic for 5 minutes
2. add broth , tomato paste , cabbage , green beans , basil , oregano and salt & pepper to taste
3. simmer for a about 5-10 minutes until all vegetables are tender then add the zucchini and simmer for another 5 or so minutes
4. i have tried different variations
5. leaving out green beans
6. adding chopped green onions in addition to the yellow onion
7. all very good
8. you can customize it a bit
target.review: LOL Like this recipe really needed another wonderful review! This recipe was fantastic! It was healthy and delicious!! I did add a can of white beans for a bit of protein Delish!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
philly cheesecake brownies

i found this recipe but have never used it. it sounds marvelous!

1. i would use my own brownie recipe but you can use a box mix
2. prepare the brownie mix as directed on package
3. pour into greased 13x9 baking pan
4. beat cream cheese with electric mixer on med
5. speed until smooth
6. add sugar , mixing until blended
7. add egg and vanilla
8. mix just until blended
9. pour cream cheese mixture over brownie mixture
10. cut through batter with knife several times for marble effect
11. bake at 350f for 35 to 40 minutes or until cream cheese mixture is lightly browned
12. cool
13. cut into squares
demonstrations.review: Who doesn't love brownies and cheesecake! these were awesome! I did make my brownie from scratch! everyone loved these!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cordon bleu sandwiches

comes together in a flash, got this recipe from one of those little cookbooks sold in supermarkets

1. cook patties as directed on package
2. top each with ham slice and swiss cheese slice during last 2 minutes of cooking time
3. meanwhile spread cut side of buns with honey mustard
4. top bottom halves of buns with lettuce and chicken patty
5. cover with top halves of buns
demonstrations.review: Loved the idea! I did change the recipe a lot to suit my family! I really liked the concept of this sandwich! I did use boneless chicken breast fried it like I normaly would if we were just having fried chicken used swiss and mozzarella cheese and all I had were some Bagel I had no rolls and honestly to lazy to go to the store...lol these were Amazing! my husband and daughter gobbeled them up! I will make these again!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s juicy hamburger burger

we all have our different tastes for burgers i like mine flavorful and juicy this recipe will give you the best of both! see the bottom of the recipe for tips on even more extra juicy burgers! --- making a indentation in the middle of the uncooked burger will prevent the burgers from puffing up into meatballs shapes while cooking and keeps them flat --- do not add any salt into the burger mixture as the dry onion soup already has a lot of salt content, you can sprinkle some on towards the end of cooking if needed, if desired you may add in 3-4 tablespoons of your favorite barbecue sauce to the ground beef mixture

1. in a bowl crumble the ground beef with clean hands
2. add in the dry soup mix , egg , garlic , breadcrumbs or crushed soda cracker crumbs , worcestershire sauce , black pepper and hot sauce
3. using clean hands mix until combined , add in more breadcrumbs or cracker crumbs if needed to just hold the mixture together
