4. divide the ground beef into 6 equal patties
5. using your large finger or the back of a small spoon make a shallow dent into the center of each patty
6. place the patties onto a large plate or a small cookie sheet
7. cover with plastic wrap and refrigerate for a minimum of 6 hours or up to 24 hours to blend flavors
8. grill or pan fry the burgers as desired until cooked through
9. serve burgers in toasted buns with choice of condiments
demonstrations.review: I guess i am the minority here lol I just didnt care for this recipe :(  It would make a delicious meatloaf but when I think of a Delicious Juicy burger This is not it!

target.recipe_text:
sweet and spicy turkey sandwich

love to make this. very yummy.

1. heat a small skillet over medium heat
2. butter one side of each of the bread slices with one teaspoon butter
3. place one slice , butter side down , in the skillet
4. top with the turkey and cheese slices
5. place the second slice of bread on top , butter side up
6. when the first side of the sandwich is golden brown , turn and brown the other side , 3 to 5 minutes per side , or until the cheese begins to melt
7. remove sandwich to a plate and top with strawberry preserves , or serve the preserves on the side
8. i always lift the top slice of bread & spread preserves on sandwich-just personal preference
target.review: This is one of my boyfriend's favorite recipes! Easy to make. I've used sourdough bread and havarti cheese. Delicious.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
leftover roast beef  stew

it only takes about an hour to change leftover roast beef or leftover steak into a new dish.  this recipe is from kalyn's kitchen blog:  http://kalynskitchen.blogspot.com/2005/11/leftover-roast-beef-italian-stew.html

1. cut onion and green pepper into 3 / 4 inch pieces , and roast beef and mushrooms into 1 1 / 2 inch pieces
2. in heavy dutch oven , saut onions in olive oil for 3 minutes , add green pepper and saut 3 minutes more
3. add beef , stock , tomatoes , oregano , basil , and mushrooms , reduce heat to very low , and simmer 45 minutes , stirring occasionally
4. taste for seasoning , add salt and pepper if desired
5. add fresh basil when stew has cook to desired consistency and cook 5-10 minutes more
6. serve hot
demonstrations.review: Easy and delicious! I added rosemary and sage to the recipe, and like many others, incorporated the potatoes, carrots, and onions I had originally cooked with the roast. I think bonus flavoring was added by the roast recipe I had used - the dijon mustard and beer I used to cook the roast were noticeable in the stew.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
dirty shrimp in butter beer sauce

herby, spicy shrimp with a kick, in a buttery-beer "sauce". fast, easy and delicious, serve as an appetizer, or a dinner over rice or with lots of crusty french bread to soak up all the tasty, herbalicious sauce!

1. saute garlic and herbs in butter until garlic is slightly browned
2. add shrimp , stirring constantly , until shrimp are pink and done
3. pour in beer , simmer 1 minute more , and serve !
demonstrations.review: The recipe was excellent! I doubled the sauce. However, I only gave it 4 stars because it is SO hot! Next time I make it I will halve the cayenne pepper. Otherwise it was great.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
turkey black bean chili

a chef made this at a cooking class in the upstairs room at the supermarket in town. when i looked over the recipe, i thought "i'm not going to like this". when i watched the prep & the end result, i thought "i'm not going to like this". she served it over a combination of white & brown rice with a side salad. was i ever wrong.  i liked it very much & i will be making it for my dh very soon!

1. heat oil in a dutch oven over medium high heat
2. add turkey , onion& garlic and cook , stirring to break up the lumps , for about 5- 7 minutes or until turkey is no longer pink
3. add seasonings , stir& cook for another 2 minutes
4. drain off any excess fat
5. add chilies , tomatoes & beans and combine thoroughly
6. heat to boiling , stirring often
7. reduce heat to low & simmer , stirring occasionally , for 30 minutes
8. stir in lime juice & remove from heat
9. serve topped with green onions & cheddar cheese
demonstrations.review: Easy to make & so tasty! It's easy to customize if you want to make it spicier - I took the advice of others and added extra garlic and chili powder as well as chili pepper flakes, cumin and cayenne pepper. I also added mushrooms, green pepper, celery, and elbow macaroni. Definitely will make it again.

target.recipe_text:
the ultimate killer cookies of all time

i got these through one of those internet recipe chain letter thingies, and you know what? these are really good!

1. preheat oven to 375f
2. in a large mixing bowl , combine oats , corn flakes , sugars , raisins and coconut
3. add eggs , vanilla and melted butter
4. mix till well blended
5. mix in chocolate chips
6. in a separate bowl , mix flour salt , baking powder and baking soda
7. add flour mixture and stir until it is all incorporated into the dough
8. drop rounded tablespoons of dough onto a greased cookie sheet and bake for 12-15 minutes or until nicely browned
9. cool on a wire rack
target.review: I, too, got this off internet 3 years ago and it is my alltime favorite to take to neighbors, ailing church members, etc.  (You should 1st check for food allergies, likes/dislikes first, cauz these cookies have about EVERYTHING in them!) Everyone goes GAGA over them! I had always made them using rounded teaspoons (I misread the recipe for 2 years), which essentially doubles the recipe but makes the cooking time critical. I bake (the smaller cookies) for 10-11 minutes and they turn out chewy.  Leave them in about 1 min longer and they are crispy. Any longer than that, they are TOO crispy -- not good at all.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
buttermilk coconut pie

found this recipe in a magazine many years ago. this is the best coconut pie recipe i ever tried.

1. combine the sugar and flour in a large bowl
2. add melted butter , eggs , buttermilk , vanilla and 2 / 3 of the coconut
3. mix well
4. pour mixture into shell
5. sprinkle with remaining coconut
6. bake at 325 degrees for 1 hour or until set
demonstrations.review: This is very rich and sooo good -- and so easy!  My father-in-law is visiting & loves coconut pie. During his last visit, I tried making a coconut cream pie. It was one of those recipes that required stirring a concoction over the stove. I stirred for what seemed like an hour and the stuff never did thicken (ARGH)!  This was easy to put together & came out perfectly.  The coconut mixed in the filling rises to the top during baking and makes a thin, sweet, slightly crisp top.  YUMMMMM!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cherry pie filling bread

this bread is out of this world delicious. wonderful served with with cream cheese.

1. beat together oil , eggs and vanilla
2. sift dry ingredients together and add to egg mixture
3. stir in cherry pie filling and nuts by hand
4. pour into 2 greased and floured loaf pans
5. bake at 350 for 50 minutes to 1 hour
demonstrations.review: BIG HIT when I took it in to the office today. A very easy recipe and the bread is very light, moist and sweet. Personally, I prefer a crustier bread (even with sweetbreads), so next time I may not sift the flour, just to see what happens. My hubby insists I make more, so there WILL be a next time. Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
autumn leaves

the title of this vegetable-rice dish refers to the colors in the dish which are similar to autumn foliage--however, you can eat it year-round (as long as you have summer squash available to you at the grocery store). the cooking time shown does not include time to cook rice, so add this if you're not using left-over rice.

1. preheat the oven to 350
2. saut the squash , onion and tomatoes in 2 t butter until tender
3. melt 1 / 4 cup butter in saucepan and stir in the flour
4. gradually add the bouillon , stirring until thickened
5. stir in the cream , basil , parsley and pepper
6. remove from the heat and stir in the vegetables and rice
7. put in a greased 2-quart casserole and sprinkle with parmesan
8. bake in oven until bubbly and heated through
demonstrations.review: LOVED this, and I didn't even get to taste the finished product! Was part of a dinner I took to a friend. Only changes I made were to drain the tomatoes/squash after sauteeing (mine were way too  juicy), and sub'd whole milk for the cream. Turned out great. The spices are very nice in this and the parmesan on top is the perfect touch. I put it all in a disposable 9x13. Am heading back to the store, to make some for us tonight! Thanks for a great recipe!

target.recipe_text:
tomato crowned cod

cod or any firm white fish prepared this way is excellent! the toppings really add a nice flavor to the fish. it's a staple in my recipe collection for variation. give it a try!

1. arrange fillets in single layer in lightly oiled baking dish
2. sprinkle with lemon juice and pepper
3. place tomato slices on fish
4. sprinkle with green pepper and onion
5. combine bread crumbs , basil and oil in bowl
6. spread bread crumb mixture evenly over tomatoes
7. bake in preheated 350 degree oven for 18 to 20 minutes or until fish flakes when pierced with fork
target.review: This recipe was really easy to prepare and the cod came out very moist which was great, but it was rather bland.  Next time I might like to try adding garlic as mama smurf suggested.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
sandra s key lime pie

i saw this in the food section of the cincinnati enquirer october 30 2002 pg e3. by chef sandra wilson. i really like key lime pie and until this recipe have never found one that satisfied me.

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees
2. beat softened cream cheese until creamy
3. add sweetened condensed milk and beat to incorporate
4. add egg yolks and beat well
5. add lime juice and beat till combined
6. pour mixture into pie crust and spread with spatula until evenly distributed
7. place on cookie sheet and then into the oven and bake for 10 min
8. until the filling begins to set
9. remove from oven and allow to cool on rack at room temp
10. then place in the refrigerator for at least an hour
11. two works better
12. cut into 8 slices and serve with a generous helping of whipped cream
demonstrations.review: This was such an incredible and simple recipe! I had a bit of trouble finding the key lime juice here in California but found that Albertson's grocery stores carry it. Using my Kitchenaid stand mixer made this recipe a breeze!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
strawberries   cream bread  strawberry or blueberry

a wonderful recipe using fresh strawberries from netherhill strawberry farm in australia. this recipe also yields a tried and true (and reviewed) great blueberry & cream bread.

1. combine flour , baking powder , baking soda , salt and cinnamon
2. set aside
3. in small bowl , beat butter until creamy
4. gradually add sugar , beat 1 minute or until light and airy
5. add brown sugar
6. beat in eggs , one at a time
7. beat in sour cream and vanilla
8. stir into flour mixture only until dry ingredients are moistened
9. fold in strawberries and nuts
10. pour into a greased 8 x 4 inch loaf pan
11. bake at 350f for 60 to 65 minutes or until toothpick comes out clean
12. let stand 10 minutes in pan
13. turn out on rack to cool
demonstrations.review: I enjoyed this bread very much!  Next time, I think I need to add a bit more strawberries and perhaps another 1/4 teaspoon of cinnamon to give it a bit more sweetness.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
korean roast chicken thighs

not sure where i found this recipe, but make it monthly for my family. i have used vegetable oil in place of the sesame oil and it still tastes great.

1. preheat oven to 375 degrees
2. place chicken skin side down in a large baking dish
3. combine the remaining ingredients in a bowl and then pour on top of the chicken
4. bake uncovered for 45 minutes
5. turn the chicken over in the dish and bake for another 15 minutes
demonstrations.review: I followed this recipe exactly with the exception of using fresh ginger in place of ground ginger and the flavor of the sauce came out perfectly balanced.  The 3 tablespoons of sesame oil was not overwhelming at all, as some are worried about.  It would not be Korean without it!  I will be making this again soon!  Thank you so much for the fantastic recipe :)

target.recipe_text:
taste of summer caprese melts

these are great any time of year, but with home grown basil and tomatoes they are so much better tasting! grill or broil so that the bread is golden brown on each side.

1. brush each side of bread lightly with olive oil
2. layer evenly with basil , tomato slices , mozzarella slices
3. sprinkle with salt and pepper
4. make into sandwiches and broil or grill until cheese is evenly melted , turning to evenly melt cheese
5. cook about two minutes on each side
6. serve immediately
target.review: Thanks so much for this simple yet delicious recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
best hamburgers in bbq sauce

this recipe is from "green hills garden club cooks...favorite recipes from vicksburg, ms" (linda styron).

1. moisten breadcrumbs with milk
2. add meat and form into 4 patties
3. season with salt and pepper
4. brown patties in oil
5. add worcestershire sauce , vinegar , sugar , ketchup , and onion
6. cover and cook 10 minutes
7. serve immediately on hamburger buns
8. recpe may be doubled
demonstrations.review: I have made these burgers many times and I think they are pretty tasty. This is one of my grandsons most favorite recipes. Now that he is older whenever we have them I let him be the chef. They are so simple to prepare, inexpensive, and a real kid pleaser.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
asian beef brisket  crock pot

a winner in bh&g magazine ($400.) see what you think!

1. in a 5-6 quart slow cooker , place all potatoes and top with the beef brisket
2. in a small bowl , combine hoisin sauce , salsa , tapioca and garlic and pour over the meat
3. spread sauce evenly over the meat
4. cover and cook on low for 10 hours or on high for 5 to 5 1 / 2 hours
5. remove meat from cooker to a cutting board and cut across the grain into slices
6. serve cooking liquid over the meat and potatoes
demonstrations.review: My DH has made this a few times and we love it. It's simple to prepare and is really delicious!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
zaxby s chicken fingers dipping sauce

this recipe was posted in the atlanta journal constitution newspaper.  zaxby's fans have tried to duplicate the restaurant chain's core dipping sauce.  this one posted on recipelink.com.  zaxby's co-founder tony townley took a look, saying the recipe was about half-right.  try it to see if you don't think it's almost right!  the cooking time is the refrigeration time for this recipe since there is actually no cooking involved.

1. mix together the mayo , ketchup , and garlic powder , blending well
2. add worcestershire sauce and blend well
3. cover the surface of sauce with lots of black pepper until just coated
4. blend well
5. repeat process covering surface with black pepper and stir until belnded well
6. refrigerate for at least two hours prior to use to allow the flavors to mingle
7. serve with chicken fingers
demonstrations.review: My son walked in, dipped his finger in the sauce and said "Wow, Zaxby's  We love this stuff!

target.recipe_text:
the other kind of german potato salad

a few years ago in an on-line fabric swap, one of the gals from germany shared with me that this is the kind of potato salad served in the bavarian part of germany today.  quite different from what we americans call "german" potato salad.   as my dad would say:  puts hair on your chest!

1. cook the potatoes in boiling water
2. slice and keep warm
3. while the potatoes are cooking , prepare the marinade: combine vinegar , sugar , salt & pepper to taste , oil , and onion in a small bowl
4. stir until sugar dissolves
5. pour marinade over warm potatoes
6. stir to mix
7. allow to "work" for at least several hours at room temperature
8. just before serving , add mayonnaise , pickles and eggs
9. "
target.review: This is a very good recipe and that's coming from someone who is from Bavaria, but just like with other dishes you can ask five different people living on the same street and they will have five different version.  My mom did not use mayonnaise but added yellow mustard to give it a zing, added a bit of chicken stock to mellow it out a bit, onions, hard-boiled eggs and pickles and served it warm. No matter what version, they are all yummy. Thanks for posting.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
diabetic broccoli in garlic sauce

from splenda.com - delicious!

1. trim broccoli and cut into florets
2. rinse broccoli , shake off excess water and place in 3-quart microwave-safe casserole dish
3. set aside
4. slice white scallion bulbs into rings and mince garlic
5. stir together scallions , garlic , beef broth , soy sauce , cornstarch , splenda and recaito or cilantro
6. pour sauce over broccoli , cover and microwave on high for 4 minutes
7. stir broccoli , replace cover , and microwave on high for 3 minutes or until broccoli is desired texture and sauce has thickened to coat broccoli
8. stir in sesame oil and serve hot
demonstrations.review: The recipe was easy to make, but I adjusted the garlic. It was a little to overpowering for my taste. I also left off the cilantro and recaito. It was still very good and something different to do with broccoli.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
perfect crock pot rice

you can cook rice in the slow cooker.

1. rub your slow cooker lightly with 1 tablespoon butter or margarine
2. pour in rice , water and salt
3. cover and cook on high 1 1 / 2 to 2 1 / 2 hours , stirring occasionally
demonstrations.review: I am so happy I found this recipe! From now on I will make rice only in the slow cooker. It is so much more efficient than my microwave rice cooker. I used brown rice and used the rice/water ratio from the bag. The only issue I had, and that was my fault, I should have added a little less water because the crock pot generates steam/water and so my rice came out a bit more watery than I like, but that is easily solved. Thanks for the recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
sloppy joe for one

this is one of my favorite lunches when i'm pressed for time. it can easily be adjusted for more than one person. add curry powder for a kick (i always do!).

1. cook the crumbles in a skillet with the onion and the salt
2. combine the other ingredients in a microwave-safe bowl and nuke on high for 30-60 seconds
3. mix the crumbles and onion with the sauce
4. serve in a whole-wheat pita , on a tortilla , or whatever
demonstrations.review: Loved it! Was in a hurry and left out the onion. Next time I make sure to make it with the onion. Thanks for a quick and tasty meal.

target.recipe_text:
lemon caper sauce for chicken or fish

a simple sauce to compliment fish, seafood and chicken

1. put broth and garlic in skillet and bring to a boil , reduce heat and simmer 1-2 minutes til garlic is tender
2. stir in lemon juice and capers
3. remove from heat and add butter stir til melted , add parsley
target.review: Great recipie! I omited the butter until later and added lemon zest and chopped onions while baking my 4 cod fillets. I later removed the fillets and transfered the sauce to the stovetop and added 1/2c milk, 2tbls butter, & thickened it with cornstarch.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
perfect pork loin   tenderloin

this is a favorite in our house!  it is always juicy, and the flavor is outstanding.  i can't remember where i found the recipe, but wish i could so that i'd be able to thank the person for so many wonderful dinners! **update:  we were out of honey one night and substituted apricot preserves for it in the marinade (hubbys idea)... i must say that i didn't like the idea of mixing fruit with my meat, but when it was done i thought it was even better made that way than with the honey!  either way you make it, it is sure to be a crowd pleaser!

1. in a large zip lock bag , mix together all ingredients and add the pork loin
2. let it marinade for at least 4 hours in the refrigerator
3. pre-heat the oven to 350 degrees
4. cook 35 minutes per pound , in an uncovered baking dish
5. remove from oven and let rest for 5-10 minutes
6. slice and serve
7. for added flavor , you can reserve and boil the marinade until reduced by 25 percent , then use it to baste pork loin , or use it as a dipping sauce
8. yum yum yum !
demonstrations.review: Awesome! Wish I read this recipe before I ruined 2lbs prior. I just used what I had in my pantry - didn't have green onion or enough Dijon. I did however have some Apricot & Pineapple preserves. Came out soft and moist. My stove is too hot, even though I reduced the temperature, I think I would cook it 5-10 mins less next time. Great way to use a cheap piece of meat. Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mozzarella  tomato and basil salad

appetizer found in the "ultimate italian cookbook". authentic and light.

1. slice tomatoes and mozzarella cheese same thickness
2. arrange the tomatoes , mozzarella , and basil alternating in a circle around a decorative serving dish
3. drizzle with olive oil
4. serve with salt and pepper to individual taste
demonstrations.review: Love this recipe and make it just like it is posted everytime I get the craving!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pressure cooker saucy baby back ribs   fast   easy

these ribs cook up fast and the meat melts in your mouth! i've only used beef ribs, my husband's preference, but you certainly could substitute pork ribs. the nutritional values would change. i adapted this recipe from a favorite slow cooker recipe. these are very saucy ribs, messy and delicious! my husband calls them awesome!

1. cut ribs into serving pieces
2. mix spices together to create a dry rub
3. apply the dry rub to the ribs
4. heat oil in pressure cooker and brown the ribs on all sides
5. insert cooking rack in pressure cooker , add beer , and load with ribs , not to exceed manufacturer's maximum fill line
6. place over high heat until control jiggles
7. reduce heat and cook 35 minutes
8. let cooker depressurize naturally
9. remove rack from cooker and add barbecue sauce , heat until simmering
10. simmer for 10-15 minutes
demonstrations.review: Super easy and delicious!

target.recipe_text:
cheesy beenie weenies

this is my granddaughters favorite lunch. it's not gourmet but it is easy and cheap. and most important, she'll eat it!!

1. combine the ketchup , mustard , molasses , and apple cider vinegar in a saucepan
2. add the hotdogs , cheese and beans
3. cook , stirring over medium-low heat for 10-15 minutes until thoroughly heated through and cheese is melted
4. season to taste with salt and pepper
target.review: Excellent quick dinner tonight!!!  I put to much cheese in so it became a dip with chips.  The kids ate it up!!  Thanks for a great quick recipe!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
blue ribbon tater tot casserole

my mom found this "contest winning recipe" in the local newspaper in the '70's  and i've enjoyed this recipe since. it's very comforting and kid-friendly the way the fried onions blend with the creamy filling. it's something i make for the flavor and not because it is so easy!

1. line an 8x12-inch casserole , or 7x11-inch pan with the potato rounds , on the bottom and sides
2. bake 10 minutes at 400f
3. brown beef
4. add broccoli , tomatoes , half the onion rings , and add to the cooked ground beef and spread on top of cooked tater tots
5. mix soup , milk , half the cheese and seasonings and pour over beef mixture
6. fill casserole dish and bake covered at 400f for 20 minutes
7. remove cover and add rest of cheese and dried onions
8. let rest couple minutes for the cheese to melt
9. serve
demonstrations.review: Excellent recipe!!!  I didn't have any french fried onions on hand so I used a half of an onion chopped and threw it in the mix.  It tasted great!!!  I can't wait to try it with the french fried onions!!!  Thanks!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
sausage potato lasagna

yes, this takes some effort but it is scrumptious. i think it is even better the next day.

1. in a large skillet , cook sausage and mushrooms over medium heat until meat is browned
2. drain and set aside
3. place potatoes in a saucepan
4. cover with water
5. bring to a boil
6. reduce heat
7. cover and cook for 5 minutes or until crisp-tender
8. drain and set aside
9. in a bowl , combine the spinach , cottage cheese , parmesan and egg
10. set aside
11. in a saucepan , saut onion and garlic in butter until tender
12. stir in flour , salt , pepper and the optional nutmeg until blended
13. gradually add milk
14. bring to a boil
15. cook and stir for 2 minutes
16. remove from heat
17. layer half the potatoes in a greased 11x7 inch casserole dish
18. top with half of the spinach mixture , sausage mixture , white sauce and mozzarella cheese
19. layer with remaining potatoes , spinach , sausage , and white sauce
20. cover and bake at 350f for 30-35 minutes or until potatoes are tender
21. sprinkle with the remaining mozzarella
22. bake , uncovered , 5 minutes more or until cheese is melted
23. let stand 15 minutes before cutting
demonstrations.review: A great recipe!!!  I used all low fat ingredients, so that might have taken away from the flavor a bit, but it was still great!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
baked beans don t get any better than this

these are my all-time favorite baked beans (and i've tried plenty). "it don't get any better than this".

1. fry bacon
2. remove from pan and set aside
3. when cooled , break up into small pieces
4. in the bacon grease , cook ground beef and onions until beef is no longer pink
5. mix all the ingredients together , stir well
6. pour in a 9 x 13 baking dish
7. bake at 350 for about 1 hour
8. these are sweet baked beans
9. you may cut back or eliminate the brown sugar according to your tastes
demonstrations.review: Absolutely amazing!!!  I served these to our neighbors for dinner and everyone loved them.  A definate staple for a summer barbeque!

target.recipe_text:
cheese and honey glazed carrots

oh my! these are the best carrots in the world.  my grandma makes these for every occasion. i usually end up hoarding the carrots for myself. haha. they are my favorite! if your kids won't eat veggies, try this dish! i would suggest doubling the recipe, because they are so good! can't get much easier than this!

1. peel carrots and cut in half crosswise
2. cook in small amount of boiling salt water until carrots are tender
3. do not overcook
4. drain and place carrots in a greased baking dish
5. drizzle with honey
6. sprinkle shredded cheese over carrots
7. bake at 400 degrees for 10 minutes , or broil until cheese melts
8. enjoy !
target.review: Awesome!  Was a bit bewildered by the generic "cheese" as an ingredient.  I went for mild - colbyjack...I was afraid of over-powering the sweet carrots.  I love my sweet & savory dishes, but I was a little skeptical about the cheese.  YUM!  This recipe goes into my cookbook of "staple" recipes.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crock pot chops that will make you eat til you pop

these have to be, hands down, the best meal i have ever made in a crock pot. i borrowed a friend's crock pot one weekend and made this for my honey. low and behold, i got a crock pot for my next birthday along with a request for this recipe to be the first thing i made. i really wish i know where i got the recipe from because i would love to give credit for it. i beg of you, do yourself a favor and try this. you will not regret it. let me know what you think!!

1. salt and pepper pork chops if desired
2. add all ingredients except water and cornstarch to the crock pot
3. cook on low for 5 1 / 2 hours
4. mix cornstarch and water together and stir into crock pot
5. cook 30 minutes more
6. serve over rice
demonstrations.review: I usually have all the ingredients for this recipe on hand, so it is good to make when my pantry needs restocking.  I wouldn't give it 5 stars as many have done though - it is OK enough to keep in my cookbook, but certainly isn't anything I (or my family) craves.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
caramel popcorn  not too sweet or sticky

i think this is a great caramel popcorn recipe, and i have tried quite a few! they were either too sticky or too sweet. this one is neither. the caramel dries well and doesn't stick to your fingers, and the sweetness is just right. i use spanish peanuts in this, but you could use other kinds of nuts, too. here i was searching for the perfect caramel corn recipe, when all the while it was right in my recipe box! this is done in the microwave, and is very simple to make.

1. prepare microwave popcorn as directed on bag
2. remove any unpopped kernels
3. in 2 quart microwave-safe bowl , microwave butter on high until melted , about 1& 1 / 2 minutes
4. stir in sugar and corn syrup , and microwave on high for 4-5 minutes
5. stir in vanilla and baking soda until blended
6. stir in popcorn , mixing well
7. if you are using nuts , add them here too
8. microwave on high for 4 to 6 minutes , stirring every 2 minutes to coat popcorn evenly
9. transfer caramel corn to tray lined with waxed paper , or parchment paper
10. cool and break popcorn apart
11. store in airtight container
demonstrations.review: Wish I could give this a great review like so many others, and I certainly wish I had read some of the reviews about the modification in the microwave time.  I followed the instructions by doing the lower end of timing.  My butter was melted in 1 minute.  4 minutes for the caramel mix was good.  However, 4 minutes with the popcorn was too much.  BURNT.  I don't have a powerful microwave by any means, but I wish that I had only cooked the popcorn for that first two minutes before the stir and quit there.  I wonder what this would taste like had it not burned, but I won't know anytime soon since that was the last of my popcorn. :(  Suggest modification of the master recipe step #8 to read "Microwave on high for 2 to 6 minutes."

demonstrations.recipe_text:
brown sugar meatloaf

i use chili sauce or salsa instead of ketchup to give a nice contrast to the sweetness of the brown sugar.  a lighter version can be made using splenda brown sugar blend, skim milk, and egg beaters. got this one from the allrecipes website. it's one of their most popular recipes.

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees
2. lightly grease a 5x9 inch loaf pan
3. press the brown sugar in the bottom of the prepared loaf pan and spread the ketchup over the sugar
4. in a mixing bowl , mix thoroughly all remaining ingredients and shape into a loaf
5. place on top of the ketchup
6. bake in preheated oven for 1 hour or until juices are clear
demonstrations.review:
This was the best meatloaf I have ever had!!  I have always liked meatloaf, but haven't had it for years because my husband hates it.  Well, he loved this one - a miracle!  My ultra-picky toddler ate it too - I think next time I will add some green peppers and carrots to sneak the veggies in.

I did notice a lot of comments about this being too sweet, but I made it as-is and it was wonderful.  I will say though that I definitely have a sweet tooth and always favour sweet, savory combinations in my meals.

This one is definitely going permanently into my recipe book of "staples."

target.recipe_text:
chevy s salsa   original recipe

my buen amigo pablo works at chevy's and was nice enough to share this with me.  he said you can adjust the number of peppers to you "heat" liking.  there is no liquid smoke added like other knock offs claim.  the key to the smokey flavor is the char-grilling that takes place first.

1. grill on open flame tomatoes , onion and jalapeno pepper
2. remove when slightly chared and tomatoes soften and split
3. remove from grill and let cool
4. drain accumulated liquid
5. remove stems from jalapenos and end core ends of tomatoes
6. place tomatoes , onions , jalapeno pepper , and all remaining ingredients into blender
7. blend until desired consistancy
8. pour into container and chill
9. serve and enjoy with your favorite chips
target.review: I don't care for the "burnt" taste of Chevy's salsa.  To me, it doesn't taste fresh.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
carrot rice pilaf

this is a friends recipes. i have mad it a few times and the flavor is wonderful. i goes with everything.

1. in large saucepan , melt butter over medium heat
2. cook carrots , rice and green onions for 2 minutes
3. stir in stock and bring to boil
4. reduce heat , cover and simmer for about 20 to 25 minutes or until rice is tender and liquid is absorbed
5. stir in parsley
6. season with salt and pepper to taste
demonstrations.review: The carrots gave the rice a strange, sweet flavor.  My family didn't care for this.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chili s salsa

you can make this sauce easily at home. from copykat.com (http://www.copykat.com)

1. in food processor place jalapenos and onions
2. process for just a few seconds
3. add both cans of tomatoes , salt , sugar , and cumin
4. process all ingredients until well blended but do not puree
5. place in covered container and chill
6. a couple of hours of chilling will help blend and enrich the flavor
7. serve with your favorite thin corn tortilla chips
demonstrations.review: Very authentic!  I have always loved the smooth texture of Chili's salsa, and you nailed this recipe!  Thank you!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
spinach and goat cheese stuffed chicken breast

the flavors in this dish are amazing, evrything melds so well.  this is a super simple meal that will definitley impress!

1. preheat oven to 300
2. in a bowl , mix spinach , goat cheese , lemon zest , 1 / 2 teaspoons salt and pepper until well combined
3. lay pounded chicken breast out and place 1 / 4 of cheese mixture on top
4. roll chicken breast and secure with toothpicks
5. dredge chicken in flour and brown on all sides in heated skillet
6. remove chicken and place in oven while completing dish
7. add 2 tbs
8. oil in skillet and add garlic , onion , thyme , 1 / 8 teaspoons salt and red pepper flakes
9. cook 3-4 minute then add 1 tbs
10. flour
11. cook 1 minute more
12. whisk in stock and cook 4-5 minute until thickened
13. add lemon juice , parsley and roasted peppers
14. when plating , slice each breast about 1 / 2 inches thick and spoon sauce on top
demonstrations.review: This recipe was just okay.  For once I'd like to see a recipe that isn't described as "amazing" or "awesome" when it's not.

target.recipe_text:
creamy burrito casserole

satisfy your craving for something different tonight. it's good and fairly easy. this is stuff i usually have on hand too.

1. brown ground meat / turkey & onion
2. drain
3. add taco seasoning and stir in refried beans
4. mix soup and sour cream in a separate bowl
5. spread 1 / 2 sour cream mixture in the bottom of a casserole dish
6. tear up 3 tortillas and spread over sour cream mixture
7. put 1 / 2 the meat bean mixture over that
8. add a layer of cheese
9. you could put some hot sauce on this now
10. repeat the layers
11. sprinkle cheese over the top and bake , uncovered , at 350f for 20-30 minutes
target.review: I always make pre make suppers for camping trips and this for sure is a new favourite!! I froze casserole in a foil pan, reheated on BBQ on low for appox. 1 hour, topped with grated cheese and let set for a few minutes to set.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kelly s crock pot  smoked  beef roast or brisket

this is awesome!  if you love brisket or beef cooked in the smoker and just don't have time to, or maybe the weather won't permit- you have to try this.  i have used every cut of beef roast or brisket, it always comes out great!  enjoy!

1. trim beef of any large extra fat
2. a little is good for flavor
3. place the roast in the middle of a large piece of aluminum foil
4. rub beef all over with all of the spices
5. sprinkle liquid smoke over beef and rap tightly in foil
6. make sure it's completely wrapped
7. do not add any liquid to the crockpot !
8. place in crock pot and cook on low setting for 8-10 hrs
9. unwrap beef and serve with the "smoker" juices in the crock pot or with your favorite barbecue sauce
demonstrations.review: This roast is drop dead delicious. I do lessen the liquid smoke to 1 Tbls. When I serve it I remove the roast from the pot and shred it adding it back to the juices with barbecue sauce to taste. I serve it between a bun topped with balsamic caramelized onions and a few crumbs of blue cheese.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
weight watchers key lime pie

my mom made this dessert for thanksgiving the first year i was a weight watcher and it went better then the pecan or pumpking pies.
3 points per serving. sorry, this recipe isn't core.

1. in a large bowl , dissolve gelatin in boiling water
2. stir in yogurt with wire whisk
3. fold in whipped topping with wooden spoon
4. spread in crust
5. refrigerate for at least 2 hours
demonstrations.review: I have made this recipe with several flavours of jello and yogurt, however the lime or lemon is the best for us. I have only made it into a pie once as we prefer it without the crust. Delicious and always make a double batch!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
uncle bill s whipped shortbread cookies

these are very easy to make shortbread cookies. they are so good that they melt in your mouth, you hardly have to chew them. i have been making them for over 35 years.

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees f
2. in a mixing bowl and using an electric mixer , combine butter , flour , icing sugar and vanilla extract
3. mix until mixture is a smooth consistency
4. prepare cookie sheets with parchment paper
5. spoon out dough onto parchment lined cookie sheets by teaspoonfuls or by tablespoons for larger cookies , spacing about 2 inches apart
6. cut maraschino cherries into quarters and place one piece in the middle of each cookie , alternating with red and green cherries
7. bake in preheated 350 f oven for 13 to 15 minutes or until bottom of cookies are lightly browned , do not overbake
8. remove from oven and let cool on cookie sheet for about 5 minutes
9. transfer onto wire racks to finish cooling
10. store in a container with a lid and separate each layer with wax paper
11. use sprinkles , half an almond or half a cashew or chocolate to the top of the cookies before baking
12. a thumbprint in the cookie , filled with your choice of jam is very tasty
13. it has been suggested that the cookies be refrigerated for at least 1 / 2 hour before baking for a different texture
demonstrations.review: Only recipe I use. I do not use vanilla and use unsalted butter and add a pinch of salt to flour. I roll into walnut size balls, flatten slightly with fork, and sprinkle with coloured sugar before baking @ 325 for 15 mins. Shortbread is always better when aged so I refrigerate cooled cookies in an air tight container after baking and attempt to wait for the magic to happen. I have kept shortbread if well hidden for up to a month.

target.recipe_text:
bacon and potato chowder

very filling, tasty, and easy to make. for best results, buy a good, very smokey bacon from a butcher shop.

1. fry bacon until crisp , and chop
2. drain and use paper towel to soak up excess fat
3. in a large pot , sautee onion and garlic with 2 tbsp bacon drippings
4. add potatoes , water , bouillon cubes to pot
5. heat to boiling , then cover and simmer until potatoes are cooked , then add bacon
6. mix flour with a small amount of evaporated milk , making a paste
7. gradually stir in remaining milk
8. add to potato mixture
9. cook over medium heat until mixture comes to a boil and thickens
10. stir often to ensure the soup doesn't burn on the bottom of the pot
target.review: I love this! I added a few chopped baby carrots and a celery stalk with the onion. I used 1 1/2 TBSP cornstarch instead of flour so it would be GF. And I didn't have evaporated milk, so I substituted one cup of whole milk. It turned out great. It's an easy, hearty, delicious soup.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
marge s zucchini pie

one of my co-workers gave me this recipe years ago, and now it's a staple.  we just don't feel like it's summer until we've eaten some.  we usually eat it for dinner, but it's equally good for breakfast or brunch.

1. preheat oven to 375 degrees
2. saute zucchini , onions and garlic in olive oil until soft
3. stir in parsley , herbes de provence , salt and pepper
4. remove from heat
5. beat the eggs and then add the cheese to the beaten eggs
6. pour into the veggie pot and combine
7. spread dijon mustard on bottom of pie crust
8. add zucchini mixture to crust
9. bake for 35-40 minutes
demonstrations.review: I love this dish! I'm sure it's great as-is, but I tweaked it a little to suit our tastes.  I left out the mustard, halved the salt and used probably about 6 oz. of cheese.  It's so delicious! It's great the next day, too.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
campbell s glazed pork chops

this is good, any time!! campbell's french onion soup gives pork chops a glaze of glory in this easy 15-minute recipe.

1. mix cornstarch and water in cup until smooth
2. heat margarine in skillet
3. add chops and cook until browned
4. add soup and sugar
5. heat to a boil
6. cover and cook over low heat 5 minutes or until done
7. remove chops and keep warm
8. add cornstarch mixture
9. cook until mixture boils and thickens , stirring
10. serve over chops
demonstrations.review: These were very good.  I served them with a garlic flavored risotto, which was too much.  White or brown rice would have been better.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
slow cooker tex mex chicken

from kraft food & family, fall 2007

1. mix chicken with seasoning and flour in slow cooker
2. stir in all remaining ingredients except the shredded cheese
3. cover with lid
4. cook on low for 6 to 8 hours
5. stir just before serving
6. top with the shredded cheese
7. serve over rice and garnished with fresh green onions and cilantro
demonstrations.review:
This is always a hit at my house. I serve it over rice, then eat the leftovers with tortillas. 
I find it only needs to cook about 3-4 hours on low.  Any longer than that and it starts to burn around the edges of the crock pot.

target.recipe_text:
bacon cheeseburger meatloaf  paula deen

this recipe comes from a "cooking with paula deen" magazine (may/june 2006).  my family loves this served with macaroni and cheese.  the leftovers made a delicious sandwich the next day, topped with your favorite burger toppings.

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. spray a baking dish with non-stick cooking spray
3. in a large mixing bowl , combine the first 9 ingredients , mixing well by hand
4. in a small bowl , combine ketchup and mustard
5. stir in 1 / 4 cup ketchup mixture into the meat mixture
6. place meat mixture in baking dish and shape into a loaf
7. spread remaining ketchup mixture over meatloaf
8. bake for 40 minutes
9. remove from oven and top with french fried onions
10. return to oven and bake 10-15 minutes longer , or until meat is no longer pink
target.review: I love this recipe, I also place two slices of bread under the loaf t absorb any fat drippings then feed the bread to my dog.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
rigatoni with steak sauce

one dish meal served in bowls topped with parmesan cheese. recipe courtesy of everyday italian.  reviewers said it was easy and enjoyed by picky eaters, too. others made with filet mignon to flat iron steak.

1. heat 2 t olive oil in heavy frying pan over high heat
2. sprinkle steaks with salt and pepper to taste
3. cook steaks until they are brown but still rare in the center , about 3 minutes each side
4. transfer steaks to a plate to cool down
5. save steak juices in plate
6. add 2 t olive oil to same pan
7. saute the onion and carrots until onions are translucent , about 8 minutes , with add'l salt & pepper to taste
8. add garlic and oregano , saute for another minute
9. add marinara sauce and broth
10. cover and simmer over medium-low heat to allow the flavors to blend , about 10 minutes
11. season with salt & pepper to taste
12. meanwhile , trim fat from each steak and cut into bite-size pieces and set aside
13. bring a large pot of salted water to boil over high heat
14. add rigatoni and boil until tender but firm to the bite , about 10 minutes , stirring often
15. drain
16. toss the rigatoni and steak pieces and any accumulated juices from the steaks with the sauce to coat
17. transfer to individual serving bowls , top with cheese
demonstrations.review: Your suppose to add the red wine to deglaze the pan after cooking the steak and veggies. This recipe taste 100 times better if you skip the red wine and add in a half a cup of heavy cream and turn it in to a cream sauce!!!! You could also make this to use up any left over pork roast.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s easy and delicious ranch parmesan chicken

there are plenty versions of this recipe, this is mine and can be on your table in less that an hour, my family loves this chicken! --- the ranch dressing is the secret it holds in all the flavor and moistness while the chicken is baking and also adds flavor, i find that hidden valley ranch dressing works the best but kraft or any other brand will do, i sometimes top the baked chicken with mozzarella cheese or cheddar, but that is optional --- although i have only made this using breasts i imagine that chicken pieces could be used although you would have to increase the breadcrumb mixture slightly, you can marinate the chicken breast in the ranch dressing for a few hours in the fridge, although you will need more than 1 cup of dressing if you are marinating .... *note* to avoid a soggy bottom crust, place the chicken breasts onto a flat rack on top the baking sheet, also it is important not to bake the chicken in a small baking pan, if you do not have a rack bake on a large baking sheet so any juices in the pan will spread out and not accumulate under the chicken causing a soggy bottom ---------------
for low-fat option: use low-fat ranch dressing and omit the melted butter on top or use a healthy butter alternative such as smart balance 50/50 blend.

1. set oven to 400 degrees
2. in a shallow bowl mix together the dry breadcrumbs with parmesan cheese , seasoned salt , black pepper and garlic powder
3. dip the chicken into the ranch dressing to coat both sides
4. coat in the breadcrumb mixture
5. place in a single layer onto a greased baking sheet or line with non-stick foil
6. lightly drizzle the melted butter over each breast
7. if desired you can sprinkle black pepper over the chicken pieces
8. bake uncovered for about 30-35 minutes or until the chicken is cooked)
demonstrations.review: Great! this was super flavorful and very easy, I forgot to pour the butter over it but it still came out great.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
potatoes with mustard and honey

i have had guests fight over these, so you might want to double the recipe.

1. peel the potatoes and cut into cubes of about 3 centimeters cut up the onions
2. mix the mustard , honey , oil , salt and pepper
3. then stir the mixture into the potatoes
4. grease a large rectangular pan and spread the mixture into it
5. bake at 200c for 50 minutes
6. after about 25 minutes , stir up the mixture
demonstrations.review: These were pretty good. Honey is an expensive ingredient so next time Ill used either pre-made honey mustard dressing or brown sugar.

target.recipe_text:
super easy coconut cream pie

this is one of those things that turn out wonderfully with little effort.
great for weeknight desserts or when you need something nice and don't have much time to make it in!
posting so we have access to the shopping list!

1. in a large bowl mix pudding and milk until pudding becomes thick
2. fold in 4 oz of the cool-whip
3. fold in 1 cup of coconut
4. spread mix into bottom of pie crust
5. spread remaining cool-whip on top
6. sprinkle with left-over coconut
7. serve cooled
8. keep refrigerated
9. enjoy !
target.review: I made this recipe for a dinner I catered and the two ladies I cooked for loved it!  I followed the recipe exactly using the coconut flavored pudding mix and a frozen pie crust.  I also toasted the coconut before I put it on top of the pie, I thought the light brown of the toasted coconut looked nice on top of it.  I will definitely be making this again.  Thank you for posting!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chicken hurry

a quick chicken recipe, serve with plain white rice and steamed baby carrots.

1. arrange chicken parts in a casserole dish
2. in a small bowl combine the ketchup , water , sugar and soup mix
3. mix together well
4. spoon over chicken , making sure the sauce is on every piece
5. bake covered at 350f for one hour
demonstrations.review: Made this for dinner tonight using boneless skinless chicken breasts.  It was quick, easy, and tasty!  I'll be making this again.  Thanks for posting!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
zesty italian crescent casserole

this is a very good, easy dish that's sure to impress.  i've had great results from others when i've made this.

1. heat oven to 375 degrees fahrenheit
2. in large skillet , brown beef and onion then drain
3. return meat to pan
4. add spaghetti sauce
5. meanwhile , in a medium bowl combine mozzarella cheese and sour cream
6. pour hot meat into an ungreased 12 x 8 inch dish
7. spoon cheese mixture over meat
8. unroll crescent roll dough over the top of the mixture
9. mix parmesan cheese and butter together , then spread over the top of the dough
10. bake 18-25 minutes or until golden brown
demonstrations.review: This casserole was very easy to make.  It tasted pretty good too...it seemed like it was missing something, though im not exactly sure what.  I may make this again and if I do im going to add some spices or maybe some red pepper flakes or something. Thanks for posting!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cream cheese cinnamon crescents

these are so yummy.  would be perfect for breakfast or brunch or anytime!  i just made a batch late this evening.  a parent brought these in for a teacher's luncheon and everyone loved them.

1. roll out one can of crescent rolls in bottom of 9x13 pan
2. i sprayed pan with cooking spray
3. cream together: 2 8oz
4. cream cheese
5. 1 cup sugar
6. 1 teaspoon vanilla
7. spread this mixture over crescent rolls
8. lay second tube of crescent rolls over mixture
9. melt 1 / 2 cup butter , mix in 3 / 4 cup sugar ,
10. 1 teaspoon cinnamon , and pour over top
11. bake at 350 for 30-35 minutes
demonstrations.review: This recipe was delicious, but so very rich!  I made this for Thanksgiving breakfast and we ate it warm out of the oven.  I only had a piece of it and set it in the fridge for the next morning.  My friend ate a piece the next day and said it was not quite as rich after it had been refrigerated.  I think next time I make it I may cut down on the cream cheese a little bit and maybe add some type of fruit.  Possibly peaches or apples.  Thanks for a great recipe!

target.recipe_text:
bird s thanksgiving leftover croquettes

a spin off of our recipe #253952, and just as tasty.
great for oamc too. the croquettes freeze well, then just pop them in the microwave for a quick meal or snack. :)

1. mix the turkey , stuffing , and eggs well
2. refrigerate 3 hours minimum
3. create a 'log' shape from about 3 / 4 cup of mixture
4. then gently drop onto the counter to flatten the bottom
5. roll the croquettes in flour , then bread crumbs
6. fry in oil in deep skillet over medium heat , turning occasionally , until golden brown on all sides and bottom , about 10-15 minutes
7. keep warm in 200 degree fahrenheit oven
8. sauce: meanwhile , mix the can of soup with the half cup milk in a saucepan
9. cook , stirring constantly , until warmed and creamy
10. pour over croquettes or serve sauce on the side
11. traditionally served atop mashed potatoes for a wonderful presentation
target.review: Wonderful recipe!!! Thank you very much for providing it.  I was so amazed to see this recipe posted showing how-to use Turkey left overs.  Great idea!!!  The "Croquettes" are made back in France where I was brought up.  Back there, The "Croquettes" are  made using Chicken.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
robert redford

this recipe, just like the person it is named after, is a "classic". if you love reese's peanut butter cups you will love this recipe.

1. melt butter
2. mix with flour and press into baking pan
3. pour pecans over and press down
4. bake 15 minutes at 350 degrees fahrenheit
5. cool
6. mix cream cheese with confectioners' sugar and peanut butter
7. mix well
8. pour over crust
9. mix vanilla and chocolate pudding mixes with the milk and cool whip
10. beat well
11. pour over peanut butter layer
12. garnish with additional cool whip
13. sprinkle with nuts and chocolate as desired
demonstrations.review: This recipe is a winner!!! Extremely delicious!!! However, it is a different version of the famous  "ROBERT REDFORD CAKE" that I was served at a Famous Hotel restaurant in San Diego CA and then at a  famous restaurant in Hollywood CA and later in Cleveland OH during my visit there.  Just for the record,  the Pastry Chefs at the three locations did not use Peanut Butter or chocolate, it was strictly done with White Cake ,Vanilla Pudding, Vanilla Icing, Whip cream and Pecans.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
arnold palmer company casserole

this recipe is easy and tastes great! very simular to a lasagna but lighter flare. usually a family pleaser. this recipe comes from a friend of my who is from rochester ny.

1. bown beef and mushrooms and 1 / 2 chopped onions
2. add tomato sause salt , pepper , and garlic salt and simmer for 1 / 2 hour
3. cook noodles
4. combine cottage cheese , sour cream , remaining chopped onions and green peppers
5. buttered casserole
6. layer meat , noodles and cheese mixture , ending with meat on top
7. bake at 300 degrees for 45 minutes
8. first 1 / 2 of cooking time with lid on casserole , remaining with lid off
demonstrations.review: I like this recipe very much because of the ease in making this casserole, and how great it tasted and also due to the use of cottage cheese in it.  I certainly pray that this is another one of the Famous Golf Champion Arnold Palmer's creation since his famous "Arnold Palmer drink" combining Ice tea and Lemonade?

demonstrations.recipe_text:
hummus  hommos  humus

my mother's family is lebanese and we pride ourselves on being able to cook delicious lebanese food.  this is a family recipe.

1. using a blender , blend the first six ingredients
2. serve in a large flat bowl
3. sprinkle paprika over the finished product and serve with bread
4. if needed , add more lemon and salt to increase a tartier tastes
5. for softer texture , add more oil
demonstrations.review: Such "Excellent" recipe.  Love it!!!.. I always use this one.  Along with the Paprika to serve, I add some shelled Pine Nuts to garnish.

target.recipe_text:
devil bites

these little bites are so good that you swear that the devil is tempting you from the diet, but they are low fat little delights that my whole family loves!

1. heat oven to 375
2. in a large bowl , beat brown sugar and margarine until light and fluffy
3. add vanilla and egg white
4. mix well
5. add flour , cocoa , baking soda and salt
6. blend well
7. stir in chips
8. drop by teaspoonfuls on to ungreased cookie sheet
9. shape gently into balls with your fingers
10. bake at 375 for 8-9 minutes
11. cool 1 minute on sheet and then transfer to let cool
target.review: I can't believe no one has tried chocolate chips in these!  (they were the only chips I had)Totally decadent! Fudgey, yummy, chocolatey bites! Love these!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
easy peanut butter   chocolate chip cookies

these are a very easy cookie and don't take a lot of time either. perfect for if you love peanut butter and chocolate-they have great taste!

1. mix together the first four ingredients until well combined
2. add the chocolate chips and mix well
3. place a spoonful of dough on cookie sheets and flatten just a little bit
4. bake at 375 degrees for about 9-10 minutes
demonstrations.review: great cookies!  My first "flour-less" cookie and I was a bit skeptical.  Great peanuty flavor! I agree that letting them cool a few minutes is necessary..if you don't they are soft enough to fall between the grids on the cooling rack. I also would not double this recipe.  I did and the last 2 pans were very crumbly.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crock pot tamale casserole supremo

absolutely flavor filled. easy to make and economical.

1. brown the ground beef and chorizo together
2. drain most of the fat off
3. pre-mix the egg , milk and cornmeal
4. except for the cheese , put all the other ingredients into the crock pot
5. mix them thoroughly
6. put the cornflour-egg-milk mix on top
7. set the crock pot to high or low
8. cook for 5-6 hours on high or 10-12 hours on low
9. 5 or 10 minutes before serving , cover the top with the grated cheese
demonstrations.review: I cheated and seasoned 1.5 lbs of burger with a "chorizo" recipe from here on *Zaar.  Ditto on the taco seasoning (mixed on up from the recipes here) Was a very tasty well received meal!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pink pancakes

this is from jessica seinfeld's cookbook called deceptively delicious.  i have not tried this, but am posting recipes for others.  when i do make them, i will make a version that does not use pancake mix and share my results.

1. in a blender or food processor , combine the water , ricotta cheese , beet puree , vanilla , and cinnamon
2. dump the cheese mixture into a medium bowl , add the pancake mix and apple
3. stir until just combined
4. do not overmix , you want the batter to be lumpy
5. coat a griddle with nonstick spray and heat to medium high
6. add 1 / 2 tsp vegetable oil
7. use 1 / 4 cup of batter at a time and pour out pancakes
8. when you see bubbles start to form , it is time to flip the pancake
9. if the bottom is too brown , turn the heat down
10. it should take about 1 to 2 minutes per side
11. serve warm , garnish with maple syrup , fresh fruit , and powdered sugar
demonstrations.review: My kids beg for these! They are so yummy!

target.recipe_text:
applebee s blonde brownies

i found this recipe for applebee's famous desert. serve it warm with vanilla ice cream or frozen yogurt

1. brownies: combine flour , baking powder , baking soda , and salt
2. add nuts , mix well , and set aside
3. melt butter , add brown sugar , and mix well
4. add egg and vanilla and mix well
5. gradually combine with flour mixture , mixing well
6. stir in white chocolate chips
7. pour into a 9-inch square pan and bake at 350 for 20-25 minutes
8. sauce: combine syrup and butter , cook over low heat until butter is melted
9. stir in brown sugar until dissolved and remove from heat
10. beat in cream cheese and maple extract until smooth
11. heat again in the microwave until it reaches desired consistency
target.review: I agree with greasing the pan--they stuck all around the edges.  But they tasted delicious.  We didn't have any ice cream on hand when I made them, but my husband is looking forward to the next time and feels it would be a wonderful complement.  We never tasted these at Applebee's, but we really enjoyed them here at home.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
easy hamburger stew

easy dinner on the table in the time it takes to steam rice.

1. saute ground beef , garlic and onion
2. add potatoes , carrots and corn
3. stir in soup , water and seasonings
4. cover and simmer until veggies are tender
5. serve over steamed white rice
demonstrations.review: Very good!  I used ground turkey instead of beef and it still turned out great.  Easy to make from on-hand items.  I'll definitely keep this one.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
authentic italian meatballs

meatball recipes are often challenged by chefs who claim, "mine are the best!" even though my meatballs are the best, i will make no such claim. try them for yourself! this meatball recipe was given to me by my father who got it from a little old lady from italy that he knew. it's amazing that she gave up her recipe to him, but i sure am glad she did!

1. mix all ingredients in a large bowl by hand
2. use your bare hands for best results
3. roll meatballs to about the size of a golf ball
4. drop raw meatballs into large pot of sauce
5. simmer for about 3 hours
demonstrations.review: I used ground turkey because we're not big red meat eaters and they STILL turned out great.  Nice & moist & flavorful.  I must confess I didn't use your sauce because I still had some of my own that I had frozen, but I'll try it another time.  Thanks for a delicious recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
dad s casserole

complete comfort food. great on a cold day.

1. heat oven to 350f
2. spray 2-3 quart casserole with non-stick cooking spray
3. cook noodles as directed on package
4. brown beef with garlic until cooked through
5. drain
6. add salt , sugar and tomato sauce and simmer for 5 minutes
7. combine sour cream , cream cheese and onion
8. layer 1 / 2 of the noodles then 1 / 2 of the meat mixture in casserole dish
9. spread with sour cream mixture
10. top with remaining noodles and the tomato sauce
11. bake for 30 minutes
12. sprinkle grated cheese on top and bake for another 5 minutes
13. enjoy !
demonstrations.review: Since we eat very little red meat, I used ground turkey instead.  I also used regular onions because it was all I had. I was sure I wouldn't like it because of the cream cheese/sour cream combination.  But was I wrong!  This is delicious!  My husband wants it on our menu on a regular basis.  Thanks, Bekah, for a truly filling and tasty meal!

target.recipe_text:
chinese roasted chicken

when i first left home i shared a flat with a chinese girl and this is one of the ways she would cook chicken. the marinade is sticky and yummy and smells wonderful.

1. marinate chicken pieces in all the other ingredients for at least 2 hours , turning pieces now and again
2. arrange in a single layer in a roasting dish and cook in a moderate oven for 30 minutes , turn pieces and cook a further 25 minutes
3. serve hot or cold
target.review: I feel like I must certainly have done something wrong with this since I just couldn't even bare to take a bite of it after smelling it cook.  I learned that my family and I don't like five-spice powder AT ALL!!!  I learned that I will never use that spice again!!!!  Since everybody else seemed to love this recipe I'm gonna blame myself and my flavor challenged family and at least rate this three stars!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
garlic horseradish sirloin roast

did this for dinner today, very delicious with apricot glazed carrots and garlic mashed potatoes, mmm so good! from canadian living magazine.

1. with a sharp knife
2. stuff each slit with a garlic sliver
3. in a small bowl , whisk together mayonnaise , horseradish , sage , salt and pepper , brush all over roast
4. place onions in centre of roasting pan , place roast on top of onions
5. roast in 325f oven until thermometer registers 160f for medium , about 2 hours
6. transfer to cutting board and tent with foil , let stand for 10 minutes before carving
7. skim fat from pan juices
8. pour in beef stock and worcestershire sauce , bring to boil , stirring scraping up brown bits
9. whisk cornstarch with 1 tablespoon water , whisk into pan and cook , whisking until thickened and glossy , about 2 minutes
10. strain and serve with beef
demonstrations.review: I'm a 'beginner'....and even I was able to impress with this one!  My husband gave it two thumbs up!   Thank you, Derf!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mom s apple crisp

one of my favorite things for mom to fix when i was a kid.

1. peel apples and remove cores
2. slice apples into thin slices and put into lightly greased casserole dish
3. mix sugar and flour together
4. cut in butter until you have course crumbs
5. stir in oats and pour over apples
6. bake at 350f for 35 minutes
demonstrations.review: Loved it!  Quick and simple!  I also added a pinch of cinnamon to the apples after reading the other reviews.  Two thumbs up!!!  My husband will finish the entire pan within an hour of removing it from the oven!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
bacon onion appetizers

these get eaten up in no time. make lots because your guests will be asking for more.

1. combine first 4 ingredients
2. unroll crescent rolls and separate into 8 rectangles
3. firmly press perforations of triangle to seal into a rectangle
4. spread butter mixture evenly over dough
5. roll up each rectangle , beginning with short side
6. pinch seam to seal
7. cut each into 4 slices
8. place pinwheels on ungreased baking sheet
9. flatten slightly
10. bake at 375 degrees for 15 minutes or until golden
demonstrations.review: Quick and easy to prepare......I just thought that they were lacking that certain 'something' if you know what I mean.  They were very tasty and I would make them again...but perhaps with some more pizzazz.  Now if only I knew what pizzazz that would be!

target.recipe_text:
rich  moist secret ingredient pumpkin bread

this is my favorite pumpkin bread recipe. it is very different from other pumpkin breads because it calls for some unusual ingredients that make it special. i almost always use freshly cooked and mashed pumpkin in this - i like to use a small pie pumpkin, which i cut into quarters, seed, and steam until tender, then remove the peel and mash. but i have used plain canned pumpkin as well - just don't accidentally use pumpkin pie filling - you need the plain puree. prep time assumes you already have some pumpkin puree handy. the extra loaf freezes well. i have been making this for years, but originally found this in one of the 

1. sift together first 8 ingredients
2. beat eggs well in another bowl
3. add oil , sugar , pumpkin , and vanilla to the eggs and mix well
4. combine wet mixture with flour mixture gently by hand , pressing out any large lumps with your spoon , just until ingredients are moistened- do not overmix
5. pour into 2 loaf pans and bake in a preheated oven at 350f for 1 hour to 1 hr 15 minutes
6. cool in pan 10 minutes then let cool completely on wire racks- don't skip of your loaves will fall apart
target.review: Excellent pumpkin bread - my new favorite. I made 24 muffins, which took 45 minutes to make. Turned out perfect.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
tsr version of ihop buttermilk pancakes by todd wilbur

from www.topsecretrecipes.com. these are my favorite pancakes...so light and fluffy.

1. preheat a skillet over medium heat
2. mix all of the ingredients til combined
3. melt a little bit of butter in the pan
4. pour the batter by spoonfuls into the hot pan , forming 5-inch circles
5. when the edges appear to harden , flip the pancakes
6. they should be golden brown
7. cook the pancakes on the other side until they are also golden brown
8. enjoy
demonstrations.review: Delicious!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
skillet macaroni   beef

this is an easy to prepare, one skillet dinner. i don't remember where i got it, but my family loves it and asks for it often. it is a good potluck dish if you double, or triple it. people will ask for your goulash recipe.

1. cook beef in a large skillet until no longer red
2. remove from skillet , using a slotted spoon so as to save liquid in the skillet
3. cook macaroni , onion and green pepper in drippings until macaroni is yellow
4. return meat to skillet along with tomato sauce , water , salt , pepper and worcestershire sauce
5. cover and simmer 25 minutes
demonstrations.review: Good comfort food! Didn't have onion or green pepper on hand, and had to substitute Tomato Soup for the tomato sauce. Tasted wonderful.  Thanks for sharing!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pistachio cheese wafers

incredibly tasty. i love the peppers which gives these wafers a hint of fire. at a recent dinner these were the hit served as an appetizer with wine.

1. in a proccesor or electic mixer beat together the butter and cheese
2. then add 1 cup of flour and mix
3. in a seperate bowl combine the , salt and black and cayenne pepper
4. add to the cheese mixture and beat until blended
5. stir in the pistachios
6. turn the dough onto a floured surface and divide in half
7. shape each piece into a log and 1 inch across
8. wrap in plastic wrap and chill until firm
9. preheat oven to 350 degrees
10. cut the chilled dough into 1 / 4 slices and place them about 2 inches apart on ungreased cookie sheet
11. bake for 10 to 12 minutes , until golden brown around the edges
12. transfer to a rack to cool
demonstrations.review: These were a hit at Easter.  I had a little trouble with the dough; didn't seem moist enough, and made it difficult to slice.

target.recipe_text:
kittencal s technique for perfect easy peel hard boiled eggs

the one and only method i use for perfect hard-boiled eggs and the only one you will use also, this is a no-fail method your eggs will come out perfectly cooked!--- don't omit the vinegar it makes peeling the eggs easier and your eggs will be bright yellow and the whites a pure white! -- it doesn't matter what amount of water or eggs that you use just make certain that you add in about 2 teaspoons of vinegar, i don't even measure i just pour the vinegar into the water from the bottle the exact 2 teaspoons does not really matter,  of course use as many eggs as you wish and the exact amount of ice is not necessary you can use more, also try to use eggs that are at least 2 weeks old fresh eggs are somewhat harder to peel.

1. place the eggs in a saucepan
2. cover the eggs with lukewarm water
3. add in vinegar and pinch salt
4. bring to a full boil over medium heat
5. boil for 2 minutes
6. remove from heat cover with a tight lid
7. allow the eggs to stand for 11 minutes
8. drain the eggs a couple times under very cold water
9. cover the eggs with cold water then add in some ice
10. allow the eggs to sit in ice water for about 3 minutes
11. drain and peel
target.review: Works like a charm, what else do you need to know! Go cook em'

demonstrations.recipe_text:
whatever floats your boat  brownies

these are absolutely the chewiest, moistest, fudgiest brownies ever! i have tried adding so many different things to the batter, and they always comes out great.  they are also great without any add-ins! but by varying the add-ins, you can make different brownies every week (or day!!) super easy prep! so, add "whatever floats your boat" and you will not believe how yummy they come out :) oh, and the recipe doubles just fine--use a 9 x 13 inch pan instead and add a few more minutes of baking!

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. grease an 8 inch square pan or line with foil
3. in a medium bowl combine melted butter and cocoa and stir until cocoa is dissolved
4. add sugar and mix well
5. add eggs one at a time and stir until well combined
6. stir in vanilla , flour and salt until you no longer see any flour
7. fold in "whatever floats your boat" !
8. spread in pan and bake for approximately 25 minutes
9. do not over-bake -- your brownies will come out dry
10. adjust time / temp accordingly for your oven
11. if you do the knife / toothpick test , it should come out with moist crumbs , not clean
12. cool completely before cutting into squares
13. for vegetarian omit the marshmallows
14. for double recipe , bake in 9x12 pan and add 5 minutes to baking time
demonstrations.review: Delicious. Nothing more to say. Rich chocolate taste, smooth texture. Serve warm with Ice Cream to make new friends lol

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chicken drumsticks pierre

this is a very easy recipe for a chicken dish that will suit people who like their chicken spicy, but not too hot. served on a bed of rice, it is colorful and elegant enough for company. update:  i suggest that you not substitute regular mustard for dry mustard. regular mustard is made by mixing dry mustard with a substantial amount of vinegar and will completely change the flavor of the dish.

1. mix together the flour , salt and pepper
2. dust the drumsticks with the seasoned flour
3. melt the butter in a skillet with a lid
4. brown the chicken over medium heat on all sides
5. remove the chicken from the pan and drain on absorbent paper
6. in the same pan , combine the tomatoes thru hot pepper sauce
7. bring to a boil
8. reduce the heat and return the chicken to the pan
9. cover and simmer about 45 minutes
10. serve with pan juice
11. good over white or brown rice
demonstrations.review: Tender, juicy, and very flavorful. Great dish! Followed directions to the T except for the celery seed which i didn't have on hand so in my mind celery salt was next best thing. lol. Still tasted awesome.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
ranch chicken thighs

needed a quick & easy weeknight meal. this is adapted from an old taste of home magazine. the chicken is tasty & juicy, with a nice crunchy crust. you won't miss the skin!  
eta -- some say this is too bland.  the ranch dressing is not enough seasoning.  i do add season salt to taste (nature's seasonings) to the bread crumb mixture for more flavor.  hopefully as a cook, you will know what to add to suit you and your family's taste.

1. in a shallow bowl , combine crumbs , parmesan cheese , cornmeal , italian seasoning , and seasoned salt
2. dip chicken into salad dressing , then coat with crumb mixture
3. place chicken in a greased 13x9 baking dish
4. bake , uncovered , at 375 degrees for 45 minutes or until juices run clear
demonstrations.review: Good tasting recipe. Fell just short of loving it. Really liked it though, so did the family. Tip: Save yourself some time and get the thighs without skin to start with (I spent about 20 mins skinning and trimming fat)

target.recipe_text:
granny s pancakes

this is the way my granny made pancakes. all the grandchildren had to have them when visiting. we sometimes have them for supper with good ole pan sausage!

1. sift flour , baking powder , salt and sugar in a large bowl
2. mix in milk , egg , melted butter and vanilla until smooth
3. heat lightly oiled griddle over medium high heat
4. pour about 1 / 4 cup for each pancake
5. brown on both sides
target.review:
Update: I've make these fairly often now, and each time I make them I always use a different amount of milk sometimes less sometimes more to get the right consistence. And sometimes the 1 1/2c. is perfect. So I just adjust accordingly. Still yummy every time though.

So VERY VERY good....I've never been able to make a good pancake (I end up with stonecakes) and I finally suceeded. My 3 year old was eating his and called from the table "Mommy these are really good". I hadn't yet tried them but he was right they really were good. I did follow TGirl,RN advice about using less milk I only used 1c. of milk and they were the perfect consistancy, for me anyway. Will totally make these again. Thanks so much for such an easy and tasty recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
low carb cheesecake mousse

this dessert keeps you on the straight and narrow with your low carb diet and is actually very refreshing. try different flavors, like cranberry.

1. melt sugar free jello in boiling water
2. stir well to dissolve and cool slightly
3. beat softened cream cheese until smooth and stir in cooled jello
4. lightly fold in heavy cream until well mixed
5. pour into serving dishes and put in fridge to chill at least 3 hours
demonstrations.review: Finally a low carb dessert that tastes good! Just a little advice, I mixed up my recipes while I was making it, I used 1/2c. water intsead of the 1/4c. like it called for. When you use 1/2c. it turns more into a firm jello. So next time I will for sure only use a 1/4c. of water. Thanx for the idea.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crustless cheeseburger quiche

i created this from another recipe i found here on zaar, only i modified it to be lower in carbs.

1. brown ground beef and onion powder in a large skillet over medium heat , drain off fat
2. mix together eggs , cream , mayonnaise , garlic powder , pepper and shredded cheddar cheese
3. put browned beef into a 9 inch pie plate , pour remaining ingredients over the beef
4. place in a preheated 350 degree oven and bake for 40-45 minutes
demonstrations.review: very tasty for someone who is low carbing, and my DH liked it too. I added some crumbled bacon to the groundbeef and used real onions instead of powder (didn't have any on hand). Definate winner.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
anytime slushy punch

my mother-in-law makes this punch for christmas. the kids love it. it's easy to make, no cooking required. you can triple the batch and have it in the freezer for any special occasion.also good for weddings,baby showers, superbowl parties or a cool drink in the summer.

1. in large bowl or pot mix first three ingredients together until dissolved
2. stir in frozen lemonade and pineapple juice
3. place in two freezer bags and freeze over night
4. take out of freezer two hours before serving time
5. place one bag in punch bowl and add half of ginger ale
6. break up big chunks of frozen mixture
7. punch will become slushy
8. ready to serve
demonstrations.review: Totally Awesome...I made it for my son's 1st Birthday. There wasn't a drop left, and everyone wanted the recipe. I loved this punch and so did the birthday Boy!!

target.recipe_text:
puffed cauliflower cheese

this is a wonderful souffle-like dish that is so easy. it is one of the first dishes that i ever made that actually came out looking like the picture in the book.

1. preheat oven to 400 degrees
2. wash cauliflower
3. remove stalk end
4. cut into quarters
5. remove hard stalk
6. divide into florets
7. cook in boiling salted water until tender
8. drain
9. heat butter in pan
10. add flour
11. stir over low heat 2 minutes
12. remove from heat
13. add milk gradually
14. stir until smooth
15. return to heat
16. stir until boiling
17. add salt , pepper and most of bread crumbs
18. stir in egg yolks , cheese and cauliflower
19. adjust seasonings to taste
20. beat egg whites until stiff
21. fold into mixture
22. put into greased ovenproof dish
23. sprinkle with remaining crumbs
24. bake in preheated 400 degree oven about 30 minutes , until well risen and brown
target.review: We were leery about this dish as it was the first time we'd tried a souffle.  However, it turned out very well.  The taste was wonderful, light yet creamy. The presentation was impressive too! This dish is good enough for a dinner party. We will make this again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
double layer pumpkin pie

this recipe comes from the kraft people. it sounded so good i just had to share.

1. mix cream cheese , 1 tablespoon milk and sugar in large bowl with wire whisk until smooth
2. gently stir in whipped topping
3. spread on bottom of crust
4. pour 1 cup cold milk into large bowl
5. add pumpkin , pudding mixes and spices
6. beat with wire whisk 2 minutes
7. the mixture will be thick
8. spread over cream cheese layer
9. refrigerate 4 hours or until set
10. garnish with additional whipped topping and chocolate-dipped pecan halves
11. store in the refrigerator until just before serving
demonstrations.review: This was a big hit at our holiday party.  Even the people who don't like pumpkin enjoyed this thoroughly.  It was easy to make and a welcome twist on the traditional pumpkin pie.  I was out of cloves but it didn't adversely impact the flavor of the pie.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
noodles romanoff

a very good side of noodles. i add a sauted chicken breast and salad, that's dinner!
