1. combine sour cream , 1 / 4 cup cheese , chives , salt , pepper and garlic
2. stir butter into hot noodles
3. stir in the sour cream mixture
4. arrange on platter , sprinkle with remaining cheese
demonstrations.review: The dish, as prepared above, was disappointing.  The sour cream taste was overwhelming.  After tasting it I added a more butter and grated cheese.  It improved the taste a little.  Next time I'll use less sour cream, more garlic and cheese.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kabak mcveri  turkish zucchini fritters

fritters are very popular in the middle east. they are eaten hot or at room temperature as a vegetable side dish or a meze. it couldn’t be simpler to make, but you can dress it up with optional garnishes of black olives, tomatoes, or hard-boiled egg. the perfect use for small, sweet new zucchini. serve alone or with a creamy garlic-lemon yogurt sauce for a perfect complement to any spicy or grilled foods that call for a cooling accompaniment.

1. grate the zucchini and place in a colander
2. sprinkle with salt and let drain for 30 minutes
3. squeeze out moisture and pat with paper towels
4. place the zucchini in a bowl and add the green and yellow onions , dill , parsley , cheese , eggs , flour and salt and pepper to taste
5. mix well
6. in a large saut pan over medium-high heat , pour in oil to a depth of inch
7. when the oil is hot , drop the batter by heaping tablespoonfuls into the pan , allow space in between fritters
8. fry for 2 minutes on the fist side , then turn to brown on the second side for about 3 minutes
9. using a slotted spatula transfer to paper towels or newspaper to drain
10. repeat with remaining batter
demonstrations.review: Absolutely fabulous.  My family loved them.  I made as directed and servered with the Creamy Cucumber Dip (Recipe #29455). We will be making this again!! Thanks for a great recipe.

target.recipe_text:
spicy indian grilled chicken

contrary to many indian dishes, this comes together quickly. great on the grill for a change.

1. combine all marinade ingredients well
2. coat chicken pieces in marinade paste
3. marinate from 1 hour , or up to overnight in the refrigerator
4. grill over medium coals until browned , about 15 minutes each side
target.review: Very good Indian-inspired dish and very quick. I used red chilli powder in place of the cayenne and half-and-half for the yogurt. I could only marinate the thighs for 2 hrs. I baked them in 350 oven for 45 mins. Next time I'll marinate them overnight. Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chicken and broccoli thai curry

this recipe started from the back of a thai kitchen curry paste jar. a few modifications and i lost my main reason for wanting to go out for thai. now we can have it whenever we want in the comfort of home. use chicken or beef or eliminate the meat and use your favorite vegetables. this is a versatile and tasty recipe.

1. in a medium saucepan combine curry paste and coconut milk and heat
2. just before boiling , reduce heat and simmer for 5 minutes
3. add remaining ingredients and simmer for 10-15 minutes
4. serve over freshly cooked rice
demonstrations.review: I love how quick this recipe was. Next time, I'll cut the fish sauce down to 2-2.5 T. Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chicken thighs oven fried

for subtle variation, add some fresh herbs or spicy paprika. simple and delicious. turns out perfect every time. the flavour comes from the combination of bread crumbs and potato flakes.

1. preheat oven to 400f
2. wash chicken , pat dry and set aside
3. in bowl beat half and half with egg
4. in another bowl combine bread crumbs , potato flakes , garlic salt and pepper
5. dip chicken in egg mixture and then in bread crumb mixture
6. sprinkle with butter and oil
7. bake at 400f for 35 minutes
8. increase heat to 450f and bake an additional 15 minutes
demonstrations.review: I was a bit skeptical, as I'm a fried chicken fanatic.. but I'm sold on this. I don't have seasoned bread crumbs, so I used plain + 1/2 t garlic powder + 1/2 t onion powder + some italian seasoning. I also used chicken drumsticks, egg white instead of the whole egg, and no butter. With these modifications, I'll add more salt next time. Thank you!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
frijoles negros  cuban black beans

ay caramba, these are good!

1. fry the onion and pepper in a little oil
2. add the garlic and saute a little
3. introduce a little of the bean liquid until all previous ingredients are soft
4. add the beans with the remaining liquid
5. add spices and simmer about 30 minutes
6. add the vinegar just before serving
7. these are quite good when served over a bed of rice seasoned with just lime
demonstrations.review: This recipe tastes just as great as the restaurant's closeby.. very easy to make. Great as leftovers!

target.recipe_text:
betty erlich s potato cake   gluten free

this is a polish recipe and it's gluten free, tastes like a baked cheese cake.from epicure , the melbourne age, written by rita erlich.

1. preheat oven to 175 cel
2. mash the potatoes throughly while warm
3. use a potato ricer , if possible because there must be no lumps at all
4. allow to cool
5. mix in eggs yolks , ground almonds and lemon juice and grated lemon peel
6. beat the egg whites until nearly stiff , then add the castor sugar and beat again
7. fold beaten egg whites into the potaot mixture
8. pour into a lightly buttered 19cm-20cm round or square cake tin and bake for about 40 minutes , or until a toothpick inserted in the centre of the cake comes out dry
target.review: tried this for passover, as I am gluten free and wanted something for everyone. I liked it, my hubby hated it and the others thought it was good, but not great,  I think next time I'll add some more lemon peel and perhaps a bit more juice to pepp it up a bit. Perhaps whipping an egg white, and adding a bit of Ammaretto would be good too. also I used a whizzer to blend the potatoes, I think that was a mistake, as it probably made the spuds a bit gooey, where as a ricer would have left them fluffier. Wasn't quite like cheesecake for me, but I did enjoy it.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
yeast free bread rolls

my sister is not allowed to eat yeast and sourdough so she can't have regular rolls for breakfast. we were very happy when we found this recipe in a leaflet from "dr.oetker". the rolls taste very good and are very versatile. you can either have them with sesame, sunflower seeds, pumpkin seeds etc. if you want to put something hearty onto them. or you can add some sugar and raisins to the dough and eat them with honey or jam.

1. preheat oven to 180c
2. in a big bowl mix flour and baking powder
3. add curd cheese , salt , milk and oil and quickly knead into a soft dough using the dough hooks of your hand mixer
4. don't overmix or the dough will become sticky
5. blend in desired ingredient by hand
6. shape dough into approximately 10 rolls and place them on a paper-lined baking tray
7. cut a cross into the top of each roll , brush with a little milk and sprinkle with whatever you like
8. bake for about 20 minutes
demonstrations.review: haven't tried this yet, and don't believe I will as it reads as I am yeast free also. You should be careful as cheese and yoghurt all have cultures in them and if you need to watch yeast, that's no good.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
gluten   yeast free italian bread

i actually adapted this recipe from gluten free girl's gluten free french bread recipe. i am ellergic to yeast and i preferred the bread with brown rice flour. i also make it in a bread loaf pan instead of two small skinny loaves. i love this recipe!!! i also used it to make bread pudding and it was perfect. i hope you all enjoy it too.

1. in a bowl , place flours , xanthan gum , salt and sugar
2. blend with mixer on low or by hand
3. add the butter , egg whites , and vinegar
4. beat on high or stir in by hand until well mixed
5. pour batter into a buttered bread pan
6. if desired , brush with melted butter
7. preheat oven to 400 degrees
8. bake for 40 to 45 minutes
9. remove from pan to cool
demonstrations.review:
tried this after I had read the reviews, and made a few changes of my own.
I use a (purchased) bread flour mix for baking,cut the egg down to 1.5 whites and used 3tsp of baking powderand olive oil instead of butter. Also I have found that if using a loaf pan, the smaller and narrower, the better the loaf will rise. I have made this 3 times, using flours as described in the recipe and also with brown flour mix, each time I bake it is better. Next time I will use sparkling water instead of tap water, to give it a bit more lift.
this makes great sandwiches and toast also keeps a few days.
Great recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
gluten free tortillas

i found this recipe at lesleycooks.tripod.com where she has a gluten free category.  i had posted a request for tortilla recipes on zaar because i needed something like a wrap i could make up for my girl's school lunches.  after trying a couple i was kindly given, i found this one had a great taste and texture my kids loved.  while it may not strictly be a tortilla it meets the purpose.  they freeze well if you separate them with greaseproof paper or baking paper.  do not be put off by the runny mixture, and do leave it to stand for 30 minutes before cooking.  i doubled the mixture so i only had to make them once a fortnight - it made up 7 large ones, but the number will depend on the pan you use.

1. place the flours and salt in a mixing bowl and mix together thoroughly
2. add the egg and beat until smooth then slowly beat in the water
3. cover with clingfilm and refrigerate for 30 minutes
4. heat a medium sized frying pan until very hot then brush with oil
5. make sure pan is still ver hot , pour in enough batter to just ocver the bottom of the pan
6. cook over a high heat until the bottom of the tortilla is golden brown and the edges begin to curl up
7. flip the tortilla over cook the other side for 30 seconds only
8. transfer tortilla on to greaseproof paper and repeat with remaining batter
9. refrigerate or freeze until ready to use
demonstrations.review: excellent recipe, finally something that works and tastes good. Not really a tortilla, but works great as a wrap, and so easy to handle compared to our other wraps, (doesn't crumble). I used them to make blintzes. Used dairy free 'cream cheese and fried filled, rolled wraps in marg. then sprinkled cinnamon sugar on them. REALLY DELICIOUS!  thanks for a geat recipe !!!

target.recipe_text:
cilantro lime mayonnaise

this zesty mayonnaise is a great alternative to traditional tartar sauce for almost any kind of seafood.  this recipe comes from bon appetit.

1. blend first 5 ingredients in food processor until cilantro is chopped
2. add mayonnaise and process just to blend
3. season with salt and pepper and refrigerate until ready to use
target.review: Delicious!  Like to die for.  Complex flavors blend beautifully with taste that lingers and expands.   I used cayenne rather than hot sauce and lemon juice, not lime.  I didn't measure anything, but followed the principal idea.  Terrific!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kombucha   no  alcohol lime mint  bubbly

i have just discovered "kombucha", and i love it! it is said to support- digestion, metabolism, immune system, appetite control, weight control, liver function, body akalinity, anti- aging, cell integrity, healthy skin and hair. this is from wikopedia- "kombucha is the western name for sweetened tea or tisane that has been fermented by a macroscopic solid mass of microorganisms called a "kombucha colony," usually consisting principally of acetobacter-species and yeast cultures. it has gained much popular support within many communities, mentioned by talk show hosts and celebrities. the increase in popularity can be seen by the many commercial brands coming onto the retail market and thousands of web pages about this fermented beverage". you can read more there at- http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/kombucha . it will even tell you how to make kombucha. i bought mine at a health food store, but i am soon going to make it myself. the drink i bought is called "synergy". i bought the gingerade, the divine grape, and the original. i love the flavored ones and can't wait to get other flavors to try. i believe the grape flavored can be used in recipes called for wine if you don't use alcohol because it has the flavor of wine to me. you can use any flavor in this drink, but the ginger one was recommended. it may be a little too tart to some people so just add a little more mint. i hope you like it as much as i do.

1. put the limes in a shaker
2. add the agave and muttle
3. add ice along with 4 or 5 mint leaves
4. add kombucha to make the shaker 3 / 4's full
5. top it off with the sparkling water to the top line of the shaker cup
6. do not strain
7. just pour into your glass and enjoy !
demonstrations.review: I'm new to the world of fermentation, altho' it's ancient and world-wide.  Still in "discovery" mode for flavorings.  It's a fine example of "Kitchen Science".  Thanks for promoting this exotica.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
ginger pear chutney

great way to use up pears, including recent windfalls as they've got to be peeled and chopped anyway. nice with pork or as a condiment with curry. very gingery.  it gets better as it ages.

1. in large preserving kettle or dutch oven , combine all ingredients and bring to a boil , stirring frequently
2. reduce heat and simmer , uncovered , for about 1 1 / 2 hours , continuing to stir occasionally
3. remove from heat and pour into hot , sterilized jars , leaving 1 / 8 inch headspace
4. add lids and rings and process jars in a boiling water bath in a canner for 15 minutes
5. take the canner off the heat and let water stop boiling before removing jars
6. carefully remove jars and let sit
7. as they cool , the jars will seal themselves with a"pop"
8. label , and store in cool , dry , dark place
9. to prepare the jars , i first wash them in the dishwasher , or in the sink with very hot , soapy water , then rinse them well and put them in a warm oven , taking the jars out one or two at a time when filling them
10. i soak the lids in very hot water and put them immediately from the hot water onto the filled jars , making sure the rims of the jars are clean , then add the rings and screw them on the jars just finger tight
demonstrations.review: So simple, easy, basic! Easy to just whip it up.  I changed nothing, but qualify that I used white raisins, and because they seem sweeter than dark raisins, reduced their amount.  Thanks, Kathleen!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pickled watermelon rind  just to make you homesick

from the us regional cookbook, chicago culinary arts institute, 1947.  for the most current canning guidelines, please go to http://www.uga.edu/nchfp/how/can_home.html.

1. pare rind and all pink edges from the watermelon
2. cut into 1-inch squares or fancy shapes as desired
3. cover with brine made by mixing 1 / 4 cup of salt with1 quart cold water
4. soak overnight
5. drain brine
6. cover with cold water and cook until fork tender , about 10 minutes
7. drain
8. tie spices in a cheesecloth bag and remove before rind is bottled
9. make a hot pickling solution of remaining ingredients and spices , add drained rind and boil rapidly ntil rind becomes clear
10. fill sterilized jars
11. adjust jar lids as in fresh-pack dills
12. process in boiling water bath for 5 minutes
13. set jars upright , several inches apart , on a wire rack to cool
demonstrations.review: I appreciate that this recipe (compared to others I've tried) dilutes Vinegar and adds lemon. I prefer the taste result of using brown sugar, not white. Commonly is cinnamon and cloves - very compatible, but allspice is also a "natural".  Save that leftover juice - works wonderfully with pork.

target.recipe_text:
the best amish meatloaf recipe

after traveling in eastern ohio and eating many different "amish-style" meatloaves, i finally asked for this wonderful meatloaf recipe.  this one is not as sweet as the typical amish recipe and has some garlic flavoring in it.  we love it!!

1. mix first 7 ingredients throughly together and pack into a loaf pan
2. next put the strips of bacon on top and bake for an hour at 350f degrees
3. while waiting , mix the sauce ingredients together
4. after the hour is up , pour and smooth the sauce onto the meatloaf and cook another 15 to 20 minutes
5. i have sometimes added 1 / 2 teaspoon of garlic salt instead of the salt to the sauce mixture and that is also delicious !
target.review:
I wish I could give this a million stars.  I'm always trying different meatloaf recipes because I've NEVER been satisfied with what I have tasted.  Well I will look no longer.  This is THE ONLY meatloaf recipe allowed in my house.  Thanks for posting.
ChefRaylene

demonstrations.recipe_text:
double banana chocolate chip upside down cake

serve this delicious cake warm topped with whipped cream yummmmmm! make certain to grease your pan very well so that the cake and banana/brown sugar mixture removes easily when inverted onto a plate.

1. set oven to 350 degrees
2. butter an 8-inch non-stick square cake pan
3. sprinkle the 3 tablespoons butter pieces into the baking pan , then sprinkle evenly with brown sugar
4. slice the whole bananas crosswise about 1 / 2-inch thick slices , then arrange the slices in a single layer in the pan over the brown sugar
5. drizzle evenly with orange juice
6. in a small bowl whisk together flour , baking powder , baking soda , cinnamon and nutmeg
7. in a large bowl using an electric mixer , beat the 1 / 4 cup softened butter with 3 / 4 cup sugar until well blended
8. beat in the egg until blended , then beat in the 1 / 2 cup mashed bananas
9. add in the floured mixture and buttermilk alternately , beating at low speed until just completely incorporated
10. mix in the chocolate chips
11. spread the batter over the sliced bananas in the pan
12. bake for about 40-45 minutes
13. cool on wire rack for 15 minutes , then run a knife between the cake and pan sides
14. invert a platter over cake , holding both together invert again , then carefully lift the pan off
15. serve warm with whipped cream
16. delicious !
demonstrations.review:
Tonight was a total Kittencal dinner except for the vegetables.  We had the Chicken Wellington with Creamy Mushroom Sauce, with the Easy Parmesan Potato Rounds and this for dessert.   I really love your recipes.  Keep posting them.  

ChefRaylene

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crab appetizer  maryland

crabs are such a part of maryland life and maryland way....that a lot of fellow zaar members from the maryland, delaware, and virgina coast will have a "bucket load" of crab recipes. and all of them are divine! you can fix a different crab dish or appetizer every night of the week for a full year. crabs are not grown on the farm. but we do have a special supplier to us called, "gibby's seafood market" that sell their steamed crabs from the night before at a reduced rate. now you have to get there soon in the morning right after they open but those crabs are seasoned with "old bay seasoning" (a staple of maryland, made in maryland) and oh so good. anyway, whenever there is a get together be it winter, spring, summer, fall there is always a crab dish. this ia a good appetizer to serve, people just grab with their hands and devour, making sure they have licked the last bit off their hands or even plates. go ahead, try it, i promise there won't be much left for you. have fun add or subtract whatever you see fit.

1. mix together ingredients except crab meat to make a thick mixture
2. carefully fold crab meat into mixture either with a your hands , or a spatula , just until mixed
3. do not over mix
4. over fill each mini phyllo shell with the crab meat ,
5. sprinkle lightly with paprika , for decoration
6. bake at 350f for 25-30 minutes or until bubbly
demonstrations.review:
Super terrific.  Wonderful, easy to make and totally yummy.  I used imitation crab and the Athens shells.  Thanks for posting.

ChefRaylene

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chicken wellington  puff pastry wrapped chicken

this is not at all hard to put together, it's an amazing dish to serve to dinner guests and i have done so many times over the years and have always receive rave reviews from everyone at my table and you will too! --- to save time saute the onion, garlic and mushrooms up to a day ahead,  the cream cheese and dijon mustard mixture may be increased slightly -- i always serve this with recipe#149547 drizzled over or on the side of the plate, you will *love* this!

1. season the chicken breast with seasoning salt and pepper on all sides
2. heat butter and oil in a skillet
3. brown the breasts on all sides until almost completely cooked through
4. transfer to a plate
5. to the same skillet add in onions , garlic and sliced mushrooms
6. saute until the mushrooms lose their moisture and the onions are tender
7. stir in parsley
8. on a floured surface , roll out each puff pastry sheet to a 14-inch square
9. cut into four even 7-inch squares
10. place each breast over each puff pastry square
11. set oven to 375 degrees
12. in a small bowl combine the softened cream cheese with mustard , then spread over each breast
13. then top with about 2-3 tablespoons mushroom / onion mixture
14. brush the edges of each pastry square with water
15. wrap pastry around the chicken breast , pressing edges to seal tightly
16. place seam-side down on greased baking sheets
17. brush the tops with egg wash
18. bake for about 20 minutes , or until puffed and golden brown
19. serve with mushroom sauce over the wellington or on the side of the plate
20. delicious !
demonstrations.review:
Terrific!!!!!!  Again I don't think I have tried a recipe of yours that hasn't been great.  Made for a dinner pary tonight and it was a hit.  Served with the Creamy Mushroom Sauce as suggested.  The sauce itself was excellent.  Thanks for posting.

ChefRaylene

target.recipe_text:
ultra rich hot chocolate

home made and ultra good! if this recipe proves to be too rich for you, simply add more milk to adjust it to your preference.

1. bring milk , cocoa powder and sugar to simmer in heavy large saucepan over medium-high heat , whisking frequently
2. add chocolate
3. whisk until melted and smooth
4. add salt
5. bring to simmer , whisking constantly until frothy
6. ladle into 4 mugs
7. sprinkle with marshmallows or dollop of whipped cream
8. makes 4 servings
target.review:
A must try :D
I smile thinking I'm gonna treat myself with another cup next saturday night too.
My DH had his with a dash of brandy and gave it 10 stars

demonstrations.recipe_text:
zucchini chocolate orange cake

awesome cake of mexican origin.
very moist because it's chock full of zucchini, and it has the most delicious glaze on top.
hope you enjoy!

1. to make the cake:
2. preheat oven to 350 degrees f
3. grease and flour bundt pan
4. in a medium bowl , sift flour , cocoa , baking powder , baking soda , salt and cinnamon
5. set aside
6. in a large bowl , cream butter and sugar until fluffy
7. add eggs , 1 teaspoon vanilla and milk to the butter mixture
8. stir in dry ingredients and mix until well blended
9. fold in zucchini , orange zest and nuts
10. pour into a greased and floured bundt cake pan
11. bake at 350 degrees f for 50 to 60 minutes , or until a toothpick inserted into center of cake comes out clean
12. allow to cool
13. to make the glaze:
14. in a small bowl mix together sugar , orange juice and vanilla
15. invert cake onto serving dish , then drizzle glaze over
demonstrations.review:
This is the best zucchini cake ever. 
I never seem to be able to cream butter, sugar eggs and milk properly so I simply put everything in a large bowl and mixed them well.
I also added 2 Tbs of oil 'cause sometimes batter made with butter alone can turn out to be kind of dry and doesn't keep well. I don't know if it was really necessary but it didn't hurt the cake.
I divided the batter in half. The first one I made according to the recipe with orange zest and nuts, the second I made with lemon zest and raisins (and lemon glaze). 
They were both delicious. A big, big hit with everybody that tasted it.
Thanks for the recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cheese enchilada chowder

from bhg. a slow-cooker chowder.

1. add the black beans , tomatoes , frozen corn , onion , bell pepper , and jalapeno pepper to a 4 quart slow-cooker
2. stir to combine
3. in a mixing bowl , add the enchilada sauce and cream soup
4. whisk together
5. gradually whisk in the milk until mixture is smooth
6. pour over vegetables in slow-cooker
7. cover and cook on low heat for 6-8 hours
8. add cheese and stir until melted
9. ladle hot soup into individual serving bowls and top with sour cream , guacamole and broken tortilla chips if desired
demonstrations.review:
I didn't take the time to review this recipe before. It was an absolute hit with all the family from the first time I made it (about 6 months ago). Even my mother who can't cook and can't follow a recipe found this one to be easy and absolutely delicious.
What I really love about it is there are no potatoes in the recipe 'cause I hate them. 
So 5 stars or more for this recipe that both me and my mom have it at least once a month. It's a big hit with everybody!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
absolutely the best amish beef stew

this is just what its name implies...the absolute best beef stew ever. it is wonderful in the colder weather and really warms you up. i got the basic recipe from an old amish cookbook and tweeked it a bit. my family loves it with home baked bread, so i always make amish white bread, recipe #26526 to go along with it.

1. melt shortening over high heat in a large pot or dutch oven
2. add beef cubes and brown over medium heat , stirring occasionally , about 15-20 minutes
3. add onions , boiling water , salt , lemon juice , sugar , worcestershire sauce , pepper , paprika , allspice and cloves
4. simmer , tightly covered , for about 2 hours , stirring occasionally
5. add vegetables and simmer another 30 minutes , or until tender
6. if this is the case , add more water to barely cover ingredients
7. mix cold water and flour together and blend until smooth
8. push meat and veggies to the side of the pot and add flour mixture slowly , incorporating into liquid
9. when gravy thickens , stir all ingredients gently to distribute gravy evenly
10. simmer another 5 or 10 minutes and enjoy !
demonstrations.review:
This is the first time I make a stew myself. And I must say I have missed a great deal of kitchen goodness in not trying it before. 
Incredibly simple to make and such a great taste to greet the cold days.
Thanks Karen for a perfect recipe.
I did everything exactly as directed and it came out wonderful. If I could give it more stars I would certainly do. 
If you could smell it too right now...

target.recipe_text:
t s golden parmesan potatoes

these are my husbands favorite potatoes! they are so good!  we love them with any kind of meat or fish.  try them and i bet they will be a family favorite at your house too! easy to fix!

1. preheat oven to 375 and melt butter in a 9x13 inch pan in oven
2. watch carefully and do not burn
3. remove pan when butter is melted and set aside
4. combine flour , parmesan cheese and bread crumbs in a shallow dish
5. cut potatoes lengthwise into wedges
6. moisten in water and coat with flour mixture , making sure potatoes are well coated
7. arrange potato wedges skin side down to start , in pan with melted butter
8. bake for 15 minutes , then turn wedges over on one side and bake for 15 minutes more
9. turn potatoes one last time to the last side and bake for 15 minutes or until potatoes are tender and golden all over
10. use salt to season
11. serve immediately and enjoy !
target.review:
Love this one, my DH keeps asking for me to make it. I baked at a little higher temp(200c)and they came out crispier.
Leah

demonstrations.recipe_text:
neufchatel cheese ball

perfect for entertaining - all the work is done 2 days in advance, you just need to serve it on the day.
if neufchatel cheese is unavailable any cream cheese can be used as a substitute.
a mild pepperoni or salami can be substituted for the cabana.

1. leave cheese to soften to room temperature
2. finely chop cabana and spring onion and combine with softened cheese
3. roll into ball and roll in sweet paprika
4. refridgerate for 2 days
demonstrations.review: Made this for Christmas Day. My son's fiance  calls it the "Evil Cheeseball" as we all kept nibbling at it. I had to remove it from the table so appetites would not be spoilt for xmas lunch. This is so easy to make and gets a great response.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
the easiest  bestest focaccia bread ever

this focaccia bread is sooo easy and tastes wonderful! tons of herbs and seasonings, and tons of flavor!! great to make sandwiches with! you can alter the toppings to your liking. i have made this with caramelized onions and sliced tomato on top...mmmmmm!!!

1. mix the yeast and water in a small bowl
2. let proof for 10 minutes
3. in large bowl , stir together flour , salt , sugar , garlic powder , oregano , thyme , basil , and black pepper
4. add the yeast mix and vegetable oil to the dry ingredients and combine
5. when dough has pulled together , turn out onto lightly floured surface and knead until smooth and elastic
6. lightly oil a large bowl , place dough in bowl , and turn to coat with oil
7. cover with damp cloth and let rise in warm place 25 minutes
8. preheat oven to 425 degrees
9. punch dough down , place on greased baking sheet
10. pat dough into 1 / 2-inch thick rectangle
11. using your knuckle , make indentations in the dough about 1 / 2-inch apart , then prick dough with fork
12. brush top with olive oil , then sprinkle with parmesan and mozzarella cheese
13. bake for 13-15 minutes until golden brown
demonstrations.review: How good is this? I mixed it in the bread machine. First I put in dry ingredients then wet ingredients. I chose to put the cheeses in the machine as well. When the machine had finished mixing I followed your directions. End result, a perfect foccacia. I served mine split in half, with fried cubed chicken and melted cheese on top. I will not buy the store bought foccacia again. Thanks for a great recipe

demonstrations.recipe_text:
bacon wrapped chicken  oamc

this is another great way to make something great ahead of time to thaw as needed or eat right now with little effort!

1. flatten chicken to 1 / 2" thickness
2. spread 3 tablespoons cream cheese over each chicken piece
3. dot with butter and sprinkle with salt
4. roll up
5. wrap each with a bacon strip
6. place , seam side down , in a greased pan
7. bake , uncovered , at 400f for 35-40 minutes or until juices run clear
8. broil 6 inches from the heat for 5 minutes or until bacon is crisp
9. if you are making these ahead for future use , freeze these uncooked on a cookie sheet in your freezer
10. when solid , wrap and put in a ziplock bag or vacuum seal desired quantities
11. to cook from frozen state , thaw before cooking and follow directions above
demonstrations.review: This recipe was a great change from our usual chicken dishes. I cooked mine in individual ramekins with the bacon tucked over the chicken. The bacon crisped up nicely and the chicken was very moist. I think this will be a regular on out menu.

target.recipe_text:
crock pot pork tenderloin with apples

this is such an easy recipe to make - put it in the crock pot & forget it. i like to add 1 tsp chili flakes. add salt if you wish.  you may use country style ribs or loin chops but you must trim off all the fat. i find that sometimes cooking too long in the crock pot dries out the meat and found after 4 hours this was just right then turned it to keep warm for 2 more hours - it was wonderful.  i found this recipe on the internet

1. put all the ingredients into the crock pot , mix
2. turn to low
3. cook for 4- 6 hours
target.review: I made this for a dinner I had for my parents and my husband and they all loved it!  I, on the other hand, didn't care too much for it.  I'm sure it's my own personal taste though.  Something about the apples with the pork...but again everyone loved it!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
oven fried chicken chimichangas

a fast and healthier way to serve chimichangas than the traditional deep fried. these are very good, and you may dress them up to you own preference. i like to serve with green chile sauce sometimes instead of the picante sauce.

1. mix chicken , picante sauce or salsa , cumin , oregano , cheese and onions
2. place about 1 / 4 cup of the chicken mixture in the center of each tortilla
3. fold opposite sides over filling
4. roll up from bottom and place seam-side down on a baking sheet
5. brush with melted margarine
6. bake at 400f for 25 minutes or until golden
7. garnish with additional cheese and green onion and serve salsa on the side
demonstrations.review: So good!  I put carrots and celery in this instead of a lot of the spices because I didn't have them on hand.  I used taco seasoning too.  These came out great!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
no bake chocolate oatmeal cookies

these simply melt in you mouth, and are so very easy to make!

1. measure out nuts and oatmeal in a large mixing bowl
2. combine sugar , cocoa , milk and butter in a saucepan and gently bring to a boil
3. boil mixture for about 1 minute
4. remove from heat and add peanut butter and vanilla and mix to combine
5. pour hot mixture over nuts and oatmeal and mix well
6. drop onto waxed or parchment paper
7. i made about 2 inch cookies , but feel free to make them smaller
8. press together to flatten a bit , and to prevent them from falling apart
9. cookies will harden slightly in about 5 to 10 minutes , and they'll be ready to enjoy !
demonstrations.review: Fantastic!!!  These have been my favorite type of cookie since I was a kid and this tastes just like it should.  Thank you!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
real red lobster cheese biscuits

i changed a previously posted recipe.  we ate at red lobster 2 days ago and this recipe duplicates their biscuits really well.

1. place grated cheese in freezer at least 30 minutes prior to the start of making the biscuits
2. heat oven to 400
3. melt butter and set aside
4. sift together bisquick , garlic powder and old bay seasoning
5. stir in milk , frozen cheddar cheese , parsley flakes and melted butter
6. drop dough by spoonfuls onto ungreased cookie sheet
7. bake 7-8 minutes
demonstrations.review: Very good!  I live in Alaska and we don't have a Red Lobster up here, so I didn't have anything to compare these to other than regular Bisquick biscuits.  I didn't have any parsley flakes or garlic powder, so I just used about 1/4 tsp of minced garlic instead and it worked out great!  I made these for a dinner I had for my parents and husband, and my father hates Bisquick biscuits, but he loved these!  I think it was the butter topping that did it for him.  I wish I could rate higher than 5 stars!

target.recipe_text:
cinnamon cream cheese roll ups

i found these in a magazine, and just had to try them. they are really different and very good! the kids were wild about these. try adding a dab of pineapple, or apricot jam.

1. flatten bread with a rolling pin
2. mix cream cheese , egg yolk , and powdered sugar
3. combine sugar and cinnamon
4. set aside
5. spread 1 t cheese mixture on each slice bread
6. roll up
7. dip in melted butter , then in cinnamon sugar
8. place on ungreased baking sheet
9. bake at 350f for 20 minutes , or until golden
target.review: Also wanted to say, I served these warm with a side of vanilla ice cream and they were perfect!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
easy snickers bar pie

this recipe is so easy. make it to take to a potluck and keep one at home for yourself! the cook time mentioned is the chill time in the fridge

1. in a large mixing bowl , beat cream cheese , sugar and peanut butter until creamy
2. stir in chopped candy bars
3. gently fold in the cool whip just until mixed
4. pour into crusts and refrigerate overnight
demonstrations.review: This was so simple and fantastic! My mom asked what was in it and I almost couldn't remember because everything so easy! We used a graham pie crusts and thought it was perfect. Didn't have time to wait overnight, just put it in the freezer for a few hours and it was great. Also, could add the chocolate "shell" on top if you wanted more chocolate. Great Recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
dad s best brisket

my dad knows how much i love this. thanks for the recipe.

1. center brisket on a large heavy piece of foil in a roaster
2. sprinkle with liquid smoke
3. sprinkle brisket with celery salt , garlic salt , onion salt , and pepper
4. fold sides of foil over to seal
5. refrigerate overnight
6. 6 1 / 2 hour before serving , open foil and season with salt , pepper , and worcestershire sauce
7. reseal and cook in a slow oven at 300 degrees for 5 hours
8. uncover and pour barbecue sauce over brisket
9. cook 1 additional hour , uncovered
10. let sit 20 minutes before slicing
demonstrations.review: Fantastic! I will be using this recipe over and over again, it was great! The only extra thing I did was  chop onion and put in slow cooker for about 2 hours, then I added the brisket and cooked on low all day. I also added garlic to the brisket, just because we love garlic. It was awesome! Thanks for adding it!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chicken pizzola

great looking chicken. looks like you fussed but you didn't. good with bread and a salad.

1. lightly grease a baking sheet
2. put breasts on the baking sheet
3. spread each with 1 tbsp tomato paste
4. combine ham , mushrooms , red pepper , tomato , garlic , onion and basil
5. spoon mixture over breasts
6. top with cheese
7. bake at 350f for 30 to 40 minutes or until chicken is cooked and cheese is golden
demonstrations.review: This was simple and fantastic! My husband loved it and thought it was even better reheated! I served it over pasta with a side salad. Yummm!!

target.recipe_text:
yes  virginia there is a great meatloaf

absolutely delicious meatloaf and sauce! those who claim they don't believe there can be such a thing as a great meatloaf will love this. based on a meatloaf given to me by a dear friend, virginia strehl, memphis, and leesburg, fla. nita holleman, 2000

1. meatloaf: combine meat loaf ingredients and place into a loaf baking dish
2. smooth out top
3. sauce: combine sauce ingredients and pour on top and sides of meatloaf
4. bake at 350f about 1 hour to 1 hour 15 minutes or until done
5. enjoy !
6. the addition of 1 or 2 teaspoons of kitchen bouquet makes this recipe very good
7. recipe should be"plump" from the addition of the milk or half & half
8. it should not be runny
9. a second batch of sauce served hot is good to serve with the meatloaf
10. nita's
11. it is wise to have some fat added to the deer -- especially to ground deer
12. maybe 25 % fat , , otherwise your results will be poor
13. i don't know about some of the other game meat some are using
14. please consult an expert
15. the recipe is delicious as it stands ! enjoy ! nita holleman
target.review: Very easy to make.  This is my go to recipe for meatloaf.  Everyone loves it.  I have used ground turkey and extra lean ground beef with excellent results.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
best ever banana cake with cream cheese frosting

this is one of (if not) the best banana cake i have ever tasted! i thought the oven temp of 275° sounded a little low, but this cake baked up (and rose) beautifully in my oven at this temp after pretty much exactly one hour. i do not know if the little "freezer trick" to this recipe is what ensured its moistness or not, but i did it, and it was exceptionally moist & delicious. would be interesting to see if it still came out as great if this step was skipped. all i know is that i followed this recipe exactly as stated (except that i had no buttermilk, so i subbed with a mix of lemon juice & milk) and i got exceptional results. so moist and yummy...a dense cake, similar in texture to a carrot cake... i personally would not call this frosted banana bread :o)  depending on the amount of frosting you like you can decide whether to half the recipe or not. i used the full recipe and had some leftover. i sprinkled on the chopped walnuts and threw this baby in the fridge and cut it the next day...to die for! i really liked it slightly chilled, but great at room temp too! it got better each day it sat, i always make this cake at least the day before i need or want it.  i was extremely pleased with this cake and will be making it over & over again!! so glad i came across this one!! (on another website).


(* * just to update the recipe, (based on some of the reviews), the baking time may vary based on individual ovens. it was right on for my oven, but some others have stated it has taken 1 hour 10 minutes, 1 hour 20 minutes, and my sister just informed me that it took 1 hour 30 minutes in her oven!!!!!)

1. preheat oven to 275f
2. grease and flour a 9 x 13 pan
3. in a small bowl , mix mashed banana with the lemon juice
4. set aside
5. in a medium bowl , mix flour , baking soda and salt
6. set aside
7. in a large bowl , cream 3 / 4 cup butter and 2 1 / 8 cups sugar until light and fluffy
8. beat in eggs , one at a time , then stir in 2 tsp vanilla
9. beat in the flour mixture alternately with the buttermilk
10. stir in banana mixture
11. pour batter into prepared pan and bake in preheated oven for one hour or until toothpick inserted in center comes out clean
12. remove from oven and place directly into the freezer for 45 minutes
13. this will make the cake very moist
14. for the frosting , cream the butter and cream cheese until smooth
15. beat in 1 teaspoon vanilla
16. add icing sugar and beat on low speed until combined , then on high speed until frosting is smooth
17. spread on cooled cake
18. sprinkle chopped walnuts over top of the frosting , if desired
demonstrations.review: This cake is fantastic!  Very moist and the frosting just makes the cake.  Delicious!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
melt in your mouth chicken breasts

the mayonnaise make these chicken breast very moist and tender--enjoy!

1. mix mayonnaise or yogurt , cheese and seasonings
2. spread mixture over chicken breast and place in baking dish
3. bake at 375f for 45 minutes
demonstrations.review: Wow!  What a great tasting chicken dish.  It comes out moist every time.  This is my families new favorite chicken dish.  I've made this several times and even made it for guests and get rave reviews.  Very flavorful.  The only thing I changed was to decrease the seasoning salt to 1 tsp.  It was a tad too salty for me.   Thank you for sharing.  Will definitely keep this one on the menu.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
creamy pink vodka sauce with penne

creamy,rich,and smooth vodka sauce. quick and easy! use a vodka that you like to drink, if you can't drink it you won't eat  this.

1. put the olive oil into the pan and add the onions and garlic
2. turn on the heat to medium-low and gently cook for a few minutes
3. add the red pepper flakes cook 1 minute add crushed tomatoes
4. raise the heat to medium and bring the mixture to a boil
5. add the vodka and a pinch of salt and pepper simmer uncovered for about 8 minutes over medium-low heat
6. add the cream and lower the heat , add drained pasta and toss in parsley
7. stir to coat well and grate a generous amount of parmesan into the pasta using our microplane grater
8. serve immediately sprinkled with more parmesan , and red pepper flakes
demonstrations.review: This recipe was excellent!  I did change a few things in the original recipe.  I added 1 Tb butter in addition to the olive oil for a little more flavor. Along with another clove of garlic (we love garlic!). I also increased the hot pepper flakes to a 1/2 tsp. As we like a little kick in our sauce.  I also added a 1/2 cup of chopped fresh basil and omitted one of the cans of crushed tomatoes. As it makes plenty.  Thanks for a great recipe!

target.recipe_text:
lemon basil shrimp

this is good done on the barbeque and can also be cooked using the grill. if you like basil you will like these prawns serve with some nice crusty bread. makes enough marinade for more then 12 prawns. marinating time not included.

1. place all the ingredients , except the prawns , in a shallow dish and mix well , taste or you want to add more mustard
2. add the prawns and toss to coat , cover , refrigerate for 1 hour
3. remove the prawns from the marinade and thread on skewers
4. cook over medium coals for 2-3 minutes on each side , basting with any remaining marinade from time to time
5. serve immediately
target.review: We really enjoyed this delicious shrimp last night.  I had seen the recipe on a thread about lemon recipes, and when I got to the market and found jumbo prawns on sale, I figured this was the day!  I got 31 shrimp from a 2 lb. bag of unpeeled "colosol" prawns.  I followed the directions as written, and they were moist and flavorful - and gone!  No leftovers here for the five of us.  The fresh basil is a must here in my opinion.  Thanks for a great treat.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s lemon cream cheese pie

a pie so good it is worthy of selling in a bakery!  prep time includes the refrigeration time --- see my recipe#66929

1. in a saucepan , combine sugar , cornstarch and pinch of salt
2. stir in water , lemon juice , lemon rind and yellow food colouring bring to a boil over medium-high heat
3. cook , and stir for 2 minutes , or until smooth and thickened
4. remove from heat
5. stir in butter
6. cool to room temperature for about 1 hour
7. meanwhile , in a mixing bowl , beat the cream cheese and the powdered sugar until smooth
8. fold in the whipped cream and the 1 tbsp lemon juice
9. remove 1 / 2 cup of the whipped cream / lemon mixture for the garnish
10. spread the remaining cream cheese mixture into the baked pastry shell
11. top with the cooled lemon filling
12. chill in the fridge for a minimum of 8 hours or overnight
13. when ready to serve , scoop the reserved 1 / 2 cup cream cheese mixture into a pastry bag with a star
14. pipe stars onto the pie , or garnish with the reserved cream cheese mixture or as desired
15. refrigerate until ready to serve-- delicious !
demonstrations.review: This is a fantastic pie!  I made it for Easter dinner, and everyone raved.  I did have to cook the filling a few minutes longer than the directions stated, but I think this is because I've never made a cream pie from scratch before, and didn't know what the filling would look like when it was to the correct stage.  I Zaarmailed Kittencal and she and was very helpful.  I just needed to cook it a little longer, and it suddenly thickened up and cleared.  After that it was a breeze.  It has a very zippy lemon flavor, so will really please a true lemon lover like me!  I made it with a shortbread crust, but am going to try it with a traditional crust next time, as I found this particular crust to be a little "thick" for the pie.  Thanks Kitten for the terrific recipe and your help when I was fumbling my way through it!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s best deviled eggs

these have been a favorite for years, when i serve these at my get togethers or make them for socials and large events they are always the first to go and everyone wants the recipe, i suggest to use large, extra large or even jumbo eggs for this, i like to make the yolk filling a day ahead and refrigerate this will blend the flavors --- for a nice presentation place each egg half in a colored paper muffin liner --- all ingredient amounts may be adjusted to taste --- see my recipe#259573

1. slice the eggs in half lengthwise
2. remove the yolks , and set whites aside
3. in a small bowl , mush yolks well with a fork , leaving no small lumps
4. add next 10 ingredients mix well to combine
5. spoon or pipe egg yolk mixture evenly into the whites
6. sprinkle with paprika
7. cover tightly with plastic wrap
8. store in the refrigerator until ready to serve
demonstrations.review: We had these wonderful eggs for Easter day appetizers, and really enjoyed them.  I especially liked the dill flavoring that came through, as I'm not much of a sweet pickle fan as you often see in a traditional deviled egg recipe.  Thanks, Kitten.  These will definately be making a repeat showing at our house.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
yummy crunchy apple pie

great pie!

1. use foil on bottom of oven rather than a cookie sheet under pie pan
2. prepare pastry for single-crust pie
3. place in pie plate and trim and crimp the edge
4. refrigerate 30 minute loosely covered with plastic wrap
5. in a large mixing bowl , stir together the sugar , flour , cinnamon , nutmeg , allspice , and salt
6. add apple slices and gently toss until they are coated well
7. transfer mixture to pie
8. for crumb topping: stir together brown sugar , flour , and oats
9. using a pastry blender , cut in the butter until topping resembles coarse crumbs
10. sprinkle over apple mixture in pie
11. to prevent over-browning while baking , cover edge of pie with foil
12. bake at 375 degrees fahrenheit for 25 minutes
13. remove foil and bake 25 to 30 minutes more , or until top is golden
14. remove from oven
15. cool on wire rack about an hour and serve !
demonstrations.review: This is a new family favorite!  I made it the first time at Thanksgiving and all the apple pie eaters raved.  No leftovers!  Made it again at Christmas and then DH requested it for his birthday 2/21.  I am really not much of a pie maker - I consider the weak point of my cooking skills - so to have a pie I made requested for a birthday dessert is a major kudo!  I used Granny Smiths and didn't put on the pecans since we aren't nut eaters.  This pie is very sweet and rich.  When I saw the caramel amount (1/4c) I thought it seemed like it wouldn't be enough, but a little really goes a long way and it covered well.  Thanks for a terrific recipe!  Steph

target.recipe_text:
orange cream cheese coffee cake

this is a very good coffee cake. it does not have a strong orange flavor. we have served it to many people and have never been disappointed. all want the recipe afterwards.

1. combine the granulated sugar , pecans and orange rind in a bowl
2. set aside for future use
3. separate biscuit dough into individual biscuits
4. then gently separate individual biscuits in half
5. place a cream cheese square between the 2 halves and pinch sides to seal each back together
6. dip in butter and dredge in granulated sugar mixture
7. stand biscuits on edge in a lightly greased 12-cup bundt pan , spacing evenly
8. drizzle with remaining butter and sprinkle with remaining granulated sugar mixture
9. bake at 350 degrees for 45 minutes or until golden
10. immediately invert onto a serving plate
11. glaze: combine powdered sugar and orange juice
12. stir well
13. drizzle over warm bread
14. serve immediately
15. you may omit the cream cheese but still separate biscuits in half and dip as normal in sugar mixture
16. we do a half and half batch
17. there is not a strong orange flavor here
target.review: I am one happy cook right now.  I had lost this recipe several years ago and just found it here on RecipeZaar today.  My family loves this coffee cake!  Make sure you use freshly grated orange peel and squeezed OJ.  The fresh taste is wonderful.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
christmas biscotti

a colorful red and green dotted biscotti.. i love it and i don't really like biscotti. my mother said to make her this if nothing else for christmas!

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees
2. butter and flour a baking sheet
3. in a bowl , cream together the butter and sugar until light and fluffy
4. beat in the eggs , vanilla , and orange zest until blended
5. in another bowl , stir together the flour , baking powder , cloves and salt
6. add the flour mixture to the butter mixture and beat until blended
7. stir in cranberries and pistachios
8. divide the dough in half
9. one at a time , place the 2 dough portions on the prepared baking sheet and form each into a log about 1 / 2 inch high , 1 1 / 2 inches wide and 14 inches long
10. space logs at least 2 inches apart
11. bake the logs for 25-30 minutes or until set and light brown
12. transfer to a cutting board and let cool 6-8 minutes
13. reduce the oven temperature to 300 degrees
14. using a very sharp knife , cut the logs in the diagonal into slices 3 / 8 inch thick
15. stand the slices upright on the baking sheet and return the sheet to the oven for 15 minutes to dry the cookies thoroughly
16. transfer to racks to cool
17. store the cookies in an airtight container for up to 4 weeks
demonstrations.review: These biscotti were terrific!!!  It was difficult to keep from eating all of the dough before they were baked.  The flavor is just fabulous.  I had to make just a couple of minor substitutions because my local stores did not have all that I needed.  I ended up using cherry-flavored Craisins and salted dry-roasted pistachio kernels.  (I just added less salt to the recipe.)  Always use freshly-grated orange zest; the dried stuff just doesn't compare.  Thanks for this wonderful recipe.  It's a keeper!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
hawaiian chicken   white rice    made simple

this recipe is simple, delicious and can be prepared and cooked in one hour. it looks as if you spent the day in the kitchen cooking (at least my husband always thought so). i found this recipe in an american heart association cookbook back in the '70's.

1. skin , bone , and flour chicken breasts and place in covered casserole dish
2. mix together the soy sauce , sugar and all of the juice from the can of pineapple
3. pour liquid over chicken breasts and sprinkle the parsley on top
4. bake covered in a 350 degree oven for 45 minutes
5. add the pineapple chunks and continue cooking for an additional 15 minutes
6. prepare the white rice during the last 15 minutes the casserole is cooking
7. serve the chicken over the rice , also place fresh parsley sprigs on the plate
8. i usually make string beans to serve with this dish
demonstrations.review: What size can (how many ounces) of pineapple chunks should I have used for this recipe?

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cherry o creme pie

simply delicious.  the tartness of the cream cheese and cherries with the sweetness of the condensed milk and graham cracker crust.  let me just say it's present at just about every family gathering.  chill time not included in time to make.

1. mix cream cheese , milk , lemon juice , and vanilla together
2. pour into pie crust
3. refrigerate until set , 1-2 hours , on a lower shelf in your fridge
4. top with cherries just before serving
demonstrations.review: Love this pie!  Here's a tip passed on to me by my MIL - add 2-3 T. melted butter (& a pinch of salt if using unsalted butter) to the pie filling.  You'll lose a tiny bit of the shiny gloss, but the flavor is enhanced and sweetness is cut just a tad. Yum!!!!

target.recipe_text:
lower fat peanut chocolate chip trail bars

these are moist brownie like bars with just the right amount of chocolate and peanuts. this recipe was originally high fat, but i successfully substitute applesauce for most of the margarine.  excellent served warm, although still very good cool.

1. stir together flour , cereal , oats , baking soda , and baking powder
2. in a separate bowl , beat margarine , sugar , brown sugar , eggs and vanilla
3. add flour mixture to wet ingredients
4. stir together
5. add in all coconut , 1 / 2 cup chocolate chips , and about 2 / 3 cup peanuts
6. spread batter evenly into a greased 9 x 13" baking pan
7. sprinkle the top of the batter evenly with remaining chocolate chips and peanuts
8. lightly press them down on batter
9. bake at 350f for 23-27 minutes , until top is lightly browned and a toothpick inserted in centre comes out clean
10. cool in pan on a rack
11. when cool , cut into 21 bars
target.review: These are Fabulous!!  I didn't have coconut on hand when I made these but look forward to adding it in next time. (and there will definately be a next time!) My friends thought I bought these at a little specialty bakery.~I hope that was a compliment(?!?) This is a nice snack when you want...something; but not too sweet, but chocolatey and a bit crunchy. This is what you're craving. Try it!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cream cheese penguins

my kids have just as much fun making these as they do eating them. they are a fun item to take as an appetizer to a holiday party.

1. cut a slit lengthwise from top to bottom in each jumbo olive
2. fill the cavity of each jumbo olive with about 1 tsp of cream cheese
3. cut carrot into 1 / 4 inch slices , then out of each slice cut a small notch , save the piece you cut out this will become the beak
4. cut a small slit in the center of each small olive and press the cut out piece of carrot into the hole with the pointed end out
5. using a frill toothpick , stack head , body and feet , adjusting so that beak , cream cheese breast and notch in carrot slice line up
demonstrations.review: These were fun on my table amongst all the other "ordinary" appitizers. Definately created some attention.  They are time consuming and shouldn't be made too far in advance.(overnight at the most) My guests dubbed them the "March of the Penguins"!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
macaroon madness bars

easy to make with a shortbread crust and a butterscotch coconut filling these please kids and adults alike.

1. prepare crust: preheat oven to 375f
2. grease 8x8-inch or 9x9-inch metal baking pan
3. line pan with foil
4. grease foil
5. with finger
6. press dough firmly onto bottom of pan
7. bake crust 15 to 20 minutes , until lightly browned
8. meanwhile , prepare pecan-butterscotch filling: in large bowl , with wire whisk or fork , beat eggs with brown sugar , flour , vanilla , and salt just until blended
9. stir in pecans , coconut , and butterscotch chips
10. pour filling over warm crust
11. bake 20 to 25 minutes , until lightly browned around the edges and filling is set
12. cool completely in pan on wire rack
13. cover and refrigerate at least 5 hours or overnight for easier cutting
14. when cold , transfer with foil to cutting board
15. cut into 8 strips , then cut each strip crosswise into 8 squares
demonstrations.review: These bars are so irrisistable!!  Everyone who sampled them has named them their new favorite bar! So hard to wait for the bars to cool before digging in!  Definately making these again!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cappuccino dessert

this one of the recipes i found at kraft food and family...its great thing and easy too!

1. pour milk and instant coffee into medium bowl
2. add pudding mix
3. beat with wire whisk 2 minutes or until well blended
4. pour into dessert dishes
5. refrigerate at least 1 hour or until ready to serve
6. just before serving , gently stir cinnamon into whipped topping
7. spread over pudding
demonstrations.review: Wonderful and simple to make.  Nice, light dessert that beautifully complements a heavy supper.  Rave reviews from all my guests!

target.recipe_text:
beth s melt in your mouth barbecue ribs  oven

i almost didn't want to share this ribs recipe because this is one of the dishes that i make that keep my sons coming back home! these can be done with baby back or regular pork ribs. i have also made split chickens this way. the ribs are tender, moist and just slide off of the bone. i know that your family will love them just as much as my family does.
i noticed that some are unable to find hickory smoked salt. you can use smoked paprika or just brush the ribs with liquid smoke before applying the rub. the smoke flavor is nice because it helps give the ribs a cooked-on-the-grill flavor.
also, the easiest way to remove the membrane is to work a spoon, or i use the tips of my kitchen shears, into the bottom center of the membrane, work it back and forth to form a "pocket," then i slide my thumbs in and work the membrane off from the center outward to the ends.

1. preheat oven to 300 degrees f
2. line a baking sheet with two layers of foil , shiny side out
3. peel off tough membrane that covers the bony side of the ribs
4. season the ribs on both sides with salt and pepper
5. if using , divide the hickory liquid smoke evenly over the ribs
6. in a medium bowl , combine the light brown sugar , paprika , garlic powder and ground red pepper
7. apply the rub to all sides of the ribs
8. lay ribs on the prepared baking sheet , meaty side down
9. lay two layers of foil on top of ribs and roll and crimp edges tightly , edges facing up to seal
10. transfer to the oven and = bake for 2-2 1 / 2 hours or until meat is starting to shrink away from the ends of the bone
11. remove from oven
12. heat broiler
13. cut ribs into serving sized portions of 2 or 3 ribs
14. arrange on broiler pan , bony side up
15. brush on sauce
16. broil for 1 or 2 minutes until sauce is cooked on and bubbly
17. turn ribs over
18. repeat on other side
19. alternately , you can grill the ribs on your grill to cook on the sauce
target.review: I will never cook ribs any other way again. Very easy to prepare,  although I too could not find the hickory salt. I don't think which sauce you use really matters; the taste is all about the ribs. Many thanks. I am cooking them for the 4th

demonstrations.recipe_text:
tuna burgers

kid favorite

1. in a bowl , combine tuna , bread crumbs , celery , mayo , onion , chili sauce , egg , salt and pepper
2. shape into four patties
3. melt butter in a skillet
4. cook patties for about 4-5 minutes per side or until lightly browned
5. serve on buns with lettuce and tomatoes , if desired
demonstrations.review: I was so intrigued by this recipe, that I had to try it as soon as I read a review. I only used 1/4 cup mayo, and while they were still pretty "wet", the consistency after cooking was perfect. I believe I like them better cold with fruit for a light lunch. I, too, would not want to hide them in a bun!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crock pot oniony pork chops with creamy mustard sauce

if you like onions, do try this crock pot dish. note that you will have a lot of sauce.

1. in a skillet , heat oil over medium-high heat and brown pork chops on both sides
2. place in bottom of slow cooker when browned
3. in same skillet , reduce heat to medium and saute onions until softened
4. add garlic , dry mustard , salt and pepper , and cayenne and cook , stirring , for 1 minute
5. add flour and cook , stirring , for 1 minute
6. add vinegar and wine and cook until thickened
7. pour this mixture over pork chops , put lid on crock pot and cook on low for 4 to 5 hours or on high for 2 to 2-1 / 2 hours , or just until pork is tender
8. remove pork chops from slow cooker and place on a warmed platter
9. stir dijon mustard and whipping cream into juices in slow cooker
10. when well combined , turn slow cooker off and pour sauce over chops on platter and serve immediately
demonstrations.review: Made this for dinner last night, although halved the recipe, for two. It is delicious with a creamy sauce that has an outstanding flavor. Chops are fork-tender, probably due to the small amount of vinegar added, although not tasted in final product. We scarfed it down!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
now this is alice springs chicken

alice springs chicken has always been one of my all time favorite chicken dishes. i looked everywhere for the recipe that looked the closest and this is the winner + or - a few to my taste. we love onions so i always sauté  some up with the mushrooms but whatever works best for you!

1. with an electric mixer combine the mustard , honey , and 1 tbsp oil , and lemon juice for 1 minute
2. pour 1 / 2 mixture over chicken in a gallon ziplock to marinate in fridge 2-24 hours
3. chill remaining marinade to serve with chicken
4. after marinating chicken , preheat oven to 375f put remaining oil in frying pan
5. heat and sear chicken on both sides
6. transfer chicken to oven safe pan and brush with marinade
7. meanwhile in frying pan add butter and saute mushrooms
8. season chicken breasts with salt and peppers
9. stack bacon across each breast , spoon mushrooms on each breast and then approx 1 / 3- 1 / 2 cup cheese on each
10. cover pan with foil and bake 7-10 minutes or until cheese is melted and bubbly
11. sprinkle with parsley and serve with honey mustard marinade
demonstrations.review: I LOVE this recipe. It may be better than Outback's. Made it exactly as stated, but baked it longer in the oven to get chicken done, then added mushrooms, bacon and cheese. May try the sauted onions with it next time.

target.recipe_text:
bacon mushroom chicken

very easy to put together, and the result is fabulous. make sure to serve mashed potatoes or rice along side of this, to mop up the great tasting sauce!

1. preheat oven to 350
2. pour melted butter into a 9x13-in baking dish
3. add chicken , skin side down , sprinkle with seasoning salt and garlic
4. turn chicken over , season and lay bacon strips on top
5. sprinkle with mushrooms
6. bake in the preheated oven for 45-60 minutes , or until chicken is no longer pink and juices run clear
7. remove chicken , bacon and mushrooms to a platter and keep warm
8. pour juices from baking dish into a small saucepan and whisk together with cream over low heat until thickened
9. pour sauce over chicken and serve warm
target.review: Very impressive!  Everyone thought I put alot of work into this, although it was extremely easy.  I never did get the gravy to thicken...not sure what went wrong there, but no one seemed to notice.  Probably because the chicken was so awesome!  I will be making this one again soon.   Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
skillet parmesan chicken

this is real comfort food. a family favorite. if you can, buy the fresh mozzarella. you won't believe the difference and it's worth it. the texture isn't rubbery like the typical mozzarella. i got it from watching an emeril show on the food network.

1. pound the chicken breasts between two slices of plastic wrap until about 1 / 4" thick
2. season with salt and pepper
3. dredge chicken in flour and shake off excess
4. dip in egg / milk mixture , then in breadcrumb / parmesan mixture
5. heat the butter and olive oil in a large deep skillet
6. brown the chicken breasts over medium heat until golden on each side
7. remove to a plate and keep warm
8. add the marinara sauce to the skillet
9. heat to boiling and simmer 10 minutes
10. add the chicken breasts to the sauce and sprinkle parmesan over them
11. place a slice of mozzarella on each piece of chicken
12. cover and simmer about 8- 10 minutes or until the cheese has melted and the chicken is tender
13. serve with your favorite pasta- we like linguine
demonstrations.review:
05-26-04:  This is even beyond 5 stars! I used Hunt's Garlic/Herb sauce, fresh mozzarella, and served over angel hair pasta. It was very easy and tasted awesome! Now that I have this recipe, I will probably never order this in a resturant again. I'm already dreaming of the new things I will try when we eat out at an italian resturant. Great Job! Thanks! 

11-10-08:  Over 4 years have gone by and this is still one of my favorite recipes to make.  It's been a keeper that continues to impress!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cheese and peas salad

great dish to take to a pot luck. it tastes so good. and it is very pretty!

1. cook frozen peas
2. drain well
3. cool
4. in large bowl combine combine first 6 ing
5. in small bowl mix mayo , vinegar , salt , and pepper
6. add to peas
7. toss
8. chill
demonstrations.review: Very good the first time.  Not so hot the next day and really not so hot the next.  Will make again though...when feeding a crowd or taking a dish to a get together.  Very pretty.  Thanks.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chicken pasta milano

a copycat recipe of the pasta milano served at macaroni grill. yum yum!

1. in a large saucepan , melt butter over low heat
2. add the minced garlic and cook for about a minute
3. add tomatoes and 3 / 4 cup of chicken broth
4. increase heat to medium and bring mixture to a boil
5. reduce heat and simmer uncovered , for about 10 minutes
6. add cream and bring to a boil again , stirring frequently
7. simmer over medium heat until sauce is thick
8. sprinkle salt and pepper over both sides of chicken
9. heat the olive oil in a skillet , then add chicken and saute until chicken is no longer pink inside
10. remove chicken from skillet , drain fat from skillet
11. in the same skillet , stir 1 / 4 cup chicken broth with the pan juices , and bring to a boil
12. reduce slightly and add to the cream sauce
13. stir in basil
14. serve chicken atop the pasta , coat with the cream sauce
demonstrations.review: This dish is awesome!  Wish I could rate higher.  It tasted almost exactly like the original version from Mac Grill.  Next time, I will cut the chicken into small pieces and mix together with the sauce and pasta.  I may also try with bow-tie pasta.  The suggestion to add mushrooms sounds good too.  I can't wait to make this again!  Thanks so much for sharing this recipe!

target.recipe_text:
crunchy  chewy flax   almond macaroons  egg free

my oma & i combined her nusskuchen recipe and my dd's egg-free diet to create this lovely, dense macaroon/biscotti-type dough.  the original german "nutcake" recipe calls for no less than 7 eggs, which we substituted here w/7x 1 tbsp flax : 3 tbsp water.  our hesitation was replaced by an eagerness to "mach es noch ein mal!", which i've done tonight, this time taking the time to convert the european measurements.  enjoy!

1. whisk the first two ingredients together in a bowl and let stand at least 2-3 minutes before use
2. using a hand mixer , beat the sugar & 5 t
3. hot water together in a large bowl for 2-3 minutes
4. gradually add the flax mixture and all the rest of the ingredients
5. mix well
6. if making as biscotti or chewy bars , grease and flour an 8x11" baking tin or a 10" round springform pan before adding the dough
7. bake at 350f for 40 minutes
8. remove promptly to a wire rack
9. if making as cookies or macaroons , grease and flour a cookie sheet before placing 1" balls of dough approximately 1 1 / 2 inches apart
10. bake at 350f for 25-30 minutes
11. remove promptly to a wire rack
12. nb if you want these to be chewy , do not allow them to brown at the edges
13. otherwise they will be as hard as hockey pucks !
14. ps i preferred using my bosch kitchen machine to a hand mixer for this heavy batter
target.review: Being vegan I'm so happy to have found this recipe. Macaroons are a favorite of mine and these are so good. I used whole spelt flour and unrefined sugar and they turned out perfect. My only complaint about this recipe is that it doesn't specify pan size if making bars, which is a pet peeve of mine. Giving the pan size should be a requirement for submitting a recipe. I used a glass 8 x 11 pan, sprayed with Pam and baked exactly 40 minutes. The edges are crispy and the middles chewy. Thanks for this great recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
maggie s house dressing

i have two versions of what we call our house dressing that i use for salads.  i have been using the first version (the original) for over 40 years, and the second version for about 5.   everyone that has eaten my salads, loves either version, and more people than i can remember asked for the recipe.  it is so simple and basic, yet it tastes great.  most of my guests always ask me to use my house dressing as opposed to bottled salad dressings.  i never measure, so i will have to estimate, but i would suggest you go with the smaller amounts first, then taste and adjust, if necessary. of course, the amount will have to be adjusted according to the size of the salad.

1. version one:
2. right before serving:
3. sprinkle the garlic salt over the salad
4. drizzle the oil over the garlic salt
5. toss
6. taste
7. adjust by adding more of either ingredient
8. version two:
9. right before serving:
10. sprinkle the garlic salt over the salad
11. drizzle the oil over the garlic salt
12. drizzle the balsamic vinegar over the oil
13. toss
14. taste
15. adjust by adding more of any one of the ingredients that you feel the salad needs
16. hint: do not do this ahead of time
17. the salad will become limp and it won't taste as good
demonstrations.review: I finally got around to trying this dressing. I used version #2 and it's really delicious. I love how easy it is. One thing I did differently was to put the oil on first, then the garlic salt, so the salt would have something to cling to. This simple dressing really lets the fresh taste of your salad come through and it's so easy to do.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
zucchini spoon bread

this spoon bread is delicious, a good way to use those zucchini out of the garden. for extra flavor or heat add 2 or 3 jalapeno peppers. recipes comes from betters homes and gardens.com.
spoon bread is a side dish, eaten with a spoon. it is called a bread because of the ingredients. enjoy

1. in a large saucepan combine , corn , onions , pepper strips , and water
2. bring to boiling
3. reduce heat , cover and simmer for 5 minutes
4. do not drain , stir in zucchini , tomatoes , cheese and cornmeal , set aside
5. in a small mixing bowl beat eggs
6. stir in milk , salt , pepper , and hot pepper sauce
7. stir egg mixture into the vegetable mixture in saucepan
8. turn mixture into a greased 1-1 / 2-quart casserole
9. bake , uncovered , in a 350 degree oven about 40 minutes or until set , let stand for 5 minutes before serving
demonstrations.review: I had to modify this to make it vegan, but the basic flavors were unchanged and it is delicious. Next time I will add nutritional yeast, which boosts the flavor and nutrition of vegan foods, and will also add scallions.  Love this recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
hummus  my version

i grew up eating hummus and just love the stuff.  i was pleasantly surprised recently when a friend informed me that it is included on ww, of course in limited amount!  it can become addictive, but it may not be for everyone, tho it can grow on you....of course, as most people know, it is a middle eastern staple, but is eaten by many people of many ethnicities.  it is sometimes used as a spread in place of butter.  most use it as a dip served with pita wedges or crudites (veggies).  it only takes 15 minutes to whip up, and 2 hours of chilling.

1. drain liquid from chick peas and save
2. combine all ingredients , including 1 / 2 cup of saved liquid , in a blender
3. i sometimes use the entire can -- if you do , you may need a little more of the liquid
4. blend at high speed until smooth
5. if too thick , add small amount of the saved liquid and blend again till smooth
6. chill covered , for a couple of hours
7. serve with pita wedges or veggies
demonstrations.review: I happened to have all the ingredients for this on hand and wanted to use up some of my sesame seeds. I had Good Seasons Italian dressing mix which is vegan so used that instead of the cheese garlic. I really like the taste of this and it's so easy. I used the food processor which didn't do a good job of breaking down the sesame seeds though. Next time I'll use the blender and blend the seeds first until they're smooth, then add the other ingredients. I think my processor is just too big for the tiny sesame seeds. I had to taste some before chilling, but I know it will be even better after it mellows for a while. A nice recipe.

target.recipe_text:
oven fried chicken chimichangas

a fast and healthier way to serve chimichangas than the traditional deep fried. these are very good, and you may dress them up to you own preference. i like to serve with green chile sauce sometimes instead of the picante sauce.

1. mix chicken , picante sauce or salsa , cumin , oregano , cheese and onions
2. place about 1 / 4 cup of the chicken mixture in the center of each tortilla
3. fold opposite sides over filling
4. roll up from bottom and place seam-side down on a baking sheet
5. brush with melted margarine
6. bake at 400f for 25 minutes or until golden
7. garnish with additional cheese and green onion and serve salsa on the side
target.review: I tried this recipe and it was very good, I added some frozen corn and brushed tops with butter instead of margarine.  Next time I think I will add some black beans, great recipe and great taste.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
ziploc bag omelet  eggs in a hurry

eggs-in-a-bag, this has got to be the easiest and tastiest way i've ever found to prepare breakfast, or even just a snack. each person prepares their own with the particular omelet ingredients that they prefer. recipe is for each serving.

1. mix all ingredients well , in a sandwich size zip-lock plastic bag and seal
2. drop bag into a pot of boiling water
3. boil for 13-15 minutes
4. remove and enjoy
demonstrations.review: We have made this recipe for years.  First time was on a Good Sam campout.  The only difference we make is we add cooked; bacon, sausage or any other cooked meat to the eggs.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
bread machine cracked wheat    flax seed bread

i use a bread machine to make the dough and bake it in the oven for an excellent, light bread for sandwiches and toast!   i am sure that you could finish it in the bread machine, but i prefer to bake it in the oven.

1. place ingredients in the bread machine in the order recommended by the manufacturer
2. utilize the whole wheat dough cycle
3. spray loaf pan with olive oil spray
4. form bread dough into greased loaf pan , let rise again
5. cover with warm damp cotton cloth and place in a warm place
6. bake at 375 degrees for 33 minutes
7. when baked , remove from pan and rub crust with cold stick of butter
demonstrations.review: Made this in the BM on dough cycle.  Then made into small loaves.  This is great bread.  I didn't have bulgar wheat so used barley flakes.  It was very good bread.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
broccoli chicken rice casserole   low fat

really good!!! 4 servings at 7 ww points each. full meal in itself.

1. bring the one cup of water to a boil and add oxo and chicken , cook until chicken is done
2. steam broccoli and carrots until tender
3. line bottom of a casserole dish with rice and top with carrots , broccoli and chicken
4. in a bowl , mix together soup , parmesan cheese , milk and seasonings , and pour over the casserole
5. mix melted butter and breadcrumbs together and sprinkle over top , bake at 350 for 30 minutes
demonstrations.review: I have made this dish several times and we both like it a lot.  It is large enough for 2  meals for us.   I have used cream of mushroom and it was still good.

target.recipe_text:
apple rhubarb crumble

this is wonderful with fresh rhubarb.

1. in a mixing bowl , add rhubarb , apples , egg , sugar , syrup , nutmeg , and cinnamon
2. stir to mix
3. pour mixture into a 2-quart greased casserole dish
4. in a bowl , add flour , brown sugar , and salt
5. stir to mix
6. with a pastry blender , cut in butter until the mixture resembles coarse crumbs
7. sprinkle crumb mixture evenly over fruit mixture
8. bake at 350 degrees for 45-55 minutes or until bubbly
target.review: This was wonderful!  I made this for my birthday instead of a cake.  Everyone really enjoyed this.  I'll be making this again (soon).  Thanks for a great recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cherry marshmallow cake

the marshmallows melt and rise to the top to form a glaze on this very easy to make and convenient cake.
