1. preheat oven to 350f
2. grease a 13x9x2 inch baking pan
3. prepare cake mix according to package directions
4. spread marshmallows in the bottom of the baking pan , pour cake mix over marshmallows , spoon cherries evenly on top
5. bake 30 to 40 minutes or until an inserted toothpick comes out clean , cool before serving
demonstrations.review: This is great!  My DH doesn't usually like sweets, but he sure liked this one.  He said it is a keeper.  This was too easy and had great results.  Will definitely make this again and again.  Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pork steak major

i happened upon a package of pork steaks at the market last week. each steak weighed at least two pounds! i thought, 

1. place pork steak in roasting pan
2. i use a two quart glass pan , but whatever works for you
3. mix together dry onion soup and warm water
4. pour over pork steak
5. cover meat with raw onion rings
6. sprinkle onions lightly with salt and pepper
7. seal pan with aluminum foil
8. place in center of 375 f
9. oven
10. bake for approximately one hour
11. i check the roast with a quick-read meat thermometer to make sure it's done
demonstrations.review: My DH and kids absolutely loved this!  This recipe is so simple.  It was very tender and incredibly tasty. It made the whole house smell wonderful.  I thickened the juice to make gravy - yum!  I will definitely be making this again and again.  Thanks for the great recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
incredibly cool and refreshing mandarin orange cake

this is sooooo refreshing on a hot day and is the perfect ending to a bbq (or any) meal. everyone who has ever tried this has raved about it. it is so yummy and light and does not last a day in our house! if you do have any left, store it in the refrigerator. (cooling time is not added to the prep or cook times.)

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees
2. grease and flour a 9 x 13 inch pan
3. in a large bowl , combine cake mix , eggs , oil and one can of oranges with juice
4. mix by hand or with mixer until smooth
5. pour into prepared pan
6. bake for 30-40 minutes or until thin steak knife inserted in center come out clean
7. allow to cool completely on rack
8. in a large bowl , mix whipped topping , the other can of mandarin oranges with juice and dry pudding mix until well combined and smooth
9. spread on cooled cake
demonstrations.review: A very nice, light and refreshing cake recipe.  My cake didn't taste very "orangy", but I realized that the mandarin oranges I used were packed in pear juice - maybe this is why.  It was very good and everyone liked it.  Will definitely make this one again.  Thanks!

target.recipe_text:
kenny s brain spread

this is a great appetizer for your next halloween party!  if you don't have a brain mold, you can substitute by lining a med. size round bowl with saran wrap and making your mold. once the mold is set, you can take the round end of a knife or a pencil eraser and create your crevices and creases to make your brain, as in the picture i have posted.  takes a little more time, but works well.  when done designing your brain, peel off the saran wrap, and plate to serve along with your crackers, chips etc.

1. heat soup , undiluted , and mix in the cream cheese
2. stir in softened gelatin , and blend well
3. fold in remaining ingredients , and pour into a lightly-oiled brain mold
4. chill until firm , and serve with your favorite crackers , pita or bagel chips or scoops
target.review: Great recipe. I made it for my Halloween party and everyone loved the crab brain. I have given the recipe to several people from the party. It is a keeper!! Thanks

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pumpkin streusel bundt cake

this is a libby's recipe and is it good! really impressive when it is cut and the streusel filling peeks through. great for the holidays.

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees f
2. grease and flour a 12 cup bundt pan
3. streusel: combine brown sugar , spices in a small bowl
4. cut in butter until crumbly
5. set aside
6. cake: add flour , cinnamon , salt and baking soda in a medium bowl
7. in a large bowl beat butter and sugar until fluffy
8. add and beat in eggs one at a time
9. add pumpkin , sour cream and vanilla
10. beat well
11. beat in flour mixture
12. spoon half of the batter into the pan
13. sprinkle streursel mixture over batter but don't let it touch the sides of the pan
14. top with remaining batter , making sure batter does touch the sides of the pan
15. bake for 55-60 minutes
16. cool in the pan for 30 minutes
17. turn out onto wire racks in order to cool completely
18. turn out on serving plate
19. drizzle with glaze
demonstrations.review: Love, loved loved it!! I wasn't sure about the pumpkin but it was moist and fabulous!!! I made it for work and everyone loved it!! This one is a keeper!! I will make over again and again!  Thanks for sharing!! ps made it in Oct but i forgot to write my review!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chocolate  chocolate  chocolate  bundt cake with chocolate glaze

need i say more...chocolate! decadently rich and moist. add a scoop of vanilla ice cream and you're in heaven.

1. cake: preheat oven to 350
2. grease and flour bundt pan , set aside
3. in large mixing bowl , combine cake mix , pudding mix and chocolate chips
4. in another bowl , combine water , eggs , and vanilla mixing well
5. add egg mixture to dry mixture and mix with spoon until just blended
6. pour into prepared pan
7. bake for 50 to 55 minutes or until cake tests done when wooden pick in center comes out clean
8. cool 15 to 20 minutes before removing cake from pan
9. when completely cool , drizzle cake with chocolate glaze
10. chocolate glaze: combine all ingredients in bowl
11. mix with spoon until smooth
demonstrations.review: Delicious chocolate cake!! So fast and easy. Great for a super chocolate fix!! I made if for a friends b-day at work and they all LOVED it and gave everyone the recipe. I also filled my bundt cake center with fresh strawberries! YUMMY Thanks  for sharing!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
brown sugar bundt cake

my mom passed this recipe along to me. it is easy to make and has been a big hit at home and at the office. i get frequent requests for the recipe. it is very moist and delicious and makes a good breakfast cake as well as a dessert. increase nuts by another 1/3 cup if you like nuts!

1. grease a 10-inch bundt pan well and sprinkle pan with granulated sugar
2. preheat oven to 350 degrees f
3. combine cake mix , pudding mix , eggs , oil and water in large bowl and beat on medium speed until well mixed , about 4 minutes
4. add brown sugar and pecans and mix to combine well
5. pour batter evenly into prepared bundt pan and bake for 1 hour or until cake tester comes out clean
6. place bundt pan on wire rack and cool 15 minutes
7. invert cake onto rack and slip pan off cake
8. let cool on rack
9. can be stored covered at room temperature
demonstrations.review: This cake is " DELICIOUS"!! It is soooo easy and it comes out so moist. I made it for a brunch and everyone LOVED it. I have made it 3 times already and have given the recipe to about 6 people. I am making it again right now. Thanks !!!!

target.recipe_text:
crispy cinnamon streusel banana nut cream cheese bread

this is the best banana bread that i have ever made! the recipe is from southern living.

1. preheat oven to 350
2. beat butter and cream cheese together with an electric mixer until creamy
3. add sugar , gradually , and beat until light and fluffy
4. add eggs , one at a time , and beat until blended
5. gradually add flour and next three ingredients to butter mixture , beating at low until just blended
6. stir in bananas , pecans , and vanilla
7. spoon batter into 2 greased and floured 8x4 loafpans
8. batter will be thick
9. for streusel: stir together 1 / 2 cup packed brown sugar , 1 / 2 cup chopped toasted pecans , 1 tablespoon flour , 1 tablespoon melted butter , and 1 / 8 teaspoon cinnamon
10. sprinkle mixture evenly over batter in pans
11. bake for 1 hour or until a wooden pick inserted in center comes out clean
12. bread may be shielded with aluminum foil that last 15 minutes to prevent excessive browning of streusel
13. cool in pans on wire rack for 10 minutes
14. remove from pans and cool 30 more minutes before slicing
15. for perfect slices , cut with a serrated or electric knife after cooling
target.review:
Delicious!!!  I added some cinnamon and nutmeg to the batter, but that was my only change.  It's the best banana bread I've ever had!!  :)

Thank you LVS

demonstrations.recipe_text:
dutch baby

i've had these a lot at b&b's, probably because they're delicious and dependable if the right technique is used. this dish is puffy around the outside and flat in the center offering the perfect nest for sliced fresh fruit. it's airy, light and makes a beautiful presentation. the batter can be made up to a day ahead and refrigerated.

1. fifteen minutes before baking preheat the oven to 450
2. have a pie plate or oven-proof skillet ready
3. whisk together the milk , flour , eggs , sugar and vanilla
4. put the butter in the pie plate or skillet and place the pan in the oven just until the butter is melted
5. with a brush coat the rim and entire inside of the pan
6. slowly pour batter into hot pan
7. bake for 20 minutes
8. reduce heat to 350 and bake another 8-10 minutes , until pancake is well-browned
9. remove from oven and sieve confectioners' sugar over the top
10. serve immediately with fruit spooned into the center of the pancake
demonstrations.review:
Soo good.  Made it per recipe, but turned the oven down a notch per reviewers' suggestions. 

Thank you for the recipe.  My whole family LOVED it!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kao pad  thai style fried rice

from sundays at moosewood.

1. choose and prepare vegetables
2. select a combination with a variety of colors
3. in a wok , heat the oil and stir fry the ginger and garlic until golden
4. remove them with a slotted spoon and save for later
5. in the same oil , stir-fry the vegetables until just cooked
6. add the harder ones first , and the tender ones last
7. remove the vegetables from the wok and set aside
8. add the rice to the wok and heat thoroughly
9. with your stirring spoon , make a hole in the center of the rice , down to the wok and put in the eggs
10. stir until they are pretty well set before you mix them into the rice
11. the more you cook the eggs before stirring them into the rice , the drier the dish will be
12. add the tomatoes , the reserved ginger and garlic and the stir-fried vegetables
13. finally , mix in the chili sauce , soy sauce and lime juice
14. for serving , top each serving with thin slices of scallions
15. put thin slices of lime on the side
demonstrations.review: My family and I really enjoyed this rice.  SPICY.  My hubby and I were surprised at how much the lemon wedges helped tame the spice.  We wouldn't change anything.  Very good.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
devil s food chocolate chip muffins

marie simmons; devilishly good. for those times when you need to indulge.

1. coat 12 muffin cups with nonstick cooking spray
2. in a mixing bowl , add the flour , cocoa powder , sugar , baking soda , and salt
3. stir to combine
4. in another bowl , add the milk , oil , eggs , and vanilla
5. whisk until blended
6. add the liquid ingredients and 1 / 2 cup chocolate chips to the dry ingredients
7. stir just until dry ingredients are moistened
8. be careful not to overmix
9. pour batter evenly into muffin cups
10. sprinkle remaining chocolate chips evenly over muffin batter
11. bake at 400 degrees for 20-22 minutes or until pick comes out clean
12. place pan on a wire rack to cool for a few minutes before removing muffins from pan
demonstrations.review: Great muffins!

target.recipe_text:
german lemon poppy seed cake

this is a very light moist loaf or bundt cake. this recipe uses very little flour.  very easy to make. goes great with coffee or tea.

1. in a medium bowl mix butter and sugar until creamy
2. blend in each egg separately
3. mix at least 2 minutes
4. add lemon juice , lemon zest , sour cream and poppy seeds
5. mix another 2 minutes
6. into a separate bowl sift flour , baking powder , and salt
7. gently blend flour mixture a little at a time into the batter mixture
8. blend well
9. pour into a greased loaf pan or bundt cake pan
10. bake at 350 degrees f or 180 degrees celsius
11. takes 60 minutes in loaf pan
12. if using bundt cake pan check for doneness at 45 minutes
target.review: I made these into muffins and were fantastic! The sour cream adds a nice tang to it, and they're very moist. I added a little more lemon juice because DH and I like a more lemony flavour. Thank you for sharing your recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
quinoa black bean salad

this is really easy to make. there were no leftovers! what a great combination of flavors and textures. serve with tortilla chips on the side.

1. cook the quinoa in the water
2. allow to cool slightly
3. in a large bowl , combine the oil , lime juice , cumin , coriander , cilantro and scallions
4. stir in the beans , tomatoes , bell peppers and chilies
5. add the cooled quinoa
6. season with salt and pepper to taste
7. serve cold
demonstrations.review: This was my first time using quinoa and I must say that I was disappointed. I couldn't even stand the smell of it cooking. DH liked the salad but I wasn't a huge fan. I thought there was just too much going on in it. Thanks for sharing the recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
hot pepper jelly

this is my signature jelly. i make it for everyone and every occasion. i have even made some and tinted purple for dreamgoddess' daughters wedding. it is very easy and can be made as hot or as mild as you want. for really hot i use 4 habarnero peppers, for milder, use in the amount called for in recipe using your preference in peppers. i just throw the peppers in the blender in large chunks with the vinegar and let the blender to the chopping for me.

1. chop peppers and put in blender with vinegar
2. blend well and pour into large boiler
3. add sugar and mix well
4. bring mixture to a rolling boil and boil for 1 minute
5. remove from heat , strain through sieve and return liquid back to a boil
6. boil for 5 minutes
7. remove from heat
8. add certo and food coloring quickly
9. put into 6 jars and seal
10. i use heated seal method , where i heat the lids in boiling water , place on jar , secure ring tightly and turn jar upside down for 5 minutes
11. turn jar up correctly and allow to cool completely before storing
12. newer studies show that it is safer to seal with the hot water bath method
13. to do this , put into a large boiler with rack on bottom , cover with 1-2 inches of water and boil for 5 minutes
14. remove to rack to cool
demonstrations.review: I made two batches at the same time (one with habaneros and one with jalapenos). I followed the recipe to a T (using 2 packets of certo per batch) and I found that it was extremely liquidy (it hardly thickened at all). It is the next day and I will try to reboil and add more pectin, then rejar. I haven't tasted it yet, but so far I've had issues with the amount of pectin needed.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
easy and tasty barbecue chicken sandwiches in the crock pot

this is almost too easy to be called a recipe, but i had to share it anyway. i came up with it one night when i wanted a nice meal but wasn't feeling too motivated. i love crock-pot cooking!

1. remove all visible fat from the chicken and toss it in the crock pot
2. place the onion slices on top of the chicken
3. pour the barbecue sauce over top
4. you may not need the entire jar , just enough to cover the chicken
5. cook it on low for 8 hours or until the chicken is nice and tender
6. shred the chicken with a fork and knife
7. scoop the mixture onto the bottom buns and top it with the top buns
8. or , if you're like my dad , you might prefer leaving the breasts whole and eating it that way
9. voila !
10. an easy weeknight meal that doesn't heat up your kitchen in the summertime !
11. i love this with potato chips and a carrot and raisin salad
demonstrations.review: I pinched a nerve in my neck last night - so the last thing I wanted to do was cook. I saw this recipe and figured it would be easy enough. I put three large frozen boneless, skinless chicken breasts in the slowcooker, and sprinkled onion salt over them (I needed to go shopping and didn`t have onions). I used a 500ml bottle of Diana`s Rib & Chicken sauce. I cooked it on high for four hours. I shredded the chicken using two meat forks. Even though they were fully cooked, I left them in for another hour on low just to soak up more flavour. I toasted a few sesame buns in some butter in a frying pan and loaded the meat on. They were really good - DH added pickles to his, but I`m more of a purest. I served it with spicy fries and corn. The sides of the chicken got a bit crispy from touching the sides of the crockpot - which we liked since it seemed more like bbq. I think it would have been even better with some creamy coleslaw on top, and baked beans on the side. DH gave this a rating of 8 out of 10. Thanks for sharing this with us!!

target.recipe_text:
gyros   an authentic recipe for making them at home

yes, you can make authentic gyros at home --> the texture and flavor of this meat is as good as you get in a good greek restaurant, without the traditional rotating spit.. but this is just the recipe and technique for making the meat, for i'm assuming you know the drill on making the classic gyro sandwich - stuff the meat in a grilled pita with sliced tomatoes, onions and tzaziki sauce.. enjoy!

1. combine all ingredients in a bowl , and mix well
2. knead the mixture on the counter for 10 minutes - just like you're kneading bread
3. you may want to use a dough-scraper to help keep the counter clean
4. pick that meat up and slam it into the counter , continuing to do so for the 10 minutes
5. this is key to getting the correct texture
6. i'm no alton brown , but i think the thing we're doing here is melting the fat so that we get a nice smooth texture in the end
7. form into a flat loaf - i like to put the meat onto a piece of wax paper , and flattening it into a 3" high slab rectangle
8. i cover it with another piece of wax and use a rolling pin to flatten it out , just make sure you straighten out the edges to form a rectangle so that when it comes time to slice , they are nice and even
9. bake the loaf on a broiler pan at 350 for about an hour
10. alternatively , you can grill it over coals , that's my favorite way , just be sure to turn often so as to distribute the juices
11. allow to cool for at least 10 minutes before slicing thin
target.review: Oh yes! EXACTLY what I was looking for! I'd try Greek Gyros before, with another recipe that turned out bland and desperately disappointing. This one was PERFECT! My husband loved it too, which is just so satisfying. Great flavor, perfect texture...just awesome! I actually only used beef and one pound of it.  And cooking it in the oven at 350 for 35 minutes cooked it beautifully. Yup! Definitely a keeper! Thanks SO much Steve!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
low carb taco bake

serve with additional toppings like shredded lettuce, jalapenos, guacamole, ripe olives, sour cream or salsa.

1. for the crust , beat the cream cheese and eggs until smooth
2. add the cream and seasoning
3. grease a 9"x13" baking dish
4. spread the cheese over the bottom
5. pour in the egg mixture as evenly as possible
6. bake at 375f , 25-30 minutes
7. let stand 5 minutes before adding the topping
8. for the topping , brown the hamburger
9. drain fat
10. stir in the seasoning , tomato sauce and chiles
11. spread over the crust
12. top with cheese
13. reduce oven to 350f and bake another 20 minutes or so until hot and bubbly
14. serve with the toppings of your choice
demonstrations.review: Superb meal! Just my husband and I ate almost the entire dish. We had the typical lettuce, tomato and salsa topping. My husband gave it four stars, but only because I didn't have sour cream. So voila! This is AWESOME! Loved it! Especially with the fact of its low carb content. Highly recommended! A+++++

demonstrations.recipe_text:
breakfast in a crock pot

an easy recipe to be done overnight and ready to serve your family or guests in the morning

1. divide potatoes , ham , vegetables and cheese so you can create several layers of each in the crock pot
2. start with the hash browns , then ham , onions , peppers and lastly cheese
3. repeat until you have several layers of each
4. beat eggs , milk , salt and pepper
5. pour this over the layers in the crock pot
6. cook on low for 10 to 12 hours overnight
demonstrations.review: Maybe I just didn't do it right somehow but this did NOT turn out well at all. It burned slightly, even on low for ten hours, didn't make the house smell that spiffy and the taste was really bland. It's a great idea, but this just didn't work out at all for me or my hubby.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
thick chocolate pudding

this is the perfect chocolate pudding. it has a rich chocolate flavor, great texture and is not high in fat. i can't count the number of times i have made this. i hope you enjoy it as much as we do.

1. in a 2-qt
2. microwave-safe bowl , combine the first four ingredients
3. stir in milk until smooth
4. microwave , uncovered on high for 3 minutes
5. stir
6. microwave 4-6 minutes longer or until thickened , stirring after each minute
7. stir in vanilla
8. pour into individual serving dishes
9. cool
10. refrigerate
11. garnish with whipped topping if desired
demonstrations.review: This recipe was good, but had an odd grainy texture my husband and I didn't especially care for. I enjoyed the chocolate flavor, and it set up beautifully! But something just seems to be missing out of this one.

target.recipe_text:
weight watchers 0 point tortilla soup

a great soup that fills you up and only 0 points on the ww program.

1. simmer onions , garlic & green onions in a pan until tender
2. put all ingredients in a pot , simmer until all veggies are tender
3. you can add chicken , divide the points by 9 servings
4. taste great with a couple toasted taco shells on the side , but count your points --
target.review: Are you sure this is 0 points!  Could I eat the entire pot?  I loved it, made it exactly as written and next time will make a double batch to last through the week.  Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
rhubarb crumble pie

this easy, old fashioned family recipe goes back more than 5 generations - from kate kelly of kanata, ontario! make your own pastry base or buy a ready made shell to save time. you can aso make this with a full pastry or lattice top. try adding a tsp of orange zest to the filling - its delicious!

1. topping: combine flour& sugar in a bowl
2. using a pastry blender or 2 knives , cut in butter until mixture is in fine crumbs
3. set aside
4. pie: combine sugar , flour& salt in a bowl
5. whisk in egg until smooth
6. add rhubarb& toss to coat
7. scrape into pie shell& dot with butter
8. sprinkle topping evenly over filling
9. bake in the bottom third of a preheated 425f oven for 10 minutes
10. reduce heat to 350f& continue baking until topping is golden& filling is bubbly , about 40 minutes
11. remove from oven& cool on a rack
demonstrations.review: Followed directions exactly, but the pie was so sweet and sugary we couldn't eat it.  We ended up dumping all but 2 pieces.  I would recommend adding less sugar.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cheesy cheesy cheesy   macaroni and cheese

this is for my son!!!! a great side but my son makes a meal out of it!

1. cook pasta aldente , drain and set aside
2. heat oven to degrees
3. in a microwave proof dish melt butter and stir in flour
4. whisk in milk and half and half
5. microwave stirring every minute , until sauce begins to thicken about 5 minutes
6. season with salt , pepper , curry and the hot sauce
7. remove from heat and stir in remaining ingredients except for parmesan cheese
8. pour in a buttered casserole pan
9. sprinkle top with parmesan
10. bake for 30 minutes until bubbly and golden
demonstrations.review: Was hoping my young children would appreciate the change from Kraft Mac & Cheese, but did not turn out as others have described.  I followed the directions exactly, minus the peas, but it was very pasty, "floury".  I didn't rate this as I may have made a mistake in the prep.  Will try again another time.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
just like loaded baked potatoes casserole

this is an awesome low-carb version of loaded baked potatoes, and tastes far better than any version of mock potatoes that i have tried. in fact, this dish is soooo good, you will not believe it!  i do not remember where i got this recipe, but it is a fabulous side to any low-carb meal. you will be pleased, i promise! yum! yum!

1. pre-heat oven to 350
2. chop cooked cauliflower into very small pieces
3. mix sour cream , 1 / 2 of the green onions , 1 / 2 of the cheese , 1 / 2 of the bacon , and salt and pepper to taste in medium bowl
4. stir in the cauliflower
5. place in medium baking dish and sprinkle remaining cheese and bacon on top
6. bake for 20 minutes
7. sprinkle the remaining green onions on top just before serving
demonstrations.review: This was delicious! I did follow some other's suggestions and due to being on a very low carb diet, exchanged the sour cream for cream cheese. Otherwise, followed the directions.  I used a potato masher and it had more of a creamy, cheesy rice consistency.  Even my picky kids thought it was good.  This is a must have recipe when watching your carbs.  I'm making it a second time for this week!  Thanks Helping Hands

target.recipe_text:
lentil croquettes

yummy!

1. place the first 10 ingredients in a large pan and bring to a boil
2. reduce heat and simmer slowly , about 30 minutes until all the liquid has been absorbed
3. remove the mixture from heat and cool slightly
4. now beat in the egg and season to taste with salt and pepper
5. let the mixture cool completely
6. combine the flour , turmeric and chili powder in a small plate
7. once lentils are cool , shape the mixture into circles
8. roll the croquettes in the above spiced flour mixture to coat well
9. heat oil in a skillet and cook the croquettes in batches , turning once until crisp and brown on both sides
10. serve immediately with chutney or a crisp salad
target.review: I did as another viewer suggested and baked them in the oven. Suggestion though, you don't need flour if you cook them in the oven. My mixture was a little too runny while making the patties, but they turned out alright. I didn't have garam marsala or turmeric, so I compensated with extra salt and pepper. I also thought the mixture could have used more peppers, perhaps some red bell peppers to contrast the green.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
legal seafood style baked scallops

whenever we get back to the boston area, it's a priority to to have a meal at legal seafoods.  i recently "re-discovered" this recipe buried in old newspaper clippings. i had tried to recreate it in the past but now know i was missing the most important ingredient - buttermilk. i made it again after posting the recipe so i have edited the original description. it's even better than i remembered, you might want to try just a dash (or more) of cayenne pepper. it's delightful !

1. preheat oven to 400f
2. place scallops in a bowl , season with salt and pepper , add thyme and buttermilk and toss to coat
3. place scallops , with buttermilk , evenly in the bottom of an oven proof dish , sprinkle with cracker crumbs and top with melted butter
4. bake for 20 minutes , squeeze lemon over scallops and serve immediately
demonstrations.review: Excellent and easy. I made half the recipe since we don't eat much. I also decreased the butter to 2.5 tbsp (instead of 4). I added a few dashes of cayenne pepper as recommended. I forgot the lemon at the end, but I didn't miss it. Will definitely make again; added to my "favorite recipes" category.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
peanut butter no bake cookies

posted in response to a request, i got this recipe from a lady at church who make them for bible school in the 1980s.  i had made chocolate no-bake cookies for years but had never heard of peanut butter no bake cookies.  so delicious that my choco-holic daughter likes them better than the chocolate variety!
no. of servings depends on how big you make the cookies.  prep time depends on how fast you are scooping the cookies onto the wax paper covered newspaper!  (you get better w/ practice!  :d )

1. in lg saucepan , mix sugar , margarine , and milk
2. bring to a full , rolling boil over med heat
3. boil for one minute , stirring constantly
4. remove from heat and stir in peanut butter and vanilla , stirring until peanut butter is melted
5. stir in oats
6. working quickly , drop by spoonfuls onto waxed paper
7. let cool completely
demonstrations.review: Rich and delicious. Hard to eat only one! Loved the texture. I used 1/2 cup brown sugar and 1.5 cups white sugar. I also threw in handful or two of milk chocolate chips. I ended up with 26 decent sized cookies.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
the best chili you will ever taste

this is the best chili recipe i have ever tried. i'm not sure where the recipe originated, but it is amazing! sometimes, i don't bother adding all four cans of the kidney beans and it still turns out wonderful. once anyone tastes this chili, they will be begging for the recipe!! enjoy!

1. heat oil
2. cook onions , garlic and meat until brown
3. add tomatoes , beer , coffee , tomato paste and beef broth
4. add spices stir in 2 cans of kidney beans and peppers
5. reduce heat and simmer for 1 1 / 2 hours
6. add 2 remaining cans of kidney beans and simmer for another 30 minutes
demonstrations.review: Not much to add to all of the other reviews. I've made this three times now and apparently have not reviewed it yet. I skip the sirloin and use more types of beans but otherwise stick pretty closely to the listed ingredients. Delicious.

target.recipe_text:
apple butter bread  two recipes

this recipe comes from the virginia apple growers assoc site. i have posted the original and my recipe that was a mistake to begin with, but we love it now. i used apple butter recipe #93886 from margo.

1. combine flour , brown sugar , baking powder , baking soda and salt in a large mixing bowl
2. in a small bowl mix 3 / 4 cup apple butter , apple juice , butter and egg together
3. fold in the raisins and chopped nuts
4. add the apple butter mixture to the dry ingredients and blend together
5. pour half the mixture in a loaf pan that has been sprayed with cooking spray
6. gently spread the reserved 3 / 4 cup apple butter over the batter
7. pour the rest of the batter over the apple butter mixture and spread evenly over the top to cover
8. bake at 350 degrees for 55 to 65 minutes or until done
9. to bake "my mistake loaf" just put all the apple butter in the wet ingredients and blend into the dry ingredients
10. i cut up dried pineapple pieces and added with the nuts instead of the raisins
11. pour the whole batter into the loaf pan and bake as above
12. this makes a heavy moist bread that is delicious
13. any kind of nuts can be used and any kind of dried fruit that your prefer
14. this can be sugar free using splenda brown sugar blend and margo's apple butter recipe using splenda
target.review:
This was really yummy.  I would not change a thing.  I used my own home made apple butter - I know this will be a oft requested bread in the future.
Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
weight watchers general tso s chicken

great ww recipe from a meeting. 8points plus per serving.

1. in a medium bowl , whisk together broth , cornstarch , sugar , soy sauce , vinegar and ginger
2. set aside
3. heat oil in a wok or large skillet over medium-high heat
4. add scallions , garlic and pepper and cook 2 minutes
5. add chicken and cook until browned all over , about 5 minutes
6. add reserved sauce and simmer until sauce thickens and chicken is cooked through , about 3 minutes
7. serve chicken and sauce over rice
8. yields about 1 cup of chicken and sauce and 1 / 2 cup of rice per serving
demonstrations.review:
This was very good - my DH prefers his General Tso's unbreaded, so this was the ticket. The sauce was very flavorful, but not hot/spicy enough for us - this can easily be remedied by adding Cayenne or stir-frying whole hot peppers prior to everything else, which we will do next time.
Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
see s fudge candy  the  original recipe

this is the original see's fudge recipe i found when i did a google search  
historical note:
 given to amy devore by emma julian c. 1930, this is “supposedly” the original recipe for see's fudge, produced by the see's candy company,  los angeles. emma allegedly worked for see's and later owned her own candy store.

1. mix 4 1 / 2 cups sugar with one can evaporated milk
2. boil 7 to 8 minutes , stirring often
3. mix together in a large bowl
4. 3 packages chocolate chips , 7 oz
5. jar marshmallow cream , 1 / 2 lb
6. melted margarine
7. cream margarine and marshmallow together and add chocolate chips
8. pour hot mixture over chocolate mixture
9. after chocolate has melted , add 2 cups of nuts and 1 teaspoons of vanilla , blend well , pour into buttered pans and chill in refrigerator
10. cut into squares before firm
11. this recipe makes about 5 lbs of fudge
12. no one has attempted a calorie count , but it's estimated that each piece contains about 47 gazillion calories
13. dieters , beware !
demonstrations.review:
I made this for my DH for Valentine's as See's fudge is his favorite ($$$!!).  It was easy and he loved it, but it makes a tremendous amount, so be prepared to share as gifts!
Thanks - I will be making again at Christmas and sharing!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
italian sausage frittata

this can be served for breakfast, brunch, lunch or dinner. it's a fairly simple recipe with ingredients that are easily found in the grocery store! i personally use the spicy turkey italian sausages when making this recipe although it calls for mild.

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees
2. brown sausage in sauce pan and drain
3. spread evenly over bottom of 9 x 13 baking dish
4. saut mushrooms and garlic in butter until almost all liquid is absorbed (you can add a few dashes of white wine at this stage if you prefer
5. spread mushrooms over sausage
6. layer swiss chard and cheese over mushrooms
7. in bowl beat the eggs , milk and dijon mustard and pour evenly over all
8. place in oven on middle rack , bake uncovered for 1 hour ,
9. remove from the oven , cover loosely with foil , and let stand 15-18 minutes
10. divide and cut into serving sizes
11. top with green onions or sour cream if you desire
demonstrations.review: I made this for an Italian themed lunch at work - was looking for something other than pasta.  This was easy and a great hit!  Everyone wanted the recipe.  It was great to be able to pop it in the oven!

target.recipe_text:
chris s barbecue chicken

one of the ladies in my mother's group made us this chicken on the barbecue for lunch one week. we all loved it, and i am putting her recipe here for safe keeping. chris suggests making extra as they are excellent cold, too! they are very easy to make. cook time includes time to marinate in the fridge.

1. put all the sauce ingredients into a large bowl and add the chops , turning to coat
2. leave to marinate in the fridge
3. the longer the better -- overnight is terrific , but just a few hours is good too
4. cook on a hot barbecue 15 - 20 minutes , turning once or twice , and basting them with any sauce left in the dish
5. or you can cook them in the oven on about 200 for slightly longer -- say 20 - 30 minutes
target.review: I've just returned from a BBQ and I took some chicken drums marinated in this recipe, would love to give it a personal rating put it was all gone by the time I got to the head of the queue, so my sons said it was brilliant.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
iced sugar cookies  cake like cookies  soft icing

there is a brand of store bought, iced sugar cookies in my area that i just love.  they are called debbie joe's.  i dare say these are better.  i can make them from home so they are economical, more fresh, and lack any of those commercial baking ingrediets.  i just love them.  you can add the vanilla but i actually find they taste better without it.

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees
2. for the cookies beat the butter and sugar until creamed
3. add in eggs and vanilla and beat until smooth
4. combine dry ingredients
5. add dry ingredients and milk into the creamed mixture in two batches
6. refrigerate dough for up to an hour
7. use 2 'tablespoons' to make 2-3 inch balls of dough
8. bake for 10-12 minutes
9. the tops of the cookies shouldn't be browned
10. for the frosting beat all ingredients together until smooth adding more milk if necessary
11. when cookies are cool , frost and add sprinkles if you like
demonstrations.review: If I could give a hundred stars I would to this yummy recipe. So popular were these cookies, that my 17 year old son has just called his brother a pig monkey for eating the last one. I cooked them exactly to the recipe, they turned out beatifully and I have to make some more tonight to keep everyone happy.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
curried quiche

this is a very tasty quiche that i put together for a tea-time spread. we had samosas, indian sweets, and this- it was a huge hit- and very simple. a great last minute addition to any menu.

1. preheat oven to 350
2. beat eggs and milk thoroughly in a bowl
3. stir in onions , tomato , chillies
4. stir in curry powder and black pepper
5. add salt according to your tastes
6. pour mixture into pie crust
7. bake 50 minutes at 350
8. complete cooking time
demonstrations.review: I liked the quiche although I thought it needed more curry powder. DH loved it but he likes his food blander.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
carrot potato casserole

haven't tried this yet, but it looks absolutely yummy.

1. in a saucepan over medium heat , melt butter
2. whisk in the flour , salt and pepper until smooth
3. gradually stir in milk
4. bring to a boil
5. cook and stir 2 minutes
6. reduce heat
7. add 1 / 2 cup cheese , stirring until melted
8. add the potatoes , carrots , and onion
9. transfer to a greased 8-in
10. square baking dish
11. cover and bake at 350 degrees for 1 hour
12. uncover
13. sprinkle with the remaining cheese
14. bake 15 minutes longer or until potatoes are tender
demonstrations.review: Decided to try this for you, and very tasty it was too, though I did add 1 teaspoon of mustard powder to add some zing. Some leftovers for tomorrow and I think it will taste just as nice cold.

target.recipe_text:
potato  green bean and bacon chowder

this is a thick and hearty potato soup. it really satisfies a hungry appetite on a cold day. i have prepared the soup and left in a crockpot on low for several hours.

1. fry bacon until crisp in large dutch oven or stock pot
2. add onion and saute for 2 or 3 minutes
3. pour off fat
4. add potatoes and water
5. bring to boil , cover and simmer 10 to 15 minutes , or until potatoes are tender
6. stir in soup and sour cream
7. gradually add milk
8. add green beans
9. add pepper and parsley
10. heat to serving temperature
11. do not boil
target.review: This was absolutely delicious.  I cheated and bought some pre-cooked diced potatoes (like they sell refrigerated with hashbrowns...don't remember the name of them.  I think it's "Simply Potatoes."I put it in the crockpot and added a can of clams, some baby shrimp and some crab for a seafood chowder.  My-Oh-My..it is delicious!  Ivars..eat your heart out!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
hamburger noodle bake

this is almost like a lasagna. very good!

1. brown hamburger , onions , and spices until cooked
2. add tomato sauce and simmer 15 minutes
3. mix cream cheese and sour cream
4. in 2-quart casserole , put 1 / 3 noodles , 1 / 3 cream mix , 1 / 3 meat mix
5. repeat twice
6. sprinkle cheddar on top
7. bake at 350 for 20 minutes
demonstrations.review:
Excellent!  I'll definitely make this again.  We liked it better than spaghetti.  I added more tomato sauce, using the entire jar (about 24 oz).  I mixed everything together instead of layering to insure a uniform creaminess and flavor.
I served it with garlic bread and it made for a yummy dinner.  Thanks for sharing.  It's a well written recipie.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
banana nut yeast bread  bread machine

something different - banana yeast bread with a hint of cinnamon and toasted chopped walnuts. bake time is per bread machine. really easy in your bread machine or you can make it the conventional way. fabulous!

1. spread walnuts in a single layer on a baking pan and bake at 350 for 5 to 10 minutes or til light brown
2. watch carefully and stir once or twice
3. add ingredients to bread machine according to manufacturer's direction , adding the banana with the milk
4. use regular or white setting
demonstrations.review: This is quite possibly the best bread machine bread I have ever made.  I added a handfull of raisens.  It makes excellent sandwiches, and is great toasted as well.  Thanks for sharing.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
roasted squash  potatoes  shallots   herbs

this is wonderful, healthy, warming dish for these cold months. i've also added sweet potatoes, parsnips, carrots and pearl onions. you can mix and match any root veggie you like.

1. preheat oven to 425f
2. combine squash , potatoes shallots and garlic in large shallow baking pan
3. drizzle with oil
4. salt and pepper to taste
5. top with herbs
6. bake 45-50 minutes , turning once after vegetables are browned on one side
7. the skins of the potatoes and squash have lots of fiber and vitamins so i leave them on you can remove them if you want
8. season with salt and pepper if desired
demonstrations.review: In addition to the veggies listed, I added a sweet potato, leek, carrots and mushrooms. I mixed a package of dry lipton onion soup to the olive oil and mixed it all up in a bowl and poured it in a roasting pan. When done, I sprinkled some parmesean cheese on top and browned it under the broiler. My family LOVED it. It's a definite keeper.

target.recipe_text:
spinach garlic pizza

i love pizza without tomato sauce or what is called white pizza. we love this! it is so good and easy!

1. mix olive oil and garlic in small microwavable bowl
2. microwave on high 30 seconds
3. place pizza crust on cookie sheet
4. brush entire surface with oil mixture
5. top with spinach , mozzarella cheese , tomato slices and feta cheese
6. sprinkle pizza with rosemary and parmesan bake at 450' f for 10 to 12 minutes or until cheese is melted and crust is golden
7. let stand 5 minutes
target.review: FANTASTIC! I did make some changes- I used a homemade dough and prebaked it for a few minutes. Spread about 2-3 tbs olive oil on, RAW spinach leaves and 3 cloves minced garlic, 2 cups mozzarella, tomatoes, mushrooms, the herb feta and left off the rosemary. Sprinkled on parmesan and crushed red pepper after. Delish! I definitely like the fresh spinach here.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
spinach   basil pesto

this is a tasty basil-spinach pesto, good on bruschetta, chicken, pasta, and more.  it is from relish magazine.

1. combine spinach , basil , pine nuts and garlic in a food processor
2. pulse for a few seconds
3. with the machine running , add olive oil
4. process until mixture is creamy
5. this may need to be done in batches
6. transfer to a glass bowl
7. stir in cheese , salt , and pepper
demonstrations.review: Very tasty! I didn't really measure, just used a bunch of basil, most of a 10oz bag of spinach, the rest of my olive oil, etc. I did use 3 cloves of garlic since we love it. This will be perfect on the turkey paninis I am making today!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pamela s gluten free brownies

this was the first thing i ever made with pamela's baking & pancake mix.  this recipe was taken from pamela's website. however, it is no longer there and i thought i'd post it - mainly for me because i have a tendency to lose recipes!!!

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees
2. mix all ingredients together until there are no lumps
3. pour into a greased 8" square pan
4. bake for 25 minutes or when a toothpick inserted in the center comes out clean
5. be careful not to overbake
demonstrations.review: I was pleasantly surprised at these! I used Arrowhead Mills GF all purpose baking mix instead of Pamelas (that's what I had here) and did everything else the same, using nuts.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
neighborhood ham and bean soup

the flavors in this bean soup remind me of the bean soup my grandmother used to make on our farm in ohio when i was a young girl.  i love to make it during the winter months -- it doesn't last long.  my daughter is now making it for her family as well.  maybe it's called "neighborhood" bean soup because the neighbors love it when i make it -- it's a wonderful soup to share with special friends. it is great served wtih a nice piece of hot corn bread. i can't remember exactly where i found the recipe -- but i'm glad i have it and i hope you will feel the same.

1. place beans in a dutch oven or soup kettle
2. add water to cover by 2
3. bring to a boil
4. boil for 2 minutes
5. remove from heat , cover and let stand for 1 hour
6. drain
7. add broth , water , ham bone , bouillon and seasonings
8. bring to a boil
9. reduce heat
10. cover and simmer for 2 hours
11. saut onions , carrots and celery in oil
12. add to soup along with cubed potato
13. cover and simmer 1 hour longer
14. debone ham and cut into chunks
15. return to soup
16. skim fat
17. i like to mash some of the beans once they get soft
18. my total cooking time is more like 6 hours than 4 hours
19. great served with corn bread
demonstrations.review: This is the best ham and bean soup I have ever had! Packed with flavor and pretty easy to make too. I used a lb of dried beans and my ham bone had TONS of meat left on it, which fell right apart after cooking in the soup for 3 1/2 hours. I will probably skip the boiullon next time as it was pretty salty (no extra salt needed!)- though it might be that we had a salty ham . Thanks for sharing this one.

target.recipe_text:
ro tel chicken spaghetti

easy, easy, easy!!! i got this recipe from an aunt who made it for a family reunion. it has a great flavor and makes alot. very good! does not include cooking time for the chicken.

1. in a bowl mix together the soup , broth& ro-tel tomatoes
2. in a 13x9 greased casserole dish layer as follows: spaghetti , chicken , soup mix , cheese
3. bake in a preheated 350 degree oven until heated through and cheese melts about 30-45 minutes
4. as soon as you remove from the oven stir to mix well , adding salt and pepper to taste
target.review: I cooked the chicken in the pot w/ the pasta, pulling it out ater a few minutes. I only had 2 whole breasts, so a can of black beans, drained & rinsed was added along w/ about 8 oz. of pepper jack cheese (skipping the Velvetta). Seems to be a recipe w/ a lot of room for fudge:). I make it early in the day for time for flabors to meld then reheat in the mw at mealtime. Tastes as you might expect w/ those flavor componets. Salt & pepper is about all you need.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
nutella cookies

i had these cookies for the first time at a football tailgate and they were so delicious that we were all amazed to find out that one of the guys had made them. he got the original recipe from a tailgating website and they are way too delicious and easy not to pass on.

1. 1
2. in one bowl , whisk together flour , baking powder , baking soda and salt
3. set aside
4. 2
5. in the bowl of a mixer , cream the butter and the two sugars until all is integrated and fluffy
6. 3
7. mix in the nutella , followed by the chopped hazelnuts
8. beat in the eggs one at a time , followed by the vanilla
9. 4
10. add the flour mixture to the mixing bowl in three increments , integrating each one before adding the next
11. 5
12. chill dough while oven preheats to 350f scoop the dough into balls and bake for about 10 minutes
demonstrations.review: Followed the recipe exactly.  I toasted my hazelnuts on a slow burner, tossing in a skillet for about 1/2 hr.  They were rolled in a towel as suggested to take the skins off before chopping.  Turned out quite nicely.  They set up after sitting a bit and are easier to handle.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
grape nuts oatmeal cranberry cookies

i recently tried these from a recipe on the post grape-nuts cereal box.  delicious!  robb

1. preheat oven to 375f
2. mix flour , baking soda and salt in small bowl
3. beat margarine in large bowl with electric mixer on medium speed to soften
4. gradually add sugars , beating until light and fluffy
5. beat in egg and vanilla
6. gradually add flour mixture , beating well after each addition
7. stir in cereal , oats and cranberries
8. drop by rounded tablespoonfuls onto ungreased cookie sheets
9. bake 8 minutes or until lightly browned
10. cooled 1 minute
11. remove from cookie sheets
12. cool completely on wire racks
demonstrations.review: Recipe goes together fast w/ a stand mixer.  Nice balance of the sweet-salt with the firm cereal base and sweet, chewy hits of cranberries intermingled in the buttery, sweet goo of oatmeal base.  I don't know if I've lost track in counting out my oatmeal, or what, but I'm always adding another 1/3 cup (quick oats).  I get abut 42 cookies, 16 rouned teaspoons per baking sheet on which they don't melt together as they bake.  So I'm feeling like I have the right amount per spoonful fort he size of cookie I want.  I do add 2 more min. to the baking time, however.  After cooling slightly, they do come off the sheet easily.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
bread machine buttermilk and honey wheat bread

this is one of my favorites. the recipe came from eagle mills. if you don't have buttermilk, you can substitute 1 cup milk plus 1 teaspoon cider vinegar, and let it sit about 10 minutes before using. you can also add 4 tbs. buttermilk powder to the dry ingredients and substitute water for the buttermilk. i have also used plain all-purpose flour with excellent results.

1. put all ingredients in bread machine for 1 1 / 2 lb
2. loaf in the order suggested by the manufacturer
3. bake using whole wheat cycle
demonstrations.review: We have a Hitachi Home Bakery bread machine, 2 lb. loaf capacity.  SO happy to have found this recipe!  We get a nice sized loaf of super-flavorful bread.  It makes great toast and is perfect for sandwiches.  Because it's a sturdy bread, we can slice it thinner than most any other breads we make.  It's just a wonderful all-around great bread.

target.recipe_text:
crab rangoon dip

i received this recipe from my sister-in-law. it is very good and hard to stop eating once you start.

1. dip: soften cream cheese in microwave
2. stir in rest of ingredients
3. spread in serving bowl
4. before serving , microwave to warm
5. top with sweet and sour sauce
6. to make wonton strips :
7. cut each wonton wrapper in half
8. spray with nonstick cooking spray and sprinkle with parmesan cheese
9. bake 5-7 minutes at 375 or until slightly brown
target.review: This was just ok for me.  I followed the recipe exactly.  If I make it again I will maybe use my electric mixer or food processor to break up the crab more.  I might also use less crab.  The best part were the wonton chips.  I might also use something like soy sauce to give it a little kick.  I seems to be lacking something.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mexican rice casserole

a great way to use a pound of ground beef and make a dinner that all will love.  it's so easy too!  if you cannot find mexicorn by green giant, you can use a regular can of corn or frozen corn.  to control the heat of the dish, you can choose mild, medium or hot salsa!

1. place the 2 cups of water and long grain rice in a medium sauce pan and bring to a boil
2. reduce heat to a simmer , place a lid on , set timer for 20 minutes and cook rice until done
3. preheat oven to 350f
4. in a skillet , brown ground beef and drain
5. place in a large mixing bowl
6. in large mixing bowl , add the jar of salsa to the ground beef
7. also add chili powder , mexicorn , rice and salt
8. mix with a wooden spoon until combined well
9. spray a 2 quart casserole dish
10. put rice mixture into dish
11. cover with a lid or foil and bake in preheated oven for 30 minutes
12. at 30 minutes , take off lid / foil
13. add shredded cheddar cheese evenly over top and bake for an additional 5 minutes
14. remove from oven and serve
demonstrations.review: This was really easy to make.  I used Jasmin rice instead of long grain.  I added southwestern corn because that is what I had on hand.  I also add taco seasoning instead of chili powder.  Still tasted great.  Served it with tortillas.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chicken pot pie with 2 crusts

this is old-fashioned, from scratch, comfort food. this has been a family favorite for years. i like to take this to other families when they are in need of a meal. it's always a winner. i like making it with leftover turkey, too! i often add some cooked diced potatoes.

1. heat butter over low heat until melted
2. blend in flour , onion , salt and pepper
3. cook over low heat , stirring constantly until smooth and bubbly
4. remove from heat
5. stir in broth and milk
6. heat to boiling
7. stirring constantly
8. boil and stir one minute
9. stir in chicken and veggies
10. reserve
11. line pie plate with prepared bottom crust
12. pour in filling
13. top with top crust
14. cut slits in center to vent
15. flute edges
16. cook uncovered in 425f oven until crust is brown
17. approximately 30-35 minutes
demonstrations.review: This tastes awesome!  It makes a little too much filling for me so I recommend that us change it to 4 servings. The sauce is very easy and quick to make. The only thing that I changed is the frozen veggies cause sometimes they are too crunchy for my taste. I used canned mixed vegetables and I added new potatoes. I prefer Mrs. Smith pie crusts. Will be making again soon!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
hamburger hash browns hotdish

this recipe is from an old cookbook from my mother's home town. very hearty and tasty.

1. butter a 9x13-inch pan
2. cover bottom of pan with hash browns
3. add hamburger , salt pepper and onions
4. sprinkle peas on top
5. mix soup and milk together and pour over peas
6. top with cheese
7. cover with foil and bake at 350f for one hour
8. sprinkle with french fried onions and return to oven for ten more minutes
demonstrations.review: Good stuff.  I never use peas for this I usually use corn or carrots or both.  It is good with or without the french-fried onions. Next time I might use cream of chicken/mushroom.  This is great for a weekday meal when you don't have a lot of time.

target.recipe_text:
weight watchers egg salad

i love egg salad and was thrilled when a friend passed this recipe along from a recent ww meeting. 3 delicious little points per serving.

1. place eggs in a medium saucepan and pour in enough water to cover them
2. set pan over high heat and bring to a boil
3. boil 10 minutes
4. drain and place eggs in an ice-water bath
5. when eggs are cool enough to handle , remove shells
6. discard yolks from two of the eggs
7. cut remaining whole eggs and whites into 1 / 2-inch pieces
8. transfer eggs to a medium bowl
9. add chives , mayonnaise , mustard , dill , salt and pepper
10. mix until blended
11. yields about 1 / 2 cup per serving
target.review: This recipe was yummy!! This was the first time I tried egg salad. I am currently doing weight watcher's Flex Plan with the point system, and this is a good recipe for so few points. My husband thought it was great also. I used Kraft's real "light" mayonaise. It won the 2007 best chef award for taste...and I agree that it is a good mayo. Even better than my usual choice, Hellmans. I am sure I will be making this quick recipe often. Thanks for sharing.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
marinated salmon seared in a pepper crust

this may seem like alot of pepper, but it is not only edible, but delicious. in fact, sometimes i add even more. we love our salmon here in the pacific nw and this is one of our favorites.

1. in a sealable plastic bag combine well the soy sauce , the garlic , the lemon juice , and the sugar , add the salmon , coating it well , and let it marinate , sealed and chilled , for 30 minutes
2. remove the salmon from the bag , discarding the marinade , pat it dry , and press 2 teaspoons of the pepper onto each piece of salmon , coating it thoroughly
3. in a heavy skillet heat the oil over moderately high heat until it is hot but not smoking and in it saut the salmon for 2 minutes on each side , or until it just flakes
4. transfer the salmon with a slotted spatula to paper towels and let it drain for 30 seconds
demonstrations.review: This was verrrrry good! My husband catches a ton of salmon and I am always looking for new ways to fix it. You were right by saying this recipe is in the top three. Great flavors. A little sweet and a little spicey...but not too spicey. We will definately use this recipe often.  Thanks!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
hawaiian chicken kabobs

the marinade is the key to these great kabobs. they only need 1 hour in the refrigerator to marinate.

1. put chicken in large shallow dish
2. drain pineapple , keep 1 / 2 cup juice
3. set pineapple aside
4. mix juice with the next 7 ingredients in small pan
5. bring to a boil
6. reduce heat and simmer for 5 minutes
7. pour over chicken
8. cover and chill for 1 hour
9. remove chicken from marinade , reserve marinade
10. alternate chicken , pineapple , green pepper , mushrooms , and tomatoes on skewers
11. grill kabobs over hot coals 20 minutes or until chicken is done
12. turn and baste frequently with marinade
13. serve over hot rice
demonstrations.review: Really liked this recipe. Nice marinade. Took them to a cookout. Received tons of compliments. Thanks....this recipe is a keeper.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
my family s favorite sloppy joes  pizza joes

i've tried many recipes, this is the best. i once 'dec-tupled' (10x) this recipe to sell sandwiches at a craft fair at my church. people were waiting in line to buy leftovers. freezes well, goes up to the lake or camping well and is a hit on halloween...it's no-fail. easy to double, triple, etc. i've been making joes this way for over 20 years.
***03-08-09, i just reinvented this recipe tonight when i went to make it for dinner and found i didn't have an 8-oz. can of tomato sauce (shame on me).  the family was upset with me when i subbed an 8-oz. can of pizza sauce and told them to suck it up and call them 'pizza joes' and then served them up with shredded mozzarella cheese on the toasted buns, top and bottom.  they loved it.  i left out the bbq sauce in this preparation and just used a 1/2 cup ketchup.  pizza joes are good to go!

1. in a large skillet , brown ground beef , celery and onion
2. drain the fat , who needs it ?
3. stir in remaining ingredients , simmer covered , 15-20 minutes , stirring occasionally
4. if joes appear too'loose' , leave cover off and let moisture evaporate
5. cook until it's the consistency you like for serving on toasted buns , with french fries and cole slaw
demonstrations.review: These sloppy joes have very good flavor. My family liked them alot. The only thing I would do different next time, would be to add a little more meat. I thought there was alot of sauce, so I think the extra meat would take care of that. Maybe an extra 1/2 lb of meat. I don't like them dry....just a little less messy. Flavor was fantastic though. Thanks for the easy recipe. Will be making them again.

target.recipe_text:
crock pot pumpkin pie pudding

just in time for the holidays. a family favorite.

1. in a large bowl mix together the first eight ingredients
2. transfer to crock pot coated with pam
3. cover and cook on low 6-7 hours
4. serve in bowls with whip cream , if desired
target.review: Not what I expected.  Basically, pumpkin pie filling in the crock pot only I didn't even think it tasted as good as pumpkin pie.  Cook time is way overstated.  I had hopes of something along the lines of bread pudding.  Nowhere close.  I would only recommend this recipe with half the cook time and only if you are looking for something extremely simple and bland.  Just my opinion.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
tortellini tomato spinach soup

really healthy soup, good to use when there's no time to spend in the kitchen!

1. in a soup pot , heat olive oil over medium high heat
2. saute the onion and garlic , stirring often until onions are translucent , about 5 to 7 minutes
3. add broth and tomatoes , turn heat up to high , and bring to a boil
4. add the tortellini and cook according to package instructions
5. when tortellini is almost done , add spinach and taste , adjusting seasonings with salt and pepper
6. serve immediately
7. garnish each serving with a sprinkling of parmesan
demonstrations.review: Too Good to be so easy!  Eating the leftovers was almost better!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
whatever floats your boat  brownies

these are absolutely the chewiest, moistest, fudgiest brownies ever! i have tried adding so many different things to the batter, and they always comes out great.  they are also great without any add-ins! but by varying the add-ins, you can make different brownies every week (or day!!) super easy prep! so, add "whatever floats your boat" and you will not believe how yummy they come out :) oh, and the recipe doubles just fine--use a 9 x 13 inch pan instead and add a few more minutes of baking!

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. grease an 8 inch square pan or line with foil
3. in a medium bowl combine melted butter and cocoa and stir until cocoa is dissolved
4. add sugar and mix well
5. add eggs one at a time and stir until well combined
6. stir in vanilla , flour and salt until you no longer see any flour
7. fold in "whatever floats your boat" !
8. spread in pan and bake for approximately 25 minutes
9. do not over-bake -- your brownies will come out dry
10. adjust time / temp accordingly for your oven
11. if you do the knife / toothpick test , it should come out with moist crumbs , not clean
12. cool completely before cutting into squares
13. for vegetarian omit the marshmallows
14. for double recipe , bake in 9x12 pan and add 5 minutes to baking time
demonstrations.review: What can I say that hasn't already been said?  I've done these several times.  I like adding butterscotch chips, white chocolate chips and coconut.  YUM YUM!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
oreo balls

my sister's co-worker brought these to a party and they were quite a hit. i don't know where the recipe came from originally.

"bark" is an artificial chocolate or vanilla candy coating/confectioner's coating used to make a treat called almond bark and can be found at most grocery stores near the chocolate chips. 

you can use chocolate chips and white chocolate chips if you don't have almond bark, but i have found that almond bark melts better and is easier to work with.

1. using a blender or hand held mixer , mix oreos and cream cheese together
2. roll into walnut size balls
3. chill for an hour
4. melt approximately 3 / 4 package of white almond bark
5. stick a toothpick in an oreo ball and dip it in the melted white almond bark
6. allow to harden on wax paper
7. takes about 15 minute
8. while waiting , melt about 1 / 4 package of chocolate almond bark
9. when oreo balls are no longer sticky to the touch , decorate with drizzles of chocolate and white almond bark
10. i just use a sandwich bag with a tiny hole cut in one corner to drizzle the almond bark
demonstrations.review: To Die For!  These were a BIG hit at Christmas and at my work.  I have made them several times.  You HAVE to use almond bark.  The other candy coatings out there don't work near as well.  These taste great with red wine.

target.recipe_text:
baked latkes

a bit less fattening than the original version.

1. preheat oven to 425f
2. drain excess liquid from potatoes
3. mix all ingredients in a large bowl
4. spray two baking sheets
5. add latke mixture by 1 / 4 cup
6. flatten
7. bake 15 minutes
8. turn latkes
9. and bake 10 minutes longer
10. serve with applesauce or sour cream
target.review:
I totally avoid this every year because of the fat and crazy amt. of calories.

This is the first time I can eat them guilt-free!

Thanks!!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chinese plum sauce

chinese plum sauce  serve this with egg rolls or brush it over chicken and ribs on the grill.

1. in large heavy saucepan , bring plums , onions , water , ginger and garlic to boil over medium heat
2. cover , reduce heat to low and simmer , stirring occasionally , until plums and onions are very tender , about 30 minutes
3. press through food mill or sieve and return to clean pan
4. stir in sugar , vinegar , coriander , salt , cinnamon , pepper and cloves
5. bring to boil , stirring
6. reduce heat to low and simmer until mixture reaches consistency of applesauce , about 45 minutes
7. fill and seal jars
8. process in boiling water bath for 30 minutes
9. makes about 4 cups
demonstrations.review: This is a 5 star sauce.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
patty melts

really good with fries and slaw.

eta:  i really like the finished sandwich fried like a grilled cheese.  when i make them that way i toast my rye on the bagel setting, assembling the sandwich "toasted side in".  i also add thousand island dressing on top of the onions.  then butter the bread and fry "like a grilled cheese sandwich".  nirvana!

1. mix together the ingredients from beef to bread crumbs-mix well and form into 4 patties
2. in a large skillet cook patties
3. meanwhile- in a medium skillet melt butter over medium , medium high heat
4. add onions and saute until light brown
5. meanwhile- toast bread and place on 4 plates
6. place hot patty on toast , then swiss , then hot onions
7. salt and pepper to taste
demonstrations.review:
I loved the addition of the herbs.

Very creative!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mom s italian pork chops

my mom put this dish together so i guessed at some of the ingredient amounts. these are so tender and delicious too!

1. heat oil in skillet over medium heat
2. whisk egg and milk together in a large bowl
3. dip pork chop in egg mixture first , then coat both sides with bread crumbs and brown pork chops in the skillet
4. spray bottom of a baking dish , pour pork chops from skillet wtih any leftover oil from the skillet also into baking dish
5. bake at 325 degrees for 45 minutes
demonstrations.review:
Try using the Italian style bread crumbs an then add grated Parmesan cheese to the breading. 

 I know what your Mom was trying to make since this s very Italian and very delicious. It is missing a certain flavor and this is the correction that I am sure you will know what I mean.

I would also like to add that you can use chicken breasts which have been pounded down to a cutlet with a meat mallet and then bread them in this mixture and lightly fried in a little olive oil and then placed in a casserole dish.

Then you add some good spaghetti sauce of choice and then top that with slices or shreds of mozzarella cheese until it is melted in a 350 degree oven let's say about 10 minutes or so.

target.recipe_text:
cherry cranberry sauce

i made this sauce for our thanksgiving dinner today.  it is sweet and really tasty with the cherries in it.

1. put everything except the agar into a large sauce pan and heat until the cranberries burst and the liquid is reduced by half
2. add the agar and stir
3. bring back to a boil and then simmer for 5 minutes
4. place in the fridge and let it set up
5. bon appetit !
target.review: Made this to go with my Christmas turkey, and I am never buying canned cranberry sauce again! I just used regular sugar, juice, and gelatin instead of agar, because that's what I had on hand. Thanks Joey Z.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
microwave poached eggs

i have been poaching eggs in the microwave for many years.  for me this is the best way to prepare poached eggs for 2.  it is quick, easy and almost foolproof.  please make sure you use a toothpick to pierce the yolk before cooking or it will explode!

1. add the water and white vinegar to a 6 ounce custard cup
2. break egg into cup , pierce egg yolk with toothpick , and cover dish loosely with plastic wrap
3. place in microwave and cook for 1 minute or until desired doneness
4. you may need to experiment with cooking times based on the wattage of your microwave and taste preference
5. immediately remove egg from hot water with a slotted spoon as it will continue to cook
6. serve with salt and pepper to taste
demonstrations.review: Worked impressively well! I exploded the first one at 55 seconds, the second try was perfect at 45 seconds.  My microwave does seem to run hot.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
columbia bar   grill s grain   cheeseburgers

nan

1. in a 10-12 inch nonstick frying pan over medium heat , cook mushrooms and green onions in butter , stirring often , until vegetables are limp
2. about 6 minutes
3. add oats and stir for 2 minutes
4. remove from heat , let cool slightly , then stir in cooked rice , mozzarella , cheddar , walnuts , cottage cheese , eggs and parsley
5. add salt and pepper to taste
6. on an oiled 12 by 15 inch baking sheet , shape into 4 patties , each 1 / 2 inch thick
7. broil 3 inches from heat until deep golden , turning once , 6 to 7 minutes total
demonstrations.review: Really excellent veggie burger with a surprisingly meaty texture. I added some cajun spice and used dried parsley. Will definitely make these again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
coconut chicken satay

forget the stick and serve this tasty chicken dish on noodles or steamed basmati rice.

1. heat wok or a large frying pan
2. add onion , garlic and ginger and cook for about 2 minutes
3. turn up heat , add chicken and stir-fry for 3-5 minutes
4. stir in peanut butter , chilli sauce , coconut milk and lime leaves if using
5. simmer for 10-15 minutes ot until chicken is cooked
6. serve with noodles or rice
demonstrations.review: This was good but I had to "doctor it up" a bit. When I first tasted it, it  was pretty bland. But I added a couple extra Tbsps of sweet chilli, some fish sauce, and some lime zest and juice (I didn't have lime leaves). I also added quite a bit of a Thai pepper-lime seasoning mix that I happened to have. I also added some broccoli, but it could've also done with some red capsicum strips. It was VERY rich! Nice and easy.

target.recipe_text:
kittencal s italian melt in your mouth meatballs

cooking the meatballs in simmering pasta sauce  will not only add so much extra flavor to the sauce the meatballs will be melt-in-your-mouth tender, you may of course oven-bake the meatballs for about 25 minutes,  --- don't be afraid to add in more parmesan cheese and a little more milk, there is no need to measure exactly, this recipe is pretty much foolproof, leftover cooked meatballs make a wonderful pizza topping just slice thinly and freeze until ready to use ----- these also make wonderful juicy burgers shaped into patties-- for more of my tried and true recipes check out my food blog at www.kittencalskitchen.com

1. mix all ingredients together in a large bowl
2. shape into small meatballs
3. drop the meatballs into simmering pasta sauce , do not stir for at least 20 minutes or you will risk breaking the meatballs
4. continue cooking in the simmering sauce for another 20 minutes
5. after the 40 minutes cooking time continue cooking your sauce with the meatballs in for as long as desired
target.review: Really, really good meatballs!  I prepared the recipe as written.  I made them about golfball size, and baked them to remove some of the fat. Then put them in my spagetti sauce to simmer until ready to serve.  The next night we didn't have quite enough left for another meal so I sliced the meatballs on top of a ready-made frozen cheese pizza, added a little of the spagetti sauce and voila, a Meatball Pizza.   This recipe is definately a keeper!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
tex mex cornbread salad

this is a really pretty and tasty layered salad...great for covered dish events!

1. use a deep glass bowl or small punch bowl
2. crumble half of the baked cornbread in the bottom of the bowl
3. top with half of the beans
4. in a small bowl , combine the tomatoes , onions , green pepper , and jalapeno peppers
5. spread half of the tomato mixture over the beans , then sprinkle with half the bacon , half the cheese and half of the corn
6. in another small bowl , stir together the sour cream , salsa , mayonnaise and ranch dressing mix
7. spread half of the sour cream mixture ofer the corn
8. repeat the process with the remaining ingredients
9. cover and chill for several hours before serving
10. garnish with a little shredded cheddar cheese if desired
demonstrations.review: I made this for a neighborhood ladies luncheon last week.  It was SO good!  Everyone was asking for the recipe even before they tasted it because it looked so pretty layered in the bowl.  I prepared it as shown except for using Red Bell Pepper instead of Green (just because I had one on hand).  I personally think it could use more cheese, but that's just me.  I gave some of the leftovers to my SIL and she called last night and said they heated them up and put more salsa on top and it tasted great!  This could be very versatile.  I can see why this has received 5 stars across the board.  Very good!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
balsamic chicken thighs

this is a quick and easy recipe that never fails to please even my picky dds. since chicken thighs are usually inexpensive it makes a economical meal. i like to serve these with some type of rice side dish and a green salad.

1. spray large frying pan , preheat
2. rinse and pat dry thighs
3. season with salt and pepper
4. brown well on all sides
5. cover , reduce heat to medium and cook for approximately 25 minutes , or'til thighs are done depending on size
6. add shallots , cook for 2-3 minutes , until they soften
7. stir in balsamic vinegar , cook for about 1 more minute , turn chicken to coat thoroughly
8. spoon sauce over thighs to serve
demonstrations.review: My DH and I really enjoyed this recipe.  It was such an easy recipe to prepare and the flavor of the balsamic vinegar and shallots was great! I served it with simple white rice and a green salad.  I will definately be making this one again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
celery cream soup

imagine the aroma of home made cream of celery soup simmering on the stove. simple, easy and rich in flavor.

1. in a large sauce pan , melt butter , add celery , onions , and garlic
2. cook over medium low heat until soft
3. add flour and cook 1-2 minutes over low heat
4. add chicken broth and bay leaf , bring to a boil reduce heat , cover and simmer 30 minutes
5. remove bay leaf , puree in a blender or processor
6. add cream , lemon juice , hot sauce , salt and pepper
7. reheat and simmer 5 minutes
8. garnish with celery leaves
demonstrations.review: This was my first time making Celery Soup and it turned out wonderful.  I may try it with a lighter cream next time just to cut down on the fat. I will be making this again.

target.recipe_text:
fusion avocado

had this in texas a couple of years ago! my sil kathie turned me on to it!
sushi without the fish, nori, and trouble of making it! ok she just had the soy but darn the pickeled ginger is so good! this is so quick and easy!!!!! it'll satisfy that i want sushi need!  i myself can eat one a day!

1. take a spoon between the meat and skin to loosen
2. pour 1 / 2 teaspoon soy sauce over each half of avocado
3. scoop out with a spoon and enjoy !
4. using optional wasabi or ginger to taste is a great healthy option !
target.review: I loved this snack.  Also tried it as a previous reviewer suggested with balsamic vinegar and it was wonderful too!  Thanks for the great keeper

demonstrations.recipe_text:
still another tuna pasta salad        mom s tuna salad

a tasty tuna salad which is easy to prepare. i frequently make it during the summer for a light supper, after a day at the pool. also works well for picnics. amounts given are estimates, i usually prepare this 

1. in a large bowl , combine all ingredients
2. mix well to blend
3. if salad is too dry , add more mayonnaise
4. taste , and adjust seasonings to your preference
5. chill well before serving
demonstrations.review: My hubby works is a contractor and during the summer heat, the last thing he wants is a heavy meal.  THIS WAS PERFECT!!  I doubled the recipe, left out the eggs (only because i was out), added red AND green pepper, Old Bay Seasoning and a little thyme.  I served it on a bed of romaine with halved grape tomatoes and it made a perfect main dish.  This will definately become a staple in our "summer fare". Thanks for a wonderfully light addition to the cookbook!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
easy cedar plank salmon

this is a bobby flay recipe that my husband tried this weekend. it was fantastic and turned out so flaky and moist! delicious

1. soak cedar plank in salted water for 2 hours , then drain
2. remove skin from salmon fillet
3. remove any remaining bones
4. rinse the salmon under cold running water and pat dry with paper towels
5. generously season the salmon with salt and pepper on both sides
6. lay the salmon on the cedar plank and carefully spread the mustard over the top and sides
7. place the brown sugar in a bowl and crumble between your fingers , then sprinkle over the mustard
8. set grill for indirect grilling and heat to medium-high
9. place the cedar plank in the center of the hot grate , away from the heat
10. cover the grill and cook until cooked through , around 20 to 30 minutes
11. the internal temperature should read 135 degrees f
12. transfer the salmon and plank to a platter and serve right off the plank
demonstrations.review: I am not sure what the other cook was talking about. I did cut down the amount of Dijon. (Only because i am not a big mustard fan) also added a splash of soy sauce.  The recipe was great.  I suspect that it was actually the fish itself that caused the "fishy" taste, because i used fresh wild caught Salmon and it was out of this world.  Thanks for your recipe, i will definately be using this method again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
to die for crock pot pork chops

i make this for my husband and daughter, and i have got nothing but smiles from this.  it's easy, cheap and oh so yummy!

1. combine cream of mushroom soup , 1 / 3 can water , softened cream cheese and garlic in a bowl
2. stir out most of the lumps , but the rest will cook out
3. pour in bottom of crock pot
4. put pork chops on top of mixture
5. add liberal amounts of salt and pepper
6. i'm usually heavy handed !
7. cook on low for 7-8 hours
8. serve over slices of warm bread or pasta of your choice
9. pork chops will fall apart
10. so tender you can cut with a spoon !
demonstrations.review: This recipe was tasty and VERY simple.  I used cream of celery instead of mushroom and as suggested added sliced potatoes and onions to the bottom of the pot, covered with soup mixture, and then added the chops.  They were very tender and while not a "five star" recipe, i will definately fix again.  My three year old absolutely LOVED this dish, and anything she will eat well is a keeper in my book.
