target.recipe_text:
kittencal s easy no fail make anytime turkey gravy

i have been using this recipe for many years, my family loves this gravy and i have served it to dinner guests over the holidays and always receive rave reviews! --- you don't need to make this gravy using all pan drippings, if you do not have 4 cups of drippings you may mix with chicken broth to make the 4 cups, or it may be made with only chicken broth, please see note on the bottom of the recipe--- this may be made slightly ahead and kept uncovered on top of the stove until ready to serve, just whisk before using if you have any left over this gravy freezes very well or you may reduce all ingredients down to half and for a thinner gravy reduce flour by 1 tablespoon  --- also see my recipe#314890
for more of my recipes visit www.kittencalskitchen.com

1. drain the pan drippings for the roasted turkey through a fine strainer
2. let sit and then remove any fat from the top of the drippings
3. add in chicken broth or water to make 4 cups if necessary
4. in a medium saucepan , melt margarine or butter
5. add in lots of black pepper
6. add in 1 / 2 cup flour plus 3 tablespoons
7. constantly whisk for about 3 minutes over low heat
8. slowly add in the 4 cups turkey broth / drippings
9. whisk constantly over medium-low heat until bubbly and thickened
10. use right away or keep warm over lowest heat setting , whisk again before serving
11. options to make this gravy using all chicken broth prepare as directed using 4 cups low sodium chicken broth and 1 tablespoon chicken boullion powder ---- or you may add in low sodium chicken broth omitting bouillon powder to pan drippings to make up 4 cups
target.review: Five stars from me! Didn't even need to add salt. It was perfect!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
berries and cream

this is a simple, lovely way to serve fresh summer berries.  i made this for brunch today and found it a refreshing end to the meal.  this dish could also be made year-round using unsweetened frozen berries that have been thawed.  note: preparation time includes time needed for berries to sit at room temperature.

1. in a medium bowl , combine berries , lemon zest and sugar
2. gently toss , being careful not to break the blackberries and raspberries too much
3. allow berry mixture to sit at room temperature for 30 minutes until berries begin to create their own juice , and sugar is dissolved
4. serve in four small serving bowls with around 2 tbs
5. cream drizzled attop per bowl
demonstrations.review: I don't have one bad thing to say about this recipe! Truly refreshing and easy to make!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
one skillet cheesy chicken and rice

this is delicious! a bit on the spicy side, but very tolerable. this is a very easy dish to make, and only dirties one skillet...hardly any clean up! i

1. melt butter in a large skillet over medium heat
2. add onions , garlic and chicken
3. stir occasionally
4. cook for 4-5 minutes until chicken cooked almost all the way through
5. add rice and toast for 3-4 minutes
6. add chicken stock , enchilada sauce , cumin , red pepper flakes and salt
7. bring to boil , reduce heat to low and cover with a tight fitting lid
8. cook , covered , 20 minutes or until liquid is absorbed
9. turn off heat
10. spread cheese over the top , replace cover and let sit for 5 minutes
11. top with sour cream and chopped cilantro when serving
demonstrations.review: Cooked this for my husband. He had three plates of it! I will definitely add this recipe to my dinner rotation!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chicken thighs with lime and curry

the lime and cilantro and a very fresh taste to this curry. i like it served over rice. a wok works well to make this in (of course, i think a wok works well to make everything in).

1. blend flour and pepper , and dredge thighs in mixture
2. brown chicken in oil
3. remove chicken to a plate
4. add onion , garlic , and flour , and saute
5. add broth , curry , and pepper sauce and stir to blend well
6. simmer mixture for 2 minutes , then bring to a boil and add chicken , lime zest and lime juice
7. cook until chicken is cooked through
8. add cilantro and sour cream just before serving
demonstrations.review: YUM! I think I will try this dish with twice the amount of lime.

target.recipe_text:
long island iced tea  applebee s tgi friday s style

shhhhhhhhhhhh, it's a secret!

1. add crushed ice to pint glass
2. add first 4 ingredients
3. shake
4. top with cola and sour mix
5. serve
6. you can add raspberry liquor to this , and call it a black opal , even more tasty !
target.review: How many ways can you say awesome?  Very very good.  Boyfriend approved.  =)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pasta with sausage  tomatoes  and cream

delicious and satisfying... i don't remember where this recipe comes from, but it's a pleaser! easily doubled.  also, works well with gf pasta and sausage

1. heat oil in a heavy skillet over medium heat
2. add sausage and crushed red pepper
3. cook until sausage is no longer pink , stirring frequently , about 7 minutes
4. add onion and garlic to skillet and cook until onion is tender and sausage is light brown , stirring occasionally , about 7 minutes
5. add tomatoes , cream , and salt
6. simmer until mixture thickens slightly , about 4 minutes
7. cook pasta in large pot of boiling water
8. drain
9. bring sauce to a simmer
10. add pasta to sauce and cook until pasta is heated through and sauce thickens , stirring occasionally , about 2 minutes
11. divide pasta between plates
12. sprinkle with parsley
13. serve , passing parmesan separately
demonstrations.review: I used Spicy Italian Chicken Sausage and used some fresh herbs from my garden (basil, oregano, parsley).   It was good, but to me, it tasted bland, and I even added a bunch more crushed red pepper.  I'm rating it a 4 star recipe because the BF really liked it and was looking forward to leftovers.  It's a quick recipe in a pinch, but not much on the flavor factor for me.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
best lemon bars

this recipe comes from gourmet magazine. it is very simple and delicious.

1. shortbread base:preheat oven to 350 degrees
2. cut butter into 1 / 2 inch pieces
3. in food processor , process all ingredients until mixture begins to form small lumps
4. press mixture evenly into 9x13 baking pan
5. bake in middle of oven until golden , about 20 minutes
6. while shortbread is baking , prepare topping
7. topping: in bowl whisk together eggs and granulated sugar until combined well
8. stir in lemon juice and flour
9. pour lemon mixture over hot shortbread base
10. reduce oven temperature to 300 degrees and bake in middle of oven until set , about 30 minutes
11. let cool completely in pan then sprinkle with confectioner's sugar
demonstrations.review: These are some pretty great lemon bars.  I almost followed the recipe almost to a "T."  I only had 3 eggs - so I had to sub the 4th egg with egg beaters, but that didn't change the consistency.  The bottom crust probably could have been done a little but more, as I couldn't tell when it was "golden brown" because of the brown sugar speckled through.  But, it was extremely tasty, very lemony without being too sweet!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
agave nectar margarita

the best ever and so fresh!! you can find agave nectar where honey is found in the grocery store, but most likely in a whole foods or central market or any specialty grocery store in your area.

1. fill a margarita glass with crushed ice
2. add the tequila , lime and lemon juices , agave nectar , triple sec and tangerine juice to a cocktail shaker filled with ice
3. shake vigorously and strain into the prepared glass
4. garnish with a lime and orange wheel
demonstrations.review: Left out the "splash" of juice, but it was awesome!  It tasted like the Nekked Margaritas sold at this local bar for $10 a glass!  =)  I can't wait to make these for Cinco de Mayo!

target.recipe_text:
grammie bea s chopped apple cake

one thing i know for sure, is that my gram knew how to cook and bake... this cake is definitely one you will want to make for sure!  just plain delish!

1. preheat oven to 350
2. grease and flour a loaf pan , or 9x9" cake pan , or makes 18 cup cakes
3. cut apples , and peel and chop into small pieces
4. add sugar , and mix and let set for 10 minutes while mixing dry ingredients
5. sift flour , salt , baking soda , cinnamon and nutmeg together well
6. add oil mixed with beaten egg , to apples
7. mix in dry ingredients , and pour into pan
8. bake at 350 for 30-45 minutes
9. test at 30 minutes with a tooth pick in center of cake -- when it comes out clean , cake is done
10. do not overbake
target.review: Outstanding is dcefinitely the word to describe this. I made cupcakes and had to eat about four of them to be sure I had actually made something THAT delicious. I did change it a little bit, only using a heaping half-cup of sugar, a quarter-cup of oil (with some applesauce to make up for the rest) and subbing cardamom for the nutmeg. Frosted with cream cheese frosting, it was the best cake I've had in recent memory AND it stayed moist for two days in and out of the fridge! Thank you so much.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
impossible peanut butter cookies

these are the quickest, simplest peanut butter cookies that you will ever make and they taste great!

1. mix peanut butter , sugar , and egg together until smooth
2. drop by teaspoon onto cookie sheet two inches apart
3. if desired , roll in extra sugar before placing on cookie sheet
4. press with fork
5. press again in opposite direction
6. bake 10 to 12 minutes at 350 degrees fahrenheit
7. do not brown
8. do not over bake
demonstrations.review: ...dangerously good. I followed the recipe, then added a 1/4 cup of chocolate chunks and 1/4 cup of toasted walnuts and a scant handful of oatmeal. These are really. Freakin. Good. And cheap and easy! Thank you.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
easy lemon pudding

this is so easy to make and has a nice sweet, lemony flavor.

1. on med-hi heat , bring sugar and water to a boil
2. mix cornstarch , lemon juice and lemon extract
3. stir into boiling mixture
4. beat the egg yolks and stir about 1 / 4 cup of the hot mixture into them
5. quickly stir this into the hot mix
6. spoon into dessert cups
7. chill
8. if you prefer you can put the mix into a baked pie shell , and cover with meringue
demonstrations.review: I tweaked this a little according to what I had; used orange extract instead of lemon, and added some lemon zest and a little vanilla extract to it. Both Grandma and Mom were surprised by my "pudding", as it came out much more like lemon curd, but everyone loved the flavor. I might add a bit of milk or something next time, to make it more of the expected, Jell-o type pudding, but five stars for taste

demonstrations.recipe_text:
banana chocolate chip muffins

wow! get this...a very low-fat muffin recipe that actually tastes great!! after failing at many attempts to create a really tasty, low-fat muffin, i came across this recipe, and it is really good...great for dieters!

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees
2. lightly coat 12 muffin tin liners with cooking spray and place in muffin tin
3. in large bowl , mash bananas with fork
4. whisk in egg , milk , granulated sugar , and brown sugar
5. in separate bowl , combine flour , baking soda , and salt
6. add flour mixture to banana mixture and combine well
7. fold in chocolate chips and walnuts
8. spoon equal amounts of batter into 12 muffin cups
9. bake 20 minutes or until toothpick inserted in center comes out clean
10. allow to cool slightly in pan , then remove to wire rack
demonstrations.review: VERY nice. I made 2/3 of the recipe, only used 1/4 cup each of brown and white sugar, and added vanilla, cinnamon and cardamom to these, and i got 23 perfect little mini-muffins. even my little sister said they were good, and she's probably the pickiest eater I know! (i also omitted the chocolate and nuts). Thanks!

target.recipe_text:
thick spinach soup

lovely and thick spinach soup. i don't like spinach normally, but this is wonderful.

1. heat the oil and butter in a large saucepan and gently cook the onion for 3 minutes until softened
2. stir in the potatoes , spinach , stock , nutmeg and seasoning
3. bring to the boil and simmer for 15 minutes
4. transfer to a food processor and blend until smooth
5. return to the pan , heat through and adjust seasoning to taste
6. ladle into soup bowls and garnish with a swirl of creme fraiche and freshly ground black pepper
7. enjoy !
target.review: I added beaten yogurt instead of cream and it was great ! What made me try this was really a short list of ingredients...please post such easy to make recipes. :-)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
easiest banana shake

shake shake shake...anytime ..anywhere !

1. put bananas , milk and vanilla ice cream in the blender and blend till absolutely smooth
2. transfer to the glasses and garnish with chopped / slivered almonds
3. slurrrrrrrp !
demonstrations.review:
Jenn
Did you say watery...I really wonder about that because this recipe always has the right consistency for a shake as banana itself is quite a fluffy fruit. But, with such simple preparation I really doubt if you had gone wrong. All I can say is better luck next time. After all the other two reviewers cannot be wrong either. What do you say...but I am thankful that you did not punish the recipe by posting one or two stars. Thanks.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
deluxe coleslaw

mom's recipe.

1. in a large bowl , whisk together mayo , milk , lemon juice , sugar , salt , pepper and paprika until well blended
2. add the shredded cabbage and carrot , pepper and onion
3. gently toss together
4. cover and refrigerate at least 1 hour for flavours to combine
demonstrations.review:
Very simple and workable...thanx for sharing the same with all of us.
Do you have some more recipes like this which are not very
elaborate to make and try ?

Smiles 
Mini

demonstrations.recipe_text:
garlic herb spread

this spread is just oozing with flavour!

1. chefs
2. in food processor , process garlic , basil and green onion
3. process until finely chopped
4. add cheeses
5. pulse until blended but still chunky
6. chill before serving
7. serve on bagels or crackers
demonstrations.review:
The recipe was very good. I added freshly ground black pepper and it just catalysed the flavours.What do you say :-)
Mini

target.recipe_text:
seared salmon with balsamic glaze

i saw this on sara's secrets and couldn't wait to try it! the sauce brings out the sweetness in the fish. enjoy!

1. stir together balsamic vinegar , water , lemon juice , and brown sugar in a small bowl
2. pat salmon dry and season with salt and pepper
3. heat oil in a 12-inch nonstick skillet over medium high heat , not smoking
4. increase heat to high , add salmon skin side up , and sear until well browned , about 4 minutes
5. turn fish over and sear until just cooked through , 3 to 4 minutes more
6. transfer salmon to plates and carefully add vinegar mixture to skillet
7. simmer , stirring , until thickened and reduced to about 1 / 3 cup , about 2 minutes
8. spoon glaze over salmon
9. serve and enjoy !
target.review: FANTASTIC!!!  Made this as directed with high quality balsamic vinegar from Italy and we loved it.  I made two salmon filets hoping to have leftovers (thinking my 5 year old wouldn't eat hers).  She ate all of hers and half of mine and still wanted more!  We will be making this often. I am going to try this glaze tonight with chicken. Thanks for the great recipe

demonstrations.recipe_text:
stir fried beef and broccoli in oyster sauce

this is a great meal for family! easy enough to make any night of the week.  enjoy!

1. cut meat across the grain into very thin slices
2. place in a bowl and combine with soy sauce , rice wine , water and cornstarch
3. allow to marinate at least 10 minutes
4. meanwhile prepare remaining ingredients and stir together sauce mixture
5. heat oil in a wok or large skillet
6. add meat and cook , stirring constantly , until meat is about 75 per cent cooked
7. remove and reserve
8. scrape out pan if necessary and return to heat
9. add another 2 tablespoons oil if needed and heat
10. add garlic , ginger and green onions and cook 30 to 60 seconds until fragrant
11. stir in cut-up broccoli and add water
12. cover and cook 3 minutes
13. re-add beef to pan and combine well
14. add sauce to mixture and bring to boil
15. cook until thickened and beef and broccoli are cooked through
16. serve with steamed rice
demonstrations.review: This was pretty good.  I made it as posted but it just seemed like something was missing.  My 5 year old thought it was good as is but I liked it better once I added a little Thai sweet chili sauce and crushed red pepper.  I think next time I will add sugar to the sauce to make it a tad bit sweeter.  Thanks for the recipe :)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
apple or pear cake

absolutely the most delicious, moist cake ever with a decadent topping. very simple to make, my family just loves this!

1. cake:
2. mix all cake ingredients by hand in order given
3. pour in a greased 9 x 13 inch pan or springform pan
4. bake at 350 degrees for 45 minutes and remove
5. topping:
6. in saucepan mix all ingredients and bring to a slow boil for 3 minutes
7. pour over cake and return to oven for 4 minutes
demonstrations.review: I made this for the first time a few months ago to bring into work.  It went fast.  Everyone LOVED it.  I even had one guy ofre to pay me to make another one for him and his son.  I used Fuji apples, I live in Japan and that seems to be the only baking apple I can find.  I also made extra topping. YUMMO!  I'm making it again tomorrow for a breakfast potluck.  Thanks for the great recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cracker barrel green beans

this is the only way i can eat canned green beans!

1. in a 2-quart saucepan over medium heat , cook bacon until lightly brown but not crisp
2. when bacon has browned , add green beans
3. add salt , sugar and pepper and mix well
4. place onion on top of green beans
5. cover saucepan with a lid and bring to a light boil
6. turn heat down to low and simmer beans for 45 minutes
demonstrations.review: I hate canned green beans.  I doubled  this for a get together that my husband was having.  Yummy!  I was amazed that I liked them.  They were a big hit at the party too.

target.recipe_text:
breakfast casserole supreme

this is a wonderful almost do ahead breakfast. great for company or christmas morning.

1. melt margarine and place in the bottom of 9" by 13" baking pan
2. spread potatoes in bottom of the pan
3. sprinkle chopped vegetables over potatoes
4. add salt and pepper to taste
5. sprinkle meat over potatoes and vegetables
6. pour beaten eggs over potatoes
7. bake at 350 degrees for 45 minutes
8. remove from oven and sprinkle cheese evenly over top
9. bake another 5-10 minutes or until cheese is hot and bubbly
10. remove from oven and let set for approximately 5 minutes
11. cut into 2
12. 5"-3" squares and serve with a spatula
13. enjoy
target.review: Great recipe!  I love the addition of fresh tomatoes....they make it feel like more of an omelet than a casserole.  I added green onions, and used some seasoned salt and garlic powder on the hashbrowns before layering everything else.  It did take longer than the 45 minutes stated to cook (more like an hour), but it could be my oven.  Thanks for sharing.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chicken and mushroom patties  kotlety or katleti

these chicken and mushroom kotleti (russian meat cakes) are so juicy and delicious. they’re healthier than the average chicken patty since they are loaded with mushrooms. these patties are perfect with mashed potatoes and pickles. you can also serve them as sliders (mini chicken burgers) – pickles on the side. you may also choose to wolf these down with a bowl of buttered noodles and a pickle.
part of the secret to juicer patties appears to be in the cooking method. covering them while sautéing makes them turn out much juicier and the flavors meld together just right.

1. saute mushrooms over med / high heat until softened and lightly browned , then mince them in a food processor or put them through the meat grinder
2. you can also finely chop cooked mushrooms by hand if youre feeling adventurous
3. in a large bowl , combine: 1 lb ground chicken , your cooked & finely chopped mushrooms , grated onion , 2 eggs , 1 / 2 cup bread crumbs and 1 1 / 2 tsp salt and 1 / 2 tsp pepper
4. using an ice cream scoop , place one scoop of the mixture at a time into the flour , then dredge it on both sides and used your hands to create oval patties , tapping off excess flour
5. if youre making sliders , make them round like mini burgers
6. 4
7. heat 2-3 tbsp of oil in a nonstick skillet
8. once oil is hot , add the fritters
9. cover and cook until golden on both sides
10. cook about 4 minutes on the first side and 2-3 minutes on the next
11. wipe your skillet with a paper towel between batches and add more oil as needed
12. remove to a plate and serve warm
demonstrations.review: WOW! This is a delicious recipe.  I added granulated garlic to the chicken and used breadcrumbs (instead of flour) to coat the patties before frying.  Instead of meatballs, I made patties and got 10 good size "burgers".  They were very moist and tender!  Thank you for posting this recipe.  It will go into my regular rotation!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
venison bacon burgers

this is one of the best venison burgers out there. if you like bacon, you will love this one. you could use ground beef as well. this is very kid friendly as well. if you are like me, i am always looking for a way to use all my ground venison during hunting season.

1. cook bacon in a skillet over medium heat until brown and crispy
2. poor bacon drippings and crumble the bacon and place in a large mixing bowl to let cool
3. use reserves bacon drippings ans saute the garlic and shallots until softened
4. add to the bacon and bacon drippings bowl
5. once cooled , add the ground venison , worcestershire , parsley , salt , pepper , and the beaten egg until evenly combined
6. refrigerate about 20 minutes
7. preheat outdoor grill for medium high heat
8. shape into 6 patties and grill until desired doneness
9. serve on hamburger buns ( i usually brush my bun with some olive oil or butter on the inside of buns and grill them slightly on the grill
10. serve with desired condiments and toppings
11. i usually top mine with cheese and more bacon and the onions
12. i always put a little condiment bar out with everything and let them pick it out
demonstrations.review: What an excellent recipe!  Easily delared the best burgers my husband and I have had.  Thanks for posting.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crspy parmesan asparagus

i love asparagus and this is a different way to fix it.

1. preheat oven to 425 degrees
2. lay a wire rack on a baking sheet and coat with non-stick spray
3. snap off the tough ends of each asparagus spear
4. on two separate plates , add the eggs whites and the panko + flour + cheese
5. season the panko mixture with salt and pepper if desires
6. coat each asparagus spear in egg whites , then lay in the panko mixture and thoroughly cover
7. if the panko wont stick , dip back in the egg whites and roll in panko once again
8. lay each spear on the wire rack
9. bake at 425 for 15 minutes , or until golden brown and crispy
demonstrations.review: Wonderful recipe!!!  I used seasoned breadcrumbs instead of panko and beat the egg whites until they were just a little frothy.  After dipping the asparagus into the egg white then breadcrumb/parmesan mixture, I stuck them in the fridge until I was ready to bake them for supper.  It was super simple, and had great flavor.  Thank you for sharing!

target.recipe_text:
moroccan sweet potato stew

this is a great vegetarian side dish.

1. place the onions and garlic into a large pot with 1 / 4 cup water
2. cook , covered , over low heat until tender , about 10 to 12 minutes , adding more water as necessary to prevent scorching
3. stir in the turmeric , cinnamon , curry , cumin , nutmeg , red pepper flakes , salt and pepper
4. cook for 3 minutes
5. stir in the sweet potatoes , bell pepper , eggplant and broth
6. raise the heat to medium and bring to a boil
7. reduce heat to low and simmer , covered , for 5 minutes
8. add garbanzo beans and tomatoes , and simmer , covered , until sweet potatoes are tender , about 45 to 60 minutes , stirring occasionally
9. garnish with fresh cilantro before serving
target.review: This was okay, but not stellar.  I did make several major changes, so you'll have to take my rating with a grain of salt.  1) Sub carrots for eggplant, 2) Made it in a crock pot, 3) Used about 2 cups chicken stock and 1 cup water, 4) Sub green bell pepper for red, 5) Used only 1 (15 oz) can of chickpeas.  I garnished with raisins and walnuts (suggested by another reviewer) and that made it quite a bit better.  Served over white rice.  My husband liked it.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
sweet potato pecan pie

sweet potato-pecan pie

1. prepare pie shell , set aside
2. make sweet potato filling: in medium bowl , with electric mixer , beat 1 egg until frothy
3. add mashed cooked sweet potatoes , sugar , butter , vanilla extract , salt , cinnamon , allspice , and nutmeg
4. beat at medium speed until the mixture is smooth , about 2 minutes
5. make pecan topping: in medium bowl , with mixer , beat eggs until frothy
6. add sugar , corn syrup , melted butter , vanilla and cinnamon
7. beat at low speed just until mixture is well blended , about 1 minute
8. stir in pecans
9. preheat oven to 350 degrees fahrenheit
10. to assemble: turn sweet potato filling into unbaked pie shell , spreading evenly
11. pour pecan topping over top
12. bake 60 to 70 minutes until set , and knife inserted in center comes out clean
13. remove pie to rack to cool
14. just before serving decorate with whipped cream
demonstrations.review: My husband's comment "This is definitely a do-over!"  Delicious!  Tasted like a pecan pie with a little texture of pumpkin pie.  I added more of each spice, used brown sugar instead of white, and half corn syrup/half maple syrup (recommended by another reviewer).  While the filling wasn't super-shallow in the pie dish, I would agree with other's recommendations to double/increase the filling.  This is such a good pie you're going to want more of it anyways!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
quick sour cream coffee cake

from the joy of cooking.  i know there are lots of sour cream coffee cakes out there, but this one is slightly different in that there is no butter in the batter.  this goes together very quickly, just like the name says, and when it is warm, the texture is just wonderful.

1. prepare streusel topping:
2. with fork , combine flour , butter and sugar till crumbly
3. add cinnamon
4. set aside
5. coffee cake:
6. preheat oven to 350
7. combine flour , sugar , baking powder , baking soda and salt
8. combine sour cream and eggs
9. beat well
10. add the dry ingredients to the cream mixture
11. beat just till smooth as overbeating tends to toughen dough
12. spread in a lightly oiled 9x9 pan
13. sprinkle with streusel
14. bake about 30-40 minutes at 350 , or till tester comes out clean
demonstrations.review: Quick, easy, and delicious.  Perfect for whipping up on a Sunday morning.  I added vanilla extract and 1 1/2 cups frozen berries (blueberry, raspberry, and blackberry blend).  I also cut out some of the sugar (maybe half).  Turned out fantastic!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
ultimate double chocolate brownies

rich, chocolately, yummy brownies! not for the faint of heart. the best one i've ever made, and i am a devout chocoholic. mine never pull away from the sides of the pan like the recipe says. be sure to test it with a toothpick in more than one place, because you might run into a chocolate chip that would make it appear that the brownies aren't done yet.

1. in a large bowl , combine cocoa and baking soda
2. blend in 1 / 3 cup melted butter
3. add boiling water , stir until well blended
4. stir in sugar , eggs , and remaining butter
5. add flour , vanilla , and salt
6. stir in pecans and chocolate chips
7. pour into a greased 13x9x2-inch pan and bake at 350 degrees f for 35-40 minutes , or until brownie starts to pull away from sides of pan
8. cool , cut into squares
demonstrations.review: Delicious!

target.recipe_text:
stan s place shrimp po boy

nan

1. take the ingredients for the remoulade sauce: mayonnaise , horseradish , pickled relish , salt , white pepper , garlic powder , paprika , lemon juice
2. combine all ingredients in a large bowl and whisk until combined
3. refrigerate
4. clean and devein 6-8 medium shrimp
5. prepare 3 bowls
6. add salt , pepper , and all other spices to the flour
7. divide the flour between the first two bowls
8. combine and beat the egg and milk in the third bowl
9. arrange the bowls so you have flour , egg wash , and flour
10. heat the oil until a drop of flour placed in the pan dances around
11. working left to right and starting with the left hand , coat the shrimp with flour from the first bowl and place into the egg wash
12. using the right hand , remove the shrimp from the egg wash and place in the last bowl of flour
13. coat evenly and carefully place into oil
14. cook until browned on both sides
15. serve with remoulade sauce on ciabatta bread "dressed" with lettuce and tomato
target.review: First of all, I was shocked that this was the ONLY shrimp po boy recipe on this site! Craziness... Anyway, I've been craving a shrimp po boy for months and this was perfect!! Absolutely delicious!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
minute steak and mushroom sauce

one of my favorite meals to eat, this is sooo easy and can be done in about 30 minutes. goes great with mashed potatoes and rolls of some kind are a must to sop up the extra mushroom sauce.

1. slice mushrooms and saute in butter until tender
2. if using a can , drain well
3. set aside
4. in a large skillet , heat oil
5. salt minute steaks and dredge in flour
6. fry until breading is brown
7. make sure when frying you leave the meat long enough for the breading to fry until it sets , as it will fall off if not fried long enough
8. this is what makes it gooood !
9. when the meat is fried , place on paper towels to drain excess oil
10. place in a 2 quart casserole dish and keep warm
11. leave 2 tablespoons of oil in the skillet and remove the rest
12. add cream of mushroom soup , milk , and mushrooms , stirring constantly
13. let soup simmer on med-low heat until throughly heated
14. pour over warm meat and serve
demonstrations.review: Really good! I felt like something was missing in the gravy, just not enough flavor for me. I added a few things trying to perk it up but it still wasn't quite perfect. Still great, though.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
shrimp and scallop scampi

this is quick and delicious. it can be served with rice or pasta.

1. heat oil in a large skillet over medium heat
2. add onions , and cook for 2 minutes
3. add garlic
4. cook for 1 minute more
5. add shrimp and scallops , and cook for 2- 3 minutes
6. add wine , basil , pepper flakes , chicken stock , and sugar
7. simmer about 4 minutes , until shrimp are pink and scallops opaque
8. add butter , lemon juice , salt and pepper
9. serve over pasta or rice
10. sprinkle with parsley and parmesan
demonstrations.review: This was really good! Took off one star, only because I would have preferred the sauce to be a little thicker. But, with a little adjustment I think that it will be perfect for us.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
german plum cake

this cake is actually known as zwetschgendatschi in bavaria, where it is most popular. roughly translated from bavarian to german, it would be called pflaumenkuchen or plum cake in english. but zwetschgen aren't ordinary plums, a datschi isn't really a kuchen, and a kuchen is most definitely not a cake! or at least not a tall, spongy cake -- it's flatter. ideally, for this dessert you want the slightly tart italian plums. if you do have to use another type of plum, be careful the variety you choose isn't too juicy.

1. in a large bowl , cream the butter , add the sugar , vanilla , egg , lemon peel , sour cream and salt
2. mix the flour and baking powder and add that into the mixture
3. grease the base of a round baking pan and spread the dough over the pan
4. liberally spread plums over the dough
5. to make the optional topping , cream the butter , add flour , sugar and cinnamon
6. sprinkle over the plums and bake for 30-45 minutes in the middle rack at 375 f
7. be careful not to let the bottom burn !
8. serve with lots of freshly-made whipped cream
9. if you like , you may also sprinkle rum or cinnamon over the fruit before baking
demonstrations.review: Wonderful and super easy! I love this cake. I have a ton of plums from a tree in my backyard that I need to do something with so I tried this out. Granted, it didn't use up as many as I would have liked! I even goofed a few of the steps in this and it still turned out perfectly. I used very soft very juicy plums so I was a little concerned since there is a specific warning against that. It cooked up just right! I also thought that the streusel topping may have been too much once I started putting it on, but I LOVE streusel so I decided to trust the recipe and it was PERFECT! Will definately make it again. Thanks for the great recipe.

target.recipe_text:
anme s garlic knots

my all time favorite garlic knots recipe. you may use your own bread dough if you want.

1. proof yeast in water , honey and oil
2. let sit for about 5 minutes or until foamy
3. once proofed add 1 cup of the flour mixed with salt and cheese to the yeast mixture stirring until very smooth
4. add the rest of the flour a little at a time stirring well after each addition of flour
5. once flour is added knead on a floured surface for about 5 minutes or until smooth
6. place dough in an oiled bowl , turning to coat , and let rise for about 1 1 / 2 hours covered with a towel
7. grease a baking sheet and preheat oven to 375f
8. roll risen dough out into a rectangle and spread oil over dough then and cut into 12 strips
9. tie each strip into a knot and place on the baking sheet
10. cover and let rise again for about 30 minutes
11. while dough is rising again mix butter and garlic in a saucepan over low heat for about 2-3 minutes
12. bake for about 20 minutes then coat with garlic butter and sprinkle with cheese and enjoy !
target.review:
These were great!  After reading the reviews I made 1.5 times the called for amount and got 9 knots out of the dough. BUT I did not anticipate how much they would double up while resting and they turned out huge! I would cut them into smaller strips next time.  I baked at 325 instead of 375 as my propane oven is HOT and burns  stuff easy. These would be great as breadsticks too (which is how I am making them tonight) brushed with just butter for my garlic hating kids. 
The only thing is I can't figure out where the olive oil in the sauce is supposed to go - there is no mention of it in the directions. I used it to brush the knots before baking instead of putting it as part of the sauce. Also steps 6 and 8 seem a bit out of order - I didn't preheat my oven until the dough was almost done rising the second time and I didn't heat the sauce until they were almost done baking.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
no bake fudge cookies

this recipe is from a church library book 

1. mix first 6 ingredients in a sauce pan and cook until it boils
2. boil for 1-3 minutes
3. remove from heat and add peanut butter and oatmeal
4. drop by teaspoonfuls on to wax paper
5. chill until set
demonstrations.review:
I've had these type of cookies before and they were great but I decided to add a little "extra" to them.  I boiled these for the full 3 minutes (so they'd set a little firmer), pressed into a foil lined 9X13 pan and topped with 1 1/2 cups of melted milk chocolate chips. YUM!
 Believe it or not 4 out of 5 of my kids turned their noses up (they don't like oatmeal). More for me! My, my, my, I'm saying bye bye to my diet right now!  I think the next batch I might try using rice crispies instead of oatmeal (the like rice crispies)....so I won't get stuck eating the whole batch myself (ok, maybe not lol).

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crumb topped banana muffins

these are so good. we love the topping.

1. in a large bowl , mix the flour , baking soda , baking powder , and salt
2. mix bananas , sugar , egg and melted butter
3. stir into dry mixture until thoroughly combined , then stop mixing
4. fill muffin cups 3 / 4 full
5. combine brown sugar , flour , and cinnamon topping ingredients
6. cut in cold butter until crumbly
7. sprinkle over muffins
8. bake at 375 degrees fahrenheit for about 20 minutes , until muffins test done
9. cool in pan for 10 minutes
demonstrations.review: These were great! Even the kids that don't like bananas ate them. I added a bit of cinnamon to the batter but otherwise followed the recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chicken legs grilled

generously seasoned crisp legs.
be sure to visit the grilling forum http://www.recipezaar.com/bb/viewforum.zsp?f=42 for any help!

1. mix all marinade ingredients in a zip lock bag add chicken
2. chill and marinade for 4 hours
3. grill chicken on a well oiled grill until well browned on all sides , turning once , 30 to 40 minutes
4. fyi
5. all grills are different temperatures
6. take advantage of indirect heat --
7. if the chicken browns quickly finish over indirect heat
8. all grills have hot spots so watch and be sure to move the chicken to spots on the grill so not to burn and completely cook the chicken
9. as the time of the year makes grilling quicker or slower
10. so take care and watch and enjoy you food as it grills
11. be sure to visit the grilling forum for any help !
demonstrations.review:
I made this tonight for the second time, the first time I used legs this time I am using thighs. The marinade is really more of a paste that is easier brushed on /rubbed into the chicken other wise it takes a bit of effort to get all the pieces covered in a bag, especially if you double (or tripple the amount of meat like I do). I solved this by simply use upping the amount of spices and oil called for (except the pepper) in order to have enough seasoning/liquid to be able to just throw it in the bag. I prefer to cook mine at a little lower temp (350-375) then up the temp to 400-425 near the end of baking to ensure tender fall off the bone meat that has crispy skin. 
I marinaded 4 hours the first time and overnight this time and they came out very tender inside and crispy outside, did not dissapoint even oven baked.

target.recipe_text:
crab quiche

we live on the oregon coast and lots of fresh crab is the benefit. this is very tasty.

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees f
2. in a medium bowl , whisk together eggs , sour cream , milk , butter , flour , salt and pepper until thoroughly blended
3. fold in crab , cheese and onions , blending well , spread into prepared pie shell
4. bake for 40 to 45 minutes or until a knife inserted in the center comes out clean
target.review: In an effort to reduce the nutritional damage, I used fat-free sour cream, skim milk, reduced-fat cheese and only 1 tbsp of butter. Didn't have any green onions, so I used 3/4 cup of chopped sweet onion instead. I also made due with 6 oz of crab meat, not wanting to open another can, and found it to be sufficient. Very nice!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
lemon sparkle cupcakes

bursting with lemony zing, these cup cakes don't require frosting. in fact, some prefer the crunchy sugar-and-spice topping.

1. in a mixing bowl , cream shortening and sugar
2. add eggs , one at a time , beating well after each addition
3. combine the flour , baking powder and salt
4. add to the creamed mixture alternately with milk
5. stir in lemon peel
6. fill paper-lined muffin cups two-thirds full
7. combine the topping ingredients
8. sprinkle a rounded 1 / 2 teaspoonful over each cupcake
9. bake at 350 for 20-24 minutes or until a toothpick comes out clean
10. cool for 10 minutes before removing from pans to wire racks to cool completely
demonstrations.review: No zing here. Maybe you're supposed to use dried lemon zest? I used fresh, and they didn't taste anything.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
tropical mango cookies

there need to be more mango recipes! i love mango! i got this from cooks.com said to be submitted by cm..i modified it a little.

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees
2. peel the mangoes and cut off the pulp around the seed
3. put in a food processor and puree
4. using an electric mixer , cream together butter and sugar until fluffy
5. beat in egg
6. stir in baking soda , fruit puree and vanilla and molasses
7. stir together the dry ingredients until well combined
8. gradually add to the butter and sugar mixture
9. mix coconut and macadamia nuts
10. stir into the cookie batter using a wooden spoon
11. drop by teaspoonfuls onto greased cookie sheets , flattening with a fork to make a criss-cross pattern
12. bake 12-15 minutes or until done
demonstrations.review: I made these with half the specified quantity of sugar, and they're sufficiently sweet for me. The ingredients sound interesting, but end result is a spongy cookie that is not particularly interesting. I won't make these again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chocolate mint pudding cakes

these are amazing!  from epicurious.com

1. preheat oven to 375f
2. lightly butter six 3 / 4-cup ramekins or custard cups
3. stir chocolate and butter in heavy small saucepan over low heat until melted and smooth
4. remove from heat and cool slightly
5. using electric mixer , beat eggs , egg yolks , and 1 / 3 cup sugar in large bowl until slightly thickened , about 5 minutes
6. add all purpose flour and beat until blended
7. add chocolate mixture , peppermint extract , and salt
8. beat just until incorporated
9. divide chocolate mixture among prepared ramekins
10. place ramekins on baking sheet
11. bake cakes until edges are set but centers look shiny and still move slightly when ramekins are gently shaken , about 11 minutes
12. remove cakes from oven
13. run small knife around each cake to loosen
14. place small plate atop 1 ramekin with pudding cake
15. using oven mitts or pot holders , hold plate and ramekin firmly together and invert , allowing cake to settle onto plate
16. repeat with remaining cakes
17. sprinkle each cake with powdered sugar or sweetened cocoa
18. place scoop of ice cream alongside
19. garnish with mint leaves and serve
demonstrations.review: Divine! I used a tablespoon of peppermint extract, and the cakes were pleasantly minty. The serving size is just right -- larger cakes or the addition of the recommended ice cream would be too much. Very easy and very rewarding.

target.recipe_text:
husker chops

nan

1. brown the chops well in small amount of fat
2. season both sides with salt and pepper , and place in 9" x 13" baking dish
3. mix together the remaining ingredients
4. pour mixture over chops and cover with foil
5. bake in a 325 degree oven for 2 hours
6. remove foil the last 1 / 2 hour of baking
target.review: I made these last night, and they were wonderful(and still will be for lunch today!).  very easy to put together, and as others had done, I also added some mushrooms & onions. No complaints from anyone! Thanks

demonstrations.recipe_text:
creamy baked brussels sprouts

these are soooo good, if you like brussels sprouts that is....

1. defrost the brussels sprouts slightly in the microwave , just so you can cut them in half easily with a sharp knife
2. cut all brussels sprouts in half , if needed so they are all similar in size
3. in another bowl , mix the rest of ingredients , add the brussels sprouts and toss lightly until they are all coated
4. put into a greased casserole dish and bake about 1 / 2 hour in 325 degree oven until bubbly hot and the brussels sprouts are nice and tender
demonstrations.review: We liked this dish very much. As the previuos reviewer suggested, I added some shredded cheddder & parmesan.  I also let it bake a little longer, around 45 minutes.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
breakfast casserole supreme

this is a wonderful almost do ahead breakfast. great for company or christmas morning.

1. melt margarine and place in the bottom of 9" by 13" baking pan
2. spread potatoes in bottom of the pan
3. sprinkle chopped vegetables over potatoes
4. add salt and pepper to taste
5. sprinkle meat over potatoes and vegetables
6. pour beaten eggs over potatoes
7. bake at 350 degrees for 45 minutes
8. remove from oven and sprinkle cheese evenly over top
9. bake another 5-10 minutes or until cheese is hot and bubbly
10. remove from oven and let set for approximately 5 minutes
11. cut into 2
12. 5"-3" squares and serve with a spatula
13. enjoy
demonstrations.review: I made this yesterday and we ALL loved it!  The only thing I changed was I added a 14.5 oz can chopped tomatoes w/ the juice (I just didn't have any fresh).And I used Jimmy Dean sausage. A definate keeper! Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cheese mushroom steak

nothing better than the 3 combined together.

1. cut steak into 4 portions
2. brush both side of each steak with worcestershire sauce
3. sprinkle with basil
4. place on a rack in a shallow roasting pan a few inches from heating element
5. broil 5 minutes on each side or until desired degree of doneness
6. combine pan drippings , mushrooms , wine , salt& pepper and 1 tbs parsley in a medium saucepan
7. cook over medium heat 5 minutes , stirring occasionally
8. with a slotted spoon , spoon mushrooms over steak , reserving liquid in saucepan
9. sprinkle cheese over mushrooms
10. broil an additional 5 minutes or until bubbly
11. transfer to a warm serving platter and sprinkle with parsley
12. add flour to cooking liquid
13. cook over medium heat , stirring constanly 3 minutes or until thickened
14. serve steak immediately with sauce
demonstrations.review: Oh Boy!  This should be illegal! It was wonderful, and as a previuos reviewer mentioned, we did the steaks on the grill.  I served with creamed new potaoes and asparagus.

target.recipe_text:
peanut butter chocolate chunk bars

great for classroom treats, bake sales, etc. quick and easy to make. do not use reduced-fat peanut butter. recipe comes from nestlé.

1. preheat oven to 350
2. in a small bowl , combine flour and baking soda
3. in a large bowl , beat together brown sugar , peanut butter , butter and granulated sugar until creamy
4. beat in egg and vanilla
5. gradually beat in flour mixture
6. stir in chocolate chunks
7. press into ungreased 13 x 9" baking pan
8. bake at 350 for 18-22 minutes or until center is set
9. cool completely in pan on wire rack before cutting into bars
target.review: These were just OK for us.  I thought they were a little dense-I guess I expected something between a chewy brownie and cake and it was a little disappointing for us.  They were very moist and easy and would be good for something in a hurry.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
peanut butter chocolate scotcheroo s

found this on the internet.   great for kids and adults!

1. generously butter a 9 x 13 inch baking pan
2. in a 3 quart saucepan mix light corn syrup , sugar and peanut butter
3. cook over medium heat , stirring until peanut butter melts , stir constantly
4. bring mixture to a boil
5. remove from heat and stir in rice krispie cereal
6. press mixture into buttered 9x13 pan
7. in double boiler , melt semi-sweet chocolate bits and butterscotch bits together
8. make sure your water is not at boiling point when doing this
9. when melted spread over top of rice krispie mixture
10. chill until top is firm and cut into squares
demonstrations.review: I have been making this exact recipe for nearly 20 years and it never lasts more than a day around this house! Crunchy and sweet and peanut butter-who can resist?

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cornflake candy squares

you will lo-o-o-ve this delightful treat that is quick and easy to make! great for kids, but somehow the adults gobble it up too!

1. in medium saucepan on medium heat , cook first three ingredients until melted
2. mixture should be very thin
3. pour over cornflakes
4. stir til cornflakes are well coated
5. spread in a greased 9x13 dish
6. cool in fridge til firm , about 10-15 minutes
7. no sticky hands !
demonstrations.review: I worked in a local bakery when I was in high school and I looked forward to Christmas candy every year because the owner's mother and original founder made this every year. She would never give out the recipe. I have looked for it over the years with very little luck-until now. No wonder she would never give it to me as easy as it is.  The only thing she did differently is she mounded the coated corn flakes on parchment paper instead of placing in the pan. Thanks for the memory!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
luscious lemon coffee cake

i haven't made this, but am having guests this weekend and don't want to lose the recipe! recipe courtesy donna's premiere lodging.

1. combine topping ingredients
2. set aside
3. in mixing bowl , combine cake and pudding mixes , sour cream , eggs , oil and lemon flavoring
4. mix on medium speed for 2 minutes
5. pour 1 / 2 of batter into a greased bundt pan
6. sprinkle half of the topping over batter
7. spoon remaining batter over topping and spread evenly
8. sprinkle with remaining topping
9. bake at 350 for 30-35 minutes or until cake tests done
demonstrations.review: I made this this week and my family has devoured it. The pineapple flavor really gives it a different but delicious flavor. I had a little trouble finding the cake mix at first but found it at one of the high end grocery stores (you know the kind, more expensive but more selections) I will be making this again.

target.recipe_text:
creamy new york deli coleslaw

you may sustitute celery seeds for the caraway seeds if you like. adapted from the america's test kitchen family cookbook, that i just got for my birthday!

1. toss the cabbage with 1 teaspoons salt and let sit in a colander for at least 1 hour or up to 4 hours
2. meanwhile , toast the caraway seeds in a small skillet over medium heat until fragrant , about 3 minutes
3. rinse the cabbage and pat dry with paper towels
4. whisk the toasted caraway seeds , mayonnaise , vinegar , mustard , sugar , and 1 / 4 teaspoons pepper together in a large bowl
5. add the cabbage , carrots , and onion and toss
6. chill for at least 1 hour before serving
7. season with salt and pepper to taste
8. enjoy !
9. the coleslaw can be prepared , covered and chilled a day in advance
10. before serving , freshen the salad with a spoon of mayonnaise and a dash of vinegar
11. season with salt and pepper to taste
target.review: I loved this recipe. I'm so glad you posted it, I had a coleslaw  recipe using caraway seeds that I lost. I used 1 bag of preshredded coleslaw mix, did not toast caraway  seeds, used 1 cup of mayonnaise, 2 tbl. vinegar, 1 tsp. dijon mustard, 2 tsp. sugar, 2 tsp. caraway seeds and 1 small onion sliced on a mandolin and let the slaw stay in refrigerator for 24 hours. It was nice and creamy and delicious!!!............Debbie

demonstrations.recipe_text:
fragrant crispy chicken legs

here's an authentic chinese recipe for drumsticks that i used to serve to large parties when i was in the catering business. it's a bit complicated but worth it. they can be frozen at any point along the way - after steaming or after deep frying. (the recipe comes from 

1. marinate the drumsticks for 4- 5 hours , refrigerated
2. improvise a steamer
3. steam the drumsticks for one hour , covered with aluminum foil that has several small holes pierced in it
4. air dry the drumsticks for a couple hours
5. when ready to deep fry , dredge the steamed drumsticks with cornstarch
6. heat oil to 350- 375 and cook the drumsticks a few at a time until golden brown
demonstrations.review: I used this recipe using 20 boneless with skin, chicken thighs, about 5 pounds. I doubled the recipe and marinated them overnight. I steamed them all in one batch for 1 hour and then ended up refrigerating them overnight. I coated them with cornstarch and deep fried them. The flavor was sooooo good and my family loved them, this is a keeper for sure.  I want to use this marinade on chicken wings next, the chicken tasted just like chicken wings from chinese restaurants. I ordered "The People's Republic of China" cookbook on ebay for $6.99 and can't wait to try new recipes. My family loves chinese food so I'm always trying to find recipes that taste like the chinese restaurants. Thank  you so much for posting this recipe.........Debbie

demonstrations.recipe_text:
denny s style french toast

i do not remember where i got this recipe, but my husband says it tastes just as good as what he had at denny's. i am just amazed at all of the great reviews on this recipe!! my family loves it, so i thought i would share it here and i'm so glad i did because it seems you all love it just as much!!! thanks to all of you who have tried it!

1. mix together the eggs , milk , flour , sugar , vanilla , salt& cinnamon
2. heat a large skillet , or griddle
3. when the skillet is hot , add 1 tablespoon butter
4. if the butter smokes , your pan is too hot
5. turn down the heat
6. dip each slice of bread into the batter for 30 seconds on each side
7. let some of the batter drip off , then put in skillet
8. cook each slice 1 1 / 2-2 minutes per side until each side is golden brown
9. add more butter , if necessary , to cook all of the slices
10. to serve , put on plate , dust with powdered sugar
11. serve with butter & hot syrup
demonstrations.review: My kids inhaled the french toast and said the recipe was a definate "keeper" . I also mixed the ingrediants with the mixer to get out the lumps and fried them in margarine the 2nd time I made the recipe because the 1st time I used butter and they burned very easily. Thank you for such a great recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
twisted sisters creamy cucumber salad

when i arrived in iceland, this was my dh’s 1st food request & i went thru a lot of rz cucumber salad recipes to be sure it wasn’t a duplicate. siggi & my sister named this because it was original w/me & because of my twissis internet identity. for best results, don’t make this a dy ahead, but do allow at least 2 hrs for the flavors to blend & the “cream” to develop from the finished ingredient mix. i promise you’ll like this. (stated time does not include refrigeration time)

1. peel & slice cucumbers in 1 / 2 in thick slices
2. then half ea slice & transfer all slices to a lrg mixing bowl
3. roughly dice red onion & add to the bowl
4. quarter tomatoes , remove seeds , rough dice the tomato meat & add to the bowl
5. thinly slice 1 / 2 green pepper , cut slices in 1 in strips & add to the bowl
6. toss prepared veggies to achieve a good distributional mix
7. add last 6 ingredients to bowl , mix well & refrigerate at least 2 hrs
8. if thinly sliced , most cucumbers wilt & do not retain their crunch
9. -- when all ingredients have been combined , the mixture will appear dry & lack a creamy texture or appearance
10. do not panic that will begin to change almost immediately
11. if you reduce further , you will likely lose any salt component in the mix
demonstrations.review: My family loved this recipe. I sliced the cucumbers and onions very thin and seeded the tomatoes and diced. I didn't have any green pepper so I left it out. I used balsamic vineger because I didn't have any white vinegar and I used 1 tablespoon of sugar because I don't like really sweet foods. Next time I will use 2 teaspoons seasoning salt, I didn't find it salty at all. I like my cuke salad to be on the "soggy" side, to me it tastes just as good or as in this salad "awesome". I mentioned to my son that I bet this would be great on a hamburger and he agreed. I will definately make this again and again and will try this on a burger the next time I make burgers. Thanks so much for posting.....Debbie

target.recipe_text:
kona inn banana bread

i got this from a garden center favorites cookbook quite a few years ago.  it is the best banana bread i have made--and i have tried a bazillion recipes. i keep coming back to this one!!  i hope you like it.

1. cream together butter and sugar
2. add bananas and eggs
3. sift dry ingredients
4. blend wet and dry mixtures but don't overmix
5. bake in a loaf pan at 350 for 45 minutes
6. makes 1 20-ounce loaf
target.review: the BEST banana bread ever...this is my stand-by recipe...sometimes i change it up by throwing in some chocolate chips but otherwise it's perfect.  Thanks for posting.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
oven baked porcupine meatballs

you can make the meatballs ahead of time and freeze.  then simply remove from the freezer, add the remaining ingredients and bake.  double this recipe for a buffet company meal or camping trip.  so easy to make as there’s no need to brown the meatballs in the skillet—saves time and bother.

1. combine ground beef , rice , milk , minced onion , salt and pepper in bowl
2. mix lightly , but well
3. drop rounded tablespoonfuls of mixture into 13 x 9 x 2 inch baking pan
4. combine tomato soup and water in bowl
5. mix well
6. pour over meatballs
7. cover baking pan tightly with aluminum foil
8. bake in 350f oven 1 hour or until hot and bubbly
9. makes 6 to 8 servings
10. farm journals best ever recipes
demonstrations.review: First time making meatballs...sooo good...I added worcestershire sauce and brown sugar as per previous reviewer's suggestion...will definitely make again. Thanks for posting.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
thai style ground beef

a wonderful recipe from cooking light.  a delicious way to use ground beef.  you can make it spicier by using more red curry paste.

1. heat a large skillet over medium-high heat
2. coat pan with cooking spray
3. add leek
4. saut 5 minutes
5. add garlic
6. saut 1 minute
7. add beef
8. cook 7 minutes or until lightly browned , stirring to crumble
9. stir in curry paste and tomato sauce
10. cook until half of liquid evaporates
11. add milk and next 4 ingredients
12. cook 2 minutes or until slightly thickened
13. serve with the rice
demonstrations.review: Delicious! I had never cooked with leeks before--it took some research online to figure out how to prepare them lol--but it was great...I tripled the recipe as I made this for a Thai themed dinner party....made with Coconut Rice and Thai Coleslaw...everyone raved...thanks for an easy recipe Redsie! :)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crock pot garlic brown sugar chicken

the house smells wonderful while this is cooking!

1. place chicken in crock pot
2. mix all remaining ingredients and pour over chicken
3. cook on low for 6-8 hours
4. serve over rice or noodles
5. you can thicken the juices after cooking with a little cornstarch
demonstrations.review: Made my first crock pot meal with this recipe! Came out great..served with mashed potatoes..thanks for posting.

target.recipe_text:
baked spaghetti by paula deen

this recipe is one of the better baked spaghetti's i've tried. i think you could easily shortcut with prepared sauce and such, but you must use angel hair pasta and jack cheese. it makes this!

**edited to add: i have tried to increase pasta per reviews, but this does not work!  you come out with a dry pasta!  please make just as written and rate on the recipe as written!

1. preheat the oven to 350 degrees f
2. in a stockpot , combine the tomatoes , tomato sauce , water , onions , peppers , garlic , parsley , seasoning mixtures , sugar , and bay leaves
3. bring to a boil over high heat , and then reduce the heat and let simmer , covered , for 1 hour
4. crumble the ground beef in a large skillet
5. cook over medium-high heat until fully cooked , with no pink color remaining
6. drain the fat from the meat , and then add the ground beef to the stockpot
7. simmer for 20 more minutes
8. cook the pasta according to the package directions
9. cover the bottom of a 13 by 9 by 2-inch pan with sauce
10. add a layer of pasta and then a little less than 1 / 2 of each cheese
11. repeat the layers , ending with the sauce
12. bake in the oven for 30 minutes
13. top the casserole with the remaining cheese , return it to the oven , and continue to cook until the cheese is melted and bubbly , about 5 more minutes
14. cut into squares before serving
15. house seasoning: mix ingredients together and store in an airtight container for up to 6 months
target.review: Loved it! Authentic Italian taste. I didn't have 8 oz. of angel hair so I used manacoti and wow, still delicious. Like all of Paula Deen's recipes I've tried, this is a dish I'll make over and over again!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
ww 2 points   mini cinnamon rolls

from ww magazine.

1. preheat oven to 375f spray a 9x13 inch baking pan with cooking spray
2. combine brown sugar , cinnamon , and butter in small bowl , set aside
3. separate breadsticks into 12 strips
4. sprinkle tops with brown sugar mixture and roll each one into a spiral , pressing to seal the ends
5. arrange in baking pan 1 inch apart
6. bake until lightly golden , about 15-18 minutes
7. cool for 10 minutes
8. to prepare frosting , combine confectioners sugar , cream cheese , and vanilla in a small bowl , adding a few drops of water if needed to make a smooth , spreadable glaze
9. drizzle over the tops of the warm rolls and let stand a few minutes to set
10. serve warm
demonstrations.review: Delicious! what a great treat, snack, breakfast or desert! I for the icing I sort of had to guess the amounts but sure was good!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
low carb lemon  cheesecake  bars

a variation of this recipe was in the woman's world magazine. since i am trying to monitor carbs and yet still enjoy dessert, this really fills the bill.

1. stir the boiling water into the box of jello , mixing for about 2 minute
2. add the cream cheese and lemon juice
3. mix until all lumps have disappeared
4. pour into an 8" square pan and chill until set
5. cut into 8 squares
demonstrations.review: This dessert set up well b/c of jello, but the taste was salty and very lemony almost sour. I used crushed almonds with a little butter for a crust, but had to top with berries and cool whip to disquise the salty taste. Next time I'll try a different flavor gelatin

demonstrations.recipe_text:
strawberry cheesecake trifle

awesome! this gives a whole new meaning to strawberry shortcake. great dessert for after any meal and a definite crowd pleaser and easy to prepare. (cooking time is estimated chill time.)

1. in a large bowl , beat cream cheese and powdered sugar until fluffy
2. add sour cream , 1 / 2 teaspoon vanilla and the almond extract
3. set aside
4. fold the cool whip into the cream cheese mixture
5. gently stir in cake pieces
6. set aside
7. combine strawberries and sugar , stirring until sugar is dissolved
8. layer in a large glass bowl , starting with 1 / 4 of the strawberries , then adding 1 / 3 of the cake mixture
9. continue layering
10. finish with strawberries
11. cover with plastic wrap
12. and chill several hours
demonstrations.review: This was very good!..the first day, don't leave it for leftovers, the next day it's soggy. GREAT on day one!

target.recipe_text:
tanya s sweet chex mix

went to an alphabet pot luck tonight where everyone signed up to bring a dish that started with a particular letter of the alphabet.  of all the dishes (and there were lots of yummy ones), this was my favorite.  i decided to name it after my friend's sweet daughter that made it.

1. preheat oven to 250f
2. melt together karo syrup , sugar and butter in a large saucepan
3. bring to a boil
4. add butter flavoring and baking soda , mix
5. pour over cereal mixture
6. spread on a large , flat cookie sheet and bake at 250f for 25 minutes
7. remove from oven and spread chex mixture on waxed paper , separating cereal pieces
8. let cool completely
target.review: Give a big THANK YOU to Tanya, this was a hit with the co-workers at our annual meeting!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
banana pudding supreme

this is delicious and easy!

1. cream the cheese with milk until smooth
2. stir in sweetened condensed milk and pudding mix
3. fold in half of the whipped topping
4. layer pudding , cookies and bananas in dish
5. top with remaining topping
6. chill
demonstrations.review: Paula Dean on the Food Network made this exact recipe, except she used Peppridge Farm Chessmen Cookies instead of Vanilla Wafers, and she ended it with a final layer of Chessmen Cookies on the top for a fabulous appearance! This recipe is definitely a keeper

demonstrations.recipe_text:
yummy banana caramel pie

yum yum!

1. preheat oven to 325f
2. fill a large saucepan with water and bring to a boil
3. pour sweetened condensed milk into a small baking dish
4. cover with aluminum foil
5. set dish in a larger baking pan
6. place pan on oven rack and pour boiling water into larger pan , to at least 1 inch deep
7. carefully slide rack back into oven
8. bake 1 hour , until milk is thick and caramelized
9. slice bananas and arrange on bottom of graham cracker crust
10. pour caramelized milk over bananas and allow to cool 30 minutes
11. in a medium bowl , whip cream until soft peaks form
12. add confectioners' sugar and continue to whip until stiff
13. spread over cooled caramel
14. sprinkle with crushed toffee
15. chill 3 hours before serving
demonstrations.review: This IS a good recipe, I have had the exact recipe given to me by a friend, except that she didn't put crushed toffee bars over hers. It sounds like a nice addition, and I  think I'll try it! I found that another easy way to caramelize the sweetened condensed milk is to boil the can of condensed milk for 3 hours, being sure to check the water every so often and adding more to the pot when it starts to evaporate too much. It works like a charm! This recipe is indeed a keeper :)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crock pot pumpkin pie pudding

just in time for the holidays. a family favorite.

1. in a large bowl mix together the first eight ingredients
2. transfer to crock pot coated with pam
3. cover and cook on low 6-7 hours
4. serve in bowls with whip cream , if desired
demonstrations.review: I have this exact recipe,which I found in a slow-cooker cookbook. I use it quite often because I like that I can set it up at noon and let it go while I do other things around the house, and 6 hours later have a scrumptious desert ready for my family. I like to add 1/2 cup of real MAPLE syrup to mine, and I serve it with vanilla ice cream.

target.recipe_text:
japanese mum s chicken

we have a japanese girl, tomoko, living with us, and tonight she and i cooked a japanese dinner for us and her friends. she phoned her mum,toshiko, in japan for this, as it's her favourite recipe, and i wanted to share it here. it's simple and so good, and tomoko, who is only 16, did such a good job of cooking this, then translating the recipe to english for me.

*the liquid will thicken to a glaze if you are patient. it just takes a bit of time. if you feel your chicken is cooked (and going to overcook) remove it before going on to reduce the liquid. same thing, if you must use breast meat, remove it (so it doesn't dry out) and continue reducing the liquid . if you do it this way rather than thickening with cornstarch you will get a richer glaze and not need to add stock or broth instead of the water. it just takes patience. and note: a glaze is sticky and coats the meat, this is not a sauce.

1. place all the ingredients in a saucepan over a high heat
2. bring to the boil , then reduce to a simmer for about 20 minutes
3. remove any scum that rises to the surface
4. increase the heat , turning the drumsticks frequently in the liquid , and cook until the liquid has reduced to a sticky glaze
5. arrange the chicken on a serving platter , remove the garlic clove and chili from the liquid , and spoon the glaze over
target.review: Very easy to make, although it took 25 minutes to thicken (after the chicken was cooked). But was WAY too overwhelmingly vinegar-y for me. Will do half vinegar, half water next time maybe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s moist cheddar garlic oven fried chicken breast

this is for serious garlic lovers. the chicken bakes out so moist and tender! grated cheese may be sprinkled on top of the breast the last 5 minutes of cooking if desired but that is optional. double all ingredients for more than four breasts and adjust the amount of garlic to suit taste. for the coating amount you might be able to get away with 5 or maybe 6 very small chicken breasts, but i would suggest to increase the amount slightly --- to take this dish to yet another level, about 10 minutes before the cooking time is finished, drizzle the top of the chicken with a little pasta sauce, then sprinkle mozzarella cheese on top. return to oven for about 10 minutes until the chicken is completely cooked and sauce is hot and cheese has melted. for a lemon-garlic flavor add in 3 tablespoons lemon juice to the melted butter/garlic mixture ---  *note* for a healthier alternative smart balance butter blend may be used in place of the melted butter --- you will love this chicken!
visit my food blog, www.kittencalskitchen.com, for more of my recipes.

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. butter an 11 x 7-inch pan
3. in a bowl , combine melted butter with fresh minced garlic , 1 teaspoon garlic powder and salt
4. in another bowl , combine the dry breadcrumbs with 1 / 2 cup finely grated cheddar cheese , parmesan cheese 1 teaspoon garlic powder and coarse ground black pepper
5. dip chicken in butter mixture
6. then in crumb mixture
7. place in prepared pan and bake uncovered for 35-45 minutes or until cooked through , larger breasts may take more time
8. top with shredded cheddar or mozzarella the last 5 minutes of cooking (this is only optional
demonstrations.review: I just don't get it. I followed the recipe exactly, and it's bland (and was undercooked).

demonstrations.recipe_text:
norma s quick rolls

these rolls are my very favorite in the world...i can remember my friend' s mother, norma making these rolls, and coming in from
outside. the smell of them cooking leaves you begging for just a taste :) they have been used in my family for 47 years :) these are especially delicious with beans!---------------  
note: 1 (1/4 oz.) package dry active yeast = 2 1/4 teaspoons = 1 (.06 oz) cake compressed fresh yeast.

1. mix all and knead on a floured surface for about 10 minutes
2. let rise 20 minutes and knead again
3. make into rolls , using a floured glass to cut out , and place on a lg
4. greased pizza pan
5. let rise 20 minutes or until double in size
6. bake at 375 , for 20 minutes
demonstrations.review: Turned out nice, but tasted bland.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
banana banana bread

why compromise the banana flavor? my banana bread is moist and delicious with loads of banana flavor! ultimate comfort food, and it's wonderful toasted!! (make sure to use bananas with a lot of black on them for the best flavor! the blacker the bananas, the stronger the banana flavor of the bread.)

1. preheat oven to 350
2. lightly grease 9 x 5 loaf pan
3. in large bowl , combine flour , soda and salt
4. in separate bowl , cream together butter and brown sugar
5. stir in eggs and mashed bananas until well blended
6. stir banana mixture into flour mixture
7. stir just to moisten
8. pour batter into prepared loaf pan
9. bake in preheated oven for 60-65 minutes until a toothpick inserted into center of loaf comes out clean
10. let bread cool in pan for 10 minutes , then turn out onto a wire rack
demonstrations.review:
WARNING - DOES NOT FREEZE WELL!
Turns to goo.
Made two, and the one we didn't freeze was alright. Too moist (pudding-ish) for my liking. Then we froze one. Yikes. It was completely gooey in the centre. Even tried to stick in back in the oven for another 1/2 hour and it did nothing.
Will go back to my usual recipe.

target.recipe_text:
krispy kreme doughnuts

i got this from my child's high school home ec teacher! yum!

1. mix together ingredients for glaze
2. melt butter in hot milk , add 1 tsp sugar and salt
3. allow to cool
4. beat in yeast , nutmeg , eggs , remaining sugar , and 3 cups flour
5. add rest of flour
6. knead for 5 minutes then allow to rise for 1-1 1 / 2 hours
7. roll out dough , cut into shapes
8. do not re-roll dough , then allow to rise for 30-45 minutes
9. heat oil to 365 and fry 1 - 2 minutes on each side or until brown
10. toss in the doughnut holes first , let those cook , and then proceed to cooking the donuts
11. let them cool on a paper towel - helps get the glaze to stick
12. dip in warm glaze
target.review: Wow.  These are amazing!  They tasted very similar to Krispy Kremes!  I added 1/3 cup more sugar to the batter and a teaspoon of vanilla.  They turned out fantastic!  I think the problem some of the other reviewers had who gave lower reviews was with the oil-- you need to make sure it is the right temperature or else they will cook too quickly making the inside too soft or else if it is not hot enough, they will cook to slow and get really oily and gross.  Monitor the temperature and these will turn out fantastic!  I will definitely make these again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
hot chai ovaltine or cocoa

a few weeks ago, i wanted something a little different from your average mug of hot ovaltine, something with a little spice. so i added various spices i knew were in chai. after that, i added the same spices to stephen's dark chocolate cocoa mix. yum! please note, there isn't any tea in this recipe, just the spices that make chai so tasty!

1. heat milk or water until it's nearly boiling
2. combine remaining ingredients in your favorite mug
3. add hot milk or water and stir
4. add whipped topping or marshmallows or your favorite cocoa toppings
demonstrations.review: This was great!  The perfect mix of spices to add warmth to a hot cup of chocolate!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
coconut blondies

these are awesome. i can't wait to try the chocolate chip version. from "the all new good housekeeping cookbook"

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. grease 13 x 9-inch baking pan
3. in small bowl , combine flour , baking powder and salt
4. in saucepan , melt butter over low heat
5. remove from heat
6. stir in brown sugar and vanilla
7. add eggs , stirring until well blended
8. stir in flour mixture into sugar mixture just until blended
9. stir in coconut and pecans
10. spread batter evenly in prepared pan
11. bake until toothpick inserted 2 inches from edge of pan comes out clean , about 30 minutes
12. do not overbake
13. blondies will firm as they cool
14. cool completely in pan on wire rack
15. when cool , cut lengthwise into 4 strips and then cut each strip crosswise into 6 pieces
16. variations: pecan blondies--leave out coconut
17. chocolate chip blondies--leave out coconut and stir in 1 package semisweet chocolate chips
demonstrations.review: So chewy and delicious!  They tasted like some little treat I had in Jamaica-- they have an island feel to them with the coconut.  Fantastic!  Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
thick chocolate pudding

this is the perfect chocolate pudding. it has a rich chocolate flavor, great texture and is not high in fat. i can't count the number of times i have made this. i hope you enjoy it as much as we do.

1. in a 2-qt
2. microwave-safe bowl , combine the first four ingredients
3. stir in milk until smooth
4. microwave , uncovered on high for 3 minutes
5. stir
6. microwave 4-6 minutes longer or until thickened , stirring after each minute
7. stir in vanilla
8. pour into individual serving dishes
9. cool
10. refrigerate
11. garnish with whipped topping if desired
demonstrations.review: Worked great in the microwave but was done at 4 minutes.  Delicious, creamy, and easy!

target.recipe_text:
traditional irish soda bread

this makes a fairly dense, rustic (ugly, even) loaf of bread that is tasty and not sweet. it is crusty and rough on the outside, chewy inside. nummy hot with lots of butter! note: sometimes (depending on humidity etc) it takes a bit more than the 1 1/2 cups of buttermilk--just keep adding a little bit at a time until it all holds together as stated in the recipe.

1. heat oven to 425 degrees f
2. brush a baking sheet with melted butter or spray with non-stick spray
3. combine dry ingredients in a deep bowl
4. gradually stir in 1 cup buttermilk , beating constantly , until dough is firm enough to be gathered into a ball
5. if dough crumbles , add up to 1 / 2 cup more buttermilk , 1 tbsp at a time , until it holds together
6. place on a lightly floured board and pat into an 8-inch flattened round loaf
7. place loaf on baking sheet and slash a 1 / 2-inch deep "x" into the top of the dough with a small , sharp knife
8. bake at 425 degrees f for about 45 minutes , or until the top is golden
9. serve hot
target.review: It was good, but I didn't think was great. My sister said, "It wasn't good and it wasn't bad."

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cheesy summer squash spears

i have been experimenting with squash recipes(we eat a lot of squash) to find one that my kids like.  i made one up that was really good for us and thought i would share.

1. cut the squash into spears about 2 inches long
2. spray cookie sheet or baking pan with olive oil spray
3. lay squash evenly on cookie sheet and sprinkle with salt , pepper , and garlic powder
4. cook in a 375 oven for 15 to 20 minutes then add a couple dollups of butter to the top and let melt in the oven
5. take out and sprinkle your cheese over the top and then put back in the oven and let the cheese melt or brown as desired
6. all the seasonings are per your taste-use more or less as needed
demonstrations.review: Very very good! My dad said that this was "divine." I added quite a bit of garlic though, so my sister said that it was too spicy. I loved it. Even better than the squash though were the baby carrots that I cooked with it. I cooked them covered in olive oil about 20 min. longer before I added the squash and spices to the pan.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
banana  raisin  and oatmeal pancakes

these pancakes are great with maple syrup, honey, marmalade, or even cottage cheese. the recipe comes from bon appetit.cook time is for each pancake.

1. whisk together first 6 ingredients in medium bowl
2. whisk yogurt , milk , eggs , and vanilla in another medium bowl to blend
3. whisk dry ingredients into yogurt mixture just until blended
4. fold in mashed bananas , raisins , and 1 / 4 cup melted butter
5. brush nonstick griddle or skillet with melted butter
6. heat over mediun heat
7. working in batches , pour batter by 1 / 3 cupfuls onto griddle
8. cook pancakes until bubbles form on top and bottoms are golden brown , about 2 minutes
9. turn pancakes over cook until bottoms are golden brown
10. about 2 minutes
demonstrations.review:
These were interesting. They were too moist at first, but then I put them on the waffle iron 
(the flat side) and they did great. The recipe makes a lot of pancakes though. Next time I'll half it. Really good flavor. I'll be making these again. Maybe with whole wheat flour next time.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
three cheese stuffed banana peppers

this is a meat-free stuffed pepper recipe that is great with spaghetti or any other pasta. i use hot banana peppers because they add great flavor and fire to the sauce, but i'm sure mild banana peppers could be substituted for the faint-of-heart!
