1. preheat oven to 375 degrees
2. mix the three cheeses in a medium-sized bowl
3. prepare the peppers by cutting off tops and carefully scraping out the seeds with a knife
4. stuff each pepper with the cheese mixture , using the end of a spoon or your finger to pack the cheeses tightly
5. after all the peppers are stuffed , pour a small amount of the sauce into a baking dish , coating the bottom
6. arrange the stuffed peppers into a single layer in the bottom of the dish
7. if you had any remaining cheese mixture left , you may sprinkle it on top of the peppers now or simply freeze it for next time
8. pour the remaining spaghetti sauce on top of the peppers , covering them completely
9. bake , covered , for 30-40 minutes , or until peppers are soft and sauce is nice and bubbly
10. serve with spaghetti or other pasta
demonstrations.review: Really really great! This is a keeper. If I could give it more stars, then I would. I had no idea what to do with these banana peppers that I had and this was perfect. The whole family loved it. I used Mozzarella cheese and some garlic dill cheddar I had to stuff them. It stayed in the peppers very well. I used a garlic flavored spaghetti sauce. The peppers really made the sauce good and spicy!

target.recipe_text:
whole wheat flax n apple muffins

these muffins are full of grains, apples and nuts that are good for you. i found the recipe on a box of milled flax seed. flax seed is nature's richest plant source of omega-3 oils!

1. blend all dry ingredients together in a bowl
2. in a seperate bowl
3. combine egg , oil , and milk
4. add dry ingredients to egg mixture and stir until just blended
5. fold in apples and nuts
6. batter will be thick
7. fill well greased muffin cups 2 / 3 full
8. bake at 400 degrees for 18 to 20 minutes , or until tops spring back when touched
target.review: My whole family LOVED these muffins!  I used applesauce in place of the oil making these even healthier.  Thank you for a wonderful recipe.  I'll be making these often.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chewy granola bars

i "borrowed" this recipe from the kitchen at my college because i fell in love with these bars. they are so much better than store-bought, and you can add or subtract ingredients as you wish. they make a perfect on-the-go snack; a much healthier alternative to chips or cookies, especially for kids (great for lunch boxes!)

1. preheat oven to 350 and lightly grease or spray 9 x 13 pan
2. in large bowl , beat brown sugar , sugar , and butter until light and fluffy
3. blend in honey , vanilla and egg
4. in separate bowl , combine flour , cinnamon , baking soda , and salt
5. add flour mixture gradually to sugar mixture and beat until combined
6. by hand , stir in almonds , chocolate chips and oats until well mixed
7. press mixture firmly in bottom of greased pan , and bake at 350 for 20-25 minutes , or until light golden brown
8. cool and cut into squares
demonstrations.review: Yum!  Very easy, chewy and makes a lot of bars.  I like these because you can use whatever you have on hand so they will probably turn out differently each time.  I will be making these again!  My kids, my husband and I all liked these.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
zucchini or yellow squash casserole

this is different from your usual squash recipe.a friend of mine brought it to a pot luck dinner 15 years ago and it has been a family favorite since then.

1. saute onions&bell pepper in margarine for 5 minutes , add squash that has been sliced and cubed
2. saute 5 min more , add tomatoes , cook 5 more minutes
3. add bread cubes and seasonings
4. put in 2 quart casserole , sprinkle top with parmesan cheese
5. bake at 350 for 30 to 40 minutes
demonstrations.review: I totally agree with all these positive reviews!  This was awesome and a great way to use up extra summer squash.  I mixed yellow squash with zucchini and did as one reviewer suggested by adding TWO cans of tomatoes with garlic & onion to the mix.  It came out wonderfully!  My kids said it tastes like pizza!  Thank you Connie, for a wonderful addition to our summer meals.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
super tender ranch chicken

after discovering the secret to feeding my flock with less, i also discovered that we had some ranch dressing that wasn't our favorite.  rather than throw it out, i put together this quick recipe and we loved it.  now, i make it often. if you have other quick-cooking side dishes to pair with this, you will have dinner on the table in less than 30 minutes.

1. put ranch dressing into medium sized bowl
2. put bread crumbs with herbs and wheat germ added into another bowl next to the ranch dressing bowl
3. pound chicken breasts into 1 / 4" thickness with cooking mallot
4. see my recipe for mysterious mul
5. cut chicken breasts into strips over the bowl of ranch dressing so that strips fall into bowl
6. stir with fingers to coat chicken pieces well
7. wash hands , then pour enough of your favorite cooking oil into the bottom of a heavy skillet just to coat
8. heat pan on med-high heat just until oil begins to smoke then turn heat to medium
9. you can use non-stick spray , but chicken doesn't get that pretty golden color and tends to get blacken as well
10. if you can handle two pans at the same time , you may want to consider that because two chicken breasts will fill two skillets worth
11. take each chicken piece and dip into the bread crumbs and carefully lay each piece in the pan leaving only enough room between pieces to turn pieces with tongs
12. cook approximately 3-4 minutes each side or until golden brown each side
13. cut into one piece to make sure it is done before removing pieces from skillet
14. enjoy your juicy tender chicken
demonstrations.review: So easy, tender & delicious!  My whole family loved this chicken.  I added a bit of Italian Seasoning to the bread crumbs but not much.  Good flavor. I will be making this again!  Thanks for a great recipe!

target.recipe_text:
turtle pumpkin pie  from kraft

from kraft foods. its really good

1. pour 1 / 4 cup caramel topping into crust
2. sprinkle with 1 / 2 cup nuts
3. beat dry pudding mixes , milk , pumpkin and spices with whisk until well blended
4. stir in 1-1 / 2 cups cool whip
5. spoon into crust
6. refrigerate 1 hour
7. top with remaining cool whip , caramel topping and nuts just before serving
target.review: I was a bit skeptical with this recipe because I love turtle pie/candy and I love pumpkin pie, but I was not sure if combining the two was a good idea. It sounded interesting though so I went ahead and tried it. What a yummy pie! I will definitely be making this again and in fact will likely add it to my Thanksgiving menu from now on! Thanks very much for a creative and delicious spin on a classic!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
the real chocolate chip cookies   neiman marcus   copycat

this is the same cookie recipe that was posted on the neiman marcus web site.

1. cream the butter with the sugars until fluffy
2. beat in the egg and the vanilla extract
3. combine the dry ingredients and beat into the butter mixture
4. stir in the chocolate chips
5. drop by large spoonfuls onto a greased cookie sheet
6. bake at 375 for 8-10 minutes or 10-12 minutes for a crispier cookie
demonstrations.review: This cookie was very good.Sometimes you want something with a little more kick than just a chocolate chip cookie and this cookie does that. I only had salted butter, so I used that. I also used 2 eggs because the dough was too dry with only 1. Additionally, I went with the previous suggestion to bake the cookies at 300 for 20 minutes. That was brilliant! I will NEVER bake another cookie at 375 again! I have tried other Neiman Marcus cookie recipes that were a lot different, but this was a first for this version. Great cookie!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
soft snickerdoodle cookies

these snickerdoodle cookies are so delicious, and they have the best texture. they are so fast to put together too! i actually got it from an old recipe that my great grandma had clipped out of a newspaper. grandma always knows best!

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. mix softened butter , 1 1 / 2 cups sugar , 1tps of vanilla extract and eggs thoroughly in a large bowl
3. combine flour , cream of tartar , baking soda and salt in a separate bowl
4. blend dry ingredients into butter mixture
5. chill dough , and chill an ungreased cookie sheet for about 10-15 minutes in the fridge
6. meanwhile , mix 3 tablespoons sugar , and 3 teaspoons cinnamon in a small bowl
7. scoop 1 inch globs of dough into the sugar / cinnamon mixture
8. coat by gently rolling balls of dough in the sugar mixture
9. place on chilled ungreased cookie sheet , and bake 10 minutes
10. remove from pan immediately
demonstrations.review: I was pleased with this recipe. I haven't made snickerdoodles in a long time and had forgotten how much I liked them. I increased the cinnamon and sugar to 4 tsp/TBSP because I got very low toward the end. I do my dough a bit backward because I roll and coat, then refrigerate. That way they go into the oven cold. Also, I saw a tip a while back to back cookies at 300 for 20 minutes instead of a higher temperature. I love what the degree/time adjustment does to my cookies! The only problem was that the cookies seemed to dry out within 2 days. Any suggestions how to avoid that? Thanks for a terrific cookie recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
unbaked chocolate chip oatmeal cookies

nan

1. put first 4 ingredients into a 2 quart saucepan and bring to a full , rolling boil
2. remove from heat and add vanilla and peanut butter
3. add oatmeal and stir well
4. drop teaspoonfuls onto a well greased cookie sheet
5. chill for 1 hour
demonstrations.review: Very good and very easy. I used creamy peanut butter instead of chunky and a little extra vanilla. My kids loved it! We will definitly be making this again.

target.recipe_text:
pork chops with applesauce

this is great if you like something sweet, but not too sweet, with your pork. another delicious comfort food.

1. season pork chops with garlic , salt and pepper
2. in heavy skillet , brown chops in small amount of cooking oil
3. mix remaining ingredients while chops are browning
4. place chops , single-layer , in shallow baking dish
5. spoon half of applesauce mixture evenly over chops
6. bake in preheated 350 oven for 20 minutes
7. turn chops and evenly spoon remaining applesauce mixture over them
8. bake for 20-30 more minutes
target.review: so sorry I forgot to add a rating to my first review...

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pasta with ground beef and yoghurt

quick, easy and tasty. yoghurt and beef can be prepared ahead so dinner is ready in the time you'll need to cook the pasta. use roasted garlic for the cooked garlic in the recipe if you have on hand. - this is my variation from a turkish recipe. the yoghurt should be very mild and creamy rich, like greek yoghurt, not tart or runny, or the dish will be too tart.

1. bring a small amount of salted water to a boil , add garlic with skin on and cook for 5-8 minutes
2. drain and rinse
3. slip from skins and crush with a press or a fork
4. stir yoghurt with salt and crushed garlic in a bowl until smooth , set aside
5. bring salted water for the pasta to a boil
6. peel onions
7. finely grate onions or chop onions in the food processor to a pulp
8. heat butter for the beef in a skillet
9. add beef , chili , onions , salt and pepper and cook over high heat , crumbling and browning the meat , about 10 minutes
10. while frying the meat , cook pasta until done , drain
11. in another small pan melt butter for the topping and stir in paprika and cayenne
12. when meat is browned and cooked through and pasta is ready , give a portion of pasta on a plate , top with some of the meat , spoon a portion of the yoghurt over it and drizzle with some of the melted butter
13. serve with a green salad on the side
demonstrations.review: I was making spaghetti bolognaise again for the kids but really wanted something different for me & husband, this was fantastic. I followed the recipe pretty exactly, though I had to use a couple of red onions along with the white as I didn't have enough left - 4 onions seemed a lot, but in fact was just right. Easy & quick to make. Will definitely do this again, I loved it & husband has requested it, thank you!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cinnamon flop

yummy and easy! kids and adults love it :) i don't remember where i got this recipe...i just have it written on an index card, but it has been requested of me many times. makes 2 - 9 inch cakes, so there is enough to go around!

1. preheat oven to 350 and grease well two 9" round pans
2. combine flour , sugar and baking powder
3. add melted butter and milk and stir until well blended
4. divide mixture evenly into two prepared pans
5. sprinkle tops evenly with flour , then brown sugar , then cinnamon
6. push chunks of butter evenly spaced into dough
7. bake for 30 minutes and cool slightly
8. cut and serve right out of pans
demonstrations.review: I am sure this would be great for breakfast - but I made it for after a light dinner, all 3 of my kids loved a big chunk with a glass of milk, I loved it too! Easy and quick to make, the cinnamon topping really lifts it as well.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
plum clafouti

i'm not much of a dessert cook, but this is foolproof and tastes great.

1. grease a shallow 18x28cm ovenproof dish with butter
2. place the plum halves , evenly over the base of the dish
3. place eggs and sugar in a food processor and blend until pale
4. add the flour and essence and process until smooth
5. add the milk
6. process until well mixed
7. pour the batter over the plums
8. bake in a moderately hot oven for 25 to 30 minutes or until the custard is set and golden
9. serve dusted with icing sugar , cream or ice cream
demonstrations.review: This was very good. I didn't have time to warm the milk and so the batter separated very slightly (I think that's why it happened!) - but still turned out well. I will be making it again.

target.recipe_text:
artichoke spinach dip from olive garden

from top secret recipes http://www.topsecretrecipes.com

1. cracker , chips or toasted -bread boil spinach and artichoke hearts in a cup of water in small saucepan over medium heat until tender , about 10 minute
2. drain
3. heat cream cheese in small bowl in microwave set on high for 1 minute
4. add spinach and artichoke hearts to the cream cheese and stir well
5. add remaining ingredients to the cream cheese and combine
6. serve hot
target.review: Fabulous! (I added less artichoke and more spinach)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
key lime cheesecake squares

this is a delightful and refreshing dessert. i found a recipe 15 years ago that is similar to mine, but i modified it to have a very good blend between the lime juice and sugar. my crust enhances the taste of the cheesecake.

1. crust---------
2. preheat oven to 350 f degrees
3. in a mixing bowl , combine graham wafer crumbs , vanilla wafer crumbs and ground almonds
4. cut in butter using a pastry blender or a fork until mixture is crumbly
5. prepare a 9 inch x 9 inch oven-proof casserole dish by spraying inside with a vegetable spray
6. press wafer mixture firmly in bottom of casserole dish
7. bake in preheated 350 f oven for 15 minutes
8. filling----------
9. in a mixing bowl using an electric mixer , beat softened cream cheese , sugar and egg until smooth
10. add lime juice , grated lime zest and tapioca starch and beat until smooth and creamy
11. spread mixture evenly over baked crust
12. return to oven and bake at 350 f for 25 to 30 minutes or until set
13. cool on wire rack
14. chill in refrigerator for at least 1 hour before cutting into squares to serve
15. if desired , decorate top of cheesecake with pieces of lime or halved small fresh strawberries or quartered maraschino cherries
16. you can also use regular lime juice or use bottled key lime juice
demonstrations.review: I brought these to work for a Mardi Gras party and people RAVED about them!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
grilled balsamic asparagus

this wonderfully flavored asparagus evolved from a cooking light recipe. prep time includes time to marinate.

1. snap off tough ends of asparagus and wash well through 2-3 changes of cold water
2. combine all ingredients in a large zip-top plastic bag , seal and marinate for 30-60 minutes
3. preheat grill on high heat
4. remove asparagus from bag and place on preheated oiled grill rack
5. grill 5 minutes on each side or until asparagus is done
demonstrations.review: The flavor on this was very good, but we ended up cooking for about 8 minutes on each side. We will definitely have again!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
sour cream and ground beef layered casserole

this is a great casserole that i have been making for years, it's one of my family's favorite dishes. feel free to adjust all ingredient amounts to suit taste. i usually season the ground beef/onion mixture with seasoned salt and add in some cayenne pepper for heat but that is optional.

1. set oven to 350f
2. grease a 13 x 9-inch baking pan
3. in a large skillet , cook the ground beef with onion , garlic and chili flakes over medium heat until meat is browned and no longer pink
4. drain fat then stir in the parmesan cheese
5. add tomato sauce and sugar
6. bring mixture to a boil
7. cover , reduce heat and simmer for about 30 minutes stirring occasionally
8. transfer meat mixture to a greased baking dish
9. set aside
10. in a bowl beat cream cheese and sour cream at low speed until smooth
11. add in green onions then stir to combine
12. spread the cream cheese mixture over the ground beef in the dish
13. top with cooked noodles , then sprinkle the shredded cheddar cheese over the noodles
14. sprinkle with paprika
15. bake for 25-30 minutes or until hot and bubbly
demonstrations.review: This recipe was awesome! It is a great and BETTER alternative to lasagna. This was quick and easy, and my whole family LOVED it!

target.recipe_text:
copycat  green giant niblets corn in butter sauce

i had to come up with this quick. every thanksgiving my mom serves green giant niblets corn in butter sauce and i promised i would pick it up for her and bring it on thanksgiving day. when i went to the store, they were sold out! i made this recipe and brought it already prepared to thanksgiving dinner. nobody was the wiser! i saved some money too, because i used store brand corn! this recipe makes a lot...you may want to half it.

1. add corn to large sauce pan along with all ingredients except water and cornstarch
2. stir corn mixture over medium heat until butter is melted
3. combine water and cornstarch and stir until cornstarch is disolved
4. slowly add water to corn in sauce pan , stirring constantly
5. reduce heat to simmer and stir until sauce thickens
6. let simmer , stirring occasionally , until corn is tender , about 10 minutes
target.review: This is really good.  I never bother with the cornstarch and water and it is still great.  Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
green beans with new potatoes

this is a paula deen recipe, but it is the way i learned to cook beans nearly 50 years ago. usually i cut my potatoes in half instead of peeling the strip from them because its faster and easier. this makes such good beans that you'll be wiggling like a speckled pup.

1. remove the ends from the beans
2. snap the beans in 2 pieces , place into a colander , wash , and set aside to drain
3. meanwhile , in a large cast iron dutch oven , lightly brown the salt pork in the bacon grease over medium heat , turning often , for approximately 10 minutes
4. toss the green beans into the pot , stirring them with a wooden spoon to coat well with the pork fat
5. add the broth , salt , pepper and garlic powder
6. cook over medium-low heat , covered tightly , for approximately 30 minutes , or until the beans are half done
7. while the beans are cooking , peel a center strip from each new potato with a potato peeler
8. at the end of 30 minutes , add the potatoes and onion to the beans
9. add 1 / 4 cup more broth , if needed
10. cook , covered tightly , until the potatoes are tender , approximately 25 to 30 minutes , periodically checking the pot to make sure a small amount of liquid remains
11. when the potatoes are tender , tilt the lid slightly , off to the side of the pot , and continue to cook until the green beans are wilted , approximately 15 minutes
12. while cooking , add the butter and season with more pepper if needed
demonstrations.review: Very flavorful!  I used two large cans of Kentucky Wonder or Italian green beans.  Didn't add the butter at the end, there's really no need.  I think it would be way too greasy.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
e z banana creme bundt cake

you will love this banana pecan bundt cake made easy with cake mix. yummy!

1. in large mixing bowl , mash bananas
2. add rest of ingredients , except pecans and mix for 2 minutes at medium speed of mixer
3. add chopped pecans
4. pour into greased and floured bundt pan
5. bake at 350 degrees for 60 minutes
6. cool in pan for 15 minutes
7. remove from pan and let cool
8. sprinkle with powdered sugar before serving
demonstrations.review: Moist! I used 2.5 bananas, cook and serve pudding (by mistake), and no nuts.  Only cooked in my oven about 45 min.  Will make this lots.  Thanks for a great recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
stove top mac n cheese by alton brown

this is from alton brown's good eats show and it's an easy and good mac n cheese recipe to have on hand. you won't be buying the boxed stuff again after eating this. (edited 8/15/2008 - this was initially posted with 3/4 tsp of dry mustard but after making this a few times i agree with the reviewer that said this amount is too much so i've reduced it to 1/2 tsp.)

1. in a large pot of boiling , salted water cook the pasta to al dente and drain
2. return to the pot and melt in the butter
3. toss to coat
4. whisk together the eggs , milk , hot sauce , salt , pepper , and mustard
5. stir into the pasta and add the cheese
6. over low heat continue to stir for 3 minutes or until creamy
demonstrations.review: Excellent. Don't be afraid of the hot sauce, it's not enough to overpower the dish.  Reheats well, too.

target.recipe_text:
caramel popcorn  not too sweet or sticky

i think this is a great caramel popcorn recipe, and i have tried quite a few! they were either too sticky or too sweet. this one is neither. the caramel dries well and doesn't stick to your fingers, and the sweetness is just right. i use spanish peanuts in this, but you could use other kinds of nuts, too. here i was searching for the perfect caramel corn recipe, when all the while it was right in my recipe box! this is done in the microwave, and is very simple to make.

1. prepare microwave popcorn as directed on bag
2. remove any unpopped kernels
3. in 2 quart microwave-safe bowl , microwave butter on high until melted , about 1& 1 / 2 minutes
4. stir in sugar and corn syrup , and microwave on high for 4-5 minutes
5. stir in vanilla and baking soda until blended
6. stir in popcorn , mixing well
7. if you are using nuts , add them here too
8. microwave on high for 4 to 6 minutes , stirring every 2 minutes to coat popcorn evenly
9. transfer caramel corn to tray lined with waxed paper , or parchment paper
10. cool and break popcorn apart
11. store in airtight container
target.review: Yummy! The best caramel popcorn recipe ever!! So easy as well! Wouldn't change a thing :)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crispy ginger beef

if you like sweet, spicy, crispy chinese food- this is for you. adapted from a recipe i saw on "fixing dinner" with sandi richard.

1. place cornstarch in a large bowl
2. add water gradually while whisking
3. beat eggs into cornstarch mixture
4. toss in beef and stir to coat
5. pour 1 inch of oil into wok , heat until boiling hot , but not smoking
6. add a quarter of the beef to the oil
7. seperate with a fork and cook , stirring frequently , until crispy , remove , drain on paper towel and set aside
8. repeat until all the beef is cooked
9. drain off all oil except for about 1 tablespoons and add carrots , onion , ginger , and garlic in that order
10. stir fry briefly over high heat
11. combine last 5 ingredients and add to vegetable mixture
12. bring to a boil and then add beef
13. heat thorough and serve immediately
demonstrations.review: I thought this was super good.  Tasted amazing! The only reason why I only gave it 4 stars was because I found it really hard to get the beef crispy.  Never really worked for me...but that was ok....The sauce was amazing....

demonstrations.recipe_text:
my family s favorite sloppy joes  pizza joes

i've tried many recipes, this is the best. i once 'dec-tupled' (10x) this recipe to sell sandwiches at a craft fair at my church. people were waiting in line to buy leftovers. freezes well, goes up to the lake or camping well and is a hit on halloween...it's no-fail. easy to double, triple, etc. i've been making joes this way for over 20 years.
***03-08-09, i just reinvented this recipe tonight when i went to make it for dinner and found i didn't have an 8-oz. can of tomato sauce (shame on me).  the family was upset with me when i subbed an 8-oz. can of pizza sauce and told them to suck it up and call them 'pizza joes' and then served them up with shredded mozzarella cheese on the toasted buns, top and bottom.  they loved it.  i left out the bbq sauce in this preparation and just used a 1/2 cup ketchup.  pizza joes are good to go!

1. in a large skillet , brown ground beef , celery and onion
2. drain the fat , who needs it ?
3. stir in remaining ingredients , simmer covered , 15-20 minutes , stirring occasionally
4. if joes appear too'loose' , leave cover off and let moisture evaporate
5. cook until it's the consistency you like for serving on toasted buns , with french fries and cole slaw
demonstrations.review: These are the best sloppy joes I have ever made! Delish!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
no dough meat crust  pizza for the low carb dieter

tastes like a pizza, cuts like a pizza, yet there is no dough....though do have a fork and knife on hand for eating purposes because it can get a little messy if eaten with hands only. i am a south beach dieter with a love for italian foods and this is what curbs my craving for pizza. i love mine with the turkey pepperoni slices, onion, green peppers and mushroom. serve with a tossed salad or marinated veggies.

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees
2. meanwhile , brown the ground beef
3. drain
4. place meat in a mixing bowl and mix with 1 cup of mozzarella
5. spread the mixture into a circle on a round pizza pan or baking stone
6. and top with 1 / 2 cup pizza sauce
7. top with the rest of the mozzarella , optional toppings and seasonings
8. bake for about 25 minutes or until cheese is melted and browned
demonstrations.review: This totally fufilled all pizza cravings that my boyfriend and I encounter on the low carb diet that we are on! Really good...Didn't even miss the crust...

target.recipe_text:
grilled rib eye steak   red onions

delicious

1. combine all ingredients except steak and onions
2. place steak in plastic zip lock bag and pour marinade over
3. marinate in refrigerator 4 hours or overnight-- turning the bag and smushing the herbs into the meat
4. pour excess marinade into skillet
5. add onions and cook until tender while grilling steaks
target.review: Extremely tasty steak, in fact, the taste is even a bit too overpowering, making it difficult to appreciate the quality of the meat. Next time I use this recipe, I intend to use only half of the recommended amount of balsamic vinegar, red wine vinegar, and soya sauce. It it woks out as well as expected, I'll revise my review.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chicken legs grilled

generously seasoned crisp legs.
be sure to visit the grilling forum http://www.recipezaar.com/bb/viewforum.zsp?f=42 for any help!

1. mix all marinade ingredients in a zip lock bag add chicken
2. chill and marinade for 4 hours
3. grill chicken on a well oiled grill until well browned on all sides , turning once , 30 to 40 minutes
4. fyi
5. all grills are different temperatures
6. take advantage of indirect heat --
7. if the chicken browns quickly finish over indirect heat
8. all grills have hot spots so watch and be sure to move the chicken to spots on the grill so not to burn and completely cook the chicken
9. as the time of the year makes grilling quicker or slower
10. so take care and watch and enjoy you food as it grills
11. be sure to visit the grilling forum for any help !
demonstrations.review: A winner! Although I might have left the chicken on a bit longer (30 minutes on indirect heat), it still came out tasting and looking great. Based on comments made by reviewers, I made a few substitutions (honey for sugar, onion salt for seasoning salt, garlic for garlic powder) and additions (a bit of sesame oil and chili flakes). I also chilled the chicken in the marinade for 8 hours. Thanks Rita.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
whatever floats your boat  brownies

these are absolutely the chewiest, moistest, fudgiest brownies ever! i have tried adding so many different things to the batter, and they always comes out great.  they are also great without any add-ins! but by varying the add-ins, you can make different brownies every week (or day!!) super easy prep! so, add "whatever floats your boat" and you will not believe how yummy they come out :) oh, and the recipe doubles just fine--use a 9 x 13 inch pan instead and add a few more minutes of baking!

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. grease an 8 inch square pan or line with foil
3. in a medium bowl combine melted butter and cocoa and stir until cocoa is dissolved
4. add sugar and mix well
5. add eggs one at a time and stir until well combined
6. stir in vanilla , flour and salt until you no longer see any flour
7. fold in "whatever floats your boat" !
8. spread in pan and bake for approximately 25 minutes
9. do not over-bake -- your brownies will come out dry
10. adjust time / temp accordingly for your oven
11. if you do the knife / toothpick test , it should come out with moist crumbs , not clean
12. cool completely before cutting into squares
13. for vegetarian omit the marshmallows
14. for double recipe , bake in 9x12 pan and add 5 minutes to baking time
demonstrations.review: When you see a recipe that over 550 people have already raved about, you get the impression that another complementary review would be a case of overkill. Well, let it be so. This is the mother of all brownies! I only added a good half cup of pecans, so the incredible taste all comes from the basic brownie itself, although "basic" just doesn't seem to apply here. Great job Karen!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
maple peanut butter cookies

these are like traditional peanut butter cookies, but unique in that they are flavored with maple! this was judith korbey's of methuen, massachusetts contribution to the 1958 pillsbury bake-off. i got the recipe from the 50th anniversay best of the bake-off cookbook.

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. in a large bowl , beat brown sugar , butter and peanut butter until light and fluffy
3. add syrup and the egg yolk and beat well
4. mix in flour , baking soda , salt and baking powder
5. if necessary , refrigerate for 15-30 minutes for easier handling
6. shape dough into 1" balls and place 2 inches apart on ungreased cookie sheets
7. with a fork dipped in sugar , flatten balls with a criss-cross pattern
8. bake at 350 for 8-12 minutes until golden brown
demonstrations.review: This is just a wonderful recipe. I made bigger cookies (24) and they turned out great. I'll probably add nuts next time (pecans or cashews) just because I love nuts... Thanks for this Roosie!

target.recipe_text:
grilled shrimp    mmmmmm

a nice modernized version of the old classic shrimp cocktail. watch 'em disappear!

1. in a 1 gal plastic food bag place shrimp and olive oil , toss to coat , sprinkle enough rub to coat the shrimp
2. the bag should look dark red
3. refrigerate for 1-4 hrs , the longer you wait the hotter they'll be
4. light the grill and while it's heating place shrimp on skewers
5. when coals are very hot , clean the area that the shrimp will be on and rub with a bit of canola oil on a rag
6. immediately place shrimp on greased grill for 2-3 minutes , turn and cook an additional 2-3 minutes
7. remove from skewers and serve hot
8. no dipping sauce required
9. this rub works well on chicken wings too !
target.review: Sorry, I wasn't thrilled with this recipe.  We found it too salty, and too sweet (even though I halved the amount of brown sugar after reading some of the reviews).  I also thought the Italian Seasoning was out of place.  Sorry.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
grandmother paul s sour cream pound cake

recipe courtesy of paula deen and the food network. i like to make this one in nordicware's 

1. preheat the oven to 325
2. cream butter and sugar together with your heavy-duty mixer
3. add the sour cream and mix thoroughly
4. sift baking soda and flour together
5. add the flour to the creamed mixture , alternating with one egg at a time
6. mix well after each addition
7. add the vanilla and mix well
8. spoon the mixture into a well greased and floured 10 inch tube or bundt pan
9. bake for 1 hour and 20 minutes , or until toothpick inserted in cake tests completely clean
10. let cake cool in the pan on a wire rack for 15 minutes
11. invert cake on wire rack , removing from pan and let cool completely
12. frost as desired or leave plain and garnish with fresh berried and freshly whipped cream
demonstrations.review:
I made this cake for a benefit we're attending tonight.  I had extra that made 6 cup cakes.  

After reading some reviews I used 1 tbspn of vanilla but I agree with some other reviewers, cake is good but needs something! Flavor is sort of bland.  Not sure what it needs. Maybe additional vanilla or almond extract?

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pav de limo

my mother taught me to prepare this no-bake, easy-to-make brazilian dessert. i love it because it’s not too sweet. use thin biscuits that are rectangular—about 35mm x 75mm. in australia, i use arnott’s malt o milk biscuits, but any similar biscuit would be fine. you can make this dessert in any size pan, depending on how many layers you want. i get four layers when i use a pan about 180mm x 280mm. time does not include two hours for refrigeration.

1. zest and juice the limes
2. set aside the zest for decoration
3. combine the condensed milk , cream and lime juice , and beat until thick
4. have your ungreased pan ready
5. pour the plain milk into a shallow dish and dip each biscuit in the milk
6. arrange a layer of biscuits in the pan , and top it with about 1 / 4 of the beaten mixture
7. keep repeating layers until you run out of the beaten mixture
8. sprinkle the top layer with the reserved lime zest
9. refrigerate for at least two hours before serving
10. you can make this a day in advance
demonstrations.review: I made this for Easter and it came out great, reminds me of key lime pie.  I used coconut Maria crackers so it had a very tropical "put the lime with the coconut"  flavor.  It really isn't too sweet, if you like key lime pie you'll love this dessert, and it's SO EASY.  Make sure you use a well chilled bowl and beaters to get the mixture to whip up.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crab stuffed mushrooms

i have always loved the stuffed mushrooms from red lobster so i created my own version which i have enjoyed even more!

1. spray a 9x12-inch glass baking dish with cooking spray
2. use an additional baking dish if needed
3. drizzle olive oil or butter in the bottom of the baking dish
4. wipe mushrooms with a damp paper towel to clean
5. remove stems , set aside caps and chop stems to add to filling
6. in a medium bowl , mix crabmeat , chopped mushroom stems , onion , dry mustard , 1 cup parmesan cheese , soft bread crumbs , parsley , red and black pepper , and garlic salt
7. mix well and then stir in egg and mayonnaise
8. use a small cookie scoop to mound filling onto each mushroom cap
9. melt butter and mix in garlic salt and drizzle over the filled mushrooms
10. mound a generous portion of the shredded parmesan cheese on top of each filled mushroom
11. bake for 20 to 25 minutes at 425f
12. best served hot
13. can be prepared ahead , refrigerated and then baked just before serving
demonstrations.review: I made this recipe for Thanksgiving a few years ago and it was a huge hit.  I used baby bella mushrooms and just added a few things: minced garlic to the stuffing mix and some Goya Adobo seasoning to the melted butter. I made the stuffing on Tuesday but didn't stuff them and cook until Thursday (don't be put off if the color of the stuffing seems to change).  They were good but to be honest the were awesome reheated on Friday.  Next time I think I'll try to add a touch of white wine to the stuffing.  Awesome recipe Diane Thanks.

target.recipe_text:
chicken and peanut noodles

quick, easy and very tasty. a chicken and noodle dish,  for all peanut butter lovers. child friendly as well. adapted from a family circle recipe.

1. in skillet , heat oil on med high
2. stir-fry chicken and garlic 3 or so minutes
3. remove the chicken
4. spoon peanut butter into skillet
5. whisk in water , vinegar , soy sauce , pepper flakes and 1 seasoning packet from noodles
6. do not use both packets
7. bring to a boil: add noodles breaking them up slightly
8. add cooked chicken and cover
9. simmer 4 minute to separate noodles
10. sprinkle with veggies cover and simmer 3 more minute stir
11. add green onions on top
12. i also added some chopped peanuts on top
13. serve and enjoy ! just as good the next day
target.review: O.K., you know the peanut chicken you get in Chinese restaurants that is soooo delicious.  This tastes almost exactly like it!!  It is wonderful.  I made peas, but didn't add them, because my kids don't like them.  However, my husband and I did add the peas and we loved it!  Thanks for posting.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
stuffing for christmas or thanksgiving

this is similar to my mom's recipe that she has made for years. she never measures and adds everything for our taste preferences. i have never been able to top her stuffing, but this comes very close. i don't measure the herbs. we like the sage flavor, so i tend to add more of that. i taste it until it tastes right to me. adjust the herbs to whatever your taste preferences are. your kitchen will smell wonderful as the herbs are cooking with the vegetables! if you like drier stuffing, adjust the amount of chicken broth. we like ours moist, so i use about 2 cans of swanson chicken broth. i always make several days ahead and freeze in ziploc bags with all the air squeezed out so that i'm not so rushed the day of the dinner.

1. if you're using bread , toast bread in a large shallow baking pan in middle of oven until just dry , 25 to 30 minutes
2. if you're using stuffing mix , you can skip this step
3. cook onions , celery , and herbs in butter in a large heavy skillet over moderately low heat , stirring occasionally , until celery is softened , about 10 minutes
4. stir together bread or stuffing mix , vegetables , broth , and salt and pepper to taste , then cool completely , uncovered
5. freezes extremely well
6. stuff in the turkey or bake at 350 for about 30 minutes
demonstrations.review: I made this with Pepperidge Farm stuffing mix, and I used 41/2 tablespoons of onion flakes instead of onions, and 4 cups of chicken broth instead of two - two was not enough for 2 packages of stuffing mix.  Everyone at our Thanksgiving dinner thought it was good, but I thought there was a little too much of one of the spices (not sure which one).  It was a little strong.  I guess for my first attempt at stuffing, it was pretty good.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
loaded hash browns potato casserole

all your favorite baked potato toppings (sour cream, cheddar cheese, bacon and chives) add a yummy twist to the traditional hash brown potato casserole.

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees
2. thaw potatoes
3. combine soup , sour cream , softened cream cheese , 1 / 4 cup melted butter , bacon bits , chives and cheese
4. mix in potatoes
5. spray 3 quart casserole dish with pam and add mixture
6. mix remaining 1 / 4 cup melted butter and crumbs and sprinkle on top
7. bake 1 hour
demonstrations.review: These potatoes were amazing!  I followed the recipe "as is" except I didn't add chives.  I loved the bacon in it.  I used the Kroger brand "Meals Made Simple" real bacon bits which come in a little package.  It was so easy to make and yet DELICIOUS!!!  I got many compliments on these potatoes.  Thanks Jenni Girl!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crunchy strawberry jello salad

nan

1. mix pretzels , melted butter and 3 tablespoons sugar in bowl
2. press into 13x9-inch pan and bake for 10 minutes at 350
3. cool
4. in medium bowl , blend cream cheese and 3 / 4 cup sugar , then add the prepared dream whip
5. pour on top of crust and chill
6. prepare jello as directed on package and partially set
7. add strawberries
8. pour over cream cheese mixture and chill until completely jelled
9. cut into squares
demonstrations.review: This recipe is absolutely delicious!  We serve it at most of our family parties.  I use Cool Whip instead of Dream Whip and it is wonderful.  Thank you!

target.recipe_text:
fluffy frosting

this has a lovely old-fashioned taste, and is sooooo easy to make.

1. in a saucepan , pour the corn syrup and bring it to a full boil
2. meanwhile , beat eggs whites with cream of tartar until they hold soft peaks
3. with the mixer still running on high , slowly add hot corn syrup in a slow , thin but steady stream
4. keep beating until frosting has stiff shiny peaks and hold their shape
5. beat in vanilla
6. this recipe makes a lot , so feel free to make only half for a small cake
7. keep frosted cake refrigerated when not serving
target.review: I made this frosting to use on a chocolate cake and together it tasted just like (a much better) Devil Dog.  This is super easy and not at all too sweet.  The consistency reminds me of marshmallow fluff.  Will definitely make again!  Thanks for posting!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
my best salad dressing

this recipe is an adaptation of two other old cookbook recipes. i think this experiment was a success. i hope you will enjoy it as much as my family does.

1. combine ingredients
2. mix well
3. enjoy over your favorite salad
demonstrations.review:
I just LOVE this dressing!  I had it last night and I'm making it again for tonight.  It's THAT good!

Why would anyone BUY dressing when there are recipes like this out there?!?

demonstrations.recipe_text:
extreme melt in your mouth steaks

not only are these these most delicious steaks they are so tender you can slice them with a butter knife! --- of coarse you may use any cut of steak desired, i prefer rib-eyes --- plan ahead the steaks needs to marinate for 6-24 hours and must be brought down to room temperature before cooking which may take a couple hours.

1. in a food processor combine all ingredients except the steaks
2. process until well blended
3. using a fork prick holes on both sides of the steaks , then place in a shallow glass baking dish or container
4. pour the marinade over steaks and turn to make certain that steaks are coated in the marinade
5. cover and refrigerate for 6-24 hours
6. a couple of hours before ready to grill remove the steaks from the fridge and the marinade , place on plates and let come down to room temperature
7. grill steaks until desired doneness
demonstrations.review: These are FANTASTIC!!  The rosemary's perfect!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
garlic hasselback potatoes with herbed sour cream

these potatoes smell amazing when they are roasting and have a wonderfully mild garlic flavor! from foodnetworktv.com courtesy of sunny anderson.

1. using a wooden spoon as a cradle , place each potato in the spoon and make several parallel slits into each potato top making sure not to slice completely through
2. place 3 garlic slices between slits at the crown of each potato
3. toss in a medium bowl with butter and olive oil
4. place on a baking sheet and sprinkle generously with salt and pepper
5. bake at 400 degrees until tops are crispy and potatoes are cooked through , about 1 hour
6. transfer to a platter and top with herbed sour cream
7. herbed sour cream
8. combine 1 / 2 cup sour cream , 1 / 2 teaspoon garlic powder , 1 tablespoon finely chopped parsley leaves , salt and freshly ground black pepper in a small bowl
9. refrigerate until use
demonstrations.review: Not only are they DELICIOUS, but so pretty, too!  I just love these!  They've become a staple.

target.recipe_text:
spiced apple slices for two

this from a southern living cookbook.  i've made it frequently when just my wife and i are home on the weekends.

1. arrange apple slices in a lightly greased 1-quart baking dish
2. combine remaining ingredients
3. pour over apple slices
4. bake at 350 degrees for 20 minutes
5. serve warm
target.review: Loved the way that the flour thickened up the "sauce".  I had to cook them longer than 20 minutes to get them soft enough--guess next time I'll have to slice the apples thinner.  Kids had fun making them for a challenge in ZWT4.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
greek baked shrimp with feta

this is a delicious recipe, and one i have enjoyed many times. it would make an excellent appetizer for entertaining as well as a great dinner idea!

1. preheat oven to 450 degrees
2. remove shells from shrimp , leaving last segment and tail intact
3. remove vein
4. rinse and dry
5. in a pan saute onion in oil until transparent , , add garlic and green onion and cook 2 minutes more
6. to the onions add the tomatoes , wine , half the parsley , oregano , and salt and pepper to taste
7. reduce heat , cover and simmer for 30 minutes until thickened
8. pour half the sauce into a shallow casserole , and arrange the shrimp on top
9. pour the rest of the sauce on , and sprinkle crumbled feta over the shrimp
10. bake at 450 degrees for 10-12 minutes or until prawns are pink and feta is lightly browned
11. garnish with remaining parsley and serve
demonstrations.review: Followed the recipe exactly using a chardonnay wine and canned diced tomatoes.  It was easy to do, and very tasty.  I think that dd alone ate over half a pound of shrimp.  Thanks for a keeper!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
irish pirate

this is from the food network website. i have not tried this yet- but i love the name of it!

1. put the milk , ice cream , mint extract and rum into a blender
2. blend on high until smooth , about 15 seconds
3. pour into 2 chilled glasses and garnish with a sprig of mint
demonstrations.review: I made this for the kids today, w/o the rum of course.  Just like drinking mint chocolate chip ice cream.  I think the rum would probably be nice to give it a more complex flavor.  But the kids adored it and want to give it 100 stars!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
easy beef and noodle dinner

i got this recipe from a pillsbury recipe magazine. my husband liked it, and scarfed it down, but i wasn't all that impressed, but not a big cooked tomato fan. you try it for yourself, and decide.

1. in 12-inch nonstick skillet , cook ground beef and onion over medium-high heat until beef is thoroughly cooked , stirring frequently
2. drain
3. add tomatoes , water , italian seasoning and contents of seasoning packet from soup mix
4. mix well
5. bring to a boil
6. break up noodles , stir in noodles and beans
7. return to a boil
8. reduce heat to low
9. cover and simmer 5 minutes or until noodles and beans are tender , stirring occasionally
demonstrations.review: We like this recipe.  It is nothing stellar, but it is quick and tasty.  We make it with some regularity on nights when we don't have much time to fix dinner.  And the kids like it too.

target.recipe_text:
kittencal s fried cabbage with bacon

this makes a wonderful side dish to pork or beef, you may omit the chili flakes if desired or adjust amount to suit taste

1. in a large skillet over medium heat cook the chopped bacon until crisp and browned
2. remove to a bowl or plate and set aside
3. add in onion
4. cook stirring until softened
5. add in cabbage and broth or water and sugar
6. cook stirring until the cabbage wilts season with salt and pepper towards the end of cooking
7. stir in the cooked bacon
target.review: This was very good. :) I will add it to my list of meals.  Very inexpensive and very tasty too.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
caramel cake frosting   icing

this recipe comes from my mennonite grandmother. an all-time favorite of hers  and mine! enjoy!

1. cook sugar and butter for two minutes
2. stir in 1 / 4 cup milk
3. bring to a boil
4. cool
5. stir in 10x sugar , until thick enough to spread
6. makes enough for 2 large cake layers
demonstrations.review: Very good. I used 1/2 cup brown and 1/2 cup white (I don't like the taste of  brown sugar). Yummy!!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
jiffy corn pudding

yum

1. mix all ingredients
2. grease 9x13-inch pan and pour in batter
3. dot with butter
4. bake at 350f for 45 minutes to 1 hour
5. cut in squares and serve
demonstrations.review: I used frozen instead of canned and i used 4 oz of sour cream and 1/4 cup heavy cream and it turned out just as good. It was gobbled (made it for thanksgiving) up fast.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
burgundy beef stroganoff

a family favourite. there's something very comforting about the rich, flavourful beef and tender egg noodles. leftovers are great too!

1. combine flour , salt , thyme and pepper in plastic bag
2. add meat and shake well
3. remove meat , shaking off excess flour
4. melt cup butter in large skillet over medium heat , add meat and brown lightly , about 3 minutes
5. add onion and stir until translucent , about 3 minutes
6. pour in broth and wine and simmer until meat is tender , about 30-45 minutes
7. melt 2 tblsps butter in small skillet over medium heat
8. add mushrooms and saut until just tender , 3-4 minutes
9. stir mushrooms into meat
10. blend sour cream , tomato paste and worcestershire sauce in small bowl
11. slowly turn into meat
12. do not allow to boil
13. mound noodles on serving platter
14. spoon meat over
15. top with parsley
demonstrations.review: Great and very tasty! Had to make a few substitutions because i had to use what was on hand.  I Used regular red wine, no sour cream, instead of tomato paste, I crushed 3 roma tomatoes.  It was very good and I will make this again.

target.recipe_text:
the best creole cajun seasoning mix

move over emeril!... you will never purchase creole or cajun seasoning again once you taste this one --- i have searched for the longest time to find the best seasoning blend, this is it! --- four tablespoons of seasoned salt will not be overly-salty if you prefer a more salty taste then add in some white salt --- this makes a fair amount of seasoning, just store in a tightly-sealed glass jar in the refrigerator to use in ground beef recipes, soups, or stews, homemade pasta sauce recipes, or use it to season roasts, chickens, pork, beef,  i use it on just about everything! if you like extreme spice then increase the cayenne up to 4-5 teaspoons. this makes a great gift for a spice-lover!

1. mix all ingredients in a glass jar
2. store in the refrigerator to keep the spices fresh
3. shake the jar before using
target.review: This was fabulous. I added 1-1/2 Tablespoons to 1 pound raw shrimp and a little olive oil, skewered them and BBQ'd them for 12 min. on med. hi.  Then I took 1/4 cup melted butter added 1/2 TBL seasoning and poured it over 2 cooked corn on the cob. So Flavourful - FABULOUS!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
best ever banana cake with cream cheese frosting

this is one of (if not) the best banana cake i have ever tasted! i thought the oven temp of 275° sounded a little low, but this cake baked up (and rose) beautifully in my oven at this temp after pretty much exactly one hour. i do not know if the little "freezer trick" to this recipe is what ensured its moistness or not, but i did it, and it was exceptionally moist & delicious. would be interesting to see if it still came out as great if this step was skipped. all i know is that i followed this recipe exactly as stated (except that i had no buttermilk, so i subbed with a mix of lemon juice & milk) and i got exceptional results. so moist and yummy...a dense cake, similar in texture to a carrot cake... i personally would not call this frosted banana bread :o)  depending on the amount of frosting you like you can decide whether to half the recipe or not. i used the full recipe and had some leftover. i sprinkled on the chopped walnuts and threw this baby in the fridge and cut it the next day...to die for! i really liked it slightly chilled, but great at room temp too! it got better each day it sat, i always make this cake at least the day before i need or want it.  i was extremely pleased with this cake and will be making it over & over again!! so glad i came across this one!! (on another website).


(* * just to update the recipe, (based on some of the reviews), the baking time may vary based on individual ovens. it was right on for my oven, but some others have stated it has taken 1 hour 10 minutes, 1 hour 20 minutes, and my sister just informed me that it took 1 hour 30 minutes in her oven!!!!!)

1. preheat oven to 275f
2. grease and flour a 9 x 13 pan
3. in a small bowl , mix mashed banana with the lemon juice
4. set aside
5. in a medium bowl , mix flour , baking soda and salt
6. set aside
7. in a large bowl , cream 3 / 4 cup butter and 2 1 / 8 cups sugar until light and fluffy
8. beat in eggs , one at a time , then stir in 2 tsp vanilla
9. beat in the flour mixture alternately with the buttermilk
10. stir in banana mixture
11. pour batter into prepared pan and bake in preheated oven for one hour or until toothpick inserted in center comes out clean
12. remove from oven and place directly into the freezer for 45 minutes
13. this will make the cake very moist
14. for the frosting , cream the butter and cream cheese until smooth
15. beat in 1 teaspoon vanilla
16. add icing sugar and beat on low speed until combined , then on high speed until frosting is smooth
17. spread on cooled cake
18. sprinkle chopped walnuts over top of the frosting , if desired
demonstrations.review: This is the best Banana cake I've ever had.Â  I've made it a dozen times now and everyone raves about it and wants the recipe.Â  The cooking time varies, I have 2 ovens and it's different with each one.Â  The toothpick check always works.Â  I have better compliments about the frosting when I use 1/3 less fat for some reason??? Oh, and I toast the walnuts.Â  Thanks for posting Rhonda *J*.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
creamy cajun chicken pasta

n'awlin's style of chicken with an updated alfredo sauce.

1. place chicken and cajun seasoning in a bowl and toss to coat
2. in a large skillet over medium heat , saut chicken in butter or margarine until chicken is tender , about 5 to 7 minutes
3. reduce heat add green onion , heavy cream , tomatoes , basil , salt , garlic powder , black pepper and heat through
4. pour over hot linguine and toss with parmesan cheese
demonstrations.review: Ok, this recipe RULES!!!  I used 1/2 n 1/2 and olive oil to cook chicken in and it was FANTASTIC.  Thanks for posting.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
smoky refried beans

once you've made your own beans you will never go back to the can. there simply is no substitute. they are quick, simple, and delicious.

1. heat oil in a heavy skillet over medium-low heat
2. add whole garlic cloves and cook , turning once , until browned on both sides , about 5 minutes
3. smash garlic cloves with a fork just enough to break them open and flatten them a little
4. add pintos and liquid and cook until heated through , about 5 minutes
5. add spices and salt to taste
6. stir well
7. turn the heat down to medium-low and smash beans with a big fork
8. you don't have to smash every single bean
9. leave some whole for texture
10. when mashed to your liking , squeeze the lime juice all over the beans and serve warm
11. these beans make a great taco filling or tostada topping
12. my husband likes them mixed with a little salsa and eaten as a dip
demonstrations.review: This couldn't of been easier and I will never buy a can of refried beans again.  Thanks for sharing!

target.recipe_text:
italian crock pot roast

the garlic in this dish actually sweetens with the long cooking time. thinly slice the roast, layer over wide egg noodles. ladle with the sauce and top with parmesan!

1. place veggies in crock pot
2. pierce beef , from top , 2" deep , eight times
3. shove a garlic clove half and parsley into each slit
4. add beef to pot
5. mix remaining ingredients and pour over top
6. cook on low heat for 8 hours
target.review: We thought this was fabulous.  My crockpot cooks hot so I cooked this on low for 4.5 hours and the meat was just falling apart.  I added mushrooms and minced garlic.  Served this over pasta and we were in heaven.  The smell while this is cooking is INSANE!  Enjoy!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
legal seafood style baked scallops

whenever we get back to the boston area, it's a priority to to have a meal at legal seafoods.  i recently "re-discovered" this recipe buried in old newspaper clippings. i had tried to recreate it in the past but now know i was missing the most important ingredient - buttermilk. i made it again after posting the recipe so i have edited the original description. it's even better than i remembered, you might want to try just a dash (or more) of cayenne pepper. it's delightful !

1. preheat oven to 400f
2. place scallops in a bowl , season with salt and pepper , add thyme and buttermilk and toss to coat
3. place scallops , with buttermilk , evenly in the bottom of an oven proof dish , sprinkle with cracker crumbs and top with melted butter
4. bake for 20 minutes , squeeze lemon over scallops and serve immediately
demonstrations.review: Really great!  I cut down on the crackers and the butter.  I used cayenne and garlic powder while mixing with the salt/pepper/buttermilk.  I drained the buttermilk, added them to the baking dish and sprinkled a bit more cayenne on the scallops.  I also added a splash of butter before and after the crackers and added lemon before the crackers as well.  SUPERB!  I cooked these about 10 minutes longer than the recipe stated and my family and I devoured them!!!!!  Thank you for a great one!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
rice with tomatoes  avocado   black olive

serve this pretty mixture of white rice studded with vibrant green, pale green, black and red either hot or cold. it goes very well with seafood.  from "the moroccan collection: traditional flavors from northern africa" by hilaire walden.

1. heat 2 tablespoons of the oil in a saucepan
2. add the onion and garlic and cook for 1 minute
3. add the rice and stir for 2 minutes , then add the stock and bring to a boil
4. stir the rice , then cover the pan and simmer very gently , without lifting the lid , for about 12 minutes , or until the rice is just tender
5. meanwhile , heat the remaining oil in a frying pan
6. add the tomato , green onions , parsley and salt and pepper and simmer for 5 minutes
7. remove the pan from the heat and stir in the olives and avocado
8. fluff up the rice with a fork and carefully stir in the tomato mixture
demonstrations.review: Very good rice dish.  The avocado makes it almost creamy in texture as it melts into the rice.  I followed the recipe closely (other than doubling the garlic and tomatoes).  I was also forced to use dried parsley rather than fresh.  Very taste side dish to recipe #235007 and #16719.  Will make this one again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
basmati italiano

nan

1. cook rice
2. put cooked basmati into large mixing bowl
3. toss hot rice with remaining ingredients using wooden spoons to avoid breaking grains
4. serve immediately
demonstrations.review: I really liked this dish but I changed things and may have messed it up.  I realized (after I'd diced all the ingredients) that I didn't have enough Basmati for the recipe.  I subbed long grain white rice and the end result was a bit dry and not super flavorful.  I added a lot of extra sun dried tomatoes and tripled the garlic and the end result was nice and cheesy.  Good flavor...maybe it would be perfect if I hadn't altered the rice, but nonetheless, the finished product was great!  I'll add stars to my review when I do it exactly as stated.

target.recipe_text:
snicker surprise peanut butter cookies

i found this recipe next to a snickers coupon. it is absolutely fabulous. the snickers is hidden inside the cookie so it makes for a nice surprise when you bite in. this cookie works perfectly as part of a xmas cookie platter. if you are a snickers fan, you are in for a real treat.

1. preheat oven to 300f
2. in a medium bowl , sift together flour , baking soda , and salt
3. in a large bowl , mix together butter , peanut butter , and sugars until light and fluffy
4. add eggs and vanilla and combine thoroughly
5. then mix in flour mixture
6. cover and chill dough 2-3 hours
7. to form cookie , scoop a tablespoon of chilled dough and flatten
8. place a miniature snickers in the center and form the dough into a ball around the snickers
9. place on a greased cookie sheet
10. bake for 10-20 minutes
11. cool cookies on a rack
12. optional: decorate cookies with powdered sugar or drizzled melted chocolate or both
target.review: I sent these to my grand daughter in VA and they loved them and requested the recipe!!! Thank you

demonstrations.recipe_text:
slow simmered spaghetti and meatballs  crock pot

this was one of those serendipitous happenings that continue to amaze/amuse me.  my ds called me on a wednesday evening around suppertime to ask if it would be alright to come visit for the weekend, bringing his boys.  they would arrive friday at suppertime.  since i knew that dd and her family would want to be included for dinner to give her more time to visit w/ her brother over the weekend... i suddenly went from "just me" for dinner to "eight" for dinner!  what to fix at the last minute like this???  a while later i was reading the paper and came across this recipe in the food section and thought:  ah ha!  dinner!  i bought the ingredients after work on thursday and, friday morning, everything went into the crock pot (i made a double batch).  when i got home after work, i made a salad, wrapped bakery italian bread in foil to heat in the oven, and started the water boiling for the spaghetti.  everyone loved it, as i did too, and the leftovers were scarfed up by the grand kids the next day for lunch.  age ranges of diners were 18 months up to ... well, let's just say i'm a grandmother of five!  this will definitely be a repeater at my house!  (recipe courtesy of b. mills & a. ross of "desperation dinners" column in the raleigh nc news & observer.)

1. pour spaghetti sauce and tomatoes with juice into a slow cooker
2. add chopped onion , garlic , and italian seasonings
3. mix well
4. add still-frozen meatballs
5. stirring to mix well
6. make sure meatballs are covered with sauce
7. cover the slow cooker , turn to low heat
8. cook 7-8 hours
9. just before serving , cook spaghetti according to package directions
10. serve sauce and meatballs over spaghetti
11. pass parmesan cheese at the table
12. the jar sizes may vary from brand to brand but this is okay
demonstrations.review: Made this for Christmas celebration and had a crockpot of spaghetti and a crockpot of sauce and meatballs with garlic bread and a salad. Was wonderful! Care free and was able to enjoy dinner too!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
something yummy for breakfast

this recipe is so good for a weekend breakfast!

1. unroll 1 can of crescent rolls in greased 9x13" pan
2. don't press seams together
3. mix cream cheese with 1 cup sugar , egg , and vanilla
4. spread over crescent rolls
5. cover with the next can of crescent rolls
6. pour stick of melted butter over top
7. top with mixture of 1 / 4 cup sugar , cinnamon , and nuts
8. bake at 350 degrees for 30-40 minutes
demonstrations.review: I made this for a brunch and it was wonderful. Thank you,

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mom s spicy hot dog sauce  crock pot

my mother-in-law gave me this recipe.  we absolutely love it!  i cook it for several hours in the crock pot, and i usually double or even triple it, because my family loves having the leftovers!

1. combine all ingredients in your crock pot
2. allow to cook at least 8 hours on low
3. i usually cook mine overnight , then even allow it to cook part of the day before turning it to warm
4. it can also be cooked on the stove , if you need it to get done sooner
5. in this case , you may want to leave the water out
6. enjoy on hot dogs or use as a sloppy joe filling !
7. i'm not sure about the serving amount below
demonstrations.review: I had a problem with it being to thin. So I doubled the ground beef and cooked it all night and all day. It had a very good taste. Clean up on the crock pot was time consuming. Thank you.

target.recipe_text:
yes  virginia there is a great meatloaf

absolutely delicious meatloaf and sauce! those who claim they don't believe there can be such a thing as a great meatloaf will love this. based on a meatloaf given to me by a dear friend, virginia strehl, memphis, and leesburg, fla. nita holleman, 2000

1. meatloaf: combine meat loaf ingredients and place into a loaf baking dish
2. smooth out top
3. sauce: combine sauce ingredients and pour on top and sides of meatloaf
4. bake at 350f about 1 hour to 1 hour 15 minutes or until done
5. enjoy !
6. the addition of 1 or 2 teaspoons of kitchen bouquet makes this recipe very good
7. recipe should be"plump" from the addition of the milk or half & half
8. it should not be runny
9. a second batch of sauce served hot is good to serve with the meatloaf
10. nita's
11. it is wise to have some fat added to the deer -- especially to ground deer
12. maybe 25 % fat , , otherwise your results will be poor
13. i don't know about some of the other game meat some are using
14. please consult an expert
15. the recipe is delicious as it stands ! enjoy ! nita holleman
target.review: This was a great Meatloaf recipe!!  I used ground Turkey and for the first time (thanks to this recipe) the turkey did not turn out dry!  I added some garlic powder, sage and a shot or two of Worcestershire sauce but otherwise followed the recipe to the tee and it was wonderful, thank you!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
real  italian bolognese sauce

after traveling throughout italy, savoring the fine tastes of bolognese from the many different regions, i decided to formulate my own. try it, you'll love it.

1. in a dutch oven or medium size pot , heat butter and olive oil over medium heat until butter begins to froth
2. add onion , celery , carrot , garlic , and bacon
3. cook until onions are translucent
4. remove bacon and remove fat
5. chop lean portions of bacon in small pieces and return to pot
6. add ground beef and ground pork , and cook until meat loses red , raw color
7. raise heat and add wine and consomme
8. cook sauce until wine and consomme are mostly evaporated
9. turn heat down to simmer and add oregano , salt , pepper , sage , red pepper flakes , and nutmeg
10. let cook for approximately 20 minutes
11. add crushed tomatoes and bring heat to a boil
12. once the mixture comes to a boil , return to simmer
13. let sauce simmer partially covered for about 2 to 4 hours , stirring occasionally to prevent sticking
14. about 5 to 10 minutes before serving , add milk
15. sauce can now be added to cooked penne pasta , spaghetti or many other pastas to your liking
16. remaining sauce may be frozen for up to two months for future use
demonstrations.review: What an awesome and easy recipe!  I forgot to add the garlic, but I don't think I missed it. I also used a "meatloaf" mix of ground beef, pork and veal.  The one step I messed up was the bacon.  I had cut the bacon before I put it in with the onion mix and then had to fish out the fatty pieces, oops! Nonetheless, it was an awesome recipe with outstanding flavor.  I will certainly be making this again!!!  Thanks for sharing!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
grilled herbed chicken thighs

this is my own recipe i dreamed up this summer. i've got an abundance of fresh herbs and wanted to try this out. turned out really good. i also use this mixture on grilled steaks. the amounts of the ingrediets are an estimate (i didn't measure anything out) so feel free to use your own judgment. hope ya like it.

1. starting with the herbs , mix all ingredients together into a rub mixture
2. rub mixture into chicken , under and on top of skin
3. set aside for an hour to let flavors soak into meat
4. leave longer if you have time
5. preheat your grill to hot
6. once the grill is heated , lower the grill temp to medium then grill on indirect heat with grill closed for 20-30 min or until juices run clear
demonstrations.review: What a wonderful and flavorful chicken thigh recipe! I didn't have fresh thyme but used dry and it wasy nice. Instead of garlic powder I used 3 cloves fresh pressed garlic. I did not use onion powder as I didn't have any, but it tasted great anyway. Instead of chili powder I used ground cayanne pepper as that's what I had on hand. I let it marinate for about 2 1/2 hours. I planned to grill it but it started raining so I broiled them instead. I preheated a broiler pan (sprayed with Pam for Grilling) in the oven and set to broil for about 5 minutes. I then added the chicken thighs skin side down and broiled about 8 inches from the coil and left the door ajar. After 15 minutes I turned the chicken and broiled for 15 minutes more. The skin crisped up very nicely was a nice alternative when I couldn't grill. Nice job Duch!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
easy chicken cordon bleu with mushroom sauce

this is a great dish to serve to guests. this is also one of my husband's favorite dishes and it is treat to serve it to him as well.

1. use a meat pounder to flatten the chicken breats
2. place 1 slice of ham and 1 slice of cheese in the center of each breast
3. roll up and place seam side down in a casserole dish
4. securing with a toothpick if necessary
5. bake , covered , for 20 minutes at 350 degrees or until the chicken is no longer pink and juices run clear
6. while it is baking , mix together remaining ingredients
7. pour over cooked chicken and bake until sauce bubbles
8. i usually serve this over egg noodles
demonstrations.review: This recipe was so yummy.  I had to make a few substitutions, such as I didn't have sour cream so I used non-fat plain yogurt and I didn't have sliced mushrooms so I omitted.  Other than that, I added some pepper and sage to the sauce and that added great flavor.  I increased the baking time to 25 minutes and cooked the sauce for about 15 minutes.  A very delicious meal, thank you Pamela!!

target.recipe_text:
oven fried chicken ii

nan

1. preheat oven to 450
2. combine all dry ingredients in a plastic bag
3. wash your chicken and shake off excess water
4. drop in bag and shake each piece
5. place in a metal pan skin side down and put in preheated oven
6. turn pieces over after about 20 minutes
7. continue baking until crisp and browned
target.review:
I used a family pack of drumsticks since they were on sale. Based on the other reviews, I used foil in my pan (I used 2 baking pans with sides because of so much chicken) and sprayed it with Pam butter spray. I  used 3/4 cup flour and doubled all the spice measurements cause I like spice. I turned it at 20 minutes then cooked another 20 minutes. Thermometer said it was done. Taste and texture of fried chicken without all the grease.

I served it with mashed potatoes and green beans that were seasoned with paprika.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
turkey soup with egg  noodles and vegetables

i was looking for a way to use up some leftover turkey - lo and behold i came up with this wonderful soup from the food network on quick fix meals with robin miller.  seeing as the holidays are right around the corner and there will be plenty of leftover turkey in our kitchens, i thought i would share my new found treasure with you ;) this recipe is super easy and tastes great!  your family will never know they are eating leftovers. i hope you enjoy this recipe as much as i did.

1. heat oil in a large stock pot or dutch oven over medium heat
2. add leeks , carrots , garlic , and celery
3. saute 4 minutes , or until soft
4. add turkey , bay leaves , thyme , salt and black pepper
5. stir to mix well
6. add chicken broth and bring mixture to a boil
7. reduce heat to medium-low , partially cover and simmer 10 minutes
8. return mixture to a boil and add egg noodles
9. cook 10 minutes , until egg noodles are just tender
10. stir in peas and cook until peas are just heated through , about 1 minute
11. remove from heat , discard bay leaves and stir in parsley
12. serves 4-6
demonstrations.review: Fantastic! I kicked up the pepper and did a bit of cayenne pepper. Also used onions instead of leeks cause I did all this with what I had on hand. Used up carrots, celery, leftover turkey, etc. Thank you for posting this!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
creamy spaghetti pie

i went to a pampered chef party where this was served. many people asked for the recipe! update: i have revised this recipe due to people having trouble with the instructions. i hope this makes it easier to follow.

1. save out 1 / 4 cup of the parmesan cheese and 1 / 4 cup shredded mozzarella cheese
2. set aside
3. mix together green onions , garlic , chopped parsley , 1 / 2 cup parmesan cheese , ricotta cheese , egg , butter , salt , italian seasoning , and 3 / 4 cup mozzarella cheese
4. mix cheese / egg mixture with cooked spaghetti and place on the bottom of a shallow casserole dish
5. in a bowl , mix spaghetti sauce with tomatoes
6. pour over spaghetti mixture
7. sprinkle with remaining 1 / 4 cup parmesan cheese and 1 / 4 cup mozzarella cheese that was set aside
8. bake about 30 minutes at 350 degrees
9. after pulling out of oven , garnish pie with chopped parsley
10. serve and enjoy !
11. pie will feel firm to the touch
12. enjoy !
demonstrations.review: I did as is, without the butter. It was too runny for me. Maybe if I had let it rest for a while after taking it out of the oven? The taste was ok but I wanted a little more oomph. I wish I could have fit it in my pie pan but it was too much so it went in a rectangular casserole dish. I was hoping for a firm pie slice with layers.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
braised balsamic chicken

received from a friend.

1. season chicken breasts with ground black pepper and garlic salt
2. heat olive oil in a medium skillet , and brown the onion and seasoned chicken breasts
3. pour tomatoes and balsamic vinegar over chicken , and season with basil , oregano , rosemary and thyme
4. simmer until chicken is no longer pink and the juices run clear , about 15 minutes
demonstrations.review: I enjoyed it. Smelled heavenly as it cooked. The other eater didn't care for it cause it was too vinegar-y. I love vinegar and didn't think it was too vinegar-y. I thought it was very herb-y. In order to make sure the herbs blended well, I used a large measuring cup to measure the vinegar, added the tomatoes to the cup, and then the herbs. I mixed it together in the cup and added that to the onions and chicken in the pan. Instead of garlic salt, I used garlic powder and salt since I didn't have garlic salt. I cooked the chicken over medium and they took a little longer than 15 minutes. This caused the sauce to reduce down which reminds me that the quality of the balsamic is very important.

target.recipe_text:
to die for crock pot roast

amazing flavor, and so simple! no salt needed here. in fact, you may wish to use half the ranch dressing mix to cut back on the saltiness. found this crock-pot pot roast recipe on of a website called www.recipegoldmine.com. it's all the rage there, so i thought i'd try it.

1. place beef roast in crock pot
2. mix the dried mixes together in a bowl and sprinkle over the roast
3. pour the water around the roast
4. cook on low for 7-9 hours
5. use onion soup mix instead of ranch
6. add one cup , of red wine
7. add potatoes , carrots , mushrooms , celery and onion 2-3 hours before end
target.review: After all the great reviews, decided to try this recipe.  Used a good roast but should have used a cheaper one.  This turned out to be a mushy potroast.  Cannot see how anyone can use leftovers in a sandwich.  Great recipe for anyone who has a hard time chewing.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
grilled chicken wings

the marinade is simply wonderful and so easy. if you bite into one of these hot off the grill the rest may not make it into the house! make extras because the kids will eat them cold the next day. i marinated the wings for 6 hours to overnight.  i also use 1 tablespoon of fresh ginger finely grated instead of ground ginger.

1. cut the chicken wings into three pieces and discard
2. mix remaining ingredients into a bowl
3. add wings and stir
4. cover and marinate for 45 minutes
5. place pieces on the grill and brush with remaining mixture
6. grill over medium-hot coals about 15-20 minutes , turning once
demonstrations.review: Made this tonight for 20 sailing instructors for a dinner ages 16 - 20.  Also served ribs, homemade bread & 2 pasta dishes.  I marinated the wings overnight & made as directed.  "Kids" came back for seconds for the pasta, ribs & bread.  No more takers for the wings.  Also made 2 homemade desserts ~ brownies & cupcakes.  The only leftovers was 1/2 the wings & 1 rib.  I saved the rib but thru the wings out.  Will not make these wings again.  Not a hit.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cheesy mostaccioli

this recipe is from an old pampered chef cookbook. simple and something my kids will eat. freezes well. see note for oamc instructions.

1. prepare the pasta according to the package directions
2. rinse and drain
3. in a non-stick skillet , cook and stir the beef over medium-high heat until meat is browned
4. drain
5. add in spaghetti sauce , soup , pepper , and italian seasoning
6. stir to combine
7. in a large bowl , mix together the pasta , sauce , and 2 cups cheese
8. transfer mixture to a greased 4-quart baking dish
9. sprinkle remaining 1 cup cheese over the top
10. bake at 350 for 40 minutes or until heated through
11. seal with foil or place in a zip top bag
12. freeze
13. to serve: thaw in fridge overnight
14. bake as directed
demonstrations.review: Made this tonight for superbowl.  Excellent!  Since I did not know what time people would feel like eating, I also placed in crockpot.  I cooked it on high for about 1 hr & then switched to low.  Even though I did not watch the game myself, I knew when the commercials were on.  That was when people were returning to the crockpot for 2nds or 3rds.  Everyone loved it!  Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
overnight french toast casserole

great make-ahead breakfast casserole.

1. melt margarine in a 9 x 13 baking pan
2. put 6 slices of bread in bottom of pan
3. in a bowl mix 1 cup brown sugar with 1 tsp cinnamon
4. sprinkle 1 / 2 of this sugar mixture over bread
5. add another layer of 6 slices of bread
6. in a bowl , whisk eggs with milk until well blended
7. pour over bread layers
8. sprinkle with remaining sugar mixture
9. cover and refrigerate overnight
10. bake covered at 350f 30 minutes
