11. uncover and continue baking 15 minutes or until set and browned
demonstrations.review:
Great Christmas breakfast!  So easy to make & bake it while opening presents.  I've been making this for Christmas the last 3 to 4 years.  I have 5 children  (youngest are now 18 yr old twins ~ oldest is 29 & will be bringing his bride to be)

Last year I had 1 request asking if I will be making this for Christmas morn.  This year I've had 2 requests from my children asking if I'll  be making it again for Christmas morning.

This recipe has become a Christmas tradition  with our family.  

Only changes I've used over the years is to make it with 5 eggs & only 2/3 c. brown sugar

Happy Holidays to all

target.recipe_text:
baked macaroni and cheese with stewed tomatoes

boy, does this bring back memories! when i was in high school, they served this every friday in the cafeteria. i guess they had to make sure we had our vegetables :) it sounds gross, but i couldn't wait until fridays, the macaroni and tomatoes were so good together. to this day, almost 20 years later, whenever i have baked macaroni & cheese, i crave stewed tomatoes. with this recipe, i don't have to.

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees
2. cook macaroni according to package directions and drain , rinse and set aside
3. in a large saucepan , over medium heat , heat the 3 cups of milk , butter , salt and pepper until hot but not boiling
4. in a small bowl or cup , combine 1 / 4 cup of milk with the cornstarch and stir until dissolved
5. slowly add this to the hot milk mixture , stirring constantly with a whisk
6. when mixture has thickened , remove from heat and stir in 2 cups of the cheese until melted
7. pour pasta into a large mixing bowl and add the cheese mixture and the stewed tomatoes
8. mix well until macaroni is well coated
9. pour into a greased 9 x 13 baking dish or 3 quart casserole and top with remaining cheese
10. bake for 35 to 45 , or until golden brown
target.review: This was good! I'd never made (or had) BAKED macaroni before so I have nothing to compare it to. My dad said it was the best mac&cheese he'd ever had. (He rarely eats it though, but still! High praise) Next time I will make sure to cut up the tomato because my family wasn't crazy about big chunks. Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crock pot chicken with black beans   cream cheese

i love this crock-pot chicken recipe for two reasons: one, my family loves it and two, it is so easy to make! i got this recipe from my sister. she has two children of her own, and they love it too! it's also the best leftovers in the world -- if there are any!

1. take 4-5 frozen , yes , frozen , boneless chicken breasts put into crock pot
2. add 1 can of black beans , drained , 1 jar of salsa , 1 can of corn drained
3. keep in crock pot on high for about 4-5 hours or until chicken is cooked
4. add 1 package of cream cheese and let sit for about 1 / 2 hour
5. all done and enjoy !
demonstrations.review:
I made this a few months ago in the summer. It was super easy to make, just throw everything in and you're set! I used half sour cream and half cream cheese like I read some people suggested.
I did stir it up a little before I served it; someone in my family remarked that it looked like puke. :S But it still tasted pretty good and was very easy! It was also great as leftovers the next day with flour tortillas

demonstrations.recipe_text:
vegetarian blt

not what you think: no fake bacon in this one!!  even the biggest meat-eaters go for this one.  seriously very very good!!

1. spray a non-stick skillet with plenty of non-stick spray and place the cheese in a single layer in the center
2. heat the skillet over medium heat
3. when the cheese bubbles and is crunchy and hard on the bottom , flip to the other side
4. once both sides of the cheese are crunchy , assemble the sandwich with the lettuce , tomato , and "bacon" , and the mayo spread over the bread
5. enjoy !
demonstrations.review: Okay, I love this fried cheese idea. And I love that I can eat my vegetarian BLT while the rest of my family has the "real thing." This was crispy and good. Thanks

demonstrations.recipe_text:
fannie farmer s classic baked macaroni   cheese

to me fannie farmer's recipe is the only "real" macaroni & cheese. it's from my 1946 edition of "fannie farmer's boston cooking school cookbook". with time on it's side - this recipe is hands down the best for traditional, homemade baked macaroni & cheese - comfort food.

please note: if you use cheap cheese you will end up with a bland and flavorless dish!

1. preheat oven to 400f
2. cook and drain macaroni according to package directions
3. set aside
4. in a large saucepan melt butter
5. add flour mixed with salt and pepper , using a whisk to stir until well blended
6. pour milk and cream in gradually
7. stirring constantly
8. bring to boiling point and boil 2 minutes
9. reduce heat and cook 10 minutes
10. add shredded cheddar little by little and simmer an additional 5 minutes , or until cheese melts
11. turn off flame
12. add macaroni to the saucepan and toss to coat with the cheese sauce
13. transfer macaroni to a buttered baking dish
14. sprinkle with breadcrumbs
15. bake 20 minutes until the top is golden brown
16. (you can also freeze this recipe in zip-lock bags for later use - once you have mixed the macaroni along with the cheese sauce allow to cool to room temperature before adding to your freezer - i generally pull it out the night before and allow macaroni and cheese to reach room temperature
17. i then add the macaroni and cheese to a buttered baking dish , sprinkle with bread crumbs and then bake for 20 to 30 minutes , until golden brown on top and bubbling
demonstrations.review: After reading all these rave reviews I thought this dish would be phenomenal! It WAS good, but I thought it was a little "blah." Maybe I'll have to add some spices to kick it up a little if I make it again.

target.recipe_text:
oatmeal banana bread

this healthy banana bread is high is fibre and low in fat, sugar and sodium. it is an excellent breakfast for your whole family.

1. heat oven to 150c lightly greased a 9x5x4 inch loaf pan with cooking spray
2. in medium bowl , combine oats and milk
3. mix well
4. let stand 10 minutes
5. stir in bananas , egg white and oil until blended
6. in large bowl , combine flour , sugar , baking powder , cinnamon and baking soda
7. mix well
8. add oat mixture to dry ingredients all at once
9. stir just until dry ingredients are moistened
10. pour batter into pan
11. bake for 25 to 30 minutes or until wooden pick inserted in center comes out clean
12. cool in pan on wire rack 10 minutes
13. remove from pan
14. cool completely
target.review:
This bread was pretty good. I like the addition of the oatmeal which makes it healthier. If I were to make it again, I think I would add a little more sugar and more spices. It could have been a little more flavorful. The fact that it is so healthy makes it a keeper (with a bit of tweeking)The cooking time needs to be adjusted also. I made 3 mini loaves and the 30 minutes in a 350' oven wasn't quite enough time.
Overall a good recipe

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crisp garlic potato skins

yummy low-fat, low-sodium appetizer.

1. one day or several hours ahead , prick potatoes with a fork
2. bake in a 425 f oven for 40 to 50 minutes or till tender
3. cool , wrap and store in refrigerator
4. at serving time , cut baking potatoes into quarters
5. scoop out the insides , leaving -inch thick shells
6. lightly brush both sides of potato skins with olive oil
7. place , cut side up , on a large baking sheet
8. bake at 425 f for about 15 minutes or until they are crisp
9. meanwhile , in a small bowl combine the chopped tomatoes , basil , and garlic powder
10. spoon some of the tomato mixture into each potato quarter
11. sprinkle with parmesan cheese , and bake for 2 to 3 minutes longer until heated through
demonstrations.review: Very yummy recipe. I had some left-over crumbled bacon and mixed it in with the tomatoes. A great way to use those summer tomatoes.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
ground turkey tomato sauce

1/2 cup servings

1. brown ground turkey with chopped onions until meat is no longer pink , and juices run clear
2. drain the excess juice
3. mix remaining ingredients in a crock pot and stir well
4. add turkey and onions to mixture and stir again
5. simmer in covered crock pot on low for approx 6 hours , stirring occasionally
demonstrations.review: I made this sauce today. It's very good. I only made half the recipe, and forgot that when I added the spices (but extra spices are good!) I did put the correct amount of sugar and cayenne. Very thick and hearty sauce. A good freezer recipe, but you would have to have a very big crock pot for this whole recipe. I made half and I only had 1 or 2 inches space left in my 4 quart crock pot.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
lazy stuffed cabbage casserole

we love stuffed cabbage, but it takes quite a bit of time to prepare, my mom gave me this delicious casserole and it sure is one of our favorites.

1. mix chopped beef , rice , onion , butter , and egg
2. salt and pepper to taste
3. grease 3 quart casserole
4. line bottom of casserole with 1 / 2 cabbage
5. add 1 / 2 meat mixture
6. top with rest of cabbage , then rest of meat mixture
7. top with chopped tomatoes or tomato sauce
8. cover , bake at 350 degrees for 1 hour
9. uncover and bake an additional 30 minutes
10. tastes just like stuffed cabbage without all the work
demonstrations.review: I haven't made stuffed cabbage in a long time because it's so much work, so this was perfect. I partially browned the meat and also added a bit of brown sugar and allspice to the mixture. I agree that it could use more sauce. I combined a pint jar of canned tomatoes and a 8 oz can of sauce and I think I would have liked even more, but it was still delicious. We also sprinkled a little parmesan cheese on our servings...yum. This recipe is definitely a keeper!

target.recipe_text:
ground beef gyros

this is a great summer meal and quick and easy to put together and tastes wonderful. refreshing served with the cucumber sauce and is even low in fat. i think this came from quick cooking. it's a favorite in our house.

1. in a bowl , combine first 5 ingredients
2. cover and refrigerate
3. in separate bowl , combine ground beef and seasonings
4. mix well
5. shape into 4 patties
6. grill , covered , over medium to high heat for 10 to 12 minutes or until meat is no longer pink , turning once
7. cut patties into thin slices
8. stuff into pitas
9. add lettuce , cucumber , tomato , and onion
10. serve with yogurt sauce
target.review: It was very good.  I baked in the oven cause it was to cold out to grill.  4 stars only because it lacked a bit in flavor.  Extra seasoning to the meat would help  Def will make it again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
jalapeo bites

these are a bit reminiscent of stuffed jalapeño peppers but much easier to make. i found this in the junior league celebrations cookbook.

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. combine the cream cheese , parmesan , jalapeo peppers and egg yolks in a bowl and mix to form a paste
3. shape a 1 / 2 tablespoonful at a time into 1 / 4-inch rounds and roll in the bread crumbs
4. place on an ungreased baking sheet and bake for 10-15 minutes or until golden brown
5. serve warm
demonstrations.review: These are great!!  Can't go to any party without these.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crock pot whole chicken

tender, fall-off-the-bone chicken! skip the overnight refrigeration if you are in a hurry. for variety, eliminate the onion and substitute a quartered lemon or two, stuffed into the chicken cavity.  chef shapeweaver had a good suggestion:  use fajita seasoning mix #28011 as another variation.  thanks!  the standard size slow cookers are a bit too small and a whole chicken won't fit.  you'll need a 6-quart slow cooker for this recipe.

1. in a small bowl , combine the spices
2. remove any giblets from chicken and clean chicken
3. rub spice mixture onto the chicken
4. place in resealable plastic bag and refrigerate overnight
5. when ready to cook , put chopped onion in bottom of crock pot
6. add chicken
7. no liquid is needed , the chicken will make its own juices
8. cook on low 4-8 hours
demonstrations.review: Loved it!!  Super moist, flavorful, and fall off the bone.  Plus it is very easy

demonstrations.recipe_text:
gumbo

this is originally a shrimp gumbo recipe, but it's gumbo, so you can add whatever turns you on. i always eat it with more than just a few dashes of tabasco. i hope you like it.

1. in a large stockpot combine oil and flour and cook over medium-high heat about 15 minutes or until it turns very dark brown , almost between brown and black
2. you will have to stir almost constantly
3. this is called the roux
4. add onions , parsley , celery , bell peppers , scallions and garlic and cook about 10 more minutes or until vegetables are tender , stirring regularly
5. add broth , salt , and creole seasoning
6. cover pot and simmer 15 minutes stirring occasionally
7. add your chosen combination of meat at this point and simmer an additional 10 minutes
8. ladle over steamed white rice
demonstrations.review: It did not turn out good for me.  It had an awful taste to it.  I followed the recipe as listed and did not change a thing.  Once I added the veggies it took on an off stir fry smell and the taste did not improve after that.

target.recipe_text:
kittencal s moist cheddar garlic oven fried chicken breast

this is for serious garlic lovers. the chicken bakes out so moist and tender! grated cheese may be sprinkled on top of the breast the last 5 minutes of cooking if desired but that is optional. double all ingredients for more than four breasts and adjust the amount of garlic to suit taste. for the coating amount you might be able to get away with 5 or maybe 6 very small chicken breasts, but i would suggest to increase the amount slightly --- to take this dish to yet another level, about 10 minutes before the cooking time is finished, drizzle the top of the chicken with a little pasta sauce, then sprinkle mozzarella cheese on top. return to oven for about 10 minutes until the chicken is completely cooked and sauce is hot and cheese has melted. for a lemon-garlic flavor add in 3 tablespoons lemon juice to the melted butter/garlic mixture ---  *note* for a healthier alternative smart balance butter blend may be used in place of the melted butter --- you will love this chicken!
visit my food blog, www.kittencalskitchen.com, for more of my recipes.

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. butter an 11 x 7-inch pan
3. in a bowl , combine melted butter with fresh minced garlic , 1 teaspoon garlic powder and salt
4. in another bowl , combine the dry breadcrumbs with 1 / 2 cup finely grated cheddar cheese , parmesan cheese 1 teaspoon garlic powder and coarse ground black pepper
5. dip chicken in butter mixture
6. then in crumb mixture
7. place in prepared pan and bake uncovered for 35-45 minutes or until cooked through , larger breasts may take more time
8. top with shredded cheddar or mozzarella the last 5 minutes of cooking (this is only optional
target.review: Great chicken :) Definitely being added as a favorite recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
oatmeal waffles or pancakes

these waffles are great for someone who needs more fiber or who is trying to lower their cholesterol. they're tasty, too.

1. mix well together
2. there should be no lumps
3. bake in a waffle iron , or like regular pancakes
4. variation: add 1 / 2 cup finely chopped apple and 1 / 2 teaspoon cinnamon
demonstrations.review: Delicious! I have made these in both the pancake and waffle format and both have been tasty. I used quick oats because I had them which made for a really thick batter. I would suggest adding a little more liquid in this case to make up for the density of the quick oats (or adding a little less oats). Thanks for sharing!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
homemade hamburger buns  bread machine

you will never want to buy hamburger buns again after trying this recipe. easy to do using a bread machine and so awesome! you can also top rolls with sesame seeds after brushing with melted butter.

1. place all ingredients , except butter , in pan of bread machine according to manufacturer's directions
2. select dough setting
3. when cycle is complete , turn out onto floured surface
4. cut dough in half and roll each half out to a 1" thick circle
5. cut each half into six 3 1 / 2" rounds with inverted glass as a cutter
6. place on greased baking sheet far apart and brush with melted butter
7. cover and let rise until doubled , about one hour
8. bake at 350 for 9 minutes
9. some reviewers baked these anywhere from 12 to 30 minutes
demonstrations.review: Fantastic buns! I made these along with homemade hamburger patties and they were amazing. I love the sweetness of them and will be using the recipe to make some rolls for dinner tonight. Thanks for the recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pete s scratch pancakes

it was the fall of 1987 when pete nyhus walked into our office, just to visit. we started talking about breakfast, and he reached into a wastepaper basket and pulled out a scrap of teletype paper. he wrote out this recipe, and my family has never used pre-mix since.

1. mix the dry items first
2. combine the eggs and melted butter to the milk and slowly stir into the flour mixture
3. let sit at least 10 minutes while heating the pan
4. these will be high , but light and fluffy --
demonstrations.review: I have been making these for a few years now and they are delicious every time. Thanks for sharing!

target.recipe_text:
caramel chocolate bars

found my old recipe box and this one was in it. can't even remember who the mcp was that gave me the recipe any more, but it sounds wonderful and she says that is is very easy.

1. preheat oven to 350
2. cream brown sugar and margarine
3. add dry ingredients reserving 3 tbsp of flour and stir in the oatmeal
4. press 1 / 2 of the mixture in the bottom of a greased 9 x 13 pan and bake for 10 minutes
5. sprinkle chocolate chips over crust
6. mix caramel topping with the reserved flour
7. drizzle this over the chips
8. sprinkle the top with the remaining crumb mixture
9. bake for an additional 15 minutes
target.review: Yummy!!!  Definitely cook it longer than 15 minutes at the end.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crock pot chicken vindaloo

for the vegetarian version: use your favorite veggies, omit the cinnamon stick. this is my sister's recipe (thank you najla! xoxo), she made it on the stove top. it's really yummy!!

1. puree first 10 ingredients in a blender
2. pour into the crock pot , add tomato sauce , cinnamon stick and onion and mix well
3. add chicken and turn to cover
4. cook on low for 5 hours
5. sprinkle with chopped parsley before serving
6. serve with rice or rolls , enjoy !
demonstrations.review: I made this for a bunch of international students at our local college and it was a big hit!  Don't worry about getting the exact measurements.  As with any stew-type recipe, add what you want and have fun with it!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
soft  spicy  heavenly ginger cookies

i found the original recipe for these cookies on allrecipes.com, and modified it to be vegan, as well as by changing the spices slightly. they are truly delicious cookies, and very easy to make.

1. in a large bowl , cream together the margarine and 1 cup sugar until light and fluffy
2. stir in the molasses
3. mix the water and baking soda and stir
4. sift together the flour , salt , and dry spices
5. add gradually to the sugar-margarine mixture
6. gradually stir the sifted ingredients , along with the ginger and raisins , into the molasses mixture
7. shape dough into walnut sized balls , and roll them in the remaining 2 tablespoons of sugar
8. place the cookies 2 inches apart onto an ungreased cookie sheet , and flatten slightly
9. bake at 350f for 10-12 minutes
demonstrations.review: These cookies were sooo good.  Ditto to all of the other comments!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pumpkin cake bars with cream cheese frosting

i love pumpkin bars all year long, and these ones take the cake! moist, delicious, and perfect everytime. everyone asks for the recipe after they've tried them!

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. grease and flour one glass 9 x 13 inch pan
3. in a mixing bowl , beat together the eggs , sugar , oil and pumpkin
4. sift together the flour , baking powder , salt , baking soda , salt and cinnamon
5. add to wet ingredients and mix thoroughly
6. spread into prepared pan
7. bake at 350 for 25 to 30 minutes
8. remove from oven and allow to cool
9. for the frosting: beat together the cream cheese , butter and confectioner's sugar
10. evenly spread over bars after they have cooled
demonstrations.review: Awesome awesome awesome... not much more I can say!  Thanks for posting.

target.recipe_text:
runza

anyone from nebraska should know this recipe. i got this particular one from the minnesotans for nebraska website. if you don't know what a runza is, i suggest you either get on the next plane to nebraska or make this recipe! prep time differs on how you make your bread.

1. thaw two loaves of frozen bread dough or make the equivalent amount using your favorite bread recipe
2. while dough thaws , make the filling
3. brown the hamburger and drain , then return to pan
4. add cabbage and onion and cook down
5. salt and pepper to taste
6. let dough rise , then punch down and roll a portion to 1 / 4" thickness
7. cut into 4" x 8" pieces and add about 1 / 2 cup meat mixture to each
8. fold dough pieces over and seal the edges , then place seam-side-down on a greased cookie sheet
9. let rise 20-30 minutes , then bake in pre-heated 375 degree oven for 20 minutes or until brown
10. call nebraska natives not in attendance and gloat
target.review: Yummy!  I used my everyday whole wheat potato bread dough, and boy were these good.  Can't wait to share them with all my Pennsylvania friends.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crock pot shredded chicken breasts for freezing   oamc

great to have on-hand for recipes. just place as many chicken breasts as you can fit into your crock pot as long as the lid fits on properly. i use bone-in, skin-on but i'm sure boneless, skinless would work too.

1. place the chicken breasts in the crock pot , mix water and spices together and pour over the chicken
2. cook on the low setting for 8-10 hours
3. remove chicken breasts , shred or pull the meat from bones , removing skin
4. place meat in individual freezer bags or containers and freeze until needed for recipes
5. defrost and add to any recipes that call for cooked chicken
6. great for casseroles , quesadillas , pizzas , burritos , pastas , soups , etc
7. or heat with bbq sauce for hot barbecue chicken sandwiches
demonstrations.review: I've made this a couple of times now with boneless skinless breasts (which makes the shredding/bagging so easy), also to freeze in preparation for a soon-to-arrive baby.  And I love that my latest Cooking Light has more than one recipe calling for shredded rotisserie chicken breast.  This is so much easier than picking the meat off a bird, not to mention less expensive!  Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
tzatziki cucumber dipping sauce

greek sauce/dip/salad dressing. serve with vegies,pitas,or with spicy dishes.

1. line a sieve with a double thickness of dampened cheesecloth
2. spoon in yogurt and set the sieve over a bowl
3. refrigerate for two to three hours or until yogurt is about half its volume , nicely thick and creamy
4. shred or cut cucumber into julienne strips
5. place in a colander in sink or over a bowl , sprinkle generously with salt , mix well and let drain for at least 30 minutes to an hour
6. rinse and gently pat dry
7. in a mortor and pestal muddle the garlic into a bit salt
8. add to the thickened yogurt , cucumber , lemon juice , olive oil , and if desired , the pepper and mint
9. mix well
10. serve or refrigerate for a day or two so flavors mingle
11. stir again before serving and sprinkle with additional minced mint leaves if desired
demonstrations.review: Thank you!  I first made this last summer when we had an abundance of cucumbers and  I loved it so much I forwarded the recipe to friends and family, but am just now getting around to reviewing it after getting a pregnancy craving for it the other day and making it again.  I'm not a huge fan of either cucumbers or plain yogurt, but something truly magical happens to the combination of ingredients in this recipes.  Plus it's such an incredibly healthy craving that I don't have to worry about giving in.  Four thumbs up from me and the baby!  Oh, and thank you to the other reviewer who suggested using coffee filters to drain the yogurt.  Brilliant!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
wholesome spelt waffles

these spelt waffles are divine! they are light, airy and crisp. the perfect platform for pure maple syrup. plus the spelt offers a wondrously nutty essence, that you just don’t get with plain old flour. the beauty is, these are my families favorite waffles. they don’t miss the white-processed flour. they don’t miss the handful of white sugar; and they don’t miss the additional 1/4 cup of oil that i took out!
so you can eat your waffles on saturday morning, without an ounce of guilt, and still have dessert saturday night!

1. preheat your waffle iron
2. mix the dry ingredients on a large bowl
3. then whisk in all the wet ingredientuntil smooth
4. scoop the batter onto the waffle iron and close
5. cook for 2-5 minutes , then repeat
6. make 12- 4 inch waffles
demonstrations.review: Thanks for posting!  These are great - very light.  I did add a couple tablespoons of sugar and a teaspoon or two of vanilla, just my personal preferences.  In my parents old 4-square waffle iron I actually got 20 4-in square waffles, but that's great since I was making them to freeze as toaster waffles for my toddler, who considers waffles with honey quite a delicacy. :)

target.recipe_text:
impossible peanut butter cookies

these are the quickest, simplest peanut butter cookies that you will ever make and they taste great!

1. mix peanut butter , sugar , and egg together until smooth
2. drop by teaspoon onto cookie sheet two inches apart
3. if desired , roll in extra sugar before placing on cookie sheet
4. press with fork
5. press again in opposite direction
6. bake 10 to 12 minutes at 350 degrees fahrenheit
7. do not brown
8. do not over bake
target.review: I've been making this same recipe for over 20 years and it's the only p-nut butter cookie I make. The only difference in mine is that I add 1 tsp. of Vanilla extract. If you like a softer cookie you can throw some in a zipper bag with a slice of bread and they get nice and chewy.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
allegheny applesauce bread

scrumptiously moist and delicious, sweet and spicy, simple and wholesome: contains no refined grains or sugars, just lots of good stuff like raisins, honey, and wheat germ. you've got to try this bread!

1. beat butter and honey together in mixing bowl
2. add eggs , applesauce , and maple extract and beat well
3. combine next six ingredients in separate bowl
4. stir in raisins
5. add dry ingredients to butter mixture , stirring until combined
6. bake in greased 5x9 loaf pan at 350 degrees for 55-60 minutes , or until tests done
7. cool in pan for 30 minutes , then remove from pan and cool completely on wire rack
8. wrap in plastic wrap and chill overnight before serving
9. this bread freezes well , so double the recipe and save one for later !
demonstrations.review: This recipe sounded really good, but I have to say I was disappointed in the result. My family didn't care for this bread. Although the texture was great and it was very moist and looked great, the taste was just so so. I had hoped it would have more apple taste. All I could taste was the wheat germ and the whole wheat flour. It had quite a bland taste to me. It needs something, I just can't put my finger on it though. As another reviewer mentioned, it needs more of a spice kick.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mom s caramel rolls

here is a recipe that i remember the most about my mom's baking. she has it committed to memory. i am glad i did get it out of her. it is a very easy recipe to make. i hope your family gets as much enjoyment out of it as mine does.

1. mix water and yeast and wait 5 minutes
2. stir in sugar , salt and 2 cups of flour
3. add egg and butter and mix
4. stir in rest of flour by hand , if dough is still sticky add just enough to make it not sticky anymore
5. let raise until dough is double in size
6. sprinkle flour on surface and roll dough out until is approx 18 x 12 inches
7. spread a very thin layer of soft butter on dough and sprinkle cinnamon / sugar mixture on it
8. roll dough from the long side , it should look like a log
9. cut into 1 inch pieces
10. should be 18 pieces
11. place brown sugar and butter into microwave dish and heat until butter is just melted
12. stir well
13. stir in 3 t water
14. divide mixture into 3 pans
15. place 6 pieces in each pan
16. let raise for about 45 minutes
17. bake for 20 minutes in a 325f oven
18. when you take out of oven , turn each pan of rolls over on a plate , otherwise you will have a hard time getting them out when they cool
19. if you can , let them cool slightly and enjoy them when they are still warm
demonstrations.review: These are dangerously good! I gave the family each a couple and then quickly froze the rest just to keep myself from eating them all!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
tanzanian tonic

delicious drink served in tanzania with fresh fruit nectar and rum. africa is the land of the freshest, sweetest and most ripe fruits in the world. i bet these are to die for when drank with the fresh fruits of tanzania
recipe was adapted from the african cookbook by bea sandler.

1. blend until smooth
2. garnish with halved orange slices and cherries
3. add a dash of dark rum as it is served
demonstrations.review: Oh my this is soooo good, and was a big hit at a recent party! I upped the nectars to a full 12 oz. can (1 1/2 c.) and adjusted the rest by the same ratio so I didn't waste any of the nectars. Also I upped the alcohol content, and used 6 oz. of orange rum and 6 oz of pineapple rum in place of the light and dark rums. VERY YUMMY, and very dangerous! You can easily drink the whole pitcher, and be completely snockered! haha Plan on making it again this week for Thanksgiving! Thanks for sharing this most excellent recipe!! My new favorite drink!

target.recipe_text:
cheesy apple breakfast quesadillas

make ahead breakfast treat the the kids can grab and microwave or eat cold on the way to school.

1. spread each flour tortillas with 1 tablespoon sour cream
2. sprinkle with
3. 1 teaspoons cinnamon sugar
4. top one tortilla 1 / 3 cup cheese , 1 / 4 cup chopped apple and second tortilla
5. for each serving , melt 1 tablespoon butter in a large skillet , brown quesadilla
6. 1 minute on each side or until lightly browned , carefully turning over tortilla
7. cut into wedges
8. serve with sour cream , if desired
target.review: pretty good.  the cinnamon sugar adds a lot more than i expected.  Quick easy snack/breakfast

demonstrations.recipe_text:
margarita cupcakes with key lime icing

yummy!!!  from the wilton website.

1. in large bowl , combine cake mix , margarita mix , egg whites and vegetable oil using electric mixer
2. stir in lime zest
3. mix completely
4. fill prepared pans 2 / 3 full
5. bake according to box directions 22-24 minutes or until toothpick inserted in center of cupcake comes out clean
6. cool in pan on cooling rack 5-8 minutes
7. remove cupcakes from pan
8. cool completely
9. for icing:
10. in large bowl , cream butter , cream cheese , juice and zest with electric mixer until light and fluffy
11. add 4 cups confectioners' sugar , one cup at a time
12. continue beating until light and fluffy
13. if icing is too thin add additional confectioners' sugar 1 tablespoon at a time
demonstrations.review: these cupcakes are so good.  i didn't get a chance to try the icing, since my cupcakes fell apart when i tried to get them out of the silicone pan...but, i ate the pieces with some cool whip...so good  :-)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crock pot stuffed cabbage

this sounds like a great way to make stuffed cabbage in the crock pot. i wanted to post this recipe so that i would have it available when i get around to making it.

1. wash cabbage leaves
2. boil 4 cups of water
3. turn heat off and soak the leaves in the water for 5 minutes
4. remove , drain and cool
5. combine remaining ingredients except tomato paste and water
6. place 2 tablespoons of mixture on each leaf and roll firmly
7. stack in the crock pot
8. combine tomato paste and water and pour over stuffed cabbage
9. cover and cook on low for 8-10 hours
demonstrations.review: my first attempt at making stuffed cabbage - i couldn't make the cabbage leaves large enough to wrap very well, but the inside mixture was lacking flavor as well - a good starting point

demonstrations.recipe_text:
spinach stuffed crescent rolls

every year i serve this at my christmas gift wrapping party along with a fruit salad, good coffee and a plate of goodies to nibble while we wrap.  i print the recipe on christmas stationery because i know newcomers will ask for it.

1. spray medium skillet with nonstick cooking spray
2. saute onion , mushrooms and garlic until onion is transparent
3. remove from heat
4. stir in spinach , ricotta , mozzarella , sour cream , salt , cayenne and nutmeg until throughly combined
5. seperate crescent rolls
6. place 3 tablespoons spinach mixture on wide end of each piece of dough
7. roll up to form crescent
8. place on nonstick baking sheet
9. bake 20 minutes at 350
demonstrations.review: These were quite good.  If I can find a way to make them healthier, I'd totally make them again.  I did try my extra filling baked in a ramekin dish - a little bit like a spinach and artichoke dip.  I couldn't fit 3 Tbsp. in each by a long shot (MAYBE 2...but they were all overflowing).  I used 2 packs of rolls and still had a lot of filling left over

target.recipe_text:
minestrone soup

this is by far the best soup that i have ever had.  i found this recipe in a cookbook called a collection of the very finest recipes.  i have slightly adapted the recipe, but not by much.

1. saute sausage until brown
2. add onion , garlic , carrots , and basil and cook for 5 minutes
3. add zucchini , tomatoes with liquid , bouillon , cabbage , salt , and pepper
4. bring soup to a boil
5. reduce heat and simmer covered for an hour
6. rinse beans
7. add the beans , rice , and wine
8. cook for 30 minutes , or until rice is done
9. you can eat this now and top with cheddar cheese , but it is even better the next day
target.review: VERY GOOD... I added additional broth for a brothier soup.. It was a little too thick with just 2 cans of broth. This is real tasty!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chocolate haystacks

when you make these you will not be able to eat just one. these are so good and fast and easy. my family goes crazy when i make these and they are gone in a minute. hope you try these

1. in a large bowl microwave chips on medium-high power for 1 minute , stir
2. microwave 10-20 second more until smooth
3. take out and add peanut butter , stir until well blended
4. add chow mein noodles and marshmallows
5. stir until all ingredients are coated
6. drop by rounded tablespoon onto cookie sheet lined with waxed paper
7. refrigerate until ready to serve
demonstrations.review: These are good..but not very attractive. I used semi sweet chips..will use milk chocolate as called for, if I make them again. Thanks

demonstrations.recipe_text:
brady bunch pork chops

i think this recipe is an absolute gem. really, in all my years of cooking, i don't think i have ever made chops as delectable as these! crispy-crunchy on the outside, meltingly tender and moist on the inside. the key, i think, is the salty milk marinade/brine, and making sure not to overcook them. thanks to gourmet magazine for this one.

1. in a large shallow dish , like a 9x13 pan , stir together milk and first amount of salt
2. add pork chops and marinate , covered and in fridge , for at least one hour
3. turn chops once , halfway through marinating / brining time
4. when ready to cook chops , preheat oven to 200f and have ready an ovenproof platter
5. in a shallow dish , combine freshly made bread crumbs with garlic powder , rosemary , thyme and remaining amount of salt
6. remove chops from milk and let excess milk drip off , then dredge chops in bread crumbs , lightly patting crumbs onto both sides of chops so they adhere
7. place breaded pork chops on a tray , keeping chops in one layer
8. in a large 12-inch skillet over high heat , place butter and oil
9. saute chops , 2 1 / 2 to 3 minutes per side only
10. do not overcook , do not crowd chops in skillet , and turn only once
11. chops should be golden brown and just cooked through
12. place cooked chops on platter and keep warm in preheated oven
13. cook remaining chops
14. add more oil and butter to pan if necessary
15. i recommend serving with applesauce
demonstrations.review: I used bought panko bread crumbs other than that followed recipe exactly.. I usually don't like pork chops but these are the moistest pan fried chops I have ever eaten.. cook only the amount specified..

demonstrations.recipe_text:
slow cooker beef short ribs

you won't believe how good these ribs are!!! i think we could have these every other night with no complaints! they're yummy!!!!

1. put flour , salt and pepper in a bag
2. add ribs and shake to coat
3. brown ribs in butter in a lg skillet
4. put in slow cooker
5. in same skillet , combine remaining ingredients
6. bring to a boil , stirring
7. pour over ribs
8. cover and cook on low for 9 hours
demonstrations.review: These were fantastic.. I only had to cook them 7 hours.. I think 9 hours would of been too long. They were even better the second day..heated, shredded and served as sandwhich on a french roll.Everyone enjoyed them in my family and I will definitely be making them again. I accidentally forgot the chili powder.. but they tasted wonderful despite it.. will try it next time.

target.recipe_text:
three cup chicken

this is a traditional taiwanese dish that we always order in our favorite chinese restaurant. i begged the chef for this recipe and he very reluctantly gave it to me! i just made it for dinner tonight and couldn't wait to post this to share it with all of you!

1. heat up the sesame oil in a wok or a large skillet on high heat
2. add garlic , ginger and serrano peppers , stir fry until fragrant , about 2 minutes
3. add the chicken pieces and cook until it's white in color , about 5 minutes
4. stir together the soy sauce , rice wine and sugar in a bowl , pour over chicken
5. bring to a boil , then turn down the heat to low
6. let cook , uncovered , until sauce thickens , about 30 minutes
7. turn heat back up to high and add basil and scallions , cook for another 2 minutes
8. serve over steamed rice
target.review: Superb dish.  I made it for me and my sister and we kept going back for 2nds and 3rds.  It had a nice amount of heat and the right amount of garlic!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
roasted garlic mashed potatoes and cauliflower

a great way to disguise cauliflower! the kids and adults love it! to roast garlic cut pointed end off bulb rub olive oil on wrap in foil and bake 375 for 1 hour.

1. boil potatoes and cauliflower together till tender
2. drain and mash potatoes , cauliflower , oil and butter
3. add rest of ingredients mix through
4. enjoy !
demonstrations.review: Loved this recipe.  My mom always make mashed cauliflower or faux-tatoes but the potatoes gave it a nicer texture.  Next time I would probably add way more sour cream and a lot more salt due to the amount of servings it made.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cabbage for those who dislike cabbage

this is so much nicer than plain steamed or boiled cabbage. try it on the cabbage haters in your family and see if it converts them.

1. in a large skillet , heat butter and oil over medium heat
2. add cabbage , garlic and brown sugar to pan
3. saut until the cabbage is limp , about 5 minutes or so
4. reduce heat to medium-low and stir in vinegar
5. cook , stirring very often , for approximately 20 minutes
6. taste and if cabbage is too crunchy for you , continue to cook for a few more minutes
7. add salt and pepper to taste and serve
demonstrations.review: Great flavors.  This has become a regular in our house.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
best ever banana cake with cream cheese frosting

this is one of (if not) the best banana cake i have ever tasted! i thought the oven temp of 275° sounded a little low, but this cake baked up (and rose) beautifully in my oven at this temp after pretty much exactly one hour. i do not know if the little "freezer trick" to this recipe is what ensured its moistness or not, but i did it, and it was exceptionally moist & delicious. would be interesting to see if it still came out as great if this step was skipped. all i know is that i followed this recipe exactly as stated (except that i had no buttermilk, so i subbed with a mix of lemon juice & milk) and i got exceptional results. so moist and yummy...a dense cake, similar in texture to a carrot cake... i personally would not call this frosted banana bread :o)  depending on the amount of frosting you like you can decide whether to half the recipe or not. i used the full recipe and had some leftover. i sprinkled on the chopped walnuts and threw this baby in the fridge and cut it the next day...to die for! i really liked it slightly chilled, but great at room temp too! it got better each day it sat, i always make this cake at least the day before i need or want it.  i was extremely pleased with this cake and will be making it over & over again!! so glad i came across this one!! (on another website).


(* * just to update the recipe, (based on some of the reviews), the baking time may vary based on individual ovens. it was right on for my oven, but some others have stated it has taken 1 hour 10 minutes, 1 hour 20 minutes, and my sister just informed me that it took 1 hour 30 minutes in her oven!!!!!)

1. preheat oven to 275f
2. grease and flour a 9 x 13 pan
3. in a small bowl , mix mashed banana with the lemon juice
4. set aside
5. in a medium bowl , mix flour , baking soda and salt
6. set aside
7. in a large bowl , cream 3 / 4 cup butter and 2 1 / 8 cups sugar until light and fluffy
8. beat in eggs , one at a time , then stir in 2 tsp vanilla
9. beat in the flour mixture alternately with the buttermilk
10. stir in banana mixture
11. pour batter into prepared pan and bake in preheated oven for one hour or until toothpick inserted in center comes out clean
12. remove from oven and place directly into the freezer for 45 minutes
13. this will make the cake very moist
14. for the frosting , cream the butter and cream cheese until smooth
15. beat in 1 teaspoon vanilla
16. add icing sugar and beat on low speed until combined , then on high speed until frosting is smooth
17. spread on cooled cake
18. sprinkle chopped walnuts over top of the frosting , if desired
demonstrations.review: This is the second time I've made this cake in less than a month. It was really yummy. I added a layer of caramel in the middle and then iced it with homemade white chocolate frosting. This cake is dangerous as you can find yourself eating more than one piece. Good thing I have a fast metabolism and not worried about my weight because I made the cake tonight and plan on eating 2 pieces!

target.recipe_text:
fresh cream of mushroom soup

this quick and easy recipe is so much better than the canned stuff. great as a first course, or with salad or sandwiches. of course, you can use it in your favorite recipes, too.  to make it thicker, use less stock and/or use heavy cream instead of the half-and-half cream or milk.

1. lighly saute mushrooms in butter
2. add flour and stir constantly for about 5 minutes
3. slowly add stock , stirring until all is incorporated
4. simmer about 10 minutes
5. add cream , stir and serve
target.review: Two quarts of stock was too much more than I like would have liked... Soup came out thin and not as creamy so next time I think I'll use less stock or more flour. Still, pretty tasty.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
whatever floats your boat  brownies

these are absolutely the chewiest, moistest, fudgiest brownies ever! i have tried adding so many different things to the batter, and they always comes out great.  they are also great without any add-ins! but by varying the add-ins, you can make different brownies every week (or day!!) super easy prep! so, add "whatever floats your boat" and you will not believe how yummy they come out :) oh, and the recipe doubles just fine--use a 9 x 13 inch pan instead and add a few more minutes of baking!

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. grease an 8 inch square pan or line with foil
3. in a medium bowl combine melted butter and cocoa and stir until cocoa is dissolved
4. add sugar and mix well
5. add eggs one at a time and stir until well combined
6. stir in vanilla , flour and salt until you no longer see any flour
7. fold in "whatever floats your boat" !
8. spread in pan and bake for approximately 25 minutes
9. do not over-bake -- your brownies will come out dry
10. adjust time / temp accordingly for your oven
11. if you do the knife / toothpick test , it should come out with moist crumbs , not clean
12. cool completely before cutting into squares
13. for vegetarian omit the marshmallows
14. for double recipe , bake in 9x12 pan and add 5 minutes to baking time
demonstrations.review:
This is not a brownie with depth. It's simple and easy though. I added about 3/4 of a cup of chopped pecans and to me, it was too much. I can't imagine how 2 cups would be -- probably way overwhelming with more add ins than brownie. I baked for 25 minutes but they were not done... In fact, it was pretty much underdone. I suppose that would make for a moisty, soft brownie but I personally like mine to be a bit more than mush.

But overall, it's decent, despite the ridiculous name. If I were to make it again, I think I would have to tweak it in a number of places to give it more texture and more depth in flavor.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
scones to die for

this recipe came from my joy of cooking. they are absolutely spectacular.i think i added a bit more sugar. taste like excellent shortbread.

1. heat oven to 425
2. mix flour , sugar , baking powder and salt
3. cut in butter with pastry blender
4. cut until size of peas
5. stir in currants or cranberries and rind
6. stir together egg , and cream and dump into dry mix
7. stir til a ball then gently knead five times
8. pat into a round 8" wide , about 3 / 4" thick
9. cut into 8 or 12 wedges and place on ungreased cookie sheet
10. brush tops with cream and sugar and cinnamon if desired
11. bake 12- 15 minutes
12. oh my , then enjoy
demonstrations.review: I too had a very dry crust -- it wouldn't even come together properly until a added a more cream (used heavy whipping cream). Afterwards, it was so hard to eat since it was breaking apart on me as I spread jam on it... Flavor was really good and the lemon zest added something incredibly intriguing so it would have been five stars had it been a bit more together.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mashed red potatoes with garlic and parmesan

the potatoes are ready in our garden, and this is the first recipe i reach for! these are so good!!

1. put potatoes and garlic in lg pan
2. cover with water
3. bring to a boil
4. reduce heat and simmer for 25 minutes , until potatoes are tender
5. drain well
6. mash with the butter , milk , and salt
7. stir in the parmesan cheese
demonstrations.review: So awesome! Very easy to make. I added more garlic, some black pepper, more salt and I used half&half instead of milk. Boiling the garlic with the potatoes is ingenious! I also mixed in a shredded cheese blend for some melty goodness. Definitely will make again.

target.recipe_text:
rotisserie chicken with dried fruit and pine nuts

pollo con frutos y frutas secas 
this recipe is as practical as it is inventive.  it features a store-bought rotisserie chicken that's deliciously doctored with a sauce of dried fruit, pine nuts and port wine.  though you can whip up the dish in less than half an hour, the flavors are sophisticated enough for a fancy dinner party.  you can roast your own chicken, if you wish.  adapted from "the new spanish table" cookbook.

1. preheat the oven to 425
2. heat the olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat
3. add the prunes , apricots , cherries , pine nuts , and orange and lemon zests and cook , stirring , until the pine nuts turn golden and the fruits are browned in spots , 3-5 minutes
4. add the port and cinnamon stick and cook until syrupy , about 5 minutes
5. add the chicken stock , and reserved chicken juices
6. increase the heat to high , bring the sauce to a boil , and cook until reduced , about 5 minutes
7. place the chicken pieces in a baking dish that can hold them snugly
8. pour the sauce over them , scraping up all the fruit and liquid from the bottom of the skillet and turning the chicken to coat it with the sauce
9. bake the chicken until it is warmed through and the sauce is further reduced , about 10 minutes
10. transfer to plates and serve at once
target.review: Food and Wine has an almost identical recipe but I'll try yours instead. They only add the chicken to the sauce for one minute before serving. I like the idea of reducing the sauce a little more the way you did!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
buca di beppo lentil soup

i have taken many of buca di beppo cooking classes and also bought the cook-book. this a great soup and easy to make.

1. bring the stock to a boil
2. add lentils , carrot , onion , celery , sausage and sage
3. turn heat down to med and cook for about 1 hour or until the soup thickens
4. stir in tomatoes salt and pepper to taste
5. serve soup in individual bowls with a little extra virgin olive oil
demonstrations.review: we LOVE this soup! so easy to make. yet, so flavorful!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
caribbean rice in a rice cooker

this side or a vegetarian main is loaded with flavor and texture. i made this in a rice cooker if you add more water will increase the cooking time and produce softer rice; reducing the amount of water will produce firmer rice. but once you've found the ratio that's right for you, it'll be very easy to have perfect rice your way. yes you can make stove top as well. be sure not to remove the lid till done cooking.

1. put aside 1 tablespoon scallions and 1 teaspoon coconut for garnish
2. place all the rest ingredients in rice cooker
3. pour broth 3 / 4 inch above the level of the rice
4. press the cook button
5. when done fluff with fork place in a serving dish and top with reserved coconut and scallions place lime along side for garnish and use as wanted
demonstrations.review: my hubby has been asking me to make a dish using jerk seasoning for a while now. i thought this would be perfect and it was!!! thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
celery   olive salad

from family circle magazine, nov 2008.

1. in a medium-sized glass or plastic bowl , stir together celery , olives , olive oil , vinegar , oregano , garlic powder , salt and pepper until well combined
2. cover and refrigerate for at least 4 hours or as long as overnight
3. serve as an accompaniment to fish or meat
demonstrations.review: I am an olive fanatic. Probably the only way to get me to eat celery! Sooooo good!

target.recipe_text:
lori s kale slaw

delicious!  and very healhty!  you can make it even healthier by using light or fat-free mayonnaise.

1. combine the kale , carrots and walnuts
2. whisk together the mayonnaise , vinegar , sugar and spices
3. toss with mix
4. cover
5. chill 1 hour
target.review: UH-mazing! I am so happy to find a recipe that makes raw kale delicious. I made exactly as written except for...now that I think about it I did change a few things. First of all, cut way back on cayenne (just a pinch and I still could taste it. And I like spicy!), swapping almonds for the walnuts because I prefer them, and cranberries and chopped apple. YUM! Husband and I agreed adding some salty chunks of broiled chicken would make this a delicious meal on it's own. And how else could you make these uber healthy greens taste like a treat?

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crumb topped banana muffins

these are so good. we love the topping.

1. in a large bowl , mix the flour , baking soda , baking powder , and salt
2. mix bananas , sugar , egg and melted butter
3. stir into dry mixture until thoroughly combined , then stop mixing
4. fill muffin cups 3 / 4 full
5. combine brown sugar , flour , and cinnamon topping ingredients
6. cut in cold butter until crumbly
7. sprinkle over muffins
8. bake at 375 degrees fahrenheit for about 20 minutes , until muffins test done
9. cool in pan for 10 minutes
demonstrations.review: I COMPLETELY forgot the sugar in the batter and these are still rockin' muffins. The sweetness from the topping saved them and the actual muffin was still very flavorful. Thanks~~!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
blueberry spice sauce

serve warm over ice cream, or a freshly baked cake or pie.

1. rinse and clean blueberries
2. if using frozen dry pack blueberries , thaw them first
3. in small saucepan , combine sugar , cornstarch , cinnamon and nutmeg
4. gradually stir in water and lemon juice
5. over medium heat , cook , stirring constantly , until mixture thickens and comes to a boil
6. add blueberries
7. cook and stir until mixture comes back to a boil
8. serve warm over ice cream or cake or frozen pies
demonstrations.review: Really really good! I omitted nutmeg because I hate it, but it made an awesome addition to buttermilk pancakes. THanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
blackened chicken and beans

this one is easy and low fat and very tasty!

1. combine the chili powder , salt and pepper
2. rub on both sides of chicken
3. in a large skillet , cook chicken in oil 4-5 minutes each side , until juices run clear
4. remove and keep warm
5. add beans , corn and salsa to skillet
6. bring to a boil
7. reduce heat , cover and simmer 2-3 minutes , until heated through
8. put bean mixture on a serving dish
9. top with chicken
demonstrations.review: Five stars for ease and eatability. I had this on the table in probably fifteen minutes and my kids did not protest any more than they usually do when something new shows up on the table. The younger one actually said "I don't mind if there's corn in this."

target.recipe_text:
allrighty then scrambled eggs   paula deen

i saw this on paula's home cooking and had to share! allrighty then!

1. in a medium size bowl , beat eggs , sour cream , water , and salt and pepper until fluffy
2. using a nonstick frying pan , melt butter and cook eggs over low heat , stirring occasionally
3. stir in the cheese
4. cook until you reach desired consistency
5. serve hot with biscuits !
6. enjoy !
target.review: Have made these many times now, with the same comments- "These are really good".  They come out very fluffy and creamier than most scrambled eggs.  I don't even use the water and find they turn out just fine.  Great eggs, and easy!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chocolate praline layer cake

this is a wonderful cake we often have at special occasions. it is a pillsbury bake off winner from many years ago.

1. heat oven to 325 degrees
2. in a heavy saucepan , combine butter , 1 / 4 cup whipping cream and brown sugar
3. cook over low heat just until butter is melted , stirring occasionally
4. pour into two 9-inch round cake pans
5. sprinkle evenly with chopped pecans
6. in a large bowl , combine remaining cake ingredients at low speed until moistened
7. beat 2 minutes at high speed
8. carefully spoon batter over pecan mixture around edges of pan
9. spoon remaining batter in center of pans
10. bake at 325 degrees for 35 to 45 minutes , or until done
11. cool 5 minutes
12. remove from pans and cool completely
13. in a small bowl , beat 1 1 / 4 cup whipping cream until soft peaks form
14. blend in powdered sugar and vanilla
15. beat until stiff peaks form
16. to assemble cake , place 1 layer on serving plate , praline side up
17. spread with half of whipped cream
18. top with second layer , praline side up
19. spread top with remaining whipped cream
20. garnish with pecan halves and chocolate curls if desired
21. store in refrigerator
demonstrations.review: Got rave reviews @ a luncheon at work. Not a crumb left to bring home.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
banana pineapple streusel muffins

mmmmmm... my 2 most favourite things--all in one muffin!! recipe can also be made into 2 medium-sized loaves, if you wish. enjoy!!!

1. preheat oven to 375 degrees f
2. streusel topping: combine sugar , flour , and cinnamon
3. with a pastry blender , cut in butter until mixture resembles crumbs
4. set aside
5. batter: combine flour , salt , baking soda , sugar and cinnamon
6. stir in pecans
7. combine eggs , vegetable oil , mashed bananas , drained crushed pineapple and vanilla extract in separate bowl
8. add to flour mixture , stirring just until dry ingredients are moistened
9. do not over stir
10. fill paper-lined muffin tins a little more than half full
11. sprinkle tops with streusel mixture
12. bake about 25 minutes
13. let cool for 10 minutes , then remove and finish cooling on wire racks
14. batter can be used to make 2 medium-sized loaves
15. bake at 350 degrees f
demonstrations.review: If you haven't made these muffins, then you don't know what you are missing. My sister came by to get some,put the rest in a Zippy bag for me (to put in the frig)-then went home with her 4, plus my bag full. By the time I got my dozen back, there were anly 4 left.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
granny s banana cream pie

so delicious !!

1. in a saucepan , combine sugar , flour , and salt
2. stir in milk and mix well
3. cook over medium heat , stirring constantly , until the mixture thickens and comes to a boil
4. boil for 2 minutes
5. remove from the heat
6. stir a small amount of cream mixture into egg yolks
7. return all to saucepan
8. cook for 2 minutes , stirring constantly
9. remove from the heat
10. add butter and vanilla
11. mix well
12. allow to cool slightly
13. slice the bananas and place evenly in pastry shell
14. pour cream mixture over bananas
15. cool
16. before serving , garnish with whipped cream or cool whip and bananas
17. refrigerate any leftovers
demonstrations.review: Made this for a work luncheon last week, then again for Easter. Got rave reviews. Did even have a sliver to bring home. Will definitely keep this one. Very easy, but Yummy!!!

target.recipe_text:
denzel washington s chicken curry

our local news station collects favorite recipes of movie stars. i have not tried this but it looks yummy to me.

1. heat olive oil in a small dutch oven or fry pan over medium to medium high heat
2. saut onion until it just starts to soften
3. add garlic and cook another minute
4. stir in curry powder , paprika , cinnamon , sugar , ginger and bay leaf
5. move spices around pan cooking for about 2 minutes
6. add a large pinch of salt
7. add chicken , chopped tomato , tomato paste , yogurt and coconut milk
8. turn up heat and bring to a boil
9. reduce heat and simmer for 25 minutes
10. add lemon juice and cayenne pepper and simmer another 5 minutes
11. remove bay leaf and serve over rice of choice
target.review: I made this tonight and it was fabulous! Very nice combo of flavors. I didn't do anything different, with one exception: At the beginning of the last 5 minute simmering step, I also added a tablespoon and a half of corn starch mixed in cold water to the pot to thicken up the sauce a bit (it was a little too liquidy for my preference), and I served it over yellow rice. I would imagine it would be good served over cooked egg noodles also... ~The Mad Slovak~

demonstrations.recipe_text:
tropical sweet potato salad

a great choice instead of the traditional potato salad.  the spices, pineapple, and toasted pecans provide the perfect complement to the naturally sweet yams.

1. in a large saucepan , cook sweet potatoes for 8-10 minutes in boiling water just until tender
2. do not overcook
3. drain and toss with lemon juice , and set aside
4. add celery , green onions , pineapple chunks , and pecans
5. in a small bowl , combine mayonnaise , orange rind , orange juice , ghoney , ginger , and salt
6. mix the mayonnaise dressing with sweet potato mixture , tossing gently
7. serve immediately , or cover and chill
demonstrations.review: I made this recipe for yesterday's bbq because it was a Caribbean theme. After we all ate, I realize that your potato salad was still in the refrigerator. I put it out anyway and it quickly disappeared! Everyone loved it, and I will definitely serve it again. Well done! "The Mad Slovak"

demonstrations.recipe_text:
black forest pumpernickel bread machine  loaf

this one i have been making for ten years, and always turns out fine for me even now in a different machine..give it a try eat with ham and cheese and homemade potato soup, yummy

1. place all ingredients into your bread maker according to manufacture
2. select type to a light crust
3. press start
4. remembering to check while starting to knead
5. if mixture is too dry add a tablespoon warm water at a time
6. if mixture is too wet add flour again a little at a time
7. mixture should go into a ball form , and just soft and slightly sticky to the finger touch
8. this goes for all types of breads when kneading
9. this recipe makes a one and half pound loaf size
demonstrations.review: I made this bread exactly as stated. I kept it in the machine for the whole process, not taking the dough out, forming it into a loaf and then placing it in the oven (why do some people do that?!) ... It was VERY good and came out in a perfectly shaped loaf ... I just want to add that my bread machine has Medium, Large and X-Large settings. I used the Large setting based on the amount of flour stated in the recipe. I hope some of you find this useful. Thanks for the recipe andypandy!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
sahara sand bread for bread machine

this is really good bread. it makes good sandwichs and lovely toast.

1. place ingredients in the pan of the bread machine in the order recommended by the manufacturer
2. select cycle
3. press start
4. makes a 1 1 / 2 lb loaf
demonstrations.review: I was a bit confused as to some of the reviews of this recipe because some, it seems, just used it to make the dough in their bread machines and then used their conventional ovens, and then wondered why it didn't turn out well. I used my bread machine for the whole process and it came out very nice, with a light texture and very good flavor. I didn't change a thing. I will definitely make it again. I think it should be noted that all recipes for "bread machines" do not automatically adapt well to just making the dough in the machine and then placing the dough in a loaf pan in the oven.

target.recipe_text:
vegetarian paella

iga, the supermarket chain in montreal hands out recipes to its shoppers in order to sell its inline products.  i sometimes buy those products, depending on my budget, but i mostly don't, because i like using my favourite brands.

1. pour 3 tablespoons water over saffron in a small bowl and set aside
2. sprinkle salt over the eggplant chunks and let stand in a colander for 30 minutes
3. rinse and drain
4. heat the oil in a large frying pan and saute the onion , garlic , peppers and eggplant for 5 minutes
5. sprinkle with paprika and toss
6. add the rice , then incorporate the vegetable stock , tomatoes , saffron and season with salt and pepper to taste
7. bring to a boil and simmer for 15 minutes , uncovered , stirring frequently
8. fold in the mushrooms , green beans and chickpeas
9. cook for another 15 minutes and serve immediately
target.review: Yum! Healthy and delicious. It also re-heats perfectly. I made a huge pot and enjoyed it for many meals!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
vegetarian quiche with potato crust

my family absolutely loves quiche, but i didn't make it frequently due to the hydrogenated oils from the pie crust and the extra calories from the heavy cream. it took me several years to perfect this recipe to make it low fat while maintaining the richness and flavor.  the idea of using potato for the crust came from elizabeth's o'brien quiche recipe (thank you elizabeth!) and this was the final substitution i needed for honing this recipe.  because i cram so much into this deep dish quiche, it is very filling.  i like to serve sliced melon (water- or cantelope) for dessert.

1. preheat oven to 375 degrees
2. press shredded potatoes into a lightly oiled large deep dish pie pan
3. place pie plate in oven for 10-15 minutes until the potatoes are just beginning to brown
4. while potato-crust is cooking , work on the veggies
5. brush fry pan with olive oil and saute the onions and peppers until onions are transparent , remove from heat
6. cook the broccoli until slightly tender -- either by steaming for about 5 minutes or zapping in a covered microwavable dish with a splash of water for about 2 minutes
7. beat the eggs in a bowl with the evaporated milk
8. after removing the potatoes from the oven , sprinkle about 2 / 3 cup of the cheese over the potato crust
9. spread the cooked onions and peppers evenly in the pie pan
10. spread the broccoli evenly over the onions and peppers
11. sprinkle the crumbled veggie bacon over the veggies
12. this should basically fill the deep dish pie pan completely
13. sprinkle the rest of cheese over the veggies
14. carefully pour the milk and egg mixture into the deep dish pie pan
15. place in the oven for 45 minutes or until egg is cooked and firm
16. cool for 5 to 10 minutes before serving
demonstrations.review: A great low-fat alternative to regular quiche! My boyfriend hates all the low cal food that I make and he could not get enough of this!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
vegan holiday lentil loaf

if you have a vegan or vegetarian coming over for the holidays or eat this way yourself, this is a great option for the holiday dinner. great served with a veggie gravy, herbed garlic mashed potatoes and a nice salad

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees f
2. chop onion and celery finely , and crush the garlic clove
3. spray a frying pan with non-stick spray , and saute the onion , garlic and celery until onion is translucent
4. add the sage
5. combine all ingredients in a large bowl and mix well
6. spray a loaf pan with non-stick spray and fill the loaf pan with the mixture
7. press down
8. bake 30 minutes covered , 10 minutes uncovered
9. let stand for 5-10 minutes before cutting and serving
demonstrations.review: I can not beleive how good this is. It is my new obsession. My boyfriend does not like lentils and he even liked this. It is a great vegetarian main dish. I did cook my lentils and rice in veggie broth to add flavor and added a little garlic salt.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
palak paneer  indian fresh spinach with paneer cheese

creamy and rich, a delight to eat. a dish i fell in love with at a local restaurant and adapted a recipe to closely resemble theirs.

1. cut spinach into shreds and cook in 3 tablespoons water until tender
2. remove from heat
3. saute onion , cinnamon , cardamom , and ginger in 1-2 tablespoons ghee or oil until onion is translucent
4. then add garlic and chopped tomatoes , and reduce heat
5. cook this briefly and slowly blend in yogurt a little at a time to prevent curdling
6. add coriander , garam masala , paprika , and salt , mixing well
7. add cooked spinach with liquid , cover and simmer on low heat for approximately 20-30 minutes
8. remove from heat
9. take half of spinach mixture and puree in food processor or blender , and return to mixture and stir
10. slowly stir in heavy cream , and heat through on low heat
11. add paneer cubes
12. serve
demonstrations.review: It is fabulous! I always add a little extra salt at the end and it just sets the flavor off perfectly!I also use nonfat cream yogurt to make it a little healthier and is still tastes fab.  My family now always requests this to be among the dishes when I am cooking an indian dinner!

target.recipe_text:
bourekakia  baklava  cigars

these are great and keep a long time. not as sweet as traditional baklava as they are not soaked in syrup, merely dusted with powdered sugar.

*please note that a few of the ingredients are showing up incorrectly on the recipe page and is not fixable currently.  the following amounts are what should appear:

syrup:
1 1/4 cups sugar
3/4 cup water
1 tablespoon fresh lemon juice
1 tablespoon honey (preferably, greek thyme)
3 cinnamon sticks
3 whole cloves
filling:
3 cups ground walnuts
1 teaspoon cinnamon
1/4 teaspoon ground cloves
2 egg whites, room temperature, beaten to consistency of mayonnaise
1 lb phyllo pastry
1 cup butter, melted
icing sugar

1. for syrup: cook all ingredients in saucepan over low heat , swirling pan occasionally , until sugar dissolves , then boil 15 minutes
2. cool completely
3. strain
4. for filling: combine walnuts , cinnamon and cloves
5. blend in 1 cup syrup and whites
6. to assemble: preheat oven to 350f
7. cut phyllo into 5 x 8 inch strips
8. cover with plastic wrap and a damp towel until ready to use
9. take a strip and brush it lightly with melted butter
10. spread 1 heaping teaspoon of filling along narrow edge
11. fold in sides inch toward center
12. brush sides lightly with butter
13. roll up tightly
14. repeat with remaining strips
15. arrange seam side down on baking sheet
16. brush with remaining butter
17. bake until golden and crisp , 20-25 minutes
18. cool completely
19. dust lightly with powdered sugar
target.review: I truly loved these, since they weren't sticky sweet as most other baklavas I've made, Since they are time-consuming, when I want to serve them, I make them ahead of time and freeze.  The only change I made was to change syrup somewhat by using 1T orange juice and 1T lemon juice. I'll be making these smokin' "cigars" for every Greek Night we have! Thanks so much!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
sunset salad

i used to eat this all the time as a kid and just ran across the recipe again in a church recipe collection cookbook. i'm not a huge fan of gelatin salads,(they always sound kinda funky) but this one, i like. a little tart, a little sweet.

1. dissolve jello in boiling water
2. add pineapple , with juice , and lemon juice
3. add carrots
4. chill until set
demonstrations.review: I made this months ago for my Super Bowl party (Da Bears' colors are orange and black...)  Then I lost the recipe and couldn't review it!  Now that I've found it again, I have to give it 5+ stars.  I've never liked jello salads with veggies in them and think most jello salads are too sweet -- but I LOVED this, as did all the people at the party!  I'll make this again an again...

demonstrations.recipe_text:
awesome bacon tomato dip

oh, you have to try this one!! my family loves dips and spreads, and even the guys got really into this one. i even caught my uncle (who thinks guys are too "macho" for dips), eating it straight from the bowl with a spoon!! best when made day of, and lettuce added just before serving. it gets soggy:(

1. in medium bowl , with mixer , blend sour cream , mayonnaise , cream cheese , cheddar cheese , chopped onion and green pepper , garlic powder , and black pepper
2. crumble bacon into small pieces and add to mixture
3. add chopped tomato and stir well
4. garnish with shredded lettuce just before serving , if desired
5. serve with townhouse crackers or wheat thins
6. also good served in a bread bowl with bread cubes to dip
demonstrations.review: A step above any BLT Dip I've had, including my own! Needless to say, I've ripped up my recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
ellinikos lemoni patatas   greek lemon potatoes

these are absolutely delicious, and easy to prepare!

1. peel potatoes and cut them in half
2. let them stand in water while preparing sauce
3. combine all other ingredients in a gallon size"zipper" bag , and shake to combine
4. dry off the potatoes , and put all of them in the bag and let marinate for 2 hours
5. preheat oven to 400 degrees
6. put the potatoes and marinade in a large casserole , preferrably a white pyrex , approximately 13 x 9 x 3 oval
7. roast for 1hr 10min , turning occasionally
8. there should be plenty of sauce left over after roasting
9. you can put these under the broiler for 5 minutes to crisp them up if you prefer
demonstrations.review: I am not rating this because I prepared the recipe incorrectly. Be sure you use a pan at least the size as recommended in the recipe. I used a smaller dish that held the halved potatoes. Because of this, the marinade about covered the potatoes. I thought it would cook down, but it didn't, and the flavor was way too intense. Because of the reviews, I will be trying again -- this time only covering potatoes with half the marinade if I bake them in a smaller pan than 13x9!

target.recipe_text:
easy oven barbecued chicken

have not tried this yet, but it sure sounds good and so easy to do. just doctor up your favorite bottled barbecue sauce with some orange marmalade and a few other ingredients, pour over chicken and bake.

1. salt and pepper chicken pieces to taste and place in single layer in baking pan
2. combine all sauce ingredients and pour over chicken
3. bake at 350 for one hour , basting occasionally
4. increase heat to 375 and bake an additional 15 minutes
target.review: I was looking for something different to do with the chicken I was about to bake and I didn't have the car to go to the market; I was so pleased to find this recipe and, with just a few changes, had all the ingredients on hand! I used apricot allfruit instead of the marmalade(not our favorite!) and chicken thighs instead of the 2 pounds of pieces;no matter! The finished product was sweet-tangy and earned me some much needed raves!Thanks Marie!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
the ultimate salmon fillets

living on the west coast, we have eaten a great deal of salmon. this is absolutely the best way we have found to cook it. it is so moist and the flavor is fantastic! many reviewers have said that they think the cheese, especially the cheddar is unnecessary, and i have to admit that i omit the cheddar cheese myself. the flavour is a little too strong and it is extra fat that is not needed. i do like the sprinkling of parmesan with the paprika because it looks so nice when it is broiled. using light mayonnaise and light sour cream or yogurt tastes just as good as the full fat versions and cuts down fat and calories even more. thanks for all the great reviews!

1. preheat oven to 450 degrees
2. if frozen , partially thaw fillets and cut into serving size pieces
3. place in a greased baking dish
4. combine sour cream or yogurt , mustard , onion , dill , and mayonnaise
5. season with salt and pepper
6. spread mixture over fish
7. bake 20 minutes per inch of thickness of fish if frozen or 10-12 minutes if thawed
8. when just done , sprinkle with the cheeses and a dash of paprika
9. broil 1 minute or until the cheese is bubbly and flecked with brown
10. serve with lemon wedges
demonstrations.review: Really excellent recipe!!  The fish was moist the sauce delicate and flavorful and we liked the addition of the cheese! This is a dish I will prepare again and again since everyone loved it! Thanks Sue!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
main course  hamburger  soup

i did a search and found that there are oodles of recipes for hamburger soup on recipezaar, but decided to post this one anyway because it's just too good not to share!  i had a craving for it one recent rainy day and it sure hit the spot.

1. fry ground beef and onion with salt and pepper until browned
2. add beef broth , tomato soup and water
3. add prepared veggies , parsley flakes and bay leaf and simmer until veggies are tender
4. if you have any leftover tomatoes or tomato sauce add that while cooking the veggies
5. remove bay leaf and add a splash of cream before serving
6. this soup is quite thick
7. for a thinner consistency add more beef broth or another tin of tomato soup
demonstrations.review: We loved this recipe! Really tasty and filling. We ate every drop! Thanks so much!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chocolate orange chocolate chip cookies

these cookies are super-packed with intense flavors.

1. heat oven to 350
2. beat 1 cup sugar , butter , 1 tablespoon grated orange peel and the egg in large bowl with electric mixer on medium speed , or mix with spoon
3. stir in flour , cocoa , salt , baking powder and baking soda
4. stir in pecans and chocolate morsels
5. shape dough into 1 1 / 2-inch balls
6. mix 1 / 3 cup sugar and 1 teaspoon grated orange peel
7. roll balls in sugar mixture
8. place about 3 inches apart on ungreased cookie sheet
9. flatten to about 1 / 2-inch thickness with bottom of glass
10. bake 9 to 11 minutes or until set
11. cool slightly
12. remove from cookie sheet
13. cool on wire rack
demonstrations.review: I was searching for a variation on the traditional chocolate chip cookie recipe and was lucky to have found this one! Loving chocolate as I do, this was an easy choice and the addition of the orange flavor was a delicious bonus! Excellent, a real 'keeper'!

target.recipe_text:
egg rolls

another one of our families 

1. in a medium size skillet , add pork
2. season with garlic powder , and ginger
3. mixing thoroughly
4. cook pork until no longer pink
5. drain off fat and set aside on paper towels
6. in a deep fryer or large skillet , add oil
7. heat oil to 375 degrees , or use medium-high heat with the skillet
8. while oil is heating , in a small bowl , combine flour and water until they form a paste
9. in a large bowl , combine cabbage , carrots , onion , green peppers and reserved pork
10. mix well
11. on a plate , lay out one egg roll skin with a corner pointed towards you
12. place about 1 / 4 to 1 / 3 cup of the vegetable mixture on an egg roll paper , and fold corner up over the mixture
13. fold left and right corners toward the center , and continue to roll
14. brush abit of the flour paste around the final corner to help seal the egg roll
15. repeat process , using up remaining ingredients
16. place egg rolls into heated oil and fry , until golden brown
17. remove from oil , and drain on paper towels
18. makes 20 egg rolls
19. serve with a sweet and sour sauce
target.review:
This recipe was very tasty..I added 2Tblsp peanut butter, and bean sprouts, and crushed chili peppers. 
These were the closest to egg rolls ordered in restaurant Ive had. I made copies for friends at work.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
corn casserole iv

nan

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. mix all ingredients together and pour into 2 quart casserole dish
3. bake for 1 hour
demonstrations.review: great sidedish, easy good with fish,chicken,chili you name it.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
italian meatball subs

i got this from a crock pot cookbook several years ago and have made it many times. we all love it. get a crusty sub roll, spread it with butter, garlic salt and pop in under the broiler for a few minutes and then make your sandwich. it is yummy and easy.

1. combine all the ingredients for meatballs
2. mix well
3. shape into 1" balls and broil or saute till brown
