I made two for myself and the only change I made was using sliced medium tomatoes instead of the cherry tomatoes.  At first I thought I should scramble the egg before adding it to the ham as other reviewers had suggested but I am glad that I didn't because it made for a perfect poached egg type presentation. I loved the taste of the tomato in the pie; the tomato, lightly baked, still retained a very fresh flavor.  I thought it might be difficult to get the pies out of the muffin tins but I didn't have a problem (I sprayed the tins before hand with cooking spray as the recipe states).  The only seasoning (aside from the chives) that I needed was pepper.  Delicious.  This will be a top recipe to make for company.  I can see also "personalizing" the pies with mushrooms or bacon bits.  Excellent, excellent, excellent.  Thank you Jewelies.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
triple berry freeze

from cooking light.
a non alcholic drink
posting for safe keeping
i would blend on a low speed to prevent to much bubbling up from the sparkling water

1. place sparkling water and sorbet in a blender , and process until well blended
2. add raspberries , blueberries , blackberries , and honey
3. process until mixture is smooth
demonstrations.review: This was a refreshing, delicious drink--a perfect non-alcoholic cocktail. Ideal for a Arizona summer happy hour on the patio. I think the key to the drink is the lemon sorbet--it gives the berries a zing and reminded me of popsicles. Delicious and easy!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
v s tri tip marinade

this is it! family favorite... :) in my family we eat this at least once a week. makes a nice sunday dinner. i prepare the marinade on saturday and let it sit until we're ready to bbq on sunday. i was absolutely honored when bobby flay did a show with this recipe slightly modified of course!  easy....delicious and the most tender flavor you'll never expect  prep time does not include time to marinade. the longer .... the better if you like a melt in your mouth tri-tip this is how i make it.

1. mix all of the ingredients except for the beef in a large mixing bowl to make the marinade
2. place trimmed tri-
3. let stand in the refrigerator for at least 6 hours heat grill to medium temperature
4. place tri-
5. remove the tri-
6. serve with your favorite side dishes
demonstrations.review:
I had this as part of a 4th of July bbq menu. The marinated tri tip was perfect off the grill. The meat was juicy and the flavors of the marinade didn't overpower the meat but added rich smoky flavors. Also, grilling the marinade created a bit of a crust that was excellent. The simplicity of the ingredients makes the recipe a keeper. Update: Over the weekend, I wanted to serve a casual dinner for my family that wouldn't be too difficult. I instantly thought of Chef V's marinated tri tip cooked on the grill. It turned out delicious--again--and got rave reviews from my mom who knows that I am truly just a fry cook. Don't be intimidated by amount of salt, it acts to tenderize the meat and cure it so that the meat comes out super flavorful. Excellent for making an impression on guests!
Update 2009 -- Still the best.  The meat is so tender.  Great for sandwiches the next day!

target.recipe_text:
potatoes tapas in garlic mayonnaise  potatoes aioli

"tapas, the little dishes of spain" by penelope cases alfred a. knopf 1986  this book contains more than 200 recipes for tapas. the word "tapa" in  spanish means top or cover( there are other meanings) spain has many bars  one for every 120 persons. they are usually small and run by families.  coffee, water, soft drinks and liquor. they serve food also. they have  the time and ingredients for these small dishes. in the early days tapas  were served on small dishes placed as a cover over drinks. the tapas were  small and sometimes they were free or sold for a small price. today the  dishes are larger and expensive. (4) recipes of the most commonly found tapas all over spain

1. boil potatoes in salt water until tender
2. peel and cut into 3 / 4 inch chunks
3. in a bowl , combine mayonnaise , garlic , and parsley
4. fold the potatoes into the sauce gently , season with salt to taste , serve at room temperature
target.review: I'm sure mine didn't turn out the way intended, as I cut the potatoes into smaller pieces (since I don't like large bites of potato). Then, on top of doing that, I left them in the water after boiling, until I was ready for them, (I knew all along what the result might be, based on the things I was doing lol). I considered posting my result on here as a new recipe, but realized that really, it's still the same recipe, with a slight variation, so others can choose which way they're in the mood for, each time they make it. What happened was that as I was mixing everything together, yes, go figure, the potatoes started falling apart. So, I ended up with something between mashed potatoes & potato salad, only far more garlicky, but very good. Oh, & I did add a tad of dried dill, sweet basil & white pepper. My son had wanted hamburgers, but I didn't want to serve the typical chips, or fries or macaroni & cheese with them, so when I found this recipe I thought it would be a nice fit, a little less plain. I also served it with my Caribbean Coleslaw recipe (#290325) which was nice & light which helped balance out the garlic flavor. For desert I served my Rocky Road Chocolate Mousse (#286486) which was nice, because it was cool & light, & we could each choose how much we wanted, I only had a little because by that time I was very full (duh).  Anyway, thanks for a great recipe that was simple and apparently infallible lol!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
yucatan marinade

from firehouse food. you can use this tangy marinade on chicken, pork, prawns, scallops, or any firm fleshed fish. makes about 1 cup which is enough for 3 pounds of poultry, meat, or seafood.

1. combine all ingredients in a medium bowl
2. if using with poultry or pork , marinate for 3 to 4 hours before grilling
3. fish and shellfish should marinate no longer than half an hour as the citrus will "cook" the seafood
demonstrations.review:
Awesome, awesome marinade!
Of course I love citrus, so I knew I'd like this. Ground, mexican oregano makes any mexican or southwestern dish better, lends a wonderful smoky flavor, very unlike regular oregano as we think of it in Italian food. The first time I identified it at a mexican restaurant, I spent the whole time trying to pinpoint the wonderful smoky, earthy flavor that I was tasting, once I figured it out, I made sure I always have it on hand for my mexican food cooking. Sorry, kind of got on an oregano tangent lol. Funny thing is, I am not crazy about regular oregano in italian food, I miss it if it's not there, but somehow it's just different. Needless to say, I added a little more oregano than 1 t to this recipe lol ;o)
Thanks~!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
curry dip ii

nan

1. mix all ingredients together and serve with fresh vegetables
2. let stand in refrigerator for 1 hour before serving
3. tastes better chilled
demonstrations.review: This recipe is very close, if not the same as how my mom has made this for years. It is absolutely fantastic, it  is great to take to parties with fresh veggies. I often make this to keep on hand in the fridge and buy an assortment of fresh veggies that I cut up & bag to go with it for snacking. It is also nice as a zippy sandwich spread. I really like curry, so I usually increase the amount of curry & add lemon or lime juice too. You just can't go wrong with this dip (if you like curry of course)!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
yucatan lime fish

saw this dish in a newspaper article about travelling in mexico, it reminded me of a dish i had in cozumel. it's a simple but different way to cook flounder and similar fish. easy to make too.

1. thinly slice garlic and saute in oil until crisp and brown
2. set aside
3. heat a large heavy pan on high heat and add oil until hot
4. add fish and jalepeno
5. saute fish until crispy on one side
6. do not disturb fish while cooking
7. fish need not be done at this point
8. lower heat to medium / low
9. squeeze juice from limes and add to pan
10. fish will now 'poach' in lime juice
11. remove fish when done and rest on a plate
12. add chopped cilantro , if using allow lime juice to thicken slightly and mingle with oil and fish juices
13. pour on top of fish and top with toasted garlic
demonstrations.review: I loved this! But I do love citrus. I added about 1/4 t of ground mexican oregano, because it makes anything mexican better with it's wonderful smoky flavor. I also added the cilantro right before serving, as I wanted it still fresh. Thanks!

target.recipe_text:
extra banana chocolate chip muffins

this is an adaptation of a recipe from another site.  it's called "extra banana muffins" because it has a lot more banana in it than most recipes- 2 1/3 cups! it smells really good while its baking. (note: chilling batter and filling the cups to the top is a must if you want dome tops!)

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. lightly grease muffins tins
3. in a large bowl , combine flour , baking soda , salt , cinnamon and nutmeg
4. in a separate bowl , cream together butter and brown sugar
5. stir in eggs and mashed bananas until well blended
6. stir flour mixture into banana mixture
7. stir just to moisten
8. stir in chocolate chips
9. chill batter at least 45 minutes in the fridge
10. fill muffin tins to the very top
11. sprinkle with cinnamon sugar mixture
12. bake in preheated oven for 30 minutes , or until a toothpick inserted into center of a muffin comes out clean
13. let cool in pan for 10 minutes , then turn out onto a wire rack
target.review: So delicious! I made the dough in the morning, covered it with plastic wrap and left it in the fridge when I went to work, and came home at the end of the day to make the muffins for dinner. It was such an easy way to have fresh muffins without having to put in a lot of effort right after work!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
japanese mum s chicken

we have a japanese girl, tomoko, living with us, and tonight she and i cooked a japanese dinner for us and her friends. she phoned her mum,toshiko, in japan for this, as it's her favourite recipe, and i wanted to share it here. it's simple and so good, and tomoko, who is only 16, did such a good job of cooking this, then translating the recipe to english for me.

*the liquid will thicken to a glaze if you are patient. it just takes a bit of time. if you feel your chicken is cooked (and going to overcook) remove it before going on to reduce the liquid. same thing, if you must use breast meat, remove it (so it doesn't dry out) and continue reducing the liquid . if you do it this way rather than thickening with cornstarch you will get a richer glaze and not need to add stock or broth instead of the water. it just takes patience. and note: a glaze is sticky and coats the meat, this is not a sauce.

1. place all the ingredients in a saucepan over a high heat
2. bring to the boil , then reduce to a simmer for about 20 minutes
3. remove any scum that rises to the surface
4. increase the heat , turning the drumsticks frequently in the liquid , and cook until the liquid has reduced to a sticky glaze
5. arrange the chicken on a serving platter , remove the garlic clove and chili from the liquid , and spoon the glaze over
demonstrations.review: My first flop in cooking with Food.com :-( I halved the balsamic vinegar and the sauce was still very runny. I feel bad to have wasted all that chicken but I just did not enjoy this. Thanks anyways for sharing.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
steak n shake 5 way chili

i got this from my brother who works at steak and shake up in missouri haha i love this chili best with their fries:)

1. in a skillet on medium low heat saut ground beef and onions
2. when beef has been cooked , drain all grease and place in a medium large sauce pan
3. add celery salt , tomato sauce , kidney beans , garlic powder , garlic salt , chili powder , pepper , water and salt , mix all ingredients
4. on low heat place a lid on sauce pan and simmer for one hour , stirring frequently
5. after chili has been cooking for a hour add tomato paste and stir well
6. place lid on pan and simmer an additional half hour
7. to assemble:
8. for individual serving :
9. in a shallow bowl or plate place:
10. generous helping of spaghetti
11. 3 / 4c chili
12. 2 tbs
13. chili sauce
14. chopped onions
15. 1 / 2c shredded monterey jack and colby cheese mix
16. top with additional onions to your taste
17. any leftover chili can be placed on crisp tortilla chips for a light lunch or a great snack
18. chili sauce can be purchased at most grocery stores in the condiement area
19. it is sold in a glass bottle , and looks somewhat like the old glass heinz ketchup bottles
demonstrations.review: Smelled great during the first hour of simmering, but after adding the tomato paste, it came to the consistency and taste of spaghetti sauce. It made me a little sick to eat it like that and ended up throwing the rest out. Probably won't attempt this again but thanks.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
creamy cajun chicken pasta

n'awlin's style of chicken with an updated alfredo sauce.

1. place chicken and cajun seasoning in a bowl and toss to coat
2. in a large skillet over medium heat , saut chicken in butter or margarine until chicken is tender , about 5 to 7 minutes
3. reduce heat add green onion , heavy cream , tomatoes , basil , salt , garlic powder , black pepper and heat through
4. pour over hot linguine and toss with parmesan cheese
demonstrations.review: Fantastic! Plenty of creamy sauce. Added a cup of milk to the one cup whipping cream; wouldn't change anything else :)

target.recipe_text:
easiest peanut butter fudge

this is unbelievably easy. i prefer using creamy peanut butter for this mouth-watering fudge. however, the chunky style works just as well.

1. in saucepan , bring sugar and milk to a boil
2. boil for 3 minutes
3. add peanut butter , marshmallow creme and vanilla
4. mix well
5. quickly pour into a buttered 8-inch square pan
6. chill until set
7. cut into squares
target.review: I bought ingredients for a different recipe but decided to use this one instead. The sugar crystalized as I was making it so it gave it a brownie type texture in the end. Still really good though. I topped it off with some chopped peanuts and I also replaced the milk with evaporated whole milk. Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
any fruit fast fat free cobbler

this fabulous dessert is 3 ww points a serving and can be made with fresh, canned, or frozen fruit. it is adapted from a recipe in the 

1. combine all of the ingredients except the fruit in a bowl
2. pour it into an 8x8 pan coated with cooking spray
3. add the fruit right on top
4. the crust will come up over the fruit and cover it
5. bake in a 350 degree oven for 40 minutes
demonstrations.review:
I had high hopes for this recipie but it tasted gross! I ate half of it because I didn't want to waste it and I just threw the other half away.

Ok I made this about 6 times and the first 6 times I still hated it. I never wanted to give up though so I tried again today but instead I put the batter on top of the fruit and it came out amazing! All crunchy and not soggy at all. Whoooo love it.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
bella s whole wheat belgian waffles

a good friend gave me this recipe and it produces a waffle that is more substantial. it's not super light and fluffy like other recipes. they are more like "eggo" waffles (in terms of texture, not sweetness). makes 16 (4 1/2" x 4") waffles. when preparing them for freezing, i undercook them slightly, so they don't burn in the toaster.

1. combine flour , sugar , baking powder and salt in a bowl
2. add milk , eggs and oil to the dry ingredients and mix until combined
3. use approximately 1 / 3 cup of batter per waffle
4. bake on waffle iron as per manufacturers instructions
5. i didn't really miss having salt in this recipe , but i thought the first reviewer of this recipe probably had a point about blandness , so i amended the recipe to include 3 / 4 teaspoon of salt
6. other comments have prompted me to add vanilla to the recipe , with wonderful results
7. thanks for your comments !
demonstrations.review: I did not really like the outcome the first time I tried this recipe with 1/2 applesauce and 1/2 oil. The second time I used all applesauce, a tablespoon of oatmeal and wheat bran, and pumpkin pie spice and it improved greatly. They came out nice and crispy, just how I like them!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
veggie pizza   no crust

i found this recipe while looking for low calorie meals.  i must say this was the best "pizza" i ever had!!  can be used as an appetizer or snack.  i use it in my low calorie diet as a dinner.

1. place the mushroom cap upside down on a cookie sheet
2. spread the marinara sauce over the mushroom , and top with the remaining ingredients - just like a normal pizza
3. bake in the oven at 350f until the cheese melts and the pizza is warmed through
demonstrations.review: This was super easy and tasted great! I had to use baby portabellos because thats all the store hand.

target.recipe_text:
outright oatmeal milk

this recipe is from the book "how it all vegan".

1. in a blender or food processor , puree all the ingredients until smooth
2. place in a container with a tight lid and refrigerate
3. it will keep approximately 4-6 days
target.review:
Thanks for posting this. They should make this commercially. Rice, soy, almond, etc. Why not oatmeal?! 

Well it was really thick so I let it set for a while and then strained all of the oatmeal out. It was really good though. Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cracked sugar cookies

my daughter and i wanted a soft and chewy cookies and after trying oodles of recipes we came up with this good sugar cookie

1. beat oleo until fluffy
2. gradually add sugars , beating well
3. add egg and vanilla , beat well
4. combine flour , soda , salt and cream of tartar
5. add gradually to creamed mixture
6. shape into 1-inch balls and roll in sugar
7. place on ungreased cookie sheet and bake at 325 for 10-12 minutes
demonstrations.review: I have been looking for a sugar cookie recipe to add to my other assorted cookies for gifts and these are as close as I am going to get. They were just right. I'm going to reduce the sugar and use a butter cream frosting. But yes I did have a SLIGHT problem with the tangy acid taste from the baking soda/cream of tartar. Of course I made them vegan. Thank you so much! I had little hope I would find a sugar cookie recipe like this.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
tsr version of ihop buttermilk pancakes by todd wilbur

from www.topsecretrecipes.com. these are my favorite pancakes...so light and fluffy.

1. preheat a skillet over medium heat
2. mix all of the ingredients til combined
3. melt a little bit of butter in the pan
4. pour the batter by spoonfuls into the hot pan , forming 5-inch circles
5. when the edges appear to harden , flip the pancakes
6. they should be golden brown
7. cook the pancakes on the other side until they are also golden brown
8. enjoy
demonstrations.review: The best pancake recipe I have found. I made mine vegan with egg re placer, soy butter milk, etc. So freaking good!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chewy vegan chocolate chocolate chip cookies

"these are brownie-like and chewy. be careful not to overbake them, they may seem like they aren't done after 10 minutes but they are! see the variations for chewy chocolate cherry cookies and chocolate hazelnut (or almond or walnut or whatever) cookies at the bottom of the directions." recipe from the post punk kitchen (www.theppk.com) and accredited to isa.

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. grind flax seeds in a blender until they become a fine powder , then add the soy milk and blend for about 30 seconds more and set aside
3. in a large bowl , sift together cocoa , flour , baking soda and salt
4. cream the sugar and oil in a separate large bowl
5. add the flax / soy milk mixture and mix well
6. stir in the vanilla
7. slowly mix in the dry ingredients
8. mix in the chocolate chips
9. roll dough into 1" balls and flatten into disks about 1 1 / 2" in diameter
10. place on an ungreased cookie sheet about 1" apart and bake for 10 minutes
11. let rest on the cookie sheet for about 5 minutes , then remove with a spatula to a cooling rack and cool completely
12. for chocolate chocolate chip cherry cookies , replace 1 teaspoon of the vanilla with almond extract , and use 3 / 4 cup chocolate chips and 3 / 4 cup chopped cherries
13. for chocolate nut cookies , replace 1 teaspoon of the vanilla with a nut extract and replace the chocolate chips with 1 1 / 2 cups chopped nuts of your choice
demonstrations.review:
These were so good!!!!! I used whole wheat and less oil, I also left out the chips seeing that I could not find vegan chips. You can omit the cocoa and you have a sugar cookie! I found this out when I made the recipe and forgot I did not have cocoa powder. Quite oily, that's why I used less oil and the consistency was better that way. 

I make these at least every month for people and myself. THANKS!!!

target.recipe_text:
tri color peppers in garlic  onions and tomatoes

generally a summer tapa (when peppers are abundant). they are colorful, taste great and make a great addition to your array of tapas. in addition this is a geat vegetarian topping to pasta or rice.

1. heat olive oil in large frying pan
2. add peppers and onions and cook gently for 2-3 minutes , stirring frequently
3. add parsley , cilantro and garlic and cook another 2-3 minutes
4. add chopped tomatoes and their juice to the pan , stir and season with salt and pepper
5. cover the pan and simmer for about 20 minutes or until the peppers are tender but somewhat crisp
6. the sauce should be somewhat thick
7. if too much liquid remains when the peppers are crisp tender , remove the peppers and onions and boil rapidly to reduce the liquid
8. check the seasoning again at this point
9. add the peppers and onions back into the sauce , if necessary
10. serve immediately
11. the dish may be made ahead of time and rewarmed when served
target.review: It was awesome.I used a yellow onion because thats what I had on hand. I also added a little zucchini as someone else did. Delicious! Thanks for the great idea for tri-colored peppers, which I loved! The picture doesn't do it justice. Went well with chicken spareribs and rice. I did reduce the liquid as suggested. It was wonderful.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
my best zucchini bread

this makes 2 loaves of the best zucchini bread i have ever tasted.

1. preheat oven to 350
2. in large bowl , mix sugar , oil , eggs , and vanilla
3. beat until well blended
4. add zucchini , applesauce and orange juice
5. stir well
6. combine flour with next 5 ingredients
7. add to zucchini mixture
8. stir well
9. add nuts
10. stir gently to combine
11. pour into 2 greased and floured 9in loaf pans
12. bake for 60-70 minutes
13. till toothpick comes out clean
14. let cool in pans 10 minutes
15. remove from pans and let cool completely
demonstrations.review: Perfect and yummy. I made my dad this for fathers day. I made 2 big and then three small loaves. I varied it only by topping one loaf with 1/2 cup of walnuts, one I made with raisins and I made a homemade chocolate frosting, then all three on one, powdered sugar on one since my kids don't like walnuts, Ours was gone in a day and I mailed 3 to my dad, brining one to hubby's dad on Sunday. I will make it again. Thank you!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chicken thigh spareribs well  sort of  lol

we love this chicken recipe. i don't know who it's from, but it's on a worn piece of paper in my recipe box. very tasty, and so easy. the sauce gets thick and coats the chicken so nicely. you can control the heat by increasing or decreasing the amount of pepper flakes.  i also like to add more garlic, about 5 cloves total.  great with rice and a steamed veggie, and the kids like it too.

1. in a large skillet , heat oil
2. add chicken and brown on both sides , for about 6-7 minutes
3. set aside cornstarch and the 1 tbsp water
4. in a mixing bowl , combine remaining ingredients and add to the chicken in the skillet
5. bring to a boil , cover and reduce heat , simmer for 20 minutes
6. in a small bowl , combine the tbsp of water and the cornstarch , add to the chicken and cook until the sauce thickens and coats the chicken pieces
demonstrations.review: I loved it. I followed the recipe exactly, using the bones to give you something to hold on to. The red peppers were just enough to leave a nice taste. I agree with others about the oriental flair. Plenty of sauce for rice, mine did thicken up nicely. I made tri- colored peppers with it along with long grain rice. Superb!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pork chops yum yum

i copied this from the orlando sentinel months ago and just now found it. we eat pork chops at least once a week and this is our favorite.

1. brown chops on both sides
2. place in greased casserole dish
3. mix all remaining ingredients and pour over pork chops
4. bake , uncovered , at 350 for one hour
demonstrations.review: Really a great recipe with stuff right on hand. Will definitely do it again! Like someone else, I used garlic instead of the garlic salt.. and I doubled the sauce because I had 7 -8 chops, but wished i had 4x it like Chef Steveo did! I also used a bit of  cornstarch at the end...and did it all stovetop as well. YUM YUM it IS! Fantastic recipe Brad!

target.recipe_text:
best cream of broccoli soup

this recipe is thick and flavorful. simple, delicious, and quick to make. hope that you enjoy it as much as my family does. i have added chicken to this soup, very good

1. melt 2 tablespoons butter in medium sized stock pot , and saut onion , garlic and celery until tender
2. add broccoli and broth
3. cover and simmer for 10 minutes
4. pure soup or mash with potato masher
5. return to heat
6. in small saucepan , over medium heat melt 3 tablespoons butter , stir in flour and add milk
7. stir until thick and bubbly , add to soup
8. add cheese
9. stir until melted
10. season with pepper and serve
target.review: Love it! Will now be a staple in my house.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s  brown sugar caramel sauce or ice cream topping

with only very few ingredients and five minutes to make it just couldn't get any easier and it tastes so good! ---it goes great with bread pudding, over ice cream and with desserts :)

1. in a small saucepan melt butter with salt
2. add the brown sugar
3. whisk until combined and thickened
4. whisk in the whipping cream , until thoroughly blended
5. mix in vanilla until combined
demonstrations.review:
OMG! This is fantastic!  I can't wait to drizzle it over a warm slice of apple pie.

I found this while trying to find a copycat for Harry&David's caramel sauce. This is awfully close!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mean guy s general tso s chicken

this is an adoptee.  i have made it many many times and want to be able to help people out when they make it!  one of the best i've ever had.  takes some time, but oh so worth it.   good eats ;-)

1. in a large bowl , thoroughly blend the 1 / 2 cup of cornstarch and the eggs
2. add the chicken and toss to coat
3. if the mixture is too thick , add some vegetable oil to separate the pieces
4. in a small bowl , prepare the sauce mixture by combining the 2 tsp cornstarch with the wine , vinegar , sugar and soy sauce
5. first-stage frying: heat 1-2 inches of peanut oil in a wok to medium-high heat
6. fry the chicken in small batches , just long enough to cook the chicken through
7. remove the chicken to absorbent paper and allow to stand
8. second-stage frying: leave a tablespoon or two of the oil in the wok
9. add the pepper pods to the oil and stir-fry briefly , awakening the aroma but not burning them
10. return the chicken to the wok and stir-fry until the pieces are crispy brown
11. the general's favorite sauce: add the sauce-mixture to the wok , tossing over the heat until the sauce caramelizes into a glaze
12. serve immediately
13. serves 4 , along with steamed broccoli and rice
demonstrations.review: Yummy! We love this one!  So much cheaper than going out and easy to make.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
banana banana bread

why compromise the banana flavor? my banana bread is moist and delicious with loads of banana flavor! ultimate comfort food, and it's wonderful toasted!! (make sure to use bananas with a lot of black on them for the best flavor! the blacker the bananas, the stronger the banana flavor of the bread.)

1. preheat oven to 350
2. lightly grease 9 x 5 loaf pan
3. in large bowl , combine flour , soda and salt
4. in separate bowl , cream together butter and brown sugar
5. stir in eggs and mashed bananas until well blended
6. stir banana mixture into flour mixture
7. stir just to moisten
8. pour batter into prepared loaf pan
9. bake in preheated oven for 60-65 minutes until a toothpick inserted into center of loaf comes out clean
10. let bread cool in pan for 10 minutes , then turn out onto a wire rack
demonstrations.review: Loved it! Will definitely add this to my regular rotation.  Easy, and sooo good for breakfast!

target.recipe_text:
pumpkin ginger scones with cinnamon chips

this is a delicious flavorful scone that is good at any time of year, not just in the fall and winter. enjoy for breakfast, with tea or coffee or even for dessert. makes a good gift, too.  just made them again for a friends birthday (1/09)  and mmmmm forgot how i love them so much.

1. combine 1 / 2 c sugar , flour , baking powder , cinnamon , baking soda and salt in a large bowl
2. cut 5 tbsp butter into dry ingredients until crumbly
3. in separate bowl combine the egg , pumpkin , sour cream and ginger
4. add wet ingredients to dry ingredients and mix well
5. mix in cinnamon chips
6. turn out on lightly floured surface and knead 10x
7. i add extra flour here as the dough is usually a bit moist
8. divide dough in half and form each half into a 1 / 2 inch thick circle
9. cut each circle into 8 wedges
10. brush wedges with melted butter and sprinkle with sugar
11. bake on ungreased cookie sheet in preheated 425 degree oven for 10 minutes or until lightly golden on edges
target.review: This is an absolute keeper!!  I've experimented with many scone recipes, and this one is always, always a big hit.  Great flavor and super easy to make.  A+++

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cinnamon mocha biscotti

delicious italian biscotti recipe that tastes like a cup of fresh cappuccino. great as a christmas gift too. just wrap a biscotto in cellophane and tie with a bow.

1. preheat oven to 325f on convection bake setting
2. combine butter , sugars and espresso or coffee granules in a large bowl and beat with an electric mixer until light and fluffy
3. add eggs , one at a time , beating well after each addition
4. add vanilla and mix briefly
5. add flour , baking powder , salt and cinnamon and mix until well blended
6. fold in pecans , chocolate morsels and cinnamon chips
7. line a baking sheet with parchment paper
8. scoop dough out onto paper and form into a large rectangle , -inch thick
9. bake 25 minutes , or until firm
10. remove from oven and cool 10 minutes
11. use a serrated knife to cut the dough into -inch thick slices
12. place on a parchment-lined baking sheet and return to the oven for 8 minutes
13. turn and bake 8 minutes more
14. remove from oven and cool completely on wire racks before storing in an airtight container
demonstrations.review: If I knew biscotti were so easy to make, I'd have made them years ago!  WONderful recipe!!  Ironically, I did not have any chocolate chips on hand but had a hearty supply of cinnamon chips, so I used double cinnamon and no chocolate.  I also substituted finely chopped walnuts instead of pecans only because that's what I had handy.  Bumping the conventional oven up to 350 degrees and keeping the same bake time worked out just fine, and I also split the dough into two loaves.  Someone mentioned using melted white chocolate to "repair" any broken pieces, which sounded brilliant!!  I will remember that tip for next time!  LOVED this recipe.  Thank you for sharing.  :)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
ground turkey and white bean chili

this delicious recipe is easy to prepare and very satisfying. it's also great for my south beach diet. it's based on a recipe in martha stewart's every day food magazine, but slightly modified.

1. heat canola oil in a dutch oven or deep skillet over medium high heat
2. add ground turkey and season with salt and pepper
3. cook until browned , stirring to break up turkey
4. add chopped onion and minced jalapeno and cook until soft , about 3 minutes
5. stir in ground cumin and tomato sauce and cook for 2 more minutes
6. add the cannellini beans , the broth and the water
7. bring to a boil
8. reduce heat and simmer until thicker , about 20 minutes
9. ladle into bowls and place a dollop of light sour cream and a sprinkling of chopped cilantro on top of each serving
demonstrations.review: Loved it ... thanks for sharing!!  I eliminated the 1 cup of water for a thicker chili (agreed w/other feedbacks that it could have been too soupy otherwise) and followed the rest of the recipe to the "T".  I let it simmer in a crock pot on low for about 4 hrs.  Super easy recipe with lots of flavor.  5 Stars :) !!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chicken curry in a hurry

watch out or you might get pulled over for a speeding ticket in the kitchen! ready in 20 minutes. :)

1. mix together flour , salt and cayenne pepper in a plastic bag
2. add chicken in small batches , shaking to coat
3. heat oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat
4. add chicken and cook until lightly browned
5. then add curry powder and toss to coat
6. remove from pan
7. add onion and garlic to pan , adding a little more oil if necessary , and cook for 2 minutes , then add broth , raisins , and tomato paste
8. return chicken to pan and simmer uncovered for 8 minutes or until chicken is cooked through and sauce has thickened
9. garnish with cilantro and a dollop of yogurt
10. serve with quick cooking minute rice , if desired
demonstrations.review: Absolutely fantastic!!  Followed the recipe exactly (minus the raisins).  Great spicy flavor.  Will definitely be hanging on to this in my "keeper" file :)

target.recipe_text:
the best easy beef and broccoli stir fry

i clipped this recipe from taste of home magazine several years ago and have found it to be the best-tasting easy beef and broccoli stir-fry. it is credited to ruth stahl. i often use charcoal chuck steak, which is very tender and lean. i also like that it doesn't call for any unusual ingredients.

1. in a bowl , combine 2 tablespoons cornstarch , 2 tablespoons water and garlic powder until smooth
2. add beef and toss
3. in a large skillet or wok over medium-high heat , stir-fry beef in 1 tablespoon oil until beef reaches desired doneness
4. remove and keep warm
5. stir-fry onion in remaining oil for 4-5 minutes until softened
6. add the broccoli and cook for 3 minutes until the broccoli is tender but still crisp
7. return beef to pan
8. combine soy sauce , brown sugar , ginger and remaining 1 tablespoon cornstarch and 1 / 2 cup water until smooth
9. add to the pan
10. cook and stir for 2 minutes
11. serve over rice and garnish with toasted sesame seeds
target.review: This is a great recipe! I will make again, maybe with chicken next time. Yum!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s easy and delicious ranch parmesan chicken

there are plenty versions of this recipe, this is mine and can be on your table in less that an hour, my family loves this chicken! --- the ranch dressing is the secret it holds in all the flavor and moistness while the chicken is baking and also adds flavor, i find that hidden valley ranch dressing works the best but kraft or any other brand will do, i sometimes top the baked chicken with mozzarella cheese or cheddar, but that is optional --- although i have only made this using breasts i imagine that chicken pieces could be used although you would have to increase the breadcrumb mixture slightly, you can marinate the chicken breast in the ranch dressing for a few hours in the fridge, although you will need more than 1 cup of dressing if you are marinating .... *note* to avoid a soggy bottom crust, place the chicken breasts onto a flat rack on top the baking sheet, also it is important not to bake the chicken in a small baking pan, if you do not have a rack bake on a large baking sheet so any juices in the pan will spread out and not accumulate under the chicken causing a soggy bottom ---------------
for low-fat option: use low-fat ranch dressing and omit the melted butter on top or use a healthy butter alternative such as smart balance 50/50 blend.

1. set oven to 400 degrees
2. in a shallow bowl mix together the dry breadcrumbs with parmesan cheese , seasoned salt , black pepper and garlic powder
3. dip the chicken into the ranch dressing to coat both sides
4. coat in the breadcrumb mixture
5. place in a single layer onto a greased baking sheet or line with non-stick foil
6. lightly drizzle the melted butter over each breast
7. if desired you can sprinkle black pepper over the chicken pieces
8. bake uncovered for about 30-35 minutes or until the chicken is cooked)
demonstrations.review: Will be making this again! Also will be sharing this with my coworkers as they are always looking for fast and simple dishes to make.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
oven fried chicken chimichangas

a fast and healthier way to serve chimichangas than the traditional deep fried. these are very good, and you may dress them up to you own preference. i like to serve with green chile sauce sometimes instead of the picante sauce.

1. mix chicken , picante sauce or salsa , cumin , oregano , cheese and onions
2. place about 1 / 4 cup of the chicken mixture in the center of each tortilla
3. fold opposite sides over filling
4. roll up from bottom and place seam-side down on a baking sheet
5. brush with melted margarine
6. bake at 400f for 25 minutes or until golden
7. garnish with additional cheese and green onion and serve salsa on the side
demonstrations.review:
Very simple, and great taste. I used the olive oil and it worked perfect. Next time I will add
the corn and black beans. Thank you for sharing.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crisp baked pork chops

nan

1. preheat oven to 400 degrees
2. coat a baking sheet with cooking spray
3. combine cornflake crumbs , flour , paprika , thyme , garlic powder , cumin , salt , pepper and sugar in a large resealable plastic bag
4. brush egg white over both surfaces of each chop
5. place them , 1 or 2 at a time , in bag with mix , and shake bag to thoroughly coat pork
6. bake for 15 to 18 minutes , or until the pork is cooked through to an internal temperature of 145 degrees
demonstrations.review: This recipe was very easy to make, makes your kitchen smell good while baking.  It was very tasty. Will be making it again very soon. (corrected spelling errors)

target.recipe_text:
chicken with banana curry sauce   caribbean

from food & wine.

1. heat the oven to 450
2. in a food processor or blender , puree the bananas , curry powder , coriander , dry mustard , butter , lime zest , lime juice , salt , pepper , and 1 / 4 cup of the water
3. make a few deep cuts in each chicken breast and put the breasts in a roasting pan
4. pour the curry sauce over the chicken , making sure the sauce gets into the cuts
5. roast in the bottom third of the oven until the chicken is just done , about 20 minutes
6. remove the roasting pan from the oven and remove the chicken breasts from the pan
7. there should be plenty of thick sauce in the bottom of the pan
8. set the pan over moderate heat and whisk in the remaining 1 / 2 cup water
9. continue to whisk until the sauce is heated through , adding more water if you want a thinner sauce
10. serve the chicken breasts with the sauce over them
11. sprinkle with parsley if you like
12. serve with steamed rice
target.review: What an absolutely delicious alternative to an Indian curry. I added more lime as I'm a fan of slightly acidic flavour combined with the sweetness of the banana. Served with basmati rice, and chopped cucumber and tomato. Top marks !

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chicken   butternut pasta with creamy sage sauce

tasty and quick.

1. heat the oven to 400f toss the squash in 1 tsp oil and
2. roast in the oven for 25 mins stirring half way through
3. while the squash is cooking , heat the remaining oil in a large frying pan , throw in the onion and saut for 5 mins until soft , add the chicken and cook for a further 5 mins until browned all over
4. pour in the broth and simmer until the chicken is cooked through and the broth has reduced
5. while the chicken is cooking , cook the pasta according to the pack instructions then drain
6. add in the roasted squash to the chicken then the sage and cheese stir well
7. add 2 spoonfuls of the sauce to the pasta and stir inches divide the pasts between 4 plates and top with the chicken
demonstrations.review: Great taste and easy to make, liked the combination of the butternut texture combined with the soft pasta and chicken. I used dried sage instead, which gave the menu quite a sweet and fragrant flavour.... Will defiantly be making this again

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cinnamon raisin bread for the bread machine

nan

1. add all the ingredients in order given except the raisins
2. add raisins in on the "add in" beep
3. bake on "sweet bread" setting
demonstrations.review: Tasted great, but unfortunately it didn't rise. Will definitely be trying again, but will activate the yeast first and reduce the salt as it was a bit too salty.... But that's perhaps because it didn't rise?

demonstrations.recipe_text:
japanese mum s chicken

we have a japanese girl, tomoko, living with us, and tonight she and i cooked a japanese dinner for us and her friends. she phoned her mum,toshiko, in japan for this, as it's her favourite recipe, and i wanted to share it here. it's simple and so good, and tomoko, who is only 16, did such a good job of cooking this, then translating the recipe to english for me.

*the liquid will thicken to a glaze if you are patient. it just takes a bit of time. if you feel your chicken is cooked (and going to overcook) remove it before going on to reduce the liquid. same thing, if you must use breast meat, remove it (so it doesn't dry out) and continue reducing the liquid . if you do it this way rather than thickening with cornstarch you will get a richer glaze and not need to add stock or broth instead of the water. it just takes patience. and note: a glaze is sticky and coats the meat, this is not a sauce.

1. place all the ingredients in a saucepan over a high heat
2. bring to the boil , then reduce to a simmer for about 20 minutes
3. remove any scum that rises to the surface
4. increase the heat , turning the drumsticks frequently in the liquid , and cook until the liquid has reduced to a sticky glaze
5. arrange the chicken on a serving platter , remove the garlic clove and chili from the liquid , and spoon the glaze over
demonstrations.review: Simple, tasty and quick.... What a great combination, my only problem was getting the sauce to thicken. Added a little extra dried chilli to the sauce, but that's just a personal preference. Great served with rice and mixed fried veg.

target.recipe_text:
split pea soup  crock pot    dairy free

very little prep, just layer in crock pot/slow cooker, leave it for the day and a filling, delicious soup will be ready for dinner.

this recipe is a very versatile base split pea soup.  for a vegan option, omit the meat. i have made this recipe using ham, ham hock, and bacon. i have used veggie broth, chicken broth and water... each tasting different but yummy! i have reduced the salt but have not adjusted the recipe as written. this soup is even better the next day, it freezes well. this tends to be a thicker soup (especially once it has cooled) so adjust liquid after cooking to desired thickness.

1. layer ingredients in crockpot
2. pour in water , so don't stir
3. cover and cook on high 4-5 hours or on low for 8-10 hours
4. remove bay leaf
5. serve with some nice crusty bread or buns
target.review: This was very simple but very delicious.  I used a smoked ham hock instead of diced ham and the soup was a keeper.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
gourmet mushroom risotto

in college, my friend angela and i went to visit her granny.  she made this for us.  it was the first time i'd ever experienced anything like it.  it was delicious and her granny gladly gave me the recipe.

1. heat the broth over low heat
2. in a large saucepan , heat 2 tablespoons of oil and cook the mushrooms until soft
3. about 3 minute
4. put the mushrooms and the liquid in a bowl and set aside
5. add the remaining 1 tablespoons oil to skillet , and cook the shallots for 1 minute
6. stir in the rice , coating it with oil , about 2 minutes
7. when the rice has taken on a pale , golden color , add the wine , stirring constantly until it is fully absorbed
8. add 1 / 2 cup broth to the rice , and stir until the broth is absorbed
9. continue adding broth 1 / 2 cup at a time , stirring continuously , until the liquid is absorbed and the rice is tender-firm
10. remove from heat , and stir in mushrooms with their liquid , butter , chives , and parmesan
11. season with salt and pepper to taste
demonstrations.review: This was my first risotto but if I hadn't said so no one would have known.  My fiance is a total foodie and praised its "clean, smooth taste."

demonstrations.recipe_text:
peta s pancakes

vegan pancakes from the good people at peta. for an added treat, stir bits of fresh or dried fruit, nuts, or-yum!-chocolate chips into the batter.

1. combine the flour , sugar , baking powder , and salt in a bowl and mix thoroughly
2. mix in the soy milk and oil , and , with an electric mixer or wire whisk , beat just until the batter is smooth
3. measure 1 / 3 cup batter onto a hot , oiled griddle
4. when bubbles appear on the upper surface of the pancake , lift with a spatula and flip the pancake
5. cook the pancake for another 2 minutes
6. remove from the pan and keep warm while you make the remaining pancakes
7. serve warm with maple syrup or fruit syrup
demonstrations.review: These were really nice and filling too.  I substituted spelt flour and vanilla soymilk but omitted the oil which worked great.  Two tablespoons of baking powder seemed overkill so I only put in one and the batter almost rose over the edge of my bowl.  Next time I'll add only half a tablespoon.  If I hadn't made them myself I never could have guessed there were no eggs or milk.  Thanks PETA!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
rote rubensalat  red beet salad

nan

1. wash beets , trim off greens , place in medium saucepan , and cook , without peeling , in salted water to cover , until beets are tender
2. peel and slice
3. prepare marinade dressing by combining remaining ingredients
4. pour over beets and let stand for several hours before serving
5. stir beets occasionally
demonstrations.review: After initially mixing all the ingredients and tasting I was a bit sceptical.  However, after several hours in the fridge everything really pulled together quite nicely.  I used olive oil instead of vegetable and omitted half the caraway as for my personal preference.  Guten appetit!

target.recipe_text:
green peas and mushrooms

this comes from "light and easy diabetes cuisine" by betty marks. i prefer to use fresh green peas if i have them; but it works well with frozen too.

1. in a saucepan , bring water to a boil , add peas and
2. cook 5 minutes or until just tender
3. drain thoroughly
4. while peas are cooking , heat oil in a non-stick skillet and saute mushrooms and green onions until tender
5. combine with peas and toss with soy sauce
6. serve immediately
target.review: Very easy, very quick, and very good. I actually used canned peas and it worked fairly well, although I'm sure fresh or frozen are much better. Thank you for this healthy side dish!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mean chef s oatmeal pecan chocolate chunk cookies

amazingly soft, delicious cookies! when i made this, i used ghirardelli chocolate and was just short on the called-for amount of pecans. the dough was really hard after refrigerating overnight, and i found it easier to roll it into balls by hand rather than the ice cream scoop. i adopted this recipe after its original poster, mean chef, departed the site. mean posted the recipe on feb 12, 2003.

1. in a medium bowl , whisk together flour , salt , baking powder , and baking soda
2. set dry ingredients aside
3. in the bowl of an electric mixer , combine butter with both sugars
4. beat until light and fluffy
5. add vanilla , milk , and eggs
6. mix well
7. add reserved dry ingredients , and beat until just combined
8. remove bowl from mixer , and fold in oats , chocolate , and pecans
9. place dough in the refrigerator until firm , at least 2 hours or overnight
10. heat oven to 350
11. line two baking sheets with parchment paper , and set aside
12. remove dough from refrigerator
13. using an ice-cream scoop , shape into 2-inch-diameter balls
14. place six balls on each baking sheet , spaced 4 inches apart , and press down transfer to oven
15. bake until golden , but still soft in center , 15 to 16 minutes
16. remove from oven , and place on a wire rack to cool completely
17. repeat with remaining dough
18. store in an airtight container up to 2 days
demonstrations.review: These are exactly what I needed! I was craving monster cookies but knew my brother would be upset if I would have finished off the peanut butter so I decided not to make them. I saw this recipe and I am SO happy because these have the texture of monster cookies. They also taste similar because I added m&m's and white chocolate chips in place of the nuts. I was forced to use our small toaster oven in place of the conventional oven so I lowered the temperature to 300 for the majority of the baking and then raised it to 350 for about 3 minutes just to brown the cookies. They turned out perfectly crisp on the outside and chewy on the inside! Thank you so much newspapergal!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
honey mustard vinaigrette   weight watchers

i have not tried this recipe. i got it from weight watchers. points® value 2 per serving.

1. in a small bowl , whisk the lemon juice , mustard , honey , dill and salt
2. whisk in the oil in a slow stream , then whisk in the water until smooth
3. serving size: 1 1 / 2 tablespoons
demonstrations.review: As written, it had too much lemon for my taste so I added a little more honey which was much better. I probably added a full tablespoon or 1 1/2 tbsp total. Thanks Internetnut, for the quick dressing.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
paula s shrimp and sausage pasta

this is a recipe i came up with to surprise my husband. his favorite foods are all in here! if i have fresh mushrooms on hand, i will slice and saute them into the dish as well.

1. drizzle sliced peppers with 2 tablespoons olive oil
2. in a 450 oven , roast red peppers for 30 to 45 minutes , turning occasionally until charred slightly
3. cook whole sausages until no longer pink
4. allow sausage to cool slightly , then slice
5. in a large skillet , saut minced garlic , shallot in remaining olive oil
6. add parsley , thyme , bouillon cube , italian seasoning , and wine
7. once the bouillon cube has dissolved , add shrimp
8. continue cooking until shrimp are pink and wine has reduced a bit
9. add peppers and sausage
10. stir to heat through
11. swirl in the butter
12. season to taste for salt and pepper
13. serve over linguini , giving a toss to incorporate sauce throughout
14. sprinkle with cheese
demonstrations.review: This definitely went beyong all expectations. The only problem I had was, the roasting time stated was too long in my oven. I tossed the peppers after 15 minutes and then checked on them again right at 30 minutes, but by that point quite of few of the peppers had burnt. My suggestion would just be to check on the peppers at 20 or 25 minutes. I served this with whole wheat pasta which was an absolutely outstanding complimentary flavor. Everyone absolutely loved this. You have a winner here, Paula! Thank you!

target.recipe_text:
plum kuchen

luscious coffeecake adapted from squalicum lake cottage bed and breakfast in bellingham, wa. the recipe was published in a lovely cookbook, northwest mornings, given to me in a zaar swap by my good friend lulu b.

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. mix flour , 1 tablespoon sugar and baking powder together
3. cut in butter until mixture looks like coarse crumbs
4. add 2 tablespoons heavy cream and 1 egg
5. press in bottom of 9-inch square pan or pie pan and arrange plums on top
6. bake for 25-30 minutes
7. while this is baking , in a bowl combine heavy cream , sugar , egg and vanilla , using a whisk to beat together well
8. pour mixture over plums and bake an additional 20-30 minutes , until custard is set
9. serve warm or cool
10. store in refrigerator
target.review: This is quite good, although a little sweeter than I expected. Also, when I added the custard filling to the hot tart, a lot of it seeped into the crust making it very, very dense. I was looking forward to the first shortcake type of crust. Next time, for a less sweet version, I might try it without the custard and just top it with real whipped cream as I serve it.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
linda s chinese duck sauce

i use this on crab rangoon, chicken fingers, spare ribs, egg rolls, marinated chicken wings, beef teriyaki, chicken teriyaki, and of course rice.

1. combined all ingredients in a med-sized pan , and bring to a boil
2. turn the heat down , and simmer uncovered until all the fruit is very soft , about 30 mins
3. , or longer
4. when room temperature , mix well
5. put in a container , and store in the refrigerator
demonstrations.review: I made this sauce with plums and apples to go with homemade Chinese egg rolls.  It had a nice flavor; but the texture was more like baby food applesauce than duck sauce.  It reminded me of apple butter - not at all what I want on my egg rolls. I guess I was expecting more of a glaze consistency and less of a puree.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
skillet chicken marsala

this is a quick one skillet recipe for chicken marsala. can be served over hot cooked pasta and you have an easy meal for a weeknight when you have little time to prepare a great meal.

1. flatten each chicken breast half to 1 / 4-inch thickness by gently pounding between sheets of plastic wrap or waxed paper
2. mix four , salt and pepper
3. coat chicken with flour mixture
4. shake off excess flour
5. heat oil in 10-inch skillet over medium-high heat
6. cook garlic and parsley in oil for 5 minutes , stirring frequently
7. add chicken to skillet
8. cook , turning once , until brown
9. add mushrooms and wine
10. cook 8 to 10 minutes , turning chicken once , until chicken is no longer pink in center
demonstrations.review: Delicious!  I made enough for 18 guests who simply loved it. I had 9 huge breasts which I halved. I omitted the flour and just browned the chicken in butter; then I placed it in a slow cooker.  Next I browned the mushrooms in 4 Tablespoons butter and added 1 cup of Marsala Wine. Then I mixed 1/4 cup of flour into 1 cup of cream and 1 T lemon juice.  I poured all onto the chicken, covered the slow cooker and cooked on low for 1 hour until it was time to serve.  Leftovers heated up well in microwave.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
beef rouladen

this recipe, from the dec/jan 1996 issue of taste of home has been a family favorite since the first time i made it. it does require a little effort, but it's worth every minute. i make this on a regular basis, as well as when we have company over. i always serve homemade dinner rolls with it but traditionally it may have been served with potato dumplings. i usually will slice my 8 meat slices in half, lengthwise, to create 16 smaller slices, which are easier to handle.  *note:  most recipes include a dill pickle slice in each roll, and after trying it with pickles my family loves this recipe even more!  i've added the pickle as an optional ingredient.  :)

1. spread mustard on one side of each slice of meat
2. sprinkle with salt and pepper
3. place one strip of bacon , dill pickle slice , and a few onion wedges on each slice of meat
4. roll up and secure with wooden toothpicks
5. put oil in dutch oven or other large pan and brown meat
6. drain
7. add broth and bring to a boil
8. reduce heat and cover and simmer for 1-1 / 2 hours or until meat is tender
9. remove meat and keep warm
10. combine flour and water until smooth and slowly stir into broth
11. bring to a boil , stirring constantly until thickened
12. remove wooden pics from meat and return to gravy
13. heat through
14. sprinkle with parsley if desired
demonstrations.review: Yum! These were gobbled up at my VAlentine Dinner Party.  I omitted the mustard but added a  4 inch finger size carrot and a similar size slice of potato to each roll. I tied all 20 with cooking twine and browned them before placing them in a slow cooker.  I covered them with Swanson hot beef broth and cooked on low for 3-4 hours then I thickened the gravy.  Perfection!  Thanks for a lovely recipe.

target.recipe_text:
strawberry   cream pinwheel appetizers

these little treats were created for rsc #11. i hope you will enjoy these light tasting appetizers, as much as we did.

1. in a large bowl , mix the cream cheese and goat cheese together , blending well , next add the milk , honey and key lime rind
2. once the cheese mixture is creamy add the coarsely chopped pecans and place in the fridge to chill for 30 minutes
3. thinly slice the strawberries and set a side until needed
4. remove the crusts from the bread
5. with a rolling pin flatten the bread slices , horizontally and vertically
6. spread 1 tablespoon of the cream cheese mixture on the prepared bread slices
7. place a piece of plastic wrap on table and place the bread on top of the plastic wrap
8. in the middle of the bread place two rows of of the thinly sliced strawberries
9. gently roll the bread into a log , cover the log with the plastic wrap , do this for each slice
10. chill the covered , cream cheese logs in the fridge for 3 hours or overnight , for the flavors to blend
11. remove the logs from fridge , take off the plastic and gently slice the logs with a bread knife
12. you should get four slices from each bread log
13. enjoy , enjoy , enjoy
target.review: Yummy! I made these for a Baby Shower and they were a hit! I loved the goat cheese mixture, much nicer than plain cream cheese... 5 stars for RSC!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
easy meatballs

an easy but good recipe for meatballs. i triple the recipe and freeze the meatballs.

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees
2. in large bowl combine egg , water , bread crumbs , onion , salt and pepper and combine
3. add ground beef , broken into chunks , and mush with your hands to combine
4. form into meatballs about 1" in diameter and place on a broiler pan
5. bake at 350 degrees for 25-30 minutes until meatballs are no longer pink in center
6. cool and use or freeze
demonstrations.review: I made this recipe for 1-2-3 Hit Wonders. It was a wonderful, moist, firm meatball. I made a double batch and added a hint of garlic because of my own personal preference. Thanks for the Great Recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
asparagus with lemon basil gouda cheese sauce

fresh bright green asparagus is just wonderful and adding a nice cheese and lemon flavored sauce, topped with sun dried tomatoes and pine nuts… not only is an appealing dish to the eye, but tasty as well! this recipe was made especially for the rsc# 11 contest.

1. place the asparagus in a microwave proof plate , sprinkle with salt water , use plastic wrap to cover , then reserve
2. combine the basil leaves , shallots , garlic , cayenne pepper and puree in a food blender
3. in a non-stick pot place 2 tablespoons margarine , pureed basil leaves and cook briefly
4. add -1 / 2 stock , bring to a boil , add lemon juice and salt to taste , add corn starch mixture and stir until smooth and very thick , let cool for about a minute
5. cook the asparagus in the microwave for 3 to 3-1 / 2 minutes
6. as the asparagus is being cooked in the microwave , add the egg yolks a little at a time to the sauce , blend , stirring with a whisk and make sure there are no lumps
7. remove the plastic wrap from the asparagus dish and discard the water
8. pour the sauce over the asparagus , sprinkle the grated cheese over the asparagus sauce
9. then place the plate under a broiler or in a toaster over for a minute or so in order for the cheese to melt
10. finally , sprinkle pine nuts and sun dried-tomatoes on top
11. serve and enjoy !
demonstrations.review:
Sinful!
Loved this decadent side dish...
The sauce was fantastic and I can't wait to try this again on top of other foods... (would be excellent on chicken breasts.).
5 stars for RSC

demonstrations.recipe_text:
orange cranberry pull apart coffee cake

the idea for this recipes comes for mary tallman of arbor vitae, wi.  her recipe was printed in may/june 2007 toh--simple and delicious.  i changed from lemon to orange, used cranberries and pecans and reduced the amount of glaze.  so easy and so delicious.

1. preheat oven to 400 and spray a 9-inch round cake pan with a non-stick baking cooking spray
2. in a medium size bowl , combine the sugar , pecans , cranberries , butter and orange zest
3. open the biscuits , separate and cut into fourths
4. toss the biscuits with the sugar mixture and pour into prepared pan
5. place in preheated oven and bake for 20 to 25 minutes
6. turn out on a dinner plate and immediately drizzle with glaze
7. serve warm
demonstrations.review:
Made for 1-2-3 Hit Wonders....
What a wonderful Coffee Cake! I used 1/3 cup of the pecans and omitted the glaze - it was perfect!
We had this for brunch this morning, it was easy to make and everyone loved it. Definately a brunch keeper! Thanks for the great recipe.

target.recipe_text:
irish champ  mashed potatoes

one of the favorite irish ways to serve potatoes. for a change try adding any of these:leeks, nettles, peas, or brown crispy onions.  instead of the green onions i added frozen peas after mashing the potatoes with the hot milk and then kept the potatoes hot looked and tasted great

1. finely chop the green onions and mix with the cold milk
2. bring slowly to a boil and simmer 3-4 minutes , turn off the heat and leave to infuse
3. peel and mash the cooked potatoesand while still hot mix with the boiled milk& green onions
4. beat in some of the butter
5. season with salt& pepper
6. put a knob of butter on top& serve
7. you can do this recipe ahead and reheat in a 350f oven , covered with foil until hot
target.review: This is an amzing dish. Warming the milk (I sometimes use cream) with the green onions makes the flavor so intense. I use red potatoes and the added color of their skins is nice. I think Yukon Gold potatoes would be delicious too.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
brussels sprouts

this is positively the ultimate recipe yet for brussel sprouts and the taste is unbelievable. once again my wonderful girlfriend betty passed this recipe onto me. bon appetit!

1. parboil the brussel sprouts for 7 minutes and drain
2. place into a 2-3 quart oven proof dish
3. saute the onion in butter until clear and then add the flour and stir
4. add the warm milk , salt , pepper , nutmeg , 3 / 4 cup cheese and stir
5. pour filling over brussel sprouts
6. top with remaining 3 / 4 cup cheese and bake at 375 for 40 minutes
7. this can be prepared and frozen until needed
demonstrations.review:
Can't wait to try this. One suggestion in answer to Brenda's comment: Maybe the "missing" thing is a splash of lemon juice. It helps with stronger tasting vegetables like this.
P.S. I did try it- and it got rave reviews!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
fillet of sole in white wine

this is a low carb recipe.

1. preheat oven to 375 degrees
2. wash and dry fillets and season with salt and pepper
3. arrange fillets in a buttered baking dish in a single layer and sprinkle with the green onions , melted butter , wine , parsely , thyme , and bay leaves
4. cover with greased paper facing down , then cover dish and bake 20 minutes
5. carefully remove fillets from baking dish
6. strain pan juices into a small saucepan , add 1 tablespoon butter , and let melt
7. blend in the flour , add the cream , and cook 4 minutes
8. pour over fish and serve
demonstrations.review: You can use flounder, whiting or halibut as well. Probably any good white fish. This is very similar to the recipe in Julia Child's cookbook. Delicious.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kohlrabi   carrots

kohlrabi is another veggie that seems hidden away. it has a mild turnip flavour and is delicious mixed with carrot or on it's own. use it raw, chopped in a green salad. it' very, very good and a nice change. you may  substitute turnip for the kohlrabi in this recipe

1. cover the kohlrabi and carrots with lightly salted water and boil until quite tender
2. drain
3. lightly mash , leave a lot of texture don't try to make them smooth like mashed potatoes
4. add nutmeg and butter
5. serve
demonstrations.review: Very good! I loved the nutmeg. I used a bit of fresh ground nutmeg. The combination of the sweet carrots with the broccoli-like kohlrabi was delicious. Bergy always has great recipes!!

target.recipe_text:
grilled maple chipotle pork chops on smoked gouda grits

from southern living.  the sweetness of the pork and the salty of the gouda grits make this a perfect combination.

1. whisk together first 4 ingredients , and set aside
2. sprinkle pork chops evenly with salt and pepper
3. grill , covered with grill lid , over medium-high heat 20 minutes or until a meat thermometer inserted into thickest portion registers 155 , turning once
4. baste with half of barbecue sauce mixture the last 5 minutes of cooking or when meat thermometer registers 145
5. spoon smoked gouda grits evenly onto 6 serving plates
6. top each with a pork chop , and drizzle evenly with remaining barbecue sauce mixture
7. gouda grits:
8. bring first 4 ingredients to a boil in a medium saucepan
9. gradually whisk in grits
10. cover , reduce heat , and simmer , stirring occasionally , 5 minutes or until thickened
11. add cheese and butter , stirring until melted
target.review: While a good recipe, I don't think I'll ever make it again. I didn't particularly love the grits (I may just not be a grits person.) but the pork chops were actually pretty great. So if you love grits, this is probably a great recipe for you.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chicken  shrimp and andouille jambalaya

a cajun classic, meal in one pot! have the hot sauce ready to splash on. serve with some crusty french bread, a nice crisp salad, and some of your favorite wine. :)

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees f
2. in a large pan or dutch oven , brown chicken in hot oil on both sides
3. remove and drain
4. add andouille , onion , celery , bell pepper , thyme , oregano , paprika , salt , and cayenne pepper to the pan , cooking and stirring for about 5 minutes until onions are tender
5. add rice , tomatoes with juice , and broth
6. bring to a boil
7. place rice mixture in a baking dish or oven-proof casserole
8. top with chicken
9. cover and bake at 350 degrees f for 40-45 minutes or until rice and chicken are done and tender
10. stir in shrimp , parsley , and green onions
11. cover and cook 5-8 minutes longer or until shrimp curl and turn bright pink and serve
demonstrations.review: So simple, yet so delicious! The only thing I did differently than the recipe was not adding shrimp. I'm sure shrimp would have been delicious if fresh but all I can really get where I am is frozen. Highly recommend this recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
japanese mum s chicken

we have a japanese girl, tomoko, living with us, and tonight she and i cooked a japanese dinner for us and her friends. she phoned her mum,toshiko, in japan for this, as it's her favourite recipe, and i wanted to share it here. it's simple and so good, and tomoko, who is only 16, did such a good job of cooking this, then translating the recipe to english for me.

*the liquid will thicken to a glaze if you are patient. it just takes a bit of time. if you feel your chicken is cooked (and going to overcook) remove it before going on to reduce the liquid. same thing, if you must use breast meat, remove it (so it doesn't dry out) and continue reducing the liquid . if you do it this way rather than thickening with cornstarch you will get a richer glaze and not need to add stock or broth instead of the water. it just takes patience. and note: a glaze is sticky and coats the meat, this is not a sauce.

1. place all the ingredients in a saucepan over a high heat
2. bring to the boil , then reduce to a simmer for about 20 minutes
3. remove any scum that rises to the surface
4. increase the heat , turning the drumsticks frequently in the liquid , and cook until the liquid has reduced to a sticky glaze
5. arrange the chicken on a serving platter , remove the garlic clove and chili from the liquid , and spoon the glaze over
demonstrations.review: Yum yum yum! Couldn't have loved this more! Just be prepared for a messy meal and have the napkins ready. I chose to double the sauce to put over rice and I don't actually think that was the right decision, it really is best as a glaze. Served with snow peas (great choice) and white rice, which probably wasn't the perfect pairing. Next time I'll pair this dish with something other than white rice...just not sure what yet. Maybe a light Asian soup or salad...

demonstrations.recipe_text:
southwestern stuffed bell peppers

simple preparation & delicious taste! use a mixture of red, green, yellow & orange peppers for a colourful presentation. recipe #2642 instead of store-bought taco seasoning mix--it makes this dish even better!

1. combine beef , onion , seasoning mix and egg in a large bowl
2. add rice and mix well
3. cut peppers in half lengthwise
4. remove seeds and membrane
5. spread tomatoes on the bottom of an ovenproof 12 x 9 inch baking dish
6. the liquid from the tomatoes will reduce during cooking so if you like lots of sauce , add about a cup of water
7. this also helps make the peppers softer
8. place peppers , cut side up , on top of the tomatoes
9. spoon beef mixture into peppers , mounding as necessary
10. top each pepper with salsa
11. bake in preheated 375f oven for 40-45 minutes or until beef is cooked thoroughly and peppers are soft
12. cover each pepper with cheese and return to oven , under the broiler , until the cheese melts- less than a minute , so watch carefully !
13. serve with sour cream and additional salsa
demonstrations.review: This turned out great!! I think next time I'd make just a couple changes to the recipe to make it even better. I'd take out about one cup of the rice and add a half cup of corn. When I made this, I had way too much filling and wished I had less rice for sure. Adding corn, I hope, would give it an even better texture. Plus who can go wrong with corn in a southwestern dish? The sour cream with this dish is an absolute must and I'm not even a sour cream lover!

target.recipe_text:
apple ginger scones

use a firm eating apple for this recipe. braeburn, gala, granny smith and haralson are all good choices. soft or excessively juicy apples will add too much moisture.

1. heat oven to 400 degrees
2. spray cooking sheet with nonstick cooking spray
3. combine flour , sugar , baking powder and salt in a medium bowl
4. mix well
5. cut in butter with a pasty blender or a fork until mixture resembles coarse crumbs
6. stir in apple and ginger
7. beat eggs in a small bowl
8. stir in cream and lemon peel
9. add to dry ingredients
10. stir just until moistened
11. gently knead dough 5 or 6 times on a lightly floured surface
12. place dough on the prepared cookie sheet pressing into an 8 inch round about 1 inch thick
13. cut into 8 wedges seperating slightly
14. bake for 15 to 20 minutes or until light golden brown and center is set
15. glaze: combine powdered sugar and lemon juice
16. blend well
17. drizzle warm scones with glaze
18. serve warm
target.review:
These have a great, complicated flavor. I had some trouble with quantities though - I had to add another half cup of flour to get the dough to the right texture. Once I'd done that, they turned out very tasty.

I just baked them on a non-stick pan, no spray or anything, and had no problems with them sticking.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chewy cocoa brownies

taken from http://www.verybestbaking.com/

1. preheat oven to 350 f
2. grease 13 x 9-inch baking pan
3. combine sugar , butter and water in large bowl
4. stir in eggs and vanilla extract
5. combine flour , cocoa , baking powder and salt in medium bowl
6. stir into sugar mixture
7. stir in nuts
8. spread into prepared baking pan
9. bake for 18 to 25 minutes or until wooden pick inserted in center comes out slightly sticky
10. cool completely in pan on wire rack
11. sprinkle with powdered sugar
12. cut into bars
demonstrations.review: These were just about perfect brownies! I loved the texture. They were very brownie-like, not cake-like. I added butterscotch chips, which actually made them too sweet, but that's not the fault of the recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
new orleans corn pudding souffle

a creamy buttery corn pudding with a "brulee" topping.  this pudding may be made ahead without the topping, chilled, and reheated - and then the topping prepared just before serving!

1. heat butter and sugar together in a saucepan until butter is melted
2. add flour and stir until combined
3. remove pan from heat
4. gradually stir in the cream , then add eggs , baking powder and salt
5. mix well
6. stir in corn and pour into a greased 2 quart baking dish
7. bake at 350 for 45 minutes
8. the mixture should slightly "wobble" in the center
9. for the topping: combine melted butter , brown sugar , and cinnamon
10. spread over baked souffle and broil for 5
demonstrations.review: This was a huge hit at Thanksgiving. I second the commenter who said it seems like a weird combo but tastes great.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
bobby flay s shrimp and grits

this yankee loves this stuff! good simple down home food

1. melt butter and oil in large saucepan
2. add onion and garlic , cook until softened
3. add milk , water and 1 tsp salt , bring to boil
4. slowly whisk in grits and bring to boil
5. reduce heat to simmer and cook 15-20 mins until thickening , whisking every few minutes
6. add cheese to melt , stirring , add salt& pepper to taste
7. for shrimp--
8. heat a pan to smoking , add bacon , cook until brown , remove and drain on paper towels
9. remove all but 3 tbsp of fat , add shrimp
10. cook until pink
11. serve shrimp over grits in soup plates , garnish with bacon and scallions
demonstrations.review: I used the grits recipe and then just spiced the shrimp my own way. The grits were very rich and creamy and perfect with the shrimp.

target.recipe_text:
kittencal s caesar tortellini salad

my family *loves* this salad, i make often in the summer with sweet cherry tomatoes from my garden, feel free to adjust all ingredient amounts and add in other ingeredints also, you can sub feta for parmesan, use your favorite caesar dressing or use my  recipe#116849. prep time does not include cooking the tortellini.

1. in a medium bowl combine the cooked tortellini with chopped lettuce , caesar dressing and parmesan cheese
2. toss well to coat
3. season with black pepper to taste and salt if desired
4. top with sliced cherry tomatoes and croutons
5. serve immediately
6. delicious !
target.review: This was easy and delicious!!!! We are blue cheese lovers, so I added some crumbled blue cheese right before serving. Our guests loved it!!! I will be making this again!! Thanks!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
breakfast casserole supreme

this is a wonderful almost do ahead breakfast. great for company or christmas morning.

1. melt margarine and place in the bottom of 9" by 13" baking pan
2. spread potatoes in bottom of the pan
3. sprinkle chopped vegetables over potatoes
4. add salt and pepper to taste
5. sprinkle meat over potatoes and vegetables
6. pour beaten eggs over potatoes
7. bake at 350 degrees for 45 minutes
8. remove from oven and sprinkle cheese evenly over top
9. bake another 5-10 minutes or until cheese is hot and bubbly
10. remove from oven and let set for approximately 5 minutes
11. cut into 2
12. 5"-3" squares and serve with a spatula
13. enjoy
demonstrations.review: Made this for Easter Bunch, and it was absolutely scrumptious!!! Everyone went back for seconds!!! Followed the recipe exactly, except added Oscar Mayer Real Crumbled Bacon, and mushrooms. Our son who loves hot and spicy food, smothered it in tabasco sauce, and said it was "delicious"!!! Will definately be making and sharing this recipe often!!! Thank You, Connie!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
whiskey weiners

these are my favorite appetizer! they're very quick, easy and good. i got the recipe out of one of those school fundraiser cookbooks.

1. mix chili sauce / ketchup , brown sugar , onion , lemon juice and whiskey in saucepan
2. bring to a boil
3. add weiners and simmer for 30 minutes
4. these can also be put in a crock pot to simmer
demonstrations.review: These were great!!! A big hit with all, quick to prepare, except for crock pot cook time.  Next time, I am going to try this sauce with meatballs, and it might be good made in a larger quantity, and served with or over shredded chicken or beef!!! The possibilities are endless!!! Thanks for a "keeper" Patti10 !!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crock pot steak and black bean chili

the weather is starting to cool off now and this is a easy chili recipe for the crock pot. this chili is very thick and rich. makes a lot.

1. cut the beef into 1-inch cubes
2. place beef in slow cooker and turn it on low
3. sprinkle the chili powder , garlic powder and cumin over the meat
4. add onion and green pepper
5. drain and rinse the cans of beans and add them to the slow cooker
6. add tomatoes and sugar
7. cover and cook on low for 8 to 10 hours
8. uncover and sir in the tomato paste
9. season with salt and pepper
10. garnish with sour cream and cheddar cheese
demonstrations.review: Wow!!! Talk about comfort food!!! My DH loved it, and is raving to everyone he knows about how wonderful it was!!!I also added some whole kernel sweet corn to the mix, along with spicy chili beans!!  Will be making this again, and thanks for posting, Mary!!!!!!

target.recipe_text:
pretzels

i just love these things. i can't ever get enough of them so i figured i'd share the recipe with you guys.

1. in a small bowl , combine yeast and warm water
2. let stand for 5 minutes while you prepare the next step
3. in a large bowl , place the brown sugar , 1 cup flour and the yeast mixture
4. mix well
5. then , stir in enough of the all-purpose flour to make a soft dough
6. turn dough onto a well-floured surface and knead for about 3 minutes
7. cover and let rest 20 minutes
8. cut dough into 12 pieces
9. roll each into a 12-15-inch long rope and shape into pretzels
10. in a shallow bowl , add 1 tablespoon baking soda to 1 cup water
