11. dip each finished pretzel shape quickly into water , shaking off excess
12. place immediately on greased baking sheet
13. sprinkle with salt
14. bake at 475 degrees for 6 minutes or until golden brown
15. remove from pan quickly and serve with melted butter brushed on top , or with your favorite dip
target.review: This recipe was fun. Easy to do and I'm expecting my grandkids will get a major kick out of it. I never thought that brown sugar would fit in but it did. For myself, I used a hot mustard dip but I suspect my munchkins would prefer something more like peanut butter.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
shrimp elegante

this is a delicious way to serve shrimp!

1. saute onion in butter until golden
2. add shrimp and mushrooms and saute until shrimp are pink
3. combine salt , pepper , chili sauce and water
4. add to shrimp mixture and bring to a boil
5. stir in rice , cover and simmer for 5 minutes
6. combine sour cream and flour
7. add to the shrimp and rice mixture and heat gently
8. divide between plates , garnish with chives and parsley and serve
demonstrations.review:
Hi CJ,
I really liked this recipe! The only modification I made was to sautÃ© the shrimp in butter first for about 3 minutes. I then set them aside in a bowl and continued on with the recipe. I added the shrimp back in immediately after the rice cooked. The balance of the cooking time warmed the shrimp to perfection and the outcome was totally delicious. For you fire breathing dragons out there, you will need to pump up the octane to get satisfaction but for the rest of us, this is a really nice recipe that would suit most family's tastes. Thank you!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
german cucumber salad with sour cream

this is a very light, tasty salad, and not sweet like many cucumber salads. it's very refreshing with a tangy bite from the green onions. i used dried herbs, of course using less, and it was still very tasty. i got the recipe many years ago from a recipe board online, but do not remember the source. however, it was attributed to a man who made this for his guests at an inn he ran in germany. i included slicing the vegetables in the approximate time.

1. in a bowl , combine all the salad ingredients
2. in another small bowl , mix together well all the dressing ingredients
3. pour over the cucumber salad mixture and toss gently
4. cover and chill for at least an hour
demonstrations.review: Perfect light tasting summer salad made with usually on-hand ingredients! I served this with Pecan Crusted Salmon (88931) from PaulaG for a terrific evening meal.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
grammy s broccoli soup

my mom is famous for this soup - it's fantastic!

1. combine broccoli , celery , carrots , water , and chicken bouillon in a large soup pot
2. boil 20-30 minutes
3. while vegetables are cooking - in a saucepan , saute onion in butter until tender
4. add cornstarch and flour to butter mixture , stirring until browned
5. gradually add milk and cook , stirring constantly , until thick
6. add shredded cheese and stir until melted
7. add the cheese sauce to the broccoli mixture and stir until well combined
8. simmer until heated through
demonstrations.review:
Hi loof,
I loved the recipe! I tend to over-shop in the grocery store (don't go there if you are hungry) so I had a large stash of broccoli to use. I now have a large stash of Grammy's Broccoli Soup to finish. I think this is a better situation. The flour and cornstarch roux was a nice touch. The flavor was not at all heavy. I have a new appreciation for broccoli! This is now a routine recipe in my rotation of favorites. Thanks loof!

target.recipe_text:
taco roll ups   oamc

this is my own little creation.  i had a recipe for italian roll ups that i got from a once a month cookbook.  i just changed it to taco style as my children love anything with a mexican flavor. these freeze well. i use my own homemade whole wheat bread instead of the frozen bread dough.

1. brown ground beef and add taco seasoning and water
2. cook for 5-10 minutes
3. set aside
4. roll thawed dough into a rectangle - about 20 x 8-inches
5. spread ground beef over dough - leaving about 1-inch of dough on one long edge free of filling
6. top beef with grated cheese
7. roll up as for cinnamon rolls starting with the long edge closest to you
8. pinch seam to seal
9. slice the roll into 1-inch thick slices with a serrated knife
10. place rolls 2" apart onto a cookie sheet that has been sprayed with cooking spray
11. if any filling falls out just press it into the top of the rolls
12. bake at 350 for 25 minutes or until golden brown
13. serve with salsa , sour cream or guacamole for dipping
14. to freeze: allow to cool completely
15. flash freeze and then place in a ziploc bag when firm
16. label , seal and freeze
17. to serve: thaw in fridge overnight or thaw / heat in microwave about 45 seconds on high
target.review:
These were lovely when warm and I did make them for a party but most of my family were eating them as they came out of the oven so I had to make more.
Thanks for posting

demonstrations.recipe_text:
burrito sauce

nan

1. in a skillet , beat butter and saute onion
2. blend in flour
3. gradually add broth , stirring to keep smooth
4. add tomato sauce , garlic salt and chili
5. cover and simmer 20 minutes
6. spoon over your favorite burrito
demonstrations.review:
wow this sauce was just right thanks i have only ever used the packet ones before but never again will always use this one.
even my children loved it

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pizza swirls

very good recipe, i always make multiple loaves of this because it goes over so well. enjoy!

1. thaw bread and follow direction on the package for rising
2. roll the bread out into a flat oval about 15 x 8 inches about 1 / 2 inch thick
3. chop pepperoni in a food processor
4. spread a cookie sheet with olive oil
5. drizzle oil evenly over the dough
6. sprinkle , garlic powder , ground oregano , and pepper over the oil
7. layer cheeses then the pepperoni over the spices leaving a 1 / 2 inch border of the dough uncovered
8. roll dough up jelly roll style rolling the from the 15 inch size of the dough
9. seal the edges by pressing dough together
10. spread olive oil sparingly over the dough
11. place onto the cookie sheet
12. bake in a preheated oven at 350 degrees
13. bake for 30 minutes or until golden brown
14. remove from oven
15. let cool 5-10 minutes then slice into pinwheels
demonstrations.review:
I made these as finger food for a party. While they were warm they were lovely but as they cooled down they went a but hard. Everyone loved them though and they disapeared quit quickly.
Thanks for a good party food

demonstrations.recipe_text:
baked applesauce oatmeal

comfort food!!  if you are a lover of oatmeal, try this wonderful dish!  a good breakfast item and very satisfying.  an easy fix-ahead dish with leftovers warmed in the microwave.

1. mix all wet ingredients and combine with dry ingredients
2. if raisins are use , plump by letting raisins sit in warm water for 10 minutes
3. may add more cinnamon to taste
4. pour into greased 9 x 9 inch baking dish
5. place in refrigerator overnight for oatmeal to dissolve into liquid
6. bake in a 350 degree oven for 30 minutes
7. top with brown sugar and milk when served
demonstrations.review: We had this for desert with custard last night. My kids loved it and my DH had second helpings. we want to try it with ice cream next time. I prepared it in the morning and left it in the fridge all day and i found the recipe very easy. thanks for a great recipe.

target.recipe_text:
chocolate eclair dessert

who would have thought something so easy could be so delicious!

1. mix together vanilla pudding mix and milk
2. fold in whipped topping
3. line 9 x 13 pan with one layer of graham crackers
4. put half of the pudding mixture over the graham crackers
5. place a second layer of graham crackers over the pudding mixture
6. put the remaining pudding mixture over the graham crackers
7. place a third layer of graham crackers over the pudding mixture
8. heat the tub of frosting in the microwave for 30 seconds to soften
9. spread frosting on the top of the last layer of graham crackers
10. cover with plastic wrap and let set a couple hours or overnight in the refrigerator
11. cut in squares
target.review: SO GLAD I decided to make this dessert for a family gathering at my house this weekend.  It was great to make the day ahead and was a complete hit.  I heated up the can of frosting for an extra few seconds until it was pourable.  That was my only worry about the dessert was not messing up the top by trying to spread the frosting.  I just poured the frosting and smoothed it a little and it set up perfectly in the fridge.  Thanks so much for making me look so good!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pudding chocolate chip cookies

these cookies melt in your mouth. the pudding makes the texture so smooth and delicious. it's funny, these cookies were originally suppossed to be made with vanilla pudding, but i made a mistake and put in chocolate pudding and they were wonderful! if you're in the mood for chocolate then makes sure to use chocolate pudding instead of vanilla!

1. mix flour and baking soda and set aside
2. then combine margarine , sugars , vanilla , and pudding mix in a large mixing bowl and beat until smooth and creamy
3. beat in eggs
4. gradually add flour mixture
5. then stir in chips
6. drop dough by rounded teaspoonfuls on ungreased baking sheet
7. bake at 375 for 8-10 minutes
demonstrations.review: These were quick and easy and the pudding does add a nice flavor.  I did notice as I scraped the last bit out of the bowl and popped it into my mouth that they were lacking salt.  The cookies still taste good but next time I'll add between 1/4 - 1/2 tsp salt to balance out the flavors.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
blackened chicken

turn off the smoke detector when you cook this chicken dish! =0...oh, just love that cast iron...=) serve with beans and rice, a salad and yum!!

1. let the chicken come to room temperature before using
2. cover chicken with butter until well coated
3. heat a cast iron skillet over high heat until very hot
4. roll each chicken breast into about 1 / 2 tsp
5. seasoning mix
6. immediately place the chicken pieces skin side down in the skillet to sear
7. pour about 1 teaspoon of the butter on top
8. cook about 2+ minutes , until a crust forms on the underside
9. turn and pour another 1 teaspoon of the butter on each of the chicken pieces
10. cook until just cooked through
demonstrations.review: Just what I was looking for.  I wanted to make blackened chicken to go on top of my alfredo and this worked perfectly.  I reduced the salt to 1 Tbs and cooked the chicken on the grill to keep the smoke out of the house.  Thanks for a great recipe that I can use again and again - I put the leftovers into a spice bottle for next time.  Should last us a while!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mandarin chicken

this is very similar to the mandarin chicken served in the malls, except i use white meat chicken. boneless chicken thighs are what the restaurant uses. it's quick, easy and delicious. sometimes i'll make this, then a quick trip to the local chinese take-out for vegetable lo mein and eggrolls for a cheap, tasty chinese meal that's almost homemade. you'll be amazed at how authentic this tastes!

*note:  i have adjusted the amount of sugar to reflect comments written in reviews.  if you like it sweet, use the full 2/3 cup.

1. spray chicken breasts with vegetable oil spray
2. grill chicken breasts 4-6 minutes per side or until done
3. chop chicken into bite size pieces , set aside
4. combine sugar , soy sauce , lemon juice , oil , garlic and ginger in a small saucepan
5. heat over medium until sugar is dissolved , stirring often
6. bring to boil
7. combine cornstarch and water
8. add to sauce pan , stirring often
9. reduce heat and simmer 4-6 minutes or until sauce thickens
10. pour chicken into a large frying pan over medium heat
11. heat until chicken sizzles , then reduce heat and pour sauce over the chicken
12. heat through
13. serve over white rice
demonstrations.review: This tasted a LOT like the Panda Express Mandarin Chicken.  I liked that the ginger flavor worked well and wasn't too much - I have found most of the Chinese food recipes I try overdo the ginger.  I added a little too much cornstarch because I couldn't get it to thicken so the flavor was slightly off but that was my bad, not the recipe.  Great recipes to have now that I don't live by a Panda!

target.recipe_text:
easy one bowl low fat breakfast cookies

these are good for you and they seem to stick with you. i like to use craisins and dried apples. this came from lowfatcooking.about.com credited to fiona haynes

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees
2. in a large bowl , combine flour , oats , baking powder , baking soda , salt and sugar
3. add egg whites , applesauce and vanilla
4. mix well with a wooden spoon
5. fold in dried fruit
6. drop by tablespoon full on to baking sheet lined with parchment or silicone mat
7. bake for 12 minutes or until lightly golden
target.review: Excellent! I also used regular flour for this and it worked fine. I also omitted the applesauce since I didn't have any, and it didn't seem to affect the taste. These were so easy that my 10 year old son helped me make them and really seems to enjoy eating them, too! Thanks for a great new recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cream  of chicken soup

from "dining in"; i've always wanted to find a kosher "cream of chicken soup" recipe, and now i have one!  i had to play around a bit with the amount of liquids, especially when cooking the rice because i used an immersion blender... it might work okay as listed with a food processor.

1. saute onion in oil until clear
2. add water and rice and cook until soft
3. blend with hand blender or puree in food processor and return to pot
4. mix in remaining ingredients and bring to a boil
5. simmer 10 to 15 minutes
6. you can add less water , if you like a thicker soup
demonstrations.review: This is one of the BEST soups I have ever had! I made this for a family dinner and everyone devoured it- asking for seconds and thirds...This is such a nice change from regular chicken soup and is really more like a meal in itself because it is so filling. When I did make it, I omitted the peas since most of my family does not like them and no one noticed that they were missing. I also followed the suggestion of cooking the rice in chicken stock instead of water for flavor and I think that did help with the flavor. I will definitely be making this again soon!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
graham streusel coffee cake

from a little taste of texas cookbook.  this is a very moist coffee cake.

1. mix crumbs , pecans , brown sugar , cinnamon and butter
2. set aside
3. blend cake mix , water , oil and eggs on medium speed for about 3 minutes
4. pour half of batter into a greased and floured 9 x 13 pan
5. sprinkle with half of the reserved crumb mixture
6. spread remaining batter evenly over crumb mixture
7. sprinkle batter with remaining crumb mixture
8. bake at 350 degrees for 45 to 50 minutes
9. cool
10. mix powdered sugar and water and drizzle glaze over cake
11. serve
demonstrations.review: I loved this cake!  I am a big fan of  yellow cake mixes (I know, not very sophisticated!) and this was a nice variation on a very easy mix. I left the graham crackers a little coarse to give it more texture and I actually like the way it came out.  Next time I might try golden grahams cereal instead, since I love that, too!  I will definatley make this again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
fresh plum cobbler

i haven't made this one yet, i got the recipe from my mom. it sounds heavenly, though!!

1. in medium bowl , combine sugar and salt
2. cut in butter til mixture is crumbly
3. add flour , cinnamon and baking powder and mix til coarse crumbs
4. remove and reserve 1 cup of this mixture
5. combine 1 beaten egg and almond extract
6. stir into remaining flour mixture to form a soft dough
7. pat dough evenly into a 9" square baking dish
8. bake at 350 for 10 minutes
9. arrange plums over baked mixture
10. combine whipping cream , 1 / 4 cup sugar 1 beaten egg , vanilla and 1 / 2 teaspoons almond extract , beat well
11. pour cream mixture over plums
12. sprinkle with reserved crumb mixture
13. mix sugar and cinnamon , sprinkle over crumb mixture
14. bake at 350 for 45 minutes or until browned and bubbly
15. serve warm with ice cream !
16. 8 servings , 4 at our house !
demonstrations.review: This was a great recipe! I also reduced the sugar by half and it was plenty sweet.  I also omitted the almond extract from the topping since I am not a big fan of almond (although it was nice in the crust).  I would make this again as it was a big hit with my family!

target.recipe_text:
parmesan rosemary muffins

from 1001 low fat recipes.

1. combine dry ingredients , cheese and rosemary in a large bowl
2. stir in buttermilk , egg and oil , mixing until just blended
3. pour batter into greased muffin tins
4. bake at 375 until muffins are browned and a toothpick inserted in the center comes out clean , about 20 minutes
target.review: I had great hopes for these but I was disappointed. In all fairness, I don't usually like rosemary... If you're a fan of rosemary, these may be for you.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
marion s michigan sauce for hot dogs

recipes for this northern new york specialty are closely guarded like barbecue down south.  try this with chopped onions on your hot dogs for a new taste treat.

1. finely chop onions and saute in a little olive oil until tender
2. add ground beef and cook until browned
3. separate meat so it is broken into very fine pieces of meat
4. add rest of ingredients , mix , and cook over low heat on the stove 1 hour or more
5. this could be cooked in a crockpot on low for six hours
6. serve as a topping on hot dogs
demonstrations.review: This is our new hot dog chili recipe! I've only ever made one other recipe but didn't care for it much and ended up with LOADS of it! I decided to try this recipe out with a quarter pound of ground beef that I siphoned off of taco night. With a slice of velveeta on the bottom, and a scoop of this sauce on top, I don't think I've ever eaten a better hot dog at home before : )  I'll definitely be making the whole recipe next time and freezing for easy use. This recipe may even manage to revive my attempt at serving chili cheese dogs as a Christmas tradition!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
stewed tomatoes jefferson

thomas jefferson was an excellent cook. he was one of the first to use tomatoes in this country.
this is an excellent dish!

source	: frugal gourmet

1. melt butter in a saucepan and saute` onion until clear
2. add remaining ingredients and simmer over low heat until tomatoes are very tender or to your liking
3. serve hot
demonstrations.review: This recipe was just great! I know I'll be using this frequently this summer and fall to stock up my freezer for the winter! I used 9 romas and white grape juice (since there wasn't any wine in the house). I also added 3 T sugar since I like my tomatoes a little bit sweet. I was going to thicken them with some cornstarch but figured they would thicken a bit with the freezing and thawing process and I can always do that when we eat them just like I used to with canned tomatoes. Being as my 9 little romas only made 2 pts of tomatoes, I doubt they'll even make it to the freezer, but we'll see! Thanks for a great recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
halushki

polish cabbage and noodles

1. finely chop cabbage
2. put in a pan with salted water to cover
3. bring to a boil
4. cook 5 minutes
5. in the meantime , chop onions and saute in 1 c margarine until tender , approximately 10 minutes
6. drain cooked cabbage , rinse with cold water , squeeze out the excess water
7. mix into the cooked onion
8. add 1 / 2 c butter , mix and cook until medium browned , approximately 30 minutes , stirring to prevent overbrowning
9. cook noodles 5-6 minutes
10. drain
11. combine with cooked cabbage , mixing well
12. season with salt and pepper
demonstrations.review: I'm not a huge fan of cabbage but I made this to take to a party of a friend who likes halushki and I have to say that I liked it. I don't know if it's something that I would make on a regular basis but it was an easy and yummy recipe. Thanks.

target.recipe_text:
gingerbread cake  spicy

adapted from a gourmet recipe, this spicy gingerbread originated from the gramercy tavern. it's excellent warm, and even better after one day. if you like a deep, spicy gingerbread, you might try this one!

1. butter a 10-inch bundt pan well and dust with flour , shaking out excess
2. preheat oven to 350f
3. generously butter bundt pan and dust with flour , knocking out excess
4. bring stout and molasses to a boil in a large saucepan and remove from heat
5. whisk in baking soda , then cool to room temperature
6. sift flour , baking powder , and spices in a large bowl
7. whisk together eggs and both sugars
8. whisk in oil , then molasses mixture
9. add to flour mixture and whisk until just combined
10. pour batter into bundt pan and bang pan sharply on counter to eliminate air bubbles
11. bake in middle of oven until a tester comes out with just a few moist crumbs adhering , about 50 minutes
12. cool cake in pan on a rack 5 minutes
13. turn out onto rack and cool completely
14. you can serve the gingerbread immediately , dusting lightly with confectioners sugar , and / or adding whipped cream
15. you can also hold the gingerbread for a day before serving , as the flavors develop with some time
target.review: I made this recipe last night for my fiancé's family and boy was it a hit!  The cake was so moist and spicy - just the way I like it!  I halved the sugar and it was plenty.  I didn't have dark brown sugar, so I took golden sugar and added a tablespoon of molasses to it.  I also didn't have any stout and I JUST ran out of coffee, so I steeped 3 bags of orange pekoe tea in 1 cup boiled water instead.  Even with all of the alterations, it turned out great!  I will definitely be making this again and next time I will try with stout.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
creamy greek salad dressing

greek salads are usually only dressed with olive oil and maybe lemon juice or red-wine vinegar. but this dressing is made of 'greek' ingredients so, it's my greek dressing.

1. in a blender or food processor , whirl all the ingredients except the buttermilk for one minute
2. with the blender running , slowly pour in the buttermilk and blend until thick and creamy
3. chill at least 1 hour so the flavours meld
4. refrigerate , tightly covered
5. this makes nearly 2 cups of dressing and stays fresh for 3-4 days
6. if the dressing separates , just give it a whizz in the blender again
demonstrations.review: Wonderful recipe! I just used a bit less regular milk and added a tablespoon of yogurt... it turned out perfectly! Will definitely keep this one in my cookbook.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
why i joined zaar carrot cake

on october 2, 2001, i discovered the recipezaar web site. i immediately joined so i could post a request for a recipe i had lost. in less than an hour, i had a reply: this recipe. unfortunately, i never posted it into the database -- until now. my mistake. this cake was the reason i joined, and the friendly response i received was the reason i stayed!

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees f
2. grease and flour a 9x13 inch pan
3. mix flour , baking soda , baking powder , salt and cinnamon
4. make a well in the center and add sugar , oil , eggs and vanilla
5. mix with wooden spoon until smooth
6. stir in carrots , coconut , walnuts and pineapple
7. pour into 9x13 inch pan and bake for about 45 minutes
8. don't panic , the centre will sink a little
9. allow to cool
10. when cool , ice the cake
11. you can certainly use your favourite cream cheese frosting to ice this cake , but the one i've included is highly recommended
12. to make the frosting: cream the butter and cream cheese until smooth
13. add the icing sugar and beat until creamy
demonstrations.review: I've made this recipe so many times and I just love it (and so does the family!). I usually skip the walnuts.  One of my batches came out too dense because I added just a bit more pineapple. Otherwise, it's fantastic! Next time I'll try the apple sauce addition.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
our favourite lemon loaf

this is soooo nummmmy!! for lemon lovers. very good warm or cold. (have been making this for years and cannot remember where it came from, probably from my mom.)

1. in a large bowl , cream butter and sugar
2. add eggs , one at a time , beating until creamy
3. blend in milk
4. in another bowl , mix together flour , baking powder , salt and lemon rind
5. pour into batter
6. stir to moisten
7. scrape into greased 9 x 5 inch loaf pan
8. bake in 350f degree oven for 55 to 60 minutes
9. cool in pan for 5 minutes
10. remove to rack and while still hot , with a toothpick poke holes all over the top of the loaf , and spoon glaze evenly over
11. cool
12. glaze: combine lemon juice and sugar in saucepan
13. stir and heat till sugar is dissolved
14. spoon evenly over top of hot loaf
demonstrations.review: WOW! This lemon loaf is amazing!! I doubled the recipe and added 1.5 cups frozen cranberries and it turned out so well. I have guests coming tonight, so I will have to hold out, but it's going to be very difficult. Really great recipe.

target.recipe_text:
deli rotisserie chicken

i have a george foreman rotisserie and love the way everything comes out of it.  this recipe makes the chicken  juicy and skin crispy.  does not include marinade time.

1. remove the giblets from chicken and discard
2. wash chicken inside and out , drying with paper towels
3. rub chicken with a little olive oil
4. tie wings and legs with cooking twine
5. mix all the spices together well
6. rub all over chicken
7. place on plate and wrap with saran
8. put in fridge 4-24 hrs
9. , the longer the better
10. put chicken onto rotisserie bar
11. set timer for 1 1 / 2 hours
12. chicken is done at 160 and no longer pink
target.review: I use this every time I rotisserie a chicken now.  It is perfect...The whole family can't get enough.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
i hate ricotta meat   2 cheese stuffed shells

my non-ricotta cheese-eating husband always raved about "the meat stuffed shells his mom used to make." his grandmother recently wrote to the tv guide (where this recipe originated) and they were kind enough to send back the recipe, dated september 13, 1976. i have to agree, these are delicious! serve with a tossed salad and garlic bread. the prep time includes the pasta/beef cooking; the cook time is the baking time for the casserole.

1. boil water for pasta
2. meanwhile , in a large skillet , brown ground beef , onion and garlic
3. drain and cool
4. cook pasta in water , drain
5. preheat oven to 400 degrees
6. meanwhile pasta is cooking , combine meat , mozzarella cheese , bread crumbs , egg and parsley
7. season with salt and pepper
8. mix spaghetti sauce with tomato sauce
9. cover bottom of a 13x9 casserole dish with 1 / 4 of the sauce
10. stuff cooked , drained shells with the meat mixture and place on top of sauce in dish in a row
11. add red wine to remaining sauce and mix well
12. cover shells with sauce and sprinkle with parmesan cheese
13. bake in oven for 20-25 minutes or until bubbly and browned
demonstrations.review: My family doesn't like ricotta either so this recipe was great.  It was easy and the mixture made enough to freeze half for another time.  The wine was a little strong for our taste so I will be leaving it out next time.  Thank you so much, I'll def make this again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s chinese chicken balls with sweet and sour sauce

don't bother ordering chinese chicken balls make these at home they are just as good if not even better and the sweet and sour sauce is the same as what is served at your chinese restaurant!-- these are a great weekend snack or can be served as appetizers, if you want some extra flavor to you chicken batter feel free to add in some garlic or onion powder or spices of choice --- this makes a large amount so you may want to reduce the chicken ball batter amount by half (using 4 chicken breasts) --- note: the sauce recipe is one you may have to make a few times before you get the consistancy and sweetness to your liking, 1 cup white sugar and 1/2 cup lightly packed brown will give you a sweet sauce you may reduce the white sugar amount by a few tablespoons

1. to make the sweet and sour sauce sauce
2. in a saucepan combine the first 5 ingredients until combined
3. in a cup or bowl whisk the cold water or pineapple juice with cornstarch until smooth and well blended , then whisk vigorously into the ketchup mixture
4. bring to a boil stirring or whisking constantly over medium-high heat until bubbly
5. reduce the heat to medium-low and continue simmering and mixing until thickened remove from heat and allow to sit at room temperature while making the chicken balls or you may cool to room temperature then refrigerate until ready to use
6. to make the chicken balls: in a large bowl combine flour , cornstarch , baking powder , baking soda , garlic powder
7. add in water and sesame oil
8. whisk vigorously until smooth
9. add in chicken pieces
10. using clean handsand mix until well coated
11. heat oil in a deep-fryer or dutch oven to 375 degrees
12. carefully dip the battered chicken pieces in hot oil and fry until golden brown
13. remove to a paper towel
14. sprinkle with seasoning salt immediately after frying if desired
15. serve immediately with sweet and sour sauce
16. delicious !
demonstrations.review: YUM!!!  And so easy.  I will be making this forever :)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mustardy fried chicken breasts

i got this recipe from an ex-boyfriend's mother.it gets rave reviews every time i make it.just be careful not to overcook the chicken.i usually use italian style bread crumbs and yellow mustard, but you could use any combination of bread crumbs and mustard that you have. i've used dijon mustard as well with very good results.you could also bake it in the oven, just be sure to cover it so it doesn't dry out.

1. wipe down chicken breast with paper towel
2. sprinkle with salt and pepper
3. in bowl , beat egg and mustard
4. in separate bowl combine cheese and bread crumbs
5. dip each breast in egg mixture then coat with cheese mixture
6. let set 10 minutes
7. saute chicken in oil for 15-20 minutes or until tender
demonstrations.review: My family loved these...ate them right up.  But we are mustard lovers...it gave such an interesting taste to the chicken and they were soooooo moist.  If both my kids eat something up it's a great night so thank you!

target.recipe_text:
low fat sugar free banana bread

yummy alternative to a higher in fat treat!

1. grease loaf pan
2. i usually just add all the ingredients together and mix
3. bake in a 350f oven for 45 to 50 minutes
4. bake until toothpick inserted in center comes out clean
5. store at room temperature up to 3 days or in refrigerator up to 1 week
target.review: this stuff is *dangerous!*  i was tempted to eat the whole loaf in one sitting. thank goodness a friend had given me the (homemade) applesauce and i was forced to share!  i loosely followed this recipe, and made it my own by: 1) exceeding the cup of bananas required, 2) substituting real sugar for splenda (i can't stand that splenda aftertaste!), 3) adding a pinch of salt, 4) a bit (1 tbsp?) of vanilla, and 5) some (1/3 c?) slivered almonds. simply amazing. thanks emma! :D

demonstrations.recipe_text:
easy cranberry mustard pork chops

a nice combination of flavors in a very easy recipe. prep time doesn't include marination.

1. in a bowl , combine the cranberry juice , mustard , and garlic
2. in a shallow dish , place the pork chops in a single layer , then pour the cranberry mixture over and coat the chops well with the liquid
3. cover the dish and refrigerate it all for at least 1 hour
4. place a large skillet over medium-high heat and when the pan is hot add a bit of oil
5. add the pork chops and marinade , cover the skillet partially , and cook for 6 to 7 minutes
6. turn the chops over and cook the other side for another 5 to 10 minutes , uncovered , until cooked through and juice runs clear
7. season to taste with salt and pepper
8. makes 4 servings
9. :)
demonstrations.review: i love this recipe.  i have made it several times.  its so quick and easy...and i usually have all of the ingredients on-hand!  one time i was lacking the grey poupon, so i substituted gouldens...it came out great just the same!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
tims  mom s blueberry muffins

my son is a chef in louisville, and he loans this recipe to his friends this is the title they give it! the second best part about these muffins(the best part is eating them) is going to the blueberry farm and picking your own blueberries! its great fun and the kids love it!

1. cut butter into flour , sugar , baking powder and salt
2. add egg , lemon , milk vegetable oil and vanilla , stir just til moist fold in blueberries
3. bake in well-greased muffin tin at 400 degrees for 20 to 25 minutes
4. muffin cups will be about 2 / 3 full
demonstrations.review: one word: yum!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
easy pasta with bell pepper and tomatoes

this is the best way to enjoy a pasta dish with the fresh flavour of a tomato-based sauce... by making it on your own!

1. bring a pot of 1 1 / 2 cups of lightly salted water to a boil , add pasta , and cook for about 10-12 minutes , or until pasta is al dente
2. drain
3. heat oil in a saucepan on a medium flame , add the onions and saute until soft and translucent
4. now add the diced tomatoes and bell-pepper strips , salt , basil , oregano and saute for about 5 minutes until the bell-peppers soften a bit
5. if you like it crispier , saute only for a couple of minutes
6. remove from heat , toss well with cooked pasta and serve hot with a sprinkling of cheddar cheese !
demonstrations.review: my roommate and i loved this.  i used penne instead of shells, and added a bit of crushed red pepper flakes to give it a little kick.  used a few dashes of parmesean cheese on each serving instead of adding cheddar to the mix...it was wonderful!

target.recipe_text:
parsnip casserole

a nice way to enjoy parsnips; especially for those who have never tried them.

1. preheat oven to 400
2. lightly grease / spray a 1 1 / 2 qt casserole dish
3. cook sliced parsnips and carrots in boiling , salted water until tender
4. drain and place in prepared casserole dish
5. meanwhile , in a small saucepan over medium heat , melt butter
6. saute the onions in butter for 3-5 minutes or until soft
7. reduce heat to med-low and add flour to saucepan
8. stirring constantly
9. add cream , tarragon , salt , pepper , paprika and ground mustard
10. add parmesan cheese and continue to heat over med-low heat , stirring frequently , until cheese is melted and mixture thickens
11. evenly pour sauce over parsnip / carrot mixture in casserole dish
12. in a small bowl , mix together bread crumbs with melted butter
13. evenly sprinkle over casserole
14. bake , uncovered , at 400 for about 20 minutes
target.review:
This is excellant! We were only 5 but we went back for more until it was gone!
I also doubled up the spices.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pineapple upside down cake in iron skillet

making this in an iron skillet is very handy and everyone thinks it makes for good flavor too.

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. melt butter in iron skillet
3. sprinkle brown sugar over butter
4. arrange pineapple slices on top brown sugar / butter
5. place cherries in center of slices
6. beat remaining ingredients till well blended
7. pour over pineapple in skillet and bake for 35 to 45 minutes or until tooth pick inserted comes out clean
8. remove from oven and turn onto heat-proof plate
demonstrations.review: This is the recipe my Nana has been making for us for as long as I can remember and it is my absolute favourite! Easy and delicious every time!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
turkey shepherd s pie with two potato topping  or chicken

this is the ultimate thanksgiving/christmas dinner leftover recipe. the recipe keeps in mind that the ingredients being used are from separate dishes that are *already* seasoned. if you are making either of the potatoes from scratch for the recipe, go ahead and season them as if you were making that dish to serve as a side. the same with the gravy, if it is not homemade roasted turkey gravy, add some more seasoning to it. of course you do not have to have leftovers to make this, but it is a good way to use up the turkey, mashed potatoes, sweet potatoes and gravy without the dish tasting like leftovers. i have also made it with chicken with excellent results. this is a real family pleaser and our 4 year old actually asks for this for dinner a lot. the original recipe was adapted from chef jimmy bradley of the red cat in new york city.  it can also be prepared in individual 1 1/2-cup ramekins; check them for doneness after 20 minutes. wine: a bighearted chardonnay will echo the texture of the smooth gravy and the soft mashed potato topping. look for a reasonably priced, fruity wine, such as australia’s 1999 rosemount or the 1999 lindemans bin 65.

1. melt 2 tablespoons of butter in a large skillet and add onion , celery , carrot and garlic
2. cook over low heat until softened , about 12 minutes
3. stir in turkey or chicken and cook until heated through
4. add the gravy and orange juice to the mixture and cook until bubbling
5. remove from the heat , stir in the parsley and sage and season with salt and pepper
6. transfer the filling to a round , oval or 9-by-12-inch baking dish and let cool
7. preheat the oven to 400
8. in a bowl , mix both potatoes together and add chives
9. season with salt and pepper and beat in the egg
10. spread the potatoes over the filling and brush the top with the melted butter
11. bake in the upper third of the oven for about 30 minutes , or until the topping is lightly browned and the filling is bubbling
12. let the pie stand for about 10 minutes before serving
demonstrations.review: Just finished dinner - yum! I didn't make quite as directed; there weren't enough mashed potatos left, so I made up the difference by mashing the leftover parsnip casserole (#152495) and I didn't have any orange juice or chives. Great, easy recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
prawns with gorgonzola cheese

not sure where i got this recipe!  hope you like it.  this recipe is for 2 servings but you can always double, etc. depending on your needs. the recipe states that it goes well with buttered rice.  sounds fattening but good.

1. saute prawns quickly in the butter and garlic until they turn opaque
2. do not overcook
3. add the lemon juice and gorgonzola and stir until creamy
4. garnish with the parsley and serve immedietly
demonstrations.review:
If you like gorgonzola, which I do, this is delicious and simple. I had it over buttered brown rice as suggested, and didn't change a thing. 
I may have been particularly hungry, but I would call this recipe one generous serving, rather than two.

target.recipe_text:
buttery baked red potatoes

it's amazing how the simplest recipes can be some of the tastiest. my mil fixed this for dinner one night and i was hooked! i hope you will be too.

1. preheat oven to 350
2. melt butter in large skillet
3. chop onion , and add to melted butter
4. saute until caramelized
5. meanwhile , chop potatoes into thirds
6. cook in boiling water until just tender
7. drain cooked potatoes and place in greased 13x9 casserole
8. top evenly with caramelized onions and butter
9. sprinkle with kosher salt and fresh ground black pepper to taste
10. bake at 350 for 15-20 minutes
target.review: simple and delicious. excellent recipe. thank you for sharing!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
tilapia

nan

1. combine oregano , chili powder , cayenne pepper , and salt
2. in a shallow bowl combine the melted butter and lemon juice
3. dip fish into butter mixture , then press into the spice mixture
4. place in a shallow casserole sprayed with non-stick cooking spray
5. bake at 450 degrees for about 15 minutes , or until fish flakes when pressed
demonstrations.review: I didn't have chili powder and I only had frozen fish on hand but the recipe still came out great.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
spiced grapes

nan

1. combine all ingredients except grapes in a small saucepan and boil for two to three minutes
2. pierce each grape two to three times with a sharp skewer or toothpick
3. place grapes in a small bowl and cover with the syrup mixture
4. refrigerate for 24 to 36 hours
5. serve with cheese or nuts
demonstrations.review: Delicious and original idea, but the syrup came out a little too sweet for my taste and it contrasted too much with the tartness of the grapes.  For me, the flavor did not soak into the grapes well enough to account for the difference in tastes.  Perhaps halving the grapes would have worked better.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
dutch babies pancakes

this puff pancake is one of our favorites! we serve it with a sprinkling of lemon juice, a dusting of powdered sugar and then some maple syrup but, fruit on top is always a nice touch! if you add fruit, layer it over the top of the batter, just before baking. we've used blueberries, sliced peaches and sliced apples (dusted with cinnamon) and all were very good!

1. preheat oven to 450 degrees
2. beat eggs until well aerated
3. add milk and beat again
4. add salt and flour and beat on low , just until blended
5. meanwhile , put butter into a 9 x 13 baking dish , or divide it into two round cake pans , or two large cast iron skillets and place in the preheated oven to melt the butter and heat the pan
6. pour batter into the warm pan , top with fruit , if you want to add some and place in the oven
7. bake for 15 minutes
demonstrations.review: Hey, great recipe. I halved it but otherwise followed it exactly. It is a little strange looking considering its a pancake, but if you don't call it that, then it just looks really pretty. It tastes great, although next time I would probably add less butter and I would add a bit of sugar to the recipe so that I could skip the syrup. Thanks for posting!

target.recipe_text:
amanda s cheese pound cake

my daughter amanda found this recipe in a old church cookbook, that i have had for years. its the kind of cake that you want to stick your face in the pan and never come up for air.

1. preheat oven to 300f
2. cream butter , cream cheese and sugar together
3. add eggs one at a time
4. add vanilla and then flour slowly
5. pour into a bundt pan or tube pan
6. bake for 1 1 / 2 hours
7. important: do not try and rush by cooking faster in a hotter oven
target.review: This was very good, I didn't change a thing!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
nana s chocolate frosting

smooth and creamy with great chocolate taste.

1. combine chocolate and butter in large saucepan
2. cook over low heat until melted
3. stirring constantly
4. remove from heat
5. cool
6. sift sugar
7. add to chocolate alternately with milk and vanilla
8. beat at high speed until of spreading consistency
demonstrations.review: This is my go to recipe for a chocolate frosting, exceptionally good and more then enough for THE chocolate cake recipe I am repeatedly asked to make! EVERYONE LOVES this frosting! Thanks SO much for posting it!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
best ever banana cake with cream cheese frosting

this is one of (if not) the best banana cake i have ever tasted! i thought the oven temp of 275° sounded a little low, but this cake baked up (and rose) beautifully in my oven at this temp after pretty much exactly one hour. i do not know if the little "freezer trick" to this recipe is what ensured its moistness or not, but i did it, and it was exceptionally moist & delicious. would be interesting to see if it still came out as great if this step was skipped. all i know is that i followed this recipe exactly as stated (except that i had no buttermilk, so i subbed with a mix of lemon juice & milk) and i got exceptional results. so moist and yummy...a dense cake, similar in texture to a carrot cake... i personally would not call this frosted banana bread :o)  depending on the amount of frosting you like you can decide whether to half the recipe or not. i used the full recipe and had some leftover. i sprinkled on the chopped walnuts and threw this baby in the fridge and cut it the next day...to die for! i really liked it slightly chilled, but great at room temp too! it got better each day it sat, i always make this cake at least the day before i need or want it.  i was extremely pleased with this cake and will be making it over & over again!! so glad i came across this one!! (on another website).


(* * just to update the recipe, (based on some of the reviews), the baking time may vary based on individual ovens. it was right on for my oven, but some others have stated it has taken 1 hour 10 minutes, 1 hour 20 minutes, and my sister just informed me that it took 1 hour 30 minutes in her oven!!!!!)

1. preheat oven to 275f
2. grease and flour a 9 x 13 pan
3. in a small bowl , mix mashed banana with the lemon juice
4. set aside
5. in a medium bowl , mix flour , baking soda and salt
6. set aside
7. in a large bowl , cream 3 / 4 cup butter and 2 1 / 8 cups sugar until light and fluffy
8. beat in eggs , one at a time , then stir in 2 tsp vanilla
9. beat in the flour mixture alternately with the buttermilk
10. stir in banana mixture
11. pour batter into prepared pan and bake in preheated oven for one hour or until toothpick inserted in center comes out clean
12. remove from oven and place directly into the freezer for 45 minutes
13. this will make the cake very moist
14. for the frosting , cream the butter and cream cheese until smooth
15. beat in 1 teaspoon vanilla
16. add icing sugar and beat on low speed until combined , then on high speed until frosting is smooth
17. spread on cooled cake
18. sprinkle chopped walnuts over top of the frosting , if desired
demonstrations.review: Ok so I made this not really thinking it was going to be any better then the MANY different recipes I've tried...BUT don't look ANY further this IS IT! Yummmmm

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chicken noodle casserole

very good!! very good!! yum yum!!! cooking time includes cooking noodles.

1. cook noodles as directed on package
2. drain
3. combine soup and milk , chicken and cheese and heat to a boil
4. add salt and noodles
5. stir together
6. place in a buttered 1-1 / 2 quart casserole
7. top with croutons or bread crumbs
8. bake at 350 degrees for 30 minutes
demonstrations.review: This was very good but next time I will use chunks of chicken breasts.

target.recipe_text:
mom s best tomato soup canning recipe

my mennonite mother's 'famous' tomato soup - hard to beat! perfect anytime of the year! enjoy!

here's what i purchased (for you to use as a baseline reference): - to yield 75 quarts of soup - 3 bushels of tomatoes, 6 lbs. butter, 5 lbs. sugar, 3 bunches celery, 5 lbs. flour. hope that helps! (recipe below is for 8-10 quarts)

(i make lots, and then frequently give this as a gift for a new mother, a hostess gift (when invited to dinner), a get-well meal, etc..) super quick - easy to make, and can easily add garlic bread and a salad and dessert for a quick meal to bless someone. enjoy!

1. chop onion& celery
2. place in large kettle w / just enough water to keep them from burning
3. while this simmers , cut tomatoes
4. add to kettle& cook until tender
5. place this all through victorio strainer
6. return to kettle
7. add sugar& salt
8. cream butter and flour together& mix thoroughly with two cups of cold juice , until dissolved , to avoid lumps of flour in the juice
9. add butter / flour mixture to warmed tomato juice
10. stir well
11. heat just until hot
12. just prior to boiling , turn off the burner
13. ladle into jars& close securely with lids
14. return to canner & process 20-30 minutes
15. remove from canner & allow to set until sealed to serve , mix equal parts tomato concentrate to milk , and add 1 / 2 t
16. of baking soda per pint as it cooks
target.review: This is very good soup. It will go in my chrismas gifts. Thanks for posting

demonstrations.recipe_text:
roasted garlic mashed potatoes   the best you ve ever had

nan

1. separate head of garlic into individual cloves
2. toss in olive oil and wrap tightly in small piece of aluminum foil
3. bake in 350f oven for 45 minutes
4. when the garlic has cooled to the touch you should be able to squeeze it out of the 'paper' shell of the individual cloves
5. mash the roasted garlic with a fork , or force through a fine strainer
6. if you use a ricer as recommended below , simply rice the garlic along with the potatoes
7. peel and boil potatoes in salted water until tender
8. force the cooked potatoes through a ricer or mash by your usual method
9. put the riced potatoes , garlic , sour cream , butter , and salt and white pepper in a mixer bowl , and whip at medium speed until smooth
10. add cream or milk to adjust consistency

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cucumber salad with spicy wasabi dressing

rice wine vinegar is milder than most western vinegars. 

1. mix the wasabi with 1 / 2 teaspoon warm water in the bottom of a mixing bowl and let it stand for 5 minutes
2. peel the cucumbers , cut each one in half lengthwise , and use a melon baller or spoon to scoop out the seeds
3. cut the cucumbers widthwise into 1 / 4-inch crescents
4. add the vinegar and sugar to the wasabi and whisk until smooth
5. whisk in the sesame oil , salt , and pepper
6. just before serving , add the cucumbers , green onion , and sesame seeds to the dressing and mix well
demonstrations.review: I made the dressing for a lettace dinner salad, my husband and I really loved it. Nice change from reg. salad dressing. If you like wasabi your going love this. Thanks Dancer for another keeper.

target.recipe_text:
ribs my way

this is the way i always prepare my bbq ribs. they result in fall off the bone tender ribs, and they are always a hit. the spices listed are what i submitted for this recipe, however i probably never use the same thing twice. play around with those ingredients you enjoy the most. prep time includes marinating time.

1. mix brown sugar , garlic powder , and cayenne together in bowl
2. add salt and pepper if you wish
3. rub spice mixture onto ribs , both sides
4. wrap ribs in aluminum foil , using two sheets of foil
5. place ribs in fridge for at least 24 hours
6. remove ribs when ready to prepare and place in oven on warm
7. (my oven goes from warm to 250f , so i say place on warm , if your oven does have temps
8. lower than 250f , i would suggest 200f bake ribs on warm for at least 4 hours , up to 6 hours
9. remove ribs , and let them sit in foil , allowing them to cool to almost room temperature
10. place ribs on hot fire , and baste with your favorite sauce
11. let ribs cook on grill for approx 15 minutes or until hot
12. remove ribs and let them rest for approx 10 minutes before serving
target.review: Excellent.  I had some rub (Grill Creations Chicken & Rib rub)  which had most of the same ingredients and added the cayenne pepper to it.  Unfortunately I didn't mix it well a few of the pieces was very spicy.  But we enjoyed them greatly.  Had it yesterday for the 4th and leftovers today.  Awesome.  Thanks for posting these.  We had them with the Recipe #29709 Best Baked   Beans everything was great!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
best baked beans

the perfect addition to picnics and barbecues! simple and delicious. sure to become one of your favorites. my mother makes this for every family get together. ham could be added, or more ketchup if desired, but try it this way first - you'll love it!

1. cut bacon into bite size pieces
2. cook bacon in microwave , checking after each minute , or cook in a skillet , draining fat
3. don't let it get crisp
4. meanwhile , mix the remaining ingredients in a 3 quart casserole dish
5. add bacon and mix a little
6. bake uncovered for one hour at 350
7. it's best if they set out to cool for one hour before you serve them
demonstrations.review: Great beans.  I made them just as listed for the 4th of July.  Loved them.  They were even better the next day.  My husband loves meat so today we added leftover hot dogs cut up.  Awesome.  Thank you for listing this.  We love it!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
ellen s yummy pasta salad

this recipe can be played with. you can use all, or just a few of the vegetables. choice of pasta goes the same. i even tried it with tortollini and it was delicious. i just suggest that you do not substitute on the dressing and salad seasoning. i have given out this recipe before and have to stress that since many did not use those. using an assortment of peppers is great for the color.

1. cook and drain pasta of your choice according to package directions
2. drain and rinse with cold water
3. may also place in an ice water bath
4. toss pasta with 1 / 2 bottle salad seasoning , or to your taste
5. add chopped veggies and dressing
6. chill for at least 2 hours before seving
demonstrations.review:
We love this salad.  Made is just as noted.  My husband wants to try it with ham pieces next time :)
Thanks for posting!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
string spaghetti pie

satisfies adults and kids alike!

1. cook the first three ingredients in a large skillet at medium heat till meat is brown , stirring to separate
2. drain fat
3. stir in spaghetti sauce
4. mix well
5. combine spaghetti , parmesan , eggs , and butter in a large bowl
6. mix well
7. place in bottom of a 13 x 9 inch pan
8. spread cottage cheese over top
9. pour sauce mixture over cottage cheese

11. bake at 350 degrees f for about 20 minutes
demonstrations.review: Wonderful.  I used Ricotta cheese.  Thanks for posting!

target.recipe_text:
simple succulent shrimp scampi

this recipe is easy, quick, and gives the impression of a gourmet chef! the ingredients are simple, but the taste is truly 

1. first , peel shrimp and devein if desired
2. then , saute garlic in olive oil for about 1 to 2 minutes
3. next , add the butter and shrimp
4. cook until shrimp are somewhat pink
5. finally , stir in wine and red pepper
6. reduce heat and allow shrimp fully cook
7. when finished , sprinkle with parsley and serve over pasta or rice
8. a few
9. i recommend the following: 1 / 4 tsp of crushed red pepper1 / 4 cup of fresh or 1 / 8 cup of dried parsley
10. add more butter if you'd like
11. serve over angel hair pasta
target.review: A wonderful scampi recipe that certainly was quick and easy to prepare.  Delicious by itself or over pasta.  For my personal taste I will either decrease the amount of olive oil and increase the butter slightly or eliminate the olive oil and just use butter.  Only a personal preference.  I liked the zing that the crushed red pepper flakes added and I used the dried parsley also.  Great flavor.  Thanks

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cherry chocolate blossoms

a beautiful little cookie for cookie trays and holidays. very simple to make yet very elegant.

1. in large bowl , combine powdered sugar , butter , cherry liquid , almond extract and food color
2. blend well
3. lightly spoon flour into measuring cup
4. level off
5. add flour and salt
6. mix well
7. stir in cherries
8. if dough is too dry , add a little more cherry liquid until dough holds together when shaped
9. shape dough into 1-inch balls
10. place 2 inches apart on ungreased cookie sheets
11. bake at 350 degrees f for 10 to 12 minutes or until edges are just slightly brown
12. immediately top each cookie with a chocolate candy , pressing down firmly
13. remove from cookie sheets and cool
demonstrations.review: Followed the receipe exactly. Cookies were good and easy to make.  Will add more sugar and flavoring next time as we have serious sweet tooth in this house.  Thanks for posting.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
calves liver and onions

i think this dish has an undeserved reputation. when it's cooked up nice and crisp it's really wonderful. i had kids eating this like crazy, because i didn't tell them what it was!

1. cut liver in small serving size pieces
2. salt and pepper pieces
3. in a 12 inch skillet heat vegetable oil
4. make sure it is good and hot
5. lightly roll pieces in flour
6. saute in hot oil till brown on one side , turn and brown the other side
7. about 4 minutes per side
8. remove from skillet and keep warm
9. add onions to skillet and fry about 5 minutes till crisp tender
10. put onions over liver and serve
demonstrations.review: Wonderful!  So easy and quick to prepare and so delicious.  I only made slight alterations.  First I soaked the calves liver in milk - why - because my Mother said so - she's almost 90 and I'm not about to argue.  I then followed your recipe.  Besides the onions I added bacon like it has come served in some restaurants when I've ordered it out.  I served it with creamed spinach and baked potatoes with butter, sour cream, bacon bits, and a little shredded cheese. I think calves liver gets a bum rap probably because the name prohibits people from trying it. It's great folks - give it a chance. Thanks for the recipe, now I can make it at home.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
supreme garlic mashed potatoes

by cooking garlic cloves and potatoes together you get a nice easy way to get a taste of garlic. make potatoes as dense or creamy as you like by adjusting milk.

1. boil potatoes and the garlic cloves together
2. when tender , mash with potato masher and add butter
3. mash some more , add sour cream and enough of milk to desired consistency
4. season with salt and pepper
5. top with a sprinkling of paprika and parsley flakes
demonstrations.review: A wonderful, simple way to make delicious garlic mashed potatoes.  I was out of sour cream and  added a little additional milk and it was still great.  Can't wait to try it with the sour cream too.  Thanks for posting.

target.recipe_text:
real alfredo sauce

don't know where i originally got this, but this is the best alfredo sauce i have ever had outside of a restaurant.  i have made it with or without the cream cheese, and with all parmesan, and it still turns out great.  the nutmeg is essential!

1. melt butter in a saucepan over medium heat
2. add cream and cream cheese , stirring constantly , until slightly thickened
3. stir in nutmeg , parmesan , romano cheese , and garlic
4. stir constantly until melted completely
5. salt to taste
6. mix in egg yolks
7. continue to simmer over medium low heat , stirring constantly , for 3 to 5 minutes
8. serve over pasta , garnished with additional grated cheese and parsley
target.review: This is the first time that I have made a "real" Alfredo Sauce and it did not disappoint!  My husband requested chicken and broccoli fettucine alfredo for his birthday supper and this is the recipe that I decided to try.  He loved it and I will definitely be using this as my go to alfredo sauce from here on out!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
the clockmaker s caramel coated popcorn  a haunted recipe

in 1921, a german born clockmaker quit his well respected job to open a popcorn stand in chicago’s wicker park district. the clockmaker’s typical fare was freshly popped popcorn drizzled with warm butter and sprinkled with salt; but his favorite, and most beloved popcorn, was his caramel coated popcorn. the recipe he used to make it was given to him from his only true love, who tragically died four years earlier during world war i. the tattered and torn recipe, which was scribbled on the inside of an old playbill, was carefully framed and sealed in an exquisite frame. the clockmaker faithfully took the framed recipe with him everywhere he went.  

by the summer of 1924, the clockmaker’s caramel coated popcorn had captivated the entire city’s attention; everyone was frantically lining up at his busy stand to buy the sweet, sticky confection. a few months later, just as the clockmaker was preparing to close his stand for the day, a small fire ignited near the stove. the clockmaker instinctively ran out to call for help. when he returned, just seconds later, he remembered leaving the framed recipe hanging on the wall. the clockmaker quickly ran into the burning stand to retrieve the recipe, but he never made it out.

when the fire inspectors went into the charred ruins to investigate the accident, they found the clockmaker’s frame lying in a pile of smoking debris. the frame was in pristine condition; not a dent, nor a blemish, could be seen on it. however, the recipe was gone.  

the recipe for the clockmaker’s caramel popcorn recently surfaced and is beginning to circulate around the globe. unfortunately, many people think the recipe is haunted because it is believed that if your clock stops running after making the recipe it’s because the clockmaker has paid you a visit in hopes of reclaiming his long, lost recipe.

note:  this recipe, as written, results in a sticky, chewy caramel popcorn.  if you prefer a crunchier caramel popcorn, bake it in the oven at 250 degrees for 1 hour, stirring every 15 minutes.

1. in a large pot , heat the margarine , brown sugar , karo syrup , and salt together over medium heat
2. while stirring , bring mixture to a boil and allow to boil for five minutes
3. remove from heat
4. add baking soda and vanilla
5. mix well
6. pour over freshly popped popcorn
7. stir until the popcorn is well coated
8. enjoy !
demonstrations.review: It's good!  It was very sticky, I started to wonder if I boiled it too long......but I followed the directions exactly.  I used 14 cups of popcorn and after mixing the caramel with the popcorn I divided it between two parchment lined baking sheets and baked it at 250 for about 45 minutes.  I stirred it a few times.  Wonderful flavor, I can't imagine another caramel popcorn tasting any better than this one!  Quick and easy to make as well.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mimi s raspberry scones

this is a basic cream scone dough that you can use to make any kind of scone.  it is delicious.

1. in a large bowl whisk together the flour , sugar , baking powder , and salt
2. with a pastry blended cut the butter in to look like coarse crumbs
3. gently fold the berries into the flour mixture
4. in a small bowl combine the cream , beaten egg , and vanilla
5. mix well
6. add this to the flour mixture and stir till just combined
7. do not overmix
8. knead dough gently on a lightly floured board being careful of the berries
9. roll or pat into a circle that is about 7" round and about 1 1 / 2" thick
10. cut the circle in half and each half into four pie-shaped wedges
11. place on a baking sheet
12. brush the tops with egg wash
13. bake in a 400-425 degree oven on the middle rack
14. to prevent browning on the bottom , place the cookie sheet on top of another cookie sheet
15. bake for about 20 minutes or till nicely browned
16. best eaten the day they are made
demonstrations.review: These were absolutely some of the best tasting scones I have ever made!  I have always steered clear of raspberry scones in the past.....for some reason I thought they would be difficult because of the fragility of the raspberries.  I read the other reviews before making these and made a few little changes based on the reviews.  I added about 1-2 T. extra sugar and 1 T. of orange zest.  I also made a little glaze that I drizzled over them after they came out of the oven with 1/2 c. of confectioners sugar and a little juice from the orange.  I baked them at 400 degrees for 20 minutes.They were phenomenal.  One thing I would note is that the dough was very wet but this did not affect the outcome of the scone.  Just more wet than I am used to working with when making scones. I will be making these often.  In fact, I am making another slight variation of them today.  I did not have raspberries so I used 1 cup of blueberries and lemon zest instead of orange.  I also added just a little lemon juice to my cream. I just sprinkled the top with a little sugar and some cinnamon.  They are in the oven right now and I would be shocked if they weren't also delicious.  The dough wasn't nearly as wet but more of a consistency that I am use to working with when making scones.  I baked them at 400 degrees for about 20 minutes as well.<br/>Well, delicious as suspected!  Thank you for posting this recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
magnolia cafe corn muffins

this is a light, moist and not too sweet corn muffin that is really good...the only one we use now..terrific with soups..

1. preheat oven to 350
2. grease well 9 cups of a 12 cup muffin tin
3. in a large bowl , mic together the dry ingredients , making a well in the center
4. stir in the liquid ingredients until just combined , being careful not to overmix
5. the batter may be lumpy
6. fill the muffin cups about three-quarters full
7. bake for 18-20 minutes until lightly golden or a cake tester inserted into center of muffin comes out with moist crumbs attached
8. do not overbake
9. some residual heat will finish muffin
demonstrations.review: Moist and delicate!  I have made many different versions of cornbread/cornmeal in a pan and as muffins and mini muffins and these are probably the best I have ever made. They are just sweet enough and very moist and delicate. I would highly recommend this recipe and plan on using it from now on.  There isn't really a reason to search for a different on any more, I have found THE ONE!!

target.recipe_text:
steak   kidney pie  the way my mother made it

i am a brit living in florida and brought this recipe with me when i moved here over 25 years ago - and it's still made on a regular basis.
the secret is slow cooking the meat to increase the flavour. the addition of a good beer is optional and you may not want to do this if it is for children also.  this recipe has a fairly long preparation time and should be cooked a day in advance of when you plan to eat it.
a good steak & kidney pie should not be fancied up with exotic herbs, spices or vegetables. some of my american friends have loved this pie although, on occasion, i had to substitute additional mushrooms (just before baking) for kidneys. you really don't taste the kidneys; they just enhance the flavour.

1. cut the meat into 1" cubes
2. cut up the kidneys into small pieces
3. season the flour with salt & pepper and place into a large ziploc bag
4. place the meat in the bag and move around until it is all coated with the flour
5. place the meat into a tall sided frying pan
6. crumble in the stock cube and cover with just enough water to cover the meat
7. cook very slowly at about 200f for about 3 hours
8. let it become cold after cooking
9. when ready to make the pie , line a pie dish with shortcrust pastry , put in the meat and add the mushrooms
10. cover with puff pastry , having wet the shortcrust to encourage the puff pastry to stick to it
11. place in a 450f pre-heated oven for 20-30 minutes until the pastry is cooked
12. serve hot with roast potatoes , carrots and gravy
target.review:
I had to join food.com just to post a good review of your recipe.
Thatnks for sharing, it's down right delicious

demonstrations.recipe_text:
praline pumpkin date bread

found this recipe years ago.

1. heat oven to 350
2. grease bottoms only of 2 loaf pans , 9x5x3 or 8 1 / 2x 4 1 / 2x 2 1 / 2 inches
3. make praline topping by mixing all ingredients until crumbly and set aside
4. mix sugar , oil , vanilla , eggs and pumpkin in large bowl
5. stir in remaining ingredients except dates
6. stir in dates
7. pour batter into pans
8. sprinkle with topping
9. bake 50 to 60 minutes or until toothpick inserted in center comes out clean
10. cool 10 minutes
11. loosen sides of loaves from pans
12. remove from pans to wire rack
13. cool completely before slicing
14. wrap tightly and store at room temperature up to 4 days or refrigerate up to 10 days
demonstrations.review: yum we all liked it

demonstrations.recipe_text:
maple grilled peaches  or nectarines

what a perfect dish for an outdoor dinner!!  using your grill won't heat up the kitchen, and grilled peaches taste absolutely divine!  choose freestone peaches, because they are easy to cut neatly into halves.  from canadian living.

1. halve peaches
2. discard pits
3. place , cut side down , on greased grill over medium-low heat
4. close lid and grill for 7 minutes
5. turn peaches
6. brush with one-quarter of the maple syrup
7. sprinkle with nutmeg or cardamom
8. grill until tender , about 8 minutes
9. serve with ice cream
10. drizzle with remaining maple syrup
11. variation: maple-grilled apricots: replace peaches with apricots
12. do not peel
13. grill for 10 minutes
demonstrations.review: Too sweet, next time I might try this using half pure maple syrup and half water

demonstrations.recipe_text:
my mother s upside down cake

one of the major reasons i joined this website, yes i know there are many recipes. but try this one and see what you think, compare with your own :) you will certainly not be disappointed. i also find it is an excuse to get kids to eat fruit! we would always demand this every sunday after a roast, and pour tonnes of golden syrup over it and let the sponge absorb all the sweet gooeyness.

1. preheat the oven to 180-190c / 350-375f / gas mark 4
2. prepare the fruit , melt the butter and pour into the bottom of a 7 inch ovenproof dish or cake tin
3. top with the brown sugar and golden syrup and arrange the pineapple rings on the glaze
4. add a piece of banana in the centre of each ring
5. for the cake: cream the butter and sugar
6. gradually beat in the eggs , then fold in the flour
7. spread over the fruit then bake for approximately 1 1 / 4 hours
8. turn out , serve hot with a helping of cool double cream which soaks so yummily into the sponge -- or even cold as a cake rather than a dessert
9. warning: to not leave the remaining cake batter on the side- you'll demolish it ! or the kids will :)
10. serves 4 as a dessert , 6 for tea
demonstrations.review: Very good.  Didn't make any changes

target.recipe_text:
coconut cranberry chews

addictive; was rated grand prize winner in cookie recipe contest--originally submitted by nancy jamison

1. with a mixer on medium speed , beat butter , sugar , orange peel and vanilla until smooth
2. in another bowl mix flour , baking powder and salt
3. add butter mixture and beat on low speed for about 5 minutes
4. stir in cranberries and coconut
5. shape dough into 1-inch balls and place 2 inches apart on buttered baking sheets
6. bake in a 350 oven for 8 minutes
7. remove from oven and let cookies cool on sheets for 5 minutes
target.review: excellent recipe.  I made these out of Sunset magazine and they are delicious.  I bake for about 13 minutes to get a crisper buttery cookie.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cream cheese banana nut bread

for a request from southern living, january edition.  submitted by willie monroe, homewood, alabama.   prep time does not include making toppings.  the nutrition facts includes all of the topping ingredients.

1. beat butter and cream cheese at medium speed with electric mixer , until creamy
2. gradually add sugar , beating until light and fluffy
3. add eggs , 1 at a time , beating just until blended after each addition
4. combine flour and next 3 ingredients
5. gradually add to butter mixture , beating at low speed just until blended
6. stir in bananas , pecans , and vanilla
7. spoon batter into 2 greased and floured 8 x 4 inch loafpans
8. bake at 350 for 1 hour , or until tests clean
9. (shield with foil the last 15 minutes to prevent browning , if necessary
10. cool bread in pans on wire racks 10 minutes
11. remove from pans , and cool 30 minutes on wire racks before slicing
12. orange pecan topping:
13. sprinkle pecans over batter before baking
14. cool bread 10 minutes , remove from pans
15. stir together sugar , orange juice and orange rind
16. drizzle evenly over warm bread
17. cinnamon-crisp topping
18. stir together brown sugar , toasted pecans , flour , melted butter and cinnamon
19. sprinle mixture evenly over batter
20. bake and cool bread
demonstrations.review: Really excellent banana bread...wonderfully moist and light.  I used cake flour (because I started it and then realized I didn't have AP) and I think that really made for a light spongy texture.  I also used the Splenda baking blend because I'm watching sugar intake.  It was terrific and there is no doubt in my mind it would be sinful as written!  I did the cinnamon topping and will try the orange one next!  Thanks so much for requesting and posting this Miss Annie!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
tsr version of popeyes buttermilk biscuits by todd wilbur

great biscuit recipe. this is a copycat for popeye's buttermilk biscuits. please don't use salted butter in this recipe (or, indeed, in any of your baking). from www.topsecretrecipes.com

1. preheat oven to 400 degrees
2. mix together flour , sugar , salt , baking powder , and baking soda in a medium bowl
3. slice cold butter into cubes and use a pastry knife or potato masher to cut butter into dry mixture until no large chunks of butter remain
4. add buttermilk and milk and stir with a spoon until dough forms
5. roll out to 1 / 2-inch thick on a floured surface
6. cut biscuits with a 3-inch biscuit cutter and arrange on a lightly-greased or parchment paper-lined baking sheet
7. bake for 22 to 24 minutes or until tops begin to turn light brown
8. remove biscuits from the oven and cool for a couple of minutes , then brush each biscuit top with melted butter
demonstrations.review: These are very good....nice and tender, a little sweet and delicious.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
zesty low fat chicken breasts

very tasty, you can make it as hot or as mild as you want. quick easy dish - no muss no fuss

1. put the breasts in a 9x13-inch baking dish
2. whisk remaining ingredients together until they are well blended
3. pour over the breasts
4. coat both sides of the breasts with the sauce
5. bake in 400f oven for approx 30 minutes or until the chicken is done
6. remove breasts , keep warm
7. pour the sauce into a sauce pan stir in the cornstarch that has been mixed with a tbsp of water , bring to a boil and allow to thicken whisk constantly
8. pour over the chicken & serve
demonstrations.review: I was also skeptical but this was wonderful...nice tender breasts with a fantastic tangy zesty sweet sauce.  Had this with rice and sauteed green beans.  Thanks for sharing!

target.recipe_text:
kittencal s juicy hamburger burger

we all have our different tastes for burgers i like mine flavorful and juicy this recipe will give you the best of both! see the bottom of the recipe for tips on even more extra juicy burgers! --- making a indentation in the middle of the uncooked burger will prevent the burgers from puffing up into meatballs shapes while cooking and keeps them flat --- do not add any salt into the burger mixture as the dry onion soup already has a lot of salt content, you can sprinkle some on towards the end of cooking if needed, if desired you may add in 3-4 tablespoons of your favorite barbecue sauce to the ground beef mixture

1. in a bowl crumble the ground beef with clean hands
2. add in the dry soup mix , egg , garlic , breadcrumbs or crushed soda cracker crumbs , worcestershire sauce , black pepper and hot sauce
3. using clean hands mix until combined , add in more breadcrumbs or cracker crumbs if needed to just hold the mixture together
4. divide the ground beef into 6 equal patties
5. using your large finger or the back of a small spoon make a shallow dent into the center of each patty
6. place the patties onto a large plate or a small cookie sheet
7. cover with plastic wrap and refrigerate for a minimum of 6 hours or up to 24 hours to blend flavors
8. grill or pan fry the burgers as desired until cooked through
9. serve burgers in toasted buns with choice of condiments
target.review: I thought the potato was kind of wierd, but you are tight!! they are delishious!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
iced hibiscus tea

this tangy and sweet beverage is found all over  egypt, but is especially popular with  street vendors. from party by the pyramids.  notes: dried hibiscus flowers can be found at specialty food stores and at latin and caribbean markets, where they are called sorrel or flor de jamaica.

1. in a medium saucepan , combine water and hibiscus flowers and bring to a boil
2. simmer over moderate heat for 5 minutes
3. add sugar and stir until dissolved
4. pour the drink into a medium bowl
5. fill a larger bowl with ice water and set the smaller bowl inside
6. stir the drink occasionally until chilled , about 10 minutes
7. strain into a pitcher and serve in tall glasses over ice
demonstrations.review: i have my own hibiscus plants, (yes i live in new england, but they are doing pretty good!) and i never knew you could make tea out of the flowers :) thanks alot!!!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chicken scaloppine with lemon glaze   low fat and delicious

this is a wonderful lower-fat restaurant-quality dish that is easy to make, i also like to add in a few tablespoons of capers and cook with the lemon glaze if you are a lover of capers then add them in as it really adds to the flavour of this dish ---  this lemon sauce is not a heavy creamy sauce which is what makes this dish lower in fat, it is more like a glaze that soaks into the chicken, and i would strongly suggest to double or even triple the glaze i most always do, and please be certain to use only dry breadcrumbs as fresh will not stick to the chicken as well --- this is *very* good!

1. in a small bowl or shallow dish whisk together mustard and eggs
2. set aside
3. combine the dry bread crumbs with poultry seasoning , garlic powder and seasoning salt
4. spread on a piece of waxed paper
5. dip the breasts firstly in egg / mustard mixture then coat well with the crumb mixture , pressing downs with hands to adhear the crumbs to the breast
6. heat the olive oil in a skillet over medium heat
7. add in the chicken and cook for about 5 minutes on each side , or until it is no longer pink inside
8. remove and transfer to a plate to keep warm
9. for the glaze
10. in the same skillet add in the broth , lemon juice and 1 / 4 teaspoon salt bring to a boil scraping any brown bits from the pan
11. add in lemon slices and parsley
12. mix to combine for about 1 minute
13. spoon the glaze / sauce over chicken
14. delicious !
demonstrations.review: i am DEFINATLY going to try this one, i don't usually go for low-fat but this looks absolutly delishious!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s italian melt in your mouth meatballs

cooking the meatballs in simmering pasta sauce  will not only add so much extra flavor to the sauce the meatballs will be melt-in-your-mouth tender, you may of course oven-bake the meatballs for about 25 minutes,  --- don't be afraid to add in more parmesan cheese and a little more milk, there is no need to measure exactly, this recipe is pretty much foolproof, leftover cooked meatballs make a wonderful pizza topping just slice thinly and freeze until ready to use ----- these also make wonderful juicy burgers shaped into patties-- for more of my tried and true recipes check out my food blog at www.kittencalskitchen.com

1. mix all ingredients together in a large bowl
2. shape into small meatballs
