demonstrations.review: This was easy and good. After turkey all week due to Thanksgiving, I was craving something else. I didn't use the potato chips and I put more hot sauce on. I only had Italian sliced bread, so I used that. I will also try this on a chicken (or turkey) sandwich. Easy and good.

target.recipe_text:
crisp rice date nut balls

this is good to make at christmas and give as gifts.

1. in sauce pan , combine sugar , margarine , salt and dates
2. allow to boil for five minutes , stirring constantly
3. remove from heat , add vanilla
4. fold in crisp rice cereal and nuts
5. while warm , roll into balls and let dry on waxed paper or racks
6. to make balls , butter hand well and keep buttering while you work
7. when cold , roll into confectioners sugar
target.review: Awesome recipe - I have some sitting in the fridge right now waiting for Christmas Day.  I've also rolled mine in dessicated coconut instead of icing sugar.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pizza crust  all purpose flour or spelt flour

do i dare post another spelt flour recipe?  after my spelt bread recipe #206562 caused a bit of a controversy, i will add the following disclaimer.  i substitute spelt flour for regular flour in recipes so my son, who is allergic to wheat, can enjoy them.  he does not seem to be bothered by it, however it has come to my attention that people with certain wheat allergies can have a reaction to this flour - so please check with your doctor.  
anyways, this pizza dough is very good and very easy.  that's all i need to say - enjoy!

1. set aside 1 cup of flour from total amount
2. mix 1 1 / 2 cup flour , yeast and salt
3. put oil in hot water
4. add water and oil to flour mixture
5. stir well
6. add extra cup of flour
7. knead
8. pay attention to the consistency of the dough
9. sometimes with spelt flour you need to add a bit extra to get the doughy consistency you need
10. let rest for 10 minutes
11. press into greased pizza pan
12. top with favorite pizza toppings
13. bake at 400 degrees for 20 minutes
14. enjoy !
demonstrations.review: Great dough, easy to work with.  I pre-cooked mine a little before adding the toppings.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
turnip soup

i got this recipe from the heritage quilters. boy was i surprised to find out this delicious soup had turnips as one of the main ingredients. i am one of the first people to turn my nose up at turnips but this soup will surprise you.

1. place turnips , potatoes , and onions in saucepan
2. cover with small amount of water and simmer until tender
3. drain
4. mash with potato masher
5. add butter
6. mix flour with 1 / 4 cup milk
7. add to mixture and blend well
8. add chicken stock
9. mix thoroughly
10. return to heat and bring to a boil
11. remove from heat and add remaining 3 / 4 cup milk
12. reheat to serving temperature taking care not to boil
13. garnish with your choice of parsley , bacon or croutons
demonstrations.review: I made this soup only because we had several turnips that needed using (Japanese turnips which are smaller and white, with a mild radish flavour).  I added a bit of bacon, and think the soup would have been very bland without it. Normal turnips would probably have provided a lot more flavour. Nonetheless, unless you really love the flavour of turnips I would still only use this recipe so I didn't waste healthy veges.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
gluten free awesome chocolate chip cookies

gluten free? you might not think so because these even fooled my husband! chewy, crunchy or how ever you like them - these are a real treat.

1. by hand blend margarine , sugars , egg , & vanilla until creamy
2. in a separate bowl blend flours , baking soda salt
3. combine both bowls and mix well
4. add chocolate chips and mix
5. roll into balls
6. bake at 375 for 12-15 minutes on a lighty greased preheated cookie sheet
demonstrations.review: These were wonderful.  They taste just like wheat flour cookies.  I replaced a 1/4 cup of the soy flour with potato flour, as I find soy flour bitter sometimes.

target.recipe_text:
rocky road

yummy rocky road for chocky lovers. put a few in a cellophane bag and tie with green and red ribbon for a tasty christmas gift.

1. line a 30cm square tin with baking paper
2. melt chocolate and copha in a heatproof bowl over gently boiling water and stir until smooth
3. combine all other ingredients in another large bowl leaving aside 2 tblsp of coconut
4. pour in melted chocolate and mix well
5. pour completed mixture into the lined tin and spread
6. sprinkle on the remaining coconut
7. refrigerate then cut into chunky squares
8. enjoy
target.review: Easy, pretty, quick to do. Made for an xmas candy assortment. I changed this from 4 to 5 stars, it was easy, pretty and wonderful, highly reccommended to solve holiday gift giving problems with class.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
edna s apple crumble  aka  apple crisp

a simple and easy to make but oh so yummy recipe. known as apple crumble in the uk and apple crisp in the us

1. put apples in an 8 or 9 inch square baking dish
2. combine the rest of the ingredients in a separate bowl and mix
3. spread crumble mixture over apples and bake for 35 minutes in a 375f degree oven
4. for an added treat top off with a little english custard
demonstrations.review: Great topping for any kind of fruit.  I had nothing but canned pears and peaches in the house and used it on that and it was fantastic.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
easy seafood quiche

my friend joyce & i skipped beauty school one day and exchanged recipes instead! i love this quiche recipe she gave me. it doesn't require any fresh seafood.

1. preheat the oven to 350 degrees
2. place the cheese in bottom of the pie shell
3. in a bowl , mix the cans of seafood
4. then spinkle on top of the cheese in the shell
5. add the onions on top of the seafood
6. mix together the remaining ingredients and then pour in the pie shell
7. bake for 40-45 minutes
demonstrations.review: This is really prett, fast and easy to do.  It would be nicer with non-canned seafood of course, but I had everything to make this in the house.  I did add some "herbs for fish" from a frozen box of mixed herbs.  One day, when I'm feeling rich, I'll do it with the fresh seafood!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
homemade  suddenly salad

i used to love that stuff years ago. here's how to make it even better homemade. (the bacon ranch one.)

1. in large bowl , mix mayo , dressing mix , bacon bits , shredded carrots and onion powder
2. chill while making the rest
3. cook pasta according to pkg
4. directions for pasta using the shortest alotted time
5. drain and cool
6. fold in pasta well
7. fold in peas last , carefully
8. chill for several hours
9. serve chilled or room temperature
10. refresh salad if needed with a tiny bit of mayo , but it usually doesn't need it
11. garnish top with more bacon bits / pieces
demonstrations.review: Very nice, better right after it is maybe, and not as good as a leftover.  Be very careful of too much saltiness though. Makes a very pretty colorful salad.

target.recipe_text:
mountain dew jelly

nan

1. pour mountian dew and lemon juice into a large pot
2. bring to boil
3. boil 3 minutes
4. cool slightly
5. then follow the sure jell directions
6. process for 10 minutes in a boiling water bath
7. you can use more mountain dew and reduce it to 3-1 / 4 c
8. for a more concentrated flavor
target.review:
I was so happy to see this recipe! I am originally from Marion, Va which is the birthplace of Mountain Dew. I can't beleive I have never heard of this jelly before. What a great gift this will make for friends and family back home!
Thanks for a great recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
banana banana bread

why compromise the banana flavor? my banana bread is moist and delicious with loads of banana flavor! ultimate comfort food, and it's wonderful toasted!! (make sure to use bananas with a lot of black on them for the best flavor! the blacker the bananas, the stronger the banana flavor of the bread.)

1. preheat oven to 350
2. lightly grease 9 x 5 loaf pan
3. in large bowl , combine flour , soda and salt
4. in separate bowl , cream together butter and brown sugar
5. stir in eggs and mashed bananas until well blended
6. stir banana mixture into flour mixture
7. stir just to moisten
8. pour batter into prepared loaf pan
9. bake in preheated oven for 60-65 minutes until a toothpick inserted into center of loaf comes out clean
10. let bread cool in pan for 10 minutes , then turn out onto a wire rack
demonstrations.review: Just made this for the second time. I made mini-muffins this time and it only took 25 minutes to bake. My DD will be so happy when she gets home from school. She loves banana bread!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
avocado lime salad

a great vegan salad using avocado, tomatoes and scallions. adapted from vegetarian times magazine. a popular spanish and mexican recipe.

1. in a medium glass or ceramic bowl , whisk together 2 tablespoons lime juice and 1 / 2 teaspoon salt
2. add tomatoes , avocados , scallions and garlic
3. using rubber spatula , gently fold to combine
4. season to taste with pepper
5. in large bowl , whisk together olive oil , cumin , remaining tablespoon lime juice and 1 / 8 teaspoon salt
6. add lettuce and toss
7. season to taste with pepper
8. divide lettuce among plates
9. top each with mound of avocado mixture
10. top with cucumber slices
11. sprinkle with cilantro and serve
demonstrations.review: This is incredible. It is now my favorite salad!! Thanks!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
blue chicken breasts

ok, there's a blue cheese sauce over these chicken breasts - what were you thinking?

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. wash chicken well and dry
3. combine herbs , salt and lots of freshly-crushed black pepper
4. sprinkle chicken pieces with seasonings
5. in non-stick skillet , melt butter and brown chicken on both sides
6. place the browned chicken in a baking dish just large enough to hold it in one layer
7. in same skillet , saut the garlic
8. reduce heat to lowest setting , add the blue cheese and the yoghurt , and stir until well blended
9. spoon sauce over chicken
10. cover and bake for 50 minutes
11. remove cover
12. add chives and cook 5 additional minutes
13. serve over rice with sauce from casserole
demonstrations.review:
Yummy!! What a wonderful dish. The sauce was excellent.
Thanks!!

target.recipe_text:
easy cabbage rolls with sauerkraut

this recipe is so easy and people just love these cabbage rolls. much of the flavor comes from the sauerkraut and tomato juice, so there is little else to it. i have substituted lean ground beef for half of the ground pork with much success.

1. combine pork , rice , onions , pepper , garlic powder , salt and paprika in large bowl
2. steam heads of cabbage until leaves remove easily take handfuls of meat mixture and roll up in cabbage leaves
3. place rolls in roasting pan
4. after covering the bottom of the pan , top with half of the sauerkraut and half of the tomatoes
5. repeat with second layer
6. pour tomato juice over top
7. cover and bake 2 1 / 2 hours at 350 degrees
target.review: Perfect,I have been searching for a recipe like my mom used to use and yours is spot on. I can't wait to try it.thanks for posting it

demonstrations.recipe_text:
easy won ton soup

my son loves won ton soup and so i learned how to make it by adjusting the ingredients slightly to ones that i could get in our small town. i blended different recipes into my own.

1. bring large kettle of water to boil for won ton
2. put chicken broth in another large pot on low heat to simmer
3. do not place cooked won ton in boiling or bubbling broth as it will tear them up
4. mix together pork , seafood , salt , pepper , sesame oil , egg and sugar in a food processor until well mixed
5. place 8- 10 wrappers on counter
6. spoon 1 tsp of won ton mixture on each wrapper
7. to help seal , baste 2 edges of wrapper with milk
8. fold into triangle and seal with finger
9. place the 8- 10 filled wrappers in boiling water in kettle for 3 minutes
10. remove gently with sieve and place in chicken broth
11. continue batches until won ton filling is used up
12. if you have extra filling , it can be formed in a ball , boiled and placed in broth as a meatball
13. to increase recipe i use approximately
14. 2 to 1 pork to seafood
15. if you like vegetables in your broth , you can add to your personal liking
16. total time to prepare and cook is about 30-40 minutes as you are preparing one batch as you are cooking the other batch
demonstrations.review: This is the only recipe close to what we are use to. Vancover B.C. has a huge china town and a great selection of chinese restaraunts. we grew up being treated with soup very close to this recipe.Good job Meg.The key is mixing shrimp with pork

demonstrations.recipe_text:
black bean cakes

a recent trip to cocso and i'm now the proud owner of a large stockpile of black beans.  that has sent me combing my cookbooks for meal options using this healthful and versatile ingredients.  keeping what i find here for quick and easy access until i have a chance to try them.  the original recipe for these delectable cakes included a tablespoon of chorizo, though i intend to make them vegetarian. these can also easily be made vegan with the use of a little soy yogurt. serve these as a substantial appetizer or along with a lovely green salad as a light meal or lunch. with the chorizo, these are 3 points per serving.  the recipe can easily be modified to be core. the cakes also freeze well for reheating later.

1. place half the rinsed beans in a blender or food processor with the broth and puree into a paste
2. add more liquid if needed
3. mix together the bean paste with the reserved whole beans in a mixing bowl
4. in a nonstick skillet , add the teaspoon of oil onions , garlic , red pepper and jalapeno and cook for 3 or 4 minutes
5. add the cumin and chili powder and continue to cook another minute
6. remove from heat and let cool a bit
7. combine the sauteed vegetables with the beans
8. add the egg white , cornmeal , lime juice , cilantro
9. let stand for 5-8 minutes to begin softening the cornmeal and allow the flavors to combine
10. form the mix into eight equal sized cakes
11. spray a non-stick skillet over medium high heat with cooking spray
12. add the bean cakes to the skillet and cook until browned , just a minute or so on each side
13. combine the salsa with the yogurt and sour cream
14. serve the bean cakes with a dollop of the dairy / salsa topping and garnish with additional cilantro if desired
demonstrations.review: I can't wait to try this recipe.I to am always looking for appetizing ways to use black beans. This recipe contains all the ingredients we love and always have on hand.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crock pot   smashed  peaches

easy and tasty dessert that doesn't heat up the kitchen, but smells heavenly! very cobbler-like.

1. spray crock pot with non-stick cooking spray
2. combine sugars and bisquick in a bowl
3. add eggs and vanilla
4. add margarine and milk
5. add peaches and cinnamon
6. pour into crock pot
7. cook on low for 6 to 8 hours
8. enjoy !
demonstrations.review: We loved it.so easy and a great way to use up peaches.Next time i will use clear vanilla and only white sugar so the color of the peaches show.YUMMY

target.recipe_text:
prawn   shrimp   rougaille

i saw this made today on food safari during a program featuring the food of mauritius. the sauce is supposedly eaten at least twice a day so i'm imagining it is used with other seafoods, meats and as a condiment. i really want to try this with my home grown tomatoes.

1. heat oil over medium heat and add onions , 1 / 2 of the garlic and cook until golden
2. pour in 1 / 2 of the wine to soften onions
3. add tomatoes and cook for a few minutes over high heat to reduce
4. stir in salt , pepper , paprika , cumin and a drizzle of olive oil
5. add thyme , parsley and chillies
6. in a separate frypan , fry remaining garlic in oil
7. add prawns , season with pepper and cook for 2 minutes
8. pour in remaining wine to deglaze pan
9. return prawns to rougaille and stir through coriander
10. serve with steamed white rice
target.review: So simple to make and yet so flavoursome.  I used peeled uncooked prawns.  I didn't have chilli so I used red chilli flakes instead, also had to omit the wine but used a splash of cider vinegar.  I served it over rice and the whole family enjoyed it.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
fantastic taco casserole

i originally found this taco casserole recipe in a taste of home magazine.  since then, i have made this recipe at least 50 times.  i love it because the ingredients list isn't complicated and, based on the layers, i can readily remember all ingredients when i am at the store without my recipe card.  i have served this for myself and had wonderful leftovers or many times i have made it for company with a nice green salad to accompany it.  i hope you enjoy it as much as i do.

1. brown ground beef and drain
2. add taco seasoning and cook according to package directions , adding proper amount of water
3. put corn chips on bottom of 8x8" dish
4. cook refried beans on stove until hot
5. add 1 cup cheese and 1 cup salsa
6. stir until combined
7. pour beans over corn chips in dish
8. add beef to top of beans
9. sprinkle remaining cheese over top
10. sprinkle green onions and black olives over cheese
11. bake in a 375 degree oven until the cheese is sufficiently melted
12. take out of oven and sprinkle chopped tomatoes on top
13. wait 1-2 minutes and then serve
demonstrations.review: I made this for a casual birthday get together and it was simple and very tasty.   Somehow I missed the part where it mentioned to add tomatoes but it still turned out good.   I will be making this one again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
banana banana bread

why compromise the banana flavor? my banana bread is moist and delicious with loads of banana flavor! ultimate comfort food, and it's wonderful toasted!! (make sure to use bananas with a lot of black on them for the best flavor! the blacker the bananas, the stronger the banana flavor of the bread.)

1. preheat oven to 350
2. lightly grease 9 x 5 loaf pan
3. in large bowl , combine flour , soda and salt
4. in separate bowl , cream together butter and brown sugar
5. stir in eggs and mashed bananas until well blended
6. stir banana mixture into flour mixture
7. stir just to moisten
8. pour batter into prepared loaf pan
9. bake in preheated oven for 60-65 minutes until a toothpick inserted into center of loaf comes out clean
10. let bread cool in pan for 10 minutes , then turn out onto a wire rack
demonstrations.review: Very easy and delicious.  I halved all the ingredients as I only had one very very ripe banana to use up.  I then poured the mix into silicone muffin pan and made six yummy muffins.  Perfect and so simple,thank you.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
roman veal scaloppine

another quick easy delicious veal dish. my butcher got 10 scallops to a pound for me, so this was inexpensive as well. serve over pasta with the sauce.

1. heat oven to 200 degrees
2. put 2 tablespoons olive oil in a medium saucepan over medium heat
3. add garlic and , when it sizzles , tomatoes and salt and pepper
4. cook , stirring occasionally , until tomatoes break down , about 10 minutes , then add olives , and turn heat to low
5. put about 3 tablespoons olive oil in a large skillet , preferably nonstick , over medium-high heat
6. sprinkle veal with salt and pepper , then dredge it in flour
7. saut as many slices as will comfortably fit in skillet , just until brown on both sides , 5 minutes or less
8. remove to a plate , and keep warm in oven while sauting remaining slices
9. taste sauce , and adjust seasoning
10. spoon it over veal slices , and arrange lemon on top
11. sprinkle with parsley , and serve
demonstrations.review: Simple but tasty dish.  I used two different types of olives and it come out lovely.  Very quick too which is important to me.

target.recipe_text:
greek lemon roast potatoes

a wonderful side dish to any meal.

1. preheat the oven to 400 degrees
2. wash and cut the potatoes into quarters lengthwise and put into a large ovenproof baking dish
3. squeeze the lemons of their juice and grate the zest from 1 or 2 , pour the lemon juice over the potatoes
4. drizzle with the olive oil coating all the potatoes
5. add the garlic , oregano and the lemon zest , seasoning the potatoes well with the salt and white pepper
6. bake uncovered for 45-60 minutes or until tender and nicely browned
7. serve with lemon wedges
target.review: Wonderful recipe.  I am on a lo-carb diet but tried one piece to rate it.  The main source is the rest of the family.  It recieved raves.  I had fresh rosemary and oregano and of course used fresh lemon and zest w/olive oil.  Thank you.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
green beans with balsamic  dijon and dill  thanksgiving

from a junior league cookbook tucked away in my thanksgiving collection.

1. cook beans in a saucepan of boiling , salted water until crisp-tender
2. drain and keep warm
3. combine shallots , mustard , vinegar , olive oil and lemon juice in a small saucepan
4. add salt and pepper to taste and whisk together
5. heat mixture , then pour over the beans
6. toss to coat
7. sprinkle with the dill and serve immediately
demonstrations.review: Wonderful dish and a much loved keeper and use it again and again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cream of coconut chicken

i tried several recipes for chicken in coconut sauce and just could not find one that suited me.  i adapted another recipe to make this one and am very pleased with the results.  my father thought it was a little too sweet, but i loved it, just like i get at a chinese restaurant.

1. in a large skillet , over med-high heat , saut onion and garlic
2. cut chicken into medium size pieces and place in skillet and brown both sides
3. reduce heat to medium
4. add carrots and jalapeno peppers , continue cooking
5. add spices to coconut milk and mix well
6. pour mixture over chicken in skillet and cover
7. continue to cook over medium heat until chicken is done
8. about 30 minutes
9. stir occasionally to keep from sticking
demonstrations.review: This is an absolutely no fail recipe.  After cooking this dish twice I changed a few things.  I marinated my chicken around 15 minutes in the garlic and real minced ginger, I used equal parts of ginger and garlic. Then I doubled the jalapeno, and added a can of chunk pineapple drained in the last five to ten minutes of cooking. Also I do not stir fry with olive oil it changes the composition and can be toxic at high temperatures.  Use I use peanut oil but any high heat resistant oil will do.  I served with stir fried baby bok choy and snow peas w/large angle sliced carrots.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
potsie s white trash dirty martini

what makes a classy martini become white trash? a pickled pod of okra instead of an olive, of course. i came up with this 10 years ago when i was out of olives and then noticed a jar of pickled okra in the fridge. a local bar that i frequent began making them for me and now it's very popular there.

1. for best results and taste keep vodka in the freezer
2. pour 1 / 4 oz of vermouth into a frozen martini glass and swirl it around til the inside of the glass has been coated
3. discard vermouth
4. combine vodka and brine in a cold shaker glass with ice and shake vigorously
5. strain into the cold martini glass swirled with vermouth
6. place pickled okra pod into glass
7. don't forget to eat the drunken okra pod after you have finished the drink !
8. repeat steps 2-6 as often as needed
demonstrations.review: Surfing through for an original martini blend this one caught my eye and that of my Son-in-law.  We had the fixing and they were a big hit.

target.recipe_text:
easy slow cooker chicken dinner

serve with a green salad, bread and wine, such as, pinot noir or zinfandel for a perfect meal. cook time is 5 to 9 hours.

1. place chicken , carrots and potatoes in slow cooker
2. combine remaining ingredients in a bowl and pour over chicken
3. cover and cook on high about 5 hours or on low for about 9 hours , until chicken leg and thigh come off easily when pulled
target.review: Made this last night for dinner and it was very good. My kids loved it and that is quite an accomplishment to find something that they agree on. It was yummy. Thank you!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crock pot oniony pork chops with creamy mustard sauce

if you like onions, do try this crock pot dish. note that you will have a lot of sauce.

1. in a skillet , heat oil over medium-high heat and brown pork chops on both sides
2. place in bottom of slow cooker when browned
3. in same skillet , reduce heat to medium and saute onions until softened
4. add garlic , dry mustard , salt and pepper , and cayenne and cook , stirring , for 1 minute
5. add flour and cook , stirring , for 1 minute
6. add vinegar and wine and cook until thickened
7. pour this mixture over pork chops , put lid on crock pot and cook on low for 4 to 5 hours or on high for 2 to 2-1 / 2 hours , or just until pork is tender
8. remove pork chops from slow cooker and place on a warmed platter
9. stir dijon mustard and whipping cream into juices in slow cooker
10. when well combined , turn slow cooker off and pour sauce over chops on platter and serve immediately
demonstrations.review: Great pork chops and the sauce was absolutely wonderful. The whole family really enjoyed it. I cut down on the onion amount some because I have picky young ones, but the taste was still great. Thank you for sharing this recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
excellent carrot cake

chock full of flavor, this is the best carrot cake! it tastes even better the next day after the flavors meld. a tad more time consuming than the average carrot cake, but well worth it!

1. combine first 5 ingredients
2. beat well
3. mix flour , soda , salt and cinnamon
4. add to creamed mixture
5. stir well
6. add carrots , walnuts , pineapple and coconut
7. stir well
8. pour batter into greased and floured 13x9 baking pan
9. bake at 350 for 55 minutes , or until pick comes out clean
10. buttermilk glaze: combine first 5 ingredients in large saucepan
11. bring to a boil
12. cook 4 minutes on medium heat
13. remove from heat
14. add vanilla
15. pour buttermilk glaze over warm cake
16. let cake cool
17. cream cheese frosting: mix cream cheese and butter
18. beat until smooth
19. gradually add sugar , beating until light and fluffy
20. stir in vanilla
21. spread cream cheese frosting on top of cooled cake
demonstrations.review: Great carrot cake. The whole family loved it! Easy to put together-Yum! Thanks for posting this.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
creamy greek salad dressing

greek salads are usually only dressed with olive oil and maybe lemon juice or red-wine vinegar. but this dressing is made of 'greek' ingredients so, it's my greek dressing.

1. in a blender or food processor , whirl all the ingredients except the buttermilk for one minute
2. with the blender running , slowly pour in the buttermilk and blend until thick and creamy
3. chill at least 1 hour so the flavours meld
4. refrigerate , tightly covered
5. this makes nearly 2 cups of dressing and stays fresh for 3-4 days
6. if the dressing separates , just give it a whizz in the blender again
demonstrations.review: This was a nice change from the regular old salad dressing that we usually have. Strong, wonderful flavors. My kids loved it too. We will be making this one often. Thank you for posting it.

target.recipe_text:
white chocolate coconut macadamia cookies

ooooh..i am just..speechless! this is incredible! 8)

1. heat oven to 375
2. in small bowl , mix the flour , baking powder& soda& salt
3. in large bowl , combine the butter , sugars& vanilla extract
4. beat at high speed , scraping the bowl often , beat mixture until creamy
5. add in the egg , beat until well mixed
6. reduce the speed to low , gradually adding in flour mixture
7. beat well after each addition
8. with your hands , stir in the white chips , coconut& nuts
9. by rounded tb , drop the dough onto nongreased cookie sheets
10. bake for 8-11 minutes or until edges are slightly browned
11. let cookies cool for 2 minutes before removing to cool on rack
target.review: These were pretty good!  I did as other reviewers suggested and rolled the dough into little balls when I put it on the cookie sheet, and they turned out very uniform and pretty.  The only changes I made were that I used 1/2 bag of white chocolate chips (6 oz.) and only 1/2 cup of macadamia nuts....wow, I'm glad I did.  There's no way the dough would have been able to contain an entire bag of white chocolate chips!  I baked for about 10 mins, and although they're somewhat soft, I'm hoping they'll soften up a bit after sitting in an airtight container for a while.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s 1 gram low fat banana blueberry muffins

less than 1 gram of fat in each muffin  but you wouldn't even know they are low-fat, these are even better the next day, and are just as delicious without the berries, of coarse you can use full-fat sour cream or yogurt, flavored yogurts only add to the taste of these muffins, i like to sprinkle a sugar/cinnamon mixture on top of each muffin before baking but that is optional, see note on bottom for doubling the recipe. for greasing see recipe#78579 --- visit www.kittencalskitchen.com for more low fat recipes!

1. set oven to 350 degrees
2. grease or line 12 regular-size muffin tins with paper liners
3. in a large bowl mix together flour , baking powder , baking soda , salt cinnamon , nutmeg and blueberries
4. in another bowl beat banana , sour cream , sugar , egg and vanilla until just blended
5. stir into the dry blueberry mixture just until combined
6. scoop / divide the mixture between the muffin tins
7. bake for 15-20 minutes or until the muffins test done
demonstrations.review: Delicious!  The only change I made was to use 1/2 whole wheat flour and 1/2 all-purpose flour.  Very moist and yummy!  Will freeze to eat for breakfast.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
fantastic banana bran muffins

this is a fantastic muffin that bakes out very high and moist, i have even added a finely chopped large apple into the flour mixture. if you prefer a sweeter muffin then add in more brown sugar. you can use 1-1/3 cup cake and pastry flour instead of all-purpose flour.

1. set oven to 350 degrees
2. line 12 muffin tins with paper liners
3. in a bowl , whisk flour , oats , bran , baking powder , baking soda and salt
4. in another bowl , whisk egg , oil and brown sugar together
5. in a small bowl mix together the mashed banana , buttermilk and molasses
6. add / mix into the oil mixture to combine
7. if you are adding in a chopped apple , peel the apple now , then mix it in with the flour mixture
8. make a well in the center of the flour mixture
9. add in the banana / oil mixture into the flour mixture
10. stirring only to combine
11. gently stir in raisins and nuts
12. divide evenly between prepared muffin cups
13. bake for 20-22 minutes , or until muffins tops spring back when lightly touched , and a toothpick comes out clean when inserted in the center of the muffin
demonstrations.review: Delicious, healthy muffin!  This is probably the best bran muffin recipe I've found.  I love that oats are incorporated along with the bran.  I used all whole wheat flour instead of all-purpose flour and added 1 cup of frozen blueberries, and they were fantastic!  I omitted the raisins and nuts since I didn't have any on hand.  I plan on freezing these and pulling one out for breakfast each morning.  Thanks, Kittencal.....your recipes never disappoint!  :)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
lemon crinkle cookies

wonderful lemon flavor.

1. cream shortening and brown sugar until fluffy
2. add egg and lemon rind , beating well
3. combine flour , baking soda , cream of tartar , ginger , and salt
4. stir into creamed mixture
5. roll dough into 1-inch balls
6. roll each in sugar
7. place 2 inches apart on ungreased cookie sheet
8. bake at 350 degrees for 10-12 minutes
demonstrations.review: Delicious!  This makes for a lovely tea/coffee cookie.  I didn't have a lemon in the house, so I used 2 tsp of lemon extract and 2 tbsp of lemon juice....such a great lemon flavor!  I also opted to coat them in powdered sugar afterwards instead of granulated sugar beforehand.  I will definitely make these again!

target.recipe_text:
tasty chickpeas

from the ayurvedic cookbook. so delicious and easy! can be made spicy or milder depending on the curry powder you use.

1. heat oil in a heavy skillet
2. when hot add mustard seeds
3. when seeds pop , add tomato and curry powder
4. cook a couple minutes then add remaining ingredients , stir , and cook 2-3 minutes or till heated through
target.review: Very good.  I made a few changes since I didn't have mustard seed.  I picked out what I could but ended up using garam masala in its place.  I added more than a tsp of curry powder and will next time add way less salt.  I added a pinch of mustard powder, about a half cup of thawed kale and about 1/3 cup of chopped fresh cilantro.  That added the umph I needed.  Thanks for sharing.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
homemade crackers

easy, tasty crackers. great with hummus or other dips.

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. combine flour , garlic , rosemary , pepper and baking soda
3. add water and mix until smooth dough forms
4. with rolling pin , flatten dough until 1 / 8 inch thick
5. sprinkle salt over dough
6. bake on cookie sheet 10 minutes until firm
7. remove and cut into desired shape with sharp knife
8. return to oven until browned and crunchy
demonstrations.review:
I can't really rate this based on the orginal recipe, but will assume following exactly would have yielded good results.  

I used chickpea flour in place of regular flour, less than 1/3 cup of water, 1 garlic clove, cracked pepper, baking soda, sesame seeds, whole flax seeds, ground almonds, and a little less than a tbsp of olive oil & freshly crushed rosemary.  I sifted the flour and baking soda, added the other dry ingredients, mixed then added the water and oil & mixed again to form a dough.  Was still very moist so added chickpea flour as needed and rolled out.  This flour tends to be sticky so I cut into pieces before putting on cookie sheet & sprinkled with sea salt.  Baked 10 min as instructed, poked holes, cooked another 10 or so minutes until firm.  I enjoyed the crackers with white bean hummus.  Thanks for sharing.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
apple banana cake

very moist, very delicious. the recipe was given to me by a friend.

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees f
2. combine all the wet ingredients in large bowl and mix well
3. combine dry ingredients in a separate bowl and mix well
4. add dry to wet ingredients and mix thoroughly
5. pour into an ungreased 9"x13" pan
6. bake for 1 hour
demonstrations.review:
I made this some months back & making again today. I deviated from the recipe since I didn't have 4 cups of apples. I made up for the apples with shredded sweet potato, used melted organic virgin coconut oil instead of vegetable oil. I also added unsweetened shredded coconut and decreased the amount of sugar.

I'll do pretty much the same thing today, but will be using cooked sweet potatoes (thought I would be making candied yams) and sweetened coconut flakes (couldn't find unsweetened) so will decrease the sugar even more.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
honey mustard curry chicken

extremely easy, addictingly delicious.

1. preheat oven to 175c
2. place chicken pieces in prepared pan
3. combine all ingredients and pour over chicken
4. bake , covered for about 2 hours in oven
demonstrations.review: I just made this for dinner tonight.  I tossed it in a skillet with carrots, onions and peppers, cubed chicken breast, and shrimp.  It was a little bland for my taste so I added more curry along with some Jamaican allspice and about 1/3 cup of coconut milk.  Perfect.  Thanks for sharing.

target.recipe_text:
easy cole slaw

this is the recipe i turn to most when i make cole slaw.  the recipe comes from stephskitchen.com.

1. combine all ingredients except cole slaw mix in a large bowl and combine well
2. add the cole slaw mix and toss to coat
3. cover and refrigerate several hours or overnight to allow flavors to blend
target.review: This is the dressing base I go to when we're craving good ol' creamy slaw.  I don't usually have the bag mix but use head cabbage and carrots.  I like to add in jicama a lot of times too.  This recipe is why my husband is so frustrated that my cole slaw turns out better than his!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
microwave caramels

great gift idea that i saw this on t.v. and put here for safe keeping.

1. combine all ingredients
2. cook 6 minutes , stirring every two minutes
3. stir and pour into lightly greased dish
4. let cool
5. cut , wrap in wax paper & store in air tight container
demonstrations.review: These were super easy and good.  The only reason I am giving 4 and not 5 stars is just personal preference.  These turn out a little blonde and milky instead of the dark cooked sugar that I prefer.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
guinness brownies

this is a dense, moist brownie. you can use semisweet chocolate rather than bittersweet and the results are just as delicious.

1. preheat the oven to 375 degrees
2. butter an 8-inch-square pan
3. in an electric mixer , combine the eggs and sugar
4. beat until light and fluffy
5. in a medium saucepan over medium heat , melt the bittersweet chocolate , white chocolate and butter , stirring until smooth
6. remove from heat and beat into the egg mixture
7. sift the flour and cocoa together and beat into the chocolate mixture
8. whisk in the guinness
9. pour into the pan and bake for 20 to 25 minutes , or until a skewer inserted in the center comes out almost clean
10. remove from the oven and let cool on a wire rack
11. to serve , dust the cake with confectioners' sugar and cut into squares
demonstrations.review: The flavor of these was just what I was looking for, just bitter and sweet enough to complement the Guinness.  However, even with the changes suggested to make them more 'fudgey' (3 eggs, 30 min) this still seemed more like a cake to me.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
creamy garlic penne pasta

this is a delicious, super quick side or main dish. i got it from the back of a pasta box and it is yummy!

1. melt butter and add garlic in a medium sauce pan
2. cook over medium for 1 minute
3. add flour and cook 1 minute , stirring constantly
4. stir in broth and milk and cook , stirring frequently , until sauce boils and thickens
5. add parsley , salt , pepper and cheese
6. stir until cheese is melted
7. toss hot pasta with sauce and serve immediately
demonstrations.review: So delicious!  I used 16oz of orzo and had to add a little extra milk. I love garlic and this was just right.

target.recipe_text:
chicken and vegetable bake

super simple and tasty...minimal prep time. this came from fix it and forget it litely...a compilation of crockpot cooker recipes. i used the garlic powder liberally, and did not limit it to the 1 tsp. listed in the original recipe. i also used a 6 qt. crockpot and only made 1/2 a recipe so it took less than the 4 hours when cooked on the high setting. if you are halving the recipe, i still recommend using the entire amount of potatoes and vege's!

1. sprinkle chicken with pepper and garlic powder
2. put chicken in bottom of slow cooker
3. pour half of the dressing over meat , making sure all pieces are glazed
4. add potatoes , vege's and water chestnuts
5. pour remaining dressing over them , making sure vege's are all lightly coated
6. cover
7. cook on high 4 hrs or on low 7-8 hours
target.review: We made this two nights ago and it was really good. My husband had it for leftovers the night after and he said it was even better! I cooked it on low for 8 hours, and about 7 1/2 hours into it I thought the sauce looked pretty thin so I took the lid off of the crockpot and turned it on high. This seemed to thicken the sauce a bit. Otherwise, a big hit!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
easy turkey chili   crock pot

so easy and tasty. throw the turkey chili all together the night before, turn it on in the morning and come home to a wonderful aroma. serve with toast and a crisp green salad.

1. cook turkey and onion in a medium fry pan over medium high heat , scramble fry until no longer pink
2. drain off fat and transfer cooked meat and onion to crock pot
3. add all remaining ingredients and mix well
4. cook on high 6 to 8 hours
demonstrations.review: This was really good! I didn't have the can of chilies, and I also did drain the cans of beans. I only had ground chicken so I used that instead of turkey. My dh said it was awesome and was looking for leftovers! And I love the easiness of throwing it all into the crockpot and going about my day! Thanks :)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
maple   mustard glazed pork roast

this dish is so gourmet and yet so easy to prepare. i found it on the internet from the national pork producers council. it makes a lot of sauce but trust me- that's a good thing!

1. in a medium bowl , combine maple syrup , dijon mustard , cider vinegar , and soy sauce
2. spread mixture over pork roast and place in a shallow baking dish
3. roast pork in a 350f oven about 1 1 / 4 hours or until internal temperature reaches 160f , basting with sauce occasionally
4. remove roast from the oven and let stand for 10 minutes before serving
5. slice roast and and smother with sauce
demonstrations.review: This was sooo good, and very easy to prepare. I used a 2 1/2 pound roast and I was out of soy sauce, so I substituted worcestershire sauce. Everybody loved it and said that was very tender. We will be making this again, very soon. Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
world s best chocolate chip cookies

there's not much to say...the name says it all. these are better than toll house in our book. i make these every christmas and it is my standard chocolate chip cookie.

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees
2. cream sugars and butter
3. add vanilla and eggs and mix well
4. combine dry ingredients together and gradually add to creamed mixture
5. stir in chips and nuts
6. roll into 1 1 / 4" balls and place on non-stick cookie sheets , about 2" apart
7. bake for 10 to 12 minutes
demonstrations.review: We thought these were good. They were a touch too dry, I like cookies a little more moist. Maybe the 3 cups of flour? But nonetheless, we did like these, and I think we will make them again.

target.recipe_text:
hot bacon dressing

a classic dressing for spinach salad, but it's also wonderful on other veggies like fresh green beans. even the avowed green bean hater in the family tried them with this dressing and went back for seconds!

1. fry bacon until crisp
2. remove bacon from pan leaving fat
3. set bacon aside
4. add onion to bacon fat in pan and cook 5 minutes until onion is soft
5. remove onion from pan leaving fat
6. set onion aside with bacon
7. pour bacon fat into measuring cup and add enough vegetable oil to equal 1 / 2 cup
8. add fat / oil to cornstarch mixture and set aside
9. combine vinegar , water , sugar , salt and pepper in small saucepan and heat to a boil
10. add cornstarch mixture and cook until thickened about 1-2 minutes
11. remove from heat and add bacon and onion
12. serve while warm
target.review: this is great, have made my second batch and keep in the frig and warm to use. Thanks for a great recipe!!!!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
creamy tomato soup

i don't like plain tomato soup, but there's nothing plain about this one and it's delicious. great for dinner parties, or just something a little different at lunch or dinner.

1. in a saucepan , saut onion in butter until tender
2. stir in tomatoes , soup , milk , sugar , basil , paprika , and garlic powder
3. bring to a boil
4. reduce heat
5. cover and simmer for 10 minutes
6. stir in cream cheese until melted
7. top each serving with croutons and / or shredded cheese
8. serve immediately
demonstrations.review: Easy and delicious, I cut back on the cream cheese after reading the other reviews and cut the recipe in half. Will make this again .

demonstrations.recipe_text:
hot pepper butter  mustard  for canning

awesome mustard for anything from pretzels, sandwiches, or glazes on hams. i add more peppers than in the recipe for a hotter butter (approx 60 ranging med-large). also i am trying other peppers as well, habenero, maybe only 10-12...i'll have to let you know how it works :) you will not be disappointed! i have sold the canned product to many family and friends and they can only say this is the best! hope you enjoy!!

1. seed and chop peppers
2. mix everything together
3. boil for 5 minutes ! stirring constantly ! or until desired thickness
4. ladle into hot , sterilized jars
5. cap with hot lid and of course the ring and process in hot water bath for 10 minutes
6. enjoy !
demonstrations.review: have made 3 batches of this and everyone loves it, had a bumper crop of banana peppers this year, great recipe . thanks!!!!!!!!!!!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
dana s homemade kahlua

this is a recipe i came up with since i enjoy white russians soo much, and also i like kahlua in my coffee too. let me know what you think if it is too strong, weak or is missing something..thanks!!

1. boil water , coffee , sugar
2. simmer for 3 hours
3. let cool and add vanilla and vodka
4. bottle and cap tightly
demonstrations.review: This is a great recipe, as everyone says, love the deep rich flavor. Thanks Dana

target.recipe_text:
very moist grilled chicken

i was really surprised at how moist and juicy this chicken turns out. i found it through cooking light and made a few changes. it's so easy to prepare, i fall back on it all the time when i don't want to mess with preparing a detailed marinade.

1. to prepare chicken , combine first 3 ingredients in a large zip-top plastic bag
2. salt and pepper chicken and add to bag
3. seal
4. marinate in refrigerator 4-6 hours , turning occasionally
5. remove chicken from bag
6. discard marinade
7. place chicken on a grill rack coated with cooking spray
8. grill 12-15 minutes on each side or until done
target.review: Super recipe!  I usually don't like the dryness of grilled chicken and this was the most moist chicken ever.  I used boneless, skinless chicken breast.  I did not find it bland at all.  It had a great garlic flavor!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s italian melt in your mouth meatballs

cooking the meatballs in simmering pasta sauce  will not only add so much extra flavor to the sauce the meatballs will be melt-in-your-mouth tender, you may of course oven-bake the meatballs for about 25 minutes,  --- don't be afraid to add in more parmesan cheese and a little more milk, there is no need to measure exactly, this recipe is pretty much foolproof, leftover cooked meatballs make a wonderful pizza topping just slice thinly and freeze until ready to use ----- these also make wonderful juicy burgers shaped into patties-- for more of my tried and true recipes check out my food blog at www.kittencalskitchen.com

1. mix all ingredients together in a large bowl
2. shape into small meatballs
3. drop the meatballs into simmering pasta sauce , do not stir for at least 20 minutes or you will risk breaking the meatballs
4. continue cooking in the simmering sauce for another 20 minutes
5. after the 40 minutes cooking time continue cooking your sauce with the meatballs in for as long as desired
demonstrations.review: Probably the only way I will ever prepare spaghetti again!  I will half the pepper, it was a little too potent for our taste.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mom s chocolate cupcakes

this recipe was given to my mom by a next door neighbor many years ago. it makes a wonderful dark chocolate cupcake, or double the recipe for a sheet or layer cake. it has become a family favorite and is always requested at birthdays.

1. mix all ingredients together until moist and well blended
2. put in cupcake cups and bake for 20-25 minutes at 350 degrees f
3. frost with your favorite icing
4. to make a layer cake , double the recipes and put in 2 round cake pans
5. increase baking time to about 35 minutes or until a toothpick inserted in the center comes out clean
demonstrations.review: Nice mild chocolate flavor and very simple.  A little crumbly, though.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crock pot ravioli

this is a recipe that i adopted from a sweet chef by the name of cbw. a real doll. "i always plan a crock pot meal for sunday afternoon so that it's all ready after church, and i wanted something different than the chicken we usually end up with. this was a big hit!"

1. pour about half of the pasta sauce in the bottom of crock pot
2. add frozen ravioli
3. pour additional pasta sauce , tomato sauce , water , and red pepper over ravioli
4. sprinkle italian seasonings over sauces
5. sprinkle cheese on top
6. turn crock pot on low and cook for 4-5 hours
demonstrations.review: You can't get any easier than this and very delicious!

target.recipe_text:
kittencal s harvard beets

since i make this for dinner parties this is a double recipe, if you are serving a very large dinner party you might want to double and serve it in two bowls, or you may reduce by half if desired, the mustard powder is only optional i always like to add in for an extra kick, 1 teaspoon onion powder is also great to add also ---  this makes a wonderful addition to a holiday dinner :)

1. drain the canned beets and reserve 2 / 3 cup of the juice
2. in a medium saucepan combine the sugar , cornstarch , salt and mustard powder
3. add in 2 / 3 cup beet juice and vinegar
4. bring to a boil over medium heat stirring constantly until simmering and thickened
5. mix in the butter until melted , then add / mix in the sliced beets
6. season with black pepper
7. delicious !
target.review:
Delicious!!!! and so easy, everyone loved them.
thank you

demonstrations.recipe_text:
buttermilk salad

my coworkers are great cooks. this is another great recipe from a former coworker. covered dish lunches at the office are a great way to discover new recipes. this is quick and easy. hope you enjoy this one!!!

1. heat undrained pineapple and jello in a saucepan till jello is dissolved
2. mix in buttermilk and cool whip
3. pour into mold or bowl
4. refrigerate for several hours or overnight
demonstrations.review: I agree this was wonderful. Light and flavorful. will make again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pumpkin coffee cake

please don't pass this by because of all the ingredients. it's really very easy and quick. it's also very delicious

1. grease or spray the bottom of a 9x13 pan
2. mix together first 8 ingredients
3. pour 1 / 2 of the mixture in the 9x13 pan
4. prepare the pumpkin exactly like the pumpkin pie recipe on the can of pumpkin except you only use 1 / 2 cup of evaporated milk or just mix together the next 8 ingredients
5. pour all of the pumpkin mixture over the batter in the 9x13 pan
6. pour the remaining half of batter over the pumpkin make the topping , put over batter
7. bake in a 325 degree over for 50-60 minutes
8. let cool completely
9. enjoy
demonstrations.review: Excellent, easy to make and delicious. I brought it to work and everyone wanted the recipe. Highly recommend you give it a try! Thank you for sharing.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
bread salad

something different for your next cookout.

1. combine bread , tomatoes and basil in large bowl
2. in food processor with metal blade , chop garlic and salt
3. add rosemary , hot pepper flakes and vinegar
4. add olive oil in a stream to emulsify
5. toss bread mixture and dressing
6. allow to stand for at least 20 minutes so the bread can absorb the dressing
demonstrations.review: This is the greatest!!!Everyone loved it, i will be making it againsoon. I wouldn't change a thing, well maybe you should double the recipe!!!

target.recipe_text:
cheesy ham and potato soup

comfort soup at its finest!  i usually make this to use up leftover ham.  this is easy to adapt with other ingredients.  i don't put celery in mine.  i have added garlic sometimes as well.

1. combine potatoes , celery , carrots , onion , ham , and water / broth in stockpot and bring to boil
2. then cook over medium heat until potatoes are tender
3. stir in the chicken bouillon , salt , and pepper
4. in separate saucepan , melt butter over medium-low heat
5. whisk in flour and cook stirring constantly until thick
6. slowly stir in milk as not to allow lumps to form and all milk is added
7. turn up to medium heat
8. continue to stir until thick
9. add in cheese and stir until melted
10. stir the cheese mixture into the stockpot and cook until heated through
target.review: Perfect recipe to use up leftover ham! Easy too, especially since I had all of the ingredients on hand. Thanks alot!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
banana banana bread

why compromise the banana flavor? my banana bread is moist and delicious with loads of banana flavor! ultimate comfort food, and it's wonderful toasted!! (make sure to use bananas with a lot of black on them for the best flavor! the blacker the bananas, the stronger the banana flavor of the bread.)

1. preheat oven to 350
2. lightly grease 9 x 5 loaf pan
3. in large bowl , combine flour , soda and salt
4. in separate bowl , cream together butter and brown sugar
5. stir in eggs and mashed bananas until well blended
6. stir banana mixture into flour mixture
7. stir just to moisten
8. pour batter into prepared loaf pan
9. bake in preheated oven for 60-65 minutes until a toothpick inserted into center of loaf comes out clean
10. let bread cool in pan for 10 minutes , then turn out onto a wire rack
demonstrations.review: Coming from a person who doesn't always enjoy the flavor of banana, this bread was fantastic! I baked mine for 60 minutes and it came out very moist and delicious. I also added 1 cup of semisweet chocolate chips to satisfy my chocolate addiction. Great recipe! :)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
sweet chicken bacon wraps  paula deen

hey you paula deen fans, she has a new magazine, "cooking with paula deen"--this recipe is from the premier issue.  it was so yummy looking, i couldn't wait to try it.  i added another 15 minutes to the cooking time suggested (30-35 minutes) and it was just right, but oven temperatures vary, so check on it during the last few minutes of cooking time.  i'm also going to add a few dashes of cayenne pepper next time for something hot and sweet!

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. cut chicken breasts into 1-inch cubes
3. cut each bacon slice into thirds
4. wrap each chicken cube with bacon and secure with a wooden pick inserted on the diagonal starting where bacon seam overlaps
5. stir together brown sugar and chili powder
6. dredge wrapped chicken in mixture
7. coat a rack and broiler pan with non-stick cooking spray
8. place chicken on rack in broiler pan
9. bake at 350f for 30 to 35 minutes , or until bacon is crisp
demonstrations.review: These are so good! I make them for dinner with a side of pasta salad and my husband devours them! Definitely passing this recipe on to others.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
the best ever waffles

every sunday morning, my mom and i used to get up early and make these wonderful waffles. this recipe has been in the family for years, and i will definitly be passing it down to my children.

1. in a large mixing bowl , whisk together all dry ingredients
2. separate the eggs , adding the yolks to the dry ingredient mixture , and placing the whites in a small mixing bowl
3. beat whites until moderately stiff
4. set aside
5. add milk and melted butter to dry ingredient mixture and blend
6. fold stiff egg whites into mixture
7. ladle mixture into hot waffle iron and bake
demonstrations.review: These were fantastic! So light and fluffy. I'll definitely be adding these to my recipe collection, thank you!

target.recipe_text:
blue ribbon stuffed mushrooms

these very easy mushrooms won a blue ribbon at the arizona state fair in the early 90's. these are great appetizers or even for a meal itself.

1. brown pork sausage and crumble well
2. drain sausage from skillet leaving a thin coating of oil behind and saut chopped onions until slightly wilted
3. return sausage to pan with onions and add cream cheese
4. over low heat stir sausage , onions , and cream cheese until well blended
5. remove stems from mushrooms and stuff each mushroom cap with the mixture
6. top with parmesan if desired
7. bake at 350f for 20-25 minutes until heated through and the mushrooms are beginning to leak their water
target.review: I made 48 of these Sunday night thinking they would last all week as appetizers/snacks/side dishes to the rest of our week-day dinners.  My husband and three kids devoured them so fast, I had to steal one from my 1 year old's plate to get one of my own!  Needless to say, this will be a regular menu item for our family.  I used Jimmy Dean sage sausage and Toffuti cream cheese (4/5 of our family have lactose protien allergies) and skipped the parm. cheese.  They were delicious!  Oh, and my youngest (1 year old) and I had the leftover stuffing and sauted mushroom stems in an omlet for dinner the next day as you suggested.  It too was delicious!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pita snacks

syrian bread is used in this snack. i make these all year and especially during the summer. my guests are disappointed if i don't supply these as one of our appetizers.

1. split the pita bread into two halves
2. score with sharp knife , but don't cut completely through
3. brush lightly with olive oil , sprinkle lightly with basil , garlic powder or garlic salt , parmesan cheese and cayenne ground pepper
4. place on cookie sheet and bake at 350f until golden or lightly browned
5. cool and break into pieces
6. we serve them as is and also with side dishes of chopped jalapeo peppers and chopped tomatoes
demonstrations.review: I baked this snack for an office party and served them with eggplant hummus and salsa.  I didn't have any ground cayenne pepper, so I used crushed red pepper, and they turned out wonderful!  A coworker even told me I could package them up and sell them in grocery stores!  I will definately be making these again.  Thanks, Judy-Jude!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
potato chip chicken nuggets   any flavor

take the challenge! any flavor potato chip will work for your own taste buds! it will work for a meal or appetizer!  i love to make it with the 2 flavors listed but i will try it next with bbq chips!  i saw this on the tv & tried it twice.  it is so simple & easy plus tasty. i really enjoyed this & hope you will.

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. spread the crushed potato chips in shallow dish
3. beat together the egg & milk in a shallow bowl
4. dip the chicken cubes into egg mixture & then dredge them in the chips
5. place the chicken nuggets on a baking sheet & drizzle with melted butter
6. bake for 15-18 minutes or until golden brown
7. the nuggets can be frozen after baking !
8. serve:
demonstrations.review: My daughter loves to make these!  We got the recipe from Paula Deen.  We've tried them with all kinds of chips including Baked Lays (not good, they turn out soggy) and our favorite is plain potato chips with Paula's honey-mustard dipping sauce.  DH (picky) and DS (2 yrs) also love them.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
spanish tomato bread with jamn serrano

these tasty tapas snacks are ready in just 5 minutes, the perfect accompaniment for a drinks, tapas or summer cocktail party. jamón serrano is a spanish ham & similar to prosciutto - which you could use instead. try to use sun ripened (not cold frame) tomatoes - they really make a huge difference to this recipe! this recipe serves 10 to 12 people, with other accompaniments on offer.

1. mix together the chopped tomatoes , garlic clove / s , olive oil , salt and pepper
2. keep the mixture in the fridge until needed
3. to serve , toast the slices of baguette
4. spoon a little tomato topping on to each piece of toast
5. tear the slices of jamn serrano into pieces and put one piece on each slice of bread
6. arrange on a large attractive plate , sprinkle with chopped basil or flat leaf parsley and eat !
demonstrations.review: Yum!  I served these at a Spanish-themed book club discussion last night along with sangria and a variety of other tapas.  They were a hit.  I couldn't find serrano ham, so I used prosciutto instead.  Thank you, French Tart, for such an easy and good recipe.

target.recipe_text:
easy mac and cheese lasagna

macaroni and cheese with a twist

1. preheat oven to 350 deg f
2. lightly grease 8x8 baking dish
3. cook and drain ground beef and mix with spaghetti sauce
4. prepare macaroni and cheese using the directions on the box
5. place a layer of mac and cheese in the baking dish , top with a layer of meat then a layer of cheese
6. after the 2 layers are complete , bake in the oven for 20 minutes or until heated through
7. then top with parm cheese
8. for meat substitute you can use pre cooked chicken
9. for a complete meatless dish you can use just the spaghetti sauce and leave out all meats
target.review: We had this when our daughter had her friend over for dinner. It was a hit. Everyone loved it.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crock pot melt in your mouth country style steak

i got this recipe from a friend at work about 8 years ago. it's been my husband's favorite meal ever since. he's requesting it for his special father's day dinner this weekend.  this meal is so super easy and so rewarding.  i usually put it all together in the crock pot before i leave for work in the morning and, when i get home, it's ready to serve.  cooks up a delicious gravy and goes great with mashed potatoes!

1. place cubed steaks in crock pot and set on "low"
2. mix together cream of mushroom soup , dry onion soup and water in bowl and pour over top of cubed steaks
3. cook for 8-10 hours
4. steaks will be so tender , they may fall apart when you take them out
demonstrations.review:
This was a really good easy dinner!
A hit with the whole family. It makes wonderful gravy. Serve with mashed potatoes!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
frito chili casserole

one of those that the men ask for.

1. put 2 cups fritos in baking dish
2. arrange onion and half the cheese on top of fritos
3. pour chili over the cheese
4. top with remaining fritos and cheese
5. bake at 350 for 15 minutes , or until hot
demonstrations.review: This was a fast quick meal. Kids and hubby loved it and I thought it was great for how easy it was!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kielbasa and fries casserole

one night my mom made up this easy recipe and my daughter begs for it weekly!  it's only 4 ingredients and takes 1/2 hour to cook! i have made it using fresh cut potatoes and it works out just as good, but just takes a little longer to cook. if you don't have a large enough skillet, i have included how to finish off in the oven as well.  i hope your family enjoys as much as mine!  ps.  tastes even better the next day!

1. bake the frozen steak fries in oven , as directed on package
2. while cooking start the rest of recipe
3. in a large non stick skillet , saute the onions slowly in 2 tbsp of olive oil till transparent and just starting to caramelize
4. add sliced kielbasa to onions , mix thoroughly and cook them together on medium heat about 10 minutes
5. once the steak fries are done , take out of oven and add to the onions and kielbasa
6. mix well
7. cover and cook about 10 minutes on medium low heat
8. you want the fries to absorb the liquid in the skillet
9. sometimes you need to add a little more olive oil , but only if it's really dry
10. it depends on the brand of fries you use
11. i use ore ida and it comes out perfect every time
12. serve
13. if you don't have a large enough skillet or wok , once the fries are done , put them in a 13 x 9 baking dish and pour the kielbasa mixture over them
14. mix well and pop into a 400f oven for about 5 minutes
15. stir again and serve
16. it's simple , but the taste is delicious !
demonstrations.review: This was great for a quick simple meal and the kids all loved which never happens!

target.recipe_text:
chicken   sausage jambalaya

this is a really simple recipe

1. cut chicken up into bite size pieces
2. season with salt , cayenne pepper , and black pepper
3. brown chicken in pot with melted butter
4. remove chicken
5. chop onions and bell pepper
6. cut garlic finely
7. brown onions , bell pepper , and garlic
8. add tomato sauce and stewed tomatoes
9. simmer 15 minutes
10. add chicken and sausage cut into bite size pieces
11. cook until chicken is tender
12. add raw rice and chopped green onions
13. stir ingredients thoroughly
14. add enough water to cover ingredients by about 1 inch
15. bring to a boil
16. cover and cook on low heat for 30 minutes or until rice is tender
target.review: We loved it! I used Extra Hot Rotel for a little extra kick! Left out the green onions and green Bell pepper cuz didn't have them. It was YUMMY!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
easy microwave breakfast sandwich

this is the quickest, easiest breakfast sandwich you can make.  variations of this recipe are very easy, just mix in what you like.  the microwave times may vary slightly to ensure light and fluffy eggs.

1. in small cup , platic bowl or ramiken melt butter in microwave for 10-15 seconds
2. add egg to butter in the bowl and beat well
3. mix in milk and hot sauce
4. add diced onion , pepper and ham to taste
5. season with salt and pepper
6. cover dish with paper towel , or lid for bowl and microwave on high for 1 minute and 30 seconds
7. toast english muffin
8. remove bowl from microwave and loosen egg with spoon around the edges
9. dump egg onto english muffin , top with cheese and serve hot
demonstrations.review: I use this when we are on vacation in the hotel room. Most hotels have a frig and a microwave now. I had gastric bypass so I have to have protein, and usually hotel breakfasts are just a bunch of carbs. This works really well.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
easy pizza pasta casserole  oamc

this is a kid pleaser-very cheesy and topped with pepperoni. it makes 2 large (9x13) casseroles or 4 small ones; i often divide it in fourths and freeze 3. this originally came from toh's quick cooking.

1. brown ground beef , onion , garlic and seasoning in oil
2. drain
3. while beef is browning , cook pasta according to the packaging
4. stir in pasta , spaghetti sauce and 3 cups cheese
5. place mixture in 2 greased 9x13x2 inch baking pans or 4 square pans
6. sprinkle with remaining mozzarella
7. top with pepperoni
8. cover and freeze up to 3 months
9. to cook now: bake uncovered at 350 degrees for 25-30 minutes , until heated through
10. to bake frozen casserole: thaw in refrigerator overnight and bake at 350 for 35-40 minutes , till hot
demonstrations.review: Very good! Kids and adults liked it. I love meals that everyone enjoys. I hate being a short order cook.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
shirley s salad

my mom's neighbor makes this and it is so good. the dressing makes it!

1. crumble package of ramen noodles
2. discard seasoning packet
3. saute noodles in butter until browned
4. mix all the salad ingredients together including the ramen noodles
5. chill
6. mix dressing ingredients and pour over salad
7. enjoy !
demonstrations.review: Took this to a party & everyone really liked it. Chose not to put in the oranges, just due to personal taste. Very yummy and different.

target.recipe_text:
wholesome homemade honey whole wheat bread

this is the most awesome wheat bread i have ever eaten. it is worth the extra effort and because this recipe makes 4 loaves, you can freeze them and have enough for awhile :) rising time included in prep.

1. dissolve yeast in warm water
2. in a large bowl , combine butter , molasses , honey and salt and mix well
3. add yeast mixture and then gradually add flours
4. turn onto floured surface and knead until smooth
5. place in buttered bowl and let rise until double
6. punch down and let rest for a few minutes
7. divide dough into 4 parts and shape into loaves
8. place in greased pans and let rise for about an hour
9. bake at 375 for 35 to 40 minutes
target.review:
Hey now, this was good bread! I used all freshly ground whole-wheat flour (about half and half red/white wheat), and dropped the temp about 10*... other than that followed the recipe exactly. Nice and light, with a good dark crust.
This will probably become my standard every-day bread.
Thanks for sharing, Karen!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
the best chicken tortilla soup

i'm in love with this soup!! a very good friend of mine made this for me recently and i fell in love. i'm very picky about my tortilla soup and this by far the best ever. she makes hers in the crock pot and i have to agree, that it's easy and tastes just wonderful!! whatever you do, do not skip the garnishes! they are the icing on the cake! update april 2010:  obviously i've made this so many times i never even look at the recipe anymore!  but i wanted to add some variations that i play around with that are great.  like many reviewers black beans and corn are great additions.  sometimes i add them to the leftovers (if there are any :-) so that is feels like something new the next day!  i have also made it several times with shredded pork which turns it into a pork carnitas type of soup.  if you like it on the spicy and smoke side buy a can of chipotle peppers in adobo sauce and mince up one or two and add it.  and lastly, a little swizzle of half and half or heavy cream just minutes before serving makes it a creamy tortilla soup that is wonderful and it is also a good way to tone down the heat if it got away from you...

1. throw everything except the garnishes in your crock pot and let it cook on high for 5-6 hours
2. dress with garnishes and give it a squeeze of lime and you're good to go !
3. enjoy !
4. if you are not using a crock pot , saute the garlic and onion in 2 tablespoons olive oil before adding the remaining ingredients
5. simmer for at least an hour so that the flavors mix together
demonstrations.review: This was a great soup! Spicy and flavorful and hearty. The different types of chili pepper all complemented eachother. I omitted the onion and added a handful each of chopped celery, carrot and corn. As the crockpot was busy, it cooked on the stove just fine. Thanks, Jill4man!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
steel cut oatmeal for the crock pot

i love the texture of steel cut oats. you can make this the night before and breakfast is ready in the morning. i like fruit additions, but my kids do not, so i've listed them as optional. also, it may sound like a lot of water, but trust me, i've experimented..

1. place all ingredients in a 2 quart slow cooker
2. cover and cook on low 6-8 hours
3. it might form a "crust" around the outside
4. just scrape it down with a spoon and stir
demonstrations.review: Sorry, this didn't work for us at all. It turned into a glue-y mess we had to throw out. I'd much rather get up a little early and make the real thing.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
jo mama s world famous spaghetti

my kids will give up a steak dinner for this spaghetti. it is a recipe i have been perfecting for years and it is so good (if i may humbly say) that my kids are disappointed when they eat spaghetti anywhere else but home! in fact they tell me i should open a restaurant and serve only this spaghetti and garlic bread. in response to requests, i have posted the recipe for recipe #28559 that uses approximately 1/2 of the sauce from this 
recipe. have spaghetti one night and lasagna later!  thanks to all of you who have tried my recipe and have written a review.  i read and appreciate every one of them!  chef note:  after i posted this recipe i remembered a funny incident--my dear husband usually has a nice bottle of wine handy so when i make a batch of spaghetti i just help myself to a splash of it. on one occasion, there wasn't a bottle opened, but there was a bottle sitting on the counter so i got out the corkscrew and helped myself. for some reason, the spaghetti that night was the best ever. my husband asked what wine i put in it and i showed him the bottle. he nearly fell off the chair. i had opened a rather expensive bottle he had bought to give his boss. goes to show you--don't use a wine for cooking you wouldn't drink. you get the best results from a good wine!

1. in large , heavy stockpot , brown italian sausage , breaking up as you stir
2. add onions and continue to cook , stirring occasionally until onions are softened
3. add garlic , tomatoes , tomato paste , tomato sauce and water
4. add basil , parsley , brown sugar , salt , crushed red pepper , and black pepper
5. stir well and barely bring to a boil
6. stir in red wine
7. simmer on low , stirring frequently for at least an hour
8. a longer simmer makes for a better sauce , just be careful not to let it burn !
9. cook spaghetti according to package directions
10. spoon sauce over drained spaghetti noodles and sprinkle with parmesan cheese
demonstrations.review: Very good sauce, it's definitely a keeper. This batch was so good (let it simmer for the better part of 5 hours) that I'll be making a BIG batch the next rainy weekend and pressure-canning for a quick delicious dinner in a hurry. I used half italian sausage and half ground beef, and chopped up a handful of leftover pulled pork, for even more richness.

target.recipe_text:
tacos in no time

for more variety chicken, steak or shredded beef can be substituted for the ground beef or scrambled eggs and fried potatoes can be substitued for the meat & the beans omitted to make breakfast tacos.

1. in an 8" skillet , over medium high heat , cook and stir meat until brown , then drain off the fat
2. stir in tomato sauce , onion , garlic salt , chili powder , and pepper , and simmer uncovered for 15 minutes
3. while meat simmers , heat taco shells as directed on the package
4. fill taco shells with meat , and top each with lettuce , cheese and any other desired toppings
5. serve with sauce
6. to make hot sauce: mix 1 / 3 cup chili sauce & 1 / 4 tsp red pepper sauce or 1 tsp minced hot chili pepper
target.review: Fast, delicious, and made with things I usually have on hand. I was out of lettuce but added red onion- Yum!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
walnut delights  koeka

for zwt6.  from larousse treasury of country cooking.  denmark.

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees
2. butter and flour 8 x 8 inch baking pan
3. in a large mixing bowl
4. mix graham crackers crumbs , sugar and baking powder
5. beat egg yolks lightly , add to the dry ingredients and stir
6. stir in walnuts and vanilla
7. mix well
8. beat egg whites in a separate bowl with a pinch of salt until stiff
9. gently fold into the graham cracker mixture
10. pour into baking pan
11. bake untill golden brown , about 25 minutes
12. let cool in pan , cut into bars
13. serve with ice cream or whipped cream on top
demonstrations.review: These are really quite good and something out of the ordinary. I didn't know what to expect with only 2 eggs as wet ingredients, but the finished texture is soft and chewy. I wonder if the beaten egg whites are what made the bars light and chewy? The graham crumbs add another layer of sweetness, almost honey like. This reminds me of something I would have found on my Grandma's cupboard. She always had simple yet tasty treats when we came to visit. I would make these again and not change a thing. After I added the mixture to the pan (it will be crumbly), I lightly patted the crumbs down with the bottom of a measuring cup to even the mixture out. I preferred these cooled and plain vs served with ice cream. Made for ZWT6- ZINGO!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
traditional banana split

there is some debate in our ice cream parlor what the "traditional" split consists of.  i did some research before we opened and it seems that this is the most consistently "traditional" split served, even though some have marshmallow, peanuts, crushed cherries and more.  i prefer hot fudge over the chocolate syrup, personally :p

1. line up ice cream scoops next to each other in an oval deep dish or a banana boat
2. cut the ends of the banana off while still in the peel
3. slice in half longways
4. pop each half of the banana out of the peel onto each side of the ice cream row , pressing down and in a little so it'll stay put
5. top the vanilla ice cream with the pineapple , the chocolate with the chocolate syrup and the strawberry with the strawberry sauce
6. spoon the wet walnuts over all three scoops of ice cream
7. top each scoop with some whipped cream and a cherry for each
8. enjoy !
demonstrations.review: I had forgotten just how good a Traditional Banana Split could be. I think I was probably a teenager that last time I had one. I thought I had walnuts here and I didn't, so I had to skip them. I had an idea on how to make the "wet" walnut topping. I thought I would toast a few walnut pieces and soak them in Torani Vanilla syrup. Hopefully I'll get to try that soon. Thanks for the memories Karen=^..^= ! Nick's Mom

demonstrations.recipe_text:
perfect basic white rice

you do not need to be afraid of cooking rice again! lol real rice is so much better for you than instant. so here is a basic recipe that will have you cooking rice like a pro! check out the options too! your friends and family will think you're a star! 

1. in a saucepan with a good fitting lid bring water , salt and optional ingredients if desired to a boil
2. the salt and butter are simply for flavor
3. the vinegar keeps your grains separated and gives you a prettier dish
4. no one will taste the vinegar at all !
5. add rice and stir
6. cover and reduce heat to medium low
7. you will know that your temperature is correct if a little steam is visible leaking from the lid
8. a lot of steam means your heat is too high
9. cook for 20 minutes
10. do not lift lid !
11. the steam that is trapped inside the pan is what allows the rice to cook properly
12. remove from heat and fluff with fork
13. serve !
demonstrations.review: Thanks Hope, this is just what I needed tonight. I made a Chicken and broccoli stir fry, and didn't want a rice dish that overpowered the mild stir fry. Thanks for posting!  Nick's Mom

target.recipe_text:
kittencal s chinese chicken balls with sweet and sour sauce

don't bother ordering chinese chicken balls make these at home they are just as good if not even better and the sweet and sour sauce is the same as what is served at your chinese restaurant!-- these are a great weekend snack or can be served as appetizers, if you want some extra flavor to you chicken batter feel free to add in some garlic or onion powder or spices of choice --- this makes a large amount so you may want to reduce the chicken ball batter amount by half (using 4 chicken breasts) --- note: the sauce recipe is one you may have to make a few times before you get the consistancy and sweetness to your liking, 1 cup white sugar and 1/2 cup lightly packed brown will give you a sweet sauce you may reduce the white sugar amount by a few tablespoons

1. to make the sweet and sour sauce sauce
2. in a saucepan combine the first 5 ingredients until combined
3. in a cup or bowl whisk the cold water or pineapple juice with cornstarch until smooth and well blended , then whisk vigorously into the ketchup mixture
4. bring to a boil stirring or whisking constantly over medium-high heat until bubbly
