demonstrations.review: I hate to admit that I didn't have high hopes for this recipe, as I'm not a casserole girl. But, we absolutely loved it. I had 1 can of garbanzo beans to use up (hoping to find a way to sneak them by DH & DS) & this recipe was perfect. Everything else is always on hand & it went together very quickly. I used one can of white corn & served it over rice. As I was putting the beef mixture into a casserole dish I envisioned it topped with mashed potatoes that were lightly broiled at the end of baking.... & then at dinner when I told the family of my daydream they got into the action & came up with a version that would be wrapped in flour tortillas with or without rice & one with pasta instead of rice. I think this is going to be a versatile & very quick go-to meal for busy weeknights. I couldn't be more pleased that I tried this one. UPDATE: Freezes very well. Would definitely recommend for OAMC. Even my picky toddler ate it! Thanks so much for posting, Angela!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chicken over pasta

this is a knock-off recipe from my shrimp and chicken over pasta, that i often make when i don't have the shrimp on hand!! this is a quick, easy dish that i always have the ingredients for in my refrigerator and pantry.

1. in 12" skillet over medium heat , add olive oil
2. add onion and garlic and cook until tender , stirring occasionally
3. with a slotted spoon , remove onion and garlic to a small bowl
4. in remaining drippings in skillet over medium high heat cook chicken pieces until slightly browned
5. add parsley , onion , tomato sauce , wine , salt , ground cayenne red pepper , basil , pepper and chicken broth
6. bring to a boil , reduce heat to low , cover and simmer 10 minutes
7. serve over angel hair pasta
demonstrations.review: OMG!  We loved this recipe!  I had to make a couple changes but nothing that would alter the flavor.  I had raw chicken that was already sliced instead of whole so I used that & DH has an aversion to the "long & wiggly" noodles so I rarely have them on hand.  Since I found this recipe just minutes before cooking I had to use penne pasta instead.  The flavor of this dish was outstanding.  The cayenne was the perfect compliment to the wine & tomato.  It was just enough to give the hint of heat but then it pulled back to let your taste buds enjoy the rest of the flavors.  The chicken was ultra tender as well & now I can't wait to try the shrimp version you have posted!  My only advice would be to add the amount of garlic called for in the ingredient list.  I got to step 2 before I knew there was garlic in the recipe.  I didn't take off any stars for that because garlic is one of those ingredients where amount can vary greatly by taste & we usually use more than the recipe calls for anyway.  In this case I used a heaping tablespoonful.  Thanks for sharing, DoubleA'sMom!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s onion patties latkes

i have been making these for over 20 years, i usually get about 15 patties but it depends on the size of the batter that you drop in the pan, these are better if fried to very brown and crispy, you can make a double recipe, fry them then freeze them on a tray then pop them into freezer bags, then just warm them in the oven to crisp up, they are very addicting and i can tell you i eat half before they even get to the table lol!  if you plan on doubling the recipe then make two separate recipes in two bowls, i have doubled the recipe into one bowl and for some reason they just are not as good ---  if desired you could add in a slightly beaten large egg and reduce the milk by 1/4 cup --- you will *love* these!  also see my
recipe#186700 *and*
recipe#244592

1. chop the onions finely then place into a bowl
2. in another large bowl mix together the flour , sugar , baking powder , seasoning salt , cayenne , garlic powder and a small amount of black pepper
3. mix to combine well
4. add in the milk and whisk until thoroughly combined
5. add in the chopped onions and green onions and mix with a wooden spoon until combined
6. in a large non-stick frypan , heat a small amount of oil to medium-hot , adding in more oil as needed as the patties will absorb too much oil if you add in a large amount of oil at one time
7. drop the batter from a tablespoon into about 1 / 2-inch of hot oil
8. flatten slightly with the spoon or spatula
9. sprinkle with a little salt
10. fry until crispy and brown on both sides
demonstrations.review: As if you need another endorsement on this one! But I will anyway. Held an outdoor bbq for friends & put these on the menu for appetizers with 4 different homemade dipping sauces, horseradish, sweet 'n' sour, bleu cheese & a creamy dijon. The onion patties never even made it to the "outdoor" part of the bbq! Everyone just gathered around my griddle in the house & gobbled them up as I dropped them onto the paper towels! They were a huge hit. You've done it again, Kitten! Thanks!

target.recipe_text:
asian steak dinner     low carb

2.7 carbs per serving but even if you are not low carbing it -- try this you will love it!!!! use the left over sauce to pour over your salad --delicious!

1. cut steak into 4 equal portions
2. place each piece between 2 pieces of plastic wrap
3. with a heavy , flat-sided mallet , pound meat firmly but gently all over to a thickness of 1 / 3 to 1 / 2 inch
4. in a small bowl , stir together broth , soy sauce , ginger , and cornstarch
5. set aside
6. melt butter in oil in a wide nonstick frying pan over medium-high heat
7. when butter sizzles , add steak
8. cook , turning once , until steak is well browned on both sides and still pink in center
9. cut to test
10. transfer to a platter and keep warm
11. stir broth mixture , then add to pan , increase heat to high , and bring to a boil , stirring
12. then continue to boil and stir until slightly thickened
13. pour sauce over steak
14. drizzle with sesame oil to taste , then sprinkle with green onions
target.review: This is a very delicious dish.  It went very well with a tossed salad with Oriental Dressing.  If not concerned about low-carbs, I would highly recommend serving it with garlic mashed potatoes and a veggie.  The sauce can also serve as a terrific gravy.  Try it, you'll like it

demonstrations.recipe_text:
low fat oat bran apricot muffins

flourless these are very moist, low in fat, sugar and contain no flour

1. preheat oven 425 degrees f
2. spray muffin tins with pan-spray
3. mix first 4 ingredients
4. set aside
5. mix egg substitute , juice , milk and oil
6. add fruit and mix into dry ingredients till just moistened
7. pour into prepared muffin tins
8. bake 15-17 minutes
demonstrations.review: This is a terrific recipe.  Over the past couple of weeks, I have tried many different bran muffin recipes and have concluded that this one was the best.  This is definitely a keeper.  My own variations were small.  I added 4 single packets of Splenda to ensure sweetness, though it probably didn't need it.  As a fruit juice, I used orange juice.  Instead of dried apricots, I used an equivalent amount of dried apples, since I had recently dehydrated them myself.  For the small grated apple in the recipe, I used a Granny Smith apple.  The recipe allows much latitude on juices and fruit one can use.  Since we're on a low-carb diet, we will use only this bran muffin recipe from now on.  It is definitely a 5-Star Recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
reduced fat eggplant  aubergine  parmesan

one of dh favorites, he can't get enough! have a loaf of crusty italian bread rubbed with some roasted garlic to go with this along with some caesar salad! mmmmmm....... :)

1. preheat oven to 400 degrees f
2. spray baking sheet with cooking spray
3. cut eggplant into 1 / 2 inch thick slices
4. season with salt and pepper
5. place eggplant on baking sheet
6. spray tops lightly with olive-oil spray
7. bake at 400 degrees f
8. for 20 minutes , or until tender
9. in the meantime , simmer tomato sauce with basil , garlic , and oregano until heated through
10. spread tomato sauce on eggplant
11. top with some chopped fresh herb , if you desire
12. sprinkle with fat-free mozzarella
13. then cover with reduced-fat mozzarella
14. bake 5-7 minutes more at 400 degrees f
15. or until cheese is melted
16. sprinkle with parmesan cheese and serve
demonstrations.review: This is an outstanding recipe.  Fixing slice eggplant in this manner was like having several little pizzas that were so light and delicious.  And, there was no leftovers either.  If one is on a low-carb diet, this is a great way to experience terrific Italian cuisine.  We'll prepare this recipe over and over again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
barley and lentil soup

another family favorite.

1. in a large saucepan , add oil and heat over medium-high heat
2. add onions and garlic
3. saute onions for 10 minutes or until clear
4. add next 6 ingredients
5. cook until red bell pepper is just softened , stirring occasionally
6. add 5 cans of broth , tomatoes , and tomato paste
7. bring to a boil
8. stir in barley and lentils
9. lower heat and simmer about 1 1 / 2 hours or until barley and lentils are tender
10. stirring occasionally
11. add more broth to reach desired consistency
12. add salt and pepper to taste
13. ladle into soup bowls and sprinkle with parsley
demonstrations.review: All of the ingredients blended together to make a terrific soup and a great one to serve on a cold winter night.  I followed the recipe quite closely except for adding an extra can of beef broth and a few more sundried tomatoes.  Didn't need any salt added as it had such a delicious flavor.  It is a five-star recipe.

target.recipe_text:
cheyenne s fudgy dutch cocoa brownies   fudge icing

this is a recipe that my 13 year old daughter came up with after trying different recipes over the past month...we all deemed it a "keeper" in our house and will keep making brownies this way from now on!  so simple, and i didn't even have to go to the store to buy any more ingredients!  looks cake-like, but tastes so fudgy and chewy...really good brownies!  p.s. my baby, cheyenne, took all of the pictures herself while i was at work!!!  awwww!  :)

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees
2. grease an 8x8x2-inch glass pan
3. in a medium saucepan , melt butter or margarine
4. remove melted butter or margarine from heat , add cocoa , and stir until well blended
5. add sugar and mix well
6. add eggs , one at a time , and beat well
7. stir in vanilla , flour and salt
8. do not overbeat
9. fold in nuts , if desired
10. spread in prepared glass pan and bake 25 to 30 minutes , or until toothpick inserted in center comes out clean , but sides are not yet hard and crusty
11. cool completely before topping with icing
12. fudge icing:
13. in a small bowl , beat melted butter , cocoa , corn syrup and vanilla until blended
14. add powdered sugar and water , and beat until spreading consistency
15. after spreading icing onto cooled brownies , cool in fridge for at least 45 minutes
target.review: The best brownies I've EVER had. I didn't use the nuts because I didn't have any, and I just used the unsweetened cocoa powder I had in my pantry instead of the Dutch-processed kind. I've never made from-scratch brownies before, and I'll never make another boxed one again!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
new england clam chowder

very rich and creamy chowder served at skipjack's restaurant in boston, massachusetts

1. bring bottled clam juice and potatoes to boil in heavy large saucepan over high heat
2. reduce heat to medium-low
3. cover and simmer until potatoes are tender , about 10 minutes
4. remove from heat
5. melt butter in heavy large pot over medium heat
6. add bacon and cook until bacon begins to brown , about 8 minutes
7. add onions , celery , garlic and bay leaf and saut until vegetables soften , about 6 minutes
8. stir in flour and cook 2 minutes
9. gradually whisk in reserved juices from clams
10. add potato mixture , clams , half and half and hot pepper sauce
11. simmer chowder 5 minutes to blend flavors , stirring frequently
12. season to taste with salt and pepper
demonstrations.review: Very tasty! The only thing i did differently was I used 2 10oz cans of clams. It seemed like a perfect amount. Everything else stayed the same. So good!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
imitation crab cakes

don't let the title fool you, these are so good! i adapted them from a regular crab cake recipe on allrecipes when our grocer had imitation crab on sale. the crab cakes may need 2 eggs as reviewers have noted, it depends on how moist your imitation crab is and how finely you flake it. the cakes won't seem to hold together well but they will cook up nicely, just be sure to make them small and carefully flip them when they're nice and brown on the bottom. 

i've also made these with finely diced red pepper and cilantro, omitting the green onions, and that is probably our new favorite way to prep.

1. heat 1 tablespoon oil in a non-stick skillet over medium heat
2. saute green onions briefly until tender
3. combine crabmeat , sauteed green onions , egg , mayonnaise , dry mustard , crushed crackers , cayenne pepper , garlic powder , old bay seasoning , lemon , salt and pepper with your hands
4. work the ingredients together so they start to stick together
5. form into 1 / 2 inch thick patties
6. heat 1 tablespoon oil in the non-stick skillet over medium-medium high heat
7. works really well on a flat griddle
8. cook cakes until nicely browned on each side
9. drain briefly on paper towels and serve hot
demonstrations.review: These were fantastic! I didn't have Old Bay so I used some Creole seasoning. They had LOTS of flavor. YUM!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
wasabi sesame tuna

if you like the flavor of wasabi you will like this recipe. these do not come out of the pan fiery hot, but with wasabi flavor. you can always add more heat if you wish.

1. in a shallow dish , combine the soy sauce , wasabi paste and cracked black pepper
2. mix well
3. add the tuna and turn until thoroughly coated on both sides
4. let sit for 10 minutes or plan ahead and let marinate overnight in a zipper bag or foodsaver bag
5. coat a pan with nonstick cooking spray and preheat over high heat
6. place the sesame seeds in another shallow dish , add the tuna and turn to coat completely
7. grill the tuna for 1 to 2 minutes per side , or until browned or cooked to desired doneness
8. slice thinly and serve with rice or stir fry
9. remember fish cooks fast and will be dry and chewy if overcooked
demonstrations.review: I didn't taste any wasabi, but it was otherwise ok.

target.recipe_text:
german fried potatoes

my grandmother got this recipe when she and my mom lived in germany.  

this is my all time favorite way to fix potatoes.

1. wash potatoes
2. sometimes i peel the potatoes and sometimes i don't
3. it's good either way
4. slice the potatoes into 1 / 8-inch thick slices
5. i take frozen bacon because it's easier to cut and cut strips down the side to get my one inch pieces
6. put enough olive oil in a large deep skillet to cover bottom of pan about 1 / 4 inch deep
7. add all of the potatoes to the pan , along with cut up bacon which hasn't been cooked yet
8. diced onions , parsley and salt and pepper
9. cook on medium high heat , stirring and watching so that potatoes don't burn because they will stick to the bottom of pan as they are cooking and you will need to scrape them up as they are browning
10. you can cover the pan for the first 20 minutes of cooking and cook on low and then turn up the heat for the last 15 minutes or so in order to brown some of the potatoes
11. good with steaks and a salad
12. estimated on servings time to make
target.review: We loved this. I used to make potatoes like this but without the bacon. The bacon adds such a good flavor. I had no problem with the bacon cooking.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
holiday rum   raisin cake

delicious cake - a nice alternative to fruitcake.

1. combine raisins and rum
2. cover and stand until rum is absorbed
3. stir together: flour , baking powder , salt
4. blend butter , sugar , eggs , and vanilla in a large bowl on low speed
5. beat on high speed for 5 minutes , scraping down sides often
6. add dry ingredients to creamed mixture alternatly with cream
7. stir in raisins and turn into baking pans
8. preheat oven to 350 degrees and bake: 12 cup bundt pan 70 to 80 minutes
9. or 2-6 cup bundt pan 40 to 45 minutes
10. this cake gets very brown on top
11. cool 10 minutes , then remove from pans
12. brush with rum & butter glaze
13. allow cake to absorb and repeat until glaze is used up
14. glaze: melt cup butter in saucepan
15. add 1 cup sugar and cup water
16. boil for 5 minutes , stirring constantly
17. remove from heat and stir in cup rum
18. cool slightly
demonstrations.review: This was a wonderful cake!! I am going to make it for Thanksgiving.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chicken roll  ups

i found this on the web somewhere and this has become my family and friends favorite dish.  i am always asked to make this and my father in law is always asking me when i am going to make him more chicken roll-ups.

1. season chicken breasts in tony chachere's or seasoning of your choice
2. cook over medium heat until done
3. cut up chicken breasts into small pieces
4. put chicken in each crescent roll and fold over
5. spray a casserole dish with non-stick cooking spray before placing roll-ups in the dish
6. on stove top , mix soup , 1 / 2 can milk , and 3 / 4 cup cheddar
7. once heated and cheese is melted , pour mixture over crescent rolls
8. top chicken roll-ups with remaining cheese
9. bake at 350 for 20 minutes or until rolls are golden brown
demonstrations.review: These are sooo good!! We loved them!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pretzel jello jell o salad dessert

this has been a family favorite for a long time.  it is great as a dessert or a side dish.  we often take this to a picnic or bring a dish type of gathering and it's always a big hit with kids and adults alike!    you might want to bring an extra container of cool whip and add a dollop to each serving.

1. lightly roll or crush pretzels
2. mix pretzels with 3 / 4 cup melted butter or margarine and 3 tablespoons of sugar and press into cake size pan or glass dish
3. bake crust at 350 for 10 minutes
4. let crust cool
5. cream together 8 - 12 ounces of cream cheese , 1
6. 5 cups of sugar and then add 12 ounces of cool whip
7. spread over cooled crust
8. mix 1 6 ounce box of instant strawberry jell-o in 2 cups of boiling water till dissolved
9. cool
10. add 2 10 ounce packages of thawed strawberries
11. spread mixture over the cream cheese layer and chill
12. enjoy !
demonstrations.review: My mother in law makes this salad and it is a favorite of the family. Really Good!!

target.recipe_text:
tomato chickpea curry

from cooking light magazine.

1. heat oil in large nonstick skillet over med heat
2. add onion , ginger , and garlic , cook 5 minute stir in garam masala , mustard seeds , and cayenne
3. cook 2 min , stirring frequently
4. stir in coconut milk and remaining ingredients except cilantro
5. bring to a boil
6. reduce heat and simmer 35 min , stirring occasionally
7. remove from heat and stir in cilantro
target.review:
I just made this from my own copy of the magazine :) I omitted the cilantro and sugar, and used regular coconut milk (unsweetended).  It turned out quite mild although the flavors deepend beautifully the next day. Next time I will grate the ginger instead of mincing it and double the coconut milk.
I served it with basmati rice and a green salad.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
arabian butternut squash casserole

this is unusual but delicious.  a tasty way to prepare butternut squash.  i make a big batch of this on sunday night and bring it to lunch all week.  i cook the squash by halving a large one and roasting it in the oven at 350 degrees for about an hour.  let it cool and scrap out the delicious meat!  adapted from the classic moosewood cookbook.

1. preheat oven to 375 degrees
2. place the mashed squash in a large bowl
3. add the remaining ingredients to the bowl and mix well
4. spread into an ungreased 9-inch square or 7 by 11 baking pan
5. bake uncovered for 25 to 30 minutes
6. optional - sprinkle the top lightly with sunflower seeds or minced walnuts - i usually omit this step
7. you may also saute the onions before adding and use fresh red peppers which you saute as well
demonstrations.review: This is delightful.  The sweetness of the butternut squash balanced nicely with the bite of the feta and yogurt.  I added a little white pepper and touch of cumin.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
bean   basil soup

got this from my friend cheryl, a kentucky girl.

1. in large saucepan , bring chicken stock to a boil over medium heat
2. add tomatoes , onion and oregano and simmer about 10 minutes
3. add beans and continue cooking until onion is tender , about another 10 minutes
4. in blender or food processor , finely chop the garlic and basil
5. add olive oil and process until combined
6. using a slotted spoon , transfer half the beans and veggies to the basil mixture
7. process until smooth , then stir puree back into the soup
8. cook pasta , reserving 1 cup of cooking water
9. stir the pasta into the soup and season with salt and pepper
10. if the soup is too thick , thin out with the pasta cooking water
11. garnish with basil and serve
demonstrations.review: Absolutely fantastic. The garlic/basil mixture blends beautifully with the base soup.  I used canned beans (which takes 3 15 oz cans, btw) and I used diced italian tomatoes. In the end I didn't need to add either salt or pepper.  This is going on my rotating soup menu. :)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
lemony fish and tomatoes

from pillsbury's one dish meals. a nice way to fix fish, and it most certainly will be even better in the summer with garden fresh tomatoes. enjoy!

1. heat oven to 400f
2. sprinkle each side of fish with salt and pepper
3. in ungreased 13x9 inch glass baking dish , arrange fish in single layer
4. squeeze juice of three lemon quarters over fish
5. arrange tomato slices on fish to cover , overlapping if necessary
6. in 8 inch skillet , heat oil over medium heat
7. add onion
8. cook 3 to 4 minutes , stirring frequently , until tender
9. add garlic
10. cook and stir 1 to 2 minutes longer
11. remove from heat
12. stir in parsley
13. sprinkle onion mixture evenly over tomatoes
14. squeeze juice of 1 lemon quarter over onion mixture
15. bake uncovered 15 to 20 minutes or until fish flakes easily with fork
16. serve with remaining lemon quarters
demonstrations.review: Since there's just two of us I semi-halved the recipie using 1/2 pound of fish, 1 lemon, and a small onion.  It turned out fantasticly.  It was very easy and quick.  My SO gave it the 'make it again' review.  I think next time I may try fresh parsley instead of the flakes or even cilantro or fresh basil.

target.recipe_text:
granny s banana cream pie

so delicious !!

1. in a saucepan , combine sugar , flour , and salt
2. stir in milk and mix well
3. cook over medium heat , stirring constantly , until the mixture thickens and comes to a boil
4. boil for 2 minutes
5. remove from the heat
6. stir a small amount of cream mixture into egg yolks
7. return all to saucepan
8. cook for 2 minutes , stirring constantly
9. remove from the heat
10. add butter and vanilla
11. mix well
12. allow to cool slightly
13. slice the bananas and place evenly in pastry shell
14. pour cream mixture over bananas
15. cool
16. before serving , garnish with whipped cream or cool whip and bananas
17. refrigerate any leftovers
target.review: The most wonderous Banana cream Pie we have ever tasted. I never. OMG!!  This is the Best Best Pie I have Enjoyed Making as well as Devouring. Made twice, once as directed, and one deep dish with 5 Banana's. I didnt change the amount of custard. even more unbelieveable. 100 Stars  A TOP "10"  Thank You for the recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
burger in a bundt

just what the recipes says! and looks really pretty!

1. preheat oven to 400 degrees
2. lightly spoon flour into a measuring cup
3. level off
4. in large bowl , combine flour , potato flakes and salt
5. cut in butter until crumbly
6. stir in chives
7. stir in milk to form dough
8. using back of spoon , form crust by pressing dough up 3 / 4 of sides of 10 or 12-cup greased and lightly floured bundt pan
9. in very large frying pan or dutch oven , brown ground beef
10. drain
11. stir in remaining filling ingredients
12. blend well
13. spoon into crust
14. bake 30 - 40 minutes
15. cool upright in pan 10 minutes
16. invert onto serving plate
17. serve with additional catsup and mustard , if desired
18. 10 - 12 servings
19. recipe may be halfed for 6-cup bundt pan
20. decrease baking time 10 minutes
21. you can also kick this up a knotch by adding / subbing bbq sauce , cayenne pepper , hot sauce , green chilies , diced tomatoes , sweet or dill pickle relish , cooked / crumbled bacon , etc --
demonstrations.review: I have made this for many years, its my April Fool's Dinner. Every year I tell the kids that they are having cake for dinner (april Fool's). They think it is awesome, and its something different for the kids, which they love.  My only difference is that I bake the Meat in the Bundt, and then I frost it with the mashed potatoe's. great recipe!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
southwestern stuffed bell peppers

simple preparation & delicious taste! use a mixture of red, green, yellow & orange peppers for a colourful presentation. recipe #2642 instead of store-bought taco seasoning mix--it makes this dish even better!

1. combine beef , onion , seasoning mix and egg in a large bowl
2. add rice and mix well
3. cut peppers in half lengthwise
4. remove seeds and membrane
5. spread tomatoes on the bottom of an ovenproof 12 x 9 inch baking dish
6. the liquid from the tomatoes will reduce during cooking so if you like lots of sauce , add about a cup of water
7. this also helps make the peppers softer
8. place peppers , cut side up , on top of the tomatoes
9. spoon beef mixture into peppers , mounding as necessary
10. top each pepper with salsa
11. bake in preheated 375f oven for 40-45 minutes or until beef is cooked thoroughly and peppers are soft
12. cover each pepper with cheese and return to oven , under the broiler , until the cheese melts- less than a minute , so watch carefully !
13. serve with sour cream and additional salsa
demonstrations.review: Made these for dinner,very very good. I added 3/4 cup of Sour Cream and a some corn to mixture, and it was awesome. DH said 10 stars. kids thought the mixture would be great in a Flour tortilla. Just a easy simple dinner. No leftover's to freeze, so I must make more.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
streusel topped triple berry coffee cake

i combined two coffee cake recipes and modified things abit to come up with this great little coffee cake. it has a wonderful fresh flavor and the house smells fabulous while it is in the oven!i like it best while it's still abit warm.

1. in a large bowl , stir together flour , sugar , baking powder and cinnamon
2. in a small bowl , mix egg , melted butter , milk and vanilla
3. stir liquids into dry ingredients just till blended
4. in a buttered 9-inch square pan , spread half of dough
5. top with berry mixture and spoon remaining dough over berries
6. in a separate bowl combine brown sugar , flour , cinnamon and nuts
7. stir in melted butter until mixture resembles moist crumbs
8. sprinkle this over top of dough and press in lightly
9. bake in a 375 oven 40 minutes or until topping is golden brown
demonstrations.review: made this for breakfast with frozen mixed berries. WONDERFUL.... the cake part was perfect in flavor and texture. Will be making again, and will use cake recipe for other goodies also. 10 stars

target.recipe_text:
pete s scratch pancakes

it was the fall of 1987 when pete nyhus walked into our office, just to visit. we started talking about breakfast, and he reached into a wastepaper basket and pulled out a scrap of teletype paper. he wrote out this recipe, and my family has never used pre-mix since.

1. mix the dry items first
2. combine the eggs and melted butter to the milk and slowly stir into the flour mixture
3. let sit at least 10 minutes while heating the pan
4. these will be high , but light and fluffy --
target.review: VERY good, light but thick and fluffy. I scaled the recipe down to make only 4 6-in. pancakes, tossed in some frozen blueberries as they cooked, and they came out great. Thanks for posting!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
blueberry picnic bars

nan

1. oven to 350
2. line an 8" square baking pan with foil , letting ends extend above pan on 2 sides
3. in a large bowl , mix oats , flour , brown sugar , baking soda and salt
4. add melted butter and stir with a fork until evenly moistened
5. reserve 1 / 2 cup crumb mixture for topping
6. press remaining mixture evenly and firmly over bottom of ungreased , foil-lined pan
7. bake 12 minute to set crust
8. filling: in a small saucepan stir berries , sugar , cornstarch and lemon juice over med
9. heat until simmering
10. simmer , stirring occasionally , until juices are no longer cloudy , about 2 minute
11. spoon over crust
12. crumble reserved crumb mixture over top
13. bake for 30 minute
14. let cool completely in pan
15. lift foil by ends onto a cutting board
16. peel off foil
17. cut into 2" squares
demonstrations.review: Delish! I used blueberry pie filling- came out fantasitc for 4th of July picnic! Thanks for sharing~

demonstrations.recipe_text:
fresh strawberry cake

i make this cake at least once every summer, when fresh strawberries are in season. it's delicious! i found the recipe in a cook book titled, 

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees f
2. for cake: sift together: flour , salt , and baking powder
3. in a separate bowl , combine butter , sugar , eggs , and vanilla
4. beat for a total of 3 minutes , scrapping the sides of the bowl
5. then add flour mixture to creamed mixture , alternating with strawberries
6. beat for two minutes
7. pour batter into two 8-inch round greased and floured cake pans
8. bake in pre-heated oven for 25-30 minutes , or until cake tests done
9. turn out on to wire cooling racks to cool
10. when cool , top with strawberry glaze
11. for strawberry glaze: mix together all ingredients
12. use enough strawberries to thin mixture
demonstrations.review: Very nice moist cake! I had it for breakfast & dessert! I used light whipping cream sprinkled with brown sugar instead of the glaze & it was amazing! Thanks for posting!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chili s salsa

you can make this sauce easily at home. from copykat.com (http://www.copykat.com)

1. in food processor place jalapenos and onions
2. process for just a few seconds
3. add both cans of tomatoes , salt , sugar , and cumin
4. process all ingredients until well blended but do not puree
5. place in covered container and chill
6. a couple of hours of chilling will help blend and enrich the flavor
7. serve with your favorite thin corn tortilla chips
demonstrations.review:
Very smooth and fairly mild taste- next time I think I will take some others' advice and add some garlic and cilantro for a little more flavor.
UPDATE: I have added about 1 T lime juice, 1/3 garlic clove, and 1 tsp dried cilantro & it makes a HUGE difference in flavor! I truly love this salsa now- so easy to make with what you have & GREAT taste!!!

target.recipe_text:
beef patties with onions

this is a very popular danish dish. it goes well with new nugget potatoes and pickled beets. you can add other spices to the patties ( eg mace) but they are really good plain so you can savour the beef and onion flavors.

1. fry the onions in 2 oz of butter until they are turning brown
2. add the water and continue cooking until it has evaporated
3. remove onions and keep them warm
4. shape the beef into round flat hamburgers and dip into seasoned flour
5. melt remaining butter and fry the hamburgers flipping once
6. the hamburgers should be crispy brown on the outside
7. , about 7 min each side
8. arrange cooked hamburgers on a platter , cover with the onions , keep warm
9. pour stock into the fry pan and bring to a boil , add salt& pepper to your taste
10. serve with the hamburgers
target.review: Wow! These were sooooo good! i have really been searching for a recipe like this. It was perfect. thanks for sharing.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s onion patties latkes

i have been making these for over 20 years, i usually get about 15 patties but it depends on the size of the batter that you drop in the pan, these are better if fried to very brown and crispy, you can make a double recipe, fry them then freeze them on a tray then pop them into freezer bags, then just warm them in the oven to crisp up, they are very addicting and i can tell you i eat half before they even get to the table lol!  if you plan on doubling the recipe then make two separate recipes in two bowls, i have doubled the recipe into one bowl and for some reason they just are not as good ---  if desired you could add in a slightly beaten large egg and reduce the milk by 1/4 cup --- you will *love* these!  also see my
recipe#186700 *and*
recipe#244592

1. chop the onions finely then place into a bowl
2. in another large bowl mix together the flour , sugar , baking powder , seasoning salt , cayenne , garlic powder and a small amount of black pepper
3. mix to combine well
4. add in the milk and whisk until thoroughly combined
5. add in the chopped onions and green onions and mix with a wooden spoon until combined
6. in a large non-stick frypan , heat a small amount of oil to medium-hot , adding in more oil as needed as the patties will absorb too much oil if you add in a large amount of oil at one time
7. drop the batter from a tablespoon into about 1 / 2-inch of hot oil
8. flatten slightly with the spoon or spatula
9. sprinkle with a little salt
10. fry until crispy and brown on both sides
demonstrations.review: I have made these a few times now and they are sooooooo good and sooooo addicting! Its very hard to not eat all of the while you are cooking them. Thanks Kitten for great recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
spinach saute with brown butter   garlic

this quick-cooking vegetable accompaniment is best with tender, young spinach. recipe from fine cooking

1. in a large saute pan over medium heat , melt the butter with the garlic until the butter is golden brown and smells nutty
2. make sure the garlic doesnt burn
3. raise the heat to high and add the spinach , in batches if need be , flipping and stirring , until just barely wilted , about 1 minute take the pan off the heat
4. remove the garlic
5. season the spinach with salt , pepper , and a squeeze of lemon
6. toss and serve immediately
demonstrations.review: I have made this 2x now and I just love it. The lemon brightens the taste and the garlic is not over powering. Followed recipe exactly. Thank you!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
old fashioned baked rice pudding

everyone loves this home-y custard type of rice pudding. one of the ultimate comfort foods. add raisins or omit according to personal preference.

1. in a large bowl , combine eggs , sugar and salt
2. gradually whisk hot scalded milk into egg mixture
3. stir in rice , raisins and vanilla
4. pour into a greased quart casserole dish
5. set casserole into a larger ovenproof dish
6. fill larger dish with hot water until water reaches halfway up the casserole dish
7. bake@ 325 for 90 minutes , or until knife pulls out clean
demonstrations.review: This was an excellent rice pudding. I wasnt quite sure about the texture at first, but once I ate it found it to be wonderful. I used a round quart dish and followed recipe exactly. Didnt add rasins cuz I dont like them. Thanks :)

target.recipe_text:
vegetarian western bacon cheeseburger

i know, this sound weird. i've been a vegetarian for 5 years and there are some items i missed from my meat eating days. i was having a craving for a carl's jr. western bacon cheeseburger one day and decided to vegetarianize it. this is super easy to make and tastes very much like the original. to save time and to make it taste more authentic, use onion rings from a fast food restaurant like sonic. i prepared the burger while i send my boyfriend down the street to sonic. also, slightly burning the lightlife smart bacon is what makes it taste like real bacon.

1. if cooking your own onion rings , preheat the oven and start those first
2. spray a small pan with cooking spray and heat to medium
3. cook smart bacon until crispy and slightly burned , turning occasionally
4. set aside
5. thaw griller patty in microwave and transfer to heated pan on medium-low
6. cook until slightly crispy , but not burned
7. while the patty is cooking , lightly toast the buns on a skillet
8. have cheese slice ready and immediately after turning the patty , place cheese on top followed by the bacon and bbq sauce
9. you may put some drops of water into the pan at this time , the steam will help melt the cheese
10. pull the bottom bun from skillet and place the onion rings on it
11. pull the rest of the burger on top
12. enjoy !
13. if you buy them from a fast food place , the cook time is closer to 10 minutes
target.review:
I've been coming up with veggie versions of old carnivorous favorites for years! This one is really yummy. I used Morningstar bacon instead, though. It's my favorite. Lots of different barbecue sauces would be good on this, I think. 

Definitely 5 stars!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
garlic    feta lovers rotini pasta for one

this is something i whipped up spur of the moment & i couldn't get enough. i love all the garlic & feta...pure bliss! since i'm the only one in my household who eats pasta i always make just enough for me.

1. cook pasta according to package , drain
2. in a small saucepan heat olive oil & garlic until garlic is lightly browned over med
3. heat
4. add pasta & feta cheese , stirring to coat
5. cook 1-2 minutes on low heat or until feta is melted to your liking
6. empty into a bowl & add a dash of salt & a few dashes of pepper to taste
7. hope you enjoy !
demonstrations.review: YUM! Simple but so good. It's easy...important as I'm the only vegetarian in the house and have to cook for myself. The feta is unique. I used at least 2 tsp. of garlic, so it wouldn't be good date food, though! Thanks, Sirpezy!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
taco potato skins

nan

1. cut each potato lengthwise into quarters
2. with a spoon , scoop out the pulp , leaving a 1 / 4 inch shell and discard pulp
3. in a small bowl , mix together the butter and taco seasoning
4. brush butter mixture over both sides of the potato skins
5. place skin side down on a greased baking sheet
6. sprinkle with cheese , bacon , and onions
7. bake at 350 degrees for 5 to 10 minutes or until the cheese is melted
8. serve with salsa and sour cream
demonstrations.review: Instead of bacon bits (although I imagine imitation ones might be interesting), I made these with Morningstar meatless crumbles (which I use for tacos). They make great taco meat with the taco seasoning. I also left out the onions (personal preference).

demonstrations.recipe_text:
ratatouille inspired by the animated film

this recipe is from the christian science monitor.  it is gorgeous when assembled and absolutely delicious prepared and served with a dab of goat cheese and crusty french bread.  choose only skinny vegetables that will slice uniformly in size.

1. preheat oven to 375 degrees f
2. in a large round or square baking dish , pour tomato puree and spread until evenly distributed
3. drop the sliced garlic and chopped onion into the puree , stir in 1 t olive oil and season the sauce generously with salt and pepper
4. trim ends of the vegetables , removing the seeds from inside the pepper , slicing all into very thin slices , like coins , about 1 / 16th of an inch thick
5. i just used a knife and it was quick and easy but the recipe says to use a mandoline
6. arrange sliced vegetables concentrically from the outer edge of the baking dish to the inside , overlapping and alternating vegetables
7. drizzle the remaining t olive oil , season with salt and pepper and strip the thyme off the stems and sprinkle over vegetables
8. cut a piece of parchment paper to fit inside and fit flush on top of the vegetables , not draped over the dish
9. bake for 50 minutes
10. you want the vegetables to have released their liquid , be cooked but not limp and the dish should not be browned around the edges
11. the tomato sauce will be bubbling around everything
demonstrations.review: Yummy! Took out the red pepper (personal preference) but absolutely fantastic. Great to eat while watching the movie too!

target.recipe_text:
chicken garlic bites

simple and fun to make, great to eat! prep time includes marinating the chicken.  use matzo meal instead of the breadcrumbs and this is good for passover as well.

1. place chicken in shallow dish
2. in small bowl , mix olive oil , garlic , and black pepper
3. pour over chicken
4. cover and marinate 30 minutes
5. drain
6. preheat oven to 475f
7. mix bread crumbs and cayenne
8. coat chicken
9. arrange in a single layer on cookie sheet
10. bake 10 minutes or until brown
target.review: This was very easy to make and can be dressed up with a variety of things, depending on your preferences. I think the best thing about this dish is being healthy since there was little fat and olive oil is used instead of other fat. I used only half (1/4 cup) of the olive oil in the recipe and it worked out fine. Also, just before breading the chicken, I seasoned it with salt. This turned out moist and tender. For the people who says that the chicken turned out to be dry, you might have overcooked your chicken. I only cooked my chicken for 10-15 minutes and they turned out perfect. Make sure you have a high temperature to have that golden brown exterior and tender chicken inside.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cold peanut noodles

serve cold or at room temp.  i prefer room temp.

1. bring a large pot of boiling water to a boil
2. cook spaghetti noodles according to package directions
3. drain
4. rinse in very cold water and drain again
5. place cooled noodles in a large bowl and toss with the carrots , scallions , bell pepper slices and cilantro
6. in a small bowl , whisk together the sauce ingredients until smooth
7. drizzle the sauce over noodles mixture
8. toss to coat well
9. serve room temp or cold
10. garnish with sesame seeds if desired
demonstrations.review: Very easy to make and quite healthy too. You can also customize the recipe by adding what you like. Chicken would work great with this recipe. Also maybe crushed peanuts for texture, fried tofu strips, prawns, etc...

demonstrations.recipe_text:
delicious chicken pot pie

this chicken pot pie recipe takes a little time, but it is well worth it!! this is an all-time favorite in our family. great on a cold winter day.

1. preheat oven to 400f
2. saute onion , celery , carrots and potatoes in margarine for 10 minutes
3. add flour to sauteed mixture , stirring well , cook one minute stirring constantly
4. combine broth and half and half
5. gradually stir into vegetable mixture
6. cook over medium heat stirring constantly until thickened and bubbly
7. stir in salt and pepper
8. add chicken and stir well
9. pour into shallow 2 quart casserole dish and top with pie shells
10. cut slits to allow steam to escape
11. bake for 40-50 minutes or until pastry is golden brown and filling is bubbly and cooked through
demonstrations.review: Delish! It was creamy and is really yummy! I used Recipe #51537 for the crust. I will definitely make this again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
my no roll pie crust

the only pie crust i will use anymore. its flaky and slightly sugary and oh so easy to do. note: due to some major discrepencies please use a good quality oil, preferably a vegetable and a good name brand like mazola, it may not seem like it will make a difference but in the end it will, also use new oil not something that has been sitting around for a while.

1. mix dry ingredients together with a fork in a pie pan
2. make a well in the center and add the oil and milk
3. mix with a fork til it makes a ball
4. flatten and press into the pan in pie crust shape and flute the edge
5. bake at 375 for 10-12 minutes until golden
6. one crust pie , excellent for cream pies and crumb topped baked pies
demonstrations.review: I used this for a Chicken Pot Pie recipe (Recipe #10744). This crust was flaky and really nice. But I find it better to use on dessert pies. And next time I will try to make it with meted butter to have the buttery flavour.

target.recipe_text:
snow peas with mushrooms

an easy and quick veggie dish that can be served with any main dish.

1. lightly cook snow peas in boiling water and drain
2. melt butter in skillet , add mushrooms with salt and pepper
3. cook stirring constantly about 2 minutes
4. add snow peas , ginger and shallots
5. toss to blend and cook about 30 seconds
6. serve immediately
target.review: A mix of some of my favourite things, loved this recipe, thanks for posting.  =)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
nanaimo bars

love em' !!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!

1. melt the first three ingredients in top of double broiler
2. add egg and stir to cook and thicken
3. remove from heat
4. stir in remaining ingredients
5. press firmly into a ungreased 8x8 pan
6. --------secondlayer--------
7. cream together butter , cream , custard powder and icing sugr
8. spread over bottom layer
9. ------thirdlayer------
10. melt chcolate and butter over low heat
11. cool
12. whe cool but still liquid pour over second layer and chill well in refirgerator
13. cut into bars and serve
demonstrations.review:
I had this recipe years ago and seem to have lost it, this is our favourite bar recipe after trying it in Canada a long time ago.
We cant get Graham Crackers here so I used 1 packet of digestive biscuits (minus 3 biscuits) and for the chocolate layer I used a medium size block of Energy chocolate. (a dark Cadbury brand chocolate)
Love them!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
low fat creamy baked salmon

from what's cooking america. delicious way to easily prepare salmon. so yummy! this recipe not only appeals to north america- u.s. and canada- also fits quite well in french, scandinavian and eastern european cultures and cuisines.

1. preheat oven to 400f rinse fish and pat dry
2. place fillets skin side down in a single layer in a greased 9x13 pan
3. whisk sour cream , mayo , flour , lemon juice , dill , cream cheese , garlic and wine in a medium bowl until smooth and spread over fish
4. season with salt , pepper and paprika to taste
5. bake uncovered for 15 to 20 minutes until internal temp is 140 f or middle inside of fish is slightly opaque
6. fish will continue to cook for a few minutes after removing from oven
7. transfer to serving platter spooning sauce over fish and sprinkling with additional paprika and dill to garnish if desired
demonstrations.review:
I only had 3 fillets so reduced quantities of ingredients, what an absolutely delicious recipe. The salmon was moist and full of flavour, I will make this a lot, in to my favourite file.
Thanks for sharing.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chicken and mushrooms with cheese

this dish was served at a party i went to, and everyone wanted seconds, and the recipe. i haven't yet made it myself but do plan on it. it was very tasty and delicious!

1. arrange chicken in a greased casserole dish
2. combine soups and wine together and pour over chicken
3. stir in mushrooms , green onions , and cheese
4. bake at 300 uncovered for 1 1 / 2-2 hours
5. let casserole sit about 20 minutes before serving
demonstrations.review:
This was really tasty, the chicken has a nice 'smooth' texture. I cut back on the chicken and soup amounts, used 3 breasts and half a can each of the soup, still had lots of 'gravy'.
Thanks for posting.

target.recipe_text:
summer cucumber salad

a nice, light summer appetizer we often have before dinner.

1. combine ingredients , mixing well
2. divide into two bowls leaving some liquid in the bottom of each bowl
3. refrigerate if desired and eat later or enjoy now !
target.review: I used pickling cukes so no need to seed :)Really good and simple recipe.  I had never put the cheese on it but it is a great addition.  Thanks for sharing.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
stroganoff

this recipe was used by both my mother and my mother-in-law. it's been a favorite of our families for years, and is both easy and delicious.

1. brown beef in large skillet
2. add onions and cook until onions are translucent
3. drain grease
4. stir in condensed soup , then garlic powder , salt , and pepper
5. allow to simmer until all other parts of meal are prepared
6. minutes before it's time to serve , stir in the sour cream completely and heat through
7. serve over egg noodles
demonstrations.review: I made this with ground turkey and fresh mushrooms and it was GREAT!!  Quick, easy, versitile meal.  I added a little water that I used to rinse the soup can out with.  Served on Dreamfield's pasta.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
vueltas de carne

to "dar vueltas," means to "flip" or "go around in circles" which is why these steaks are named so! a quick flip in the pan and they're done! these make great sandwiches, or are good alone served with crusty french bread to soak up the sauce. garlic mayo really compliments the meat too. they can be made with beef, pork or chicken, as long as the cut of meat is very thin. they get better with time, too, so if you want, you could make them a day ahead and just heat them up when you're ready.

1. pound steaks with a meat mallet until very thin
2. salt and pepper both sides of steaks
3. combine remaining ingredients , and brush onto steaks
4. allow to marinate for at least 1 / 2 an hour
5. heat a small amount of olive oil over fairly high heat , until just about smoking , fry steaks very quickly on each side , just enough for it to lose the pink--don't worry if it isn't cooked completely through--it will be after the next step
6. remove any burned garlic
7. transfer steaks to a shallow pot and cover
8. with the juices remaining in the pan , add a little white wine and reduce just a bit and pour over steaks
9. heat through
10. the steam from the sauce will have cooked the steaks through
11. serve with crusty french bread and garlic mayo
12. these can be made into sandwiches too !
demonstrations.review: What a great way to us thinly sliced round steaks!  Tons of flavor for very few ingredients.  I served with a horseradish mayo dip.  Will try it on sandwiches next time.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
uncle bill s petite pea salad

a very light salad to add to any dinner meals. i developed this recipe in 1995 and it has been a highly rated salad.

1. in a microwave-proof dish , microwave peas on high for 2 minutes
2. stir
3. continue to microwave for an additional 2 minutes on high
4. drain and cool completely with cold water and ice cubes
5. then drain
6. in a large mixing bowl , mix together peas , sour cream , mayonnaise , dill weed , onions and celery and mix well to blend
7. chill for at least 30 minutes in refrigerator
8. meanwhile , fry bacon until well done and crispy
9. do not burn
10. place fried bacon on paper toweling to drain
11. crumble bacon and garnish salad when serving
demonstrations.review: I really liked this.  I did not use the bacon cause I am trying really hard to cut down on that stuff.  Used low fat mayo and low fat sour cream.  Thought there was plenty of "juice" so I add another cup of peas and another couple of tablespoons of onions and had lunch for 2 days!  Thanks Unk.

target.recipe_text:
linda s twice baked potatoes

these are just plain gooooooood!  these yummy babies go great with just about any meat, fish, or poultry dish!

1. heat oven to 350
2. wash potatoes
3. pierce tops of potatoes with fork several times
4. do not wrap in aluminum foil
5. bake potatoes on oven rack 70-85 minutes or until tender when pierced
6. remove from oven , and cool 10-15 minutes
7. meanwhile , in lg
8. bowl , combine all remaining ingredients
9. cut a thin slice off top of each potato
10. using a teaspoon , scoop out center of each , leaving a thin shell
11. add potato centers to cheese mixture
12. using fork , break up potatoes , and mix until well blended
13. spoon mixture into potato shells
14. transfer to baking sheet
15. position potatoes under broiler so that tops are 5" from heat source
16. broil 4-6 mins
17. , or until tops are golden brown
18. turn off heat , close oven door , and leave potatoes in oven for an additional 7-10 mins
19. , or until heated through
target.review: These  were great - really really cheesy.  I used the bagged shredded cheese that was a mix of cheddar and monterey jack and it worked nicely. I really liked how soft they stayed. Will be making these again - thanks!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
turkey and balsamic onion quesadillas

from eating well (feb-march 2005). they suggest using the leftover vinegar (whisked with olive oil, salt and pepper) to dress a green salad to accompany these treats.

1. marinate onion in vinegar for 5 minutes
2. over med-high heat , warm tortillas for about 45 seconds
3. place 1 / 4 of the filling items in each quesadilla and fold tortilla over the top
4. flatten with spatula and cook until golden on both sides
demonstrations.review: This is a quick dinner and it tastes great. We loved it!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pasta with sausage  tomatoes  and cream

delicious and satisfying... i don't remember where this recipe comes from, but it's a pleaser! easily doubled.  also, works well with gf pasta and sausage

1. heat oil in a heavy skillet over medium heat
2. add sausage and crushed red pepper
3. cook until sausage is no longer pink , stirring frequently , about 7 minutes
4. add onion and garlic to skillet and cook until onion is tender and sausage is light brown , stirring occasionally , about 7 minutes
5. add tomatoes , cream , and salt
6. simmer until mixture thickens slightly , about 4 minutes
7. cook pasta in large pot of boiling water
8. drain
9. bring sauce to a simmer
10. add pasta to sauce and cook until pasta is heated through and sauce thickens , stirring occasionally , about 2 minutes
11. divide pasta between plates
12. sprinkle with parsley
13. serve , passing parmesan separately
demonstrations.review: What a great recipe. The mixture is fantastic. I changed it a bit and used chicken instead of sausage and used fresh red peppers. Thanks for posting

demonstrations.recipe_text:
awesome twice baked potatoes

mom gave me this recipe and i can't wait to try it. i assume that it came from pace but it sounds wonderful.

1. cut each potato in half lengthwise
2. scoop out potatoes , leaving a thin shell
3. in a bowl , mash potatoes
4. add 3 / 4 c cheese , sour cream , picante sauce , bacon and onions
5. mix well
6. spoon back into shells
7. place shells on a cookie sheet and broil until nicely browned
8. sprinkle with remaining 1 / 4 c cheese and broil until cheese is bubbly
9. top with salsa to serve
demonstrations.review: This was the best twice baked potatoes ever!!  I just used salsa and it turned out fine. I used  shredded cheese mix of cheddar and monterey jack cheese.  This is a "keeper"

target.recipe_text:
italian sausage pie

this pie makes a lovely light supper dish. it takes very little time to put together and bake. serve it with your favorite salad. this recipe is adapted from a cookbook by the sons of italy florida foundation.

1. place pie shell in oven during the pre-heating time for about 5- 10 minutes in order to firm the bottom some
2. don't overcook !
3. remove casing from the sausage and crumble
4. saut sausage and onions
5. drain well and spoon into prepared pie shell
6. blend eggs , milk , cheese , salt and pepper
7. pour over sausage mixture
8. bake at 350 degrees f
9. for 35 minutes , or until custard sets and tests clean with a knife
10. allow to cool slightly
11. cut into 8 wedges and serve
target.review: I followed the recipe exactly. It turned out great and I LOVED IT!  Thanks

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chicken and flour tortilla dumplings

these taste just like the one's your grandmother use to make. they are so thin and perfect. unless you tell i promise nobody will ever know they are flour tortilla's. if you want to make for a really big crowd, follow the same instructions just use a 6 qt pot and an additional small pack of 8.5 oz shells. also you can omit the chicken if you want and use canned chicken broth or bouillon cubes.

1. fill 4-quart pot half full with water
2. boil chicken until tender
3. while chicken is cooking , slice tortillas with a sharp knife 5 slices across and one slice through the middle
4. remove cooked chicken and shred with a fork or cut into cubes
5. place chicken , cream of chicken soup , butter , salt and pepper into boiling chicken broth
6. bring to a rolling boil
7. drop individual tortillas into pot one piece at a time
8. do not stir , you can pat the top of the dumplings and move them around slightly with a wooden spoon
9. boil medium / high heat for 12 minutes
10. remove from heat
11. add 1 cup of milk and move the dumplings around gently to mix the milk
demonstrations.review:
Very good.  Very easy!
I'll make this again!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cheese stuffed mushrooms

garlic and cheese filled

1. remove mushroom stems and chop finely
2. in a small pan , cook stems , green onions , garlic and butter over medium heat til tender , about 5 minutes
3. remove from heat and add all remaining ingredients except caps
4. fill caps with mixture , place in baking dish
5. bake 350f for 15 minutes
demonstrations.review: Easy flavorful recipe.  No leftovers!  This recipe is a keeper!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cheese ball with tuna

possibly the easiest and quickest thing you can throw together!

time does not include chilling time, as you can chill for as long or as little as you want or serve immediately. flavours blend better with a little time to rest though.

1. using a fork flake tuna into small little bits into a bowl
2. add the cream cheese to the bowl and mash with the fork until everything is well combined
3. add the dijon a small sprinkle of salt and pepper to taste and continue mashing
4. add the hot sauce to taste ! i add up to a full tablespoon , sometimes more , but this is entirely up to your preference
5. add a small amount at a time and taste as you mash until you achieve a flavour you like !
6. scoop the mixture onto the center of a piece of plastic wrap
7. wrap tightly and shape into a ball as you roll
8. toss it into th fridge until chilled , or into the freezer for 30 mins or so it you are really strapped for time
9. serve on a platter with crackers !
10. options
11. you can use a different canned fish too ! try crab or salmon !
12. try rolling the ball in finely chopped nuts or grated cheese !
13. you can omit the hot sauce and dijon and try other seasonings of your choice !
demonstrations.review: I've been making this for years and it's always a hit.  Try using horseradish mustard instead of dijon.  Yum!

target.recipe_text:
cherry pie

i got this recipe from my sister-in-law when i got married and my husband's aunt had a cherry tree. it is our favorite! prep time does not include the time it takes to pit the cherries or make the pie crust. ;) i use the pie crust recipe in the fanny farmer baking book. recipe #13619 is the recipe for 2 8-inch crust. (i've found i have to refrigerate it for the pie filling to firm up and not be "soupy" when it has cooled. once it has completely chilled, you can store it at room temperature and it doesn't lose its firmness. or, store it in the fridge and warm it in the microwave a little bit before serving it with ice cream or whipped cream if desired.)

1. mix ingredients for filling
2. place in pastry-lined pie pan
3. put top crust on
4. cut vent slits in top crust , and flute edges
5. brush with milk and sprinkle with sugar
6. bake at 425f for 25 minutes , reduce heat to 350f and bake for 25-30 minutes more
7. add the cherries and toss to coat
8. this coats them more even than doing it in a bowl and the filling is firmer
target.review: We lived in our house for 6 years and I have never made anything from the cherries off of our cherry tree until now.  My neighbor asked me when I was going to make him a cherry pie.  I decided to try it.  I knew the cherries were tart so I could only use them for baking.  My neighbor said that it was "pretty darn good for your first pie."  I think that the cherries were a little too juicy because even with the flour it was pretty runny.  Next time I am going to add some almond extract and a little more cinnamon.  I'll also try cornstarch since these cherries are really juicy.  I used the refrigerated pie crust and it came out fine. I will definitely be using this recipe again!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
queso con gouda

just goes to prove that queso can be made with almost any cheese.  the important factor in making good queso is to use a processed cheese (like velveeta) for at least one of the cheese choices. a mixture of smoked gouda and regular gouda is recommended and gives this a subtle smoke flavor that really adds depth.  if necessary, this can be made using 8 oz of regular gouda.  developed for rsc #11.

1. heat the oil in a medium size pan , saute the shallots and garlic until soft , stir in the chili peppers
2. add the milk starting with 3 / 4 cup and adding the additional 1 / 2 cup as needed for proper consistency
3. add tomatoes , cayenne pepper , and cheese
4. heat over low heat until cheese melts
5. season as desired with salt and pepper
6. serve warm with tortilla chips , hamburger patty , hamburger steak or chicken
demonstrations.review: This was a great tasting dip and a good alternative to the traditional queso that is made.  I didn't have any sun-dried tomatoes but it was still good.  I loved the taste of the smoked Gouda and will probably use more of that when making it next time.  My guests loved it, too!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
couscous with sausage  pine nuts and cranberries

i adapted this recipe from a weight watcher recipe. the ingredients really compliment each other. we live in northern alaska and used a spicy caribou sausage but i think turkey sausage or pork sausage will taste just as good.

1. in a nonstick skillet , cook sausage over medium heat , breaking it up as it cooks
2. stir in onion , cumin , cinnamon , coriander
3. cook until onion has softened
4. stir in cranberries and chicken broth and bring to a simmer
5. stir in couscous , cover , remove from heat and let stand 5 minutes
6. fluff with a fork , sprinkle with pine nuts and serve
demonstrations.review: Tried this recipe last nite.  Was really good.  I used turkey sausage and it tasted great!!  Very easy!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
navy bean pie  muslim

i got hooked on the bean pie i used to get from the muslim bakery back home, so had to try and recreate it! this is very good and reminds me of pumpkin pie, except it's made from beans. :-)

(to get the beans smoothly mashed, i would recommend a food processor).

1. preheat oven to 425 degrees
2. combine eggs and evaporated milk in a bowl
3. add beans , sugar and all spices
4. beat at low speed of a mixer until well blended
5. pour into unbaked pie shell
6. bake at 425 degrees for 15 minutes
7. reduce heat to 350 degrees and bake for another 35 minutes or until knife inserted in center comes out clean
8. serve warm with whipped cream or you can even enjoy it cold
9. :-)
demonstrations.review: It was hard to get people to try.  But once they did, they really liked it!!  The only thing is I would cut back on the nutmeg to maybe 1/2 tsp.  Thanks!!!

target.recipe_text:
california bowl

like california rolls but don't want seaweed? not too skilled at rolling your own sushi? try this easy and flexible recipe. you can easily add or subtract whichever sushi ingredients you like to make your favorite flavor. enjoy!

1. cook rice with 1-1 / 2 cups of water for 20 minutes or until soft and sticky
2. cool the cooked rice in the refrigerator until room temperature
3. meanwhile , shell the crab legs and tear the crabmeat into small pieces
4. dice the carrot and cucumber into small pieces
5. press rice into two bowls
6. pressed rice should have a dip in the middle
7. add crab , avocado , carrot and cucumber into the dip in the rice
8. drizzle with soy sauce
9. top with ginger and sesame seeds
target.review: My 11 year old daughter and I had eaten California Rolls earlier today and she wanted more, so we went searching for a recipe that she could make. She did everything herself and loved it. We used imitation crab leg (all we had) and I splashed teriyaki sauce over the top of mine instead of soy. We also didn't use the ginger or sesame seeds, and diced the avocado since it really didn't say what to do with it. But overall it was an awesome meal!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cilantro lime cream sauce

this makes everything delicious. we eat it on fish (especially salmon), chicken, vegetables, bread...the combination of cool and spicy is great and it's so easy to make

1. put container of sour cream and good sized bunch of chopped cilantro into blender , add juice of 1 lime
2. blend until smooth
3. chop jalapeno , add to blender
4. add salt and more lime to taste , blend everything until smooth
demonstrations.review: I made & refrigerated this for several hours before using it as a dip for boiled shrimp.  Al I have to say is WOW!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chunked venison

the deer hunters in my family think this is the greatest venison recipe. this recipe was adapted from a recipe for beef birds, and the seasonings have been adjusted.

1. cut pieces of venison into 1 - inch squares
2. take a thin slice of bacon and cut it just long enough to wrap around the meat
3. secure with a toothpick
4. make about 2 dozen pieces
5. put in a heavy skillet
6. add water , salt , lots of black pepper and worcestershire sauce
7. boil rapidly until liquid is nearly gone
8. reduce heat and cover skillet
9. continue cooking at low heat until meat is brown
10. the meat will be very rich
demonstrations.review: I made this last night and it was great! Everyone in the family loved it. Like Aunt Paula I am always looking for new ways to cook venison and I will definitely make this again. Thanks!(Note-If you sip wine while wrapping the "chunks" it goes faster:)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
quick and easy sausage and cheese muffins

i'm from the country and throughly enjoy breakfast food at any time of the day.  these are so quick and easy and they satisfy my craving for breakfast food, but i can give some to pop for his breakfast at work.  they're also great for kids, as they are muffins - just right for little hands.

1. preheat oven to 400 degrees
2. brown the sausage and drain well
3. mix in milk , soup , and sage
4. stir in the bisquick just until moistened
5. fill greased muffin cups
6. bake until golden brown , 25-30 min
demonstrations.review: I have been making these for years.  This is a simple but great recipe.  I am expected to make these for every family gathering or threats are made.

target.recipe_text:
cheddar horseradish burgers

a new twist to an old favorite from everyday foods.  i like it with sharp cheddar cheese-double slice. top with your favorite burger add-ons.

1. heat grill to medium-high
2. in a medium bowl , place beef , horseradish , worcestershire sauce , and dash of coarse salt and pepper
3. mix very gently with a fork to combine , being careful not to over work meat
4. gently form into 4 equal size patties--4 inches in diameter and 1 inch thick
5. with thumb make a 1 / 2-inch deep indentation in the center of each patty to keep burgers flat during grilling
6. moisten a folded paper towel with oil
7. holding with tongs--rub over grill grate
8. season burgers again with salt and pepper , if desired
9. grill 4-7 minutes per side for medium-rate , placing cheese on second side for last 3 minutes
10. serve in grill-toasted english muffins with your choice of add-ons
target.review: Nice burgers.  We under seasoned ours, I'd add more salt and pepper next time, but I was worried about the salt from the worcestershire.  We did also find it hard to make thinner patties- for us, one inch was a bit thick but without a binder like egg, the patties started to crack apart.  But I'd add the seasonings again for sure.  We served on hamburger buns with salad and onion.  Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
almost cake mix vanilla cupcakes

for pretty pastel coloured cupcakes, add in a few drop of desired food colouring my recipe#80118 goes wonderful with these cupcakes --- i use 2 cups icing sugar and 1/2 cup white granulated sugar instead of processing the sugar, it works out fine this way.

1. set oven to 375 degrees
2. line 24 muffin pans with paper cupcake liners
3. in an electric mixer , cream butter and shortening until fluffy
4. add in the eggs and the extracts and beat about 3-4 minutes on high speed
5. add in the sugar
6. beat well until sugar is completely combined
7. in a bowl , sift together flour , salt and baking powder
8. blend into the creamed ingredients , along with the warm milk until smooth
9. fill the prepared pans about two-thirds full
10. immediately , reduce oven temperature to 350 degrees
11. place the cupcakes in oven , and bake for about 20-24 minutes , or until the cupcakes test done
demonstrations.review: Yay for Kittencal! I wanted to make cupcakes with that dense but light texture you can't get anywhere else.  This recipe was what I was looking for! And totally easy as well.  I don't agree that they don't have a tonne of flavour, there is a lot of vanilla in there and I also used that tiny bit of lemon extract which I think was a really nice touch and not something I would have thought of.  My husband ate them unfrosted! I used margarine as we don't really have much shortening here.  I kept them in an airtight container in the fridge, and they were fine 24 hours later (once they reached room temperature).

demonstrations.recipe_text:
microwave spaghetti oamc

i don't recall where i got this recipe from but i use to make it all the time when i was in college. this also freezes nicely.

1. in a 3 quart microwave safe casserole , crumble beef and add onions
2. microwave on high for 3-4 minutes , stirring to break up meat
3. microwave on high for 2 more minutes and drain off fat
4. add spaghetti sauce , water , basil and uncooked spaghetti
5. mix to combine
6. cover with lid and microwave on high for 5 minutes
7. stir
8. cover casserole again and microwave on high for 8-10 minutes longer
9. stir
10. if you want to freeze this dish , at this point cool the casserole in the refrigerator
11. wrap , label , and attach a freezer bag with the grated parmesan cheese
12. freeze up to 3 months
13. to thaw and reheat , thaw overnight in refrigerator
14. cover casserole with microwave safe paper towel and microwave on medium for 7-8 minutes until warm
15. sprinkle with cheese and continue as directed below
16. if not freezing , sprinkle with cheese , cover again and microwave on high for 7-8 minutes longer until spaghetti is tender
17. let stand 4 minutes before serving
demonstrations.review: What an easy recipe! Who'd have thought it could be so simple. I knocked this up for some lunchpacks for my husband.  I used kangaroo mince, and Italian herbs, and added about 2 tablespoons of balsamic vinegar for a bit more flavour. I also used stock instead of water. Thanks, I'll be making this again!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pumpkin   sweet basil pasta

a simple but tasty pasta to throw together, great for a hurried weeknight meal.

1. combine soup with wine & basil in a saucepan , stirring well , simmer until hot
2. add the pasta to the sauce & toss to combine
3. serve garnished with pine nuts , crumled bacon & parmesan cheese
demonstrations.review: Thanks Mandy, this was exactly what I was looking for! A quick tasty weeknight meal that makes a change from a red or white sauce.  Next time I would add some roasted pumpkin pieces at DH's request.  Cheers!

target.recipe_text:
chocolate meringue stars

these are easy and attractive cookies. they are light and chewy and you can't eat just one. i usually make them at christmas, but they will do for any occasion.

1. in a mixing bowl , beat egg whites and vanilla until soft peaks form
2. gradually add sugar , about 2 tablespoons at a time , beating until stiff peaks form
3. gently fold in cocoa
4. place in a pastry bag with a large open star
5. line baking sheets with foil and coat the foil with nonstick cooking spray
6. pipe stars , about 1 1 / 4 in
7. diameter , onto foil , or drop by rounded teaspoons
8. bake at 300 for 30-35 minutes or util lightly browned
9. remove from foil
10. cool on wire racks
11. in a microwave or double boiler , melt chocolate and shortening
12. stir until smooth
13. dip the cookies halfway into glaze
14. place on waxed paper to harden
target.review: It is true that you can not just eat one.  I ended up making a double batch.  I knew I wouldn't have time or patience for the glaze so I sprinkled them with chocolate sprinkles before I baked them.  Looked pretty and tasted great.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
peanut butter chocolate chip brownies

i was at a "ladies' coffee" and one of the hostesses made these amazing peanut butter brownies. i asked her for the recipe and she was kind enough to share it with me. she said it originally had come from an issue of bon appetit magazine. she cut these into 25 very tiny cubes,because they are quite rich. you can cut them as large or small as you like- i generally get 16 small brownies out of one batch.

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees f
2. generously grease& flour an 8" square baking pan
3. cream butter using an electric mixer
4. add peanut butter and beat until blended , scraping down the sides of the bowl with a spatula as needed
5. beat in brown sugar
6. beat in 1 egg at a time , then add the vanilla
7. in another bowl , sift together the flour , salt , and baking powder
8. add the flour mixture to the peanut butter mixture and beat until blended
9. using a wooden spoon , stir in the chocolate chips
10. spread evenly into the prepared pan and bake about 37-55 minutes , or until top is lightly browned all over and no longer shiny , and a toothpick poked in the center comes out with just a few moist crumbs stuck to it
11. check early - the earlier you pull them out of the oven , the more moist they will be
12. let cool before cutting
13. they should be like moist , fudgey brownies in texture and they will firm up when they are fully cooled
demonstrations.review: I made these for dessert for some lunch guests we had today.  They were a big hit.  Of course my family loves anything with the peanut butter and chocolate combination.  I did make one change.  I always find that when I put chocolate chips in a cake type recipe they sink to the bottom so instead I melted the chocolate chips and swirled them into the batter.  These looked really pretty and tasted great too!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
rice with almonds and raisins

i created this dish to serve with the moroccan lemon chicken. however, this is a great side dish for any meal.

1. boil rice according to package directions
2. saute' the almonds in butter until soft
3. add raisins and cook until a little soft
4. mix the cooked rice and the almond / raisin mixture together
demonstrations.review: This is a very common dish in Israel.  I usually serve my rice with fried onions, but tried this for a change.  Presentation was nice and it realy livened up the rice.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
instant pudding biscuits  cookies

had this recipe since the 1970's...

1. cream butter and sugar , add egg and instant pudding
2. beat well , add sifted flour and baking powder
3. roll into small balls , flatten with fork on a cold greased tray
4. bake 180c degrees for 15-20 minutes
5. you may add sultanas , cherries or nuts if wished
6. ice if desired
demonstrations.review: I was looking for a fast and easy cookie recipe to make that I had all the ingredients already in the pantry.  This was perfect.  I used vanilla pudding and sprinkled the cookies with colored sprinkles.  My kids gobbled them right up!

target.recipe_text:
blackberry pork chops

pork and fruit is a great combination-here's a fast cooking grilled dinner that will make your mouth water!

1. sprinkle both sides of pork with steak seasoning
2. please
3. just sprinkle the pork with seasoning
4. don't rub it in , don't coat it
5. just sprinkle !
6. cook on grill for 8-10 minutes or until done
7. in saucepan , combine remaining ingredients and bring just to a boil , stirring occasionally
8. pour sauce over pork to serve , garnishing with fresh blackberries if desired
target.review: A hit!  So good!  I love the savory-sweet combination of flavors.  I'll definitely make this again!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crab linguine

my husband loves this dish and can prepare this one himself! got it out of an ad for louis kemp seafood products. we have used imitation lobster and crab. i bet it would be awesome with shrimp.

1. cook pasta according to package direction
2. on low to medium heat , saute garlic and oregano in butter for 1 minute , stir frequently
3. add tomatoes and stir 3 minutes
4. add remaining ingredients , until cheese is melted
5. serve sauce over hot cooked pasta
demonstrations.review: Yum!  Easy to prepare, and the whole family loved it, even though we don't generally like the imitation crab.  I used cherry tomatoes, quartered, as I had them on hand, and fresh chives from my garden instead of green onions.  Will definitely make this again!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
comfort soup  spinach   meatballs

this simple soup is a savory dish passed on to me by a childhood friend's mother. she raised 6 kids and knew how to please a hungry crowd (the boys are all over 6'5") on a tight budget in a hurry! soup is comforting but i have found this one to be especially soothing to body and soul. update: the meat juices are what make the flavor of the broth, so if the beef is too lean (or not enough is used), there won't be an oily sheen to the soup, which is what gives it the wonderful taste.

1. heat chicken broth to boiling
2. meanwhile , combine beef , cheese and pepper
3. knead lightly to mix but don't overdo it
4. roll into 1 inch meatballs
5. drop meatballs into boiling broth and reduce heat to simmering
6. cook for 10 minutes
7. add spinach and cook for 10 more minutes
8. serve with french bread if you have it
demonstrations.review: YUM!  This is definitely a keeper.  So easy!!  I accidentally broke my pepper grinder into the meat & the whole peppercorns really added a punch.  I add them whole on purpose now.  I always double the recipe for my family of 5 - we eat it all up!  Sometimes there\'s a little left over for my husband to take to work for lunch.  I have used broccoli instead of spinach on occasion with good results.  And I grate my own Parmesan or Romano cheese.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
brady bunch pork chops
