i think this recipe is an absolute gem. really, in all my years of cooking, i don't think i have ever made chops as delectable as these! crispy-crunchy on the outside, meltingly tender and moist on the inside. the key, i think, is the salty milk marinade/brine, and making sure not to overcook them. thanks to gourmet magazine for this one.

1. in a large shallow dish , like a 9x13 pan , stir together milk and first amount of salt
2. add pork chops and marinate , covered and in fridge , for at least one hour
3. turn chops once , halfway through marinating / brining time
4. when ready to cook chops , preheat oven to 200f and have ready an ovenproof platter
5. in a shallow dish , combine freshly made bread crumbs with garlic powder , rosemary , thyme and remaining amount of salt
6. remove chops from milk and let excess milk drip off , then dredge chops in bread crumbs , lightly patting crumbs onto both sides of chops so they adhere
7. place breaded pork chops on a tray , keeping chops in one layer
8. in a large 12-inch skillet over high heat , place butter and oil
9. saute chops , 2 1 / 2 to 3 minutes per side only
10. do not overcook , do not crowd chops in skillet , and turn only once
11. chops should be golden brown and just cooked through
12. place cooked chops on platter and keep warm in preheated oven
13. cook remaining chops
14. add more oil and butter to pan if necessary
15. i recommend serving with applesauce
demonstrations.review: oh! Goodbye dry pork chops!  Everyone loved this!   yummy yummy yummy!  I don't make pork chops any other way now.

target.recipe_text:
chicken fried   fish fingers

i know fish is good for you, but i’m one of those people that don't care for the "fishy taste" that some fish seem to have. my so convinced me to try different types of mild fish, so i decided to try orange roughy, and used my fried chicken recipe. this recipe is the great result. actual prep time is 2 hours 10 minutes, (2 hours chill, 10 minutes actual prep).  if you try this, be careful turning, as some of the coating might flake off, but it still just as good.  submitted on april 25th,2006

1. put fish into a medium sized bowl
2. cover with buttermilk
3. chill for at least 2 hours
4. mix together flour , seasoning salt , and pepper in a large bowl
5. coat each piece of fish in flour mixture
6. set aside
7. in remaining buttermilk , add egg , mixing well
8. coat floured fish in buttermilk / egg mix
9. repeat step 4
10. heat oil till hot but not smoking in a large skillet
11. add fish six pieces at a time
12. do not crowd fish
13. cook until fish is golden brown and flakes easily
target.review: I have to agree with OzMan that this is outstanding! The buttermilk makes the fish moist and flaky, and the breading seasonings are on-point. I prepared half of this recipe with lemon juice in the marinade and half without -- and I actually preferred the recipe without, as written. The buttermilk gives the fish all the tang and flavor it needs. Nice job, Chef shapeweaver!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
sinful red velvet cookies

this is based on a paula deen recipe, so it's quite rich ;) this is by far the most luxurious cookie i make. they never last long. they're painfully easy to make, which may be bad news for your waistline.

1. in a large bowl with an electric mixer , cream the cream cheese and butter until smooth
2. beat in the egg
3. beat in the vanilla extract
4. beat in the cake mix
5. cover and refrigerate for at least 2 hours to firm up so that you can roll the batter into balls
6. i've chilled batter overnight and it comes out fine
7. after batter has chilled and you're ready to make the cookies , preheat the oven to 350f
8. roll the chilled batter into tablespoon sized balls and then roll them in confectioner's sugar
9. place on an ungreased cookie sheet , 2 inches apart
10. bake 12 minutes
11. the cookies should remain soft and gooey
12. cool completely and sprinkle with more confectioners' sugar , if desired
13. to make these devilishly rich , i also top the cookies with cream cheese frosting , which is simple to make
14. i use bev's cream cheese frosting , but double the vanilla
15. or , if i'm making them for people i know have more of a savory tooth than sweet , i'll triple it to a full tablespoon
demonstrations.review: These cookies ROCK! I made these on Valentine's Day for my family... There's not a single one left!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pan seared cajun tilapia

based on recipe from grouprecipes.com.  hubby loves it!  great with steamed broccoli and red potatoes.  quick and easy!  pretty spicy though.

1. thaw and dry filets
2. mix all but the oils in a small bowl
3. dry rub spice mix onto both sides of each filet
4. heat 1 / 2 of both oils in a large skillet over med-hi heat
5. in batches , cook about 2-3 minutes on each side depending on the thickness
6. repeat for the rest of the fish adding oil as needed
7. serve with lemon wedges
demonstrations.review: This is an unbeatable recipe. I didn't change a thing and the flavors were umami-perfect! I served this alongside Foodie Friend's "Smashed Cauliflower-Potatoes" for ALL YOU CAN COOK BUFFET 2011. I will definitely be making this again. Thanks, BetterLate!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
green enchiladas

from "recipe hall of fame" cookbook.  this is the best !  creamy & cheesy.  may be prepared the day before or may be frozen. if preparing ahead, add sauce just before baking.

1. brown meat , the small onion , and garlic until thouroughly cooked
2. add chili powder , salt , and pepper and set aside
3. soften tortillas by frying in 1 / 2 inch of oil for only a few seconds each
4. do not let them become crisp
5. stack tortillas as you cook
6. to prepare: place a spoonful of meat mixture on a tortilla
7. add a tablespoon each of chopped onion and cheese
8. roll up and place seam-side down in a 9 x 13 inch baking dish
9. prepare remaining tortillas in the same manner
10. sprinkle any remaining meat and cheese on top
11. in a saucepan melt butter on medium heat and add flour and salt
12. stir until bubbly and add milk
13. stir until smooth and slightly thickened
14. add green chilis and remove from heat
15. pour over enchilads and sprinkle more cheese on top , if desired
16. bake at 350 for twenty minutes , or until hot
demonstrations.review: I'm giving this 5 stars because the sauce is OFF THE HOOK! I've never had enchiladas with such a creamy-rich, wonderful sauce. However, I felt the chili-powder seasoned ground beef seemed a little dry and out of place with the green chiles in the sauce, or that it needed a "binder' somehow, since the ground beef crumbles out of these while eating (perhaps I should have added more cheese?). Regardless -- the overall flavor is excellent. I feel that chunked or shredded meat -- especially chicken or pork -- would be even better (maybe throw in some cumin, mix a little sauce with the meat, add sliced green onions and diced green chiles to the filling?). I will definitely make these again, with these minor revisions. I teetered between 4 and 5 stars, then settled on five, because of this AWESOME, unforgettable sauce! (PLEASE NOTE: I used a 7 ounce can of diced green chiles in the sauce rather than 4 ounces, since it was all I had. I added all 7 ounces). Thank you for sharing! Made for PAC Spring 2010.

target.recipe_text:
the best  banana bread  or muffins

okay, another banana bread recipe...but maybe the other ones don't have at least one ingredient that this one does...my family loves the muffins from this recipe...especially when i make mini-muffins! (i usually halve the recipe!) makes 4 loaves or 60 muffins

1. cream together butter and sugar
2. blend in eggs
3. add bananas , water , soda , salt , and baking powder
4. blend well
5. stir in flour
6. add nuts and / or chips , if desired
7. pour into 4 greased / floured loaf pans or lined muffin tins
8. bake at 350: loaves need 35-40 minutes , or until toothpick inserted in center comes out clean
9. muffins need only 18-20 minutes
10. with this recipe , i usually always make muffins to cut down bake time
target.review: I made half the recipe and got 2 very nice, moist loafs.  Good tasting.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
fairest wheels  chicken pinwheels

i had these at a girlfriends bridal shower and i just had to get the recipe from her sister, these are the tastiest little things.  i could have eaten half the tray myself! great little party snack or appetizer!

1. in medium bowl , combine chicken , lettuce , cheddar cheese , green onions and red pepper
2. set aside
3. in small bowl , beat together cream cheese , sour cream , and red pepper jelly on low speed of electric mixer
4. spread 1 / 3 cream cheese mixture over one side of tortilla
5. sprinkle with 1 / 3 chicken mixture , leaving 1 / 2 inch border at top just covered with cream cheese mixture roll up tightly , jelly roll style
6. wrap tortilla roll in plastic wrap
7. repeat with remaining tortillas and filling
8. refrigerate for 2 hours
9. trim off the ends and cut each roll into 8 slices , serve cold
demonstrations.review: Very tasty and easy to make.  My family enjoyed this recipe and I will make it again.  Like another interviewer, I will add more of the hot pepper jelly - can't get enough of that stuff!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
tomato  cucumber    avocado sandwich

this delicious sandwich is a re-creation of one i ate in a lovely lunch cafe in natchitoches, louisiana. this was served with slices of fresh melon,kiwi,strawberries,and orange on the side drizzled with some honey mustard dressing.

1. lightly toast bread or roll
2. toss avocado slices with a tiny bit of lemon juice to keep from getting brown
3. spread some of the honey mustard on the bread
4. place lettuce on bread , followed by tomato slices , cucumbers , red onion , and avocado slices
5. drizzle remaining honey mustard over the vegetables
6. top with sprouts and close up sandwich , securing with a toothpick
7. to make honey mustard salad dressing , simply add a little mayonnaise to the same mixture and thin with a tiny bit of milk if needed , to suit your taste
8. of course , both honey mustard and honey mustard salad dressings are now sold in stores if you prefer to use ready made
demonstrations.review: Excellent sandwich.  I used seeded, whole-wheat rolls and the whole family ate them up.  Good to take on a picnic too (keep ingredients in separate containers and make up sandwiches on the spot - they don't get soggy).

demonstrations.recipe_text:
one pan chicken and rice

yummy and sophisticated tasting dish that is cooked in and served in only one pan.

1. sprinkle chicken with steak seasoning
2. melt butter in a large thick skillet
3. add chicken and brown for 5 minutes
4. turn
5. add onion , garlic , mushrooms and bay leaf
6. stir vegetables and cook for 5-10 minutes
7. add wine
8. allow to boil and reduce until it is almost all evaporated
9. add rice , tomatoes and water
10. make sure all the rice is in the liquid
11. cover and cook for 20 minutes
demonstrations.review: We really enjoyed this very easy and tasty dinner.  I did not change a thing.  I will make this again.

target.recipe_text:
paul prudhomme s hoppin  john

based on the recipe in seasoned america.  note that even though this recipe uses dried peas, they are not presoaked or precooked.

1. combine seasoning mix ingredients in a small bowl and set aside
2. place bacon in a large ovenproof pot and cook over high heat until bacon begins to brown , about 6 minutes
3. stir in 2 cups onions , 1 cup peppers , 1 cup celery , 2 tablespoons plus 1 teaspoon seasoning mix , bay leaves , and half the peas
4. cover and cook , stirring occasionally , for 10 minutes
5. stir in the garlic and 2 cups stock
6. scrape bottom of pot
7. bring to a boil and cook , stirring occasionally , about 20 minutes
8. add 1 cup stock and scrape bottom of pot
9. add sausage , 6 cups stock , remaining onions , remaining peppers , remaining celery , remaining peas , and remaining seasoning mix
10. cover and bring to a boil over high heat
11. reduce heat to low , cover , and simmer until peas are tender , about 1 1 / 4 hours
12. preheat oven to 350
13. stir in rice and remaining stock
14. bring to a boil over high heat
15. cover pot and bake in oven 15 minutes
target.review:
This is a keeper! Great flavor, I will do this one again.

I added 1 LB of precooked salad shrimp about 5 minutes before it was done.

I prefer the salad shrimp because they are small; I don't like large chunks of shrimp because it makes the dish seem to be unprepared.

You want to add the shrimp a few minutes before the meal is done so the shrimp have time to warm-up to the correct temperature. You do not want to add the shrimp much earlier than five minutes before the meal comes out of the oven so as to avoid overcooking the shrimp.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chorizo  shrimp and rice

i've made this a couple of times, to rave reviews from my family. it's really easy to make, it's tasty and hearty, and makes the shrimp go a long way.

1. heat the oil in a large lidded frying pan over medium-high heat , add the onion and bell peppers and cook for 2 minutes
2. add the garlic , and continue to cook for a further 3 minutes , stirring occasionally
3. add the tomato , rice , salt and pepper to taste and cook for 2 minutes
4. stir in the chorizo , then the stock and bring to the boil
5. reduce the heat to low , cover and simmer for 15 minutes until the rice is tender , but the dish is still moist
6. add the shrimp , stir through and cover
7. cook for about 5 minutes or until the shrimp turn pink and the liquid has been absorbed
8. if it looks too moist , simmer an additional 2 minutes uncovered
9. taste , adjust the seasoning if necessary , sprinkle with the parsley and serve
demonstrations.review:
Wow!  This was great!

I used andouille instead of chorizo. (Yum!)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
potato salad with chipotle peppers a man s salad

warning warning !! this tex mex salad is very spicy !!!  use your best judgment in how much chipotle peppers you use. taste as you add just don't dump them all in. each pepper has it's own heat level. yes us girls love it too! ;)

1. mix first 7 ingredients together
2. toss in remaining ingredients except 1 tablespoon bacon and salt and pepper
3. mix well
4. taste to see if you need to add salt and pepper
5. i myself like lots of pepper
6. top with bacon bits
7. chill& serve
demonstrations.review:
This was excellent.  I used  about five chilies, seeds and all, because I LIKE heat.  I also added all of the adobo sauce from the can. 

I will definitally bring this to the next cookout, but without the extra chilies.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
roasted asparagus with feta

very simple to make and so flavorful- this is a real treat!

1. preheat oven to 400f
2. heat olive oil , minced garlic , lemon zest , oregano , and red pepper flakes in a small pan over low heat until garlic becomes golden and oil becomes fragrant
3. remove from heat and allow to cool
4. bend asparagus gently until it breaks at a natural point and discard ends
5. toss asparagus pieces with infused olive oil and place in a single layer on a baking sheet
6. season asparagus with salt and pepper
7. sprinkle asparagus with crumbled feta cheese
8. roast at 400f for 12 minutes or until cooked to your liking
9. sprinkle with chopped parsley and squeeze the lemons over the asparagus , being careful to catch the seeds
10. serve hot
demonstrations.review:
Even my girl friend—who is the most persnickety eater I know—liked it!  

Tip: I spread the sautéed garlic used to make the infused olive oil onto the asparagus before I sprinkled the feta over everything.  Yum!

target.recipe_text:
apple oatmeal bread

i found (and lost) a great recipe from sunset or family circle magazine about 25 years ago.  this is my version from my spotty memory!  batter will be thick!  works best with grated apple.

1. preheat oven to 350
2. grease and flour a 9 x 5 inch loaf pan
3. mix all dry ingredients together
4. lightly beat eggs in small bowl
5. add oil and eggs to dry ingredients and stir until moistened
6. fold in apples and nuts and pour into loaf pan
7. bake 1 hour or until toothpick comes out clean
8. cool in pan on wire rack for 10 minutes
9. remove from pan
10. cool on rack
target.review: I specifically wanted a bread that contained apples and oatmeal, and I was very happy how this turned out.  It is a bit of effort to grate the apples, but it's worth it.  The dough is very thick before you add the apples, but the moisture from the grated apples turns it into the perfect consistency.  I think I have a smaller loaf pan because I got one loaf and four muffins out of the recipe.  It works well as muffins as well.  I also substituted craisins for raisins, and it was a very nice addition.  I think the next time I make it, I will reduce the sugar to 3/4 of a cup.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
moroccan chickpea and vegetable stew with couscous

this is delicious stew. very flavorful from the spices, but not too spicy, just right. there is no meat in it, and you most likely won't miss it, as the chickpeas are very "meaty" themselves. but i don't see why you couldn't add some meat if you really wanted to. it also goes from prep to table in about 30 minutes, great for weeknight dinners. from cooking light.

1. heat the oil in a large skillet on medium high heat
2. add the zucchini , onion , carrot and garlic
3. saute 5 minutes
4. stir in the broth , and the next 9 ingredients , and bring to a boil
5. cover , reduce the heat , and simmer for 8 minutes or until tender
6. stir occasionally
7. while the stew simmers , bring the 1 1 / 2 cups water to a boil , stir in couscous , and remove from heat
8. cover and let stand for 5 minutes
9. serve stew over couscous
demonstrations.review: I really wanted to like this, but it ended up being un-exciting.  I left out the raisins due to personal preference, and I used an entire can of chicken broth, and I upped the spices slightly to compensate, but it maybe wasn't enough.  The end product had a lovely texture and fragrance, but served over couscous, it just didn't have the spicy flavor I'd expected.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
banana banana bread

why compromise the banana flavor? my banana bread is moist and delicious with loads of banana flavor! ultimate comfort food, and it's wonderful toasted!! (make sure to use bananas with a lot of black on them for the best flavor! the blacker the bananas, the stronger the banana flavor of the bread.)

1. preheat oven to 350
2. lightly grease 9 x 5 loaf pan
3. in large bowl , combine flour , soda and salt
4. in separate bowl , cream together butter and brown sugar
5. stir in eggs and mashed bananas until well blended
6. stir banana mixture into flour mixture
7. stir just to moisten
8. pour batter into prepared loaf pan
9. bake in preheated oven for 60-65 minutes until a toothpick inserted into center of loaf comes out clean
10. let bread cool in pan for 10 minutes , then turn out onto a wire rack
demonstrations.review: I get funny looks when I tell people that it's "Banana Banana Bread," but that's exactly what it is!  I used six medium bananas total when I made the bread, half of them from the freezer.  The bread is very, very moist, and the banana-flavor is marvelously pronounced.  It's not a great slicing bread, but I think it'd work well as muffins.  I hope to make again when I collect enough overripe bananas.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
no cheese whiz broccoli rice casserole

my sister-in-law served this at a family function and it's been a hit ever since. no cheese whiz, just real cheddar cheese. delicious, and kid-friendly. my now-grown son would request this when he came home from college. this recipe is very adaptable as well - add crushed ritz crackers or panko crumbs on top during the last 5 minutes of cooking for a crunchy topping. add bacon bits to the mixture for some extra flavor, or add a couple teaspoons of hot sauce for some heat. i also have used brown rice successfully with this recipe, and frozen broccoli cuts instead of chopped.

1. cook onion in butter in large skillet until soft
2. add remaining ingredients and cook just until cheese is melted
3. put in 2 quart casserole dish
4. bake at 350 for 1 hour
5. to make ahead and freeze: mix all ingredients together and spoon into two or even three smaller casserole dishes , cover , label and freeze
6. if you thaw overnight , just cook the one hour
7. if cooking from frozen state , add ten minutes or so , check for doneness
8. many thanks to tornado ali , for her wonderful
demonstrations.review: I used brown rice, probably added nearly a cup extra, and one can of cream of chicken and one can of cream of celery just because that's what I had sitting in the cabinet.  I Froze one half in an 8x8 pan, and I cooked the other. It was a big hit for dinner, and I expect the frozen casserole will also be tasty.  This is an easy recipe to sneak brown rice into because you can't really tell under all the creamy cheesyness.

target.recipe_text:
maryland crab sweet corn chowder

this is a recipe from a bed and breakfast here in maryland. once we tried it, it became a family favorite and a traditional thanksgiving dish.

1. in a 2 qt saucepan , cook half of the whole kernel corn , the onion and garlic in hot cooking oil till onion is tender , not brown
2. carefully add chicken broth
3. bring to boiling
4. reduce heat
5. simmer , uncovered for 10 minutes
6. stir in whipping cream , salt , and white pepper
7. simmer , uncovered , for 10 min
8. or until slightly thickened
9. watch carefully because it may foam and rise in pan
10. remove from heat
11. cool slightly
12. pour the cooled mixture into a blender container
13. cover and blend until smooth
14. return to same sauce pan
15. keep warm
16. meanwhile , in a small covered saucepan cook remaining corn and potato in boiling , salted water for two minutes
17. add chopped sweet pepper
18. cover and cook about 1 minute or til tender
19. drain
20. stir the drained vegetables into the soup
21. add the fresh or frozen crab meat
22. heat through
23. if desired , garnish with parsley and red pepper strips
target.review: This was so good!!  Everyone loved it.  I used canned corn instead of frozen, but it still turned out wonderful.  This will be something I will make at Thanksgiving from now on.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
ramsay s sticky chicken drumsticks

watched gordon ramsay make these on rachael ray and they looked so good i had to try them - and they rocked!  it's from his healthy appetite cookbook and they're a regular in my rotation - as soon as drumsticks are on sale, we have them for dinner!  great leftover - if there is any.

1. heat the oven to 400f lightly oil a large baking dish
2. season the drumsticks with salt and pepper and arrange in the dish in a single layer
3. drizzle over a little olive oil and bake in the hot oven for 20 minutes
4. prepare the glaze in the meantime
5. mix all the ingredients together in a small bowl until evenly combined
6. take the chicken out of the oven and pour over the glaze , to coat each drumstick
7. return to the oven and bake for another 20 to 30 minutes , turning several times , until the chicken is tender and nicely glazed
8. let the chicken rest for a few minutes before serving
demonstrations.review: This was very good!  I did not use the fish sauce, I subbed in fresh garlic and it was fantastic.  Easy recipe to follow and tasted great!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crock pot garlic rosemary chicken breast

this is a nice simple way to prepare chicken in the crock pot, but it tastes like you put a lot of work into it!

1. place butter and garlic in microwave-safe bowl and heat until butter is soft
2. blend together
3. roll chicken breasts in garlic-butter mixture and place in crock pot
4. sprinkle chicken breasts with salt , pepper , parsley and rosemary
5. add broth to bowl with remaining garlic-butter , reheat if necessary to allow smooth blending , and add mixture to crock pot
6. cook on low setting for 6 - 8 hours
7. serving size is approximately half a chicken breast and a small amount of sauce
demonstrations.review: Excellent!  Very tasty and great for people doing low carb diets.  The leftover juice after cooking can be made into a very nice gravy.  Thanks for sharing.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
banana banana bread

why compromise the banana flavor? my banana bread is moist and delicious with loads of banana flavor! ultimate comfort food, and it's wonderful toasted!! (make sure to use bananas with a lot of black on them for the best flavor! the blacker the bananas, the stronger the banana flavor of the bread.)

1. preheat oven to 350
2. lightly grease 9 x 5 loaf pan
3. in large bowl , combine flour , soda and salt
4. in separate bowl , cream together butter and brown sugar
5. stir in eggs and mashed bananas until well blended
6. stir banana mixture into flour mixture
7. stir just to moisten
8. pour batter into prepared loaf pan
9. bake in preheated oven for 60-65 minutes until a toothpick inserted into center of loaf comes out clean
10. let bread cool in pan for 10 minutes , then turn out onto a wire rack
demonstrations.review: This was the easiest banana bread recipe that I've ever tried!  It turned out delicious!  Thank you for sharing!

target.recipe_text:
amish apple crisp

another wonderful amish inspired dish. we serve this for dessert, or for breakfast. very tasty!

1. place apple mixture in a deep dish pie pan
2. sprinkle with sugar and cinnamon
3. mix topping ingredients , except the cinnamon and butter , with a fork until blended
4. sprinkle topping over apples
5. drizzle melted butter over topping
6. sprinkle with cinnamon
7. bake at 375f degrees for 40 minutes
target.review: Yum!  This recipe is great!  I switched it up a little.  I used whole wheat flour.  I also doubled the topping (I love the top), and added an extra egg.  It turned out SO good!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
awesome and simple italian garlicky meatloaf

this meat loaf is so flavorful, but doesn't require endless ingredients! it is simple and soooo good. i almost always have the ingredients on hand straight from the pantry.    my family loves it, it tastes even better leftover, and it makes the house smell delicious! can be frozen for oamc. i have adjusted the breadcrumbs per the reviews, the key is to use only as much as you need to make a moist dough.  if your ground beef is very low in fat, like sirloin, you will need fewer breadcrumbs, however higher fat beef, like chuck, will absorb a larger amount of breadcrumbs.

1. preheat oven to 350f and grease a large loaf pan
2. mix 1 / 2 cup bread crumbs , cheese , parsley , garlic , salt and pepper , reserving the remaining bread crumbs to use as necessary
3. add the meat and use a fork to mix the ingredients uniformly
4. add the eggs and knead it with your hands until a "dough" ball forms , it should hold its shape and not be too dry and crumbly or too sticky sloppy
5. mold the meat mixture into the loaf pan and top with a layer of ketchup as desired
6. bake for 70 minutes
7. slices best when cooled and tastes even better reheated as leftovers !
8. for oamc: slice cooled loaf and flash freeze slices on a cookie sheet
9. once frozen , store in a freezer bag or container
10. to reheat: remove as many slices as necessary and reheat in microwave
demonstrations.review: Loved it!  I did change it a little.  Instead of 2 lbs of hamburger, I used 1 lb hamburger, 1 lb sausage, and 1/2 lb ground turkey.  I also added seasoned salt.  It turned out wonderful!  I have made many meatloafs, and never used parmesan.  That must have been what made it SO good!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s ranch potato salad or macaroni salad

i have made this many times over the years for large gatherings, everyone loves it and i am always asked for the recipe --- the dressing is wonderful with potatoes or cooked pasta,  you may of coarse double the amounts to feed more people --- all ingredients may be adjusted to suit taste, throw in some cooked ham or bacon if desired, plan ahead this salad must chill for at least 3 or more hours before serving, the longer chilling time the better! --- if making the potato salad and prefer a creamier salad then double the dressing amount

1. in a large bowl , combine the cooked cubed potatoes or cooked pasta with peas
2. celery , green onions , cheddar cheese and chopped eggs
3. toss to combine
4. in a small bowl , combine relish , mayo , ranch salad dressing and mustard and garlic powder mix well then add to macaroni mixture
5. toss to coat then season with salt and pepper
6. add in chopped yum yum pickles if using
7. mix to combine
8. season with more salt and black pepper to taste
9. cover and refrigerate for 3 or more hours to blend flavors
10. delicious !
demonstrations.review: Absolutely the best macaroni salad I have ever had!  I didnt have sweet relish so I used chopped up dill pickles... and it turned out great!  I also added green peppers and green onions just because I love the extra veggies! :)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
my no roll pie crust

the only pie crust i will use anymore. its flaky and slightly sugary and oh so easy to do. note: due to some major discrepencies please use a good quality oil, preferably a vegetable and a good name brand like mazola, it may not seem like it will make a difference but in the end it will, also use new oil not something that has been sitting around for a while.

1. mix dry ingredients together with a fork in a pie pan
2. make a well in the center and add the oil and milk
3. mix with a fork til it makes a ball
4. flatten and press into the pan in pie crust shape and flute the edge
5. bake at 375 for 10-12 minutes until golden
6. one crust pie , excellent for cream pies and crumb topped baked pies
demonstrations.review: Ok, a little dry for me.  Maybe I will add less flour next time.  But SUPER easy to make!

target.recipe_text:
spinach pinwheel appetizers

these are pretty to look at, but even better to eat! enjoy!! i can't remember how many pinwheels you get, but i know it makes a lot.

1. in medium mixing bowl , combine cream cheese , sour cream and mayonnaise
2. beat in dip mix
3. add green onion , bacon bits and spinach
4. mix thoroughly
5. spread mixture onto tortillas , leaving a 1 / 2" space around edge
6. roll up each tortilla tightly , and wrap each in plastic wrap
7. chill for several hours or overnight
8. to serve , cut off ends and cut into 1 / 2" slices
target.review:
These were absolutely delicious !!! I will certainly make these again... everybody loved them.

For me half the recipe was enough. To halve I used 1 TBSP of Ranch Salad dressing(I did not have Ranch dip mix), and half a pack of spinach. And I used real bacon.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
purple cow popsicles

fun name for a yummy hot weather treat. made with milk and purple grape juice these are easy to make and great for the kids to eat. (cook time is freezer time.)

1. whisk all ingredients
2. pour into 8 tupperware popsicle makers
3. place lids on tightly
4. freeze for at least three hours
demonstrations.review: Loved these.  I didn't have grape juice on hand so I substituted some tropical juice (sort of orangy, mango flavored).  Delicious !  I do plan on making this with grape juice too.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
fudge popsicles  fudgesicles

recipe from a friend.  without instant pudding mix.  kid approved!  prep time does not include freezing time.

1. in a small saucepan , combine sugar , cornstarch , cocoa , and milk
2. cook on medium until thick
3. remove from heat and add vanilla and butter and stir until combined
4. place in molds and freeze until firm
demonstrations.review: Delicious and so easy.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
dana s sloppy joes

my daughter hates sloppy joes, i got her to try these and now this is the only kind she will eat.

1. in a large skillet , brown beef with onions
2. mix the rest of the ingredients together
3. add to beef and onions
4. cook for 1 hour over medium heat , stirring occasionally
5. serve on warm hamburger buns
demonstrations.review:
Dana, these were wonderful.  I had already chosen this as a recipe I wanted to try the next time our niece and nephew were here and they just happened to come during the Danathon !  Dana they loved it and they really are picky eaters.  
I also explained to them that this was a special meal for you.  This is bound to become one of our traditional meals when they visit.

target.recipe_text:
cheese tortellini pesto pasta salad

this is most definately my favorite pasta salad in the world! i have been making it for years, but never wrote it down....well...thanks to recipezaar i'm learning to "measure", lol!!!! very happy to share! this recipe is for a small crowd. if making just for your family, omit the rotini, and add only as much of the rest of the ingredients (about half) that you'd like. don't worry, it's really simple and easy!

1. cook pastas , set aside to drain and cool a bit
2. in large bowl or punch bowl , add rest of ingredients , folding gently til well mixed
3. gently fold in pastas well
4. adjust seasoning to taste , meaning , add more salt , parmesan , etc
5. , til you like it
6. serve immediately , or refrigerate
7. if you make this say a day ahead of time , you'll need to "refresh" this
8. just add a bit more olive oil , salt and parmesan before serving
9. this salad is best , though , room temp , or even slightly warm
target.review:
I made this on a visit to my MIL house.  OH MY GOODNESS was it great!  She demanded the recipe and has shared it with her entire church and three friends already.  We had LOADS of left overs and found that once it sat overnight the flavors really took off.   I only omitted the tomatoes as I don't care for them, other than that we followed the recipe exact and it was sensational.
Thanks for the perfect salad Wildflour.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
campbell s chicken   broccoli alfredo

nan

1. cook linguine according to package directions
2. add broccoli for the last 4 minutes of cooking time
3. drain
4. heat butter in skillet
5. add chicken and cook until browned , stirring often
6. add soup , milk , cheese , pepper , and linguine mixture and heat through
7. serve with additional parmesan cheese
demonstrations.review: Very Tasty!  DH and Kids all loved it.  I couldn't believe how easy and quick this was to prepare.  Next time I'm going to try adding mushrooms for more texture.  Thanks Recipenut for a great family meal.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
ramen beef casserole

posted in response to the january topic of the month.  this is simple and is very easy to adapt to personal tastes.  inexpensive for college kids or if finances are just running low.

1. pre-heat oven to 375
2. in a bowl , combine crusted noodles , 1 packet of seasoning , sour cream , soup water , milk , and onion
3. stir and pour into a 9x9 oven-safe casserole dish
4. brown meat and drain grease
5. add meat to ramen and stir to combine
6. cover and place in oven , do not put on cheese and french onions
7. after 20 minutes , take casserole out and mix , sprinkle french onion over top
8. place back in oven uncovered and cook for 10 minutes
9. take it out and sprinkle cheese on it
demonstrations.review: I've made this twice now and the kids and DH both LOVE it.  I put mozarella cheese on top as the ingredients don't list cheese but the instructions do.  My pregnant sister begged me for the recipe!!! It's a super easy, tasty, and inexpensive meal. Thanks

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pesto chicken or shrimp pizza

came up with this one for pizza night...a hit with everyone in my family. great with chicken or shrimp...whatever you have leftover. i think the balance of the savory pesto with the sweetness of tomato and caramelized onions turned out really nice. if you use a sweet onion such as vidalia, you can omit the sugar. i used recipe #144195 with great results. hope you enjoy!

1. preheat oven to 400
2. melt 1 tbs butter over med-high heat until it starts to foam
3. sautee mushrooms 5-7 minutes or until softened
4. remove and set aside
5. add reminaing 1 tbs of butter and onion to pan and stir
6. cover and let cook about 5 minutes until onions soften
7. remove lid and let cook 15-20 minutes or until nicely browned and caramelized , stirring midway
8. pour balsamic vinegar and sprinkle sugar over onions and stir to combine
9. meanwhile , spread roasted garlic over crust
10. spread pesto over crust
11. top with chicken or shrimp , onions , mushrooms , tomato and cheeses
12. bake 10-12 minutes or until crust is brown and cheese is melted and bubbly and slightly browned
demonstrations.review: WOW!!  DH and I had this last night and it was amazing!!  We were unable to find roasted garlic so we mixed regular garlic with a 1/4 cup more pesto and spread that on the crust as well.  We paired this with "WILDFLOURs" Cheese and Pesto stuffed mushrooms it was a delicious meal!! Thanks.  We are fighting over the leftovers today:)

target.recipe_text:
ant  kelly s london broil marinade

my niece shwana loves this!  she always writes my name "ant" kelly when we play rummy or scrabble - started when she was little and stuck.  
i always make this when we go tubing in wisconsin.  

prep time includes does not include time to marinate.

1. mix all marinade ingredients together
2. lightly score meat in a diamond pattern on each side
3. place meat in a resealable bag
4. pour in marinade
5. squish meat and marinade around to get all the nooks and crannies
6. marinate in refrigerator 2-3 hours or up to 24 hours , rotating occasionally
7. can be frozen in the marinade too
8. 20-30 minutes before cooking take meat out of the refrigerator to come up in temperature
9. cook in the broiler or on the grill on high heat for 5-7 minutes per side depending on thickness and desired doneness
10. i have been asked about roasting temperatures , i have never done this , always grill or broil
11. for camping - place the fresh london broil and marinade in a zipperbag , squeeze out as much air as possible , seal , place inside a vacuum pack bag
12. vacuum pack and freeze
13. put frozen in the camping cooler , after a day or two it is defrosted and can be cooked on the grill with minimal preparation and mess
target.review: This is my "go to" recipe for whenever I find London broil on sale.  The only thing I do differently is to use low-sodium soy sauce.  Perfect every time.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
low fat spinach and artichoke dip

i love spinach and artichoke dip, but hate the fat... i came up with this fast and easy recipe that tastes great, is easy to put together, low in fat but big on taste! flavored with roasted red peppers and parmesan cheese, no yicky mayo here! makes enough for a large crowd. can be made in the microwave for even faster preparation. also delicious served cold. note: recipe can be made with fat-free marinade artichokes, i usually buy two small jars, adds a little extra zing!  ww points = 1/serving

1. preheat oven to 375f and lightly spritz a shallow baking dish with cooking spray
2. using food processor , mix light cream cheese , sour cream and artichoke hearts by pulsing until even consistency
3. add roasted bell pepper and parmesan cheese and pulse until creamy
4. to bake dip: place mixture into prepared baking dish
5. add spinach and stir until combined
6. bake for 25 minutes , stirring half way through
7. dip is done when browned and bubbly around the edges
8. to keep warm , lower temperature in oven to 250f and stir every 10 minutes until dip is served
9. for microwave directions: place mixture into microwave safe dish , add spinach and stir until combined
10. cover with plastic wrap , leaving room for steam to escape
11. microwave on high for 7 minutes or until dip is hot and boiling on the sides - microwaves vary , check often
12. mix well before serving
demonstrations.review: What a treat to get a low fat version of an old favorite!  Thanks Brooke it was gone before I knew it!  The only problem I had was that the food processor took away the typical chunkiness of the traditional version of this dip.  I will definitely make again, but next time will experiment without the food processor.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
old fashioned devil s food cake  cake mix doctor

this cake is delicious but truly it is "the icing on the cake" that makes it.  use the "perfect chocolate frosting" and this cake will be perfect.  both the cake and icing recipes are from the cake mix doctor cookbook.

1. place rack in center of oven and preheat oven to 350f
2. grease two 9-inch round cake pans
3. place the cake mix , cocoa , buttermilk , oil , eggs , and vanilla in a large mixing bowl
4. blend with an electric mixer on low speed 1 minute
5. stop the machine and scrape down sides
6. increase the speed to medium and beat 2 minutes more , scraping sides if needed
7. the batter will look well combined
8. divide the batter evenly between cake pans , smoothing with rubber spatula
9. place pans side by side in oven
10. bake the cakes until they spring back when lightly pressed with your finger , 28 to 30 minutes
11. remove from the oven and cool on wire racks for 10 minutes
12. run a knife around the edges and invert onto rack , and again until right side up and cool another 30 minutes
demonstrations.review: Nice cake!  Very light and chocolaty, but unlike the other reviewer, did not seem extremely moist.  Made with the perfect chocolate frosting which gave it the moistness I desired.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
honey salmon

nan

1. combine the oil , honey , mustard , garlic , cayenne , coriander , lemon juice and salt in a shallow dish
2. mix well
3. add the salmon and let marinate for 30 minutes at room temp
4. place the salmon on a med
5. -hot fire , grill the salmon five to six minutes per side or until they flake easily
6. remove from grill and garnish with the dill sprigs
demonstrations.review: Very nice!  We all loved having a marinade that did NOT have soy sauce in it.  This was easy and delicious-what more can you ask for!  I baked the fish in the marinade at 400 for 17 minutes.

target.recipe_text:
linda s fantabulous baked potatoes

you have to try these potatoes to see how good they are. don't rub them with butter or oil or salt before cooking.  don't wrap them with foil and keep the temperature of the oven high.  yummmmmmy!

1. preheat oven to 500 degrees
2. yep , 500
3. scrub potatoes well , dry them , and prick with a fork all over
4. bake for one hour
5. yep , 1 hour
6. carefully cut potatoes open - they will be steamy and fluffy so be careful
7. add optional toppings and enjoy the best baked potato you ever had !
target.review: They are Recipe #197960 for sure! It is important to prick them as they close up the holes as they cook... if not enough holes they DO explode... ahhhh, but what a wonderful smell!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
sicilian tomato   onion salad

i found this recipe in an attempt for something different to use up an over abundance of summer tomatoes! the garlic salt brings out the juices in the tomatoes, it works as an acid, so there is no need for vinegar. my family just went nuts over this! great as a side dish or as a lite lunch!  
the ratio of vegetables can be adjusted to suit your own taste.

1. cut tomatoes into bite size pieces
2. sprinkle with garlic salt and pepper
3. peel a cut onion in half vertically
4. along edge of open side , sliver cut onion and add to tomatoes
5. add the rest of ingredients and toss lightly
6. marinate for at least an hour
7. serve with italian bread , provolone cheese and hard salami
demonstrations.review: Yes! I have too many tomatoes also. I have canned some, dried some, made salsa (canned some of that too), and no one wants any more tomatoes from me. This is a great recipe, it is tasty, easy, and it keeps the tomatoes fresh in the frig. If several days go by, I can always make some more salsa from this batch. I also cut back on the onions. Thanks for such a winner!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
japanese pickled ginger

great used to cleanse the palate while eating sushi.  i happen to love it to eat along with my sushi :)

1. wash fresh ginger root and rub off skin
2. slice the ginger thinly
3. sprinkle salt on ginger
4. leave salted ginger slices in a bowl for 1 hour
5. dry the ginger slices with paper towels , and put them in a sterilized container / jar
6. mix rice vinegar and sugar in a pan , and bring to a boil
7. pour the hot mixture of vinegar and sugar over the ginger slices
8. cool
9. the ginger will change color to light pink
10. cover the jar , and store it in the refrigerator
demonstrations.review: Thanks again for all!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
simple roasted butternut squash cinnamon soup

booyah!  this velvety soup is a sweet and savory bowl of comfort with a surprising cinnamon kick.

1. roast the butternut squash , flesh side down onto a lightly oiled roasting pan for 40 to 45 minutes in a 425 degree oven
2. in the mean time , sautee the onion , ginger , and garlic in butter until soft
3. add the broth , simmer for ten minutes
4. add pulp from the butternut squash
5. puree in a food processor or blender
6. return to pan
7. add cream , salt , pepper , and a pinch or 2 of cinnamon
8. simmer until heated through
demonstrations.review: My husband said, "This is really nice." The soup was easy to fix. We had roasted the squash (from our garden) the night before, and had eaten part of it, saving most of it for the soup. We had also had a chicken earlier in the week, and I had made chicken broth. I used the fat on top of the broth, and less butter to saute the onion, garlic, and ginger. The soup was very delicate, and we enjoyed it. Thank you for this recipe. Made for the Australian/New Zealand recipe swap #14.

target.recipe_text:
lemon raspberry muffins

lemon raspberry muffins recipe from festival foods, a grocery store in green bay. this was featured on the local morning news.

1. in a large bowl , combine flour , sugar , baking powder and salt
2. in a small bowl , mix eggs , buttermilk , oil and lemon juice and zest
3. stir into flour mixture just until moistened
4. fold in raspberries
5. fill greased or paper-lined muffin cups two-thirds full
6. bake at 350 degrees f for 15-20 minutes or until center of muffin springs back when lightly touched
7. for glaze:: mix powdered sugar and lemon juice
8. add milk until smooth
9. drizzle glaze on top of slightly cooled muffins
target.review: These were wonderful.  I used fresh picked raspberries that were very sweet so I also threw in a couple handfuls of blueberries for contrast.  My son ate one before I could glaze them and liked it.  Then after glazing, he LOVED it!  Will make again and again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
french canadian frosted maple gingerbread

molasses, ginger and maple syrup are inextricably linked with early canadian foods.

1. sift together the flour , soda , ginger and salt
2. beat the egg until it is foamy , then gradually beat in the maple syrup , sour cream , and butter or bacon fat
3. gradually add the dry ingredients , beating until well blended
4. pour into a greased and lightly floured 11 x 7 x 1 1 / 2 inch baking pan
5. bake at 350 f
6. for 30 to 40 minutes , or until cake pulls away from the sides of the pan
7. remove from the oven and let it cool
8. combine all the frosting ingredients in a bowl , beat with an electric mixer until smooth , creamy and of spreading consistency
9. place the icing in big swirls on the cake and sprinkle to taste with chopped walnuts
10. the canadian cook book
demonstrations.review: This is more cake-like than gingerbready to me.  It's the first time my son has eaten the cake instead of the frosting first. I used butter in the cake and sourcream-2 tbl-in the frosting.  And real maple syrup is a must for this. Left off the walnuts but still so tasty-thankns!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
moist pumpkin bread

very moist pumpkin bread with special topping.  this makes a very nice gift-giving bread.  you can make it all year long because it uses a can of 100% pure pumpkin puree.  i use libby's brand.  the spices are just right in this recipe and enhance the flavor of the pumpkin.  it's best served after it has mellowed for one day.  a family favorite.

1. in a medium size bowl beat eggs and mix with sugar , oil , water and pumpkin
2. in another bowl mix flour , baking soda , baking powder , salt , nutmeg , cinnamon and pumpkin pie spice
3. combine wet ingredients with dry ingredients only until just blended
4. do not overmix
5. pour into a greased and floured loaf pan
6. this bread fits perfectly in an 8
7. 5 x 4
8. 5 loaf pan
9. bake in a 325 degree oven for 50 to 60 minutes
10. for topping: in a small saucepan mix butter , brown sugar and milk
11. boil only 2 1 / 2 minutes while stirring constantly
12. immediately drizzle on top of loaf
13. sprinkle with chopped pecans and press pecans lightly into topping
14. wrap and store until next day for serving
15. this will keep moisture inside
16. it is ok if bread "sweats" while wrapped
demonstrations.review: After seeing the picture, I had to make this.  I followed the recipe exactly but doubled it to make 2 loaves for the kids' teachers.  My bread came out looking just like the one pictured, made the house smell great and I also topped it with orange sparkling sugar then wrapped each well and tied with Halloween ribbon.  Thanks-will certainly make again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
beef patties in onion gravy

good 

1. combine all patty ingredients
2. mix thouroughly with your hands and shape into 4 patties
3. spray a non-stick skillet , and brown patties on both sides
4. add dry onion soup mix and 1 1 / 2 cup water
5. cover pan tightly and simmer for 20 minutes
6. remove patties to a plate
7. in a gravy shaker or jar , combine 1 / 2 cup water with 2 tbs
8. flour
9. stir flour and water into onion gravy
10. stir constantly with a whisk until it comes to a boil
11. boil 1 minute
12. return patties to pan
13. serve with mashed potatoes or hot cooked noodles
demonstrations.review: I can't believe I haven't reviewed this.  I've made this monthly for the past year.  I use ground turkey and Lipton Golden Herb dried soup mix.  We like it over mashed potatoes with veggies on the side.  Quick, comforting and delicious, not to mention economical when you can get ground turkey on sale.

target.recipe_text:
kielbasa with tomatoes and white beans

a polish-italian quick fix main dish!

1. heat oil or butter in a large skillet , add kielbasa and cook over medium high heat until lightly browned , remove with slotted spoon
2. reduce heat to medium , add onions and cook until transparent
3. reduce heat to low , add garlic and herbs and cook 1 minute
4. add kielbasa , tomatoes and white beans , bring to a boil , reduce heat and simmer 10 minutes
target.review: A wonderful stew type dinner with tons of flavor and packed with nutrients.  I followed previous reviewers suggestions and added some chopped fresh spinach.  It would have been good with or without.  My hubby requested that I add an additional can of beans next time and I see his point.  Delicious, quick and easy.  Thank you!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pineapple upside down cake

this recipe is by far the best pineapple upside down cake that i've ever made.  it is also quick and easy.  the cake is very moist and rises much higher than the average recipe.  the combination of pineapple cake mix and pineapple juice isn't overwhelming either.  i've been meaning to edit this for ages, however it looks so much better if you use dark brown sugar.  also if you'd like more topping, use 3/4 cup butter with 1 1/2 cups dark brown sugar.

1. preheat oven to 325 degrees fahrenheit
2. melt butter in a 9x13 pan in oven
3. sprinkle brown sugar evenly over butter in pan
4. drain canned pineapple into a measuring cup
5. place pineapple slices evenly in pan , cutting the last two in half to cover pan
6. place the maraschino cherry halves in the center of the pineapple slices , cut side up
7. combine the rest of ingredients in a large mixing bowl on slow speed for 30 seconds
8. beat on medium speed for 2 minutes
9. pour batter into pan
10. bake for 45 to 55 minutes , or until a toothpick comes out clean
11. cool 5 minutes and turn cake out onto a serving platter , pineapple side up
demonstrations.review: Yep! It's that good. I went with the crushed pineapple, pecans and no "extra" topping. It isn't overly sweet and soooooo moist. I had DH flip the cake onto the serving tray and waited anxiously as he removed the pan. There wasn't even in topping stuck in the pan, it all stayed beautifully on the cake. Thank you. This is definitely a keeper.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pinto beans and rice in a crock pot  or on stove top

this is one of those good ol' down home meals. add a pan of cornbread and you've got it made! you can obviously make this spicier by adding more chili powder, cayenne, jalapenos or just pass the tabasco.  please note that the time shown is an estimate only as there will be a variance of heat from one crockpot to the next.

1. rinse beans in colander
2. put in a crock pot
3. cover with water , plus about 2 inches over top of beans
4. add all ingredients , except rice
5. cook on high in crock pot about 3 hours til tender
6. may also cook on low overnight
7. add rice and cook until rice is warm
8. serve with cornbread
demonstrations.review: I chose to do this on the stovetop.  It required a lot more water because of that.  I also added about 1 1/2 cups of salsa in place of the picante sauce.  I threw the uncooked rice in the last two hours of cooking.  Continued to add water as necessary and then served it with dirty shrimp in butter beer sauce and a simple salad with vinegarette.  It was a great meal.  The leftover beans and rice went to my Mom and Dad's.  They served it with grilled smoked sausage and raved as well!  Great, tasty dinner.  Thank you!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
banana walnut buttermilk bread

this is a recipe i got off the side of a sugar bag. i haven't made it but it sounds so good.

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees f
2. in a large bowl cream together the sugar and the butter
3. add eggs one at a time , beating after each addition
4. beat in mashed bananas and vanilla and continue beating until mixture is smooth
5. in a large measuring cup stir baking soda into the buttermilk and add it to the banana mixture along with the flour and chopped nuts
6. stir the batter until it is just combined
7. pour batter into a greased and floured 9x5 inch loaf pan and bake for one hour or until tooth pick inserted in the center comes out clean
8. transfer the bread to a rack and let it cool in the pan for 10 minutes
9. turn it out onto a rack and let it cool completely
demonstrations.review: I intentionally buy too many bananas in order to have enough to make this bread.  Co-workers and family all request it regularly.  I use previously frozen mushy bananas and it turns out a bread that tastes gourmet.  Love it.

target.recipe_text:
sage sausage  apple   walnut stuffing dressing

this was a big hit at thanksgiving last year.

1. preheat oven to 325 degrees f
2. put the stuffing cubes in a large bowl and set aside
3. butter a 3-quart casserole dish
4. melt 2 tablespoons of butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat
5. add the sausage and break up with a wooden spoon
6. cook until it loses most of its pink color , but not so much that it's dry , about 5 minutes
7. add the sausage and pan drippings to the stuffing cubes
8. melt the remaining butter in the pan
9. add the onion , apple , celery , and salt
10. cook until the vegetables get soft , about 5 minutes
11. add the broth and parsley and bring to a boil
12. pour the vegetable mixture over the stuffing cubes and toss until evenly moistened
13. mix in the walnuts and eggs
14. loosely pack the dressing in the prepared pan and cook uncovered until the top forms a crust , about 40 minutes
15. drizzle about 2 tablespoons of turkey pan drippings or melted butter over the top
16. cook until the top is crisp and golden , about 20 minutes more
17. set immediately or warm
target.review: I make a couple different stuffings each year for Thanksgiving.  I make one in the turkey, one in a pot with the giblets and sometimes another with no onions.  I made traditional for in the turkey this year, and made this recipe in a bean pot with the giblets.  I also added pumpkin to the recipe, since the my family are big pumpkin fans.  Let me tell you!  It was sooooo good!  It was everyones favorite!  I asked everyone which one they would like for Christmas...This one!  It was absolutely wonderful!  If my family likes it, that means it is a big hit.  I will be making it again, for sure!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pumpkin zucchini bread

pumpkin adds a twist of fall to the ever popular zucchini bread. haven't tried this one yet but it looked like a winner so i thought i'd share it.

1. before beginning , preheat your oven to 350 f and grease and flour two loaf pans
2. mix eggs and sugar together , then stir in the pumpkin and butter
3. stir dry ingredients together and add to egg mixture
4. mix well
5. stir in the zucchini and nuts
6. divide into pans and bake 45 to 50 minutes or until the loaves test done
7. cool in pans ten minutes before removing to wire racks to cool completely
demonstrations.review: I must say that this bread is awsome!!  My daughter and I were planning a baking day at her house, we planned on donuts and bread.  This recipe is easy, moist, and very tasty.  I did change one thing, I used oil instead of butter.  I knew it would change the taste slightly, but that didn't matter.  It was awesome!!!  It has become a family favorite already!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
guacamole with sour cream

my guacamole is very free-form, but here are the basics:  figure about 1/2 large avocado per person. i don't care whether i'm using haas or regular avocados - some people do. pick ones that give to mild pressure but are not mushy. if you can't find any that are ripe, get hard ones and keep them in a paper bag for a couple of days until they ripen.

1. cut the avocado in half , scoop out the flesh with a spoon
2. mash 3 / 4 of it well and chop the remaining 1 / 4 coarsely
3. mix it into the mashed portion
4. mix all remaining ingredients together
5. serve immediately , or cover with plastic wrap , pressing wrap firmly to surface of guacamole and refrigerate up to 4 hours before serving
demonstrations.review: This was an awesome recipe!! I love guacamole but this recipe was better than any I had had before.  Be sure, I will be making this one from now on!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
my best zucchini bread

this makes 2 loaves of the best zucchini bread i have ever tasted.

1. preheat oven to 350
2. in large bowl , mix sugar , oil , eggs , and vanilla
3. beat until well blended
4. add zucchini , applesauce and orange juice
5. stir well
6. combine flour with next 5 ingredients
7. add to zucchini mixture
8. stir well
9. add nuts
10. stir gently to combine
11. pour into 2 greased and floured 9in loaf pans
12. bake for 60-70 minutes
13. till toothpick comes out clean
14. let cool in pans 10 minutes
15. remove from pans and let cool completely
demonstrations.review: I made this today and it was awesome!!  I made a slight change to the recipe though. I didn't have any applesauce, so I added grated carrot and some apple juice.  I found I didn't have any nutmeg, so I added an equal amount of added cinnamon.  It turned out terrific!!  The bread is moist, tasty and bakes up well.  This will be a favorite of the family's.  It is one of mine already!!

target.recipe_text:
sesame pork and broccoli

quick and easy way to satisfy my chinese food cravings. also great w/some hoisin sauce and ginger.

1. combine chicken broth , cornstarch , and soy sauce , blend well
2. add chopped green onions , toss lightly and set aside
3. cut tenderloin into bite-size pieces
4. heat oil in skillet over medium-high heat
5. add pork and garlic , stir fry until meat is cooked
6. remove pork and set aside
7. add broccoli and broth , cover and simmer on low for approximately 10 minutes
8. add the pork and cook until hot , stirring frequently
9. sprinkle sesame seeds and serve with rice
target.review: This was a real winner in my house! Even my picky teenager liked it. The only change I made was adding a bag of frozen Chinese stir fry vegetables. I will defiantly be making this again! Thank you Jelisa for a wonderful recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chi chi s seafood enchilada   copycat

supposedly this is the same as chi chi's "cancun"

1. in mixing bowl , stir together soup , onion , nutmeg and black pepper
2. in another bowl , place half of the soup mixture , crab and 1 cup of the jack cheese
3. set aside
4. wrap the tortillas in paper towels , microwave on 100 percent power for 30 to 60 seconds
5. place 1 / 3 cup mixture on each tortilla and roll up
6. place seam side down in greased 12 x 7-1 / 2 dish
7. stir milk into the reserved soup mixture , pour over enchiladas
8. microwave , covered , on high for 12 to 14 minutes
9. sprinkle with remaining cheese
10. let stand for 10 minutes
11. add a dash of hot pepper sauce to soup mix if desired
demonstrations.review: We didn't care for this at all. I don't think there is anything wrong with the recipe, it's just a matter of taste.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
ham and smoked gouda salad

i love gouda cheese. you can substitute smoked cheddar if you want. this is a quick, easy salad that is satisfying.

1. cook pasta according to package directions
2. rinse in cold water
3. drain
4. in a small bowl , mix together the mayo , honey and mustard
5. in a serving bowl , add the pasta , ham , celery , and cheese
6. stir to combine
7. add the dressing mixture
8. toss to coat
9. season with salt and pepper if desired
10. serve now or chill and serve later
demonstrations.review: Just wonderful! This salad was so easy to throw together and tasted even better the next day. Thank you NurseDi for such a nice way to use up left over ham!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chipotle chicken salad tacos

nan

1. the filling: in a large bowl , whisk together the vinegar , olive oil and chipotles
2. season generously with salt , usually about a generous 1 / 4 teaspoon
3. add the cabbage , carrot , onion , cilantro and chicken
4. toss everything together and let stand for 15 minutes
5. taste and season with additional salt if necessary
6. finishing the dish: scoop the filling into a wide shallow serving bowl , dot with the cubed avocado and dust generously with the cheese
7. serve with warm tortillas
demonstrations.review: This has become a weekly meal in my house! My hubby and I find ourselves craving these tacos every Friday night! Very easy to make and totally satisfies my mexican food addiction. Defiantly one of the BEST recipes on Zarr. Thank you Kirstin a thousand times for posting this YUMMY dish!

target.recipe_text:
kittencal s famous caesar salad

i developed this dressing years ago, and i can honestly say that you won't be able to keep your spoon out of the fridge for a taste, it is *that* good! --- although i do think the dressing is better with the anchovy it can certainly be made without them. in a pinch i have even substituted buttermilk for the half and half cream, just use about the same amount --- this dressing gets stronger with refrigeration time so a small amount of fresh garlic goes a long way! ---- usually one recipe without doubling is perfect for one large romaine lettuce, if you are serving a large crowd of people you might want to double -- salad dressing will not work for this use *only* mayonnaise, i find hellman's brand mayonnaise works the best and for the  perfect companion to this salad see my recipe#125034-------------lower-fat option use reduced fat mayonnaise and fat-free half and half or low-fat milk --- also see my recipe#66596

1. in a small 2-cup mini food processor , process / mince the anchovy fillets and garlic together until finely minced
2. add in the remaining ingredients , and process for 30 seconds , or more until well mixed
3. adjust seasonings to taste
4. thin with buttermilk for a thinner consistency if desired
5. store in fridge , covered in a glass container for 3 or more hours before using
6. toss desired amount of dressing with romaine lettuce and croutons
7. sprinkle with more grated parmesan cheese if desired
target.review: Delicious! I have tried a number of store bought and home made versions of this, but this was definately the best so far! I have made this approx 10 times as I am a huge fan of caeser salad! I add a bit more garlic and let it sit in ther refrigerator for at least 24 hours before using it. FANTASTIC!!! I am so glad I tried it. I will definitely have it this way again! Thanks for a wonderfull recipe!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mashed red potatoes with garlic and parmesan

the potatoes are ready in our garden, and this is the first recipe i reach for! these are so good!!

1. put potatoes and garlic in lg pan
2. cover with water
3. bring to a boil
4. reduce heat and simmer for 25 minutes , until potatoes are tender
5. drain well
6. mash with the butter , milk , and salt
7. stir in the parmesan cheese
demonstrations.review: VERY NICE! As the biggest meat and potatoe guy I know I really thought this recipe was great! I also added a bit of evaparated milk for a little bit of tang. Great Recipe! Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
super sesame chicken wings

so easy to make and a sure bet for superbowl parties and potlucks...best of all, no frying!

1. in a large food storage bag , combine soy sauce , water , sugar , sesame oil , green onions , garlic , sesame seeds , and peppers
2. add chicken wings
3. turn bag to coat well
4. seal and refrigerate for at least 2 hours , or overnight , turning occasionally
5. i've often marinate them for 2 days for that extra flavor
6. remove chicken to a shallow rack in baking dish or roasting pan
7. discard the marinade
8. bake wings , uncovered , at 350 for 30 minutes
9. turn wings and bake 25 minutes longer , or until tender
10. at first i thought 55 minutes baking time would be too long , but they turn out tender and moist
11. these are not as high calorie as stated to the right because nearly all of the ingredients are discarded with the marinade
12. enjoy
demonstrations.review: Great Recipe! I made these for a family gathering and everyone loved them! Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
swiss cheese and onion ring chicken breasts

a quick and simple recipe that even the kids will love!

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. place chicken breasts in baking dish
3. cover chicken with mushroom soup
4. cover dish with foil and bake for 45 minutes
5. remove from oven
6. remove foil
7. place cheese slices over chicken pieces
8. top with durkee fried onions
9. leave uncovered and return to oven for an additional 15 minutes
demonstrations.review: As a lover of Chicken, this was definately a winner! I made it exactly as the recipe states with NO substitutions! Fabulous! Thanks Croft Girl!

target.recipe_text:
crabbies  paula deen

a tasty appetizer from paula deen of food network. these are a great make-ahead that freeze well.

1. preheat oven to 425f
2. in large bowl , combine all ingredients except bread and parsley
3. spread mixture over bread rounds
4. score each round into quarters and place on parchment-covered or greased baking sheet
5. bake until topping is heated through and golden brown , about 10-15 minutes
6. sprinkle with chopped fresh parsley and serve hot
target.review: Absolutely amazing treat! I have used english muffins for the bread. These are wonderful little snacks for any occasion Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
authentic watergate salad

i checked all the other recipes here, and each one is a little different in one way or another. this is the real deal. i got the recipe from the chef at the watergate hotel in washington, dc where the recipe originated. if you want the same one served there that was made famous there....this is it.

1. stir pudding mix , pineapple with juice , marshmallows and nuts in a large bowl until well blended
2. gently stir in whipped topping
3. refrigerate one hour or until ready to serve
demonstrations.review: This salad is wonderful. We have always made it this way and there is no need for any additions or subtractions - it is perfect as written!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
lower carb pancakes for one

i thought it sounded weird but they're actually really good. a little chewy but with sugar free maple syrup it's a high fiber/high protein breakfast.

1. combine all ingredients in a blender and blend until consistency of pancake batter
2. pour into hot skillet and cook both sides
3. makes about 3 small pancakes
demonstrations.review: I just enjoyed these pancakes tonight. They were great! I was a little hesitant to try them because there was no baking poweder or soda mentioned in the recipe like other pancakes call for. I decided to give them a shot and just omitted the wheat germ because I didn't have any on hand. I follwed the rest of the directions exactly and was rewarded with great pancakes! Thanks for posting, this was a fast and easy recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
layered pudding dessert

this is an awesome dessert.my daughter makes it all year. it is so easy to make it to suit your tastes.

1. combine butter , flour , and pecans
2. press into 13x9 inch pan and bake at 350 degrees for 20 minutes
3. cool
4. blend cream cheese , powdered sugar , and 1 cup cool whip
5. spread over cooled crust
6. blend instant puddings with milk until thick
7. spread over cream cheese filling
8. top with remaining cool whip and chill well
9. you can use whatever flavor instant pudding you like
demonstrations.review: This recipe is awesome. I've only had it with walnuts in the crust but I bet it would be great with pecans as well. This dessert is so good that my brother used to request it for his birthday dessert! Try it, you'll love it!

target.recipe_text:
porketta roast

this is from the seasonal cabin cookbook. i haven't tried this recipe although i intend to. it is being posted in responce to a request.

1. combine first 4 ingredients and coaresly crush with a mortar and pestle , combine with remaining seasoning ingredients
2. rub pork roast all over with olive oil , place in a large plastic storage bag
3. combine seasoning mix with garlic
4. sprinkle over roast , rub into roast with fingers
5. let the roast stand at room temp 1 hour or up to 12 hours in the refrigerator
6. heat oven to 450f degrees
7. place pork , fat-side up in a roasting pan
8. top with any loose seasonings in the plastic bag
9. roast uncovered for 10 minutes
10. reduce temp to 300f and continue roasting until internal temp reaches 155f about 1 to 1-1 / 2 hours
11. when done , remove from oven and tent loosely with foil
12. let stand 15 minutes before carving
target.review:
Loved this one! I added 1/4 c of white vinegar for extra tang and cooked mine on the grill. Best pork roast I've made.

Thank you!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kfc chicken secret spices

i've never tried this, just saw it on another board and had to snatch it up! there are actually 11 spices in the above combination, but an additional 3 ingredients were necessary to get that special flavor.

1. place all ingredients in blender and pulse for 3-4 minutes to grind well
2. store in an airtight container
3. makes about 3 / 4 cup
4. to use with flour , add 1 oz mix to 1 cup of flour for coating chicken
demonstrations.review:
Excellent! Very close to the "secret spices" I remember from the early 70's KFC chicken. Also, does any one else remember that the crinkle cut fries that used to come with the chicken were sprinkled with the secret spices. After a couple of years they stopped this and served the fries plain. Too bad they used to taste great. 

I  added 1/4 tsp of nutmeg to mine.

Thanks for the memories!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
homemade poultry seasoning

nan

1. mix all ingredients thoroughly
2. store in a clean used spice bottle
3. tightly covered
demonstrations.review: Thank you. I am a "spice-aholic" but always on a budget. I used it to make Chicken Fried Chicken With Milk Gravy by Inez Willenborg #22227). I wasn't crazy about the recipe but the spice mix was perfect. Smelled just like Thanksgiving stuffing.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mic s wonderful hot wings

very tasty dish for anytime. if you like spicy, this is the one. the sauce may be used seperate for a wonderful toping, dip, or marinade. enjoy and try variations to you liking. you can grill these wings as well vor diff. taste add smoking chips.

1. combine all dry ingredients and mix thourghly
2. add vinegar and orange juice
3. mix well
4. wash and remove skin , fold wings
5. place in a deep baking dish and cover with sauce
6. refidgerate for 6-12 hrs
7. remove wings from sauce and place on broiling pan , return sauce to a sauce pan
8. place wings under broiler about 6 inc
9. broil for 20-25 min , turning to stop burning
10. bring sauce to a boil and cook till thinkened
11. using a spoon , spoon thickened sauce over wings many times while broiling 10-12 more minutes
12. remaining sauce can be used for dipping
13. break out the napkins and finger bowls , enjoy
demonstrations.review:
Exquisite! I modified as follows. 2 additional tbsp of brown sugar. I was'nt sure about the qty for the 2 pkgs of chili hot mix were, so I used  2 tsp of chilli powder. This balanced the sweet and hot perfectly. I love wings and am defintely keeping this one!

Thanks!

target.recipe_text:
polenta triangles

diabetic, low-fat

1. combine grits and 1 / 2 cup broth
2. mix well and set aside
3. pour remaining 1 cup broth into heavy , large saucepan
4. bring to a boil
5. add garlic and moistened grits
6. mix well and return to a boil
7. reduce heat to low
8. cover and cook 20 minutes
9. remove from heat
10. add feta cheese
11. stir until cheese is completely melted
12. add red pepper
13. mix well
14. spray 8-inch square pan with cooking spray
15. spoon grits mixture into prepared pan
16. press grits evenly into pan with wet finger
17. refrigerate until cold
18. preheat broiler
19. spray baking sheet with cooking spray
20. turn polenta out onto cutting board and cut into 2-inch squares
21. cut each square diagonally into 2 triangles
22. place polenta triangles on prepared baking sheet and spray tops lightly with cooking spray
23. place under broiler until lightly browned and crisp
24. serve warm or at room temperature
25. garnish with fresh oregano and chives if desired
26. exchanges 1 starch / bread
target.review:
First time polenta maker here and I just wanted to say thanks to Dancer for posting a recipe with a relatively small yield.  My experiment in polenta making proved successful so maybe next time I'll double it.

One note.  I did not need to boil the polenta for 20 minutes.  It was thickened and ready to spread into the pan after 8 minutes.  Also, just for fun I cut my polenta into cookie cutter shapes rather than diamonds.  Polenta is exceptionally amenable to cookie cutters and I had the cutest polenta "pumpkins".   Another experiment.  I topped a few of the pumpkins with blue cheese before broiling.  YUM!  These were extremely flavorful and relatively healthy.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
caramelized garlic chicken

nan

1. heat oven to 500 degrees
2. line shallow roasting pan with foil
3. spray foil with nonstick cooking spray
4. heat oil in small nonstick skillet over medium-low heat until hot
5. add garlic
6. cook 1 to 2 minutes or until garlic begins to soften
7. remove from heat
8. stir in brown sugar until well mixed
9. place chicken breast halves in sprayed foil-lined pan
10. spread garlic mixture evenly over chicken
11. bake at 500 degrees for 10 to 15 minutes or until chicken is fork-tender and juices run clear
demonstrations.review: Why did I wait so long to try this recipe?  Guess I didn't believe something with so few ingredients (and so easy!) could be so good.  Like others, I doubled the sauce ingredients.  The end result was terrific and I'll be making this one quite often.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chicken with 40 cloves of garlic in a clay pot

i found this recipe in consumer guide to clay cookery. though it sounds like a lot of garlic - the peeled cloves cook into sweet, mellow nuggets of flavor - great to spread on crusty french bread. the chicken cooks up moist and tender. this recipe is cooked in a clay pot that must be soaked in cold water for 15 minutes and is placed in a cold oven to start.

1. soak top and bottom of 3 1 / 4 quart clay cooker in water about 15 minutes
2. drain
3. line bottom and sides of cooker with parchment paper
4. combine olive oil , garlic and herbs in cooker
5. rinse and pat dry chicken reserving neck and giblets for other use
6. place chicken over garlic mixture
7. drizzle with lemon juice
8. sprinkle with salt and pepper
9. place covered cooker in cold oven
10. set oven at 475 degrees f
11. bake until chicken is tender and juices run clear when thigh is pierced , about 1 1 / 4 hours
12. remove cover
13. bake until chicken is crisp and brown
14. 5 to 10 minutes
15. carve chicken and spoon cooking liquid over chicken
16. serve with garlic and french bread
demonstrations.review: This is one of my husband's favorite chicken recipes.  If you have a claypot, you can't go wrong.  Also, if you're trying to cut fat feel free to leave out the olive oil.  The clay pot keeps the chicken moist.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
orange chicken crock pot

chicken with zing!

1. combine salt , cayenne pepper , chili powder and paprika
2. sprinkle over chicken
3. set aside
4. place onion , celery , bell peppers and garlic in bottom of slow cooker
5. place chicken on top
6. mix orange juice , peel , honey , worcestershire sauce and ginger
7. pour over chicken
8. cook for 6 to 8 hours on low
demonstrations.review:
Great recipe!  Very low in fat, spicy, sweet (but not overly) and flavorful. I omitted the celery and used both red and green peppers for extra color.  Served over white rice, this recipe makes a nice sauce that looks great on the plate.  I'll definitely make this again.

Note:  I thought ths was very spicy, but I have super-sensitive taste buds.  My husband didn't think it was spicy at all.  Also, I cooked the chicken breast for 5 hours on low.  I'm sure 6 hours would work too, but I find 5 hours is plenty when cooking boneless, skinless breasts.

target.recipe_text:
double quick dinner rolls

a no need to knead yeast dinner roll. i found this on the bisquick site in answer to a request.

1. mix 1 1 / 4 cups of the flour , and the sugar , salt and yeast in large bowl
2. add water , shortening and egg
3. beat with spoon until smooth
4. stir in remaining flour until smooth
5. scrape batter from side of bowl
6. cover and let rise in warm place about 30 minutes or until double
7. grease 12 regular-size muffin cups
8. stir down batter by beating about 25 strokes
9. spoon into muffin cups
10. let rise 20 to 30 minutes or until batter rounds over tops of cups
11. heat oven to 400f
12. bake 15 to 20 minutes or until golden brown
target.review: Wonderful quick rolls!  I used 1/4 cup sugar As suggested by another reviewer but I think it would be good either way.  This recipe is definitely a keeper because it is very quick, it only makes 12 rolls, and is delicious.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
creamy wild rice soup with smoked turkey
