this came from cooking light 2001 magazine and it has been our favorite since i found it. it is the best cold, rainy, gloomy, any day soup ever!!

1. melt butter in a dutch oven over med high heat
2. add carrot and next 5 ingredients
3. saute 8 minutes or until brown
4. stir in broth scraping pan to loosen browned bits
5. stir in turkey and rice
6. cover and simmer 1 hour 15 minutes or until rice is tender
7. combine flour and milk in a small bowl stirring with a whisk
8. add flour / milk mixture to pan and cook over medium heat about 8 minutes or until thick
9. stir in sherry and salt
demonstrations.review: It was a very good soup!  I added a frozen bag of soup vegetables to bump up the veggies and thus the nutritional value.  It was a hit with my family.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s easy one bowl vanilla cupcakes

this recipe goes back over 20 years, i like the simplicity of this recipe and for a one bowl cupcake they are pretty darn good, 1-1/2 teaspoons almond extract may be used in place of the vanilla, using butter in place of shortening will alter the texture it is best to only use shortening --- if you don't have paper liners grease the tins generously or see my recipe#78579

1. set oven to 350 degrees f
2. in a large bowl , mix together the flour with sugar , baking powder and salt until combined
3. add in the shortening cream or milk , vanilla and eggs
4. beat on medium speed of an electric mixer scraping the bowl constantly until just blended
5. pour into paper-lined regular size muffin tins filling under just three-quarters full
6. bake for 20-22 minutes or until the cupcakes test done
7. immediately remove from pans
8. cool completely before frosting
demonstrations.review:
These were the best cupcakes I have ever had!!! I am a frosting fiend and even I could just eat them plain. I'm still debating whether or not to frost them. I made them into rainbow cupcakes by following this tutorial:

http://www.food.com/recipe/kittencals-easy-one-bowl-vanilla-cupcakes-89751

And I will make them like this and plain again!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
roasted tomato soup

recently had an extra pint of cherry tomatoes on hand and was in search of comfort food. devised this soup in a pinch and thought it was worth sharing. mine was a quick soup for one but the recipe has been scaled up and uses the more economical roma tomato. if you have lots of cherry or grape tomatoes -- they have a sweetness that pairs beautifully with the vinegar -- use them or do a mix with the roma tomatoes. if you are making this kosher, skip the cheese or be sure to use vegetable broth.

1. pre-heat oven to 375 degrees
2. wash and cut tomatoes , placing in a shallow baking dish cut side down
3. add onion pieces , garlic , oregano and basil to the pan
4. drizzle vegetables with olive oil and balsamic vinegar
5. season with salt and pepper
6. bake for 45 minutes
7. place roasted vegetables in food processor bowl or blender and begin puree
8. slowly add broth or water until soup has desired consistency
9. continue blending until smooth
10. an immersion blender also works very well
11. serve garnished with cheese if desired
demonstrations.review: This was really good!  (and that is coming from someone who hates canned tomato soup and has never had homemade)  Like some other posters recommended I roasted a couple of carrots, a stalk of celery and a bit more onion with my tomatoes.  I also added about 1/3 cup of milk and a dash of cayenne pepper to the soup.  This is a great soup and my kitchen smells great!  Just what I was looking for to serve with my turkey and swiss Stromboli.

target.recipe_text:
chocolate macadamia nut cookies

this was in a toh cokbook, and we really liked it.

1. in a large bowl
2. cream butter , sugar and vanilla
3. add egg
4. mix together dry ingredients
5. add to creamed mixture
6. mix well
7. fold in chocolate chips and nuts
8. drop by teaspoons on greased sheets
9. bake at 350f degrees for 10 minutes or until golden
10. glaze---
11. melt caramels and cream
12. drizzle over cooled cookies
target.review: Outstanding cookies!  I can't believe this recipe hasn't been discovered yet!  I would think it would have all kinds of reviews by now.   This one must have fallen through the cracks because they are awesome!  Had along with a nice cold glass of milk and I was happy happy HAPPY!  Will make very chance I get. We loved them that much!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
marinated flank steak with blue cheese schmear

this recipe is from the washington state beef commission. it is excellent on sandwiches the next day, so i usually make two!

1. trip steak of any excess fat or silver skin
2. place steak in large zip lock bag
3. combine marinade ingredients and pour over steak
4. close bag& press out any air
5. move steak around in the bag to marinate
6. refrigerate over night , or at least six hours
7. mix schmear ingredients in a small bowl until smooth
8. refrigerate schmear
9. bring schmear to room temperature one hour before serving
10. prior to cooking , remove steak from marinade& drain well
11. grill steak over hot fire , about 5 minutes a side for rare
12. place steak on a platter with the side just off the grill up and immediately top with the schmear
13. spread schmear over steak
14. let rest 10 minutes before serving
15. thinly slice at an angle across the grain
16. spoon sauce& juices back over meat when serving
demonstrations.review: Perfectly cooked steak that yielded some of the best steak I have ever eaten!  Followed the recipe to a T and it was out of this world good!  Had along with Recipe #254586 which was a great addition also to our meal.  Will make again and again on the grill.  A new favorite for sure!  Thanks for sharing this one with us Queer Eye!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mashed red potatoes with garlic and parmesan

the potatoes are ready in our garden, and this is the first recipe i reach for! these are so good!!

1. put potatoes and garlic in lg pan
2. cover with water
3. bring to a boil
4. reduce heat and simmer for 25 minutes , until potatoes are tender
5. drain well
6. mash with the butter , milk , and salt
7. stir in the parmesan cheese
demonstrations.review: My DW and I love these and so does company that comes to the house.  They quickly became well known with us!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
grammie bea s blueberry feather cake

this cake never lasted long when gram made it...it is delicious!!!

1. cream shortening and sugar together
2. add beaten eggs and vanilla
3. sift together cake flour , salt , and baking powder
4. add milk alternately with dry ingredients and mix well
5. flour blueberries , and then add to mix
6. sprinkle top with a little sugar before baking
7. bake in 375 oven for 35-40 minutes in a 9x13" square pan
demonstrations.review: Oh My Gosh! This is so good there aren't even words to describe it!  I guess awesome will have to do for now!  I used big huge cultivated blueberries the first time around, but  I can't wait to make it with the wild Maine blueberries this summer.  Wowwy is all I can say. Oh yeah, nice and moist and delicious too!

target.recipe_text:
microwave chocolate mug brownie

this makes a delicious brownie for one in about a minute. 60 seconds makes a molten center brownie. 75 seconds make a uniformly done brownie. be careful not to overcook.

1. in a coffee mug , add water / milk , melted butter / oil , a dash of salt and vanilla extract
2. whisk well
3. add cocoa powder , whisk well
4. add sugar , whisk well
5. add flour , whisk well
6. microwave for 60 seconds
7. center should be slightly molten
8. careful not to overcook
9. enjoy with a spoon
10. careful , brownie will be hot
target.review: ummmm...just made it.  perfect for 90 degree summer afternoon chocolate attack.  Thank you.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
grandpaw s granola

healthy and delicious!

1. mix the dry ingredients together in one huge or two normal mixing bowls
2. mix the liquid ingredients in a separate bowl , stirring vigorously until they become well-blended
3. quickly , while still blended , stir the liquid into the dry ingredients until every morsel has been evenly moistened
4. preheat oven to 350f
5. spread the completed mixture in a 1 / 2-inch layer on three heavy , ungreased cookie-sheets and slide into hot oven
6. allow 20 minutes basic cooking time with one turning-over of the cereal after first 10 minutes
7. after the first 20 minutes , turn granola again and return to oven at 250 deg f rechecking at 10 minute intervals turning with every recheck until showing signs of browning throughout
8. cooking will continue after removing from oven
9. cool , crumble and store refrigerated in air-tight containers
demonstrations.review: Really delicious.  Made exactly as stated but have also made several different variations with other dried fruits and nuts.  Thank you.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
red lentil and swiss chard stew

i thought this sounded interesting and something a bit different. bon appetit (december 2005)

1. in a large soup pot or saucepan , saute the onion in oil over medium high heat for 10-15 minutes or until onion is golden
2. stir in curry powder and cayenne
3. add the broth and chard and increase heat to high and bring to a boil
4. reduce heat to medium and stir in lentils and garbanzos
5. cover pan and simmer for 10 minutes or until lentils are tender , stirring occasionally
6. divide soup into bowls and top with sour cream or yogurt , if desired
demonstrations.review: Made almost exactly as written but only had chicken broth and chopped up a fresh jalepeno pepper with the onion in the beginning.  Really great stuff.  I would have to say I probably got 8 to 9 servings out of this though.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
zucchini and summer squash casserole

a great summertime casserole using yellow squash and zucchini. but if the little zucchini buggers are taking over your house, it's o.k. to use all zucchini in this recipe! :)

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees f
2. grease a 9 x 13 inch baking dish or casserole and set aside
3. in a large skillet , heat 2 tablespoons butter
4. add onions and cook until tender
5. add zucchini and yellow squash and cook , stirring until just tender
6. season to taste with salt and pepper
7. add the condensed soup , sour cream , and mushrooms , mixing well
8. in a large bowl , combine the melted butter with the stuffing mix
9. pour half the stuffing mix into the baking dish
10. layer the squash mixture over the stuffing mix
11. cover with the remaining stuffing mix
12. bake uncovered at 350 degrees f for 30-35 minutes , or until topping is golden brown and casserole is bubbly
demonstrations.review: Really good stuff.  I didn't have mushrooms and I used green onions instead of regular onions.  I also put shredded parmesan on top so it made like a crispy web over the top.  Cool presentation and yummy food.  Going to try it with lite sour cream to see if I can get away with that...

target.recipe_text:
maw maw s thanksgiving dressing

this was my maw maw's recipe for homemade dressing. it is the best!!! my family has been using this particular dressing recipe for years!

1. pre-heat oven to 350f
2. in a very large mixing bowl , combine bread crumbs , crumbled cornbread , crumbled biscuits , yellow onions , celery , green onions , fresh parsley , sage , salt and pepper
3. toss well
4. add melted butter and eggs
5. mix
6. add chicken broth , a little at a time , mixing lightly , but well
7. add enough broth to make mixture extra moist
8. place mixture into a well-greased baking dish
9. bake about 45 minutes or until top is golden brown
10. ~
11. to bake , remove from refrigerator and let sit at room temperature for about 30 minutes
12. then , remove foil and bake for about 45 minutes
target.review: Added to my Thanksgiving menu. Awesome dressing. Used just cornbread and biscuits, no white bread. I saute the onions and celery first out of habit. Also, my mom told me to add some chopped boiled eggs, as her mom always made it. I'm not a fan of it, but just an idea for anyone else.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s easy no fail make anytime turkey gravy

i have been using this recipe for many years, my family loves this gravy and i have served it to dinner guests over the holidays and always receive rave reviews! --- you don't need to make this gravy using all pan drippings, if you do not have 4 cups of drippings you may mix with chicken broth to make the 4 cups, or it may be made with only chicken broth, please see note on the bottom of the recipe--- this may be made slightly ahead and kept uncovered on top of the stove until ready to serve, just whisk before using if you have any left over this gravy freezes very well or you may reduce all ingredients down to half and for a thinner gravy reduce flour by 1 tablespoon  --- also see my recipe#314890
for more of my recipes visit www.kittencalskitchen.com

1. drain the pan drippings for the roasted turkey through a fine strainer
2. let sit and then remove any fat from the top of the drippings
3. add in chicken broth or water to make 4 cups if necessary
4. in a medium saucepan , melt margarine or butter
5. add in lots of black pepper
6. add in 1 / 2 cup flour plus 3 tablespoons
7. constantly whisk for about 3 minutes over low heat
8. slowly add in the 4 cups turkey broth / drippings
9. whisk constantly over medium-low heat until bubbly and thickened
10. use right away or keep warm over lowest heat setting , whisk again before serving
11. options to make this gravy using all chicken broth prepare as directed using 4 cups low sodium chicken broth and 1 tablespoon chicken boullion powder ---- or you may add in low sodium chicken broth omitting bouillon powder to pan drippings to make up 4 cups
demonstrations.review: Made this over Thanksgiving. My aunt was amazed that I didn't get lumps. Thought that I had bought it somewhere. Best gravy I've ever had, or made.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
fresh peach ice cream  regular and diet versions

(for electric ice cream machines) this recipe makes a delicious, soft, custard-type ice cream. if you prefer a firmer ice cream, you can chill it for an extra cycle in your ice cream machine or place it in a bowl in your freezer for an hour before serving. prep time includes the 1 hour chilling time and the 1/2 hour beat/freezing time.

1. in food processor / blender , puree peaches
2. blend peach puree and all ingredients until very smooth
3. chill ice cream mix until cold , about 1-2 hours
4. pour mix into your ice cream machine and process according to manufacturer's directions
5. it may be necessary to continue the"chill / beat" cycle for 15-30 minutes after the first cycle stops
demonstrations.review: My first time making peach ice cream, and it's awesome. The almond extract really shows, and the flavor is awesome. I used fat free Half & Half, and the texture was great. You don't need tons of fat for a good ice cream flavor.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
to die for brownies

no other recipe i've found compares. the ultimate cake-like brownie. after many years this recipe still holds strong in our family.

1. combine flour , baking powder and salt
2. combine melted butter , cocoa , sugar , eggs and vanilla
3. blend dry mix into moist mixture
4. add nuts and pour batter into a greased 9x13-inch pan
5. bake at 350f degrees for 35 minutes or until it just starts to pull away from sides
6. icing: melt butter in saucepan with milk on medium / low
7. combine cocoa with sugar and stir into milk mixture
8. add vanilla and let cool till spreading consistency
9. sprinkle with more nuts if desired
demonstrations.review: Great brownies. I usually prefer more fudgy brownies, but these are great. Didn't add the frosting, don't like it on brownies.

target.recipe_text:
top secret recipes waffle house waffles by todd wilbur

try the recipe that has sold millions of waffles. if you prefer pecan waffles, add 1/4 cup chopped pecans before pouring the batter onto the waffle iron

recipe created by todd wilbur www.topsecretrecipes.com

1. combine flour , salt and baking soda in a medium bowl and stir to combine
2. lightly beat the egg in another medium bowl and combine with sugar , butter , and shortening , mixing well until smooth
3. add the half & half , milk , buttermilk and vanilla and mix well
4. add the dry flour mixture to the wet mixture while beating and mix until smooth
5. if you can , cover and chill overnight , though the batter can be used right away
6. rub a light coating of vegetable oil on a waffle iron , and preheat it
7. leave the batter out of the refrigerator to warm up a bit as your waffle iron is preheating
8. spoon 1 / 3 to 1 / 2 cup of batter into the waffle iron and cook for 3 to 4 minutes or until the waffles are light brown
target.review: I made belgian waffles and definitely needed a double batch. They were great and had nice color.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
paul bocuse s creme brulee

this is an awesome creme brulee.  i'm asked for the recipe each time i serve it.  it is great for company because you fix it the day before. zwt south region (french burnt cream).

1. preheat the oven to 275f
2. in a medium bowl , whisk the egg yolks with half of the granulated sugar
3. in a small saucepan , warm the cream with the vanilla scrapings and the remaining granulated sugar until steaming
4. gradually whisk the hot cream into the egg yolks until blended
5. strain the custard and pour it into 5-ounce ramekins or shallow gratin dishes
6. set the ramekins in a small baking dish and add enough hot tap water to the dish to reach halfway up the sides of the ramekins
7. bake for about 1 hour and 15 minutes , or until just set
8. let cool in the water bath for 10 minutes , them remove and let cool completely
9. cover and refrigerate for at least 4 hours or overnight
10. preheat the broiler
11. sift a thin even layer of the air-dried brown sugar over each custard
12. broil 1 ramekin at a time as close as possible to the heat source , until the sugar melts , forming a caramelized crust
13. serve immediately
14. if it's humid , the sifted sugar can also be dried in a 250f oven for 20 minutes
demonstrations.review: Excellent.  Although we used sugar on top as I was out of brown sugar.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
quick yellow cake

you can mix this up in a hurry.

1. heat oven to 350
2. mix dry ingredients in lg bowl
3. add shortening , milk and vanilla
4. beat on med for 2 minutes
5. add eggs and beat for 30 seconds more
6. bake in greased 13x9 pan for 35 minutes , or until pick comes out clean
demonstrations.review:
I wanted an alternative to a box mix. Made this cake for my co-workers and they are giving rave reviews. I used organic sugar and home-made vanilla with chocolate frosting and it turned out well.
I left off 1 start b/c I didn't find it very moist and I like a moist cake but it is still very good.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
smoked salmon omelet with red onions and capers

i love smoked salmon, cream cheese, red onions and capers on a bagel. this uses the same ingredients in an omelet.

1. whisk eggs , salt and pepper in a large bowl to blend
2. melt 2 teaspoons butter in a 8-inch diameter nonstick skillet over medium heat
3. ladle 3 / 4 cup of the egg mixture into the skillet
4. cook until eggs are softly set , stirring often and lifting edge of eggs to allow uncooked portion to run under , covering skillet if necessary to help set the top
5. place 1 / 4 of the salmon on half of the omelet
6. sprinkle with 1 tablespoon onion and 1 teaspoon capers
7. top with 2 tablespoons cream cheese
8. fold omelet in half and slid out onto plate
9. repeat with ingredients to make 3 more omelets
demonstrations.review: We liked this but it was a bit too much cream cheese.

target.recipe_text:
quick   easy chicken and dumplings

i saw this being made on 'semi-homemade' with sandra lee.  it looked so good and although i rarely use convenience products, i did break down and buy a jar of chicken gravy and the canned biscuit dough so that i could try this.  the original recipe called for buying containers of already chopped up onion, celery and carrot but, come on now, how hard is that to do in your kitchen??  so, i'm giving the amounts i used for each of those ingredients.  here is the revised recipe, as i made it (and my family loved it!)

1. remove skin from chicken and chop or shred meat into large pieces
2. set aside
3. in a small frying pan , add vegetable oil and heat over medium heat
4. add chopped onions and saute until soft
5. in a large pot or dutch oven , add broth , poultry seasoning , salt , pepper , carrots , celery and sauteed onion
6. bring to a boil
7. reduce heat to simmer for about 10 minutes to soften vegetables and then add shredded chicken
8. continue to simmer while preparing dumplings
9. open can and remove biscuits
10. on a lightly floured surface , roll each biscuit to about 1 / 4-inch thick
11. cut each biscuit into 4 wedges
12. set aside
13. skim surface of stew for any scum that has risen to top
14. stir in chicken gravy
15. with the stew simmering over low heat , stir in dumplings a few at a time
16. once all dumplings are in the pot , cover with a tight fitting lid and cook for 10 minutes
17. ladle into bowls and serve piping hot
target.review: I saw the same episode, but didn't try the recipe until I saw your posting.  This makes a great meal, and is so easy.  Thanks for posting.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
fish stick supper

this is good, easy kid food. a simple, quick,and hearty meal for those busy weeknights.

1. break apart hash browns
2. set aside
3. in a large bowl , beat eggs and milk
4. add onion , dill , seasoned salt , and pepper
5. stir in hash browns and cheese
6. put mixture into a sprayed or greased 11x7x2-inch baking pan
7. arrange fish sticks over the top
8. bake uncovered at 350f for 50 minutes , or until top is golden brown and fish flakes with a fork
9. let stand for 5 minutes before cutting
demonstrations.review: I knew I'd love this dish. I used O'Brian potatos.  I cubed some pepper jack cheese and mixed it in, then topped the dish with extra sharp cheddar.  Every one loved it.  Thanks for posting.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
thai spicy beef

adpated from "simply thai cooking" by wandee young and byron ayanoglu.  this excellent beef curry is a bit time consuming to prepare.  the complex seasonings, though, are a real treat, and make this dish worth the time invested.  i've tweaked slightly as the portion sizes were a bit small in my family's opinion.  otherwise, the recipe is a published in the book.

(edited to correct fish sauce amount 3/19/09)

1. heat oil in wok or large frying pan
2. add vegetables and stir-fry until crisp tender
3. remove and keep warm
4. add garlic and curry paste and stirfry for 45 seconds
5. immediately add coconut milk and lime zest
6. stir-cook for 1-2 minutes until it's bubbling and thick
7. add beef
8. stir-fry for 1 minute
9. add fish sauce and sugar and stir-fry for 2-3 minutes
10. return veges to pan
11. add 3 / 4 of basil leaves
12. stir-fry just until veges are hot
13. transfer to serving dish and garnish with remaining basil
14. serve immediately accompanied by steamed rice
demonstrations.review: Great dish.  I've spent a lot of time in Thailand, and this is as good as any beef dish I ever had in Korat.  Thanks for posting.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
fantastic chicken wings with honey soy garlic glaze

i have made these many times in the past for my parties and there is never any left everyone loves these and i always get asked for the recipe! if you are serving this for a get together i suggest to double the recipe to make 40 wings --- plan ahead the wings have to marinate for 24 hours, frozen thawed wings retain more moisture it is best to use fresh chicken for this --- make certain to have lots of napkins when you serve these!

1. paper towel dry all the wings to remove as much moisture as possible
2. in a large bowl stir together the first 8 ingredients
3. stir in the chicken wings
4. toss to coat
5. cover and refrigerate for 24 hours
6. when ready to bake set oven to 400 degrees f
7. arrange the wings on greased baking sheet / s
8. pour the marinade into a small saucepan
9. bake the wings for about 50-60 minutes , turning and basting with the marinade occasionally
10. arrange the cooked wings on a platter
11. sprinkle with sesame seeds
12. boil the reserved marinade until slightly thickened
13. serve the wings with the boiled marinade as a dipping sauce
14. delicious !
demonstrations.review: These were a huge hit this weekend!  I did whole wings and drumsticks.  I cooked them on the grill, of course, using indirect heat, and mesquite for smoke.  After they came off the grill and were still sticky, I hit them again with some Tony's.  Apparently the wings weren't done though, because they simply flew off the plate ;0).  I will be making these again.  Thanks for posting.

target.recipe_text:
red lobster cheddar bay biscuits copycat

these are copycats of the delicious "cheddar bay biscuits" served at red lobster.

1. heat oven to 450 degrees
2. mix bisquick , milk and cheese until a soft dough forms
3. drop by spoonfuls onto an ungreased cookie sheet
4. bake 6-8 minutes or until golden brown
5. mix butter or margarine and garlic powder
6. brush mixture over warm biscuits before removing from cookie sheet
target.review:
I absolutely LOVE these biscuits. The first time I made them DH said "We're never going to Red Lobster again." We would literally go for the biscuits but hated the food. No need any more. I mix these up once a week because they're so easy. 
There is one thing I've changed. Instead of garlic powder in the butter that gets brushed on top I use some garlic salt, that's what they use at Red Lobster and it makes a HUGE difference. They do get a bit brown on the bottom because of the cheese but cooking smaller biscuits and using a pan that isn't really dark helps. 
THANK YOU! THANK YOU! THANK YOU! JodiGirl!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
really really good candied sweet potatoes

we like sweet potatoes a lot, and don't wait for a holiday to fix these.

1. cover potatoes with water , bring to a boil
2. lower heat and simmer for 25 minutes , until done
3. when cooled , peel and cut into chunks
4. place in 2-qt baking dish
5. in small saucepan combine remaining ingredients , cook and stir until mixture boils
6. pour over potatoes
7. bake at 350f for 40 minutes
demonstrations.review: These were awesome. Got tired of the "same old" mashed sweet potatoes and made these instead. I added chopped candied pecans into the sauce and topped with mini-marshmallows as others had. We REALLY loved them. They were very sweet and extremely decadent but that's what Thanksgiving is for!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
barefoot contessa s shortbread hearts   ina garten

i got this recipe from the food tv website after seeing the cookies made by the barefoot contessa herself, ina garten.  it's been my go-to recipe for shortbread cutouts for years now, and i was surprised to see that it was not already posted on the zaar.  it's the first recipe for cutout cookies that rolled, cut and baked with ease for me, just as shown on tv!  not only does it make great holiday shortbread cutouts, it's the perfect recipe to roll thin and sandwich with your favorite jam, or my personal favorite, cutout using a kaiser-brand, wavy-edged square cookie cutter and place an after eight-brand thin chocolate mint between 2 cookies, immediately after removing them from your baking sheet!  no matter what shape you make or how you embellish, you will always receive two thumbs up from anyone who tries them!

1. preheat the oven to 350f
2. in the bowl of an electric mixer with the paddle attachment , cream together the butter and 1 cup of the sugar until they are just combined
3. add the vanilla
4. in a medium bowl , sift together the flour and salt
5. then add them to the butter and sugar mixture
6. mix on low speed until the dough starts to come together
7. dump onto a surface dusted with flour and shape into a flat disk
8. wrap in plastic and chill for 30 minutes
9. roll dough 1 / 2-inch thick and cut with a 3-inch heart-shaped cutter
10. place the hearts on an ungreased sheet pan and sprinkle with sugar
11. bake for 20 to 25 minutes , until the edges begin to brown
12. allow to cool to room temperature
13. leave plain or dip in or paint with melted chocolate or royal icing
14. a
15. i cut out the cookies days ahead and bake them the day i serve them
16. for me , i loosely wrap each baked cookie in bakery-type waxed 'tissue' paper and store them in the fridge in a tightly sealed tupperware-type container -- they will keep for weeks this way and still taste great !
demonstrations.review:
These are super delicious. I've made them with both salted and unsalted butter and I prefer salted. They were a little too bland for me without the extra salt. I cut them into large rounds with a biscuit cutter and used a tablespoon to make a divet in each of the cookies and filled them with blueberry and blackberry preserves. DELISH!
On a side note, I don't know if it was just me but the texture wasn't the same when I tried to double the recipe. Not sure if it's just too much dough for the KA or what but, I just take the time to mix batches separately if I'm making more than one recipe. :)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mimi s cafe whiskey sauce

serve with mimi's cafe bread pudding.

1. melt butter in a small saucepan over low heat
2. add sugar and stir will
3. remove from heat , let cool slightly , then quickly whisk in the beaten eggs and whiskey
4. put the sauce back on the stove over low heat and whisk constantly until the sauce has thickened slightly
5. keep the sauce warm until serving
6. if you like , you can serve the bread pudding with a sprinkle of powdered sugar and a scoop of your favorite ice cream
demonstrations.review: This whiskey sauce is to die for when prepared properly... be really careful not to overcook as it curdles when taken too far. Mimi's uses Jack Daniels in their version which gives it a slightly banana flavor (YUM!) Be careful of using too strong a whiskey (like Jamesons) as you won't be able to get rid of the strong Whiskey flavor by the time the eggs are done setting. :)

target.recipe_text:
hot taco dip

this is my version of the touchdown taco dip that i had at a pampered chef party.

1. preheat oven to 350f degrees
2. mix beans , cream cheese , sour cream and taco seasoning until well combined
3. stir in garlic
4. spread in bottom of baking pan
5. sprinkle tomato and olives over top
6. cover with cheese
7. bake for 15-18 minutes
8. serve with tortilla chips
target.review: Very good!  I used 1/2 can of refried beans, but followed the recipe aside from that.  I will be making this again.  Thanks for sharing = )

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crock pot pork and cabbage dinner

an easy, no fuss crock pot dinner.  i serve this aside of mashed potatoes or recipe #64252  and applesauce.  recipe is courtesy of "fix it and forget about it" cookbook, with a few of my own adaptations to the recipe.

1. place the chops in the bottom of the crock pot
2. layer onions , parsley and cabbage on top of chops
3. salt and pepper
4. pour beef broth over layers
5. add apple cider vinegar
6. cover
7. cook on low for 5 to 6 hours
demonstrations.review: This was very good; my husband really liked it and said it reminded him of Chow Mein.  I used bone-in chicken breasts instead of pork.  At the end I chopped the chicken and let it soak up the sauce before serving.  I also used pre shredded cabbage/carrot mix sold for Cole Slaw instead of chopped cabbage and veg. broth in place of beef broth.  I did use the apple cider vinegar--Yum!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
bread machine monkey pull aparts

i love to have the bread maker make my dough. it is foolproof. shaping and finishing dough is usually not a big chore and the results are wonderful! i am unsure where i got this recipe as it is written in my handwriting but no indication of where it came from.

1. add ingredients to your bread maker , according to manufacturer's instructions
2. process on dough cycle
3. remove dough from machine at end of dough cycle
4. using glaze ingredients , grease tube pan with 2 t butter
5. sprinkle pan with 2 t brown sugar
6. mix remaining brown sugar and cinnamon
7. melt remaining 4 t butter
8. divide dough into 12 pieces
9. roll in melted butter then into brown sugar and cinnamon
10. arrange dough in layers
11. let rise in warm place 30 minutes or until doubled
12. preheat oven to 350
13. bake 25-30 minutes
14. turn out of pan immediately
demonstrations.review: I tried this recipe and the dough turned out too sticky to use.  I figured I did something wrong, tried again, and still no good....  I was able to form and bake, but still didn't turn out tasting very good.  I'm thinking it may have been my ingredients/bread machine?  I don't want to rate this because I don't think it's the recipe but possibly something that went wrong here.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
italian pork loin for the slow cooker  crock pot

very simple great tasting, tender pork loin.  this is also great using, pork chops, chicken breast even beef.

1. place pork loin in crock pot
2. in bowl mix everything else
3. pour over chops
4. cook on low 6-8 hours
5. serve with cooked pasta , rice or mashed potatoes , salad and garlic bread
demonstrations.review: This was enjoyed by the entire family.  I followed the recipe exactly as listed.

target.recipe_text:
best banana bread

you'll never need another banana bread recipe ever again!

1. remove odd pots and pans from oven
2. preheat oven to 350 / 180
3. cream together butter and sugar
4. add eggs and crushed bananas
5. combine well
6. sift together flour , soda and salt
7. add to creamed mixture
8. add vanilla
9. mix just until combined
10. do not overmix
11. pour into greased and floured loaf pan
12. bake at 350 / 180 for 55 minutes
13. keeps well , refrigerated
target.review: I added a teaspoon of cinnamon and 1/4 teaspoon of nutmeg, and it was great!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
ginger glazed mahi

this is a great way to make fish.  this will work with any dense fish like salmon or mahi mahi or even tuna.  i like to do this in the winter when i can't get to my snow covered grill.  a great wine to pair with this is a pinot noir--i'm partial to schug.

1. mix all ingredients in a ziploc bag and add fish
2. leave in fridge to marinate for up to 2 hours
3. preheat oven to 400
4. in an oven safe skillet , heat 1 tbsp olive oil on medium high heat
5. place fish in skillet , but be careful--it will splatter a bit
6. leave the fish to sizzle away for 5 minutes
7. flip the fish over and place entire pan in the oven for 15 minutes
8. enjoy
demonstrations.review: This was a great recipe to get my boyfriend to eat fish!  I served it with Hawaiian fried rice.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
the best peanut butter oatmeal cookies

the oatmeal makes all the difference. these are the very best! they vanish quickly.

1. in large bowl mix the butter , shortning , sugars and peanut butter
2. add eggs one at a time
3. blend flour , soda and salt then add to sugar mixture
4. then add oats
5. form into 1 1 / 2 inch balls these come out perfectly round bake 350 degrees for 12 minutes
demonstrations.review: Oh yes, they're the best!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
tzatziki cucumber dipping sauce

greek sauce/dip/salad dressing. serve with vegies,pitas,or with spicy dishes.

1. line a sieve with a double thickness of dampened cheesecloth
2. spoon in yogurt and set the sieve over a bowl
3. refrigerate for two to three hours or until yogurt is about half its volume , nicely thick and creamy
4. shred or cut cucumber into julienne strips
5. place in a colander in sink or over a bowl , sprinkle generously with salt , mix well and let drain for at least 30 minutes to an hour
6. rinse and gently pat dry
7. in a mortor and pestal muddle the garlic into a bit salt
8. add to the thickened yogurt , cucumber , lemon juice , olive oil , and if desired , the pepper and mint
9. mix well
10. serve or refrigerate for a day or two so flavors mingle
11. stir again before serving and sprinkle with additional minced mint leaves if desired
demonstrations.review: Great recipe!  I'm glad I drained the cucumber in the cheese cloth too, because it would have been too runny otherwise.  I used one English cucumber for a half recipe.

target.recipe_text:
german lowenbrau  lwenbru  coleslaw

source: germanfoods.org

1. wash the cabbage under cold running water
2. remove tough outer leaves , and cut the cabbage into quarters
3. to shred the cabbage , cut out the core and slice the quarters crosswise into 1 / 8 inch-wide strips
4. drop the cabbage into a large mixing bowl
5. add the onion and bell pepper , and mix well with a spoon
6. in a small bowl , combine the mayonnaise , beer , celery seed , salt and a few grindings of black pepper
7. stir with a wire whisk until all the ingredients are blended
8. pour the mixture over the cabbage and toss together gently but thoroughly
9. taste for seasoning
10. cover the bowl with plastic wrap and refrigerate the coleslaw for about an hour before serving
target.review: Yum!! Found the Lowenbrau (lions's brew) at my local specialty store). This is a unique and tasty coleslaw - thank you for sharing!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cilantro buttermilk dressing

this dressing is out of this world!! my husband and i were eating it with a spoon, dipping bread in it, serving it as a sauce over our chicken - very versatile!! would be great too served over iceberg lettuce wedges!!

1. in a bowl , combine the sour cream , buttermilk and mayonnaise until smooth
2. stir in the bell pepper , onion , cilantro and garlic
3. season to taste with salt and pepper
4. refrigerate any extra dressing in a sealed container for up to 1 week
demonstrations.review: This is great on any grilled meats!!! To die for!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mashed white sweet potato bake

found this in the kraft food & family and i thought this would be great for the holidays! i love the idea of the layers being visible through a clear casserole dish if possible.

1. preheat oven to 375f place white and sweet potatoes in separate bowls
2. add half each of the cream cheese and sour cream to the potatoes in each bowl
3. season with salt and pepper
4. mash with potato masher or fork until creamy
5. stir half of the parmesan into the bowl of white potato mix
6. mix half of the cheddar cheese into the bowl of sweet potatoes
7. alternately layer half each of the white potato mixture and sweet potato mixture in a 2 qt clear glass casserole dish
8. repeat layers
9. bake 15 minutes
10. sprinkle with remaining cheeses and continue baking 5 minutes or until cheeses are melted
demonstrations.review: Great recipe!! Wonderful addition to the holiday menu!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
banana strawberry freezer jam

yummy! you can use fresh or frozen strawberries and ripe bananas!! perfect for gift giving or with your favorite breakfast pastry!! note: cooking time is actually the time for the jam to sit.

1. combine mashed bananas and strawberries in medium bowl
2. set aside
3. combine sugar and freezer jam pectin in small bowl , stirring to blend evenly
4. gradually stir pectin mixture into prepared fruit , stirring for 3 minutes
5. ladle jam into freezer jars , leaving 1 / 2 inch headspace
6. let jam stand to thicken , not to exceed 30 minutes
7. serve immediately
8. refrigerate up to 3 weeks or freeze up to one year
9. yield: 5 - 8 oz
10. jars
demonstrations.review: I made this for holiday gifts to family and friends, everyone loved it and is begging me to make more.

target.recipe_text:
sherry mushroom chowder

nan

1. combine mushrooms , onions , carrots , celery
2. sherry , thyme salt and pepper in a 3 quart saucepan
3. place on medium heat and cook stir frequently until the vegetables are tender and most of the liquid has evaporated
4. add 2 1 / 2 cups milk and all of the evaporated milk
5. cook stirring until the mixture comes to a simmer
6. in jar with lid combine the remaining 1 / 2 cup milk with the flour shake until smooth
7. stir into soup continue cooking and stirring until soup thickens and is bubbling
8. divide into serving bowls top with parmesan cheese
target.review: Delicious! And sort of unorthodox methods. Don't be tempted to add more than the 3 tablespoons of sherry to the mushrooms and veggies - the mushrooms will make their own juices eventually. And, the shaking together of the remaining milk and flour makes a wonderful smooth soup with absolutely no lumps. Beautiful soup, onlyme!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
elswet s rosemary rice

this is the perfect side dish for roast chicken, shrimp scampi, or a nice roast (it works so well with pork and beef!). if used with beef, substitute the chicken broth/bulion cubes for beef flavored ones, and pork bulion for pork. also, if you don't have the 16-oz can of chicken broth on hand, you can substitute or 2 cups hot water with 6 (flavored to match the meat you're serving) bulion cubes melted within.

1. heat the oil over medium high heat in a medium-sized sauce pan that has a lid
2. add the rosemary , garlic , and red pepper
3. then cook the green onions and parsley until soft- 2-3 minutes
4. add rice , and salt , and cook , stirring constantly for 30 seconds
5. pour in the chicken broth and let rice cook on low heat until liquid is absorbed- 15-17 minutes
6. add one cup of hot water , add the gumbo fil [or sassafras leaves] and continue to cook until rice is done
7. remove from heat and let sit for 5 minutes
8. stir in vinegar and serve hot
demonstrations.review: This is truly fantastic and is going in my cookbook of classics (when I create it...). I'm sure I don't need to tell everyone how wonderful the garlic and rosemary smelled sauteing together ;o), it's one of those fabulously aromatic dishes that drive you nuts with anticipation. The cooking technique is a bit different than what I'm used to, but the rice came out perfectly. And FD, don't forget to edit this recipe to include the adding of the gumbo file in the instructions... it's not there and I almost didn't add it and that would have been a shame coming from a good part-Cajun girl! Wonderful recipe, thank you so much!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cheese almond rice

i call this my 'kitchen cabinet side dish' because i usually have most of the ingredients on hand and can sub the rest (dry parsley for fresh, etc.) my family loves it and it goes well with just about anything, from fish to steak. adapted from a sunset recipe.

1. combine drained mushrooms with onions , almonds , cheese , rice and pepper
2. turn into a greased 2-qt casserole
3. add water to the mushroom liquid to make 3 1 / 2 cups liquid
4. heat to the simmering point then add the bouillon cubes and soy sauce to the hot liquid and stir until cubes are dissolved
5. pour over rice mixture
6. cover and bake in a 375 oven for 45 minutes to 1 hour , or until liquid has been absorbed
7. stir in parsley and pimiento just before serving
demonstrations.review: This was a fabulous rice dish and one that will be made often in my home! As you said, it really lends itself to those "kitchen cabinet" substitutions... I used about 2 tsp. fresh minced onion and subbed 2 cups beef broth + 1-1/2 cups water. The aroma of this dish is a killer, and it cooked up in exactly the time as stated - the rice is perfectly tender and the almond slivers remain absolutely crunchy, not soggy at all. It's cheesy but it's not the only thing you can taste. Just enough soy sauce to taste but not too much to overpower. A wonderful rice side dish; DEFINITELY a staple around here! Thanks so much Judy!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
watermelon  cucumber and tomato salad

from parade magazine. serve with a side dish of coarse salt.

1. prepare all ingredients ahead of time and store separately
2. just before serving , drain the water from the watermelon , tomato and cucumber in a colander and place them in a serving bowl
3. toss with olive oil , basil and pepper
4. serve immediately
demonstrations.review: I was going to post this very recipe; I'll just talk it up instead! I'm not usually into weird combos, but I love what Sheila Lukins does with food. You DO have to wait to combine the ingredients so they don't get sloppy, but this makes a terrific side dish, very refreshing; I prepared it with stuffed chicken breasts. Thanks for posting this recipe, Cathleen!

target.recipe_text:
indian tofu and spinach over almond rice

365:no repeats. rachael ray

1. prepare the rice according to the package directions
2. preheat a large , deep nonstick skillet over medium-high heat with the vegetable oil
3. add the tofu , season with salt and pepper , and lightly brown , 2 to 3 minutes per side
4. remove the tofu from the skillet and reserve on a plate
5. to the same skillet , add the garlic , ginger , onions , cumin and coriander
6. saut together for 4 to 5 minutes or until the onions are tender
7. add the spinach and continue to cook for 2 minutes
8. add the flour and cook for 1 minute
9. add the vegetable stock and bring to a bubble
10. add the curry paste , mango chutney , and chick peas , then return the browned tofu to the skillet , reduce the heat to medium low , and simmer the curry for 8 to 10 minutes
11. while the curry is simmering , toast the almonds in a small dry skillet over medium heat until golden
12. once the rice is cooked , fluff it with a fork , add the toasted almonds , and stir with the fork
13. serve the curry in shallow bowls with a scoop of almond rice on top
target.review: It was interesting at first bite, but after 3  or 4 bites it really becomes a very tasty dish.  I'll attempt to post our photo. thanks  A

demonstrations.recipe_text:
linda s thai  sweet chili  sauce for dipping  egg rolls  sushi

i created this recipe to make thai chicken wings this weekend, and it was great! use this sauce in any of your thai recipes asking for sweet chili sauce. this recipe is medium hot, so use the chilis according to your taste!  i also use it on my sushi, egg rolls, and spring rolls, and it is incredible!

1. in a small pan add the first 6 ingredients together , over low heat
2. stir constantly until mixture thickens to a syrupy consistency , about 5 minutes once it starts to simmer
3. it reduces quite a bit
4. mix well , and let sit until hot
5. mix the cornstarch and water together in a small bowl and add to the sauce
6. mix well
7. let cook until it starts to thicken , then remove from heat
8. let cool , and use in any of your thai recipes asking for sweet chili sauce
demonstrations.review: Sorry, but this was not, in our estimation , a good dipping sauce for sushi. Maybe for wing ??

demonstrations.recipe_text:
zucchini salsa  canned

this recipe is from a friend's, daughter's mother-in-law (kinda like a 5th cousin twice removed and it is delicious! if you want it "hot" just add a dozen finely chopped jalapenos.  i do not water bath the jars but i am very careful with sterilizing and make sure the lids are sealed.  i you feel better waterbathing them do it for 15 minutes.

1. day one:in a large bowl combine
2. zucchini , onions , green pepper , red pepper and the salt mix together cover and let stand over night
3. day two
4. next day rinse , drain well and put into a large pot then add mustard , garlic , cumin , vinegar , brown sugar , pepper flakes , salt , cornstarch , nutmeg , pepper , 1 tablespoon salt , tomatoes and tomato paste
5. bring to a boil and simmer for 15 minutes
6. pour into sterilized jars and seal
7. water bath jars for 15 minutes if they have not sealed properly
demonstrations.review: It is very good, but I'd call it a great hot relish instead of salsa. For my liking the next time I make it, I will eliminate the nutmeg sugar and vinegar, add cilantro and a few fresh hot peppers, of choice.  Thanks for sharing.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
zucchini basil muffins

from just hungry - they adapted it from bernard clayton's new complete book of breads,

1. preheat the oven to 200c / 425f
2. grease muffin tins
3. combine the eggs , milk and oil in a large bowl
4. combine the flour , sugar , salt and baking powder in another bowl and add to the liquid mixture in batches , stirring to blend
5. don't overblend !
6. add the zucchini and basil and stir to blend
7. fill each muffin cup about 1 / 2 full
8. sprinkle the top with the cheese
9. bake for about 20-25 minutes for regular size muffins , 15-20 minutes for the mini muffins , until the tops are golden brown and puffy
10. serve while still warm
demonstrations.review: Great crusty outside tender inside. I'd use 1/2 olive oil & 1/2 corn oil just beccause they are a tad bit too olive oily in flavor.  Good one thanks

target.recipe_text:
dark chocolate cake

while it takes slightly longer to prepare this recipe than a box mix, the resulting moist, delicious cake makes it very worth the little extra time. i consider this 'perfect' chocolate cake. this cake is excellent with  both with recipe #261024 and recipe #208959 (the dark flavor version). (i use recipe #95416 when i'm decorating the cake.) i love how the leftovers are still moist even a day or two later. (i store my loosely covered with plastic wrap.)
my father adores this cake with recipe #261024 on it. for his birthday, father's day etc. i make him cupcakes with the icing on them and individually wrap them. he keeps them in his freezer for when he wants "a piece of cake". he claims they are as good as when they are fresh. 
(even though it isn't where i got the recipe from so i can't vouch for it, reviewers have said it is the recipe on the hershey's cocoa can. i would recommend using their special dark cocoa if possible.)

1. heat oven to 350f
2. grease and flour two 9 inch round baking pans or one 13x9 inch pan
3. in large mixer bowl , stir together dry ingredients
4. add eggs , milk , oil , and vanilla
5. beat on medium speed for 2 minutes
6. stir in boiling water by hand
7. i usually use between 2 / 3 & 3 / 4 cups
8. the cake is still very moist but it doesn't seem to "fall" as much as it cools
9. this might have to do with our high humidity or brand of flour or other factors so i don't know if it will work for everyone
10. pour into prepared pan
11. bake 30 to 35 minutes for round 9-inch pans , 35 to 40 minutes for rectangular pan or until wooden pick inserted in center comes out clean
12. because they have a tendency to overflow if you fill them more than 2 / 3 full , i usually get about 27-28 cupcakes per batch
13. bake for approximately 18-20 minutes
14. cool 10 minutes
15. remove from pan to wire racks
16. please
17. chocolate drink mixes that you add to milk or water to drink will not work in this recipe
target.review: Moist, rich, delicious cake - exactly what I was looking for! I would definitely make this again. Very easy to put together and received many compliments all around. I topped with buttercream frosting and the sweet icing complimented the cocoa flavour very well. Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
strawberry julius

the ultimate mall fruity shake at home! i modified this recipe one day from one i found online. i have sensitive teeth so i don't like ice much anyway. guaranteed not to give you "slushie headache".

1. slice up fresh strawberries until you have enough to fill a one cup measure
2. add to a blender or food processor , or if you only have a stick mixer , just put it in a large pyrex jug
3. add rest of ingredients
4. blend until smooth
5. you may want to try this a little bit cooler for summer days , omit the water and add a few ice cubes
6. i only leave out the ice cubes because my food processor can't handle hard ice
7. also it does tend to separate if you leave it sitting around for a minute , don't let this put you off , just stir it up a bit , it tastes the same , just tends to be more frothy at the top then
demonstrations.review: Rich, decadent and refreshing. Works well with other fruits as well - love it with mangoes!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
sweet  creamy coleslaw

i never liked coleslaw until i tried my husband's great aunt's. now i can't get enough of it! great with bbq pork sandwiches. you can also use a bag of slaw mix instead of shredding the cabbage and carrots yourself.

1. shred cabbage and carrots into a bowl
2. mix mayonnaise , vinegar and sugar in a separate bowl
3. blending well
4. pour over shredded vegetables and stir to coat
5. chill
6. amounts of dressing ingredients can be adjusted to suit taste but always use the same amount of vinegar as sugar
demonstrations.review: Sometimes I forget just how good a simple recipe can taste. This was perfect - not slimey, not buried in cream, just a well balanced and tasty 'slaw. Thank you!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
super soft pretzel rolls  easy too

this is the quick soft breadsticks recipe with a modified cooking technique for the best pretzel rolls ever! the dough only has to rise once for 20-30 min.--so easy.  i serve them with sauerkraut chowder for a bavarian theme dinner.  everyone loves these!

1. mix together brown sugar , salt , and yeast in big bowl
2. mix together oil and water and add this to the sugar and yeast mix
3. add the flour and mix to a nice doughy consistency
4. knead with mixer a few minutes
5. divide dough into 12 balls and shape into rolls and let rise on greased foil cover sheet for 20-30 minute until nice and puffy
6. meanwhile , bring water and baking soda to a simmer in a wide pan with straight sides and preheat oven to 375
7. place 4 rolls in the water and simmer 1 minute then flip and simmer 1 minute more
8. drain and place on cookie sheet
9. repeat with remaining rolls
10. brush rolls with egg white and sprinkle generously with kosher salt
11. slash decoratively with a sharp blade
12. bake until 'pretzel' brown , about 12-15 minutes
13. enjoy !
demonstrations.review: Soft, chewy and slightly sweet with a beautiful looking crust. These come together very quickly - which is good because I ended up having to make a second batch on the first day I made them! I definitely recommend cooking them long enough to get that nice reddish brown crust - they are moist enough inside that you don't have to worry so much about overcooking them!

target.recipe_text:
grilled cauliflower

i actually won a cash prize in our local paper for this recipe. my husband and i will eat the whole thing ourselves - make several if you're having guests. if someone you love doesn't care for cauliflower, this may be the ticket!

1. remove stem& leaves from cauliflower
2. wash& pat dry
3. spread the butter over the cauliflower
4. sprinkle with seasoned salt& cheese
5. wrap head of cauliflower in heavy duty aluminum foil
6. grill over medium heat about 40 minutes or until desired tenderness
target.review: We loved this.  We probably overcooked it - it was very soft, and most of the butter and cheese stuck to the foil - but it was delicious.  Next time, I may replace the butter with olive oil, and stick some whole cloves of garlic in between the cauliflower florets.  Thanks for posting!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
rice  black bean   feta salad

fast easy salad for summer evenings.

1. mix all ingredients
2. refrigerate
3. serve
demonstrations.review: This was a great side to grilled chicken on a hot evening.  I omitted the celery, and used fat free dressing and reduced fat feta, with good success.  We think it would also be good with grilled shrimp.  Thanks for posting!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mini meatballs in cranberry sauce

these cute little meatballs go very quickly at holiday gatherings.

1. in a large bowl , combine the ground meat , bread crumbs , parsley , eggs , garlic , onion powder , basil and pepper
2. mix well but do not overwork or meat will become tough when cooked
3. form into small balls the size of a walnut or smaller
4. place meatballs in a slow oven of 300 degrees f and bake for 25 minutes
5. in the meantime , in a crock pot set at 325 degrees f , mix together the cranberry sauce add remaining sauce ingredients
6. when meatballs are baked , transfer them to the crock pot and stir into the sauce
7. cook in crock pot for 1 hour
8. lower heat to keep warm for serving
demonstrations.review: This was a big hit for our mid-day snacks on Christmas.  I baked the meatballs about a week in advance and flash-froze.  I let them thaw overnight in the refrigerator.  In the morning, I mixed the meatballs and sauce, and set the crock-pot on low.  They were at a perfect temperature after about 3 hours.  I used regular breadcrumbs and dried herbs instead of fresh, and the meatballs were still great, although I may add some salt to the meat mixture next time.  We served 9 people for midday snacks, and there were only a few cups of meatballs and sauce left.  Thanks for sharing!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
silly  simple cheese and garlic filled crescents

these are so simple it's silly, but my husband loves them so much i thought i'd post this. i like them, too! i've tried making these a few different ways, but i believe good old processed american cheese singles works the best for this - it's clean and easy to measure and roll up, and it melts perfectly during the allotted baking time. you can skip the cooking spray and foil if you want and just bake these directly on the baking sheet, but i like to do it this way because it makes clean up easier, and any leftovers can be stored and reheated right in the foil.

1. preheat oven to 375f
2. line a cookie sheet with aluminum foil and spray with butter flavored cooking spray
3. unroll crescent roll dough and separate into 8 triangles
4. sprinkle each with garlic powder
5. cut or divide each cheese slice into quarters to make 8 small squares of cheese
6. cut or fold one piece of cheese in half
7. stack the halves on top of each other and place them on the bottom end of one crescent triangle
8. roll triangle up starting with this end
9. fold the two side points of the dough towards the center of the dough so that all three triangle points are on the same side
10. place roll on the sheet with the points facing down
11. repeat for each dough triangle and bake for 11-13 minutes or until golden
demonstrations.review: Very tasty and easy.  I used 2 pieces of string cheese, quartered, instead of the American.  It was a great side to a pasta dinner.  Thanks.

target.recipe_text:
parmesan cheese twists

okay, go out and buy some puff pastry sheets! then go back to your kitchen, and make these! you won't be sorry!

1. thaw pastry sheet at room temperature 30 minutes
2. preheat oven to 400f
3. mix egg and water
4. mix cheese , parsley and oregano
5. unfold pastry on lightly floured surface
6. roll into 14x10-inch rectangle
7. cut in half lengthwise
8. brush both halves with egg mixture
9. top 1 rectangle with cheese mixture
10. place remaining rectangle over cheese-topped rectangle , egg side down
11. roll gently with rolling pin to seal
12. cut crosswise into 28 strips
13. twist strips and place 2" apart on greased baking sheet , pressing down ends
14. brush with egg mixture
15. sprinkle with black pepper
16. bake 10 minutes or until golden
17. serve warm or at room temperature
18. makes 28 appetizers
19. another
20. place on baking sheet and brush with egg mixture
21. freeze
22. when frozen , store in plastic bag for up to 1 month
23. to bake , preheat oven to 400f place frozen strips on greased baking sheet
24. bake 15 minutes or until golden
target.review: I couldn't find puff pastry dough at the store I went to, but it was a small one.  So I improved and bought a can of breadsticks, followed the rest of the recipe and they were so yummy.  Can't wait to use the pastry dough, bet they are even better.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
fannie farmer s scalloped potatoes

this is a recipe in my fannie farmer cookbook that i just recently found and tried. i didn't know that scalloped potatoes was such a simple dish to make.

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees f
2. butter a 1 1 / 2 quart casserole
3. cover the bottom of the casserole with a single layer of potatoes& onion
4. sprinkle generously with salt , pepper , flour and a few dots of butter
5. repeat until all of the potato slices & onion are used
6. pour milk over the potato slices until the top is almost covered
7. dot with the remaining butter
8. bake for 1 hour or until the potatoes are soft
demonstrations.review: SOOOO YUMMY!  I added 2 cups of cheese like others but the ones on the bottom without cheese were still amazing.  I will be making this a lot in the future.  So quick and easy.  THANKS for such a great recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
rosemary potatoes   microwave

nummy, nummy!! good with steak or anything else. from cooking light.

1. place the butter and garlic in an 8 inch square baking dish
2. microwave at medium high 45 seconds or until butter melts
3. add rosemary , salt , 1 / 4 teaspoon black pepper and potatoes , toss well
4. cover and microwave at high 15 minutes or until potatoes are tender
demonstrations.review: AWESOME!!!!!  Similar to a recipe I had that used the oven but this is so much faster and easier.  Loved it.  Definitely a keeper!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
my homemade sloppy joes

this is a recipe that i have had, and been making for quite a while,(15 years), this is my favorite sloppy joes, they are so good.  this will make enough for about 16-18 sloppy joes.

1. brown ground beef , garlic , and onion in a very large skillet , and drain
2. combine remaining ingredients in a sprayed 5 quart slow cooker , and stir in meat mixture
3. cover and cook on low for 6-7 hours
demonstrations.review: This was so good.  I had never made sloppy joes before and found this recipe.  Quick, easy and so tasty.  I did cut back on the ground beef to 2 lbs and left everything else the same.  It was perfect.  Thank you for this great recipe.

target.recipe_text:
crock pot rice pudding

this company's coming recipe for rice pudding is by far the easiest one i have ever made. i might add an extra tablespoon or so of sugar next time, and maybe top the vanilla up to a full 2 teaspoons. however, it did taste just fine as is. the cinnamon taste is very mild, so you may want to sprinkle more cinnamon on top of individual servings.

1. combine all ingredients in slow cooker
2. stir well
3. cover and cook on low for 4 to 5 hours or on high for 2 to 2-1 / 2 hours
4. stir twice during cooking period
target.review: I agree with all of the above.  I used "Sugar in the Raw" brand sugar and three cinnamon sticks and the pudding was fine.  Even more cinnamon could be used.  I will make this again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
waldorf astoria beef stew   crock pot  copycat

yum

1. place all in a large crock pot
2. cover and cook at low setting for 5 hours
3. do not stir
4. add whatever additional vegetables you like
demonstrations.review: Excellent.  The sauce came out thick (was that from the tapioca?) and the meal was hearty.  I served it over rice.  Next time I will throw in some green beans or broccoli.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crock pot ginger teriyaki pork chops

i got this recipe from the kikkoman site. instead of grilling i put it in the crock pot. talk about tender and flavorful! i also used a teaspoon of ground ginger. ummm ummm good!

1. mix kikkoman teriyaki sauce , brown sugar and ginger together
2. place chops in crock pot
3. pour sauce over the chops
4. cook on low for 7 hours
demonstrations.review: I agree with the reviwers who wrote that 8 hours is too much for these.  My pork chops were too dry but they did taste good.  Next time I will cook for 6.5 to 7 hours.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crock pot tuna casserole

i'm so excited! i just found this recipe and made some changes more to my liking. i would make it tomorrow, but dh will be away on business. i love tuna casserole, but never thought of making one in a crock pot. prep time does not include hard boiling the eggs.

1. combine all ingredients , except 1 1 / 2 cup potato chips , in slow cooker and stir well
2. top mixture with remaining 1 1 / 2 cup potato chips
3. cover and cook on low 5 to 8 hours
demonstrations.review: This is creamy and tasty and surprisingly thick for a casserole without noodles.  However, I found that I really needed bread to go with it - otherwise, it wasn't filling enough on its own.  I like garlic so next time I might double the amount.

target.recipe_text:
heidesand  my famous sugar cookies

these cookies never last out the day at work, church get-togethers or wherever i take them. i got this recipe back in high school in my german class and have been making them ever since. yummy!  they've become my annual blue ribbon winner at the local county fair.

1. cream butter or margarine and the sugars in a large bowl til fluffy
2. add egg and vanilla to butter / sugar mixture and blend well
3. in another bowl combine flour , cream of tartar , baking soda and salt
4. stir flour mixture into butter / sugar mixture til all is incorporated
5. form dough into 1-inch balls
6. roll balls of dough in sugar , place on an ungreased cookie sheet , and flatten
7. bake at 350 degrees for 10-15 minutes , until very lightly brown
target.review: These cookies are perfection, they kind of remind me of shortbread and sugar cookie mixed. Thanks for sharing :)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
oats  n honey granola pie

a pillsbury bake-off winner..enjoy the old-fashioned flavors of oats, brown sugar and walnuts in a pie filling that goes together in minutes.  please feel free to use your best crust recipe.

1. heat oven to 350f
2. place pie crust in 9-inch glass pie pan as directed on box for one-crust filled pie
3. in large microwavable bowl , microwave butter on high 50 to 60 seconds or until melted
4. stir in brown sugar and corn syrup until blended
5. beat in salt , vanilla and eggs
6. stir crushed granola bars , walnuts , oats and chocolate chips into brown sugar mixture
7. pour into crust-lined pan
8. bake 40 to 50 minutes or until filling is set and crust is golden brown
9. during last 15 to 20 minutes of baking , cover crust edge with strips of foil to prevent excessive browning
10. cool at least 30 minutes before serving
11. serve warm , at room temperature or chilled with whipped cream or ice cream
12. store in refrigerator
13. to easily crush granola bars , do not unwrap
14. use rolling pin to crush bars
demonstrations.review: This pie is delicious and so simple to make, my best friend ate over a fourth of it!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
low calorie apple cinnamon pancakes

these are my own creation, and since my boyfriend and i love pancakes we make them often!!

1. heat skillet and coat in cooking spray
2. combine ingredients in medium size bowl
3. ladle out 2 tbsp of batter per pancake and lightly brown each side of the cake
4. try leaving the very center gooey for a different texture and flavor
demonstrations.review: These pancakes were fabulous. I made the recipe for one and they turned out great,I loved how I didn't have to go out andbuy any ingredients! I will surely these make again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
better than sex aka texas dessert

this is my husbands favorite birthday dessert. a friend gave my mother this recipe years ago. i've known it as texas dessert, better than sex, as good as robert redford plus a few more that cannot be posted. great for valentines day too! for extra richness, use french vanilla cool whip.

1. mix together in processor the flour , chopped pecans and butter
2. spread into 9x13 pan and bake 15 minutes at 350
3. let cool completely
4. in medium bowl mix together cream cheese , powdered suar and cool whip
5. mix well
6. spread over cool crust
7. prepare vanilla pudding using only 1-3 / 4 cup milk
8. spread over cream cheese layer
9. prepare chocolate pudding using only 1-3 / 4 cup milk
10. spread over vanilla pudding layer
11. top with remaining cool whip
12. grate hersheys chocolate bar over the top
13. sprinkle with chopped pecans if desired
14. cover
15. chill overnight
demonstrations.review: My mom always makes this! It is so delicious.

target.recipe_text:
banana maple pecan bread muffins  gluten free

i bought a 20lb bag of bananas at krogers for $1.00 and have been trying to use them all up. this is one of the recipes i made in the process. it was by far the most scrumptious recipe that i made. it could also be made into a bread, but i made muffins. this is definitely my new default banana bread recipe! imade a double batch and ended up with 39 muffins. i made half with the called for maple syrup/pecan topping and half with a cream cheese topping. to make the cream cheese topping, i whipped 6oz cream cheese with 1/4 cup brown sugar and 1/4 cup maple syrup. these were absolutely heavenly fresh out of the oven. *for the gluten free flour, i used bette hagman's mix: 2 parts garfava bean flour, 1 part sorghum flour, 3 parts cornstarch, and 3 parts tapioca flour.

1. combine bananas with 1 / 3 cup maple syrup and 1 / 2 cup pecans
2. mix well and set aside
3. combine flour , xanthan gum , sugar , baking soda , salt , pumpkin pie spice , and dry buttermilk
4. alternatively if you do not have premixed pumpkin pie mix , use equal parts cinnamon , ginger and nutmeg
5. make a well in the center of the dry ingredients
6. combine eggs , oil , and water
7. pour into the center of the dry ingredients and stir with a wooden spoon just until dry ingredients are incorporated
8. use a spatula or knife to make three or four "troughs" in the dough / batter
9. spoon banana mixture into troughs
10. gently fold bananas into dough with knife
11. spoon dough into muffin cups
12. top with pecan-maple mixture
13. if using cream cheese frosting , coat tops of muffins after they are baked , not before
14. bake at 375 for 20 minutes
15. makes about 18 good sized muffins
target.review: These are awesome!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
gluten free pizza dough

a simple, straightforward gluten free pizza dough recipe.  also egg free!  from one of the mom's that raised me...thanks alice! omit the xanthan gum if your mix already includes it.

1. mix dry ingredients together and add oil and water , mixing well
2. pat onto lightly oiled pizza pan with hands
3. bake in pre-heated 425 oven for 20 minutes
4. add your choice of delicious toppings
5. bake another 15 minutes , or until cheese and crust start to get golden brown
6. enjoy !
demonstrations.review: Not bad considering the ingredient constraints! It puffed up in the oven then deflated as I added the toppings. I will be sharing this recipe with my food-allergic relatives. Thanks for posting this recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
absolutely the best gluten free peanut butter cookies

not just for the celiacs! i was skeptical, since the last recipe i tried was gritty, heavy and nasty.  these are light, rich and absolutely perfect.  i actually like these better than "regular" peanut butter cookies, and from a big fat momma, that's saying something!  adapted from catherine's recipe.

1. preheat oven to 375
2. make sure you have beaters that can handle thick batter
3. in a medium bowl , cream margarine and sugars
4. beat in egg and peanut butter
5. in a separate bowl , mix flours and baking soda evenly
6. add in two parts to wet ingredients , beating on med-high speed until thoroughly blended
7. roll dough into 1-inch balls , and place 2 inches apart onto ungreased baking sheet
8. you can press them with a fork if desired , but not necessary
9. bake 8-10 minutes
10. let cool 5 minutes before removing from baking sheet
demonstrations.review: These cookies are soft and wonderful. Just remember to bake them until barely browned. To cover the "beany" taste some complain of, I add 1 teaspoon of vanilla and 1/4 teaspoon of cinnamon to the recipe.  Perfection. Thanks so much for posting this recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
gluten free danish

wow! i just made these delicious danish's. not only were they fabulous, but they were really quick and easy to make!! although they don't have a flaky pastry taste like the gluten containing danish's, they have their own little marvalous taste.you won't be able to eat just one! you can make these with your favourite jam. i used a tablespoon of raspberry jam on each danish and drizzled some icing on top.

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees
2. combine all ingredients , mix well to removie all lumps
3. place approximately 1 / 4 cup of dough in a small oval on greased baking sheet
4. flatten down alittle
5. repeat until dough is used
6. make a small dent in the middle of the danish with your thumb for the filling
7. set aside
8. now take about 1 tablespoon of your favourite jam and spoon into the imprinted middle of each danish
9. bake for approximately 15 minutes , until golden brown
10. while danishes are baking prepare icing
11. use powdered sugar and water to make a runny icing , or prepare your favourite icing making it abit runny
12. when danishes are finished remove from oven and let cool alittle bit
13. then drizzle icing over danishes
demonstrations.review: I'm so glad I found this recipe; cream cheese danish is my fave. The one thing I did to make these from great to WOW - I swapped the 1/4 cup of potato starch for rice flour or another flour such as sorghum. They were less gummy this way. I used the back of a wet spoon to make a crater in the middle of the danish. More room to hold all the yummy filling. This is a keeper recipe.

target.recipe_text:
tsr version of dairy queen blizzard by todd wilbur

here's the recipe for the heath bar blizzard. this recipe is from todd wilbur's book top secret recipes. www.topsecretrecipes.com

1. freeze heath bar
2. break candy into pieces while still in the wrapper
3. combine all of the ingredients in a blender and blend on medium for 30 seconds or until well mixed
4. pour into a 16 oz glass
target.review: A really fun recipe! Made this last night for my hubby and my date night. I let him pick the candy bar (Reeses Peanut Butter Cup), and followed the recipe. Turned out so good! Will be making again with other candy bar flavors.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
ham chowder

creamy ham chowder. perfect for winter nights and quick dinners. this is another of my mother's geraldine lefever recipes she used while we were growing up. our children have loved it too!

1. cook onion in butter til soft , not brown
2. combine with all else , and heat
3. serve
demonstrations.review: Very yummy! Made a double batch so hubby could take some to work the next day...wasn't enough left!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
olive garden style chicken and gnocchi soup

this is very close to the olive garden soup. there's another recipe on the web, which was the basis of this recipe, however, i have changed it to use less cream. still tastes good! i did end up using a little cornstarch to thicken. i guess you could sub heavy cream for the half-and-half to make it a little thicker without using cornstarch. the gnocchi is usually in the spaghetti section of the grocery store.

1. saute the onion , celery , garlic , carrot in oil over medium heat until onion is translucent
2. add chicken , chicken stock , half and half , salt and pepper , thyme
3. heat to boiling , then add gnocchi
4. gently boil for 4 minutes , then turn down to a simmer for 10 minutes
5. add spinach and cook for another 1-2 minutes until spinach is wilted
6. ladle into bowls and serve !
demonstrations.review: Yum, yum, yum! So easy to make! I used canned sodium free chicken broth and left over rotisserie chicken. Turned out wonderful!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cinnamon quick bread

yummy and easy!  good with a cup of tea in the afternoon when energy levels are running low!

1. filling: mix and set aside
2. mix flour , baking soda , sugar , cinnamon and salt together , add all wet ingredients and mix well
3. pour 1 / 3 of batter into a greased loaf pan and sprinkle 1 / 3 of sugar / cinnamon topping over this
4. repeat twice more with layers of batter and sugar / cinnamon
5. bake at 350f for 50-60 minutes
6. cool for 5 minutes in pan then turn out to cool completely
demonstrations.review: This is definately a family favorite! So moist, so filling, and so delicious. No complaints from anyone, even the picky eater.

target.recipe_text:
rack of lamb

i made this for dinner last night and it was awesome. the baked breadcrumb topping mixture is to die for! recipe found on the internet.

1. sear rack of lamb all over in skillet that can be used in the oven
2. with food processor running , drop shallot and garlic into top tube and process until finely minced
3. add parsley and process until finely chopped
4. add pieces of fresh bread and process to fine crumbs
5. remove from processor to a bowl and mix in melted butter
6. pat bread crumb mixture onto top of rack of lamb
7. roast at 450 for 15 to 20 minutes
8. if crumbs brown too quickly , turn oven down to 425
9. test with oven thermometer until done to your liking
target.review: It's great when the hardest part of a recipe is 'frenching' the chops.  The topping was 'tops'. I didn't put all of it on the lamb -- I put the rest in the fry pan.  Into the oven it went.  We served it to the guests who raved over it.  Would I change anything -- no.  It is ideal as it is written.  Thanks for this one.  (PS.  Sorry to see that Food.com resorts to INTRUSIVE 'pop ups'.  So, negative ***** (stars) to them for cluttering our computer with unwelcome advertising.)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
lemon garlic chicken

yummy and tangy, very easy to do!

1. remove excess skin and fat from chicken , rinse and pat dry
2. in a small bowl combine oregano , seasoned salt and pepper , rub mixture onto chicken using all of the mixture
3. in a large skillet over medium heat brown chicken in the butter
4. transfer chicken to slow cooker
5. to the skillet add the water , lemon juice , garlic and chicken bouillion
6. stirring over medium heat bring mixture to a boil , loosening browned bits from the bottom of the skillet
7. pour over chicken , cover and cook on high for 2 1 / 2 to 3 hours or on low for 5 to 6 hours until chicken is almost tender
8. add parsley cover and cook on high for 15-30 minutes more !
demonstrations.review: A slow cooker recipe with a difference -- I had come to the conclusion slow cooker recipes meant a stew like dinner.  I was concerned at the start when there was not a lot of liquid in the pot.  Still, I went ahead.  The result is terrific!!!  Tasty chicken and a light 'jus' in the bottom of the pot.  All who had lunch with us today enjoyed the dish.  I will change nothing next time we make this one.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
egg and brown rice salad

found this recipe about 10 years ago in the "working woman's cookbook" it makes alot, and has been a hit at picnics.

1. rinse peas under cold water to separate
2. drain
3. in a very large bowl mix together peas , eggs , rice , celery , onion , cheese , and pimiento
4. in a small bowl combine mayonnaise , mustard , lemon juice , salt , pepper , and dill weed
5. toss with egg mixture
6. sprinkle with paprika
7. cover and refrigerate at least 4 hours , but no longer than 24 hours
demonstrations.review: Yum, yum, yum -- this salad recipe is a treat.  As reviewers suggest, it can be changed - and we did.  We used half the mayonnaise and omitted the peas.  We may adapt it further for our use.  So far, it impressed our family and a luncheon party.  Well done Kathy!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
roasted garlic mashed potatoes   the best you ve ever had

nan

1. separate head of garlic into individual cloves
2. toss in olive oil and wrap tightly in small piece of aluminum foil
3. bake in 350f oven for 45 minutes
