4. when the garlic has cooled to the touch you should be able to squeeze it out of the 'paper' shell of the individual cloves
5. mash the roasted garlic with a fork , or force through a fine strainer
6. if you use a ricer as recommended below , simply rice the garlic along with the potatoes
7. peel and boil potatoes in salted water until tender
8. force the cooked potatoes through a ricer or mash by your usual method
9. put the riced potatoes , garlic , sour cream , butter , and salt and white pepper in a mixer bowl , and whip at medium speed until smooth
10. add cream or milk to adjust consistency
demonstrations.review: Mimi.  You help to prove a winning recipe is easy to prepare and does not have packaged ingredients.  I am planning ahead to the next time we prepare this one!!!

target.recipe_text:
pork chops   southern style

simple, quick and tasty. something i threw together with the 'scraps' in my fridge and surprised me with how great it tasted. feel free to remove as much 'fat' from the pan as you need to... the more you leave, the better it tastes! great with mashed potatoes!

1. in 12" skillet , cook bacon on med hi heat
2. remove bacon from skillet , but leave bacon drippings
3. add 1 tbsp butter and diced onion
4. when transparent , remove from skillet
5. reduce heat to medium , lightly salt and pepper both sides of pork chops and place in skillet
6. brown both sides
7. chop up bacon , and add both bacon and cooked onion to skillet
8. add 3 / 4 cup water , 1 tbsp butter , cover and simmer until cooked
9. just before serving , mix 2 tbsp cornstarch with cool tap water
10. place pork chops on plates , add corn starch / water mixture to gravy / drippings in skillet and bring to quick boil stirring frequently to form thick gravy
target.review: Easy and tasty!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
spicy glazed almonds

everyone loves these almonds and they're very easy to make. i always use less cayenne and tabasco than called for but if you like heat use the full amounts. store in a freezer bag in the freezer. great for hostess gifts!

1. bring corn syrup , butter and water to a boil in a saucepan large enough to hold the almonds
2. stir in spices
3. add almonds and stir to coat
4. place on a parchment-lined rimmed baking sheet and bake at 275 degrees for 1 hour
5. stir every 15 minutes to distribute the glaze and separate the nuts
6. cool and break apart any nuts that are stuck together
demonstrations.review: Delicious!  Not too spicy.  Served on top of Nantucket Bleu Spinach Salad, #50875.  Balanced it perfectly and add just the right crunch.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
yes  virginia there is a great meatloaf

absolutely delicious meatloaf and sauce! those who claim they don't believe there can be such a thing as a great meatloaf will love this. based on a meatloaf given to me by a dear friend, virginia strehl, memphis, and leesburg, fla. nita holleman, 2000

1. meatloaf: combine meat loaf ingredients and place into a loaf baking dish
2. smooth out top
3. sauce: combine sauce ingredients and pour on top and sides of meatloaf
4. bake at 350f about 1 hour to 1 hour 15 minutes or until done
5. enjoy !
6. the addition of 1 or 2 teaspoons of kitchen bouquet makes this recipe very good
7. recipe should be"plump" from the addition of the milk or half & half
8. it should not be runny
9. a second batch of sauce served hot is good to serve with the meatloaf
10. nita's
11. it is wise to have some fat added to the deer -- especially to ground deer
12. maybe 25 % fat , , otherwise your results will be poor
13. i don't know about some of the other game meat some are using
14. please consult an expert
15. the recipe is delicious as it stands ! enjoy ! nita holleman
demonstrations.review: made this gf/df by using a slice of gf bread and soy milk.  nobody knew the difference.  my husband, who is not a ketchup eater, even liked the sauce

demonstrations.recipe_text:
leftover ham   cabbage casserole

this is a great meal in one dish. i have made this in advance, added buttered crumbs and reheated in a 350f the oven for 25 minutes.

1. saut the onion & cabbage in the melted butter , stir fry until translucent
2. add potatoes , garlic , wine salt & pepper , stir
3. add parsley & ham , mix well , cover
4. simmer 20 minutes or until the potatoes are tender
5. serve
demonstrations.review: Was a little skeptical at first, but this recipe really surprised me.  Followed the recipe with one exception, no potatoes.  Definitely agree with "highplainsdrifter" in that it should be called a hash and took their advice and served it with a poached egg.  My 9 yr old son was curious and asked for a taste, then another and finally got his own serving!

target.recipe_text:
glazed carrots for two

a yummy glazed carrot dish done in the microwave. add salt and pepper to taste, if you wish.

1. in a 3-cup casserole dish that's microwave-safe , whisk together the sugar , cornstarch and cinnamon
2. whisk in orange juice
3. add carrots and stir
4. dot with butter
5. cover dish with vented plastic wrap and microwave on high for 3 minutes
6. partially remove plastic and stir carrots
7. put plastic wrap back in place and microwave on high until carrots are crisp-tender , 2 to 4 minutes longer
8. this recipe can be cut in half to serve one , but cooking time will be shorter
target.review: Too sweet for my taste, but the cooked firmness of the carrots was nice.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
tender lemon parsleyed chicken  stove or oven

my quick and easy recipe for tender, juicy  chicken with a nice, light lemon flavor!

1. in deep frying pan with lid , melt butter over medium heat
2. add onion
3. add chicken pieces seasoned with salt and pepper , good side down
4. brown chicken
5. turn pieces over , sprinkle chicken with lemon juice , place on lid
6. reduce heat to a simmer
7. cook for about 40 minutes , stirring onions and turning chicken only once or twice as needed
8. or pour into a casserole dish , arrange chicken nicely , sprinkle with lemon juice and bake , covered , in a 350 oven for 45 minutes or til done
9. sprinkle chicken liberally with parsley and recover during last 2 minutes
demonstrations.review: Super recipe, proves simple can be the best way to go, wonderful depth to the flavors. I added a sprig of rosemary to mine as well, very tasty and doesn't need a lot of salt; the lemon flavors it nicely which is nice for people who are watching their salt intake. I also started this in the same pan that I cooked my onions in...at the last minute I turned the heat up to high on the burner and then seared both sides of the chicken (I used breasts) to lightly brown them and then finished it in the casserole dish in the oven. Mother-in-law also raved about it and husband says he wants it again. Thank you!!!!!!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
lois  cole slaw

my mother made this for a side for her thanksgiving dinner in 2007.  the best part of the meal - honestly.  i highly recommend letting it sit overnight for best flavor.

1. mix mayonnaise and sugar together
2. pour over shredded cabbage and bacon pieces
3. toss in the cashews
4. mix
5. best if served the next day
demonstrations.review: Really quick, easy and tasty, I really liked it. I added shredded carrots and raisins to mine as well to make up for less sugar and a bit of lemon juice. Also added salted shelled sunflower seeds and a bit of pepper. Delicious.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chicken cutlet supreme

this is a delicious and easy to make dish which goes well with a variety of side dishes.

1. remove cutlets from package and season with salt , pepper , and paprika
2. lightly flour each chicken breast
3. dip cutlet into egg mixture and allow excess to fully drip off
4. dip into cornflake crumbs
5. can be fried on heated pan with oil or baked on a lightly greased pan at 375 degrees for 35-40 minutes
6. either way , delicious
7. enjoy !
demonstrations.review: Very nice, came out well, very crispy and chicken was done just right. I did have to crush about 1 1/2 times more corn flakes to cover the cutlets so don't skimp or you'll end up doing it with batter-coated fingers. I baked it in the oven to save the fat and calories of pan frying. Like one of the other reviews states, it is dry with the corn flake coating and the white meat...it definitely needed gravy or some kind of sauce on it -pasta sauce & cheese was suggested & I think that would be wonderful. I had a jar of Boston Market roasted turkey gravy and heated that up and it definitely helped take away some of the dryness. Anyhow, all said, it's a very healthy and wonderful meal, I served mine w/white rice & steamed vegetables.

target.recipe_text:
toll house butterscotch chip cookies

these are my absolute favorite cookie. ever. i have licked many a beater after mixing these cookies up. they are of course from the back of the toll house package.

1. mix together the flour , salt and baking soda in a small bowl , set aside
2. cream the sugars and butter together , add the vanilla
3. add the eggs one at a time
4. slowly add the flour mixture
5. when completely mixed , add the butterscotch chips
6. drop by the spoonful onto an ungreased cookie sheet
7. bake 8-10 minutes at 375f degrees
target.review: Very good!! I used 1 cup butterscotch chips and 1 cup chocolate chips and everyone loved them!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
best pumpkin cookies

what can i say about these amazing pumpkin cookies... they are absolutely delicious! let me put it this way. i baked these every year at thanksgiving time for my job. my co-workers would come up to me two months in advance to make sure i was making them. one girl who resigned actually called me and asked what day i was bringing them in so that she could stop by - just for these cookies! another co-worker said she didn't even like pumpkin, but she loved these. the consistency is more cake-like than cookie. the glaze on top of these cookies is fabulous! at least, i think so. i noticed a few of you who rated this recipe said it was too sweet. that is why i suggested it may be omitted, or if you wish, use your own icing. lots of you have added nutmeg.. hey, make it all your own. that's what this is all about! : )

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees
2. have ready some ungreased baking sheets
3. in a large mixing bowl , cream butter and the sugars together until light and fluffy
4. blend in pumpkin , egg and vanilla extract
5. in separate bowl , stir together flour , baking soda , baking powder , cinnamon , nutmeg and salt
6. mix flour mixture into butter-sugar mixture
7. drop tablespoonfuls 3 inches apart on ungreased baking sheets
8. bake the cookies for 10-12 minutes until golden around the edges
9. remove warm cookies and transfer to racks
10. let cool completely for a least one half hour , then frost with glaze
11. for glaze:
12. in a medium saucepan , heat butter and brown sugar over medium heat until bubbly
13. cook , stirring constantly , for one minute or until slightly thickened
14. beat in the milk
15. blend in confectioner's sugar until the glaze is smooth and spreadable
16. using a silicone basting brush , which i love and use religiously now , or a butter knife to spread glaze on cookies is the best
17. please
18. i suggest that you keep the saucepan over the stove on the lowest heat possible to prevent it from hardening
demonstrations.review: Wow! These are so good! Definitely love the glaze. I used 2 cups confectioners suger. These are really nice and soft and I can't wait to make again!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
miss daisy s deviled eggs

these are the best deviled eggs i have ever tried. i usually have to double this recipe because they are gone almost as soon as i put them out.

1. cut eggs in half lengthwise , remove yolks , and reserve whites
2. mash yolks until smooth
3. combine yolks , mayo , worcestershire sauce , mustard , salt , pepper , and mix until smooth
4. stir in onion , and pickle relish
5. spoon mixture into center of egg whites
6. sprinkle tops with paprika
demonstrations.review: Very good! Didn't change a thing and everyone loved them! I will definitely makes these again :)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
creamy potato salad

have you ever posted a recipe and just love reading the reviews for it?  this is my signature potato salad.  whenever there is a pot luck function at work, i am told that i have to bring the potato salad.  no one else is allowed to and i am never given a choice.  thank you everyone who ever tried this potato salad and for leaving such glowing reviews for it.  you all have made me look so good.  i personally can not stand eggs or raw onions, so i leave them out but i know most people don't think a potato salad is complete without them.  thanks again for so many wonderful reviews. (psssst....check out my recipe #123107 as well.  it shares the dressing with this recipe but tastes much much different because of the different ingredients) please see recipe #242966 for bacon bit tips.

1. cook potatoes in boiling , salted water until tender
2. drain well
3. peel and cube potatoes
4. transfer to a large bowl
5. add celery , onion , sweet relish and bacon bits
6. combine mayo , sugar , celery seed , vinegar , mustard , and salt
7. add mayo mixture to potatoes
8. toss lightly to coat potato mixture
9. carefully fold in the chopped eggs
10. cover and chill thoroughly
11. bacon bit
12. use a sharp knife and cut the frozen bacon into long strips about 1 / 4 inch wide
13. turn the bacon and cut the strips into pieces also about 1 / 4 in wide
14. you now have perfect raw bacon pieces to fast fry
15. no need to separate
16. they will separate during cooking
17. perfect bacon bits
demonstrations.review: This was very yummy! I didn't use celery or onion because I dislike them but it was still a big hit at our 4th of July bbq.

target.recipe_text:
scalloped asparagus casserole

this asparagus casserole is baked with white sauce, made with cheese and a topping of buttered bread crumbs. i found this recipe at southernfoods.com and was impressed that it was so easy to make as well as tasty.

1. wash asparagus , remove woody part of stalks and cut into 2 1 / 2-inch pieces
2. cook asparagus in boiling salted water until just tender
3. drain and place in a shallow baking dish or casserole
4. melt 2 tablespoons butter in saucepan
5. mix 2 tablespoons of the butter with the soft bread crumbs
6. set aside for topping casserole later
7. blend flour , salt , and pepper into remaining butter in saucepan
8. continue cooking and stirring over low heat
9. gradually add milk , stirring until thickened
10. add worcestershire sauce , red pepper , and cheese
11. stir until cheese is melted
12. pour sauce over asparagus in casserole
13. top with buttered crumbs
14. bake at 350 for 20 minutes or until bubbly
target.review:
This was pretty good... my DH went for seconds and my picky 6 year old even ate it.

I modified it a bit.  I used 1 lb of fresh asparagus, 4 tbsp butter total, 1 cup milk (1%) and substituted mozzarella for the cheddar.  I also sprinkled in some seasoning salt to the milk mixture before pouring it on top of the asparagus.  I'm not a huge asparagus fan so that's why only 4 stars.  Overall it was good and I will make again.  It's a good way to disguise the vegetables.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
take out fried rice

i was very impressed with this fried rice recipe. the flavour is wonderful, and it's so easy to make, why order take-out?
i serve it with recipe #137627.

1. in a large skillet heat the sesame oil
2. add the celery , carrots , onions , and garlic stirring while cooking to tender crisp
3. stir in the frozen peas and ham or pork , continue to stir and cook until vegetables have softened
4. lower the heat and add the beaten egg , stirring until it is finely scrambled
5. add the soya sauce , and rice , blend well
6. splash a little more sesame oil over the rice if necessary
demonstrations.review:
This recipe is a keeper.

I made it with brown rice, green onions and omitted the ham/pork.  DS had 3 servings and DD also liked it but picked out the peas.

I used 1 cup of raw brown rice and it  made slightly more than the 1 1/2 cups of cooked rice the recipe calls for.  I used all of the cooked rice and kept the same measurements for the veggies and it turned out perfect.  I will definitely make this again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
wonderful parmesan zucchini strips

this was from a granny's coupon. we had it last night and it is another zucchini hit!

1. preheat oven to 450 degrees
2. in a bowl , combine bread crumbs and cheese topping
3. dip zucchini strips into egg , then into crumb mixture
4. place on baking sheet coated with nonstick cooking spray
5. bake at 450 degrees for 20-25 minutes or until golden brown and tender
demonstrations.review: Served this last night with pasta.  I used Progresso Italian bread crumbs and added some garlic powder.  I thought they were on the salty side.  Next time I'll use plain bread crumbs and add italian seasonings myself.  Overall we enjoyed these.  My son (10) was not thrilled but my 6 year old daughter liked them.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
creamy garlic penne pasta

this is a delicious, super quick side or main dish. i got it from the back of a pasta box and it is yummy!

1. melt butter and add garlic in a medium sauce pan
2. cook over medium for 1 minute
3. add flour and cook 1 minute , stirring constantly
4. stir in broth and milk and cook , stirring frequently , until sauce boils and thickens
5. add parsley , salt , pepper and cheese
6. stir until cheese is melted
7. toss hot pasta with sauce and serve immediately
demonstrations.review: Served this last night with zucchini strips, a green salad and garlic bread.  I enjoyed this as I am not a red sauce fan.  This is basically fettucini alfredo.  I made as directed except for using olive oil in place of the butter.  Next time I would add more garlic and double the sauce.  I found that the pasta absorbed most of the sauce after sitting for a few minutes.  Overall, a quick and easy meal and one that I will make again.

target.recipe_text:
cannellini florentine

found this recipe in a coupon insert in the newspaper. it is from the kitchen of bush's best beans. i have not made this recipe yet, but when i do, i think i will use a 10 oz. box of frozen chopped spinach that i will thaw and squeeze dry because i am not a big fan of canned spinach. with the chill of autumn and winter coming, this soup sounds like it will be really tasty. would probably be nice served with corn bread.

1. brown bacon over high heat in large stockpot , about 8 minutes
2. add garlic and onion , saute 6 minutes
3. add spinach , saute 2 minutes
4. add beans and all remaining ingredients
5. simmer 10 minutes
6. garnish and serve
target.review: Most excellent. Whole family enjoyed. I will make this again. Thank you so much. Jim

demonstrations.recipe_text:
roasted red potatoes

these are delicious with chicken or beef, and very easy to prepare. easy enough for weeknights but special enough for company.

1. preheat oven to 375 degrees
2. spray 13x9 dish with cooking spray
3. slice potatoes fairly thin and place in dish
4. drizzle with olive oil
5. toss to coat
6. sprinkle italian seasoning and parmesan cheese on top
7. bake for 45 minutes or until golden brown
demonstrations.review: Very nice recipe. Thanks

demonstrations.recipe_text:
the ultimate salmon fillets

living on the west coast, we have eaten a great deal of salmon. this is absolutely the best way we have found to cook it. it is so moist and the flavor is fantastic! many reviewers have said that they think the cheese, especially the cheddar is unnecessary, and i have to admit that i omit the cheddar cheese myself. the flavour is a little too strong and it is extra fat that is not needed. i do like the sprinkling of parmesan with the paprika because it looks so nice when it is broiled. using light mayonnaise and light sour cream or yogurt tastes just as good as the full fat versions and cuts down fat and calories even more. thanks for all the great reviews!

1. preheat oven to 450 degrees
2. if frozen , partially thaw fillets and cut into serving size pieces
3. place in a greased baking dish
4. combine sour cream or yogurt , mustard , onion , dill , and mayonnaise
5. season with salt and pepper
6. spread mixture over fish
7. bake 20 minutes per inch of thickness of fish if frozen or 10-12 minutes if thawed
8. when just done , sprinkle with the cheeses and a dash of paprika
9. broil 1 minute or until the cheese is bubbly and flecked with brown
10. serve with lemon wedges
demonstrations.review: The whole family loved this one. Top notch. Thanks so much for posting. Jim

demonstrations.recipe_text:
saucy tomato pork chops

got this one from an old president's choice magazine. good anytime.

1. in large skillet over medium-high heat , melt margarine
2. brown chops 3 minutes on each side
3. remove from skillet
4. set aside
5. pour off fat
6. in same skillet , saut mushrooms with garlic until liquid is evaporated
7. stir in soup , water , thyme , oregano and balsamic vinager or honey
8. bring to boil
9. return chops to skillet
10. reduce heat to low
11. cover
12. simmer 25 to 30 minutes or until tender , stirring occasionally
13. serve with noodles
14. garnish with parsley
demonstrations.review: Most excellent. Easy to prepare for a novice such as myself. The family loved it. Thanks. Jim from Michigan.

target.recipe_text:
to die for crock pot pork chops

i make this for my husband and daughter, and i have got nothing but smiles from this.  it's easy, cheap and oh so yummy!

1. combine cream of mushroom soup , 1 / 3 can water , softened cream cheese and garlic in a bowl
2. stir out most of the lumps , but the rest will cook out
3. pour in bottom of crock pot
4. put pork chops on top of mixture
5. add liberal amounts of salt and pepper
6. i'm usually heavy handed !
7. cook on low for 7-8 hours
8. serve over slices of warm bread or pasta of your choice
9. pork chops will fall apart
10. so tender you can cut with a spoon !
target.review: Made this tonight and it got a thumbs up from DD. I used Campbells Cream of Mushroom with Roasted Garlic Soup and added some diced onion as well. The gravy was actually a bit too thick so I added nearly a cup of milk at the very end to loosen it up a bit. Turned out perfect. Served it over mashed potatoes and just broke the pork chops up in the gravy. Next time, I will cut back to about 2/3 a block of cream cheese and add sliced mushrooms as well.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
caramel corn on the cob seasoned with chipotle peppers

yes, i use prepared caramel ice cream toppers to give this sweetness and to kick it up chipotle pepper. this will please children and adults!

1. place corn in a very large piece of heavy duty foil or each one can have separate foils
2. pour butter over corn to coat each cob and to butter the foils
3. sprinkle minced peppers over some all or none ot the corn
4. pour caramel evenly over the cobs
5. seal foil around corn tightly
6. grill over hot coals for 5-8 minutes turning a couple of times
7. season with salt and top with additional caramel if you like
demonstrations.review: This was a great twist to my favorite summertime veggie (roasted corn).  I like my food to have a kick of spice, but I have to admit that just the chipoltle was WAY too much heat for my taste.  The adobo sauce had absorbed a lot of heat itself, so I ended up using a bit of the adobo sauce with the butter.  I still ended up with a nice spice.  I also had made fresh salsa that day, and added my leftover chopped cilantro to the corn packets.  YUM!  Will definitely make this again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mock chicken fried steak with milk gravy

my mother made these for us four girls. money was tight and she couldn't afford steak very often. these use ground beef. i use a 80/20 lean to fat. you can use ground round but it tends to be a little too dry. this is great with mashed potatoes. everyone i have ever made it for loved it. the first time my dh had it he never knew it was ground beef. he just commented on the tenderness of the steak!

1. mix 2 cups flour with salt and pepper
2. shape ground beef into four thin patties
3. dip patties into flour , then beaten egg , then flour again
4. put shortening , oil or lard into a heavy skillet over medium high heat
5. when a little flour sprinkled into skillet begins to sizzle , add patties
6. cook for about 5 minutes per side
7. remove and drain on paper towels
8. to make gravy:
9. remove all but four tablespoons of fat from skillet
10. stir in 4 tablespoons of dredging flour and 1 / 4 teaspoon salt
11. stir , scraping up browned bits , for about one minute till light brown
12. whisk in milk gradually
13. whisk until thick and bubbly
14. remove from heat
15. add 1 / 2 teaspoon black pepper or to taste
16. stir well
demonstrations.review: This was SO easy and very tasty! I loved how tender it was compared to using cube steak. The gravy was delicious. I seasoned my meat with some Montreal Steak Seasoning before making the patties and otherwise followed the recipe exactly. My DD is picky and she raved "Oh Mom, this is SOOOO good!" Anything that pleases her pleases me.. 5 stars! :D

demonstrations.recipe_text:
shrimp scampi with pasta alfredo

it just doesn't get any easier than this! not including the marinating and pasta water heating time, dinner is on the table in ten minutes. my family has been passing around this little jewel of a recipe for a couple of years and i usually make it about twice a month. i just eyeball the amount of ingredients, so use your own judgment if things don't look right. to make it even easier, i usually prepare the raw shrimp/marinade mixture in ziploc bags and stuff them in the freezer for super-quick mid-week dinners (i cook the shrimp without thawing them-justs takes a minute or two longer). my mom likes to add 1/2 teaspoon of dry mustard to her marinade, but i omit it due to personal preference.

1. marinate the shrimp in the other ingredients until you are ready for them
2. thirty minutes before you are ready to serve , start heating the pasta water and place the half-and-half and butter in a large serving bowl to soften
3. put a large skillet over high heat to get it really hot
4. when the pasta is about three minutes away from being done , dump the shrimp and marinade into the hot skillet
5. toss the shrimp around as they cook
6. once the shrimp are pink and curled-up , remove the skillet from the heat
7. drain the pasta and dump it into the serving bowl with the half-and-half and butter
8. add the parmesan cheese , a pinch of salt and a few grinds of black pepper and toss together gently
9. pour the shrimp and sauce over the top and serve immediately
demonstrations.review: LOVED the shrimp! I used 1/2 of the salt it called for and it didn't seem to need any more.I have my own recipe for Alfredo, but  I did try this one the first time and it was easy and tasted good. The shrimp is the star though. I now use this as my go to marinade for lots of shrimp dishes. I also love the idea another reviewer had..double the marinade, finish with about 3T of butter, and toss the whole thing with some angel hair pasta. It's AMAZING, and I've made it countless times since I first tried it.

target.recipe_text:
cinnamon chocolate chip banana bread

a delicious adaption of traditional banana bread, decided to make it for my mom for mother's day, first time ever making it, and everyone loved it. best bananas to use to this recipe is right before you would normally throw them away, when the skins are turning black.

1. peel the bananas , cutting out any of the bruised or brown spots on the banana themselves
2. place them in a large bowl
3. take a potato masher and mash the bananas until very well mushed
4. take both sugars and add to the bowl
5. stir the mixture to coat the mushed bananas really well with the sugar
6. place in the refrigerator for 20 minutes
7. preheat the oven to 350f add the applesauce and eggs to the banana sugar mixture and beat well
8. add the remaining ingredients and mix well
9. i use an 8x8 glass dish for this recipe your welcome to use the traditional 9x5 loaf pan
10. grease the pan or dish you decide to use with olive oil spray
11. pour in the mixture and bake for about 35-40 mins and check with a toothpick to see if it is ready
12. if it is not due to different ovens , place back in the oven for 5 minute increments until done
13. cool it for about 15 minutes and its ready to enjoy !
target.review:
Wow! This is delicious. Moist and rich. I added some walnuts, too. The batter was too much for my loaf pan, so I used the excess to make 6 muffins.
So good and banana-y and chocolatey!
Thanks for sharing.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kahlua baked brie appetizer

a quick and easy appetizer. if you like brie, you will love this recipe.

1. spread pecans in a 9" pie plate
2. microwave on high 4 to 6 minutes , stirring every 2 minutes until toasted
3. add kahlua and sugar
4. stir well
5. remove rind from top of brie and discard rind
6. place brie on microwave safe plate
7. spoon pecan mixture over top of brie
8. microwave , uncovered , at high for 1 to 1 1 / 2 minutes or until soft , turning halfway through cooking
9. serve with melba rounds or crackers
demonstrations.review:
yum!
Popular appetizer!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mulled wine

a favourite winter drink

1. in a large stainless steel stockpot , combine all ingredients
2. place over medium heat and bring to a simmer
3. reduce heat to very low and keep warm for about 30 minutes to let the flavours blend
4. strain out the cloves and the cinnamon before serving
5. ladle in to heatproof cups
demonstrations.review: I served this sweet and spicy mulled wine at an Arbonne/Angela's Adornments party and everyone loved it! Now I've had a request to bring it to another party.  Excellent!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
stardust chocolate pancakes

these are just heavenly!

1. in a small bowl , combine milk , egg and butter
2. whisk until blended
3. in another bowl , combine flour , cocoa powder , sugar , baking soda and salt
4. mix well
5. add milk mixture
6. whisk just until dry ingredients are moistened
7. heat griddle over medium heat until hot
8. for each pancake , pour scant 1 / 4 cup batter into griddle
9. cook 1-2 minutes or until batter is set around edges
10. carefully turn over pancake
11. cook 1-2 minutes or until pancakes are cooked through
12. repeat with remaining batter
13. sprinkle pancakes with powdered sugar
14. serve warm with desired toppings
15. try using metal star shaped cookie cutters !
demonstrations.review:
So delicious and chocolatey (but not too much!) moist and fluffy.  My family loved them.
I added overripe, mashed bananas to mine and mmm heaven.
Thanks for sharing this delicious recipe!

target.recipe_text:
herbed carrot and beet salad

low calorie, low sodium, non fat with "high" vitamins and high flavor. this salad is best if it is allowed time for the flavors to marry. recipe from, "the mayo clinic williams sonoma cookbook."

1. in a bowl , combine the carrots , beets , garlic , and cilantro
2. add the rice vinegar and toss to mix well
3. cover and refrigerate for at least 1 hour to allow the flavors to marry
4. to serve , toss well and divide among individual plates
target.review: I had to use canned beets, because the beets at the store didn't look to happy!  This turned out really well none the less...I cannot wait to make them with raw beets too!  I will update once that happens!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
spanish dinner salad  ensalata de marina

i spent last summer with a family in madrid and every night without fail, we had this salad.  i have not had the typical american dinner salad since i've been back and all my friends request it as well.  even my boyfriend, who swore he could never give up his ranch dressing, has yet to go back.  very simple yet delicious.  enjoy.

1. in a large salad bowl , cut up the tomatoes and add the sliced onions
2. add bag of romaine lettuce
3. add avocado and the entire can of tuna , with the olive oil
4. if i only have tuna with regular vegetable oil , i usually drain out as much of the oil as i can before adding the tuna
5. sprinkle a couple pinches of sea salt over the salad
6. douse with balsamic vinegar and olive oil
7. i have never measured the amount , so whatever suits your tastes
8. i usually use more vinegar than oil since the tuna has olive oil
9. toss well and serve
demonstrations.review: I spent last summer in Spain as well, and frankly I started making tuna salads with lemon juice instead of balsamic, but the rest was the same.  The only thing I miss is their tuna in sunflower oil!  You can even add a few olives stuffed with anchovies or just chop up manzilla olives!  Tastes great!  Thanks for posting greenlove00!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mean chef s sauteed mushrooms

i adopted this recipe from  mean chef.

1. in a large skillet , heat the oil over high heat
2. add the mushrooms
3. do not move the mushrooms until they have caramelized on the bottom
4. if you toss them too soon , they will release their liquid and begin to steam
5. when the bottoms are caramelized , toss them and continue to cook for about 5 minutes
6. add the butter and continue to cook and toss for 5 minutes , until beautifully browned
7. season with salt and pepper
8. add the garlic
9. saute another 2 minutes , and add the thyme and lemon juice
10. cook to evaporate the liquid
11. add the wine and reduce until the mushrooms are glazed with the sauce
12. toss in the parsley and serve immediately
demonstrations.review: This is my 2nd time making them and frankly, we are mushroom eaters and they are absolutely fantastic!  The technique makes it, so others...be sure to follow it to the T first!  If you want to make changes be sure to do it after you try this method.  The only thing I can say is the thyme is a tad too much for us, but 1/4 teaspoon works just fine.  Also, the lemon (even though I love it!) is not necessary.  Thanks Bekah for adopting and thanks to Mean Chef.  I wonder what happened to him...I never got that story!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
extremely healthy fiber packed zucchini carrot cranberry bars

this is a recipe i came up with myself after getting sick of on the run meals and i wanted to make something that would keep well during the day and energize me--while also giving me the fiber, veggies, and nutrition i need. a bar for quick snack to tide you over or even a few "bars" for a meal replacement. 
obviously i like being healthy, so if you like the bread bar sweeter then use 3/4 cup of both brown and white sugar. this is good served warm with a slice of fat free cream cheese, cottage cheese, or even honey.

1. preheat the oven to 350 degrees f
2. spray a cake pan with nonstick cooking spray
3. mix together milk with lemon juice
4. set aside for 5 minutes
5. beat egg well , then add brown sugar , sugar , oil and beat together again
6. add in vanilla , zucchini , carrots , cranberries and the milk and lemon mixture
7. mix together well
8. put the flour , cinnamon , baking soda , salt and nuts if you added any in another bowl
9. mix them together
10. add the dry mixture with the wet mixture , mix together until just combined
11. spoon the mixture into the oiled pan and sprinkle some cinnamon sugar mixture onto the top if desired
12. bake for about 35-40 minutes or until wooden stick inserted into the middle comes out clean and the bars are not sticky in the middle
13. turn off the oven but don't open the oven or take the pan out , just leave it in there for 5 minutes if you like the outside crispy
14. don't overbake , they become really dry and hard
demonstrations.review: I am a student as well and my friends as well as professors loved these (I used them as the guinea pigs)!  I actually used equal instead of the white sugar and granulated brown sugar and loosely packed them and did not use peanut butter but did use almonds.  Also, I used pumpkin pie spice instead of cinnamon and it was great!  Full of energy, tastes great and is healthy for you!  Great job!

target.recipe_text:
reese s peanut butter squares  no bake

tastes like reese's peanut butter cups!

1. in a bowl mix all ingredients together except chocolate chips and shortening
2. press the mixture into a 9 x 13-inch baking pan
3. in microwave melt the chocolate chips and shortening until melted
4. remove and stir until smooth
5. spread the melted chocolate evenly over top
6. cool until firm
7. cut into squares
target.review: You are evil Kittencal!!These were sooooo good.Extremely easy to make,great for kids to do.Very peanutty and yummy.Like a peanut butter fudge.Thank you!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
honey mustard crock pot chicken

super easy to make and a fantastic family or entertaining dinner if served with fluffy white rice and some buttered sugar snap peas. makes great next-day leftovers.

1. mix all the sauce ingredients together in a bowl or pyrex measuring cup
2. pour over chicken in the slow cooker
3. cover and cook on low for 8-10 hours
demonstrations.review: yummy,very tasty and easy.I recommend this for an easy crockpot meal.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
whatever floats your boat  brownies

these are absolutely the chewiest, moistest, fudgiest brownies ever! i have tried adding so many different things to the batter, and they always comes out great.  they are also great without any add-ins! but by varying the add-ins, you can make different brownies every week (or day!!) super easy prep! so, add "whatever floats your boat" and you will not believe how yummy they come out :) oh, and the recipe doubles just fine--use a 9 x 13 inch pan instead and add a few more minutes of baking!

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. grease an 8 inch square pan or line with foil
3. in a medium bowl combine melted butter and cocoa and stir until cocoa is dissolved
4. add sugar and mix well
5. add eggs one at a time and stir until well combined
6. stir in vanilla , flour and salt until you no longer see any flour
7. fold in "whatever floats your boat" !
8. spread in pan and bake for approximately 25 minutes
9. do not over-bake -- your brownies will come out dry
10. adjust time / temp accordingly for your oven
11. if you do the knife / toothpick test , it should come out with moist crumbs , not clean
12. cool completely before cutting into squares
13. for vegetarian omit the marshmallows
14. for double recipe , bake in 9x12 pan and add 5 minutes to baking time
demonstrations.review: very very good.I didn't add anything and these were awesome.Next time I'll add some stuff.Thank you for a fab recipe!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
easy cheesy fondue

the best way to get your kids to eat their broccoli.  this is great for every day,special occasions, an even large groups. my kids get so exited when they find out this is for dinner. there are six of us so i always double it.

1. in sauce pan , melt butter
2. stir in salt , flour , pepper , mustard , and worcestershire sauce until smooth
3. gradually add milk
4. bring to a boil , cook and stir 2 minutes or until thick
5. reduce heat , add cheese , cook and stir till melted
6. rub fondue pan well with garlic clove
7. then transfer fondue , keep warm
8. serve with: cubed ham , broccoli , apples , cubed breads , and any other meat or veggie you prefer
demonstrations.review: Fantastic!My son LOVES fondue and is the one thing he will definately eat with no problem,he gave this recipe the thumbs up.Thanks

target.recipe_text:
awesome baked ham

i love this recipe because it is so easy and it calls for hardly any ingredients, and i always have these ingredients in my pantry. this recipe came from a good friend's mother, who was always asked to bake the ham for get-togethers and family dinners. now i get those requests. people who ordinarily aren't too fond of ham rave over this one. after i carve, i spoon a little of the glaze over the meat in the platter - yummmm!

1. in a medium size mixing bowl , mix yellow mustard and brown sugar until you have a thick"paste"
2. take all wrappers off of ham and trim away excess fat
3. line baking pan with aluminum foil
4. place ham on foil and spread brown sugar / mustard paste on top
5. fold and seal foil
6. do not open again until ham is done
7. bake at 350 for 4 hours
8. let set for about 1 hr then carve
9. one of the best tasting hams you will ever have !
target.review: I know this recipe doesn't need another rating but I just had to.  It was so good.  I roasted a 16 pound ham in an electric roaster for about 4 1/2 hours.  The ham was juicy and very flavorful.  I scored the ham before I put the paste on it and that helped the flavor infuse into the ham.  I will make this again for sure.  I fed about 40 people and everyone loved it.  No one comlplained about dry tasteless ham.  Thanks for an easy winner!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
peanutty caramel bars

people can't get enough of these! i got this recipe from the oct/nov 2001 taste of home.

1. in a large bowl , heat caramels , water and 1 / 2 cup peanut butter on high for 1 minute , stir
2. microwave 1-2 minutes longer or until melted
3. add cereal and peanuts
4. stir until coated
5. spread into a greased 13x9x2-in pan
6. set aside
7. in another bowl , heat chips , butter and remaining peanut butter on high for 30-60 seconds or until melted
8. spread over cereal mixture
9. chill before cutting
demonstrations.review: These are awesome.  I took them to an all day scrapbooking event I hosted and everyone loved them.  This is a keeper!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crock pot cheeseburgers

i make these for dh and friends for football sunday's. they love them. they are very easy to make and everybody can help themselves and add their own condiments. serve with chips and plenty of cold beer! they are sure to disappear! i leave the green peppers out since i hate them! this is a great recipe to take to a potluck and can easily be doubled.

1. in a large skillet over medium heat , brown ground beef with green pepper , onion and black pepper until beef is cooked through
2. drain off excess fat and transfer beef to a 3 1 / 2 to 5-quart crock pot
3. add all other ingredients except hamburger buns , lettuce and tomato
4. cover and cook on low for 5 to 7 hours
5. serve the beef on toasted sandwich buns with an assortment of condiments
demonstrations.review: I thought this was a great recipe.  I served it to about 25 people during a youth devotional at our home.  Everyone loved it.  I did take the advise from the other reviews and added several spices with some worestershire sauce and upped the velveeta to about 8 oz.  Very different from the plain old sloppy joe.  I will make this again!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
suzanne s caramel oatmeal bars

i received these from my christmas bake exchange and i just love these little treats! thanks suzanne for sharing the recipe with me.

1. press half of oatmeal mixture into a 9 x 13 pan bake at 350 for 10 to 15 minutes
2. remove from oven and sprinkle on enough chocolate chips to cover
3. then top with caramel mixture , then remaining oatmeal mixture
4. bake another 15-18 minutes
5. cool and cut
demonstrations.review: These are the best ever!!  I have made them twice already!  These will be my go-to dessert for any type of pot luck occasion.  Thanks!!

target.recipe_text:
stuffed turban squash

very savory and makes for a very hearty side dish.

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. cut the top off the turban squash , as you would for a jack-o-lantern type pumpkin
3. scoop out seeds and pulp and discard
4. place turban squash , cut sides down , on an oiled or foil covered baking sheet , and cover with more foil
5. roast for 50-60 minutes or until tender
6. scoop out tender pulp from cavity of squash
7. in a saucepan , saute onions , celery , sausage and diced carrot in butter until vegetables are tender
8. drain any fat
9. mix in brown sugar , bread crumbs , salt , pepper , and cooked squash
10. stir until well-mixed
11. spoon filling lightly into the cavity of the turban squash , and cover with the top
12. place extra filling into a separate dish
13. bake squash and any extra filling for 20-25 minutes or until heated through
14. serve hot
target.review: Thanks Sue. I have been looking for something to do with winter squash. This was fantastic! I didn't have the turban so I used a buttercup squash and I used maple flavored sausage. The turban must have a thicker rind because it fell apart and I just mixed it in a bowl and put it in a small cassarole. I did everything else the same.  Thank you again I definetly will make this again. Bonnie

demonstrations.recipe_text:
laurel s marinated mushrooms  easy canning

i've been making these for more than 20 years. i usually give them in holiday gift baskets, and if i don't, then i'm in trouble! not only are they delicious tasting, they are very pretty, too! only one thing about this recipe is that you have to find tiny mushrooms, 1-1/4 inch or less across, and that might not be easy. our fred meyer store sells them, and when i'm ready to can them, i just pick up the whole case out of the produce section and plop it in my cart! this recipe came from my county exchange master canner, 1989.

1. wash mushrooms and cut stems even with caps
2. bring water and lemon juice to boil , add mushrooms and boil 5 minutes
3. drain
4. mix oil , vinegar , oregano , basil and salt
5. stir in onions and pimiento , and bring to boil
6. in hot , sterilized 1 / 2-pint jars , put 1 clove garlic , 2 peppercorns , and pack with mushrooms
7. add stirred , well-mixed oil-vinegar solution , leaving 1 / 2 inch head space
8. wipe rims , cover with sterilized lids and rings
9. process in boiling water bath 20 minutes
10. let sealed jars sit undisturbed for 24 hours
11. allow 6 weeks for full flavor to develop
demonstrations.review:
I found a really good deal on mushrooms and had saved this recipe for "future use". We loved it. I definetly will be making this again. Thank you for this post.
Bonnie P

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chicken pesto

this was my daughter's favorite dish (along with some of her friends). she enjoyed it so much that we had to make it a weekly recipe.

1. prepare pesto sauce according to package direction
2. heat oven to 350 degrees
3. spray rectangular dish with no-stick spray
4. moisten chicken with water , shake off excess , and coat complete with bread crumbs
5. place chicken in baking dish
6. spread pesto sauce evenly over chicken breasts
7. cover each breast with slice of provolone cheese
8. spread mushrooms over cheese
9. bake in oven for 45- 50 minutes
10. serve with pasta
demonstrations.review: I made this recipe today using a Basil pesto recipe I got on the Recipezaar site. This made a great dinner and I definatly will be making it often.  This would make a wonderful "company" dish and it's so easy. Thanks again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
basil pesto

this is a wonderful lemon-flavored pesto. this was my first taste of pesto and i've never gone back!

update as of 2/13/04
i'm glad that you all like this.  i freeze this now and keep it on hand for my spaghetti sauce or others sauces.  it freezes great!

1. mix everything together in food processor except the oil and lemon
2. once everything is mixed well , drizzle with lemon and oil
3. mix until well blended
4. serve on pasta or just about anything that needs a pick me up
5. will keep in refrigerator for 2-3 days
6. enjoy !
demonstrations.review:
Excelllent recipe!! I did use walnuts instead of the pine nuts but it was still great. 
I made the Chicken pesto recipe from Recipezaar today and used this instead of the packaged pesto. Thanks Bonnie.

target.recipe_text:
crock pot chicken  gravy and stuffing

nan

1. season chicken breasts with salt and pepper and place chicken breasts in crock pot
2. pour chicken broth over breasts
3. put one slice of swiss cheese on each breast
4. combine both cans of soup and milk
5. cover chicken breasts with soup mixture
6. sprinkle stuffing mix over all
7. drizzle melted butter on top
8. cook on low for 6 hours or high for 3
target.review:
Followed the recipe as written but used chedder cheese as we are not fans of swiss and that is what we had in the house.  
Chicken was moist and very tender.  I would add more stuffing next time as I only had a small box of cornbread stuffing.  I would probably go for the light version of the soups as well to decrease the salt content.  But overall, this was an easy recipe and the flavor was great.  I would definately make this again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
oil free tofu mayonnaise

this can be stored, covered in the refrigerator for up to 4 weeks.

1. combine ingredients in container of blender or food processor
2. process about 1 minute until smooth or beat ingredients together
3. place in a screw-top jar
demonstrations.review: As a mayo I was not too sure of it.  I added a little sweetener to it and increased the mustard and it is now a great dip for my veggies.  It is free for weight watchers points so that works well. Would I make it again... probably.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
prize winning crusty rolls  bread machine dough cycle

these crisp on the outside, tender on the inside rolls won a blue ribbon at the state fair. they have a great flavor!

1. place ingredients in bread machine pan as suggested by manufacturer
2. choose dough cycle and start machine
3. upon completion of the dough cycle , remove dough
4. form rolls , place on a greased baking sheet
5. cover with a towel and let rise in a warm , draft-free location for 30 to 40 minutes
6. bake in a preheated 400 degree oven for 12-15 minutes
demonstrations.review: Have made them several times.  Tonight DH said they were perfection.  Put a pan of water in the oven when I preheated it and kept it there while baking the rolls above it.  Came out with a nice crust and very soft inside.  Great flavor too.  Thanks for the wonderful recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
multigrain bread  bread machine

a friend asked me to make a bread suitable for a person with acid reflux. i did a little research and came up with this loaf. despite the varied ingredients, this makes a light loaf. times are estimated.

1. place all ingredients in bread machine in the order recommended by the manufacturer
2. select the dough cycle and start
3. check the consistency after 10 minutes or so , and add flour or water , as needed
4. at end of cycle , remove from pan , shape as desired and place on parchment paper or on cornmeal sprinkled baking sheet
5. let rise until almost doubled
6. slash and place in 400 deg
7. oven for 35 to 40 minutes
8. substitute whole wheat if you have no rye flour
9. i'm sure this can also be baked in the machine , if you so wish
demonstrations.review: Wonderful bread.  Rose beautifully and great texture and crust when baked.  I added caraway seeds as I love the taste of them and mixed this all in my KA mixer.  This is going to be a staple on my bread making.  Thanks for the great recipe.

target.recipe_text:
mermaid s tender roast chicken

this is one of my newly adopted recipes.  this is mermaid's original description:  the most tender, juicy chicken anywhere. my mom has made this for years. great with baked potatoes and veggie.

1. preheat oven to 325
2. place 1 tablespoon oil on the bottom of glass pan
3. thoroughly clean chicken , removing all excess from cavity
4. put 1 tablespoon oil on a paper towel and lightly rub the chicken down with oil salt and pepper the skin
5. insert 1 tablespoon butter , garlic and some chopped onion into cavity
6. place the chicken on it's back and insert one tablespoon of butter between the skin and the breast , for each breast
7. cook for approx 2 hours , basting every 30 minutes if possible
target.review: This chicken got good reviews from my family.  I am fasting so did not partake but it was very tempting.  I made two whole chickens (trying to minimize my time in the kitchen), so what was left from the one chick I chopped up to make a little over two cups which I intend to use in a chicken tetrazzini (sp?) also I scraped up all the onion and garlic from both chicks to use in this future dish.  Thanks for the easy recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
eggplant  aubergine  tart

this crust-less tart will make your kitchen smell like a sweet italian evening! a crusty baguette is perfect to soak up the sauce!

1. slice eggplants on the slant: lightly score and lay on cookie sheet
2. sprinkle with salt and pepper
3. broil for 5- 10 minutes , until just turning brown
4. remove: turn oven to 450
5. heat oil in pan on stovetop
6. toss in minced garlic , salt& pepper , herbs
7. stir
8. add tomatoes , capers , and mushrooms
9. heat thoroughly for about 10 minutes , until mixture begins to thicken
10. remove from heat
11. in pie plate , arrange as follows: tomato mix , eggplant , tomato mix , eggplant , remaining tomato mix
12. arrange goat cheese evenly
13. garnish with fresh basil leaves
14. bake in oven for about 15-20 minutes , until cheese begins to brown and the edges are bubbly
demonstrations.review:
The only way I've ever made eggplant in the past is breaded and fried.  I've been wanting to try a meatless recipe, so finally took the plunge with yours.  I did'nt have the fresh thyme so I used 1 and 1/2 dried teaspoons.  My husband liked it, and he does'nt eat eggplant.  I told him after he admitted to liking it what it was, and he was cool with that.  You were also correct about the kitchen smelling good.  Thanks
Sansy

demonstrations.recipe_text:
hamburger rice  skillet

i found this  in better homes and gardens low-cost cooking cookbook.  i've had the cookbook for about 25 years and only recently discovered this recipe.  it's one of those recipes that i make just about anytime because i always have the ingredients on hand and my family (especially my youngest son) loves it!

1. in a skillet coated with spray oil , brown ground beef , onion , green pepper , and garlic until meat is browned
2. drain off fat
3. add rice
4. cook stirring constantly , for 2 minutes
5. add remaining ingredients
6. bring to a boil , reduce heat
7. cover and simmer for 25 to 30 minutes or until rice is tender , stirring occasionally
8. remove cover , sprinkle with cheese , if desired
demonstrations.review: Tried this tonight.  Out of a table of 8 there were 6 of us that really liked it.  The 5 and 8 year old are frustratingly picky so no surprise there.  The surprise was that I liked it as much as I did.  I chose to take even more of a short cut and used a 26oz jar of chunky garden spaghetti sauce instead of the other tomatoe cans.  Also used minced dehydrated onions rehydrated to a1/2cup, and about a1/2 of a green pepper finely chopped.  Thanks for this quick and easy alternative to Helper dinner which I detest.  Really Good.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
shanna s favorite chicken kiev

my daughter shanna loves this recipe.

1. make seasoned butter: in a medium sized bowl , mix butter , garlic powder , and parsley
2. slowly add the soy sauce to incorporate
3. place in the fridge to firm up a bit while you prep the chicken
4. prepare chicken: preheat oven to 350 degrees fahrenheit
5. place one chicken breast between two sheets of plastic wrap
6. using a mallet , flatten to an even thickness of about 1 / 2"
7. repeat with remaining breasts
8. dredge chicken breast in flour and place it on the counter smooth side down
9. take 1 / 8 of the butter and roll it in a log shape the width of a breast
10. place the butter log on one end of the breast
11. dust with a little more flour
12. roll the breast up , securing with a toothpick if needed
13. take another 1 / 8 of the butter and spread over top
14. place in baking dish
15. continue with the other 3 breasts
16. bake for 35 to 40 minutes
demonstrations.review: All the adults (4 in all) loved it, then 13 year old stepson liked it and 7 year old daughter ate it without complaint (which is big by itself).  It is a very pretty dish.  My best friend made it at my house, I just helped.  But it is fairly easy to do. We made 6 breast but didnt change any other amounts butter or otherwise. I suggest being careful about the sprinkling of the flour before placing the butter in the breast.  If you sprinkle a little heavy it can be a little doughy.  Served with brown rice and candied carrots.  All went well together.  My girlfriend took a copy of the recipe home and intends to share with other friends.  Thanks for sharing this recipe!

target.recipe_text:
the best chili you will ever taste

this is the best chili recipe i have ever tried. i'm not sure where the recipe originated, but it is amazing! sometimes, i don't bother adding all four cans of the kidney beans and it still turns out wonderful. once anyone tastes this chili, they will be begging for the recipe!! enjoy!

1. heat oil
2. cook onions , garlic and meat until brown
3. add tomatoes , beer , coffee , tomato paste and beef broth
4. add spices stir in 2 cans of kidney beans and peppers
5. reduce heat and simmer for 1 1 / 2 hours
6. add 2 remaining cans of kidney beans and simmer for another 30 minutes
target.review: Great chili recipe. Liked using the chili sauce instead of chili powder. Will make this again!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
grilled romaine salad

saw this on a food network show called "guy's big bite. it looked so good, i had to try it. the mix of flavors is wonderful!

1. cut bacon into small pieces
2. add 1 tbs olive oil to a large skillet on med-high heat
3. add bacon to the pan
4. when it has started to cook and render down , add onions
5. cook , stirring frequently until onions and bacon are done
6. be careful not to burn
7. carefully pour the vinegar into the pan and stir to deglaze the pan
8. simmer for a few minutes , or until liquid is decreased by half
9. turn heat down to lowest possible setting , just to keep warm
10. cut lettuce in half lengthwise
11. brush cut side with remaining olive oil
12. place lettuce , cut side down on a hot grill for 2-3 minutes , just long enough to char it lightly
13. remove from grill , and place cut side up on serving platter
14. spoon the bacon mixture over the lettuce , dividing it evenly
15. sprinkle blue cheese over lettuce
16. add the black pepper to taste
17. serve immediately
demonstrations.review: Awesome recipe for a salad! So easy when you make the bacon dressing ahead of time. Grilling the lettuce takes just a couple of minutes. I chose to grill the other side too.  I put the blue cheese on the table so each person could add their own.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chicken legs grilled

generously seasoned crisp legs.
be sure to visit the grilling forum http://www.recipezaar.com/bb/viewforum.zsp?f=42 for any help!

1. mix all marinade ingredients in a zip lock bag add chicken
2. chill and marinade for 4 hours
3. grill chicken on a well oiled grill until well browned on all sides , turning once , 30 to 40 minutes
4. fyi
5. all grills are different temperatures
6. take advantage of indirect heat --
7. if the chicken browns quickly finish over indirect heat
8. all grills have hot spots so watch and be sure to move the chicken to spots on the grill so not to burn and completely cook the chicken
9. as the time of the year makes grilling quicker or slower
10. so take care and watch and enjoy you food as it grills
11. be sure to visit the grilling forum for any help !
demonstrations.review: Pretty good.  I will use marinade again, but really watch the grill. Mine flared up & burnt the outside.  The inside was super moist, but we were unable to eat the skin and ousted the raw suar.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
world s best ribs

this recipe is quite simple and the results are incredible. i usually double the rub recipe and store it in a jar for next time. if you've never tried ribs before, try this recipe. this recipe can be made on the grill or in the oven.

1. mix brown sugar , emeril's essence , salt , pepper , paprika , cumin , garlic and cayenne pepper thoroughly , and sprinkle on both sides of ribs to taste
2. for grilling , carefully wrap in aluminum foil and cook bone side down approximately 1 1 / 2 hours on low temperature
3. no need to turn
4. after ribs become tender , remove from foil and continue cooking on both sides to desired crispness
5. apply barbecue sauce liberally to both sides and allow approximately 10 minutes for barbecue sauce to caramelize
6. brush a second time if desired , and allow to caramelize
7. remove from grill and enjoy !
8. for oven baking , wrap in aluminum foil and place on a cookie sheet in a 275f oven for 4 hours
9. place a pan with water in the oven also to keep them moist
10. remove and discard foil and brush with barbecue sauce and allow 10 minutes to caramelize
11. brush a second time if desired
12. remove from oven and enjoy !
demonstrations.review: easiest ribs. made in oven. came out juicy and tender.

target.recipe_text:
easy butterscotch yams

this is a really neat recipe! if you love yams and butterscotch, this recipe is for you! very nice and quite simple to prepare! 8)

1. preheat oven to 325
2. arrange cooked and chopped yams in a single layer in a 9x13-inch baking dish
3. combine remaining ingredients in a saucepan and bring to a boil
4. stirring constantly , boil 5 minutes
5. pour over the cooked yams
6. bake 25-30 minutes , basting occasionally , until glazed
7. serve hot and enjoy !
target.review: I served these tonight with an Apple Glazed Pork Roast.  These were very easy to make and the taste was scrumptious!  The whole family enjoyed these - even the kids - and that makes it a keeper in my book.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
italian broccoli with bacon

my family loves broccoli, but it seems most of my recipes call for cheese or a heavy sauce.  i threw this together last night for a lighter dish that is still full of flavor. if you have fresh broccoli in a microwave safe bag, it makes this dish even quicker!  a 12 oz. bag of broccoli microwaves in just 4 minutes.

1. steam fresh broccoli , or microwave frozen or fresh bagged broccoli according to package directions
2. drain any excess liquid and set aside
3. meanwhile , cook bacon in nonstick skillet until done
4. remove from skillet and crumble
5. wipe most of the excess grease from the skillet
6. saute onions and mushrooms in skillet until tender
7. add broccoli to skillet
8. stir in salad dressing
9. add crumbled bacon
10. serve immediately
demonstrations.review: This broccoli was a huge hit with the family.  We all love Italian dressing and it gave a great flavor to the broccoli.  Easy to make.  Made for ZWTIII

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mother bensen s red devil cocktail sauce

you know those recipes printed on index cards you sometimes see at the grocery? well, this one is so old it came from a fishmarket. (remember when grocery stores didn't even have seafood departments, and buying a pound of shrimp was a major project??) this sauce is so quick and easy and versatile. it can be doubled, tripled or cut in half with no problem. if you don't like things quite as zippy, use a little more ketchup and a little less chili sauce instead of the suggested 50/50 ratio. if you adore heat, keep adding horseradish until the beads of sweat pop out. :) if you like a squeeze of fresh lemon juice in your sauce, go for it. it's a great base that you can fiddle with until you think it's just perfect!

1. combine first 5 ingredients in a small bowl , mixing well
2. add horseradish gradually until the sauce has the amount of'bite' you want
3. cover with plastic wrap or lid and refrigerate until serving time
demonstrations.review: Oh wow, this was fantastic!  I boiled shrimp last night and made this to serve with it.  I used 1/2 t of garlic powder just because I love garlic.  I also added 3 t of horseradish.  The final product was delicious.  Thanks a bunch for sharing this recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
creamy garden cucumber salad

delicious vegetables with a creamy dill dressing. prep time does not include marination time, so allow for that.

1. combine salad ingredients in a medium bowl
2. combine dressing ingredients in a small bowl , mixing well
3. toss together dressing with salad and allow to marinate for several hours before serving
demonstrations.review: Wonderful salad and I really enjoyed the flavor of the dressing.  Made for the Tastebud Tickling Travellers during ZWT 4

target.recipe_text:
the only chocolate cake recipe you ll ever need   devil s food

this chocolate cake is absolutely thee best we have ever had. it is so moist and rich, i never make anything else (unless i am short on time :) the frosting recipe included goes perfectly with this cake, but you can use any frosting you like. try this once and you'll see why i call it "the only chocolate cake recipe you'll ever need"!!  adding 2/18/06: i want to note that i recently used sweetened whipped heavy cream with vanilla and it was just as fabulous as the frosting recipe listed, plus much easier.  i also used hazelnut coffee in the cake and it added even more of a little extra something!

1. preheat oven to 325f
2. in a large mixing bowl , sift together dry ingredients
3. add oil , coffee and milk and mix at medium speed for 2 minutes
4. add eggs and vanilla and beat 2 more minutes
5. expect batter to be thin
6. pour into a 9" x 13" greased and floured pan or 2- 9" round pans
7. bake 9 x 13 pan for about 45 minutes or 9" pans for about 30 minutes
8. cool in pans for about 15 minutes and then cool completely on racks
9. while cake is cooling make the icing: combine the milk and flour in a saucepan and cook over low heat until thick , whisking constantly
10. cover and refrigerate until chilled
11. in a medium bowl , beat butter , shortening , sugar and vanilla until creamy
12. add chilled milk and flour mixture and beat for 10 minutes
13. frost cooled cake and enjoy ! the frosting sounds intimidating , but it is worth it ! by the way , for some reason , we prefer this cake chilled , right out of the refrigerator
14. the rich chocolate and cool frosting just seem to taste best this way
target.review: Well I am going to give my opinion of this wonderful, moist, delicious, luscious chocolate cake, oops I already did. I believe I enjoyed it because it was not too sweet. The frosting matched since it was also not too sweet. Just like apple pie and ice cream. Maybe I will try the chocolate frosting recipe # 31809. Anyway to wrap it all up in a neat little package all had the same reaction as I. Thanks a big bunch Karen for this awesome recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
city market peach cobbler

a wonderfully tangy peach cobbler that i found in a supplement to the sunday newspaper years ago. i don't think i've ever served it to anyone who hasn't liked it. the filling is also great for a pie. for a really decadent dessert, serve this with a scoop of blue bell homemade vanilla ice cream! yum!! the preparation time is approximate since i've never timed it. the cook time includes chill time for the dough.

1. combine peaches , lemon juice and orange juice
2. in a separate bowl , mix sugar , spices and cornstarch
3. heat peaches , juices and butter in a saucepan over medium heat until butter is melted
4. mix in dry ingredients
5. remove from heat and set aside while you prepare crust
6. sift flour , sugar and salt together
7. add shortening and mix until crumbly
8. whip egg and water together , then sprinkle onto flour mixture
9. mix just until dough forms
10. chill for 30 minutes
11. roll out 1 / 2 of dough and put in bottom and 1 / 2" up the sides of a 9"x 13" baking dish
12. bake in 350 oven for 20 minutes
13. pour peach filling into crust
14. roll out remaining dough and cut into strips
15. cover filling with dough strips
16. sprinkle with 1 tablespoon sugar and 1 tablespoon melted butter
17. bake 35-40 minutes
demonstrations.review: I had some peaches that were going to go bad, searched for a good peach recipe, found this one, made it, tasted it then I went straight to heaven. With a scoop of ice cream I went to 7th heaven. Thanks for a great recipe

demonstrations.recipe_text:
bill s blue cheese dressing

this came from all recipes and was loved by many people.

1. in a large bowl , whisk together the sour cream , mayonnaise , and worcestershire sauce
2. season with mustard , garlic powder , salt , and pepper
3. stir in blue cheese
4. cover , and refrigerate for 24 hours before serving
demonstrations.review: This lucious dressing deserves oh so many more stars!!!!! Just the right amount of spices to give it just a little tang. Also makes a great dip for veggies or by the spoonfuls.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chocolate kisses cookies

this recipe was given to me by a family member of my dh i think, and was published in the elk ladies of "518" nevada city, ca volumn iii cookbook some eons ago.  i make these especially at christmastime, but not only for that time of the year, as my grandchildren ask for them as much as their mothers do whenever they come to visit. i have the kids unwrap the kisses, their favorite part about making these in the first place. part of the preparation time is chill time, and i don't include unwrapping the kisses cuz the kids do that...lol.  *** just a bit of a warning due to some consternation of the part of people who have tried to make perfect little round balls from this recipe...these cookies do flatten out.  if anyone gets them to make little perfect round balls please let us know how you did it.***

1. cream butter , sugar and vanilla together
2. add flour gradually until well blended
3. stir in pecans
4. cover and chill the dough
5. mold about 1 teaspoon of cookie dough around each unwrapped chocolate kiss , covering candy
6. bake at 375 degrees until they turn a golden brown around the edges , about 10 minutes
7. when completely cool , dust with powdered sugar
8. store in airtight container
demonstrations.review: This is the 3rd time that I made this recipe & I apologize for not giving my review. I love anything shortbread & chocolate, so I figured this had to be good. Well it was not good, it was awesome, delicious, heavenly all rolled into this little surprise cookie. The dough was very easy to work with especially after adding the nuts. I do mine very fine in the food processor. I also used my small cookie scoop, pressed it somewhat flat with my thumb, put the kiss inside and wrapped up that little surprise in the shortbread blanket. I have had to give this recipe out to a lot of people. Thank you Chabea01 for this luscious cookie from Pat Merwin

target.recipe_text:
herbed pork tenderloin

this special pork is tender and juicy and seasoned just right.

1. mix the first 11 ingredients
2. rub over the pork
3. put on a rack in a shallow roasting pan
4. bake , uncovered , at 400 for 45 minutes
5. remove from oven , cover with foil and let set for 10 minutes
6. slice into servings
target.review: I have made this over and over again and its wonderful everytime, my man cannot get enough. Thanks for sharing!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
denny s style french toast

i do not remember where i got this recipe, but my husband says it tastes just as good as what he had at denny's. i am just amazed at all of the great reviews on this recipe!! my family loves it, so i thought i would share it here and i'm so glad i did because it seems you all love it just as much!!! thanks to all of you who have tried it!

1. mix together the eggs , milk , flour , sugar , vanilla , salt& cinnamon
2. heat a large skillet , or griddle
3. when the skillet is hot , add 1 tablespoon butter
4. if the butter smokes , your pan is too hot
5. turn down the heat
6. dip each slice of bread into the batter for 30 seconds on each side
7. let some of the batter drip off , then put in skillet
8. cook each slice 1 1 / 2-2 minutes per side until each side is golden brown
9. add more butter , if necessary , to cook all of the slices
10. to serve , put on plate , dust with powdered sugar
11. serve with butter & hot syrup
demonstrations.review: FANTASTIC! A simple and fast recipe that tastes incredible! I added a little more cinnamon and used regular toast and they came out great! Thanks so much for sharing.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
do at home onion rings

so much fresher and better than the frozen ones.

1. mix egg , oil , and milk on low speed of mixer for 1 minute
2. add dry ingredients and mix until smooth
3. coat onions in flour
4. dip in batter
5. when one side is golden turn to the other side
6. fry in hot oil 375 until desired shade of brown
demonstrations.review: Great recipe but I found them very greasy, but then again they are fried onions rings. wonderful taste! thanks for sharing!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
tasty buns

these are so good we eat them plain. no butter needed, though if you want to go through all the trouble of getting it out of the frig and getting a knife, etc. be my guest. actually got this recipe from allrecipes.com (but that was before i found this website...i'll never go back!) ha!

1. mix 2 c flour& yeast
2. in a separate bowl , heat milk , water , oil , sugar& salt to lukewarm in microwave
3. add all at once to flour mixture and beat till smooth
4. mix in enough flour to make a soft dough
5. mix well , then turn out onto floured surface and let rest under a bowl for about 10 minutes
6. shape dough into 12 slightly flat balls and place on greased baking sheet to rise till doubled in size
7. bake in preheated 400 degree oven 12-15 minutes
demonstrations.review: theres only one word to describe these......YUMMY!!!!!! But I really suggest using the recommended parchment paper because I didnt one of the times I made these and they got a little burnt at the bottom.

target.recipe_text:
egg foo yung with chinese brown sauce

tastes just like your local chinese take out

1. mix all ingredients for sauce in small pan
2. cook , stirring constantly until thickened
3. set aside but keep warm
4. beat eggs in large bowl
5. add all other ingredients
6. drop by spoonfuls into hot oil , cook on both sides to brown
7. drain well on paper towels
8. serve with sauce
target.review: Pleasant enough but far too bland compared to my local takeaways Foo Yung.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
thai pineapple fried rice   pad kao saparod

this is also nice with lychees added.

1. in a wok , heat oil over medium heat and stir-fry onion and garlic until golden brown
2. add the carrots and green beans and stir-fry 2 minutes
3. add pineapple , rice , ketchup , and salt , mixing well and stir-frying for 3 minutes
4. garnish with green onion and cilantro before serving
5. serve with soy sauce , if desired
demonstrations.review:
Lovely tasty rice, I was thinking it may come out a bit bland but it was excellent.

I used 1/2 the oil and mixed the chopped cilantro into the rice while cooking. I think the cilantro makes the recipe-will have often now.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
steven s world famous to die for sour cream chicken

i've modified my grandmother's recipe for the 21st century. i can't have a dinner party and not asked to make this simple dish. enjoy!

1. clean chicken and pour sour cream over it and let marinate for about an hour in the refrigerator
2. meanwhile , take crackers and crush into medium course crumbs , mix in parmesan cheese and tarragon / marjoram
3. melt half of the butter and pour on the bottom of a 9x13 baking dish
4. dredge chicken in the cracker mixture and set in baking dish
5. repeat until complete
6. melt rest of butter and pour on top of chicken
7. bake@ 350 for 35-45 minutes or until golden brown
demonstrations.review: Just used 2 tbsp of butter and mixed cheddar cheese with parmesan.Put the chicken in a dish added the yoghurt and then tipped in the rest of the ingredients-it came out fab the top was crunchy and the sauce was lovely.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pumpkin seeds

one of the best things about halloween when i was a kid was the pumpkin seeds baking while we were finishing up the details on the carving. serving size depends on the pumpkin

1. wash your pumpkin seeds
2. boil 1 quart of water
3. after water has boiled , place the clean seeds and 1 / 8 cup of salt into water for 10 minutes- stir the whole time
4. melt 2 tbs of butter
5. drain the seeds and mix them with the butter
6. place the seeds on a 2 layer tin foiled pan and place in oven at 350 f for 30 minutes
7. do not refrigerate seeds- put them in a sealed bowl and leave them on the kitchen table
demonstrations.review: Oh these are possibly the nicest snacky food I have ever had, DH loved them so much he said they were better than peanuts or crisps (chips)

target.recipe_text:
panera s cream cheese potato soup

this is my favorite recipe for potato soup.  it's a copycat of the one they use to serve at the st. louis bread company (panera).  the recipe originally called for shredding your potatoes, but i never could get them to cook that way. i know they should cook faster, but i never could get it to work.

1. combine broth , potatoes , and spices
2. boil on medium heat until potatoes are tender
3. smash a few of the potatoes to release their starch for thickening
4. reduce to low heat
5. add cream cheese
6. heat , stirring frequently , until cheese melts
target.review:
This is dangerous!  It is so delicious and so easy you're liable to make it every day and look like a blimp in a very short time!  I would definitely add more potatoes and I loved the idea to add cheddar cheese and scallions on top - maybe a little bacon as well.  Also, chopped dill would be wonderful.
Talk about comfort food - this is the ultimate!
Thank you, Shawn H. - this is definitely a grand slam.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
best apple pie jam

a friend gave me this wonderful recipe, and oh my, it is so good. just like a extra good apple pie filling, but in jam form. if you love apple pie, you are going to have to make this wonderful recipe. my husband who only likes strawberry jam, said, "this recipe was excellent!" it is excellent on english muffins, pancakes or toast. even over ice cream too!!

1. measure apples in a measuring cup , now add in the same measuring cup water to fill up to the 4 cup line
2. add pectin and the butter and spices , lemon juice
3. bring to a boil
4. add sugars and bring back to a full rolling boil , boil 1 minute
5. stir constantly
6. remove from the heat
7. skim off any foam
8. ladle into hot jars leaving 1 / 4-inch headspace
9. put on lids
10. process in water bath 10 minutes
demonstrations.review:
Wow - what a great recipe.  Fast and delicious.  Next time I would cut down a little on the sugar and  make it 4 heaping cups of apples.  
Thanks so much for this recipe - a real keeper.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
extreme lemon bundt cake

lemon lovers only! this is one moist and very lemony pound cake that stays moist in a cake keeper for a week! needs no icing whatsoever!

1. preheat oven as directed
2. mix all ingredients and bake as directed
3. i use a bundt pan or you may also use 2 large loaf pans
4. these cakes can be frozen for 30 days and still taste like you just baked them !
demonstrations.review: This cake is so light and so delicious.  I used the optional lemon extract and I frosted it with a mixture of almond extract, confectioner's sugar and cream.  Stays moist and wonderful for days!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crumb topped banana muffins

these are so good. we love the topping.

1. in a large bowl , mix the flour , baking soda , baking powder , and salt
2. mix bananas , sugar , egg and melted butter
3. stir into dry mixture until thoroughly combined , then stop mixing
4. fill muffin cups 3 / 4 full
5. combine brown sugar , flour , and cinnamon topping ingredients
