5. chill dough , and chill an ungreased cookie sheet for about 10-15 minutes in the fridge
6. meanwhile , mix 3 tablespoons sugar , and 3 teaspoons cinnamon in a small bowl
7. scoop 1 inch globs of dough into the sugar / cinnamon mixture
8. coat by gently rolling balls of dough in the sugar mixture
9. place on chilled ungreased cookie sheet , and bake 10 minutes
10. remove from pan immediately
demonstrations.review: Why is you only crave cookies when you have minimal ingredients lying around?my daughter and I whipped a batch of these yummies up tonight after I decided if I didn't have something sweet I would go out to get it(really didn't want to do that!!!)we followed the recipe as written and they turned out perfect! Slightly crispy outside soft and fluffy inside,impossible to stop eating them.I really love that these were made with stuff I already had in the house,and that's always a positive for cooks who decide they NEED sugar later in the evening;)thanks for a great recipe we will use again for sure.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
i hate ricotta meat   2 cheese stuffed shells

my non-ricotta cheese-eating husband always raved about "the meat stuffed shells his mom used to make." his grandmother recently wrote to the tv guide (where this recipe originated) and they were kind enough to send back the recipe, dated september 13, 1976. i have to agree, these are delicious! serve with a tossed salad and garlic bread. the prep time includes the pasta/beef cooking; the cook time is the baking time for the casserole.

1. boil water for pasta
2. meanwhile , in a large skillet , brown ground beef , onion and garlic
3. drain and cool
4. cook pasta in water , drain
5. preheat oven to 400 degrees
6. meanwhile pasta is cooking , combine meat , mozzarella cheese , bread crumbs , egg and parsley
7. season with salt and pepper
8. mix spaghetti sauce with tomato sauce
9. cover bottom of a 13x9 casserole dish with 1 / 4 of the sauce
10. stuff cooked , drained shells with the meat mixture and place on top of sauce in dish in a row
11. add red wine to remaining sauce and mix well
12. cover shells with sauce and sprinkle with parmesan cheese
13. bake in oven for 20-25 minutes or until bubbly and browned
demonstrations.review: Wow these were so good!Definitely a nice change from spaghetti.Hubby loved them,he had two helpings and was looking like he would like to go for more but he was too full.Even my fussy four year old daughter gave it two thumbs up!I followed the instructions,except I left out the red wine because we didn't have any.This recipe is definitely a keeper,thanks to TheDancingCook for posting!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
avocado smoothie

ok...here in the us avocados are used in savory salads...but in brazil we eat them sweet.  this is known as "creme de abacate", when blended with sugar and milk this comes out to be a creamy goodness, trust me!  before making this make sure you chill the entire avocado so it is nice and cold.

1. put everything in blender , and blend until smooth and free of lumps
2. taste the smoothie if you think you need more sugar add it
3. it will really depend on the size of the avocado
4. this is best eaten right away , because if you store the smoothie in the fridge it will turn a slight brown on top and alter the taste
demonstrations.review: yum! this was such a fast and easy breakfast smoothie.It was creamy fresh and sweet,thanks for a new way to use avocado as I love them and always have them in my house:)

target.recipe_text:
that mustard

a sweet and spicy homemade mustard. it got its name from people saying, 

1. mix the first 5 ingredients in a small sauce pan
2. add the sugar and beaten eggs
3. cook on low until thickened and the sugar is dissolved
4. keep in fridge
5. serve this with cocktail franks , or cubes of cheese
6. great on sandwiches and summer sausage
7. for a gift idea , put in small jar and make a cheese and sausage basket
target.review: Love this! Huge hit at Christmas dinner.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pasta primavera salad

this is a very fresh, colorful, and vitamin and nutrient rich salad.  one large pot of boiling water does all the cooking for the vegetables in this salad.  the addition of the vegetables has been timed so that they're all done at the same time.  using a strainer to remove the vegetables from the water stops the cooking fast and leaves you with a hot, lightly seasoned broth to boil the pasta in.  from vegetarian times.

1. bring large pot of salted water to a boil
2. prepare a large ice water bath
3. add carrots to the boiled water , and simmer 2 minutes
4. add squash , and cook 2 minutes more
5. add broccoli and bell pepper , and cook 2 minutes more
6. add sugar snap peas , and cook 2 minutes more
7. scoop vegetables from simmering water with strainer
8. transfer to ice water bath
9. drain when cool , and pat dry
10. bring pot of water to a rolling boil
11. add pasta and cook according to package directions for al dente
12. drain , and rinse under cold water to cool
13. meanwhile , whisk together olive oil and lemon juice in large serving bowl
14. stir in shallots and garlic
15. add pasta , blanche vegetables , tomatoes , and cheese , and toss to coat with dressing
16. season with salt and pepper , and serve
demonstrations.review: Very good. I used grape tomatoes instead of chopped so they wouldn't water down the dish.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
olive oil and garlic bruschetta

here is a simple idea for a grilled snack. in addition to the olive oil and garlic this grilled bread snack gets a kick from red pepper flakes.

1. slice the garlic cloves lengthwise into paper-thin slices
2. warm a small skillet over a medium flame
3. add the 1 / 3 cup olive oil and the garlic
4. stirring constantly , cook until the garlic is aromatic and golden
5. remove the skillet from the flame and stir in the chili or red pepper flakes and parsley
6. cover and set aside
7. grill the bread on both sides until lightly browned and crisp , then sprinkle with olive oil
8. spoon the garlic-olive oil mixture over each slice
9. serve immediately
demonstrations.review:
Just out of curiosity I looked it up in the Food Dictionary
bruschetta
[broo-SKEH-tah, broo-SHEH-tah]
From the Italian bruscare  meaning "to roast over coals," this traditional garlic bread is made by rubbing slices of toasted bread with garlic cloves, then drizzling the bread with extra-virgin olive oil. The bread is salted and peppered, then heated and served warm. 

© Copyright Barron's Educational Services, Inc. 1995 based on THE FOOD LOVER'S COMPANION, 2nd edition, by Sharon Tyler Herbst

demonstrations.recipe_text:
borracho beans  drunk beans

this is way beans are made in south texas!! 
serve with any mexican dish and of course homemade tortillas!!

1. cook bacon , drain on paper towels and chop when cooled
2. cook beans according to instructions on package
3. after 1 and 1 / 2 hours of cooking beans , add bacon , bean seasonings , cilantro , tomatoes and beer
4. cover and continue to cook for an additional 30 minutes or until beans are tender
5. serve immediately or refrigerate overnight
6. you can add fresh jalapeno at the same time you add the tomatoes for an extra kick !
7. i use texas spice company bean seasoning and it is sold only at all heb grocery stores
demonstrations.review:
Great recipe. I used Goya seasoning, couldn't find the Bean Seasoning even tho I was at HEB. I added the jalepenos as suggested. Better than Mexican restaurant beans.
I used Corona beer.

target.recipe_text:
baked ziti with spinach  sausage  and mozzarella

delicious ziti recipe with fresh spinach. easy!

1. preheat oven to 375 degrees
2. heat heavy large saucepan over medium heat
3. add sausage , onion , and garlic , and saute until sausage cooked through , about 10 minutes , breaking up meat with back of spoon
4. add tomatoes with juice to pan
5. simmer until sauce thickens slightly , stirring occasionally , about 10 minutes
6. stir in pesto sauce
7. season with salt and pepper
8. lightly oil 13 x 9 glass baking dish
9. combine pasta , spinach , mozzarella , and 1 / 3 cup parmesan cheese in large bowl
10. stir in hot tomato sauce
11. mix gently until spinach is wilted
12. transfer mixture to prepared baking dish
13. sprinkle remaining 2 / 3 cup parmesan cheese over top
14. bake until sauce bubbles and cheese melt , about 30 minutes
target.review: YUMMY! my boyfriend had one bite and said he was glad there was enough for leftovers tomorrow. very tasty. i think next time i will add black olives. very yummy and easy to keep an eye on. thank you so much for this recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
nutella ravioli cookies

made these for my cookie swap this year.  delish!

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. roll out cookie dough to about a 1 / 4 inch
3. thickness
4. using a cookie cutter or a glass dipped in flour , cut out rounds
5. using a piping bag or plastic bag with the end snipped off , pipe about 1 / 2 teaspoon of nutella into the center of each round
6. fold rounds over to create half moon shapes and gently seal edges
7. place on an ungreased cookie sheet and bake for 9-10 minutes
8. remove to racks and cool completely
9. when cookies are completely cooled , melt chocolate chips in microwave
10. remove and using a fork , drizzle chocolate over cookies
11. repeat steps 9 & 10 with white chocolate chips
demonstrations.review: yummy! the nutella is subtle but deff. a wonderful punch of taste. mine came out pretty well, im making more for chirstmas presents, and will post pictures of that batch. while slightly time consuming pretty easy when you get to it. thank you for posting!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pizza dough  with no yeast

i like this recipe because it's simple and uses ingredients i always have on hand. i got it from my dad, i can't say for sure where it originally came from, but maybe from a betty crocker cookbook. this dough also works well for making meat pies.

1. heat oven to 425f
2. measure ingredients into a bowl
3. stir vigorously until mixture leaves the side of the bowl
4. gather dough together and press into a ball
5. knead dough in bowl 10 times to make smooth then divide dough in half
6. on lightly floured surface roll each half into a 13-inch circle
7. place on pizza pan
8. turn up edges 1 / 2 inch and pinch
9. brush circles with remaining 2t of salad oil
10. add toppings and bake for 20-25 minutes or until it looks done
demonstrations.review: i was craving home made pizza but-gasp!-no yeast. i found this recipe and figured id give it a shot. i added italian seasonings to the dough before i baked it and rubbed olive oil before i put sauce on the dough. however, it took a little longer to cook, the middle gave me a little trouble but when it did cook my family loved it. they told me to make sure the keep the recipe on hand and i i will, next time i will put the oven higher and itll get a five star!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
my favorite comfort food egg sandwich

the mayonnaise, believe it or not, makes all the difference in this sandwich. i and my family just have to have one every now and then. good for a quick breakfast (if not on a diet!)

1. spread mayonnaise on bread
2. scramble eggs in butter
3. pile cooked eggs on bread
4. liberally salt and pepper
5. while skillet is still hot , place cheese slice in skillet
6. let it start to melt , then scoop it up and place on eggs
7. of course , put other slice of bread on and oh my it is good
demonstrations.review: i love these, the are so simlpe. i usually put cheese on the eggs while finishing in the pan and also, usually openfaced. but the mayo does make all the difference. my boyfriend hates mayo and has no idea what hes missing.if ive got a busy day and only a few to eat i usually fry up an egg, mayo some toast and go.

target.recipe_text:
vegan wheat free chocolate chip cookies

i haven't tried these, but the word on the street is that they are excellent vegan and gluten free cookies. a nice plus? you can eat the dough without worrying about raw eggs. :) from theppk.com

1. preheat oven to 375
2. sift together oat flour , soda and salt
3. in a seperate bowl , combine the flax meal and soymilk
4. add sugar , vanilla and oil and mix until well combined
5. fold wet ingredients into dry
6. fold in chocolate chips
7. drop dough by tablespoons onto an ungreased baking sheet , leaving about 1 1 / 2 inches between cookies
8. bake 12-15 minutes until golden
9. remove from oven and let cool slightly on the pan , then remove with a spatula and let cool completely on a cooling rack
target.review: Great vegan and wheat free cookie without expensive "gluten-free" ingredients.  They taste like a chocolate chip oatmeal cookie...texture is a little rough. I also think they might taste even better with butter. I'll be trying that next time.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pepper  corn  and zucchini muffins

to go with soups, salads, chili, etc...

1. preheat oven to 400
2. grease a muffin tin real well or put in paper liners
3. in a large mixing bowl , combine the flour , cornmeal , sugar , baking powder , and salt
4. make a well in the center
5. in another bowl , whisk the milk , egg , and margarine together
6. add this mixture to the dry ingredients
7. stir just until moistened and blended
8. stir in zucchini and peppers
9. spoon batter into muffin tin
10. bake for 20-25 minutes or until test done
demonstrations.review: These are a nice option for savory muffins. I used shredded carrot instead of red peppers and they were still good.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
my grandmother s fresh peach cobbler

my grandmother used this recipe every summer when the peaches were ripe. she got the recipe from her church cookbook. you can use any almost any kind of fruit in the cobbler, it will still be good.

1. preheat oven to 350
2. pour melted butter into an 8x8 pan
3. whisk together the flour , 3 / 4 cup of sugar , baking powder and milk
4. pour over melted butter
5. cover with peach slices
6. cover with 3 / 4 cup sugar
7. bake until batter rises to top and forms a nice brown crust , about 20 - 30 minutes
demonstrations.review: LOVED IT! This tastes like my mom's peach cobbler. Very easy and I made it with a large can of peaches minus the juice. It was also great with whole wheat pastry flour. Next time I will add a pinch of salt because I always use unsalted butter and I like the sweet and salty combo.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
lemon glazed zucchini muffins

great way to use up your surplus zucchini, from this weeks newspaper.

1. grease a muffin tin or line with paper liners
2. preheat oven to 400f
3. combine flour , sugar , baking powder , salt , nutmeg , and zest in a large bowl
4. mix in nuts and fruit
5. combine milk , oil and eggs in a small bowl , whisking until well blended
6. pour liquid into flour mixture , stirring well
7. add zucchini , stir until moistened
8. spoon evenly into muffin cups
9. bake 20-25 minutes until toothpick inserted in center comes out clean
10. remove from pan and place on a rack
11. mix confectioners sugar and lemon juice until smooth , and drizzle over warm muffins
demonstrations.review: My husband and I loved these. The texture is great, they are not too sweet and overall delicious. I omitted the fruit and nuts and they were still very flavorful.

target.recipe_text:
fried eggplant  aubergine

an adopted recipe i've not tried. here's hwat the op says about it: "very easy fried eggplant. just like shake n' bake!my husband really likes this recipe. he says it's the best fried eggplant he ever had. easy to make this "parmesan" by adding sauce, mozzerella and baking. very cheap too!! one small eggplant feeds 6!"

1. preheat oil in pan on medium till a splash of water sizzles on it
2. put everything in a giant freezer ziploc bag except the eggplant , oil and eggs
3. skake it up well
4. lightly beat eggs in a bowl
5. dip eggplant slices in egg and add to bag about 3-4 at a time
6. shake them up good
7. place battered slices in hot oil
8. flip after 2 minutes
9. remove when browned on both sides , about 4 minutes total
10. continue until all slices are done
11. i always make this with pasta , garlic bread and my stuffed mushrooms
target.review: Very good, very tasty.  Made this for my husband and neighbor, and it's all gone. Thanks for a good, yet simple recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
reeses squares   5 ingredients   no bake  reese s

these bars are extremely rich and not for people with a fear of chocolate and peanut butter (if those people actually exist)!!! very easy no bake 5 ingredient recipe!

1. combine graham crumbs , sugar and peanut butter and mix well
2. blend in melted butter until well combined
3. press mixture evenly into a 9 x 13 inch pan
4. melt chocolate chips in microwave or in double boiler
5. spread over peanut butter mixture
6. chill until just set and cut into bars (these are very hard to cut if the chocolate gets "rock hard"
demonstrations.review: I made these for my boyfriend and his athletic training staff....well, needless to say, football players, the staff, even outsiders were taking them! Once the word got around..they were gone! These were super easy to make..I think the hardest part was evening the mixture out into the waxed paper lining! They tasted just like Reeces...and were delicious! They are very rich..everyone who had one immediately went for a something to drink...ha ha.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cinnamon nuts

i make this out-of-this-world tasting homemade nut mixture every christmas season... no matter how much i make, they never last long, i'll be lucky if they even make it to the table.... so my advice to you, is make lots and lots, then hide some for your guests.

1. in a skillet , toast nuts slightly , tossing then so they won't burn
2. remove from skillet
3. melt butter in the same skillet
4. stir in the nuts and the 1 / 2 cup sugar , stirring occasionally , until sugar melts
5. in a large bowl , mix the spices and remaining 3 tbsp sugar
6. stir in the nuts
7. spread on waxed paper
8. cool about 20 mins
9. break them apart
10. store in covered containers
demonstrations.review: Very nice snack :) Easy to make, great to give away as gifts! Even makes the kitchen smell nice while baking!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
why i joined zaar carrot cake

on october 2, 2001, i discovered the recipezaar web site. i immediately joined so i could post a request for a recipe i had lost. in less than an hour, i had a reply: this recipe. unfortunately, i never posted it into the database -- until now. my mistake. this cake was the reason i joined, and the friendly response i received was the reason i stayed!

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees f
2. grease and flour a 9x13 inch pan
3. mix flour , baking soda , baking powder , salt and cinnamon
4. make a well in the center and add sugar , oil , eggs and vanilla
5. mix with wooden spoon until smooth
6. stir in carrots , coconut , walnuts and pineapple
7. pour into 9x13 inch pan and bake for about 45 minutes
8. don't panic , the centre will sink a little
9. allow to cool
10. when cool , ice the cake
11. you can certainly use your favourite cream cheese frosting to ice this cake , but the one i've included is highly recommended
12. to make the frosting: cream the butter and cream cheese until smooth
13. add the icing sugar and beat until creamy
demonstrations.review: My fiance who told me he didnt like carrot cake, had two pieces this evening! Very moist, rich in flavor and delicious. Will defintely make this recipe again. Thank you!

target.recipe_text:
low fat italian meatloaf

i'm on the atkins diet, so i follow a lot of low fat/no carb dishes. these are ones i make myself, ... trial and error. this was a success. my family loves this italian version of a meat loaf that i make with ground turkey. calories, fat and cholesterol wre reduced by: using egg whites instead of a whole egg replacing ground beef with ground turkey breast using shredded apples to add moisture that is lost by eliminating the beef fat using a reduced-fat spaghetti sauce. 445 calories per serving before, 227 after.

1. preheat the oven to 350 degrees
2. in a large bowl , stir together the egg whites , garlic , basil , salt , rosemary and red pepper
3. then stir in the apples , onions and bread crumbs
4. add the turkey and mix until well combined
5. spray a 8x4x2" loaf pan with non-stick spray
6. pat the turkey mixture into the pan
7. bake for 15 minutes
8. spread the spaghetti sauce over the top of the turkey
9. bake about 25 minutes more , or until the turkey is no longer pink
10. let stand for 5 minutes
11. transfer the loaf to a serving plate
12. sprinkle the parmean cheese over the top
13. slice and serve
target.review: It had a great flavor, though it came out a little softer than I liked.  Maybe I needed to cook it longer?

demonstrations.recipe_text:
macaroni and cheese pea salad

made from boxed macaroni&cheese dinner. the cheese/macaroni mixture gives this a unique twist to typical macaroni salad. i've never made it from homemade cheese & macaroni, but i imagine it would work fine. sometimes i use leftover macaroni & cheese dinner and adjust the rest of the ingredients accordingly. this is one of our  quick and easy family favorites.  enjoy!!

1. cook macaroni & cheese dinner per box directions
2. cool
3. add chopped eggs , celery , onion , green onion to cooled macaroni & cheese
4. stir in mayonnaise and seasonings
5. gently stir in thawed peas and season to taste
6. as with all salads , season to taste
demonstrations.review: I followed the recipe exactly and it was great!  My fiance that doesn't usually like mayo-based pasta salads even had seconds!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
orange chicken stir fry

a yummy dinner that's easy to whip up if you keep the ingredients on hand, both in the cupboard and in the freezer.

1. heat oil at medium-high in large skillet and add chicken and stir-fry 5 minutes or until browned
2. set aside
3. reduce heat to medium
4. add broccoli and garlic to skillet
5. stir-fry 2 minutes
6. stir in soup , liquid drained from mandarin orange segments , and oregano
7. heat to a boil , stirring often
8. reduce heat to low and stir in chicken
9. simmer until chicken is cooked through , about 5 minutes
10. stir in orange segments and serve
11. particularly nice with rice , or serve with thin asian-style noodles
demonstrations.review: It tasted good, but the sauce didn't thicken as much as I'd like. I will also use more broccoli the next time I make it.  Thanks for posting a unique recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s 5 minute cinnamon flop brunch cake

except for the the milk and small amount in the egg, the cake itself has very little fat and using low-fat milk will keep the fat to a minimum, i have stated the egg as optional, i strongly suggest to add it in for a more cake-like texture --  if you are looking for a fancy cake to serve then this is not it however for the ease of this cake it is darn good and makes a great weekend brunch cake, it's like a combination of a cake and cinnamon bun all in one,  ridiculously simple to make as it's all mixed by hand and takes like 5 minutes to throw together, try adding in some chopped strawberries, apples or blueberries, raisins or dried cranberries, this recipe is a blank canvas, so go ahead and add in fruit, nuts chocolate chips whatever you wish, and to kick this up a notch drizzle recipe#120835 on top :) --- servings are only estimated

1. set oven to 350 degrees f
2. prepare a greased 13 x 9-inch baking dish , or two 8 or 9-inch round cake pans
3. in a bowl mix the 2 cups flour , 1-1 / 4 cups white sugar , milk , vanilla or almond extract , baking powder , pinch of salt and egg until just combined careful not to overmix
4. pour into prepared baking pan / s
5. generously spread brown sugar and cinnamon on top
6. if desired sprinkle chopped walnuts or pecans over top
7. drizzle melted butter over top
8. bake for about 20-25 minutes for 8 or 9-inch round cake pan , and about 30 minutes for a 13 x 9-inch pan
demonstrations.review: Very easy to make. I used 1 cup white flour, 1 cup whole wheat flour and skim milk. Turned out great!

target.recipe_text:
carrot and raisin salad with pineapple

quick and easy

1. toss raisins , carrots , and pineapple together lightly
2. set aside
3. stir together mayonnaise , lemon juice , salt and sugar and add to the raisin mixture
4. refrigerate until served
target.review: This was really yummy!!  I also added some of the juice from the pineapple!  It was wonderful! My crew ate it right up.  Thanks for the recipe Trisha - its definately a keeper!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
refreshing pina colada cake

this cake is so light and refreshing.   very good summer cake.  it's a tried and true recipe.

1. bake cake as suggested on box in a large sheet-cake pan
2. cool
3. combine puddings , milk , and cream cheese and beat with electric mixer
4. refrigerate pudding mixture for an hour
5. spread pudding mixture on cake then add a layer of drained pineapple
6. top with a layer of cool whip
7. store in fridge
demonstrations.review:
I made this cake for my 2 year old DD's Birthday - it was soooo yummy!  Usually I end up throwing away left over cake, cause no one really likes cake around here, but this one was ALL gone the day after the party!
 
I also squished the cake down using waxed paper (thatnks for the tip!) when it came out of the oven so all of the ingredients would fit on top.  I used instant vanilla pudding mix but the coconut pudding was not instant, cause I couldn't find the instant stuff.  I also added 1 cup of shredded coconut to the pudding / cream cheese mixture.  It turned out really really well!
I have given this recipe out a few times already!  Thanks for the recipe queenkungfu - it's a definate keeper!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
uncle bill s whipped shortbread cookies

these are very easy to make shortbread cookies. they are so good that they melt in your mouth, you hardly have to chew them. i have been making them for over 35 years.

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees f
2. in a mixing bowl and using an electric mixer , combine butter , flour , icing sugar and vanilla extract
3. mix until mixture is a smooth consistency
4. prepare cookie sheets with parchment paper
5. spoon out dough onto parchment lined cookie sheets by teaspoonfuls or by tablespoons for larger cookies , spacing about 2 inches apart
6. cut maraschino cherries into quarters and place one piece in the middle of each cookie , alternating with red and green cherries
7. bake in preheated 350 f oven for 13 to 15 minutes or until bottom of cookies are lightly browned , do not overbake
8. remove from oven and let cool on cookie sheet for about 5 minutes
9. transfer onto wire racks to finish cooling
10. store in a container with a lid and separate each layer with wax paper
11. use sprinkles , half an almond or half a cashew or chocolate to the top of the cookies before baking
12. a thumbprint in the cookie , filled with your choice of jam is very tasty
13. it has been suggested that the cookies be refrigerated for at least 1 / 2 hour before baking for a different texture
demonstrations.review: Mmmmm...  I had never made shortbreads before I gave these a whirl.  They were melt-in-your-mouth good!!  Not to mention quick and easy.  This recipe made 4 dozen small cookies and my crew (7 in all) finished them off in less than 24 hours!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pan roasted asparagus

quick & easy - a great way to cook thin asparagus!

1. trim the bottom inch or two off the asparagus
2. cut spears in half crosswise
3. heat olive oil in a large heavy skillet
4. add asparagus
5. toss well
6. sprinkle with salt and garlic
7. toss well for one to two minutes
8. serve hot or at room temperature
demonstrations.review: OMG!!  This is super-easy and super-yummy!!  I love this recipe - can't wait to make it again!!

target.recipe_text:
thai dipping sauce for spring wrap or egg rolls

this is very tasty and low fat dipping sauce - use this as a dip for a variety of appetizers or as a sauce to go with stir fry.

1. whisk together all the ingredients in a small saucepan
2. bring to a boil , whisking all the while until it thickens
3. remove from heat and cool to room temperature
target.review: This was a simple recipe that took no time at all and it was very good.  I used it as a dipping sauce for pot stickers and my husband and I really enjoyed it.  I will make this again when I make egg rolls.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
perfect greek orzo salad

an irresistibly refreshing and delicious combination of classic greek ingredients and orzo pasta.

1. in large bowl , combine cucumber , feta , black olives , tomatoes & parsley
2. bring large pot of salted water to a boil
3. cook orzo as directed on box
4. drain and rinse with water to cool
5. return pasta to pot
6. mix cucumber mixture into orzo
7. whisk together dressing ingredients and pour over salad
8. mix well to combine
9. refrigerate for 20 minutes before serving
demonstrations.review: This was a delicious light and fresh tasting salad. I added about 1/4 cup of fresh dill. I'll be making this again and again. Thanks for posting!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
southwest spaghetti squash

i found this recipe in a low-carb cookbook. the sweetness of the squash mixes well with the spice of the other ingredients. low-carb and vegetarian!

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. cut squash in half lengthwise
3. remove and discard seeds
4. place squash , cut side down , in greased baking pan
5. bake 45 minutes to 1 hour or until just tender
6. using fork , remove spaghetti-like strands from hot squash and place strands in large bowl
7. add tomatoes with juice , beans , 1 / 2 cup cheese , cilantro , cumin , garlic salt and pepper
8. toss well
9. spray 1 1 / 2 quart casserole with nonstick cooking spray
10. spoon mixture into casserole
11. sprinkle with remaining 1 / 4 cup cheese
12. bake uncovered , 30 to 35 minutes or until heated through
13. serve immediately
demonstrations.review: I added some chopped green peppers and white onions and it was delicious! I will definitely make this again and again-thanks for sharing!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pasta with hot tomato   bacon sauce

great change from regular pasta sauce. fast to assemble--40 minutes to the plate. kick it up by adding extra red pepper flakes if you like--i do!

1. fry bacon till crisp
2. drain on paper towel
3. pour all grease from pan except 1 tablespoon
4. add olive oil and onions
5. saut till onions wilt , about 5 minutes
6. stir in garlic , tomatoes , salt , sugar , basil and red pepper flakes
7. crumble bacon in and add parsley
8. simmer 30 minutes
9. remove from heat
10. cook pasta while sauce is simmering
11. drain well
12. toss sauce and pasta together
13. serve
14. pass cheese to garnish
demonstrations.review: This is a delicious recipe that my husband and I absolutely loved! I served it with gnocchi instead of pasta and it was a great combination!

target.recipe_text:
mexican casserole   6 5 weight watcher points

this is a delicious mexican casserole recipe with only 6.5 weight watcher points per large serving!  yum!  (on the new, points plus system of weight watchers, this recipe is 9 points)

1. brown ground beef and chopped onions in large skillet
2. brown 10 to 12 minutes or until thoroughly cooked , stirring constantly
3. drain well and rinse with warm water to remove all fat
4. return beef / onions to skillet
5. add corn , black beans , tomatoes , chilies / jalapenos and taco seasoning mix
6. mix well
7. reduce heat
8. simmer 5 minutes
9. meanwhile spray 12x8-inch baking dish with nonstick cooking spray
10. cut each tortilla in half
11. place 8 halves in bottom of sprayed baking dish , overlapping slightly
12. spoon half of beef mixture evenly over tortillas
13. spoon sour cream over beef mixture
14. spread evenly
15. top with remaining 8 tortilla halves and remaining beef mixture
16. heat oven to 350f
17. bake at 350f for 25 minutes
18. remove from oven
19. sprinkle with cheese
20. cover
21. let stand 5 minutes or until cheese is melted
22. sprinkle with chopped cilantro and serve with fresh chopped lettuce , tomatoes , salsa , black olives , etc /
23. makes 6 large servings at 6
24. 5 weight watcher pts / each
target.review: We really enjoyed this dish.  Maybe I simmered it too long, but it was really spicy.  I would either cut down on the jalapenos or the simmering time.  Also, the recipe didn't state the size of corn tortillas to use.  I bought mission corn tortillas (the only ones I could find at my grocery store) and found that the eight halves didn't cover the bottom of my baking dish.  I used 10 halves.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chicken garlic bites

simple and fun to make, great to eat! prep time includes marinating the chicken.  use matzo meal instead of the breadcrumbs and this is good for passover as well.

1. place chicken in shallow dish
2. in small bowl , mix olive oil , garlic , and black pepper
3. pour over chicken
4. cover and marinate 30 minutes
5. drain
6. preheat oven to 475f
7. mix bread crumbs and cayenne
8. coat chicken
9. arrange in a single layer on cookie sheet
10. bake 10 minutes or until brown
demonstrations.review: Not only was this yummy, but quick!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pepperoni puffs

a co-worker brought these to a recent function, and they quickly disappeared from the table. i had to have the recipe. i'll probably add a pinch of dried red peppers or cayenne to this. i also usually 'nuke' pepperoni before cooking with it, to get rid of overabundant grease.

1. combine first 5 ingredients until well mixed
2. add pepperoni , and allow batter to stand for 15 minutes
3. grease mini muffin pans and fill 3 / 4 full
4. bake at 350-degrees for 25-30 minutes , or until golden brown
demonstrations.review: These were pretty good.  I don't think I'd make them again...I like pepperoni pizza rolls better for the time investment.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
zesty low fat chicken breasts

very tasty, you can make it as hot or as mild as you want. quick easy dish - no muss no fuss

1. put the breasts in a 9x13-inch baking dish
2. whisk remaining ingredients together until they are well blended
3. pour over the breasts
4. coat both sides of the breasts with the sauce
5. bake in 400f oven for approx 30 minutes or until the chicken is done
6. remove breasts , keep warm
7. pour the sauce into a sauce pan stir in the cornstarch that has been mixed with a tbsp of water , bring to a boil and allow to thicken whisk constantly
8. pour over the chicken & serve
demonstrations.review: We weren't overly crazy about the flavor combination.  That said...The chicken was very moist and we didn't need to thicken the sauce with cornstarch.  While we weren't nuts about this recipe, my toddler licked the sauce off his chicken!

target.recipe_text:
crock pot sweet potatoes with apricot pie filling

my mother thinks this sounds like the recipe she used at thanksgiving that i have been bugging her for.  she can't find her book and she found this at about.com.  i tried it today to take to a friend's ayyam-i-ha party, as he was making turkey.  it was really good and got many compliments.  i have to admit that during its day of cooking it reeked of garlic and i was a little worried about it.  but when it was all done, it smelled good and tasted wonderful.

1. place potatoes in a 3-1 / 2 to 4 quart crock pot and sprinkle with garlic
2. in a medium bowl , combine the remaining ingredients and blend well
3. pour into slow cooker
4. cover and cook on low for 6-8 hours or until potatoes are tender and glazed , stirring once during cooking time
target.review: This was an awesome side dish. During the day while cooking, my kids thought I was making pizza because of the garlic smell but it is not as garlic strong tasting as it smells while cooking. The true test was my picky kids. They were of course reluctant to try but when they were finally  convinced to taste, they loved it! Thanks for the recipe. Is a keeper.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s best blasted rapid roast whole chicken

blasting with high heat will shrink the skin and seal in all the juices to create an extremely moist and tender chicken with lovely crispy skin - and it will be on your table in about an hour. this method will also work with a larger chicken, but cooking time will need to be increased. you may adjust all seasonings to taste. if you are not a lemon lover, then you may omit the lemon juice. you really can use whatever seasoning that you like for this. i like to use seasoned salt. make certain to use a fork and poke holes all over in the lemon, then place it into the cavity of the chicken. roast roast as stated. the chicken with be moist and have a faint lemon flavor. for more of my tried-and-true recipes, visit my food blog at www.kittencalskitchen.com.

1. rinse the chicken inside and out well under cold water , then pat dry using a paper towel
2. in a small bowl mix the lemon juice with oil and melted butter until blended , then rub all over the chicken
3. using clean hands rub the inside and outside of the chicken with seasoned salt , garlic powder , black pepper and cayenne
4. place the lemon / s inside the cavity
5. place the chicken into a baking dish
6. using cotton string tie the legs together tightly
7. at this point you may cover and refrigerate for up to 6 hours
8. set oven to 450 degrees f
9. roast the chicken at 450 degrees for 20 minutes , then reduce the heat to 400 degrees and continue roasting for about 40 minutes
10. cover with foil and let sit for 15 minutes before slicing
demonstrations.review: This chicken was amazing!!!! It really does cook that fast. So tasty and juicy. I didn't have any cayanne pepper so I used chipolte chili instead but it was so good. First time trying it, I was having company and every single person said it was the best roast chicken they ever had. I had no left overs which I usually would be elated about but it left me wanting more.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
not your mama s fish n  chips  halibut

my daughter got the recipe from a friend. living in alaska we eat a lot of halibut. this has got to be some of the best!!!! it is quick and easy to make and a crowd pleaser.

1. preheat oven to 375 degrees
2. rinse halibut and pat dry with paper towels
3. cut fish into large cubes or thick fingers
4. add salt and pepper to melted butter , to taste
5. dip fish pieces into butter and then coat with crushed potato chips
6. place on ungreased baking stone or cookie sheet
7. bake in 375 degree oven for 20 minutes or until fish is flaky and opaque
8. do not over cook
9. alternate method:
10. if you are watching your fat intake , use beaten eggs in place of the butter
11. serve hot plain or with tartar sauce
12. these make great appetizers when cut into smaller pieces
demonstrations.review: What a great recipe. I t was delicious. My kids ate it right up. I also passed this recipe on to my friend who has a wheat allergy. Finally she can have fish and chips again with no allergic reaction!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
nifty carrots

i got this from the best of bridge. i made it for christmas and thanksgiving dinner in korea and people raved about it. one male friend asked if i was making those awesome carrots when i invited him to christmas dinner.

1. boil or steam carrots , reserving carrot water
2. i always steam them to preserve the carrot flavor
3. place cooked carrots in a shallow casserole
4. combine the rest of the ingredients , pour over carrots and mix
5. i use alot of horseradish because we like it
6. you can use less if you want
7. i didn't care for it and i always omit this
8. if you want to try it , melt the butter , mix with breadcrumbs and sprinkle on top
9. bake at 375 f
10. for 30 minutes or until horseradish sauce is bubbly
demonstrations.review:
Good carrot side dish. Everyone at the table enjoyed it. I took your word for it and did not include the bread crumbs.
Thanks for the recipe.

target.recipe_text:
creamy garlic penne pasta

this is a delicious, super quick side or main dish. i got it from the back of a pasta box and it is yummy!

1. melt butter and add garlic in a medium sauce pan
2. cook over medium for 1 minute
3. add flour and cook 1 minute , stirring constantly
4. stir in broth and milk and cook , stirring frequently , until sauce boils and thickens
5. add parsley , salt , pepper and cheese
6. stir until cheese is melted
7. toss hot pasta with sauce and serve immediately
target.review: Very quick & yummy!  I mixed in some left over chicken.  This was a great weeknight dinner.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
rhubarb crisp

mom's recipe! easy to make and easy to eat.

1. combine rhubarb , sugar , flour and cinnamon and put into 8" x 8" x 2" glass baking dish
2. combine flour , brown sugar , rolled oats and melted butter and sprinkle streusel over rhubarb mixture
3. bake at 375 for 35 minutes
demonstrations.review: I am now asked to bring this to every summer gathering!  It is wonderful!  Thank you so much for posting.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cherry chocolate blossoms

a beautiful little cookie for cookie trays and holidays. very simple to make yet very elegant.

1. in large bowl , combine powdered sugar , butter , cherry liquid , almond extract and food color
2. blend well
3. lightly spoon flour into measuring cup
4. level off
5. add flour and salt
6. mix well
7. stir in cherries
8. if dough is too dry , add a little more cherry liquid until dough holds together when shaped
9. shape dough into 1-inch balls
10. place 2 inches apart on ungreased cookie sheets
11. bake at 350 degrees f for 10 to 12 minutes or until edges are just slightly brown
12. immediately top each cookie with a chocolate candy , pressing down firmly
13. remove from cookie sheets and cool
demonstrations.review: I loved these!  Quick, simple and yummy.  I used the cherry cordial kisses for the top and that really brought the whole thing together.  This is a Christmas keeper!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
carrots in butter almond sauce

wonderfully aromatic and tasty, this makes a nice change from ordinary carrots!

1. steam carrots until crisp-tender or to preferred doneness
2. transfer to a serving dish and keep warm
3. in a skillet , saut the green onions in butter until tender
4. in a bowl , combine the cornstarch , water , and sherry and whisk until smooth , then stir into onions
5. add the bouillon granules , coriander , basil , pepper , and almonds
6. bring sauce to a boil over medium heat , stirring , and cook for 2 to 3 minutes or until thickened and bubbly
7. pour the sauce over carrots in the serving dish , stirring gently to coat
demonstrations.review: Such a unique and tasty way to serve carrots.  There were wonderful for Thanksgiving and will be appearing again at Chirstmas time!

target.recipe_text:
chicago italian beef

you'll be sorry you didn't grow up in chicago, and eat one of those wonderful beef sandwiches from carm's. this tastes identical. this wonderful recipe came from my sister linda knowing how homesick i am for chicago food. start cooking 18 hours before you want to eat.

1. cook first 5 ingredients in a crockpot on low for 18 hours
2. turn over at the 6th and 12th hour interval
3. at the 17th hour cut sweet green peppers into 1 / 8 ths lengthwise and cook in water on low heat until soft
4. cut bread into 6 inch lengths and slice on the side lengthwise
5. pull roast apart with a fork , and using tongs , pile bread with meat and juice
6. lay strips of green pepper on top of the meat
7. salt to taste
8. open wide and enjoy the most wonderful taste sensation
9. may be frozen when cooked
target.review: phenomenal! i wish i could eat it on a whole wheat sour dough roll but i have to make due with serving it on a broiled portabella due to gluten issues. this is a new staple food in my house.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
fijian honey cake

honey cake is one of the highly popular desserts of fiji.  the cake becomes moister and its flavors deepen a day or two after it is made.

1. preheat the oven to 350f
2. coat a 9" x 5" loaf pan with nonstick cooking spray
3. in a large bowl , combine all the ingredients except the almonds and beat until well blended
4. pour the batter into the loaf pan and sprinkle with the almonds
5. bake for 45 to 55 minutes or until a wooden toothpick inserted in the center comes out clean
6. allow to cool for 10 minutes then remove from pan to wire rack to cool completely
demonstrations.review: I made this for the GF Pacific Challenge on ZWT7. I removed the regular sugar and flour, and added 1/2 cup coconut flour and upped the eggs to a half dozen. I added a little oil and lessened the honey a touch, because I don't like a lot of sweet. I sprinkled almonds on half and shredded coconut on half. I baked in cupcakes and small loaves because coconut flour cakes stay very moist so you do not want anything large. It was fantabulous.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
shortcake  sockerkaka

nan

1. butter a cake pan , cover sides with breadcrumbs
2. turn on oven 350 f
3. whip sugar and eggs until almost white
4. mix flour , baking powder and flavoring
5. melt the margarine
6. add all ingredients to batter
7. stir quickly until smooth
8. pour into cake pan , bake for about 30-40 min , until golden brown
demonstrations.review: tastes great! i added lemon rind and vanilla. i'm making a strawberry shortcake with vanilla pudding. kind of a cheater trifle, lol. this goes perfectly with it!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
indian coconut soup

i have long enjoyed coconut soup in indian restaurants, and i finally set about to make my own. now i like mine best of all! :-) it's quick and easy, and it has a nice texture.

1. sautee coconut in butter until toasted , stirring well
2. add 1 / 4 cup pistachios , sauting a little longer
3. add honey and spices and stir
4. add milk and coconut milk , stirring slowly
5. heat but don't boil
6. froth individual servings in blender or espresso machine if desired
7. caution: be careful not to put more than one serving at a time in the blender or it may overflow and scald you
8. serve garnished with pistachios
demonstrations.review: This soup was wonderful! I wasn't sure how to froth it, but it tasted great. I added a bit of hot chili sauce (that is served in oriental restaurants) to give it a little bite and really liked the flavor mixture of the sweet and spicy :)

target.recipe_text:
yes  virginia there is a great meatloaf

absolutely delicious meatloaf and sauce! those who claim they don't believe there can be such a thing as a great meatloaf will love this. based on a meatloaf given to me by a dear friend, virginia strehl, memphis, and leesburg, fla. nita holleman, 2000

1. meatloaf: combine meat loaf ingredients and place into a loaf baking dish
2. smooth out top
3. sauce: combine sauce ingredients and pour on top and sides of meatloaf
4. bake at 350f about 1 hour to 1 hour 15 minutes or until done
5. enjoy !
6. the addition of 1 or 2 teaspoons of kitchen bouquet makes this recipe very good
7. recipe should be"plump" from the addition of the milk or half & half
8. it should not be runny
9. a second batch of sauce served hot is good to serve with the meatloaf
10. nita's
11. it is wise to have some fat added to the deer -- especially to ground deer
12. maybe 25 % fat , , otherwise your results will be poor
13. i don't know about some of the other game meat some are using
14. please consult an expert
15. the recipe is delicious as it stands ! enjoy ! nita holleman
target.review: very good.  added some red and green pepper for color.  thanks for the recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
comfort meatballs the pioneer woman

make a double batch and keep some in the freezer for busy cold nights.  make extra sauce for dipping! from ree drummond's  episode potluck sunday, this has many excellent reviews!

1. for the meatballs: in bowl , combine the ground beef and oats
2. pour in the milk , and then add the onions , salt and pepper
3. stir to combine
4. roll the mixture into tablespoon-size balls and refrigerate them for 30 to 45 minutes to firm
5. preheat the oven to 350 degrees f
6. heat the canola oil in a large skillet over medium heat
7. dredge the meatballs in the flour , and then brown the meatballs in batches until light brown
8. as they brown , place them into a rectangular baking dish
9. for the sauce: stir together the ketchup , onions , vinegar , sugar , worcestershire sauce and hot sauce
10. drizzle the sauce evenly on the meatballs
11. bake until bubbly and hot , about 45 minutes
demonstrations.review: i love these! pioneer woman does it again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
delicious crock pot barbecue ribs

these can also be cooked in the oven and i have done so many times, prep time includes browning the ribs ;-)

1. set oven to 400 degrees f
2. season ribs with seasoned salt or white salt and pepper
3. place the ribs on a greased baking sheet
4. bake / brown for 20 minutes , then turn over and bake / brown for another 20 minutes
5. place the ribs in the crock pot
6. in a large bowl mix together ketchup , bbq sauce , brown sugar , apple cider vinegar , worcestershire sauce , tabasco to taste and garlic
7. mix well to combine
8. pour over the ribs then turn to coat with the sauce
9. cover and cook on low for 6-8 hours or until ribs are tender
10. delicious !
demonstrations.review: another delicious recipe from kittencal!  okay, my changes when i made the second time, sprinkled some worcestershire sauce on top on the ribs on both sides before searing in oven.   used local-store bought bar-be-que sauce instead and added chopped onion and garlic.  both times i've cooked these, about 5 hours on low in crock-pot has been perfect, but cooking time will depend on meat.  these are some very, very good ribs.  thanks so much for the recipe, kittencal!  don't skip the searing the ribs in the oven step.  i think this is what make these ribs so great.  first, it seals in the meat juices, and it gets rid of some the excess fat from the ribs.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
yummy crunchy apple pie

great pie!

1. use foil on bottom of oven rather than a cookie sheet under pie pan
2. prepare pastry for single-crust pie
3. place in pie plate and trim and crimp the edge
4. refrigerate 30 minute loosely covered with plastic wrap
5. in a large mixing bowl , stir together the sugar , flour , cinnamon , nutmeg , allspice , and salt
6. add apple slices and gently toss until they are coated well
7. transfer mixture to pie
8. for crumb topping: stir together brown sugar , flour , and oats
9. using a pastry blender , cut in the butter until topping resembles coarse crumbs
10. sprinkle over apple mixture in pie
11. to prevent over-browning while baking , cover edge of pie with foil
12. bake at 375 degrees fahrenheit for 25 minutes
13. remove foil and bake 25 to 30 minutes more , or until top is golden
14. remove from oven
15. cool on wire rack about an hour and serve !
demonstrations.review: i don't really care for apple pie, but several people who ate this pie said it was the best apple pie they ever had!  it was also an extremely pretty pie...lots of oohs and aahs when it was brought out.  served with ice cream.  thanks for posting!

target.recipe_text:
rosemary   garlic focaccia

i was lucky enough to have my italian uncle pat make this for me all through my teens. i like to think now that it sustained me more than physically. i could eat this every day and never get tired of it - it's the perfect bread.

1. in a bowl , stir together yeast , sugar and 1 cups lukewarm water and proof yeast for 10-15 minutes , or until foamy
2. stir in 4 cup of flour , 1 tblsps of the olive oil and the salt , adding as much of the remaining flour as necessary to form a soft and slightly sticky dough
3. transfer to a lightly-oiled bowl , turn to coat , and let rise , covered , in a warm place for 1 hour , or until double in size
4. knead dough down and press with lightly-oiled hands into a well-oiled 15 x 10 inch jelly-roll pan and let it rise , covered loosely , for 30 minutes
5. preheat oven to 375 degrees f
6. set rack in center of oven
7. dimple dough with your fingers in places , drizzle 2 tblsps olive oil over and spread over dough
8. sprinkle with rosemary , garlic and sea salt
9. bake for 35-40 minutes or until pale golden
10. let cool for 10 minutes before cutting
11. serve warm or at room temperature
12. dried oregano is also a great add-in
target.review: I have made many focaccia breads, but this one is over the top.  It is now in my regular bread rotation.  Thanks for posting.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
easiest ever fettuccine alfredo

no separate cooking for the sauce in this awesome dish. ready for the table in minutes.

1. boil fettucini according to package directions
2. meantime , cream butter until fluffy , then add egg yolk and cream
3. beating constantly , add parmesan cheese
4. drain noodles and toss in butter mixture immediately to melt
5. season with salt and pepper and add some chopped parsley for color
6. serve immediately
demonstrations.review: This is a vey kid friendly dish, both to cook and eat.  I'm teaching my 12 year old great nephew to cook and this was the perfect recipe, he was thrilled with the end result and all the compliments he received from  adults.  However, I think the biggest compliment was that his little brother liked it so much.  Thanks so much for posting this keeper.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
broccoli cheddar casserole

this takes minutes to throw together and everything is mixed in one bowl, sharp cheddar cheese is recommended to use for this, you may also sprinkle grated cheddar on top the last few minutes of baking --- to serve a crowd double the recipe and bake in a 13 x 9-inch baking dish, i also add in some tabasco sauce.

1. set oven to 350 degrees f
2. butter a 9 x 9 or a 11 x 7-inch baking dish
3. in a medium bowl combine undiluted soup with mayonnaise , sour cream , beaten egg , garlic powder , chopped onion , seasoned salt and black pepper
4. whisk until well combined
5. mix in the grated cheese and chopped broccoli
6. spread into baking dish
7. sprinkle the parmesan cheese on top
8. bake uncovered for about 45 minutes or until hot and bubbly
demonstrations.review: Made this for our family Thanksgiving dinner and it was a major hit even with the kids who are normally anti vegetable.  Followed the recipe and would not change a thing.  You did it again, thanks for another great recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cannellini bean stew

tuscan-inspired soups often seem to be overladen with ingredients, leaving them rather expensive and time consuming to make.  in spite of the simplicity of this recipe, i don't find anything lacking.  it has an excellent flavor and i can make it many times a year because it's so fast and inexpensive.  serve with crusty bread and a salad.

1. in a dutch oven over medium heat , bring the beans , broth , garlic , bay leaf , and carrots to a boil
2. cover , reduce heat , and simmer for 15 minutes
3. remove and discard the bay leaf
4. add he spinach , salt and pepper , and stir for 1 minute
5. spoon the stew into bowls
6. drizzle with the oil
7. if desired , add either some of vinegar or parmesan
demonstrations.review: I must say I was pleasantly surprised, this is a very simple and tasty dish.  Served it with Simple Crusty Bread and it made quite a nice combination.  Thanks for posting.

target.recipe_text:
corned beef and cabbage in guinness

the irish butcher at my market gave me a new (to me anyway) recipe for corned beef & cabbage; he told me to cook it in guinness draught. (guinness stout will make the dish bitter).  since everyone raved about it, i thought i'd share the recipe he gave me. 

note: some reviewers have mentioned that the broth/sauce is very salty. it is important to rinse your corned beef in cold water before cooking it to remove some of the excess salt from the corning process. (i usually soak mine in cold water for a bit depending on the brand - some are much saltier than others).  --- i have tried 5 times today to change the wording of the last ingredient on the list from "1-2lbs carrot, peeled and cut into 3-inch pieces" to "1 - 2 pounds of carrots, peeled and cut into 3-inch pieces". every time the change "goes through," it does not reflect the new wording. grrrrrrr!

1. rinse corned beef under cold water , and pat dry
2. in a dutch oven , or other large pot with a cover , brown corned beef well on all sides over high heat
3. pour guinness over the meat , and add enough water to just cover the brisket
4. add the onion , garlic , bay leaf , cinnamon , cloves , allspice and pepper to the pot
5. bring pot to a boil and skim off any foam
6. reduce heat to a simmer
7. cover pot and simmer for 3 hours
8. add carrots , then potatoes and then the cabbage wedges to the pot
9. cover pot , and continue cooking until meat and vegetables are tender
10. remove meat and vegetables to warm serving platter / dishes , leaving the cooking liquid / sauce in the pot
11. over high heat , bring the cooking liquid to a boil , and cook until the amount of liquid is reduced by half
12. slice the corned beef
13. serve with the vegetables and the sauce on the side
target.review: This was DELICIOUS!  I made it tonight for St. Patrick's Day dinner.  I loved the flavor, even though I'm not a huge fan of cabbage.  Even my picky husband loved it!  Thanks for the great recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
hamburg gravy

no one will probably like this, but it was a staple recipe when i was growing up. my mom used ground venison b/c we were poor and that's all we had. i still like to make it once in awhile, but i use ground beef. it's really easy and filling. my mom only added the peas if she need to stretch it a little bit more. time is a guess b/c i have never timed making it.

1. mix flour , water and salt together
2. add to meat
3. cook until thickened
4. add peas if desired
5. serve over mashed potatoes
demonstrations.review: Yummy!  My husband and I both loved this!  I made it with corn instead of peas because I didn't have any.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
warp speed pumpkin butter

warp-speed because you make it in the microwave - no all-day cooking for this spicy-sweet spread! my kids like to put it on their toast, and pretend they're having pumpkin pie for breakfast! it does taste like pumpkin pie filling, and makes a wonderful hostess gift. make sure your recipient puts this right into the refrigerator! note: don't try to 

1. combine everything except the canned pumpkin in a microwaveable one quart bowl
2. mix well
3. microwave on high for 3 minutes , then stir
4. mix in the pumpkin well , and microwave on high 5 minutes longer
5. it should be bubbly
6. put into clean , sterilized jars for gift-giving , or into other clean , airtight containers for home use
7. let cool slightly , then refrigerate
8. this will keep several weeks in refrigerator or can be frozen for longer storage
9. this cannot be kept in your pantry- must be refrigerated or frozen
demonstrations.review: SOOOO GOOD!!!  SOOO EASY!!!  What else is there to say?

demonstrations.recipe_text:
roasted potatoes dijon

very simple potatoes that are tastier than you would think. they soak up the liquid and absorb all the flavor.  good, no fuss side dish.  

1. mix first 4 ingredients in a small bowl
2. lightly grease 13 x 9 pan or shallow baking sheet
3. toss potatoes with mixture
4. bake at 425 for about 40 minutes , or until tender , stirring occasionally
demonstrations.review: Delish!  I would never have thought I'd like this, but it was very tasty.  I did as many of the others suggested by lowering the baking temp to 375 and leaving them in for a full hour.  They turned out perfect.  Thanks for a great recipe, Kelly!

target.recipe_text:
foolproof buttercream frosting

you can make this up to a week ahead; cover airtight and chill. before using, let it come to room temperature and beat briefly at medium speed to restore texture. for interesting variations, replace vanilla with 2 to 3 tablespoons of liqeur, 6 ounces melted bittersweet chocolate, or up to 1/2 cup strained jam of any flavor. this recipe is from sunset magazine.

1. in mixer bowl at high speed , beat egg yolks until pale yellow , 4 to 5 minutes
2. butter a 2-cup glass measuring cup
3. in a 2- to 3-quart pan , combine sugar and corn syrup
4. cook over medium-high heat and stir until sugar is dissolved and mixture comes to a rolling boil
5. immediately pour into the butter glass measuring cup
6. beating constantly at medium speed , pour syrup in a thin , steady stream into egg yolks
7. continue beating until mixture is at room temperature
8. add butter and vanilla
9. beat just until smooth
target.review: This was less intensely sweet than my usual beaten butter & icing sugar buttercream, with a richer, smoother mouth feel: I loved it! I added the sugar syrup directly from the pan rather than transferring it to a measuring jug and it still worked fine. I also tried the chocolate version and found that it still worked well with up to twice as much chocolate as the notes suggested and, of course, tasted even more chocolatey as a result! I would perhaps be more likely to use it as a filling for a cake rather than the top-and-sides frosting however: it has a different texture and quality of sweetness from that which I'm used to in a frosting (it's still delicious though!). And I'm not sure I'd want to tackle it if I didn't have an electric whisk: it does need a lot of beating!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
tofu scramble with hollandaise sauce

the hollandaise sauce makes this dish truly decadent. i often eat this atop a piece of toast.

1. -----------tofuscramble-----------
2. drizzle enough oil to cover bottom of fry pan
3. heat over medium heat and add onion , bell pepper and tofu
4. cook , stirring frequently , until tofu loses most of it's moisture
5. add the rest of the ingredients and turn the heat up a little
6. continue cooking until mixture resembles scrambled eggs
7. ---------hollandaisesauce----------
8. put nutritional yeast flakes , flour , soy milk , paprika and salt in a saucepan and whisk over medium heat until mixture thickens and bubbles
9. cook for one more minute after you see it start bubbling
10. remove from heat and add margarine and mustard
11. whisk together until margarine is incorporated
12. drizzle over tofu scramble and serve
demonstrations.review: I just made the sauce as I already have a favourite recipe for scrambled tofu. The sauce was nice, but I found it to be way too thick and salty: try starting with half the amount of flour and salt and working up from there if necessary. Also, although the sauce was tasty in its own way, if you're looking for a convincing vegan analogue of real hollandaise sauce you will be disappointed by this recipe. Don't get me wrong, though: I did enjoy it, and Carol is right - it does make a plain old plate of scrambled tofu into something rather special!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pancakes with vanilla banana  using an egg replacer

i don't like eggs and i always use an egg substitute unless i'm not having the recipe. if you want to try the recipe with egg just don’t use the tablespoon of water.  the idea for the banana topping came from recipe #173220 and the idea for the pancake came from the leaflet in the box of egg-like 'the egg replacer'

1. peel and slice bananas , place them in a small casserole dish , pour over vanilla essence , brown sugar , orange juice , chopped butter and sprinkle cinnamon
2. cover to not allow any steam to escape and place it under the griller for 10 minutes
3. while the topping is cooking mix egg replacer with water until completely combined
4. then add in milk , flour and oil and stir until batter is smooth
5. i use a hand wand / blender
6. use a non-stick fry pan or pancake pan , spray cooking oil , heat
7. place small amount or large amount of batter pancake into pan
8. fry , flip over when brown and fry second side
9. to serve:
10. large pancake place the pancake in the middle of a plate , and spread some vanilla banana in the middle and roll the pancake , cut it half , drizzle over the vanilla banana juices and if your using ice cream , scope and serve it on top
11. small pancake layer each pancake on top of each other , spread some vanilla banana on top , if your using ice cream , scope and serve it on top and drizzle over the vanilla vanana juices
12. serve immediately
demonstrations.review: I just tried the topping with my usual pancake recipe: it was nice, but there was WAY too much vanilla. I have my suspicions that it should actually be 4 TEASPOONS, not tablespoons. Also, there's an ounce of butter in the ingredients list, but no mention of it in the instructions, so I just left it out without any apparent detriment! But maybe one could try dotting it over the bananas before grilling them...

demonstrations.recipe_text:
peanut butter graham squares with dark chocolate drizzle

fast, easy and yummy!  adapted from a king arthur flour recipe

1. arrange whole graham crackers in the bottom of an 8x8" square baking dish
2. in a medium mixing bowl , beat together graham cracker crumbs , butter , sugar , peanut butter , vanilla and salt until smooth
3. scoop this mixture into the baking dish and gently spread over the graham crackers
4. cover and place in the refrigerator for at least 1 hour
5. cut into squares and drizzle with melted dark chocolate
demonstrations.review: Fabulous! You can't get graham crackers in the UK, so I made a biscuit base by melting 2oz butter with 2 tbsp golden syrup, then stirring in 6oz crushed bourbon biscuits (Oreo cookies would probably be the closest US equivalent). I then pressed this into the base of the tin and chilled it while making the topping. Not only did it add a delicious chocolatey flavour, but it also provided a lovely colour contrast with the light brown topping. I used real butter, ordinary peanut butter and digestive biscuit crumbs for the topping and had no problems with it being too sloppy, even when stored at room temperature.

target.recipe_text:
cheesecake lemon bars

these are some quick and easy bars that everyone loves. they are nothing to whip up real quick and i always have the ingredients on hand.

1. mix together the cake mix , butter and 1 egg
2. pat into the bottom of a greased 9"x13" baking pan
3. mix together the cream cheese , 2 eggs and powdered sugar
4. pour over the cake mixture in the pan
5. bake at 325 degrees f for 35-40 minutes
6. cool and cut into bars
target.review: Great Recipe, it tasted good and was very easy to prepare. I sprinkled a little powdered sugar on top for presentation :) Looked great !

demonstrations.recipe_text:
4 layer vanilla chocolate raspberry bars

i love recipes like this! the vanilla chips are creamy and combine well with the raspberry! it is just perfect for any occasion! 8)

1. heat oven to 350
2. in large mixing bowl , combine sugar , butter , salt and vanilla extract
3. beat at medium speed , scraping bowl often and then reduce speed to low
4. beat , adding in flour 1 cup at a time , scraping bowl often , until mixture is crumbly
5. set aside 1 cup of mixture
6. add eggs to remaining crumb mixture in the bowl
7. beat until mixture forms dough
8. evenly press into ungreased 13x9-inch pan
9. bake 30 minutes or until lightly browned
10. slather preserves over the hot , partially baked bars
11. sprinkle vanilla chips over and add reserved crumb mixture
12. baking for additional 20-25 minutes or until topping is lightly browned
13. allow to cool thoroughly before cutting into bars
demonstrations.review: This is a great recipe! It would be especially good for holidays to brighten up the table because they make a beatiful looking dessert square

demonstrations.recipe_text:
margarita parfaits

ole! what a way to finish a summer dinner. light and refreshing with a touch of tequila. change the yogurt flavor and the garnish for a new desert every time.

1. mix yogurt with triple sec , tequila , and lime zest
2. fold yogurt mixture into dessert topping until well incorporated
3. spoon into magarita glasses and garnish with a slice of lime
demonstrations.review:
Very good !! Also by using the No fat whip and low fat yogurt, this is a great guiltless pleasure !!! 
I also could not find Lime Yogurt, but found key lime pie yogurt and it tasted YUMMY !!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mr  food honey mustard chicken

dbmnmr

1. preheat the oven to 425 degrees f
2. coat a 10- by 15-inch rimmed baking sheet with nonstick cooking spray
3. place the chicken breasts on the baking sheet
4. in a small bowl , combine the remaining ingredients
5. mix well
6. spread the mixture evenly over the chicken breasts
7. bake for 12 to 15 minutes , or until the topping is golden and no pink remains in the chicken
demonstrations.review: excellent recipe...I added some coursely ground mustard to it for a littly zing :) Very yummy

target.recipe_text:
spicy black beans and rice with mangoes  crock pot

this is so good and it's easy too. this recipe was found in fresh from the vegetarian slow cooker.

1. heat oil in large skillet over medium heat
2. add onion , bell pepper , garlic and jalapeno , cover , and cook 5 minutes until softened
3. add in seasonings , mix well and cook for 1 minute
4. transfer mixture into a 3 1 / 2 to 4 quart slow cooker
5. add bean , water , brown sugar , salt and pepper
6. stir well
7. cover and cook on low for 6 to 8 hours
8. add the cooked rice and the mangoes
9. allow to cook another 10 minutes
10. serve and enjoy
target.review: I was so amazed at how this dish came out!  It was awesome and really didnt take that long to make.  It filled us up without getting the kitchen hot and the leftovers were even better.  This is easily a stand alone dinner or a side for a BBQ or other bigger dinner.  Thank you for posting.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
easy chicken bundles

this is a simple -- yet tasty -- recipe that can be tweaked to individual taste, just by changing the flavor of cheese spread used!

1. in large skillet , melt butter , sprinkle chicken breasts with pepper and add to skillet
2. cook 8 to 10 minutes or until well browned on all sides
3. set aside to cool slightly
4. unroll both cans of the dough and separate into 8 rectangles
5. press each into 6x4-inch rectangle , firmly pressing perforations to seal
6. spread cheese evenly in center of each dough rectangle and place chicken over cheese
7. bring corners of dough together over chicken and press to seal
8. place on cookie sheet that has been sprayed with cooking spray
9. bake at 375 degrees for 18 to 22 minutes or until deep golden brown
10. if you would like , brush lightly with egg during last 5 minutes of baking time
11. variations: try different cheese spreads such as swiss , cheddar , etc
12. to get different flavors
13. also , try adding a thin slice of ham and using swiss spread for a different take on cordon bleu
demonstrations.review: I made this last night with a slight variation because I could not find a spreadable cheese.  I sprinkled shredded cheese on the dough sections then added my chicken and poured some BBQ on top and then wrapped them up.  They were perfect after 18 minutes in the oven and were eaten up by the family.  Thank you posting such a great recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
potatoes a l alsacienne

wonderful french dish!
a different way to serve potatoes that my whole family just loves.
enjoy!

1. peel the potatoes and cut into 1 inch pieces
2. place in a pan of salted water , bring to the boil and cook for 5 minutes
3. drain well and set aside
4. melt the butter in a frying pan with the olive oil , add the onions and bacon and cook for about 5 minutes or until the bacon fat begins to run
5. add the potatoes and cook for a further 10 minutes or until the potatoes are tender and crisp turning occasionally
6. add the herbs , salt and pepper and mix well
7. serve immediately
demonstrations.review: These were so yummy, I used turkey bacon and everyone in the family loved them!  We had a few left over so I am hoping that they taste even better today.  Thank you for posting such a yummy and easy recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
waldorf salad   no mayonnaise

another vt recipe that sounds too good to lose. this is a lightened up version of waldorf salad that uses yogurt iinstead of mayonnaise and also, for a surprise treat, includes pears. if you don't have ripe pears, use canned. you may peel the apples and pears if desired.
the cooking time includes time to cool down the cooked cider.

1. boil cider over high heat in a small saucepan until reduced to 3 tbsp
2. allow cider to cool completely
3. mix together the cooled cider , yogurt and cinnamon and set aside
4. mix the apples , pears , grapes , celery , raisins and nuts in a bowl
5. add the yogurt mixture to the apple mixture and toss to coat
6. place a lettuce leaf of each plate and top with waldorf salad
demonstrations.review: THANK YOU!!!! I could live off of this recipe for the rest of my life.  I used Braeburn Apples and D'Anjou pears and have made it with dark raisins and sultanas.  You cannot beat this.  Everyone in the house loved it and I have printed out about 3 copies and passed them around as well.  Thanks again!

target.recipe_text:
world s best ribs

this recipe is quite simple and the results are incredible. i usually double the rub recipe and store it in a jar for next time. if you've never tried ribs before, try this recipe. this recipe can be made on the grill or in the oven.

1. mix brown sugar , emeril's essence , salt , pepper , paprika , cumin , garlic and cayenne pepper thoroughly , and sprinkle on both sides of ribs to taste
2. for grilling , carefully wrap in aluminum foil and cook bone side down approximately 1 1 / 2 hours on low temperature
3. no need to turn
4. after ribs become tender , remove from foil and continue cooking on both sides to desired crispness
5. apply barbecue sauce liberally to both sides and allow approximately 10 minutes for barbecue sauce to caramelize
6. brush a second time if desired , and allow to caramelize
7. remove from grill and enjoy !
8. for oven baking , wrap in aluminum foil and place on a cookie sheet in a 275f oven for 4 hours
9. place a pan with water in the oven also to keep them moist
10. remove and discard foil and brush with barbecue sauce and allow 10 minutes to caramelize
11. brush a second time if desired
12. remove from oven and enjoy !
target.review: Easy recipe that tasted delicious.  Be sure to turn the ribs frequently after removing the foil.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
bbq brats  n beer

i made this recipe last night for the first time and they are good! this is great if you are having a gang in and want a "do it yourself" style dinner (whatever) have baked beans on the side.

1. put the brats , onions , peppercorns , cloves , garlic in a saucepan , pour in the beer
2. bring to a boil and simmer the brats 15 minutes
3. drain
4. bbq the brats about 10 minutes
5. spray with water while bbqing to form a crisp skin
6. serve on the roll with mustard and hot peppers or other relish or serve them as your meat for dinner
demonstrations.review: Brats turned out great - juicy and flavorful.  Only watch-out is to make sure after boiling in beer to keep the simmer low - otherwise the brats split, losing much of their juice (similarly, need to BBQ on low-to-medium to avoid splitting).

demonstrations.recipe_text:
virginia barbecue chicken

summer saturdays in virginia are filled with the smell of this chicken. it is the chicken that all the churches, boy scouts and other organizations fix for fund raisers. it is one of our favorite ways to grill chicken legs or halves. it works really well to grill the chicken and then eat later cold too. great for a picnic!

1. mix all ingredients , except chicken
2. use a small amount to marinade about 5-10 chicken halves or 12-20 drumsticks for a couple hours or over night
3. grill over very medium coals until pieces test done , basting often
4. it works best if you use a grilling pit and allow it to slow cook for a couple hours
demonstrations.review: Excellent recipe!  I used a gas grill, cooked the chicken using the indirect method for about 1.5 hours.  Turned out crispy on the outside, juicy on the inside.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s easy no fail make anytime turkey gravy

i have been using this recipe for many years, my family loves this gravy and i have served it to dinner guests over the holidays and always receive rave reviews! --- you don't need to make this gravy using all pan drippings, if you do not have 4 cups of drippings you may mix with chicken broth to make the 4 cups, or it may be made with only chicken broth, please see note on the bottom of the recipe--- this may be made slightly ahead and kept uncovered on top of the stove until ready to serve, just whisk before using if you have any left over this gravy freezes very well or you may reduce all ingredients down to half and for a thinner gravy reduce flour by 1 tablespoon  --- also see my recipe#314890
for more of my recipes visit www.kittencalskitchen.com

1. drain the pan drippings for the roasted turkey through a fine strainer
2. let sit and then remove any fat from the top of the drippings
3. add in chicken broth or water to make 4 cups if necessary
4. in a medium saucepan , melt margarine or butter
5. add in lots of black pepper
6. add in 1 / 2 cup flour plus 3 tablespoons
7. constantly whisk for about 3 minutes over low heat
8. slowly add in the 4 cups turkey broth / drippings
9. whisk constantly over medium-low heat until bubbly and thickened
10. use right away or keep warm over lowest heat setting , whisk again before serving
11. options to make this gravy using all chicken broth prepare as directed using 4 cups low sodium chicken broth and 1 tablespoon chicken boullion powder ---- or you may add in low sodium chicken broth omitting bouillon powder to pan drippings to make up 4 cups
demonstrations.review: Great gravy - needed to stir a long time (10-15 minutes) to get it to adequetly thicken.  I used 1/4 tsp pepper.

target.recipe_text:
persian eggs poached in tomato sauce

i am fortunate to work at a place where the manager of the cafeteria is a moroccan native.  our mutual love of food has resulted in endless exchange of recipes, spices and samplings.  (indeed, some of the items now served in the cafeteria are recipes from this site.) one one occasion, i was lucky enough to be able to share in the lunch he prepared for the staff. i love eggs and his were just amazing.  this recipe from world vegetarian seems like a close approximate - though i know his version included a generous bit of cumin and cilantro.  i'm posting the original here and will begin to tinker.  once perfected, i'll post that version as a second recipe.  will experiment to see if this works as well with canned tomatoes.

1. put the oil in a non-stick skillet over medium high heat
2. add onions and garlic
3. stir-fry for a minute , then reduce heat to medium
4. continue cooking vegetables for 3 or 4 minutes so that the onion becomes translucent with a little color around the edges
5. add the tomatoes and simmer
6. cook uncovered for 10 minutes
7. season with salt and pepper to taste
8. once the sauce has cooked , use the back of a spoon to create 4 rounded wells , one in each quarter of the pan
9. carefully break each egg and place into each of the hollows
10. cover pan with a lid leaving it partially open to allow some heat and moisture to escape
11. cook until eggs reach your preferred level of doneness
12. carefully scoop egg with some sauce onto serving plates
13. garnish with chives
