14. serve with warmed pita or other flatbread of choice
15. variation: you can make this a little spicier , add a small chili to the onions
16. if you do so , you may want to omit the chives and instead garnish with finely chopped parsley
target.review: Very tasty recipe!  I think next time we'll use canned tomatoes instead of peeling and seeding our own.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
savory sea scallops in white wine sauce

this is such an easy dish but with great end results! i serve it with a pasta such as my recipe #55679. yummy!

1. heat oil in heavy skillet over high heat
2. when oil begins to smoke add scallops
3. sear each side for one minute or until each side is golden brown
4. add 1 / 2 cup of wine and lower heat to medium
5. simmer for 2 minutes
6. remove scallops from pan
7. add remaining wine and lemon juice , and garlic
8. bring to a boil and reduce by half
9. add butter , parsley and season with pepper
10. place scallops on a plate and smother with sauce
11. serve
demonstrations.review: Not bad, but nothing extraordinary.  I felt the wine taste in the recipe was a little strong.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
quesadillas for one or two

nice quick lunch for yourself or for you and your honey. recipe can be cut in half to make for one. we like to add 1 or 2 of the variations, there's always something left over in the fridge to be used up, use your imagination.  (the oil can be replaced with veggie cooking spray, it works just as well) our standard is deli chicken slices, a mix of cheddar and parmesan, green pepper sticks, and chopped green onions and fresh cilantro, served with hot salsa. yummy!!!

1. brush pan with oil and heat
2. place tortilla in pan and heat on one side
3. turn tortilla over and sprinkle with cheese , tomato and chile pepper
4. cook until cheese melts
5. remove tortilla to plate
6. top with guacamole or salsa if desired
7. any one or more of the variations ingredients can be added
8. fold in half , cut into quarters and serve hot
demonstrations.review: I've been making quesadillas for years, but it wasn't until this recipe that I even thought to use oil to cook them.  It made my normal quesadillas 10 times better.  This recipe was fast and easy too

demonstrations.recipe_text:
asparagus and wild rice soup

quick, delicious homemade soup. discovered this recipe in the good start magazine, when i was pregnant. excellent source of calcium, nutrients and energy. we just love it!

1. prepare rice according to package directions , set aside
2. heat oil in large saucepan on medium-high
3. add onion , garlic and asparagus , cook 3-5 minutes and stir occassionly
4. add rice , broth , salt and pepper
5. bring to boil
6. mix evaporated milk with constarch in small bowl until smooth
7. add to saucepan
8. cook 3-5 minutes , stirring occasionally until thickened
9. stir in parsley
10. for vegetarians use the vegetable stock
demonstrations.review: Cooked close to as listed, I was out of vegetable oil, so I used olive oil.  It was good!  I would probably add more rice next time.

target.recipe_text:
prosciutto feta cheese strata

a lovely greek-style breakfast, lunch or brunch dish from the rockledge inn in colorado.  while it is very easy to prepare, it does need to be assembled the night before, refrigerated overnight and then allowed to sit at room temperature before baking for an hour, so prep time includes 8 hours in the fridge and half an hour sitting time.

1. line bottom of 13x9x2" glass baking dish completely with 1 layer of bread , cutting some to fit
2. arrange 1 / 2 of prosciutto evenly over bread
3. sprinkle 1 / 2 feta cheese and 1 / 2 provolone over the ham
4. sprinkle with 1 / 2 green onions and basil
5. top with 2nd layer of bread and repeat
6. cut crusts into cubes and sprinkle on top
7. whisk eggs , milk , mustard , and salt in bowl and season with salt and pepper
8. pour egg mixture over strata
9. press down on bread with spatula
10. drizzle melted butter over strata
11. cover and refrigerate overnight
12. preheat oven to 350f
13. uncover strata and let stand at room temperature 30 minutes
14. bake until center is set , about 1 hour
15. remove from oven
16. preheat broiler and place strata under about 30 seconds , until top is golden
17. cut into large squares and serve
target.review: ZWT4: Worth all 5 stars plus more! This is an easy to prepare dish that yields tasty results!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
caramel bananas

another recipe i found on-line while looking for south africa recipes to post for zwt.

1. in a small skillet , heat 1 / 2 cup white sugar
2. 1 cup light brown sugar
3. 3 tbs
4. evaporated milk
5. 2 tbs
6. butter
7. cook until sugar caramelizes
8. stir in 2 oz
9. white rum and cool
10. arrange 1 / 2 banana per person in compote dish
11. spoon 3 to 4 tbs
12. caramel sauce over bananas
13. sprinkle 1 to 2 teaspoons chopped peanuts over caramel sauce
demonstrations.review: ZWT4: Made for the African Dessert Challenge. I substituted both the white and brown sugar for half the amount using the Splenda sugar blends. EXCELLENT!! I loved it and now it is even better knowing I cut alot of calories out!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
orange shake m up cake

this recipe is for kids, it encourages kids to get involved in the kitchen and at the same time to have fun! - the idea of this recipe was from http://pubs.cas.psu.edu/freepubs/pdfs/ua209.pdf  - the kids (little miss (dd) and my niece) made this for their grandmother.  they had lots of fun counting and watching the jar change when the different ingredients were added.  they were quite proud of themselves when they seen the end result.  we topped it with melted white chocolate with a little copha and orange food dye. suggestion with the recipe is grease the base or use baking paper on the bottom.

1. pre-heat oven at 180oc / 350oc / gas 4
2. break 2 eggs into a large top jar / container with a tight fitting lid
3. seal and shake 10 times
4. add , sugar , oil , orange juice , seal and shake 20 more times or until blended
5. add , self raising flour , baking powder , salt , seal and shake 50 more times or until smooth
6. pour into square cake pan and bake for 20 minutes or until cake comes away from the sides or until skewer comes out clean when inserted into the centre of the cake
7. ice with your favourite icing / frosting or sprinkle icing sugar
demonstrations.review: Aussie Swap#17: What a wonderful citrusy-taste!! I truly enjoyed this cake!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
barbie birthday cake

i was very surprised to not see a recipe for this cake. it is very popular with mothers of young girls. my daughters 4th is tomorrow and i can't wait to see the look on her face when she sees her cake! i welcome as many pics as possible to show all the different styles you can create with this idea.
jan 31st,08 edit: i used my pampered chef measuring/mixing bowl to bake this in, and it also was too short for the doll to fit down in. i ended up buying a cheap dime store imitation that had hollow legs and just cut them off at the correct height. :)

1. you must also have a barbie doll for this recipe , but i could not include it in the ingredients list as it is a non-food item
2. preheat oven to 350 degrees farenheit
3. grease and flour a an 8 cup rounded glass measuring cup , or you can use a metal mixing bowl
4. prepare cake mix by adding first 4 ingredients and mixing for 2 minutes
5. pour cake mix into prepared measuring cup (or metal mixing bowl , and bake 50-60 mins until knife inserted in center comes out clean
6. let cool for 15 mins , then invert onto cake tray
7. let cool completely before frosting , about 3 hours
8. after completely cool use frosting to decorate cake to look like barbie's dress
9. insert barbie legs all the way down into middle of the cake , then use remaining frosting to cover her bosoms to complete the dress
10. enjoy !
demonstrations.review: Followed instructions except I added two 8" cake layers underneath to add the heigth!

target.recipe_text:
roasted veggies over creamy polenta

weight watchers recipe. roasted zucchini and asparagus are served over a creamy polenta, low in fat and calories, but still very filling!  takes less than 30 minutes!

1. preheat oven to 475 degree's and line 15x10x1 pan with non-stick foil and / or spray with cooking spray
2. toss veggies together , drizzle with olive oil and roast for 18 minutes , stirring once
3. while veggies are roasting , combine red wine vinegar and splenda , set aside
4. pour milk into saucepan and set over medium heat , slowly add cornmeal and basil or rosemary , if using , and stir constantly
5. heat for 5-7 minutes , until mixture thickens
6. this is a light & creamy polenta , so should not be dense or lumpy
7. pour polenta into three serving bowls
8. remove veggies from oven and pour red wine mixture over top , stirring to combine
9. top polenta with veggies and grated parmesan cheese
target.review: This is a good base recipe, but I feel like it needs a little tweaking. The veggies turned out very flavorful - the instructions don't say what to do with the garlic clove or the olive oil, so I sliced two medium sized garlic cloves with the veggies, then used olive oil spray to coat them evenly during roasting. I also added half a red bell pepper, yum!  The polenta was very creamy, but needed some seasoning. I added about a teaspoon of kosher salt, but we felt like it still needed something... Unfortunately, I was out of parmesan for sprinkling on top, I'm sure that would have added to the great flavor in the veggies.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
wild rice with spicy pecans

delicious

1. combine the water , bay leaves , salt , and pepper in a pot with a tight fitting lid
2. bring to a boil
3. add the rice , reduce to a simmer , and cook for 40 to 45 minutes
4. when cooked stir in the butter , cover again and keep warm
5. combine the pecans , cayenne , maple syrup and salt in a saute pan and quickly cook over low heat until the nuts have lightly toasted
6. remove from the heat and combine with the cooked wild rice
demonstrations.review:
Perfection!  DH grew up on wild rice, with a family from Iowa and Minnesota.  In the south, it can be hard to find, and costs a pretty penny.  When we do find it, it's great to have a recipe like this that's worth waiting for!
I soaked my rice overnight and rinsed it well.  Also, instead of 3 cups water, I used half homemade chicken stock, half water - next time I'll use all stock for added depth of flavor.  My cooking time was a little longer, maybe by 15 minutes, but that's personal preference on the texture of the cooked rice.
I only had cashews on hand, and it turned out great.  I didn't mix them in, as they had quite a kick - I served them on top, and left them off of the kids' servings.  DH and I loved the spice they added, and they weren't too sweet - they blended very well with the rice.  
This is an excellent recipe that we'll use often!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chinese chilli chicken

this is one of our favorite quick and easy stir fry chicken dishes with a slight kick, lots of flavor too. it's about a medium spice.you can easily adjust the heat to your taste. i use boneless thigh fillet because i find the breast is a little dry in this.

1. slice the chicken
2. roughly chop the onion and pepper
3. grate or finely chop the garlic
4. cut the chilli in half , discard the seed and finely chop
5. heat the oil in a wok or a large deep frying pan
6. add the chicken , onion , peppers , chilli , garlic , and ginger
7. fry for about 5 minutes on high heat
8. add the remaining ingredients to the pan and continue cooking about 10-15 minutes until most of the liquid has evaporated and the chicken has cooked through
9. serve with rice or chinese noodles
demonstrations.review:
This is a terrific recipe that went together easily and was enjoyed by the entire family.  I had to make some adjustments for the kids - I omitted the jalepeno entirely, and only used about 1 tsp of chili sauce.  DH and I added more at the table.  I also used a red bell pepper instead of a green one.
The only thing that I would change is to start with less broth - by the time it cooked down, the chicken was very done, and it was still a bit soupy.  I think I'd cut the broth in half, and maybe add a tsp of cornstarch to thicken it up.
Thanks for a keeper!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
almost  starbucks frappuccino

since i serve this is very large glasses i have listed at two servings, you may divide into as many servings as you wish, make certain to use very strong coffee for this --- this is very good!

1. in a blender combine coffee with ice cream and chocolate syrup
2. blend until smooth
3. add in sugar and blend slightly until combined
4. place about 1 cup crushed ice in two large tall glasses
5. divide the mixture into the glasses
6. top with a dollup of whipped cream
demonstrations.review: Yumyumyum! This is excellent. The only problem is, even though I'm saving the 5 bucks and change, now that I know what's IN it, I think the guilt is even worse! I think the sweetness is perfect without adding any more sugar. I did use fresh whipped cream, too, because it just wasn't fattening enough already. :D

target.recipe_text:
warm chocolate molten cakes

oh so good! these little cakes are so simple to make and your guests with think you spent ages on them. good quality chocolate is key here. if you don't have souffle dishes or custard dishes, you could use muffin tins, but it would make more little cakes (then you could have two each!). use heart shaped moulds for valentine's day and top with whipped cream and raspberry coulis. mmmmm. enjoy!

1. preheat oven to 425 degrees
2. butter six 6-ounce custard cups , souffle dishes or other moulds
3. mix the 2 tbsp sugar and cocoa powder together and dust the inside of each mould
4. set aside
5. melt chocolate and 2 / 3 cup butter together over low heat
6. cool slightly
7. beat together 1 / 3 cup sugar and egg yolks with electric mixer or hand beater until thick and creamy
8. pour into chocolate mixture and beat together for about 4 minutes until smooth and creamy
9. in a separate bowl , beat egg whites on medium to high speed until they form stiff peaks
10. fold egg whites into chocolate mixture along with flour
11. pour into moulds
12. bake for 7 minutes until edges are set , but centre is still jiggly
13. cool for 5 minutes and carefully remove to serving dishes
14. serve with whipped cream or good quality french vanilla or coffee ice cream
target.review: We loved these!  I had my first molten cake in Hawaii for my birthday and thought it must be so difficult to make.  When I saw how easy this recipe looked, I decided to try it for our "Easy and Romantic" menu and it was wonderful!   7 minutes baking time was perfect.  I used heart-shaped ramekins, added some whipped cream on top and a few fresh raspberries and wow!  It's nice to be able to make a dessert that isn't a ton of work, so you can enjoy your guest(s)!   Too bad my kids didn't get to try these, but I will be making them soon again!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
arugula salad with shaved manchego

great presentation! salad is quick and easy to make, and great to eat! this was given to me by my best-friend, judy this is one of her favorites.

1. in a large bowl , whisk honey and vinegar until combined
2. whisk in oil
3. season with salt and pepper
4. add arugula , sun-dried tomatoes and almonds to the dressing
5. lightly toss
6. using a vegetable peeler , thinly shave the manchego
7. add half to the bowl , and toss to combine
8. divide among four serving or salad plates
9. top with remaining manchego
10. serve immediately
demonstrations.review: I've made this twice already this week. My family totally digs it! The dressing was simple and delicious. All of the ingredients, except for the cheese was on hand. I hurried to the store to get the cheese and it was totally worth the trip!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pecan crusted chicken with raspberry drizzle

easy crispy chicken with a simple raspberry sauce. you could also do this with boneless breasts if you like, but thighs are so much more flavorful and give the dish that extra boost. adjust the cook time to about 25 minutes if using boneless breasts.  this recipe was a contest entry for rsc #11.

1. preheat oven to 425f
2. mix flour , cayenne , 1 / 8 tsp salt and a few turns of the pepper mill in a shallow bowl
3. mix egg and milk in another small bowl
4. combine pecans and breadcrumbs and remaining salt on waxed paper or in a shallow dish
5. pat thighs dry and dredge in flour mixture , then dip in egg mixture , then coat with pecan mixture on both sides , pressing in gently to help them adhere
6. place on a shallow baking sheet and bake for 35 minutes or until chicken is done
7. don't overcook or chicken will be dry
8. while chicken is cooking , in a small bowl combine raspberry preserves , mustard and honey , mixing well
9. heat in microwave until hot
10. this can also be done in a small saucepan on the stove , but it's just as good in the microwave and you don't have to dirty another pan
11. place chicken on plate and drizzle with raspberry sauce
demonstrations.review: This has become a family favorite. Easy and quick to make for a great weeknight family meal. Chicken thighs make it heartier than breasts, so it really sticks with you! Yum! It's even good with no sauce, if you want to cut back on sugar/calories.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mike s brisket

this brisket wows guests! prep time includes time for marinating. we found this recipe stuck to a package of beef brisket about 10 years ago.

1. poke holes all over brisket with fork
2. mix all ingredients except brisket , and marinate brisket in 1 / 2 of the sauce overnight
3. place whole brisket on hot grill to sear and brown fat
4. remove from grill and place in foilware pan
5. cover pan tightly with foil , close hood , and cook on low heat for about 4 hours , or until meat is tender
6. for best results , use a meat thermometer
7. it should be 170 degrees f for medium
8. slice brisket very thinly across grain at an angle
9. heat remaining 1 / 2 of sauce , pour over slices and serve
demonstrations.review: I have many recipes for brisket, as I make it quite often. It's great to have a new recipe to my repertoire. This may well be a new favorite. Very delicious. Lots of ingredients for the sauce, but everything I normally have on hand, so it was very easy. Very tender. Delicious! Made it for PAC '11.

target.recipe_text:
pumpkin pancakes with pumpkin maple sauce

this is an autumn treat for pumpkin lovers! i found the recipe on meals.com, although i added my own touches. if you use soy milk, it's dairy-free!

1. to make pumpkin maple sauce: heat maple syrup , pumpkin , and cinnamon or pumpkin pie spice in small saucepan until warm
2. cover and set aside
3. to make pancakes: combine flour , brown sugar , baking powder , pumpkin pie spice and salt in large bowl
4. combine milk , pumpkin , egg and vegetable oil in small bowl
5. mix well
6. add to flour mixture
7. stir just until moistened
8. batter may be lumpy
9. heat griddle or skillet over medium heat
10. brush lightly with vegetable oil
11. pour 1 / 4 cup batter onto hot griddle
12. cook until bubbles begin to burst
13. turn and continue cooking 1 to 2 minutes
14. repeat with remaining batter
15. serve with prepared pumpkin maple sauce
target.review: Made this breakfast dish the day before thanksgiving.  Very unique flavor, my boyfriend and I agree that the pumpkin maple syrup was the best part!  We put the leftover pancakes in the freezer...I wonder how well they will hold up.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pepsi pork roast

this recipe sounds strange and tastes wonderful. we have experimented with other brands of soda, but none worked as well. you can also cook potatoes and carrots with the roast for a complete meal.

1. place roast in crock pot
2. mix soup mix with soup
3. add cola to soup mixture and pour over roast
4. cook on high for 4-5 hours
5. when done , remove roast and thicken juices with cornstarch for wonderful gravy
demonstrations.review: We made this pork recipe for friends who were coming over for a New Year's Day poker game.  Overall it was good, but I was disappointed with how dry the pork was.  There were very few pieces that were juicy and tender, the majority was dry and not very flavorful.  Perhaps next time I will use two cans of soup and the entire can of Pepsi (only used 3/4 since many reviewers commented on the sweetness).  If there was more gravy then maybe the pork would have turned out better.  But the gravy that it did make was incredible!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
greek style turkey burgers

the best turkey burgers i have ever tried .... i freeze left-overs, and heat in the microwave later ...

1. combine all the ingredients in a large bowl
2. form into 4 patties , then grill
3. i have served this on regular burger buns with tomatoes and mayo , and on pita with tahini , tomatoes and lettuce
demonstrations.review: This recipe is great!!  I used about 1-1/4 pounds and made four big burgers.  I grilled them on my George Foreman and put them in the fridge to take for lunches for the week.  I didnt use any italian seasonings (i didnt have any) but they ended up perfect anyway!!  I will  continue to use this one. Thanks for the healthy recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
jo mama s world famous spaghetti

my kids will give up a steak dinner for this spaghetti. it is a recipe i have been perfecting for years and it is so good (if i may humbly say) that my kids are disappointed when they eat spaghetti anywhere else but home! in fact they tell me i should open a restaurant and serve only this spaghetti and garlic bread. in response to requests, i have posted the recipe for recipe #28559 that uses approximately 1/2 of the sauce from this 
recipe. have spaghetti one night and lasagna later!  thanks to all of you who have tried my recipe and have written a review.  i read and appreciate every one of them!  chef note:  after i posted this recipe i remembered a funny incident--my dear husband usually has a nice bottle of wine handy so when i make a batch of spaghetti i just help myself to a splash of it. on one occasion, there wasn't a bottle opened, but there was a bottle sitting on the counter so i got out the corkscrew and helped myself. for some reason, the spaghetti that night was the best ever. my husband asked what wine i put in it and i showed him the bottle. he nearly fell off the chair. i had opened a rather expensive bottle he had bought to give his boss. goes to show you--don't use a wine for cooking you wouldn't drink. you get the best results from a good wine!

1. in large , heavy stockpot , brown italian sausage , breaking up as you stir
2. add onions and continue to cook , stirring occasionally until onions are softened
3. add garlic , tomatoes , tomato paste , tomato sauce and water
4. add basil , parsley , brown sugar , salt , crushed red pepper , and black pepper
5. stir well and barely bring to a boil
6. stir in red wine
7. simmer on low , stirring frequently for at least an hour
8. a longer simmer makes for a better sauce , just be careful not to let it burn !
9. cook spaghetti according to package directions
10. spoon sauce over drained spaghetti noodles and sprinkle with parmesan cheese
demonstrations.review: This makes alot of sauce!!!  I wouldnt try making it without the wine--that's what gives it it's great taste.  I am not usually a big fan of red sauce but this has such a mild flavor that I really enjoy it.  After reading the reviews before making, I only used enough water to rinse out the little can of tomato paste.  I think any more would be too runny.  Next time I will try putting in more garlic than it calls for.  This is a great recipe!!!

target.recipe_text:
unknownchef86 s very best dinner rolls

these rolls are very soft and light. they make children and husbands very happy. my husband asked, "can you make these all the time?"

1. sprinkle the yeast over the warm milk and let sit for approximately 5 minutes to proof
2. add sugar , 1 / 2 cup melted butter , salt and eggs
3. mix well
4. add flour and mix well
5. blend at medium-low speed for about 5-10 minutes , scraping down sides once or twice
6. cover bowl with plastic wrap and a towel
7. let rise in bowl about 1 hour or til doubled
8. remove the towel and plastic wrap and turn mixer on low to"punch down" the dough
9. if you wish , you can let the dough raise a second time as it makes for a more flavorful roll
10. remove the dough from the bowl and divide into 36"plops"
11. the dough will be very sticky
12. place"plops" , edges just touching , in a buttered 9x13 baking pan
13. don't bother trying to smooth out the"plops"-- they will smooth out as they raise
14. cover pan with plastic wrap and let rise til doubled , about 30-40 minutes
15. melt the reserved butter and drizzle over the top of the rolls before baking
16. bake at 400f for 10-15 minutes or until golden
target.review: Yes, the best dinner rolls ever.  They go perfectly with any dinner and have great flavor and consistency. Thank you for the recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
ground beef chili

the best beef chili in my book. freezes well.

1. in a large dutch oven , cook the beef and next 3 ingredients over medium heat until meat is browned and vegetables are tender
2. drain
3. stir in the beans and remaining ingredients , except for additional onions and cheddar cheese
4. bring to a boil
5. reduce heat
6. simmer uncovered , for 30 minutes or until chili reaches desired thickness
7. ladle into serving bowls
8. garnish with chopped onion and cheddar cheese , if desired
demonstrations.review: I made a big pot and we ate this chili for days in several ways. It was really good. The reason why it didn't get 5 stars is because we like our chili to be thicker above and beyond just cooking it longer, plus we like it with some bite and tanginess. However, I would recommend this chili to others.  Thank you!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mama s supper club tilapia parmesan

you asked for it. here it is. thanks so much to mama's supper club. wish we could all go there.

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees
2. in buttered 13-by-9-inch baking dish or jellyroll pan , lay fillets in single layer
3. do not stack fillets
4. brush top with juice
5. in bowl combine cheese , butter , mayonnaise , onions and seasonings
6. mix well with fork
7. bake fish in preheated oven 10 to 20 minutes or until fish just starts to flake
8. spread with cheese mixture and bake until golden brown , about 5 minutes
9. baking time will depend on the thickness of the fish you use
10. watch fish closely so that it does not overcook
11. makes 4 servings
12. broil 3 to 4 minutes or until almost done
13. add cheese and broil another 2 to 3 minutes or until browned
14. thank you mama's supper club in wisconsin
demonstrations.review: Definitely delicious. This is the first recipe from here that I made a second time. I tripled the amount of sauce per fish because we like it with plenty of sauce and flavor and the sauce is so good that there needs to be enough. However, DO NOT triple the amount of butter in the sauce or it will leave a pool of melted butter in the bottom of the dish. The other ingredients are what make it so good anyway. Thank you so much for this great recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
baby carrots with scallions

delicious baby carrots glazed with scallions in butter.

1. place carrots in salted water , bring to boil , simmer to tender crisp , about 10 minutes
2. drain well and set aside
3. in a non stick frypan , melt butter and oil , add scallions , cook about 2 minutes , add orange juice and sugar twin brown or splenda , simmer 2 minutes , add carrots
4. stir to cover carrots with glaze , while simmering another 2 to 3 minutes
5. serve hot
demonstrations.review: My husband and I loved the carrots. They are such a treat. The scallions in the dish were a perfect match, and the carrots were sweet without being too sweet. I would like to have these as a side dish with every meal. Thanks for the recipe.

target.recipe_text:
my own lazy day recipe   chicken noodle soup

i made this up one day when i wanted some old-fashioned tasting chicken soup without all the bother and i love it.

1. grate carrot and cook with chicken in chicken broth and 4 cups water
2. cook chicken about 10 minutes then add noodles and cook till done
3. add cream of chicken soup and cook about 5 minutes longer
4. mmm mmm good
target.review: A nice simple soup - easy to make when you're not feeling so hot and you're the mamma.  Tasted great to my poor sick throat, but my kids were a bit more picky.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
sweet jalapeno chicken

fast and easy, and delicious, with the flavors of jalapeno jelly, dijon mustard and honey. do try to use the red jalapeno jelly, however; the green-colored one looks much less appetizing (though it still tastes fine)!

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees f
2. in a small bowl , mix together honey , mustard and jalapeno jelly
3. place chicken breasts in a baking dish
4. sprinkle with salt and pepper to taste , and pour honey-mustard-jelly sauce over all , coating well
5. bake uncovered for about 1 hour , basting occasionally , until chicken juices run clear and meat is no longer pink
demonstrations.review: This is delicious and easy.  Expect more of a honey mustard chicken than jalapeno.  I halfed the sauce ingredients and used 3 boneless skinless chicken breasts.  I cooked them for about 40 minutes, and it was a little dry, so maybe about 30 minutes at 350 - so so good.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
swedish apple pie

this is a "no crust" apple pie that my mom used to make. it is great served alone or with vanilla ice cream. this is a "must" for our family at holiday gatherings.

1. preheat oven to 350
2. fill pie pan 3 / 4 full with apples
3. mix 1 / 4 cup sugar and 3 tsp cinnamon
4. sprinkle over apples
5. in saucepan , melt butter and remove from heat
6. add remaining ingredients
7. pour evenly over the apples in pan
8. bake 45 minutes
demonstrations.review: I didn't change anything, but my family loves this pie.  Of course the apples you choose affect who it tastes too.  We love it with Fuji apples.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
beth s melt in your mouth barbecue ribs  oven

i almost didn't want to share this ribs recipe because this is one of the dishes that i make that keep my sons coming back home! these can be done with baby back or regular pork ribs. i have also made split chickens this way. the ribs are tender, moist and just slide off of the bone. i know that your family will love them just as much as my family does.
i noticed that some are unable to find hickory smoked salt. you can use smoked paprika or just brush the ribs with liquid smoke before applying the rub. the smoke flavor is nice because it helps give the ribs a cooked-on-the-grill flavor.
also, the easiest way to remove the membrane is to work a spoon, or i use the tips of my kitchen shears, into the bottom center of the membrane, work it back and forth to form a "pocket," then i slide my thumbs in and work the membrane off from the center outward to the ends.

1. preheat oven to 300 degrees f
2. line a baking sheet with two layers of foil , shiny side out
3. peel off tough membrane that covers the bony side of the ribs
4. season the ribs on both sides with salt and pepper
5. if using , divide the hickory liquid smoke evenly over the ribs
6. in a medium bowl , combine the light brown sugar , paprika , garlic powder and ground red pepper
7. apply the rub to all sides of the ribs
8. lay ribs on the prepared baking sheet , meaty side down
9. lay two layers of foil on top of ribs and roll and crimp edges tightly , edges facing up to seal
10. transfer to the oven and = bake for 2-2 1 / 2 hours or until meat is starting to shrink away from the ends of the bone
11. remove from oven
12. heat broiler
13. cut ribs into serving sized portions of 2 or 3 ribs
14. arrange on broiler pan , bony side up
15. brush on sauce
16. broil for 1 or 2 minutes until sauce is cooked on and bubbly
17. turn ribs over
18. repeat on other side
19. alternately , you can grill the ribs on your grill to cook on the sauce
demonstrations.review: This turns out awesome every time I make them.  I use a ready made rub from the store - I think maple smokehouse or something like that.  Also use country style pork ribs already cut up.  I follow the rest of the directions and everyone loves them.

target.recipe_text:
quinoa tabouli

i love new twists on classic dishes. in this one, quinoa - a latin american grain rich in protein - replaces bulgar as the base of this mediterranean-middle eastern salad.

1. place quinoa in a colander and rinse several times rubbing the grains together to remove the bitter outer layer
2. place water and quinoa into a 2-quart saucepan
3. bring to a boil
4. reduce heat to a simmer and cover
5. cook for 10 to 15 minutes or until all water has been absorbed
6. while the quinoa is cooking , finely chop the tomatoes , parsley , and scallions
7. add lemon juice , olive oil and fresh mint to the tomato mixture
8. stir in cooked quinoa and salt
9. mix well
10. let tabouli sit in the refrigerator for a day to blend flavors
11. tabouli is traditionally served at room temperature so remove from fridge 30 to 60 minutes before serving
target.review: This is a good recipe for tabouli.  I cooked the quinoa in the rice cooker and it was a bit mushy so when I make it again I will cook the grains in the manner suggested,

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pandora s feast   veggie rice cooker dish

this is from wikicookbooks.  i have never tried it but here for safe keeping.  pandora's feast is a complete vegan meal that can be served several times a week due to the ease with which it can be modified. the meal is easy to prepare in a rice cooker.

1. add the brown rice and water to the rice cooker
2. if you have "thai sweet black rice" or "chinese forbidden black rice" , replace about 10% of your brown rice with this and your finished product will be a lovely purple and will have a different taste
3. the beans should either be pre-soaked or from a can
4. drain , rinse , and add these to the rice cooker
5. if you're presoaking , the beans need about 8 hours to soak
6. if using , add the garlic the cooker
7. if using , add the sweet potato , squash , beet or potato , chop into cubes 1cm x 1cm for optimal cooking
8. on a fuzzy logic cooker , set the cooker to the brown rice setting and turn it on
9. for an on / off cooker , turn it on
10. if using , chop the kale
11. in about 2040 minutes , your cooker will complete cooking the rice
12. when the cooker is finished , open the lid , add the kale , and wait about another minute or two
13. open and serve
14. top with oil , yeast , soy sauce and / or sesame seeds , to taste
demonstrations.review: This was delicious.  I just added 2Tbs of forbidden rice to the 1 cup of brown rice (the whole 10% thing was too much to think about).  I used sesame oil for the garnish.  My only problem was that my rice cooker took so long my stomach thought my throat was cut!  The kale was a nice crunch addition.  The recipe also had great visual appeal - wish I had thought to take a picture.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
fruit salad with pudding

i get compliments on this fruit salad wherever i take it. it is super easy to make and a great dish to bring to a potluck or family party. kids love it too. everyone asks "what's in the sauce"? the secret ingredient is the vanilla pudding mix.

1. in a large bowl , combine peaches , pineapples , and vanilla pudding mix
2. this includes the juices from the cans
3. mix well until pudding is dissolved
4. stir in strawberries , banana , blueberries , grapes , and sugar if desired
5. chill
demonstrations.review: This is amazing.  I made it three times in the past week because the family enjoyed it so much.  I used the sugar-free pudding and no sugar pineapple tidbits.  This recipe works well with any fruit I have on had.  I also start by adding just the pineapple juice to the pudding and then adding additional juice if needed to thin it out just a bit.  No added sugar was needed.  Thanks for an easy way to finally get my family to eat a variety of fresh fruits!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mixed grain mushroom casserole

a friend gave me this recipe, its my comfort food now.

1. combine grains in a mixing bowl and set aside
2. pour the oil into a 2 to 3 quart casserole which is safe for both stovetop and oven cooking , and place on medium heat
3. when hot , saute onion and garlic until tender and translucent , about 5 to 6 minutes
4. add the mixed grains and saute for 1 minute , stirring constantly
5. meanwhile melt butter or margarine in a separate pan on medium high heat
6. when hot , add mushrooms and saute quickly , stirring frequently , until the mushrooms are hot and have just absorbed the"butter"
7. immediately remove from heat
8. add the broth , herbs , and mushrooms to the casserole with the onions and grains , and bring to a boil
9. season with salt and pepper to taste , cover tightly , and bake at 350 degrees for 1 hour
demonstrations.review:
I found this recipe while looking for a way to use up my mushrooms. I followed the recipe exactly (I think, but I only had wild sweet rice). I had to cook it an additional 20 minutes to get the moisture to absorb. Then what I had was rice with what tasted like Italian seasoning. I didn't taste much of the mushroom. I definitely wouldn't call this a Main Dish unless I were eating alone.

I won't make this again. There are too many other recipes out there that really showcase the flavor and texture of mushrooms.

target.recipe_text:
french wedge

i was going to call it french wench for no other reason but that it sounds funny, but then no one could immediately make sense of it.  but seeing as how the wedge salads have become well-known, this should do. a simple, but tasty version with toasted walnuts, avocado, vinaigrette and crumbled roquefort.  *le yum*.  prep time doesn’t include however long it takes you to grow an extra hand for holding the bowl while you pour in the olive oil and whisk at the same time.

1. toast the walnut pieces in 350f oven for up to 5 minutes , tossing regularly and being careful not to burn
2. in mixing bowl , add mustard , red wine vinegar , salt and pepper
3. slowly drizzle in olive oil while whisking
4. chill until ready to dress salad
5. halve the iceberg lettuce half and put each quarter head on a salad plate
6. arrange the avocado slices next to the wedge
7. re-whisk then pour the dressing to taste over each wedge
8. top with walnuts , tomatoes and roquefort
9. feastie
target.review: Quite delicious, Sandi. The combo of veggies blended well with the cheese and nuts. The dressing was the piece de resistance, tho! Made for French Food and Foto Fun.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
white bean and sausage stew

this recipe is a combination of things i had on hand and wanted to make a hearty stew--something to stick to the ribs.  serve with rolls, salad for a complete meal.

1. soak the beans overnight , covered with water
2. drain
3. in a heavy 6-quart dutch oven or cast- iron pot , heat the oil over medium-high heat
4. add the flour and cook , stirring continuously , until it becomes dark brown , for 20 to 25 minutes
5. add the onion , bell pepper , celery , salt , thyme , bay leaves , cayenne and black pepper
6. cook , stirring , for 5 minutes
7. add the ham and sausage and cook , stirring , for 3 minutes or until the ham and sausage begin to cook
8. stir in the beans and garlic
9. stir in the chicken broth
10. bring to a boil , reduce the heat and simmer , uncovered , for 1 1 / 2 hours or until the beans are tender , stirring occasionally
11. if the stew becomes too thick , stir in more broth
12. add the mushrooms
13. cook for 30 minutes longer
demonstrations.review: I wish there were 10 stars for this recipe! It's a WOWser! After making the roux and softening the pepper,celery and onion in oil---added everything to the crockpot, cooking for 7 hours---5 of which I was over-whelmed by the deeeelightful smells in my kitchen!! This would be great over rice, too---but just as wonderful in a bowl with mightyro's cornbread. This goes right into my HardDrive recipe file. It's a keeper, for sure!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
impossible coconut pie

i love this dessert. it tastes like a coconut macaroon, and it is simple to make. drizzle melted chocolate on top and it tastes like a "mounds" bar. this comes from bisquick.

1. heat oven to 350f
2. grease 9-inch pie plate
3. stir all ingredients until blended
4. pour into pie plate
5. bake 50 to 55 minutes or until golden brown and knife inserted in the center comes out clean
6. cover and refrigerate any remaining pie
demonstrations.review: Impossibly easy--as stated---AND incredibly delicious. This goes into my CD food files. THX for posting. Caroline

demonstrations.recipe_text:
to die for crock pot roast

amazing flavor, and so simple! no salt needed here. in fact, you may wish to use half the ranch dressing mix to cut back on the saltiness. found this crock-pot pot roast recipe on of a website called www.recipegoldmine.com. it's all the rage there, so i thought i'd try it.

1. place beef roast in crock pot
2. mix the dried mixes together in a bowl and sprinkle over the roast
3. pour the water around the roast
4. cook on low for 7-9 hours
5. use onion soup mix instead of ranch
6. add one cup , of red wine
7. add potatoes , carrots , mushrooms , celery and onion 2-3 hours before end
demonstrations.review:
With over 800 review--how could I go wrong. DIDN'T! 10 stars, for sure!!  This is awesome. Love the flavors!! WOW! This goes into my HD cookbook for my family generations to enjoy.
Thank you for posting it, yooper!

target.recipe_text:
chicken taco wraps for oamc

wraps, wraps, wraps.  so many of them can be frozen and used for a quick lunck, snack, or lite dinner.  you may want to play with the ingredients but this is what i've come up with so far!

1. combine chicken , water , salsa and seasonings in a saucepan
2. bring to a boil
3. add rice , and simmer on for 5 minutes
4. spoon mixture into center of tortillas
5. add cheese if you want it and wrap
6. flash freeze
7. to reheat: microwave until heated through
target.review: Fantastic! Easy quick meal for a busy family. My kids (6,4,1) LOVE them.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
healthier olive garden pasta e fagioli soup

this recipe is wonderful.  it tastes just like olive garden's, but a tiny bit healthier because of the ground turkey breast vs. beef.  both ways are wonderful!

1. brown the ground turkey in a large saucepan or pot over medium heat
2. strain the fat
3. add onion , carrot , celery and garlic and saut for 10 minutes
4. add remaining ingredients , except pasta , and simmer for 1 hour
5. about 50 minutes into simmer time , cook the pasta in 1 1 / 2 to 2 quarts of boiling water over high heat
6. cook for 10 minutes or just until pasta is al dente , or slightly tough
7. drain
8. add the pasta to the large pot of soup
9. simmer for 5-10 minutes and serve
10. i sometimes cook the noodles and leave out of the soup-this way , the guests can add as many as they would like and it freezes better without the noodles in it !
demonstrations.review: Oh my Yum Yum! I used ground beef because I forgot the turkey but it was SO good. Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pork chops   southern style

simple, quick and tasty. something i threw together with the 'scraps' in my fridge and surprised me with how great it tasted. feel free to remove as much 'fat' from the pan as you need to... the more you leave, the better it tastes! great with mashed potatoes!

1. in 12" skillet , cook bacon on med hi heat
2. remove bacon from skillet , but leave bacon drippings
3. add 1 tbsp butter and diced onion
4. when transparent , remove from skillet
5. reduce heat to medium , lightly salt and pepper both sides of pork chops and place in skillet
6. brown both sides
7. chop up bacon , and add both bacon and cooked onion to skillet
8. add 3 / 4 cup water , 1 tbsp butter , cover and simmer until cooked
9. just before serving , mix 2 tbsp cornstarch with cool tap water
10. place pork chops on plates , add corn starch / water mixture to gravy / drippings in skillet and bring to quick boil stirring frequently to form thick gravy
demonstrations.review:
Yum Yum!
I added Tony Chachere's Spice n'Herb seasoning to the pork chops for a little extra kick and used 4 tlbs of flour as a cornstarch substitute. Served with mushroom rice. It was wonderful!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
my super simple spaghetti sauce

i needed some sauce and quick!  i am not a fan of the jarred stuff...plus i didn't want to go to the store.  this is a rendition of my favorite sauce recipe #133806, just made simple and it doesn't have to cook all day.

1. throw it all in a sauce pan , stir , simmer , cover and continue to simmer for 20-30 minutes
2. season again to taste
3. we like a spicy sweet sauce -- so please adjust the sugar and crushed red to your liking
4. enjoy !
demonstrations.review: Amazing!!! So easy and simple yet so GOOD!

target.recipe_text:
7 layer bean dip

this 7 layer bean dip is great for super bowl parties, work parties, other gatherings! pretty easy to make...you can use store bought guacamole if you can't find ripe avocados.

1. mix avocados , lemon juice , salt , and pepper
2. mix mayonnaise , sour cream , and taco seasoning mix
3. layer ingredients as follows
4. bottom layer: bean dip
5. second layer: avocado mixture
6. third layer: sour cream mixture
7. fourth layer: tomatoes
8. fifth layer: onions
9. sixth layer: olives
10. seventh layer: cheese
11. top with extra sour cream / olives / salsa , etc
12. if desired
13. serve with tortilla chips
14. this seems to be a little bit better if you can chill it for a few hours or over night to let the flavors intensify
target.review: This dip is FANTASTIC. I even blogged about it, check out http://legallyeating.blogspot.com/2009/07/babymaking-dip.html for the full story! And yes, it IS called the babymakin' dip, haha! The bean dip vs. refried beans is so fantastic, not to mention the mayo in the sour cream layer, and the fantastically smooth but simple avo layer. Thanks Marilee, you got a shout out on my page!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
tangy pan fried tilapia

i don't remember where i got this recipe from but is is lower cal that most.  you can also bake but the crust is much better when you pan-fry.

1. coat tilapia fillets in dijon mustard
2. then dip in panko to coat
3. heat oil in skillet on med / high - i try to use as little as i can get away with
4. pan fry fillets until golden brown on both sides
5. try to turn fillets only once since tilapia is delicate and can fall apart
6. season with salt and pepper while still hot
demonstrations.review: I loved this! I got really excited about it, but then couldn't find my panko. Eventually they came out, and it was worth all the trouble! It didn't need lemon or anything extra, like I usually eat with fish. I will definitely make this again!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chilled potato and leek soup   vichyssoise

most recipes for chilled potato soup have lots and lots of heavy cream thus fat.  this recipe is very simple to put together and very low in fat.  as it chills it becomes super thick and creamy.  after having tried this both chilled and at room temperature, i highly recommend room temperature.  the recipe is from william-sonoma essentials of healthy cooking.

1. in a heavy saucepan , over medium-high heat , combine the leeks , green onions and 1 / 2 cup of the chicken stock
2. bring to a boil , reduce heat to low , cover and cook until the vegetables have wilted and begin to soften , approximately 8 minutes
3. add the diced potatoes and remaining 2 1 / 2 cups chicken stock , replace the cover and cook until vegetables are very soft , 20 to 25 minutes
4. remove from heat , uncover and allow the soup to stand for 15 minutes to cool slightly
5. stir in the butter
6. very carefully transfer the hot vegetable mixture to blender container , puree until very smooth and in several batches if needed
7. season with salt and pepper
8. allow the soup to cool to room temperature before placing in the refrigerator
9. when cool , cover and place in refrigerate until well chilled , 3 to 4 hours or serve at room temperature
10. adjusting seasoning if needed
11. to serve , divide into individual serving bowls and garnish with some of the reserved green onion tops that have been thinly sliced
demonstrations.review:
Fantastic! I made this for my Bastille Day feast and it was easy, creamy, perfectly delicious. Pictures and reference featured on my blog: http://legallyeating.com/2009/07/14/vive-la-france-but-you-know-in-america/

Thanks PaulaG!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
aloo gobi

great aloo gobi recipe from the film bend it like beckham

1. heat vegetable oil in a large saucepan
2. add the chopped onion and one teaspoon of cumin seeds to the oil
3. stir together and cook until onions become creamy , golden , and translucent
4. add chopped coriander stalks , two teaspoons of turmeric , and one teaspoon of salt
5. add chopped chillis stir tomatoes into onion mixture
6. add ginger and garlic
7. mix thoroughly
8. add potatoes and cauliflower to the sauce plus a few tablespoons of water
9. ensure that the potatoes and cauliflower are coated with the curry sauce
10. cover and allow to simmer for twenty minutes
11. add two teaspoons of garam masala and stir
12. sprinkle chopped coriander leaves on top of the curry
13. turn off the heat , cover , and leave for as long as possible before serving
demonstrations.review: I love the taste of this recipe, but it took me forever to get the potatoes completely cooked through. I'm not sure exactly what I'd do to fix that next time, but I'd better figure something out! I loved this recipe, otherwise.

target.recipe_text:
swiss chard  stir fried  with feta cheese

low cal veggie, high iron. great with the touch of feta & pine nuts. don't overcook. you can include this in a chinese meal as an exta vegetable dish

1. in a wok heat the oil
2. add shallots
3. stir fry 1 minute or until just beginning to brown
4. add swiss chard , toss and cover
5. cook 2 minutes
6. remove cover and cook about another minute
7. if there is any liqiud drain it off
8. stir in the feta cheese , cook 30 seconds or until it starts to melt
9. add pine nuts and season
10. serve immediately
target.review: i also subbed olive oil for the peanut oil  but will try it next time to see if the flavor changes significantly.  even without, it was fantastic.  oh, and i didn't have shallots, so i subbed onions instead.  the fact that my husband loves this too is a testimony to how good it is--he hardly EVER eats veggies!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
leg of lamb in the crock pot

i love lamb and was happy to have discovered this simple recipe using a crock pot.

1. combine all ingredients in a crock pot
2. cook 8 to 10 hours on low
3. remove roast and let set 20 minutes before carving
4. slice thin
demonstrations.review: not too bad.  i guess all the ratings raised my expectations too much. it's easy, for sure, which i appreciate, but i expected more flavor in the actual lamb.  i browned the boneless leg for a few minutes on each side after trimming as much fat as possible.  i used only 4 cups of water, as others recommended and added a 1/2 t. of rosemary (which i ended up not tasting at all).  cooked on slow for 8 hours.  added 2 tsp. dried mint to 3 c. of broth with flour to make gravy, as previous poster sugggested.  if it wasn't for the gravy (which was still just ok), i wouldn't have finished my lamb...i just need more flavor.  it was very tender and i'll also try the remaining broth as soup as some suggested.  might try one more time, but let the lamb marinade for a few hours or overnight in the recipe and then dump the whole thing in the crockpot the next day to see if that brings out some flavor.  the upside is i'll be able to use the leftovers in various other recipes without having to worry about conflicting flavors.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
not fried  fried ice cream

can't remember where i found this recipe, but it's great for mexican night, or cinco de mayo!! (new note: if you use the new special k cereal with cinnamon and pecans, this is real delicious!  add the sugar and not as much cinnamon, no butter, and you don't have to bake it! very crunchy and so delicious!!! i used about 1 1/4 c special k.)

1. make 8 vanilla ice cream balls and freeze on wax-lined cookie sheet for about an hour
2. mix remaining ingredients and spread on a cookie sheet to bake at 350f until crisp and golden
3. let cool
4. roll ice cream balls in the cooled mixture and refreeze for 2 hours more
5. serve with honey drizzled over each and enjoy !
6. see new
demonstrations.review: great recipe.  however, a couple things...first, i melted the butter before adding it to the ingredients.  second, i am lazy and even though this tastes just like fried ice cream, i think next time i'm just going to make the coating ahead of time, scoop my ice cream in the bowl and dump a bunch of coating on top and drizzle honey on top.  that way, i don't get messy AND i get to eat it several hours sooner!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
spinach mushroom lasagna roll ups with gorgonzola cream sauce

this is a wonderfully flavored dish that my hubby swears is my best dinner yet! served with asparagus topped with some of the sauce is superb.

1. saut mushrooms , chopped onion and garlic in oil over med heat , until mushrooms give off their juice and onion is tender- 7-8 minutes
2. season with salt and pepper
3. add dry chopped spinach to the pan and heat through
4. add ricotta , adjust salt and pepper and heat through
5. remove from burner , but leave in warm skillet
6. heat broth in small sauce pan
7. add gorgonzola into broth , and bring to a bubble
8. stir in cream and thicken about 2 minutes
9. place cooked noodles on work surface
10. place a dollop of spinach mixture on one end of noodles and roll each one up
11. arrange rolled packages , seam side down , in shallow casserole dish
12. pour warm sauce over and top with mozzarella
13. place casserole under broiler to melt mozzarella and slightly brown
demonstrations.review: this was yummy!  a little more prep work than i'd like, but not much.  i didn't have gorgonzola, just a big costco tub of bleu cheese, so i used that.  as it was cooking, i was like, mmm, walnuts would go good w/the cheese.  but didn't have walnuts!  so i used toasted pecans instead, chopped and sprinkled on top as a garnish and omg!  it was perfect!

target.recipe_text:
crock pot brisket

shamelessly adopted and adapted from a recipe given to me by lea bruce.

1. mix all ingredients except for the brisket
2. place the brisket into the crock pot and pour the cola mixture over the meat
3. cook on high for 8 hours or overnight on low
4. slice and serve
target.review: I did this yesterday with a brisket of undetermined age I found in my freezer (I really need to teach my husband to label things!).  I followed the recipe as written using dijon mustard; however, I put my brisket in frozen solid and cooked it on high for just under 9 hours.  I gave some to my mother-in-law without telling her the ingredients and she could not tell there was cola in the recipe.  A very good everyday meal.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
hummus amongus

there's a large middle eastern population in bayridge brooklyn and amazing restaurants line the avenues...hummus is served with every dish on the menu...it's one of my favorite things in the whole wide world...if you haven't tried it, please do. i think you'll love it!

1. drain beans
2. reserve water
3. in a food processor or blender add beans and all the ingredients
4. process until smooth
5. if mixture is too thick , add some of the reserved liquid from the beans to dilute to a desired consistency
6. serve at room temperature with pita bread , grilled pork , lamb or chicken
demonstrations.review: I'm not a hummous expert at all, but I was looking for an alternative to the usual cream cheese/sour cream dips for my parties.  This hummous got rave reviews from my guests, including a number of people who said they don't normally like hummous.  Many thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
baked mexican bananas

i don't eat bananas often, even though i love them. when i do have bananas, they have to be very special, and i promise you, these babies are very very special! try serving them over vanilla frozen yogurt, or with an intensely chocolate ice cream.

1. preheat the oven to 375f
2. in a shallow baking dish just large enough to hold them , arrange the bananas in a single layer
3. in a small bowl , combine the zests , juices , raisins , vanilla , and cinnamon and whisk to blend
4. pour over the bananas and bake , uncovered , for about 20 minutes or until the bananas are lightly browned and bubbling
5. use a spatula to put 3 banana pieces in the center of each plate and spoon the sauce from the dish over them
demonstrations.review: I really hate bananas, so I didn't even taste this recipe.  However, a friend of mine has a 2 year old daughter who is allergic to dairy products, flour, and soy products.  They were visiting today and I struggled to find something to cook.  I had made this once before for some vegan friends who liked it.  My friend's daughter gobbled it right up - thank you!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
leftover steak skillet

i had leftover steak and didn''t want fajitas, so i improvised a noodle skillet dish that was pretty tasty.  i wanted to remember what was in it, hence the post.

1. in a large skillet with a lid , brown steaks and garlic
2. add tomato , cumins and cardamon and cook for 1-2 minutes
3. add broth and bring to boil
4. add noodles , cover and cook until noodles are done dente
5. in a small bowl , combine cornstarch with some of the broth from the skillet and whisk until cornstarch is dissolved
6. add to skillet and simmer for 3-5 minutes , until mixture starts to thicken
7. stir in sour cream
8. serve
demonstrations.review: Shockingly (as it contains a vegetable), my kids really liked this. Next time, I would push the envelope a little more and put in a chunk of frozen spinach - just to get some green in there. Very flavourful. I did 1/2 tsp of ground cumin as I didn't have any cumin seeds, and I used high fat plain yoghurt as I didn't have any sour cream. I will definitely make this again!

target.recipe_text:
nana s burgundy beef

my dh loves stew, this is his favorite, made the way his mother prepared it.  it's a quick and easy stew that is big on flavor.   this is a great recipe for using up the rest of the red wine that you didn't finish last night. 

*please note that the sitting time in fridge  is  not listed in cooking time.*

1. preheat oven to 325 degrees f
2. brown the foured and seasoned beef in the hot bacon fat
3. place the vegetables and ketchup in a saucepan , pour in the wine to cover and bring to a boil
4. reduce heat and simmer for 10 minutes
5. put the browned meat and vegetable mixture into a covered casserole , add the bay leaf and the garlic and bake for 2 hours
6. remove and cool then place in fridge
7. let sit overnight in the fridge and warm the next day for best results
8. lovely served as is or over steamed rice
target.review: Really good with nice rich flavor.   Made for Zaar Stars

demonstrations.recipe_text:
really  really good  and easy   buttercream frosting

first off, i have to give all credit to the confessions of a cookbook queen blog, because that's where i found this recipe. it is the best country (non-cook) buttercream frosting that i have ever had. if you're decorating a cake or cupcakes, it also holds up well. i guessed on the yield, but this recipe will easily frost 24 cupcakes.

1. put butter , milk , and vanilla in the bowl of a stand mixer
2. mix on low speed until it just starts to come together , about a minute
3. scrape the sides of the bowl with a spatula
4. increase to medium low speed and beat for about another minute
5. increase mixer speed to medium high and beat for about another or minute or so
6. add powdered sugar
7. beat on low speed until sugar is just barely incorporated
8. scrape down the sides of the bowl , and increase speed slowly to medium
9. beat for about a minute
10. check your consistency
11. this is very important because if your frosting is too thick , it will not spread well
12. if your spatula does not glide through the frosting , add about a tablespoon of corn syrup and beat on medium for about 30 seconds
13. when the frosting is just holding its shape , it is too thick
14. add another tablespoon of corn syrup and beat on medium for 30 seconds
15. repeat until the frosting seems to be of a good spreadable consistency
16. once you get your frosting to a good , spreadable consistency , increase mixer speed to medium high and beat for one minute
17. this will get your frosting nice and fluffy
demonstrations.review: This made a wonderful chocolate frosting.  Made for Fall PAC 2012.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
lime jello salad   aka  the green stuff

my step-mom first served this salad and it has become a family tradition since.  i always make it for holiday dinners and one year i decided to try new things as i was a little tired and bored with the regulars.  i didn't make this one year, and my grown son told me that i should not mess with tradition - this salad was the holidays.  my kids all call this 'the green stuff'. zwt west (hawaiian pineapple).

1. melt the marshmallows in milk in medium saucepan over medium heat
2. stir frequently
3. pour the milk and marshmallow mixture over lime jello in a large bowl
4. stir until dissolved
5. stir in cream cheese with beater
6. add undrained pineapple
7. mix well
8. cool in the refrigerator for several hours or overnight
9. blend mayonnaise and cool whip into the jello mixture
demonstrations.review: This is delicious.  I followed the recipe except I used cherry jello-o because we make a similar recipe for holidays using cherry jello and that is what we like.  Made for Market Tag 2007

demonstrations.recipe_text:
sour cream and chive potato bake

a donna hay recipe

1. preheat oven to 200 c
2. boil potatoes till tender , about 15 minutes
3. drain , cut in half , place in baking dish cut side up
4. whisk together sour cream , cream , cheeses , chives , salt and pepper
5. pour over potatoes
6. cook 20 - 30 minutes until top is golden
demonstrations.review: We love potatoe dishes and this one did not disappoint.  We used red potatoes because that is  what we had on hand.  Made for Aus/NZ swap.

target.recipe_text:
adorable veggie melts

these open face sandwiches will be a hit with the whole family!

1. preheat the broiler
2. arrange the bread slices in a single layer on a baking sheet
3. broil 4 to 5 inches from the heat source for about 2 minutes per side , or until lightly toasted
4. spread 1 side of each slice with mayonnaise
5. to make the topping: heat the olive oil in a large nonstick skillet over medium-high heat
6. add the mushrooms , zucchini , onion , and garlic
7. cook , stirring occasionally , until tender , about 5 minutes
8. remove from the heat
9. stir in the salt and pepper
10. taste and adjust the seasoning
11. combine the cheeses in a small bowl
12. top each bread slice with 2 tomato slices , a sprinkling of pepper , and half of the sauted vegetables , lettuce or bean sprouts , and the cheese mixture
13. place the sandwiches on the baking sheet
14. broil for about 2 minutes , or until the cheese is melted
15. enjoy !
target.review: Yummy! made others jealous when they saw me pull it out of the oven. be sure to do shredded lettuce, as written. i made the mistake of doing a leaf of lettuce, which ended up coming off when i took a bite. added chopped mild green chilies, and worked great.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
easy sweet pea soup

one saturday afternoon i really wanted pea soup, but didn't have any in the cupboard and i didn't want to go to the store. so instead, i made my own. oh-so-easy, this soup is yummy!

1. cook frozen peas in a saucepan with water
2. cover and cook until peas are very tender
3. then drain and whir the peas in the blender or food processor until soup-like in texture , adding the chicken stock as necessary
4. take whirred peas from blender and put back into the saucepan , adding the pinch sugar , nutmeg , and salt / pepper
5. heat through
6. swirl a little sour cream into each serving , and this dish looks and tastes great !
7. makes 3 to 4 servings
8. you can add a little bit of minced onion in , if you like , and a few sliced mushrooms are good , too
demonstrations.review: nice and very easy! i used an electric mixer instead of a blender, and it didn't get the perfect creamy texture, but still turned out great. took the suggestions for         s and garlic, and worked very well.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chicken garlic bites

simple and fun to make, great to eat! prep time includes marinating the chicken.  use matzo meal instead of the breadcrumbs and this is good for passover as well.

1. place chicken in shallow dish
2. in small bowl , mix olive oil , garlic , and black pepper
3. pour over chicken
4. cover and marinate 30 minutes
5. drain
6. preheat oven to 475f
7. mix bread crumbs and cayenne
8. coat chicken
9. arrange in a single layer on cookie sheet
10. bake 10 minutes or until brown
demonstrations.review: very good and hard to stop eating. like spicy chicken nuggets. good with ketchup or BBQ sauce. though i repeat was very spicy. i liked it, but it was too spicy for some others' tastes. adjust based on who your making it for. i used half cumin and half cayenne, which tasted good. tripled the recipe for seven people. though it wasn't finished, no one is complaining about having leftovers. i don't think double would have been enough. they were very delicious!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s onion patties latkes

i have been making these for over 20 years, i usually get about 15 patties but it depends on the size of the batter that you drop in the pan, these are better if fried to very brown and crispy, you can make a double recipe, fry them then freeze them on a tray then pop them into freezer bags, then just warm them in the oven to crisp up, they are very addicting and i can tell you i eat half before they even get to the table lol!  if you plan on doubling the recipe then make two separate recipes in two bowls, i have doubled the recipe into one bowl and for some reason they just are not as good ---  if desired you could add in a slightly beaten large egg and reduce the milk by 1/4 cup --- you will *love* these!  also see my
recipe#186700 *and*
recipe#244592

1. chop the onions finely then place into a bowl
2. in another large bowl mix together the flour , sugar , baking powder , seasoning salt , cayenne , garlic powder and a small amount of black pepper
3. mix to combine well
4. add in the milk and whisk until thoroughly combined
5. add in the chopped onions and green onions and mix with a wooden spoon until combined
6. in a large non-stick frypan , heat a small amount of oil to medium-hot , adding in more oil as needed as the patties will absorb too much oil if you add in a large amount of oil at one time
7. drop the batter from a tablespoon into about 1 / 2-inch of hot oil
8. flatten slightly with the spoon or spatula
9. sprinkle with a little salt
10. fry until crispy and brown on both sides
demonstrations.review: if you like onions, these are wonderful! perhaps due to the fact that i used a food processor to chop the onions, which actually makes them so small it is almost a sauce, my batter was to thin when i followed the recipe. when i added more flour though it turned out perfectly. GREAT side dish.

target.recipe_text:
joe s crab shack crab dip

copy cat recipe from google search. posted in reply to a request.

1. mix cream cheese , mayo , sour cream , and butter until smooth
2. blend in salt and paprika
3. stir in onion , green pepper , cheese , and crab meat
4. bake at 350f for 10-15 minutes , until bubbly
target.review: Great low carb dip if you use pork rein chips for dipping.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
parmesan sage pork chops

this is so delicious! my mother-in-law made it for us and i have made it ever since.  it came from a magazine--i don't know what one but this is amazingly good! this makes a lot of crumbs. i froze mine in a ziplock and also used it on chicken.  enjoy!

1. preheat oven to 425f degrees
2. mix in bowl , bread crumbs , grated parmesan cheese , dried rubbed sage and grated lemon peel
3. then , on a plate put flour seasoned with salt and pepper
4. coat chops with flour
5. dip in egg
6. then dip in bread crumb mixture
7. melt butter and olive oil in a oven-proof skillet
8. brown chops until golden
9. transfer to oven and bake until meat thermometer says 150 degrees , about 20 minutes
demonstrations.review: Best Dog gone Chops Ive had in years.. thanks!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
spaghetti squash  tomato  mushroom   cheese casserole

nan

1. slice squash in half lengthwise and scoop out seeds
2. bake it face down on a buttered tray for 30 to 40 minutes or until easily pierced by a fork
3. cool until ready to be handled
4. scoop out the insides gently with a fork which will form into spaghetti strands
5. while the squash bakes , saute the onions and garlic with salt , pepper , mushrooms and herbs
6. when onions are soft , add freshly chopped tomatoes
7. cook until most of liquid is evaporated
8. combine the ingredients
9. pour into buttered 2 quart casserole
10. top with lots of grated parmesan cheese
11. bake uncovered about 40 minutes in a 375 degrees oven
demonstrations.review: This sounds very good.  I have not made it but would like to.  I only wish the instructions were better.  Not real sure what to do after the saute instructions.  Like what do I do with the cheese and bread crumbs?  I think I will ommit the bread crumbs (for low carb purpose) and layer the cheese and squash like a lasagna.  Thanks for posting and cant wait to try it.  I will post again after tying this recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
reeses squares   5 ingredients   no bake  reese s

these bars are extremely rich and not for people with a fear of chocolate and peanut butter (if those people actually exist)!!! very easy no bake 5 ingredient recipe!

1. combine graham crumbs , sugar and peanut butter and mix well
2. blend in melted butter until well combined
3. press mixture evenly into a 9 x 13 inch pan
4. melt chocolate chips in microwave or in double boiler
5. spread over peanut butter mixture
6. chill until just set and cut into bars (these are very hard to cut if the chocolate gets "rock hard"
demonstrations.review: Now yea went and did it.. now I got to try this recipie.  I thank you but my body says OMG not again.

target.recipe_text:
cream of chicken potato bake

this is for all you cream soup lovers like me. easy, no fuss and great with ham, pork chops or fried chicken. enjoy!

1. in a 2 1 / 2 quart casserole layer some of the potatoes , top with onion slices , dot with butter
2. sprinkle with salt and pepper lightly
3. repeat process until all potatoes and onions are used
4. combine soup and milk
5. whisk till blended
6. pour over potatoes
7. cover and bake at 325 for 45 minutes till hot and bubbly and potatoes test tender with a fork
target.review:
I thought this was really good....and it does say test the potatoes for doneness.  

Good one...a keeper

demonstrations.recipe_text:
grandma bessie s beef stew

grandma's beef stew. this was passed down from grandma's mother to grandma to my mom to me.

1. if it is cool or cold weather , it is best to put this in the oven and let cook for a while
2. take a large pot on med high heat and add whole bottle of ketchup
3. fill empty bottle with water and rinse out bottle with it , pour this water in pot with ketchup
4. add carrots , celery , potatoes , garlic and onion
5. when all of this has been cooking for a 1 / 2 hour or so , coat meat with flour and brown in large pan with a little oil
6. cover with a lid and let this simmer for a few minutes
7. meat will be soooooo tender
8. add meat mixture to the veggies
9. mix well
10. add the salt and pepper
11. let this cook until it is thick and the veggies are tender
12. the"secret" is the ketchup
13. the stew doesn't taste a thing like ketchup though
demonstrations.review: This recipe turned out great for me.  I was particularly drawn to it because my dear grandmother was named Bessie....anyways...turned out wonderfully...thanks

demonstrations.recipe_text:
easy caramel biscuits

these breakfast biscuits are a family favorite. very simple to make and everyone who tries them always asks for the recipe. they are sweet and gooey. guaranteed to disapear quickly! make sure to serve them warm.

1. preheat oven to 400
2. heat sugar , nuts , butter and water until melted
3. separate biscuits and cut into 4th's and place in bowl
4. pour sugar mixture over biscuits and toss
5. spoon biscuits into greased bundt pan
6. bake 20-25 minutes
7. let stand in pan 3 minutes then invert onto serving plate
8. serve warm
demonstrations.review: These are great....I changed a couple things though,  I used brown sugar instead of white...and I used one can of "layered" biscuits.  They turned out great....and needless to say there arent any left....good recipe...a keeper.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
yogurt biscuits

this are a great quick bread that is good with breakfast or supper!

1. preheat oven to 425 degrees f
2. grease an 8 x 8 pan
3. stir dry ingredients together
4. cut in shortening
5. gently stir in yogurt mixture until sticky dough is formed
6. place dough on floured surface
7. dust top with flour and gently pat dough with hands until 1 / 2 in thick
8. cut into 8-10 rounds
9. place in pan
10. brush with shortening
11. bake 15 minutes
12. turn out of pan 5 minutes after removing from over
13. cover with tea towel and serve
demonstrations.review: wow...thanks a bundle for this recipe....its what ive been looking for....delicious

target.recipe_text:
greek baklava

sweet and nutty!

1. preheat oven to 325
2. layer half of the sheets of phyllo one sheet at a time , in a greased 11x7x2 baking pan , brushing each sheet evenly with butter and folding ends over if necessary to fit into pan
3. keep unused sheets covered with plastic wrap while assembling baklava to prevent drying
4. mix 1 / 4 cup of the sugar and cinnamon
5. stir in walnuts
6. sprinkle nut mixture evenly over buttered phyllo in pan
7. layer remaining phyllo , one sheet at a time , over nut mixture , brushing each sheet evenly with butter
8. cut diagonally into squares , cutting completely through all layers
9. bake in preheated oven until crisp and golden , about one hour
10. combine remaining sugar , the water , lemon juice and honey in small saucepan
11. cook and stir over low heat until sugar dissolves
12. heat to boiling
13. pour evenly over hot baklava
14. let stand loosely covered 8 hours or overnight
target.review: I baked it at 335 for almost an hour and it seemed right.  Easy & delicious!  The layers got tough though and was hard to cut through but other than that it was great.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
spinach salad with honey bacon dressing

the best spinach salad i've ever had. every time i serve this to guests, i get requests for the recipe. i found this in taste of home soups, salads and sandwiches.

1. combine first 6 ingredients with 5 of the cooked , crumbled bacon strips in a large bowl
2. in a small bowl , whisk together the honey , vinegar , oil , mustard lemon juice and remaining 2 strips of cooked , crumbled bacon
3. pour over salad
4. serve immediately
demonstrations.review: Delicious!  Will make again!Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
onion fried mandarin orange chicken

what a wonderful combination--caramelized onions and tender chicken complimented by a light orange sauce. are you hungry yet? the dish is not only delicious it is quick to fix. this recipe is from pillsbury fast and healthy, june 1996.

1. season the chicken with the basil , salt , and cayenne pepper
2. melt the margarine in large nonstick skillet
3. add chicken and cook over medium-high heat for 5 minutes
4. turn chicken
5. add onion and cook an additional 4 to 6 minutes or until chicken is fork tender and juices run clear
6. in a small bowl , combine the chicken broth , reserved orange liquid and cornstarch
7. blend well
8. add to skillet with chicken and cook stirring until thick and bubbly
9. gently stir in orange segments
10. cook until heated through
demonstrations.review: Very good & different!  Not a hit with the kids though, "too spicy!" they said.  I added noodles to the mix and it made a great meal.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mean chef s yucatan style chicken  lime  and orzo soup

i adopted this recipe from mean chef, who described it as "quick easy and delicious." i agree--it's simple to make, very yummy, and reasonably filling. it makes a good, light meal.

1. cook orzo in pot of boiling salted water until just tender
2. drain well
3. heat oil in large saucepan over medium heat
4. add onion , garlic , and chiles
5. saut until onion begins to brown , about 4 minutes
6. add chicken
7. saut 1 minute
8. add broth , lime juice , and tomato
9. simmer until chicken is cooked through , about 3 minutes
10. mix in orzo , then chopped cilantro
11. season soup with salt and pepper
12. ladle soup into 4 bowls
13. garnish with cilantro sprigs
demonstrations.review: A good healthy soup but I felt something was missing.  I did modify the recipe some by reducing the onion & jal. pepper amounts.  I am hoping tomorrow it will be even better.

target.recipe_text:
caraway rye bread

i got this recipe from my breadman pro bread maker.  it was soooo delicious that i had to share it!  for a variation, add the optional dehydrated onion for another excellent recipe :-d

1. you want the eggs at room temperature
2. add enough water to the eggs to equal 1 1 / 3 cups
3. bake in bread machine according to its instructions on the 2 lb
4. whole wheat setting
target.review: Excellent! I've thrown out many breads over the years but this is my go-to rye. I am going to reduce the honey slightly next time around. Thanks so much for sharing.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
dark chocolate cake

while it takes slightly longer to prepare this recipe than a box mix, the resulting moist, delicious cake makes it very worth the little extra time. i consider this 'perfect' chocolate cake. this cake is excellent with  both with recipe #261024 and recipe #208959 (the dark flavor version). (i use recipe #95416 when i'm decorating the cake.) i love how the leftovers are still moist even a day or two later. (i store my loosely covered with plastic wrap.)
my father adores this cake with recipe #261024 on it. for his birthday, father's day etc. i make him cupcakes with the icing on them and individually wrap them. he keeps them in his freezer for when he wants "a piece of cake". he claims they are as good as when they are fresh. 
(even though it isn't where i got the recipe from so i can't vouch for it, reviewers have said it is the recipe on the hershey's cocoa can. i would recommend using their special dark cocoa if possible.)

1. heat oven to 350f
2. grease and flour two 9 inch round baking pans or one 13x9 inch pan
3. in large mixer bowl , stir together dry ingredients
4. add eggs , milk , oil , and vanilla
