5. beat on medium speed for 2 minutes
6. stir in boiling water by hand
7. i usually use between 2 / 3 & 3 / 4 cups
8. the cake is still very moist but it doesn't seem to "fall" as much as it cools
9. this might have to do with our high humidity or brand of flour or other factors so i don't know if it will work for everyone
10. pour into prepared pan
11. bake 30 to 35 minutes for round 9-inch pans , 35 to 40 minutes for rectangular pan or until wooden pick inserted in center comes out clean
12. because they have a tendency to overflow if you fill them more than 2 / 3 full , i usually get about 27-28 cupcakes per batch
13. bake for approximately 18-20 minutes
14. cool 10 minutes
15. remove from pan to wire racks
16. please
17. chocolate drink mixes that you add to milk or water to drink will not work in this recipe
demonstrations.review: I found the flavor very good, but I made cupcakes with paper wrappers and they would not peel off. If I make this again I'm making sure to use a non-stick metal pan only.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
minestrone with italian sausage

crock-pot minestrone with italian sausage

1. brown the sausage
2. add the cooked sausage and all the ingredients except for the ditalini into a seven quart crock pot
3. cook on high for 6 hours
4. add the ditalini and cook for another half hour
demonstrations.review: I searched by "cole slaw mix" (I had extra chopped cabbage and carrots) and found this great idea. I only made half, using some chicken sauages and it was terrific. Thanks, Bill.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
texas red enchilada sauce

this sauce can be used with beef or cheese enchiladas. the amount of "heat" in the sauce depends on the type and amount of chili powder you use.

1. melt butter / margarine in a sauce pan
2. make a roux by browning flour in melted butter / margarine
3. add spices and tomato paste
4. stir until well blended into roux
5. add water gradually , stirring constantly
6. heat until boiling
7. continue simmering and stirring until desired thickness is achieved
8. taste every so often and adjust spices as needed
9. once desired consistency and taste is reached , coat the bottom of a pan with the sauce , add freshly rolled enchiladas , then pour the remainder of the red sauce over enchiladas
10. place pan in oven and cook until enchiladas are done
demonstrations.review: Excellent and Easy.

target.recipe_text:
seventies almond rice

growing up, this is what my mom was famous for at church.  no matter the occasion, she was always asked to bring a dish of almond rice.   it has a bit more salt and fat to it than newer recipes.  it would easily adapt to crock pot cooking or vegetarian requirements.

1. in a large skillet , melt 1 stick of margarine
2. add the rice and stir thoroughly
3. dissolve the bouillon into the hot water and add it to the rice
4. cover and cook for 20 to 30 minutes , until the water has been absorbed
5. turn the heat off and add almonds , green onions , and soy sauce
6. crock pot modification: premelt the butter
7. add butter and rice to crock pot , then stir to combine
8. add bouillon and water
9. cook -- 1
10. 5 to 2 hours on hi and 4-6 hours on lo
11. i've checked on hi but please let me know what your times are
12. finish recipe as above
13. brown rice modification: same as normal , but add 1 / 2 cup more liquid
14. times would be 50 minutes in a skillet
15. add 30-60 minutes to crock pot times
16. modern version: substitute 1 tablespoon olive oil and 1 tablespoon butter for the margarine
17. use brown rice
18. use low sodium chicken or vegetable stock in place of the bouillon and water
19. use low sodium soy sauce
20. and -- it will still taste good
21. cooking methods sure have changed !
target.review: I served this with Melt In Your Mouth Chicken Breasts. The flavor is wonderful. We all liked the addition of almonds.  This is kind of like a fancy but easy to fix dish. I'm going to add the left over chicken to the extra rice for lunch tomorrow. The only change I would make is to cut back on the butter. Thanks for posting.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pan grilled pork chops

these chops are so easy and very tender. it's based on a recipe in the mama dip's kitchen cookbook. be sure to follow the important steps of letting the chops rest with the salt and seasoning before cooking, then browning the sides slowly, followed by a covered "rest".  mama dip is a traditional southern u.s. cook, chef, restauranteur and cookbook author.

1. sprinkle the salt , thyme and pepper on the pork chops
2. let sit on counter top for 30 minutes
3. place oil in large cast iron skillet and heat until medium hot
4. place chops in the pan , placing them so they don't touch each other
5. cook each side slowly until nice and golden brown on each side
6. this will take about 4 minutes per side
7. cover the pan with a tight fitting lid
8. turn off the heat , and let the chops sit for about 8- 10 minutes , depending on thickness of chops
9. after removing chops , you can de-glaze the pan with a little water , wine or broth and a touch of butter and serve as a sauce
demonstrations.review: I love pork chops and tend to make them with some sort of sauce to keep them from drying out. Not any more. These were moist, tender, and tasty. So easy to cook too. We've had these twice this month. Thank you for an easy and delicious recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
one dish chicken and bows

i love this meal for it's ease and down home goodness. you can make this one dish meal in less than 30 minutes. it's pretty too! you could substitute chopped carrots for the red pepper if you'd prefer. it reminds me of chicken pot pie without the 'pie'. comfort! it makes a lot so you can serve half of it and freeze the other half for a quick dinner some other night. from simple & delicious courtesy of danette forbes. *note: this recipe does not include many spices, etc.. it is meant to be a comfort food type of recipe. if you enjoy spice, go ahead and throw some in!! this recipe is also versatile in terms of what veggies you like. have fun with it. :)

1. cook the pasta according to the pkg
2. directions
3. meanwhile , in a large skillet or dutch oven , cook the chicken and red pepper in melted butter over medium heat for about 6 minutes or until chicken juices run clear
4. stir in the soup , peas , milk , garlic powder , salt and pepper
5. bring to a boil
6. reduce the heat and simmer , uncovered , for about 2 minutes
7. stir in parmesan cheese
8. drain pasta and add to the chicken mixture , tossing to coat
9. serve !
10. if freezing: cool remaining mixture and transfer to a freezer container
11. cover and freeze for up to 3 months
12. to use frozen casserole: thaw in the fridge overnight
13. transfer to an ungreased , shallow 3 quart microwave-safe dish
14. cover and microwave on high for 8-10 minutes or until heated through , stirring once
demonstrations.review:
I am giving this 5 stars despite the subtitution I made. I used frozen mixed veggies because that is what I had on hand. DS said he would prefer a single veggie next time. Putting this together was so easy and quick and the taste was wonderful. This would be a nice branching out recipe for a begining cook.
Without the pasta this would be great as a pot pie filling or served over potatoes or rice.
Super easy and yummy.
Thanks

demonstrations.recipe_text:
buttermilk bay chicken

although the recipe calls for boneless chicken, i have never made it that way - i always use bone-in chicken thighs, for both the price and the flavor. if you use chicken on the bone, cooking time will be about 45 minutes. preparation time listed is overnight marinating.  recipe shared on saveur.com.

1. place the chicken pieces into a large plastic freezer bag and add the buttermilk and vegetable oil
2. add the lightly crushed garlic cloves to the bag along with the crushed peppercorns and salt
3. sprinkle in the bay seasoning and add the maple syrup , then gently squeeze the bag to mix the marinade ingredients together and coat the chicken
4. seal the bag and leave the chicken to marinate in the fridge , ideally overnight , or out of the fridge for at least 30 minutes and up to two hours
5. preheat the oven to 425 degrees
6. take the chicken pieces out of the bag , shaking off the excess marinade , and arrange them in a roasting tin lined with foil
7. drizzle over a little oil , then transfer to the oven and roast for about 30 minutes , or until golden-brown and completely cooked through
demonstrations.review: Didn't have any maple syrup, but I don't know if we missed it. Used boneless, skinless chicken breasts and was surprised at how moist the chicken was. Only got to marinade it a few hours. Next time I'll plan better and put it together the night before. Thanks for sharing this easy and delicious recipe.

target.recipe_text:
butter pecan cookies

simple basic cookie that most everyone loves.  i love pecans so this is right up my alley.

1. cream butter and sugar
2. add egg
3. add flour , salt , baking powder and pecans
4. mix in vanilla
5. chill dough 1 hour
6. roll out 1 / 8 inch thick and cut with any size cutter
7. bake at 400 for 8 minutes or until nice and light brown
target.review: I actually made these last night and my whole family just loved them. I will make these again!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mushroom chicken with honey mustard

my sister gave me this recipe, she found it in a book for meals in 30 minutes. it's so easy and tasty too. i recommend serving with a salad or bread sticks (to mop up the honey mustard sauce).

1. tenderize meat and season with a little salt and pepper
2. melt butter in a large frying pan on medium-high heat
3. put chicken in pan and brown both sides
4. after it's browned , turn to medium heat and add mushrooms
5. cover with a lid for 20 minutes
6. cut into chicken to make sure it's done
7. if not , check it every 5 minutes
8. remove chicken only from the pan , leaving the mushrooms
9. in a small bowl , combine equal amounts of honey and mustard and mix together
10. if you need to add more than stated , add according to taste
11. add honey and mustard mixture to mushrooms
12. do not replace the lid
13. stir until mushroom sauce thickens up and pour over the chicken to complete the dish
demonstrations.review: Awesome recipe. Easy to make and tasty. Love it!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
butterscotch pudding cake  quick and easy

i got this from a friend at church. i thought she had slaved for hours preparing this wonderful cake. just proves once more, it is the simple things in life that are good. take this to your next pot-luck dinner party and you will be swamped with requests for your secret recipe.

1. prepare pudding according to package directions and allow to cool
2. stir cake mix into pudding and mix well
3. batter will be thick
4. spread batter into greased and floured 9x13x2 baking dish
5. sprinkle nuts and butterscotch morsel evenly on top of the batter
6. bake in 350 degree oven for 45-60 minutes or until tooth pick inserted in center comes out clean
7. can be served with cool whip or ice cream but is great all by itself
demonstrations.review: Amazing moist cake. I brought it to my spring potluck and it was a winner winner. I will def. make this again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
my thai sesame noodles

after tinkering with a few different recipes, this is my family's favorite version! sooooo good, i could eat the whole bowl! you can easily add cooked chicken and make it a main dish! the honey is an optional ingredient; leave it out if you don't like the noodles sweet.

1. heat peanut butter in microwave for 20 seconds to soften
2. in a large bowl whisk together softened peanut butter , soy sauce , vinegar , sesame oil , sambal oelek and honey
3. add spaghetti , green onions and sesame seeds
4. toss well
5. chill until ready to serve - or serve at room temperature
demonstrations.review: I loved this recipe; the flavors were outstanding.

target.recipe_text:
chinese spicy beef lettuce wraps

from oregonlive.com.  i loved the beef lettuce wraps from a restaurant in montauk, ny called east by northeast. this was the closest i have found to recreating it with a few minor adjustments from me.

1. spray large , heavy skillet with nonstick cooking spray
2. in skillet set over medium-high heat , brown ground beef
3. drain if necessary
4. add garlic , sherry , soy sauce , sesame oil , chili paste , five-spice powder , white part of green onions , water chestnuts and minced chile
5. turn down heat and simmer about 10 minutes
6. add cornstarch-water mixture to beef mixture and stir until it thickens slightly
7. add green part of green onions and cook just until heated through
8. separate lettuce leaves , wash and pat dry
9. arrange lettuce cups on platter and serve alongside beef mixture
10. serve with my sweet soy dipping sauce a must-have for the lettuce wraps !
target.review: Excellent the only thing I did was add rice vinegar instead of sherry wine. I also added a little hoesen sauce about 1 Tbs. Great recipe

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pork tenderloin in bourbon brown sugar marinade

i love to cook pork like this. i have also used this marinade with pork chops. i have adapted this from lean and loving it.

1. in a shallow glass casserole dish , combine bourbon , brown sugar , soy sauce , cilantro , lemon juice , worcestershire sauce , water , and thyme , stirring until the sugar is dissolved
2. add the pork , cover , and marinate in the refrigerator , turning occasionally , for 8 to 12 hours
3. preheat the oven to 450f
4. coat a baking sheet or the bottom of your roasting pan with tin foil , making sure the entire sheet is covered
5. the marinade tends to burn on and its a pain to wash
6. for tenderloin: place the tenderloins , side by side without touching , on a wire rack in a shallow roasting pan
7. for chops: place pork chops on a baking sheet
8. roast for 30 minutes , or until a meat thermometer registers 160f , basting occasionally with the marinade
9. discard any unused marinade
demonstrations.review:
My pork roast did not look anything like this one.  
This picture is a misrepresentation  of the dish... This picture looks like spare ribs.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s baked potato salad casserole  or cold potato salad

this may be served hot as a casserole or reduce the melted butter amount down to 2 tablespoons and serve as a cold potato salad, either way it's delicious! --- if you are serving hot as a casserole i strongly recommend to have the potatoes cooled to room temperature before using in this recipe or use cold potatoes that have been cooked a day ahead, i have even made this using about 5 cups of thawed frozen hash browns, the complete casserole may be assembled and refrigerated for up to 2 days ahead before baking although it's so delicious cold it might not even make it to the oven, and also makes a large amount which makes this *perfect* dish for potlucks --- if you are baking as a casserole use only mayonnaise such as hellman's using salad dressing will not be as good.

1. to serve hot as a casserole
2. grease a 13 x 9-inch baking dish
3. set oven to 350 degrees f
4. in a large bowl , mix mayonnaise , sour cream and melted butter , garlic powder , seasoned salt and black pepper until well combined
5. mix in green onion and yellow onion
6. add in the cooked cubed potatoes , cubed cheese and ham mix with a large spatula until well combined
7. transfer / spread the mixture to prepared casserole dish
8. at this point you may cover and refrigerate for up to 24 hours until ready to bake
9. bake 25-30 minutes or until hot and bubbly
10. remove from oven and sprinkle the grated cheddar on top
11. return to oven and bake 5-8 minutes more or until the cheese has melted
12. to serve as a cold potato salad
13. make as stated in steps 3-5 reducing the melted butter to 2 tablespoons
14. place in a bowl , cover and refrigerate for at least 4 hours or more before serving
15. delicious !
demonstrations.review: Outstanding.  Instead of potatoes I used noodles.  Very filling and satisfying.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
french country casserole

i am sure that the french used actual dried beans, soaked and cooked. however, this one is very quick to make if your evening is hectic.

1. combine all ingredients in a bowl
2. transfer to an ungreased 3-quart baking dish
3. cover and bake at 375f for 60 to 70 minutes or until carrots are tender
demonstrations.review: This was  very good.  I was turned off by all the beans at first but it was a really good meal for kielbasa.  I will make it again.   Thanks

target.recipe_text:
swiss  round steak with onion gravy

we always called this "salisbury steak", but it does not have tomatoes. comfort food at it's best...

1. cut round steak into 6 serving size pieces
2. on a cutting board , dredge pieces with flour , salt and pepper
3. pound flour into the meat with a meat mallet
4. turn pieces , dredge , and pound until they can't hold any more flour
5. in a large non-stick skillet , heat oil and brown steak pieces on both sides
6. place in a covered casserole
7. add onions and garlic to the skillet
8. saute until onions are limp
9. place onions and garlic over steak pieces in casserole dish
10. add enough beef broth to barely cover meat
11. the flour from the meat will thicken the broth as it bakes and will make its own gravy
12. bake at 300f for 2 hours or until fork-tender
13. serve over noodles or mashed potatoes
target.review: This had good flavor and the meat was moist and tender. I did brown the floured meat well, but the coating still seemed a bit gummy to me - though DH had two helpings. I'll make this again, maybe adding some tomato paste to the sauce.  Thanks for a useful recipe, goddess!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
rhubarb oatmeal bars

a delicious rhubarb bar, great for the first rhubarb of the season, or to use up the last. i have found that cooking the rhubarb in half water half fruit juice (i've used orange or pineapple) enhances the flavour nicely.

1. crust: combine all ingredients until crumbly
2. pat half of mixture into 13x9" baking pan and bake for about 20 minutes before pouring filling on top
3. filling: in saucepan combine rhubarb , sugar , cornstarch and water
4. cook until clear
5. blend in vanilla
6. pour over baked crust
7. sprinkle with remaining crumb mixture
8. bake at 350 for 20 minutes
demonstrations.review: I used butter and skipped the first bake (of just the bottom crust) ; just short on time. Otherwise, I made these as written. Delicious!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kool   aid   jello popsicles

this delicious recipe is quick and easy! grew up on these. thanks, mom!

1. in a 2-quart glass measure , combine the kool-aid , jello powder and sugar
2. add hot water and stir until completely dissolved
3. stir in cold water
4. pour into popsicle molds and freeze
demonstrations.review: This is a great mixture that makes a softer textured popsicle that kids love; solid but not rock-hard.  I like them for a low-carb treat - using the sugar-free versions of the drink mix and gelatin and no added sweetener.  I reduce the water to a total of three cups (just 1 cup of boiling water, then 2 cups of ice water).  Thanks for posting this recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
beef   broccoli

a nice stir-fry with tender beef and crisp-tender broccoli in a savory sauce. great over jasmine rice. recipe by jasper carparnay

1. slice beef across the grain into thin slices
2. mix together 1 tsp brown sugar with 4 tsp sesame oil , 4 tsp rice wine , and 2 tsp cornstarch
3. pour this mixture over beef and allow beef to rest for 30 minutes
4. in a small bowl , combine remaining 4 tsp rice wine , 2 tbsp oyster sauce , 2 tsp cornstarch , and 4 tbsp water
5. heat wok or deep skillet on high heat
6. add 2 tbsp vegetable oil , and when it is hot , and ginger and salt
7. wait a few seconds , then add the broccoli , and stir-fry for one minute
8. then add the water to the broccoli , and steam-fry the broccoli until the water evaporates
9. remove broccoli from wok or skillet
10. reheat wok or skillet on high and add remaining 2 tbsp vegetable oil
11. add beef and stir-fry , but do not stir too much- allow the beef to sear against the pan
12. when it has browned , add the seasoning sauce
13. add broccoli back to wok or skillet and stir to mix
14. when sauce has thickened and stir-fry is hot , serve
demonstrations.review: Yum! I added a bit of garlic, too, and doubled the sauce just because it was so good. Thanks for this great recipe, Sue.

target.recipe_text:
crab artichoke dip

serve with crackers, melba toast rounds, toast points or whatever you like. always a big hit.

1. directions:
2. preheat oven to 350
3. melt butter
4. stir in onion , garlic and parsley
5. cook till onion is tender
6. add cream cheese and keep on low heat until creamy
7. add other ingredients , except crab , and mix well
8. pour into large oven proof serving dish and fold in crab meat
9. bake until bubbly and hot
target.review:
This was absolutely FANTASTIC! I made this recipe for PAC Spring 2009. In making this I was hoping the end product would be similar to Red Lobster's Crab Artichoke dip and it was just as good if not better! The only changes I made to this recipe were: 1) I added a can of baby shrimp to mellow out the artichoke flavor, 2) I mixed in 1 cup of Montery Cheddar Jack Cheese into the stovetop mixture and 3) when it was all finish I topped it with more Montery Cheddar Jack cheese and more Parmesan cheese. Loved this recipe, thanks MomB for a keeper!!
P.S. I served with tortilla chips sprinkled with Lowry's Seasoning salt and warmed in the oven for 10 minutes!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
lee s hot crab dip

lee's hot crab dip

1. remove cartilage from crab meat
2. in a large bowl , mix cream cheese , sour cream , mayonnaise , lemon juice , worcestershire sauce , dry mustard , and garlic salt until smooth
3. add enough milk to make mixture creamy
4. stir in 2 tablespoons of the grated cheese
5. fold crab meat into cream cheese mixture
6. pour into greased 1-quart casserole
7. top with remaining cheese and paprika
8. bake at 325 degrees fahrenheit until mixture is bubbly and browned on top , about 30 minutes
demonstrations.review: I loved this dish. My dear old dad found it on here and made it for my boyfriend and I for supper. It was so delicious! Dad likes it better the next day after it has chilled in the refrigerator over night and all of the flavors have blended. Served hot or cold its a hit!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
heath bar toffee coffee cake

this is a dangerous cake to have around, it's *so* delicious! for the members that live in canada and cannot get heath bars use hershey's skor toffee pieces, sold in a 200 gram package. this cake has a sweet crunchy topping and is really easy to make. this cake is like no other, just make it and see! this cake can also be made in an 11 x 7-inch baking pan or a springform pan also.

1. set oven to 350 degrees
2. butter a 13 x 9-inch baking pan
3. in a medium bowl using an electric mixer on low speed , beat together flour , brown sugar , white sugar , butter and salt until the mixture resembles coarse meal
4. transfer 1 / 2 cup butter mixture to a bowl and mix in chopped heath bars (or toffee bits mini chocolate chips and pecans
5. set aside
6. stir in the baking soda into the remaining butter / sugar mixture
7. add in buttermilk , egg and vanilla
8. beat until just combined
9. transfer to prepared baking dish
10. sprinkle with reserved toffee topping evenly over batter
11. bake for about 35 minutes , or until golden brown and the cake tests done
12. cool completely in baking dish and cut into squares
demonstrations.review: I've been making this recipe for years, it was one of the first recipes I learned how to cook! Never had an unsatisfied customer when this dessert is what is being served! Perfect for every occasion and easy enough for any experience level!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
peanut butter s more cookie bars

this easy cookie bar recipe starts with refrigerated cookie dough from pillsbury.

1. heat oven to 350f spray 13x9-inch pan with nonstick cooking spray
2. spoon cookie dough in bottom of sprayed pan
3. with floured fingers , press dough evenly to form crust
4. bake at 350f for 16 to 19 minutes or until golden brown
5. remove pan from oven
6. sprinkle with marshmallows
7. return to oven
8. bake an additional 2 to 3 minutes or until marshmallows are puffy
9. meanwhile , in small saucepan , melt chocolate chips with oil over low heat , stirring until smooth
10. remove pan from oven
11. sprinkle with colored candy pieces
12. drizzle melted chocolate mixture over warm bars
13. cool 45 minutes or until completely cooled
14. cut into bars
demonstrations.review: These were absolutely wonderful! It makes a nice large batch perfect for sharing with all of our family and friends. Quick, easy, and delicious we'll be sure to make this one again and again!

target.recipe_text:
herb crusted roast beef

nan

1. put the roast with the fat side up , in an ungreased roasting pan
2. mix together the cloves , mustard , lemon juice , oil , and worcestershire sauce
3. stir to mix well
4. pour over and evenly coat the roast
5. in a bowl , add the next 6 ingredients
6. mixing well
7. rub herb mixture over roast
8. bake roast , uncovered , at 325 degrees for 1 3 / 4 to 2 1 / 4 hours or until desired degree of doneness
9. remove from oven and place roast on a warm serving platter
10. let stand for 10-15 minutes
11. add 2 cups water and bouillon granules to pan drippings
12. bring mixture to a boil
13. mix together flour and 1 / 3 cup of water
14. stirring until smooth
15. gradually add to pan
16. cook until bubbly and thickened , stirring constantly
17. slice roast and serve with gravy
target.review: Truly wonderful. I used a smaller roast, but kept the rest of the amounts the same. Divine smelling, visually appealing, and also delicious. 5 stars without a doubt!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
grilled balsamic london broil

prep time is 5 minutes. the rest is time marinating.

1. put all ingredients , except meat , in a container fitted with a lid
2. cover and shake
3. pour the marinade over the top round steak and cover
4. marinate in the refrigerator for 4 hours or overnight , turning the meat occasionally
5. grill or broil until done as desired
6. slice thinly
demonstrations.review: This was outstanding. No changes made and no changes necessary. (I did use lower sodium soy.) I am not usually a fan of london broil. It never tastes right. I marinaded for 1/2 a day. Used it on a mixed green salad with a really nice blue cheese, expecting the meat to not be good enough to eat alone. Boy was I wrong. What a waste of a good blue cheese!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
southwestern quinoa vegetable casserole

this is a pretty good healthy and easy to prepare dish

1. preheat oven to 400
2. combine all ingredients except cheese and sour cream in a 2 quart casserole
3. cover with foil and bake for 30 minutes
4. remove and stir
5. bake for another 20 minutes or until all liquid has been absorbed and quinoa is tender
6. cover with cheese and broil till cheese is melted
7. serve with sour cream
demonstrations.review: Easy, healthy, cheap, and, and kid-approved! I changed a bit based on what I had on hand and personal tastes, but the followed the core of the recipe. Used no-salt diced tomatoes (no ro-tel), a larger amount of rehydrated dried black beans (I make them in the crockpot & freeze them in baggies) 16 oz package of frozen mixed veggies (not corn), used a Tblspn homemade blend of spices similar to a less spicy Emeril's Essence, but still added in the listed herbs. I used extra broth (made from low sodium better than boullion) to make up for extra veggies. I added a small amount of cheddar on top, but did not need to broil it because it melted on contact. The adults added lime juice - a MUST as far as I am concerned - and jalapenos at the table, didn't put them in because of the bland loving children. We used plain fat free greek yogurt instead of sour cream - the difference is never noticed anymore.I know this sounds very changed, but I am sure that the differences in taste from the original recipe are small.  I would skip the cheese next time because it was unnecessary. I will do this many times again. It is very rare to get my family to approve of a one dish meal, or a healthy meal, or a meatless without pasta meal, or one that cost very little. All at once and smiles! SCORE! THANK YOU!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
dry rub pork ribs

a simple, no hassle, no mess and delicious method for 

1. preheat oven to 325f
2. cut pork ribs into sections of 3 or 4 bones
3. mix remaining ingredients well , sprinkle on both sides of ribs and rub into the meat
4. seal rib sections in foil with a tablespoon of water in each package , and bake for 2 hours on a cookie sheet in the center of the oven
5. open foil carefully as steam escapes
6. can be crisped on a hot bbq if desired but will be great just the way it is
demonstrations.review: Just want to say, "Thank you." I am making ribs for a large party and needed to make a portion for my FIL with no salt at all. Every recipe I checked out required basting with bbq sauce, or some other salt laden liquid. With this recipe, I was able to remove the salt, and up the other spices. I just tasted the resulting rub and it is fabulous, even without the sauce. The method used is perfect! A bit of water in foil with a rub instead of braising with some other liquid fit the bill. Thank you for taking the stress out of my day!

target.recipe_text:
mom s oyster dressing stuffing

the best thing about a stuffed turkey is the oyster dressing.  my grandma (gigi) and mom would argue every year as to whether it was better made with cornbread cubes or regular bread.  i prefer regular bread, but you decide for yourself.

1. heat milk , butter , and oyster liquid in small pan
2. combine bread cubes , celery , onion , spices , and oysters
3. add liquid and stir
4. stuff poultry or place in greased foil lined baking dish
5. bake 350 degrees for 1 hour , or until poultry is done
target.review:
I just made this last night for Thanksgiving. I'm so pleased that I did! What attracted me to this recipe was the ease of making it (the recipe that I have is more difficult and not as tasty.)

I took the cornbread route (hey, I'm a southerner.) I noted that it used all the cornbread from my cast iron skillet, so that's easy to remember. I used a pint of fresh Apalachicola oysters (yum) and threw in some fresh mushrooms. Soooo good!!

The only thing I'll do differently next time is cut back on the salt. This is not the fault of the recipe: I bake my cornbread in bacon fat, so it's got a bit of saltiness already.

Thank you for posting this excellent recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
creamy shrimp marsala linguine

a yummy and creamy shrimp pasta dinner

1. wash and chop green onion
2. in a medium sauce pan , mix 8 tbsp butter , 1 / 4 cup chopped green onion , 2 tsp thyme leaves and 2 tbsp minced garlic over medium heat
3. cook for 5 minutes , stirring frequently
4. add 1 cup of dry marsala wine and continue cooking an additional 5 minutes
5. lower heat and set aside
6. do not cover
7. in a large saute pan , add 2 tbsp of butter and 8 oz of sliced muchrooms over meduim-high heat , stirring frequently until muchrooms are browned on both sides
8. add medium cooked shrimp and continue cooking with the muchrooms for 5 more minutes
9. lower heat and set aside
10. in the medium sauce pan , add 2 cups of heavy whipping cream , 1 cup whole milk and 1 / 2 cup grated parmesan cheese to the marsala wine mixture
11. cook over medium heat for 5 minutes and then add the mushrooms and shrimp to mixture
12. lower heat to a low boil and set aside
13. cook linguine noodles and drain
14. pour creamy marsala and shrimp sauce over linguine and enjoy
demonstrations.review: Wow. This sauce is sinfully delicious! I followed the recipe exactly, and would only advise that folks bake plenty of French bread to sop this up...or you will be licking your plate! Great recipe. Thank you.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cheese filled peppers

i prefer these vegetarian, but you can add the ground beef.

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees
2. divide peppers in two , remove stem and seeds
3. sprinkle the coarse salt on baking pan
4. mix meat , tabasco , garlic salt , pepper , lemon juice , crumbs , and half of jarlsberg cheese
5. divide evenly between the peppers
6. top the peppers with remainder of the cheese
7. melt butter , add garlic salt , and brush over the peppers
8. place on top of coarse salt on baking sheet , and bake in 350f oven about 35 minutes
demonstrations.review: I've been meaning to review this. I initially hunted you down because I love the way you photograph food! I was attracted to this recipe because meat was optional. Since my DIL is a vegetarian, I figured I'd stick a carton of mushrooms with a small onion in the food processor, and saute that. I drained it and proceeded with the recipe. Fantastic! Next time I did this for her, I was too lazy to go through all the rigamarole, so I just sautéed and drained a carton of sliced mushrooms, and followed the recipe. This was actually her preferred method. The ingredients are spot on, and the Jarlsberg cheese, while pricey, is a must! Thanks for the recipe....and your beautiful pics of food!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
easy maple pecan monkey bread

from pillsbury.  sounds ooey-gooey and delicious.

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees and generously coat a 3 quart bundt pan with non-stick cooking spray
2. combine the sugar and cinnamon in a gallon sized plastic bag
3. remove dough from canisters and separate into 16 biscuits
4. use a sharp knife to cut each biscuit into quarters
5. place 4 pieces in the bag and shake it up to coat the pieces well
6. arrange in pan , and repeat with remaining biscuit pieces , sprinkling with chopped pecans as you layer
7. in a small bowl , combine melted butter , brown sugar , and maple syrup
8. spoon the mixture evenly over the biscuit pieces
9. bake 25 to 30 minutes or until golden brown and cooked through
10. allow bread to cool in pan 10 minutes
11. carefully invert onto serving plate and serve warm
demonstrations.review: Wow. Not only is this easy, it is pretty and delicious! I made this for company, so I just threw the pecans on top, so that if someone wanted nuts, they could grab from the bottom. This will be my new Christmas morning go-to recipe. Thanks!

target.recipe_text:
low carb mexi baked chicken

another personal south beach diet friendly favorite of mine. it's flavorful and easy to throw together, bakes in less than 1 hour. i serve this with a side of my mexican jumping beans. for the taco seasoning, i like to make my own (no sugar added; there are plenty of taco seasoning zaar recipes to choose from, if you would like to make your own.

1. preheat oven to 375 degrees
2. spray a shallow , small baking dish with non-stick spray
3. coat chicken lightly with taco seasoning , on both sides
4. spoon salsa over top of breast
5. bake , uncovered , about 45 minutes
6. sprinkle cheese on both breasts evenly
7. bake for another 5 minutes or until cheese is melted through
target.review: This gets five stars from me and hubby. I used Penzey's Fajita seasoning and colby-jack cheese. I didn't make this in the oven, but cooked it in a skillet on the stove and it worked out well. I served it with extra cheese and sour cream for garnish along with bell/sweet pepper stir fry and salad. The leftovers were just as good today for lunch. Thank you!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
low carb taco bake

serve with additional toppings like shredded lettuce, jalapenos, guacamole, ripe olives, sour cream or salsa.

1. for the crust , beat the cream cheese and eggs until smooth
2. add the cream and seasoning
3. grease a 9"x13" baking dish
4. spread the cheese over the bottom
5. pour in the egg mixture as evenly as possible
6. bake at 375f , 25-30 minutes
7. let stand 5 minutes before adding the topping
8. for the topping , brown the hamburger
9. drain fat
10. stir in the seasoning , tomato sauce and chiles
11. spread over the crust
12. top with cheese
13. reduce oven to 350f and bake another 20 minutes or so until hot and bubbly
14. serve with the toppings of your choice
demonstrations.review: My husband and I loved this. Really, really loved it!!! I did modify the seasoning for the ground beef, only because I didn't have any tomato sauce or chilies on hand, and it was still outstanding. I plan to experiment with this crust recipe and make an Italian-type dish with spaghetti sauce and mozzarella cheese. Thank you!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
german apple bread

this recipe came from a friend of my mothers nancy mckaig

1. heat oven to 325f
2. mix all ingredients in large bowl
3. grease and flour 2 loaf pans
4. divide dough between 2 pans
5. bake for 1 hour and 15 minute
demonstrations.review: I agree with Klyn that the batter was extremely thick and added a splash of milk to make it more manageable. I left out the raisins, but other than that followed the recipe exactly. This makes a wonderful dense, moist bread. I think it tastes better the next day. I will definately be making this one again. Thank you!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
just like loaded baked potatoes casserole

this is an awesome low-carb version of loaded baked potatoes, and tastes far better than any version of mock potatoes that i have tried. in fact, this dish is soooo good, you will not believe it!  i do not remember where i got this recipe, but it is a fabulous side to any low-carb meal. you will be pleased, i promise! yum! yum!

1. pre-heat oven to 350
2. chop cooked cauliflower into very small pieces
3. mix sour cream , 1 / 2 of the green onions , 1 / 2 of the cheese , 1 / 2 of the bacon , and salt and pepper to taste in medium bowl
4. stir in the cauliflower
5. place in medium baking dish and sprinkle remaining cheese and bacon on top
6. bake for 20 minutes
7. sprinkle the remaining green onions on top just before serving
demonstrations.review: I will definately make this dish again! I served it with steak and asparagus and both my hubby and I loved it. Thank you!

target.recipe_text:
best ever meatloaf

this is my family's favorite meatloaf. it is seasoned with tomato and onion and comes out very moist and flavorful. recipe is from campbell's kitchen.

1. mix thoroughly 1 / 2 cup tomato soup , beef , onion soup mix , bread crumbs and egg
2. shape firmly into 8x4 inch loaf baking pan
3. bake at 350f for 1 1 / 4 hour or until done
4. mix 2 t drippings , remaining tomato soup and water in saucepan
5. heat through
6. serve with meatloaf
target.review: This was delicious!! Very moist and tasty. Thanks Lainey!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
parmesan creamed corn au gratin

this is enough for 4 smaller servings, the recipe can easily be doubled. i have even made this using frozen peas, in place of corn, or mix 1/2 pound each corn and peas together!

1. butter oven-proof small serving dishes or one dish large enough to hold the corn mixture
2. in a heavy-bottomed saucepan combine the frozen corn , whipping cream , salt , sugar and white pepper
3. bring to a boil
4. boil for 5 minutes
5. in another saucepan melt butter
6. add in flour and whisk for 1 minute
7. add in the corn mixture
8. mix to combine , then add in about 2 tablespoons grated parmesan cheese
9. season with salt to taste
10. set oven to broil
11. place the corn in a casserole dish , or small oven-proof serving dishes and sprinkle with about 1 / 4 cup grated parmesan cheese
12. broil under heat until browned
demonstrations.review: Very good! I scaled back on the whipping cream due to other posts. I ended up using about 3/4 cup of the cream. This was a nice addition to our Christmas dinner. Thanks KittenCal!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
buffalo chicken wing dip

i first tried this buffalo chicken wing dip at my neighbor's picnic.  a friend of theirs brought it and we munched on it all night til it was gone!  i love this recipe for picnics, potlucks and tailgate parties.  it's a much less messy way of enjoying chicken wings.  my oldest son loves it.  you can make it as spicy hot as you want...or leave it mild.  it's best served warm, but you can also eat it cool.

1. preaheat oven top 350
2. in a large bowl , mix shredded chicken , celery and cheese
3. in a saucepan over med-low heat , combine cream cheese and salad dressing and stir until smooth
4. stir in bottle of hot sauce
5. pour heated mixture into bowl with chicken mixture
6. stir to mix well
7. pour into a 13" x 9" baking pan
8. bake uncovered for 40 minutes or until bubbly----make sure top doesn't get browned
9. let stand for 10 minutes
10. serve warm or cold-----tastes best warm--- with celery or other veggies and crackers
demonstrations.review: I used 1/2 bottle of Frank's Red Hot Buffalo Wing Sauce and bleu cheese dressing. I really liked the taste. The only drawback for me was the amount of oil that was on top the dish. I dabbed a paper towel over the top to absorb some of it. All in all it was good and I'll be making it again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pizza casserole   easy and kid pleasing

i have a hard time getting my toddler to eat meat. he gobbles this up! it's also low-cost and you can double the recipe and freeze one for another day.

1. heat oven to 350
2. cook noodles according to package directions
3. drain and reserve
4. meanwhile , cook ground beef , onion , and garlic over medium high heat for 6 minutes or until beef is no longer pink
5. drain off excess liquid
6. stir in oregano , salt , soup , 1 / 3 c water , and noodles
7. remove from heat and add half the cheese
8. spoon into 11x7 baking dish and sprinkle the remaining cheese over the top
9. bake for 25-30 minutes until bubbly
10. allow to cool for 5-10 minutes before serving
11. "
demonstrations.review:
I made this for a friend of mine-- a single mom of four who is going through Chemo for stage three breast cancer. I did not try it but her kids loved it and asked that I make this again. The only change I made was I substituted spaghetti sauce for tomato soup.

Thanks for a great, easy recipe~!

target.recipe_text:
custard with kiwi

a simple summer dessert. recipe source: shopper's magazine

1. in a saucepan combine 1 / 3 cup of the sugar and the cornstarch
2. stir in the milk and ook over medium heat , stirring constantly , until mixture thickens and comes to a boil
3. reduce heat to low
4. add egg yolks , one at a time , beating after each one
5. simmer for one more minute
6. remove from heat and add vanilla
7. cool custard and refrigerate until cold
8. to prepare meringue , in a saucepan , combine egg whites , remaining sugar , water and cream of tartar , beating with portable beaters or a whisk
9. cook over low heat until egg whites reach 160 degrees f but do not boil
10. pour into bowl of electric mixer and continue beating until softr peaks form
11. to serve: line dessert dishes with sliced kiwi , spoon custard over fruit and top with merinque
target.review: Deeeeelicious!!!  Two of my favorite things in one dessert glass, custard and meringue.  Farm-raised eggs lent a beautiful yellow color to the custard.  I substitued turbinado sugar for regular in the custard to give a more complex flavor.  We piled in the kiwis for a beautiful, sweet, dessert!!!  Could probably use any fresh fruit.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
gnocchi with sausage and spinach

from real simple.

1. cook the gnocchi according to the package directions , reserving 1 / 4 cup of the cooking liquid
2. meanwhile , heat the oil in a large skillet over medium heat
3. add the onion and cook until softened , about 5 minutes
4. add the sausage and cook , crumbling it with a spoon , until browned , 5 to 7 minutes
5. add the garlic , spinach , salt , and pepper and cook , tossing frequently , until the spinach wilts , about 3 minutes
6. add the drained gnocchi , the reserved cooking liquid , and the parmesan and toss
7. divide among individual bowls and sprinkle with additional parmesan
demonstrations.review: Delicious!!!  Gnocchi is a favorite in our family, and this was a nice new way to serve it.  I did cook the sausage separately prior to putting it in with the rest of the ingredients so it was not greasy.  Very satisfying!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mexicali chicken  slow cooker

very easy, yummy, and inexpensive.  found this in the, "simple 1-2-3 cookbook."  if you want to make the sauce thicker, you can blend 1 tablespoon cornstarch and 2 tablespoons water until smooth and stir into cooking liquid when the ketchup, cumin, and salt is added.  hope you guys enjoy this one!

1. put sliced peppers and onions in slow cooker and top with chicken
2. sprinkle chili powder and oregano over chicken and add salsa
3. cover and cook on low for 7 to 8 hours or on high for 2 to 3 hours
4. remove chicken from slow cooker and place in a serving bowl to keep warm
5. stir ketchup cumin , and salt into mixture in slow cooker
6. cook , uncovered , on high 15 minutes or until hot
7. pour mixture over top of noodles or rice
demonstrations.review: Wonderful flavor from the salsa (I used Pace Picante), chili, and oregano (had to sub Italian seasoning).  All of this bakes into the chicken, and is plate-lickin' good.  The ketchup and cumin made for a great sauce.  Served with brown rice and corn.  Ended up mixing sauce, rice and corn together for a fabulous "spanish rice".  Can't wait for leftovers tomorrow!!!:)  Made for ZWT5 Zingo!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
shortcake

i got this recipe from the wife of a co-worker.  it's a very simple cake, buttery & not too sweet -- perfect with seasonal fruit & whipped topping or ice cream.

1. preheat oven to 325 degrees
2. grease a 9x9 dish & set aside
3. in a large bowl , cut flour , sugar & butter together until mixture resembles coarse crumbs
4. set aside 1 / 2 cup of this mixture
5. to the remaining butter mixture , add the rest of the ingredients & mix well
6. pour into prepared dish & sprinkle topping over
7. bake 30-40 minutes or until toothpick inserted in center comes out clean
demonstrations.review: This is so good!!!  I used a little extra vanilla.  It is sweet, and the crumb top makes this one a winner with berries in my book!!!

target.recipe_text:
tiny cinnamon rolls

southern living. my kids adore these tiny little treats. we have fun making them together.

1. unroll dough , and separate into 4 rectangles
2. pinch seams together
3. stir together sugar and cinnamon
4. sprinkle evenly over rectangles
5. roll up jellyroll fashion , starting with a long side
6. press edges to seal
7. cut each log into 5 slices and place slices , cut side down in a lightly greased 8-inch round cakepan
8. bake at 350 degrees for 12 minutes
9. stir together powdered sugar , milk , and vanilla in a small bowl until smooth
10. drizzle over warm rolls
target.review: What a yummy simple little treat!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
raspberry shortbread cookies

melt in your mouth.

1. in a mixing bowl , cream butter and sugar
2. beat in extract
3. gradually add flour until dough forms a ball
4. cover and refrigerate for 1 hour or until easy to handle
5. roll into 1 inch balls
6. place 1 inch apart on ungreased baking sheets
7. using the end of a wooden spoon handle , make an indentation in the center
8. fill with jam
9. bake at 350 degrees for 14-18 minutes or until edges are lightly browned
10. remove to wire racks to cool
11. spoon additional into cookies if desired
12. combine glaze ingredients and drizzle over cookies
demonstrations.review: These are wonderful cookies.  They melt inyour mouth.  I will be including them in my holiday tray.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
sourdough  bread starter

this is your basic sour dough bread starter to be used over and over again. look for the sour dough bread recipe to make use of this starter.
there are two ways to make sour dough starter one without yeast where you feed the starter daily and this recipe where you just let the yeast do the work and  let it sit for 3 or 4 days. be sure that you clean the jar well before putting the saved starter back in it.

1. dissolve yeast in 1 / 2 cup warm water , rest for ten minutes
2. mix in flour , sugar& remaining water
3. allow to stand , loosely covered , in a warm place for 3 or 4 days
4. use a large bowl as it will rise considerably
5. every time the batter is used to make a product set aside 1 cup to be used as a"starter" for another batch
6. keep covered in the fridge
7. to make it into a basic batter again , add another 2 cups flour& 2 cups warm water and allow to stand at room temp overnight it is now ready to use , but again reserve a cup of the starter
demonstrations.review: This is a great recipe for sourdough starter.  I keep a cup in my fridge and make it into sourdough bread whenever we want some.  It makes great bread!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cinnamon swirl quick bread

this rich quick bread is a favorite with my family. i often give my husband a few slices to take with him on his commute to work, along with a tall travel mug of coffee.

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. in a large mixing bowl , beat together butter , 1 cup sugar , and egg
3. combine the flour , baking powder , baking soda , and salt
4. add the flour mixture to the egg mixture alternately with the buttermilk
5. in a small bowl , combine the cinnamon and remaining 1 / 3 cup sugar
6. pour a third of the batter into a greased 8x4x2-inch loaf pan
7. sprinkle a third of the cinnamon sugar on top of batter
8. repeat layers twice
9. bake for 45-50 minutes , until a toothpick inserted near the center comes out clean
10. cool in pan for 10 minutes
11. remove from pan to a wire rack to cool completely
demonstrations.review: I just made this as an after school snack for my kids.  I made it into 12 muffins.  They were delicious!  The kids loved them and so did I.

target.recipe_text:
yes  virginia there is a great meatloaf

absolutely delicious meatloaf and sauce! those who claim they don't believe there can be such a thing as a great meatloaf will love this. based on a meatloaf given to me by a dear friend, virginia strehl, memphis, and leesburg, fla. nita holleman, 2000

1. meatloaf: combine meat loaf ingredients and place into a loaf baking dish
2. smooth out top
3. sauce: combine sauce ingredients and pour on top and sides of meatloaf
4. bake at 350f about 1 hour to 1 hour 15 minutes or until done
5. enjoy !
6. the addition of 1 or 2 teaspoons of kitchen bouquet makes this recipe very good
7. recipe should be"plump" from the addition of the milk or half & half
8. it should not be runny
9. a second batch of sauce served hot is good to serve with the meatloaf
10. nita's
11. it is wise to have some fat added to the deer -- especially to ground deer
12. maybe 25 % fat , , otherwise your results will be poor
13. i don't know about some of the other game meat some are using
14. please consult an expert
15. the recipe is delicious as it stands ! enjoy ! nita holleman
target.review: Best tomato-based meatloaf ever!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pork chops yum yum

i copied this from the orlando sentinel months ago and just now found it. we eat pork chops at least once a week and this is our favorite.

1. brown chops on both sides
2. place in greased casserole dish
3. mix all remaining ingredients and pour over pork chops
4. bake , uncovered , at 350 for one hour
demonstrations.review: This was NOT tasty.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
awesome golden oven fried chicken

you will swear that this is fried chicken. it is the best oven fried i have ever tasted.

1. wash chicken and soak in salt water for about 20 minutes
2. i use a large bowl and 1 teaspoon of salt
3. preheat oven to 425
4. place oil and butter in a shallow baking pan and set in the oven to heat and melt
5. combine the flour and seasonings and dredge the chicken in the flour mixture
6. remove hot pan from the oven and arrange the chicken in the pan skin side down , but do not crowd
7. place in the oven and bake for 30 minutes , turn chicken so that the skin side is up and continue baking for 20 to 30 minutes more , until nicely browned and juices run clear
8. remove onto a platter and let cool at least 10 minutes
demonstrations.review: Great recipe and technique

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pepsi pork roast

this recipe sounds strange and tastes wonderful. we have experimented with other brands of soda, but none worked as well. you can also cook potatoes and carrots with the roast for a complete meal.

1. place roast in crock pot
2. mix soup mix with soup
3. add cola to soup mixture and pour over roast
4. cook on high for 4-5 hours
5. when done , remove roast and thicken juices with cornstarch for wonderful gravy
demonstrations.review: This is the simplest, most tasty recipe on this site! Love, love, love it. Crowd pleaser for sure!

target.recipe_text:
crock pot chicken w  blue cheese and mustard sauce

a friend gave me this recipe to use with any type of poultry. i have used it with partridge, pheasant and even rabbit! yummy!

1. rinse chicken and pat dry
2. then arrange , overlapping pieces slightly , in a 4 qt or larger electric slow cooker
3. sprinkle with pepper , thyme , and savory
4. insert bay leaf between two chicken pieces
5. mix mustard and wine
6. pour over chicken
7. cover and cook at low setting until meat in thickest part is very tender when pierced
8. carefully lift chicken to warm serving dish
9. keep warm
10. mix cornstarch and cream
11. blend into cooking liquid
12. increase cooker heat setting to high
13. cover and cook , stirring 2 or 3 time , until sauce is thickened
14. add 1 / 4 cup of the cheese , cover , and let stand for 3 to 5 minutes
15. stir until cheese is melted
16. pour sauce over chicken
17. sprinkle with remaining 1 / 4 cup of cheese
target.review: I substituted half and half for the whipping cream, and used skinless chicken thighs. I could not get the sauce to thicken in my crockpot, so I placed the sauce in a micrwavable dish and nuked it for 45 seconds. It turned out beautifully. I shall make this dish again and again as my wife and mother both raved about the unusual flavor of the blue cheese sauce.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crock pot potato soup

this is a very tasty potato soup recipe adapted from one that appeared in midwest living.

1. stir together the potatoes , onion and bacon in the crock pot
2. in a large mixing bowl , combine the cream cheese , chicken broth , cream of chicken soup , water , milk and pepper
3. add the mixture to the crock
4. cook on low for 8 to 10 hours or on high for 4 to 5 hours
5. before serving , put some of the mixture into the blender , and mix back in to thicken the soup
demonstrations.review: I followed the directions except for the following: I did not have any bacon, so I used artificial bacon bits. This was a very good substitute. I pureed some of the potatoes in the crockpot using a hand blender. This thickened the soup to a suitable level, without having to add corn starch to thicken it. My wife and I enjoyed the soup, which I cooked on high for 5 1/2 hours. The potato chunks were too big, so I had to cut many of them in 1/2. I recommend that \

demonstrations.recipe_text:
parmesan chicken  crock pot

long time family favourite.

1. mix together dry soup mix , cream soups , milk and rice in medium bowl
2. lay chicken breasts in the bottom of lightly greased crock pot
3. place 1 tbsp butter on each breast and pour soup mixture over all
4. season with salt and pepper and sprinkle with parmesan cheese
5. cook on low for 8 to 10 hours , or on high for 4 to 6 hours
demonstrations.review: This made for a good meal; easy to make and tasty. I would not add the salt due to the fact that the onion soup mix is very salty by itself. You could go on a sodium high!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
israeli simmered vegetables over spiced couscous

this is a recipezaar 2005 adoptee.  it sounded like an easy vegetarian dinner that my whole family would like.  the original stated that this recipe came from "the vegetarian gourmet's easy low-fat favorites".

1. put cabbage wedges in a large soup pot
2. put carrots , zucchini , onions , potatoes and chickpeas on top
3. pour broth on top , and add garlic powder , salt and pepper
4. bring to a boil
5. reduce heat , cover , and simmer 30 minutes , or until vegetables are tender
6. when vegetables are almost ready , bring water to boil in a small saucepan
7. stir in couscous , cinnamon and cumin
8. cover and remove from heat
9. let stand for 5 minutes
10. fluff with a fork
11. place a mound of couscous in the centre of each soup bowl
12. arrange vegetables and chickpeas around couscous
13. spoon broth on top
14. sprinkle with salt and freshly ground black pepper
demonstrations.review: Loved this dish. It made a great change to eat a purely vegan dinner. However, next time, I would reduce the cinnamon to 1/8 tsp. as not everyone is a fan of cinnamon in a main dish.

target.recipe_text:
hamburger helper soup

ok - go ahead and laugh! this comforting soup is well received in times of sadness or trouble. i keep the ingredients in the pantry for just those times, i kid you not!!!

1. brown ground beef and onion in dutch oven until beef is no longer pink- drain
2. stir in cheese sauce mix from hamburger helper package
3. stir in water , basil , salt , pepper& tomatoes , and heat to boiling , stirring constantly
4. reduce heat , cover& simmer 10 minutes
5. stir in macaroni from the hamburger helper package , add veg-all , cover& simmer until pasta is tender , about 15 minutes
6. stir in parsely& serve
target.review: The soup base is a little bland - I might add some beef stock or chicken stock in place of some of the water. I used a can of mild Ro-Tel instead of the plain tomatoes, as another poster suggested, but it's still bland.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
new england pork and applesauce

with apples and applesauce plus several other nice but simple ingredients,using a pork loin.from a cookbook of new england recipes.

1. in large dutch oven over med-high heat combine pork , applesauce , cinnamon , nutmeg , and cloves
2. cover tightly and cook 15 minutes , then reduce heat and simmer about 6 hours
3. about 1 1 / 2 hours before serving , add the potatoes , carrots , celery , and onions
4. fifteen minutes before it is done , add the apple slices
demonstrations.review: Very tasty! I reduced the cloves to 1/2 tsp (though it would have been fine at the full amount), grated in about half a nutmeg kernel, and added about 3/4 tsp ground ginger and 1/2 cup dried cranberries. I put it in the crockpot on low for 6 hours, then added the vegetables for another 2 hours, adding the apple in the last 10 minutes. Easy and delicious.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
brussels sprouts with candied walnuts and green apple

i love brussels sprouts! i hope you enjoy this one!  recipe courtesy mile end restaurant on the  show: unique eats, episode: sandwiches.

1. to candy the walnuts:
2. toast the nuts in a saute pan over medium heat with 1 tablespoon butter and 1 teaspoon salt
3. when the nuts start to take on a light golden color , add the rosemary and saute for 1 more minute
4. add the honey to the pan and remove from the heat
5. to roast the brussels sprouts:
6. preheat the oven to 450 degrees f
7. toss the brussels sprouts with the canola oil , 1 teaspoon salt and pinch freshly ground black pepper
8. lay out onto a sheet tray and roast for 10 to 12 minutes until they take color , but retain some texture
9. remove from oven and set aside
10. to finish the dish:
11. saute the granny smith apple pieces in 1 tablespoon butter until they just take on color , about 2 minutes
12. add the candied walnuts and roasted brussels sprouts
13. toss , and then add the juice of 1 lemon and adjust the seasoning as necessary
demonstrations.review: The honey didn't really get hot enough to "candy" the walnuts; it mostly dripped off into the bowl. I used thyme instead of rosemary. It was delicious.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s light as a feather matzo balls

these are the *best* and fluffiest matzo balls on the planet, matzo meal can be found in the jewish or deli section of any major super market chain or in a deli store, store any leftover matzo meal in the fridge or freezer ---these really expand when simmering in the broth so make sure that you have lots of broth in the pot before adding them in :)

1. in a medium-size bowl , whisk eggs and oil together with a small whisk or fork until well blended
2. in a medium bowl combine the matzo meal , baking powder salt , garlic powder and black pepper
3. add in the egg / oil mixture
4. mix lightly until combined
5. refrigerate for 1 hour
6. using lightly greased hands shape the mixture into 1-inch round balls
7. drop the balls into a large pot of simmering chicken broth
8. cover and reduce heat to low
9. simmer for 30 minutes or until soft and tender
demonstrations.review: The baking powder gave them an off, metallic flavor. They were huge and pillowy, but not tasty. (To other reviewers: matzo balls can be frozen, but will often be dry and mealy when reheated.)

target.recipe_text:
italian peasant soup

i found this in toh quick cooking magazine. i haven't tried it yet but it looks like something my family and i would love. plan on trying it soon.

1. in a large pot , cook sausage over medium heat until browned and no longer pink
2. drain
3. add onions and garlic
4. saute until tender
5. add chicken
6. saute and stir until no longer pink
7. add in the beans , broth , tomatoes , basil , and oregano
8. stir to mix
9. cook uncovered , for 10 minutes
10. add the spinach and heat just until wilted
11. serve with parmesan cheese sprinkled on top
target.review: Delicious! My husband says it's the best soup he's ever had.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chicken scaloppine with lemon glaze   low fat and delicious

this is a wonderful lower-fat restaurant-quality dish that is easy to make, i also like to add in a few tablespoons of capers and cook with the lemon glaze if you are a lover of capers then add them in as it really adds to the flavour of this dish ---  this lemon sauce is not a heavy creamy sauce which is what makes this dish lower in fat, it is more like a glaze that soaks into the chicken, and i would strongly suggest to double or even triple the glaze i most always do, and please be certain to use only dry breadcrumbs as fresh will not stick to the chicken as well --- this is *very* good!

1. in a small bowl or shallow dish whisk together mustard and eggs
2. set aside
3. combine the dry bread crumbs with poultry seasoning , garlic powder and seasoning salt
4. spread on a piece of waxed paper
5. dip the breasts firstly in egg / mustard mixture then coat well with the crumb mixture , pressing downs with hands to adhear the crumbs to the breast
6. heat the olive oil in a skillet over medium heat
7. add in the chicken and cook for about 5 minutes on each side , or until it is no longer pink inside
8. remove and transfer to a plate to keep warm
9. for the glaze
10. in the same skillet add in the broth , lemon juice and 1 / 4 teaspoon salt bring to a boil scraping any brown bits from the pan
11. add in lemon slices and parsley
12. mix to combine for about 1 minute
13. spoon the glaze / sauce over chicken
14. delicious !
demonstrations.review: So delicious! My family loved this (all of them - picky ones included!). Used panko as suggested and should definitely have made extra lemon sauce. We'll be having this again!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
steak  or chicken  fajitas

these are so quick and tasty. you can use strips of boneless chicken breast instead of the beef. feel free to double the marinade. the flavor is so great for such a short marination time. you can can do them up ahead of time and have the meat sit longer if you wish.

1. slice steak into thin strips
2. in bowl , mix together 1 tablespoons olive oil , lime juice , garlic , chili powder , cumin , hot pepper flakes , black pepper & salt
3. add beef strips and stir to coat , set aside
4. wrap tortillas in foil and place in 350 oven for 5-10 minutes or until heated through
5. cut onions in half lengthwise and slice into strips , cut your peppers into strips
6. in large non stick skillet over medium high heat , heat remaining tablespoons of olive oil
7. add onions & peppers stirring for 3-4 minutes , until softened
8. transfer to a bowl and set aside
9. add beef to skillet , cook , stirring for 3-4 minutes or until they lose their red color
10. return onions and peppers to skillet
11. stir for about one minute
12. to serve , spoon a portion of the beef mixture down the centre of each tortilla , top with your desired toppings , fold bottom of tortilla up over filling , fold the sides in , overlapping
demonstrations.review: So delicious! Thanks for a great recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s chocolate frosting icing

a wonderful frosting i have used for years made in very little time with perfect results and 100% better than any canned, this frosting is so good you will find yourself eating a fair amount of it before even using it to frost with! --- choose the amount of cocoa powder you desire for either a light, medium or dark frosting, and make certain to sift the cocoa powder and the confectioners sugar before using for the recipe--- this frosting *freezes* very well so double the recipe and freeze one batch for next time --- *note* for an ultra creamy fluffy milk chocolate frosting add in 1 to 1-1/2 cups thawed cool whip topping at the end of mixing the frosting and beat on low speed until blended ------- also see my recipe#80118 ---- recipe#282040 --- recipe#90142

1. cream the butter in a small bowl
2. blend in the cocoa powder , vanilla , confectioners sugar , alternately with the cream
3. beat with an electric mixer , until the desired texture is achieved
demonstrations.review: Delicious and so easy!

target.recipe_text:
spicy potato soup

my husband loves spicy food, and the hotter the better. this is a soup we can both enjoy without being too hot.

1. in a dutch oven or large kettle , brown ground beef
2. drain
3. add potatoes , onion and tomato sauce
4. stir in water , salt , pepper , and hot pepper sauce
5. bring to a boil
6. reduce heat and simmer for 1 hour or until potatoes are tender and the soup has thickened
target.review: This is good. Easy winter recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pork roast over sweet potatoes for the crock pot

my husband always requests this recipe. i cook it 11 hours so the meat barely holds together. works for low glycemic index diets.

1. combine first 6 ingredients
2. rub into pork
3. put potatoes in the crock pot
4. place pork on top of potatoes
5. pour broth over all
6. cover and cook on low for 8 to 10 hours
demonstrations.review: Made the recipe "as is" and it is incredible! Don't forget the fennel seeds, it MAKES the recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cabbage with apples

this dish makes cabbage tempting even for the little kids! this recipe was in my amc cookbook and looks so good, i'm going to have to make it real soon:)

1. rinse the cabbage , apples and onion well
2. place in a saucepan
3. sprinkle with sugar and season lightly
4. cover and cook on low flame for 25 minutes , stirring occasionally
5. mix well before serving
demonstrations.review: This is a really easy, super yummy recipe. Left out the onion because we dont eat them. A+++

demonstrations.recipe_text:
corn and  broccoli bake

#1 requested veggie side dish recipe.

1. combine cracker crumbs and butter , and reserve 1 / 2 cup for topping
2. in bowl , combine broccoli , both cans of corns and remaining crumbs
3. transfer to a greased 2 quart baking dish
4. top with remaining crumb mixture
5. bake , uncovered@ 375 degrees for 25-30 minutes or until lightly browned
demonstrations.review: This was pretty good, my family like it. I wonder if you could add a "cream of" soup to the recipe. I think I will try that next time.

target.recipe_text:
amazing cream cheese spread

use this spread on your bagels, toast, or whatever else you have that requires cream cheese!  stuff your chicken breasts with this!  use this spread for cream cheese roll ups, chicken/crescent packets... use your imagination and use this spread!  :)  obviously double or halve this recipe for the amount of cream cheese you need.  store it in a tupperware or bowl with a lid in the fridge for later use. ** note: i recently added a tablespoon or two of chopped fresh mint leaves to the mix and it was really good!  i'm sure you could experiment with other herbs as well, but this mix is divine.

1. place cream cheese into a bowl
2. let soften for a few minutes
3. add jalapeno , green onions , cilantro , salt , pepper , and stir until completely mixed through
4. refrigerate for 30 minutes or more , and then spread on your favorite bagel , toast , etc
5. store with tight fitting lid in fridge
target.review: Excellent! Thank you! UPDATE: I took your advice on the fresh mint and I think it is ESSENTIAL - I absolutely love the mint in this, and I'm not necessarily a mint worshipper.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
red bell pepper soup

this one doesn't use roasted capsicums, but it is delicious.   i make it every year and freeze it.  i have made it with red, yellow and orange capsicums, they all have a slightly different taste.  all good.

1. melt the butter in a saucepan over medium heat
2. add the bell peppers and onion
3. cook , stirring occasionally , until the onion is soft but not browned
4. mix in the cumin and cayenne
5. add the chicken broth
6. bring to a boil
7. cover
8. reduce heat
9. simmer for 20 minutes
10. scoop out the vegetables
11. transfer the vegetables to a blender or food processor
12. add a little broth
13. process until smooth
14. return the puree to the broth in the pan
15. mix in the lemon juice
16. adjust seasoning
17. reheat to serving temperature
18. serve hot
19. cheers doreen doreen randal , wanganui
20. new zealand
demonstrations.review: This was WONDERFUL. I only had 2 red peppers so I subbed 2 large carrots as well, used half the butter and sprayed the veggies down with olive oil spray instead to make it lighter. It was very nice and light, a lot lighter than I was expecting, but that was a nice surprise. I added some brown rice and black beans to it to make a simple soup meal for my preteen son. He ate the whole bowl and asked for seconds!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
spinach   dill salad

a nice fresh, light spinach salad with a touch of dill. i formulated this recipe years ago as i grow some very tasty spinach and dill weed.

1. wash spinach in cold water
2. remove coarse stems and discard
3. dry spinach on paper towelling
4. chop into bite size pieces and place into a large mixing bowl
5. in a small bowl , combine olive oil , lemon juice , salt , sugar and pepper , mix well to blend
6. add seeded chopped cucumber to dressing and mix
7. pour dressing over spinach and toss to coat
8. add chopped fresh dill and toss to mix
9. serve immediately
10. if desired , add 1 / 4 teaspoon of dry mustard when mixing dressing
demonstrations.review: This was pretty tasty, a little bland but still very good. I used agave nectar instead of sugar (it's a staple in my house) and added the mustard powder. We added some radishes and sliced almonds as well. Thanks for sharing!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
smashed fingerling potatoes

a great side dish to any meal, these unusually prepared potatoes are an attention-getter and taste divine!  spark them up even further with another herb of your choice.  prep/cook times are approximate. note: some of the photos posted are of baby yukon potatoes (i think!) which are very similar in taste, texture and color to fingerlings.

1. wash / scrub the fingerling potatoes and boil , unpeeled , for 12 minutes
2. drain and let cool
3. take each fingerling between your hands and squash it between your palms
4. the idea is to beak the skin and flatten the potato , but not to crush it completely
5. it should still stay intact as much as possible
6. heat a skillet with to 1 of oil on high heat
7. when the oil is hot , about 350f , deep-fry each fingerling , turning them over midway when each side is browned
8. drain on paper towels
9. in another pan , melt butter and add minced garlic and parsley
10. stir briefly over medium heat to release flavors , then toss fingerling potatoes into this mixture
demonstrations.review: These were so, so good. Everyone enjoyed them immensely. Simple, easy and tasty - thanks!

target.recipe_text:
mary s zucchini bread

this is my mother-in-law's favorite recipe and for very good reason!  this recipe makes two very moist and flavorful loaves.  i hope you will enjoy it!

1. place eggs , oil , zucchini and vanilla extract in blender and puree
2. sift together sugar , flour , baking soda , salt and baking powder and cinnamon
3. pour liquid ingredients into dry and mix
4. add nuts
5. divide batter into two loaf pans
6. bake at 325f degrees for 1 hour
target.review: we really liked the zucchini bread recipe, so very moist. thank You

demonstrations.recipe_text:
roasted brussels sprouts

i got this from the barefoot contessa cookbook. so good.

1. preheat oven to 400f
2. cut off the ends of the brussels sprouts and pull off any yellow outer leaves
3. mix them in a bowl with the olive oil , salt , and lemon-pepper seasoning
4. transfer them to a sheet pan and roast for 35 to 40 minutes , until crisp outside and tender inside
5. shake the pan from time to time to brown the brussels sprouts evenly
6. sprinkle with more kosher salt , if you like , and serve hot
demonstrations.review: This is how I fix my brussel sprouts except I cut mine in half even Brussel sprout haters love them....thanks for sharing

demonstrations.recipe_text:
sam s chicken casserole

this is an old recipe that i got from my mother inlaw many years ago, it is fast and easy and very tasty. i hope you like it as much as we do.

1. grease a casserole
2. put a layer of rice in the bottom
3. lay the chicken pieces over the rice
4. mix the boiling water and mushroom soup
5. pour mushroom mixture over chicken
6. shake dry onion soup mix over top of chicken
7. sprinkle a little garlic and parsley over all
8. place in pre heated oven at 325 degrees farenheit for 11 / 2 hours
9. (the original recipe stated that you were not to cover , but i cover it with tin foil for the first hour and remove it for the last 1 / 2 hr as it makes the rice more moist which is how we prefer it
demonstrations.review: I love this recipe also, thanks for reminding us  of such a great casserole,,, I am making it tommow.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
patti labelle s macaroni and cheese

got this off of the "good morning america" website after i saw her cook this on the show. this is the best macaroni and cheese i have ever tasted!!

1. preheat oven to 350
2. lightly butter a deep 2 1 / 2 quart baking dish
3. fill a large pot with water and bring to a rapid boil
4. add macaroni and the 1 tb oil
5. cook for 7 minutes , or until somewhat tender
6. drain well , and return to the pot
7. meanwhile , in a small saucepan , melt 8 tb of the butter
8. stir into macaroni
9. in a large bowl , combine all of the shredded cheeses
10. to the macaroni , add 1 1 / 2 cups of shredded cheeses , half and half , the cubed cheese and the eggs , and the seasoned salt and pepper
11. transfer to the prepared casserole dish , and top with remaining 1 / 2 cup shredded cheese
12. dot with remaining 1 tb of the butter
13. bake for 30-35 minutes or until the edges are golden brown and bubbly
14. serve hot
15. serves 8
demonstrations.review: I made this Sunday for the family as we get together first Sunday of every month and this was a great hit ,everyone loved it. thank you for sharing !!!!!!

target.recipe_text:
strawberry jam  pectin added

this recipes is from the ball blue book.  the only thing i did differently is to add lemon zest.  it's really refreshing, because the lemon zest/juice keeps it from being overly sweet.  this is one of my favorite jams that i make each year.

1. wash strawberries
2. drain
3. remove stems
4. crush strawberries on layer at a time
5. combine strawberries , powdered pectin , lemon juice , and lemon zest in a large saucepot
6. bring to a boil , stirring occasionally
7. add sugar , stirring until dissolved
8. return to a rolling boil
9. boil hard 1 minute , stirring constantly
10. remove from heat , and skim foam if necessary
11. ladle into hot , sterilized jars , leaving 1 / 4 inch head space
12. adjust 2-piece caps
13. process 10 minutes in a boiling water canner
target.review: Wonderful Strawberry Jam! I followed this recipe out of my box of pectin, so I didn't add the lemon juice or lemon zest! This is a very easy recipe to follow, my 11 year old DS even made some for fair! He didn't like the chunks of strawberries so big, so I decided to use my food processor! He liked the way it came out but I felt that the pieces were to small. So maybe when I make this again I will just cut up all the strawberries and see how that turns out! This recipe is as easy as canning can get! We love the homemade taste of jams so I will be making this recipe again. When Strawberry season comes again. Thanks for posing this wonderful recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
simple and inexpensive spaghetti

so easy and cheap, not to mention tasty!

1. cook pasta according to package directions
2. meanwhile , warm chopped tomatoes in microwave
3. drain pasta and return to pot
4. add butter and cheese , stirring until melted
5. add warmed tomatoes and stir well
6. leftovers can be placed in casserole dish and baked at 350 until warmed through
demonstrations.review: This is very easy to put together and a tasty meal.  When I make this again I will be adding spices. I felt it needed something to spice it up a little!! Maybe a little garlic powder as Parsley suggested. But I wanted to make the recipe as stated first before I started adding ingredients.  I will be putting the leftovers in a casserole dish and reheating for DH. Thanks for posting this easy ricipe!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
jam sweethearts

cute for valentine's day, but good enough for every day!

1. beat butter & sugar together in a bowl
2. add yolk and vanilla and beat the mixture until smooth
3. add flour and salt and mix everything to form a smooth dough
4. wrap in plastic wrap and refrigerate for 30 minutes
5. preheat oven to 350f
6. roll out dough to 1 / 4 inch thickness
7. cut out with 1 1 / 2-2in circle cookie cutters
8. arrange cookies on baking sheet
9. cut hearts from half of the cookies with 1in heart cutters
10. bake for 12 minutes
11. cool completely
12. make frostingby beating butter until smooth , then gradually adding icing sugar , water and vanilla
13. spread frosting over whole cookies
14. drop a small spoonful of jam on top of frosting
15. press heart cookies on top of whole cookies
demonstrations.review: This is a delicious cookie!! It was very easy to mix together. My only problem was rolling it out. It cracked on me like it was to dried out. But the taste make up for that. I made a whole batch of the cookies then only rolled out half of the dough and baked them. I put the other half back it the fridge to see if I could figure out how to roll it better without cracking. The frosting and jam (I used strawberry) make it a very pretty cookie especially for Valentine's Day!! Great recipe!! I will be making these again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
really easy broccoli soup

this comes from the company's coming soup and sandwich cookbook by jean pare.
