it's so quick and easy to make after a long day at work.

1. cook broccoli in water until tender
2. do not drain
3. add remaining ingredients except cheese and simmer for 3 or 4 minutes
4. run through blender until you have desired consistency
5. stir in cheese if using
6. for vegetarian do not use cream of chicken
demonstrations.review: This is delicious soup! Very easy to put together, I just love it. I did add more cheese than the recipe calls for but that was by choice. I put the soup in the blender and just lightly chopped because I wanted somewhat bigger pieces of broccoli. But you have the choice that the best part of this soup. I will be making this many, many more time. It's a snap to make and taste really good. Thanks for posting this recipe!

target.recipe_text:
quiche   master recipe

master recipe for quiche.

1. preheat oven to 375
2. fill parbaked shells and bake until set
3. any filling you wish to use
4. serve warm or at room temperature
target.review: Perfect. We enjoyed this three different ways on Christmas morning!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
awesome bacon tomato dip

oh, you have to try this one!! my family loves dips and spreads, and even the guys got really into this one. i even caught my uncle (who thinks guys are too "macho" for dips), eating it straight from the bowl with a spoon!! best when made day of, and lettuce added just before serving. it gets soggy:(

1. in medium bowl , with mixer , blend sour cream , mayonnaise , cream cheese , cheddar cheese , chopped onion and green pepper , garlic powder , and black pepper
2. crumble bacon into small pieces and add to mixture
3. add chopped tomato and stir well
4. garnish with shredded lettuce just before serving , if desired
5. serve with townhouse crackers or wheat thins
6. also good served in a bread bowl with bread cubes to dip
demonstrations.review: Today was my second time for taking this dip to a gathering. This one was at the bowling alley for Christmas. Both times I gave what was left away, thrilling the recipient. It's great!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
braised pork with beer   juniper berries

this recipe is posted by request i have not tried it but it sounds good!  be aware that juniper berries are the flavoring used in gin - the taste may not appeal to everyone

1. brown the roast on all sides in a dutch oven in the heated olive oil , as you turn the roast season with salt& pepper
2. drain off any fat
3. sprinkle the veggies with the flour
4. add the veggies to the pot and the bay leaf
5. add the beer
6. bring to a boil
7. add cloves , thyme& juniper berries
8. cook covered for apprx 1 1 / 4 hours or until the meat is tender and apprx 160f in the center of the roast
9. remove the roast from the pot
10. skim off any fat
11. puree the sauce
12. slice the roast& serve with the onion sauce
demonstrations.review: Scrumptous! and, I used canned - repeat - canned veggies. I'll bet it would out of this world with fresh stuff. Thanks, Bergy!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cracker barrel green beans

this is the only way i can eat canned green beans!

1. in a 2-quart saucepan over medium heat , cook bacon until lightly brown but not crisp
2. when bacon has browned , add green beans
3. add salt , sugar and pepper and mix well
4. place onion on top of green beans
5. cover saucepan with a lid and bring to a light boil
6. turn heat down to low and simmer beans for 45 minutes
demonstrations.review:
Good, good, good! I used minced onion because I just cook for two and it was excellent.

jahoody

target.recipe_text:
chili cheddar biscuits

an outstanding biscuit recipe that is especially good with tex-mex inspired meals like chili con carne or a spicy beef stew. or, just split and stuff with scrambled egg and ham or bacon and you've got a mean breakfast!

1. make biscuits: into a bowl , sift together flour , baking powder , baking soda and the salt
2. add the butter and blend the mixture until it resembles coarse meal
3. stir in the cheddar and the chilies
4. add the sour cream and stir the mixture until it just forms a soft , but not sticky , dough
5. knead the dough gently for 20 seconds on a lightly-floured surface
6. roll or pat it out inch thick and with a 3 inch cookie cutter , cut out 8 rounds
7. bake on an ungreased baking sheet in the middle of a preheated 430f oven for 15-17 minutes , or until they are golden
target.review: Very good biscuits.  Loved the Jalapenos in them.  I will be making these again.  Thanks for the great recipe. Shawna

demonstrations.recipe_text:
broccoli with lemon almond butter

a quick and oh so tasty use for broccoli. yumm.

1. steam or boil broccoli until tender , approximately 4 to 8 minutes
2. drain
3. in a small saucepan , melt butter over medium low heat , remove from heat
4. stir in lemon juice
5. lemon zest , and almonds
6. pour over hot broccoli , and serve
demonstrations.review: This was good.  My kids prefers it with no lemon but I did enjoy it.  Thanks Shawna

demonstrations.recipe_text:
sugar cookie icing

this recipe is quick, easy, dries hard and shiny and tastes good too. i originally got if from allrecipes.

1. stir the powdered sugar and the milk until smooth
2. beat in corn syrup and vanilla until icing is smooth and glossy
3. if it's too thick , add more corn syrup
4. divide icing into separate bowls and stir in food coloring as desired
5. you can dip the cookies , paint them with a paint brush or spread them using a knife or the back of a spoon
demonstrations.review: I loved the shine to the cookies.  This icing set really fast which was great I was making soccer balls for my daughthers' team and doing to different colors.  I will be using this recipe lots. Next week for sure for my sons' soccer team.  Thanks.  My kids loved the taste also.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
jalapeno burger buns

this recipe started out as kelly canfield's jalapeno bread and through evolution a couple of trys, with a few changed ingredients ended up as burger buns. if you love a good burger with a bun that compliments it try these. if you like smaller burgers just make more buns out of this same recipe,

1. allow the frozen dough to rise overnight in the fridge
2. knead in your mixer for 5 minutes
3. add all the ingredients to the dough and knead for a further 10 minutes
4. cut into 14 equal pieces
5. the dough is a bit moist from all the ingredients in it so you may want to use a little flour on your hands to form the buns- do not use too much flour or the buns will not rise as easily place buns on a baking sheet that has been sprayed with veggie oil
6. for best results bake the buns on a baking stone , covered with a piece of parchment and lightly sprayed with veggie oil cover and place in a warm spot until the buns have doubled in size
7. this step may take 1-2 hours dependinbg on your dough
8. bake in 350f oven for apprx 20-25 minutes
9. place on a rack to cool
10. they freeze well
demonstrations.review: I made these buns last night to go with Devious Diners Devilishly Delicious Southwest Burger#232118 and they were so good together.  My littles could not wait for the buns to get done.  They ate them without the burger but was running for water into half the bun. They loved them at first but when the spicy hit them they did not.  But as for me they had an excellent flavor not to hot just right.  I used my own recipe for dinner rolls.  This is something I plan on making again. Thanks for the great buns!!!

target.recipe_text:
citrus marinated pork chops  oamc

adapted from "prevention's freezer cookbook" by s. sanders. can be made without freezing first, just be sure to marinate chops at least 6 hours before cooking for best flavour.

1. combine ingredients in a large ziploc freezer bag
2. remove as much air as possible
3. label and freeze
4. defrost overnight in the fridge
5. pork will marinate as it defrosts
6. to serve , remove chops from bag and place in a non-stick skillet
7. reserve marinade
8. cook for 5 minutes , or until brown , repeat for other side
9. add marinade , and reduce heat to medium
10. cover and cook for 7 minutes , or until chops are no longer pink in the middle
11. transfer pork to a plate and cover
12. turn heat to high and whisk for 3-5 minutes until sauce is thick
13. spoon over pork
14. pork chops can also be made on the bbq / grill if desired
target.review: These are very tasty, especially when grilled. The sauce is delicious and more substantial than you would expect, since it is so healthy & low fat! My 7 yo son loved helping squeeze the citrus and he proudly claimed his contribution each time we took a batch out of the freezer. Thanks for a great recipe. It's definitely a keeper!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
tunnel of fudge cake  cake mix

this is a very rich cake, but using a mix makes it that much easier. everyone loves it when i make it.

1. place milk in pan and whisk in pudding , cook until comes to a boil , 4-5 minutes
2. remove from heat and stir in chips and butter until smooth and thick
3. set aside
4. preheat oven to 350f
5. prepare 12 cup bundt pan
6. mix cake , oil , sour cream , irish cream , eggs , and vanilla in a bowl
7. reserve 2 cups of batter
8. pour remaining batter into pan
9. spoon pudding in a ring on top spoon reserved batter on top
10. bake for 45-50 minutes
11. you can frost , drizzle melted chocolate or just dust with powdered sugar
demonstrations.review: This cake was deliciously moist and the filling was great. For my tastes, the Bailey's flavor was too strong. If I made it again, I would find a replacement for most (if not all) the Bailey's.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
guacamole salad  barefoot contessa  ina garten

i watched ina make this on tv today and it looked so colorful i just have to try it. you may want to adjust the jalapeños to taste, add some mango, and if you are watching your calories- eliminate or reduce the olive oil.

1. place the tomatoes , yellow pepper , black beans , red onion , jalapeo peppers , and lime zest in a large bowl
2. whisk together the lime juice , olive oil , salt , black pepper , garlic , and cayenne pepper and pour over the vegetables
3. toss well
4. just before you're ready to serve the salad , fold the avocados into the salad
5. check the seasoning and serve at room temperature
demonstrations.review: Most awesome salad ever. Can totally be a main course. If I follow it to the letter, it's perfect. If I tweak it a little bit, it's just as perfect. I often swap out half the olive oil for flax seed oil, just for the extra healthy flax seed oil fat, but that doesn't impact the awesome flavor. I use whatever tomatoes look best at the store. Always delicious, and I feel AWESOME after eating this -- I think it's just so crazy healthy that I just feel like superwoman for hours after eating it. :) I love to serve it with grilled fish for a perfect, complete meal. Enjoy!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
stuffed chicken cutlets  oamc

from freeze it in "everyday food". an elegant recipe for supper from the freezer. use 6 boneless skinless chicken breasts, if desired.

1. combine feta , peppers , scallions , oregano , and basil in a medium bowl
2. place cutlets on a flat surface , smooth side down
3. spoon about 2 tbsp of feta mixture into the center of each cutler and the fold short sides in and then long sides creating a packet
4. arrange packets , seam side down on a wax paper lined baking sheet making sure they do not touch each other
5. freeze until firm-about an hour
6. place into a ziploc bag , label and date
7. these can be frozen up to 8 weeks
8. to serve: preheat oven to 400f
9. lightly grease two baking sheets and place frozen cutlets , seam side down
10. lightly season with salt and pepper and bake for 30-40 minutes or until chicken is cooked through
11. if desired , top with warmed tomato sauce
demonstrations.review: Our whole family, kids included, love it! I'm allergic to poultry so make it with pork chops (cut thin and pounded thinner) and it's super. I think I stuff them extra generously, so I use more of the filling than the recipe called for. They freeze perfectly. We serve it with a nice marinara sauce. Delicious! LOVE IT! We especially enjoy how different it is from many of our other OAMC favorites. It really is a lovely, "facncy" but easy dish. Thanks!! It's become a staple in our OAMC rotation and I'm making our third batch (larger batch every time -- 10 lbs of pork this time, 36 cutlets. . .) for the freezer tonight.

target.recipe_text:
butter lime cilantro rice

this is an oriental style cilantro rice. perfect to accompany meats or fish that are cooked with any soy sauce base.

1. chopped the cilantro
2. mix the melted butter , rice vinegar , lime juice and cilantro to warm , cooked rice , and stir until evenly distributed
3. serve immediately
target.review: This was really good! I made it to accompany Crock Pot Cream Cheese and Black Bean Chicken (Recipe #89204).  It was so good! I loved the mix of flavors.  I followed recipe as written.  Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kim s sweet potato casserole

this thanksgiving my boyfriend's step mom's daughter-in-law, kim, brought this sweet potato casserole for our feast. not being a huge fan of sweet potatoes, i was reluctant to try it. boy am i glad i did! it isn't as sweet as most sweet potato casseroles and doesn't have tons the marshmallow goop on it. i begged her for the recipe so that i could have it every holiday and decided to post it on *zaar so that i don't lose it. she stated on the recipe card that she always doubles the recipe and that when it does, it fills a 1 1/2 quart casserole dish.

1. mix all of the casserole ingredients together until well blended
2. spread into a buttered casserole dish
3. mix topping ingredients together and sprinkle over the casserole
4. bake uncovered in a 350 degree oven for 35 minutes
5. remove from oven
6. if topping with marshmallows , place them on the casserole and bake for an addition 5-7 minutes or until marshmallows have melted
7. serve
demonstrations.review: What can I say? Delicious! Left out the marshmallows but followed everything else to a "T". Thanks for posting!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
a chicken in every pot pie

easy and my kids love this.

1. in a saucepan , combine chicken and next 6 ingredients
2. bring to a boil , stirring occasionally
3. meanwhile , combine bisquick and next 3 ingredients
4. pour the hot chicken mixture into eight greased 10 oz
5. ramekins
6. immediately spoon 1 / 4 cup of biscuit mixture evenly on top of each
7. sprinkle with paprika
8. bake , uncovered , at 350 degrees for 30-35 minutes or until topping is golden brown
demonstrations.review: Delish! I always make it exactly as written, and it's always a hit. Thank you!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pork chops yum yum

i copied this from the orlando sentinel months ago and just now found it. we eat pork chops at least once a week and this is our favorite.

1. brown chops on both sides
2. place in greased casserole dish
3. mix all remaining ingredients and pour over pork chops
4. bake , uncovered , at 350 for one hour
demonstrations.review: Delicious! As I can see, I agree with everyone else!

target.recipe_text:
christmas biscotti

a colorful red and green dotted biscotti.. i love it and i don't really like biscotti. my mother said to make her this if nothing else for christmas!

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees
2. butter and flour a baking sheet
3. in a bowl , cream together the butter and sugar until light and fluffy
4. beat in the eggs , vanilla , and orange zest until blended
5. in another bowl , stir together the flour , baking powder , cloves and salt
6. add the flour mixture to the butter mixture and beat until blended
7. stir in cranberries and pistachios
8. divide the dough in half
9. one at a time , place the 2 dough portions on the prepared baking sheet and form each into a log about 1 / 2 inch high , 1 1 / 2 inches wide and 14 inches long
10. space logs at least 2 inches apart
11. bake the logs for 25-30 minutes or until set and light brown
12. transfer to a cutting board and let cool 6-8 minutes
13. reduce the oven temperature to 300 degrees
14. using a very sharp knife , cut the logs in the diagonal into slices 3 / 8 inch thick
15. stand the slices upright on the baking sheet and return the sheet to the oven for 15 minutes to dry the cookies thoroughly
16. transfer to racks to cool
17. store the cookies in an airtight container for up to 4 weeks
target.review: This was my first attempt at biscotti and they turned out great.  I couldn't find raw pistachios or plain dried cranberries at my local store and didn't want to make a special trip, so I bought a bag of roasted, salted pistachios and craisins.  It was a little bit of work to remove all the pistachios from the shells, but it was well worth the effort.  I also used Splenda sugar blend instead of regular sugar.  I dipped each piece half way in white chocolate.  Wow!  I will be making these all year.  The hint of clove and orange just really set off all the flavors.  Thanks for the great treat Mary.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
florida seafood casserole

i found this while cookbook hunting!  rich and yummy!

1. saute' onion in butter till tender- blend in flour and add milk and flour
2. cook and stir till thick cream sauce consistency
3. remove from heat and stir in everything except 1 / 2 c cheese
4. put into a greased 7-1 / 2 by 11 inch casserole and bake 350 for 25 minutes
5. remove from oven and sprinkle remaining cheese over top
demonstrations.review: This was very good with a nice rich flavor and perfect for using up the leftover shrimp and crab I had from our sushi night.  I used fresh red pepper and added the water chestnuts, which added a nice little crunch.  I would have given it 5 stars because my husband and I loved it, but for some reason the kids didn't care for it, which was strange because they usually like seafood and anything with cheese on it.  Perhaps it was just an off night for them so I may try it again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
ww caramel baked pears

this is really an excellent dessert!it is out of an old weight watchers cookbook called "simple goodness" it has only 5 points. hope you enjoy.

1. combine first 3 ingredients in a small saucepan
2. bring to a boil , and cook 3 minutes or until slightly thick
3. remove pan from heat
4. set carmel mixture aside
5. peel and core pears
6. cut pears in half lenghtwise
7. arrange pear halves , cut side up , in an 8 inch square baking dish
8. drizzle caramel mixture over pears
9. cover and bake at 350 degrees for 25 minutes
10. uncover and bake an additional 25 minutes or until tender
11. place 2 pear halves in each of 2 dessert dishes
12. spoon caramel mixture evenly over pears
13. top each serving with 1 tbls yogurt and 1 tsp almonds
demonstrations.review: Oh my! These were so good.  I made them just as written - I would not change a thing.  I will be making these again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chicken and spinach pasta casserole

great tasting casserole; i'm not a big spinach fan myself but these greens are covered up well. look out popeye!

1. preheat oven to 375f
2. cook pasta and drain
3. cook bacon on stove or in microwave
4. cook chicken and drain
5. return above into saucepan with 2 / 3 cup french fried onions
6. in separate bowl , combine soup , sour cream , spinach , garlic powder and 1 cup cheddar cheese
7. spoon half of the macaroni mixture into a greased 12x8-inch baking dish and cover with half of the "dip" mix
8. repeat layers
9. bake uncovered at 375f for 30 minutes or until heat through
10. then top with remaining cheese and 2 / 3 cup onions and bake at same temp , uncovered for about 3 to 5 minutes until golden brown
demonstrations.review: Oh my, was this good!  I had every intention of following the recipe but had to make some last minute changes to work with what I had on hand.  I used fresh spinach instead of frozen, cream of chicken soup instead of cream of mushroom, and since I only had about 1/4 cup of sour cream I added about 4 oz of softened cream cheese.  I had some last minute guests show up while I was preparing dinner so I had to figure out how to make the meal stretch.  I had a little extra pasta but no more chicken so I added a 4 oz. can of mushroom and a 14 oz. can of diced tomatoes.  This was so creamy and flavorful.  This got rave reviews and I will be making this again.

target.recipe_text:
pasta with zucchini ricotta sauce

from today's ny times, this is a great way to use up your garden surplus.

1. bring a large pot of water to a boil and salt it
2. put olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat
3. when hot add zucchini , along with a large pinch of salt and a sprinkling of pepper
4. cook , stirring occasionally , until zucchini begins to brown , then lower heat and cook until it is quite tender , about 15 minutes total
5. about 5 minutes before it is done , stir in garlic and begin to cook pasta
6. while pasta cooks , warm a serving bowl and put ricotta in it , along with about half the basil
7. when pasta is tender but not mushy , remove and drain it , reserving about a cup of its cooking liquid
8. use as much of this liquid as necessary , a bit at a time , to thin ricotta until it reaches a saucy consistency
9. toss with pasta , zucchini , remaining basil and parmesan , if you are using it , then taste and adjust seasoning
10. serve
target.review:
Just made and ate this for dinner tonight.  It was sooooo good and creamy and fresh tasting!

I added a little onion and red pepper flakes to the saute.  And at the very end added a little shredded roast chicken (just because I happen to have it on hand).

I'm doing WW so excluded the olive oil altogether and used a olive oil spray instead.  It worked just fine and did not harm the finished taste.

I will make this recipe again for sure.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
gourmet s roasted cauliflower soup

adopted 9/15 by me.  this recipe is from  gourmet issue december 1997.  i finally traced it down.

1. preheat oven to 425f
2. cut cauliflower into 1-inch flowerets
3. in a large baking pan toss cauliflower , garlic , and shallots with oil to coat and roast in middle of oven about 30 minutes , or until golden
4. turn frequently and remove any of the garlic and shallots if they are done soone
5. in a 4-quart pot simmer stock / broth , water , roasted cauliflower mixture , and herbs 30 minutes , or until cauliflower is very tender
6. discard bay leaf and in a blender puree soup in batches until smooth , transferring to a bowl
7. return soup to pot and stir in cream and salt and pepper to taste
8. heat soup over moderate heat until just heated through
demonstrations.review:
I gave my version of this soup 3 stars.  I had organic vegetable broth on hand, and used this in place of the chicken stock.  I believe this made a big difference in the taste, which was very bland.  Next time I'll use homemade chicken stock.

I also added milk instead of cream, as I'm trying to keep it light.  I will do this again next time.

I like the idea of roasting the veggies as this adds a nice sweetness to the soup.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
barbecue ranch chicken salad

delicious salad with a southwestern flair!  one of my favorites!  just make sure the red onion you use isn't a strong one.  cooking time is refrigeration time.

1. mix all of the salad ingredients in a large bowl
2. whisk dressing ingredients together in a small bowl , and pour over the salad
3. toss to coat , and chill 1 hour before serving
4. you can serve this over some shredded lettuce , if desired
demonstrations.review:
I LOVE THIS SALAD!  I made as written, but didn't have the bell pepper or red onion on hand.  I used green onion and a very small dice of carrot instead and it was very good.  I will add cilantro next time I make this as I think that would be a good addition.

The dressing is so easy and 'to die for' LOL.

Great salad for these hot Texas summer days.  Thanks for sharing!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
7 vegetable chicken stew with dumplings

a delicious meal on a cold evening. you can also use skinless boneless chicken thighs if you prefer dark meat. i sometimes add mushrooms too, making it an 8-veg stew!

1. in a large pot , combine chicken , all veg except peas , stock and spices
2. bring to a boil over high heat
3. reduce heat to medium-low and simmer , covered , for 20 minutes
4. stir in peas
5. meanwhile , in a food processor or by hand , make dumplings: combine flour , parsley , butter , baking powder and salt until mixture is in coarse crumbs
6. stir in milk , then drop by tablespoonfuls onto the hot stew
7. you should have about 6 mounds
8. cover pot and simmer-- don't boil hard and don't lift the lid-- for 15 minutes or until dumplings have risen
demonstrations.review:
I made this twice in less than 2 weeks.  Once for myself and then again for my parents.  

I did tweak it, but only because I was in the middle of a move and used just what I had on hand the first time.  It was so good I made it the same way for my parents.

I used a roasted chicken from the market.  Took the meat off the bone and then used the carcass to make my chicken stock.  I strained the stock and then added the veggies.  I had all except the sweet potatoe and rutabagas, although I'm sure I would love it with those veggies as well.

I added the chicken just before I put the dumplings in.  For the dumplings I used 1 1/2 tablespoon of baking powder. They were light and fluffy!

Growing-up, chicken and dumplings was always my request for my birthday dinner.  This is my new favorite recipe...I LOVE IT!

target.recipe_text:
hungarian goulash

this is my mother's recipe for goulash but i've made a couple of alterations to improve it, such as using beef broth instead of water and real hungarian paprika instead of spanish paprika. you can use spanish paprika if hungarian is unavailable, but it tastes much better with hungarian paprika. it is also nice made with stewing veal. when i was a child, i liked this so much that i used to eat it for breakfast if there was any left over from supper!

1. heat oil in a large dutch oven and add stewing beef
2. saute until nicely browned
3. remove meat from pan with slotted spoon and put to one side
4. add onions and cook until slightly softened and caramelized
5. return meat to pan
6. sprinkle meat and onions with paprika , salt and pepper
7. add broth and bring to a boil
8. cover and simmer for 1-1 / 2 hours or until tender
9. mix flour with water to make a smooth paste and add to simmering goulash
10. bring back to a boil and cook until the sauce thickens
11. add sour cream and heat through
12. serve over potato dumplings or egg noodles
target.review: So very, very tasty - better than five stars. The meat was so tender and melted in the mouth.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kentucky apple festival apple pie

i adopted this recipe during the recipezaar abandoned account recipe adoption. this is a delicious pie with an easy, no fuss crust. the crust is tender and flaky at the same time and the flavor is just the perfect amount of sweetness! try it and you'll see why it is a festival winning apple pie! 10/12/04, edited: cooking time/temperature

1. crust: mix shortening , 1 / 3 cup butter and flour
2. add boiling water , salt and baking powder
3. mix well
4. separate into 2 balls
5. place between 2 pieces of wax paper
6. roll
7. filling: peel , core and slice apples
8. lightly mix cinnamon and sugar with the apples
9. heap into pastry lined pie pan and dot with 1 1 / 2 tablespoons butter
10. cover with topping crust
11. slit to allow steam to escape
12. bake at 425f for 15 minutes then reduce temperature to 350 and continue baking 45-60 minutes
demonstrations.review: Used cooking apples but otherwise followed recipe exactly. This is a very good apple pie.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
venison tenderloin with cabernet sauce

another favourite venison recipe. this recipe considers farm-raised deer which is readily available in better butcher shops, or some larger super markets. a favourite cook offers up this recipe, and can be found in 

1. preheat the oven to 450 degrees f
2. rub the venison with garlic and sprinkle with salt and pepper
3. put olive oil in a heavy skillet
4. add venison and sear over high heat until browned on all sides- about 3 minutes place in oven and roast until medium-rare
5. for 16- 20 minutes , turning once
6. meanwhile , combine the wine with the vegetables and herbs and bring to a boil
7. reduce by half over medium heat- about 8 minutes
8. strain out vegetables and discard
9. in a saucepan , reduce broth by half over high heat- about 7 minutes
10. combine all the liquids
11. when meat is done , remove to cutting board and cover loosely with foil
12. pour any fat from the pan and deglaze with the reduced liquids
13. whisk in the cold butter and add salt and pepper
14. spoon a bit of sauce over each meat serving
demonstrations.review: Used haunch of venison and follwed recipe exactly - it was really tasty.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
ground beef   cabbage stew

one day i made this stew for myself (god forbid the kids ever put cabbage in their mouths)they(the kids) accidently ate it mistaking it for my beef stew. they called me on my cell phone and told me that was the best stew i had ever made. i just let it be my little secret about cabbage.

1. brown ground beef and drain
2. set aside
3. heat olive oil in skillet and add onion and cook 2-3 minutes
4. add cabbage , tomatoes , potatoes , carrots , bell pepper , thyme
5. mix well
6. add broth
7. heat to boiling
8. reduce heat
9. cover and cook 20 minutes
10. stir in corn and beans
11. cover and cook 15 minutes
demonstrations.review: Followed recipe exactly - a very tasty one pot meal.

target.recipe_text:
apple pie filling with vanilla   buttershots  canning

my dd went apple picking and brought me a nice bunch of organic apples. this can top ice cream waffles, pan cakes, french toast. make an apple pie with it or stuff puff pastry with it. pour it over a hot ricotta cheese cake.

1. in a large pot place first 5 ingredients and optional spices , bring to a boil and cook till thick and bubbly
2. stirring so it doesn`t stick to the bottom and burn
3. meanwhile pack 4-6 sliced apples in sterilized quart jars
4. remove from heat and add the lemon juice and zest and buttershots
5. pour over apples removing as much air as you can
6. this is thick so use a butter knife to help it seep down to the bottom
7. leaving 1 inch head space
8. wipe rims and place hot lids and screw tops on
9. process in a water bath for 25 minutes
10. optional packing:
11. mix apple slices into the syrup then pack
target.review: This apple pie filling is the best thing since bubble gum. I didn't have any vanilla bean so I used regular vanilla, clear gel instead of cornstarch and apple juice instead of water. I cut the apples into smaller chunks and canned in pints for waffle topping. It is really good made into a crumb topped pie. For the topping I used flour, butter, brown sugar and butterscotch chips.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
romano s macaroni grill rosemary bread

this is an attempt to immitate the excellent bread that is served in the macaroni grill restaurant.

1. place yeast , sugar and water in large bowl or food processor and allow mixture to become bubbly
2. mix in 1 t butter , salt , and 2 cups of flour
3. add one tablespoon of the fresh chopped rosemary
4. knead for about 10 minutes by hand or in food processor about 5 minutes until smooth and elastic
5. add more flour if necessary
6. oil a bowl , put dough in it and cover with a towel
7. let dough rise in a warm place for one hour until doubled
8. punch down dough and divide in half
9. let dough rest about 5 minutes
10. spray baking pan or cookie sheet with cooking spray
11. shape the dough into 2 small rounded oval loaves
12. sprinkle remaining 1 tablespoon of rosemary over the loaves and press lightly into the surface
13. let loaves rise again until doubled , about 45 minutes
14. preheat oven to 375f
15. bake for 15 to 20 minutes , until lightly browned
16. carefully remove from oven , brush with remaining butter
demonstrations.review: We cooked the bread on our Traeger grill. Absolutely Delicious!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cupboard turkey kielbasa cassoulet

from walgreens.com

1. preheat oven to 375 degrees
2. drain and rinse black beans , navy beans , and kidney beans
3. mix all ingredients in an ungreased 3-quart casserole dish
4. cover and bake for 1 hour or until hot and carrots are tender
5. remove bay leaf before serving
demonstrations.review: Very easy to make, but we didn't feel for our taste it was anything special. We will finish the leftovers, just won't make again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mom bennett s venison gravy

my ex-mother-in-law made this. it's great over mashed potatoes and something you can do with that deer that someone brought home.  see beachgirl's recipe #53234 for canned venison. you can pressure cook the venison for 90 minutes  to get the same consistency of the meat.

1. mix flour and oil in skillet over medium heat until brown , stirring constantly
2. add canned milk and water enough to make gravy
3. add canned soup and a quart jar of canned venison
4. salt and pepper to taste
5. cook till thick
6. serve over mashed potatoes
demonstrations.review: We added an extra cup of water and a can of French Onion soup, and served it over buttermilk biscuits. We have been searching for more recipes that use canned venison, this one is a keeper. Gotta Love Comfort Food!

target.recipe_text:
low carb  pancakes

this sounds a little strange, but it makes the best low carb pancakes i've ever eaten! if you're doing atkins or south beach these will become a regular on your breakfast menu....

1. crush pork rinds and set aside
2. beat eggs and then fold in cream , splenda , cinnamon , and vanilla flavoring
3. add crushed pork rinds and let the mixture sit for 5 minutes
4. meanwhile heat skillet with butter or oil and then fry mixture pancake style
5. serve with low carb pancake syrup
6. only 6 net carbs for the entire batch !
target.review: Mine turned into a thick blob. Okay taste but will not make again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
low carb chocolate mints   choco peanut cups

made either chocolate mints or choco-peanut butter cups from the same recipe.

1. put cream cheese and butter in a microwave safe bowl
2. microwave for 1 minute to soften
3. blend all ingredients in bowl
4. use either extract or peanut butter , depending on which type of chocolate you desire
5. spoon into paper muffins cups and chill
6. store in refrigerator
7. enjoy
demonstrations.review: I did not care for these. Ended up throwing the whole batch out. The texture and taste was off.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
easy mashed cauliflower with nutmeg  low carb

some people make this as a low-carb substitute for mashed potatoes. we make it because we love the flavours.

1. steam the cauliflower until very tender
2. add the remaining ingredients
3. mash everything together until you have the consistency you like
demonstrations.review: Pretty good.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
another mock mashed potatoes  mashed cauliflower  low carb

i saw this recipe made on the new low carb cooking show on food network. i tried the recipe tonight and it is really so good - this is my spin on the recipe. this time, i omitted the rosemary and used raw minced garlic, but you may also use a few cloves of roasted garlic if you prefer. this version is different from many others as there is no sour cream and no mayonnaise. real comfort without all that starch. (note: smart balance is a lower calorie, cholesterol reducing butter substitute).

1. bring a medium-large pot of water to boil
2. cut cauliflower into smaller pieces , add to the pot , and boil until fork tender , approximately 6 minutes
3. drain well
4. using a stick blender or potato masher , mash the cauliflower with the cream cheese , garlic , rosemary , parmesan cheese , butter , and bouillon powder
5. add some salt and pepper to taste- test and adjust seasonings as needed
demonstrations.review: One of my first times cooking and eating cauliflower. I must say I really liked this recipe. The rosemary adds such a great flavor. Great side for a low carb diet.

target.recipe_text:
lemon pepper fish greek style

serves 2. a simple marinade for a quick cook meal
serve with veges or a salad on the side
you can use any type of fish fillet- 1 per serve or two smaller per serve as required. cooking time includes marinating time

1. combine the garlic , oil , lemon juice , lemon zest , cracked black pepper , sea salt and the dried oregano in a large bowl
2. use the bowl in which you will marinate your fish
3. add the fish and ensure it is thoroughly coated in the marinade
4. cover and refrigerate for 15-20 minutes
5. line a broiler / griller tray with aluminium foil and place the fish on in a single layer
6. broil / grill the fish for 5-10 minutes each side
7. only turn the fish once during the cooking
8. grill until the fish is cooked
9. serve with a salad or veges
target.review: I made this to marinate some lovely salmon steaks.  All the ingredients went into a zip-lock bag and refrigerated for 3 hours.  I then grilled the salmon lightly, brushing with marinade.  The lemon and pepper cut through the 'richness' of the slamon, made it light and refreshing.  Can't wait to ty it on other types of fish and also chicken.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mussel fritters

i found this recipe on the geocities website.  whipped it up for lunch today and these fritters are devine.  light and tasty and they go down a treat.  the recipe notes that basil is the secret ingredient in this recipe.

1. lightly steam mussels until they just open
2. remove beards , take from shell and chop roughly
3. in a bowl , beat the eggs , sift in the flour and baking powder and beat with a fork to combine
4. stir in the mussels , salt , pepper , basil and parsley
5. melt butter over a medium heat
6. drop mixture into butter and fry pancake style until golden brown , then flip and cook until golden on other side
7. enjoy !
demonstrations.review: What delicate wee morsels these are.  At last, mussel fritters that aren't like small, windowless buildings.  Super easy, super taste, ingredients are spot on.  I didn't have any basil, not overly fond of it anyway, so just added a good handful of flat leaf parsley.  Mussels are cheap here and out of 2 dozen I got 8 fritters, a pot of mussel chowder and 1/2 litre of stock.  Thankyou Kiwi Kathy for a great recipe, I next plan to make these for a party, I'll make them small and serve with a sour cream and sweet chilli dipping sauce.  From one kiwi to another.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
lori s cheapo chicken

normally i would not cook this way, but this was extremely good and cheap!

1. combine all
2. let stand 1 hour
3. heat oven 400
4. place chicken in a large sprayed baking dish
5. bake 1 hour
demonstrations.review: Maybe if you use a "spray-on" type of oil, the same sort as you would use to spray the baking dish, and sprayed the chicken pieces with it.  Or, cut the oil out completely, I can't see it's absence making any difference to the flavour or quality of this dish.  I think applesauce might add an unwanted extra sweetness, the ketchup provides enough sweetness as it is.  This is a lovely, tasty and easy dish to prepare and eat.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
easy cheddar potato cakes  made with instant potatoes

if you looking for ways to use your instant potato flakes then here is a really great recipe! feel free to adjust all amounts to taste, this takes only minutes to make and my family loves them, don't try this recipe using regular mashed potatoes, it will not work --- this recipe was tested using  idahoan brand mashed potato flakes but i am sure any brand will work fine, servings is only estimated.

1. in a bowl combine the first 9 ingredients
2. in another bowl mix the milk with egg and melted butter whisk until well combined
3. add to the dry mixture
4. mix well
5. let mixture stand for about 10-12 minutes until the liquid is absorbed
6. heat oil in a skillet over medium heat
7. using slightly wet hands tightly shape into small balls place into hot oil then press down lightly with back of a spoon)
8. cook about 3 minutes on each side or until browned adding in more oil as needed
9. remove to paper towels
demonstrations.review: Oh, Kittencal...you've done it again.  It's Kismet.  DH brought home a 5kg bag of instant potatoes 'cos they 'were on special'.  Sheeeesh..there's only the 2 of us here !!!!  I made these, so easy, so forgiving, because we've got alot of leftover Christmas ham (also a DH purchase, 'on special') to wade through as well, so I threw a handful of the damn stuff, finely chopped, into these potatoe cakes and they were delicious.

target.recipe_text:
brussels sprouts in garlic butter

this is a recipe from joy of cooking... totally changed my mind about brussels sprouts! it's imperative that you use fresh sprouts, the texture would be way off with the frozen ones.

1. melt butter and olive oil in a medium skillet until butter is foamy
2. reduce heat to medium , add smashed garlic and cook until lightly browned
3. remove garlic and discard
4. add sprouts cut side down , cover , and cook without stirring on medium-low heat 10-15 minutes or until tender when pierced with a knife
5. the cut side of the sprouts should get nice and browned , with a nutty , buttery flavor enhanced by garlic
6. top with freshly grated parmesan and salt& pepper to taste
target.review: This was easy to make and delicious! The Parmesan sprinkled on at the end sent it over the top! I'll be making these over and over again...thank you!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
baked italian sausage  with potatoes and rosemary

a hearty, flavoursome really quick to prepare and assemble one dish meal.  bill granger's recipe from the lifestyle food channel.

1. preheat the oven to 200c
2. slice the sausages into 4cm pieces and place in a large roasting pan
3. add the potatoes , paprika , rosemary , garlic cloves , sea salt and pepper
4. tear the ciabatta into bite size pieces and add to the roasting tray
5. drizzle over the oil and gently toss to combine
6. place in the oven and cook , stirring occasionally , for 30-40 minutes or until the potatoes are tender and the sausages and bread are golden brown
7. top with continental parsley and serve with a green salad
demonstrations.review: My family LOVED this -- so quick and easy, yet delicious!  Thank you so much for a wonderful recipe!  We made with a garlic infused evoo and red potatoes and added chopped onions; next time I'll add more bread because that was my favorite part...except for the sausage which was so juicy!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cheesy egg potato and ham frittata brunch casserole

this makes a wonderful weekend brunch, i have made it many time in the past, it's very easy to make too! you can make this using cold cooked finely diced potatoes in place of hash browns, i have made this using leftover potatoes with great success! feel free to add in green bell pepper, jalapeno peppers, skiced mushrooms, or whatever you wish! the skillet cooking time will take slightly longer.

1. set oven to 375 degrees
2. butter a 13 x 9-inch baking dish
3. heat oil and butter in a skillet
4. add in frozen shredded potatoes , both onions , cayenne pepper 1 teaspoon seasoned salt and black pepper to taste
5. cook for about 8-10 minutes or until just very lightly browned
6. add in ham and cook for 3 minutes more , mixing occasionally with a wooden spoon or spatula
7. transfer the mixture to the prepared baking dish
8. in a bowl whisk together the eggs with whipping cream , italian seasoning and 1 teaspoon seasoned salt then pour the egg mixture into the baking dish
9. toss with the potatoes
10. bake for 20-22 minutes
11. remove from oven and sprinkle with about 2 cups grated cheddar cheese
12. return to oven uncovered for another 5-8 minutes until the cheese is melted and eggs are set
13. cool for about 10 minutes before slicing
demonstrations.review: I followed littlebug's suggestion and made two of these -- one following the original recipe and the other with spinach, onion and parm cheese.  Every single person who tried it, loved it.  Next time I'll try with sausage instead of ham.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
baked pork chops and apples

i found this in a pamphlet from the orchard (about maryland apple orchards) a few years ago when we were picking apples. it is one of the tastiest things i have ever made!

1. peel , core , and slice the apples
2. preheat the oven to 350 degrees
3. melt the butter in a skillet
4. brown the pork chops on both sides in the butter
5. grease a large baking dish
6. put the apple slices in the bottom of the dish
7. mix the brown sugar and cinnamon
8. sprinkle the cinnamon and sugar over the apples
9. place the pork chops on top of the apples
10. cover with foil and bake for 1 and 1 / 2 hours
demonstrations.review: We added apple juice to the casserole dish as another reviewer suggested and baked for a total of 45 minutes for two butterflied pork chops.  Everyone in our family loved it!

target.recipe_text:
sex in a pan

i made this last thanksgiving and i have requests for a repeat performance this year! i have not met a single person that hasn't like this, because it's light but rich! this dessert really lives up to its name!

1. mix together the icing sugar , margarine , flour , and chopped pecans and press into a 9x13" pan
2. bake for about 15 minutes at 350 degrees f
3. cool
4. mix cream cheese , white sugar , and one cup of cool whip
5. spread on cool base
6. mix both packages of pudding and add 3 cups of milk
7. beat and spread on filling layer
8. spread remaining cool whip on top , add some shaved chocolate if you want and set in the fridge
target.review: Hahaha, good point paula&matt.  We tell the kids its "Ecstacy in a pan"  ;)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
baked spaghetti with chicken and spinach

one of our favourite ways to serve spaghetti, leaves a nice tingle. serve with a fresh green salad and crusty rolls.

1. cook spaghetti , al dente , drain and set aside
2. heat oil in large saucepan
3. add garlic and onion , cook until soft , but not browned
4. add chicken , brown on all sides , turning often , until no longer pink
5. sauce: in a blender or food processor , add stewed tomatoes , basil , tarragon , salt , chili flakes , parsley , garlic and cheese
6. pulse until just chunky , not smooth
7. add sauce to chicken mixture
8. stir and simmer for 15 minutes
9. line an oven proof casserole with the spinach
10. lay the spaghetti over the spinach
11. pour the chicken / sauce mixture over the spaghetti
12. bring a spoon up through the layers to mix lightly and turn the spinach throughout
13. sprinkle cheeses on top and add another dash of chili flakes if desired
14. bake at 400f for 20 to 30 minutes
demonstrations.review: This was delicious, and I also skipped the blending process and took the suggestion to use Italian stewed tomoatoes.  Great flavour, although found it a little too garlicky.  Next time will use less garlic and more chicken, tomatoes and spinach!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
baked cherry tomatoes with parmesan topping

another winner from bon appetit. a wonderful side dish or appetizer course.

1. pour oil into 13x9x2-inch broilerproof ceramic baking dish
2. add tomatoes , turn to coat with oil
3. sprinkle with salt and pepper
4. top with parsley and cheese
5. preheat oven to 400
6. bake tomatoes just until plump and shiny but not split , about 10 minutes
7. preheat broiler
8. broil until tomatoes begin to split and cheese begins to color , about 2 minutes
9. serve hot or warm
demonstrations.review: I added some tarragon into the mix, which gave it a yummy sweetness.  I discovered my oven was broken after i had them all ready to go, so I cooked them in a covered pot on the stove for 10 mins or so.  The cheese burnt, but even so, Delicious!  I can't wait to try it when my appliances are actually working!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mom s potato casserole

easy, delicious, and takes virtually no time to throw together! the busy person's all-purpose dish, absolutely wonderful!

1. combine sour cream , mushroom soup , onion and hash browns
2. mix well and pat into a 9x13 casserole dish
3. combine crushed crackers and melted margarine and spread evenly over top
4. bake at 350f for 35-40 minutes
demonstrations.review: You can also throw in a cup of shredded cheddar cheese for an extra zing.

target.recipe_text:
taffy apple pizza

a pampered chef winner! one of my favorites. the crust is sugar cookie dough! did you know taffy originated in germany? and apples are used extensively in germany too! i guess that makes this a german recipe!(lol)

1. put sliced apples into the lemon-lime soda to soak so they won't brown
2. preheat oven to 350
3. roll cookie dough into a 12-inch circle on a 13" baking stone that has been lightly floured
4. bake approximately 5 minutes longer than directions on package say
5. let cool
6. in a bowl , mix peanut butter , cream cheese , sugar and vanilla
7. spread over cooled cookie crust
8. then drain apples and arrange in a spiral , to cover entire "pizza"
9. srinkle with cinnamon and pour over caramel topping
10. it's ready to serve !
11. enjoy !
target.review: Some little elves in my house ate the caramel topping so I had to leave that out!  Still a fantastic recipe.  Very rich; all you need is a small piece.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mean chef s oatmeal pecan chocolate chunk cookies

amazingly soft, delicious cookies! when i made this, i used ghirardelli chocolate and was just short on the called-for amount of pecans. the dough was really hard after refrigerating overnight, and i found it easier to roll it into balls by hand rather than the ice cream scoop. i adopted this recipe after its original poster, mean chef, departed the site. mean posted the recipe on feb 12, 2003.

1. in a medium bowl , whisk together flour , salt , baking powder , and baking soda
2. set dry ingredients aside
3. in the bowl of an electric mixer , combine butter with both sugars
4. beat until light and fluffy
5. add vanilla , milk , and eggs
6. mix well
7. add reserved dry ingredients , and beat until just combined
8. remove bowl from mixer , and fold in oats , chocolate , and pecans
9. place dough in the refrigerator until firm , at least 2 hours or overnight
10. heat oven to 350
11. line two baking sheets with parchment paper , and set aside
12. remove dough from refrigerator
13. using an ice-cream scoop , shape into 2-inch-diameter balls
14. place six balls on each baking sheet , spaced 4 inches apart , and press down transfer to oven
15. bake until golden , but still soft in center , 15 to 16 minutes
16. remove from oven , and place on a wire rack to cool completely
17. repeat with remaining dough
18. store in an airtight container up to 2 days
demonstrations.review: Sigh. I am in cookie nirvana.  Made the recipe exactly as written, down to refrigerating the dough.  Perfect cookie, not too sweet, rich and chewy.  Cooked in 14 minutes, but I must have made them slightly smaller than Mean directs, because I got 26 cookies instead of 22.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
brunch enchiladas

from feb/mar 2000 issue of taste of home. another great breakfast that is so conveniently put together the night before. prep time includes 30 minutes actual labor and 8-1/2 hours refrigeration and standing time. cook time is 38 minutes and 10 minutes standing time.  re: review posted by 5hungrykids (who does not accept zmail): the recipe i posted here has never differed from the original recipe published in the toh magazine, in ingredients or baking instructions.  i did a quick check of their website to see if it had been changed since 2000 but it's still exactly the same as this posting.   i think baking it at 325° is reasonable enough, but that would account for your longer bake time.  :)

1. combine ham and onion
2. place 1 / 3 cup down the center of each tortilla
3. top with 2 tablespoons cheese
4. roll up and place seam side down in a greased 13x9x2 baking dish
5. in a bowl , combine flour , cream , eggs and salt until smooth
6. pour over tortillas
7. cover and refrigerate for 8 hours or overnight
8. remove from refrigerator 30 minutes before baking
9. cover and bake at 350 degrees for 25 minutes
10. sprinkle with remaining cheese
11. bake 3 minutes longer or until cheese is melted
12. let stand 10 minutes before serving
demonstrations.review: Excellent recipe.  Assembled the night before; fantastic flavor.  I only had one cup of milk, and 8 tortillas so the proportions I used were slightly different from what's posted, but the outcome fantastic.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
d s roasted butternut squash

easy and delicious.

1. peel and chop squash into 2 inch cubes and put in a bowl
2. add all other ingredients and toss
3. spray a cookie sheet with non-stick veg spray
4. put the tray near the bottom of the oven and roast at 350 until tender
demonstrations.review: Perfect for this crisp fall evening! I didn't have any honey, so I used a touch of maple syrup instead, but otherwise followed the recipe exactly. It was in the oven about 45 minutes while awaiting the rest of dinner to be finished. Two of us ate a whole squash!  Thanks for such a great recipe!

target.recipe_text:
cheesy broccoli chowder

very yummy on a cold winter day

1. melt margarine in a saucepan , add onion , celery & carrot , cook until softened , about 3 min
2. add flour & mustard , cook stirring for a minute or two
3. 'stir in broth & broccoli , bring to a boil
4. simmer covered , stirring occasionally until broccoli & veggies are tender , about 10 min
5. place broccoli mixture in a blender & process until smooth
6. return to pan & stir in milk
7. bring to a boil over medium heat
8. add cheese , stir just until melted
target.review: This is very good, I just wish it were a bit thicker.  I followed the instructions to a T and mine came out a bit runny for a chowder.  Nonetheless, it tasted great and is a nice alternative to going out to a restaurant for broccoli cheese soup.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
homemade pie crust

a nice all purpose pie crust. when i need a crust for a cobbler, i change it to self rising flour because i like lots of crust in my cobblers.

1. put flour into a mixing bowl with the butter
2. using a pastry cutter , cut the butter into the flour
3. add salt and water
4. mix until dough is formed
5. roll out on flat surface
6. bake at 375 degrees until brown
7. prick crust prior to baking for non filled baked pies
demonstrations.review: Thank you, thank you, THANK YOU!  This is the first pie crust I have ever made that wasn't too stiff to deal with.  I am so excited that I found this recipe.  I used one crust for a summer beef pie, and I'll probably use the other for an apple pie.  Easy and pretty!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
low fat  sugar free cornbread

this is a low cal modification of my mom's cornbread recipe. using splenda instead of sugar and 

1. combine ingredients in a large bowl , then mix by hand until batter is just moistened
2. pour into 9 large muffin cups or a 9x9 cake pan sprayed with pam
3. bake for 25-30 minutes at 350 degrees f
demonstrations.review: I made this today and it was really good.  I did make a few changes based on what we had on hand.  I used Masa corn flour instead of cornmeal, real sugar instead of Splenda, and canola oil instead of margarine.  It came out sort of like a corn biscuit.  It was yummy with the lentil and brown rice chili we had!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
sweet potato bacon and onion soup

from the take three book. haven't tried it, but will! guessing at the times. will update them when i've made it.

1. heat the oven to 180c cut the sweet potatoes in half lengthwise , rub with the olive oil and bake , cut side down for 1 hour until tender
2. allow to cool , then scoop the flesh out of the skins and discard the skins
3. arrange the bacon on a foil-covered baking tray and grill or fry in a non-stick frying pan until super crisp
4. remove and drain on kitchen paper , then crumble into small pieces
5. cook the onions in the bacon fat or in 1 tbs olive oil over a moderate heat for 5 minutes until they start to soften
6. add the sweet potato flesh , bay leaves , chicken stock , nutmeg , salt and pepper and bring to the boil , stirring
7. simmer for 15 minutes , stirring occasionally
8. if its too lumpy for your taste , whip out the bay leaves and whiz the whole lot in the food processor , otherwise leave it alone
9. serve in warmed soup bowls , topped with crumbled crisp bacon
demonstrations.review: This was absolutely fantastic.  I've made it both with and without the bacon, but it really does something for the presentation to see the crumbled bacon on top.  The taste is delicious.  Don't be shocked if everyone eats more than one bowl. :)

target.recipe_text:
creamy tomato pasta sauce

a quick, different pasta sauce. use whatever herbs you wish.

1. in a large skillet , heat oil over medium heat and cook onions for about 3 minutes or until softened
2. add tomatoes and spices and bring up to a boil
3. reduce heat and simmer for about 10 minutes , or until thickened

demonstrations.recipe_text:
roasted garlic   pearl onions with herbs

i've made anything from 1 bulb to a whole bag full at one time. when i make a bag full i squeeze all the garlic into a jar then cover with olive oil and refrigerate till i need it. which is very soon! use as a spread on bread, potatoes, roasts, add to butter or olive oil. put into dressings. mashed potatoes just love them!!!in the picture is the roasted garlic and the  roasted garlic spread #92370 check out this thread http://www.recipezaar.com/bb/viewtopic.zsp?t=226006 of different versions of roasting garlic.

fiesta corn

1. cook the corn according to package directions
2. in a nonstick skillet sprayed with nonstick cooking spray
3. melt the margarine

Just got back from the supermarket and had to fix myself a quick dinner.So i decided on trying this salad after taking a peek at pamelas colouurful photo.))..
I cant begin to tell you how wonderful this tasted......and my hubby was surprised as this was not a cold one ,the only he is used to eating......I must add that i made a few changes to suit our palette..
I added a clove of garlic and instead of green chillies which i did nothave on hand,added red chillie flakes,red chilli powder and pepper powder...it was steamy and very yummyyyyyy.Thnx again for a lovely recipe...

demonstrations.recipe_text:

i have had this recipe for years in my

2. grease a 2 quart rectangular baking dish
3. combine the 1 / 4 c
4. melted butter and lemon juice in a shallow bowl

target.recipe_text:
smoked  salmon  cracker spread

from the land of lakes cookbook via a friend who knows how i like to play. great as an appetizer spread, rolled in a tortilla, or in sandwiches. lots of possibilities for innovation here! cook time is chilling time.

1. in small mixer bowl beat cream cheese at med
2. speed , scraping bowl often , until light and fluffy add salt , lemon juice , onion , and liquid smoke

6. store refrigerated
7. garnish with chives , green onions , olives , pimiento , etc
8. to taste

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mexican pork   black beans

nan

1. put beans in crockpot
2. toss pork with chili powder , coriander and salt
3. lightly brown onion and garlic with pork in ungreased skillet
4. mix tomatoes into crockpot with their juice
5. add meat , pepper and 2 cups water

demonstrations.review: This is JUST what I was looking for! I have been wanting this recipe for awhile, so Thank You, Dancer! I had to improvise about 16 oz of HOT salsa for the tomatoes, but it gave it just the right amount of heat for me!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
atkins yogurt  strawberry banana smoothie

just learning how to eat right and came up with these ingredients. don't care for bananas in it, maybe next time i will try just strawberry. taste good though. hope you enjoy :)

1. add all ingredients to blender
2. use ice breaker mode on blender to chop fruit and ice
3. then finish blending and enjoy
demonstrations.review: Thanks, Miss J! I needed a recipe with yogurt in it. I have been dreaming of one of these for awhile! I don't care for bananas too much either, so I used about 12 fresh strawberries and vanilla-flavored yogurt. This does not come out very sweet, so add some sugar if you like it like that!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
thick  soft  and chewy chocolate chip cookies

i moved out of the house in 1992 but my dad still insist i make his chocolate chip cookies for him. after much searching these are the ones we deemed "best". soft and chewy but with a lightly crisp outer layer. if you don't want the crispness, substitute more butter for the shortening. 

i have found that you need to follow the directions *exactly* to get the best cookies. not using real butter or all brown sugar, not beating the eggs in one at a time, not baking them at a higher temp than the "traditional" recipe, all make a difference in the end result. 

i have also found that land o' lake butter makes a better cookie than some generic brand butter. don't let the butter sit out too long. it needs to soften but if it sits until the moisture starts to separate from the butter, it is too soft and it will affect the resulting cookies. if that happens, refrigerate the dough for about an hour to help them not spread as much. it also helps to use the mixer on the dough in between batches going into the oven. it helps keep the dough from starting to separate if it is a warm day. 

another thing i've learned is you have to make sure there is plenty of circulation in your oven. when i moved, my cookies started turning out flat again. i finally realized that my oven was smaller at the new house and when i switched to smaller cookie sheets, my cookies turned out perfectly!

1. mix flour , baking soda , and salt in a small bowl
2. in a separate bowl , beat butter and shortening until creamy
3. add sugar and vanilla and beat with a mixer on medium speed until well blended
4. beat in eggs , one at a time , mixing well
5. add flour mixture , and beat slowly to incorporate , then beat to blend well
6. stir in chocolate chips and nuts
7. drop batter in 2-tablespoon portions about 2 inches apart on baking sheets
8. bake in a 375f preheated oven until edges of cookies are brown but an area about 1 inch wide in the center is still pale , about 10 minutes
9. if using 2 pans in 1 oven , switch positions at half-time
10. let cookies cool on pan about 5 minutes , then transfer to racks with a spatula
11. serve warm or cool
demonstrations.review: Excellent! The very concise instructions were a great help! I had to use margarine, since I did not have butter in the house, but they still come out very well-chewy and gooey-just the way I like them! I will be making these often!

target.recipe_text:
tilapia al ajillo  garlic tilapia

you can do this with any white fish, sea bass is great this way. fish is often served this way in the canary islands, though usually it is the whole fish instead of fillets. yum!

1. season tilapia fillets with salt and pepper
2. heat oil in a skillet over medium heat
3. put fillets in first , and when they start to turn color a bit add garlic slices
4. continue cooking about 4 minutes or so , then flip fillets
5. fry until cooked through , and fish flakes easily with a fork-- this will depend entirely on the thickness of your fillets , so you will need to watch them carefully
6. the garlic should turn a dark golden brown , but not be burned , if you notice that the garlic is starting to burn , spoon it over the fish , so it is no longer in contact with the pan
7. serve with freshly squeezed lemon juice and garnish with chopped parsley
target.review: Delicious!! But,so,umm.. I did make a few changes. I used garlic in the jar, as I didn't have any garlic cloves, and I added about 1/4 tsp of cayenne ( I like things spicy ). I also used a sprinkle of Natures Seasons seasoning at the table. Lovely.. I will be taking the leftovers to work, and will make again for my DH soon :)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
grilled bbq bananas with rum

dessert from the grill! simple and sweet!

1. take 4 pieces of foil and coat each with the butter on one side
2. mix the brown sugar , rum and lemon juice in a small bowl
3. coat each banana with the mixture and wrap tightly in the butter lined foil
4. place on the grill for about 15- 20 minutes and enjoy
demonstrations.review:
Well.. The flavor was wonderful, but unfortunatly, we just couldnt quite get around the texture :o\ (my MIL isn't much on fruit that soft, and the texture was unfortunatly too close to the over cooked veggies I had to eat as a child)
 As this is not Oolala's fault by any means,and the flavor is divine (how could it not be?), we didn't want to lower her rating just cause we weren't expecting mushy textured banana's, lol (silly, I know - if they are soft to begin with, they'll get softer as they cook..). 
 Since we really like the flavor, I am saving the remaining 2 bananas, and using them in my favorite banana nut bread tomorrow (and they would be great in banana pudding, too :).
 Thank you for submitting, Oolala :)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
my  best ever  breadmaker pizza dough

this is 

1. measure all ingredients except cornmeal into bread pan in order listed
2. select dough setting
3. remove dough to lightly floured surface and cover with plastic wrap
4. let rise in a warm place for 30 minutes
5. sprinkle cornmeal on large 16 inch pizza pan or on a pizza stone and press dough into pizza shape
6. cover with a towel and let rise for another 30 minutes
7. spread with desired sauce , seasonings and toppings
8. bake at 425f for 20-30 minutes
9. i like to partially bake the pizza on a pan for about 8 minutes and then transfer it to a hot pizza stone sprinkled with the cornmeal for the remainder of the cooking time
10. i find by baking it initially on the pan it is easier to transfer to a pizza stone thus maintaining its large size
demonstrations.review: Great recipe, my families favorite for pizza dough, when we have the time (it takes 2 batches for my horde, lol). Has a wonderful flavor, easy to work with, and hasn't disappointed us yet. We like to add 1/3 to 1/2 cup grated hard cheese of choice (asiago, parm, etc) during the dough cycle :)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
garlic lime chicken

from leanne ely's book, saving dinner (fall). serve with garlic mashed potatoes, steamed broccoli, or baked sweet potatoes.  the seasonings are relatively mild. you could probably safely add any seasoning left over after sprinkling breasts to the pan without it being too spicy.

1. on a plate , mix together first seven ingredients
2. sprinkle mixture on both sides of chicken breasts
3. in a skillet heat butter and olive oil together over medium-high heat
4. saute chicken until golden brown and done through
5. remove chicken and add lime juice and chicken broth to the pan , whisking up the browned bits off the bottom of the pan
6. keep cooking until sauce has reduced slightly
7. add chicken back to the pan to thoroughly cover and serve
demonstrations.review: This was awesome! my 12 y/o loved it( helped me fix it, actually ), and we both thought that the sauce made a great counterpoint to the spices. It's not too spicy, although if your mouth is extremely sensative, you might find it a bit much. The only problem that we had was uneven chicken pieces - that will be simple enough to fix next time. Will definatly make for my husband when he comes back off deployment! :)

target.recipe_text:
peanut butter chocolate chunk cookies

these are impossible to stop eating.

1. cream the butter and peanut butter together until fully incorporated
2. add the sugars and cream on medium speed
3. add the egg and vanilla and mix until completely incorporated
4. add the flour and baking soda , mix until no white remains , then add the chocolate and mix on low just until everything comes together
5. drop by teaspoonfuls onto parchment-lined baking sheets
6. bake at 350 for 9 minutes or until golden brown
target.review: These were really good!  I used my scoop (which is about a heaping tablespoon), so got 30 cookies.  Baked for 12 minutes, let cool on baking sheet for a few minutes - and they were perfect.  Definitely will add this to my keeper file.  Thanks for posting PetitFour!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
all the frills egg sandwiches

like having an omelet sandwich--yum

1. beat eggs
2. add onions , ham and seasonings
3. mix well
4. cook over medium heat
5. as mixture begins to set , draw in to center with your pancake turner till all is set
6. turn and cook for a very short time and then cut into 4ths
7. put each serving on a piece of buttered toast and top with another slice of toast
8. serve at once
demonstrations.review: This is almost identical to one of my favorite low cost, quick meals. I almost always add cheese (because I add cheese to everything)  Thanks for posting Darlene.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mini ham quiches

very versatile; you can replace the ham with bacon, sausage, chicken or shrimp or substitute chopped onion, red pepper or zucchini for the olives.  from taste of home magazine.

1. in a bowl , combine the ham , cheddar cheese and olives
2. divide among 12 greased muffin cups
3. in a mixing bowl , combine the remaining ingredients just until blended
4. pour over ham mixture
5. bake at 375 for 20-25 minutes or until a knife inserted near the center comes out clean
6. let stand for 5 minutes before serving
demonstrations.review: These were really good! I work as a cook at a homeless shelter. We had a breakfast/tour this morning for potential contributors. I was to provide a light breakfast. I made 24 ham and swiss, 24 sausage and pepper jack and 24 asparagus and cheddar. I served with fruit salad and bagels/cream cheese. I had to print out several copies of your recipe. They loved them!  — Apr 20, 2006

demonstrations.recipe_text:
excellent carrot cake

chock full of flavor, this is the best carrot cake! it tastes even better the next day after the flavors meld. a tad more time consuming than the average carrot cake, but well worth it!

1. combine first 5 ingredients
2. beat well
3. mix flour , soda , salt and cinnamon
4. add to creamed mixture
5. stir well
6. add carrots , walnuts , pineapple and coconut
7. stir well
8. pour batter into greased and floured 13x9 baking pan
9. bake at 350 for 55 minutes , or until pick comes out clean
10. buttermilk glaze: combine first 5 ingredients in large saucepan
11. bring to a boil
12. cook 4 minutes on medium heat
13. remove from heat
14. add vanilla
15. pour buttermilk glaze over warm cake
16. let cake cool
17. cream cheese frosting: mix cream cheese and butter
18. beat until smooth
19. gradually add sugar , beating until light and fluffy
20. stir in vanilla
21. spread cream cheese frosting on top of cooled cake
demonstrations.review: Made this for my mom's 86th birthday (she requested carrot cake)...she loved it and so did the rest of the family.  I did add a cup of raisins to the cake and the juice of one lemon to the frosting - otherwise followed the recipe exactly. Great recipe Inez, definitely a keeper!

target.recipe_text:
mexican enchilada sauce

i got this recipe from by grmil who was born and raised in mexico city. the secret to its flavor is the cocoa

1. combine all dry ingredients in a small bowl
2. stirring constantly , slowly add enough of the water to make a thin paste
3. pour into pan and add rest of water
4. cook over medium heat , stirring constantly , until mixture thickens
5. stir in tomato sauce
6. use in your favorite enchilada recipe
7. the amounts on the ingredients are very flexible
8. for instance , if i am feeding my kids who do not like"spicy" , i will halve the chili powder and double the tomato sauce
9. experiment to suit your taste , but don't leave out the cocoa
10. for a quick meal , we will soften a corn tortilla in a bit of hot oil , drag it through the sauce , and lay it flat on a plate
11. cover it with grated cheddar cheese , sprinkle with chopped onions and sliced black olives
12. then cover with another softened sauced tortilla and melt the cheese in the microwave for 1 minute on high
target.review: This sauce was really good.  It sure beats the expensive cans of preservative and sodium filled sauce at the store!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
banana bread ii

nan

1. preheat oven to 350
2. spray a 9 x 5 loaf pan with non-stick cooking spray
3. combine flour , baking powder , baking soda and cinnamon and set aside
4. in a large bowl , whisk together applesauce , sugar , egg whites , banana and vanilla
5. add flour mixture all at once and stir gently to blend
6. pour batter into prepared loaf pan and bake for 50-60 minutes or until knife inserted comes out clean
7. cool bread completely before slicing
demonstrations.review: My husband and I have been on the search for a banana bread recipe that doesn't come out gooey on the top, and this recipe is what we have been looking for!  I love how low fat it is.  To cut down on the sugar, I put in 1/2 cup of a sugar/splenda mix instead of the 1 cup sugar.  Also, I used 1/2 cup egg whites from a carton instead of separating three eggs and wasting the yolk.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
lebanese lentil rice pilaf with blackened onions

this recipe first appeared as part of a "meatless week-night meal" in the november, 2003 bon appetit. originally posted by mean chef.  vegans can omit the yogurt.

1. heat 2 tablespoons oil in large saucepan over medium-high heat
2. add chopped onion and next 4 ingredients
3. saut until onion softens , about 4 minutes
4. add broth and lentils
5. bring to boil
6. reduce heat to medium-low and simmer , covered , 10 minutes
7. stir in rice
8. return to boil
9. reduce heat to medium-low
10. cover and cook until liquid is absorbed and rice and lentils are tender , about 15 minutes longer
11. meanwhile , heat 2 tablespoons oil in heavy large skillet over medium-high heat
12. add sliced onions
13. saut until soft and beginning to blacken , about 20 minutes
14. season pilaf to taste with salt and pepper
15. transfer to plates
16. top with blackened onions
17. place tomatoes and cucumber alongside
18. top pilaf with dollop of yogurt
19. sprinkle with mint
demonstrations.review: Wow, this was absolutely delicious! I used chicken broth instead of vegetable, and a wild rice mixture instead of the white rice, but didn't change anything else.  I was sad when I got full, because I wanted to eat more!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
fava bean salad

a fresh spring-time salad with pronounced mediterranean flavours.

1. combine fava beans , chopped cucumber , tomato , olives , red onion , romaine , and parsley in a bowl
2. for the dressing , combine olive oil , red wine vinegar , water , and the remainder of the spices in a lidded jar
3. shake jar until dressing ingredients are thoroughly mixed
4. pour dressing over salad and mix ingredients until well coated
5. refrigerate at least 1 hour before serving
6. serve salad on top of extra romaine or butter lettuce leaves for an attractive presentation
7. makes 4 main dish or 6 side-dish servings
8. variations on a theme: if fava beans are not available or not in season , substitute 2 cups cooked cannellini or great northern white beans in the recipe
demonstrations.review: Wow, this was so good that I'll be making it two times in one week!

target.recipe_text:
tastes like apple pie apple squares

from my favourite church cookbook, where all the recipes are tried and true!  **like most of the reviews state, if you don't want to fight with the pastry to make it fit a cookie sheet - make 1.5x the dough recipe or use a smaller pan.

1. mix flour and salt and cut in shortening
2. add egg and milk mixture and mix till it forms a ball
3. divide dough in half
4. roll first half in 17 x 12 inch rectangle
5. place in cookie sheet and bring pastry up sides
6. cover pastry with apples and sprinkle with sugar and cinnamon
7. roll out second half of dough and place on top of apples
8. moisten edges with milk and pinch together
9. beat egg white until stiff and brush on crust
10. bake at 400f for 1 hour
11. mix glaze ingredients together and brush on crust
12. this square freezes beautifully
target.review:
Very yummy and easy to make for someone like me who is not skilled at making pie-crust. I made extra dough (per suggestions) and used a 9x13 inch pan. I did reduce the sugar a little since I had very sweet apples.   
It turned out very wet though, I had to take the juices out with a turkey baster. Maybe next time I'll dredge the apple slices in flour first or add cornflakes like someone else suggested.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
jam bars

these are so good.  fast and easy too.  they are very versatile, any jam will work but our personal favorite is raspberry.

1. place dry ingredients in a bowl
2. stir in oats and sugar
3. cut in margarine until crumbly
4. pat 2 / 3 of crumbs in a 11 by 17 inch pan
5. spread with jam and top with remaining crumbs
6. bake at 375 for about 45 minutes
7. cool and cut into bars
demonstrations.review: Both very yummy and very simple to make! I used a jar of pineapple/apricot preserves (which no one wanted to eat by itself) and every bite disappeared.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
sauteed fennel

this recipe came from the foodtv.com kitchens

1. heat a medium saute pan over medium-high heat until just smoking
2. add the oil , garlic , fennel , and start tossing , to coat fennel in oil
3. season with salt and pepper , to taste
4. as the fennel starts to caramelize , add a splash of water to steam for 1 minute
5. remove from the heat
demonstrations.review: Quick & easy to prepare. I kept adding water & letting it cook off, since I like it a bit softer. My picky toddler even ate some!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
banana banana bread

why compromise the banana flavor? my banana bread is moist and delicious with loads of banana flavor! ultimate comfort food, and it's wonderful toasted!! (make sure to use bananas with a lot of black on them for the best flavor! the blacker the bananas, the stronger the banana flavor of the bread.)

1. preheat oven to 350
2. lightly grease 9 x 5 loaf pan
3. in large bowl , combine flour , soda and salt
4. in separate bowl , cream together butter and brown sugar
5. stir in eggs and mashed bananas until well blended
6. stir banana mixture into flour mixture
7. stir just to moisten
8. pour batter into prepared loaf pan
9. bake in preheated oven for 60-65 minutes until a toothpick inserted into center of loaf comes out clean
10. let bread cool in pan for 10 minutes , then turn out onto a wire rack
demonstrations.review: A "classic" banana bread with a good, moist texture. I added a handful of chocolate chips and dried cranberries and it turned out nice.

target.recipe_text:
creamy burrito casserole

satisfy your craving for something different tonight. it's good and fairly easy. this is stuff i usually have on hand too.

1. brown ground meat / turkey & onion
2. drain
3. add taco seasoning and stir in refried beans
4. mix soup and sour cream in a separate bowl
5. spread 1 / 2 sour cream mixture in the bottom of a casserole dish
6. tear up 3 tortillas and spread over sour cream mixture
7. put 1 / 2 the meat bean mixture over that
8. add a layer of cheese
9. you could put some hot sauce on this now
10. repeat the layers
11. sprinkle cheese over the top and bake , uncovered , at 350f for 20-30 minutes
