target.review: HIts the spot.  I was looking for something to use up some cooked ground turkey meat and refried beans.  This was just satisfying and yummy and simple enough for my daughter to prepare and have ready for a weeknight meal.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mexican quinoa casserole

a very healthy alternative to a pasta casserole!  mostly hands off once everything is mixed, and yet another way to use the latest super food!

1. 1
2. preheat oven to 400 degrees farenheit
3. 2
4. in a large bowl , mix together the first seven ingredients , tomatoes through quinoa
5. 3
6. pour into a 2 quart baking dish and cover with foil
7. bake for 30 minutes
8. remove from oven and stir
9. replace foil and bake another 30 minutes
10. 4
11. while quinoa mixture is baking , prepare ground beef with taco seasoning and water
12. simmer until water has evaporated
13. 5
14. when quinoa mixture has finished baking , remove from oven and fluff with a fork
15. stir in taco seasoning beef
16. top with cheddar cheese and run under broiler until cheese is melted and bubbling
17. 6
18. serve with optional sour cream , chopped cilantro and lime juice squeezed over
demonstrations.review: With a dubious family, I made this as part of my attempt at removing starching rice from some of our meals and using more quinoa.  And it was a huge hit.  The flavor with seasoning the beef was probably a big part of it but even more so was topping with a creamy ranch dressing I made with buttermilk and fat free sour cream   seasonings and avocado.  I toasted the quinoa ahead of time and then it was simply a matter of mixing up the beans, corn and tomatos to throw it in the oven while the meat was cooking.  I could easily see this as a vegetarian dish if you sub'd in lentils in place of the beef.  Next time I may try some ground Turkey and see how that tastes.  Definitely a keeper.  And it was quick enough for a weekday if you needed something ready to go.  Wonder how it would do in a crock pot and melt the cheese on it at the end?

demonstrations.recipe_text:
the best chicken tortilla soup

i'm in love with this soup!! a very good friend of mine made this for me recently and i fell in love. i'm very picky about my tortilla soup and this by far the best ever. she makes hers in the crock pot and i have to agree, that it's easy and tastes just wonderful!! whatever you do, do not skip the garnishes! they are the icing on the cake! update april 2010:  obviously i've made this so many times i never even look at the recipe anymore!  but i wanted to add some variations that i play around with that are great.  like many reviewers black beans and corn are great additions.  sometimes i add them to the leftovers (if there are any :-) so that is feels like something new the next day!  i have also made it several times with shredded pork which turns it into a pork carnitas type of soup.  if you like it on the spicy and smoke side buy a can of chipotle peppers in adobo sauce and mince up one or two and add it.  and lastly, a little swizzle of half and half or heavy cream just minutes before serving makes it a creamy tortilla soup that is wonderful and it is also a good way to tone down the heat if it got away from you...

1. throw everything except the garnishes in your crock pot and let it cook on high for 5-6 hours
2. dress with garnishes and give it a squeeze of lime and you're good to go !
3. enjoy !
4. if you are not using a crock pot , saute the garlic and onion in 2 tablespoons olive oil before adding the remaining ingredients
5. simmer for at least an hour so that the flavors mix together
demonstrations.review: Our traditional New Years recipe is a new soup and this was great.  A little more spicy for some to eat a bunch so I'll cut down on the chili powder next time.  Only changes was I left out the tabasco sauce as I didn't have any on hand and I used a 32oz of broth box and didn't add more since it was soupy enough.  To use what was available, we just thru in frozen chicken tenders and then shredded them once they were cooked through and simmered some more. Next time around I'm going to thicken it up with corn and beans per what some other reviewers have done.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crock pot chicken with black beans   cream cheese

i love this crock-pot chicken recipe for two reasons: one, my family loves it and two, it is so easy to make! i got this recipe from my sister. she has two children of her own, and they love it too! it's also the best leftovers in the world -- if there are any!

1. take 4-5 frozen , yes , frozen , boneless chicken breasts put into crock pot
2. add 1 can of black beans , drained , 1 jar of salsa , 1 can of corn drained
3. keep in crock pot on high for about 4-5 hours or until chicken is cooked
4. add 1 package of cream cheese and let sit for about 1 / 2 hour
5. all done and enjoy !
demonstrations.review: Really enjoyed it.  It's a winner for a weekday meal; easy to put together in the AM and dive into in the PM.  I used frozen chicken thighs because that's what I had. It turned out juicier than I thought it would but over rice it was no problem.  It wouldn't have worked wrapped in a tortilla.

target.recipe_text:
chicken fried steak w cream gravy

this is a recipe for chicken fried steak, one of the staple foods of texas. like with fried chicken, folks in each family or restaurant tend to have their own little "secrets" to preparing chicken fried steak, so you can play with the recipe a bit. but if it don't include the cream gravy, it ain't been prepared right and it ain't a "secret" worth keeping.

1. heat about 1 / 4-1 / 2 inch of oil or shortening in a frying pan
2. beat eggs then combine with milk
3. dredge tenderized beef cutlets in flour , then egg-milk wash , then a second time in flour
4. place dredged cutlets into heated oil and fry until golden , about 10 minutes
5. turn steak over and cook for another 5 minutes or so until both sides are golden
6. remove to a plate lined with paper towels and allow to drain
7. time to make the gravy: drain all but 1-2 tablespoons of drippings from the frying pan
8. leave all the cooked bits you can
9. combine flour and seasonings with milk , then pour into the pan with drippings and bits
10. continually stir / whisk the gravy over medium heat for 10-15 minutes , or until desired consistency
11. taste and add more salt or pepper if necessary
12. serve generously over each piece of chicken fried steak
13. sop up any extra gravy with a biscuit
target.review: This was so fast to make for dinner and inexpensive too. I only used one egg and 2/3 cup of milk for my egg wash. It was enough to coat 4 minute steaks. My daughter just loved this and she never eats meat so this was great.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
japanese mum s chicken

we have a japanese girl, tomoko, living with us, and tonight she and i cooked a japanese dinner for us and her friends. she phoned her mum,toshiko, in japan for this, as it's her favourite recipe, and i wanted to share it here. it's simple and so good, and tomoko, who is only 16, did such a good job of cooking this, then translating the recipe to english for me.

*the liquid will thicken to a glaze if you are patient. it just takes a bit of time. if you feel your chicken is cooked (and going to overcook) remove it before going on to reduce the liquid. same thing, if you must use breast meat, remove it (so it doesn't dry out) and continue reducing the liquid . if you do it this way rather than thickening with cornstarch you will get a richer glaze and not need to add stock or broth instead of the water. it just takes patience. and note: a glaze is sticky and coats the meat, this is not a sauce.

1. place all the ingredients in a saucepan over a high heat
2. bring to the boil , then reduce to a simmer for about 20 minutes
3. remove any scum that rises to the surface
4. increase the heat , turning the drumsticks frequently in the liquid , and cook until the liquid has reduced to a sticky glaze
5. arrange the chicken on a serving platter , remove the garlic clove and chili from the liquid , and spoon the glaze over
demonstrations.review: This was very simple to make. My whole family loved the flavor.  I have added this to my freezer menu.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
watermelon and feta salad

the saltyness of the feta brings out the flavor and sweetness of watermelon beautifully.

1. in a large bowl , combine the watermelon , feta , and black pepper to taste
2. add red pepper flakes if you like
3. serve immediately
demonstrations.review: Made this for my PAC 2006.  The flavor was amazing.  I love the spicy zing you get after the sweetness of the melon.  Great salad to serve with a BBQ chicken.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
creamy burrito casserole

satisfy your craving for something different tonight. it's good and fairly easy. this is stuff i usually have on hand too.

1. brown ground meat / turkey & onion
2. drain
3. add taco seasoning and stir in refried beans
4. mix soup and sour cream in a separate bowl
5. spread 1 / 2 sour cream mixture in the bottom of a casserole dish
6. tear up 3 tortillas and spread over sour cream mixture
7. put 1 / 2 the meat bean mixture over that
8. add a layer of cheese
9. you could put some hot sauce on this now
10. repeat the layers
11. sprinkle cheese over the top and bake , uncovered , at 350f for 20-30 minutes
demonstrations.review: This was great.  I froze the leftovers in single serving containers and everyone has been loving them for quick lunches.

target.recipe_text:
barb s gingerbread biscotti

these biscotti are great for "dunking" in a cup of tea or a glass of milk. friends will love these, great as a gift. low fat, diabetic exchange: 1 starch

1. in a large bowl , combine the first seven ingredients
2. in another bowl , combine the egg and egg whites , brown sugar , molasses and vanilla until smooth
3. stir the egg mixture into dry ingredients just until moistened
4. fold in pecans and currants
5. cover and refrigerate for 30 minutes
6. divide dough in half
7. shape each half into a ball
8. on a baking sheet coated with nonstick cooking spray , roll each ball into a 14-inch x 1 1 / 2-inch rectangle
9. bake at 325 for 24 to 28 minutes or until frim to touch
10. remove from the oven and reduce heat to 300 degrees
11. cool for 5 minutes , transfer to cutting board
12. cut diagonally with a serrated knife into 1 / 2-inch slices
13. place cut side down on baking sheets coated with nonstick cooking spray
14. bake for 15 to 20 minutes or until lightly browned turning once , remove to wire racks to cool , store in an airtight container
target.review: I made these for an Election Day bake sale at my son's school, and the PTG president asked me for the recipe!  I omitted the dried currants and pecans because I didn't have any on hand, and I drizzled the biscotti with white chocolate.  Delicious dunked in coffee!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chocolate crinkles

although these aren't exactly the recipe we used at cookies by design (it would be wrong for me to give that out), it's very close and they taste exactly the same: absolutely wonderful! :) and so easy to make, too! my husband made these last year for his annual cookie tin gifts, and they were very popular.  makes about 72 cookies.  these are different from most of the recipes you’ll find for chocolate crinkles in that they use cocoa powder rather than baking chocolate or liquid forms of chocolate (kind of nice, actually... no messy melted chocolate all over the kitchen! *chuckle*).

1. in a medium bowl , mix together the cocoa powder , sugar , and vegetable oil
2. beat in eggs one at a time , then stir in the vanilla
3. in another bowl combine the flour , baking powder , and salt
4. stir flour mixture into the cocoa mixture
5. cover dough bowl with plastic wrap , put in refrigerator , and chill for at least 4 hours
6. preheat oven to 350 degrees f
7. line cookie sheets with parchment paper
8. roll the dough into one inch balls
9. coat each ball in powdered sugar before placing onto parchment-lined cookie sheets
10. bake in preheated 350 degrees f oven for 10 to 12 minutes
11. let the cooked cookies stand on the cookie sheet for at least 1 minute before transferring to wire racks to cool
demonstrations.review: These cookies taste so good!  The dough/batter is a little difficult to work with because it's sticky but they are so divine once cooked that it's worth it.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
snickerdoodle biscotti

so yummy and quite healthy: 84 calories each, 1 g of fat. from cooking light's november 2000 issue (my favorite issue)

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees f
2. measure flour into a large bowl using the scoop and level method
3. add 1 cup sugar , baking powder and salt
4. mix oil , vanilla and whole eggs in a small bowl , and add to the large bowl
5. turn dough out onto a floured surface and knead 7 or 8 times
6. divide in half
7. shape each portion into a roll about 8 inches long , and place them six or so inches apart on a cookie sheet lined with parchment
8. flatten each roll to 1 inch thick
9. combine the 2 tablespoons sugar and cinnamon , then gently brush the tops of the rolls with the egg white and sprinkle with cinnamon sugar
10. bake at 350 for 30 minutes
11. remove from the sheet and cool for 15 minutes
12. cut diagonally into 1 / 2 inch slices and lay them cut sides down on the cookie sheet again
13. reduce oven temp to 325 degrees f and then bake 10 more minutes , turn over and bake 10 more
14. they'll be soft in the middle but will harden as they cool
15. cool completely on a wire rack
demonstrations.review: I made these for an Election Day bake sale and they sold out!  I dipped one side of the cookies in melted chocolate.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
white velvet cutout cookies

this is in response to a request. the recipe is from the taste of home magazine. it is a cream cheese cutout cookie.  frost with recipe #48001.

1. in a mixing bowl , cream butter and cream cheese until light and fluffy
2. add sugar , egg yolks and vanilla: mix well
3. gradually add flour
4. cover and chill 2 hours or until firm
5. preheat oven to 350f
6. roll out on a lightly floured surface to 1 / 4-inch thickness
7. cut into 3-inch shapes
8. place 1 inch apart on greased baking sheets
9. bake for 10-12 minutes or until set
10. cool for 5 minutes
11. remove to wire racks to continue cooling
12. frost after completely cool with white velvet buttercream cookie frosting
demonstrations.review: Fantastic cookies and the dough is so easy to work with!  I divide my dough onto pieces of plastic wrap, then flatten them to about 1/2 inch thickness.  This way they only need to chill about an hour.

target.recipe_text:
puff pastry cheese stick appetizers

these are quick, fabulous, and definitely a crowd pleaser :) hope you enjoy them! they will keep in a tightly covered container for about 4 days, but they are best served right from the oven. instead of using the herbs you can also try this recipe using poppy seeds or caraway seeds!

1. preheat your oven to 400f
2. then take a bowl , and a cheese grater and grate cheese into the bowl , or in the food processor
3. add your herbs , garlic powder , pepper and sesame seeds to the cheese , and stir to combine
4. beat eggs in a long baking dish
5. dip both sides of defrosted dough in the beaten eggs and dredge it lightly in the cheese mixture
6. then take the seasoned sheets of dough and place them on sheets of wax paper
7. using a pastry wheel , cut dough into 6x1 inch strips
8. then take those strips , and twist each of them into spiral shapes and place about 1 inch apart from one another on a foil-lined baking sheet
9. bake your cheese sticks in the oven and bake for approximately 15 minutes
10. using a wide spatula , carefully remove from pan and serve
target.review: These were very good. I served them with mussels, but next time I will serve them when my husband makes his fabulous Bolognese Sauce.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
the very best salisbury steak

this is our favorite salisbury steak recipe. i always make enough extra sauce to serve over potatoes. tastes like it took all day to cook.

1. in a large bowl , mix together 1 / 3 cup condensed french onion soup with ground beef , bread crumbs , egg , salt and black pepper
2. shape into 6 oval patties
3. in a large skillet over medium-high heat , brown both sides of patties
4. pour off excess fat
5. in a small bowl , blend flour and remaining soup until smooth
6. mix in ketchup , water , worcestershire sauce and mustard powder
7. pour over meat in skillet
8. cover , and cook for 20 minutes , stirring occasionally
demonstrations.review: Oh boy, did we love this.The only thing I changed was the soup. I couldn't find "french onion soup" so I used Campell's fat free Vegetable Broth with Onions. So freakin' delicious. I will be passing this one around!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
failproof french bread  bread machine

this makes two loaves of long baguette type french bread that has wonderful flavor and is so easy to make!

1. place ingredients in bread machine according to manufacturers directions
2. start machine on dough setting
3. when dough cycle is complete , remove dough with floured hands and cut in half on floured surface
4. take each half of dough and roll to make a loaf about 12 inches long in the shape of french bread
5. place on greased baking sheet and cover with a towel
6. let rise until doubled , about 1 hour
7. preheat oven to 450
8. bake for 15 to 20 minutes or until golden brown , turning pan around once halfway during baking
9. remove baked loaves to wire racks to cool
demonstrations.review: What can I say? We are going to fondue tonight, New Years Eve, and I made this recipe. Well, absolutely fabulous! Thank you for posting...

demonstrations.recipe_text:
south beach  stuffed bell peppers

this is a recipe i made up when i was in phase 1 of the south beach diet. my kids have begun to request it for supper!

1. wash the peppers , cut the tops off , and place in oiled glass dish
2. cover and microwave the peppers for 5 minutes
3. saute the veggies and ground turkey with a dollop of olive oil
4. add the tomatoes and seasonings
5. cook for 3-4 minutes to evaporate some of the liquid
6. stuff the peppers and top with cheese
7. bake at 350 for 10 minutes or until the peppers are soft and the cheese is toasted
8. add ins: you could add cooked rice or stir in extra cheese to the mixture before baking
demonstrations.review: We absolutely loved these stuffed peppers! Made them exactly as the recipe said except I hade no Spike seasoning so I had to improvise. :) We will absolutely be making these again...

target.recipe_text:
my family s favorite sloppy joes  pizza joes

i've tried many recipes, this is the best. i once 'dec-tupled' (10x) this recipe to sell sandwiches at a craft fair at my church. people were waiting in line to buy leftovers. freezes well, goes up to the lake or camping well and is a hit on halloween...it's no-fail. easy to double, triple, etc. i've been making joes this way for over 20 years.
***03-08-09, i just reinvented this recipe tonight when i went to make it for dinner and found i didn't have an 8-oz. can of tomato sauce (shame on me).  the family was upset with me when i subbed an 8-oz. can of pizza sauce and told them to suck it up and call them 'pizza joes' and then served them up with shredded mozzarella cheese on the toasted buns, top and bottom.  they loved it.  i left out the bbq sauce in this preparation and just used a 1/2 cup ketchup.  pizza joes are good to go!

1. in a large skillet , brown ground beef , celery and onion
2. drain the fat , who needs it ?
3. stir in remaining ingredients , simmer covered , 15-20 minutes , stirring occasionally
4. if joes appear too'loose' , leave cover off and let moisture evaporate
5. cook until it's the consistency you like for serving on toasted buns , with french fries and cole slaw
target.review: I had never had Sloppy Joe's before, and my BF had requested them for dinner. This recipe struck my eye because of the variety of ingredients in it. The first couple I had seen seemed kind of bland looking.I loved them. I will prbably use a different BBQ sauce then I did last time, but all together I thought they were great. I followed the recipe exactly.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
greek potatoes  oven roasted and delicious

these potatoes are a staple in our home. whether accompanying roast lamb or chicken, or just on their own, we have them a couple of times a week. they are delicious and the ones that get overly-brown in the pan and stick a bit are mine!  clean up is a little tricky with this recipe, unless you line your pans with foil, but i find that just filling the pan up with hot, sudsy water and forgetting for an hour (something i apparently have no problem doing ;-)) helps a lot.

1. preheat oven to 420f a reviewer has suggested spraying the baking pan with pam - that sounds like a great idea !
2. put all the ingredients into a baking pan large enough to hold them
3. season generously with sea salt and black pepper
4. make sure your hands are very clean and put them in the pan and give everything a toss to distribute
5. the garlic will drop into the water / oil solution but its flavour will permeate the potatoes , and this way , it won't burn
6. bake for 40 minutes
7. when a nice golden-brown crust has formed on the potatoes , give them a stir to bring the white underside up , season lightly with a bit more sea salt and pepper and just a light sprinkling of oregano
8. add 1 / 2 cup more water if pan appears to be getting dry , and pop back into oven to brown other side of potatoes
9. this will take about another 40 minutes
10. do not be afraid of overcooking the potatoes- they will be delicious
demonstrations.review:
These were so tasty - crispy on the outside buttery soft on the inside, and full of flavour all the way though!! The lemon is fantastic!

Changes I made: I used unpeeled red potatoes and I added about 2 tsp (approx) liquid chicken bouillon.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
blueberry lime jam

from the ball blue book, this is a yummy jam! cook time is estimated.

1. crush blueberries one layer at a time
2. combine crushed blueberries and pectin in a large saucepot
3. bring to a boil , stirring frequently
4. add sugar , stirring until dissolved
5. stir in grated lime peel and lime juice
6. return to a rolling boil
7. boil hard 1 minute , stirring constantly
8. remove from heat
9. skim foam if necessary
10. ladle hot jam into hot jars , leaving 1 / 4-inch headspace
11. adjust two-piece caps
12. process 15 minutes in a boiling water canner
13. yield: about 6 half-pints
demonstrations.review:
This was excellent!

I made this recipe using wild blueberries we picked one afternoon. This was my first attempt at making jam, and I hit a few obstacles along the way (canning rack broke, ran out to buy a new one and then it didn't fit. Bought the wrong type of pectin, had to go to the store again! etc) but the end result was worth the running around! I loved the subtle lime taste you get from the lime zest. I added a little more blueberries to use up some of what I had and added a small amount more sugar just to balance. Everyone who has tried it has loved it!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
oven fried zucchini chips

these are so tasty.
points 1.

1. cut zucchini into 1 / 4 inch thick slices
2. set aside
3. combine egg substitute and italian dressing in a small bowl , stir well
4. combine bread crumbs ,
5. parmesan cheese and pepper in a small bowl
6. stir well
7. dip zucchini in egg mixture , dredge in bread crumb mixture
8. place zucchini on a baking sheet coated with cooking spray
9. bake at 475 degrees for 5 minutes , turn and bake an additional 5 minutes or until golden
10. serve immediately
demonstrations.review:
I made these last night. I loved the flavour but the coating peeled off most of them when they were served. Next time I will let the zucchini sit longer to get the water out of them after they are sliced. 
 I also made a few slight changes. For the coating I used half bread crumbs, half cormeal. I didn't have any italian dressing so I used "garlic house" dressing. I also added some chopped parsley to the coating mixture for some colour. Lastly after placing the zucchini on the sprayed cookie sheet I sprayed the zucchini themselves with cooking spray to help them get crispy. In the last few minutes of cooking i placed these under the broiler to really crisp them up! Good recipe!

target.recipe_text:
vegetarian blt

not what you think: no fake bacon in this one!!  even the biggest meat-eaters go for this one.  seriously very very good!!

1. spray a non-stick skillet with plenty of non-stick spray and place the cheese in a single layer in the center
2. heat the skillet over medium heat
3. when the cheese bubbles and is crunchy and hard on the bottom , flip to the other side
4. once both sides of the cheese are crunchy , assemble the sandwich with the lettuce , tomato , and "bacon" , and the mayo spread over the bread
5. enjoy !
target.review: Amazing! I've been a vegetarian for over 20 years. I wish I had known about this a long time ago. Love the crunch it adds. Who knew. Next time I'll try smoked provolone to see how that is.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
potato pierogies

got this recipe from a lovely polish lady i worked with. they are so good!

1. sift flour , mix with salt , butter and eggs
2. add warm milk to make a soft dough
3. roll out dough on floured surface
4. roll to about 1 / 8 inch thickness
5. cut in 2inch squares
6. put 1 t filling on each
7. fold in 1 / 2 to make a triangle
8. pinch edges
9. drop into boiling water until they float
10. drain
11. fry briefly in the butter
demonstrations.review: These were really good.  I found the dough was hard to work with.  I felt like they were too thick.  I made mashed potatoes and added some finely diced onion and sharp white cheddar cheese.  I sauteed in butter and onion.  This is the second time I have made pierogies and after the first time, I swore I wouldn't make them again.  I used a different recipe the first time and will probably use this recipe again when I feel like going to the trouble of making them.  They were good though.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cheesy artichoke cups

these are from the pampered chef recipes from the heart cookbook. they are best served warm.

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. press wonton wrappers into lightly greased mini-muffin cups
3. pat artichoke hearts dry
4. chop and place in medium bowl
5. add mayonnaise , cheese , and garlic
6. mix well
7. stir in olives and bell pepper
8. spoon into prepared muffin cups
9. bake 12-14 minutes or until lightly browned
10. remove from oven
11. cool in pan 2 minutes before carefully removing from pan
12. serve warm
demonstrations.review: These are the best appetizer ever.  I have been making them for years.  Everyone wants the recipe everytime I make them.  They are so delicious you could eat a whole tray!  The filling can be made ahead of time and the cups can be assembled last minute.  I add some hot chopped peppers to mine for some bite.  These are an elegant, classy appetizer and are a snap to make.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
quick spanish rice

great side dish for your mexican fiesta. try with recipe #17130!  it is as good as you'll find in any mexican restaurant.  update:  1 teaspoon cumin was added to original recipe.  i took some of my reviewers suggestion and added 1 teaspoon of cumin to the recipe. they were right. cumin definitely adds to the taste.

1. in medium saucepan , combine all ingredients
2. bring to a boil
3. reduce heat to low
4. cover and simmer 25 minutes or until rice is done
5. garnish with green onions and / or cheddar cheese
demonstrations.review: I have been in search of the right Spanish Rice recipe to go with my enchiladas.  I have tried many and I really like this one, however I made a little change.  I added some chopped onion and green pepper.  I sauteed them with some canola oil first, then added the rice and the rest of the ingredients and cooked as directed.  I may add just a little more spice next time.  I will definitely keep this recipe around.

target.recipe_text:
zucchini chocolate cake

don't you just love it when you can get your daily vegetable requirements from the dessert you eat? and a chocolate dessert at that!

1. cream butter then add oil and sugar
2. mix
3. add next 8 ingredients
4. mix well
5. fold in the chips and nuts by hand
6. put in a greased and floured 9 x 13 pan
7. bake at 325 for 1 hour or until done
target.review: Super moist and oh so good. I made it just as the recipe stated except for the walnuts. My family does not care for walnuts. The 2nd time I made it, I used applesauce instead od the oil. UUUMMM Good. No need for icing on this cake. This recipe is a keeper. Thanks for a great recipe and another way to use up the Zucchini.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
savory pepper steak

a tasty pepper steak, that cooks for 8-10 hours, and makes it very tender.  so good.

1. cut steak into strips
2. combine 1 / 4 cup flour , the salt and pepper
3. toss with steak strips to coat thoroughly
4. add to crock pot with onion , garlic , and half of green pepper strips
5. stir
6. combine tomatoes with beef base , soy sauce and worcestershire sauce
7. pour into crock pot , moistening meat well
8. cover and cook on low for 8-10 hours
9. one hour before serving , turn on high and stir in remaining green pepper strips
10. if thickened gravy is desired , make a smooth paste of 3 tablespooons flour and 3 tablespoons water
11. stir into crock pot
12. cover and cook until thickened
13. serve gravy with pepper steak over fluffy rice
demonstrations.review: Wow this was oh sooo good and easy. I  served it over rice. Great recipe for those busy days. And the round steak was falling apart tender. Thanks for a great recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chicken honey glazed

serve with a green salad and a your favorite rice.

1. dredge chicken in seasoned flour
2. place chicken in a greased baking pan
3. bake 350 degrees for 1 / 2 hour
4. while baking , combine honey , lemon juice , soy sauce and oil
5. remove chicken from oven and drizzle with honey mixture
6. bake another half-hour or 'til desired doneness , basting occasionally
demonstrations.review: We loved this recipe. I changed the lemon juice to orange juice. Chicken did not dry out and made a nice thick coating on the chicken.  I baked it longer than with the syrup and basted it often. Thank you for a great recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
bev s spaghetti sauce

this is a recipe i have developed over a number of years. this is the only spaghetti sauce my family will request! very easy to make. i hope your family enjoys it as much as mine does!

1. brown the ground beef , onion and garlic in olive oil with bay leaves , oregano , basil , italian seasoning , salt and pepper
2. add tomato paste , tomato sauce and diced tomatoes
3. stir well and bring to a simmer over medium heat
4. cover and simmer for 1 1 / 2 hours
5. use sauce to top your cooked spaghetti
6. top with sauteed mushroom
7. pass the parmesan
demonstrations.review: Best Spaghetti I have ever had. Thanks for a great recipe.

target.recipe_text:
sassy s beef and broccoli

this is a great week-day supper. fast and delicious! we always have this with a big bowl of rice, and everyone just loves it - even the kids! you can add any other veggies that your family likes!

1. marinate steak in mixture of 1 / 2 of water , soya sauce , sugar , vinegar , garlic , ginger and cornstarch
2. drain well , reserving marinade
3. heat oil in wok or skillet
4. add steak and brown
5. add broccoli and onion
6. cook at medium-high heat , stirring for 1 minutes
7. add remaining water , cover and steam for 3-4 minutes until broccoli is tender-crisp
8. add marinade and cook until sauce is hot and thick
target.review: I donâ€™t normally donâ€™t put beef and broccoli on my plate when I go to a Chinese Buffet. So I ask my wife.  She said this is very good and give it 5 stars. It did need more cornstarch. Next time we make it we will add a heaping tablespoon of cornstarch to it. The sauce never thicken up for us and we did not want to wilt the broccoli.  It tasted very good!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
sourdough  bread starter

this is your basic sour dough bread starter to be used over and over again. look for the sour dough bread recipe to make use of this starter.
there are two ways to make sour dough starter one without yeast where you feed the starter daily and this recipe where you just let the yeast do the work and  let it sit for 3 or 4 days. be sure that you clean the jar well before putting the saved starter back in it.

1. dissolve yeast in 1 / 2 cup warm water , rest for ten minutes
2. mix in flour , sugar& remaining water
3. allow to stand , loosely covered , in a warm place for 3 or 4 days
4. use a large bowl as it will rise considerably
5. every time the batter is used to make a product set aside 1 cup to be used as a"starter" for another batch
6. keep covered in the fridge
7. to make it into a basic batter again , add another 2 cups flour& 2 cups warm water and allow to stand at room temp overnight it is now ready to use , but again reserve a cup of the starter
demonstrations.review: It worked real good. Thanks for the recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
yummy crispy baked fish

easy and healthier way to get crispy tasty fish. note: you must use the right pan! please be sure to use a broiler pan so the breading gets hot air on the bottom too and isn't soggy on the bottom when you go to turn it. or use a cooling rack on a cookie sheet. do not use a pan with sides as that will steam the fish, not make it crispy. i have never had the breading fall off using the correct methods. if you don't care for cornmeal use panko. 

i have used mostly mild whitefish like catfish or tilapia with great results. don't be scared by the number of ingredients—it is mostly spices and herbs. please adjust the spices, especially salt, to your taste. i have tried to post a balanced blend here but feel free to adjust mild, spicy, lower sodium etc...

1. mix milk , vinegar and mustard and let set for 15 minutes
2. this will make a mustardy , buttermilky dressing to coat the fish
3. in a separate bowl mix cornmeal or panko with all the seasonings
4. dip fish fillets in the milk mixture and then in the dry mixture
5. spray broiling pan with cooking spray or brush with a little olive oil
6. place fillets on prepared pan and place pan under broiler 4 inches from heat
7. broil for 4 minutes per side or until fish flakes easily with a fork
8. serve with lemon wedges if desired
demonstrations.review: This was excellent we really enjoyed it.  Like fish sticks for grownups and we used cod. This is a keeper and thanks for posting it.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pb rice  krispies squares

we made these tonight, bet they won't last till tomorrow! i hunted for a recipe here, and gasp, there wasn't one!?! anyway, this is the one we made (get someone with a strong arm to help mix it!)

1. grease a 13" x 9" pan
2. in a huge pot , melt the butter and peanut butter at the lowest heat
3. add the marshmallows and melt stirring constantly until smooth
4. mix in the rice krispies until blended
5. chocolate addicts , add the chips here !
6. press into the greased pan
7. cool
8. cut into squares
demonstrations.review:
We made them.
We ate them.
Yummy!

target.recipe_text:
melting cheese and roast beef sandwiches

rare roast beef works best with these. that way they don't get too done in the hot broth.

1. in 12 inch skillet , melt butter
2. add onions and cook until tender
3. add soup
4. bring to a boil
5. add roast beef
6. remove from heat
7. divide beef and onions among 4 rolls
8. top each with a slice of cheese
9. place under broiler until cheese melts
10. serve broth for dipping
target.review: A new favorite in our household.  So easy - I think "soaking" the roast beef is the key, making a flavorful, juicy sandwich.  Have made as written, and also have made without the sliced onions - just depends on how many "extra"  onions you prefer - fantastic both ways.  For the bread we prefer to use a crusty artisan bread or ciabatta.  A wonderful, satisfying quick dinner too!  Definitely a keeper at our house.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
bipsy apple teddy er   tipsy apple betty

here is a nice fall apple recipe. i live in florida, so i really don't know what a season is.. but i have to go with the majority who claim this is fall. the tipsy apple betty got it's origin from the fact that i have a bottle of amaretto sitting around and i don't drink the stuff, so i've tried to add it to recipes i've made just to use it up. the amaretto corn beef hash was a disaster, but this recipe is fabulous! the topping creats a struesal cover for the tender appples, soaking up a nice cocktail of amaretto and orange juice. the recipe is just as good without the liqueur, so if you don't have a 6 year old bottle hanging around...don't worry!

1. preheat oven to 375 degrees f
2. place sliced apples in 9 inch pie plate and sprinkle with orange juice and amaretto
3. combine sugar , flour , and spices in a medium mixing bowl
4. cut in butter until mixture is crumbly
5. sprinkle mixture over apples evenly
6. bake at 375 degrees f for 45 minutes until apples are tender and topping is crisp
7. may serve with a scoop of vanilla ice cream
demonstrations.review: Very tasty and so easy!  I may increase the topping ingredients next time, as we like crust!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
light peach upside down cake

this makes a beautiful cake. i made it this week for a lunch at work. the recipe comes from the february/march 2002 taste of home's light and tasty magazine. i made some minor adjustments to reduce the amount of sugar.

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. spray a 9 inch round baking pan with nonstick cooking spray and set aside
3. drain peaches , reserving 2 tablespoons of the juice
4. pat peaches dry between layers of paper towels and cut the peaches in half lengthwise
5. in small bowl , combine the brown sugar , cinnamon , nutmeg , reserved juice and 1 tablespoon of the melted butter
6. spread into prepared baking pan and top with peaches
7. in a large bowl , combine the flours , sugar , baking powder , baking soda and salt
8. in separate bowl , combine the buttermilk , egg or egg substitute , vanilla and remaining butter
9. add to dry ingredients and stir until blended well
10. spoon over peaches and bake in preheated oven for 30-35 minutes or until toothpick inserted near center comes out clean
11. cool for 10 minutes before inverting onto serving plan
12. best served warm
13. please
demonstrations.review: This does make a beautiful cake, which I would rename to Peach Cobbler Cake because that's what it tastes like!  Delicious, easy, and beautiful to boot - a winner!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
texas cranberry jalapeno bread

this recipe is similar to a contest winning recipe featured by our local electrical coop. sounds crazy, but this bread is addictive!

1. preheat oven to 350
2. in a large bowl , mix dry ingredients
3. in a medium bowl , mix eggs , juice , vanilla , jelly , and butter
4. make a well in center of dry ingredients
5. fold wet ingredients into dry and mix only until ingredients are combined
6. pour into 2 well greased loaf pans
7. bake 50-60 minutes
demonstrations.review: Awesome!  I love this bread!  I may use it next year as a gift item.  Because I couldn't wait to taste it, I tried to slice it right out of the oven and it crumbled to pieces - but after cooling thoroughly, it slices up nicely.  Definitely a keeper for me!

target.recipe_text:
sinfully delicious hot chocolate mix

this is so much better than the store bought dry mix. dont be afraid to be creative with the coffee mate....i have used the french vanilla on more than one occasion.

1. this makes 1 gallon dry mix
2. mix all ingredients together and store sealed
3. when you are ready for this sinful drink just fill a cup half full of mix and top off with boiling water
4. its out of this world
target.review:
I use Dutched Chocolate with mine to make it a bit more chocolatie.  Also, you can try to use a bit of orange liquer or mint with the recipe, but do it in small batches.  The liquer can be dropped into the milk and pulverized with a blender.  Just experiment.  You may try a bit of burnt Almond also.  I would pulverize it in the blender too.

My husband loves this so much, he requested it for his Christmas Present.  My children _Have_ to have it for camping.
Shepardes

demonstrations.recipe_text:
excellent carrot cake

chock full of flavor, this is the best carrot cake! it tastes even better the next day after the flavors meld. a tad more time consuming than the average carrot cake, but well worth it!

1. combine first 5 ingredients
2. beat well
3. mix flour , soda , salt and cinnamon
4. add to creamed mixture
5. stir well
6. add carrots , walnuts , pineapple and coconut
7. stir well
8. pour batter into greased and floured 13x9 baking pan
9. bake at 350 for 55 minutes , or until pick comes out clean
10. buttermilk glaze: combine first 5 ingredients in large saucepan
11. bring to a boil
12. cook 4 minutes on medium heat
13. remove from heat
14. add vanilla
15. pour buttermilk glaze over warm cake
16. let cake cool
17. cream cheese frosting: mix cream cheese and butter
18. beat until smooth
19. gradually add sugar , beating until light and fluffy
20. stir in vanilla
21. spread cream cheese frosting on top of cooled cake
demonstrations.review:
I looked and looked for a carrot cake recipe that had all of the "goodies" in it and was also moist and tender - after all of my searching I have at LAST found it with this recipe!!
I put golden and regular raisins in the mix along with the nuts and coconut.  On of the reasons that this cake came out so wonderful, was the buttermilk glaze that was put on it while warm.  It's a wonderful cake and my family LOVED IT!  It's a KEEPER!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
patriotic 4th of july cupcakes

patriotic cupcakes that can be used for any occasion.  you can always substitute your own recipe for white cake and white frosting.  in regards to the comment below, i went back to the original recipe to check and it does call for 2 tablespoons of batter per color -- i have never had any problems and i actually get 12 cupcakes out of this recipe.  i use scant tablespoons.  if anyone is worried, try it with teaspoons instead of tablespoons or even 1 tablespoon of the batters per cupcake.

1. prepare cake mix according to package directions
2. in a small bowl , combine 1 1 / 3 cups batter with blue food coloring
3. in another small bowl , combine red food coloring with 1 1 / 3 cups batter
4. leave the remaining batter plain
5. fill paper-lined muffin tins with 2 tablespoons red batter , 2 tablespoons plain batter , and 2 tablespoons blue batter
6. do not swirl batter , leave it layered
7. bake at 350f for 20-24 minutes or until a toothpick inserted in a cupcake comes out clean
8. cool 10 minutes in pan and then remove cupcakes to a wire rack to cool completely
9. frost with vanilla frosting and decorate with sprinkles
demonstrations.review: I loved these cupcakes and they were a huge smash with my grandkids! I would suggest getting a Red Velvet cake mix along with the white, so that one doesn't use too much of the red food coloring to make this. <br/><br/>As for the frosting....get a good cream cheese frosting mix to put on the top. With a very large frosting bag and a very large star tip, paste blue and red colored frosting (or just professional color paste) on the sides of the bag and carefully place the white frosting inside. Squeeze out the frosting for a bit until you get the nice mix of colors. Just to let you know, the colors will fade quickly, so with that in mind, you may wish to only figure on about 6 cupcake per bag of frosting to get the red, white, and blue colors to stand out. <br/><br/>I wish I knew where to find the cute cupcake papers, as those just top the whole presentation off. My grandkids didn't mind the regular blue, pink and yellow ones, but loved the cake.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
ginger vegetable lo mein

this is a wonderful, light lo mein. if you've never tried fresh gingerroot, try it--it has great flavor combined with the sesame oil. you could also try different combinations of vegetables.

1. place mushrooms in small bowl with boiling water , let stand 20 minutes while proceeding with recipe
2. after 20 minutes , drain mushrooms and reserve 1 / 2 cup liquid
3. chop mushrooms
4. cook noodles according to package directions , toss with 1 tsp sesame oil , return to pan
5. combine egg whites and egg
6. heat 1 tsp cooking oil and 1 tsp sesame oil in large skillet over medium heat
7. add egg mixture
8. cook without stirring until egg is set
9. flip egg and cook until set on other side
10. remove from pan and cut into short strips
11. heat remaining 1 tsp cooking oil and 1 tsp sesame oil in same skillet on medium-heat heat
12. add mushrooms , red bell pepper , garlic , ginger , crushed red pepper , and peas
13. cook and stir for 2-3 minutes
14. add mushroom liquid and teriyaki sauce
15. bring to a low boil , cook for 3-4 minutes
16. toss with noodles and egg strips , sprinkle with salt if desired
17. serve with low-sodium soy sauce
demonstrations.review: We loved the recipe, but added shredded cabbage and half a sweet onion to it.  The Shiitake mushroom gives it a unique flavor and was a hit with my family.  This one's a keeper!!!  Four stars because we added more stuff to it.

target.recipe_text:
chicken with mushrooms and mustard

this creamy dish is not only delicious but it is quite low in fat. suitable for dinner guests or a quick meal for your family. what do they say. . . "try it you'll like it."

1. pound breasts until 1 / 4" thick
2. dredge in flour mixture
3. heat oil over medium heat
4. add chicken and saute about 7 minutes , turning once
5. remove and keep warm
6. add butter to frypan and increase heat to high
7. add onion and mushrooms
8. saute about 5 minutes
9. reduce heat to low
10. add cream , parsley , mustard and lemon juice
11. bring to a boil stirring constantly
12. add juices from chicken into cream mixture
13. pour sauce over chicken and serve
target.review: This was pretty good even without the Dijon mustard, i swear I had a bottle somewhere.... should have double checked before going along with this recipe but still was very good. my boyfriend who doesn't really like mushrooms gobbled up this recipe and licked his plate clean! The sauce is very good. ;)   I served it with some rice pilaf, nice combination :)   I will try it again with the dijon, and maybe I'll boost it another star!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chicken pesto

this was my daughter's favorite dish (along with some of her friends). she enjoyed it so much that we had to make it a weekly recipe.

1. prepare pesto sauce according to package direction
2. heat oven to 350 degrees
3. spray rectangular dish with no-stick spray
4. moisten chicken with water , shake off excess , and coat complete with bread crumbs
5. place chicken in baking dish
6. spread pesto sauce evenly over chicken breasts
7. cover each breast with slice of provolone cheese
8. spread mushrooms over cheese
9. bake in oven for 45- 50 minutes
10. serve with pasta
demonstrations.review: wow, this was delicious! defintely a keeper.  the only difference i made was used a "creamy pesto mix" instead of just pesto and also I used sauteed fresh mushrooms. Thanks for a great recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cherry balsamic chicken breasts

i really like this recipe because it is simple and has a nice presentation.  i serve with crusty french bread and a salad.

1. combine flour , basil , salt and pepper in large resealable plastic bag
2. shake to mix well
3. add chicken
4. seal and shake to coat
5. set aside
6. melt 2 tablespoon of the butter in a large nonstick skillet over medium-high heat
7. add chicken breasts
8. place onion around the edges of chicken
9. cook chicken for 4 minutes per side to lightly brown
10. stir onion occasionally
11. pour broth and vinegar around chicken
12. add cherries to pan
13. cover
14. reduce heat and simmer 4 minutes until no longer pink
15. remove chicken to platter
16. cover to keep warm
17. increase heat until mixture bubbles
18. cook 2 to 4 minutes to reduce liquid , stirring occasionally
19. reduce heat to low
20. stir in remaining 1 tablespoon butter until blended
21. serve chicken with sauce
demonstrations.review:
i was actually recommended this recipe from a friend so i came to the site, (ended up becoming a member and all- haha) and tried ur recipe out. i liked it quite a bit, my hubby loved it (prolly 4 stars for him). it is different but pretty good, will make again in our home.

4/23/08
EDIT:  I wanted to add that I've made this recipe a few more times since the last time i reviewed it and it has defintely grown on me, i love it now and i try to make this at least once every other week. Its healthy and truly delicious. Oh, and I changed it to 4 stars !

demonstrations.recipe_text:
saucy chicken skillet

amazing little sauce with fresh veggies and browned chicken breast. simple enough for any weeknight yet still special and flavorful enough for guests. adapted from a recipe i found at kraft.com and changed quite a bit for my family.

1. saute chicken and peppers in a sprayed or lightly oiled skillet until browned on both sides
2. add garlic and cook , stirring constantly for about 30 seconds
3. stir in cream cheese , broth , dressing , onions and basil
4. cook stirring often until sauce begins to thicken and chicken is cooked through
5. stir in tomatoes and cook for 2 minutes
6. serve over pasta or rice
demonstrations.review: I have made this dish about 10 times already so far, and figured it was time for a review!  this is one of my absoulte favorite dinners to have.  I always serve it with some white rice.. the sauce is absoultely delish to mix in some rice and gobble up.  I use red bell pepper as husband doesnt like green. Also I always use a little extra garlic & green onions!  Amazing dish, I love it!

target.recipe_text:
caramelized baked chicken legs wings

delicious! yummy  caramelized legs, kids love these! so quick and easy and no marinating required. just prepare the sauce, pour over the chicken and pop in the oven!  i actually like this with wings better ;-)
 

very important to leave it in the oven until it has caramelized to avoid disappointment. 

thank you to everyone for their positive reviews!

try adding sambal oelek as chef  #27416 has suggested in his review. what a great idea ;-)

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees fahrenheit or 180 degrees celsius
2. place chicken in a 9x13 inch baking dish
3. mix together the oil , soy sauce , ketchup , honey , garlic , salt and pepper
4. pour over the chicken
5. bake in preheated oven for one hour , or until sauce is caramelized
6. could also use wings or pork ribs
target.review: I thought this was wonderful!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
better than olive garden alfredo sauce

this is the best alfredo sauce ever. this is several recipes combined into one. you can also add your choice of meat (chicken,  shrimp or even crab). the closest olive garden is an hour away and i will never drive that far again just for alfredo sauce. i promise this is the best sauce ever. definitely a dish you would want to impress your guest with.

1. melt butter in medium saucepan with olive oil over medium / low heat
2. add the garlic , cream , white pepper and bring mixture to a simmer
3. stir often
4. add the parmesan cheese and simmer sauce for 8-10 minutes or until sauce has thickened and is smooth
5. when sauce has thickened add the mozzarella cheese and stir until smooth
6. stir frequently
7. while the sauce cooks , boil noodles for 3-5 minutes
8. place pasta on serving plates and spoon sauce over pasta
9. garnish with parsley , freshly cracked black pepper and more grated parmesan
demonstrations.review: I really enjoyed this recipe.  Thanks for sharing.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s famous coleslaw

this is the most delicious coleslaw that you will ever have! i make this for weddings, large socials and in the summer for bbq's and parties, and there is never anything left it all goes and everyone wants the recipe --- plan ahead the coleslaw needs to be refrigerated for the stated time to blend the flavors, this coleslaw will intensify in flavor with chilling time --- this is not a thick heavy dressing like some other coleslaw recipes it's the perfect texture and flavor and what makes this coleslaw stand out from all others is the fresh lemon juice so please use only fresh i have used bottled in the past and it is just not the same --- the dressing amount will yield enough for two 16-ounce packages prepared coleslaw mix or 1 head of green cabbage --- for one 16-ounce package prepared coleslaw mix use the dressing amounts posted on bottom of recipe and add in 3 or more large of chopped green onions.   for more kittencal's recipes, visit my recipe site www.recipezazz.com

1. in a food processor chop the cabbage into small pieces or shred the cabbage
2. transfer to a large mixing bowl
3. with a fine shredder , shred the peeled carrots
4. add to the cabbage in the bowl
5. chop the green onion finely
6. add to the cabbage / carrot mixture along with the celery seed
7. mix the three veggies all together with a wooden spoon
8. to make the dressing: in a medium glass bowl whisk together all the dressing ingredients starting with the lower amounts then adding in and adjusting to suit taste but using 1 / 3 cup plus 2 tablespoons sugar
9. pour over the veggies in the bowl , and mix well to combine
10. store covered in the refrigerator for at least 8 hours or overnight to blend flavors
11. for one 16-ounce package coleslaw mix use the following amounts
12. 1 / 2 cup mayonnaise / 2-1 / 2 tablespoons milk / 2-1 / 2 tablespoons buttermilk / 1-1 / 2 tablespoons vinegar / 1-1 / 2 tablespoons fresh lemon juice / 3-1 / 2 tablespoons sugar / 1 / 2 teaspoon garlic powder / 1 / 2 teaspoon seasoned salt , or to taste
demonstrations.review: Kit, this was awesome!!!  I think I'm just going to make your recipes, that way I'll always know they'll turn out and taste great!!  Thanks again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
creamy turkey soup

this goes together in a flash-and is really flexible for using ingredients on hand. you can either make this with noodles or dumplings, or leave them out. we like our soup salty, so adjust that to your taste.

1. saute onions and carrots in butter until soft , not brown
2. add flour and mix well
3. gradually add 2 cups broth and milk
4. cook and stir until it thickens
5. stir in remaining 3 cups broth , and all remaining ingredients
6. simmer 10-12 minutes until noodles are tender , stirring occasionally
demonstrations.review: I made this with my leftover turkey and loved it!!!!!  I added garlic, celery and carrots... it was GREAT

target.recipe_text:
the best garlic butter

this makes great garlic bread. you can use more garlic to taste.

1. in a small bowl , combine softened butter , minced garlic and parmesan cheese
2. season with italian seasoning , pepper and paprika
3. mix until smooth
target.review:
Delicious!
I didn't use butter though - i used "halvarine" i think it's similar to "can't believe it's not butter" - it's a soft spread but not margarine. 
i also used only 1/4 tsp black pepper and just 1 tbsp pressed garlic... thank goodness b/c 1 tbsp was more than enough...
everyone loved it. Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
celery   apricot soup

nan

1. trim the celery , wash and thinly slice
2. peel and finely chop the onion
3. finely chop the apricots
4. heat oil
5. add celery and onion , cover and saute , without browning , for 10 minutes
6. shake the pan occasionally to prevent sticking
7. add apricots , stock and seasonings
8. bring to a boil , cover and simmer for 45 minutes
9. allow to cool slightly before blending in a blender
10. return to a pan and reheat
11. serve hot
demonstrations.review: yummy. i wouldn't change a thing about it.  i did sprinkle parsley and cumin powder on top but that's it. delicious.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
gingery chickpeas in spicy tomato sauce

one of my favorite vegetarian/vegan meals.  it's wonderful served with a green salad and soft flatbread.  i've provided directions for both stovetop and crock-pot cooking methods, although i originally found the recipe in judith finlayson's 150 best slow cooker recipes.

1. in a large pot or dutch oven , heat oil over medium heat
2. and diced onion and cook , stirring , for about 10 minutes , until it begins to brown
3. add garlic , ginger , cumin , salt , and pepper
4. cook , stirring , for 1 minute
5. add balsamic vinegar and tomatoes , and bring to a boil over medium-high heat
6. stir in chickpeas , reduce heat to low
7. cover and simmer 45 minutes , lifting lid to stir occasionally
8. when serving , top each bowl with chopped green onions if desired
9. slow cooker method: after step 3 , add chickpeas to crock-pot
10. pour in hot tomato mixture and stir to combine
11. cook on high for 2-3 hours , or low for 6 hours
demonstrations.review: Delicious... made it exact except for using ground ginger about 1 tablespoon - and it was wonderful - every one like it and ate it up :) we served it with warmed pitas... i will make it again!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
easy dhal soup

for comfort food with a touch of the exotic, this dhal is quite simple but soooo tasty and has become a staple of our diet.

1. in large saucepan , warm olive oil and add garlic and onion
2. saute , stirring 2-3 minutes
3. add turmeric , garam masala , chili powder , and cumin
4. stir in tomatoes , lentils , lemon juice , vegetable stock , coconut milk , and bring to a boil
5. reduce heat to low and simmer , uncovered , for 25-30 minutes or until lentils are tender
6. serve warm
7. you can garnish with lemon slices and cilantro if desired
8. also good with naan bread
demonstrations.review: I was just going to add this recipe myself - when I thought, better see if someone else already has - I just tried this same recipe today - from the Cook's Library Parragon Publishing cookbook - it's so good - i took it to a Church soup - potluck - everyone loved it and was asking for the recipe... now i can send them here!

target.recipe_text:
roasted kielbasa   potatoes

another recipe from mom. these are good and easy to throw together.

1. preheat oven to 425 degrees
2. mix all ingredients in a large bowl
3. pour into a 9x13" baking pan
4. cook in oven , covered with foil for approximately 1 hour
5. you can stir after 1 / 2 hour of cooking
target.review: We enjoyed this quick and easy recipe. I added onion and garlic and reduced the oil in half. After eating it we think this would be good with eggs and plan on trying that next time..

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s easy and delicious ranch parmesan chicken

there are plenty versions of this recipe, this is mine and can be on your table in less that an hour, my family loves this chicken! --- the ranch dressing is the secret it holds in all the flavor and moistness while the chicken is baking and also adds flavor, i find that hidden valley ranch dressing works the best but kraft or any other brand will do, i sometimes top the baked chicken with mozzarella cheese or cheddar, but that is optional --- although i have only made this using breasts i imagine that chicken pieces could be used although you would have to increase the breadcrumb mixture slightly, you can marinate the chicken breast in the ranch dressing for a few hours in the fridge, although you will need more than 1 cup of dressing if you are marinating .... *note* to avoid a soggy bottom crust, place the chicken breasts onto a flat rack on top the baking sheet, also it is important not to bake the chicken in a small baking pan, if you do not have a rack bake on a large baking sheet so any juices in the pan will spread out and not accumulate under the chicken causing a soggy bottom ---------------
for low-fat option: use low-fat ranch dressing and omit the melted butter on top or use a healthy butter alternative such as smart balance 50/50 blend.

1. set oven to 400 degrees
2. in a shallow bowl mix together the dry breadcrumbs with parmesan cheese , seasoned salt , black pepper and garlic powder
3. dip the chicken into the ranch dressing to coat both sides
4. coat in the breadcrumb mixture
5. place in a single layer onto a greased baking sheet or line with non-stick foil
6. lightly drizzle the melted butter over each breast
7. if desired you can sprinkle black pepper over the chicken pieces
8. bake uncovered for about 30-35 minutes or until the chicken is cooked)
demonstrations.review: I loved this recipe! Baked it on a rack in the cookie sheet which made it crispy, and melted mozzarella cheese on top to make it chicken parm with spaghetti.  Excellent and very easy to make. Will make again!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
oven baked sweet bbq chops

these have a really good sweet onion bbq sauce on them.  at first i thought that 1/4 c. would be way too much onion, but it cooks in really well, and the sauce isn't overpowered by them at all.
the original recipe called for this amount of sauce on 5 chops, but i usually only put in 3 chops (i'm not a fan of left-over meat and i'm only cooking for 2).  if you were to make 5 chops, i would suggest doubling the sauce.
also, depending on the type of chop, you may not need to cook as long (i've used small boneless loin chops and they only took about 1 hr 15 min)

1. combine everything in a small saucepan and bring to a boil
2. simmer 5 minutes
3. place 3 pork chops in a pan
4. spoon sauce on top and cover
5. bake at 375 for 45 minutes to 1 hour
demonstrations.review: We enjoyed these very much and I will make them again. I followed the recipe exactly and see no need to change it. I think this will work good with chicken or spare ribs and will try those soon.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
awesome slow cooker pot roast

i found this on the all recipes site. this is a very easy recipe for a delicious pot roast. it makes its own gravy. it's designed especially for the working person who does not have time to cook all day, but it tastes like you did. you'll want the cut to be between 5 and 6 pounds.

1. in a slow cooker , mix cream of mushroom soup , dry onion soup mix and water
2. place pot roast in slow cooker and coat with soup mixture
3. cook on high setting for 3 to 4 hours , or on low setting for 8 to 9 hours
demonstrations.review: This was great - will definitely make it again. The only thing extra I did was add mushrooms, and I would do that again.

target.recipe_text:
peach custard pie with streusel topping

this pie is the best pie i have ever tasted.  no joke!  i love this so much and my peach crazed hubby loves it even more!  you can't go wrong with this yummy pie.  the filling is just perfect and the streusel topping gives it a nice crunchy layer on top.  mmm... its amazing!

1. preheat oven to 425f
2. crust:
3. combine flour , salt and butter with fork until crumbly
4. add in water one tbs at a time until soft dough forms
5. gather into a ball and roll out into a circle about 1 / 8 inch thick
6. place 9 inch pie plate upside down on crust and cut off excess dough , leaving 1 inch overhang
7. place crust into pie plate and arrange as you wish
8. filling:
9. peel and slice peaches 1 / 4 inch thick and line the crust in a circle , slightly overlapping each other until you have an outer circle and inner circle
10. whisk together sour cream , egg yokes , sugar , flour and vanilla until just blended and pour over top of the peaches
11. bake for 30 minutes until custard in mostly set
12. streusel topping:
13. combine butter , flour , sugar and cinnamon with your fingers until crumbly
14. sprinkle evenly over top of pie and bake for an additional 15 minutes until custard is set
15. let pie cool and serve cold or warm
16. enjoy !
target.review: This was delicious! My pie plate wasn't deep enough so I couldn't put all the custard on but it still tasted lovely. Thanks for posting this recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
raspberry lazy daisy cake

my grandma's recipe. raspberries are her favorite fruit. this cake is incredibly moist, so the topping is optional.

1. beat eggs , sugar and vanilla until thick
2. add the dry ingredients
3. heat milk and butter to the boiling point , then add to the batter
4. pour into a lightly greased 9x13 inch pan
5. sprinkle the raspberries over the top
6. sprinkle 3 tbsp sugar over the raspberries
7. bake at 350 degrees f for 30-40 minutes or until golden brown
8. topping: combine all ingredients
9. frost cake-return to hot oven or broiler to brown
demonstrations.review: This was a lovely moist cake. The topping gave it a special touch. Thanks for sharing!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
celery and rice

a stove top recipe that is oh, so good.
been making this for years and have no idea where the recipe came from, i've had it for more years than i can remember..lol..

1. saute onion , rice , celery in butter
2. stir in rest ingredients , bring to a boil
3. then simmer 20 minute or until rice is cooked
demonstrations.review: I really didn't expect this to be so good! I didn't quite have enough celery so I used carrot and then added raisins after having read the other review. I fried the leftovers up the next day and that was even better than the first. Thanks for this recipe!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
jamaica banana jam

if you like banana and peanut-butter sandwiches, you'll love this jam and peanut-butter on a sandwich! (recipe courtesy: elizabeth barcelo)

1. place lime juice in a one quart measure
2. peel bananas and dice directly into lime juice
3. stir with a wooden spoon
4. keep stirring as you dice each banana into the lime juice to prevent darkening
5. measure sugar and water into a wide 2 quart saucepan , and stir to dissolve sugar as you bring syrup to a boil
6. cover tightly for the first 2 minutes then uncover , add bananas and boil over low heat for about 30 minutes or until thick
7. stir often to prevent sticking , especially during last 10 minutes
8. jam is done when a spoon scraped across bottom of pan leaves a track that closes slowly , or when jam mounds while stirring
9. fill hot , sterilized jars quickly with the hot jelly or jam mixture , leaving 1 / 4 inch headspace
10. wipe the sealing surface of the jars with a clean paper towel , dampened with hot water , to remove any jam or sugar crystals
11. place lids , screw on bands finger-tight and process jars for 10 minutes in boiling water bath
12. cool jars upright for 12-24 hours while vacuum seal is drawn and jam or jelly sets up
13. let the jars sit undisturbed while they cool
demonstrations.review: Even though it wasn't a great success with the rest of the family (all the more for me!) I've really enjoyed this jam.

target.recipe_text:
miso shiru soup

a very traditional japanese soup

1. ----------make the dashi---------
2. bring water to a boil
3. wash kelp under cold water tap
4. add to water when it comes to a boil
5. stir and let boil 3 minutes
6. remove kelp from the water and add the bonito
7. allow to come to boil and remove from heat immediately
8. let it settle for a few minutes
9. strain off the bonito and set aside for whenever you need the dashi
10. ---------make the miso shiru-----------
11. bring the dashi to a boil
12. mix a little hot liquid with the bean paste , stirring until smooth
13. pour mixture back into the saucepan , stir well
14. add tofu and return to boil
15. simmer for a few seconds only
16. ladle into bowls and garnish with green onion and a slice or two of mushroom
target.review: Very Traditional.  It turned out perfectly!  The time was well worth it.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
creamy  cheesy potato and kumara bake

this is a tasty, easy sidedish with a cheesy, crispy top.

1. slice potatoes and kumara thinly
2. place into a casserole dish in layers
3. chop onion & garlic finely and sprinkle over potato and kumara
4. crumble the stock cube over onion , then add herbs
5. pour the cream over
6. follow with the cheese
7. sprinkle the breadcrumbs evenly on top
8. bake in a 180c oven for approx 1 hour and 10 minutes , or until potatoes are tender and top is golden and crispy
demonstrations.review: I would have liked it to be more cheesy.  Also, I think the breadcrumbs didn't do it any justice.  Ok though.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
bacon wrapped chicken  oamc

this is another great way to make something great ahead of time to thaw as needed or eat right now with little effort!

1. flatten chicken to 1 / 2" thickness
2. spread 3 tablespoons cream cheese over each chicken piece
3. dot with butter and sprinkle with salt
4. roll up
5. wrap each with a bacon strip
6. place , seam side down , in a greased pan
7. bake , uncovered , at 400f for 35-40 minutes or until juices run clear
8. broil 6 inches from the heat for 5 minutes or until bacon is crisp
9. if you are making these ahead for future use , freeze these uncooked on a cookie sheet in your freezer
10. when solid , wrap and put in a ziplock bag or vacuum seal desired quantities
11. to cook from frozen state , thaw before cooking and follow directions above
demonstrations.review:
I can't say enough good things about this dish!!!

A fantastic recipe for guests.  Everyone loves this.  I've made upto 27 at a time!  It's good the next day for lunch too!  I will never stop singing it's praises.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mars bars rice krispies squares  no bake

i have been making ever since my son was small and even though my son is all grown up now they are still requested --- these bars are best if eaten the same day.

1. melt butter and mars bars over med-low heat in a large saucepan until smooth
2. remove from heat
3. stir in rice krispies cereal , and nuts ,
4. press into a greased 8x8 pan
5. top with chocolate chips , and place under broiler for 30 seconds remove from oven and spread chocolate evenly over squares
6. store in fridge
7. cut into squares , and serve
demonstrations.review: Golden!

target.recipe_text:
poverty meal

when i was a child, my family used to eat this at least once a week due to the fact that it is inexpensive and a little goes a long way. we also added fresh herbs or sometimes whole kernel corn. its even better the next day and it freezes well.

1. saute onions and garlic in olive oil until translucent
2. brown ground beef and drain
3. add ground beef , tomatoes , water , raw macaroni , salt and pepper to the onion and garlic mixture
4. cook for 15 to 20 minutes or until macaroni is tender
5. if desired , top with parmesan cheese
6. serve with crusty bread and a salad
target.review: Quick, easy and super yummy!   DH loved it!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
black pepper shrimp  paula deen

this recipe from paula deen of food network couldn't be easier. it seems like a lot of black pepper, but trust me--it works. you get it all over your fingers as you shell the shrimp and eat them, so have some wet wash cloths rolled up and ready. this cooks up in just a few minutes, so have the rest of your dinner ready before you start (i suggest a hearty salad and bread).

1. preheat oven to 450f
2. rinse and drain shrimp and place in shallow baking pan
3. melt the butter in a small saucepan
4. add the garlic and saut for 3 to 4 minutes
5. pour the garlic butter mixture over shrimp and toss to coat
6. sprinkle about half the pepper over shrimp until they are well covered
7. remember--don't be afraid !
8. bake until pink
9. turn shrimp over sprinkle with remaining pepper and bake a few minutes longer
10. don't overcook !
demonstrations.review: Delicious!  This recipe is definitely a keeper.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crispy baked chicken wings

i made these for my family & everyone enjoyed them.

1. fill a pot half way with water then add the salt & cayenne
2. bring to a boil then add the wings
3. boil for 15 minutes then drain
4. meanwhile , mix the remaining ingredients together in a small bowl
5. heat in the microwave for 45 seconds or until the butter is melted
6. preheat the oven to 450f
7. place the wings in a shallow glass baking dish
8. pour half the sauce over the wings then bake in the oven for 15 minutes
9. turn the wings over then pour over the rest of the sauce , continue to bake for 10-15 minutes
demonstrations.review: Delicious! I doubled the sauce and the wings were very flavorful. DH loved them!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cabbage for those who dislike cabbage

this is so much nicer than plain steamed or boiled cabbage. try it on the cabbage haters in your family and see if it converts them.

1. in a large skillet , heat butter and oil over medium heat
2. add cabbage , garlic and brown sugar to pan
3. saut until the cabbage is limp , about 5 minutes or so
4. reduce heat to medium-low and stir in vinegar
5. cook , stirring very often , for approximately 20 minutes
6. taste and if cabbage is too crunchy for you , continue to cook for a few more minutes
7. add salt and pepper to taste and serve
demonstrations.review: Delicious.  I doubled the sauce ingredients and used balsamic vinegar.  I'll definitely make this again.

target.recipe_text:
interesting crock pot chicken

so simple, and so good! add a veggie or salad and dinner's done! i like to serve this over rice, but it is equally as tasty over cooked egg noodles. i also add extra 'shrooms cause we love them!

1. mix together dressing mix , chicken , mushrooms , butter , and chicken broth in crock pot
2. cook on high 5-6 hours
3. about 1 hour prior to serving , mix mushroom soup , cream cheese , and garlic
4. add to crock pot
5. cook on high for 1 more hour
6. season with salt and pepper to taste , and serve over rice or noodles
target.review: Wow was this YUMMY!!!!! This is the 3rd crockpot recipe I have tried this week and this is a keeper!! Its sooo hot here. Heat index of 105 so I've been on here looking for new crockpot recipes. Thanks for this one!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
to die for crock pot roast

amazing flavor, and so simple! no salt needed here. in fact, you may wish to use half the ranch dressing mix to cut back on the saltiness. found this crock-pot pot roast recipe on of a website called www.recipegoldmine.com. it's all the rage there, so i thought i'd try it.

1. place beef roast in crock pot
2. mix the dried mixes together in a bowl and sprinkle over the roast
3. pour the water around the roast
4. cook on low for 7-9 hours
5. use onion soup mix instead of ranch
6. add one cup , of red wine
7. add potatoes , carrots , mushrooms , celery and onion 2-3 hours before end
demonstrations.review: This was soooooo GOOD!!!!!! I used half thr ranch and it was perfect!! I made some noodles and put the broth over them. What a great recipe!!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kielbasa stew

nan

1. slice sausage and put in crockpot
2. add cabbage potatoes carrots chicken broth and diced tomatoes
3. add italian seasoning for flavor
4. cook on high for 3 to 4 hours
5. it will cook down and make more juice
demonstrations.review: This was very good! I cooked on high for 4 hours and it was perfect. Thanks for this great recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
the original chex party mix

clipped from the coupon section, the chex party mix has a few more ingredients than the traditional chex mix.

1. heat oven to 250 degrees
2. melt butter in large roasting pan in oven
3. stir in seasonings
4. gradually stir in remaining ingredients until evenly coated
5. bake 1 hour , stirring every 15 minutes
6. spread on paper towels to cool
7. store in airtight container
demonstrations.review:
Simple and so good!
And It must be the original 
Chex party mix because
its the same on posted on my Chex cereal box!
I always add an extra tablespoon
of worcestershire.

target.recipe_text:
easy breakfast egg casserole

this is perfect for a weekend family breakfast because it can be prepared the night before and then popped into the oven in the morning.

1. heat oven to 350f
2. grease a 13x9-inch baking pan
3. place bread in the bottom and sprinkle with sausage and cheese
4. beat eggs , milk , salt and pepper with a whisk
5. pour over the bread mixture
6. bake 40-45 minutes or until eggs are set in the center and lightly browned
target.review:
My Mom makes this every year for Christmas breakfast.  We have anywhere from 12-20 people so there are lots of dishes.  This casserole as well as fried oysters, oyster stew, and fruit salad are ALWAYS on the table.  

I'm glad to be reminded of it so that I can start making it for my family on regular breakfast days too.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cucumber with feta cheese and mint

this is for the world tour. this is from greek cuisine.

1. wash and dry the cucumber and cut it into very thin crosswise slices
2. place the slices in a salad bowl , sprinkle with feta cheese and mint
3. in a small whisk the oil and lemon juice with the salt and pepper to make a vinaigrette made with lemon juice
4. pour over the salad and toss thoroughly
5. serve immediately
demonstrations.review: This is a very attractive side salad dish.  I used an English cucumber to minimize the water and seeds which worked very well.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
honey mustard sprouts

from toh. i'm one of the few people i know that actually like brussels sprouts. this recipe could also be used on broccoli.

1. place brussels spouts in a steamer basket
2. place in a saucepan over 1 inch of water
3. bring to a boil
4. cover and cook until crisp-tender
5. drain
6. in a bowl , combine the butter , honey , mustard , onion powder and dill
7. add the sprouts and toss to coat
demonstrations.review: This is really yummy.  I served this last night and my nephews and husband cleaned the bowl.  We had to divide the last spoonful evenly around the table.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
easy breakfast casserole

this is the easiest, best tasting breakfast casserole ever.

1. spread grated cheese in a 9 x 13 inch pan that has been buttered
2. spread green chilies evenly over the cheese
3. beat eggs and add salt and pepper to taste
4. pour the eggs over the cheese and green chilies
5. bake at 350 degrees for 25 to 30 minutes or until set
6. cut into squares and serve
demonstrations.review: This rocks.  It's low carb and high protein!  Perfect for my kids before school as they don't get the carb tiredness an hour later.

target.recipe_text:
grilled t bone steaks

this is an excellent marinade for any steak.  the flavor is just wonderful.  our t-bones came out perfect.  very tender with a wonderful flavor. the original recipe is from toh with some changes to suit our taste. prep time does not include the time it takes to marinate the steaks.

1. in a large resealable plastic bag , combine the first 11 ingredients
2. add steaks
3. seal the bag and turn to coat
4. refrigerate overnight , turning as often as you can
5. drain and discard marinade
6. grill steaks , over high heat for about 5 minutes on each side or until meat reaches desired doneness
target.review: What a awesome recipe. Made this for Father's Day. You know when you have a good steak when they melt in your mouth and the family puts the steak sauce down, due to "these are so good without any steak sauce"! The flavor speaks for itself. Thanks for the posting. This is Top of the list in marinades!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
best ever baked beans  crock pot
