10. slide parchment sheet , cookies and all , carefully off pan and onto your counter , set a new piece of parchment paper onto your baking sheet and repeat until all dough is baked
11. meanwhile , as the next batch bakes , remove baked cookies from the parchment and let cool completely on wire racks
12. wipe off the crumbs from the old sheet of parchment and you can reuse it for your next batch
13. these will keep about 3 days stored in a cookie tin or an airtight plastic container
target.review: I just made these cookies for my widower neighbor to say "thank you" for bringing us his fishing "catch of the day."  I have to make another batch because my family ate them all!  They are REALLY good!  ALSO: I added 2 cups of milk chocolate chips and 1 cup of peanut butter chips instead of just the chocolate.  YUMMY!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
asparagus with bow ties

i adapted this from a recipe found in bon appetit, using the ingredients i had on hand

1. in a large pot boil pasta according to package directions
2. drain reserving 1 c of water
3. return pasta to pot heat oven to 450
4. place asparagus on a baking pan
5. drizzle with olive oil , season with salt and pepper and roast 10 minutes
6. add cream cheese and asparagus to the pasta over medium low heat
7. stir in 2 / 3 c parmesan cheese
8. stir until creamy , add some cooking liquid if pasta is too dry put pasta in a large bowl , garnish with pine nuts , chives and 1 / 3 parmesan cheese
demonstrations.review: Yum!  This is really good & easy, too!  - thanx for posting

demonstrations.recipe_text:
santa fe soup

this is so good! it's nice and cheesy and oh so easy to put together. really good with slices of hot cornbread. i got this recipe from my mother who is a wonderful cook. cook time is time it takes to melt the cheese in the soup mixture.

1. brown ground beef with onion
2. drain fat well
3. in a large pot combine ground beef , corn , beans and stewed tomatoes and ro-tel tomatoes
4. cube cheese and add to soup pot
5. stir over low flame until melted and blended
demonstrations.review: Ohmygosh!  I thought with so little time and ingredients this couldn't possibly be that good...but it is!  My family ate it up (although I added a can of diced green chiles and a can of diced jalepenos) and I wished I had doubled the recipe.  Give it a try and kudos to the recipe submitter!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
squashed cabbage

this recipe was submitted by another member, and i adopted it when she made a dramatic exit from the site.  i have not tried it, but will make my own comments when i do.  her original intro:  "i actually made this up, i am getting braver. it is the simplest thing in the world and very tasty, i served it with grilled chicken."

1. shred cabbage
2. shred onion , i used my cheese grater
3. shred squash
4. dice garlic
5. in medium pot melt butter
6. add the cabbage , onion , squash and garlic
7. stir often
8. cook until the veggies are still a little crisp
9. salt and pepper to taste
demonstrations.review: VERY SIMPLE...Yet VERY GOOD!!! Thanx for posting!!!

target.recipe_text:
should be illegal oven bbq ribs

after not being able to find restaurant ribs that satified my hot sweet appetite, i carefully attempted various combinations of flavors until i found one that i and my family thought was perfect. hope you enjoy them too.

1. place all ingredients together in large roasting pan
2. cut ribs apart for easier serving
3. mix together making sure to coat all ribs with this semi-dry paste
4. spread ribs out evenly on bottom of pan
5. cover lightly with foil
6. bake at 375 degrees for approximately 1 hour
7. turning or stirring occasionally
8. you can use broiler for these ribs , just watch more closely , and adjust cooking time
9. these ribs are also great finished on the grill for a few minutes on each side
target.review: This sauce is simply delicious.  I used the sauce on Beef Baby Back Ribs and they turned out simply scrumptous. This is a winner and I will be using the recipe from now on. Thanx for posting.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
amish apple crisp

another wonderful amish inspired dish. we serve this for dessert, or for breakfast. very tasty!

1. place apple mixture in a deep dish pie pan
2. sprinkle with sugar and cinnamon
3. mix topping ingredients , except the cinnamon and butter , with a fork until blended
4. sprinkle topping over apples
5. drizzle melted butter over topping
6. sprinkle with cinnamon
7. bake at 375f degrees for 40 minutes
demonstrations.review: I have been in search for an apple crisp recipe to suit my sweet tooth for many years.  This has got to be the best.  Thanx so much for helping me conclude my search.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
italian saucy sausage sub

yet again another carnival favorite!  sausage and tomato sauce--you just can't beat that!

1. fry , boil or grill your sausage
2. saut onion and bell pepper with a dash of pepper flakes
3. assembly----------
4. place sausage on bun
5. place saut mixture on top
6. place warm sauce on top
7. enjoy !
demonstrations.review: This recipe is definately a winner.  I had it for dinner with some broccoli, however, I ommitted the hoagie and added green peppers and a tablespoon of sugar.  VIOLA!!!!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cajun pork chops and rice

nan

1. preheat oven to 350
2. brown the pork chops , onion , bell pepper , and garlic together in small amount of oil in heavy skillet
3. when chops are browned and vegetables are tender , place in a casserole dish with cajun seasoning , rice , broth , and worcestershire sauce
4. bake covered about 20 minutes or until rice is done and chops are tender
demonstrations.review: Viola!!!  I had this for dinner tonight with cinnamon apples.  This recipe is sooooo!!!!! good.  It was extremely easy and the chops came out so tender.  I did'nt have the beef broth, and I substituted with beef boullian cubes.  Again, VIOLA!!!!!

target.recipe_text:
x boyfriend low fat microwave fudge

need a quick chocolate pick-me-up? don't drown yourself in chocolate sorrows and blow the bank in fat grams. a small piece of this will satisfy your craving but you'll keep your slim figure...your best revenge! your favorite nuts on top are optional!

1. line 8" x 8" pan with foil
2. sift sugar and cocoa into a heatproof bowl
3. add milk and butter
4. do not stir
5. microwave on high for 2 1 / 2 minutes or until butter is melted
6. add vanilla
7. stir to blend
8. turn into pan and smooth the top
9. put in freezer 10 minutes to set
target.review: We couldn't even wait long enough for the fudge to become solid before we ate it! This is SOOOOO EASY and SOOOOOO GOOD!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
fireball chicken

ever eaten an atomic fireball and a piece of chicken?  no???  well give this a try instead. 

cook time includes marinating time.

1. in a medium size bowl , mix the liquor , honey , garlic , salt and pepper
2. add the chicken and toss to a evenly coat
3. cover and marinate in the refrigerator 8 hours , or overnight
4. to cook , preheat the oven to 350 degrees
5. remove the chicken , shaking off excess marinade
6. pour the marinade into a small saucepan
7. and bring to a boil
8. boil until it begins to thicken and about 1 cup remains , 5 to 10 minutes
9. heat the oil in an ovenproof skillet over medium high heat
10. sear the chicken until golden on both sides
11. pour the reduced marinade over the chicken and place in the oven
12. bake about 20 minutes and serve
demonstrations.review: Interesting idea, but kinda bland.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
taco pollo   spicy chicken filled tortillas

for a mexican-style dinner, serve these as a starter with creamy avocado or sour cream dip, followed by your favourite hot and spicy mexican dish.  or serve them with a mexican vegetable side dish such as mexican potato crisps with lime salsa recipe #139461, fried mexican capsicum & potatoes recipe #139465 or mexican bean hotpot recipe #139476.  i've posted this recipe for the 2005 zaar world tour from a recipe on an international masters 'recipes for pan or wok' recipe card.

1. cut the chicken into thin strips , peel and crush the garlic , peel and slice the onion , de-seed and roughly chop the tomatoes and deseed and slice the capsicum into strips
2. heat the oil in a large pan or wok , preferably non-stick and fry the chicken over a high heat , stirring for 2-3 minutes until it is starting to brown
3. add the garlic and onion and fry for another 2 minutes
4. stir in the chilli powder , tomatoes and capsicum and cook for 2-3 minutes , stirring , until the chicken is cooked through
5. preheat the grill to medium , grill the tortillas for 6 seconds on each side , or until warm
6. transfer them to a work surface and spoon equal amounts of the chicken filling onto the centre of each tortilla and roll up tightly
7. transfer the filled tortillas to an ovenproof dish and sprinkle with cheesse
8. cook under a hot grill for 2 minutes , or until golden
9. garnish with parsley and lemon and serve
demonstrations.review: Made for Zaar Tag. Good recipe! I did use corn tortillas and lime juice rather than the flour tortillas and lemon juice, just personal taste. Turned out good!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
anne s pasta salad  made lighter

my aunt anne makes the absolute best macaroni salad.  it is a must for all family functions. i've taken her recipe and lightened it for a more healthy diet.

1. mix vegetables and cheese with macaroni
2. mix mayo , sugar , vinegar and black pepper
3. mix dressing with macaroni
4. allow to sit in fridge for about 30 minutes
5. this gets better the longer it sits
6. enjoy
demonstrations.review: This was just okay for us. I followed the recipe exactly, except I left out the cucumbers because we don't like them and added black olives in their place.

target.recipe_text:
country style fried skillet potatoes

if possible use a cast-iron skillet for this but any skillet will do, also use only shortening for this. cooking time is only estimated depending on the size you cut the potatoes, adjust all seasonings to taste. make certain that you the cooked cubed potatoes are cold before using in this recipe!

1. in a large cast-iron skillet heat the shortening over medium-high heat
2. add in the cubed potatoes and cook stirring until the potatoes are golden brown
3. season with seasoned salt , black pepper , garlic and paprika
4. serve hot
5. delicious !
target.review:
I made for dinner the other night, and mmmmmmmmm. I'm really glad I dug out the cast iron pan for this, it makes them taste so good. I did over crowd the pan a bit, so the first serving wasn't as crispy as I would have like, but the second serving (which had been sitting in the still warm pan) were nice and crispy on the outside and soft inside. I used diced potatoes that I had cooked by covering with water, bringing to a boil, and then boiling for 10 minutes. I drained the potatoes, covered them in cold water, and placed in the fridge until ready to use.
Thanks Kittencal!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
supper time cheese bread

an easy bread to serve with dinner.

1. beat eggs in bowl
2. stir in water , biscuit mix , mustard , minced onion , cheese , salt and cayenne pepper
3. mix thoroughly
4. pour into greased 9 x 5 loaf pan
5. bake at 350 degrees for 45 minutes
6. let bread cool in pan before removing and slicing
demonstrations.review: This was a good dinner bread. I've made a recipe similar to this as biscuits, but never as a loaf. I used a little bit of dehydrated minced onions instead of freash, but otherwise followed the recipe. We were also too impatient to wait for the bread to cool completely before serving, so it was a little difficult to cut. Thanks for sharing!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mock nutrigrain bars

wrapped individually, these easy to make cereal bars are a great breakfast-on-the-go. their filling layer can be made using apricot, raspberry, strawberry, or any other flavor of jam that you enjoy. a recipe found on the internet.

1. combine cake mix , oatmeal , and melted margarine
2. cover the bottom of a 9x13" baking pan with half of this mixture and press firmly into place
3. combine jam and water
4. spoon evenly over mixture in pan
5. crumble remaining mixture evenly over jam layer and press lightly into place
6. bake at 375 for 20 minutes , or until lightly browned on top
7. cool completely before cutting into bars
demonstrations.review: These were very good. I made them with blackberry preserves this time (forgot to mix with the water, though) and it turned out well. I'll try with apricot or strawberry filling next time. I cut, wrapped and froze mine for an easy breakfast on my way out the door to work. They are a little bit crumbly to eat, but they're worth the mess!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chex school fuel

a kid pleasing treat for children of all ages. if you want to get creative, add nuts or m&m's. from the chex cereal company.

1. cover cookie sheet with waxed paper
2. microwave first three ingredients uncovered in large microwavable bowl , until butter is melted
3. stir after one minute
4. stir in baking soda until dissolved
5. add cereals and stir
6. microwave on high 3 minutes , stirring every 60 seconds
7. spread on cookie sheet
8. cool 10 minutes
9. break into bite-size pieces
10. melt chocolate chips in small microwavable bowl until chocolate can be stirred smooth
11. drizzle chocolate over snack
12. refrigerate 30 minutes or until chocolate is set
13. store in airtight container
demonstrations.review: I made a double batch of these for my ds class, and they LOVED them! The only things I changed were that I cooked this on the stove (stirring for about 5 minutes after getting the cereal coated with the sugar mixture), and using leftover white candy coating instead of the chocolate chips. Thank you for posting!

target.recipe_text:
fajita seasoning

theinternetcookbook.com

1. combine ingredients in a bowl
2. use for cooking fajita
3. meat
4. store in an air-tight container
target.review: I didn't really care for this but BF liked it alot. Thanks for giving me a chance to try this.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
parmesan crusted tilapia

fast, easy and healthy! this recipe is for 2, but i have easily doubled it for more.  this bakes so quickly that i often make a bunch of these fillets and eat them leftover for lunches.

1. thaw and wash tilapia fillets if frozen
2. pat dry on paper towels
3. combine crumbs , parmesan , italian seasoning and garlic powder on a plate , mixing well
4. on a different plate , pour 1 tbsp lemon juice
5. working 1 at a time , place a fillet on the plate in the lemon juice , sprinkle with desired amount of kosher salt , black pepper , and garlic powder
6. turn the fillet over in the lemon juice and sprinkle seasoning on the other side
7. dredge fillet in the parmesan mixture patting it all over to coat
8. place in an oiled baking dish , repeat with remaining fillets
9. sprinkle a little lemon juice over fillets and drizzle or spray them lightly with olive oil
10. bake at 425f for about 20 minutes or until they easily flake with a fork and edges are browning
11. you can also bake these faster at 450f
demonstrations.review: We loved this. I broiled to get it a little crispy on top. It was the first time I have ever made Tilapia and will definitely be making it again. Thanks for a great recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
vampire killer cheese spread mix

when my best friend moved away, her mom's good friend made a cheese spread for the going-away party that was so good i spent an entire year trying to find where she got the mix. i finally found it online, but at $12.50 each after shipping, i decided i could probably come close enough on my own. so, with a little experimentation, this is what i came up with. i warn you, it's quite addicting and you'll want to stay a polite distance from others when speaking after you eat it. you can put the dry ingredients together and store them in ziploc bags or small containers so that you can just pull out a mix and add it to the wet ingredients in a snap. i serve it with crackers or beer bread. it can also be rolled into a cheese ball or log for a nice presentation if you're feeling ambitious.

1. combine all of the dried spices
2. these can be stored for later use or used immediately
3. mix together spices , softened cream cheese and wine until it is well incorporated and uniform
4. stir in shredded cheese
5. keep refrigerated until about 1 / 2 hour before serving
6. i recommend letting it rest in the fridge for at least 2 hours before serving to allow the spices re-hydrate and the flavors to come out
7. if you have any left-overs they can be safely refrigerated and stored for up to a week or two in an air-tight container
demonstrations.review: We made this for Black Friday, as ex-retail employees we stay home and enjoy not having to work. We absolutely loved this. I used 1 Tbs of Minced garlic, because we love garlic.  We added some worcestershire sauce to a small amount we put aside at the request of my BF and it was very tastey too.  We will be making this again (today actually...since we are stuck inside due to the weather.)  Thanks so much Reeces.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
oreo balls

my sister's co-worker brought these to a party and they were quite a hit. i don't know where the recipe came from originally.

"bark" is an artificial chocolate or vanilla candy coating/confectioner's coating used to make a treat called almond bark and can be found at most grocery stores near the chocolate chips. 

you can use chocolate chips and white chocolate chips if you don't have almond bark, but i have found that almond bark melts better and is easier to work with.

1. using a blender or hand held mixer , mix oreos and cream cheese together
2. roll into walnut size balls
3. chill for an hour
4. melt approximately 3 / 4 package of white almond bark
5. stick a toothpick in an oreo ball and dip it in the melted white almond bark
6. allow to harden on wax paper
7. takes about 15 minute
8. while waiting , melt about 1 / 4 package of chocolate almond bark
9. when oreo balls are no longer sticky to the touch , decorate with drizzles of chocolate and white almond bark
10. i just use a sandwich bag with a tiny hole cut in one corner to drizzle the almond bark
demonstrations.review: I made these last year for Christmas Dinner and as gifts. Everyone loved them.  I'm just back printing off the recipe so I can make them again, since I was told I would not be allowed in without them. LOL I may try making a batch with Mint Oreo's too.

target.recipe_text:
the very best salisbury steak

this is our favorite salisbury steak recipe. i always make enough extra sauce to serve over potatoes. tastes like it took all day to cook.

1. in a large bowl , mix together 1 / 3 cup condensed french onion soup with ground beef , bread crumbs , egg , salt and black pepper
2. shape into 6 oval patties
3. in a large skillet over medium-high heat , brown both sides of patties
4. pour off excess fat
5. in a small bowl , blend flour and remaining soup until smooth
6. mix in ketchup , water , worcestershire sauce and mustard powder
7. pour over meat in skillet
8. cover , and cook for 20 minutes , stirring occasionally
target.review: I followed Ginny Sue's lead and added more liquid. All I had was chicken broth - so I added a cup of chicken broth and a little cornstarch. This is very easy and very good.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
aloo paratha  indian potato stuffed flatbreads

this indian-styled stovetop bread is a wonderful addition to any meal. however, it has been my humble experience that it goes fantastically with chef dave's roasted eggplant soup!

1. boil potatoes in salted water to cover , until tender
2. while potatoes cook , mix the flours , cumin , and 1 teaspoon of salt
3. add 2 tablespoons of oil , then water
4. mix until this becomes a defined ball of dough
5. remove and knead until smooth , adding flour or water as necessary
6. cover dough with plastic wrap and set aside while preparing potatoes
7. when potatoes are finished , remove , drain and mash them with cayenne , salt , pepper , citrus juice , olives and 1 tablespoon of oil
8. taste and adjust seasonings as necessary
9. on a lightly floured surface , roll dough into 12-inch long snake and cut into 12 pieces
10. roll each piece into about 4-inch round
11. spoon 1-2 tablespoon of potato mixture into round , then fold over edges to enclose completely
12. pinch dough closed and press down to distribute filling evenly
13. heat a large cast iron pan over medium-high heat for 2-3 minutes
14. add another tablespoon of oil to skillet , then pour out
15. cook each bread for about 3 minutes per side , until brown spots appear
16. repeat until all are done
17. serve hot or room temperature
demonstrations.review: Yum. I will make these again and again

demonstrations.recipe_text:
potato pie

i thought i better post this so that i would know where it is every time i go to make it. i am tired of searching through umpteem books each time. it is my husband's favorite dish and if i have to be honest i really enjoy it as well. it's a supper dish found in both monmouthshire and the welsh counties, traditionally served with pickled beets or pickled red cabbage. we like it with crusty brown bread and pickled beets. it's delicious!

1. boil the potatoes in salted water until cooked
2. preheat oven to 425f
3. drain the potatoes well , add the milk and butter and mash until smooth , then stir in the cheese and seasoning
4. butter a 1 1 / 2 to 2 pint pie dish and sprinkle with the breadcrumbs , pressing them to the base and sides with the back of a spoon
5. spoon the potato and cheese mixture into the dish and rough up the top with a fork
6. brush with the melted butter
7. bake for 20 to 30 minutes or until golden brown
8. serve with pickled beets or red cabbage and thick slices of crusty brown bread
demonstrations.review: I made Salisbury steak and added this as a side (as per Marilyn Collari's suggestion). Good choice!!! I added minced onion, substituted freshly grated parmesan and doubled the breadcrumbs. I will make this all the time.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
world s best cookies aka that 70s elusive cornflake cookies

this wonderful recipe was in circulation when i was a kid in the 70s. years later, a woman brought a tray of these to the office, which i instantly recognized as those cookies from my childhood, and she refused to give me the recipe (said it was her babysitter's secret recipe)! i searched online (tried several recipes) and asked my friends and family off and on if they'd heard of it, for 10 years. i finally just found this online! they are so good! bake them for your friends and family and share the recipe with the world! note, the number of cookies you get will vary - depending on how big you roll the balls.

1. preheat oven to 325
2. cream butter , sugars , vanilla and egg
3. add oil
4. mix in dry ingredients
5. form dough into walnut sized balls
6. place on cookie sheet and flatten with a fork dipped in water
7. bake for 10- 12 minutes
8. cool on pan for a minute or two , then transfer to a rack to cook
demonstrations.review: So, I was out of oil and used an ENTIRE POUND of butter in these. This was a fabulous idea.  Crumbly, yes, fattening, yes, but good? I'd say so. My husband stood up and cheered.

target.recipe_text:
chili s spicy garlic   lime shrimp

i have not had these shrimp at the chili's restaurant, but have frequently made this recipe. we like to serve them as appetizers. however, they are equally as good tossed with some pasta (with or without alfredo sauce). the recipe came from top secret recipes and has been a favorite at our house for quite some time.

1. make the seasoning blend by combining all the spices in a small bowl
2. preheat a large skillet over medium heat
3. add butter to the pan
4. when the butter is melted , stir in the pressed garlic
5. immediately , add the shrimp to the pan
6. cut the lime in half and squeeze each half into the pan over the shrimp
7. sprinkle the entire seasoning blend over the shrimp , and give it all a good stir
8. saute the shrimp for 5 to 8 minutes or until they begin to brown
9. be sure to cook both sides of all the shrimp
target.review: Better than a restaurants! Simply great!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
wonderful parmesan zucchini strips

this was from a granny's coupon. we had it last night and it is another zucchini hit!

1. preheat oven to 450 degrees
2. in a bowl , combine bread crumbs and cheese topping
3. dip zucchini strips into egg , then into crumb mixture
4. place on baking sheet coated with nonstick cooking spray
5. bake at 450 degrees for 20-25 minutes or until golden brown and tender
demonstrations.review: Love this simple quick recipe for a snack or to serve guests. However, needs a little kick to it.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chicken breast stuffed with feta cheese  sun dried tomato

a stuffed chicken breast where the sweetness of the sun-dried tomatoes harmonizes with the saltiness of the feta cheese.

1. saut garlic and red bell pepper , in olive oil , for about 3 minutes
2. put aside to cool
3. in a bowl , combine feta cheese , breadcrumbs , thyme , sun-dried tomatoes , and garlic and red pepper mixture
4. toss until well mixed
5. lay a flattened piece of chicken breast on a cutting board or your counter
6. put a 1 / 4 of the above mixture on the flattened chicken breast like you would be making a burrito and roll as tight as you can get it
7. secure it with a toothpick or butcher string
8. place chicken breast "roll" on a baking sheet , brush with olive oil , and season with salt and pepper
9. preheat oven to 350f
10. cook for about 35 minutes or until the internal temperature reaches 180f
11. i guess you could try it on a grill , but i never attempted it yet !
12. garnish with chopped green onion and serve hot
demonstrations.review: This recipe is simple and just DELICIOUS! One to keep!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chicken with a red pepper cream sauce

fresh herbs marinate the chicken all day, and then topped with a savory red pepper cream. served over angel hair pasta lightly tossed with olive oil, basil,  and grated parmesan.

if you can't get fresh herbs, please feel free to use dry herbs for the marinade.  just use 1 teaspoon dried vs. 1 tablespoon of fresh.

also, by all means, substitute turkey breasts, pork tenderloin or cut a tenderloin in thick slices, or even use chicken thighs (boneless skinless).  secondly, this is great on fish, but obviously you only want the fish to marinade for just a couple of hours, depending on the thickness.  you don't want to over power the fish flavor.

1. marinade -- in a large baggie , add the first 8 ingredients and toss well until the chicken is well coated
2. let marinade all day
3. after marinating all day , remove and let come to room temperature
4. as the chicken rests , make the red pepper cream sauce
5. add the red peppers to a mini food processor and puree
6. add to the heavy cream in a small pan and cook on medium low for about 20 minutes to slightly reduce and thicken
7. before serving , add a little black pepper to the sauce
8. chicken -- grill the chicken , inside or outside
9. grill until golden brown
10. about 15 minutes depending on the thickness of the chicken
11. this can also be pan seared if you prefer to do that method
12. once cooked , remove and cover with foil
13. pasta -- as the chicken rests , cook the pasta accordingly in a large pot of boiling water
14. it only takes 5 minutes
15. drain and toss with the olive oil , grated parmesan , pepper and fresh basil
16. serve a bed of pasta topped with your chicken breasts sliced and then top with the red pepper cream
demonstrations.review: Absolutely delicious! I would give it five stars however the wait time for marinating is just not possible in my busy days sometimes. GREAT RECIPE THOUGH FOR THE WEEKEND!

target.recipe_text:
caesar salad sandwich

this is from the barefoot contessa. i modified it a bit to suit my family's tastes.

1. heat oven to 350 degrees
2. place the pancetta on a baking sheet in a single layer
3. roast for 10 to 15 minutes , until crisp
4. place the garlic and parsley in the bowl of a food processor fitted with a steel blade and process until minced
5. add mustard , lemon juice , and mayonnaise and process again to make a smooth dressing
6. slice the ciabatta in half horizontally and separate the top from the bottom
7. toast the bread in the oven , cut side up , for 5 to 7 minutes
8. cool slightly
9. spread the cut sides of each piece with the caesar dressing
10. place half the chopped romaine on the bottom piece of bread and then layer in order: the parmesan , crispy pancetta , and sliced chicken
11. sprinkle with salt and pepper and finish with another layer of romaine
12. place the top slice of ciabatta on top and cut into four pieces crosswise
13. serve at room temperature
target.review: This was scrumptious !!!! I just downsized the recipe because we were only 2. I found these mini Ciabatta breads at Super Target of all places which worked out perfectly because when cut in half it served the two of us. I had cooked the pancetta in the morning and made the dressing as well, then just brought everything to work and assembled there for lunch. I loved the taste the pancetta gave in this sandwich. I also buttered the bread before putting in the oven. When I grilled my chicken I had put a little bit of salt, pepper and Italian seasonings. But this was a great delicious sandwich and very filling. Thanks so much for sharing Lori I will be making this one again, we loved it.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pickled eggs 101

easy to make and keeps for weeks in the fridge. i like to give the peppercorns a bit of a whack to help release their peppery goodness. i sometimes make these in quart jars and give away for "guy gifts"... as in ..."playing poker tonight, sweetums?? here, take this jar with you to give to harold." ( woo hoo! ... a quiet night alone...thank you, harold!!!!)

1. tap a tiny air hole into the large end of each egg with a needle , sharp knife or egg piercer
2. put eggs in a pan and fill with cold water
3. bring to a boil , turn heat to low and simmer for 12 minutes
4. drain water from eggs and immediately replace with ice cold water
5. crack the egg shells against the side of the pan and keep eggs immersed in cold water while you are in the peeling process
6. peel shells from eggs and return eggs to cold water until all are finished
7. remove eggs from water and rinse thoroughly to remove any bits of shell
8. place first seven ingredients in a 2+ quart container
9. add eggs and place covered container in the refrigerator for 8+ days for flavors to "set"
demonstrations.review: Yep, these are delicious. I love the flavour of them. I never had a problem peeling my eggs the way I have been doing them , so I still cooked them my way but used this recipe . I really enjoy them, had to stop myself with just one though.  Thanks for posting the recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
creamy vegetarian lentil mushroom soup

creamy lentil soup cooked in a crockpot. serve with crusty bread or rolls for a comfort food fix! feel free to double this recipe.

1. in a saucepan , saute onions , mushrooms , garlic , and celery till just slightly browned , about 10 minutes
2. in a 3 1 / 2 or 4 quart crockpot , combine the lentils , carrots , onion , garlic , mushrooms , celery& parsley
3. stir in water , mushroom soup , and bouillon
4. cover
5. cook on low 10 to 12 hours or high 5 to 6 hours
6. top each serving with a dollop of sour cream
7. 4 servings
demonstrations.review: This soup was fantastic !!! I too did it on the stove top because it was too late for a crock pot. So I simmered it for about an hour and stirring in between. For the veggie bouillon mine was as a paste so I blended it in about 1 1/2 cups of boiled water and added that. Plus I had about 1 cup of leftover seasoned pork so I cut that up into pieces and threw it in and it added a nice flavor from the seasonings that were on the pork. Delicious flavor and great consistency, worked out perfect. We all enjoyed this at lunch. Made it with Recipe #430383 and it was yummy and so filling. Thanks for sharing your wonderful recipe Sharon. Made in honor of your DH.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
ham  noodle and swiss cheese casserole

trying to use up easter ham i threw this together using what i had in the pantry and fridge! amounts are approximate, feel free to add more or less of any ingredient! edited to change the size bag of noodles. i think it was an 8 ounce bag not 16 ounce!

1. preheat oven to 325 degrees
2. prepare egg noodles in a large dutch oven , boiling as described on package
3. drain and return to the dutch oven
4. while the noodles are boiling , melt butter in skillet over medium to medium high heat
5. stir in flour until thickened a bit
6. slowly add half and half and chicken broth , stirring to prevent lumps
7. cut heat up a bit if needed
8. slowly add swiss cheese , dry mustard and salt and pepper , stirring constantly
9. when the sauce is medium thickness , cut heat down to low
10. in the large dutch oven containing the drained noodles , add the frozen peas , ham and the sauce
11. mix well and pour into rectangular baking dish approximately 9 by 13
12. cover with french fried onions
13. bake for 20 minutes
demonstrations.review: I was looking for a recipe to use up some of my leftover ham and came across this recipe and it looked interesting. I was going to cut the recipe in half since we were only two but changed my mind. Figured leftovers could be frozen for another lunch or two. The only thing I changed was I added a handful of broccoli, I put it in the same pot of the noodles when they were almost cooked. I prepared it in the morning before going to work and then just popped it in the oven at work. Cooked it for the 20 minutes but I think it is better to put the fried onions after it comes out of the oven. Only cause in the 20 minutes I found they overcooked the fried onions. As well I would really prefer more sauce, just didn't find it saucy enough when it came out of the oven. But it definitely has a delicious flavor, the Swiss cheese was very nice and creamy tasting. Will be making this one again with a bit of extra sauce the next time. So, thanks for sharing a great recipe carolinajewel... it was a great yummy way of getting leftover ham gone.

target.recipe_text:
crock pot stifado

a tasty greek stew, made easy with a crock pot.

1. heat oil in a skillet over medium-high heat and brown beef-- in batches if necessary , adding more oil if needed
2. transfer beef to crock pot with a slotted spoon
3. reduce heat to medium and add onions to skillet , cooking until soft
4. add garlic , cinnamon and allspice and cook for 1 minute
5. add vinegar , tomato sauce , sugar and bay leaf and stir well to combine
6. pour mixture over meat
7. cover and cook on low for 8 to 10 hours or on high for 4 to 5 hours , until beef is tender
8. add feta cheese , cover again , and cook on high for 10 minutes
9. discard bay leaf and serve over hot buttered pasta or mashed potatoes
target.review: My husband who never cooks made this for me and boy was this amazing!! I'm definately making this one again!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
molasses maple glazed beef brisket crock pot

from the rival crock pot cookbook, this has a nice tangy glaze you won't want to miss!

1. combine cayenne pepper , salt and pepper in a small bowl
2. rub mixture all over the brisket
3. place brisket in resealable plastic bag
4. combine olive oil , maple syrup , molasses , brown sugar , tomato paste , orange juice , garlic and orange peel in a small bowl
5. pour mixture over brisket in plastic bag
6. refrigerate marinated brisket for at least 2 hours or overnight , turning bag several times
7. transfer brisket and marinade to crockpot and cook on low for 7-9 hours or on high for 3 1 / 2-4 hours , turning once or twice
8. adjust seasonings to taste
9. slice thinly across the grain and serve
10. enjoy
demonstrations.review: Very good and really easy. Thanks for submitting!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
slow cooker  crock pot  pumpkin apple dessert

just got this from betty crocker and had to post it for the holidays! yummy!!

1. spray 3 1 / 2- to 6-quart slow cooker with cooking spray
2. spoon pie filling into cooker
3. spread evenly
4. beat remaining ingredients except ice cream with electric mixer on low speed 1 minute , scraping bowl constantly
5. beat on medium speed 2 minutes , scraping bowl occasionally
6. pour batter over pie filling
7. cover and cook on high heat setting 1 hour 30 minutes to 2 hours or until toothpick inserted in center comes out clean
8. serve with ice cream
9. for slow cookers with just a heated base , follow the manufacturers directions for layering ingredients and choosing a temperature
demonstrations.review: Good but lacked a bit of flavour I would add a bit more sugar to the dough. Thanks for the recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
dark chocolate cake

while it takes slightly longer to prepare this recipe than a box mix, the resulting moist, delicious cake makes it very worth the little extra time. i consider this 'perfect' chocolate cake. this cake is excellent with  both with recipe #261024 and recipe #208959 (the dark flavor version). (i use recipe #95416 when i'm decorating the cake.) i love how the leftovers are still moist even a day or two later. (i store my loosely covered with plastic wrap.)
my father adores this cake with recipe #261024 on it. for his birthday, father's day etc. i make him cupcakes with the icing on them and individually wrap them. he keeps them in his freezer for when he wants "a piece of cake". he claims they are as good as when they are fresh. 
(even though it isn't where i got the recipe from so i can't vouch for it, reviewers have said it is the recipe on the hershey's cocoa can. i would recommend using their special dark cocoa if possible.)

1. heat oven to 350f
2. grease and flour two 9 inch round baking pans or one 13x9 inch pan
3. in large mixer bowl , stir together dry ingredients
4. add eggs , milk , oil , and vanilla
5. beat on medium speed for 2 minutes
6. stir in boiling water by hand
7. i usually use between 2 / 3 & 3 / 4 cups
8. the cake is still very moist but it doesn't seem to "fall" as much as it cools
9. this might have to do with our high humidity or brand of flour or other factors so i don't know if it will work for everyone
10. pour into prepared pan
11. bake 30 to 35 minutes for round 9-inch pans , 35 to 40 minutes for rectangular pan or until wooden pick inserted in center comes out clean
12. because they have a tendency to overflow if you fill them more than 2 / 3 full , i usually get about 27-28 cupcakes per batch
13. bake for approximately 18-20 minutes
14. cool 10 minutes
15. remove from pan to wire racks
16. please
17. chocolate drink mixes that you add to milk or water to drink will not work in this recipe
demonstrations.review: amazing and soooo moist!!!!!!!!!! Great, easy recipie. Bye bye mixes

target.recipe_text:
awesome  hawaiian haystacks

this is great for large groups. has an absolutely wonderful taste and easy to make. feeds a large family easily.

1. cook chicken and cut into bite size pieces
2. melt butter in large pan
3. add flour , salt and milk
4. stir well
5. add 2 cans of cream of mushroom soup , can of mushrooms and chicken
6. simmer
7. cook rice with rice cooker , amount for number of people to feed
8. layer on plate: rice , chow mein noodles , soup mixture , pineapple , cheese , celery , green onions , coconut , almonds , and soy sauce
9. use toppings to suit your tastes
target.review: I was just going to enter this very recipe but saw it already done for me.  I love this recipe and so does EVERYONE I serve it to!  It really is great for groups... set it up like a taco bar and everyone is happy with what's on their plate.  It's very filling, sometimes we even omit the chicken and make it a vegetarian-type meal.  I also use chopped tomatoes and diced bell pepper.  I've never tried the mushrooms, almonds, or cheese, but will in the future.  Also, you can use a can of chicken gravy or a mix, that's what we do.  Love this recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
simply oven baked pork chops and rice

this is dh's recipe. it is simple comfort food and is very versatile. you can use chicken quarters in place of chops or chicken broth in place of water. feel free to experiment with different herbs. we never make this the same way twice. a side note: i would recommend using a bone in, fattier cut of pork and not loin chops in this recipe.

1. stir together soup , water , rice and 1 / 4 teaspoons pepper in a 3 quart casserole
2. add onions
3. salt and pepper chops and place on top of rice
4. cover and bake at 350 for 1 1 / 4 hours or until meat is done and liquid is absorbed
5. remove from oven and let rest 5 minutes
demonstrations.review: Super Yummy!  I browned the meat and put it in-and-out of the oven, my 9-year old son did the rest.  The whole (super-picky) family LOVED IT!!!<br/><br/>Substitutions:<br/>Cream of Chicken Soup instead of Mushroom Soup<br/>1.5 tea chicken base instead of chicken bouillon<br/>1.5 tea onion powder instead of onion<br/><br/>Additions:<br/>1 tea Mrs. Dash Seasoning Salt<br/>3/4 cup shredded cheddar cheese (stirred into rice)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chimichangas

some friends of ours made these for a party at their house, and they were fantastic. particularly delicious with chile con queso on top. these are also fantastic from the fridge the next day; just grab one, heat it up, and eat it like a burrito!

1. cook chicken in skillet with a touch of oil
2. add bell peppers and salsa
3. add spanish rice , right from the package , and water
4. bring it all to a boil , then let simmer for 15 minutes
5. lay out the tortillas and spoon some of the mixture into each one
6. sprinkle each with cheddar cheese
7. roll each tortilla , 1 side , both ends , then the other side
8. use a toothpick to hold it closed
9. fry each tortilla in a skillet of preheated oil
10. set on paper towel to dry
11. optionally , place rolled tortillas in a 350 degree oven for 10 to 15 minutes instead of frying them
demonstrations.review: "A+ Keeper!" rates my husband.  I used the 6.8 oz Rice-A-Roni and it came out great.  I fried on the stove in a small cast iron skillet with about 3/8" canola oil - they weren't greasy tasting at all!  I served with a dollop of sour cream.  Next time I may toast the vermicelli first.  They do heat up well (I warmed it in a toaster oven at 350F for about 10 minutes).  I froze half of the filling to use later because this does make 8-10 good size chimichangas.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
oven fried southern style cinnamon honey chicken

while watching foodtv, i saw a piece about amy ruth's restaurant in new york where the owner made fried chicken dipped in a honey cinnamon mixture. it looked so good i began searching on the web for a recipe which approximated it... and after much browsing of webpages i put together a recipe that i thought might taste something like it. i don't fry my chicken, so here's a baked version, tweaked to my own tastes.

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees f
2. spray a large roasting pan lightly with cooking spray
3. combine the flour with the salt , cinnamon , turmeric , black pepper , and a pinch nutmeg
4. coat the chicken pieces well with the flour mixture
5. beat together the egg and milk
6. dredge the flour-coated chicken pieces in the egg mixture , then into the breadcrumbs
7. arrange pieces skin side up in the sprayed roasting pan , making sure that the pieces are not touching each other to ensure they bake crispy
8. spray chicken pieces with oil spray or sprinkle with 2 tablespoons oil and place the chicken in the oven to bake
9. while the chicken is baking , in a saucepan over medium low heat combine the butter , honey , pinches of cinnamon , and lemon juice
10. after the chicken has baked for 25 minutes , pour the butter and honey mixture generously over the pieces
11. bake for an additional 15 minutes or until the juices run clear and the chicken is crisp and brown
demonstrations.review: Tasty!  Hot or cold, this tastes delicious.  (I keep wanting more hours after the meal.)  I made this last night and my husband said "nice change", then after eating seconds he said "you can keep this recipe."  We had to test it for leftovers, and we liked it that way too.  Cold you taste more of the honey, warm the cinnamon; both ways are delicious.  I made it with boneless skinless breasts baked at 350 F for 20-30 minutes... so juicy and tender!  Thanks for sharing this keeper.  :)

target.recipe_text:
vegetarian taco soup

this is a quick and healthy meatless soup. i usually serve it with cornbread.

1. drain and rinse first six ingredients in a large colander
2. put in a crockpot or large pot
3. add all other ingredients , stirring to mix well
4. simmer about 30 minutes to an hour or cook in your crockpot on high for 2 hours
target.review: I served this at a party and it was a big hit! It's easy to make and it tastes great.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
easy slow cooked vegetarian taco soup

this recipe was one of many given to us in a pretty recipe box at my wedding shower. easy and delicious, this comforting, aromatic soup is perfect for cold winter days. we like it with salad and quesadillas for a simple, delicious mexican meal.

1. combine all ingredients in slow cooker
2. simmer for three or more hours
3. serve with grated cheese , tortilla chips , extra fresh cilantro and diced onions , shredded cabbage or diced radishes
demonstrations.review: Great recipe. I use one can of mexican tomatoes, and one or two regular diced tomatoes as my kids and husband dont' like things very spicey. I've made it several times now, and once I left out the broth - didn't notice a huge difference and it made it vegetarian for us. We're having it again tonight! Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
raspberry pie

this is so good. all i can saw is mmm mmm good.

1. in a bowl combine flour and confectioners sugar , cut in butter until crumbly
2. press onto bottom and sides of a ungreased 9 inch pan
3. bake at 350f for 22 minutes or until edges are golden brown
4. cool on wire rack
5. in a saucepan , combine sugar and cornstarch
6. stir in water until smooth , then stir in corn syrup
7. bring to a boil
8. cook and stir for 2 minutes or until thick
9. remove from heat
10. stir in gelatin and vanilla until gelatin is dissolved
11. cool to room temp , about 30 minutes
12. add raspberries , stirring gently to coat
13. spoon into crust
14. refrigerate until set , about 3 hours
demonstrations.review: What a great treat and a good way to use fresh raspberries! We loved the taste of this raspberry dessert. I didn't have strawberry gelatin, so I used cherry. I didn't see a measurement for vanilla, so I went through my cookbooks to find comparable recipes and ended up adding about 1/4 tsp vanilla. I don't have a 9x9 pan, so I used one that is closer to 8x10. I wish I'd had the right size pan. I didn't press the crust up the sides of the pan, and I should have because the crust was a little thick on the bottom. I have two small children, and I liked that I could work on part of the recipe and then come back later to do something else. It didn't require me to stand in the kitchen for hours on end. Just 15 minutes here and there. My husband had been skeptical, but really liked the dessert. We'll be making this again! Thanks for a fun, easy recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
easy  creamy hamburger stroganoff

this easy version of stroganoff is so delicious. i have people beg me to make it for them when they come over for dinner. hope you enjoy it!

1. brown hamburger in large skillet with onion and garlic
2. drain out fat and add soup , sour cream , mustard and milk
3. simmer for 5 minutes
4. add salt and pepper for taste , and serve with egg noodles or rice
demonstrations.review: I've made this twice now. Once cooking the hamburger in worcestershire sauce, and once making it without it. I liked it best with the worcestershire sauce. I didn't have the dry mustard and I used cream of chicken soup instead of mushroom. We ate it over rice and loved it! It's a simple and easy recipe that tastes great!

target.recipe_text:
the realtor s buttermilk  garlic salad dressing

i love this dressing!  it's so creamy and delicious!  if you are out of buttermilk, you can substitute 1/4 cup sour cream and 1/4 cup milk.  i have done that many times with very good results.  this one tastes great either way.  make it the day before you plan to use it if you can.  that way the flavors will have time to blend.

1. place mayo and buttermilk in a covered container and shake to combine
2. add all the other ingredients and shake until well blended
3. store in refrigerator for up to 1 week
4. shake before using
target.review: Yum! I just hate bottled dressings so I finally decided to take the leap and make my own and this recipe was great.  I admit that the taste was probably a bit different since I used low-fat Hellmann's and skim milk/lemon juice for the buttermilk, but the taste was still fresh and tasty!  I used it on salads and for dipping veggies all week long-makes the perfect amount!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
baked chicken teriyaki

easy and delicious weeknight meal.  the sauce thickens while cooking so prep time is at a minimum and is perfect with rice and broccoli.  you can use any cut of chicken you like - just adjust the cooking time accordingly.

1. preheat oven to 425 degrees f
2. combine the first 10 ingredients in a bowl
3. place chicken pieces in a lightly greased 9x13 inch baking dish
4. pour sauce over chicken and turn to thoroughly coat
5. bake in the preheated oven for 30 minutes
6. turn pieces over , and bake for another 10 minutes , until no longer pink and juices run clear
7. spoon sauce over chicken and serve
8. if using bone-in chicken breasts , bake at 375 for 35-40 minutes
9. if using boneless chicken breasts , bake at 375 for 20-25 minutes
10. if you prefer , bring all the ingredients to a boil in a saucepan on the stove and let simmer until thick
11. brush the chicken with the resulting glaze
demonstrations.review: This will definitely be my go-to teriyaki chicken recipe from now on.  So easy, I just whisked the ingredients together while my oven preheated, put the chicken in the pan, poured the sauce on top and dinner is good as done!  I like how the sauce reduced, though next time I might add a smidge more cornstarch, and I love how the chicken got a bit crispy on the edges...mmmm.  Thanks CFRP!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s baked potato salad casserole  or cold potato salad

this may be served hot as a casserole or reduce the melted butter amount down to 2 tablespoons and serve as a cold potato salad, either way it's delicious! --- if you are serving hot as a casserole i strongly recommend to have the potatoes cooled to room temperature before using in this recipe or use cold potatoes that have been cooked a day ahead, i have even made this using about 5 cups of thawed frozen hash browns, the complete casserole may be assembled and refrigerated for up to 2 days ahead before baking although it's so delicious cold it might not even make it to the oven, and also makes a large amount which makes this *perfect* dish for potlucks --- if you are baking as a casserole use only mayonnaise such as hellman's using salad dressing will not be as good.

1. to serve hot as a casserole
2. grease a 13 x 9-inch baking dish
3. set oven to 350 degrees f
4. in a large bowl , mix mayonnaise , sour cream and melted butter , garlic powder , seasoned salt and black pepper until well combined
5. mix in green onion and yellow onion
6. add in the cooked cubed potatoes , cubed cheese and ham mix with a large spatula until well combined
7. transfer / spread the mixture to prepared casserole dish
8. at this point you may cover and refrigerate for up to 24 hours until ready to bake
9. bake 25-30 minutes or until hot and bubbly
10. remove from oven and sprinkle the grated cheddar on top
11. return to oven and bake 5-8 minutes more or until the cheese has melted
12. to serve as a cold potato salad
13. make as stated in steps 3-5 reducing the melted butter to 2 tablespoons
14. place in a bowl , cover and refrigerate for at least 4 hours or more before serving
15. delicious !
demonstrations.review: "oh, yeah..." these are my husbands exact words when I served this with a steak dinner.  So easy to put together and so creamy and tasty.  I used Miracle Whip light, light sour cream, low fat cheese and turkey bacon and it was still fantastic!  A definite keeper and I'll make this often.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s honey garlic sauce

this sauce may be used with meatballs, ribs, chicken wings anything you desire, and may be doubled if desired but do increase the fresh garlic too much or the garlic flavor will be to strong, the chili flakes are only optional i like to add them in for some heat :)

1. in a bowl whisk together the chicken broth with cornstarch until smooth and no lumps remain
2. add in honey , soy sauce , vinegar and brown sugar
3. whisk vigorously until well combined
4. in a medium saucepan heat oil over medium-low heat
5. add in garlic and chili flakes cook stirring until softened
6. whisk in cornstarch mixture
7. bring to a simmer stirring constantly and cook until the sauce is slightly thickened
8. delicious !
demonstrations.review: 5 BIG stars from our dinner table Kitten!  I made two asian sauces for roasted chicken thighs and DH and I both preferred this sweet, thick sauce.  I had to make this recipe twice due to my own error and the second time I simply sauteed the red pepper/garlic in the oil, then added all other ingredients except for half the water and the cornstarch.  I let it come to a boil, then added the slurry, gave it a whisk and it was done!  Yum, yum, yum...I think next time I'll try using splenda to see if I can't lower the calorie content a bit.  Thanks!

target.recipe_text:
amazing vegan cinnamon buns

i got this recipe form foodgeeks.com and it is the best thing i've ever eaten in my life! it works best if you cook them in a glass pan.

1. combine tepid water and sugar in small bowl , add yeast and stir
2. allow to proof for 10 minutes
3. in bread machine using dough cycle , or in heavy duty mixer with dough hook , combine yeast mixture with flour nutmeg and salt
4. mix / knead until smooth and elastic
5. transfer to bowl oiled with 1 tablespoons oil , cover with plastic wrap and let rise until double , about 1 hour
6. mix remaining ingredients in bowl until well blended
7. refrigerate
8. punch down dough and divide into 2 balls
9. roll 1 ball into 9x13-inch rectangle
10. spread half of filling mixture on dough and roll up
11. cut roll into 1 to 1-1 / 2-inch slices
12. place slices into non-stick 8-inch cake pan , cover and allow to rise 1 / 2 hour
13. when risen , bake in preheated 350f oven for 15 to 20 minutes , or until golden brown
target.review: Just wanted to point out, that while these are very good, they are not vegan. Yeast and sugar included in this recipe make that claim false.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
soba salad with miso dressing

superfast veggie dinner or side dish.  courtesy of mark bittman, the minimalist, from the october 1 2009 ny times.  he's not sure whether to call this a warm salad or a room-temperature noodle dish.  i love edamame beans, and buying them frozen is fine for this dish.  pick up a bag of pre-washed spinach for this too.  tossing the spinach with the warm noodles and veggies should wilt the spinach, or stir fry them together in a little water to wilt a bit more.  soba noodles are a staple of japan.  they have a slightly firm texture and nutty flavor.

1. bring a large pot of water to a boil and salt it
2. drop in the noodles and carrot and cook until tender , 2 to 4 minutes
3. add the edamame for about 30 seconds to 1 minute just to warm , then drain everything in a colander
4. set aside
5. in a large salad bowl , whisk together the soy sauce , lime juice , miso and mirin or sugar
6. add spinach , noodles , carrot , edamame , scallion and toss
7. then taste and season with salt and pepper as needed
8. garnish with grated ginger at the table
demonstrations.review: Excellent. I mostly wanted to try this recipe for the dressing and it was delicious. I can only imagine how much better it'll be with edamame the next time I make it. I used mixed greens instead of spinach and topped with sesame seeds. Served as a main dish for myself and with salmon on the side for BF. Yummy recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chickpea dahl

dahl is a staple in india, usually eaten with every meal.  my family always eats dahl when we make indian food.  this is a new recipe for dahl made and demonstrated by cinda sanders on a cooking show titled "indian cuisine."

1. cook potatoes in salted water until tender yet firm
2. drain and set aside
3. saute onion in 1 tablespoons oil until clear
4. transfer to a food processor along with the tomatoes and fresh ginger , and blend until smooth
5. set aside
6. in a large saucepan , melt margarine and add the curry powder and cumin
7. saute for 4-5 minutes over medium heat
8. stir often to avoid burning
9. add the tomato mixture and continue to cook for 5 - 6 minutes , stirring often
10. add the chickpeas , potatoes and frozen peas
11. cook 5 - 10 minutes more
12. serve hot over rice
demonstrations.review: Pretty good. Not sure if I was supposed to add the juice from the canned tomatos though as it seemed a little too soupy. I added a can of mixed beans to compensate. Tastes nice and fresh. Served over leftover macaroni (strange I know, but it's what was needing to be used up) Delicious. Would probably serve over couscous or rice if I make it again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
braised cabbage  carrots   onions

nan

1. add cabbage , carrots and parsley , to butter in a medium sauce pan , and mix until well coated with butter
2. stir in salt , pepper and broth
3. cover , bring to a boil , reduce heat to low and cook for 10 to 15 minutes or until vegetables are tender-crisp and still quite bright in colour
4. if too much liquid remains in skillet near the end of the cooking time , uncover and increase heat to high for a minute
5. stir often while liquid evaporates
demonstrations.review: Great recipe to play around with. Reminds me of the cabbage and apples dish my mother always makes. I followed the recipe , but subbed olive oil for the butter, left out the parsley because I didn't have any and used veggie stock instead of chicken. Tastes pretty good, but I did eat it with ketchup because it needs a bit more zing to it. Enjoyed it a lot!!

target.recipe_text:
turmeric rice

this has a nice golden color and goes well with curries

1. melt 1 tbsp butter in saucepan , add onion and garlic , cook until softened
2. add rice and turmeric
3. stir to coat
4. add remaining ingredients , bring to boil , cover and simmer 17 minutes
5. stir in remaining butter , remove bay leaf , serve
target.review: My husband is very particular about the meals that he eats.  He said this rice was an excellent combination of flavors and was delicious!!  We served this as a side dish to Costa Rican Jalapeno Pepper Steak, recipe #66695.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
costa rican jalapeno pepper steak

i came across this recipe in costa rica and asked the chef for his recipe.it turned out he was also canadian.delicious and easy to make. try it.

1. grill , broil or pan fry steaks to your preference
2. in a fry pan add butter chopped onion and chopped jalapeno and cook for 1-2 minutes
3. add evaporated milk and chicken cube to pan and bring to boil stirring often
4. lower heat and simmer for about 2 minutes
5. place pre cooked steaks in sauce and heat through
6. place steak on platters and pour sauce over steaks
7. serve with rice and broccoli
8. enjoy
demonstrations.review: The sauce makes the steak....anyone can have a plain steak, but the sauce really makes this steak.  We used sirloin.  We served Tumeric Rice (recipe # 48162) and broccoli as sides.  Delicious!!  My husband is very in tune with what he puts in his body and he loved this meal!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crock pot lamb chops dinner

i only recently discovered lamb, but we found we love it. here is my first attempt to 'create' my own dish using lamb chops. hope you enjoy it as much as we did!

1. spray crock pot with non-stick spray
2. brown lamb chops on both sides if desired
3. place in bottom of crock pot
4. in fry pan used to brown lamb chops , cook onions and garlic , with curry powder , just until beginning to turn transparent
5. transfer onions and garlic to crock pot , spreading evenly over lamb chops
6. lay bay leaves on top
7. arrange potato quarters evenly on top of previously arranged ingredients being sure they do not touch the sides of the crock pot
8. arrange carrots over top
9. try to avoid leaving any potatoes exposed as they will tend to turn dark
10. salt and pepper to taste
11. cover
12. cook on high for at least 3 hours , or cook on low for at least 6 hours , or cook on high , then reduce to low allowing 2 hours on low for each hour on high
13. when there is only an hour left of cooking time , place asparagus spears on top of all and sprinkle a little more curry powder on top
14. if you wish , you can add a tablespoon of butter on top of the asparagus
demonstrations.review: My husband loved this!  He used to have lamb as a child, and this flavor brought him back!  I had to buy more lamb today (we just had this the first time 4 nights ago) and am about to prepare this meal again!  I also mixed the water and soy sauce and poured it around the chops after arranging the vegetables.  Delicious!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
fahdreiteh chicken

i originally got this recipe from dudi gur who donated it to a community cookbook. fahdreiteh means mixed-up in yiddish, but this chicken is anything but. a heavenly and delicious smell will pervade the house which is in equal only to the taste of the chicken itself.

1. clean the chicken well and wipe dry
2. prepare a marinade with the crushed garlic , paprika , sea salt , salt , oil and soy sauce
3. let the mixture rest of 20 minutes
4. place the chicken pieces in the marinade and turn to cover well
5. cover the dish and place in the refrigerator for 24 hours
6. bake uncovered for approximately one hour at 250 degrees celsius
demonstrations.review: Just like it says....smells wonderful when it's cooking!!  I used just one dish for the entire meal!  I mixed the marinade in a glass lasagna dish, added the chicken, flipped the chicken to get all of the flavors.  Covered and refrigerated for 24 hours, then put that same dish from the refrigerator right into the oven at 350 for one hour.  Came out great!!

target.recipe_text:
chocolate banana cake

this is a very moist & very fudgey cake. it tastes best the second day.

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees f
2. cream margarine with sugar and eggs
3. mix in banana and vanilla
4. mix flour with remaining dry ingredients
5. add flour mixture to margarine mixture in 3 parts , alternately with sour milk
6. begin and end with flour
7. spread in 2 greased 8" cake pans
8. bake in oven about 40 minutes
9. when cool , frost generously with chocolate butter frosting
target.review: OMG absolute heaven, moist banana background flavor with an iceable cake not like most breadish consistencies from the bananas, I made it in a 13X9 pan since it would stay fresher after cut that way, at least in our family it lasts better, i iced it with kittencals choc buttercream (using only 1/3 cup cocoa powder) perfect light choclate icing for this moist cake! I am not a great baker and this one came out perfect, thank you!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
the best belgian waffles

these waffles are super crisp on the outside, light as a feather inside and so scrumptious! avoid removing them from the waffle iron too soon; they should be a golden brown. enjoy!

1. oil the waffle maker
2. sift the dry ingredients together in a large bowl
3. in separate bowl , separate egg whites and beat until stiff peaks form
4. in a separate bowl , mix together the egg yolks , milk , oil , and vanilla , stir slightly
5. add to dry ingredients and mix well
6. fold in egg whites
7. cook in waffle iron on medium-high heat for around 5-10 minutes
demonstrations.review: I love this recipe, simple to remember and I add vanilla and then sometimes crumble cooked bacon or pecans into the waffle iron as I add the batter....always crisp outer waffle and delicate inner never heavy or doughy!!!  Thanks so much for sharing this one!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s chocolate frosting icing

a wonderful frosting i have used for years made in very little time with perfect results and 100% better than any canned, this frosting is so good you will find yourself eating a fair amount of it before even using it to frost with! --- choose the amount of cocoa powder you desire for either a light, medium or dark frosting, and make certain to sift the cocoa powder and the confectioners sugar before using for the recipe--- this frosting *freezes* very well so double the recipe and freeze one batch for next time --- *note* for an ultra creamy fluffy milk chocolate frosting add in 1 to 1-1/2 cups thawed cool whip topping at the end of mixing the frosting and beat on low speed until blended ------- also see my recipe#80118 ---- recipe#282040 --- recipe#90142

1. cream the butter in a small bowl
2. blend in the cocoa powder , vanilla , confectioners sugar , alternately with the cream
3. beat with an electric mixer , until the desired texture is achieved
demonstrations.review: wow this was good, and yep I ate some before icing the cake.....yummy and held up nicely on a sheet cake that I iced too warm!!! thank you!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
iced oatmeal cookies

my grandma used to make these cookies when i was a little girl.  i had lost the recipe and just found it a couple weeks ago, so i want to share it with you all.

1. cream together butter and sugar
2. add eggs , honey and vanilla
3. combine flour , baking soda , cinnamon and salt
4. gradually add to creamed mixture
5. stir in oats
6. drop by the teaspoonfuls onto cookie sheet
7. bake at 350f for 6-7 minutes
8. mix together powdered sugar and milk until smooth
9. cool cookies for about a minute on wire rack , then ice with a thick powdered sugar glaze
demonstrations.review: great recipe, makes a ton of cookies and I used regular oats, did not have any quick ones and 1/2 cinnamon, 1/2 ginger powder, since I am not a cinnamon fan.....i made them to give as valentines gifts, thanks for sharing!

target.recipe_text:
southern fried salmon patties

salmon patties are quick and easy.  i got this recipe from my son's babysitter many years ago.  my son is now 20 and we still eat these at least a few times a month.  these are very moist when done.

1. open salmon and drain thoroughly
2. place drained salmon in mixing bowl and flake evenly with a fork
3. add onion , corn meal , flour , mayonnaise , and egg
4. stir until well blended
5. shape the mixture into patties about the size of an average burger or less
6. cook in oil in skillet over medium heat until browned on each side
7. turn once while frying
target.review: These are good.  I had to get used to the onion in the patties (as I've always made them without before) but I liked them.  I made them exactly as the recipe states and they seemed a bit soft, but very good!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crunchy granola

this granola makes a great, filling snack. good dry or with milk. it is very addictive, but it's good for you, so enjoy!

1. heat oven to 275 degrees f
2. line 2 cookie sheets with parchment paper
3. combine brown sugar and water in a 4 cup microwave proof cup
4. microwave on high 5 minutes until sugar is completely dissolved
5. remove from microwave and stir in vanilla and salt
6. in large mixing bowl , mix oats , nuts , and brown sugar mixture
7. mix thoroughly
8. spread onto cookie sheets and bake 45 minutes-1 hour until golden brown
9. when granola has cooled completely , add fruits if you wish and store in airtight container
demonstrations.review: Excellent!  I made half a batch and added a little bit of cinnamon.  It was so easy to make and so much better than store bought.  I will definitely be making this again.  Thank you!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
spicy baked sweet potato  fries

this recipe is adapted from a weight loss websites newsletter. posted for 2006 zaar world tour - mexico

1. preheat oven to 450f with aluminum foil or parchment paper , line a cookie sheet
2. in a medium bowl , combine sweet potatoes with olive oil and seasonings
3. mix well to evenly coat potatoes
4. place potato strips on the foil or parchment lined cookie sheet and leave space between strips for even baking
5. bake for approximately 15 minutes or until potatoes become crispy
6. turn strips every 5 to 7 minutes as needed
7. serve immediately
demonstrations.review: I have made these several times and absolutely love these.  Yum, yum yum!  Haven't changed a thing.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
healthy no bake cookies

i played around with my family's no bake cookie recipe and produced a single portion of this cookie that i feel is healthy enough to eat as a meal.  they’re still very good but are much healthier. i keep getting asked for the recipe, so i finally decided to measure out the exact portions and post the recipe. this recipe is very flexible! when i make them i never measure out anything and i often add more or less of ingredients and they still taste great.  i sometimes leave out the wheat germ and flax seeds and just add more oatmeal.  i have made these replacing the sugar with about 3 tablespoons of honey.  i have changed the recipe from 1 tsp. to 1 tbsp. of cocoa powder.

1. heat milk , sugar and cocoa powder over high heat until boiling , stirring constantly
2. take off heat and stir in vanilla and peanut butter
3. stir until peanut butter has melted completely
4. stir in wheat germ and oatmeal
5. drop by large spoonfuls onto wax paper or eat immediately
6. as i
7. if you don't have wheat germ or flax seed , just use more oatmeal
8. the recipe above should work out just perfectly and does most of the time , but if your cookies come out crumbly , use less oatmeal next time
9. if they never set , use more oatmeal next time
demonstrations.review:
I made it without the wheat germ, and added a bit more flax seeds. I also substituted the skim milk with soy milk. They are good, but I'm not a no-bake cookie convert!

Update 5/2011: Made these again with all specific ingredients and I had to downgrade my rating. I do not like these. I put in more cocoa and upped the peanut butter. I'm not sure what is missing, but I don't want to make another batch to find out.

target.recipe_text:
zucchini lasagna  lasagne    low carb

great for anyone going low carb or who has so many zucchini, they don't know what to do!! :) we found the sauce to be very mild. i think it would be better with twice as much garlic. i boiled my zucchini slices for about 3 minutes so they were partially cooked. i wanted to make sure they were soft in the finished dish or i knew the kids wouldn't eat them. ;) the cottage cheese provides a slightly tangy note. i think we would have preferred ricotta, but that is personal taste. i use my 11x7 baking dish and got 6 pieces the size of what you see in my photos. both of the guys ate two so it fed 4 of us, and i double the meat. adjust the recipe accordingly for your family.

1. cook zucchini until tender , drain and set aside
2. fry meat and onions until meat is brown and onions are tender
3. drain fat
4. add next 8 ingredients and bring to a boil
5. reduce heat
6. simmer , uncovered 10 minutes or until reduced to 2 cups
7. in small bowl slightly beat egg
8. add cottage cheese , half of shredded cheese and flour
9. in baking-roasting pan arrange half of the meat mixture
10. top with half of the zucchini and all the cottage cheese mixture
11. top with remaining meat and zucchini
12. bake uncovered at 375 degrees f for 30 minutes
13. sprinkle with remaining cheese
14. bake 10 minutes longer
15. let stand 10 minutes before serving
target.review: This was great and easy to make; a good one to make ahead of time. I put it in the fridge in the afternoon so all I had to do was pop it in the oven in the evening. I assume the cottage cheese was probably suggested to keep this a low-fat meal, but I used fat-free ricotta to keep my calories down and still get the Italian taste of ricotta. I also doubled the meat portions--because my boyfriend is a meat head...and we love us some meat.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mediterranean spinach turkey wrap

this is a good for lunch. you can make pinweels out of these and serve them as a finger food for parties.

1. chop up olives
2. combine cream cheese , feta cheese , olives and oregano in bowl and mix
3. evenly spread the mixture over entire tortilla
4. place turkey over the cream cheese mixture on half of each tortilla
5. place spinach leaves on top of turkey
6. to assemble just start with the side that is topped with the turkey and roll up tightly
7. wrap each sandwich with saran wrap
8. refrigerate wraps at least 1 hour
9. before serving , unwrap , and trim of ends of each roll
10. cut wraps into 3 sections
11. cut each section on a slight diagonal into half
12. wraps can be made a day ahead
13. enjoy
demonstrations.review: This was a very tasty wrap, but the feta and cream cheese mix was a little too overpowering for me. Next time, I think I might try adding some cottage cheese or something else to give it it's bulk, but still seem light. I can see this being an ideal appetizer cut into mini pin-wheels as suggested, but sitting down for an entire wrap--the flavors were just too heavy for me.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pork chops

this is a fantastic easy meal that is a real winner each time. i make mine with lots of ground pepper for a slighty hotter sauce and the trick is to have a pan with a very tight lid i use a pan that is used for soup making.

1. fry the bacon on a medium heat until brown and slightly crisp
2. remove and set aside
3. turn the heat down and into the same pan add 1 tbs of oil and fry the onions until golden , add the garlc , bay leaf and thyme-remove and set aside
4. heat the oil in a large skillet over high heat until shimmering , 2 to 3minutes
5. meanwhile , pat the chops dry with paper towels and season generously with salt and pepper
6. place the chops in the pan in a single layer and cook until a deep brown crust forms , about 2 minutes
7. turn the chops over and cook for another 2 minutes
8. transfer to a pan that has a very tight lid
9. arrange the chops on the bottom and cover with the onions
10. mix the packet of instant gravy mix with the stock and the flour and pour over the top of the onions
11. sprinkle with remaining bacon and place the lid on tightly cook for 20 minutes on a medium heat
12. remove the lid and keep reducing the sauce until it is of a gravy like consistency
demonstrations.review: This dish was delicious; I also served with paprika mashed potatoes and a salad. I've had a few requests to make it again and it's only been a week!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
italian pepper and sausage dinner

it seems like i make this with my eyes closed already. the family loves it as well as guests. you can make as much as you want and if you are lucky to have leftovers, it's better the second time around. enjoy!

1. in a large , skillet brown the sausage until it is cooked through
2. drain the fat and drain the sausage on paper towels
3. in the same pan heat your olive oil add and saut the peppers , and onions , until the onion is translucent , then add the garlic and saut gently but do not brown your garlic
4. this will make the dish bitter
5. the vegetables should be tender
6. stir in the tomatoes , spices , romano cheese and sausage
7. cover the pan and simmer all over a medium-low heat for 8-10 minute
8. if your mixture seems too thick you can add a little water or red wine
9. while the meat mixture is cooking , the pasta can be prepared as per directions
10. you do not want to overcook your pasta
11. you want a little firmness to your noodles
12. when you are ready to serve use a large platter
13. the noodles first , then spoon the meat mixture over
14. mix slightly
15. sprinkle with the parigiano-reggiano and place your fresh basil leaves atop
16. this goes well with a full bodied red wine , a green salad with italian oil and vinegar dressing , and most of all a good hard crusted peasant bread
demonstrations.review: I've made this once with sausage, and my boyfriend raved about it. I'm not a huge sausage fan, so the second time I replaced it with grilled chicken--it was still spectacular. The boyfriend still loved it too. Thank you!

target.recipe_text:
oatmeal apple pear crisp

i've been making this (or versions of it) since i was 12 years old. this is an evolved version of the 

1. while peeling apples and pears , keep them in the lemon juice so they don't turn brown
2. place apples in a greased shallow 9 square baking dish
3. sprinkle brown sugar , ground cinnamon , ground nutmeg and water
4. combine remaining dry ingredients in a separate bowl
5. add melted butter , mixing until crumbly
6. sprinkle crumb mixture on top of the apples
7. bake at 375f for 30-40 minutes or until apples are tender
8. serve with vanilla ice cream or yogurt , great by itself too
target.review: This recipe is excellent and great for using up extra pears/apples.  I followed the recipe exactly, and the result was a very rich and satisfying dessert.  Hubby added a scoop of butterfinger ice cream, and it was to die for.  He was still talking about this recipe this morning.  Thanks for posting this lovely simple recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
beth s melt in your mouth barbecue ribs  oven

i almost didn't want to share this ribs recipe because this is one of the dishes that i make that keep my sons coming back home! these can be done with baby back or regular pork ribs. i have also made split chickens this way. the ribs are tender, moist and just slide off of the bone. i know that your family will love them just as much as my family does.
i noticed that some are unable to find hickory smoked salt. you can use smoked paprika or just brush the ribs with liquid smoke before applying the rub. the smoke flavor is nice because it helps give the ribs a cooked-on-the-grill flavor.
also, the easiest way to remove the membrane is to work a spoon, or i use the tips of my kitchen shears, into the bottom center of the membrane, work it back and forth to form a "pocket," then i slide my thumbs in and work the membrane off from the center outward to the ends.

1. preheat oven to 300 degrees f
2. line a baking sheet with two layers of foil , shiny side out
3. peel off tough membrane that covers the bony side of the ribs
4. season the ribs on both sides with salt and pepper
5. if using , divide the hickory liquid smoke evenly over the ribs
6. in a medium bowl , combine the light brown sugar , paprika , garlic powder and ground red pepper
7. apply the rub to all sides of the ribs
8. lay ribs on the prepared baking sheet , meaty side down
9. lay two layers of foil on top of ribs and roll and crimp edges tightly , edges facing up to seal
