10. transfer to the oven and = bake for 2-2 1 / 2 hours or until meat is starting to shrink away from the ends of the bone
11. remove from oven
12. heat broiler
13. cut ribs into serving sized portions of 2 or 3 ribs
14. arrange on broiler pan , bony side up
15. brush on sauce
16. broil for 1 or 2 minutes until sauce is cooked on and bubbly
17. turn ribs over
18. repeat on other side
19. alternately , you can grill the ribs on your grill to cook on the sauce
demonstrations.review: These were excellent!  Nice easy way to cook ribs without slaving over the smoker or BBQ and very tasty, falling off the bone tender.  Got rave reviews from all of our guests and will definately make again!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
elvis  favorite sweet potato casserole

this is from my "recipes from graceland" cookbook that i got this summer. this is typical elvis.

1. cook sweet potatoes , peel and mash
2. in a large mixing bowl , blend sweet potatoes , brown sugar , cinnamon , vanilla and a pinch of salt
3. stir in eggs and milk
4. pour into a square baking dish
5. bake at 375f for 35 minutes
6. remove from oven
7. top with pecans and marshmallows and return to oven for 5 minutes or until marshmallows are puffed and browned
demonstrations.review:
What can I say that already hasn't been said?  Fabulous!  Great blend of flavor and texture, loved by all!

Made the recipe exactly as stated and had compliments all around.  

Thanks John!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
beer  n bbq braised country style pork ribs

this recipe comes originally from the 

1. brown the pork in a lightly sprayed skillet on all sides
2. place the ribs in an oven proof pan and scatter the onions all around them
3. pour in the beer and seal with a lid or tin foil
4. bake at 375f until the pork is tender 1 1 / 2- 2 hours
5. pour out the beer
6. slather the pork with the bbq sauce and bake uncovered for 1 more hour or until the meat is brown and the sauce is thick
7. enjoy
demonstrations.review: Even my mother in law Loved this! It is a great recipe!  It's easy to put together and the taste is great!  I really enjoy meals that allow me to mingle with my company, and this one is very friendly in that respect.  I used Sweet Baby Ray's BBQ sauce and added the garlic as suggested.  This was a definate hit with everyone, and there were NO leftovers.

target.recipe_text:
day after the holiday turkey soup

nan

1. in a heavy saucepan , heat olive oil over medium-high heat
2. reduce heat and add finely diced onions , carrots , and celery
3. cook until soft and golden brown , about 5 to 6 minutes
4. add corn , turkey , salt and pepper and the chicken stock then bring to a boil
5. let the soup simmer uncovered for 10 to 15 minutes
6. season with salt and pepper
7. before serving squeeze in the juice of a lemon
8. leftover rice may be substituted for the corn
target.review: Great recipe, I made a couple  alterations to suite our tastes, I substituted a couple fresh mushrooms sliced up instead of the corn and to make it more filling added about a cup of instant white rice and let it set until the rice was soft. Overall a good recipe and a great way to use up those leftovers.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
simple shepherd s pie

i've made this for years and my friends and family love it.  it's such a hearty and easy meal to make.  leftovers are like a hug after a hard day of work.  yum!

you need to flavor the meat, so you can use a taco seasoning packet, onion soup mix, or your own concoction).  here's an example...

http://www.recipezaar.com/38756

1. make instant potatoes according to box set aside
2. preheat oven 375 degrees
3. saut onion in butter until clear
4. brown ground beef until its crumbled and cooked thoroughly - drain fat if needed
5. stir in spices with cup water and cook for a few minutes
6. spread a thin layer of potatoes on the bottom of a lasagna pan
7. next , spread a layer ground beef
8. sprinkle cheese
9. layer corn and peas
10. top with the remaining potatoes
11. bake in the preheated oven for 30 minutes , or until hot and golden brown
demonstrations.review: This was so good! The reason I only gave 4 stars instead of 5 was because I made a couple small changes. I used real mashed potatoes, and I had green beans on hand in my freezer so I just used those instead of the peas and corn. Very good though I will definitely make again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pretend chocolate peanut butter pie

pretend because pie can't be this easy! and there are no dishes to do !! except the spoon. edit: i haven't tried it yet, but i was thinking it might be yummy to put a layer of chocolate pudding in the pie crust under the peanut butter mixture.

1. mix together peanut butter and cool whip in the cool whip container
2. this works better if the cool whip isn't frozen
3. put the peanut butter-cool whip mixture in the oreo pie crust , cover in the chocolate syrup , and freeze
4. or don't !
5. yum !
demonstrations.review: Good recipe, I love the filling! The only change I would make is use less chocolate syrup.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s juicy hamburger burger

we all have our different tastes for burgers i like mine flavorful and juicy this recipe will give you the best of both! see the bottom of the recipe for tips on even more extra juicy burgers! --- making a indentation in the middle of the uncooked burger will prevent the burgers from puffing up into meatballs shapes while cooking and keeps them flat --- do not add any salt into the burger mixture as the dry onion soup already has a lot of salt content, you can sprinkle some on towards the end of cooking if needed, if desired you may add in 3-4 tablespoons of your favorite barbecue sauce to the ground beef mixture

1. in a bowl crumble the ground beef with clean hands
2. add in the dry soup mix , egg , garlic , breadcrumbs or crushed soda cracker crumbs , worcestershire sauce , black pepper and hot sauce
3. using clean hands mix until combined , add in more breadcrumbs or cracker crumbs if needed to just hold the mixture together
4. divide the ground beef into 6 equal patties
5. using your large finger or the back of a small spoon make a shallow dent into the center of each patty
6. place the patties onto a large plate or a small cookie sheet
7. cover with plastic wrap and refrigerate for a minimum of 6 hours or up to 24 hours to blend flavors
8. grill or pan fry the burgers as desired until cooked through
9. serve burgers in toasted buns with choice of condiments
demonstrations.review: Wonderful recipe, loved them!

target.recipe_text:
palak paneer  indian fresh spinach with paneer cheese

creamy and rich, a delight to eat. a dish i fell in love with at a local restaurant and adapted a recipe to closely resemble theirs.

1. cut spinach into shreds and cook in 3 tablespoons water until tender
2. remove from heat
3. saute onion , cinnamon , cardamom , and ginger in 1-2 tablespoons ghee or oil until onion is translucent
4. then add garlic and chopped tomatoes , and reduce heat
5. cook this briefly and slowly blend in yogurt a little at a time to prevent curdling
6. add coriander , garam masala , paprika , and salt , mixing well
7. add cooked spinach with liquid , cover and simmer on low heat for approximately 20-30 minutes
8. remove from heat
9. take half of spinach mixture and puree in food processor or blender , and return to mixture and stir
10. slowly stir in heavy cream , and heat through on low heat
11. add paneer cubes
12. serve
target.review: If you can't find paneer in your grocery store, no worries- it's SUPER easy to make paneer at home.  I found this recipe: http://www.recipezaar.com/139897   (As always, read the reviews to learn more.)  The best part about making paneer at home is you can add your own seasonings while the curds are still hot and fresh.  I like to stir in a little bit of fresh garlic and chopped cilantro myself.  Then bundle it up in a cloth, twist to tighten a bit, set it in a sieve with something heavy on top of it to press it, and leave overnight in the fridge, setting the whole kaboodle over a bowl or tray of course, to catch the drips.  It's so EASY.  Also, the recipe above calls for lemon juice, but any acidic juice will work.  I like lime, myself.  Heather U, I hope you'll give it a try!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
ploye

this occupies a place of choice in our community.  the ploye looks like a pancake but is prepared with buckweat flour. it is used in place of bread.  if you come from northern new brunswick and you are a brayon, it is a common thing to eat and is delicious.
i posted it here so i would'nt loose it. after they are cooked, we spread butter on, roll them up and eat them that way.  some people like to finish a meal with one of these ploye drizzled with molasses as a dessert.

1. mix dry ingredients
2. add 2 cups cold water to the dry ingredients and mix well
3. let stand 5 minutes
4. add 1 cup boiling water and mix vigorously
5. if batter looks too thick , add a little bit of cold water
6. pour batter as you would a pancake in cast iron skillet or i have used a breakfast plate to cook mine and they came out very good
7. let the ploye cook , you will see little holes come up everywhere , the more holes , the better your ploye is
8. when you see that the mixture is not liquid anymore , your ploye is ready
9. only cook on one side , a ploye is not to be turned to cook
10. to really have good ployes you have to mix your batter between each ploye
demonstrations.review: My mom is from New Brunswick and adores ploye.  This is exactly the way to make these wonderful regional pancakes... thanks for posting!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mushroom risotto in pressure cooker

easy risotto recipe that will have everyone asking for seconds.

1. in a presssure cooker , heat 4tbs olive oil and 2 tbs butter
2. add onion and garlic
3. saute until translucent
4. add portabella and rice
5. stir until rice is coated with oil
6. add chicken broth
7. cover and cook under high pressure for 7 minutes
8. release pressure and add remaining 2 tbs of butter
9. stir in parmesan cheese and serve
demonstrations.review: I cook a LOT but haven't added risotto to my repertoire because I was put off by the thought of standing at the stove, stirring, for the better part of an hour. So I was really excited to find this recipe... so excited I got up off the sofa and went to the store to buy ingredients for it right then and there... at 10:30 at night. :P  I followed the recipe as written, adding a couple of sprigs of fresh rosemary and several basil leaves cut in ribbons.  It's EXCELLENT and I can't thank you enough.  This one's a keeper for sure.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
basic batter waffles

this hearty waffle recipe comes from an issue of parent's magazine. ive made it every week for years and it comes out great every time. i double it and freeze the leftover waffles and reheat in toaster oven.

1. mix all dry ingredients together using a large whisk
2. mix the wet ingredients together
3. gently combine but don't overmix
4. cook as your waffle maker directs
5. sprinkle with powdered sugar
6. cover with toasted nuts , bananas , and real maple syrup
7. pour on log cabin and michele's maple cream syrup for my husband !
demonstrations.review: I didn't have any maple extract but otherwise followed the recipe to the letter.  Added a handful of chopped pecans to each cup of batter.  Really easy and delicious; thanks for posting.

target.recipe_text:
incredible oven fried chicken

this recipe is the most flavorful home made fried chicken i have ever had. also great picnic food.

1. whisk buttermilk , oil , hot pepper sauce , mustard , garlic , 1 tsp salt and 1 / 2 teaspoon pepper in a large bowl
2. add the onion and then the chicken turning to coat each piece with the marinade
3. cover
4. chill at least three hours or up to one day turning the chicken occasionally
5. combine breadcrumbs , cheese , flour , thyme , paprika , cayenne and 1 tsp salt in a large baking dish
6. remove the chicken from the marinade and roll in the breadcrumb mixture
7. set chicken on a rack to dry for about 30 minutes
8. preheat oven to 400f degrees
9. place chicken in large baking dish and pour butter over the chicken
10. bake until crisp and brown , approximately 50 minutes
target.review: We enjoyed this recipe, but did find it a bit too spicy, and I had reduced the amount of cayenne that the recipe called for. I would not make the dish very often because it was time consuming, but I do think it tastes great!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
whatever floats your boat  brownies

these are absolutely the chewiest, moistest, fudgiest brownies ever! i have tried adding so many different things to the batter, and they always comes out great.  they are also great without any add-ins! but by varying the add-ins, you can make different brownies every week (or day!!) super easy prep! so, add "whatever floats your boat" and you will not believe how yummy they come out :) oh, and the recipe doubles just fine--use a 9 x 13 inch pan instead and add a few more minutes of baking!

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. grease an 8 inch square pan or line with foil
3. in a medium bowl combine melted butter and cocoa and stir until cocoa is dissolved
4. add sugar and mix well
5. add eggs one at a time and stir until well combined
6. stir in vanilla , flour and salt until you no longer see any flour
7. fold in "whatever floats your boat" !
8. spread in pan and bake for approximately 25 minutes
9. do not over-bake -- your brownies will come out dry
10. adjust time / temp accordingly for your oven
11. if you do the knife / toothpick test , it should come out with moist crumbs , not clean
12. cool completely before cutting into squares
13. for vegetarian omit the marshmallows
14. for double recipe , bake in 9x12 pan and add 5 minutes to baking time
demonstrations.review: Made these last night. Such an easy, quick recipe. Nice, fudgy style brownie. We added seedless raspberry preserves and pecans because we LOVE chocolate and raspberry together and everyone in the house loved them. I will definitely hold onto this recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
maple oat nut scones   starbucks

this is a copycat recipe from starbucks. i've altered the recipe a little so i could use a mixer instead of a processor....soooo very yummy!!!

1. preheat oven to 425f
2. using a food processor or blender , finely grind oats
3. in a mixer , mix flour , oats , sugar , salt and baking powder
4. add maple syrup and butter and mix well
5. in a small bowl , beat the egg with the cream and maple extract
6. pour the egg mixture into the flour mixture and mix well
7. add pecans and mix just to incorporate
8. place dough on a floured surface
9. knead and pat dough into a 8 to 10 inch circle and cut into 8 wedges
10. spray a baking sheet with cooking spray
11. place wedges on top and bake for 13 to 15 minutes , or until light brown
12. remove scones from oven to wire rack
13. let cool about 3 to 5 minutes
14. mix glaze ingredients until smooth
15. adjust the amount of water to get to the desired consistency
16. i like the glaze to be rather thick
17. spread lots of glaze over each scone and dry about 15 minutes before serving
demonstrations.review: Good flavor. I would increase the maple extract a bit next time. I love the ones at Starbucks, so I will make these again and again.  Be sure to keep them in an airtight container or else they dry out a bit.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mckinley tea cakes

this recipe is posted in honor of my grandmother. when i was a little girl, i stayed with her during the day while my mom worked. we made these tea cakes at least once a week. she was the most wonderful cook i've ever known. i hope someday to be as good as she was. (on the servings, i'm only guessing! prep time includes chilling the dough.)

1. combine the powdered sugar , granulated sugar , margarine , oil , eggs and vanilla
2. cream well
3. add in the flour , baking soda , baking powder , and cream of tartar
4. mix well
5. chill the dough in the refrigerator for 1 hour
6. pinch off pieces of the dough and roll in small walnut-sized balls
7. place on a cookie sheet
8. bake at 300-325 degrees for 10-15 minutes , depending on your oven and how crisp you like them
9. baking for approx
10. 10 minutes will yield a softer cookie , as they get crisper the longer they bake
demonstrations.review: These were great. My dad talk fondly of tea cakes that his Mom made in the 1930's and 40's so I decided to try these. They were gobbled up so fast. Very easy recipe, especially using my mixer and I loved that they don't have to be rolled out. Will definitely be making these again and again.

target.recipe_text:
roasted red pepper and tomato pasta sauce

my own creation after many trials and errors. the key here is the roasted garlic; it really gives the recipe a robust flavour. the result is a sweet, lovely and flavourful sauce.

1. preheat oven to 375f
2. cut top 1 / 4 off garlic head and cut around to expose as many cloves as possible
3. drizzle with olive oil and place on a baking dish or in a roasting pan
4. place whole red pepper in dish and place in oven
5. roast for 1 hour or until cloves are soft and mushy inside
6. place red pepper in plastic ziploc bag and seal , let sit about 10-15 minutes or until it cools and is easy enough to handle
7. meanwhile , pour can of diced tomatoes in blender
8. add balsamic vinegar , salt , sugar and red pepper flakes
9. squeeze cloves out of garlic head
10. once pepper has cooled , peel off skin , cut open , take out seeds and remove stem
11. place pepper in blender
12. puree mixture until blended
13. stir in cornstarch
14. heat up on stove when ready to eat or store in container and freeze for later
target.review: We enjoyed this very much!!Will make again,tripled then froze in seperate containers.Thanks.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
feta roast potatoes

yummy greek inspired potato dish. serve with recipe #72412.

1. preheat your oven to 200c
2. grease a large baking dish
3. cut potatoes into 1 cm thick slices
4. arrange them in the baking dish
5. drizzle potatoes with oil and add the thyme
6. toss the potatoes to coat in oil and herb
7. roast potatoes for 45 to 50 minutes or until tender
8. increase temperature to 220c
9. crumble feta over potatoes and toss through
10. return dish to oven for 10 minutes until feta softens
11. serve with barbecued greek lamb
demonstrations.review: these were great,thanks

demonstrations.recipe_text:
shannon s sooo good barbecued spareribs

these are so tender. we always get compliments when we make these with the easy to make homemade sauce.  i often have to quadruple the recipe!!

1. season ribs with salt , pepper and garlic powder
2. in a large dutch oven or kettle , place ribs and onion
3. sprinkle with salt and pepper
4. add enough water to cover
5. bring to a boil
6. reduce heat
7. cover and simmer for 1-1 1 / 2 hours or until tender
8. meanwhile , combine sauce ingredients in a saucepan
9. simmer , uncovered , for 1 hour or until slightly thickened , stirring occasionally
10. drain ribs , place on a rack in broiler or on a hot grill
11. brush with sauce
12. broil 5 inches from the heat for 5 minutes on each side , brushing frequently with sauce
demonstrations.review: The ribs&sauce were great!Next time I will double the sauce,It was so good,thanks for posting.Linda.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
boneless pork chops with gravy

i looked high and low for a recipe like this here and could not find it so i just hopefully made this one up. it is to easy not to be here.

1. place chops in ziplock bag add the dressing
2. marinade for 3 hours
3. drain dressing off and flour and fry in frying pan
4. drain any oil left over and put the chops back in fring pan
5. mix soup and milk together and pour over chops
6. let simmer till they are tender
7. gravy is great over potatoes
demonstrations.review: this was very easy and tasty thanks.

target.recipe_text:
baked pumpkin donuts

haven't tried these, but they sound fun

1. for doughnuts: in a medium mixing bowl stir together flour , brown sugar , baking powder , pumpkin pie spice , salt , and baking soda
2. add pumpkin , eggs , milk , and shortening , butter , or margarine
3. beat with an electric mixer on low speed till mixed
4. spoon the mixture into a pastry bag fitted with a large star
5. pipe onto 2 greased baking sheets in 3-inch circles
6. bake in a preheated 375 oven for 10 minutes , or till golden brown
7. cool doughnuts on a rack over waxed paper
8. for icing: in a small mixing bowl stir together powdered sugar and vanilla
9. stir in enough milk to make a smooth icing of glazing consistency
10. spoon icing over doughnuts
target.review: These have an excellent flavor even if they're not exactly like a fried donut.  I took the liberty of making a maple glaze for them but substituting maple syrup for some of the vanilla extract and milk.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
southwestern potato salad

a spin on bobby flay's very distinctive southwestern, egg-less potato salad.  to better soak in the flavors, make sure you pour the sauce over the warmed/hot potatoes.

1. combine all the ingredients , except the potatoes , in a medium bowl and season with salt and pepper , to taste
2. place warm potatoes in a large bowl and pour the mixture over potatoes and mix well
3. season again with salt and pepper , to taste
4. can be eaten warm or cold
demonstrations.review: Outstanding! and a nice change from the norm.  I made some changes because I decided to make this at the last minute and didn't have the exact ingredients on hand:  I used larger red potatoes (peeled) and cut them into chunks rather than slicing them.  I also omitted the bacon because I had none, but added some thawed frozen kernel corn.  I opted for extra cayenne pepper and garnished the salad with fresh cilantro and a sprinkling of sliced scallions.  Served this with grilled garlic shrimp and pita bread heated on the grill.  This is truly a keeper.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
tastes like apple pie apple squares

from my favourite church cookbook, where all the recipes are tried and true!  **like most of the reviews state, if you don't want to fight with the pastry to make it fit a cookie sheet - make 1.5x the dough recipe or use a smaller pan.

1. mix flour and salt and cut in shortening
2. add egg and milk mixture and mix till it forms a ball
3. divide dough in half
4. roll first half in 17 x 12 inch rectangle
5. place in cookie sheet and bring pastry up sides
6. cover pastry with apples and sprinkle with sugar and cinnamon
7. roll out second half of dough and place on top of apples
8. moisten edges with milk and pinch together
9. beat egg white until stiff and brush on crust
10. bake at 400f for 1 hour
11. mix glaze ingredients together and brush on crust
12. this square freezes beautifully
demonstrations.review: I thought this crust was very bland; I prefer a buttery crust. The filling is also bland even though I added more ground cinnamon and also ground nutmeg. I won't be making this again, sorry.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
horse   buggy wet bottom shoo fly pie

they serve this at amish spring break, right after the "wet hat contest"

1. mix together the flour , brown sugar and shortening
2. set aside cup of this mixture for the topping
3. add to the remaining mixture the egg , molasses , boiling water and baking soda
4. spread this mixture into the un-baked pie shell
5. spread the cup of crumb topping over the pie
6. bake at 375f for 10 minutes
7. reduce temperature to 350f and bake for 30 minutes or until firm
demonstrations.review: My, this was good.  First time baking and eating shoofly pie.  I baked mine in a 9" deep dish pie plate because I was afraid the filling would overflow when it expanded while baking.  Served warm with lightly-sweetened whipped cream.  Totally satisfying if you need a real sweet "fix."

target.recipe_text:
sausage breakfast muffins  oamc

this is a recipe i found online and adapted to suit my family's taste. you can use either chorizo or regular bulk breakfast sausage, depending on your tastes. they're both good. if you like spicy foods, add a 4 oz can of chopped and drain green chilies.

1. line muffin tins with paper liners , and set aside
2. fry , crumble and drain sausage
3. preheat oven to 375 degrees
4. mix together bisquick , cornmeal , eggs , and milk
5. add drained sausage , and cheese , and stir well
6. ladle the filling into the prepared muffin tins , filling almost to top
7. bake for 11-15 minutes
8. allow to cool completely
9. store in freezer in a large airtight container
10. or place each in a sandwich bag , and then place a dozen in a large ziploc bag
11. microwave on high for approx 90 seconds
target.review: These are really nice and versatile. I add green onions and red peppers  and took them to work for an early meeting and they were gone in minutes.  I really like the different texture the corn meal gave.  Thanks

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s fluffiest scrambled eggs

once you make these eggs you will *never* go back to your old way again, this is the way the higher end restaurants prepare their eggs ----for six eggs you may increase the milk by 1 tablespoon, do not add in more than 1/4 teaspoon baking powder --- if you are not afraid of some extra calories for 4 eggs use 2 tablespoons whipping cream in place of low-fat milk :)

1. in a bowl whisk the eggs vigorously with milk , baking powder , salt and black pepper until very well combined
2. let stand at room temperature for 5-7 minutes
3. heat butter until sizzling over medium-high heat in a large skillet
4. whisk eggs again briefly then mix in the cheese
5. pour into the hot skillet , stirring constantly with a small heat-proof spatula until they have reached desired consistency
demonstrations.review: Wonderfully fluffy and light

demonstrations.recipe_text:
saucy bacon roll ups

these are very easy to make for a buffett or appetizer party. i usually double this, because they go fast!  note:  the last time i made these, i fried the bacon after i cut it into thirds until it was almost done, cooled slightly on paper towels then wrapped around the water chestnuts and secured with toothpicks.  the sauce was a lot less greasy.  i cooked for about 5 minutes less.  enjoy!

1. preheat oven to 350
2. seperate bacon into slices
3. cut each slice in thirds
4. wrap each cut slice of bacon around a water chestnut
5. secure with a toothpick
6. place in a baking dish
7. in a bowl combine chili sauce , mayonnaise , and brown sugar
8. pour sauce over bacon roll ups and bake in the preheated oven for 35 to 40 minutes
demonstrations.review: These were very tasty and my guest enjoyed them.  I will make them again only next time i will add some hot pepper flakes to kick it up a bit.  Thanks

demonstrations.recipe_text:
best ever banana bread  honestly

this was posted by nlb in epicurious. it is from necessities & temptations from the junior league of austin. i have never, ever, had a banana bread this good.

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees f
2. cream butter and sugar
3. mash bananas , beat 2 eggs and add to the bananas with vanilla and buttermilk
4. mix well and add to creamed butter and sugar
5. sift together flour , soda and salt
6. add to banana mixture , beat well
7. pour into 2 greased and floured 9x5x3-inch loaf pans
8. bake 45 to 50 minutes or until bread pulls away from sides of pan
9. add topping
10. to prepare topping: melt butter in saucepan
11. add sugar and milk
12. cook until syrupy
13. remove from heat and add chopped pecans
14. pour over bread spreading to all the corners and place under broiler until bubbly and brown
15. watch closely
demonstrations.review: This was Wonderful! I try this with three other recipes and this was the star for sure.  Thanks

target.recipe_text:
pink party sandwich cookies

very pretty sandwich cookies for showers and parties. of course, you can use any food coloring to go with the theme of your choice.

1. cream butter and sugar until smooth
2. blend in eggs and vanilla
3. stir together flour , cornstarch and cream of tartar
4. gradually add flour mixture to creamed mixture , blending well
5. chill dough until firm
6. roll out on a lightly floured surface to 1 / 8" thickness
7. cut out with 3" round cookie cutter and place on greased baking sheet
8. bake at 400 for about 8 minutes or until edges are golden
9. remove to a wire rack to cool
10. fill with pink butter frosting
11. pink butter frosting: cream butter until light and fluffy
12. gradually beat in sugar , cream and vanilla
13. tint with red food coloring
14. beat until filling is of spreading consistency
target.review: These cookies were rated "really good" by the kids I made them for, but I was disappointed.  Once in the oven, the cookie batter turned really soft and the cookies all ran together prompting me to wonder why I had bothered to roll them out and cut them.  In addition, the finished cookies were really bubbly, lacy almost like a florentine or something.  I just had pictured something entirely different in my mind's eye, I guess. The butter cream was a solid recipe.  I probably won't be doing these again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
orange chicken magic

orange and chicken compliment each other very well. add some triple sec to the sauce for a real orange kick. serve with rice or cous cous

1. brown chicken slowly in margarine , about 15 minutes
2. add rind , 1 / 4 cup orange juice , onion , paprika , ginger& tarragon
3. cover , cook over low heat 30 minutes
4. remove chicken to dish& arrange orange slices over chicken and keep warm
5. blend 1 / 4 orange juice with cornstarch
6. stir into sauce in pan and cook until thickened
demonstrations.review: This was excellent and easy! I used chicken breasts, browned them on both sides, then transferred them to my 350 oven (they were still a little frozen when I threw them in pan, so I knew they'd need to bake a bit).  Then I deglazed the frying pan with the orange juice, rind, onion, paprika, ginger and tarragon.  I simmered these ingredients until they were thickened and then poured them over the chicken breasts in the oven. I did double all the herbs/spices.  Also, the chicken breasts I was using had been brined so they were juicier--I think regular b/l, s/l breasts would dry out too much in this application.  Will try it next time with the chicken legs or with b/l, s/l thighs.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chocolate syrup brownies

these brownies have a very different taste than boxed. they're very good though, and easy to make. i didn't time myself so i'm over guessing on the prep time. and how many servings you get depends on how large you like to cut your brownies.

1. pre-heat oven to 350
2. grease a 13x9 pan
3. for the bars: beat together sugar and softened butter until creamy
4. add vanilla , eggs and chocolate syrup
5. blend well
6. lightly spoon flour into measuring cup
7. level off
8. stir into chocolate mixture and mix well
9. pour into prepared pan and bake for 25-30 minutes
10. cool
11. for the frosting: melt butter in a saucepan
12. blend in cocoa and heat just until mixture comes to a boil , stirring constantly
13. cool
14. blend in powdered sugar , milk , and vanilla until smooth
15. you may need to add additional milk if frosting is too dry
16. stir in nuts , if you are using them
17. spread carefully over brownies
18. let sit for a bit to firm up frosting
19. enjoy !
demonstrations.review: While fine, they are still a little too cakey for my tastes. You can't beat them for quickness, though.  Seems like these would be good as the cake portion of a chocolate trifle.  I was tempted to chop up and stir in a chocolate bar but was just too tired.  i would make these again in a pinch, otherwise, I'd go with the ones that involve cocoa powder.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
lemon pepper tarragon chicken with sour cream  mushroom and wine

this is one of the easiest and most impressive chicken recipes i have ever encountered!  absolutely perfect for impressing the husband's boss!

1. preheat oven to 350
2. place chicken breasts in baking dish and sprinkle with lemon pepper and tarragon
3. in medium bowl , combine mushroom soup , mushrooms , garlic salt and wine and pour over chicken breasts
4. bake in oven for 30-45 minutes
5. remove chicken breasts onto warming dish and pour the pan drippings into medium saucepan
6. add sour cream to pan drippings , stir and heat until warm
7. to serve , place a chicken breast over white rice and ladle sour cream , wine and mushroom sauce over all
demonstrations.review: This was really nice.  I was in a hurry to make a nice dinner with hastily gathered ingredients to celebrate my housemate's birthday.  We had been out "playing" during the day and I forgot to think of something in advance for dinner...Anyway, this fit the bill and got rave reviews.  I had to use a 'zaar mushroom soup recipe (#17634) because I can't get canned mushroom soup where we live, but I think that it took this recipe up a definitive notch. Because of the richness of the homemade mushroom soup--to which I had added the wine and reduced before pouring it over the chicken--I didn't use all the sour cream called for in this recipe.  One caveat: the chicken breasts I purchased were brined, so they were plenty salty. Maybe it was also because I reduced the soup? Next time I would cut back on the salt in all the components or use unbrined chicken.

target.recipe_text:
grilled pineapple pork chops

these are easy, sweet and tangy.

1. drain pineapple , reserving 1 / 4 cup of the juice for marinade
2. combine all marinade ingredients
3. use 2 / 3 cup to marinate pork , and reserve the rest for basting
4. let meat marinate for at least 3 hours
5. grill pork chops on medium heat for 8 minutes on each side
6. grill pineapple for a total of 5 minutes
7. baste both pork and pineapple with reserved marinade
8. place one or two pineapple slices on each pork chop
target.review: This was very tasty.  We loved the pineapple.  Thanks for posting.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
sweet potato dumplings

i found this recipe in a local church cookbook. i have not tried it myself, but i thought it sounded very interesting. i might experiment on my guests for thanksgiving! any other brave souls out there?

1. spray a 13 x 9 x 2 inch baking pan
2. flatten each biscuit with a rolling pin
3. add 1 heaping tablespoonful of sweet potato to the center of each biscuit
4. fold in half and crimp the edges to seal
5. lay in pan appx
6. 8 per side
7. you can overlap them
8. combine butter , sugars , cinnamon , and water in a saucepan and bring to a boil
9. pour over biscuits
10. they may float , but they will settle
11. bake@ 350f , uncovered , 35-45 minutes until golden brown
demonstrations.review: Absolutely wonderful!  Best treat I've had in a while.  I've been thinking about fixing these for a while now.  Boy did I miss out by not fixing them sooner.  Thanks for the lovely lovely treat.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
favorite scallops

this is my favorite way to prepare scallops. recipe adapted from bon appetit ( october, 1981).

1. melt butter in skillet over medium heat
2. stir in garlic , tarragon and oregano
3. add scallops and season with paprika , salt and pepper
4. squeeze lemon juice over scallops and saute for 5 minutes or until scallops turn opaque
5. increase heat to medium-high and add sherry cooking until there is almost no liquid in pan
6. transfer to serving dish
7. sprinkle with paprika , parsley and lemon slices
demonstrations.review: Excellent recipe.  My family just loved it.  Served it over angel hair pasta.  Thanks for posting.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cheesy ham and potato soup

comfort soup at its finest!  i usually make this to use up leftover ham.  this is easy to adapt with other ingredients.  i don't put celery in mine.  i have added garlic sometimes as well.

1. combine potatoes , celery , carrots , onion , ham , and water / broth in stockpot and bring to boil
2. then cook over medium heat until potatoes are tender
3. stir in the chicken bouillon , salt , and pepper
4. in separate saucepan , melt butter over medium-low heat
5. whisk in flour and cook stirring constantly until thick
6. slowly stir in milk as not to allow lumps to form and all milk is added
7. turn up to medium heat
8. continue to stir until thick
9. add in cheese and stir until melted
10. stir the cheese mixture into the stockpot and cook until heated through
demonstrations.review: This soup is so delicious.  We loved the addition of the ham.  Thanks for posting this wonderful recipe.

target.recipe_text:
maid rite sandwiches

this is a very tasty, juicy, loose meat sandwich filling. in reading thru this recipe you will notice the use of both fresh and dried onion.....please use the onion type specified in the recipe step you are on for maximum flavor. although traditionally served on hamburger buns, this filling can be messy for young children trying to keep filling in. try using hotdog rolls for the youngsters. mustard & onions are the seasonings of choice for this recipe.

added 11/12/2008
maid rite sandwiches are made across the country. one would think as a franchise all would be made and served the same way.  this is not the case.... we have maid rites being served that are boiled or steamed, with water, chicken broth, beef broth, coke, or beer.  there are those that add vinegar or sugar to the mix. some top with mustard, onions, ketsup, and pickles......well, move over mcdonalds! this is the way i made my maid rite sandwiches....faux or real....the name stands.  as they say,,,variety is the spice of life. you can make changes to suite your tastes, share your changes here with me, i will try them all...unless we have some bazarre ingredients. chocolate syrup will not intice me no matter how much i love chocolate.

1. soak the dried onions in the water
2. crumble ground beef into a hot skillet and cook over medium high heat
3. when the soaked onions have begun to soften and expand , add it and any remaining water to the beef
4. stir frequently as the meat browns , using a wooden spoon to break the meat into small crumbles
5. when the meat has browned , add the chicken broth , salt and pepper
6. cook until liquid is almost gone , about 10 minutes
7. serve meat on buns with mustard and fresh chopped onions
8. enjoy !
target.review: I thought this was a very good, simple recipe and will make again.  In my family of 6, it got mixed reviews, some loved it, some thought it was just okay. I think I will use hot dog buns next time as it was very messy. Thanks for sharing!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
amazing cinnamon apple rice stuffed chicken gfcf

this is a different take on a traditional persian dish that i love.  my sister, naomi and i came up with the recipe together.  we were trying to use ingredients that would not only taste great for kids and adults alike but also follow a gluten free casein free diet for her son with autism.  when she served this for dinner to her husband, who is very picky, he exclaimed, "wow,amazing! you have to make this for christmas dinner. the entire chicken disappeared very quickly and he was disappointed that she had not made two!

1. wash the chicken in cold water , and clean the inside cavity out too
2. then pat dry and rub with 1 tsp of salt
3. then move chicken to greased baking dish / roasting pan
4. in a skillet , heat 1 tbsp oil over medium heat
5. add the uncooked rice , cinnamon , orange peel , 1 tsp salt and pepper
6. stir fry for 2 minutes
7. add chicken stock , cover and simmer over low heat for 20 minutes
8. please make sure your to cover the rice , it needs to be cooked prior to stuffing into the chicken
9. preheat oven to 400 degrees
10. add the raisins , orange cranberries , lemon juice and chopped apples
11. mix together and then remove from heat
12. stuff the chicken with the rice stuffing mixture
13. preferred method: melt 2 tbsp butter and pour over stuffed chicken
14. rub melted butter over all areas of the chicken
15. cover with foil or baking lid
16. roast for 1 1 / 2 hours till tender
demonstrations.review: I have not made this yet, but it sounds delicious! We are in our second week of the GFCF diet for our autistic daughter and adhd son and I have to tell you, I am struggling to find good recipes that don't require a bunch of strange, expensive ingredients.  I was so happy to see this...THANK YOU, THANK YOU, THANK YOU! ChefRD and sister, Naomi, I'd love to hear about more recipes if you have them!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
honey garlic chicken skewers

these can be grilled on the bbq for about 5-6 minutes also. make certain to soak the wooden skewers for minimum 30 minutes to prevent from burning, this recipe makes about 12 skewers but can be doubled if desired, these are popular at my bbq get togethers, hope you enjoy!

1. for the marinade: combine all ingredients
2. coat the chicken strips in the marinade to coat well
3. transfer to a glass dish
4. cover and marinate overnight
5. thread the chicken strips on the water-soaked wooden skewers
6. preheat the broiler to high heat
7. arrange the skewers on a greased foil-lined baking sheet
8. broil for about 6-7 minutes until well browned and thoroughly cooked
demonstrations.review: Super yummy! We are a family of 6 and every one of us loved these. I made them exactly according to the recipe and (too cold for the grill) broiled them in the oven. I'll be making these again for sure.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
bravo ristorante italiano rigatoni alla buttera

this is a quick and easy weekday meal, and a tricky way to sneak peas into a kids diet!  to spice this up bit, try using a tomato sauce like barilla's tomato and basil and hot italian sausage.  if you like pink sauce, you can also add more cream.  overall, this is a tasty, easy dish!

1. cook sausage in a large frying pan , until well browned
2. drain fat
3. pour tomato sauce and broth on top of sausage and cook for 3 minutes on medium heat
4. add peas and cream and cook for 1 1 / 2 minutes more
5. fill a large saucepan 2 / 3 full with salted water
6. bring to a boil
7. add rigatoni
8. bring water back to a boil and cook uncovered until rigatoni is al dente
9. place a single serving of pasta on a plate , and top with as much sauce as you like !
10. serve immediately
11. grated parmigiano cheese may be added at table , if desired
demonstrations.review: Made this for dinner the other night and thought it was too salty and pretty boring. I added alot of parmesan to kick it up a little, but it was pretty blah.

target.recipe_text:
brown sugar brownies  blondies

an easy & yummy brownie that makes a nice no-chocolate treat! fun to vary the mix-ins - we like to add candy corn! it's a moist slightly cakey brownie that everyone will enjoy!

1. mix all ingredients well
2. bake in 9 inch square pan that you have sprayed well with pam at 350f for 25 to 30 minutes
3. cool before cutting
target.review: Yum!! I'm on a mission to find a brownie closest to one I used to make all the time when I was a kid. This one is pretty close! (My recipe was called a butterscotch brownie.) I added a little maple syrup instead to try to make it closer to the one I was imitating. They are so nice and soft and so easy to make. But definitely don't underbake and let them cool before cutting them, as the recipe says. Think soft and cakey, not chewy-gooey.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chocolate chip biscuits aussie style

these are a very "moresome" bikky:) i used to sell these at the local markets, and they always sold out first. very easy to make, and to really show off, you can throw a handful of chopped macadamia nuts in, gives them an extra crunch!!!

please note, these are nothing like american choc chip cookies, which are soft and chewy.
i have also added coco powder to the mix and used white chips, looks good, but the white chips stay very hard.

1. cream together the butter and sugar
2. add the condensed milk and keep beating for 2 minutes
3. fold through the flour , then the choc chips
4. the mixture will be tacky
5. place teaspoons full on your baking tray
6. flatten slightly with a floured fork
7. bake at about 160c for about 15 minutes , or till golden
8. leave on trays for 3 minutes , then cool on wire racks
demonstrations.review: These are so yummy and so EASY. They also make a lot. I bake half of them and then with the rest of the dough I make it into balls, flash freeze, and then dump them in a zipper bag. You can pull them out and bake them as desired or--oh joy!--eat little balls of frozen cookie dough as desired.;-)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
black bean and  sweet potato soup

i love black beans and sweet potatoes... this is a wonderful blend of flavors. i like to cook this in the crockpot but it can also easily be done on the stovetop.

1. heat oil in a skillet and saute onion and garlic in oil until soft
2. add all ingredients to crockpot and cook on low for 8 hours or until sweet potatoes are tender
3. serve hot with sour cream and lime if desired
demonstrations.review: Yummy! I made this in the crockpot. I used dried black beans and I didn't have coriander so I used a little chili powder in addition the cumin. I might have added extra cumin, too, I didn't really measure. (I love cumin!) The corn added really good texture and the sour cream is a good suggestion, too. (Didn't have limes.) This is one of those meals that I think is perfect for the crockpot and I probably wouldn't like it *as* well on the stovetop as I think the long cooking time is really essential for optimum flavor. Thanks for the great recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
twisted sisters creamy cucumber salad

when i arrived in iceland, this was my dh’s 1st food request & i went thru a lot of rz cucumber salad recipes to be sure it wasn’t a duplicate. siggi & my sister named this because it was original w/me & because of my twissis internet identity. for best results, don’t make this a dy ahead, but do allow at least 2 hrs for the flavors to blend & the “cream” to develop from the finished ingredient mix. i promise you’ll like this. (stated time does not include refrigeration time)

1. peel & slice cucumbers in 1 / 2 in thick slices
2. then half ea slice & transfer all slices to a lrg mixing bowl
3. roughly dice red onion & add to the bowl
4. quarter tomatoes , remove seeds , rough dice the tomato meat & add to the bowl
5. thinly slice 1 / 2 green pepper , cut slices in 1 in strips & add to the bowl
6. toss prepared veggies to achieve a good distributional mix
7. add last 6 ingredients to bowl , mix well & refrigerate at least 2 hrs
8. if thinly sliced , most cucumbers wilt & do not retain their crunch
9. -- when all ingredients have been combined , the mixture will appear dry & lack a creamy texture or appearance
10. do not panic that will begin to change almost immediately
11. if you reduce further , you will likely lose any salt component in the mix
demonstrations.review: Thank you! This is so good. My mom used to make this only she didn't have a recipe, just threw stuff together. My attempts to do the same haven't turned out so well but this recipe gave just the result I wanted. It does get "soupy" after being refrigerated for awhile but it's still really good and the leftover liquid is really good on lettuce. Or, um, you could just eat it by the spoonful if you're me...:-o

target.recipe_text:
basic muffin recipe

this is, as the title says a basic muffin recipe. you can add ¾ cup of your fruit of choice, blueberries, raspberries, peaches……. 
if using frozen fruit, do not thaw.
you can also have them plain.

1. sift together dry ingredients
2. make a well in the centre
3. combine the wet ingredients then mix with dry ingredients
4. stir only until combined
5. if using fruit , add to batter
6. fill paper-lined muffin cups 2 / 3 full
7. bake in preheated 400 degree fahrenheit oven for 20 to 25 minute , or until toothpick inserted in centre comes out clean
target.review: First let me say I am a horrible baker.  I can cook but not bake.  The fact that these came out for me speaks volumes about the simplicity of the recipe.  I will say that the sugar being 2TB is much less than other muffin recipes.  However, I am of the opinion that a really sweet muffin is simply a cupcake without icing.  I think sweetness should be for cupcakes, so I was not disappointed in the lack of sweetness.  You can always up the sugar amount.  I did not have milk, so I used 1/2 c half and half and then added water to make it a full cup. (I told you I was not a baker!) I am sure that changed the texture, even though the texture was fine.  It looked more like a biscuit but again, I am sure that is my fault.  I used those fancy cupcake paper things that are higher up?  They looked great, and I added mini chocolate chips.  To make it a tiny bit sweeter for my daughter I put a little powder sugar on the top.  She said it was delicious.  So...five stars because it was cheap to make, few ingredients, ingredients that most people have on hand in the house, easy to make, my daughter loved it and it is flexible so that you can add many different extras.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
iced italian cookies

posted by request, these pretty little cookies are very often served at holiday gatherings in many italian american families. you may shape them any way you prefer, and change the flavoring of the icing slightly to suit your tastes. the original recipe came from one of my favorite community style cookbooks called "preserving our italian heritage" compiled by the sons of italy florida foundation. i combined several variations submitted by 5 different ladies, all of whom used the same basic cookie recipe but used slightly different methods in shaping and icing the cookies. the yield will vary depending upon how you shape your cookies.

1. cream butter and sugar until soft and creamy
2. add eggs and vanilla , mixing well
3. combine flour and baking powder , then blend into the butter mixture
4. break off small , walnut sized pieces of dough and shape into bows , braids , knots , "s" shapes , or any shape you desire
5. bake in a preheated oven at 375 f until lightly browned , about 15-20 minutes
6. cool on wire racks , then ice as desired
7. icing: blend sugar and your choice of flavoring , adding milk slowly to form a soft , smooth icing
8. sprinkle with colored sugar or confettini before icing sets
demonstrations.review: Great recipe that is easy and has ingredients my budget stressed pantry could afford so that I could make Christmas cookies with my daughter.  The cookies are delicious and taste exactly like the ones my Italian grandmother use to make.  We made one batch with powdered sugar ( I wanted the Italian wedding cookies but I had no almonds or walnuts) and the powdered sugar stuck nicely to them.  Another batch wecdippedvin the icing then rolled in organic sprinkles. The last batch we rolled in icing and left like that.  All delicious.  Thanks for sharing!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
avocado stuffed eggs

i found this recipe several years ago in our local newspaper. this is a different kind of deviled egg. the creamy avocado replaces the mayo. i have subbed lime juice for the lemon. the flavor is best when only slightly chilled or at room temp.

1. boil the eggs for three minutes
2. peel and slice each egg in half lengthways
3. remove egg yolks and place the egg white halves on a serving platter
4. mash avocados and egg yolks together
5. fold in minced onions , lemon juice and salt
6. spoon mixture into the egg whites
7. garnish with a sprinkle of paprika and diced olives
demonstrations.review: This was a terrific recipe.  I was trying to find a way to incorporate the avocado into my diet, but in a very simple way to take it to work with me.   This was quick, simple, inexpensive and I can take it to work without breaking out forks, knives, etc... .  I followed the recipe exactly, but I did sub sun dried tomatoes instead of olives.  I will definitely make this again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
fresh pumpkin soup by kerry simon

one of my favorite "star" chef's, this sounds divine.  found it on food network.  prep time does not include time to roast the pumpkin

1. in a stockpot over medium heat , melt butter and saute onion , carrot , apple , and sage until all are tender , add roasted pumpkin and cook about 8 to 10 minutes
2. puree the mixture in a food mill
3. if you do not have a food mill , then puree in a food processor or blender
4. return the puree to the stockpot , add the chicken stock and simmer for 15 minutes
5. then add the cream and simmer for 5 more minutes , lowering the heat if necessary so it does not boil
6. season , to taste , with salt and pepper
7. divide soup among 4 soup bowls and serve immediately
8. cooks
9. cut whole pumpkin in half and then cut each half into several pieces
10. discard seeds or reserve for another use
11. place pumpkin on a baking sheet , drizzle with olive oil , and season with salt and pepper
12. roast in oven until tender but not falling apart , about 30 to 40 minutes
13. let cool , peel away skin , and dice
demonstrations.review: This soup was so easy to make and I had all of the ingredients in the house which makes it even better.  I used all organic ingredients but I did substitute 1/2 and 1/2 for the milk and I threw in a pinch of crushed red pepper flakes.  I will make this soup again.  It was easy, super fast and delicious.  I like that I didn't have to add flour like the other recipes.  It was thick, but not pasty which is usually what I get when I make the recipes with the flour.  Thanks for sharing!

target.recipe_text:
sloppy joe sandwich

this recipe has been a work in progress.  this is what i came up with and my family loves it.  i guess that is what's most important!  hope you enjoy it too.  i never did come up with an exact measurement for the water.  just add a little at a time until you get the consistancy you like.  we like ours relatively thick.  (like a "not-so-sloppy joe")

1. brown the beef in a large pot and drain
2. add the onion , celery , green pepper , and cook until tender
3. add the remaining ingredients and stir
4. add water until desired consistency achieved
5. simmer over low heat until hot
target.review: Delicious!   I made this one night, froze it for a night and then put it in a slow cooker for a potluck the next day.  I added about 1 cup water to get it to be a slightly sloppy texture.  I received many compliments.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
white chocolate iced blueberry loaf

here is another easy and yummy recipe. it can be made with frozen blueberries but it is better with fresh as the color does not bleed into the batter. i make this in the summertime when the blueberries are in season.

1. heat oven to 350 degrees fahrenheit
2. grease bottom only of 9x5-inch loaf pan
3. in large bowl , mix flour , sugar , baking powder , salt and allspice with spoon
4. beat in buttermilk , butter and eggs until blended
5. stir in blueberries and pecans
6. spread batter in pan
7. bake 1 hour 15 minutes to 1 hour 20 minutes or until toothpick inserted in center comes out clean
8. cool in pan on wire rack 10 minutes
9. run knife round edges of pan to loosen loaf
10. remove loaf from pan
11. place on wire rack
12. cool completely , about 1 hours
13. in small microwavable bowl , microwave white chocolate chips on high 30 seconds
14. stir until melted
15. if necessary microwave in additional 10 second increments until melted
16. beat in powdered sugar and enough milk until smooth and desired drizzling consistency
17. drizzle icing over loaf
18. let stand until icing is set before storing
demonstrations.review: This recipe was so good I made it 2 days in a row. The first loaf I froze to take to a pot luck in 2 weeks.  The 2nd loaf I cut into and shared.  It is delicious!  Very easy to put together as you can mix it up with just a wooden spoon.  I used frozen blueberries which I kept frozen until I was ready to add them to the batter.  Thanks for a really great recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
italian sausage florentine for the crock pot

a hearty dish for a busy day. also good as party or potluck food. the flavors of italian sausage, spaghetti sauce, onions, and spinach meld perfectly in the crock pot. despite all the healthy veggies its a real guy pleaser! ;)

1. brown sausages in skillet or on grill
2. peel and slice onions
3. put in bottom of 6qt crock pot
4. if using peppers , seed and slice vertically
5. layer on top of the onions
6. pour frozen spinach into crock pot
7. arrange sausages on top of the spinach
8. pour spaghetti sauce evenly over top of everything
9. cook on high for 2 hours then on low for 3-4 hours
10. or , thaw the spinach first and cook on low for 6+ hours
11. serve over pasta , over rice , or with a hearty , crusty , bread
12. pass grated parmesan at the table
13. this version could have shredded mozzarella incorporated into the layers and on top
demonstrations.review: This was really good.  I didn't get to eat it until 2 days after I made it, but I still rate it an 'outstanding'.  I served it over a rigatoni type of pasta and sprinkled a little bit of mozzarella on the plate.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
roasted pork loin with sweet tangy sauce

this roast is so tender and juicy and has a sweet tangy sauce that will melt in your mouth.i got this from another website and tweaked it to my likings. i roast this is a glass baking dish on top of an onion cut into 4 pieces. if you are preparing a larger roast just double the ingredients. the sauce is also good on rice if you'd like. prep time does not include marinating time. i plate this with the onions that were in the bottom-oh so good!

1. preheat oven to 325f
2. in a bowl , combine sage , salt , pepper , and garlic
3. rub roast with olive oil so rub will stick to the roast
4. rub mix all over roast
5. cover with plastic wrap tightly
6. marinate for about 2 hours (if you don't have time for that it'll still be fine
7. sprinkle the worcestershire sauce on right before you put it in the oven
8. place roast in either a roasting pan or glass dish on top of the onion
9. pour 1 / 4 cup water in bottom
10. place in oven on middle rack
11. cover for the first 2 hours then uncover for remaining time
12. bake approximately 3 hours or until internal temperature is at least 150f depending on your desired doneness
13. meanwhile , place sugar , flour , vinegar , water and soy sauce in small saucepan
14. heat , stirring occasionally until mixture begins to bubble and thicken slightly
15. brush roast with glaze 3 or 4 times during last half hour of cooking
16. when roast is done
17. take out of oven , pour remaining glaze on and let rest set about 10 minutes before carving
demonstrations.review: The tenderloin turned out very tender.  The sauce is delicious. I especially liked the onions that cooked in the bottom of the pan. I used apple cider vinegar.  I recommend this recipe and I will use it again.

target.recipe_text:
chicken thigh spareribs well  sort of  lol

we love this chicken recipe. i don't know who it's from, but it's on a worn piece of paper in my recipe box. very tasty, and so easy. the sauce gets thick and coats the chicken so nicely. you can control the heat by increasing or decreasing the amount of pepper flakes.  i also like to add more garlic, about 5 cloves total.  great with rice and a steamed veggie, and the kids like it too.

1. in a large skillet , heat oil
2. add chicken and brown on both sides , for about 6-7 minutes
3. set aside cornstarch and the 1 tbsp water
4. in a mixing bowl , combine remaining ingredients and add to the chicken in the skillet
5. bring to a boil , cover and reduce heat , simmer for 20 minutes
6. in a small bowl , combine the tbsp of water and the cornstarch , add to the chicken and cook until the sauce thickens and coats the chicken pieces
target.review: Made this tonight for dinner... really good and really easy! It's a definite keeper :^)  Thanks for sharing.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s low fat oven baked zucchini sticks

a recipe that goes back years and a great way to use up all that zucchini left over from summers crop, you may adjust all seasonings to taste --- if you are a garlic lover then you may increase to 1 teaspoon, i also add in a pinch of cayenne pepper for a little heat --- use only dry breadcrumbs for this --- if your seasoned breadcrumbs already have salt added then omit the 1/4 teaspoon salt --- as one reviewer mentioned that she dipped the sticks into ranch dressing so you might want to give that a try using a low fat dressing or dip :)

1. in a bowl combine bread crumbs , parmesan cheese , garlic powder , salt and pepper
2. mix well
3. in another bowl , beat egg / s lightly
4. dip zucchini sticks into eggs , then into breadcrumb mixture
5. transfer to a greased baking sheet that has been coated with nonstick spray
6. bake at 425 degrees f for about 20-25 minutes , or until lightly browned
demonstrations.review: Delicious! I used panko breadcrumbs and followed the recipe exactly... I guess my zucchini were big because I needed to make another batch of the breadcrumb mixture and add another egg.  These were a huge hit with my teenage daughter and her friends... and I loved them too! Thanks for a great recipe that I will surely be making again :^)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
easy microwave alfredo sauce

taken from "micro ways" cookbook written by my good friend norene gilletz at gourmaia.com --- there's  enough sauce to combine with 1 pound of noodles, if you are doubling this recipe make it separately not in the same pyrex cup --- follow microwave times and you will have a perfect alfredo sauce, the parmesan cheese may be increase to taste -- this will separate if heated the following day so i suggest to use it all at one time.

1. place butter and garlic in a 4-cup pyrex measuring cup
2. microwave uncovered in high for 2 minutes
3. remove and stir in whipping cream , nutmeg basil and black pepper
4. return to the microwave uncovered on high for another 2-3 minutes , until bubbling
5. remove and stir in parmesan cheese , return to the microwave for 2-3 minutes longer until thick and smooth
6. season with salt and black pepper to taste
demonstrations.review: Excellent!!  This was really yummy!  I did add some extra parmesan and a little extra basil for flavor but I can't believe that Alfredo Sauce this good came from the microwave! Thanks so much :^)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s 5 minute cinnamon flop brunch cake

except for the the milk and small amount in the egg, the cake itself has very little fat and using low-fat milk will keep the fat to a minimum, i have stated the egg as optional, i strongly suggest to add it in for a more cake-like texture --  if you are looking for a fancy cake to serve then this is not it however for the ease of this cake it is darn good and makes a great weekend brunch cake, it's like a combination of a cake and cinnamon bun all in one,  ridiculously simple to make as it's all mixed by hand and takes like 5 minutes to throw together, try adding in some chopped strawberries, apples or blueberries, raisins or dried cranberries, this recipe is a blank canvas, so go ahead and add in fruit, nuts chocolate chips whatever you wish, and to kick this up a notch drizzle recipe#120835 on top :) --- servings are only estimated

1. set oven to 350 degrees f
2. prepare a greased 13 x 9-inch baking dish , or two 8 or 9-inch round cake pans
3. in a bowl mix the 2 cups flour , 1-1 / 4 cups white sugar , milk , vanilla or almond extract , baking powder , pinch of salt and egg until just combined careful not to overmix
4. pour into prepared baking pan / s
5. generously spread brown sugar and cinnamon on top
6. if desired sprinkle chopped walnuts or pecans over top
7. drizzle melted butter over top
8. bake for about 20-25 minutes for 8 or 9-inch round cake pan , and about 30 minutes for a 13 x 9-inch pan
demonstrations.review: My family really liked this recipe.  It was soooo quick and easy to throw together in the morning.  I chopped up some apples and threw it on top of the batter before adding the brown sugar and cinnamon.  Really Yummy!!! Thanks!

target.recipe_text:
my choc chip cookies

these are my favourite cookies & this is the only recipe i'll ever use because it's soooo good! i always end up adding more choc chips than called for.

1. set oven to 180c
2. sift flour& soda together , set aside
3. cream butter& sugars together until light& fluffy
4. add egg& vanilla , beat well
5. stir in sifted dry ingredients& choc chips , until well blended
6. form into small balls& place on greased baking trays- leaving room for spreading
7. bake in oven for 12- 15 minutes , until light& golden brown
8. cool on a wire rack& store in an airtight container
target.review: As a Brit this was my first attempt at a real, homemade cookie (as opposed to a biscuit..our version of cookies) and I couldn't be more pleased with the result. Quick and easy to make and the end product was  beautifully buttery! I used white choc chips this time but can't wait to experiment with other fillings.I followed other reviewers'advice and flattened the balls and the mixture made about 20 meduim sized cookies.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
sticky soy wings

a family favorite at the cabin.....

1. wash the chicken wings and dry as much as possible
2. preheat oven at 400 degrees
3. place chicken in a deep baking dish
4. mix all other ingredients together in a bowl
5. pour over chicken
6. place in oven or 1 1 / 2 hours or until chicken is done and sauce is sticky
7. important: due to the hot cooked sugar , chicken will be extra hot and easy to burn
8. be careful and let chicken sit for at least 15-20 minutes before serving
demonstrations.review: WOW-These are so tasty; really dark and sticky and full of flavour. The salt definitely isn't needed in my opinion due to all the soy and I may use heaped tablespoons of both garlic and ginger the next time I make them but there will absolutely be a next time and, I'm guessing, not too far in the future. Thanks for all the tips re lining the dish - it saved me a lot of scrubbing!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
yes  virginia there is a great meatloaf

absolutely delicious meatloaf and sauce! those who claim they don't believe there can be such a thing as a great meatloaf will love this. based on a meatloaf given to me by a dear friend, virginia strehl, memphis, and leesburg, fla. nita holleman, 2000

1. meatloaf: combine meat loaf ingredients and place into a loaf baking dish
2. smooth out top
3. sauce: combine sauce ingredients and pour on top and sides of meatloaf
4. bake at 350f about 1 hour to 1 hour 15 minutes or until done
5. enjoy !
6. the addition of 1 or 2 teaspoons of kitchen bouquet makes this recipe very good
7. recipe should be"plump" from the addition of the milk or half & half
8. it should not be runny
9. a second batch of sauce served hot is good to serve with the meatloaf
10. nita's
11. it is wise to have some fat added to the deer -- especially to ground deer
12. maybe 25 % fat , , otherwise your results will be poor
13. i don't know about some of the other game meat some are using
14. please consult an expert
15. the recipe is delicious as it stands ! enjoy ! nita holleman
demonstrations.review: We don't really have meatloaf in the UK, so I've never even tried it, let alone attempted to cook it. I went with this recipe because of all the fab reviews and because it appeared really easy. I followed the ingredients almost to the letter. The only change I made was to substitute mushroom soup for the cream as I didn't have any in (and I've not the first clue what half and half is! :0/)<br/>The result was very tasty, beautifully moist and so easy to prepare! I simmered the sauce before using it to make it richer and less acidic and it was the perfect combination to the meat. <br/>Quick, easy, tasty and cheap! Definitely a keeper!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
quick and easy pizza dough

a very quick way to make your own home-made pizza.  this dough rises up nice and has a very light flavour.  it can also be made in your bread machine on the 'dough' cycle.

1. mix 1 cup of flour with all other ingredients
2. gradually add 2nd cup of flour until it forms a ball
3. use your hands to form and knead the dough
4. let the dough rest 10-15 minutes in a bowl covered with a dish towel or saran to keep it warm
5. spread out onto greased pizza pan and top with your favorite toppings
6. bake at 375 degrees for approximately 15 minutes
7. enjoy !
demonstrations.review: Delicious pizza base! This is quick and pretty easy to make. The mixing in of the last cup of flour was quite difficult, I found it easier to tip the whole thing out onto a board and kneed it in. I also have no idea what the extra couple of tbsp of water is for, as it doesn't say, so I didn't use it. The end result is a little sweet but healthier for having less salt, so great for the kids! Otherwise this recipe is a cracker - super speedy and it rises beautifully. Thank you.
